Questions.Q: What information did Luke, the writer of this book, give in this introduction?
Questions.A: Luke reminded his readers that he was about to continue the true story about Jesus and his apostles that Luke had written in his first book. (1)
He also reminded his readers that Jesus had promised that his Father would send his followers the Holy Spirit. (5)

Questions.Q: What do you think an apostle of Jesus is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: To be an apostle of Jesus means to be a messenger/ambassador, who represents Jesus, who proclaims the message about Jesus.
Questions.Note: See "apostle" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to make a promise?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that someone will make a declaration that he will do or will refrain from doing something specified. (See "promise" in KBT in the "covenant" entry.)

Questions.Q: Who do you think the Holy Spirit is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He is God's spirit, through whom he acts, reveals His will, and empowers individuals. (See "Holy Spirit" in KBT in the "spirit" entry.)

Questions.Q: To whom did the writer of Acts address this book?
Questions.A: He addressed this book to a person whom he respected. The person's name was Theophilus. (1-2)

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason for a person or place to have a name?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A name is a label that identifies a person or place.
Questions.Note: See "name" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What had the writer written about in his first book?
Questions.A: In his first book the writer had told about all the things that Jesus did and taught while he lived on earth. (1-2)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do in the forty days just before he returned to heaven?
Questions.A: The Holy Spirit guided Jesus as Jesus gave the men, whom he had chosen as apostles, teaching/commands/instructions beyond what he had given them before that time. (1-3)

Questions.Q: How did the apostles of Jesus know that Jesus was truly alive again?
Questions.A: He showed himself to them many times in ways that convinced them that he was truly alive again. (3)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus talk to them about during those forty days?
Questions.A: He continued to teach them about the kingdom of God. (3)

Questions.Q: What do you think the kingdom of God is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The kingdom of God, rather than being a territory over which God rules, is the presence of God ruling in the lives of men.
Questions.Note: See "kingdom of God" in KBT.

Questions.Q: For what reason had Jesus again talked with his apostles about the kingdom of God?
Questions.A: Jesus was preparing the apostles to tell people about him in all parts of the earth. They would begin spreading the message about him after they received the Holy Spirit. (3)

Questions.Q: Who do you think God is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He is the supreme being to be worshiped. In English, the term "God" with a capital "G" is used to refer to the one supreme Creator. The term "god" with a small "g", as in "a god" or "many gods", can refer to any spiritual being that people worship. The Greek word theos can be used in the same two ways.
Questions.Note: In many languages the term for God is a proper name and cannot be used to refer to anyone except the one supreme creator of the world. It cannot be pluralized. (Or, if it can be pluralized, the meaning may be something very different from the English "gods". In one language, the plural form of God, meant "God and those who follow him" and was an appropriate way to translate "saints".) (See "God" in KBT.)

Questions.Q: For what reason did Jesus tell the apostles to wait in Jerusalem?
Questions.A: He told them to continue to wait in Jerusalem for a few days, until [God,] his Father, sent them the Holy Spirit. (4-5)

Questions.Q: To what did Jesus compare the coming of the Holy Spirit upon the apostles?
Questions.A: Jesus compared receiving the Holy Spirit to being baptized with water by John the Baptist. (4-5)

Questions.Q: What do you think happens when someone is baptized?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In ordinary language the Greek verb baptizô (and related words) had both literal and figurative uses. The literal sense of baptizô was "to plunge or drench or immerse something", usually in water. In religious contexts, however, it came to have two more specific senses:
(a) To wash someone or something in or with water to make him or it ceremonially clean.

(b) To wash someone in or with water as part of their initiation into the religious community. When a person is baptized he is showing publicly his commitment to and union with Jesus Christ. (See "baptize, baptism" in KBT.)

Questions.Q: Can you think of a reason for which Jesus implied that when the apostles received the Holy Spirit, it was going to be like when John baptized them?
Questions.A: In both cases, what the apostles received was a sign that they were beginning a new way of life. (5)
Questions.Note: The fact that Jesus used the word "baptize" for both events implies that they are/were similar.

Section.heading: Acts 1:6-11 Jesus was taken up to heaven [by God].

Questions.Q: What question did the apostles ask Jesus about his kingdom?
Questions.A: The apostles asked Jesus whether he was soon going to set up his kingdom in a way that everybody could see. He would cause the people of Israel to have power in that kingdom. (6)

Questions.Q: What do you know about the name "Israel"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In the New Testament, the terms "Israel" and "Israelite" are used by Jews to refer to themselves, and also by God to refer to them as his people.
Questions.Note: See "Israel" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to the apostles when they asked this question?
Questions.A: Jesus did not tell the apostles when the kingdom would be given back to the people of Israel. He said that his Father had set the time at which that would happen. (7)

Questions.Q: How would the apostles be able to continue to act as the representatives of Jesus Christ after he was no longer among them?
Questions.A: After Jesus left the earth, he would send the Holy Spirit to be with his apostles, and the Spirit would give them power. Jesus then gave the apostles a commission to be his witnesses in all of the inhabited world as they knew it. (8)

Questions.Q: What happened after Jesus told his apostles that they would be his witnesses?
Questions.A: Jesus was taken up to heaven [by God] as the apostles watched him disappear into a cloud. (9)

Questions.Q: Where do you think heaven is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It is that part of God's creation above the earth and the waters, including "air" and "space," and serves as home for God and the spirits who serve Him.
Questions.Note: See "heaven" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did the apostles think Jesus would do soon?
Questions.A: They thought that Jesus would set up the kingdom of God in a way that everyone could see. (6)
Questions.Note: The apostles thought that God would soon cause the Romans, who ruled over Palestine, to be driven away. They thought, in that way the nation of Israel would be free.

Questions.Q: Who did they think would then rule over Israel?
Questions.A: They thought that God (or perhaps Jesus, the Messiah) would then rule the Jewish nation. (6)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell the apostles in his answer?
Questions.A: Jesus told them that they did not need to know when events, that they thought were important, would take place. Only his Father decides at what time each event in this world will take place. (7)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell the apostles would happen within a short time?
Questions.A: He told them that they would receive the Holy Spirit, and when they received Him, they would also receive power. (8)

Questions.Q: What would the apostles do after they received the Holy Spirit?
Questions.A: They would witness to many people about Jesus. (8)

Questions.Q: To what places did Jesus tell the apostles that they would go after they had received the Holy Spirit?
Questions.A: Jesus told the apostles that they would be his witnesses in Jerusalem [where they were at that time] in all of Judea, in Samaria, and in the places of the world that were farthest away. (8)
Questions.Note: See Luke 24:47-48.

Questions.Q: Jesus had told the apostles that they were to be witnesses for him in many parts of the world. For what reason or reasons could the apostles know that Jesus would not return to earth immediately?
Questions.A: They were to witness about him in places that were close and also places that were far away. (8)

Questions.Q: What happened immediately after Jesus said that?
Questions.A: The apostles saw Jesus rise up into the air. Then a cloud covered him and he had completely disappeared. (9)

Questions.Q: Whom did the apostles see next?
Questions.A: They saw two men dressed in white standing beside them. (10)

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that the apostles kept looking up into the sky where Jesus was taken up into heaven [by God]?
Questions.Note: They may have thought that Jesus would reappear suddenly. They probably were surprised and wondered what they should do.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think is the reason that the apostles kept looking up into the sky where Jesus was taken up into heaven by God?
What do you think is the reason that the apostles kept looking up into the sky where Jesus was taken up into heaven?

Questions.Q: What did the two heavenly messengers say about the return of Jesus to the earth?
Questions.A: They said that Jesus would return to the earth in the same way that he had gone up into heaven. (11)

Section.heading: Acts 1:12-26 The disciples of Jesus chose an apostle to replace Judas Iscariot.

Questions.Q: What did the apostles do first after Jesus had been taken up into heaven [by God]?
Questions.A: After Jesus had ascended into heaven, the apostles returned to Jerusalem and gathered in the room where they had been staying, along with several women who were believers in Jesus. They prayed together there. After that, they chose a man to replace Judas Iscariot as an apostle. (13, 14, 21-26)
Questions.Alternative: What did the apostles do first after Jesus had been taken up into heaven by God?
What did the apostles do first after Jesus had been taken up into heaven?

Questions.Q: From what place did Jesus go up again into heaven?
Questions.A: Jesus went up into heaven from the Mount of Olives. (12)

Questions.Q: Where did the apostles go after they left the Mount of Olives?
Questions.A: The apostles returned to the upper room of a house in Jerusalem, where they had been staying. (12-13)

Questions.Q: What people were in the group that joined together frequently to pray?
Questions.A: All eleven of the apostles were in the group staying there. They were Peter, John, James and Andrew, Philip and Thomas, Bartholomew and Matthew, James the son of Alphaeus, Simon the Zealot, and Judas the son of James.
Certain women [who had given help to Jesus and the apostles during Jesus's life on earth] were in that group.
Mary the mother of Jesus, and Jesus's brothers [that is, his half-brothers], were also there. (13-14)

Questions.Q: Soon after that, Peter addressed a group of people who had believed in Jesus Christ. About how many believers were there?
Questions.A: There were about one hundred and twenty believers in that group. (15)

Questions.Q: What did Peter say about the fact that Judas Iscariot had betrayed Jesus?
Questions.A: He said that a long time previously David had foretold that someone would betray a close companion or friend. David had been guided by the Holy Spirit to write that in the Scriptures. (16)

Questions.Q: To what do you think the writer of this book was referring as "scripture"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The scriptures are the contents of the Old Testament as God gave them to men to write down.
Questions.Note: See "scripture" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What position or work did Judas Iscariot have?
Questions.A: Peter said that Judas had been one of Jesus's apostles. (17)

Questions.Q: How did Peter describe the death of Judas?
Questions.A: He said that Judas had bought a field, and in that field he had fallen violently, so that his body had burst open. (18)

Questions.Q: What did the people, who lived in Jerusalem, call the field in which Judas died?
Questions.A: In the language that they spoke, they called it Akeldama, which means Field of Blood. (19)

Questions.Q: From which part of the Old Testament did Peter quote?
Questions.A: Peter quoted from one of the Psalms. (20)

Questions.Q: What is the meaning of the first part of the Psalm from which Peter quoted?
Questions.A: That part of the Psalm means that the house of the person referred to would be deserted. No one would live there anymore. (20)

Questions.Q: What is the meaning of the second part of the quotation?
Questions.A: It means that someone else would do the work that the other person had done. (20)

Questions.Q: How did Peter apply each of these quotations to Judas?
Questions.A: Since Judas was dead, it was necessary for Peter and the other apostles to choose someone else to be an apostle of Jesus. (21)

Questions.Q: What did Peter say would be required of any believer to be chosen as an apostle to replace Judas? [Your answer should include two points.]
Questions.A: He must be a man who was a witness of the fact that Jesus had risen from death.
He must have been a man who kept company with Jesus from the time that John the Baptist was baptizing people until Jesus was taken up [by God] to heaven. (21-22)
Questions.Alternative: What did Peter say would be required of any believer to be chosen as an apostle to replace Judas? Your answer should include two points.
What did Peter say would be required of any believer to be chosen as an apostle to replace Judas?

Questions.Q: Which of these requirements did Judas Iscariot not meet?
Questions.A: Because Judas killed himself, he was not a witness of the resurrection of Jesus. Also Judas had not been present when the other apostles saw Jesus going up to heaven. (18, 21-22)

Questions.Q: What were the names of the two men who [the believers] nominated as people who might be able to replace Judas Iscariot?
Questions.A: The two men whose names they suggested were Joseph, also known as Barsabbas or as Justus, and Matthias. (23)
Questions.Alternative: What were the names of the two men who the believers nominated as people who might be able to replace Judas Iscariot?
What were the names of the two men who nominated as people who might be able to replace Judas Iscariot?

Questions.Q: The believers did two things to find out which of the two men should become an apostle. What two things did they do?
Questions.A: They prayed that God would show them which man he chose,
and after that they cast lots. (24, 26)
Questions.Alternative: What two things did the believers do to find out which of the two men should become an apostle?
What did the believers do to find out which of the two men should become an apostle?
Questions.Note: Casting lots was the usual way in that culture to decide certain kinds of questions. When they prayed, they were probably asking God to cause the lot to come out for the man that he would choose to be an apostle.

Questions.Q: The believers [then prayed and] said that Judas had abandoned his position as an apostle of Jesus. What else did they say [about Judas], and what did that mean?
Questions.A: They said that Judas had left [his position of being an apostle and died] to go where he belonged. (25)
Questions.Alternative: The believers then prayed and said that Judas had abandoned his position as an apostle of Jesus. What else did they say about Judas, and what did that mean?
The believers then prayed and said that Judas had abandoned his position as an apostle of Jesus. What else did they say, and what did that mean?
The believers said that Judas had abandoned his position as an apostle of Jesus. What else did they say, and what did that mean?
The believers said that Judas had abandoned his position as an apostle of Jesus. What else did they say about Judas, and what did that mean?
Questions.Note: Most commentators agree that this refers to Judas' place in eternal damnation, though some interpreters have taken this expression to refer to Mathias' place in apostolic office.

Questions.Q: Which of the two men who [the believers] had named was chosen to be an apostle?
Questions.A: The name of Matthias was chosen, so he joined the other eleven apostles. (26)
Questions.Note: The method people used at that time to cast lots was to put objects with names on them into a container. Then someone would shake the container until one of the objects fell out of it. The name on that object was considered to show which person was chosen.
Questions.Alternative: Which of the two men who the believers had named was chosen to be an apostle?
Which of the two men who had named was chosen to be an apostle?

Section.heading: Acts 2:1-13 The Holy Spirit came upon the believers.

Questions.Q: What promise, which Jesus had given the apostles, was fulfilled after he ascended to where his Father was?
Questions.A: Jesus had promised the apostles that after he had ascended to where his Father was, he would send the Holy Spirit to be with his followers. (1-4)

Questions.Q: Where were the believers on the Day of Pentecost?
Questions.A: The believers were all together in one place, apparently in the house where they had been staying. (1-2)
Questions.Note: The Jews celebrated the Day of Pentecost fifty days after the Feast of the Passover. Jesus had been crucified during the Feast of the Passover, so it was fifty days since Jesus had been crucified. About ten days after Jesus ascended to heaven, the Feast of Pentecost took place.

Questions.Q: On the day of Pentecost, what did the believers hear?
Questions.A: They heard a sound like a strong wind blowing. The sound filled the house where they were sitting. (2)
Questions.Alternative: What did the believers hear?

Questions.Q: What did they see?
Questions.A: They saw a fire coming that separated into many small flames that looked like tongues of fire. Each of these tongues came down upon the heads of the believers and rested there, one upon the head of each believer. (3)
Questions.Alternative: What did the believers see?

Questions.Q: What caused these unusual sights and sounds?
Questions.A: The Holy Spirit caused these unusual sounds and sights. (2-4)

Questions.Q: What other sign was there which showed that the Holy Spirit was present?
Questions.A: The Holy Spirit caused each of the believers to speak in some language that he had never learned. (4)

Questions.Q: What people other than the believers were also in Jerusalem at that time?
Questions.A: Many Jews and some Gentiles who had converted to the Jewish religion were in Jerusalem at that time. (5)

Questions.Q: What do you know about Jews?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A Jew was a member of the nation of Palestine from the 6th century B.C. to the first century A.D. It refers to the descendants of Abraham through his son Isaac. A Jew was a member of the people of Israel. He was committed to the Jewish religious system. All male Jews were circumcised on the 8th day after their birth and this was a mark of being a Jew. (See "Jew" in KBT in the "Israel" entry.)

Questions.Q: From where had these other Jews come?
Questions.A: They had come from all the countries that were known to be inhabited at that time. Probably they had come from most of the parts of the Roman Empire. (5)

Questions.Q: What caused these many visitors from other countries to come to the place where the believers were assembled?
Questions.A: They heard a loud sound and went quickly to the place where the believers were assembled. (6)
Questions.Note: The phrase "this sound/noise" refers back to the believers speaking in other tongues.

Questions.Q: What surprised the crowd of visitors who had come to the place where the believers, who had received the Holy Spirit, had gathered?
Questions.A: The people in the crowd were bewildered, because they heard those believers speaking in many languages that were not their native languages. (6)

Questions.Q: When the many people had come to where the believers were gathered, what did they think about what they saw and heard?
Questions.A: They were amazed and wondered how the believers, who were all from Galilee (province), were able to speak in many different languages. (6b-8)

Questions.Q: From what different nationalities and language groups had these visitors to Jerusalem come?
Questions.A: The visitors to Jerusalem had come from Parthia, Media, Elam, Mesopotamia, Judea, Cappadocia, Pontus, Asia (not present-day Asia), Phrygia, Pamphylia, Egypt, Libya which is near Cyrene, and even from Rome. The visitors from Rome were Jews and Gentiles converted to Judaism. Some of the people who had come lived on the island of Crete and some of them lived in the region of Arabia.
These visitors spoke the many languages that people spoke in those many places. (9-11a)

Questions.Q: What did these many visitors hear the believers speaking about in the languages that the visitors spoke?
Questions.A: They heard the believers speaking in each of the languages of the visitors, telling about the wonderful things God had done. (11b)

Questions.Q: What did the visitors think and say about what they heard?
Questions.A: They were surprised and puzzled, and they asked one another, "What does this mean?" (12)

Questions.Q: What did some of the visitors say about the believers who were speaking in different languages?
Questions.A: Some of the visitors made fun of them/laughed at them and said that the believers were probably drunk/had too much wine. (13)

Section.heading: Acts 2:14-41 Peter preached to the crowd about Jesus Christ.

Questions.Q: What did Peter do to explain to the crowd that had gathered the strange event that they were seeing and hearing?
Questions.A: Peter told the crowd that the Holy Spirit had come upon God's people and caused the signs that they were seeing and hearing. Peter cited a passage from the prophecy of Joel that foretold that some unusual things would happen when God sent his Spirit upon many of his people.

Questions.Q: About what time was it when Peter began speaking to the crowd?
Questions.A: It was about nine o'clock in the morning. (14-15)

Questions.Q: What did Peter tell the crowd to show that the believers were not drunk?
Questions.A: He said it was only nine o'clock in the morning. (15)
Questions.Note: He mentioned the time because Jewish people did not drink wine in the morning. Therefore, it was not possible for the believers to be drunk at that time of day.

Questions.Q: What did Peter say about the prophet Joel?
Questions.A: Peter said that the prophet Joel had predicted the unusual things that were happening on that day. That is, Joel had said that God would send his Spirit upon many people. (16-18)

Questions.Q: What do you know about prophets?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A prophet is someone who speaks for God and is inspired by Him. He often foretells future events. Prophets were mainly spokespersons who called His people to obedience by appealing to Israel's past and future.
Questions.Note: See "prophet" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think someone is doing when they prophesy?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: When someone prophesies they speak out a direct message from God. (See "prophesy" in KBT in the "prophet" entry.)

Questions.Q: To what period of time had the prophet Joel referred?
Questions.A: The events that Joel had prophesied would take place "in the last days." (17)
Questions.Note: A respondent might also identify the time period as the time in which these events were taking place, since Peter says that the events were a fulfillment of this prophecy.

Questions.Q: What had God promised to do "in the last days"?
Questions.A: God promised to send his Spirit down upon all of the people [who believed in and honored him].
God promised to send his Spirit upon men and also women, upon young people and also old people. (17-18)

Questions.Q: What did the prophet Joel say would happen when the people of God received his Spirit?
Questions.A: When these many people of God received the Holy Spirit, they would prophesy. That is, God's Spirit would cause them all to speak messages that he would give them. (18)

Questions.Q: What parts of the quotation from Joel did Peter say were being fulfilled at the time that he was speaking?
Questions.A: Peter told the crowd that the believers were speaking in languages they had not learned because the Holy Spirit had come down upon them. They were prophesying, as Joel had foretold. (17-18)
Questions.Alternative: What parts of the quotation from Joel were being fulfilled at the time that Peter was speaking?
Questions.Note: The Greek, and most N.T. versions, use "Spirit." The Living Bible uses "Holy Spirit."

Questions.Q: What other kinds of signs and wonders did Joel predict would happen?
Questions.A: Strange things would happen up in the sky and also on earth. (19)

Questions.Q: What do you think "signs" are?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Miraculous signs show that something important is going to happen in the world.
Questions.Note: See "sign" in KBT in the "miracle" entry.

Questions.Q: What kind of things causes people's blood to be shed and many fires to burn?
Questions.A: In times of war, many people shed their blood.
Buildings are burned, and sometimes fields of crops are burned causing a lot of smoke.
Some of these things happen also at the time of natural disasters such as earthquakes.
When there are revolutions, people may do violent acts, causing destruction. (19b)

Questions.Q: What strange things would happen up in the sky?
Questions.A: The sun would give much less light than usually, and the moon would appear to be red, so it also would not give much light. (20a)

Questions.Q: When would these "signs" and "wonders" happen?
Questions.A: These things would happen before the time which Joel called "the day of the Lord." (20b)

Questions.Q: What did Joel mean by "the day of the Lord"?
Questions.A: "The day of the Lord" means the time when God will judge all people for what they have done while they lived on earth. (20b)

Questions.Q: When would these events about which Joel prophesied take place [in relation to the "day of the Lord"]?
Questions.A: All of the events that Peter mentioned in what he quoted from the prophet Joel would take place before the "day of the Lord." They would happen before the time when God judges people for what they have done. (20b)
Questions.Alternative: When would these events about which Joel prophesied take place in relation to the "day of the Lord"?
When would these events about which Joel prophesied take place?

Questions.Q: What statement that Joel made did Peter use as the most important fact that he quoted from this prophecy?
Questions.A: Joel also said that before the "day of the Lord," everyone who calls on the name of the Lord would be saved by him/the Lord would save everyone who calls upon his name. (21)

Questions.Q: What does it mean to you to have someone as your lord?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A lord is someone who has power and exercises it responsibly. To call someone your lord means that you have given him control over your life. The Lord in this case is Jesus. Every Christian strives to make Jesus lord in his or her life by giving Him complete control. (See "Lord" in KBT in the "God" entry.)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to save you?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that a person will rescue someone else out of a dangerous situation.
Questions.Note: See "save" in KBT.

Questions.Q: When Peter said "the name of the Lord," to whom was he referring?
Questions.A: He was referring to Jesus Christ. (21)

Questions.Q: About what had many of the people in the crowd of Jews either seen or heard?
Questions.A: They had heard that a man from Nazareth whose name was Jesus had done many miracles. (22)

Questions.Q: What could those people have known about Jesus because of the many miracles that he did?
Questions.A: They could have known that God had sent Jesus as his special personal representative. (22)

Questions.Q: What do you think a miracle is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A miracle is an unusual event that can only be explained as a special action by God.
Questions.Note: See "miracle" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Whom did Peter say had caused Jesus to be killed?
Questions.A: Peter said that the Jews used the help of godless men to have Jesus killed by nailing him to a cross. (23b)

Questions.Q: What do you know about the cross?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The cross was constructed of two pieces of wood. One piece was a thick wooden post, which was placed/planted upright into a hole in the ground. The other piece was the crossbeam, which was fastened across the upright post so that it formed a + or T shape.
Questions.Note: See "cross" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What else did Peter say about the death of Jesus?
Questions.A: He also said that God had planned in advance that Jesus should be killed by his own people in that way. (23a)

Questions.Q: Which of these two things that Peter said did the Jews already know?
Questions.A: They knew that they were responsible for having the Roman authorities kill Jesus. (23)

Questions.Q: As Peter reminded the Jewish crowd that they had killed Jesus, what did he tell them that they had not known before?
Questions.A: They did not know that God had known beforehand that God had a purpose in allowing them to kill Jesus. (23)

Questions.Q: In what way did God show that Jesus was much more than a very good man to whom he had given special power?
Questions.A: After three days, God raised Jesus to life again. (24)

Questions.Q: What final statement did Peter make here about the death of Jesus?
Questions.A: He said that it was not possible for Jesus to remain dead. (24)

Questions.Q: What was the reason that it was not possible for Jesus to remain dead?
Questions.A: Although Jesus was a human being, he was the Messiah. He was not like all the rest of human beings who die and whose bodies decay. For that reason, it was not possible for him to remain dead. (24b)

Questions.Q: In the verses which Peter quoted, to whom does the phrase "the Lord" refer?
Questions.A: In these verses "the Lord" refers to God the Father. (25-28)

Questions.Q: In these verses, whom did David represent as the person who was speaking to "the Lord"?
Questions.A: David wrote as though a person called the "Holy One" was speaking to God the Father. (25-28)

Questions.Q: To whom does the phrase "your Holy One" refer?
Questions.A: It is referring to the Messiah. (27)
Questions.Note: See Mark 1:24b, John 6:69.

Questions.Q: In what part of these verses was David clearly not speaking about himself?
Questions.A: When David said, "because you will not abandon me to the grave, nor will you let your Holy One see decay," he was not speaking about himself. (27)

Questions.Q: What did Peter mention to prove that David was not speaking about himself as the Lord's "Holy One"?
Questions.A: Peter said that David had died and his body had been buried [by the people]. Everyone knew that because David's tomb was in Jerusalem. (29)

Questions.Q: How was it possible for David to write something that would be true of the Messiah?
Questions.A: David was a prophet, and therefore the Holy Spirit enabled him to speak about what would happen to the Messiah. (30)
Questions.Note: The Messiah would come into the world many centuries after David had died.

Questions.Q: What promise had God made to David that Peter referred to in this address?
Questions.A: God had promised David that one of his descendants would be a king, just as David was. (30)

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that it was necessary that God should raise Jesus to life again?
Questions.A: The Jews believed that if Jesus had remained dead, that would have proved that he was not the Messiah. (31-32a)
Questions.Note: Many Jews knew that in certain parts of the Old Testament, God had promised that the Messiah would live forever. Some of the Jews asked Jesus whether this was not true. See John 12:34.

Questions.Q: When Peter said, "we are all witnesses to this fact," to whom did Peter refer?
Questions.A: Peter referred at least to himself and the other eleven apostles. Some of the other believers who were included in the 120 mentioned in 1:15 may also have seen Jesus after he had risen from death. (32)
Questions.Note: See 1 Corinthians 15:6.

Questions.Q: After stating that Jesus had truly come alive again and had been seen by many witnesses, Peter said two other things about Christ. What did he say about him?
Questions.A: Peter said that God the Father had placed Jesus at his right side in heaven. This gave Jesus authority to rule along with his Father. (33)

Questions.Q: Peter included a statement about God the Father and one about the Holy Spirit. What did he say about each of these Persons?
Questions.A: Peter said that God the Father had promised that he would send the Holy Spirit to those who believed in Jesus.
The Father gave Jesus the Holy Spirit, authorizing him to send the Holy Spirit down upon the believers. This fulfilled the word about Jesus that John the Baptist had told his followers. (33)
Questions.Note: See Luke 3:16.

Questions.Q: What reason did Peter state for the unusual things that the believers were doing at that time?
Questions.A: Peter said that the unusual sights and sounds were caused by the Holy Spirit controlling, or "filling," the believers.

It was the Spirit who sent down what appeared to be tongues of fire that rested upon the believers' heads. It was also the Spirit who caused them to speak clearly and understandably in languages they had never learned. (33b)

Questions.Q: What did Peter say about David in the Psalm from which he quoted?
Questions.A: Peter pointed out that David could not have been speaking about himself, because David had not ascended into heaven. (34b-35)

Questions.Q: In the verses that Peter quoted from the Psalm, whom did David say spoke, and to whom did that person speak?
Questions.A: David wrote that a person whom he described as "The Lord" spoke to another person, whom David described as "my Lord." When David said "The Lord," he meant God the Father. When David said "my Lord" he meant a different person who was also David's superior in authority. The person whom David described as his Lord was the Messiah. Therefore, these verses tell what God the Father said to the Messiah. (34b-35)

Questions.Q: What did God the Father say to the one whom David described as "my Lord"?
Questions.A: God the Father told the Messiah to sit at his right hand until God had put all of the Messiah's enemies under his feet. (34b-35)

Questions.Q: What did God mean when he said, "Sit at my right hand"?
Questions.A: This meant that God was giving the Messiah the place of authority closest to him. (34d)

Questions.Q: What did God mean when he said he would put all of the Messiah's enemies under his feet?
Questions.A: God meant that he would conquer all the Messiah's enemies and make them helpless. (35)

Questions.Q: Peter then explained what those verses from the Psalm meant. What did they mean about Jesus?
Questions.A: Peter used this portion of the Psalm to prove that God had shown that Jesus was the Messiah and had made him Lord. That is, God had given Jesus the place of authority next to his own. (36)

Questions.Q: What did Peter want the people, who were listening, to know for sure?
Questions.A: He wanted them to know for sure that God had made this Jesus both Lord and Christ.
He wanted them to know for sure that this was the same Jesus that they had [caused to be] crucified. (36)

Questions.Q: What do you think is the meaning of "Christ"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "Christ" is the English rendering of the Greek word Christos, which means "anointed one."
Questions.Note: See "Christ" in KBT.

Questions.Q: How did the people who heard the message about Jesus Christ react?
Questions.A: They were overcome with feelings of guilt and asked what they should do. (37)

Questions.Q: What did Peter answer to the question "Brothers, what shall we do?"
Questions.A: He told the people to repent and to believe in Jesus as their Messiah and to be baptized [by the apostles]. (38)

Questions.Q: When Peter told the people that they must repent, of what do you think he meant that they should repent?
Questions.A: Peter meant that they should repent of their sins/stop their sinful ways. (38)
Questions.Note: The specific sin that the people had committed was rejecting Jesus and asking that he be killed on the cross.

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when someone repents?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The verb "to repent" and the noun "repentance" refer to the act of deliberately turning away from sin, expressing sorrow for past sins, and determining not to sin any more.
Questions.Note: See "repent" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What does a person do when he sins?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He disobeys God. He deliberately keeps on doing those things that please himself and displease God.
Questions.Note: See "sin" in KBT.

Questions.Q: When the people had done the things that Peter told them to do, what would be the result?
Questions.A: If they would repent of their sins, believe that Jesus was the Christ, and be baptized, [God] would forgive their sins and would give them the Holy Spirit to be with them. (38)

Questions.Q: What do you think happens when someone forgives someone else?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Forgiveness always involves two people, one of whom has done something wrong to the other and offended him. Forgiveness takes place when the one, who was offended, sets aside his right to justice and decides not to punish the offender, as he deserved. If the one who offended repents and accepts this forgiveness, the result is that the relationship between the two, which was broken by the offense, is restored and the guilt of the offender is removed.
Questions.Note: See "forgive" in KBT.

Questions.Q: To whom had God promised that he would send the Holy Spirit?
Questions.A: God had promised to send the Holy Spirit to all of his people. The people to whom Peter was speaking had shown that they were God's people by believing in Jesus as the Messiah. (39)

Questions.Q: To what other people had God promised to send the Holy Spirit?
Questions.A: Peter said that the promise of the Holy Spirit was to all believers and their children, also to many others who were at that time "far off." (39b)

Questions.Q: What else did Peter say about the people to whom God would send the Holy Spirit?
Questions.A: He said that God would call all of those people, [and this implied that all of them would believe in Jesus]. (39b)
Questions.Alternative: What is the common thing between all those who receive God's promise of the Holy Spirit?

Questions.Q: What else did Peter exhort the people listening to do?
Questions.A: He urged them to save themselves from "this corrupt generation." (40)

Questions.Q: To whom did Peter refer in this way?
Questions.A: He referred to the generation in which the people present lived. (40)

Questions.Q: What had those people done which showed that they were corrupt?
Questions.A: They rejected Jesus as the Messiah and asked for him to be crucified. Although God restored him to life, they refused to believe in him. (40)

Questions.Q: About how many people believed Peter's message about Jesus?
Questions.A: About three thousand people believed the message about Jesus and received him as their Messiah. (41)

Questions.Q: What did these new believers do which showed that they had committed themselves to believing in Jesus Christ?
Questions.A: They were baptized [by the disciples]. (41)

Section.heading: Acts 2:42-47 The believers lived as a united group and cared for one another.

Questions.Q: How could people tell that the believers were directed by the Holy Spirit?
Questions.A: The way the believers lived together showed that the Holy Spirit directed them. They cared for and helped one another as though they all belonged to the same family.

Questions.Q: What were some of the things the new believers did frequently to show that they really believed in Jesus Christ?
Questions.A: They went often to hear the apostles preach.
They joined with the other believers to pray and to eat together.
When they ate together, they frequently celebrated the Lord's Supper. (42)

Questions.Q: What signs did [God] give to show that he authorized the message that the apostles taught?
Questions.A: [God] enabled the apostles to do miracles, and many people heard about those miracles. (43)
Questions.Alternative: What signs did God give to show that he authorized the message that the apostles taught?
What signs did God to through the apostles to show that he authorized the message they taught?
What signs were done through the apostles?
What signs did the apostles do to show that their message was authorized by God?
What signs did the apostles do to show that their message was from God?

Questions.Q: What did the people who heard about those miracles think about the believers?
Questions.A: They very much respected the believers, and they feared God. They were convinced that God was giving power to the apostles to do miracles. (43)

Questions.Q: What did the believers do with their possessions?
Questions.A: Those who had more than they needed shared with others who had less than they needed. They sold some of their possessions and gave them to those who did not have enough of the things that they needed. (44-45)

Questions.Q: Where did the believers meet together every day?
Questions.A: Every day they met together in the temple courts. (46)

Questions.Q: For what do you think a temple is to be used by people?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The people were supposed to use the temple as a place to worship God.
Questions.Note: See "temple" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: For what purpose do you think people used a temple?
For what do you think the temple is to be used by people?
For what purpose do you think people used the temple?
What was the purpose of the temple?
How do you think people used the temple?

Questions.Q: What did they do in their homes?
Questions.A: They frequently ate together, observing the Lord's Supper, and they praised God. (46-47a)

Questions.Q: What resulted from the way the believers lived and shared with one another?
Questions.A: All the people were favorably impressed about the believers.
For this reason, every day, people who had not yet believed in Jesus Christ believed in him and joined the group of believers. (47b)

Section.heading: Acts 3:1-10 Peter healed a lame beggar at a gate of the temple.

Questions.Q: What did Peter do for a lame beggar who the writer described in these verses?
Questions.A: With the power and in the name of Jesus, Peter healed a lame beggar. (6-7)

Questions.Q: Whom did Peter and John see as they arrived at the gate of the temple that was called "Beautiful"?
Questions.A: They saw a lame beggar who was sitting there. (4)

Questions.Q: How had the lame man arrived there?
Questions.A: Every day, friends or relatives of the man carried him to the Beautiful gate and put him there. (2)

Questions.Q: What did he do there?
Questions.A: He begged for money from the people who were about to go into the temple courts. (2b)

Questions.Q: What did Peter and John do when the lame man asked them for money?
Questions.A: Peter and John looked directly at the lame man. Peter told the lame man to look at them. (4)

Questions.Q: What did the lame man expect?
Questions.A: He was expecting to get something (money or perhaps food) from them. (4)

Questions.Q: What did Peter tell the man next?
Questions.A: Peter told the lame man that he did not have any money, but he would do what he could to help him. (6b)

Questions.Q: How did Peter help the lame man?
Questions.A: Peter spoke to the lame man with the authority and name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth and told him to walk.
He grasped the man's right hand and helped him to stand on his feet. (6b-7a)

Questions.Q: What did the writer state in these verses that suggests that the lame man also believed that Jesus had power to heal?
Questions.A: When Peter commanded him in the name of Jesus to walk and took him by the hand, the cripple jumped to his feet and began to walk. (7- 8)
Questions.Alternative: What did the writer state in these verses that suggests that the cripple also believed that Jesus had power to heal?

Questions.Q: What else happened that showed that Jesus had healed the man?
Questions.A: The bones of his feet and ankles became strong. (7b)

Questions.Q: What did the man do right away when he was healed?
Questions.A: He jumped to his feet and went with Peter and John into the temple courts, jumping for joy. He also praised God. (8b)

Questions.Q: What did the other worshipers think when they saw the man walking, jumping, and praising God?
Questions.A: The other worshipers were amazed, because they recognized the man as the person who for many years had been a lame beggar. (9-10)
Questions.Alternative: What did the other worshippers think when they saw the man walking, jumping, and praising God?
What did the people think when they saw the man walking, jumping, and praising God?

Section.heading: Acts 3:11-26 Peter spoke to the people who had gathered there.

Questions.Q: In what way did Peter begin to spread the message of Jesus to the people of Jerusalem who gathered at the temple?
Questions.A: A curious crowd of people had witnessed the miracle of the lame beggar being healed. Peter told the crowd that he and John had not healed the lame man. Jesus, by his power, had healed him. Then Peter preached to the crowd about Jesus.

Questions.Q: What did the rest of the worshipers do?
Questions.A: They all ran to where Peter and John and the healed beggar were. (11)
Questions.Alternative: What did the rest of the worshippers do?
What did the rest of the people do?
What did the people do?
What did all the people do?

Questions.Q: In what part of the temple courts were they?
Questions.A: They were in a porch that was called Solomon's Colonnade. (11)

Questions.Q: What else did the other worshipers do?
Questions.A: They stared at Peter and John and also at the man who had been healed [by Jesus]. (12a)
Questions.Alternative: What else did the other worshippers do?
What else did the other people do?
What else did the people do?
What else did the people do to show their surprise?
How were the people looking at Peter and John?
How were the people looking at Peter and John and the man who had been healed?

Questions.Q: Who did the crowd of people think had healed the man who had been a cripple?
Questions.A: They thought that Peter and John had healed him. (12b)

Questions.Q: What did Peter tell the crowd?
Questions.A: He told them that he and John did not have power to have healed the man. Also, they should not think that because he and John were very godly, they had by themselves been able to heal the man. (12b)

Questions.Q: As Peter talked to the crowd of people, how did he refer to God?
Questions.A: He referred to God as the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. He also called God "the God of our fathers." (13)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Peter called Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob "our fathers"?
Questions.A: Peter and John and the people in the crowd were all Jews, so Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob were their ancestors. (13)

Questions.Q: What did Peter mean when he said that "the God of our fathers has glorified his servant Jesus"?
Questions.A: Peter meant that God had shown that Jesus was "his servant" by healing the cripple in the name of Jesus. (13)

Questions.Q: Of what action did Peter remind the people who were listening?
Questions.A: He reminded the people that they had disowned Jesus and asked Pilate to have him killed. (13-14)

Questions.Q: What did Peter say about Pilate?
Questions.A: He said that Pilate had decided to free Jesus, but the Jews demanded that Pilate say he should be killed. (13)

Questions.Q: What other titles did Peter use to refer to Jesus?
Questions.A: He referred to Jesus as "the Holy and Righteous One." (14)

Questions.Q: What did that title mean to the Jews?
Questions.A: "The Holy and Righteous One" was a title for the Messiah. (14)

Questions.Q: What did Peter say next about Jesus?
Questions.A: He said that they had killed "the author of life," but God had raised him up to life again. (15)

Questions.Q: What did Peter say next about Jesus?
Questions.A: He said that "through faith in the name of Jesus" the man who had been a crippled beggar had been made strong. (16)

Questions.Q: What did Peter mean by "faith in the name of Jesus"?
Questions.A: Peter meant that [the crippled man and Peter and John] had believed that Jesus was powerful and was able to heal people. (16a)
Questions.Note: See comments on this verse in T.N. on Acts.

Questions.Q: What was the reason that the Jews and their religious leaders demanded that Jesus be killed?
Questions.A: They had demanded that Jesus be killed because they did not know that he was their Messiah. (17)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that God allowed this to happen?
Questions.A: God allowed this to happen because it was his plan that the Messiah should be killed. (18)

Questions.Q: How was it possible to know before Jesus was crucified that God had planned that it would happen?
Questions.A: Many years before Jesus came into the world, God caused the prophets to write about the Messiah. They wrote that he would suffer unjustly. (18b)

Questions.Q: What did Peter next tell the crowd to do?
Questions.A: He told them to recognize that they had sinned in rejecting their Messiah, so they should repent and ask God to forgive them. (19)

Questions.Q: What did Peter say the result would be if they repented and turned to God?
Questions.A: He said that God would forgive them and would refresh their souls. (19)

Questions.Q: What else did Peter say that God would do?
Questions.A: He said that God would send Jesus [back to the earth]. (20)

Questions.Q: When will God send Jesus Christ back to earth?
Questions.A: God will send Jesus Christ back to earth when it is time for him to restore everything to the state that he has planned for it. (21)

Questions.Q: What reason do we have to believe this will happen?
Questions.A: Long ago God promised to do that and he chose prophets to tell that to people. // The prophets wrote in the Scriptures of the Old Testament that God will in the future restore the world to the perfect condition that he has planned for it. (21)

Questions.Q: Whom did Peter mention next as a prophet?
Questions.A: Peter next spoke about Moses. (22)

Questions.Q: What had Moses promised that God would do?
Questions.A: Moses promised the Israelites that God would send them a prophet who would be an Israelite also. (22)

Questions.Q: What else did Moses say about that prophet whom God would send?
Questions.A: He said that it would be necessary for the people to listen to everything that prophet said and to obey him. (22)

Questions.Q: How would anyone who refused to obey that prophet be punished?
Questions.A: Anyone who refused to obey that prophet would be "completely cut off from his people." (23)

Questions.Q: What does it mean "to be completely cut off from his people"?
Questions.A: It means that the person would be rejected as one of God's people, and he would be killed [by God]/[God] would cause him to die. (23)
Questions.Note: See Deuteronomy 18:15, 18, 19.

Questions.Q: What had other prophets written about the time when the Messiah would come to the Jewish people?
Questions.A: All of the prophets, beginning with Samuel, had foretold the time when the Messiah would come. (24)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Peter thought the people whom he was addressing were interested in what the prophets had foretold?
Questions.A: They were interested because they were Jews. God had promised to the Jews the things that the prophets had promised. (25a)

Questions.Q: What promise had God made to Abraham concerning one of his descendants?
Questions.A: God had promised Abraham that he would bless all the peoples of the earth through one of Abraham's descendants. (25b)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to bless someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means to make someone happy, to give good fortune or satisfaction, to confer prosperity upon someone.
Questions.Note: See "grace" and "bless, blessed, blessing" in KBT.

Questions.Q: To whom did this promise of God refer?
Questions.A: This promise referred to Jesus, the Messiah. (26)

Questions.Q: With what phrase did Peter describe Jesus as he quoted God's promise?
Questions.A: Peter referred to Jesus as God's servant. (26)

Questions.Q: To whom did God first send his servant Jesus?
Questions.A: God sent Jesus first to the Jews, because they were his own people. (26)

Questions.Q: What blessing had Jesus come to give his people?
Questions.A: Jesus had come to bless the Jews by causing them to repent and turn away from their wicked ways. (26)

Section.heading: Acts 4:1-22 The Sanhedrin questioned and rebuked Peter and John.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the Jewish religious leaders opposed Peter and John for preaching about Jesus to the many people who had gathered?
Questions.A: The Jewish religious leaders opposed Peter and John for telling the people about Jesus, because they did not believe he was their Messiah. Therefore, they did not want the people to believe the teaching of Peter and the other apostles. (2)

Questions.Q: Who came to where Peter and John were and interrupted Peter's address to the crowd?
Questions.A: The priests, the captain of the guards who kept order in the temple, and the Sadducees came up to where Peter and John were. (1)

Questions.Q: Who do you think the Sadducees were?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The Sadducees were a religious party or denomination of the Jews.
Questions.Note: See "Sadducee" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did those people want?
Questions.A: They wanted Peter and John to stop telling people about Jesus and saying that God will raise to life again people who have died. (2)

Questions.Q: What did the Sadducees believe about people who die?
Questions.A: They believed that no one who dies will live again. Therefore they did not believe that Jesus had risen alive after he died. (2)

Questions.Q: What did the temple guards do then?
Questions.A: They grabbed Peter and John and put them in jail. (They were probably ordered by the priests and Sadducees to do that.) (3)

Questions.Q: What was the result of Peter's preaching to the crowd?
Questions.A: Many people heard and believed the message about Jesus. (4)

Questions.Q: About how many men were now believers in Jesus Christ?
Questions.A: Now there were about five thousand men who were believers. (4)

Questions.Q: What group of people met in Jerusalem the next day?
Questions.A: A large number of the religious leaders and the teachers of the religious laws and traditions met in Jerusalem the next day. (5)

Questions.Q: Who were Annas and Caiaphas?
Questions.A: Annas was the high priest.
Caiaphas was a member of the family of the high priest. (6a)

Questions.Q: What do you know about the high priest?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He was the one supreme priest, that is, the chief of all the priests who was chosen for a special function.
Questions.Note: See "high priest" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What other people were there?
Questions.A: John, Alexander and other men who were members of the family of the high priest were also there. (6b)

Questions.Q: What had this group of religious leaders met to do?
Questions.A: They met together to determine how Peter and John had performed the miracle of healing the lame man. (5-7)

Questions.Q: What questions did the religious leaders ask Peter and John?
Questions.A: They asked them who gave them the power to heal the lame man.
They also asked them who gave them the authority/right to heal the lame man. (7)

Questions.Q: To whom did Peter address his answer?
Questions.A: Peter addressed the religious rulers and elders of the people. (8)

Questions.Q: What did Peter answer?
Questions.A: Peter answered that the power of Jesus Christ of Nazareth had healed the lame man. (8-10)

Questions.Q: How did Peter interpret the intent of their questioning?
Questions.A: Peter understood that they were conducting an examination to discern whether he and John had done something for which they could be found guilty. (9)

Questions.Q: What title did Peter use for Jesus in his answer to the religious leaders?
Questions.A: Peter called Jesus "Jesus Christ of Nazareth." (10)

Questions.Q: What three things did Peter next tell the religious leaders about Jesus?
Questions.A: He reminded the religious leaders that they had crucified Jesus.
He said that God had raised Jesus to life again.
He said that it was by the authority of Jesus Christ of Nazareth that the lame man had been healed. (10)

Questions.Q: What figure of speech, which he quoted from one of the Psalms, did Peter use next in describing Jesus?
Questions.A: Peter said that Jesus was [like] the stone that the builders had rejected. But, [God] had made Jesus [like] the most important stone. (11)

Questions.Q: Whom did Peter compare to the builders who rejected the stone?
Questions.A: Peter compared the leaders of the Jewish religion to the builders who had rejected the stone. (11)

Questions.Q: Although Peter did not state what the building was in which Jesus was the most important stone, what do you think that building represents?
Questions.Note: The building in which Jesus was the most important stone was the religious system in which God had revealed himself to the human race.

Questions.Q: What reason did Peter give for saying that God had made Jesus the most important stone/person?
Questions.A: Peter said that Jesus was the most important person on earth, because only in Jesus Christ can people find salvation/be saved/because God saves only the people who trust in Jesus Christ. (12)
Questions.Alternative: What reason did Peter give for saying that God had made Jesus the most important stone?
What reason did Peter give for saying that God had made Jesus the most important person?

Questions.Q: What do you think "salvation" means?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The noun and the adjective form in the New Testament usually refer to eternal salvation from sin, evil and death. "To save" or "salvation" may refer either to rescuing from a physical danger (like death or captivity to an enemy) or to rescuing from spiritual and eternal danger (captivity to sin and condemnation by God).
Questions.Note: See "salvation" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What amazed the religious leaders about Peter and John?
Questions.A: They were amazed at their boldness and confidence in speaking, despite their lack of education. (13)

Questions.Q: What did the writer of Acts mean when he wrote that Peter and John "were unschooled, ordinary men"?
Questions.A: This meant that Peter and John had not studied under Jewish rabbis. They had not had the kind of education that the priests and the scribes had. (13)

Questions.Q: What could the religious leaders not say that they would like to have said?
Questions.A: The religious leaders could not deny that through the authority of Jesus, Peter and John had healed a lame beggar. (14)

Questions.Q: What did the religious leaders do next?
Questions.A: They ordered Peter and John to leave their presence.
Then they discussed what they could do to prevent Peter and John from continuing to spread the word about Jesus. (15-17)

Questions.Q: What did the members of the Sanhedrin tell Peter and John, after calling them back into the place where they were meeting?
Questions.A: They ordered them not to speak to people or teach at all any more about Jesus. (18)

Questions.Q: What did Peter and John reply to this command?
Questions.A: They replied that if they obeyed the orders given by the members of the Sanhedrin, they would be disobeying God. Then they told the religious leaders, "You tell us, which is the right thing for us to do?" (19-20)

Questions.Q: What command do you think Peter and John would have been disobeying if they had stopped teaching and preaching about Jesus?
Questions.Note: Jesus had told his disciples that they must spread the news about him.

Questions.Q: What did the members of the Sanhedrin do when they heard this reply?
Questions.A: They threatened to punish Peter and John if they continued to teach and preach about Jesus. Then they let them go. (21)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the members of the Sanhedrin were afraid to punish Peter and John?
Questions.A: They were afraid to punish Peter and John, because everyone in Jerusalem knew that with the authority and power of Jesus, the apostles had healed a man who had been lame since he had been born.
They knew that the people would be very angry at them if they punished Peter and John. (16, 21)

Questions.Q: How did the common people feel about what Peter and John had done?
Questions.A: The common people were very happy that the lame beggar had been healed. They were praising God for that fact and giving God the credit for the man's healing. (21)

Section.heading: Acts 4:23-31 The believers prayed that God would give them courage.

Questions.Q: How did the apostles and other believers react when they heard about the hostility of the religious leaders towards their teaching people about Jesus?
Questions.A: When the believers heard about the hostility of the religious leaders and the threats against them, they remembered part of a Psalm that says that God frustrates the earthly rulers who oppose him. They also prayed for courage, and that God would show his power through them.

Questions.Q: What did Peter and John do after the religious authorities/leaders set them free?
Questions.A: They went back to where the other believers were and told them what the chief priests and elders had said to them. (23)
Questions.Alternative: What did Peter and John do after the religious authorities set them free?
What did Peter and John do after the religious leaders set them free?

Questions.Q: What do you know about the chief/leading priests?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Arndt and Gingrich say the following: "The plural is used to denote members of the Sanhedrin who belonged to high-priestly families: ruling high priests, those who had been deposed, and adult male members of the most prominent priestly families." Jeremiah argues that the last of these categories should rather be the leading priests who held the chief executive posts in the Temple. They were, in any case, an influential group of the most important priests.
Questions.Alternative: What do you know about the chief priests?
What do you know about the leading priests?
Questions.Note: See "chief priest" in KBT.

Questions.Q: When the other believers heard that, what did they do?
Questions.A: The other believers unitedly prayed to God. (24a)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the believers reminded God, as they prayed, that he made everything on earth and in heaven and that he rules over all of it?
Questions.A: The believers reminded God of his greatness and power because [they believed that God could help them overcome the opposition of the Jewish authorities]. (24b)

Questions.Q: The believers then quoted from a portion of a Psalm. What does the Psalm say?
Questions.A: The portion of the Psalm that the believers quoted says that the rulers of the earth had gathered together to oppose the Lord God and the Messiah. (25-26)

Questions.Q: How did the believers apply this Psalm to their own situation?
Questions.A: They recognized that when Herod, Pontius Pilate, the Gentiles/Roman soldiers and the people of Israel had opposed Jesus and condemned him to die, they had done what David had said earthly rulers would do to the Messiah. (27)

Questions.Q: What did the believers say next in their prayer that showed they believed God controls what earthly rulers do?
Questions.A: They said that the rulers who had condemned Jesus to die did what God had already planned that they should do. (28)

Questions.Q: What did the believers ask God to do for them, now that they had been opposed by the Jewish leaders?
Questions.A: They asked God to [overrule the threats of the Jewish authorities] and to give them/the believers courage and boldness, so that they would continue to proclaim the news about Jesus Christ. (29)

Questions.Q: What else did the believers ask God to do for them?
Questions.A: They asked God to continue to heal people who needed healing, as they used the authority and name of Jesus. (30)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they asked God to heal people?
Questions.A: They asked God to heal people miraculously to show that the message that they spread about Jesus was God's message. (30)

Questions.Q: What two things happened after the believers had finished praying in this way?
Questions.A: The place where the believers were meeting shook/was shaken [by God]
and the Holy Spirit filled them all. (31a)

Questions.Q: What was the result of the Holy Spirit filling them all?
Questions.A: The believers boldly spoke the word of God to people. (31)

Section.heading: Acts 4:32-37 The believers shared with one another their material possessions.

Questions.Q: What did the believers, who had plenty of material possessions, do to help the believers who were poor?
Questions.A: They shared what they had with the believers who were poor in material goods.

Questions.Q: How did the believers show that they were united in what they thought and desired?
Questions.A: They did not try to keep for themselves the things that they had. Instead, those who had plenty of material things shared with those who did not have enough. (32)

Questions.Q: When the apostles told people how the Lord Jesus died, what else did they always tell the people?
Questions.A: When they told people about the Lord Jesus, they told them that although Jesus had died, he had risen to life again and now is alive forever. (33a)

Questions.Q: What do you think the writer of Acts meant when he wrote that "much grace/great blessing was upon them all"?
Questions.Alternative: What do you think the writer of Acts meant when he wrote that "much grace was upon them all"?
What do you think the writer of Acts meant when he wrote that "great blessing was upon them all"?
Questions.Note: This means that God blessed the believers in many ways. It may also mean that the believers showed forth the grace of God in the way that they lived together and helped one another. (See comments in T.N. on Acts for this verse.) (33b)

Questions.Q: How did believers who had many possessions share with those who were in need?
Questions.A: The believers who owned lands or houses would occasionally sell some of their property.
They gave the apostles the money they received for selling the property.
Then the apostles distributed/gave that money to the believers who had less than they needed. (34-35)

Questions.Q: Tell what this verse says about a believer whose name was Joseph.
Questions.A: Joseph was a descendant of Levi.
He was a native of the island of Cyprus.
The apostles called him Barnabas. (36a)

Questions.Q: What does the name Barnabas mean?
Questions.A: The name Barnabas means a person who encourages others. (36b)

Questions.Q: What did Barnabas do?
Questions.A: Barnabas sold a field that belonged to him and gave the money that he was paid for it to the apostles [to distribute to those believers who needed it]. (37)
Questions.Note: The text implies that Barnabas was not giving this money to the apostles to keep for themselves. The apostles would then give it to believers who were needy.

Section.heading: Acts 5:1-11 Ananias and Sapphira tried to deceive the apostles.

Questions.Q: What happened that the writer described in these verses?
Questions.A: A man and his wife, [who had joined the believers], suddenly died. This was the way that God punished them for lying about the amount of money they were giving to the apostles [to give to other believers].
Questions.Note: There is some difference of opinion as to whether Ananias and Sapphira were actually believers or only appeared to be. See comments on 5:1 in T.N. on Acts.

Questions.Q: Who were Ananias and Sapphira, and what did they do?
Questions.A: Ananias and his wife Sapphira [had professed to believe in Jesus Christ and had joined the group of believers].
They sold a field/some land that they owned. (1)

Questions.Q: What did Ananias do with the money he received from selling the field/land?
Questions.A: He brought some of the money to the apostles [to distribute to other believers], but he kept some of the money for himself and his wife. (2)
Questions.Alternative: What did Ananias do with the money he received from selling the field?
What did Ananias do with the money he received from selling the land?

Questions.Q: What did Ananias tell the apostles when he gave them the money?
Questions.A: He told them that what he gave them was what he had been paid for the field. (2-3)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Ananias and his wife decided to lie to the apostles about the price they had received for selling their field?
Questions.A: Satan had caused Ananias and Sapphira to try to deceive the apostles about the amount of money they were going to turn over to them. They probably did not realize that lying to the apostles would be the same as lying to God. (3)

Questions.Q: What do you know about Satan?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Satan is the chief enemy of God. He is the supreme evil spiritual being who leads and directs all other evil spiritual beings.
Questions.Note: See "Satan" in KBT.

Questions.Q: How did Peter know that Ananias was telling him a lie about the money?
Questions.A: The [Holy Spirit] had shown Peter that Ananias was trying to deceive him. (3)

Questions.Q: What did Peter say to Ananias about the money which Ananias said was the price he had been paid for the field?
Questions.A: Peter said that the field had belonged to Ananias.
He also told Ananias that when he sold the field, the money [someone] paid to him was his to do with as he chose. He could have kept the entire price he was paid for it. (4)

Questions.Q: What was wrong about what Ananias did?
Questions.A: It was wrong/a sin for Ananias to try to deceive the apostles. (3b-4b)

Questions.Q: Whom had Ananias lied to besides the apostles?
Questions.A: He had also lied to the Holy Spirit and to God. (3-4)

Questions.Q: What happened when Ananias heard Peter say that he had lied to God?
Questions.A: Ananias immediately fell down and died. (5a)

Questions.Q: What happened next?
Questions.A: Some young men, who were there when Ananias fell down dead, or perhaps were nearby, wrapped the body of Ananias [with a cloth/sheet] and took him out of the house/building/place to a place where they buried him. (6)

Questions.Q: What did the wife of Ananias do?
Questions.A: About three hours after Ananias had died and been buried by the young men, Sapphira, the wife of Ananias, went to where the apostles were who received and distributed money. (7)

Questions.Q: What did Peter ask her?
Questions.A: Peter asked Sapphira if the money that Ananias had given him was the amount that they had received for the field. (8a)

Questions.Q: What did Sapphira answer?
Questions.A: Sapphira answered yes, that was the amount they had been paid for their field. (8b)

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that Peter asked her that question?
Questions.Note: Probably Peter asked her that in order to know whether Sapphira had known that Ananias was going to lie about the money he received for their field.

Questions.Q: What did Peter then say to her?
Questions.A: Peter then rebuked Sapphira for having agreed with her husband to try to deceive the apostles by telling them a lie. (9)
Questions.Alternative: What did Peter then ask her?

Questions.Q: How did Peter describe the sin of Ananias and Sapphira?
Questions.A: Peter said that Sapphira and her husband had agreed to lie to the Holy Spirit. (9b)

Questions.Q: How was Sapphira punished for her part in that sin?
Questions.A: Sapphira received the same punishment that Ananias had received. She immediately fell down dead, just as Ananias had. (10)

Questions.Q: Who buried Sapphira?
Questions.A: The young men who had buried Ananias came in, carried her body out and buried it beside the body of her husband. (10)

Questions.Q: What did the other believers feel who heard about the sudden death of Ananias and Sapphira?
Questions.A: They were very much afraid. (11)

Questions.Q: For what reason do you think they were afraid?
Questions.Note: They understood that God knows everything and that he is liable to severely punish his people if they do or say something dishonest.

Section.heading: Acts 5:12-16 The apostles healed many sick people and people who were troubled by evil spirits.

Questions.Q: What did the apostles do that is described in these verses?
Questions.A: The apostles healed many people who were ill and those who were tormented by evil spirits. Other people brought sick people and those tormented by evil spirits to public places. The apostles went to where they were and healed them with power that God gave them. Many who were healed also believed in Jesus.

Questions.Q: What did the apostles do that showed that [God was giving them power]?
Questions.A: The apostles did many miracles of healing. [God gave them power to heal the sick.] (12)
Questions.Alternative: What did the apostles do that showed that God was giving them power?
What did the apostles do that showed that?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that non-believers did not join the believers in their meetings at that time?
Questions.A: They did not join the believers because they were afraid. Many people had heard what happened to Ananias and Sapphira. (13)

Questions.Q: What was continuing to happen in spite of the fear some of the people had of meeting with the believers?
Questions.A: People who were not believers greatly respected the believers. (13)
More and more people believed in the Lord and joined the group of believers. (14)

Questions.Q: In what way did many people have contact with the apostles, even before they believed in Jesus Christ?
Questions.A: Many people who heard that the apostles healed people brought sick people that they knew, and those who were troubled by evil spirits. They put the sick people on mats on the streets where they knew that the apostle Peter would pass, and everyone they brought was healed [by God]. (15-16)

Questions.Q: How do you think the healing of people by the apostles resulted in the conversion of many who had not believed until that time?
Questions.Note: Other passages in Acts imply or state that the apostles told the people whom they healed that the power that had healed them came from God. The apostles also told the people that Jesus was the Messiah. A good number of people were convinced that the message about Jesus Christ was true and believed it. Gradually those who had believed the message in this way joined with the other believers in their times of worship and teaching.

Questions.Q: What do you think an evil spirit is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The terms "evil spirit", "unclean spirit", and "demon" are used interchangeably in the New Testament. They all refer to spiritual beings who serve Satan as his agents, being under his authority. These spiritual beings have power to oppress a human being and even take control of him.
Questions.Note: See "evil spirit" in KBT.

Section.heading: Acts 5:17-42 The Jewish Council leaders persecuted the apostles.

Questions.Q: How did the high priest and the other members of the Jewish Supreme Council react to the continued preaching of the apostles?
Questions.A: The apostles were called before the Jewish Supreme Council, and these leaders decided they should be put to death. However, one member of the Council who was a Pharisee advised them to delay judgment and see whether perhaps God was on the side of the apostles.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the high priest and the other Sadducees were angry with the apostles?
Questions.A: They were jealous because many people were going to the apostles and greatly respected them. [Those people now believed the message that Jesus was the Messiah.] (17)

Questions.Q: How did the high priest and his associates try to stop the work of the apostles?
Questions.A: They had the apostles put in prison. (18)

Questions.Q: What happened to the apostles after they were put in prison?
Questions.A: An angel came during the night and let them out of the prison. (19)

Questions.Q: What do you know about angels?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Angels are spiritual messengers, who either deliver a message to humans, carry out God's will, praise God, or guard God's throne.
Questions.Note: See "angel" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did the angel tell them to do?
Questions.A: He told them to go to the temple courts and teach the people about the new life [that Jesus gives to believers]. (20)

Questions.Q: Where were the apostles at daybreak?
Questions.A: They were again in the temple courts, teaching the people who had gathered there, as the angel had ordered them. (21a)

Questions.Q: What did the high priest and his associates do that morning?
Questions.A: They called a meeting of all the religious elders of Israel.
Then they sent officers to the jail to bring the apostles. (21b)

Questions.Q: What did the officers do?
Questions.A: They went to the jail and discovered that the apostles were not in it.
Then they went back to the religious leaders and told them that the apostles were not in the jail, even though it had been locked and the guards were standing at the doors. (22-23)

Questions.Q: How did the religious leaders and the captain of the temple guards find out where the apostles were?
Questions.A: Someone came and told them that the apostles were in the temple courts, teaching the people there. (24-25)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the captain and the temple guards did not use force to bring the apostles to the assembly of the religious leaders?
Questions.A: The guards did not use force, because [they knew that many people had heard that the apostles had healed many people]. So they were afraid that the people would stone them if they harmed the apostles. (26)

Questions.Q: When the apostles arrived where the elders of the Jews were assembled, what did the high priest say to them?
Questions.A: He accused them of having disobeyed his orders not to continue to teach and preach about Jesus. Instead, they had taught everyone in Jerusalem about Jesus.
He also accused the apostles of telling people that he and the other religious leaders were responsible for the death of Jesus. (27-28)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Peter and the other apostles dared to disobey the high priest and the other religious leaders?
Questions.A: Peter and the other apostles had obeyed what God had ordered them to do, even though they had to disobey the high priest and the other religious leaders. (29)

Questions.Q: What things about Jesus did Peter say in replying to the high priest?
Questions.A: He said that the high priest and the other religious leaders had ordered that Jesus be killed, but God had raised Jesus to life again.
He also said that God had taken Jesus up into heaven and placed him next to himself, at the place of highest authority.
