He said that God had made Jesus the Savior/the one who could save them. God did this to give the Jewish people the opportunity to repent of their sin, so that he/God could forgive them. (30-31)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to be a savior?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The personal noun "savior" is used in the New Testament to mean "one who saves from spiritual and eternal danger". It may refer to either God or Jesus Christ.
Questions.Note: See "savior" in KBT.

Questions.Q: How did Peter show that these things that he said about Jesus were true?
Questions.A: Peter said that he and the other apostles had personally seen Jesus after he rose again, alive. He said they had seen him when he was taken up into heaven [by God].
He said the Holy Spirit was also a witness that these things were true. (32)

Questions.Q: How did the high priest and the other members of the Council react to these things that Peter said?
Questions.A: They were furiously angry and they wanted to kill the apostles [by throwing stones at them]. (33)

Questions.Q: Who was Gamaliel?
Questions.A: Gamaliel was a member of the Council.
He was a Pharisee and a teacher of the [Mosaic] law.
The Jewish people greatly respected him. (34)

Questions.Q: What do you know about the teachers of the law?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The TEV and NIV translate "scribe" as "teacher of the law." The scribes were important people in the Jewish religious system. They were experts in knowing and interpreting the laws of Moses and in applying them to everyday life. (See "teacher of the law" in KBT in the "scribe" entry.)
Questions.Alternative: What do you know about the experts in religious law?
What do you know about the scribes?

Questions.Q: What do you know about Pharisees?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The Semitic words mean "the separated ones," which was transliterated into Greek. It came to mean a certain group of Jewish people. So the idea of "separated" does not need to be included here. The name "Pharisee" means "the separated ones." They were the largest and most important of the Jewish religious groups. They controlled the synagogues and exercised great control over the general population. They taught that the way to God was through obeying the law. They opposed Jesus because He refused to accept the teachings of their oral law.
Questions.Note: See "Pharisee" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did Gamaliel order [the guards] to do with the apostles?
Questions.A: He ordered [the guards] to take the apostles out of the room for a while. (34)
Questions.Alternative: What did Gamaliel order the guards to do with the apostles?
What did Gamaliel order to do with the apostles?

Questions.Q: What advice did Gamaliel give to the Council members concerning what they were planning to do to the apostles?
Questions.A: Gamaliel advised the Council members to think carefully about what they were planning to do to the apostles. (35)

Questions.Q: What examples from their recent history did Gamaliel tell to the Council members?
Questions.A: Gamaliel reminded the Council members about two men, Theudas and Judas. Judas was a man from the province of Galilee, who in recent years had gathered people to follow him. Each of these men had planned to revolt against the Roman government. However, people killed each of them. Then their followers scattered, and no revolt took place. (36-37)

Questions.Q: What did Gamaliel advise the Council members to do, considering the two examples he had told them?
Questions.A: He advised them to let the apostles go free. (38)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Gamaliel told them to let the apostles go free?
Questions.A: Gamaliel said that if only men had planned what the apostles were doing, the work of the apostles would fail, [like the work of Theudas and Judas the Galilean]. (38)
If God had planned the work that the apostles were doing, it was bound to succeed. (39)

Questions.Q: Whom would the Council members be fighting against if the apostles' activity had been planned by God?
Questions.A: They would be fighting against God. (39)

Questions.Q: What did the Council members do after they heard what Gamaliel said?
Questions.A: They called the apostles in again and told [the guards] to flog the apostles, [which the guards did].
Then they ordered the apostles not to teach or speak any more about Jesus.
After that, they allowed the apostles to go free. (40)

Questions.Q: How did the apostles react to being flogged?
Questions.A: They were joyful that the Council members had rebuked them and ordered the guards to punish them because they followed the Lord Jesus. (41a)

Questions.Q: What did the apostles do after they were set free by the Council?
Questions.A: Every day the apostles continued to preach and teach people that Jesus is the Messiah. They did that in the temple courts and also went from house to house doing it.
[They also told people that Jesus was the one who could save them from their sins and give them a new life.] (42)

Questions.Q: What do you think someone is doing when they preach?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: When someone preaches they are proclaiming the gospel to those who are listening. This also means that a person/preacher urges others to accept or abandon an idea or course of action.

Section.heading: Acts 6:1-7 The apostles chose seven men to care for the needs of the widows.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that the author of Acts gave details about how the church took care of widows among the believers who had needs?
Questions.Note: Luke made it clear that the church took care of the widows who had no one to provide for them. The apostles were doing this work of caring for the widows. This was taking time which they needed to teach and preach the Word of God, and for prayer. So the members of the church chose a group of seven men to do the other tasks.

Questions.Q: What two groups of believers did the author mention?
Questions.A: He mentioned that there were Grecian Jews and Hebraic Jews in the congregation. (1a)

Questions.Q: In what way were these two groups different?
Questions.A: The Grecian Jews spoke Greek and the Hebraic Jews spoke Aramaic. (1)

Questions.Q: Who complained, and about what did they complain?
Questions.A: The Grecian Jews complained that when the [Hebraic Jews] distributed food (or possibly money for food) each day to the widows, they gave more to the Aramaic-speaking widows than to the Greek-speaking widows. (1b)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the apostles themselves did not wish to continue to distribute food [or money] to the widows of the congregation?
Questions.A: The apostles said that if they continued to give time and attention to taking care of the needs of the widows, they would not have as much time as they needed to teach and preach the Word of God. (2, 4)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that the apostles themselves did not wish to continue to distribute food or money to the widows of the congregation?
What is the reason that the apostles themselves did not wish to continue to distribute food to the widows of the congregation?

Questions.Q: How did the apostles take care of the needs of the widows?
Questions.A: The apostles called a meeting of the believers and told them to choose seven men who they knew were suitable for that work and to give to those men the responsibility for distributing the food [and money] to the widows. (2-3)

Questions.Q: What qualifications did the apostles say these men needed to have?
Questions.A: The believers were to choose men in whom they had confidence because they were controlled by the Holy Spirit and were very wise. (3)

Questions.Q: One of the seven men they chose was Stephen. What qualifications did Stephen have?
Questions.A: Stephen had great faith [in God],
and he was controlled by the Holy Spirit. (5)

Questions.Q: How many of the men whom the believers chose to serve the needs of the widows do you think were Jews?
Questions.Note: The text implies that they were all Jews by birth except for Nicholas, who was from Antioch and was a convert to the Jewish religion.

Questions.Q: How did the apostles authorize/appoint for their work the seven men who had been chosen?
Questions.A: The apostles authorized/appointed the seven men by praying for them and laying their hands upon the heads of the men. (6)
Questions.Alternative: How did the apostles authorize for their work the seven men who had been chosen?
How did the apostles appoint for their work the seven men who had been chosen?

Questions.Q: Who became believers at this time who previously had not accepted Jesus as their Messiah?
Questions.A: Many people believed the message about Jesus Christ at this time, including a large number of priests. (7)

Section.heading: Acts 6:8-15 The religious officials arrested Stephen.

Questions.Q: What happened to Stephen that the writer described in these verses?
Questions.A: A large crowd that was angry at him grabbed him and took him to the Jewish Council. (12)

Questions.Q: What kind of person was Stephen?
Questions.A: He was full of the power and the grace of God.
God enabled Stephen to do many miracles among the people. (8)

Questions.Q: Who opposed the work of Stephen?
Questions.A: The people who opposed Stephen were Jews who belonged to a certain synagogue called "the Synagogue of the Freedmen." These Jews had come from the cities of Cyrene and Alexandria and from the provinces of Cilicia and Asia. [These provinces of the Roman Empire were outside of the land of Israel.] (9)

Questions.Q: What do you think a synagogue is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A synagogue is a building or place of assembly used by Jewish communities primarily for religious worship.
Questions.Note: See "synagogue" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that they opposed the teaching of Stephen?
Questions.Note: They argued with him because they did not believe the message about Jesus that he preached. They may have been angry because a large number of Jewish priests had joined the people who believed that Jesus was the Christ.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the men from the "Synagogue of the Freedmen" were not able to win out over Stephen/prove that Stephen was wrong when they argued with him?
Questions.A: They were not able to win/prove him wrong when they argued with Stephen, because he spoke with wisdom that the Holy Spirit gave him. (10)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that the men from the "Synagogue of the Freedmen" were not able to win out over Stephen when they argued with him?
What is the reason that the men from the "Synagogue of the Freedmen" were not able to prove that Stephen was wrong when they argued with him?

Questions.Q: What did this group of Jews who opposed Stephen do next, when they found they could not win out over his arguments and defeat him?
Questions.A: They persuaded some men to falsely accuse Stephen of speaking disrespectfully [of the laws of] Moses and of God. (11)

Questions.Q: What did the Jews from the "Synagogue of the Freedmen" do next, in order to increase the number of people who opposed Stephen?
Questions.A: They spread the false accusations about Stephen to many of the people in Jerusalem. They also spread those lies to the religious elders and the teachers of the law [of Moses]. (11-12)

Questions.Q: What else did the opponents of Stephen do to further hinder him from continuing to teach and preach about Jesus Christ?
Questions.A: A group of them ran to Stephen, grabbed him, and took him by force before the Supreme Council of the Jews, [so that they could try him for spreading false teachings]. (12b-13a)

Questions.Q: Who accused Stephen before the Supreme Council, and of what did they accuse him?
Questions.A: The group of people who had taken Stephen before the Supreme Council found some men who accused Stephen falsely of repeatedly speaking disrespectfully of the temple and of the Law of Moses. (13)

Questions.Q: What did these false witnesses say that Stephen had said about Jesus?
Questions.A: The false witnesses said that Stephen had said that Jesus of Nazareth would destroy the temple and would change the laws and customs that Moses had taught the Israelite people. (14)

Questions.Q: What did Stephen look like to the priests and elders and other people present?
Questions.A: His face looked like the face of an angel. (15)

Section.heading: Acts 7:1-53 Stephen defended himself before the Council of Elders. [As part of his defense, he reviewed the history of Israel.]

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that Stephen gave a summary of the history of the Israelites instead of just telling the members of the Sanhedrin that the accusations against him were false?
Questions.Note: In giving a summary of the history of the Israelites, Stephen showed that he believed in the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and respected the Law of Moses. He pointed out that the religious rulers of his time had rejected what God was offering them, just as their ancestors had.

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to be a slave of someone/something?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means the person is totally responsible to and dependent upon another person, or the person has become completely subservient to a dominating influence. (See "slave" in KBT in the "servant, slave" entry.)
Questions.Alternative: What do you think it means to be a slave of someone?
What do you think it means to be a slave of something?

Questions.Q: What did the high priest ask Stephen?
Questions.A: He asked him if the things that the false witnesses accused him of were true. (1)

Questions.Q: What well known person in Jewish history did Stephen speak about as he began his defense?
Questions.A: Stephen spoke about Abraham. He said that God told Abraham to leave his country and the people among whom he lived and go to another land which God would show him. (2-3)

Questions.Q: When Abraham arrived there/in that country, what land did God give to him?
Questions.A: When Abraham arrived there, God did not give him any of the land to belong to him. (5a)
Questions.Alternative: When Abraham arrived there, what land did God give to him?
When Abraham arrived in that country, what land did God give to him?

Questions.Q: What did God promise Abraham at that time?
Questions.A: God promised that he would give that land to Abraham and Abraham's descendants, even though at that time Abraham had no children. (5b)

Questions.Q: What else did God tell Abraham would happen to his descendants?
Questions.A: God told Abraham that his descendants would live in a foreign country and stay there four hundred years.
The people of that country would mistreat them and would make them work as slaves. (6)

Questions.Q: What did God tell Abraham he would do to the people who had made his descendants slaves?
Questions.A: He said he would punish the people of that nation. (7)

Questions.Q: What did God say he would do to Abraham's descendants after punishing the people who made them slaves?
Questions.A: God would bring them back to the land that he had given them. (7)

Questions.Q: What would the descendants of Abraham do when they returned to the land that God had given them [Canaan]?
Questions.A: When they returned to that land [Canaan] they would worship God there. (7b)
Questions.Alternative: What would the descendants of Abraham do when they returned to the land that God had given them?
What would the descendants of Abraham do when they returned to the land of Canaan?
What would the descendants of Abraham do when they returned to Canaan?
What would the descendants of Abraham do when they returned to the land of Canaan, that God had given them?
What would the descendants of Abraham do when they returned to Canaan, the land that God had given them?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to worship God?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means to give him respect and devotion. It may be regarded as the direct acknowledgment to God, of his nature, attributes, ways and claims, whether by the outgoing of the heart in praise and thanksgiving or by deed done in such acknowledgment.

Questions.Q: Who circumcised Isaac, Jacob and the twelve sons of Jacob?
Questions.A: Abraham circumcised his son, Isaac, and Isaac circumcised his son, Jacob, and Jacob circumcised his twelve sons. (8)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to circumcise someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that someone removes the foreskin of the male genital.

Questions.Q: How did the Israelites later refer to the twelve sons of Jacob?
Questions.A: The Israelites later referred to the sons of Jacob as the patriarchs of their nation. (8b)

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that Stephen mentioned the fact that Abraham and his descendants were all circumcised?
Questions.Note: Stephen probably mentioned that because circumcision was a sign that God had made them his own people and that they had promised to obey him. His mention of circumcision here takes on deeper significance later in his speech when he comes back to the idea of circumcision in a figurative sense, accusing his hearers of having their hearts and ears uncircumcised. (The respondent might not remember this or be able to make the connection right away).

Questions.Q: What relation was Abraham to Jacob and to Joseph?
Questions.A: Abraham was the ancestor of Jacob and of Joseph. (8)

Questions.Q: What did the patriarchs/Joseph's brothers do to him?
Questions.A: Joseph's brothers/the patriarchs sold him [to some traders/merchants who took him] into Egypt, where he became a slave. (9)
Questions.Alternative: What did the patriarchs brothers do to him?
What did Joseph's brothers do to him?

Questions.Q: What happened to Joseph after he had been in Egypt for some time?
Questions.A: Joseph gained the favor of Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, who made him the ruler over the whole country. (10b)

Questions.Q: For what reason did Joseph have this important position?
Questions.A: God had given Joseph special wisdom and caused Pharaoh to have confidence in him. (10a)

Questions.Q: In what countries was there a famine after Joseph became the ruler in Egypt?
Questions.A: There was a famine in Egypt and also in Canaan. (11)

Questions.Q: Who heard that there was grain in Egypt, and what did he do when he heard that?
Questions.A: In Canaan, Joseph's father, Jacob, and his brothers heard that there was grain in Egypt, and Jacob sent his sons to Egypt to buy grain. (12)

Questions.Q: How do you think it happened that there was grain in Egypt, even during the years of famine?
Questions.Note: Because God had given Joseph unusual wisdom, Joseph had caused the people of Egypt to store up their extra grain during years when there were good crops. So when the famine years came, there was grain in Egypt.
(Respondent will probably not be able to answer this question unless he has familiarity with the original account from Genesis.)

Questions.Q: How many times did Joseph's brother go to Egypt to buy grain?
Questions.A: Joseph's brothers went to Egypt twice and bought grain. Then they took the grain back to Canaan. (13)

Questions.Q: When did Joseph tell his brothers who he was?
Questions.A: Joseph told his brothers who he was on their second visit to Egypt [because they had not recognized him]. (13)

Questions.Q: For what reason did Jacob and all of his descendants go down to Egypt and stay there for many years?
Questions.A: Joseph [told his brothers] to bring their father and all the members of their families down to Egypt to stay there. (14-15)

Questions.Q: How long did Joseph's father and his brothers stay in Egypt?
Questions.A: Jacob and all of Joseph's brothers stayed in Egypt for the rest of their lives, and they died there. (15)

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that Stephen mentioned the fact that the bodies of Joseph's father and brothers were taken to Canaan to be buried?
Questions.Note: Joseph and his family were Israelites, and it was their choice to be buried in their own country, Canaan. When Stephen mentioned that Jacob and his sons were buried in Canaan, he implied that they had remembered the promise that God had given to Abraham. (Also see Genesis 50:5, 25)

Questions.Q: What promise that God had given to Abraham did Stephen refer to next, in his account of Israel's history?
Questions.A: God had promised that after the Israelites had been in a foreign country for four hundred years, he would bring them back to Canaan, the country that he had given to them. (17)

Questions.Q: What had happened to the Israelites during that time?
Questions.A: During the many years that the Israelites had been in Egypt, they had multiplied to be a large nation. (17b)

Questions.Q: What kind of king ruled Egypt when the Israelites had increased to a large number?
Questions.A: When the Israelites had become very many, a different Pharaoh ruled in Egypt.
That Pharaoh knew nothing about Joseph. (18)
He hated the Israelites and ordered them to throw all of their babies [into the river] so that they would die. [In this way, their nation would not continue to increase in number.] (19)

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that the parents of Moses cared for him inside their home for only three months?
Questions.A: After Moses was more than three months old, it was impossible for his parents to hide the fact that they had a baby in their home. Someone who served Pharaoh would have told Pharaoh that a Hebrew couple were hiding a baby boy, and Moses would have been taken away from them and killed.

Questions.Q: What happened after his parents hid Moses inside a basket at an edge of the river?
Questions.A: The daughter of Pharaoh found Moses and took him to her home.
She kept him and brought him up as though he were her own son. (21)

Questions.Q: What kind of person did Moses grow up to be?
Questions.A: [The Egyptian teachers] trained and taught him everything that the Egyptians knew,
and he was a strong, energetic man who could express himself well. (22)

Questions.Q: Although Moses was brought up in the household of the king of Egypt, he knew that he was an Israelite. How do you think he knew that?
Questions.Note: When Moses was still small enough to need a lot of personal care, his mother cared for him. When he grew into a boy and then into a man, no doubt his parents continued to visit him and talk with him, and to have him visit them. So he knew he was an Israelite, even though he had been taught and trained like an Egyptian child.

Questions.Q: What did Moses do one day when he was forty years old?
Questions.A: One day when Moses was forty years old, he went to where the Israelites [were working as slaves. He wanted to see what was happening]. (23)

Questions.Q: What did Moses see that made him angry?
Questions.A: He saw an Egyptian hurting an Israelite, [probably a man who was working for him]. So he hit the Egyptian with such force that he killed him. (24)

Questions.Q: What was the reason that Moses was not afraid to punish the Egyptian whom he saw mistreating an Israelite?
Questions.A: Moses thought that the Israelites would understand that God had sent him to set them free [from the Egyptians]. (25)

Questions.Q: Those Israelites saw Moses kill the Egyptian. How did they feel about what he had done?
Questions.Note: The Israelites did not understand that Moses was trying to help them. They were afraid of him because he had suddenly killed one of the people for whom they were working. (27-28)

Questions.Q: What happened that made Moses suddenly leave Egypt and go to Midian?
Questions.A: The day after Moses had killed the Egyptian, he tried to separate two Israelites who were fighting. One of them said to him, "Who made you ruler and judge over us? Are you going to kill me, the way you killed the Egyptian yesterday?" (27-29)

Questions.Q: What did Moses do in Midian?
Questions.A: Moses settled as a foreigner in Midian,
[married a young woman there],
and had two sons. (29)

Questions.Q: What happened after Moses had lived in Midian for forty years?
Questions.A: After Moses had lived in Midian for forty years, one day when he was in the desert, he saw a bush that was burning, but the bush was not burnt up. An angel appeared to him in the flames of the burning bush. (30)

Questions.Q: When Moses went close to the bush to see why it was not being burned up, what happened?
Questions.A: When Moses went close to the bush, God spoke to him through the angel that was in the bush. (31)

Questions.Q: How did Moses know that the voice speaking to him was God's voice?
Questions.A: The voice that spoke to Moses from the bush said, "I am the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob." (32a)

Questions.Q: What did Moses feel when he understood that God was present there?
Questions.A: Moses was afraid. He trembled and covered his face so as not to look at God. (32b)

Questions.Q: What was God's purpose in speaking to Moses?
Questions.A: God spoke to Moses to tell him that he, God, had seen how the Israelites were suffering in Egypt as slaves, and he was going to set them free.
God also told Moses that he was going to send him back to Egypt [in order to set the Israelites free]. (34)

Questions.Q: What was the work and responsibility of Moses after he returned to Egypt?
Questions.A: After Moses went back to Egypt, God made him the ruler of the Israelites.
God also made him their deliverer, [because he represented the Israelites before Pharaoh and repeatedly asked him to let the Israelites leave]. (35)

Questions.Q: What do you think a deliverer does?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A deliverer is a person who comes to obtain the freedom of others, a liberator. (See "deliverer" in KBT in the "redeem" entry.)

Questions.Q: What did God do to show the Israelites that Moses was the man whom he had sent to help them?
Questions.A: God gave Moses power to do miracles that showed that God was with him.
After performing many miracles [by which God punished the Egyptian people], Moses finally led the Israelites out of Egypt.
By means of a miracle, he led them across the Red Sea.
Then Moses led them through the desert and did many miracles to help them while they were there. (36)

Questions.Q: Whom did Moses say that God would send to the Israelites?
Questions.A: Moses told the Israelites that God would send them a prophet who would also be an Israelite. (37)

Questions.Q: How and where did God give laws to Moses to pass on to the Israelites?
Questions.A: On Mount Sinai, an angel of the Lord told Moses the laws that God told him. He commanded Moses to teach those laws to the Israelites. (38)

Questions.Q: How did the Israelites feel towards Moses for bringing them out of Egypt and leading them through the desert?
Questions.A: The Israelites did not want Moses to continue to lead them through the desert.
They wanted to return to Egypt and asked Aaron to make gods for them who would lead them as they marched back to Egypt. (39-40)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the Israelites asked Aaron to make them some gods to lead them?
Questions.A: They said that they did not know what had happened to Moses. [They had not seen him for a long time, because he had stayed on Mount Sinai for forty days.] (40b)

Questions.Q: What did the people do when they asked Aaron to make them gods to lead them?
Questions.A: [They gave Aaron their gold jewelry, which he melted down and made into a golden calf.] Then the people brought [animals] which they sacrificed to the golden calf. That was a celebration to worship it. (41)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when someone sacrifices something to an idol?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The sacrifice of something to an idol is a religious act of making a gift to some powerful spiritual being in order to establish, maintain, or restore a proper relationship between the sacrificer and the deity. Something is given up in order to achieve a purpose.
Questions.Note: See "sacrifice" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What else did the Israelites worship, after the golden calf had been made?
Questions.A: They worshiped the sun, moon and stars. (42)

Questions.Q: What did Stephen say was the reason the Israelites had turned to worshiping false gods?
Questions.A: Stephen said that God became disgusted with the Israelites and just let them worship whatever gods they wanted to worship. (42a)
Questions.Alternative: What did Stephen say was the reason the Israelites had turned to worshipping false gods?
According to Stephen, why had the Israelites had turned to worshiping false gods?

Questions.Q: What did God say about the sacrifices that the Israelites offered when they were in the desert?
Questions.A: God said that when the Israelites had offered sacrifices, they were not really offering those sacrifices to him. They were really worshiping the idols they had made. (42b-43)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when someone practices idolatry?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that a person gives respect and devotion to a physical object as a god. The idol can be a representation or symbol of a deity, or any other being, or a thing made or used as an idol of worship.

Questions.Q: How did God punish his people for turning away from him to worship other gods?
Questions.A: God told his people that he would send them away from their own country as exiles to a place beyond Babylon. (43b)

Questions.Q: What do you think the tabernacle was?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It was a place to worship God. The tabernacle was the portable sanctuary that the people of Israel built under God's direction in the early years of their history, while they were traveling in the wilderness. God was present in the tabernacle in a very special way. In some passages the reference is not to the man-made tabernacle which existed in this world, but to the corresponding tabernacle in heaven, the spiritual reality which the earthly tabernacle represents. (See "tabernacle" in KBT in the "tent" entry.) (44)

Questions.Q: For how long did the Israelites use the tabernacle?
Questions.A: When Joshua led the Israelites into Canaan, they carried the tabernacle with them.
From the time they entered Canaan through the time when David was their king, the Israelites used the tabernacle as the place at which they worshiped God. (45)

Questions.Q: What did Stephen say that showed that he no longer thought the Temple was the only correct place at which God's people could worship him?
Questions.A: Stephen described the Temple at Jerusalem as "the house that Solomon built for the Most High." Then he went on to say that since God made the heavens and the earth and all that they contain, no house that a human being has built is good enough for God. (47-50)

Questions.Q: What did Stephen mean when he told the religious leaders that they had "uncircumcised hearts and ears"?
Questions.A: He meant that they did not listen when God spoke to them, and they never obeyed him. (51a)

Questions.Q: In what way did Stephen say the people he was speaking to were like their ancestors?
Questions.A: Stephen said that the religious leaders were like their ancestors because their ancestors had resisted/disobeyed the Holy Spirit. (52)

Questions.Q: What had the prophets, whom the Israelites had killed, predicted in earlier times?
Questions.A: In earlier times certain prophets had predicted the coming of the Messiah, whom Stephen referred to as "the Holy One." (52a)

Questions.Q: Then, when the Messiah came, how had the religious leaders to whom Stephen was speaking acted towards him/the Messiah?
Questions.A: The religious leaders to whom Stephen was speaking had betrayed and killed the Messiah. (52b)
Questions.Alternative: Then, when the Messiah came, how had the religious leaders to whom Stephen was speaking acted towards him?
Then, when the Messiah came, how had the religious leaders to whom Stephen was speaking acted towards the Messiah?
When the Messiah came, how had the religious leaders to whom Stephen was speaking acted towards him?
When the Messiah came, how had the religious leaders to whom Stephen was speaking acted towards the Messiah?

Questions.Q: Of what else did Stephen accuse his hearers?
Questions.A: Stephen told them that although they had received the law of God, they had disobeyed it. (53)

Section.heading: Acts 7:54-8:1a The religious leaders were very angry, so they killed Stephen by stoning him.

Questions.Q: What had Stephen said in his speech about the history of the Israelites that made the religious leaders very angry?
Questions.A: Stephen had described how the Israelites in past times had repeatedly refused to obey God. They had disobeyed him each time they refused to listen to the messengers whom God had sent to them. Finally, Stephen accused the religious leaders that they had disobeyed God by rejecting and killing the Messiah whom God had sent.
The religious leaders believed that Stephen had blasphemed God by calling Jesus the Messiah. The punishment for a person who blasphemed God was death.

Questions.Q: Who do you think the Son of Man is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It is Jesus. "Son of Man" is the title Christ used of Himself.
Questions.Note: See "son of man" in KBT.

Questions.Q: How did Stephen respond when he saw that the religious leaders were furiously angry with him?
Questions.A: He was controlled by the Holy Spirit and looked up into the sky (55).
He was enabled by the Holy Spirit to see into heaven, where he saw the bright light that shone from God, and he saw Jesus standing at the right hand of God. (55-56)

Questions.Q: What did Stephen tell his hearers when he saw Jesus?
Questions.A: He told the people listening that he could see the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God. (56)

Questions.Q: What did the religious leaders do when they heard this?
Questions.A: They yelled loudly, stopping their ears, and all together rushed at Stephen. (57)

Questions.Q: What did their actions show?
Questions.A: They covered their ears, because they did not want to listen to what Stephen said. [They believed it was blasphemy]. (57)
Questions.Note: When Stephen referred to Jesus as the Son of Man and said he was standing at God's right hand in heaven, he was saying that Jesus was the Messiah. The religious leaders believed that this was blasphemy, so they covered their ears, in order not to hear Stephen blaspheming.

Questions.Q: How did those religious leaders punish Stephen?
Questions.A: They dragged him out of the city and began to throw stones at him in order to kill him. (58a)

Questions.Q: For what reason do you think the author of Acts mentions the witnesses who were present?
Questions.Note: According to the law of Moses, the Israelites were not allowed to execute a person unless at least two witnesses were present who knew that the person had done something punishable by death.

Questions.Q: Who were the witnesses and what did the witnesses do?
Questions.A: The people who had heard what Stephen had said about Jesus were the witnesses. They were getting ready to throw stones at Stephen to kill him. So they took off their outer garments and laid them on the ground near Saul, [in order to throw stones more easily]. (58)

Questions.Q: What did Stephen do while the people repeatedly threw stones at him?
Questions.A: He prayed, "Lord Jesus, receive my spirit." (59)

Questions.Q: What did he do next?
Questions.A: Then, he fell down on his knees and prayed that the Lord would not hold this sin against them/would not punish them for this sin.
After he had prayed, he died. (60)

Questions.Q: Who is mentioned as one of the witnesses that said it was right that they should kill Stephen?
Questions.A: Saul was there watching, and he had agreed that they should kill Stephen, [because that was the punishment for blaspheming God]. (8:1)

Section.heading: Acts 8:1b-3 Saul persecuted the believers, causing most of them to leave Jerusalem.

Questions.Q: What happened on the day that Stephen was stoned to death [by the religious leaders]?
Questions.A: The people who rejected the message about Jesus as the Messiah began to persecute the other believers. So all of them except the apostles left Jerusalem and went to other places in Judea (province) and Samaria (province). (1)
Questions.Alternative: What happened on the day that Stephen was stoned to death by the religious leaders?
What happened on the day that Stephen was stoned to death?

Questions.Q: What did most of the believers in Jerusalem do when [people] persecuted them?
Questions.A: Except for the apostles, they left Jerusalem and went to many places in Judea and Samaria. (1b)
Questions.Alternative: What did most of the believers in Jerusalem do when people persecuted them?
What did most of the believers in Jerusalem do when persecuted them?

Questions.Q: What did Saul do to the believers?
Questions.A: He hated the believers and wanted to destroy all of them.
He went to their homes, dragged them out and took them to prison. (3)

Section.heading: Acts 8:4-8 Philip preached in a city of Samaria (province), and many people in that city rejoiced.

Questions.Q: Where did Philip go when he left Jerusalem?
Questions.A: Philip went to a city in Samaria (province). (5)

Questions.Q: What did he do in that town?
Questions.A: He preached to the people that Jesus of Nazareth was the Messiah. (5)
He also performed many miracles of healing. (6)

Questions.Q: How did the people respond to the message that Philip preached?
Questions.A: Many people of that city believed and were healed, and they were very happy. (7-8)

Questions.Q: What did the believers who left Jerusalem do in those places to which they went?
Questions.A: Wherever they went, the believers preached the message [about Jesus]. (4)

Questions.Q: Who was Philip and what did he do?
Questions.A: Philip was one of the believers who left Jerusalem when the [people] persecuted the believers.
He went to a city in Samaria and preached to the people there [that Jesus is] the Messiah. (5)

Questions.Q: What else did Philip do?
Questions.A: As he preached to the people in that city, Philip healed many crippled and lame people.
[God gave him the power to heal people.]
He also cast evil spirits out of the people whom they troubled. (6-7)

Questions.Q: How did the people in that city react to what Philip did?
Questions.A: Many people in that city rejoiced/were happy. (8)

Section.heading: Acts 8:9-25 A sorcerer professed to believe in Jesus but had not recognized his sin.

Questions.Q: What person in Samaria did the people refer to as "the Great Power"?
Questions.A: A man who practiced magic was famous in that city. His name was Simon.
People spoke about him as "the Great Power."
Many people believed that Simon had power that came from God, and they believed what he said. (9-11)

Questions.Q: How did Simon learn about a power greater than the power that he had?
Questions.A: Simon heard Philip preach, and he believed the message about Jesus Christ.
He saw Philip perform many miracles and he could see that Philip had a power greater than he, Simon, had. (13)

Questions.Q: What was the reason that Simon was famous?
Questions.A: He had amazed the people of that city for a long time by the things that he did through magic. (9)
Many people believed that Simon had power that came from God, and they believed what he said. (10-11)

Questions.Q: What happened when the people heard Philip preach about Jesus Christ and the good news of the kingdom of God?
Questions.A: They listened to him and they saw the miracles that he performed, and they believed the message about Jesus Christ. (12)

Questions.Q: What did the people do who believed the message about Jesus Christ?
Questions.A: They were baptized [by Philip]. (12b)

Questions.Q: What did Simon think about the message that Philip preached?
Questions.A: He believed that what Philip preached was true, so he was baptized [by Philip] also. (13)

Questions.Q: What did Simon do after he was baptized [by Philip]?
Questions.A: He followed Philip wherever he went, watching as Philip continued to perform many miracles. (13)
Questions.Alternative: What did Simon do after he was baptized by Philip?
What did Simon do after he was baptized?

Questions.Q: What did Simon think about the miracles that he saw Philip doing?
Questions.A: Simon was continually amazed by the great signs and miracles that Philip did. (13)

Questions.Q: When the apostles in Jerusalem heard that many people in Samaria had believed the message about Jesus Christ, whom did they send there? What was their reason for sending them?
Questions.A: The apostles sent Peter and John to see the new believers in Samaria. (14)

Questions.Q: What did Peter and John do when they arrived in Samaria?
Questions.A: They prayed that the new believers would receive the Holy Spirit. (15)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they needed to do that?
Questions.A: They needed to do that, because the Holy Spirit had not yet come upon those believers. Philip had baptized them but had not prayed that they would receive the Holy Spirit. (16)

Questions.Q: What did Peter and John do for the believers in Samaria?
Questions.A: They placed their hands upon them, and then those believers all received the Holy Spirit. (17)
Questions.Note: In Acts, the laying on of hands is usually accompanied by prayer.

Questions.Q: What did Simon do when he saw that [God] gave the Holy Spirit [to the believers] when Peter and John laid their hands on them?
Questions.A: He offered Peter and John money. (18)
Questions.Alternative: What did Simon do when he saw that God gave the Holy Spirit to the believers when Peter and John laid their hands on them?
What did Simon do when he saw that God gave the Holy Spirit when Peter and John laid their hands on the believers?
What did Simon do when he saw that the Holy Spirit was given to the believers when Peter and John laid their hands on them?
What did Simon do when he saw that the Holy Spirit was given when Peter and John laid their hands on the believers?
What did Simon do when he saw that the believers received the Holy Spirit when Peter and John laid their hands on them?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Simon offered them money?
Questions.A: He thought that he could buy the ability/power to cause people to receive the Holy Spirit when he laid his hands on them. (19)

Questions.Q: What did Peter describe as "the gift of God"?
Questions.A: Peter described [the presence of the Holy Spirit] in a believer's life as "the gift of God." (20b)

Questions.Q: When Peter rebuked Simon for offering money to him and to John, what warning did he give to Simon?
Questions.A: Peter told Simon that he and his money would perish [if he did not change the way that he thought. That meant that Simon would be eternally lost]. (20)

Questions.Q: What else did Peter say about Simon's spiritual condition?
Questions.A: Peter told Simon that his heart was not right before God.
He told Simon that he had not repented of his sins. (21)

Questions.Q: What does the "heart" mean to you?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The most common use of the word "heart" in the Bible is to refer to the spiritual center or innermost part of a human being. In Hebrew and Greek "heart" is most commonly associated with thoughts and ideas.
Questions.Note: See "heart" in KBT.

Questions.Q: When Peter told Simon he needed to repent, of what two sins did he tell Simon he was guilty?
Questions.A: Peter told Simon that he needed to repent of thinking that he could work along with the apostles and cause people to receive the Holy Spirit.
He also told Simon that he needed to repent of being envious of the power that Peter and John had. (22-23)

Questions.Q: How did Simon reply to the warning Peter had given to him that he would be eternally lost?
Questions.A: Simon was frightened by Peter's warning and asked him and John to pray that the bad things that Peter had warned him about would not happen to him. (24)

Questions.Q: What did Peter and John do after that?
Questions.A: They preached to the people in that town about Jesus Christ and told them what they personally knew about him, since they had both known Jesus while he was on earth.
Then they returned to Jerusalem, preaching to people in many Samaritan villages along the way about the Lord Jesus. (25)

Section.heading: Acts 8:26-40 Philip evangelized an official who was returning to Ethiopia.

Questions.Q: For what reason did Philip leave the city in Samaria, and where did he go?
Questions.A: Philip was told by an angel, whom the Lord [God] had sent, to leave Samaria and go south to the road that went from Jerusalem to Gaza through a desert area. (26)

Questions.Q: Whom did Philip meet on the road to which he went?
Questions.A: Philip met a man who was an official of the queen of Ethiopia. (27)
He was riding in a chariot, and he was reading from a scroll. The scroll had written on it part of the prophecy of Isaiah. (28)
Philip overtook the man and asked him whether he understood what he was reading. (30)
The man replied that he needed someone to help him, so Philip told him that the part of the scroll which the man was reading was about the Lord Jesus. (31, 34-35)

Questions.Q: How did their conversation end?
Questions.A: The official became a believer in the Lord Jesus, and when they came to a pool of water, he asked Philip to baptize him. (36-38)

Questions.Q: What was the official from Ethiopia doing so far away from his own country?
Questions.A: He had been to Jerusalem to worship God and was now on his way home. (27b-28)

Questions.Q: What was the man doing as he rode along in his chariot?
Questions.A: He was reading from a book [or perhaps from a scroll] which contained what the prophet Isaiah had written long ago. (28)

Questions.Q: What did Philip do when he saw the man reading?
Questions.A: The Holy Spirit told Philip to go to where the Ethiopian was riding along in his chariot and to stay near him in the road, and Philip went there. (29)

Questions.Q: What did Philip and the Ethiopian say to one another when Philip was close enough to be able to speak to the Ethiopian?
Questions.A: Philip asked the Ethiopian whether he understood what he was reading, and the Ethiopian replied that he needed somebody to explain it to him.
Then he asked Philip to get up beside him in the chariot. (30-31)

Questions.Q: What was the passage from Isaiah about that the Ethiopian was reading?
Questions.A: The passage, [which was from Isaiah 53:7-8], described someone who was caused to suffer unjustly. (32-33)

Questions.Q: What did the Ethiopian ask Philip?
Questions.A: He asked Philip to tell him to whom the passage referred. (34)

Questions.Q: What answer did Philip give to the Ethiopian?
Questions.A: Philip explained to him that the passage was about someone who had suffered unjustly.
Philip then told the Ethiopian that Jesus was the Messiah. (35)

Questions.Q: How did the Ethiopian respond after Philip told him the passage was about Jesus?
Questions.A: When the Ethiopian understood that the passage was about Jesus and [why Jesus had suffered], he believed in Jesus and wanted to be baptized. (36)

Questions.Q: What happened next?
Questions.A: Although the road they were traveling was through a desert area, they came upon a pool of water, or possibly a stream. Philip believed that the Ethiopian had understood the message about Jesus Christ and now believed in him, so Philip baptized him. (38)

Questions.Q: What happened when the two men came up out of the water?
Questions.A: Philip suddenly disappeared, because the Holy Spirit/Spirit of the Lord took him to Azotus. [The town Azotus was some distance away.] (39a, 40)

Questions.Q: What did the man from Ethiopia do after Philip disappeared?
Questions.A: The man from Ethiopia continued on his way back to his own country. He was happy because he now knew what the prophecy meant that he had been reading. He had put his trust in the Lord Jesus [who suffered for him]. (39b)

Questions.Q: What did Philip do after arriving in Azotus?
Questions.A: He preached the message about Jesus Christ there and in all the other towns that he passed through on his way to Caesarea. (40)

Section.heading: Acts 9:1-19a Saul, the persecutor, saw Jesus, his risen Lord, and became his servant.

Questions.Q: What happened to Saul that the writer recorded in these verses?
Questions.A: Saul was blind for three days. (8-9)
He became a believer in Jesus. (18)

Questions.Q: What did Saul plan to do in order to continue persecuting the believers?
Questions.A: He planned to go to Damascus, so he first went to the high priest, who gave him letters that authorized him to persecute any believers that he found in Damascus. (1-2)

Questions.Q: Describe what happened to him as he was getting near Damascus.
Questions.A: A light from heaven [brighter than the sun at noon] flashed around him, and he fell to the ground.
He heard a voice say to him, "Saul, Saul why are you persecuting me?" (3-4)

Questions.Q: Who was speaking to Saul?
Questions.A: It was Jesus speaking. (5)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus mean when he asked Saul why he was persecuting him?
Questions.A: He meant that when Saul persecuted the believers, it was the same as persecuting Jesus himself. (5)
Questions.Note: This is implied information.

Questions.Q: What else did the voice/Jesus tell Saul?
Questions.A: He told Saul to get up and continue on his way into the city, and there [someone] would tell him what to do. (6)
Questions.Alternative: What else did the voice tell Saul?
What else did Jesus tell Saul?

Questions.Q: What did the men who were traveling with Saul see and hear when these things happened?
Questions.A: They saw Saul fall on the ground, and they heard a voice, but they did not see Jesus. (7)

Questions.Q: What did Saul and his companions do next?
Questions.A: Saul got up but he could not see, so his companions led him by the hand until they arrived in Damascus.
For three days after they arrived there, Saul continued to be blind and did not eat or drink anything during that time. (8-9)

Questions.Q: What did the Lord say to Ananias in a vision?
Questions.A: The Lord told him to go to Straight Street and find Saul at the house of Judas. (10-11)

Questions.Q: What was the reason that the Lord told Ananias to go and find Saul?
Questions.A: The Lord told him to go to Saul and place his hands on him so that he would regain his sight. (12)

Questions.Q: What did Ananias reply when the Lord told him to go and help Saul?
Questions.A: He did not want to go, because he knew that Saul had persecuted many believers in Jerusalem and had come [to Damascus] to persecute the believers there. (13-14)

Questions.Q: What did the Lord then tell Ananias about Saul?
Questions.A: The Lord then told Ananias that he had especially chosen Saul to serve him.
Saul was going to witness about him before the Gentiles and their kings and before the people of Israel.
He also told him that Saul from now on was going to suffer much persecution for the sake of Christ. (15-16)

Questions.Q: What did Ananias do when he heard what the Lord Jesus told him about Saul?
Questions.A: He went to the house where Saul was staying and told Saul that the Lord Jesus had sent him in order to enable Saul to see again and to be filled with the Holy Spirit.
Then Ananias laid his hands on Saul, and Saul was able to see again. (17-18a)

Questions.Q: What did Saul do after he was able to see again?
Questions.A: He stood up and he was baptized [by Ananias].
After that he ate and regained his usual strength. (18b-19a)

Section.heading: Acts 9:19b-31 Saul fearlessly preached that Jesus was the Messiah, both in Damascus and in Jerusalem.

Questions.Q: What did Saul do in Damascus after he became a believer?
Questions.A: He went to the synagogues in Damascus and preached to the Jews.
He told them that Jesus was the Messiah. (20)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Saul left Damascus secretly?
Questions.A: The Jews who rejected the message about Jesus planned to kill him. (23)
People who had become believers in the Lord Jesus helped Saul to escape at night. (25)

Questions.Q: Where did Saul go next?
Questions.A: Saul went to Jerusalem and tried to join the believers there. (26)
The believers in Jerusalem did not believe he had really become a believer until Barnabas told them about Saul's conversion. (26-27)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the believers in Jerusalem sent Saul to Tarsus?
Questions.A: While he was in Jerusalem, Saul tried to convince the Jews there that Jesus was the Messiah. They planned to kill him, but again the believers helped Saul to escape. (28-30)

Questions.Q: What did Saul do during the time that he stayed in Damascus?
Questions.A: He went to the synagogue where the Jews met to worship,
and he repeatedly preached to them that Jesus is the Son of God. (19b-22)

Questions.Q: What did the Jews there say when they heard that Saul now was saying that Jesus was the Messiah?
Questions.A: They were very much surprised, because they had heard that Saul was the same person who had persecuted/killed the people in Jerusalem who believed in Jesus.
They also knew that Saul had come to Damascus to arrest the believers and take them back to Jerusalem to be punished/judged by the chief priests. (19b-22)

Questions.Q: How did the Jews react to Saul's conversion and preaching?
Questions.A: They were very angry, but they could not deny the reasons that Saul gave to prove that Jesus was the Messiah.
Therefore they planned to kill him. (22-23)

Questions.Q: How did those Jews plan to get hold of Saul and kill him?
Questions.A: They posted guards at the gates of the city, day and night, [and the guards were instructed to grab Saul and kill him when he tried to leave the city]. (24)

Questions.Q: How did Saul escape?
Questions.A: Some people who believed what Saul preached hid him in a room that had a window in one of the walls of the city.
They put Saul in a large basket to which they attached a rope.
Then they let him down to the ground outside the city wall. (25)

Questions.Q: How did the believers in Jerusalem react when they heard that Saul had become a believer in Jesus?
Questions.A: They were afraid of Saul.
They thought he was only pretending to believe in the Lord Jesus [and was planning to continue persecuting them]. (26)

Questions.Q: How did Barnabas help the other believers to accept Saul?
Questions.A: Barnabas took Saul to where the apostles were and told them how Saul had seen the Lord Jesus as he had traveled [to Damascus].
He told them that the Lord Jesus had spoken to Saul, [showing Saul that he was truly the Lord].
Barnabas also told the apostles that Saul had already spent some time in Damascus, preaching that Jesus was the Messiah. (27)

Questions.Q: What did the apostles believe about Saul after Barnabas told them how Saul had become a believer?
Questions.A: When the apostles heard what Barnabas told them, they accepted Saul as a believer, and they let Saul stay with them. (28a)
Questions.Note: This is implied information.
Questions.Alternative: What did the apostles do, after they believed what Barnabas told them about Saul and how he become a believer?
What did the apostles do after hearing what Barnabas told them about Saul and how he become a believer?
What did the apostles do after hearing what Barnabas told them about Saul?
What did the apostles do after hearing what Barnabas told them?
What did the apostles do after listening to Barnabas?

Questions.Q: What did Saul do while he stayed in Jerusalem at that time?
Questions.A: He boldly preached the message that Jesus is the Lord.
He preached both to the Jews who spoke Hebrew (or Aramaic) and to the Jews who spoke Greek.
He also debated/argued from the scriptures with the Jews who spoke Greek. (28b-29)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the believers in Jerusalem arranged for Saul to leave? Where did they send him?
Questions.A: They heard that the Greek-speaking Jews were planning to kill Saul, so they took him down to the port of Caesarea and arranged that from there he would go to Tarsus. (29-30)
Questions.Note: Saul was a native of Tarsus.

Questions.Q: What happened to the believers who lived in Judea, Galilee, and Samaria after that?
Questions.A: The believers in those three areas enjoyed a time of peace.
The Holy Spirit strengthened and encouraged them.
They had increased in number as they lived in reverence/honor for the Lord. (31)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to be at peace?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: To be at peace is to have a mental or spiritual condition marked by freedom of disquieting or oppressive thoughts or emotions.
Questions.Note: See "peace" in KBT.

Section.heading: Acts 9:32-43 Peter visited believers in many places and performed miracles in Lydda and Joppa.

Questions.Q: Who was Aeneas and where did he live?
Questions.A: Aeneas was a man in Lydda who had been paralyzed for eight years. (33)

Questions.Q: How did Peter help him?
Questions.A: Peter healed Aeneas, using the power of Jesus, and Aeneas immediately became well. (34)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the believers in Joppa requested Peter to come there?
Questions.A: The believers in Joppa had seen Aeneas after he became well, and they sent for Peter to come and heal someone in Joppa. (35, 38)

Questions.Q: What did Peter do in Joppa?
Questions.A: In Joppa, Peter raised Tabitha to life after she had died. (40)

Questions.Q: What did the apostle Peter do as he traveled from one town to another where there were already believers?
Questions.A: He visited the believers who lived in each place. (32)

Questions.Q: What else did Peter do in [the town of] Lydda?
Questions.A: He healed a man whose name was Aeneas, who was paralyzed and had not been able to get out of bed for eight years. (32b-34)
Questions.Alternative: What else did Peter do in the town of Lydda?
What else did Peter do in Lydda?

Questions.Q: What did Peter do in order to heal him?
Questions.A: Peter said to him, "Jesus Christ makes you well."
Then he told Aeneas to get up, and Aeneas did so at once. (34)

Questions.Q: What happened as a result of Aeneas being healed?
Questions.A: All the people in Lydda (a town) and Sharon (an area of the coastal plain) learned about it, and many of them believed in the Lord Jesus. (35)

Questions.Q: What kind of person was the woman whose name was Tabitha (also called Dorcas), and where did she live?
Questions.A: She was a believer in Jesus.
She lived in Joppa (a town).
She was a kind and generous person who helped many poor people [by giving them things like money and clothing that they needed]. She made pieces of clothing for widows who lived there. (36)

Questions.Q: What happened when Tabitha became sick and died?
Questions.A: [Some women] washed her body and placed it in an upstairs room.
The believers in Joppa had heard that Peter was in Lydda, [and that he had healed a sick man there].
So they sent two men to Lydda, asking Peter to come to Joppa as soon as he could.
Peter went back with them. (37-39a)

Questions.Q: What did Peter find when he arrived at Tabitha's house?
Questions.A: He was taken to the upstairs room where [some women] had laid Tabitha's body.
All of the widows had gathered there. They were weeping and showing Peter the pieces of clothing that Tabitha had made [for them]. (39)

Questions.Q: What did Peter do, and what happened?
Questions.A: He told all of the people to leave the room.
Then he knelt down beside Tabitha and prayed.
After that he looked directly at her and said, "Tabitha, get up!"
She opened her eyes and saw Peter. Then she sat up.
Peter took her by the hand and helped her to stand up on her feet.
Then he called the widows and the other believers who had gathered there to come in to the room.
He showed them that she was alive again. (40-41)

Questions.Q: Who else knew that Peter had raised Tabitha to life again after she had died?
Questions.A: Everyone in Joppa heard about it. (42)

Questions.Q: What was the result of this miracle?
Questions.A: Many of those who heard about the miracle became believers in the Lord Jesus. (42)

Questions.Q: What did Peter do after that?
Questions.A: Peter stayed in Joppa for many days with a man whose name was Simon.
Simon made animal hides into leather as his trade. (43)

Section.heading: Acts 10:1-33 Peter visited a Gentile in his home.

Questions.Q: Who was Cornelius and where did he live?
Questions.A: Cornelius was a Gentile.
He lived in Caesarea (a town).
He was the captain of a regiment in the Roman army.
He was a God-fearing person, and he prayed regularly.
He and his family worshiped the God whom the Jews worshiped.
Cornelius helped poor people among the [Jews]. (1-2)

Questions.Q: For what reason did Cornelius send for Peter to come to his home?
Questions.A: He sent for Peter because one afternoon an angel appeared to him in a vision.
The angel told Cornelius to send word to Peter to come to his home. (3-5)

Questions.Q: What happened in the home of Cornelius at three o'clock in the afternoon one day?
Questions.A: An angel appeared to Cornelius in a vision, probably while he was praying.

The angel told Cornelius that God was pleased with his praying and with his helping the poor. The angel told Cornelius to send some men to the town Joppa and bring back a man whose name was Simon Peter. (3-6)
Questions.Note: It was the custom of the Jews to pray at that time. See 3:1.

Questions.Q: What did Cornelius do after he heard what the angel said?
Questions.A: He called two of his household servants and a God-fearing soldier who also served him.
He told them what the angel had said and then sent them to Joppa to bring Simon Peter [to Caesarea]. (7-8)

Questions.Q: What was Peter doing in Joppa the next day at about noon, when the three men whom Cornelius had sent were about to arrive there?
Questions.A: Peter went up on the top of the house to pray.
Peter/he became hungry and wanted something to eat.
Peter saw a vision while the meal was being prepared [by the people downstairs]. (9-10)

Questions.Q: What did Peter see in the vision?
Questions.A: He saw heaven/the sky open and something like a large square cloth which [someone] was letting down from the sky to the ground by its four corners.
The cloth had a number of live animals and wild birds in it, including some snakes and lizards. (11-12)
Questions.Note: They were animals, reptiles and birds that non-Jewish people could eat, but they were all animals, reptiles, and birds that Jews were forbidden by their ritual laws to eat.

Questions.Q: What did Peter hear [as he looked at the animals, reptiles and birds that were on that sheet]?
Questions.A: He heard a voice speaking to him. He knew that it was the Lord.
The Lord said to him, "Stand up, Peter. Kill something and eat the meat." (13)
Questions.Alternative: What did Peter hear as he looked at the animals, reptiles and birds that were on that sheet?
What did Peter hear?

Questions.Q: What did Peter reply?
Questions.A: Peter refused. He said to the Lord "No, Lord. I have never eaten any meat that our [Jewish law] forbids us to eat." (14)

Questions.Q: What did the Lord say to him after that?
Questions.A: The Lord said to him, "Do not say that something is not fit for you to eat which God has said is fit for you to eat." (15)

Questions.Q: How many times did this happen?
Questions.A: It happened three times. (16)
Questions.Note: T.N. on Acts states that "this happened" refers to what God had just said to Peter: "Do not call anything impure that God has made clean." Undoubtedly, God said those words three times in order to emphasize their importance. It seems unlikely that Peter had the vision of the sheet containing ritually unclean animals three times." See 11:10.

Questions.Q: What happened to the sheet after the Lord finished speaking?
Questions.A: The sheet was taken back to heaven [by someone]. (16)

Questions.Q: What did Peter think about the vision?
Questions.A: He wondered about the meaning of the vision. // He tried to understand what the vision meant. (17)

Questions.Q: What happened while Peter was wondering about the meaning of the vision?
Questions.A: The three men whom Cornelius had sent arrived at the gate of the house of Simon the tanner where Peter was staying. They asked the person who met them at the gate if Simon Peter was staying there. (17b-18)

Questions.Q: How did Peter know that he should go down from the roof to meet someone who was looking for him?
Questions.A: The Holy Spirit told Peter that three men had come looking for him.
The Holy Spirit also told him that he should go with the three men, because he/the Holy Spirit had sent them. (19-20)

Questions.Q: What did Peter do?
Questions.A: Peter went down and met the men whom Cornelius had sent.
He told them that he was the one for whom they were looking.
He asked them for what purpose they had come there. (21)

Questions.Q: What did the three men reply/answer to Peter?
Questions.A: The men told Peter that Cornelius had sent them, and that he was a worshiper of God.
The men told Peter that the Jewish people in Caesarea knew about Cornelius and respected him highly.
The men told Peter that an angel had told Cornelius that he should invite Peter to come to his home so that he could hear what Peter would tell him. (22)
Questions.Alternative: What did the three men reply to Peter?
What did the three men answer to Peter?

Questions.Q: How did Peter reply to this invitation?
Questions.A: [Peter agreed to go with them, but since it was already afternoon, they would not go until the next day.] So Peter invited the men to come in and spend the night there.
The next day, Peter started the trip to Caesarea with the three men whom Cornelius had sent.
He took with him several believers from Joppa. (23)

Questions.Q: When did they arrive in Caesarea?
Questions.A: They arrived the following day. (24)

Questions.Q: Whom had Cornelius invited to come to his house?
Questions.A: He had called his relatives and close friends to come [and hear what Peter had to say]. (24)

Questions.Q: Describe what happened when Peter arrived at the house of Cornelius.
Questions.A: When Peter arrived at the door of Cornelius's house, Cornelius came out and bowed down before him, showing a great amount of reverence.
Peter told him to get up, because he himself was also only a human being.
So they went inside the house, where Peter saw the group of relatives and friends whom Cornelius had invited to come to his home. [They were all waiting to hear what Peter was going to say.] (25-27)

Questions.Q: What did Peter say first when he began to speak to that group of people?
Questions.A: He told them they all knew that it is against the [Jewish] law for a Jew to associate with or visit a Gentile.
He told them that God had shown him [in a vision] that he should not say that Gentiles/non-Jews are not acceptable to God and not fit for a Jew with whom they could associate.
Peter told them that when the messengers from Cornelius had arrived and asked him to go and visit Cornelius, he willingly agreed and went with them. (28-29)
Questions.Note: Cornelius and his friends and relatives were Gentiles.

Questions.Q: What answer did Cornelius give when Peter asked him, "Why did you send for me?"
Questions.A: Cornelius told Peter about the angel who had appeared to him and told him to send messengers to Joppa to bring Peter to his home.
Cornelius said the angel told him in whose house Peter was staying.
Then Cornelius said, now that Peter had come, he and the people whom he had invited were all waiting to hear what the Lord had told Peter to tell them. (30-33)

Section.heading: Acts 10:34-48 Peter preached to Cornelius and his household about Jesus Christ. They believed and immediately received the Holy Spirit.

Questions.Q: What did Peter tell the people who had gathered in the home of Cornelius about Jesus?
Questions.A: Peter reminded those people what Jesus of Nazareth had done during his years on earth. (36-38)
He also told them that although the Jews had killed Jesus, God had raised him to life. (39-40)

Questions.Q: How did the people who were listening respond to what Peter had preached about Jesus?
Questions.A: The people who were listening believed in Jesus and immediately received the Holy Spirit. (44)

Questions.Q: As Peter began to speak to the people in the home of Cornelius, what did he say that he now understood?
Questions.A: He said that now he understood/realized that God does not favor only certain people. (34)
God accepts/welcomes/receives anyone who reveres/honors him and who does what pleases him. (35)

Questions.Q: As Peter preached about Jesus in Cornelius's home, how did he describe the message he was going to tell them?
Questions.A: Peter said the gospel was the message that God sent to the people of Israel through Jesus Christ.
Peter also said that God had proclaimed that he would cause people to be rightly related with him/at peace with him because of what Jesus Christ had done for all people. (36)

Questions.Q: What did Peter remind Cornelius and his relatives and friends that they knew/had heard?
Questions.A: He reminded them that a man named Jesus of Nazareth had lived in Judea.
He reminded them what had happened throughout Judea when Jesus was there.
He reminded them that they knew that God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Spirit and power.
They also knew that Jesus had traveled around in his own country/the land of the Jews doing good by healing all those who were sick and who were tormented by the devil. (37-38)
Questions.Alternative: What did Peter remind Cornelius and his relatives and friends that they knew?
What did Peter remind Cornelius and his relatives and friends that they had heard?

Questions.Q: What do you know about the Devil?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The name "Devil" is the Greek equivalent of the Hebrew name for "Satan". Satan is the chief enemy of God. He is the supreme evil spiritual being, who leads and directs all other evil spiritual beings. (See "Devil" in KBT in the "Satan" entry.)

Questions.Q: What additional facts about Jesus did Peter say that he and the other apostles had personally seen and heard?
Questions.A: Peter said that he and the other apostles had personally seen what Jesus did when he was among the people of Israel/in the country of the Jews, including Jerusalem.
He said they had also seen him being killed by being nailed to a cross [by the leaders in Jerusalem].
Peter and the other apostles had also seen him after God had raised him to life again three days later.
They had even eaten and drunk with Jesus after God had raised him to life again. (39-41)

Questions.Q: What message had Jesus told his followers to preach?
Questions.A: Jesus had told his followers to tell [the Jewish] people that he is the person whom God has chosen to judge all people, both the living and those who have died. (42)

Questions.Q: What did the prophets write about Jesus/the Messiah long ago?
Questions.A: They wrote that [God] will forgive the sins of anyone who believes in Jesus. (43)
Questions.Alternative: What did the prophets write about Jesus long ago?
What did the prophets write about the Messiah long ago?

Questions.Q: What showed that Cornelius and his relatives and friends who were listening to Peter preach believed the message about Jesus Christ?
Questions.A: While Peter was still preaching, those who were listening received the Holy Spirit/the Holy Spirit came on all who heard the message.
[The Holy Spirit] enabled them to speak in languages different from their own languages.
They were praising God in those languages.
[This was a sign that God had received them as his people.] (44, 46)

Questions.Q: What did the believers who had come with Peter from Joppa think and say?
Questions.A: They were very much surprised that God had given the Holy Spirit even to the non-Jews/Gentiles. [This was a sign that God accepts non-Jews as his people as freely and completely as he accepts Jewish people when they believe in Jesus Christ.] (45)
Questions.Note: The Jews thought that God gave the Holy Spirit only to Jews who became believers in Jesus Christ.
Questions.Alternative: What did the believers who had come with Peter from Joppa think?
How did the believers who had come with Peter from Joppa react?
How did the believers who had come with Peter from Joppa react when they saw that God had given the Holy Spirit to non-Jews?
How did the believers who had come with Peter from Joppa react when they saw that God had given the Holy Spirit to Gentiles?

Questions.Q: What was the reason that Peter believed that [he and the other Jewish believers] should baptize these non-Jewish believers?
Questions.A: He believed this because God had given the Holy Spirit to these non-Jews just as he had given the Holy Spirit to the Jewish believers. (47)
Questions.Alternative: What was the reason that Peter believed that he and the other Jewish believers should baptize these non-Jewish believers?
What was the reason that Peter believed that should baptize these non-Jewish believers?

Questions.Q: What did Peter do then?
Questions.A: He said that [he] should baptize them [to show that they had believed] in the [Lord] Jesus Christ. (48)

Section.heading: Acts 11:1-18 Peter explained to the believers in Jerusalem the reason that he had visited the home of the Gentile, Cornelius.

Questions.Q: What did the apostles and other believers in Judea hear about the Gentiles?
Questions.A: They heard that the Gentiles had heard the word of God and believed it. (1)

Questions.Q: What group of believers in Jerusalem criticized Peter because he had visited a Gentile and eaten meals in his home?
Questions.A: The believers in Jerusalem who thought that Gentiles who became believers needed to be circumcised in order for God to accept them criticized Peter. (2-3)

Questions.Q: In what way did Peter answer them?
Questions.A: Peter told them all about his visit to the home of Cornelius and what God had taught him through that visit.

Questions.Q: Who heard that some Gentiles had believed the message about Jesus Christ/received the word of God?
Questions.A: The apostles and other believers who were living throughout the area of Judea (province) heard that some Gentiles had believed in Jesus Christ. (1)
Questions.Alternative: Who heard that some Gentiles had believed the message about Jesus Christ?
Who heard that some Gentiles had received the word of God?
Who heard that some Gentiles had believed the message about Jesus Christ and received the word of God?

Questions.Q: What was the reason that some of the Jewish believers in Jerusalem criticized Peter?
Questions.A: They criticized him for going into the house of non-Jewish people and eating with them. (2-3)

Questions.Q: Who were the people who criticized him?
Questions.A: The Jewish believers in Jerusalem who believed that all believers needed to be circumcised criticized Peter. (2-3)

Questions.Q: What did Peter reply to those who criticized him?
Questions.A: Peter told the Jewish believers in Jerusalem that while he was in Joppa praying he had seen a vision. (5)
Peter described the vision of a large sheet containing many animals, including reptiles and birds of the air that were edible [but which Jews were ritually prohibited to eat]. (5-6)
He told how a voice/God had told him to kill something and eat the meat. (7)
Peter refused, because he had never eaten any meat that the [Jewish law] did not allow Jews to eat. (8)
Three times [God] told Peter not to call anything impure that God had made clean. (9-10)

Questions.Q: What did Peter then tell those believers in Jerusalem had happened after the vision had disappeared?
Questions.A: He told them that just after the vision disappeared, the three men [whom Cornelius] had sent to get Peter arrived at the house where Peter was staying [and asked him to go with them to Caesarea].

The Holy Spirit showed Peter that he should go with those men confidently/without doubting. So he went, taking six [Jewish] believers [from Joppa] with him, and they went into the [non-Jewish] man's house.
Peter told those believers that Cornelius had been instructed by an angel to send to Joppa for Peter, so that he could tell Cornelius and his household how they could be saved [by God]. (11-14)

Questions.Q: How did Peter describe the coming of the Holy Spirit upon Cornelius and the others in his house?
Questions.A: Peter said that when he had begun to tell the message about Jesus, the Holy Spirit had come down on those who were listening just like he did on the first group of believers [on the Day of Pentecost]. (15)

Questions.Q: What promise that Jesus had given to his disciples did Peter quote as he told the Jewish believers in Jerusalem about his visit in Caesarea?
Questions.A: He quoted the promise that Jesus had given to his followers. Jesus said, "John baptized you with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit." (16)

Questions.Q: In what way did Peter apply this promise to the Gentile believers in the house of Cornelius?
Questions.A: Jesus had promised that the Holy Spirit would be given to his disciples.
Now, God had given the Holy Spirit to Cornelius and the others in his home as they listened to the gospel message.
This was proof that God had accepted them as believers, just as he had accepted Jews who believed in Jesus as their Lord and their Messiah.
Peter said that because of this, he could not possibly oppose God for receiving those people as believers in Jesus Christ. (17)

Questions.Q: What did the Jewish believers who had criticized Peter do after they heard what he had to say?
Questions.A: They stopped criticizing Peter and [instead] they praised God.
They believed that God had enabled non-Jews to repent [and believe in Jesus]. In this way, he had given Gentiles the opportunity to live [eternally]. (18)

Section.heading: Acts 11:19-30 Believers who left Jerusalem spread the message about Jesus Christ to Gentiles in many places.

Questions.Q: For what reason did many of the believers who had lived in Jerusalem leave there?
Questions.A: When Stephen was stoned [by the Jewish religious leaders], the Jews who were hostile to the believers persecuted many other believers also. The believers went to many places, including Phoenicia (a coastal plain), (the island of) Cyprus, and (the city of) Antioch, which was in Syria (a province). (19a)

Questions.Q: What did these believers do in the places where they settled?
Questions.A: They told the message [about Jesus Christ] only to the Jews. (19b)

Questions.Q: What did some believers from the island of Cyprus and from the town of Cyrene do in the city of Antioch?
Questions.A: They told the message about the Lord Jesus to non-Jews/Gentiles as well as to Jews. (20)

Questions.Q: In what town did [people] first call believers in Jesus Christians?
Questions.A: [People] first called believers Christians in Antioch. (26)
Questions.Alternative: In what town did people first call believers in Jesus Christians?
In what town did first call believers in Jesus Christians?

Questions.Q: What was the result of God helping those believers with his power to preach the message about the Lord Jesus to non-Jews?
Questions.A: The result was that many of the Gentiles who heard the message about the Lord Jesus believed it and became his followers. (21)

Questions.Q: What did the Jewish believers in Jerusalem do when they heard that there was a large group of Gentile believers in Antioch?
Questions.A: [They wanted to be sure that the people in Antioch were truly believers, so] they sent [one of their own number], Barnabas, to Antioch to see what was happening there. (22)

Questions.Q: What kind of person was Barnabas?
Questions.A: Barnabas was a good man.
He was controlled by the Holy Spirit,
