and he had a strong faith [in God]. (24)

Questions.Q: What did Barnabas see and do in Antioch?
Questions.A: When Barnabas arrived in Antioch, he could see that many people had truly believed in the Lord Jesus and that God had blessed them.
He was happy to see that, and he encouraged the believers to continue to trust in the Lord Jesus and to obey his teachings.
Barnabas helped many people to believe in the Lord Jesus. (23-24)
Questions.Alternative: What did Barnabas see in Antioch and how did he respond?

Questions.Q: For what reason did Barnabas go to Tarsus and bring Saul to Antioch?
Questions.A: He went to Tarsus and brought Saul to Antioch to help teach the new believers.
Barnabas and Saul stayed in Antioch for a year, teaching the group of believers there. (25-26)

Questions.Q: Who was Agabus?
Questions.A: Agabus was one of several prophets who went down from Jerusalem to the group of believers in Antioch. (27-28)

Questions.Q: What did Agabus tell the believers was going to happen?
Questions.A: Agabus prophesied that there would be a severe famine in all the countries known at that time to be inhabited. The famine did happen during the reign of the Roman emperor Claudius. (28)

Questions.Q: What did the believers in Antioch do after they heard that there was a famine in the district of Judea?
Questions.A: Each of them gave as much [money] as they could to send to the believers in Judea (a province).
After they had collected it, they gave it to Barnabas and Saul and [asked them] to take it to the elders [of the church in Jerusalem]. (29-30)

Section.heading: Acts 12:1-19a Peter was freed from prison by an angel and escaped being killed [by Herod].

Questions.Q: What was the attitude of King Herod towards the believers?
Questions.A: King Herod persecuted some of the members of the church [in Jerusalem]. (1)

Questions.Q: Which two apostles whom Herod persecuted are mentioned?
Questions.A: Herod ordered [a soldier] to kill James, the brother of John, with a sword. (2)
After that, Herod ordered [soldiers] to arrest Peter and put him in prison. (3-4)

Questions.Q: For what reason did Herod persecute the believers?
Questions.A: The [leaders of the] Jewish people were pleased when Herod did that. (3)

Questions.Q: What happened that prevented Herod from carrying out his plan to have Peter killed?
Questions.A: At night an angel went to the prison cell where Peter was and brought him out of the jail into the city. (7-10)

Questions.Q: What did Herod plan to do after the Passover festival?
Questions.A: Herod was planning to have [the soldiers] bring Peter out of prison for a public trial after the Passover. [He would give him into the authority of the Jewish leaders, and they would condemn him to be killed by soldiers.] (4b)

Questions.Q: What did the other believers do when they heard that Peter was put in prison [by soldiers]?
Questions.A: They prayed to God earnestly that Peter [would be set free and would not be killed by soldiers]. (5)
Questions.Alternative: What did the other believers do when they heard that Peter was put in prison by soldiers?
What did the other believers do when they heard that Peter was put in prison?

Questions.Q: Describe how the angel took Peter out of the prison.
Questions.A: An angel appeared suddenly in the prison cell where Peter was.
Peter was asleep between two guards and was fastened with two chains. [Those guards did not see the angel.]
The angel tapped/nudged Peter on the side to wake him up.
Then the angel told him to quickly get up, and as he got up, the chains fell off his wrists. [The guards did not see this, because God had caused them to be asleep.]
Then the angel told Peter to fasten his belt and to put on his sandals and his cloak and to go with him.
So Peter did what the angel told him to do and followed the angel out of the prison. (6-9a)

Questions.Q: What did Peter think while he was following the angel out of the prison?
Questions.A: Peter thought he must be seeing a vision. He could not believe that he was really leaving the prison. (9b)

Questions.Q: How did Peter and the angel pass by two places where guards were stationed and, after that, pass through the outer gate of the prison and go out into the city?
Questions.A: Peter and the angel passed by the two sets of guards. [Those guards did not see them.]
When they reached the main gate of the prison, it swung open by itself, and they went out into the city. (10)

Questions.Q: When did the angel disappear?
Questions.A: When they had walked down one street of the city [which Peter recognized], the angel suddenly disappeared. (10)

Questions.Q: What did Peter think when he realized that now he was free but the angel had disappeared?
Questions.A: He realized that what he had thought must be a vision had really happened.
He knew that God had sent an angel to deliver him from the prison and from being turned over by Herod to the Jewish authorities.
[He knew that Herod's soldiers would surely have killed him.] (11)

Questions.Q: Where did Peter go after he realized that he was free?
Questions.A: He went to the home of Mary, the mother of John Mark. (12)

Questions.Q: What were the people doing who had gathered at the home of Mary?
Questions.A: The [believers] who had gathered there were praying. (12)

Questions.Q: What happened when Peter knocked on the gate?
Questions.A: A servant girl whose name was Rhoda came to the gate but did not open it.
She asked who was there, and when Peter answered, she recognized his voice.
Without opening the gate, she went back inside the house and joyfully told the other people that Peter was at the gate. (13-14)

Questions.Q: What do you think a servant does?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A servant is a person who is required to work for another person and obey him. Servants are usually paid for their work, while slaves are not paid.

Questions.Q: What did the other people in the house say when Rhoda told them that Peter had arrived?
Questions.A: The other people did not believe Peter could be there.
They told Rhoda she was crazy, or else that it must be Peter's angel that was there. (15)

Questions.Q: What happened when [someone] finally opened the gate and the people inside had come and seen Peter?
Questions.A: The people inside were amazed. [They were excited and probably were asking many questions.]
So Peter made a sign for them to be quiet.
Then he explained to them how the Lord had brought him out of prison.
He also told them that they should tell James and the other believers [that he was now free]. Then he left for another place. (16-17)
Questions.Alternative: What happened when someone finally opened the gate and the people inside had come and seen Peter?
What happened when finally opened the gate and the people inside had come and seen Peter?

Questions.Q: What happened the next day when the guards discovered that Peter had escaped?
Questions.A: The guards [and possibly other soldiers] searched carefully for Peter but did not find him. Herod questioned the guards [about how Peter could have escaped].
Then Herod ordered [other soldiers] to execute the guards. (18-19a)
Questions.Note: This was the way the Romans punished soldiers and guards for failing to do what they had been assigned to do.

Questions.Q: Why were the guards concerned about Peter's escape?
Questions.A: The guards knew that they would be held responsible (and would probably be executed).

Questions.Q: What was the purpose in Herod questioning the guards?
Questions.A: He was probably trying to determine whether they had let Peter escape on purpose. He might have been trying to see if someone had bribed them or threatened them.

Section.heading: Acts 12:19b-25 King Herod accepted praise [from the people] that was due only to God. He died soon afterwards.

Questions.Q: For what reason did the group of people from Tyre and Sidon need to speak to Herod?
Questions.A: The people of Tyre and Sidon had previously received their food supplies from the district governed by Herod.
But, he had become angry with the people of Tyre and Sidon and had stopped sending them food supplies. (20)

Questions.Q: Who was Blastus, and how did he help those people to regain the favor of Herod?
Questions.A: Blastus was a personal servant of Herod whom he trusted. He spoke to Herod, asking him to continue to send the people of Tyre and Sidon food supplies. (20)

Questions.Q: What did those people say when Herod, dressed in his royal robes, made a speech to them in public?
Questions.A: They were so pleased that they shouted that Herod was not just a man but was a god. (22)

Questions.Q: What happened that showed that God was not pleased with Herod?
Questions.A: When Herod accepted the people's praise, he immediately became very ill.
God caused that to happen because Herod had allowed the people to give him praise that only God deserves.
Soon after that, Herod died. (23)

Questions.Q: What did Herod do next?
Questions.A: Herod left the district of Judea and went to Caesarea, [where there was a palace for the Roman governor]. (19b)

Questions.Q: What attitude did King Herod have towards the people of Tyre and Sidon?
Questions.A: Herod was angry with the people of Tyre and Sidon. (20a)

Questions.Q: What did Herod do to the people of Tyre and Sidon as a result of his anger towards them?
Questions.A: [He did not allow grain from the part of Judea that he governed to be sent to Tyre and Sidon.] (20)

Questions.Q: What did the people of Tyre and Sidon do?
Questions.A: A group of the people from Tyre and Sidon [went to Caesarea] to make peace with Herod, because they needed the grain supplies that he had refused to send to them.
They were able to make arrangements with Blastus, who was the king's trusted personal servant, to get permission for them to talk with King Herod. (20b)

Questions.Q: What else happened at the time that the delegation from Tyre and Sidon was there?
Questions.A: On a day which Herod had chosen, he appeared in public in his royal robes and sat on his throne.
Then he made a speech to the crowd of people. (21)

Questions.Q: What did the people say when they heard Herod's speech?
Questions.A: His speech pleased them very much. They shouted that Herod was not just a man, he was a god. (22)

Questions.Q: What happened then?
Questions.A: An angel of the Lord caused Herod immediately to fall down in great pain.
[A few days later] Herod died from an illness in which worms ate his body. (23)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that God punished Herod?
Questions.A: God punished him because Herod showed no respect for God when he allowed the crowd to compare him to a god.
He should have told them that God is great and there is no man like him. (23)

Questions.Q: What effect did King Herod have on the believers by persecuting them?
Questions.A: In spite of his persecution of the believers, more and more people in different places heard the message about the Lord Jesus and became his disciples. (24)

Questions.Q: Whom did Paul and Barnabas bring back to Antioch with them?
Questions.A: They brought back John Mark. (25)

Section.heading: Acts 13:1-3 The Holy Spirit told leaders in the church in Antioch to appoint Barnabas and Saul to do a special work for God.

Questions.Q: For what reason did Barnabas and Saul leave Antioch?
Questions.A: While the believers in Antioch who had gifts as prophets and teachers were praying and fasting, the Holy Spirit told them that he had chosen Saul and Barnabas for a special work. (1-2)

Questions.Q: Five men who were leaders in the group of believers in Antioch had certain spiritual gifts. Who were these men, and what spiritual gifts did they have?
Questions.A: The men with gifts were Barnabas, Simeon, Lucius, Manaen, and Saul.
[They ministered to the other believers] by prophesying and by teaching [the Word of God]. (1)

Questions.Q: What happened while these men were praying and fasting?
Questions.A: The Holy Spirit told them that he had chosen Barnabas and Saul to do a special work for him. The Holy Spirit told them to appoint those men to do that work. (2)

Questions.Q: What did these men, and perhaps others of the believers, do after they had received this word from the Holy Spirit?
Questions.A: They fasted and prayed some more and then they placed their hands on Barnabas and Saul, authorizing them to go [and do the work that the Holy Spirit had given them to do]. (3)

Section.heading: Acts 13:4-12 Barnabas and Saul went to Cyprus and preached to people there about the Lord Jesus.

Questions.Q: With what two people on Cyprus did Paul and Barnabas meet and speak?
Questions.A: Saul and Barnabas met and preached to Sergius Paulus.
Sergius Paulus was the Governor of the island, and he wanted to hear the word of God. (7)
Saul and Barnabas also met a man whose name was Elymas.
Elymas opposed the message that Saul and Barnabas told the Governor. (6, 8)

Questions.Q: To what place did the Holy Spirit instruct Barnabas and Saul to go, and who went with them?
Questions.A: Barnabas and Saul went to (the island of) Cyprus.
They took with them John Mark as their helper. (4-5)

Questions.Q: Where did Barnabas and Saul first tell the people the message [about Jesus Christ]?
Questions.A: In (the town of) Salamis, (on the eastern coast of Cyprus), Barnabas and Saul went to the Jewish synagogues and told the people that message. (5)
Questions.Alternative: Where did Barnabas and Saul first tell the people the message about Jesus Christ?
Where did Barnabas and Saul first tell the people the message?

Questions.Q: Where did Barnabas, Saul and John Mark meet Bar-Jesus?
Questions.A: They met Bar-Jesus in (the town of) Paphos, (which was at the west end of Cyprus). (6)

Questions.Q: What kind of person was Bar-Jesus?
Questions.A: Bar-Jesus was a Jewish magician/sorcerer and a false prophet. (6b)
He was also an attendant of the [Roman] governor [of the island]. (7a)

Questions.Q: What do you think a false prophet did?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A false prophet was a person who claimed to be a prophet of God, but was not. His messages were deceptive and led to confusion. (See "false prophet" in KBT in the "prophet" entry.)

Questions.Q: What was the name of the governor of the island, and how did Barnabas and Saul meet him?
Questions.A: The name of the governor was Sergius Paulus.
He sent [someone] to bring Barnabas and Saul to him because he wanted them to tell him the message from God [about Jesus]. (7b)

Questions.Q: What other name did [people] call Bar-Jesus?
Questions.A: [People] also called Bar-Jesus by the name Elymas. [In the Greek language] Elymas means "the sorcerer." (8)
Questions.Note: Several people who Luke has mentioned in Acts had two names. For example, Tabitha, or Dorcas (9:36), Bar-Jesus, or Elymas (13:6, 8), and Saul, or Paul (13:9). (See the NIV footnote on 9:36.) The reason that these people had two names was that one was the person's name in Hebrew, or Aramaic, and the other was his or her name in Greek.
Questions.Alternative: What other name did people call Bar-Jesus?
What other name did call Bar-Jesus?

Questions.Q: What did Elymas do when he knew that the governor had listened to Barnabas and Saul tell him the message about Jesus?
Questions.A: He tried to persuade Sergius Paulus that what Barnabas and Saul preached was not true.
He tried to keep the governor from believing [in Jesus].
He may also have acted toward Barnabas and Saul in a hostile manner. (8)

Questions.Q: What did Paul do when Elymas tried to keep Sergius Paulus from believing the message about Jesus Christ?
Questions.A: Paul looked straight at Elymas and called him a son of the Devil.
He said that Elymas opposed everything which is right/good/true.
He said that Elymas was always lying to people and doing other evil things to them.
He said that Elymas repeatedly persuaded people that the truths of the word of God were lies. (9-10)

Questions.Q: What did Paul tell Elymas was going to happen to him because he opposed Barnabas and Paul?
Questions.A: Paul told Elymas that the Lord was going to make him completely blind for a while.
God would punish him in this way for opposing the message that Barnabas and Paul preached. (11)

Questions.Q: What happened to Elymas after Paul said this?
Questions.A: Elymas immediately became so blind that everything became dark for him.
He could not even see where he was going and had to find someone to take him by the hand and lead him. (11b)

Questions.Q: What did the governor do when he saw what happened to Elymas?
Questions.A: The governor believed that the message that Paul preached [about the Lord Jesus] was true when he saw that Elymas became blind, just as Paul had told him he would. (12)

Section.heading: Acts 13:13-52 Paul and Barnabas preached in Pisidia (province) about the Lord Jesus.

Questions.Q: What happened on the first Sabbath that Paul and Barnabas went to the synagogue in Antioch?
Questions.A: The officials of the synagogue invited Paul and Barnabas to speak, and Paul preached to them about the Lord Jesus.
He told the people that Jesus was the Messiah.

Questions.Q: How did the people in the synagogue respond to that message?
Questions.A: Some of the people invited them to come back on the following Sabbath to tell them more. (42)

Questions.Q: Where did Paul and his companions go when they left Paphos [on the island of Cyprus]?
Questions.A: Paul, Barnabas, and John Mark sailed by ship from Paphos to the town Perga in the province of Pamphylia. (13a)
Questions.Alternative: Where did Paul and his companions go when they left Paphos on the island of Cyprus?
Where did Paul and his companions go when they left Paphos?

Questions.Q: Where did they go from Perga?
Questions.A: After they arrived in Perga, John Mark left the others and started on his way back to Jerusalem.
Paul and Barnabas went north to (the town of) Antioch (which was near the district of Pisidia). (13b-14a)

Questions.Q: What do you think the Sabbath means?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The Sabbath is the name of the seventh and last day of the week. It was set aside by the Jews as a strict day of rest from the normal work that was done on the six other days of the week. The Jews continue to observe the Sabbath on Saturday.
Questions.Note: See "Sabbath" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did Paul and Barnabas do on the first Sabbath that they were in Antioch?
Questions.A: On the first Sabbath that Paul and Barnabas were in Antioch, they went to the synagogue to worship God, and they sat down.

[One of the men] read from the [books of the] Law [which Moses had written] and from what the [other] prophets [had written]. Then the rulers of the synagogue sent [someone] who invited Paul and Barnabas to speak to the people/congregation. (14b-15)

Questions.Q: What did Paul speak about in the first part of his message?
Questions.A: In the first part of his message, Paul gave a brief review of the history of the people of Israel, from the time when they were in Egypt until the time they entered Canaan. (16-20a)

Questions.Q: What two events did Paul mention that especially showed how God helped the Israelites in ways that showed his power?
Questions.A: God showed his great power when he made it possible for the Israelites to leave Egypt, [even though Pharaoh repeatedly forbade them to leave].
[When the Israelites arrived in Canaan], God again showed his power by helping them to claim the land of Canaan for themselves.
The land of Canaan belonged to seven other people groups. But, God gave the Israelites victory over those people groups. (17b-19)

Questions.Q: What part of the history of the Israelites did Paul review next?
Questions.A: In the next part of his sermon Paul mentioned the time when the Israelites were [ruled] by judges. After that, Paul mentioned the time when they began to be ruled by kings. (20b-22)

Questions.Q: What well known men in Israel's history did Paul mention in this period of Israel's history?
Questions.A: Paul mentioned Samuel, who was the last of the judges and was also a prophet.
He also spoke about two kings. The kings were Saul and David. (20b-22)

Questions.Q: In describing David, Paul said two things about him which suggested why God chose him to be the king of Israel after he removed Saul. What were those two things?
Questions.A: God chose David to be the king of Israel because he was "a man after God's own heart" and because David would do everything that God wanted him to do. (22)

Questions.Q: What important fact did Paul say about David?
Questions.A: Paul said that David was the person [to whom] God had promised that one of his descendants would be the Savior for the people of Israel.
That descendant was Jesus. (23)

Questions.Q: What person in Israel's history did Paul remind his hearers of next?
Questions.A: Next, Paul spoke about John [the Baptist], who had preached that the Israelites should turn from their sins and be baptized.
As he preached that they should repent, John also told them that [the Messiah they had been waiting for] was about to appear. (24-25)

Questions.Q: What did Paul call his Jewish and non-Jewish hearers when he began to talk about the message of salvation?
Questions.A: Paul addressed his hearers as the descendants of Abraham and God-fearing Gentiles.
He told them that [God] has caused us [all] to hear this message about [Jesus, who is] the one who can save [us all]. (26)

Questions.Q: Paul then reviewed the facts about how Jesus died. As he did this, he mentioned the Old Testament scriptures. What did he say about those scriptures?
Questions.A: Paul said that every Sabbath, [someone] read the scriptures in which the prophets [wrote about the Messiah].
They prophesied that [the Messiah's] own people would condemn him [and that people would kill him]. (27)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means if/that someone condemns someone else?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that someone pronounces someone else guilty with the clear implication that the person will be punished for what he did. (See "condemn" in KBT in the "judge, judgment" entry.)
Questions.Alternative: What do you think it means if someone condemns someone else?
What do you think it means that someone condemns someone else?

Questions.Q: What was the reason that the people of Jerusalem and their rulers demanded that Jesus be killed [by people], even though they had heard those prophecies about the Messiah many times?
Questions.A: They demanded that Jesus be killed, because they did not recognize that Jesus [was the Messiah about whom the prophets had written]. (27)
Questions.Alternative: What was the reason that the people of Jerusalem and their rulers demanded that Jesus be killed by people, even though they had heard those prophecies about the Messiah many times?
What was the reason that the people of Jerusalem and their rulers demanded that Jesus be killed, even though they had heard those prophecies about the Messiah many times?

Questions.Q: What else did Paul say about the rulers of the Jews?
Questions.A: He said that when they demanded that Jesus [should be killed by people], they did what the prophets had written [people would do to the Messiah]. (27)

Questions.Q: What other event in the life of Jesus fulfilled a promise that God had made to the people of Israel?
Questions.A: God fulfilled a promise he had made to the people of Israel when he raised Jesus from the dead [three days after Jesus was crucified by people]. (32-33)

Questions.Q: In the verse from Psalm 2 which Paul quoted, who was speaking, and to whom did he speak?
Questions.A: God was speaking to the Messiah. (33)

Questions.Q: To what event in the life of Jesus did Paul apply the verse from Psalm 2?
Questions.A: Paul said that the verse from Psalm 2 referred to the resurrection of Jesus.
He said that when God caused Jesus to rise again, God showed that Jesus was the Messiah and also was his Son. (33)

Questions.Q: What promise that God had given to David did Paul quote?
Questions.A: Paul quoted this verse from the prophecy of Isaiah, "I will give you the holy and sure blessings promised to David." (34)
Questions.Note: This prophecy is from Isaiah 55:3

Questions.Q: What did God refer to when he made this promise?
Questions.A: When God made this promise, he had told David that he would cause one of David's descendants to be the Savior of the people of Israel.
He/that person would bring many blessings to God's people. (34)
Questions.Note: See 13:23 for the promise that God made with David.

Questions.Q: In what way did Jesus fulfill the promise that God would give his people "the holy and sure blessings promised to David"?
Questions.A: Jesus fulfilled the promise when God raised him to life after he had died. [This proved that Jesus was the descendant of David who God had promised to send to the Israelites]. (34)
Questions.Note: See John 12:34.

Questions.Q: For what reason did Paul remind the people in the synagogue that after David had died and [people] had buried his body, his body had decayed?
Questions.A: Paul wanted the people in the synagogue to recognize that David was not speaking about himself when he wrote: "You will not let your Holy One undergo decay." (35-37)
Questions.Alternative: For what reason did Paul remind the people in the synagogue that after David had died and people had buried his body, his body had decayed?
For what reason did Paul remind the people in the synagogue that after David had died and had buried his body, his body had decayed?

Questions.Q: What was the most important fact that Paul told the people in the synagogue about Jesus?
Questions.A: He told them that [God] would forgive them for their sins and count them as justified/righteous if they would believe [in Jesus as their Savior]. (38-39)

Questions.Q: What did Paul tell the people in the synagogue that obeying the law of Moses could not do for them?
Questions.A: He told them that [God] would not count them as righteous even if they had obeyed the law of Moses. (39)
Questions.Note: The people who practiced the religion of the Jews thought that if they obeyed the laws of Moses very carefully, God would forgive their sins and say they were righteous.

Questions.Q: What did Paul next warn the people in the synagogue not to do when he quoted this prophecy?
Questions.A: Paul warned them not to scoff at/reject what he had preached about [Jesus].
If they rejected the message about Jesus, God was also going to punish them severely. (40-41)
Questions.Note: When the prophet Habakkuk wrote those words, God was soon going to severely punish his people, the Israelites. Paul was warning those in the synagogue in Antioch of Pisidia that if they rejected the message about Jesus Christ, God was also going to punish them severely.

Questions.Q: What did [many of] the people who heard the message that Paul gave ask Paul and Barnabas to do?
Questions.A: They asked Paul and Barnabas to come [to the synagogue] again the following Sabbath and preach/speak to them again about the things [which Paul had just told them]. (42)
Questions.Alternative: What did many of the people who heard the message that Paul gave ask Paul and Barnabas to do?
What did the people who heard the message that Paul gave ask Paul and Barnabas to do?

Questions.Q: What did Paul and Barnabas mean when they told the people who wanted to hear [about the Lord Jesus again] that they should "continue in the grace of God"?
Questions.A: Paul and Barnabas told them to continue to believe that it was only through trusting in Jesus/the Savior, whom God had sent, that [God] would forgive their sins. (43)
Questions.Alternative: What did Paul and Barnabas mean when they told the people who wanted to hear about the Lord Jesus again that they should "continue in the grace of God"?
What did Paul and Barnabas mean when they told the people who wanted to hear that they should "continue in the grace of God"?

Questions.Q: What happened when Paul and Barnabas returned [to the synagogue] on the next Sabbath?
Questions.A: Almost all the people in the city, both Jews and Gentiles, gathered to hear [Paul preach again] about Jesus Christ.
But, when the [leaders of the] Jews, [who had rejected that message], saw how many people had gathered to hear Paul and Barnabas, they were jealous.
So they opposed Paul and said abusive things about his message/what he was saying. (44-45)
Questions.Alternative: What happened when Paul and Barnabas returned to the synagogue on the next Sabbath?
What happened when Paul and Barnabas returned on the next Sabbath?

Questions.Q: How did Paul and Barnabas reply to the Jews who spoke against them and tried to keep people from believing the message about the Lord Jesus?
Questions.A: They told those Jews that it had been necessary to tell them the message from God [about Jesus] before they told it to the Gentiles. Because those Jews had rejected the message from God [about Jesus/the Savior who God had sent to them] now Paul and Barnabas would preach to the Gentiles. (46-47)

Questions.Q: What other reason did Paul say that he and Barnabas would now preach to the Gentiles?
Questions.A: He said they would preach to the Gentiles because the Lord had commanded them to do it. (47a)

Questions.Q: To whom did Paul apply the verse from the prophet Isaiah that he quoted?
Questions.A: Paul applied this word from the writings of Isaiah to himself. (47a)

Questions.Q: What do you think the figure of speech "a light for the Gentiles" means?
Questions.A: Paul applied this to himself. God was saying that he had appointed Paul to [reveal things about him/God] to non-Jewish people [like] a light [reveals things to people]. (46-47)

Questions.Q: How did the Gentiles who had heard Paul's sermon respond to it?
Questions.A: Many Gentiles/non-Jews were happy to hear the message about the Lord Jesus.

All of those non-Jewish people whom [God] had chosen to live eternally [with him] believed the message about the Lord Jesus. // They believed that the message was truly from God and trusted in the Lord Jesus for eternal life. (48)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for a person to have eternal life?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that a person will live forever with God.
Questions.Note: This eternal life is in the spiritual realm not the physical.

Questions.Q: What was the final result of the preaching of Paul and Barnabas in Antioch of Pisidia?
Questions.A: [Many believers] told the message about the Lord [Jesus] to other people in and around Antioch.
[Many more people believed in the Lord Jesus.] (49)

Questions.Q: What was the reason that Paul and Barnabas left Antioch and the surrounding area soon afterwards?
Questions.A: [Leaders of] the Jews [who had opposed the message of Paul and Barnabas] incited some of the men and women who had power in the city to join them in persecuting Paul and Barnabas.
So Paul and Barnabas had to leave that region. (50)

Questions.Q: What was the reason that Paul and Barnabas shook the dust off their feet when they left Antioch?
Questions.A: Paul and Barnabas shook the dust off their feet [to show those Jews that God had rejected them and would punish them]. (51)
Questions.Note: When Paul and Barnabas did this, they obeyed an instruction that Jesus had given to his disciples to shake the dust off of their feet when they and their message were rejected by the people.

Questions.Q: How did the disciples/believers in and around [Antioch] react when they heard that Paul and Barnabas were persecuted [by people] and had left?
Questions.A: They continued to rejoice greatly, and the Holy Spirit continued to control them. (52)
Questions.Alternative: How did the disciples in and around Antioch react when they heard that Paul and Barnabas were persecuted by people and had left?
How did the believers in and around Antioch react when they heard that Paul and Barnabas were persecuted by people and had left?
How did the disciples in and around Antioch react when they heard that Paul and Barnabas were persecuted and had left?
How did the believers in and around Antioch react when they heard that Paul and Barnabas were persecuted and had left?
How did the disciples in and around react when they heard that Paul and Barnabas were persecuted by people and had left?
How did the believers in and around react when they heard that Paul and Barnabas were persecuted by people and had left?
How did the disciples in and around react when they heard that Paul and Barnabas were persecuted and had left?
How did the believers in and around react when they heard that Paul and Barnabas were persecuted and had left?

Section.heading: Acts 14:1-7 Paul and Barnabas preached to the people in Iconium.

Questions.Q: In what ways was the time that Paul and Barnabas spent in Iconium like the time they had spent in Antioch of Pisidia?
Questions.A: In Iconium, Paul and Barnabas went to the Jewish synagogue [first] and preached there [about Jesus the Messiah and Savior].
A large number of both Jews and Gentiles became believers, just as both Jews and Gentiles in Antioch had done. (1)

Questions.Q: What did the Jews do who did not believe [the message that Paul preached]?
Questions.A: Those Jews told the Gentiles who had listened to Paul and Barnabas not to believe what they preached and taught.
They said that Paul and Barnabas were bad people and should not be trusted. (2)
Questions.Alternative: What did the Jews do who did not believe the message that Paul preached?
What did the Jews do who did not believe?

Questions.Q: What did Paul and Barnabas do after the Jews had opposed them and what they preached?
Questions.A: They stayed in Iconium for a long time and continued to preach and teach [the gospel] boldly, and they relied on the Lord [Jesus] to help them. (3a)

Questions.Q: In what way did the Lord Jesus show many people in Iconium that the message Paul and Barnabas preached was true?
Questions.A: The Lord Jesus gave Paul and Barnabas power to perform many miracles which helped the people.
In this way they knew that the message that Paul and Barnabas told them about the [Lord Jesus] was true. (3b)

Questions.Q: What phrase in this verse describes the message that Paul and Barnabas taught?
Questions.A: The writer of Acts described the message as "the message of [the Lord's] grace." (3)

Questions.Q: What did the people of Iconium think about the message Paul and Barnabas preached and taught?
Questions.A: The people of Iconium were divided about what they thought.
Some sided with the Jews [and opposed Paul and Barnabas and their preaching].
Others believed what Paul and Barnabas preached. (4)

Questions.Q: Many of the Jews, some of the Gentiles and some important leaders [opposed Paul and Barnabas]. What did those people plan to do?
Questions.A: The Jews and Gentiles and certain leaders in the city of Iconium together planned to stone Paul and Barnabas in order to kill them. (5)
Questions.Alternative: Many of the Jews, some of the Gentiles and some important leaders opposed Paul and Barnabas. What did those people plan to do?
What did the people who opposed Paul and Barnabas plan to do?
What did the people who sided with the Jews and opposed Paul and Barnabas plan to do?
What did many of the Jews, some of the Gentiles and some important leaders who opposed Paul and Barnabas plan to do?
What did the Jews, Gentiles and important leaders who opposed Paul and Barnabas plan to do?

Questions.Q: What did Paul and Barnabas do when they knew this?
Questions.A: They left quickly and went to another district, called Lycaonia.
They went to the towns of Lystra and Derbe in that district. (6)

Section.heading: Acts 14:8-20 In Lystra, Paul healed a lame man. Paul and Barnabas had to restrain the crowd from worshiping them as gods.

Questions.Q: What miracle did [God] enable Paul to do in Lystra?
Questions.A: Paul preached to a crowd of people [about the Lord Jesus].
A man who had been born lame believed the message and was instantly healed [by the Lord Jesus]. (8-10)
Questions.Alternative: What miracle did God enable Paul to do in Lystra?
What miracle was Paul able to do in Lystra?
What miracle did Paul do in Lystra?

Questions.Q: What did the rest of the people in the crowd say when they saw the man who had been lame, walking around?
Questions.A: When the rest of the people saw that the man was now healed, they said that Paul and Barnabas must be gods who had made themselves look like men. (11-12)

Questions.Q: In what way did the priest at the temple of Zeus and the crowd want to honor Paul and Barnabas, thinking that they were gods?
Questions.A: They wanted to offer a sacrifice to Paul and Barnabas, so the priest at the temple of Zeus brought two bulls to the city gates.
Then the priest at the temple of Zeus was going to sacrifice the bulls and lead the people in worshiping Paul and Barnabas. (13)

Questions.Q: What did Paul and Barnabas do to show the people that they should not worship them?
Questions.A: They rushed among the people, tearing their clothes to show that they were much concerned. They told the people they should not [worship them], because they were just men, like the Lystrans themselves. (14-15a)

Questions.Q: What did Paul tell the crowd of people about the gods that those people worshiped?
Questions.A: Paul told the people that the gods they worshiped were useless.
He told them that there is a living God, and they should turn to him and worship him. (15b)
Questions.Alternative: What did Paul tell the crowd of people about the gods that those people worshipped?

Questions.Q: What were some of the other things that Paul told the people about the living God?
Questions.A: Paul told the people that the living God has made heaven and the earth and the sea and all that is in them.
He has shown them that he is kind and generous by causing the rain to fall and the crops to grow.
He has given them plenty of food to eat and caused them to enjoy living/be happy.
Paul told them that the God who made everything wants people of all nations to worship him. (15, 17)

Questions.Q: How did the people respond after hearing what Paul said?
Questions.A: The people heard what Paul said, but they still thought they should kill those two bulls to honor Paul and Barnabas. But finally, Paul persuaded the people not to kill the bulls. (18)

Questions.Q: What happened that made Paul and Barnabas decide to leave Lystra?
Questions.A: Jews who had opposed Paul and Barnabas in Antioch and Iconium came to Lystra.
They persuaded a crowd of people there that Paul and Barnabas were bad people and that the message Paul was preaching was not true.
So the Jews and possibly some of those in the crowd threw stones at Paul until he fell down unconscious.
They all thought he was dead so they dragged him outside of the city and left him there. (19)

Questions.Q: What happened after that?
Questions.A: The disciples who had believed what Paul and Barnabas taught went out of the city and stood around Paul.
Then Paul [regained consciousness], stood up and went back into the city [with the disciples].
The next day, Paul and Barnabas left Lystra and went on their way to Derbe (a town). (20)

Section.heading: Acts 14:21-28 Paul and Barnabas preached in Derbe. They revisited the believers in three towns and then returned to Antioch in Syria.

Questions.Q: What did Paul and Barnabas do in Derbe?
Questions.A: They preached the message [about the Lord Jesus] and a large number of people believed in him/the Lord Jesus. (21a)

Questions.Q: Where did Paul and Barnabas go when they left the town Derbe?
Questions.A: They went back to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch in Pisidia. (21b)

Questions.Q: What word of counsel/reminder/warning did Paul and Barnabas give to those believers to encourage them to continue to trust the Lord Jesus when they had to suffer for believing in Jesus?
Questions.A: In order to encourage the believers to continue trusting in the Lord Jesus, Paul and Barnabas told them that we believers will endure many hardships before we will arrive in the presence of God/the time when God will rule [over us forever]. (22b)
Questions.Alternative: What word of counsel did Paul and Barnabas give to those believers to encourage them to continue to trust the Lord Jesus when they had to suffer for believing in Jesus?
What counsel did Paul and Barnabas give to those believers to encourage them to continue to trust the Lord Jesus when they had to suffer for believing in Jesus?
What reminder did Paul and Barnabas give to those believers to encourage them to continue to trust the Lord Jesus when they had to suffer for believing in Jesus?
What warning did Paul and Barnabas give to those believers to encourage them to continue to trust the Lord Jesus when they had to suffer for believing in Jesus?
What counsel did Paul and Barnabas give to those believers to encourage them to continue to trust the Lord Jesus when they would have to suffer for believing in Jesus?
What reminder did Paul and Barnabas give to those believers to encourage them to continue to trust the Lord Jesus when they would have to suffer for believing in Jesus?
What warning did Paul and Barnabas give to those believers to encourage them to continue to trust the Lord Jesus when they would have to suffer for believing in Jesus?

Questions.Q: How do you think this reminder/warning would encourage the believers?
Questions.Alternative: How do you think this reminder would encourage the believers?
How do you think this warning would encourage the believers?
How do you think this word of counsel would encourage the believers?
How do you think this counsel would encourage the believers?
Questions.Note: It is probable that those believers had endured some opposition from Jews and others who rejected the message about the Lord Jesus. They also knew that Paul and Barnabas had been persecuted repeatedly. Paul and Barnabas assured them that although they would be persecuted, they should be confident that they were on the road to heaven, "the kingdom of God."

Questions.Q: What did Paul and Barnabas do for each of the churches/group of believers?
Questions.A: They appointed elders for each of the churches.
[Just before Paul and Barnabas went on to the next town] they prayed and fasted and asked the Lord to strengthen and help the elders and the other believers. (23)
Questions.Alternative: What did Paul and Barnabas do for each of the churches?
What did Paul and Barnabas do for each of the group of believers?

Questions.Q: Where did Paul and Barnabas go next?
Questions.A: They traveled to (the district of) Pamphylia and preached the word of God at Perga (a town in Pamphylia).
Then they went to Attalia (a seaport town).
From Attalia they sailed back to Antioch (a town in the province of Syria). (24-26)

Questions.Q: What had happened earlier in Antioch?
Questions.A: The group of believers in Antioch had sent Paul and Barnabas to go on a journey to preach the message about Jesus Christ in places where the people had not yet heard that message. [The Holy Spirit had indicated that Paul and Barnabas should do that special work for him.] (26)

Questions.Q: What did Paul and Barnabas tell the group of believers in Antioch?
Questions.A: Paul and Barnabas told them about all the things that God had done through them.
They told them that God had enabled many Gentiles to become believers [in the Lord Jesus Christ]. (27)

Section.heading: Acts 15:1-21 The leaders of the Jerusalem church met and discussed a question which Christians/believers from Antioch asked.

Questions.Q: For what reason did Christians in Antioch think that God required them to be circumcised? What did they do about this important question?
Questions.A: Certain Jewish believers from Jerusalem had gone to Antioch and told the Gentile believers there that unless they were circumcised, God would not save them.
So/therefore, the people in Antioch chose a delegation to go to Jerusalem and ask the leaders of that church what they needed to do.

Questions.Q: Who were the visitors who arrived in Antioch? What did they tell the Gentile Christians there?
Questions.A: Some Jewish Christians came from Judea and told the Gentile Christians that they needed to be circumcised in order for God to save them. (1)

Questions.Q: What did the Christians/believers in Antioch do when they heard this teaching?
Questions.A: They decided to send Paul and Barnabas and a few other believers to Jerusalem to ask the leaders of the church there if that was/were true. (2)
Questions.Alternative: What did the Christians in Antioch do when they heard this teaching?
What did the believers in Antioch do when they heard this teaching?

Questions.Q: What did Paul and Barnabas do as they traveled through Phoenicia and Samaria?
Questions.A: They told the believers there that many Gentiles had believed in Jesus Christ. (3a)

Questions.Q: When the believers in Samaria heard that many Gentiles in other places had trusted in the Lord Jesus to save them, how did they respond?
Questions.A: The believers in Samaria were very happy when they heard that many Gentiles had trusted in the Lord Jesus. (3b)

Questions.Q: In Jerusalem, some of the Jewish Christians told the group of believers who had come from Antioch that Gentile believers needed to be circumcised and keep the rest of the Law of Moses. If they did not keep the Law of Moses, God would not forgive their sins and accept them. For what reason did they think that was true?
Questions.A: The believers who told Paul and Barnabas that still belonged to the group of Pharisees, and they were very careful to obey the Law of Moses. (5)

Questions.Q: Did the apostles and elders in Jerusalem think what those men said was true? What did they do to settle the question?
Questions.A: The apostles and elders had a meeting in which they discussed the question: "What does God require of Gentiles who become believers in the Lord Jesus?" (6)

Questions.Q: What did the apostle Peter say to answer this question?
Questions.A: Peter told that when he had preached to the Gentiles about the Lord Jesus, they had believed.
He said that while he was preaching, those Gentiles had received the Holy Spirit.
This showed that God had accepted them just as they were. (7-8)

Questions.Q: What does someone do when he believes?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He puts his trust and commitment in another person.
Questions.Note: See "believe" in KBT.

Questions.Q: When God gave those Gentiles the Holy Spirit, what else did that show/indicate?
Questions.A: When God gave the Gentiles the Holy Spirit as soon as they believed, that showed/indicated that he had forgiven their sins and accepted them as belonging to him. (9)
Questions.Alternative: When God gave those Gentiles the Holy Spirit, what else did that show?
When God gave those Gentiles the Holy Spirit, what else did that indicate?

Questions.Q: The Jewish Christians who were still Pharisees had said that Gentile Christians had to keep the Law of Moses in order for God to save them. To what did Peter compare that?
Questions.A: Peter said that requiring Gentile believers to keep the Law of Moses would be like asking them to do what even the Jews had never been able to do. (10)

Questions.Q: According to what Peter said, how does God save Jewish people?
Questions.A: God saves Jews in the same way that he saves Gentiles.
He saves both Jews and Gentiles by forgiving their sins when they trust in the Lord Jesus. (11)

Questions.Q: How did the other people present at that meeting respond when they heard what Barnabas and Paul told what happened when they preached to Gentiles?
Questions.A: The rest of the people listened quietly as Barnabas and Paul told about the many miracles that God had enabled them to do as they preached and taught his Word to the Gentiles. (12)

Questions.Q: What did the apostle James say about the Gentiles?
Questions.A: The apostle James said that long ago the Old Testament prophets had written that, in the future, a time would come when God would call Gentiles to seek after him and put their trust in him.
What Peter had just told about the conversion of Gentiles fulfilled that prophecy. (13-18)

Questions.Q: What advice did James give concerning the Gentiles who were turning to the true God?
Questions.A: James advised that the Gentiles who were now worshiping God should not be required to keep all of the Law of Moses.
There were just four things/practices [which Moses had] written in the Law that he believed the Gentiles should no longer do when they became Christians. (19-20)

Questions.Q: What were these four things/practices?
Questions.A: Gentiles who became Christians were to be advised not to eat food that had been offered to idols.
They were not to have a sexual relationship with any person except the one/husband or wife to whom they were married.
They were not to eat the meat of any animal that had been killed without draining its blood.
They were not to eat or drink the animal's blood. (20)
Questions.Alternative: What were these four things?
What were these four practices?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that James said that Gentiles who became Christians should avoid those four practices?
Questions.A: James said that the Law of Moses prohibited those four practices, as well as many others. Many Gentiles attended the Jewish synagogue before they believed in the true God and in his Son, Jesus.
They had heard the Law of Moses read many times.
Therefore, it would please the Jews if the Gentiles who became believers in Jesus Christ would observe/obey those parts of the Mosaic Law. (21)

Section.heading: Acts 15:22-35 The church leaders in Jerusalem sent a letter to the believers/Christians in Antioch.

Questions.Q: What did the church leaders in Jerusalem say in the letter that they sent to the Christians in Antioch?
Questions.A: The church leaders in Jerusalem told the [Gentile] believers in Antioch that they did not need to be circumcised.
However, there were four rules in the Law of Moses that they needed to obey.

Questions.Q: How did the leaders of the church in Jerusalem inform the Gentile believers in Antioch what they had decided?
Questions.A: The leaders of the Jerusalem church chose two of their own members to accompany Paul and Barnabas to Antioch.

Also, the leaders wrote a letter to the believers in Antioch, telling them what they had decided Gentile believers should do about the Law of Moses. The leaders sent this letter with the four men to Antioch. (22-23)

Questions.Q: Who were the members of the Jerusalem church that went to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas?
Questions.A: Judas Barsabbas and Silas, who were leaders in the Jerusalem church, went with Paul and Barnabas to Antioch. (22b)

Questions.Q: How did the apostles and elders in Jerusalem, who wrote the letter, describe themselves? To whom was the letter addressed?
Questions.A: The apostles and elders, who wrote the letter, described themselves as "your brothers."
The letter was addressed "To the Gentile believers/Christians in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia." (23)

Questions.Q: What did the letter say about the men who had gone from Judea to Antioch and told the believers there that they must keep the Mosaic Law?
Questions.A: The letter said that, although those people had gone from the Jerusalem church, the apostles and elders had not authorized nor sent them. (24)

Questions.Q: How did the writers of the letter describe Barnabas and Paul?
Questions.A: Barnabas and Paul were described as "our dear friends, who have risked their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ." (25b-26)

Questions.Q: Whom did the apostles and elders, who wrote the letter, say had decided what Gentile believers/Christians should do about keeping the Law of Moses?
Questions.A: They said in the letter that the Holy Spirit, together with the apostles and elders of the Jerusalem church, had decided that Gentile believers did not need to obey all of the Law. They had decided upon only a few things/rules that Gentile believers needed to obey. (28)
Questions.Alternative: Whom did the apostles and elders, who wrote the letter, say had decided what Gentile believers should do about keeping the Law of Moses?
Whom did the apostles and elders, who wrote the letter, say had decided what Gentile Christians should do about keeping the Law of Moses?

Questions.Q: What four rules from the Law of Moses did their letter mention?
Questions.A: The same four rules/practices that the apostle James had named/mentioned at the meeting in the church in Jerusalem were listed in the letter to the believers in Antioch. (29)
Questions.Note: However, in this letter, they were named in a different order. See 15:19-20.

Questions.Q: What did the men, who wrote the letter, say about the Gentile believers if they would keep those rules?
Questions.A: The writers of the letter said that if the Gentile believers would obey the four rules listed in the letter, they would do well. (29b)

Questions.Q: How did the Gentiles in the church in Antioch feel when someone read the letter from the Jerusalem church to them?
Questions.A: When the Gentile believers heard what the letter said, they were encouraged and very happy. (30-31)

Questions.Q: What did Judas Barsabbas and Silas do while they were in Antioch?
Questions.A: Judas and Silas were both prophets.
They spent time teaching the believers.
They encouraged the believers to continue to believe that God had saved them [through the grace of the Lord Jesus]. (32)

Section.heading: Acts 15:36-41 Paul and Barnabas separated and went to different places.

Questions.Q: What happened when Paul and Barnabas disagreed about whom they should take with them on their next trip?
Questions.A: Paul and Barnabas decided each to take a different companion and to go to different places. (39-40)

Questions.Q: Some time after Judas and Silas had returned to Jerusalem, Paul talked to Barnabas about something they could do together. What did Paul want to do?
Questions.A: Paul suggested to Barnabas that together they revisit the towns where they had preached on their previous trip.
They would see how each of the groups of believers was doing. (36)

Questions.Q: What did Barnabas answer?
Questions.A: Barnabas was willing to go with Paul to revisit those groups of believers, but he wanted to take John Mark with them. (37)

Questions.Q: Paul was not willing to take John Mark with them again. For what reason did Paul not want to take him?
Questions.A: John Mark had gone with Paul and Barnabas on the first part of their first trip, but he had left them and returned home right after they reached Pamphylia. (38)

Questions.Q: How did Paul and Barnabas settle their disagreement/argument?
Questions.A: Barnabas took John Mark and returned to Cyprus, and Paul decided to take a different companion. (39-40a)
Questions.Alternative: How did Paul and Barnabas settle their disagreement?
How did Paul and Barnabas settle their argument?

Questions.Q: Whom did Paul choose as a new companion, and where did they go?
Questions.A: Paul chose Silas as his companion.
The believers in Antioch prayed for Paul and Silas as they prepared to go on a trip together.
Then Paul and Silas set out to revisit the groups of Christians in Syria and Cilicia.
They traveled through Syria and Cilicia [provinces] encouraging the believers in each group. (40-41)

Section.heading: Acts 16:1-5 Paul chose Timothy to accompany him in his work.

Questions.Q: Who was Timothy? Where did Paul become acquainted with him?
Questions.A: Timothy was a believer with whom Paul became acquainted in Lystra.
His father was a Greek and his mother was a Jewish believer. (1)

Questions.Q: What did Paul do to be sure that Jewish Christians would receive Timothy well as his helper?
Questions.A: The Jewish Christians knew that Timothy had not been circumcised by his father because his father was Greek.
For that reason, Paul circumcised Timothy before taking him as a helper in his work. (3)

Questions.Q: When had Paul been to Lystra before?
Questions.A: On their first trip, Paul and Barnabas preached in places where people had not yet heard about Jesus Christ.
They had visited Lystra and had stayed long enough to win some disciples.
They had visited those disciples again before returning to Antioch in Syria. (See 14:8, 21.)

Questions.Q: What did the believers in Lystra and Iconium tell Paul and Silas about Timothy?
Questions.A: They said that Timothy was a good person. (2)

Questions.Q: As Paul and Silas traveled, visiting the groups of Gentile believers in various towns, what did they tell those believers?
Questions.A: They told those believers about the rules for Gentile Christians on which the leaders of the Jerusalem church had decided. (4)

Questions.Q: What happened when Paul and his companions visited the non-Jewish believers?
Questions.A: The Christians trusted more firmly in the Lord Jesus when they understood that he/God does not require people to obey the Law of Moses.
He/God saves people because they trust in the Lord Jesus.
As a result, more people became Christians in the places where Gentiles lived. (5)

Section.heading: Acts 16:6-10 Paul and his companions were guided by the Holy Spirit to go to Macedonia.

Questions.Q: To what places had Paul and his companions hoped to go and preach the message about the Lord Jesus?
Questions.A: They had hoped to go to the province of Asia, but were not able to.
Then they wanted to go to [the province of] Bithynia.
But the Holy Spirit hindered them from going to both of those provinces. (6-8)

Questions.Q: At what place did Paul have a vision by which God directed him where he and his companions should go?
Questions.A: When Paul and his companions were in Troas, Paul had a vision of a man from Macedonia.
The man called Paul to go over to Macedonia and help them.
So Paul and his companions went to Macedonia as soon as they were able to. (9-10)

Questions.Q: In what regions did Paul and his companions travel next?
Questions.A: Next, Paul and his companions traveled through the regions of Phrygia and Galatia.
[They preached to people about the true God and the message about the Lord Jesus.] (6a)
Questions.Alternative: In what regions did Paul and his companions travel, in this verse?
Where did Paul and his companions travel next?

Questions.Q: After that, the Holy Spirit hindered Paul and his companions from entering the region of Bithynia. Where did they go, instead?
Questions.A: When the Holy Spirit hindered them from entering Bithynia, Paul and his companions traveled along the border of Mysia and arrived at a port town called Troas. (7-8)

Questions.Q: What did Paul see in the vision? What did he believe the vision meant?
Questions.A: In his vision, Paul saw a man, standing at some distance from him.
The man urgently asked them to come to Macedonia.
[Macedonia was in Greece, on the other side of a stretch of sea.]
Paul and his companions decided that God was speaking to them through this vision. (9b)

Questions.Q: Who were Paul's traveling companions when he had the vision of the man from Macedonia?
Questions.A: The writer of Acts does not name Paul's companions here.
But from other parts of the story, we know that Timothy was there, as well as Silas.
Another person joined them in Troas, and he was the one who wrote about that part of the trip. (10)

Section.heading: Acts 16:11-15 In Philippi, Paul preached to Lydia, and she believed.

Questions.Q: To what city in Macedonia did Paul and his companions go? To whom did Paul preach there?
Questions.A: They went to Philippi, which was probably the largest city in that province. (12)
Paul preached to a group of women at the riverside who had met to worship God. (13)

Questions.Q: Who was Lydia? How did she help Paul and his companions?
Questions.A: Lydia was one of the women to whom Paul preached.
She believed the message about the Lord Jesus.
After she and the others of her household were baptized, Lydia invited Paul and his companions to stay in her home. (14-15)

Questions.Q: How did Paul and his companions travel to Macedonia?
Questions.A: They went on a ship from Troas to Macedonia. (11)
Questions.Note: Macedonia was in a province of the Roman Empire which was west of the province of Asia, where the town Troas was.

Questions.Q: To what city did they go, and what was that city like?
Questions.A: They went to Philippi, a city which was a Roman colony in Macedonia.
The officials who governed the city were Romans. (12)

Questions.Q: What did Paul and his companions do on the Sabbath/rest day of the Jews?
Questions.A: Because there was no synagogue in Philippi, Paul and his companions went along the river and found a group of women who had met to worship God.
Paul preached to them about the Lord Jesus. (13)
Questions.Alternative: What did Paul and his companions do on the Sabbath of the Jews?
What did Paul and his companions do on the Sabbath day of the Jews?
What did Paul and his companions do on the rest day of the Jews?

Questions.Q: Tell about the woman who was named Lydia.
Questions.A: Lydia was one of the women who had gathered to pray to the true God.
She was a Gentile, a native of a city called Thyatira, [which was] in the province of Asia.
She had a business of buying and selling purple cloth.
God "spoke to her heart"/enabled her to believe in the Lord Jesus.
The other people in her household also believed. (14)

Section.heading: Acts 16:16-40 Paul and Silas were put in prison. They preached to the jailer about the Lord Jesus, and he and his family believed.

Questions.Q: For what reason were Paul and Silas put in prison?
Questions.A: Paul cast an evil spirit out of a slave girl who told fortunes.
The owners of the girl took Paul and Silas to the Roman authorities and complained that they were teaching people to disobey the law.
The authorities ordered guards to whip Paul and Silas and then to put them in prison. (18-23)

Questions.Q: What happened to Paul and Silas? What happened to the jailer?
Questions.A: An earthquake freed Paul and Silas and the other prisoners from their chains.
It wakened the jailer and caused him to be afraid.
The jailer came and asked Paul and Silas how he could be saved.
Paul and Silas preached to him, and he believed in the Lord Jesus.
His family also believed. (26-32)

Questions.Q: When did Paul and Silas leave the prison? What message did Paul send to the Roman authorities?
Questions.A: The next morning, Paul sent word to the authorities that he and Silas were Roman citizens.
He complained that they/he and Silas had been punished without having committed any crime.
[That was against the laws of Rome.]
The authorities apologized and asked Paul and Silas to leave Philippi quietly and soon, and they did. (37-39)

Questions.Q: Tell about the slave girl whom Paul and his companions met on another Sabbath.
Questions.A: On another day Paul and his companions met a slave girl who was controlled by an evil spirit.
Paul and his companions met this girl several times.
The girl earned a lot of money for her owners, because the spirit enabled her to foretell the future. (16)

Questions.Q: What did the slave girl do each time that she met Paul and his companions?
Questions.A: Each time that she met Paul and the others, the slave girl followed them shouting, "These men are servants of the Most High God.
They are telling you how to be saved." (17)

Questions.Q: What did Paul do to stop the girl from following them and shouting about him and Silas?
Questions.A: Paul recognized that an evil spirit was causing the girl to follow them repeatedly and shout about them.
So Paul by the authority of Jesus Christ commanded the spirit to come out of her.
The spirit left her immediately. (18a)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the owners of the slave girl were angry when Paul did that?
Questions.A: After the evil spirit had come out of the girl, she was no longer able to predict the future.
So she was no longer able to earn money for her owners. (19a)

Questions.Q: What did the owners of the slave girl do then?
Questions.A: They seized Paul and Silas and dragged them to the marketplace.
There, they accused Paul and Silas before the town authorities.
They said that Paul and Silas were Jews and were causing much trouble in the city by teaching the people to obey customs that were contrary to the laws of the Roman Empire. (19b-21)

Questions.Q: Who helped the owners of the slave girl to accuse Paul and Silas before the authorities?
Questions.A: A crowd had joined the owners of the slave girl in the market place.
This crowd went with the owners of the girl to the city authorities and also accused Paul and Silas before them. (22a)

Questions.Q: What did the city authorities do when they heard what these people accused Paul and Silas of doing?
Questions.A: The town authorities ordered guards to strip and beat Paul and Silas.
The guards beat Paul and Silas severely [on their backs].
Then the authorities ordered the guards to take Paul and Silas to the prison and to tell the jailer to lock them up securely. (22b-23)

Questions.Q: What did the jailer do with/to Paul and Silas?
Questions.A: The jailer put Paul and Silas in the part of the prison that was farthest inside.
He made them sit on the floor and he put their feet in stocks. (24)
Questions.Note: Having their feet in stocks prevented them from being able to move.
Questions.Alternative: What did the jailer do with Paul and Silas?
What did the jailer do to Paul and Silas?

Questions.Q: What did Paul and Silas do while they were in prison?
Questions.A: They prayed to God and sang hymns, and the other prisoners listened to them. (25)

Questions.Q: What happened at about midnight?
Questions.A: About midnight, there was a powerful earthquake which caused all the doors of the prison to open wide.
The earthquake also caused the chains on all the prisoners to fall off. (26)

Questions.Q: What did the jailer do when the earthquake awakened him?
Questions.A: He went at once to the jail and saw that the doors were all open and that the prisoners could escape.
He was alarmed, and he drew his sword and was about to kill himself. (27)
Questions.Note: He did that because he knew that he would be executed if the prisoners escaped.

Questions.Q: What did Paul do when he saw that the jailer was about to kill himself?
Questions.A: He shouted to the jailer, "Do not harm yourself! We are all here!" (28)

Questions.Q: What did the jailer do when he heard what Paul told him?
Questions.A: The jailer called for someone to bring a light.
He went to Paul and Silas and knelt down before them, trembling with fear.
Then he brought them out of the prison. (29-30a)

Questions.Q: What did the jailer ask Paul and Silas? What did they reply?
Questions.A: The jailer asked Paul and Silas what he needed to do in order for God to save him.
Paul and Silas told him, "Believe in the Lord Jesus and you will be saved-you and your household." (30b-31)

Questions.Q: Whom else did Paul and Silas tell the message about the Lord Jesus?
Questions.A: Paul and Silas told all the members of the jailer's household the message about the true God. He told them that God saves people who trust in the Lord Jesus. (32)

Questions.Q: What did the jailer and the other people in his home do to show that they believed in Jesus?
Questions.A: The jailer immediately took Paul and Silas to a place where there was water and washed their wounds.
Then [Paul and Silas] baptized the jailer and all of his family. (33)

Questions.Q: What else did the jailer do that same night?
Questions.A: He took Paul and Silas into his house and served them a meal. (34)

Questions.Q: How did the jailer feel, after all that had happened?
Questions.A: The jailer was joyful, because he and all his family had believed in the true God. (34)

Questions.Q: What happened to Paul and Silas the next morning at the prison?
Questions.A: The next morning, the city authorities sent a couple of police officers to the prison.
The officers told the jailer that he should let Paul and Silas out of prison and allow them to leave. (35-36)

Questions.Q: What did Paul do when he and Silas heard that?
Questions.A: They did not leave the jail right away.
Instead, Paul told the messengers to go back and tell the city authorities that they had treated him and Silas unfairly, even though they were Roman citizens.
The authorities had not given them a trial but had ordered them to be whipped and put in jail. (37a)
Questions.Note: It was against Roman law for authorities to punish Roman citizens without first giving them a trial.

Questions.Q: What else did Paul tell the messengers to tell the city authorities?
Questions.A: Paul told the messengers to request the city authorities to come themselves to the prison and to release/free him and Silas and bring them out. (37b)

Questions.Q: What did the city authorities do when they heard that Paul and Silas were Roman citizens?
Questions.A: The authorities were alarmed when they heard that Paul and Silas were Roman citizens.
They themselves came to the prison and apologized to Paul and Silas.
They escorted them out of the prison and asked them to leave Philippi soon. (38b-39)

Questions.Q: What did Paul and Silas do before they left Philippi?
Questions.A: After Paul and Silas left the prison, they went to Lydia's house and encouraged the group of believers/Christians [to continue to trust God and believe in the Lord Jesus].
Then they left Philippi. (40)

Section.heading: Acts 17:1-9 Paul preached in the synagogue in Thessalonica, and some people believed in the Lord Jesus.

Questions.Q: Where did Paul and Silas go next to preach the message about Jesus Christ?
Questions.A: Next, Paul and Silas went to the (city) Thessalonica.
Paul went to the Jewish synagogue and preached there. (1-2)

Questions.Q: What message did he preach to the people in the synagogue?
Questions.A: He explained to the people that the [Old Testament] Scriptures show that Jesus was the Messiah.
He told them that the Scriptures say that people would kill the Messiah, but that he would rise again, alive. (2-3)

Questions.Q: How many times did Paul preach in the synagogue?
Questions.A: For three Sabbaths Paul spoke to the people from the [Old Testament] Scriptures. (2b)

Questions.Q: How did the people who heard Paul preach respond to that message?
Questions.A: Some of the Jewish people believed that the message about Jesus was true.
Many Greeks who worshiped God, both men and women, also believed in Jesus. (4)
Others of the Jews did not believe what Paul preached but made plans to drive him out. (5-7)

Questions.Q: What did the Jews who rejected the message about Jesus do?
Questions.A: The Jews who rejected the message about Jesus stirred up a crowd of people to oppose Paul and Silas.
They found some men of bad character in the marketplace, and with these they formed a mob and started a riot in the city. (5a)

Questions.Q: Where did the mob go, and what did they plan to do?
Questions.A: They went to the house of a citizen named Jason, [because they had heard that Jason had received Paul and Silas into his home].
They were going to bring Paul and Silas out to the mob [and would have treated them roughly/violently]. (5b)

Questions.Q: What did the mob and the Jews who opposed Paul and Silas do at Jason's house/home?
Questions.A: They did not find Paul and Silas there.
So they dragged Jason and a few other believers [out of the house and took them] before the city officials and accused them. (6a)
Questions.Alternative: What did the mob and the Jews who opposed Paul and Silas do at Jason's house?
What did the mob and the Jews who opposed Paul and Silas do at Jason's home?

Questions.Q: What did those Jews tell the city officials that Paul and Silas had done?
Questions.A: They said that Paul and Silas had been disturbing people everywhere they went, and now they had come to Thessalonica to cause trouble there.
Jason had helped Paul and Silas by receiving them into his house/home. (6b-7a)

Questions.Q: What did the Jews and the rest of the crowd say which the city officials thought was very serious/bad?
Questions.A: They said that Paul and Silas were teaching people that they did not need to obey the laws/decrees of the Roman Emperor.
They were teaching people that there was another king whom they should obey.
That king's name was Jesus. (7b)
Questions.Alternative: What did the Jews and the rest of the crowd say which the city officials thought was very serious?
What did the Jews and the rest of the crowd say which the city officials thought was very bad?

Questions.Q: How did the city authorities punish Jason and the other Christians [for helping Paul and Silas]?
Questions.A: They made Jason and the Christians with him promise not to allow Paul and Silas to stir up the people of the city again.
They also made them provide bail. (9)
Questions.Alternative: How did the city authorities punish Jason and the other Christians for helping Paul and Silas?
How did the city authorities punish Jason and the other Christians?

Section.heading: Acts 17:10-15 In Berea, the people carefully checked the Scriptures to determine whether or not Paul and Silas preached the truth.

Questions.Q: In what way were the people in the synagogue of Berea different from the people in Thessalonica?
Questions.A: The Bereans were of more noble character than the Thessalonians.
The Bereans listened eagerly to the message about Jesus.
The Bereans checked the Scriptures every day to determine if Paul was preaching the truth. (11)

Questions.Q: What caused Paul to leave Berea and go to a different part of Greece?
Questions.A: The Jews in Thessalonica heard that Paul was preaching the Word of God in Berea.
So they went to Berea and began to stir up the crowds against Paul. (13)

Questions.Q: When Paul and Silas went to Berea and preached there, in what way did those people respond?
Questions.A: Those people listened eagerly to what Paul and Silas preached and taught about Jesus Christ. They compared it with what they read in the Scriptures, and many of them believed the message about Jesus.
The Greek women who believed [were women who] were respected in that town. (10-12)

Questions.Q: What did the believers in Berea do when that happened?
Questions.A: They arranged for Paul to leave Berea that night, but Silas and Timothy continued to stay there.
Several of the Christians took Paul to the seacoast [of the province of Macedonia].
They all boarded a ship and went to Athens. (14-15)
Questions.Note: Athens was a large city and was the capital of the province of Achaia.

Questions.Q: What instructions did Paul give the believers who had taken him to Athens before they returned to Berea?
Questions.A: Paul instructed them to tell Silas and Timothy to join him in Athens as soon as they could. (15)

Section.heading: Acts 17:16-34 In Athens, Paul preached about the God who created the heavens and the earth and all people.

Questions.Q: What did Paul see in [the city of] Athens that made him feel very concerned/upset?
Questions.A: As Paul walked about in Athens, he saw many altars and shrines, so he knew that the people worshiped many idols.
He was concerned because the people did not worship the true God. (16)
Questions.Alternative: What did Paul see in the city of Athens that made him feel very concerned?
What did Paul see in the city of Athens that made him feel very upset?
What did Paul see in Athens that made him feel very concerned?
What did Paul see in Athens that made him feel very upset?

Questions.Q: To what places did Paul go to tell people about Jesus and the true God?
Questions.A: Paul went to the synagogue and discussed with the Jews and God-fearing Greeks who met there what they believed. [He told them what the prophets had written in the Old Testament Scriptures about Jesus.]
Paul also went to the marketplace and talked to whomever he met there. (17)

Questions.Q: Who were the people with whom Paul spoke in the marketplace? What did they think about what Paul was trying to teach?
Questions.A: Certain of the people whom Paul met in the marketplace were teachers whom people called "philosophers."
They thought that Paul had some strange beliefs, and they did not think that what Paul said was important.
Other philosophers who talked with Paul decided that he must be trying to teach them about gods whom people in some other place worshiped. (18)

Questions.Q: For what reason did certain men invite Paul to go with them to the place where the important men of Athens met?
Questions.A: Some of the people with whom Paul had talked in the marketplace wanted to hear more about the gods whom Paul had told them about.
So they took him with them to a meeting of the council of Athens, which met in a place called the Areopagus.
They wanted Paul to tell them what he believed. (19-20)

Questions.Q: For what reason did the teachers with whom Paul had talked want him to speak again about what he believed?
Questions.A: The people who lived in Athens very much liked to hear people discuss the new ideas which they had heard. (20-21)

Questions.Q: When Paul addressed the council members, what god did he talk about first?
Questions.A: Paul had seen in Athens an altar on which was written: "To an Unknown God."
He told the people at the council meeting that he was going to tell them about that God whom they worshiped but whom they did not know. (22-23)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say first about the true God and about human beings?
Questions.A: Paul said that God does not need human beings to serve/help him, and he does not live in the temples or shrines that people have made.
He said that it is God who gives all people life and breath and everything else that we need to live. (24-25)

Questions.Q: What do you think this verse means by the "world"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It refers to the entire universe that God created, the whole creation, including both heaven and earth.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think verse 14 means by the "world"?
Questions.Note: See "world" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did Paul say about the different nations that are in the world?
Questions.A: Paul said that God had made one man, and from that man, he/God had made all the nations/people-groups in the world.
God had decided in what part of the world and during what years each of those nations/people-groups were going to live. (26)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say that God wants all the people in the world to do?
Questions.A: God wants all the people in the world to know that he is God, and to try to find him. (27)

Questions.Q: Paul then quoted a saying that a well-known Greek poet had written. What was that saying, and what did Paul say it meant?
Questions.A: [The people listening to Paul were Greeks.]
The saying which Paul quoted was written by a Greek poet whom all the people listening respected.
That poet had said, "We are his [God's] offspring."
This saying meant that God has created us people and made us [to be] like him. (28)

Questions.Q: What did Paul next tell the people about the true God?
Questions.A: Paul told them that we ought not to think that [the true] God is anything like the images of gold, silver, or stone which people worship.
Because God has created made us to be like him, we know that he/God is not like any gods which people make. (29)

Questions.Q: When God judges the people of the world, for what sin/offense will he judge them?
Questions.A: Paul implied that it is wrong/sin for people to worship idols.
In past times, people had worshiped idols because they did not know God.
Because they did not know him/God, he/God had not punished them.
But now, God was commanding people everywhere to repent and stop doing evil.
On a certain day, God was going to judge all people for the evil things that they have done. (29-31)
