Questions.Alternative: When God judges the people of the world, for what sin will he judge them?
When God judges the people of the world, for what offense will he judge them?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for a person to judge someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means someone/a judge will determine if a person is guilty or not of committing a crime. He does this by assessing the evidence connected to the person and what he may have done.
Questions.Note: See "judge" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Paul then said that in past times, God had not punished people for the evil things that they did. What kind of wrong/sin did Paul mention?
Questions.A: People had worshiped idols/other gods when they did not know who the true God was/is.
But when people did not know who the true God was/is, God did not punish them for worshiping idols. (30a)
Questions.Alternative: Paul then said that in past times, God had not punished people for the evil things that they did. What kind of wrong did Paul mention?
Paul then said that in past times, God had not punished people for the evil things that they did. What kind of sin did Paul mention?

Questions.Q: For what reason did Paul say that God now was commanding all people everywhere to repent? Of what should people repent?
Questions.A: Paul said that now people could now know who the true God is/was, they should turn away from their evil ways.
Paul implied that when people know who God is, they should no longer worship false gods. They should worship only him. (30b)

Questions.Q: What reason did Paul give for people to repent and worship only [the true] God?
Questions.A: Paul said that God had already appointed a man who was one day going to judge all people, and he would judge them justly/fairly.
God had shown which man he had chosen to be the judge by raising him to life again after he had been killed. (31)
Questions.Alternative: What reason did Paul give for people to repent and worship only the true God?
What reason did Paul give for people to repent and worship only God?

Questions.Q: How did the people who were at the meeting respond to the message about Jesus?
Questions.A: Some of them made fun of Paul when he said that a man had come alive again after he died.
Others said that they wanted to hear Paul speak to them again about that.
A few of the people believed. Among those who believed was a man named Dionysius, who was a member of the council. Also a woman named Damaris was among those who believed. (32-34)

Questions.Q: For what reason did Paul then end his message and leave the meeting of the council members?
Questions.A: Paul left the meeting [because most of the people did not want to hear him speak any longer]. (33)

Section.heading: Acts 18:1-17 In Corinth, Paul preached about Jesus Christ to many of the people, and many people believed.

Questions.Q: Where did Paul begin to preach the message about Jesus?
Questions.A: Paul went to the synagogue every Sabbath and preached both to Jews and Greeks.
He tried to persuade them [that Jesus is/was the Messiah]. (4-5)

Questions.Q: Where did Paul go to preach and teach when the Jews rejected his message about Jesus?
Questions.A: Paul stopped going to the synagogue and went and stayed in the home of a Gentile named Titius Justus. [He continued to preach and teach about Jesus there.]
Many people including Crispus, the leader of the synagogue, and his family believed and were baptized [by Paul]. (6-8)

Questions.Q: Where did Paul go next to preach and teach?
Questions.A: He left Athens and went to Corinth. (1)

Questions.Q: Who were Aquila and Priscilla?
Questions.A: Aquila and Priscilla was a Jewish couple who had come to Corinth from Rome.
They practiced the trade of tent making.
Paul stayed with them.
Paul joined them in their work of tent making since he was also a tent maker. (2-3)

Questions.Q: In what way did Paul work differently after Silas and Timothy arrived from Macedonia?
Questions.A: After Silas and Timothy arrived in Corinth, Paul spent all of his time preaching.
Before they had arrived, Paul had spent some of his time making tents.
He had preached in the time that he did not need to work to earn his living expenses. (5)

Questions.Q: Because the Jews refused to believe his message, what did Paul say?
Questions.A: Since the Jews had rejected the message about Jesus, Paul warned them that they were going to suffer eternal punishment for their sins, and it would not be his fault. (6b)

Questions.Q: What vision did God give Paul in order to encourage him?
Questions.A: The Lord Jesus appeared to Paul and told him to continue preaching, because there were many people who were going to believe.
The Lord implied that people might oppose Paul and try to harm him, but he told Paul that they would not be successful. (9-11)

Questions.Q: How long did Paul continue to preach and teach the word of God in Corinth after the Lord had spoken to him in that vision?
Questions.A: Paul stayed a year and a half longer preaching and teaching the word of God. (11)

Questions.Q: In what way did the Jews who rejected the teaching about Jesus make further trouble for Paul?
Questions.A: They seized Paul and took him before the Roman Governor, accusing Paul of teaching people to disobey the laws of the Roman Empire. (12-13)

Questions.Q: How did the Roman Governor, Gallio, respond to the accusations against Paul?
Questions.A: After Gallio heard the complaints of the Jews, he knew that they were not crimes against the Roman government.
Therefore, he refused to judge Paul.
Instead, He had the Jews who accused Paul thrown out of the court [by the guards].
When a mob/crowd grabbed Sosthenes, the leader of the synagogue, and beat him, Gallio did nothing to stop them. (14-17)

Questions.Q: How did Gallio describe what the Jews and Paul were arguing about?
Questions.A: Gallio said that the Jews and Paul were arguing [only] about questions that had to do with "words and names" from the religious laws of the Jews.
He said that the Jews should settle their own arguments. (15b)

Section.heading: Acts 18:18-28 Paul left Corinth and set out for Syria. He took Aquila and Priscilla with him as far as Ephesus.

Questions.Q: At what places did Paul stop as he returned from Corinth [in Greece/Achaia] to Antioch [in Syria]?
Questions.A: Paul, accompanied by Priscilla and Aquila, stopped at the port of Cenchrea.
There, they boarded a ship and sailed to Ephesus, a large city in the province of Asia. (18b-19a)
Questions.Alternative: At what places did Paul stop as he returned from Corinth in Greece to Antioch in Syria?
At what places did Paul stop as he returned from Corinth in Achaia to Antioch in Syria?
At what places did Paul stop as he returned from Corinth in Greece to Antioch?
At what places did Paul stop as he returned from Corinth in Achaia to Antioch?
At what places did Paul stop as he returned from Corinth to Antioch in Syria?
At what places did Paul stop as he returned from Corinth to Antioch?

Questions.Q: What did Paul do in Ephesus?
Questions.A: In Ephesus, Paul went to the Jewish synagogue and reasoned with the Jews who met there.
He told them that Jesus was the Messiah.
They listened well to the message and wanted Paul to stay longer with them and continue to teach them. (19b-20a)

Questions.Q: What stops did Paul make as he returned from Corinth to Antioch [in Syria]? Who went with him?
Questions.A: Paul, accompanied by Priscilla and Aquila, went to the port of Cenchrea. (18-22)
Questions.Alternative: What stops did Paul make as he returned from Corinth to Antioch in Syria? Who went with him?
What stops did Paul make as he returned from Corinth to Antioch? Who went with him?

Questions.Q: For what reason did Paul have his hair cut off in Cenchrea?
Questions.A: In Cenchrea, Paul had his hair cut off in order to fulfill a ritual vow. (18)

Questions.Q: To what place did Priscilla and Aquila go with Paul?
Questions.A: Priscilla and Aquila went with Paul as far as Ephesus, and they stayed there. (19)

Questions.Q: What did Paul do in Ephesus at that time?
Questions.A: Paul went to the synagogue and reasoned with the Jews. (19)

Questions.Q: The Jews listened well to the message about Jesus. What did Paul reply when they asked him to stay longer and continue to teach them?
Questions.A: Paul was not willing to stay for a longer time, because he wanted to go to Jerusalem and then back to Antioch in Syria.
He told the Jews in Ephesus that he would return if it was God's will.
He then sailed for Syria. (20-21)

Questions.Q: Where did Paul go after he arrived in Syria?
Questions.A: After arriving at Caesarea in Syria, Paul went up [to Jerusalem].
He visited the believers there and then went to Antioch, where he spent some time.
From Antioch, Paul went to different places in Galatia and Phrygia and visited the believers there. He encouraged them to continue to believe in God and Jesus. (22-23)

Questions.Q: Who was Apollos and what did he teach the people in the synagogue at Ephesus?
Questions.A: Apollos was a Jew.
Apollos was a native of Alexandria.
He knew the Scriptures well and had also heard about Jesus and believed what he knew about him.
In the synagogue in Ephesus, Apollos told the people what he knew about Jesus.
What he said was correct, and he spoke with great enthusiasm. (24-25a)

Questions.Q: Who had baptized Apollos? For what reason had Apollos been baptized?
Questions.A: Apollos had been baptized by someone who was a follower of John the Baptist.
That person had baptized Apollos to show that he/Apollos repented of his sins.
He had not baptized Apollos as a believer in the Lord Jesus. (25b)

Questions.Q: Where did Priscilla and Aquila become acquainted with Apollos?
Questions.A: Priscilla and Aquila had heard Apollos speak in the synagogue.
They recognized/realized that he knew only part of what it means to be a follower of Jesus.
They invited him to their home and taught him some things that he had not learned before.
[Apollos believed what Aquila and Priscilla taught him about the Lord Jesus.]
After that, the other Christians in Ephesus accepted Apollos as a believer. (26)

Questions.Q: After Apollos had been with the believers for a time, what did he want to do?
Questions.A: He wanted to go to Achaia and visit the believers there. (27a)

Questions.Q: For what reason do you think the believers in Ephesus encouraged Apollos to go to Achaia?
Questions.A: The believers in Ephesus had heard Apollos preach from the [Old Testament] Scriptures which show that Jesus was the Messiah.
They knew that Apollos would be able to teach the believers in Corinth. (27a)

Questions.Q: In what way did Apollos help the believers in Corinth?
Questions.A: He taught the Christians from the [Old Testament] Scriptures.
In this way he helped them to know more about God and to understand who the Lord Jesus was/is.
He also debated in a public place with Jews who refused to believe that Jesus was the Messiah.
The Jews were not able to deny that what Apollos told them about the Scriptures was true.
[Thus, many people were convinced that Jesus was/is truly the Messiah.] (27b-28)

Section.heading: Acts 19:1-7 In Ephesus, Paul baptized some disciples in the name of Jesus, and they received the Holy Spirit.

Questions.Q: Paul spent some time with the believers in Antioch of Syria. Where did he go after that?
Questions.A: Paul traveled through the central part of Asia and arrived at Ephesus. (1)

Questions.Q: What did Paul do in Ephesus?
Questions.A: He baptized some disciples in the name of the Lord Jesus and the Holy Spirit came on them. (5-6)

Questions.Q: In Ephesus, Paul met a group of men who were followers of the Lord Jesus. What did Paul ask those men?
Questions.A: Paul asked them whether they had received the Holy Spirit when they first believed in Jesus. (1b-2a)

Questions.Q: What did the men answer?
Questions.A: They said that they had not heard that there is a Holy Spirit. (2b)

Questions.Q: What did Paul then ask them, and what did they reply?
Questions.A: He asked them who had baptized them, and what did it mean [when he baptized them]?
They replied that they had been baptized [by a disciple] of John the Baptist.
That person had baptized them because they had repented and asked God to forgive them for their sins. (3)

Questions.Q: What did Paul tell those men about John the Baptist that they had not understood before?
Questions.A: Paul told them that John the Baptist had also told people to believe in Jesus, the Messiah, who was just about to come. (4)

Questions.Q: What did the men do when they heard that?
Questions.A: They were baptized [by Paul] to show that they believed in the Lord Jesus. (5)

Questions.Q: What happened when Paul baptized the men?
Questions.A: Paul placed his hands on them, and they received the Holy Spirit.
Immediately, they spoke in languages they had not learned, and they said/spoke messages which God told them to say. (6)

Section.heading: Acts 19:8-12 God showed his power in Ephesus as Paul taught both Jews and Gentiles about the Lord.

Questions.Q: What miracles convinced the people that God was giving Paul power?
Questions.A: God enabled Paul to do many miracles of healing and to cast evil spirits out of many people whom they controlled.
When it was not possible for the sick or demon-controlled people to come to Paul, he sent a small piece of clothing that he had used/worn to them, and they were healed. (11-12)

Questions.Q: In what place in Ephesus did Paul teach and preach to people about the kingdom of God?
Questions.A: For about three months Paul taught people in the Jewish synagogue about the kingdom of God.
[Paul also taught the people that Jesus was the Messiah whom God had promised to send to the Jews.] (8)

Questions.Q: How did the people, who heard Paul teach in the synagogue, respond to what he taught about Jesus?
Questions.A: Some of the people believed, but others refused to believe the message about the Lord Jesus. They said before all the other people [in the synagogue] that the teachings that people called the teachings about Jesus/the "Jesus's Way" were bad. (9a)

Questions.Q: When Paul decided not to teach any more in the synagogue, where did he go?
Questions.A: After that, Paul went to a house that people called "the lecture hall of Tyrannus."
The people who had believed what Paul taught in the synagogue also went to the lecture hall. There, Paul continued to teach them about Jesus Christ. (9b)

Questions.Q: Tell about Paul's teaching and preaching the message about Jesus Christ in the lecture hall of Tyrannus.
Questions.A: Paul continued to teach and preach there for two years.
During that time, very many Jews and Greeks from different parts of the province of Asia came to Ephesus and heard the message about the Lord Jesus. (10)

Section.heading: Acts 19:13-22 Some Jews who cast out evil spirits learned that only Jesus has the power to command evil spirits.

Questions.Q: What happened when the sons of Sceva ordered an evil spirit to leave a man, using the name of Jesus?
Questions.A: The evil spirit answered them.
He said that he knew Jesus and he knew Paul, but he did not know the person who was commanding him at that time. [The men who were speaking to him did not have authority to command him.] (15)

Questions.Q: When the spirit who controlled that man refused to obey the sons of Sceva, what did the man do?
Questions.A: That man jumped upon the sons of Sceva, attacked them violently, and overpowered them all.
He tore off their clothes and beat them up, leaving them wounded.
They all ran away from that house, terrified. (16)

Questions.Q: Who were the sons of Sceva, and what authority did they believe they had?
Questions.A: They were the sons of a Jewish priest named Sceva.
They believed that they had authority over evil spirits, because they had cast evil spirits out of some people whom the spirits controlled. (13-14)

Questions.Q: One time, they used the name of Jesus when they tried to cast an evil spirit out of a certain man. For what reason did they use Jesus's name?
Questions.A: They knew that when Paul cast evil spirits out of people, he used the authority and name of Jesus.
[So they knew that the name of Jesus must have power.] (13b)

Questions.Q: What did both Jews and Gentiles learn when they heard what happened to the sons of Sceva?
Questions.A: They learned that people who do not believe in Jesus are not able to use Jesus's name/authority to command evil spirits.
They also learned that even evil spirits know and respect the name and authority of Jesus. (17)

Questions.Q: What did many of the Christians learn when they heard how the evil spirit had punished the sons of Sceva for trying to cast him out?
Questions.A: Many of the Christians who had practiced sorcery before they believed in the Lord Jesus now knew that they should no longer practice sorcery. [18-19a]

Questions.Q: What did they do to show that they were not going to use sorcery any more?
Questions.A: They came to a public place, bringing the scrolls that contained the words that they had used when they practiced sorcery.
Those scrolls were worth a lot of money, but they burned all of them. (19b)

Questions.Q: What did some of the Christians learn about God and Jesus that they had not known/understood before?
Questions.A: The things that happened to the sons of Sceva showed both Christians and unbelievers that Jesus has more power than the power of evil spirits [and the power of Satan]. (20)
Questions.Alternative: What did some of the Christians learn about God and Jesus that they had not known before?
What did some of the Christians learn about God and Jesus that they had not understood before?

Questions.Q: How did those things that had happened cause many people to believe the message about the Lord Jesus?
Questions.A: The Christians understood more about the power and authority of the Lord Jesus.
Many people who had not yet believed the message about the Lord Jesus now believed it. (20)

Questions.Q: What did Paul decide to do after there were many groups of believers in the province of Asia?
Questions.A: Paul decided that he would return to Jerusalem, but he would go through Macedonia and Achaia on the way.
He also decided that after he had revisited Jerusalem, he wanted to visit Rome, [which was the capital city of the Empire]. (21)

Questions.Q: For what reason did Paul not leave Ephesus right away?
Questions.A: Paul wanted to stay in Ephesus/Asia a little longer.
He sent two of his helpers, Timothy and Erastus, to Macedonia ahead of him.
[Paul himself expected to go to Macedonia soon.] (22)
Questions.Note: This verse does not explicitly state why Paul wanted to remain in Asia. It might make sense to omit this question and ask only the following question.
Questions.Alternative: Did Paul leave Ephesus right away, and what did he do first?
Why did Paul not leave Ephesus right away?

Questions.Q: What did Paul do while remaining in Asia for a while?
Questions.A: He sent two of his helpers, Timothy and Erastus, to Macedonia ahead of him.
Questions.Note: If asking the previous question, depending on how it is worded, you might ask this question as well (unless the respondent has already given this information).
Questions.Alternative: What did Paul do while remaining in Ephesus for a while?
What did Paul do in order to remain in Ephesus for a while?
What did Paul do in order to remain in Asia for a while?

Section.heading: Acts 19:23-41 In Ephesus, worshipers of the goddess Artemis rioted against Paul and his teaching.

Questions.Q: What happened during the days that Paul stayed in Ephesus after Timothy and Erastus had left?
Questions.A: Many of the people in Ephesus rioted against Paul because he taught that people should not worship idols. (28-29)

Questions.Q: What was the cause of a great disturbance in Ephesus?
Questions.A: Many people had listened to the teaching of Paul about [the true] God and the Lord Jesus.
Those who had become Christians no longer worshiped the goddess Artemis.
Unbelievers called the Christians "the people of the Way," and they complained against them. (23)

Questions.Q: Who was Demetrius? What group of people did he call to a meeting?
Questions.A: Demetrius was the manager/"boss" of the silversmiths.
The silversmiths made small silver shrines of the goddess Artemis, and they made much/a lot of money in that business.
Demetrius called together all the silversmiths and also men of other trades who took some part in selling the shrines. (24-25)

Questions.Q: What did Demetrius say that Paul was doing? How did Demetrius say that Paul might hurt the business of the silversmiths?
Questions.A: Demetrius said that Paul was teaching people throughout the province of Asia something false.
Paul was telling people that the gods that people make are not really gods, and that no one should worship them.
Demetrius said that many people believed what Paul taught. (26)

Questions.Q: What dangerous/very bad result did Demetrius say might happen if people continued to believe what Paul taught?
Questions.A: Demetrius said that their business of making silver shrines of the goddess Artemis will get a bad name.
Demetrius said that if people continued to believe what Paul taught, many people in Ephesus and also in other parts of the world would stop worshiping Artemis.
People would no longer reverence/respect their famous and powerful goddess.
So they would not continue to come to her temple in Ephesus and worship her. (27)
Questions.Alternative: What dangerous result did Demetrius say might happen if people continued to believe what Paul taught?
What very bad result did Demetrius say might happen if people continued to believe what Paul taught?

Questions.Q: When the silversmiths heard that, what did they do?
Questions.A: They became angry, and they all shouted together: "Our goddess Artemis is very great/important!" (28)

Questions.Q: Who else went to the theater and shouted with the silversmiths?
Questions.A: Many other people in Ephesus had heard the silversmiths shouting, and they hurried to the theater.
A large crowd gathered, and they all shouted [, along with the silversmiths]. (29a)

Questions.Q: Who were Gaius and Aristarchus? What happened to them?
Questions.A: Gaius and Aristarchus had traveled with Paul from Macedonia to Ephesus.
[They were somewhere near where the crowd had gathered.]
Some people in the crowd had seen Gaius and Aristarchus with Paul, so they grabbed them.
Then the whole crowd rushed to the town theater, taking Gaius and Aristarchus with them. (29b)

Questions.Q: What did Paul want to do when he heard that a large crowd of angry people had gathered in the theater?
Questions.A: Paul wanted to enter the theater and speak to the crowd.
But the believers [knew it would be dangerous], and they would not let Paul enter the theater. (30)

Questions.Q: Who else advised Paul not to go into the theater and appear before the crowd?
Questions.A: Some of the officials of the government were Paul's friends, and they also strongly advised him not to enter the theater. (31)

Questions.Q: What was the crowd of people doing?
Questions.A: They were all shouting, and they continued to shout for a long time.
Most of the crowd who had gathered did not know what the silversmiths were shouting about, but they shouted also.
Those people shouted many different things. (32)

Questions.Q: There were some Jews also in the stadium, and they wanted to quiet the crowd. How did they try to do that?
Questions.A: Those Jews thought that they could explain to the crowd that there was no reason for them to be angry and to keep shouting.
They/the Jews thought that if one of them talked to the crowd, the crowd would become quiet and would listen.
So they pushed a Jew whose name was Alexander to the front of the crowd.
Alexander made a sign with his hand, to show that he wanted to speak to the people. (33)

Questions.Q: For what reason did the crowd of people not allow Alexander to speak to them?
Questions.A: The crowd recognized that Alexander was a Jew, so they did not give him a chance to speak to them.
They did not want to listen to him [because they knew that Jews did not worship the goddess Artemis]. (34a)

Questions.Q: What did the crowd do then?
Questions.A: The crowd all joined together shouting, "We Ephesians praise our goddess Artemis!"
OR "Our goddess Artemis is very great/important!"
They continued shouting that way, all together, for about two hours. (34b)

Questions.Q: The town clerk finally came to the stadium and spoke to the crowd. What did he tell them?
Questions.A: The town clerk told the crowd of people that the whole world knew that the temple of Artemis was in Ephesus.
He said that people would certainly continue to respect her and [would continue to] come to her temple. (35)

Questions.Q: What else did the town clerk tell the crowd?
Questions.A: He told them to be quiet, and he warned them not to do anything violent. (36)

Questions.Q: What did the town clerk say about Paul's two companions?
Questions.A: He told the people that there was no reason for them to have seized those two men, because they had done nothing wrong.
They had not taken anything from the temples of the gods nor spoken evil about Artemis. (37)

Questions.Q: What did the town clerk tell the crowd that they should do when they had complaints against anyone?
Questions.A: He reminded them that the Roman government had set up courts to which people could go and complain if someone had done them some wrong.
Those courts met at regular times, and the judges at those courts were appointed by the Government.
The people of Ephesus could assemble there and report whatever/any problems [which they had] to those judges. (38-39)

Questions.Q: For what reason did the town clerk order the people to stop shouting?
Questions.A: The town clerk told the people that there was no reason for them to have rioted.
He was afraid that if higher authorities [in the government] should ask him why the people had rioted, he would be in trouble. (40)

Questions.Q: What did the town clerk tell the people after that?
Questions.A: Then he told the crowd to leave the theater, and they did. (41)

Section.heading: Acts 20:1-12 Paul again went to Macedonia and Achaia, and then to Troas, visiting the believers/Christians.

Questions.Q: Where did Paul go next?
Questions.A: Paul went to Macedonia and visited the groups of Christians there.
Then he went to the province of Achaia and visited the believers in Greece [probably in Corinth].
He stayed with them for three months. (1-3)

Questions.Q: With whom did Paul travel from Philippi to Troas?
Questions.A: The seven believers who had come with Paul from Achaia had gone ahead to Troas [by ship].
Paul and his companion [probably Luke] remained in Philippi until after the festival of Passover.
Then they sailed to Troas and met the other believers there. (5-6)

Questions.Q: What did Paul do just before he left Ephesus?
Questions.A: When the city became quiet again, Paul sent for the believers.
He encouraged them [not to fear, but to continue to trust the Lord].
Then he said good-bye to those believers. (1)

Questions.Q: Paul had planned to travel by ship from Achaia to Syria. For what reason did he go instead through Macedonia?
Questions.A: Someone told Paul that certain Jews were planning to kill him if he returned to Syria by ship. So he decided to return to Macedonia and sail from there to the province of Asia. (3)

Questions.Q: Who went with Paul as companions from Corinth to Troas?
Questions.A: A group of seven believers accompanied Paul from Corinth back through Macedonia and across to Troas.
Two of these believers were from the province of Asia. (4-5)

Questions.Q: What did Paul and his companion do on the night before they left Troas?
Questions.A: The night before Paul [and Luke] left, the believers met together to celebrate the Lord's Supper. (7a)

Questions.Q: For what reason did Paul continue preaching until midnight?
Questions.A: Paul preached to the believers until [about] midnight, because he was going to leave Troas the next morning. (7b)

Questions.Q: Where had the believers met?
Questions.A: The believers met that night in a room on the third floor of a house.
There were many oil lamps burning in the room. (8)

Questions.Q: Who was Eutychus? What happened to him?
Questions.A: Eutychus was a young man who was seated by an open window.
As Paul continued his sermon until almost midnight, Eutychus became very sleepy.
Finally, he fell asleep and fell out of the window down to the courtyard, which was two stories below. (9a-b)

Questions.Q: What did the other people in the meeting do when that happened?
Questions.A: Right away, the other people at the meeting went downstairs and picked up Eutychus.
But he was dead. (9c)

Questions.Q: When Paul also went downstairs, what did he do?
Questions.A: Paul stretched himself upon Eutychus and put his arms around him.
Then he told the other believers, "Don't be alarmed/cry over him! He is alive!" (10)

Questions.Q: What did the believers do after they heard what Paul said?
Questions.A: They all went upstairs again and celebrated the Lord's Supper.
Then they ate [a meal] together. (11a)

Questions.Q: In what way did the meeting end?
Questions.A: Paul conversed with the other Christians until daylight, and then he left.
The believers [who lived in Troas] went home, feeling comforted, because Eutychus was alive and well. (11-12)

Section.heading: Acts 20:13-38 Paul said good-by to the elders of the church of Ephesus. He charged them to take care of the believers who were in their care.

Questions.Q: What did Paul do that showed his love and concern for the believers in Ephesus?
Questions.A: He sent a message to the elders, asking them to come to Miletus to meet him there. (17-18a)

Questions.Q: What warning did Paul give the elders about the believers whom he charged them to care for?
Questions.A: Paul warned the elders that after he was no longer with them, some of the people among the believers were going to reject the truth.
Those people were going to teach what sounded good but was really false.
They would try to persuade some of the believers to leave the group and follow them. (29-30)

Questions.Q: How did Paul and his companions travel from Troas to Assos?
Questions.A: Paul's companions went [without him] by ship from Troas to Assos.
Paul had decided to walk to Assos, instead.
He met the other men in Assos and boarded the ship on which the others were traveling. (13-14)

Questions.Q: At how many places did the ship stop between Assos and Miletus?
Questions.A: The ship stopped at three places before it arrived in Miletus. (15)

Questions.Q: For what reason did Paul choose to travel on a ship that was not going to stop at the port of Ephesus?
Questions.A: Paul was in a hurry to get to Jerusalem in time for the feast of Pentecost. (16)

Questions.Q: When the elders came and met with Paul, what were some of the things that Paul said to them?
Questions.A: Paul reminded the elders how he had lived among them in Ephesus.
He had been humble and had earnestly served the Lord.
He often wept because of the things that happened while he taught them the Word of God. (18-19a)

Questions.Q: What kind of trials did Paul suffer repeatedly?
Questions.A: Jews who opposed Paul and the message about Jesus Christ had several times planned to kill him. (19b)

Questions.Q: What message did Paul preach and teach to the people of Ephesus?
Questions.A: He taught them everything from the Word of God that they needed to know. (20a)

Questions.Q: Where did Paul teach and preach?
Questions.A: Paul taught the people in public places, and he also taught them in their homes. (20b)

Questions.Q: What was Paul's main message, and to whom did he preach it?
Questions.A: Paul preached to both Jews and Gentiles.
He had told them all that they needed to repent of their sins and turn to God.
He had told them that they needed to trust in the Lord Jesus to save them. (21)

Questions.Q: For what reason was Paul planning to go to Jerusalem? What did he believe would happen to him there?
Questions.A: The Holy Spirit had told Paul that he must go to Jerusalem.
Paul did not know exactly what was going to happen to him there.
But in each city where Paul stopped, the Holy Spirit had warned him that he was going to have troubles in Jerusalem.
People were going to put him in prison and cause him to suffer. (22-23)

Questions.Q: For what reason was Paul determined to go to Jerusalem?
Questions.A: Paul was determined to complete the task which the Lord Jesus had given to him.
He did not care what people might do to him while he was finishing that work, even if someone was going to kill him. (24a)

Questions.Q: What task had the Lord Jesus given Paul that Paul said that he must complete?
Questions.A: The Lord Jesus had given Paul the work of telling people the good news that God is kind. (24b)

Questions.Q: For what reason did Paul speak with the elders a long time, telling them many things?
Questions.A: Paul knew that he would never see them again.
He reviewed with them how he had lived and what he had taught them during the years that he had lived among them. (25)

Questions.Q: What do you think Paul meant when he said that if anyone should be lost, it would be his own fault, and not Paul's?
Questions.A: Paul reminded the church leaders that he had always taught/preached that people will suffer eternal punishment if they do not repent of their sins and ask the Lord Jesus to save them.
Therefore, if people refused to believe that message, they were going to be eternally lost, but it would not be Paul's fault. (26) (Also see 18:6.)

Questions.Q: What do you think Paul meant by "the whole will of God"?
Questions.A: Paul meant that he had told people the entire/complete message which God had given to him.
He had told them all that they needed to know about what God has done for them. (27)

Questions.Q: With what did Paul compare the believers and the church leaders/elders whom he had appointed to watch over them?
Questions.A: Paul compared the believers with a flock of sheep, and the elders with the shepherds who watch over the flock. (28)
Questions.Alternative: With what did Paul compare the believers and the church leaders whom he had appointed to watch over them?
With what did Paul compare the believers and the elders whom he had appointed to watch over them?

Questions.Q: How did Paul describe the group of believers/the church?
Questions.A: Paul described the group of believers as the "church of God," because the Lord Jesus shed his blood in order to save them. (28b)
Questions.Alternative: How did Paul describe the group of believers?
How did Paul describe the church?

Questions.Q: With what did Paul compare the false teachers who were going to try to deceive the other believers?
Questions.A: Paul compared the false teachers with fierce wolves that come among a flock of sheep and attack them. (29)

Questions.Q: How long had Paul preached and taught God's Word in Ephesus?
Questions.A: Paul had been in Ephesus for three years, preaching and teaching the Word of God.
During the three years that Paul had been in Ephesus he had repeatedly warned the believers about false teachers who would try to deceive some of them. (31)

Questions.Q: For what reason had Paul wept when he taught the believers?
Questions.A: He often wept as he told them about the "wolves" that were going to come among the flock." (31b)

Questions.Q: As Paul was about to say good-bye to the elders, he committed them into God's care. What else did Paul tell them?
Questions.A: Paul told the elders that they should continue to believe the message that God saves people only because they trust in the Lord Jesus.
If they continued to believe that message, they were going to trust God more and more, and God would give them many good things. (32a)

Questions.Q: In what other way would God help the elders and the other believers?
Questions.A: God has promised to give many blessings to the people whom he has made his own.
He/God will give those blessings/good things to believers who continue to trust him and to believe the truth. (32b)

Questions.Q: What had Paul's way of life been like when he lived among the people of Ephesus?
Questions.A: Paul had lived humbly.
He had not wanted to have plenty of money and material things for himself. (33)

Questions.Q: Who had paid Paul's living expenses?
Questions.A: Paul had worked hard with his hands and in that way had paid his own living expenses. (34)

Questions.Q: What had Paul also been able to do by working to pay his own living expenses?
Questions.A: By working hard, Paul had not only paid for his own expenses but he had been able to help his companions. (34)

Questions.Q: What word that the Lord Jesus spoke did Paul quote, although it is not in any of the Gospels?
Questions.A: Paul reminded the elders that the Lord Jesus had said, "It is more blessed to give than to receive." (35)

Questions.Q: What did the elders do when Paul was ready to return to the ship?
Questions.A: When Paul finished speaking to the elders, they all knelt down, and Paul prayed.
Then they embraced Paul and kissed him, and they wept as they did that. (36-37)

Questions.Q: What made the elders all weep?
Questions.A: The elders wept when Paul told them that he would never see them again. That made them all very sad. (38)

Section.heading: Acts 21:1-16 Paul and his companions traveled from Miletus to Jerusalem.

Questions.Q: At what three places during the trip from Miletus to Jerusalem did Paul and his companions disembark?
Questions.A: Paul and his companions disembarked from the ships on which they were traveling at Tyre, at Ptolemais, and at Caesarea. (1, 7, 8)

Questions.Q: What did they do in the places where they disembarked?
Questions.A: In each of those towns, they spent some time with the Christians. (4, 7, 8)

Questions.Q: In which two towns did the Christians warn Paul that he should not go to Jerusalem? For what reason did they tell Paul that?
Questions.A: In Tyre and again in Caesarea, some of the believers prophesied that Paul should not go to Jerusalem.
The Holy Spirit had told them that Paul should not go there. (4, 11)

Questions.Q: At what port in Syria did the ship in which Paul and his companions traveled make its first stop?
Questions.A: Tyre was the first port in Syria at which the ship stopped. (1-3a)

Questions.Q: What did Paul and his companions do when the ship reached Tyre?
Questions.A: Paul and the others left/got off the ship in Tyre and stayed there while the crew unloaded the ship's cargo.
They found/learned that there were believers there, and they stayed with them for seven days. (3b-4a)

Questions.Q: What message did the Holy Spirit tell the believers in Tyre to tell Paul?
Questions.A: The believers were guided by the Holy Spirit, and they warned Paul that he should not go to Jerusalem. (4b)

Questions.Q: How did Paul respond/react to what those believers told him?
Questions.A: Paul and his companions continued on their journey towards Jerusalem. (5)
Questions.Alternative: How did Paul respond to what those believers told him?
How did Paul react to what those believers told him?

Questions.Q: What did the believers in Tyre do when Paul and his companions left?
Questions.A: The Christians in Tyre went to the beach with them, and they all knelt together and prayed.
Then they all said good-by to one another, and the people from Tyre returned to their homes. (5-6)

Questions.Q: What was the next port at which Paul spent some time with the believers?
Questions.A: The ship stopped next at Ptolemais.
Paul and the others left/got off the ship and stayed with the believers there for one day. (7)

Questions.Q: Describe what Paul and his companions did when the ship reached Caesarea.
Questions.A: Paul and his companions left/got off the ship and went to the home of a Christian whose name was Philip.
Philip lived with his four unmarried daughters in Caesarea. (8-9)

Questions.Q: In what places had Philip earlier been a leader among the Christians?
Questions.A: Philip was one of the seven men who had been chosen to give/to be responsible for giving the needy widows in that group of believers some food, or possibly money for food, each day. (8) (Also see 6:1-6)
He was also an evangelist and had preached to many people in Samaria. (8) (See also 8:4-25.)

Questions.Q: Who was Agabus? What message did he tell Paul?
Questions.A: Agabus was a Christian who had come from Jerusalem to Caesarea.
The Holy Spirit enabled him to prophesy/speak messages about what was going to happen.
Agabus told Paul that the Holy Spirit had shown him that the Jews in Jerusalem were going to make Paul a prisoner.
They were also going to turn Paul over to the Gentiles, and the Gentiles were going to judge him.
Agabus acted this out by using Paul's belt to tie his own hands and then his own feet. (10-11)

Questions.Q: What did the Christians in Caesarea say when they heard the prophecy that Agabus gave to Paul?
Questions.A: The Christians who heard what Agabus said was going to happen to Paul wept and begged Paul not to go to Jerusalem. (12)

Questions.Q: What did Paul reply?
Questions.A: Paul told them to stop trying to persuade him not to go to Jerusalem.
He was determined to go there, even if the Jews were going to tie him up as a prisoner.
Even if they were going to kill him, Paul was willing to die for the Lord Jesus. (13)

Questions.Q: What did the other Christians/believers say when they heard that?
Questions.A: They could see that Paul was determined to go to Jerusalem, so they said, "The Lord's will be done." (14)
Questions.Alternative: What did the other Christians say when they heard that?
What did the other believers say when they heard that?

Questions.Q: At what other place did Paul and his companions stay before they arrived in Jerusalem?
Questions.A: Some of the believers from Caesarea took Paul and his companions to the home of a believer whose name was Mnason, and they stayed there.
Mnason was a native of Cyprus.
He had been among the first people who had believed in the Lord Jesus. (16)

Section.heading: Acts 21:17-26 In Jerusalem, James advised Paul to go to the Temple with four men who had made a promise to God.

Questions.Q: What did the elders/leaders tell Paul that [they thought] he needed to know?
Questions.A: They told Paul that "many thousands" of Jews had become Christians, and they were all very careful to continue to keep the laws of Moses.
But people had told those Jewish believers that Paul no longer paid attention to the laws of Moses.
They had heard that, instead, Paul was teaching people who became Christians that they need not circumcise their sons nor observe any of the other Jewish customs. (20b-21)
Questions.Alternative: What did the elders tell Paul that they thought he needed to know?
What did the leaders tell Paul that they thought he needed to know?
What did the elders tell Paul that he needed to know?
What did the leaders tell Paul that he needed to know?

Questions.Q: What did James advise Paul to do in order to show that Paul still respected the laws of Moses and practiced the customs that Moses taught?
Questions.A: James advised Paul to go to [the Temple] with four Jewish believers who had made a promise to God.
When those men did/performed the rituals that the Law concerning their promise required, Paul should perform them, too.
Paul was also to pay for the animals that those men were going to offer [to God] when they completed the rituals. (23-24)

Questions.Q: What did Paul and his companions do the day after they arrived in Jerusalem?
Questions.A: The next day, Paul and his companions went to report to James and the other elders/leaders of the Jerusalem church. (17-18)

Questions.Q: What did Paul tell the group of leaders/elders? What did they then say to him?
Questions.A: Paul told them that many Gentiles had believed in the Lord Jesus after they heard him preach and teach.
The elders/church leaders were happy to hear that now there were many believers among the Gentiles. (19-20a)
Questions.Alternative: What did Paul tell the group of leaders? What did they then say to him?
What did Paul tell the group of elders? What did they then say to him?

Questions.Q: What else had James and the other elders/leaders told Gentile Christians [they should do] about the Law of Moses?
Questions.A: James reminded Paul that the Jerusalem leaders/elders had written a letter to Gentile Christians, giving them advice about the Law of Moses.
In that letter, the elders had said that there were only four things/acts that the Gentiles should not do. (25)
Questions.Alternative: What else had James and the other elders told Gentile Christians they should do about the Law of Moses?
What else had James and the other leaders told Gentile Christians they should do about the Law of Moses?
What else had James and the other elders told Gentile Christians about the Law of Moses?
What else had James and the other leaders told Gentile Christians about the Law of Moses?

Questions.Q: What were those four things that the Law of Moses stated that they should not do?
Questions.A: They should not eat any food that had been offered to idols.
They should not eat the blood of an animal [that had been slaughtered].
They should not eat the meat of an animal that had been strangled.
They should not have sexual relations with any person except their spouse/husband or wife. (25)

Questions.Q: What did Paul do on the next day?
Questions.A: The next day, Paul and the four men who had made a promise to God purified themselves in the way that the ritual law required.
After that, Paul went to [the Temple] and told the priest(s) that seven days later he and the four men were going to fulfill what they had promised [to God].
On that day, they were going to bring the animals that the Mosaic law required them to sacrifice [to God]. (26)

Section.heading: Acts 21:27-40 Angry Jews seized Paul in the Temple, and the Roman commander arrested him.

Questions.Q: What happened when some Jews saw Paul at the Temple?
Questions.A: The Jews became very angry and shouted to the other people who were in the Temple.
A crowd then seized him. (27a)

Questions.Q: What did those Jews from Asia shout which excited the other people in the Temple?
Questions.A: Those Jews shouted to the other people that Paul was the person who had gone everywhere, teaching everybody that they should not respect the Jewish nation, nor the laws of Moses, nor the Temple itself. The people who heard that were angry and formed a crowd that seized Paul. (27b-28a)

Questions.Q: What else did the Jews from Asia accuse Paul of doing?
Questions.A: They said that Paul had defiled the Temple by bringing Gentiles into the Temple. (28b)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when someone defiles something?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In this verse it means that someone would cause the temple to be unfit for God's presence by contact with ritually unclean persons. (See "defile" in KBT in the "unclean" entry.)

Questions.Q: Whom did the Jews from Asia think (mistakenly) that Paul had brought into the Temple?
Questions.A: The Jews from Asia had earlier seen Paul somewhere in Jerusalem accompanied by Trophimus, who was a Gentile.
When they saw Paul in the Temple, they [mistakenly] thought that he had brought Trophimus there with him. (29)

Questions.Q: What happened next?
Questions.A: People from all over the city heard that someone was ruining/spoiling the holiness of the Temple.
They ran and joined the crowd in the Temple, and some of the people grabbed Paul and dragged him outside.
Right away, [the Temple guards] closed the gates. (30)

Questions.Q: Who went to the Temple to find out why the people were rioting?
Questions.A: While the crowd was trying to kill Paul, someone had told the commander of the Roman troops that the people were rioting.
The Roman commander who was in charge took some of the soldiers and ran down to the crowd.
When the crowd saw the Roman soldiers and the commander, they stopped beating Paul. (31-32)

Questions.Q: What did the Roman commander do when he reached Paul?
Questions.A: He arrested Paul and ordered some of the soldiers to put chains on him.
Then he asked people in the crowd who Paul was and what he had done [to make them angry]. (33)

Questions.Q: For what reason was the commander not able to find out who Paul was nor what he had done?
Questions.A: The people in the crowd shouted many different things, each person trying to tell the commander about Paul.
They made so much noise that the commander could not tell what they were saying. (34a)

Questions.Q: What did the commander do in order to be able to hear/find out what Paul had done?
Questions.A: He ordered his soldiers to take Paul up into the fort/barracks [where they stayed]. (34b)
Questions.Alternative: What did the commander do in order to be able to hear what Paul had done?
What did the commander do in order to be able to find out what Paul had done?

Questions.Q: When the soldiers reached the steps of the barracks with Paul, they lifted Paul onto their shoulders. What is the reason that they did that?
Questions.A: The mob that was crowding around Paul and the soldiers had become very violent.
They were screaming, "Away with him!"
The soldiers had to carry Paul [on their shoulders] up to the entrance of the barracks, so that the [crowd of] people could not reach him. (35b-36)

Questions.Q: As the soldiers were about to take Paul into the fort/barracks, what did he ask the Roman commander?
Questions.A: Paul asked the commander for permission to tell him something. (37a)
Questions.Alternative: As the soldiers were about to take Paul into the fort, what did he ask the Roman commander?
As the soldiers were about to take Paul into the barracks, what did he ask the Roman commander?

Questions.Q: In what language did Paul speak to him/the commander?
Questions.A: He spoke to the commander in Greek. (37b)
Questions.Alternative: In what language did Paul speak to him?
In what language did Paul speak to the commander?

Questions.Q: What did the commander ask Paul when he heard Paul speak to him in Greek?
Questions.A: The commander asked him, "Are you not the Egyptian man who led an uprising against the Roman government?" (38)

Questions.Q: What did Paul answer?
Questions.A: Paul answered, "I am a Jew. [I am] a citizen of Tarsus, [which is] an important city in [the province of] Cilicia." (39a)

Questions.Q: What did Paul then request the Roman commander to do?
Questions.A: Paul asked the Roman commander to give him permission to speak to the crowd. (39)

Questions.Q: What did Paul do after the commander gave him permission to speak to the crowd?
Questions.A: Paul motioned to the people with his hand [showing that he wanted to speak to them].
When the people became quiet, Paul spoke to them in Aramaic.
[That was the language that the people in the crowd spoke.] (39b-40b)

Section.heading: Acts 22:1-21 Paul told the crowd of Jews who he was and how he had become a believer and a witness for the Lord Jesus.

Questions.Q: When Paul spoke to the crowd of Jews, what did he say to show them that he was a Jew?
Questions.A: Paul spoke to the crowd of Jews in the language which they spoke, which was Aramaic/Hebrew.
He addressed them as "brothers and fathers."
He told them that he had studied the Law of Moses with a well-known rabbi, Gamaliel, for several years.
He worshiped God and carefully obeyed the Law, just as many of them did. (1-3)

Questions.Q: What happened to Paul that caused him to change his mind about who Jesus was?
Questions.A: Paul was on the way to Damascus.
When he was almost there, the Lord Jesus appeared to him in blazing light from the sky.
The light was so bright/intense that it blinded Paul and he fell to the ground. (6-7a)

Questions.Q: What did Paul mean when he spoke about "followers of this Way"?
Questions.A: During the early years when people were beginning to believe in the Lord Jesus, people called that religion "the Way," or "the Way of the Lord." (4) (Also see Acts 9:2; 18:25; 19:9, 23)

Questions.Q: What did Paul tell the crowd of Jews that he had done before he was converted?
Questions.A: Paul told them that before he became a believer in the Lord Jesus, he had vigorously persecuted the followers of Jesus, even ordering people to kill them.
He thought that if he told the Jewish crowd that he had persecuted the Christians, they would think that he was a loyal Jew. (4-5)

Questions.Q: What did the Lord Jesus say to Paul and what did Paul reply?
Questions.A: The Lord Jesus spoke to Saul by name.
He said, "Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?"
Saul asked him, "Who are you, Lord?"
The Lord answered: "I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom you are persecuting." (7b-8)
Questions.Alternative: What did the Lord Jesus say to Saul and what did Saul reply?
Questions.Note: Paul's name was Saul before he became a believer in Jesus.

Questions.Q: When those things happened to Saul, what did the men who were traveling with him see and hear?
Questions.A: Those men saw the extremely bright light.
Also, they heard a voice speaking from the sky, but they did not understand what the voice said. (9)

Questions.Q: For what reason did Saul address Jesus as "Lord"?
Questions.A: When Saul addressed Jesus as "Lord" it showed that he knew that he was addressing a divine king. (8, 10)
Questions.Note: See Exegetical Helps on Acts for two interpretations.

Questions.Q: What else did Saul ask the Lord Jesus? What did the Lord Jesus tell him?
Questions.A: Saul asked the Lord Jesus what he wanted him to do.
The Lord replied, "Get up from the ground and go into Damascus.
Someone who is there will tell you what I have planned for you to do." (10)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Saul's companions had to lead Saul by the hand into Damascus?
Questions.A: They had to lead him by the hand because the bright light had blinded him. (11)

Questions.Q: Who came to see Saul after he arrived in Damascus?
Questions.A: A Jew whose name was Ananias came to see Saul.
Ananias carefully kept the Law, and he was also a believer. (12)

Questions.Q: What did he say to Saul?
Questions.A: Ananias stood beside Saul and addressed him as "Brother Saul."
He told Saul that he was going to be able to see again, and immediately Saul was able to see. (13)

Questions.Q: What message from God did Ananias tell Saul?
Questions.A: Ananias told Saul that the God whom the Jews worship had chosen him.
God had chosen him to know what he had planned for him to do, and to see the Messiah.
Also God had chosen Saul to hear the Messiah speak. (14)

Questions.Q: What else did Ananias tell Saul that God had planned that he would do?
Questions.A: God had chosen him to tell all kinds of people that he had seen and heard the Lord Jesus. (15)

Questions.Q: What did Ananias tell Saul that he should do right away?
Questions.A: Ananias told Saul that he should not delay, but that he should be baptized right away.
He should pray to the Lord, asking him to wash away/cleanse him from his sins. (16)

Questions.Q: After some time Saul had returned to Jerusalem. What did he do there?
Questions.A: Saul had gone to the Temple and had prayed to the Lord Jesus. (17)
Questions.Alternative: After some years Saul had returned to Jerusalem. What did he do there?
After some time Saul returned to Jerusalem. What had he done there?
What did Saul do when he returned to Jerusalem?
What did Saul do when he later returned to Jerusalem?
What had Saul done when he later returned to Jerusalem?
What had Saul done when he returned to Jerusalem?

Questions.Q: What did the Lord Jesus tell Saul while he was praying?
Questions.A: The Lord told Saul to leave Jerusalem immediately, because the Jews there would not believe him when he told them about the Lord Jesus. (17-18)

Questions.Q: What did Saul reply to the Lord?
Questions.A: He reminded the Lord that the Jews knew that he [Saul] had gone to one synagogue after another and had persecuted the people who believed in the Lord Jesus.
[He also said that] the Jews would also remember that when they stoned Stephen to death, he/Saul had helped the men who had thrown the stones.
[Therefore, Saul thought that the Jews now were going to believe what he told them about Jesus.] (19-20)

Questions.Q: What did the Lord reply to Saul?
Questions.A: The Lord repeated the same command.
He told Saul again, "Leave Jerusalem.
I will send you far away to the Gentiles." (21)

Section.heading: Acts 22:22-29 Paul prevented soldiers from whipping him by telling them he was a Roman citizen.

Questions.Q: What did Paul say to the centurion who had ordered the soldiers to beat him (Paul)?
Questions.A: Paul asked the centurion whether the Roman law permitted soldiers to whip/beat a person who was a Roman citizen, and who had not been tried by a judge.
[The centurion did not know that Paul was a Roman citizen before/until Paul asked him that question.] (25)

Questions.Q: What did the soldiers do when they heard that Paul was a Roman citizen?
Questions.A: The soldiers did not beat Paul.
They left him alone. (29a)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the crowd of Jews became very angry when Paul said that the Lord had told him to go [and preach] to the Gentiles?
Questions.A: They became very angry when they heard Paul say that, because the Jews did not believe that God loved the Gentiles.
[They were angry with Paul also because they did not believe that Jesus was the Messiah.] (22a)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that the crowd of Jews became very angry when Paul said that the Lord had told him to go and preach to the Gentiles?
What is the reason that the crowd of Jews became very angry when Paul said that the Lord had told him to go to the Gentiles?

Questions.Q: What did the Jews in that crowd say and do to show their anger?
Questions.A: They shouted, "Kill him! He doesn't deserve to live!"
They took off their cloaks and waved them, and they grabbed handfuls of dust and threw it up in the air. (22b-23)

Questions.Q: What did the Roman commander do when he saw that the crowd of Jews was threatening to kill Paul?
Questions.A: The Roman commander ordered some soldiers to take Paul into their barracks.
He told them to find out what Paul had done to make the crowd so angry.
In order to make Paul tell the truth, the commander ordered the soldiers to whip/beat him.
[That was the usual way that the Romans made a prisoner confess what he had done.] (24)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say to the centurion who had ordered the soldiers to beat him (Paul)?
Questions.A: Paul asked the centurion whether the Roman law permitted soldiers to whip/beat a person who was a Roman citizen, and who had not been tried by a judge.
[The centurion did not know that Paul was a Roman citizen before/until Paul asked him that question.] (25)

Questions.Q: What did the centurion do when Paul asked him that question?
Questions.A: The centurion went right away and told the commander that Paul was a Roman citizen.
He reminded the commander that it was against the law of Rome to whip/beat a Roman citizen who had not committed some crime. (26)

Questions.Q: What did the commander do when he heard what the centurion told him?
Questions.A: The commander went personally and asked Paul whether he was a Roman citizen.
Paul replied, "Yes, I was born a Roman citizen."
OR: "Yes, I was a Roman citizen when I was born." (27)
Questions.Alternative: What did the commander do when he heard what the officer told him?
What did the commanding officer do when he heard what the centurion told him?
What did the tribune do when he heard what the centurion told him?
What did the chief captain do when he heard what the centurion told him?
What did the captain do when he heard what the centurion told him?
What did the chief captain do when he heard what the officer told him?
What did the captain do when he heard what the officer told him?
What did the commander do?
What did the commander do after hearing what the centurion told him?

Questions.Q: What did the soldiers do when they heard that Paul was a Roman citizen?
Questions.A: The soldiers did not beat Paul.
They left him alone. (29a)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the commander was alarmed when he heard that Paul was a Roman citizen?
Questions.A: The commander was alarmed, [because he knew that someone with authority higher than his would probably punish him for ordering solders to whip Paul].
[Roman law prohibited any officer from ordering soldiers to make a Roman citizen a prisoner until that person had been tried and it had been proved that he had committed some crime.] (29b)

Section.heading: Acts 22:30-23:11 Paul defended himself before the Supreme Court of the Jews.

Questions.Q: How did Paul address the members of the Sanhedrin? What did he tell them about himself?
Questions.A: Paul addressed the members of the Sanhedrin as "my brothers/fellow countrymen."
He then told them that for all of his life he had fulfilled his duty to God. (1)

Questions.Q: What did the high priest do when he heard Paul say that?
Questions.A: He ordered one or two of the people who were standing near Paul to hit/slap him on the mouth. (2)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say was the reason for which the Sanhedrin was trying him?
Questions.A: Paul said that the Sanhedrin was trying him because he believed that people who have died will one day become alive again. (6c)

Questions.Q: What did the commander do in order to find out for what reason the Jews were accusing Paul?
Questions.A: The next day, the commander arranged with the Sanhedrin to question Paul.
[The Sanhedrin was the Supreme Court of the Jews.]
Then he took the chains off Paul and arranged to have him brought before the Sanhedrin.
The Sanhedrin was then going to ask Paul questions and judge him. (30)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say when someone hit him on the mouth?
Questions.A: Paul called the high priest a "whitewashed wall" and told him that God was going to hit him. (3a)

Questions.Q: In what way had the high priest disobeyed the laws of Moses?
Questions.A: The high priest had ordered someone to strike Paul. (3b)
Questions.Note: He/The high priest was authorized to judge Paul's case, but it was against the laws of Moses for a judge to punish a person before that person defended himself.

Questions.Q: Of what did the people who were standing near Paul accuse him?
Questions.A: They accused Paul of insulting the high priest.
They rebuked him/Paul, because the high priest served God. (4)

Questions.Q: What did Paul reply?
Questions.A: Paul replied that he knew the law prohibited people from speaking evil about the ruler of the people.
Paul also said that he had not known that the man whom he had insulted was the high priest. (5)

Questions.Q: What were the two kinds/groups of Jews who were present in the meeting of the Sanhedrin?
Questions.A: Some of the people who were present were Pharisees and others were Sadducees. (6a)
Questions.Alternative: What were the two kinds of Jews who were present in the meeting of the Sanhedrin?
What were the two groups of Jews who were present in the meeting of the Sanhedrin?

Questions.Q: To which of these kinds/groups of Jews did Paul belong?
Questions.A: Paul told them that he was a Pharisee, and his father had been a Pharisee. (6b)
Questions.Alternative: To which of these kinds of Jews did Paul belong?
To which of these groups of Jews did Paul belong?

Questions.Q: When the members of the Sanhedrin heard what Paul believed, what did they do?
Questions.A: When the members of the Sanhedrin heard what Paul believed, the two groups began to argue violently.
They argued, because the Pharisees believed what Paul believed, and the Sadducees disagreed with the Pharisees and with Paul. (7)

Questions.Q: What did the Sadducees not believe?
Questions.A: The Sadducees did not believe that the people who have died will ever become alive again. They also did not believe that there are any angels or other kinds of spirits. (8a-b)

Questions.Q: What did the Pharisees believe?
Questions.A: The Pharisees believed that the time will come when God will cause everyone who has died to become alive again.
They also believed that there are angels and other kinds of spirits. (8c)

Questions.Q: The two groups/kinds of Jews argued very loudly and violently. What did the Pharisees say about Paul?
Questions.A: Some of the Pharisees said that they did not think there was anything wrong with Paul nor in what he believed.
[They said that, because they also believed several of the things/doctrines which Paul believed.] (9)
Questions.Alternative: The two groups of Jews argued very loudly and violently. What did the Pharisees say about Paul?
The two kinds of Jews argued very loudly and violently. What did the Pharisees say about Paul?

Questions.Q: What else did the Pharisees say in order to defend Paul?
Questions.A: Those Pharisees said that perhaps an angel or some other spirit had spoken to Paul. (9)

Questions.Q: What did the commander do when he saw that the Sadducees and Pharisees were fighting violently all around Paul?
Questions.A: The commander was afraid that the men who were arguing would tear Paul to pieces.
So the commander ordered some of his soldiers to go and forcibly take Paul away from the men who were fighting and take him to their barracks. (10)

Questions.Q: In what way did the Lord Jesus encourage Paul at that time?
Questions.A: The next night, Paul saw the Lord Jesus standing beside him.
The Lord said, "Do not be discouraged. You have told people in Jerusalem about me, and you are going to do it also in Rome." (11)

Section.heading: Acts 23:12-22 More than forty Jews made a promise/took an oath that they would kill Paul, but Paul's nephew warned him.

Questions.Q: Who met in order to plan a way to kill Paul? What did they promise when they decided to do that?
Questions.A: More than forty Jews met and decided that they were going to kill Paul.
Together they promised each other that they would not eat or drink anything until they had killed Paul. (12-13)

Questions.Q: What did those Jews tell the chief priests and elders [who also hated Paul]?
Questions.A: A few of the forty Jews went to the chief priests and elders and told them about the promise/vow that they had made to kill Paul. (14)
Questions.Alternative: What did those Jews tell the chief priests and elders who also hated Paul?
What did those Jews tell the chief priests and elders?

Questions.Q: What did those Jews ask the priests and elders of the Sanhedrin/Supreme Council to do?
Questions.A: The Jews who had made a promise asked the priests and elders to go to the Roman commander and request that the commander order someone to bring Paul before the Sanhedrin so that they could ask him more questions.
Then, while [the soldiers] were bringing Paul there [from the barracks] to meet with the Sanhedrin, the Jews were going to come out of where they were hiding and kill Paul/him. (15)
Questions.Alternative: What did those Jews ask the priests and elders of the Sanhedrin to do?
What did those Jews ask the priests and elders of the Supreme Council to do?

Questions.Q: What happened which hindered those Jews from killing Paul?
Questions.A: Paul's nephew had heard what those Jews had planned.
So he went to the barracks where Paul was and told Paul what he had heard. (16)

Questions.Q: What did Paul do when his nephew told him what the Jews were planning to do?
Questions.A: Paul asked one of the officers/centurions to take his nephew to the commander.
He told the officer/centurion that his nephew needed to tell the commander something. (17)

Questions.Q: What did Paul's nephew tell the commander?
Questions.A: Paul's nephew told the commander that certain Jews were going to ask the commander to order that Paul go to meet again with the Sanhedrin.
Those Jews were going to tell the commander that the Sanhedrin needed to ask Paul some more questions.
Paul's nephew also told the commander that it was not true that the Sanhedrin wanted to meet with Paul again and ask him more questions. (20)

Questions.Q: What did Paul's nephew ask/request the commander not to do?
Questions.A: Paul's nephew told the commander not to order that Paul go to meet the Sanhedrin again. (21)
Questions.Alternative: What did Paul's nephew ask the commander not to do?
What did Paul's nephew request the commander not to do?

Questions.Q: What else did he tell the commander?
Questions.A: He told the commander that more than forty Jews were planning to kill Paul.
They had made a promise with each other that they would not eat or drink anything until they had killed him/Paul.
They were already waiting for the commander to order a guard to take Paul to where the Sanhedrin was going to meet.
But they/the Jews were going to wait in hiding, and they were going to kill Paul as he was on the way. (21)

Questions.Q: After the commander heard what Paul's nephew told him, what did he do?
Questions.A: The commander told Paul's nephew not to let anyone know what he had told him.
Then the commander dismissed him. (22)

Section.heading: Acts 23:23-35 The commander sent Paul from Jerusalem to Caesarea, escorted by a guard of Roman soldiers.

Questions.Q: What did the commander do in order to protect Paul from being killed by the Jews?
Questions.A: He ordered two of his centurions to assemble a group of 200 foot soldiers, 70 horsemen, and 200 soldiers carrying spears to be ready to leave for Caesarea at nine o'clock that night.
They were to provide Paul with two horses to ride.
Then they were to escort Paul to Caesarea and leave him in the charge of the Governor, Felix. (23-24)

Questions.Q: What was the name of the commander who gave those orders about Paul?
Questions.A: The name of the commander was Claudius Lysias. (25-26)

Questions.Q: What did the commander write about Paul in the letter that he sent to Governor Felix?
Questions.A: He told the Governor that Paul was a Roman citizen, and that he (the commander) had prevented the Jews from killing Paul. (27)

Questions.Q: For what reason had Claudius Lysias taken Paul to a meeting of the Sanhedrin?
Questions.A: Claudius Lysias had taken Paul to a meeting of the Sanhedrin so that he could find out what Paul had done to cause the Jews to be angry with him. (28)

Questions.Q: In the letter that Claudius Lysias wrote, what charges/accusations did he say/write that the members of the Sanhedrin made against Paul?
Questions.A: He wrote that the Jews had accused Paul of disagreeing with them about certain of their religious laws.
He also said/wrote that the Jews had not accused Paul of any crime for which he deserved to be executed or even put in prison. (29)
Questions.Alternative: In the letter that Claudius Lysias wrote, what charges did he say that the members of the Sanhedrin made against Paul?
In the letter that Claudius Lysias wrote, what charges did he write that the members of the Sanhedrin made against Paul?
In the letter that Claudius Lysias wrote, what accusations did he say that the members of the Sanhedrin made against Paul?
In the letter that Claudius Lysias wrote, what accusations did he write that the members of the Sanhedrin made against Paul?

Questions.Q: What else did the commander write to the Governor in his letter?
Questions.A: He wrote that he had told the Jews, who were accusing Paul, to go to Caesarea and present their charges against Paul before the Governor. (30)

Questions.Q: Describe the trip that the soldiers made with Paul from Jerusalem to Caesarea.
Questions.A: The soldiers went with Paul as far as [the town] Antipatris that night.
The next day, the foot soldiers returned to Jerusalem, while the horsemen went on with Paul to Caesarea.
They gave the Governor the letter from Claudius Lysias and delivered Paul into his care. (31-33)

Questions.Q: What did the Governor say to Paul after he had read the letter from the commander?
Questions.A: After the Governor read the letter, he asked Paul what province he was from, and Paul replied, "Cilicia." (34)

Questions.Q: What else did the Governor say to Paul?
Questions.A: He told Paul that he would listen to his defense after the Jews, who were accusing him, had come from Jerusalem. (35a)

Questions.Q: Where did the Governor arrange for Paul to stay?
Questions.A: The Governor gave orders that Paul was to stay in the building that had earlier been Herod's palace.
A guard was to be with him all the time. (35b)

Section.heading: Acts 24:1-27 Paul defended himself before the Governor, Felix, and several men of the Sanhedrin.

Questions.Q: What did Paul say to prove that he had not done the crimes which Tertullus said he had done?
Questions.A: Paul told the Governor that only twelve days had passed since he had gone up to Jerusalem. When he was in Jerusalem, the Jews had not found him arguing with anyone in the Temple, nor had they seen him stirring up the people anywhere else in the city of Jerusalem.
Therefore, it was not true that he went everywhere stirring up the Jews to riot. (10-12)

Questions.Q: Who came from Jerusalem to Caesarea to accuse Paul before Felix?
Questions.A: The high priest, Ananias, and a few other members of the Sanhedrin came from Jerusalem to accuse Paul before Felix.
A lawyer whose name was Tertullus also came to present his charges against Paul. (1)

Questions.Q: In what way did Tertullus describe Paul? What bad things did he say Paul had done?
Questions.A: Tertullus said that Paul was a dangerous trouble-maker.
He said that everywhere in the world Paul had stirred up the Jews to riot.
He also said that Paul was the leader of a group called the Nazarenes. (5)

Questions.Q: Tertullus said that Paul had disobeyed the laws of the Jews. In what way had Paul done that?
Questions.A: Tertullus said that Paul had tried to defile the Temple in Jerusalem.
For those reasons the Jews had had Paul arrested. (6a)

Questions.Q: Who was Lysias?
Questions.A: The chief captain (of the Roman soldiers in Jerusalem).
Questions.Alternative: Who was Lysius?

Questions.Q: What did Lysias do?
Questions.A: He took Paul away from the Jews (rescuing him from what probably would have been "mob justice").
He had Paul kept in custody so that a legal trial could take place according to Roman law.
He instructed the Jews who were accusing Paul to appear before Felix with their charges.
Questions.Alternative: What did Lysius do?

Questions.Q: What did Tertullus hope Felix would do?
Questions.A: Tertullus said that Felix should examine/question Paul and find him guilty of the things about which the Jews were accusing him.

Questions.Q: What did the priests/religious leaders say about the things that Tertullus accused Paul of doing?
Questions.A: They agreed that Paul had done all the things that Tertullus said he/Paul had done. (9)
Questions.Alternative: What did the priests say about the things that Tertullus accused Paul of doing?
What did the religious leaders say about the things that Tertullus accused Paul of doing?

Questions.Q: What did Paul say to prove that he had not done the crimes which Tertullus said he had done?
Questions.A: Paul told the Governor that only twelve days had passed since he had gone up to Jerusalem. When he was in Jerusalem, the Jews had not found him arguing with anyone in the Temple, nor had they seen him stirring up the people anywhere else in the city of Jerusalem.
Therefore, it was not true that he went everywhere stirring up the Jews to riot. (10-12)

Questions.Q: What else did Paul say about the Jews who accused him?
Questions.A: Paul said that the Jews could not prove that he had done any of the crimes of which they accused him. (13)

Questions.Q: Which of the crimes of which Tertullus accused Paul, did Paul say were true?
Questions.A: Paul said it was true that he followed the "Way," which the Jews called a false sect. (14a)

Questions.Q: What else did Paul say about his religious beliefs?
Questions.A: Paul said that he worshiped the God whom the Jews had always worshiped.
He also believed everything that had been written in the Law of Moses, and he believed everything that the prophets had written. (14b)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say he believed which the Jews who were accusing him also believed?
Questions.A: Paul said that he believed that God will cause all people to come alive who have died.
God will cause people to come alive again who were/are good and also people who were/are wicked.
He said that the Jews, who had come to accuse him, also believed that God will do that. (15)

Questions.Q: For what reason did Paul always try to keep his conscience clear before God and man?
Questions.A: Paul knew that when God causes the people who have died to live again, each person will stand before him/God.
God will judge each person for the way that he or she lived. (16)

Questions.Q: What had Paul been doing in the Temple on the day that certain Jews had seen him there?
Questions.A: On that day Paul had gone to the Temple to take some money for other Jews, and to offer sacrifices to God.
He had already completed the ritual for purification when he went there.
He was not with a large number of people, but he was there quietly by himself. (17b-18)

Questions.Q: Which people did Paul say should have come and accused him before the Governor?
Questions.A: Paul said that certain Jews from the province of Asia should have come and accused him before the Governor. (19)

Questions.Q: Who else did Paul say should have come and accused him before the Governor?
Questions.A: Paul said that the members of the Sanhedrin should themselves have come and accused him, if they thought he had committed a crime. (20)

Questions.Q: What had Paul said, when he stood before the Sanhedrin in Jerusalem, that some of them would have said was a crime?
Questions.A: When Paul stood before the Sanhedrin, he had shouted that they were trying him because of what he believed.
They were trying/judging him because he believed that one day God will cause to live again all people who have died. (21)

Questions.Q: For what reason did Felix not wish to hear Paul continue to defend himself?
Questions.A: Felix knew what the people of "the Way" believed, so he did not wish to hear any more. (22a)

Questions.Q: What did Felix say which ended Paul's defense?
Questions.A: Felix said he would decide Paul's case when the commander Lysias arrived.
Then he dismissed the court. (22b)

Questions.Q: What did Felix tell the centurion who had accompanied Paul?
Questions.A: Felix told the centurion to keep a guard with Paul all the time, but he should not require Paul always to stay in one place.
If Paul's friends should come, the centurion was to allow them to bring him/Paul things that he needed. (23)

Questions.Q: Who came with Felix when Felix sent for Paul again?
Questions.A: Drusilla, the wife of Felix, came with him to listen to Paul.
Drusilla was Jewish. (24)

Questions.Q: What did Paul speak about before Felix and Drusilla?
Questions.A: Paul told them about what it is like to believe in Christ Jesus. (24b)

Questions.Q: What else did Paul tell Felix and Drusilla about what God requires of people who believe in Jesus Christ?
Questions.A: Paul also told Felix and his wife that God requires people to do what is righteous/just and to control what their bodies want.
He told them that God will one day judge each person for the things he/she has done. (25a)

Questions.Q: What did Felix say after he heard that one day God will judge each person?
Questions.A: Felix was afraid and said to Paul, "That is enough for today.
Some other time I will send for you, and you can speak to me again." (25b)
