Questions.Q: Felix frequently sent for Paul to come again and talk with him. For what reason did he send for him?
Questions.A: Felix thought that if he spoke with Paul many times, Paul would offer him money [so that Felix/he would set him free]. (26)

Questions.Q: How long did Paul remain as a prisoner in Caesarea?
Questions.A: Paul remained as a prisoner in Caesarea for two years.
After two years, another governor, whose name was Festus, became the governor [in place of Felix]. (27a)

Questions.Q: For what reason did Felix leave Paul in prison?
Questions.A: Felix left Paul in prison because he wanted to do the Jews a favor. (27b)

Section.heading: Acts 25:1-12 The Jewish leaders accused Paul before the Governor, Festus.

Questions.Q: What did the chief priests and the Jewish religious leaders tell Festus when he was in Jerusalem?
Questions.A: The chief priests and the religious leaders went to Festus and told him that Paul had done many evil things for which he should be tried. (1-2a)

Questions.Q: What did the chief priests and the religious leaders want Festus to do?
Questions.A: They urgently requested Festus to send Paul back to Jerusalem and let them try Paul there. (2b-3a)

Questions.Q: For what reason did the Jewish leaders want Festus to send Paul back to Jerusalem?
Questions.A: They wanted Festus to send Paul back to Jerusalem because they were planning to kill him on the road before he arrived in Jerusalem. (3b)

Questions.Q: What did Festus answer them?
Questions.A: He said that Paul was being held in Caesarea as a prisoner and that he [Festus] would soon be going there.
He told the Jewish leaders they should go to Caesarea with him and accuse Paul there, if he had done anything wrong. (4-5)

Questions.Q: Of what did the Jewish leaders accuse Paul when they stood before Festus in Caesarea?
Questions.A: The Jewish leaders accused Paul before Festus of having done many evil things.
But they could not prove that Paul/he had done those things. (6-7)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say when he defended himself?
Questions.A: He told Festus that he had not done anything against the law of the Jewish religion, nor anything against the Temple.
He also told Festus that he had not done anything against the Roman Emperor. (8)

Questions.Q: What favor did the Jewish religious leaders want Festus to do for them?
Questions.A: They wanted Festus to order Paul to go up to Jerusalem again and to try Paul there.
So Festus asked Paul if he was willing to return to Jerusalem and have the Jews accuse him there. (9)

Questions.Q: What did Paul reply to Festus?
Questions.A: Paul replied that the court of Festus [in Caesarea] was a court of the Roman government, and he had a right to be judged there.
Paul then repeated that he had done no wrong to the Jews, and that Festus knew that. (10)

Questions.Q: What else did Paul say about the Roman Government?
Questions.A: He also said that if he had committed any crime against the Roman government and deserved to die/be killed, he was willing to die for that crime. (11a)

Questions.Q: For what reason did Paul refuse to agree to allow the Jews to judge him?
Questions.A: Paul repeated that he had not done the things of which the Jews accused him.
The Jews had not been able to prove that Paul had done any wrong to them.
Therefore, no one had the right to give the Jews the authority to judge him. (11b)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say to Festus after that?
Questions.A: Paul said, "I appeal to the Emperor (Caesar)!" (11c)
Questions.Note: When he said that, Paul was asking that the highest Roman court judge him. The court of the Emperor in Rome was the highest court.

Questions.Q: What did Festus do when Paul asked that the Emperor's/Caesar's court judge him?
Questions.A: Festus talked with some men who advised him what to do about Paul.
Then he told Paul, "You have asked that the Emperor's court judge you, so we will send you to Rome [to be judged there]." (12)
Questions.Alternative: What did Festus do when Paul asked that the Emperor's court judge him?
What did Festus do when Paul asked that Caesar's court judge him?
What did Festus do when Paul appealed to the Emperor?
What did Festus do when Paul appealed to Caesar?

Section.heading: Acts 25:13-22 Festus told Agrippa about Paul and asked Agrippa to advise him.

Questions.Q: Whom did Festus ask for advice about what he should do with a prisoner named Paul?
Questions.A: Felix told King Agrippa about Paul and asked how he ought to decide Paul's case. (13-14, 21-22)

Questions.Q: Who was King Agrippa?
Questions.A: Agrippa was an important official of the Roman government. (13)
Questions.Note: King Agrippa ruled over an area northeast of Judea. Bernice was his sister.

Questions.Q: For what purpose had King Agrippa and Bernice come to Caesarea?
Questions.A: After Festus had become the Governor of Judea, Agrippa and Bernice came to Caesarea to welcome him. (13)

Questions.Q: What had Festus told Agrippa about Paul?
Questions.A: Festus told Agrippa that Paul had been left as a prisoner by Felix. (14)

Questions.Q: What had the Jewish leaders done when Festus had been in Jerusalem?
Questions.A: The Jewish leaders had come to him and had made charges against Paul. (15a)

Questions.Q: What had the Jewish leaders asked Festus to do?
Questions.A: Festus said that the Jewish religious leaders in Jerusalem had asked him to judge/condemn Paul. (15)

Questions.Q: What did Festus say was his reason for refusing to judge Paul?
Questions.A: Festus said that he had refused to judge/condemn Paul because Paul had not yet had a chance to defend himself against the people who had accused him. (16)

Questions.Q: What did Festus tell Agrippa about the trial of Paul?
Questions.A: Festus said that the day after the Jewish leaders arrived in Caesarea, he had held court, and had sent for Paul in order to judge his case. (17)

Questions.Q: What kinds of things did the Jewish leaders accuse Paul before Festus?
Questions.A: The Jewish leaders did not accuse Paul of any crime against the Roman government.
They told Festus only that Paul had argued with them about certain religious beliefs. (18-19a)

Questions.Q: What did the Jewish leaders say about Jesus, and what did Paul say?
Questions.A: Festus told Agrippa that Paul and the Jewish leaders had argued about a man named Jesus.
The Jewish leaders said that Jesus was dead, but Paul claimed that Jesus was alive. (19b)

Questions.Q: For what reason did Festus say that he had asked Paul if he was willing to go to Jerusalem and be judged there?
Questions.A: Festus said that he did not feel able to judge Paul's case, because the accusations against Paul were entirely about the Jewish religion. (20)

Questions.Q: For what reason did Festus want Agrippa to advise him how to decide Paul's case?
Questions.A: Festus told Agrippa that Paul had asked to be judged by the Emperor's court.
He wanted Agrippa to advise him whether he should do that. (21)
Questions.Note: In order to be judged by the Emperor's court, Paul would need to go to Rome. So Festus planned to keep Paul under guard until he could send him to Rome.

Questions.Q: What did Agrippa say after he had heard what Festus told him about Paul?
Questions.A: Agrippa said that he himself would like to hear Paul defend himself.
Festus promised him that he would hold court the next day and send for Paul to present himself. (22)

Section.heading: Acts 25:23-26:32 Paul defended himself before Agrippa, Bernice, and many other people.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what the author has written in these verses.
Questions.A: In these verses Paul defended himself before King Agrippa.

Questions.Q: What people came into the hall where Festus held court, in order to hear Paul?
Questions.A: Agrippa came with his sister, Bernice.
They were escorted by the military chiefs and the most important men of Caesarea.
A ceremony took place to celebrate/announce their arrival because they were important people.
Then Festus ordered a guard, and the guard brought Paul into the hall. (23)

Questions.Q: What did Festus tell King Agrippa and the other people present that the Jews had said about Paul?
Questions.A: Festus said that all the Jews in Caesarea and in Jerusalem shouted that Paul was not fit to live. (24)

Questions.Q: What did Festus himself say about Paul?
Questions.A: Festus told Agrippa that when he listened to Paul defending himself, he had decided that Paul had not done anything for which he deserved to be executed/killed.
However, Paul himself had requested that he be tried/judged by the Emperor in Rome.
So Festus had decided to send him there. (25)

Questions.Q: For what reason had Festus wanted King Agrippa to listen to Paul's defense?
Questions.A: He said that there was nothing for which he could charge/accuse Paul, but he was sending him to Rome as a prisoner.
So he wanted Agrippa to tell him what to say about Paul in the letter he was going to send to the Emperor. (26-27)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say to Agrippa when he began to speak? For what reason did he say that?
Questions.A: Paul said that he was pleased that he was going to defend himself before King Agrippa.
Agrippa knew all about the customs of the Jews and the questions that they argued about.
For that reason, Paul asked Agrippa to listen to him patiently. (1-3)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say about his life before he became a Christian?
Questions.A: He said that he had always lived as a strict Pharisee, both when he had lived in the province where he was born, and later, in Jerusalem.
He said that all the Jews had known him, and they could testify that he had lived as a Pharisee who carefully kept the rules and customs of their religion. (4-5)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say was the reason that he was being tried?
Questions.A: Paul said that he was being tried because he believed that God would do what he had promised to the patriarchs/Jewish ancestors that he would do. (6)

Questions.Q: What else did Paul say about the promise that God had made to the patriarchs?
Questions.A: Paul said that many God-fearing Jews from all of the twelve tribes also believed that God was going to do what he had promised.
The Jews accused Paul of wrongdoing because Paul believed that God will do what he had promised to do. (7)

Questions.Q: What did Paul then ask the people who were present?
Questions.A: Paul asked them, "Why are you not able to believe that God is able to cause a person who has died to live again?" (8)
Questions.Note: Paul implied that the people who were listening did not believe that God could do that.

Questions.Q: Earlier, when Paul had lived in Jerusalem, what had he done to show that he was a zealous Jew?
Questions.A: Paul had persecuted the followers of Jesus of Nazareth in every way that he could.
He received authority from the chief priests to put many of the Christians in prison.
He also agreed with the Jews who voted that they should kill the Christians. (9-10a)

Questions.Q: What other things had Paul done to try to destroy the Christians?
Questions.A: Paul many times went from one synagogue to another, looking for followers of Jesus and ordering [other Jews] to punish them.
He had repeatedly tried to make the Christians deny that they believed in Jesus.
He even went from Jerusalem to foreign cities and persecuted the Christians whom he found there. (11)

Questions.Q: What did Paul tell Agrippa about how he became a believer in the Lord Jesus?
Questions.A: Paul told Agrippa that he had been on the way to Damascus, where he was planning to find and persecute the Christians.
Before he arrived, a light brighter than the noonday sun blazed around Paul and his companions, making them fall to the ground.
A voice from the sky spoke to Saul in his own language, calling him by name.
The person speaking said to Saul, "Why are you persecuting me?" (12-14a)

Questions.Q: What else did the Lord Jesus say to Saul?
Questions.A: He said to Saul, "It is hard for you to kick against the goads." (14b)
Questions.Note: He/The Lord was comparing Saul to a stubborn ox which kicks back against the pointed stick with which his owner prods him to move ahead. When the ox kicks back against the pointed stick, it hurts his legs.

Questions.Q: What did Saul ask the person who was speaking to him?
Questions.A: Saul asked the person who was speaking, "Who are you, Lord?" (15)

Questions.Q: What did the person in the sky answer?
Questions.A: The person answered, "I am Jesus. I am the one whom you are persecuting." (15)

Questions.Q: What else did the Lord Jesus tell Saul at that time?
Questions.A: The Lord Jesus told Saul to stand up.
Then Jesus told Saul that he had appeared in order to appoint him to be his servant.
Saul was to tell people how he had seen the Lord Jesus on that day.
The Lord would show Saul more about himself later, and Saul was to tell people that, too. (16)

Questions.Q: What did the Lord Jesus tell Saul about the people to whom he was to witness?
Questions.A: The Lord told Saul that he was to witness to his own people, the Jews, and also to Gentiles. But they would oppose him.
When they persecuted him, the Lord would rescue him. (17)

Questions.Q: What did the Lord Jesus say that the message about him would do for/to the Jews and for/to the Gentiles?
Questions.A: The message that Saul was to give people was going to open the eyes of the people who believed it.
It would bring them out of the darkness where they lived and into the light.
It would bring them out of the control of Satan and into the control of God. (18a)
Questions.Alternative: What did the Lord Jesus say that the message about him would do for the Jews and for the Gentiles?
What did the Lord Jesus say that the message about him would do for the Jews and to the Gentiles?
What did the Lord Jesus say that the message about him would do to the Jews and for the Gentiles?
What did the Lord Jesus say that the message about him would do to the Jews and to the Gentiles?

Questions.Q: Those are figures of speech. What do you think they mean?
Questions.A: Those figures of speech mean that people who do not know the true God are spiritually blind.
They live in spiritual darkness and they are controlled by Satan.
They do not know the true God and he/God does not control them. (18)

Questions.Q: In what way would Saul help those people by telling them about the Lord Jesus?
Questions.A: When people believe in the Lord Jesus, he opens their minds so that they know the true God.
The Lord Jesus brings them out of the control of Satan and into the control of God. (18a)

Questions.Q: What did God say he was going to do for the people who would believe the message about the Lord Jesus?
Questions.A: God would not punish those people for their sins. Instead, he was going to forgive their sins.
He/God was going to receive them as his own people and care for them. (18b)

Questions.Q: What did Paul do after the Lord Jesus revealed himself to him from heaven?
Questions.A: Paul very soon began to tell many people that they should repent of their sins and begin to live in a way that would honor God. (19-20)

Questions.Q: Where did Paul preach?
Questions.A: Paul preached first in Damascus, then in Jerusalem, and after that, [he preached] in all of the province of Judea.
He also went to many other places and preached to the Gentiles. (20a)

Questions.Q: When Paul was in the Temple grounds, the Jews seized him and tried to kill him. For what reason did they do that?
Questions.A: The Jews seized him and tried to kill him because he preached that they needed to repent of their sins and turn to God. (21)

Questions.Q: Many people had wanted to kill Paul, but they had not done it. What did he say was the reason that he was still alive?
Questions.A: Paul was still alive because God had protected him from all of the people who planned to kill him. (22)

Questions.Q: What else did Paul tell the Jews when he preached?
Questions.A: Paul also told them/the Jews that the things that Moses and the other prophets had written were going to happen to the Messiah had happened to Jesus. (22b)

Questions.Q: What things had the prophets written were going to happen to the Messiah?
Questions.A: The prophets had written that people were going to mistreat the Messiah, causing him to die.
The Messiah was going to be the first person who would live again after he had died.
Because of the Messiah both Jews and Gentiles would know that God wanted to save them from their sins. (23a)

Questions.Q: What did the Governor, Festus, say to Paul to show that he did not want Paul to continue talking about the Scriptures?
Questions.A: Festus said to Paul, "You are crazy!
You study too much and you are going crazy!" (24)

Questions.Q: What did Paul answer?
Questions.A: Paul answered that he was not crazy.
All that he had said was true, and it all made good sense. (25)

Questions.Q: Paul then spoke to Agrippa. What did he say about him?
Questions.A: Paul said that he could speak with confidence to Agrippa, because he knew what Paul had been talking about.
Paul was sure that Agrippa knew about whom he had been speaking, because many people had heard about Jesus. (26)

Questions.Q: What did Paul ask Agrippa?
Questions.A: Paul first asked King Agrippa whether he believed what the prophets had written.
Then he said, "I know that you believe them." (27)

Questions.Q: In what way did Agrippa answer?
Questions.A: He said, "Do you think that with the few things you have said, you can persuade me to become a Christian?" (28)

Questions.Q: What did Paul answer?
Questions.A: Paul said that he prayed to God that King Agrippa and also all the others who were listening to him would become believers in Jesus. (29)

Questions.Q: What did King Agrippa, Festus, Bernice and the other people say to one another about Paul as they left the room/hall?
Questions.A: They said, "That man has not done anything for which he should be killed or even put in prison." (30-31)
Questions.Alternative: What did King Agrippa, Festus, Bernice and the other people say to one another about Paul as they left the room?
What did King Agrippa, Festus, Bernice and the other people say to one another about Paul as they left the hall?

Questions.Q: What did Agrippa say to Festus about Paul?
Questions.A: Agrippa said that Paul could have been set free if he had not requested that the Emperor judge his case. (32)

Section.heading: Acts 27:1-12 Roman soldiers take Paul and they begin to sail to Rome on a ship.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what the author had written in these verses.
Questions.A: The author described the sea voyage that Paul took by ship from Caesarea to the island of Crete.

Questions.Q: Who was in charge of Paul and the other prisoners who sailed for Rome?
Questions.A: An officer who commanded one of the regiments of the Roman army was in charge of the prisoners.
The officer's name was Julius. (1)

Questions.Q: Where did Paul and the other prisoners board the first ship in which they traveled?
Questions.A: Paul and the other prisoners who were going to Rome boarded that ship in Caesarea.
The ship had come from the port of Adramyttium.
The ship was going to return to other seaports on the coast of the province of Asia. (2a)

Questions.Q: Who else, whom Paul already knew, boarded the ship?
Questions.A: When Paul and the other passengers boarded the ship in Caesarea, a believer named Aristarchus, who was from Thessalonica, also boarded that ship. (2b)

Questions.Q: Where did the ship arrive the next day, and what did Paul do there?
Questions.A: The next day, the ship arrived at the port of Sidon.
Julius, the Roman officer, gave Paul permission to go and visit his friends and to receive whatever they wanted to give him. (3)

Questions.Q: After the ship left Sidon, what island did it pass?
Questions.A: After that, the ship passed along the eastern side of the island of Cyprus.
The eastern side of Cyprus was protected from the wind. (4)

Questions.Q: At what port did the passengers on that ship get off and board another ship?
Questions.A: When the ship reached the port of Myra, all the passengers, of whom Julius was in charge, got off.
The officer, Julius, arranged for all of them to board another ship. (5-6)

Questions.Q: Where was the second ship going?
Questions.A: That ship was going to sail for [the country] Italy. (5-6)

Questions.Q: Where did that ship make its first stop?
Questions.A: The ship stopped at a port called Cnidus, [which was a town on the northwest coast of the province of Asia]. (7)

Questions.Q: For what reason did the ship then sail south, towards the island of Crete?
Questions.A: A strong wind kept blowing against the front of the ship, so it was impossible for the ship to continue traveling straight ahead.
The ship then sailed south to the island of Crete.
Then the ship traveled slowly along the south coastline of the island, [which was sheltered from the wind]. (7-8)

Questions.Q: At what harbor on the coast of Crete did the ship stop?
Questions.A: The ship stopped at a harbor called Fair Havens. (8)

Questions.Q: The trip that far had taken much longer than the captain had planned that it would take. What had made it very slow?
Questions.A: The ship had traveled against strong winds striking it from the front, so that it had to move slowly. (7-8)

Questions.Q: At what time did people who knew about the sea think/say it was no longer safe to travel on the sea?
Questions.A: People who knew about the sea knew that after the Day of Atonement had passed, there would be many storms.
After that time, it would be dangerous to travel on the sea. (9b)
Questions.Note: The Day of Atonement was observed in the early autumn.
Questions.Alternative: At what time did people who knew about the sea think it was no longer safe to travel on the sea?
At what time did people who knew about the sea say it was no longer safe to travel on the sea?

Questions.Q: What did Paul say to the other people on the ship about continuing to sail at that time?
Questions.A: Paul told the other people that it would be dangerous [to leave Fair Havens and continue their voyage]. (10a)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say he believed was going to happen if they sailed farther?
Questions.A: Paul said that if they traveled farther at that time, the cargo and also the ship would be damaged.
In addition, some of the passengers would lose their lives. (10b)

Questions.Q: Whom did the officer, Julius, believe when Paul said what would happen?
Questions.A: Julius did not believe that what Paul said would happen was really going to happen.
Instead, he listened to what the captain and the owner of the ship said. (11)

Questions.Q: To what harbor did most of the men on the ship think they should go?
Questions.A: Most of the men thought they should try to reach a harbor farther west which was called Phoenix. (12)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they wanted to leave Fair Havens and go to Phoenix?
Questions.A: They thought/said that the harbor at Fair Havens was not much sheltered from the wind.
And [they thought/said that] the harbor at Phoenix was more sheltered from the wind than the harbor at Fair Havens.
So they thought that Phoenix would be a good place for the ship to spend the winter months. (12a)

Section.heading: Acts 27:13-26 The ship in which Paul and the other prisoners traveled was battered by a severe storm.

Questions.Q: What happened before the ship had traveled very far?
Questions.A: A very strong wind blew down from the island.
It was a stormy wind that sailors called "the northeaster." (14)

Questions.Q: In what direction did the ship travel after "the northeaster" struck it?
Questions.A: "The northeaster" blew against the ship so violently that the ship could not continue sailing along the coast of Crete [towards Phoenix].
So they let the wind drive the ship in the direction that the wind was blowing. (15)

Questions.Q: What was the weather like when the ship sailed from Fair Havens?
Questions.A: A gentle wind from the south began to blow, so the captain and crew thought the weather was just right to sail.
They pulled up the anchor and steered the ship west along the southern coast of Crete. (13)

Questions.Q: What did the crew of the ship do when they passed on one side of the island Cauda?
Questions.A: When the ship passed on the south side of the island Cauda, it was protected from the wind for a little while.
The crew worked hard and succeeded in pulling the lifeboat up out of the sea.
Then they tied it to the deck of the [large] ship.
They also tied ropes around the hull of the ship, to hold it together. (16b-17a)

Questions.Q: For what reason was the crew afraid to let the wind continue to drive the ship in the direction that it was blowing?
Questions.A: The crew was afraid that the wind would drive the ship onto some sandbars of Syrtis.
If that happened, the ship would be stuck on those sandbars. (17b)

Questions.Q: What did the crew do to cause the ship to move a little slower/not quite so fast?
Questions.A: They put a piece of apparatus/equipment into the water that floated/dragged behind the ship, in order to make it move more slowly. (17c)
Questions.Alternative: What did the crew do to cause the ship to move a little slower?
What did the crew do to cause the ship to move not quite so fast?

Questions.Q: What did the crew do next, when they saw that the wind continued to blow very hard?
Questions.A: The crew threw the ship's cargo overboard, [in order to make the ship lighter].
On the next day, they also threw some pieces of the ship's equipment overboard. (18-19)

Questions.Q: What was the weather like as the storm continued?
Questions.A: The wind continued to blow very hard, and no one saw either the sun or the stars for many days. (20a)

Questions.Q: How did the people on board the ship think/feel at that time?
Questions.A: The people no longer believed that the ship would reach land anywhere.
They thought they would all drown. (20b)
Questions.Alternative: How did the people on board the ship think at that time?
How did the people on board the ship feel at that time?

Questions.Q: After the people on the ship had not eaten for many days, what did Paul tell them?
Questions.A: Paul reminded them of what he had told them before they left Crete.
He had advised the Roman officer and the captain of the ship to stay in Fair Havens.
He said that if they had stayed there, they would not have suffered what they had suffered.
The ship would not have been damaged, and the cargo and the equipment would not have been lost. (21)

Questions.Q: What did Paul tell the people in order to encourage them?
Questions.A: Paul told them that they should be hopeful, because nobody was going to lose his life.
However, he told them that the ship would be lost/destroyed. (22)

Questions.Q: What reason did Paul have for saying that to the other people?
Questions.A: Paul told them that God had sent an angel who had stood beside him during the night.
The angel had given Paul the message which he/Paul was now telling them. (23)

Questions.Q: What else did Paul tell the other passengers about God?
Questions.A: Paul said that God was the one to whom he belonged and the one whom he worshiped. (23)

Questions.Q: What else had the angel told Paul?
Questions.A: The angel had told Paul not to be afraid, because God had told him that he/Paul was going to [arrive in Rome] and stand trial before the Emperor.
The angel also told Paul that all of the other passengers would arrive there safely. (24)

Questions.Q: What did Paul tell the other passengers in order to encourage them?
Questions.A: Paul told the other passengers to be encouraged, because he was sure that everything was going to happen which the angel had told him [would happen].
Paul also told them that the ship would be driven onto the shore of some island. (25-26)

Section.heading: Acts 27:27-44 The ship was destroyed by the waves, but all the passengers reached land.

Questions.Q: What happened to the ship?
Questions.A: It was destroyed by the waves.

Questions.Q: What happened to all the passengers who were on the ship?
Questions.A: They all reached land safely.

Questions.Q: How long had the storm lasted, and where was the ship by that time?
Questions.A: The storm had lasted fourteen days, and the wind was driving the ship about on the Adriatic Sea. (27a)

Questions.Q: What happened about midnight of the fourteenth day of the storm?
Questions.A: About midnight of the fourteenth night, the sailors thought that the ship was approaching land. (27)

Questions.Q: What did the sailors do to find out whether they were getting near land?
Questions.A: The sailors let a weight on the end of a long cord down into the water.
After the ship had sailed a little farther, they let down the weight again.
Each time when they pulled the cord up out of the water, they measured how much of it had gone down into the water when it reached the floor of the ocean.
Each time that they measured the rope, they saw that the distance to the bottom of the ocean was less.
In that way, they learned that the ship was gradually moving closer to the land. (28)

Questions.Q: What else did the sailors do while they waited for the day to dawn?
Questions.A: They let down four anchors into the sea at the back end of the ship.
They did that because they were afraid that the wind would drive the ship onto the rocks. (29)

Questions.Q: What else did the sailors do while it was still dark?
Questions.A: The sailors took the lifeboat off the deck.
They let it down into the sea with the ropes that tied it to the ship.
They were planning to get into the lifeboat by themselves and head for the shore, leaving all the other passengers on the ship. (30)

Questions.Q: What did Paul do to stop the sailors from leaving?
Questions.A: Paul saw what the sailors were trying to do, so he told the Roman officer and the soldiers.
He told them that if the sailors did not stay on the ship, the other passengers would all drown. (31)

Questions.Q: What did the soldiers do when they heard what Paul said?
Questions.A: The soldiers cut the ropes that fastened the lifeboat to the ship, and the lifeboat fell into the water and drifted away. (32)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say to the other passengers as day was beginning to dawn?
Questions.A: As the day was beginning to dawn, Paul reminded the other passengers that they had eaten hardly anything for the past fourteen days.
He persuaded them all to eat and he assured them that they would all survive and would not suffer any personal harm. (33-34)

Questions.Q: What did Paul do?
Questions.A: Paul took some bread and thanked God for it where the other people saw him and heard him. Then he broke the bread and began to eat it. (35)

Questions.Q: What did the other passengers do?
Questions.A: The other passengers also ate some bread and felt encouraged. (36)

Questions.Q: How many people in all were on the ship?
Questions.A: There were 276 people on the ship. (37)

Questions.Q: What did all the people on the boat do next?
Questions.A: After they had all eaten as much as they wanted, they threw the wheat that remained in the ship into the sea.
They did that in order to make the ship lighter. (38)

Questions.Q: When the sailors saw a beach at the edge of the shore, not far ahead, what did they plan to do?
Questions.A: The sailors planned to try to sail the ship close to the shore.
They hoped that it would become grounded on the beach. (39)

Questions.Q: What did the sailors do next?
Questions.A: Next, they cut the ropes of the anchors that they had lowered at the back end of the ship and left the anchors in the sea.
Then they untied the ropes that held the rudders.
Then they raised a sail at the front of the ship, so that the wind would drive the ship to the shore. (40)

Questions.Q: What happened to the ship after that?
Questions.A: The ship did not move ahead to the shore.
Instead, the front end of the ship stuck on a sandbar and could not move any farther.
The back end was not stuck, but heavy waves beat against it and broke it to pieces. (41)

Questions.Q: What did the soldiers think they should do with the prisoners?
Questions.A: The soldiers thought they should execute all the prisoners to prevent them from reaching the shore and escaping. (42)
Questions.Note: The soldiers knew that if they did not deliver all the prisoners to Rome, they themselves would be executed.

Questions.Q: For what reason did the Roman officer not want the soldiers to kill the prisoners?
Questions.A: The Roman officer did not want Paul to be killed, so he did not allow the soldiers to kill/execute any of the prisoners. (43a)

Questions.Q: What did the Roman officer tell the prisoners to do?
Questions.A: He told the prisoners who could swim to jump overboard first and swim to shore.
He told the ones who could not swim that they should take hold of any plank or other piece of wood from the ship and hold onto it.
In that way, the people who could not swim would stay afloat and reach the shore. (43b-44)

Questions.Q: How many of the people on the ship reached the shore?
Questions.A: All of the 276 people who had been on the ship reached the shore safely. (44b)

Section.heading: Acts 28:1-10 The people of Malta were kind to the people from the wrecked ship. Paul healed many sick people of Malta with the power of God.

Questions.Q: How did the natives of Malta receive the people who arrived from the wrecked ship?
Questions.A: The people of Malta kindly received the people who arrived there from the ship.
They built a fire and invited the people from the ship to warm themselves. (1-2)

Questions.Q: What did Paul do that helped Publius?
Questions.A: The father of Publius was sick with dysentery and a fever.
Paul went into the room where the sick man was and prayed for him.
Then Paul laid his hands on him and healed him. (8)

Questions.Q: What happened after that?
Questions.A: After that happened all the other sick people on the island came to be healed by Paul.
Paul prayed for them all, and they were all healed. (9)

Questions.Q: What did Paul do that caused the people of Malta to wonder what kind of person he was?
Questions.A: Paul gathered a pile of brush. As he was putting it on the fire, a poisonous snake came out of the brush and fastened itself to Paul's hand.
The people thought that Paul was a murderer and that the snake had bitten Paul as a judgment from some god.
The people thought that even though Paul had not drowned, the god had punished him by causing a poisonous snake to bite him.
They were sure that he would soon swell up or suddenly fall down dead [because the snake was a poisonous one]. (3-6)

Questions.Q: What did the people of Malta think when they saw that Paul was not harmed by the snake?
Questions.A: After several hours had passed and Paul still had not been harmed by the poison/venom of the snake, the natives decided that Paul was a god. (6)

Questions.Q: Where did Paul and a few of the other people from the ship stay for three days?
Questions.A: The chief of the people on the island was named Publius.
He had a large property near the place where the people from the shipwreck had arrived.
He invited Paul, [Luke] and probably a few others to stay in his home for three days. (7)

Questions.Q: What did the people of Malta do to show their gratitude to Paul for having healed their sick relatives/friends?
Questions.A: The people of Malta brought Paul and his companions many gifts.
When it was time for Paul and the other people from the ship to leave, the natives brought them things that they would need on the voyage to Rome. (10)
Questions.Alternative: What did the people of Malta do to show their gratitude to Paul for having healed their sick relatives?
What did the people of Malta do to show their gratitude to Paul for having healed their sick friends?

Section.heading: Acts 28:11-16 Paul and the other travelers sailed from Malta and arrived in Rome.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what the author had written in these verses.
Questions.A: The author described the sea voyage that Paul took by ship from the island of Malta to Puteoli.
The author also described what had happened on the road between Puteoli and Rome.

Questions.Q: How long had Paul and the others stayed on the island of Malta?
Questions.A: They stayed on Malta for three months. (11a)

Questions.Q: Tell about the ship on which those travelers sailed from Malta to Italy.
Questions.A: Paul and the other travelers sailed on a ship that had come from Alexandria.
That ship had stayed through the winter in Malta. It was going to sail for Italy.
It was named for two gods who were twins, whose names were Castor and Pollux. (11b)

Questions.Q: What was the trip from Malta to Italy like?
Questions.A: The trip took only a few days. (12-14)

Questions.Q: At what places did the ship stop?
Questions.A: The first stop was at the city of Syracuse, and the next stop was at the city of Rhegium.
The last stop was at the town of Puteoli, which was not far from Rome. (12-14)

Questions.Q: What did Paul and [Luke] do in Puteoli?
Questions.A: They heard that there were believers/Christians there, and they went to see them.
The believers asked them to stay with them for a week. (14)
Questions.Alternative: What did Paul and Luke do in Puteoli?
What did Paul and do in Puteoli?

Questions.Q: What did the believers in Rome do when they heard that Paul had arrived in Puteoli and was on his way to Rome?
Questions.A: A group of the believers from Rome went to meet Paul on the road between Puteoli to Rome.
Some of them met Paul at a place called the Forum of Appius.
Others met him at a place called the Three Taverns.
[Then they all continued/went on to Rome together.] (15a-b)

Questions.Q: How did Paul feel when the believers from Rome welcomed him?
Questions.A: When Paul met the believers from Rome, he thanked God and felt encouraged. (15c)

Questions.Q: Where did Paul stay after he arrived in Rome?
Questions.A: After he arrived in Rome, Paul was given permission to live by himself in a house which he rented.
Because he was still a prisoner, a soldier guarded him all the time. (16, 30)

Section.heading: Acts 28:17-31 In Rome, Paul preached for two years to the Jews and to many other people.

Questions.Q: Whom did Paul want to speak to, soon after he arrived in Rome?
Questions.A: Three days after he had arrived, Paul sent word to the Jewish leaders, asking them to come and meet with him. (17a)

Questions.Q: For what reason did Paul want to talk to the local Jewish leaders?
Questions.A: Paul wanted to tell them the real reason why he had been arrested and sent to Rome as a prisoner. (17b)

Questions.Q: What blessings did Paul enjoy for two whole years as he lived in the house which he had rented?
Questions.A: Many people came to visit Paul and asked him to tell them what he believed.
Nobody threatened him or hindered him from preaching to them.
He explained the message [from the Scriptures] clearly and without fear.
So he welcomed all of his visitors and taught them what the Kingdom of God is and who the Lord Jesus Christ is. (30-31)

Questions.Q: How did Paul address the Jewish leaders?
Questions.A: Paul addressed them as "my brothers." (17a)
Questions.Note: Paul addressed them as "my brothers" because he wanted the Jewish leaders in Rome to know that he was a loyal Jew.

Questions.Q: What did he tell them first?
Questions.A: Paul told them that he had done nothing against the Jewish people, nor had he disobeyed their religious customs.
However, some Jews in Jerusalem had caused the Roman authorities to arrest him and make him a prisoner. (17b)
Questions.Alternative: What did Paul tell them first?
What was the first thing Paul told them?
What was the first thing Paul said?

Questions.Q: What else did Paul explain to the Jewish leaders?
Questions.A: Next, Paul explained that the Roman authorities had questioned him [and found that he had not broken any of the laws of the Emperor].
Therefore, the Roman authorities said that he did not deserve to be executed, and they wanted to let him go free. (18)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Paul appealed to the Emperor in Rome to judge his case?
Questions.A: Paul appealed to the Emperor to judge his case, because the Jews had told the Roman authorities that they should not set Paul free.
So Paul asked to be sent to the court of the Emperor. (19a)

Questions.Q: What else did Paul tell the Jewish leaders about why he had come to Rome?
Questions.A: Paul told the Jews that he had not come to accuse the Jews of his own country in the court of the Emperor. (19b)
Questions.Alternative: What else did Paul tell the Jewish leaders about his appeal to the Emperor?
What else did Paul tell the Jewish leaders about his intentions?

Questions.Q: After that, Paul told the Jews the real reason why he was a prisoner. What was it?
Questions.A: The real reason that Paul had been sent to Rome as a prisoner was because the Jews [in Jerusalem] hated him because of what he believed.
Paul believed that God had fulfilled his promise to send the Jewish people a Messiah.
That was what God had promised to the Jews many years before. (20)

Questions.Q: What did the Jewish leaders answer, after listening to what Paul explained to them?
Questions.A: The Jewish leaders told Paul that they had not heard anything bad about him.
The Jews in Jerusalem had not sent any letters in which they accused Paul.
Nor had any of the Jews who had come to Rome from Judea told them anything about Paul. (21)

Questions.Q: What else did the Jewish leaders say?
Questions.A: They said that they would like to hear what Paul believed.
They had heard many people say that the group/people to which Paul belonged were following a religion that was bad. (22)

Questions.Q: What did Paul arrange with them when he heard that?
Questions.A: He arranged with those Jews a day at which they would come to the place where he was staying, and he would tell them what he believed. (23a)

Questions.Q: What happened when that day arrived?
Questions.A: A large number of Jews came along with those leaders to hear what Paul had to say.
He spoke to them from morning until evening, explaining to them what the Kingdom of God is. (23b)

Questions.Q: What parts of the [Old Testament] Scriptures did Paul share with them as he told them what he believed?
Questions.A: Paul quoted to them from the Law of Moses and from the writings of the prophets.
Paul tried to convince them that those Scriptures say clearly that Jesus [was the Messiah whom God had long ago promised to send to his people]. (23c)
Questions.Alternative: What parts of the Old Testament Scriptures did Paul share with them as he told them what he believed?
What parts of the Scriptures did Paul share with them as he told them what he believed?

Questions.Q: How did those Jews respond when Paul tried to convince them that Jesus was the Messiah?
Questions.A: Some of them were convinced that what Paul told them was true.
Others refused to believe that what Paul told them was true.
So they argued with one another. (24-25a)

Questions.Q: When the Jews were about to leave, what did Paul say to them?
Questions.A: Paul quoted from the prophet Isaiah.
He told the Jews to whom he had spoken that what the Holy Spirit had said to their ancestors through Isaiah was true. (25b)

Questions.Q: What did the prophecy of Isaiah mean?
Questions.A: The prophecy which Paul quoted meant that the Jews of Isaiah's time could not see what God was doing nor hear what God was telling them.
It meant that although they kept hearing [with their ears] what God was saying and seeing [with their eyes] what God was doing, they did not understand what those things meant. (26)

Questions.Q: For what reason did the Jews not understand what God was saying to them?
Questions.A: They had already decided that they were not going to pay attention to what God was saying to them.
That was why they were unable to understand what God was doing [among them] and saying.
So they were unable to repent and turn to God for salvation. (27)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Paul reminded the Jewish leaders in Rome what Isaiah had said?
Questions.A: Paul quoted that prophecy because what Isaiah had said about the Jews of his day was also true of the Jews to whom Paul had preached that day about Jesus. (26-27)

Questions.Q: What else did Paul tell those Jews as they left?
Questions.A: Paul told them that they had refused to believe the message about the Savior whom God had sent. However, God was going to save the Gentiles.
Paul would tell them about Jesus, and he was sure they would listen and believe. (28)

Questions.Q: What happened after Paul had told the Jews what Isaiah had said about the Jews of his time?
Questions.A: The Jews to whom he had spoken left, still arguing violently among themselves. (29)

Section.heading: Colossians 1:1-2 Paul sent greetings from himself and from Timothy to the Christians at Colosse.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what Paul wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: Paul and Timothy sent greetings to the holy and faithful brothers in Christ, who were living in [the town of] Colosse. (1-2)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone/a person to be holy?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He is/They are good, as God desires. Someone who is "holy" is set apart [by God] and dedicated to the service or worship of God. Anything that is "holy" for God must reflect his character by being physically unblemished or reflecting, to some degree, his purity.
Questions.Note: See "holy" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think it means for someone to be holy?
What do you think it means for a person to be holy?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when a person is faithful?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that the person will do what he says he will do. A person is worthy of being believed by someone else. He is trustworthy, reliable. (See "faithful" in KBT in the "believe" entry.)

Questions.Q: What do you think Paul meant when he said "the brothers"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He meant those who were fellow-believers in Jesus. (See "brothers" in KBT in the "disciple" entry.)

Questions.Q: Who wrote this letter?
Questions.A: Paul wrote this letter. (1)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say he was?
Questions.A: He said he was an apostle of Christ Jesus. (1)

Questions.Q: What do you think an apostle of Christ Jesus is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: To be an apostle of Christ Jesus means to be a messenger/ambassador, who represents Christ Jesus, who proclaims the message about Christ Jesus.
Questions.Note: See "apostle" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Paul was an apostle?
Questions.A: He was an apostle because God wanted him to be one. (1)

Questions.Q: Who do you think God is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In English, the term "God," with a capital "G," is used to refer to the one supreme Creator. The term "god," with a lower case "g", as in "a god" or "many gods", can refer to any spiritual being that people worship. The Greek word "theos," can be used in the same two ways. In many languages the term for God is a proper name and cannot be used to refer to anyone except the one supreme creator of the world. It cannot be pluralized.
Questions.Note: See "God" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did Paul say about Timothy?
Questions.A: Paul said that Timothy was their [including the Colossians'] brother/fellow believer. (1)

Questions.Q: What do you think is the meaning of "Christ"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "Christ" in this verse is used as a name.
Questions.Note: See "Christ" in KBT.

Questions.Q: How do you think one man could be a brother to all those people? // Why does Paul call these people "brothers"?
Questions.A: Paul was not referring to a human relationship, but to a relationship between believers. They are all children of God.
Questions.Alternative: How do you think one man could be a brother to all those people?
Why does Paul call these people "brothers"?

Questions.Q: What did Paul want God to do for the Colossian believers?
Questions.A: He wanted God our Father to [continue to] give them grace and peace. (2)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to have/use grace in this verse?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that God would show favor towards those people.
Questions.Note: See "grace" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think it means to have grace in this verse?
What do you think it means to use grace in this verse?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to be at peace?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: To be at peace is to have a mental or spiritual condition marked by freedom of disquieting or oppressive thoughts or emotions in their relationship with one another and with God.

Section.heading: Colossians 1:3-12 Paul and Timothy thanked God for the Colossian Christians because they believed in Christ and because of their love for others who believed in Christ.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what Paul wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: Paul told the Colossian believers that he [and Timothy] thanked God for them every time they prayed for them. (3)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Paul [and Timothy] thanked God for the Colossian believers?
Questions.A: They thanked God for the Colossian believers because they believed in Christ Jesus.
They thanked God for the Colossian believers because they loved all of God's people. (3-4)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that Paul and Timothy thanked God for the Colossian believers?
What is the reason that Paul thanked God for the Colossian believers?

Questions.Q: What does a person do when he believes?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: When a person believes, he puts his trust and commitment in another person.
Questions.Note: See "believe" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when a person loves someone else?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The person, who loves another person, seeks the good of that person. His attitude to the one whom he loves is an attitude of persistent and selfless goodwill.
Questions.Note: See "love" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the Colossians believed in Christ Jesus and loved all of God's people?
Questions.A: The Colossians did that because of what they hoped/expected to receive from God in heaven. (5)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to hope in something?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means to have a desire/expectation to see something happen or to obtain something.

Questions.Q: Where do you think heaven is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It is that part of God's creation above the earth and the waters, including "air" and "space," and serves as home for God and the spirits who serve Him.
Questions.Note: See "heaven" in KBT.

Questions.Q: How had the believers heard about what God will do for them?
Questions.A: They had previously heard about what God will do for them [when people told them] the gospel [about Jesus Christ]. (5-6)

Questions.Q: What do you think the gospel is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The word "gospel" is a translation of the Greek noun euangelion. In the New Testament the noun euangelion is used in a restricted sense. It does not mean just any kind of good news, but specifically the good news, or joyful report, that God has made a way of salvation for sinful human beings. In the New Testament it is always used with this one sense and is usually translated in the RSV, and most modern English versions, as "gospel".
Questions.Note: See "gospel" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Who else has heard this/the gospel?
Questions.A: Many people in many places have heard this/the gospel. (6)
Questions.Alternative: Who else has heard this gospel?
Who else has heard the gospel?

Questions.Q: What happens when people believe this/the gospel?
Questions.A: When people believe this/the gospel, they start to live in a way that pleases God. (6)
Questions.Alternative: What happens when people believe this gospel?
What happens when people believe the gospel?

Questions.Q: Who taught this/the gospel to the people of Colosse?
Questions.A: Epaphras taught them this/the gospel. (7)
Questions.Alternative: Who taught this gospel to the people of Colosse?
Who taught the gospel to the people of Colosse?

Questions.Q: Who was Epaphras?
Questions.A: Epaphras served Christ along with Paul and Timothy.
He faithfully served Christ among the believers to help them. (7-8)
Questions.Note: Some Greek manuscripts say, "on our behalf" and some say, "on your behalf". See the comments in T.N. on Colossians for this verse.

Questions.Q: What do you think a servant does?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A servant is a person who is required to work for another person and obey him. Servants are usually paid for their work, while slaves are not paid.

Questions.Q: How did Paul know that the Colossian believers loved [God's people]?
Questions.A: Epaphras told him that the believers loved [God's people]. (8)
Questions.Alternative: How did Paul know that the Colossian believers loved God's people?
How did Paul know that the Colossian believers loved?

Questions.Q: How were the believers able to love [God's people]?
Questions.A: They were able to love [God's people] because the [Holy] Spirit was helping/causing them to do that. (8)
Questions.Alternative: How were the believers able to love God's people?
How were the believers able to love?

Questions.Q: Who do you think the Holy Spirit is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He is God's spirit, through whom he acts, reveals His will, and empowers individuals. (See "Holy Spirit" in KBT in the "spirit" entry.)

Questions.Q: When did Paul [and Timothy] start praying for the Colossian believers?
Questions.A: They started praying for the believers the day that they first heard the report about them. (9)
Questions.Alternative: When did Paul and Timothy start praying for the Colossian believers?
When did Paul start praying for the Colossian believers?

Questions.Q: What did they pray that God would do for the believers?
Questions.A: They prayed that God would enable them to fully understand what God wanted them to do.
They prayed that God would cause them to become very wise, and that God would enable them to understand spiritual things (what God does). (9)
Questions.Note: See comments on this verse in T.N. on Colossians.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Paul and [Timothy] prayed in that way for the believers in verse 9?
Questions.A: They prayed in that way so that the believers would behave in a way that pleases the Lord. (10)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that Paul and Timothy prayed in that way for the believers in verse 9?
What is the reason that Paul and prayed in that way for the believers in verse 9?

Questions.Q: What does it mean to you to have someone as your lord?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A lord is a person/someone who has authority over someone. To call someone your "Lord" means that you have given him control of/over your life. The Lord, in this case, is Jesus. Every Christian strives to make Jesus his lord by giving Him complete control. (See "Lord" in KBT in the "God" entry.)
Questions.Note: T.N. on Colossians states that the "Lord" in this verse is probably the Lord Jesus.

Questions.Q: In order to live in a way that pleases the Lord, what will the believers do?
Questions.A: They will do all kinds of good deeds.
They will learn/strive to know God better and better. (10)

Questions.Q: What else did Paul [and Timothy] pray that God would do for the believers?
Questions.A: They prayed that God would make the believers strong [in their spirits/in their hearts]. (11)
Questions.Alternative: What else did Paul and Timothy pray that God would do for the believers?
What else did Paul pray that God would do for the believers?

Questions.Q: How would God make the believers strong [in their spirits]?
Questions.A: God would make them strong by the power of his glorious might. (11)
Questions.Alternative: How would God make the believers strong in their spirits?
How would God make the believers strong?

Questions.Q: What do you think "glorious might" means?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "Glorious might" means his wonderful power that is so surpassingly strong/great.
Questions.Note: See "glorious" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the believers need to be strong [in their spirits]?
Questions.A: They need to be strong [in their spirits] so that they can endure with patience [any difficult problems or persecution] and be joyful. (11)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that the believers need to be strong in their spirits?
What is the reason that the believers need to be strong?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Paul said that the believers should thank [God] the Father?
Questions.A: He said that they should thank [God] the Father because they will share in all that he will give his people in heaven. (12)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that Paul said that the believers should thank God the Father?
What is the reason that Paul said that the believers should thank the Father?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that believers are able to share in all that [God] the Father will give to them?
Questions.A: [God] the Father has caused them to be worthy/made them fit/qualified them to share in all that he will give to them. (12)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that believers are able to share in all that God the Father will give to them?
What is the reason that believers are able to share in all that the Father will give to them?

Section.heading: Colossians 1:13-23 Paul wrote about the supreme position that Christ has over everything.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what Paul wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: Paul wrote about the supreme position that Christ has over everything.

Questions.Q: From what did God rescue the believers?
Questions.A: He rescued them from the power of darkness/power of Satan. (13)

Questions.Q: Who rules the believers now? // To whom do the believers now belong?
Questions.A: God has now caused his Son, Jesus, whom he loves, to rule the believers. // God has now caused the believers to become Christ's people. (13)
Questions.Alternative: Who rules the believers now?
To whom do the believers now belong?

Questions.Q: What did God's Son do?
Questions.A: He paid for people's sins [by dying for them]. That is how God freed the believers and forgave them for sinning against God. (13-14)

Questions.Q: What does a person do when he sins?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He does those things that displease God.
Questions.Note: See "sin" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think happens when a person forgives someone else?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Forgiveness always involves two people, one of whom has done something wrong to the other and offended him. Forgiveness takes place when the one, who was offended, sets aside his right to justice and decides not to punish the offender, as he deserved.
Questions.Note: See "forgive" in KBT.

Questions.Q: How did Paul compare Christ to God?
Questions.A: Paul said that Christ is exactly like God.
Paul said that Christ reveals God to people/causes people to understand what God is like. (15)

Questions.Q: What authority did Paul say that Christ has over everything that [God] has created?
Questions.A: Paul said that Christ has the greatest authority to rule over everything that [God] has created in the same way that a firstborn son has the greatest authority to rule of all the children in the family. (15)
Questions.Alternative: What authority did Paul say that Christ has over everything that God has created?
What authority did Paul say that Christ has over everything that he has created?
What authority did Paul say that Christ has over everything that has been created?
What authority did Paul say that Christ has over all creation?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Christ has the greatest authority to rule over everything?
Questions.A: Christ has the greatest authority to rule over everything because God caused him to create everything. (16)

Questions.Q: What are some of the things that Christ created?
Questions.A: He created everything that is in heaven and everything that is on the earth.
He created everything that we can see and everything that we cannot see.
He created the angels and other spiritual beings who have great power and authority. (16)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say about Christ in verse 17?
Questions.A: Paul said that Christ existed before anything else existed.
Paul said that Christ sustains/holds everything together. (17)

Questions.Q: What does Christ do for his church/those who follow him?
Questions.A: He rules over them and protects them.
He gives them [spiritual] life. // He causes them to live spiritually/eternally. (18)
Questions.Alternative: What does Christ do for his church?
What does Christ do for those who follow him?

Questions.Q: What do you think the church is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In this verse, it is the community of believers-in-Christ in general, i.e. the whole church of Christ, the universal church.
Questions.Note: See "church" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What else did Paul say about Christ in verse 18?
Questions.A: Paul said that Christ was the first one whom God raised from the dead [and caused to live forever so that he will never die again]. (18)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that God raised Christ from the dead?
Questions.A: [God planned it that way] in order that Christ alone should be the supreme ruler over all that exists. (18)

Questions.Q: What had God decided to do?
Questions.A: God decided that his Son/Christ would completely possess all of God's character/nature. (19)

Questions.Q: How did God reconcile everything to himself?
Questions.A: He reconciled everything to himself by sending his Son, Jesus, to die on the cross. (20)

Questions.Q: What do you think Jesus did when he reconciled everything to God?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: When Jesus reconciled everything to God he made everything come to be at peace with him, through the blood that he shed when he died on the cross.
Questions.Note: See "reconcile" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you know about the cross?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The cross was constructed of two pieces of wood. One piece was a thick wooden post, which was placed/planted upright into a hole in the ground. The other piece was the crossbeam, which was fastened across the upright post so that it formed a + or T shape.
Questions.Note: See "cross" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What had been the relationship between the Colossians and God in the past [before they believed in Christ]?
Questions.A: In the past the Colossians had been enemies of God. (21)
Questions.Alternative: What had been the relationship between the Colossians and God in the past before they believed in Christ?
What had been the relationship between the Colossians and God in the past?

Questions.Q: How did the Colossians behave toward God when they were his enemies?
Questions.A: They did not respect him in their thoughts.
They did evil deeds. (21)

Questions.Q: What did God do for the Colossians?
Questions.A: He reconciled them to himself. // He restored harmony between himself and them. (22)

Questions.Q: How did God reconcile them to himself?
Questions.A: He sent his Son, Jesus Christ, to die for them. (22)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that God reconciled the Colossians to himself?
Questions.A: He reconciled them to himself so that they will be holy/(good ones) and not guilty of sin, when they come into his presence. (22)

Questions.Q: What did Paul tell the Colossian believers to do?
Questions.A: He told them that they must continue to believe in Christ.
He told them that they must continue to believe the gospel.
He told them not to stop hoping for what God promised them in the gospel. (23)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say about this gospel?
Questions.A: Paul said that they had already heard this gospel.
Paul said that people have told others/other people this gospel in many places all over the world.
Paul said that he had become a person /one who worked to proclaim this gospel. (23)

Section.heading: Colossians 1:24-2:5 Paul said that God gave him the work of preaching the gospel to the Gentiles in Colosse.

Questions.Q: What work did God give Paul to do?
Questions.A: God gave Paul the work of teaching the word of God to the [Gentiles]. (25)

Questions.Q: About what was Paul happy?
Questions.A: Paul was happy to suffer for the [Gentiles] because he knew it was for their benefit. (24)

Questions.Q: How much did Paul say that he was willing to suffer?
Questions.A: He said that he was willing to suffer as much as Christ required him to suffer on his behalf. (24)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Paul was willing to suffer?
Questions.A: He was willing to suffer in order to help the church, Christ's people, who are like his body. (24)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Paul needed to teach/preach the word of God [to them/the Gentiles]?
Questions.A: He needed to teach the word of God to them because God's message/plan was not completely known in past times; but now God wants his people to know it. (26)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that Paul needed to teach the word of God to the Gentiles?
What is the reason that Paul needed to teach the word of God to them?
What is the reason that Paul needed to teach the word of God?
What is the reason that Paul needed to preach the word of God to the Gentiles?
What is the reason that Paul needed to preach the word of God to them?
What is the reason that Paul needed to preach the word of God?
Why did Paul need to teach the word of God to the Gentiles?
Why did Paul need to teach the word of God to them?
Why did Paul need to teach the word of God?
Why did Paul need to preach the word of God to the Gentiles?
Why did Paul need to preach the word of God to them?
Why did Paul need to preach the word of God?

Questions.Q: What did God decide to reveal to his people?
Questions.A: He decided to reveal to his people how truly wonderful his plan is and how it will benefit the Gentiles. (27)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say that God's plan is?
Questions.A: Paul said that God's plan is that Christ lives in the [Gentiles]. (27)

Questions.Q: Because Christ lives in them, what can the Gentiles expect from God?
Questions.A: They can expect that God will cause them to become perfect/wonderful as He is. // They can expect to share God's glory in the future. (27)
Questions.Note: See comments in T.N. on Colossians for this verse.

Questions.Q: Who do you think the Gentiles are?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In this verse, they are those people who are not Jews.
Questions.Note: See "Gentiles" in KBT.

Questions.Q: About whom did Paul and others teach people?
Questions.A: They taught people about Christ, and they advised the people to follow Christ. (28)

Questions.Q: How did they teach people about Christ?
Questions.A: They taught people with all the wisdom that they had. // They taught people as wisely as they could. (28)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Paul and others worked so hard to teach people about Christ?
Questions.A: They worked hard to teach people about Christ because they wanted them/people to become mature/strong believers in Christ. (28)

Questions.Q: How was Paul able to work so hard at teaching them about Christ?
Questions.A: Paul was able to work hard because Christ gave him the strength to do it. (29)

Questions.Q: In addition to the believers in Colosse, for whom did Paul say that he was greatly exerting himself?
Questions.A: He said that he was exerting himself for the believers living in [the town of] Laodicea.
He said that he was exerting himself for the believers who had not seen him personally. (1)

Questions.Q: What did Paul want for all of the believers?
Questions.A: He wanted them to believe strongly/earnestly/without doubting in Christ.
He wanted them to be united together because they loved each other.
He wanted them to enjoy the blessings/good things that result from their understanding God's message thoroughly/completely/well.
He wanted them to know completely about Christ. // He wanted them to know all there is to know about Christ. (2)

Questions.Q: What did Paul tell the believers about Christ?
Questions.A: Paul told them that only Christ can cause them to be wise and cause them to understand God's message thoroughly. (3)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Paul told the believers that Christ is the only one who can cause them to understand God's message?
Questions.A: He told them that, so that no one else could persuade them to believe their false teachings. (4)

Questions.Q: Even though Paul was not there with the believers, about what did he rejoice?
Questions.A: He rejoiced that they were united in what they believed.
He rejoiced that they believed firmly/resolutely/without doubting or wavering in Christ. (5)

Section.heading: Colossians 2:6-23 Paul told the Colossian Christians to live according to the new life they now had because they belonged to Christ; and he told them not to become entangled again in human rules and regulations.

Questions.Q: In order to live the way that they should, what did Paul instruct the believers to do?
Questions.A: Paul told them to continue believing more and more in Christ/trusting Christ more and more.
Paul told them to continue believing more and more what [people] had taught them about Christ.
Paul told them to continue thanking God very much/to continue to give thanks to God very much. (7)

Questions.Q: About what did Paul warn the believers?
Questions.A: He warned the believers not to let anyone/false teachers convince/force them to believe what they taught. (8)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that what those false teachers taught had no value?
Questions.A: They did not base their teaching(s)/what they taught on the truth.
The ideas they taught were merely ideas that they learned from other people.
They taught people to obey regulations/rules made up by people/that people have made up.
They did not teach the truth/true teachings about Christ. (8)

Questions.Q: Can you think of examples of deceptive ideas or empty traditions that go against the teaching of Christ?
What do you think is something spiritual?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Something spiritual is relating to or consisting of spirit. It is of the nature of spirit rather than material. // It is by nature spirit rather than material. Spiritual things cannot be seen with the human eye. (See "spiritual" in KBT in the "spirit" entry.)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say about the Colossian believers?
Questions.A: He said that they had already accepted Christ Jesus as their Lord. (6)

Questions.Q: Since they had accepted Christ as Lord, how should they now behave?
Questions.A: They should behave in a way that is fitting for those who are united with Christ. (6)
They should be firm in their faith, not doubting or easily convinced to believe something contrary to the teaching they had received. (7)
With thankfulness [to God] [for their salvation]. (7)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say about Christ in verse 9 and 10?
Questions.A: Paul said that God dwells completely in Christ's body. (9)
Paul said that Christ rules over every ruler and authority. (10)

Questions.Q: What has God done for the Colossian believers?
Questions.A: God has caused them to be spiritually complete/fully accepted by God by uniting them with Christ. (10)

Questions.Q: How did Paul compare circumcision with the union believers have with Christ?
Questions.A: Paul said that because believers are united to Christ, it is as though someone has circumcised [their hearts]/[their innermost desires]. (11)

Questions.Q: What did Christ remove from the believers when God united them with Christ?
Questions.A: Christ has removed them from the power of their evil nature when God united them with Christ. // Christ has given them the power not to be controlled by the desire to sin, when God united them with Christ. // Christ freed them from the power in their human nature that caused them to sin. (11)
Questions.Note: In circumcision a piece of skin is taken off. Paul compared circumcision with how Christ circumcised them spiritually. He cut away and removed the part of their nature that caused them to sin because they are united to him. See comments on this verse in T.N on Colossians.

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to circumcise someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that someone removes the foreskin of the male genital.
Questions.Note: In this verse, the word is being used in a symbolic sense.

Questions.Q: How did Paul compare baptism with being buried with Christ and being raised with Christ?
Questions.A: Paul said that when people baptized the believers, it was like people buried the believers together with Christ. It was also as though God had raised the believers to live again together with Christ. God raised the believers to live in a new way because they believed that God raised Christ from the dead. (12)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when someone is baptized?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "Baptism" is the outward sign by which a person's commitment to and union with Jesus Christ are publicly demonstrated.
Questions.Note: See "baptize" in KBT.

Questions.Q: How did Paul describe the condition of the Colossians before they became believers?
Questions.A: Paul said that they were dead [spiritually] because they sinned [and did not repent].
Paul said that they had no relationship to him/were dead [spiritually] because they were controlled by their evil/sinful nature. (13)

Questions.Q: What did God do for the believers?
Questions.A: God gave the believers a new relationship with Christ. // God made the believers alive spiritually with Christ. (13)

Questions.Q: What did God do for all believers?
Questions.A: God forgave all believers of all their sins. // He forgave all of their sins. (13)

Questions.Q: How did Paul illustrate what God did when he forgave all believers of all their sins?
Questions.A: Paul said that it was like God had written down all the sins they had done and had condemned them to die because they had disobeyed the law.
But then it was as though God destroyed/like God destroyed that record by nailing it to the cross [when Jesus died]. (14)

Questions.Q: What else did God do?
Questions.A: He defeated the evil spirits who have power and who rule other evil spirits [and over people in the world who listen to them]. (15)
Questions.Note: Depending on how the phrase "rulers and authorities" is translated, it might not be evident that Paul is talking about evil spirits? Additional questions might be needed to ensure the respondent understands this.

Questions.Q: How did God defeat those evil spirits?
Questions.A: He defeated them by means of Christ dying on the cross. (15)

Questions.Q: In defeating the evil spirits, what else did God do?
Questions.A: God caused everyone to know that he had defeated the evil spirits. (15)

Questions.Q: Who do you think are evil spirits?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The terms "evil spirit", "unclean spirit", and "demon" are used interchangeably in the New Testament. They all refer to spiritual beings who serve Satan as his agents, being under his authority. These spiritual beings have power to oppress a human being and even take control of him.
Questions.Note: See "evil spirit" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did Paul tell the Colossian believers to do?
Questions.A: He told them not to pay any attention to people/false teachers who judged them because they did not obey their rules about what they could eat and drink or did not celebrate religious festivals, a new moon celebration, or a Sabbath day. (16)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to judge someone in this verse?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In this verse it means to criticize someone/to find fault with someone.
Questions.Note: See "judge" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think the Sabbath means?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The Sabbath is the name of the seventh and last day of the week. The Sabbath was set aside by God in the law he gave to Moses as a strict day of rest from the normal work that was done on the other six days of the week. The Jews continue to observe the Sabbath on Saturday.
Questions.Note: See "Sabbath" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did Paul say about the customs he mentioned in verse 16?
Questions.A: Paul said that those customs were nothing more than symbols of the good things [that God said he would do] in the future. (17)

Questions.Q: Of whom did Paul say that those customs were symbols?
Questions.A: Paul said that Christ is the one of whom all those customs were symbols. // He said that all those customs were symbols of Christ. (17)

Questions.Q: What did Paul tell the Colossian believers that they should do?
Questions.A: He told them not to follow people who teach false teachings.
He told them not to follow people who say that we must humble ourselves and worship angels [in order for God to accept us]. (18)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to worship angels?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means to give them respect and devotion.

Questions.Q: What do you know about angels?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Angels are God's messengers, who deliver a message to humans, carry out God's will, praise God, or guard God's throne.
Questions.Note: See "angel" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What were the reasons that Paul said/For what reasons did Paul say that the believers should not pay attention to a false teacher?
Questions.A: Paul said that, if they listened to a false teacher, they would lose the prize/would not get the blessings [that God wanted to give to them].
Paul said that a false teacher bases his teaching on visions which he [falsely] claims to have seen.
Paul said that a false teacher is proud. (18)
Paul said that a false teacher does not teach the truth about/true teachings about Christ. (19)
Questions.Alternative: What were the reasons that Paul said that the believers should not pay attention to a false teacher?
For what reasons did Paul say that the believers should not pay attention to a false teacher?

Questions.Q: What does Christ do for the body/the church/the believers?
Questions.A: Christ rules over them and protects them [in the same way that the head directs the physical body].
Christ gives them [spiritual] life. // Christ causes them to live spiritually/eternally.
Christ nourishes/cares for the spiritual body, the believers.
Christ gives his people strength and unites them in the same way that ligaments and sinews support and hold a physical body together. (19)
Questions.Alternative: What does Christ do for the body?
What does Christ do for the church?
What does Christ do for the believers?

Questions.Q: How are the believers able to do as God desires?
Questions.A: The believers are able to do as God desires by the power of God/by His, God's, power. (19)

Questions.Q: Of what did Paul remind the believers?
Questions.A: Paul reminded the believers that it was as though they had died together with Christ [and had been united with him]. Therefore, [God] freed them from having to obey religious rules/laws made by men. (20)

Questions.Q: If the believers continued to obey those religious rules/laws, taught by the false teachers, what were they actually doing?
Questions.A: They were behaving as though they were still controlled by those religious rules/laws. (20)
Questions.Alternative: If the believers continued to obey those religious rules, taught by the false teachers, what were they actually doing?
If the believers continued to obey those religious laws, taught by the false teachers, what were they actually doing?
