Questions.Q: What is the reason that many people think that following those rules/laws is wise?
Questions.A: People, who follow those rules, willingly do difficult deeds to show that they are devoted to God.
People, who follow those rules, think that they are humble.
People, who follow those rules, treat their bodies harshly. (23)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that many people think that following those rules is wise?
What is the reason that many people think that following those laws is wise?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that there is no real value in people carefully obeying/for people to carefully obey such rules?
Questions.A: Those rules do not help them to control their evil desires. (23)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that there is no real value in people carefully obeying such rules?
What is the reason that there is no real value for people to carefully obey such rules?

Section.heading: Colossians 3:1-17 Paul told the Colossian Christians to stop living the way that they did, before they came to know Christ, and to start living the new life that they had found from knowing Christ.

Questions.Q: About what did Paul tell the believers to think?
Questions.A: He told them to think about what is in heaven. // He told them to think about the concerns of their/what concerned [their new life, which is united to Christ] in heaven. (2)

Questions.Q: About what did Paul tell the believers not to think?
Questions.A: He told them not to think about doing the evil deeds practiced by people who do not know God. (2)

Questions.Q: What did God do for the believers [when they believed in Christ]?
Questions.A: It is as though God raised the believers from death, when he raised Christ from death. // God caused them to have a new way to live, because he raised Christ from the dead. (1)
God caused them to live spiritually. (1)
Questions.Alternative: What did God do for the believers when they believed in Christ?
What did God do for the believers?

Questions.Q: Where is Christ now?
Questions.A: Christ is sitting on the right hand/side of God, which is the place of highest honor in heaven. (1)

Questions.Q: Since God raised the believers from death, what should they always be wanting/desiring?
Questions.A: The believers should always be wanting/desiring what is in heaven. (1)
Questions.Alternative: Since God raised the believers from death, what should they always be wanting?
Since God raised the believers from death, what should they always be desiring?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Paul told the believers to think about what is in heaven?
Questions.A: They should think about what is in heaven because it is as though they have died to the old way of life on earth/because they don't have to live evil lives as they formerly did. (3)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say about the new life that the believers have now?
Questions.A: Paul said that the believers now have new/spiritual life, in the same way that Christ, who is with God [in heaven], has new life. [At this time], this new life that they have is not visible to anybody. // Paul said that the believers now live united with Christ, and Christ lives where God is. [Right now] people do not see/know [yet] that they live their lives together with Christ. (3)
Questions.Note: See comments on this verse in T.N. on Colossians.

Questions.Q: What did Paul say about Christ in verse 4?
Questions.A: Paul said that Christ causes believers to live [with him in this new, spiritual way]. (4)

Questions.Q: When Christ appears [to the people of the earth], what will happen to the believers?
Questions.A: The believers will appear with Christ when he appears [to the people of the earth], and the believers also will be glorious [in the same way that he will be glorious]. (4)
Questions.Alternative: When Christ appears to the people of the earth, what will happen to the believers?
When Christ appears, what will happen to the believers?

Questions.Q: What did Paul tell the believers to stop doing?
Questions.A: He told the believers to stop doing the evil deeds that were a part of their old, sinful way of life. (5)

Questions.Q: What deeds did Paul tell the believers to stop doing?
Questions.A: Paul told them not to commit sexual immorality/any kind of unlawful sexual intercourse.
They should not do impure deeds/do indecent deeds or shameful deeds.
They should not lust/have strong sexual desires.
They should not do other kinds of evil deeds.
They should not be greedy to get more and more things, because that is like idolatry. (5)

Questions.Q: How do you think a person who is greedy to obtain/procure things is practicing idolatry?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: When people are greedy to obtain/procure/gain things, it is as though they are worshiping/like worshiping something other than God.
Questions.Alternative: How do you think a person who is greedy to obtain things is practicing idolatry?
How do you think a person who is greedy to procure things is practicing idolatry?
How do you think a person who is greedy is practicing idolatry?
How do you think a person who is covetous is practicing idolatry?

Questions.Q: What will God do to those who continue to do such evil deeds?
Questions.A: God will punish anyone for doing such deeds. (6)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say about how the Colossian believers behaved before they trusted in Christ?
Questions.A: Paul said that they had done all those evil deeds before they trusted in Christ. (7)

Questions.Q: What did Paul tell the believers to stop doing?
Questions.A: He told them not to be angry.
He told them not to act in malice toward others/act in wicked, hateful ways to others.
He told them not to say mean, hateful, unkind things about people.
He told them not to use profanity, obscene talk, cursing, saying unkind, hurtful things to people using rude, impolite words. (8)
He told them not to lie to each other. (9)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Paul told the believers not to do the evil deeds he mentioned anymore?
Questions.A: Paul told the believers not to do evil deeds anymore because they should no longer live the way they used to live before they trusted in Christ.
Paul told the believers, now that they trust in Christ, they should think and act in a new way. (9-10)

Questions.Q: Who caused the believers to have this new life/nature/character?
Questions.A: God caused the believers to have this new life. (10)
Questions.Alternative: Who caused the believers to have this new life?
Who caused the believers to have this new nature?
Who caused the believers to have this new character?

Questions.Q: What is God causing to happen in the believers?
Questions.A: God is causing them to become more and more like himself. (10)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that God is causing the believers to become more like him?
Questions.A: God is causing the believers to become more and more like him so that they will be able to know God completely. (10)

Questions.Q: Since God has caused the believers to have a new life, what did Paul say was not important?
Questions.A: He said that it was not important whether/if a person was a Greek or a Jew, circumcised or uncircumcised, a barbarian, a Scythian, a slave or a free person. (11)

Questions.Q: What do you know about Jews?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The term "Jews"/It refers to the descendants of Abraham through his son Isaac. A Jew is a member of the people of Israel. He is committed to the Jewish religious system. All male Jews were circumcised on the 8th day after their birth, and that was a mark of being a Jew. (See "Jew" in KBT in the "Israel" entry.)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to be a slave of someone/something?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that the person, who is a slave, is totally responsible to and dependent upon another person, or that the person has become completely subservient to a dominating influence.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think it means for someone to be a slave of someone?
What do you think it means for someone to be a slave of something?

Questions.Q: Who did Paul say is really important?
Questions.A: Paul said that it is Christ who is supremely important. (11)

Questions.Q: In whom did Paul say that Christ lives?
Questions.A: Paul said that Christ lives in all those who trust in him. (11)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Paul told the Colossian believers that they should behave well toward one another?
Questions.A: Paul told the believers to behave well toward one another, because God has chosen them.
They have been reserved for God himself.
God loves them. (12)

Questions.Q: How did Paul tell the believers to behave toward one another?
Questions.A: He told them that they should be compassionate to one-another/have feelings of sympathy toward someone that needs help, show concern for those who need help.
They should be kind to one another/act in helpful, loving ways toward people, behave helpfully toward people, and be "goodhearted".
They should be humble with one another/not be proud and arrogant, not act as though they/you are better than other people.
They should be gentle with one another/willing to give in, not demand their own way, and be considerate of the rights and feelings of other people.
They should be patient with one another/calmly endure unfair or unkind treatment by others, not become angry quickly when other people do something unpleasant. (12)
They should calmly endure the things which other people do regularly, each day, that annoy them.
They should forgive anyone who has done something wrong against them in the same way that the Lord has forgiven them. (13)
They should love one another. (14)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Paul told the believers that it was more important for them to love one another than to do the other things that he had mentioned?
Questions.A: He said that it was more important for the believers to love one another because it will perfectly unite them together. (14)

Questions.Q: How did Paul say the Colossian believers should live?
Questions.A: He said that Christ has caused the believers to be at peace with one another, so they should continue to live in peace with one another. (15)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Paul said the believers should live in peace with one another?
Questions.A: He said that the believers should live in peace, because they were called/chosen by God to live in peace. (15)

Questions.Q: What else did Paul tell the believers to do?
Questions.A: Paul told the believers that they should always be thanking God. (15)

Questions.Q: What did Paul tell the believers that they should be learning?
Questions.A: He told the believers that they should be learning the message about Christ more and more/thoroughly. (16)

Questions.Q: How did Paul tell the believers that they should learn the message about Christ more/thoroughly?
Questions.A: Paul told them that they should do that/this by teaching one another the message about Christ and counseling/warning one another very wisely. (16)
Paul also told them that they should do that/this by singing psalms, hymns of praise to God, and spiritual songs. They should thank God as they sang/were singing. (16)
Questions.Alternative: How did Paul tell the believers that they should learn the message about Christ more?
How did Paul tell the believers that they should learn the message about Christ thoroughly?

Questions.Q: How did Paul tell the believers to behave in everything they did and said?
Questions.A: Paul told the believers that everything they did and said should be done in a way that is fitting to those who follow the Lord Jesus. (17)

Questions.Q: What else did Paul say the believers should do?
Questions.A: Paul said that they should always thank God the Father. (17)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Paul told the believers to thank God the Father?
Questions.A: Paul told the believers to thank God the Father because of all that Christ has done for them. (17)

Questions.Q: What do you think "God the Father" means?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that God is the father of Jesus Christ and of anyone who accepts Jesus as his or her Savior and Lord.
Questions.Note: See "God the Father" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think the title "God the Father" means?
What do you think the term "God the Father" means?

Section.heading: Colossians 3:18-4:1 Wives, submit to your husbands; husbands, love your wives; children, obey your parents; and slaves, obey your masters.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what Paul wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: Paul stated how husbands and wives should treat each other. He also stated how [Christian] masters and their slaves should treat each other.

Questions.Q: What did Paul say that wives should do?
Questions.A: Paul said that wives should submit to their husbands. (18)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that wives should submit to their husbands?
Questions.A: They should submit to their husbands, because that is what is proper for followers of the Lord to do. (18)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say that husbands should do?
Questions.A: Paul said that husbands should love their wives.
Paul said that husbands should not be harsh with their wives. (19)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say that children should do?
Questions.A: Paul said that children should always obey their parents. (20)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that children should obey their parents?
Questions.A: They should obey their parents because the Lord is pleased when they do that. (20)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say that parents/fathers should not do?
Questions.A: Paul said that parents/fathers should not cause their children to become bitter/resentful. (21)
Questions.Alternative: What did Paul say that parents should not do?
What did Paul say that fathers should not do?

Questions.Q: What did Paul say will happen, if they cause their children to become bitter/resentful?
Questions.A: Paul said that their children will become discouraged. (21)
Questions.Alternative: What did Paul say will happen, if they cause their children to become bitter?
What did Paul say will happen, if they cause their children to become resentful?

Questions.Q: What did Paul say that [Christian] slaves should do?
Questions.A: Paul said that slaves should always obey their masters. They are to obey them not only/just when their masters are watching them or so that they will like them or praise them.
Paul said that slaves should work honestly and sincerely because that will/they honor the Lord. (22)
Questions.Alternative: What did Paul say that Christian slaves should do?
What did Paul say that slaves should do?

Questions.Q: How or in what manner should slaves do their/that work?
Questions.A: They should do that/their work with all their strength.
They should do that/their work in a willing/happy way.
They should work as though they were working for the Lord. They should not work as though they were working only for people. (23)
Questions.Alternative: How or in what manner should slaves do their work?
How or in what manner should slaves do that work?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that slaves should work in the way Paul stated in verse 23?
Questions.A: Slaves should work in that way because they were serving the Lord Christ, and he will reward/repay them properly. (24)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say will happen to those who do evil deeds?
Questions.A: Paul said that God will punish them all alike/without partiality according to what they do. (25)

Questions.Q: How did Paul say that [Christian] masters should treat their slaves?
Questions.A: Paul said that [Christian] masters should treat their slaves in a just and fair way. (1)
Questions.Alternative: How did Paul say that Christian masters should treat their slaves?
How did Paul say that masters should treat their slaves?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that masters should treat their slaves in a just and fair way?
Questions.A: Masters should treat their slaves in a just and fair way because they know that they also serve a master in heaven. (1)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for a person/someone to treat someone else in a just way?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: When someone treats another person/someone else in a just way, they are doing what is right in the sight of God, consistent with God's laws, being upright.
Questions.Note: See "just" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think it means for a person to treat someone else in a just way?
What do you think it means for someone to treat someone else in a just way?

Section.heading: Colossians 4:2-6 Paul told/asked the Christians to pray to God and to pray for him.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what Paul wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: Paul told the Colossian believers that they should pray to God persistently. (2)
Paul told the believers how they should act toward non-believers. (5-6)

Questions.Q: What did Paul teach the believers about prayer in verse 2?
Questions.A: Paul told the believers that they should pray to God persistently.
Paul told the believers that, when they are praying, they should remain alert and that they should thank God. (2)

Questions.Q: For whom did Paul ask the believers to pray?
Questions.A: Paul asked the believers to pray for him and for his companions. (3)

Questions.Q: In praying for Paul and his companions, about what specifically did Paul want the believers to pray?
Questions.A: Paul wanted the believers to pray that God will/would give him and his companions opportunities to tell people this message about Christ, which people did not understand/know before. (3)
Paul wanted the believers to pray that he would be able to proclaim the/this message about Christ clearly. (4)

Questions.Q: At an earlier time when Paul was telling people the message about Christ, what happened to him?
Questions.A: He was put in prison. (3)

Questions.Q: Where was Paul when he wrote/was writing this letter?
Questions.A: He was in prison. (3)
Questions.Alternative: Where was Paul when he wrote this letter?
Where was Paul when he was writing this letter?

Questions.Q: How did Paul say that the believers should act toward those who are not believers?
Questions.A: Paul said that the believers should act wisely toward those who are not believers. (5)
Paul said that the believers should make good use of the opportunities [they have to help those who are not believers to become believers]. (5)

Questions.Q: How did Paul say that the believers should talk to those who are not believers?
Questions.A: Paul said that the believers should always speak to non-believers in a kind/polite way. (6)

Questions.Q: What should the believers say to the non-believers?
Questions.A: Believers should say things that are pleasant/kind. (6)

Questions.Q: If the believers continually act that way/kindly toward non-believers whom/that Paul mentioned, what will be the result?
Questions.A: Believers will learn the manner in which they are to respond to non-believers when they ask about the believer's faith in Jesus. (6)
Questions.Alternative: If the believers continually act that way toward non-believers whom Paul mentioned, what will be the result?
If the believers continually act that way toward non-believers that Paul mentioned, what will be the result?
If the believers continually act that kindly toward non-believers whom Paul mentioned, what will be the result?
If the believers continually act that kindly toward non-believers that Paul mentioned, what will be the result?

Section.heading: Colossians 4:7-18 Paul sent his final greetings to the Colossian believers.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what Paul wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: Paul sent Tychicus and Onesimus to the Colossians. (7-9)
Paul also sent greetings to the Colossians from several people/friends. (10-12, 14)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say about Tychicus?
Questions.A: Paul said that he was a brother/fellow-believer whom he loved very much.
Paul said that he was a faithful helper/worker.
Paul said that he was a fellow servant in the Lord. (7)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Paul sent Tychicus to the Colossians?
Questions.A: Paul sent Tychicus to the Colossians so that the Colossians would know what had been happening to Paul and his companions.
Paul sent Tychicus to the Colossians so that he might encourage them. (8)

Questions.Q: Who accompanied/went with Tychicus?
Questions.A: Onesimus went with him. (9)
Questions.Alternative: Who accompanied Tychicus?
Who went with Tychicus?

Questions.Q: What did Paul say about Onesimus?
Questions.A: Paul said that Onesimus was his faithful brother/fellow-believer whom he loved.
Paul said that Onesimus was one of the Colossians/one of them/a fellow townsman. (9)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say that Tychicus and Onesimus would tell the Colossians?
Questions.A: Paul said that they would tell the Colossians everything that was happening to Paul and his companions. (9)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say about Aristarchus?
Questions.A: Paul said that Aristarchus was in prison with him. (10)

Questions.Q: Who was Mark?
Questions.A: Mark was the cousin of Barnabas. (10)

Questions.Q: What did Paul tell the Colossians to do, if Mark came to Colosse?
Questions.A: Paul told them to welcome Mark. (10)

Questions.Q: Who, besides/except for Paul, sent greetings to the Colossian believers?
Questions.A: Aristarchus and Mark sent greetings. (10)
Jesus sent greetings. (11)
Epaphras sent greetings. (12)
Luke and Demas sent greetings. (14)
Questions.Alternative: Who, besides Paul, sent greetings to the Colossian believers?
Who, except for Paul, sent greetings to the Colossian believers?

Questions.Q: One of Paul's companions was called Jesus. What other name was Jesus called?
Questions.A: Jesus was also called Justus. (11)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say about Aristarchus, Mark, and Jesus?
Questions.A: Paul said that those three men were the only Jewish believers who were working with him to teach people to become members of God's Kingdom.
Paul said that they were a great comfort/had been a great help to him. (11)

Questions.Q: What do you think the kingdom of God is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The kingdom of God, rather than being a territory over which God rules, is the presence of God ruling in the lives of men.
Questions.Note: See "kingdom of God" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did Paul say about Epaphras?
Questions.A: Paul said that Epaphras was one of the Colossians/one of them/a fellow townsman.
Paul said that Epaphras was one who worked for Christ Jesus.
Paul said that Epaphras always prayed earnestly for the Colossians. (12)

Questions.Q: What did Epaphras pray for the Colossian believers?
Questions.A: He prayed that they will/would continue to be spiritually strong/mature.
He prayed that they will/would be very sure about all that God wants/wanted them to do. (12)

Questions.Q: What else did Paul say about Epaphras?
Questions.A: Paul said that Epaphras worked hard for those believers living in [the towns of] Colosse, Laodicea, and Hierapolis. (13)

Questions.Q: Who was Luke?
Questions.A: Luke was a doctor whom Paul and his companions loved very much. (14)

Questions.Q: To whom did Paul send his greetings in verse 15?
Questions.A: He sent his greetings to the believers who lived in [the town of] Laodicea. (15)
He also sent his greetings to a lady called Nympha and to the church/believers that/who met in her house. (15)

Questions.Q: What did Paul tell the Colossians to do with this letter?
Questions.A: Paul told the Colossians that someone should read this letter publicly to them.
Paul told the Colossians that, after they had heard this letter, they should read it/this letter publicly to the church/believers in Laodicea. (16)

Questions.Q: What did Paul tell the Colossians to do with the letter he had written to the church/believers in Laodicea?
Questions.A: Paul told the Colossians that someone should read that letter publicly to them. (16)
Questions.Alternative: What did Paul tell the Colossians to do with the letter he had written to the church in Laodicea?
What did Paul tell the Colossians to do with the letter he had written to the believers in Laodicea?

Questions.Q: To whom else did Paul send a message?
Questions.A: Paul sent a message to Archippus. (17)

Questions.Q: What did Paul tell Archippus in his message?
Questions.A: Paul told Archippus that he should finish the work that the Lord gave him to do. (17)

Questions.Q: This greeting was written by Paul himself. What do you think is the reason that he did that?
Questions.A: Paul wrote this greeting so that the Colossians would know that the letter truly came from him. (18)
Questions.Note: See comments in T.N. on Colossians.

Questions.Q: How do you think the rest of the letter was written?
Questions.A: Paul dictated it to someone else to write down.

Questions.Q: What did Paul ask the Colossian believers to remember?
Questions.A: He asked them to remember to pray for him there in prison. (18)

Questions.Q: What did Paul want God to do for the Colossian believers?
Questions.A: Paul wanted God to bless them/show favor toward them. (18)

Section.heading: Ephesians 1:1-2 Paul greeted the saints in Ephesus.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what Paul wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: Paul sent greetings to the saints in Ephesus [a city]. (1)

Questions.Q: What do you think a saint is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A saint is someone who belongs to God/a believer in Jesus. (See "saint" in KBT in the "disciple" entry.)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say he was?
Questions.A: He said he was an apostle of Christ Jesus. (1)

Questions.Q: What do you think an apostle of Christ Jesus is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: To be an apostle of Christ Jesus means to be a messenger/ambassador, who represents Christ Jesus, who proclaims the message about Christ Jesus.
Questions.Note: See "apostle" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the meaning of "Christ"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "Christ" in this verse is used as a name.
Questions.Note: See "Christ" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Paul was an apostle?
Questions.A: He was an apostle because God wanted him to be one. (1)

Questions.Q: Who do you think God is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In English, the term "God," with a capital "G," is used to refer to the one supreme Creator. The term "god," with a lower case "g", as in "a god" or "many gods", can refer to any spiritual being that people worship. The Greek word theos can be used in the same two ways. In many languages the term for God is a proper name and can not be used to refer to anyone except the one supreme creator of the world. It can not be pluralized.
Questions.Note: See "God" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did Paul say about the saints he wrote to in Ephesus?
Questions.A: He said that they were believers in Christ Jesus. (1)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when someone is faithful?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In this verse "faithful" means primarily someone who is "full of faith." That is, a "believer" who is convinced that Jesus has been raised from the dead and that he is the Messiah and Savior. More than a mere intellectual position, a faithful person has trusted in Christ for salvation. (See "faithful" in KBT in the "believe" entry.)
Questions.Note: "Faithful" can also mean that someone will do what he says he will do. A person is worthy of being believed by someone else. They are trustworthy, reliable.

Questions.Q: What did Paul want God and Christ to do for the Ephesian believers?
Questions.A: He wanted both, God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ, to give them grace and peace. (2)

Questions.Q: What does it mean to you to have someone as your lord?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A lord is someone who has authority over someone. To call someone your "Lord" means that you have given him control over your life. The Lord, in this case, is Jesus. Every Christian strives to make Jesus his lord by giving Him complete control. (See "Lord" in KBT in the "God" entry.)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to have/use grace in this verse?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that God would show favor towards those people.
Questions.Note: See "grace" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think it means to have grace in this verse?
What do you think it means to use grace in this verse?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to be at peace?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: To be at peace is to have a mental or spiritual condition marked by freedom of disquieting or oppressive thoughts or emotions.

Section.heading: Ephesians 1:3-14 God has blessed Christians with every spiritual gift in the heavenly realms because of what Christ has done.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what Paul wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: Paul exhorts his readers to thank God for all the blessings/good that they have received from him.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Paul praised/gave thanks to God?
Questions.A: He praised God because God has blessed us with all the blessings which come from heaven. (3)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that Paul praised God?
What is the reason that Paul gave thanks to God?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for God to bless people?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that God has done something good for them.
Questions.Note: See "bless, blessed, blessing" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think are the "heavenly realms"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The meaning of "heavenly realms" seems to be "the supernatural world", that is, the world where spiritual forces operate, as opposed to the earthly world where physical forces operate. (See "heavenly places" in KBT in the "heaven" entry.)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that God has blessed us in this way?
Questions.A: He has blessed us in this way because [he has] united us with Christ/because we are united with Christ. (3)

Questions.Q: What did God do before he made the world?
Questions.A: He chose us to be his own people. (4)

Questions.Q: How did we become his people?
Questions.A: He chose us to be his people by uniting us to Christ. (4)

Questions.Q: As believers in Christ, what kind of people did God plan for us to become?
Questions.A: He planned that we should become holy and without fault. (4)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to be holy?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means to be pure, clean, without any sin.
Questions.Note: See "holy" in KBT.

Questions.Q: How did God show that he loved us?
Questions.A: He planned [that by believing] in Jesus Christ we would become his sons/children. (5)

Questions.Q: What do you think "love" means in this verse?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In this verse, love means the affection that God has for us.
Questions.Note: See "love" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think "love" means here?

Questions.Q: What should we do because God has shown his great love for us in this way?
Questions.A: We should praise him. (6)

Questions.Q: What did God charge us for his gift of love/kindness?
Questions.A: He did not charge us anything, he gave it to us freely. (6)
Questions.Alternative: What did God charge us for his gift of love?
What did God charge us for his gift of kindness?

Questions.Q: What good thing did God do for us?
Questions.A: He forgave our sins. (7)

Questions.Q: What do you think happens when someone forgives someone else?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Forgiveness always involves two people, one of whom has done something wrong to the other and offended him. Forgiveness takes place when the one, who was offended, sets aside his right to justice and decides not to punish the offender as he deserved.
Questions.Note: See "forgive" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What does a person do when he sins?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He does those things that displease God.
Questions.Note: See "sin" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that God forgave our sins?
Questions.A: He forgave our sins because Christ died/shed his blood for our sins. (7)

Questions.Q: In what way did God forgive us?
Questions.A: He freely forgave us. (8)

Questions.Q: To whom do the words "all wisdom and understanding" refer: to God's qualities or to man's?
Questions.Note: This answer will depend on the exegetical choice you have made i.e., (1) man, or (2) God. See Exegetical Helps on Ephesians, page 30. According to T.N. on Ephesians: the qualities of "wisdom and understanding" refer to God.

Questions.Q: What did God reveal/make known to us?
Questions.A: He made known to us his secret plan. (8-9)
Questions.Alternative: What did God reveal to us?
What did God make known to us?

Questions.Q: What was God's plan?
Questions.A: He planned to have Christ rule everything in heaven and on earth. (10)

Questions.Q: What do you think he meant when he said "heaven and earth"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "Heaven and earth" in this verse mean the "whole universe".
Questions.Note: See "heaven" in KBT.

Questions.Q: When will God complete this plan?
Questions.A: He will complete this plan when the right time comes. (10)

Questions.Q: How did we become God's sons/children?
Questions.A: We became his sons/children when he united us with Christ. (11)
Questions.Note: According to T.N. on Ephesians, the "we" in this verse could be either: only the Jewish believers or it could be all believers.
Questions.Alternative: How did we become God's sons?
How did we become God's children?

Questions.Q: When did God choose us?
Questions.A: He chose us from the very beginning/long ago. (11)
Questions.Note: See comments on this verse in the T.H. on Ephesians and in T.N. on Ephesians.

Questions.Q: What was God's purpose for choosing us as sons?
Questions.A: He did that so that the Jews, who were the first to hope in Christ, would cause other people to praise him because he is wonderful. (12)
Questions.Note: According to T.N. on Ephesians, the "we who were the first to hope in Christ" is referring to the Jews.

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when you give glory to someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: When you give glory to someone, you reveal their greatness, you demonstrate or show openly that the person is worthy of receiving honor.
Questions.Note: See "glory" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What happened when the non-Jews believed the Good News/the Gospel?
Questions.A: When they believed the gospel they too became God's sons/children. (13)
Questions.Alternative: What happened when the non-Jews believed the Good News?
What happened when the non-Jews believed the Gospel?
What happened when the Gentiles believed the Good News?
What happened when the Gentiles believed the Gospel?

Questions.Q: What does someone do when he believes?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: When someone believes he puts his trust and commitment in another person.
Questions.Note: See "believe" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think the gospel is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The word "gospel" is a translation of the Greek noun euangelion. In the New Testament the noun euangelion is used in a restricted sense. It does not mean just any kind of good news, but specifically the good news or joyful report that God has made a way to save sinful human beings. In the New Testament it is always used with this one sense and is usually translated in the RSV, and in most modern English versions, as "gospel".
Questions.Note: See "gospel" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did Paul tell the non-Jews that God had given to them because they believed in Christ?
Questions.A: He told them that God gave them the Holy Spirit that he had promised to all of his people. (13)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to "make a promise"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that someone will make a declaration to someone else that he will do or will refrain from doing something specified. (See "promise" in KBT in the "covenant" entry.)

Questions.Q: Who do you think the Holy Spirit is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He is God's spirit, through whom he acts, reveals His will, and empowers individuals. (See "Holy Spirit" in KBT in the "spirit" entry.)

Questions.Q: What does it show for all believers to have God's Holy Spirit?
Questions.A: Having God's Holy Spirit shows that all believers are God's people/belong to God. (13)
It also shows that believers are going to inherit salvation. (14)
Questions.Note: T.N. on Ephesians states that the Holy Spirit is like a tribal mark which shows that a believer belongs to God.

Questions.Q: How do we know that God will give us all that he has promised?
Questions.A: He has already given us the Holy Spirit whom he promised, therefore, we can be sure that he will also give us all the other things he has promised to us. (14)

Questions.Q: Since God has saved/redeemed us and has given us his Holy Spirit, what should we do?
Questions.A: We should praise him because he is wonderful. (14)
Questions.Alternative: Since God has saved us and has given us his Holy Spirit, what should we do?
Since God has redeemed us and has given us his Holy Spirit, what should we do?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to redeem someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: With only one or two exceptions in the New Testament, the words "to redeem", "redemption", "ransom" refer to Christ's action in giving up his own life in order that God forgive the sins of those who believe in him.
Questions.Note: See "redeem" in KBT.

Section.heading: Ephesians 1:15-23 Paul gave thanks to God for the Christians in Ephesus because they believed in the Lord Jesus. He prayed that they would learn to know God better.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what Paul wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: He prayed for the believers at Ephesus. (16)
He told them about God's mighty power and about how God has exalted Christ. (19-20)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Paul continued to give thanks for the Ephesian believers?
Questions.A: He continued to give thanks for them because he heard that they had believed in the Lord Jesus.
He continued to give thanks for them because he heard that they loved all of God's people. (15-16)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to have faith in someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Faith is the quality of trusting someone. (See "faith" in KBT in the "believe, believing, belief, faith, trust" entry.)

Questions.Q: What did Paul ask God to do for the Ephesian believers?
Questions.A: He asked God to make them wise.
He asked God to reveal himself to them. (17)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Paul wanted God to do those things for the Ephesian believers?
Questions.A: He wanted God to do those things so that the Ephesians might know God better. (17)

Questions.Q: What else did Paul pray that [God] would do for the believers?
Questions.A: He prayed that [God] would help them to understand more about him and his ways. (18)
Questions.Alternative: What else did Paul pray that God would do for the believers?
What else did Paul pray would be done for the believers?
What else did Paul pray for the believers?
How else did Paul ask God to help the believers?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Paul wanted God to do that?
Questions.A: He wanted God to do that, so that they would know/realize/be confident that the good/wonderful things which God had promised them will happen/come to pass. (18)
They would know how great the inheritance is which God had given them. (18)
They would know, that is, experience the power of God in their lives. (19)

Questions.Q: Paul had stated that there is power available to us who are believers. To what did Paul compare that power?
Questions.A: He said that the power is like the mighty power of God which raised Christ from the dead and seated him at God's right hand in heaven. (19-20)

Questions.Q: Where do you think heaven is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It is that part of God's creation above the earth and the waters, including "air" and "space," and serves as home for God and the spirits who serve Him.
Questions.Note: See "heaven" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What is Christ doing in heaven?
Questions.A: He is sitting at the right hand [the place of honor or prominence] of God [his Father]. (20)
He is ruling over all authorities, powers and lords. // He is ruling over beings that have power. (21)

Questions.Q: How long will he have this authority?
Questions.A: He will have this authority both now and into the future. (21)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that he is able to rule with complete authority?
Questions.A: He can rule that way/like that because God gave him an authority that is superior to all other powers. (22)

Questions.Q: When God appointed Christ as supreme head over all things, who benefited/received the good from that action?
Questions.A: The church/All believers benefited from that action. (22)
Questions.Alternative: When God appointed Christ as supreme head over all things, who benefited from that action?
When God appointed Christ as supreme head over all things, who received the good from that action?

Questions.Q: What do you think the church is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In this verse, it is the community of believers-in-Christ in general, i.e. the whole church of Christ, the universal church.
Questions.Note: See "church" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What is the relationship of the church to Christ?
Questions.A: Christ is [like] the head of the church and the church is [like] Christ's body. (22-23)

Questions.Q: What do you think he meant by "body" in this verse?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "Body," in this verse, means the whole group of people who are individually united to Christ.
Questions.Note: See "body" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What does the church/the body of Christ have available to it?
Questions.A: We, as God's people, have fully available to us the power that Christ has. (23)
Questions.Note: T.N. on Ephesians favors this interpretation of this verse.
Questions.Alternative: What does the church have available to it?
What does the body of Christ have available to it?

Questions.Q: What does Christ do?
Questions.A: He fills everything. // He is the one who gives life to everything everywhere. (23)

Section.heading: Ephesians 2:1-10 All people do not belong to God because of their sins; but because He loves us, God made us His people when we believed in Jesus.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what Paul wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: Paul described how we all [both Jews and non-Jews] lived before we became Christians. (1-3)
Paul described what God did for all believers. (4-7)

Questions.Q: Against whom had the Ephesians sinned?
Questions.A: They had sinned against God. (1)

Questions.Q: Because they sinned and disobeyed God, what happened?
Questions.A: They were [spiritually] dead. // They were like dead people. (1)

Questions.Q: How did they show that condition?
Questions.A: They showed that condition by the things that they did which were evil like that of other unbelievers.
They showed that condition by the way in which they lived their lives in obedience to Satan. (2)

Questions.Q: What do you know about Satan?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Satan is the chief enemy of God. He is the supreme evil spiritual being who leads and directs all other evil spiritual beings.
Questions.Note: See "Satan" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: What do you know about this prince?
What do you know about this prince of the power of the air?
What do you know about this powerful evil spirit?

Questions.Q: Over whom else does Satan have power and authority?
Questions.A: He has power and authority over evil spirits/demons.
He has power and authority over those people who disobey God. (2)

Questions.Q: Who do you think that demons and evil spirits are?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The terms "evil spirit", "unclean spirit", and "demon" are used interchangeably in the New Testament. They all refer to spiritual beings who serve Satan as his agents, being under his authority. These spiritual beings have power to oppress a human being and even take control of him.
Questions.Note: See "evil spirit" in KBT.

Questions.Q: In what way did Paul say we were the same as the other sinners he mentioned above?
Questions.A: Paul said we have all lived according to our evil desires. (3)

Questions.Q: How did God feel about us because we had lived according to our evil desires?
Questions.A: God was angry with us. (3)

Questions.Q: Since God did not punish us, as we deserved, what did he do?
Questions.A: He showed us merciful love. (4)
He made us spiritually alive. (5)
He saved us. (5)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to save you?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that a person will rescue someone else from a dangerous situation.
Questions.Note: See "save" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that God saved us?
Questions.A: God saved us because he loved us so much,
and because he was very merciful to us. (4)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means that someone is merciful to someone else?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "Mercy" in the New Testament is an act of kindness by God or someone else toward people who are in need. The person (God or man) acts to relieve some kind of suffering or distress.
Questions.Note: See "mercy" in KBT.

Questions.Q: How did God show his love and mercy to us?
Questions.A: He joined us with Christ and he gave us new life. (5)

Questions.Q: Since God did that in spite of the fact that we were spiritually dead/like dead people, what do we know about God?
Questions.A: We know that he saved us because of his grace/kindness. (5, 7)
Questions.Alternative: Since God did that in spite of the fact that we were spiritually dead, what do we know about God?
Since God did that in spite of the fact that we were spiritually like dead people, what do we know about God?
Since God saved us when we were spiritually dead, what do we know about God?
What does this show about God?

Questions.Q: What happened when God joined us with Christ?
Questions.A: It is/was as though God raised us up [to rule] with Christ. (6)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that God has saved us?
Questions.A: He saved us so that, in future years, he can show everyone how kind he is to us. (7)

Questions.Q: What good deeds can we do so that God will save us?
Questions.A: We can not do any good deeds so that God will save us. (8-9)

Questions.Q: What is the reason for this?
Questions.A: The reason is that God saves us only because he is kind to us. (8-9)

Questions.Q: How do we obtain God's grace/kindness?
Questions.A: We obtain this grace through believing/placing our faith in Christ. (8)
Questions.Alternative: How do we obtain God's grace?
How do we obtain God's kindness?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that it is impossible for us to boast and claim that we are saved by doing good deeds?
Questions.A: It is impossible for us to boast about this because God is the one who saves us. (9)

Questions.Q: How is it possible for us to do good deeds, now that we are believers?
Questions.A: It is possible for us to do good deeds because God has created us/made us like new beings for the very purpose of doing the good deeds which he had planned for us to do. (10)

Questions.Q: What happened in order to bring about this change in the way we live?
Questions.A: God united/joined us with Jesus Christ. (10)

Section.heading: Ephesians 2:11-22 Because Christ died God has united the Gentile and the Jew together in Christ.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what Paul wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: The Gentile people had previously not known God. As far as the Jews were concerned, the Gentiles were outcasts [from God]. Now Christ has united both the Gentiles and the Jews as one people. God has been kind to both groups (of people). Because they believed Christ they are now God's people.

Questions.Q: What did Paul tell the Gentiles to remember?
Questions.A: He told them to remember that, in the past, they were called "the uncircumcised" [by the Jews]. (11)
Questions.Note: That was the Jews' way of showing contempt for the Gentiles because the Jews considered themselves to be the people of God because they had been circumcised.

Questions.Q: What is the reason Paul said that circumcision refers only to the body?
Questions.A: He said that because it is only an outward, physical sign. (11)

Questions.Q: Who do you think the Gentiles are?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In this verse, they are those people who are not Jews.
Questions.Note: See "Gentiles" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to circumcise someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that someone removes the foreskin of the male genital. Traditionally the father, or someone else, would perform this on his son on the 8th day after his birth. This was a mark of being a Jew. (See "the circumcised" in KBT in the "Israel, Jew, Hebrew" entry.)

Questions.Q: What was the condition of the Gentiles in the past, before they believed in Christ?
Questions.A: They were separated from Christ. // They had no relationship with Christ.
They were not chosen to be God's people because God had originally chosen the Jews as his special people.
They had been excluded from the promises which God had made to the Jewish people.
They lived without hope for anything good.
They did not know God. // They had no relationship with God. (12)

Questions.Q: Whom do you think Paul meant by "citizenship in Israel"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: After the resurrection of Jesus Christ, Christians regarded themselves as being the true people of God because of their belief in Jesus Christ. They, therefore, referred to themselves as "Israel" and regarded themselves as the spiritual successors of the people of Israel. In this sense the focus is on being the people of God; racial origin is not important.
Questions.Note: See "Israel" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to hope in something?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means to have a desire to see something happen or to obtain something.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus Christ do so that they might not be separated from God any longer?
Questions.A: Jesus Christ shed his blood and died for them,
and through union with him, they are now related to God. (13)

Questions.Q: Whom has Christ reconciled/caused to be at peace?
Questions.A: He has caused the Jewish believers and the Gentile believers to be at peace with each other. (14)
Questions.Alternative: Whom has Christ reconciled?
Whom has Christ caused to be at peace?

Questions.Q: Previously the Jews and the Gentiles had hated each other. What was one of the reasons for their hatred?
Questions.A: They hated each other because of the Jewish law. (15)

Questions.Q: What did Christ do in order to make peace between the two groups?
Questions.A: He abolished/removed/negated the law. (15)

Questions.Q: In place of that law, in what were those two groups supposed to trust?
Questions.A: They were supposed to trust in Christ. (15)

Questions.Q: When that happened/happens what became/becomes of the two [formerly antagonistic] groups?
Questions.A: The two groups became/become one harmonious group. (15)
Questions.Alternative: When that happened what became of the two formerly antagonistic groups?
When that happened what becomes of the two formerly antagonistic groups?
When that happens what became of the two formerly antagonistic groups?
When that happens what becomes of the two formerly antagonistic groups?
When that happened what became of the two groups?
When that happened what becomes of the two groups?
When that happens what became of the two groups?
When that happens what becomes of the two groups?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Christ died?
Questions.A: He died to reconcile the Jews and the Gentiles to God. (16)

Questions.Q: What do you think Christ did when he reconciled them to God?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that he changed them from being enemies of God to being his friends.
Questions.Note: See "reconcile" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What happened to the two groups when Christ reconciled them to God?
Questions.A: They became united into one group.
They stopped hating each other. (16)

Questions.Q: What message/teaching did Jesus Christ preach to the people?
Questions.A: He preached the way to have peace with God. (17)
Questions.Alternative: What message did Jesus Christ preach to the people?
What teaching did Jesus Christ preach to the people?

Questions.Q: To whom did he preach that message of peace?
Questions.A: He preached that message to the Gentiles and to the Jews. (17)

Questions.Q: What do you think someone is doing when they preach?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: When someone preaches, they are proclaiming the gospel to those who are listening. This also means a person urges others to accept or abandon an idea or course of action.

Questions.Q: Who is able to come into the presence of God, the Father, now?
Questions.A: All of us, both Jews and Gentiles can come into the presence of God. (18)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that we are able to do this?
Questions.A: We all can approach God by the power of the Holy Spirit because of what Christ has done/is doing for us. (18)

Questions.Q: What relationship do the Gentiles, who believe in Christ, now have with God because of what Christ has done?
Questions.A: They are no longer outsiders/foreigners/strangers, but they are now members of God's family. (19)

Questions.Q: To what did Paul compare believers?
Questions.A: He said they were [like bricks] in a building. They were built on the apostles and prophets who were like the foundation of a building. Jesus was like the cornerstone of a building. // He said they were [like bricks] in a building that were built on a foundation. The foundation was like the message about Christ that the apostles and prophets taught. Jesus was like the cornerstone of a building. (20)

Questions.Q: What do you know about prophets?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In this verse prophets are people in the church to whom God has given the gift of proclaiming a message from him. This gift is the ability to speak a message given directly from God, by the power of the Holy Spirit.
Questions.Note: See "prophet" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did Paul say the believers in Christ were like?
Questions.A: He said they were like a holy temple/building that belonged to God. (21)

Questions.Q: What do you think Paul meant by "temple" in this verse?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "Temple" in this verse is used as a metaphor for the Christians. The meaning of "temple" is a person, or group of people, within whom God is present, or where God lives in a special way.
Questions.Note: See "temple" in KBT.

Questions.Q: As believers in Christ, what is true of those Ephesian Christians, as well as of all other believers, in regard to this temple?
Questions.A: They/we all are part of it. (22)

Questions.Q: In this metaphor of a temple, what is Christ's relationship to us believers who are this temple?
Questions.A: Christ as the cornerstone, which supports the whole structure, is the one who supports/sustains each believer so that they become a fitting dwelling place for God to live in. (22)

Questions.Q: How does God actually dwell in his people?
Questions.A: He dwells in them by the presence of his Spirit in his people. (22)

Section.heading: Ephesians 3:1-13 God wanted Paul to preach the gospel to the Gentiles in Ephesus.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the meaning (theme) of what Paul wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: Paul wrote that God had chosen him to preach the gospel to the Gentiles in Ephesus. (1-3, 7)

Questions.Q: What was the reason that Paul [prayed] for the Gentiles?
Questions.A: He [prayed] for them because of the things he said about them previously in this letter. (1)
Questions.Note: According to T.N. on Ephesians, Paul intended to /meant to/was going to pray/had in mind praying for them in verse 1; but then he talked about his ministry until verse 14, where he continued the prayer he almost began in verse 1.
Questions.Alternative: What was the reason that Paul prayed for the Gentiles?
What was the reason that Paul for the Gentiles?

Questions.Q: What was the reason that Paul was in prison?
Questions.A: He was in prison because he had been teaching/preaching the Good News about Christ to the Gentiles. (1)

Questions.Q: Who gave Paul the right/authority to teach the Good News?
Questions.A: God gave him the right/authority. (2)
Questions.Alternative: Who gave Paul the right to teach the Good News?
Who gave Paul the authority to teach the Good News?

Questions.Q: What was the reason that God chose Paul to do that work?
Questions.A: God chose Paul because he was gracious to Paul,
and because he wanted Paul to do that work in order to help/for the benefit of the Gentiles. (2)

Questions.Q: What had [God] caused Paul to know?
Questions.A: [God] had caused Paul to know what people, who lived before, had not known about his secret plan. (3)
Questions.Alternative: What had God caused Paul to know?
What had God revealed to Paul?
What had been made known to Paul?
What had God made known to Paul?
What did Paul know through a divine revelation?
What did Paul know through a revelation?

Questions.Q: How could the Ephesian believers learn more about this mystery/secret plan?
Questions.A: They could read what Paul had already written about Christ in this letter. (4)
Questions.Alternative: How could the Ephesian believers learn more about this mystery?
How could the Ephesian believers learn more about this secret plan?

Questions.Q: Since this plan was previously a secret, how did God reveal it to people?
Questions.A: God caused his Spirit to reveal it to his apostles and prophets. (5)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say about the apostles and prophets?
Questions.A: Paul said that they were people whom God chose/appointed to be apostles and prophets. (5)

Questions.Q: What is God's mystery/secret plan?
Questions.A: God's mystery/secret plan is that the Gentile [believers] and the Jewish [believers] will share equally in God's blessings and promises. (6)
Questions.Alternative: What is God's mystery?
What is God's secret plan?

Questions.Q: What happened so that the Gentiles could receive these blessings and promises?
Questions.A: They [heard and believed] the gospel.
They were united to Christ. (6)

Questions.Q: Since the Gentile [believers along with the Jewish believers] are now united to Christ, how are they related to him?
Questions.A: They belong to the same body [of Christ]. // They belong to Christ as one group. (6)
Questions.Alternative: Since the Gentile believers along with the Jewish believers are now united to Christ, how are they related to him?
Since the Gentile are now united to Christ, how are they related to him?

Questions.Q: What was the reason that God chose Paul to be a servant of/preach the Good News?
Questions.A: God chose Paul to preach the Good News because he was gracious to him. (7)
Questions.Alternative: What was the reason that God chose Paul to be a servant of the Good News?
What was the reason that God chose Paul to preach the Good News?

Questions.Q: What was the reason that Paul was able to preach the Good News?
Questions.A: He was able to preach the Good News because God caused his power to work in Paul. (7)

Questions.Q: How did Paul consider himself in comparison to his fellow believers in Christ?
Questions.A: He considered himself the least important among them. (8)

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that Paul said that about himself?
Questions.A: He said that about himself to show that his privilege/right of preaching the Good News was because God chose him to do so, not because of anything which he had done or said. (8)
Questions.Note: The respondent might not find this answer in the text.

Questions.Q: What did Paul say about all the many ways that Christ helps the believers?
Questions.A: He said that believers can not completely understand/imagine them. (8)

Questions.Q: What did Paul want all people to understand?
Questions.A: He wanted all people to understand how God would accomplish his secret plan. (9)

Questions.Q: What had God kept secret, since before he created everything?
Questions.A: He had kept his plan a secret. (9)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that God was now making his plan known?
Questions.A: He was making his plan known, so that the spiritual powers, who rule in the heavenly realms, might learn how wise God is by what he has done for the church/believers. (10)

Questions.Q: When did God make this plan?
Questions.A: God decided to do this long ago, before he made the world. (11)

Questions.Q: Whom did God choose to fulfill his plan?
Questions.A: He chose Christ Jesus to fulfill his plan. (11)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that we believers can be bold to pray to God with freedom and confidence/without fear?
Questions.A: We can do this because we are united to/we have fellowship with Christ and believe in him. (12)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that we believers can be bold to pray to God with freedom and confidence?
What is the reason that we believers can be bold to pray to God without fear?
What is the reason that we believers can be bold to pray to God with freedom and without fear?

Questions.Q: What was the reason that Paul asked those Ephesian believers not to become discouraged, even though he was suffering?
Questions.A: He asked them not to become discouraged about his sufferings because he was suffering for their good/benefit. (13)

Section.heading: Ephesians 3:14-21 Paul prayed for the Christians in Ephesus.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the meaning (theme) of what Paul wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: Paul prayed to [God] the Father that he might give the Ephesian believers strength in their hearts/minds/wills by his Spirit. (16)

Questions.Q: What does the "heart" mean to you?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The most common use of the word "heart" in the Bible is to refer to the spiritual center or innermost part of a human being. In Hebrew and Greek the word "heart" is most commonly associated with thoughts and ideas.
Questions.Note: See "heart" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What was the reason that Paul prayed to [God] the Father?
Questions.A: He was thinking of God's wonderful plan mentioned previously. (14)
Questions.Note: According to T.N. on Ephesians, Paul was referring to everything he said about God's wonderful plan and all the good things he does for his people.
Questions.Alternative: What was the reason that Paul prayed to God the Father?
What was the reason that Paul prayed to the Father?

Questions.Q: Of what is God the source/originator?
Questions.A: He is the source/originator of every family in heaven and on earth. // His people in heaven and on earth are in families because he is our Father. (15)
Questions.Alternative: Of what is God the source?
Of what is God the originator?

Questions.Q: How long did Paul expect Christ to live/dwell in their hearts/with them?
Questions.A: He expected Christ to live/dwell in their hearts/with them forever/always. (17)
Questions.Alternative: How long did Paul expect Christ to live in their hearts?
How long did Paul expect Christ to live with them?
How long did Paul expect Christ to dwell in their hearts?
How long did Paul expect Christ to dwell with them?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Christ would live/dwell in their hearts/with them?
Questions.A: He would live in their hearts because they believed in him. (17)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that Christ would live in their hearts?
What is the reason that Christ would live with them?
What is the reason that Christ would dwell in their hearts?
What is the reason that Christ would dwell with them?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Paul prayed that their love might be strong/firm?
Questions.A: He prayed that their love might be strong, so that they might understand that Christ loved them very much. (17-18)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that Paul prayed that their love might be strong?
What is the reason that Paul prayed that their love might be firm?

Questions.Q: What is it that no one can completely know/understand?
Questions.A: No one can understand completely how much Christ loves us. (19)
Questions.Alternative: What is it that no one can completely know?
What is it that no one can completely understand?

Questions.Q: What will they become as they know more and more of Christ's love for them?
Questions.A: They will become all that God wants/intends them to be. // They will become complete/mature in every way, just as God is. (19)

Questions.Q: What is God able to do?
Questions.A: He can do more than we can ask or think /comprehend concerning his great power to help us. (20)

Questions.Q: Who should glorify/praise God?
Questions.A: The church/all believers should glorify/praise him. (21)
Questions.Alternative: Who should glorify God?
Who should praise God?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that all believers should glorify/praise God?
Questions.A: All believers should glorify/praise God because of what he has done through the believers/the church and through Christ Jesus. (21)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that all believers should glorify God?
What is the reason that all believers should praise God?

Questions.Q: How long should all believers glorify/praise God?
Questions.A: All believers should glorify/praise him forever. (21)
Questions.Alternative: How long should all believers glorify God?
How long should all believers praise God?

Section.heading: Ephesians 4:1-16 Paul encouraged the Christians in Ephesus to live united with one another.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the meaning (theme) of what Paul wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: He wrote that the Ephesian Christians should live the kind of life that God intended/planned for/wanted them to live. (1)

Questions.Q: What was the reason that Paul was in jail?
Questions.A: He was in jail because he was serving the Lord/doing the Lord's work. (1)
Questions.Note: See 3:1.

Questions.Q: In what way did Paul say they were supposed to live?
Questions.A: He said that they should live in the way that God wanted them to be living/live when he called them to be his children. (1)

Questions.Q: In what way did God want them to treat one another?
Questions.A: He wanted them to be humble,
patient,
to show love to each other,
and to strive for unity/live together in harmony. (2-3)

Questions.Q: How should they show that they love one another?
Questions.A: They should show that they love one another by not becoming angry with others when they do the wrong things. (2)

Questions.Q: What should they try their best to do?
Questions.A: They should try their best to live together in peace, so that they will remain united among themselves. (3)

Questions.Q: Who was it that united them?
Questions.A: God's Spirit/The Holy Spirit united them. (3)

Questions.Q: What characteristics/qualities did Paul state/list in verses 4-6 as being ones that unite all believers?
Questions.A: One body/The body of Christ/all believers. // They all belong/belonged to Christ.
One Spirit/God's Spirit. // They all have/had God's Spirit.
One hope/That for which all believers hope. // They all have/had the same hope of being forever with God/Christ.
One Lord. // They worshiped only one as their Lord.
One faith/That in which all Christians believe. // We as believers believe the same way (about God).
One baptism/One person in whose name all believers are baptized. // Because we belong to Christ, we were baptized.
One God. // We believe in only God. (4-6)
Questions.Alternative: What characteristics did Paul state in verses 4-6 as being ones that unite all believers?
What characteristics did Paul list in verses 4-6 as being ones that unite all believers?
What qualities did Paul state in verses 4-6 as being ones that unite all believers?
What qualities did Paul list in verses 4-6 as being ones that unite all believers?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when someone is baptized?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "Baptism" is the outward sign by which a person's commitment to and union with Jesus Christ are publicly demonstrated.
Questions.Note: See "baptize" in KBT.

Questions.Q: In what way are all seven of these characteristics similar?
Questions.A: Each one is a single entity. (4-6)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say about God in verse 6?
Questions.A: He is only one God.
He is the Father of all believers.
He is Lord over all people. // He is Lord over all believers.
He does his work through all his people.
He abides in all believers [by his Spirit]. (6)

Questions.Q: What has Christ given to each believer?
Questions.A: Christ gave each believer different abilities. (7)

Questions.Q: Who ascended into a high place?
Questions.A: Christ ascended to heaven. (8)
Questions.Note: According to T.N. on Ephesians, this verse refers to a quote from Psalm 68:18 that describes a Jewish king who had defeated his enemies and was returning in victory. Paul saw that as a picture of Christ ascending to heaven. Just as the king won a victory, and then went up to a high place and gave gifts to people; so also Christ won a victory (over sin and death), and then went up to a high place (God's right side in heaven) and gave gifts (special abilities) to his followers.

Questions.Q: What did he do when he went into a high place?
Questions.A: He took the enemies with him whom he had conquered.
He gave gifts to people. (8)

Questions.Q: What did Paul ask the Ephesian believers?
Questions.A: He asked them what the words "he ascended" meant. (9)
Questions.Note: This is a rhetorical question.

Questions.Q: What did Paul say that the words "he ascended" meant?
Questions.A: He said that those words meant that, before he [Christ] went up, he came down to earth. (9)

Questions.Q: What did he/Christ accomplish/do when he returned to heaven?
Questions.A: Christ brought everything to perfection in order that he would fulfill everything/would make everything be as it should be. (10)
Questions.Note: This is the choice that was made in T.N. on Ephesians from the three possible interpretations. Also see 4:10 in the UBS Handbook on Ephesians.
Questions.Alternative: What did he accomplish when he returned to heaven?
What did he do when he returned to heaven?
What did Christ accomplish when he returned to heaven?
What did Christ do when he returned to heaven?

Questions.Q: What abilities/authority did Christ give to some of his people?
Questions.A: He gave some people the ability/authority to be apostles,
some people to be prophets,
some people to be evangelists,
some people to be pastors,
and some people to be teachers. (11)
Questions.Alternative: What abilities did Christ give to some of his people?
What authority did Christ give to some of his people?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Christ gave some of his people those special abilities?
Questions.A: He gave them those abilities so that they could make all of God's people ready to serve/work for him. (12)
He gave them those abilities so that all of God's people might become strong in their relationship with Christ and with each other. (12)

Questions.Q: What is the purpose/goal of Christ in making his people strong in their relationship with him and with each other?
Questions.A: The purpose/goal of Christ is that his people will become united by the way they trust [God] and know his Son,
that they will become mature/strong Christians,
and that they will become more and more like Christ. (13)
Questions.Alternative: What is the purpose of Christ in making his people strong in their relationship with him and with each other?
What is the goal of Christ in making his people strong in their relationship with him and with each other?

Questions.Q: What did Paul say will no longer happen to them when they became mature Christians?
Questions.A: They will no longer be like a boat that strong winds and waves push around here and there on the water.
Cunning people, who teach lies, will no longer be able to deceive them and make them believe the wrong things/false doctrines/clever lies. (14)

Questions.Q: Instead of being easily swayed/convinced by clever lies, what should they do?
Questions.A: They should speak the truth [about God]. (15)
Questions.Note: Speaking the truth means more than just saying the truth, it also means living the truth. See comments on this verse in T.N. on Ephesians and T.H. on Ephesians.
Questions.Alternative: Instead of being easily swayed by clever lies, what should they do?
Instead of being easily convinced by clever lies, what should they do?

Questions.Q: In what way/manner should they "speak the truth"?
Questions.A: They should show their love to others as they speak the truth [about God]. (15)
Questions.Alternative: In what way should they "speak the truth"?
In what manner should they "speak the truth"?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they should speak the truth [about God] in this way/manner?
Questions.A: They should speak the truth [about God] in a loving way, so that they will become more and more like Christ. (15)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that they should speak the truth about God in this way?
What is the reason that they should speak the truth about God in this manner?
What is the reason that they should speak the truth in this way?
What is the reason that they should speak the truth in this manner?

Questions.Q: How is Christ related to all of his followers?
Questions.A: He is like the head/chief who rules over all his followers. (15)

Questions.Q: How did Paul compare the physical body of a person with the body of Christ?
Questions.A: He said that, just as the different parts of the physical body of a person are held together by the joints or ligaments, so it is Christ who holds together his body/the church/all believers. (16)

If each part of the physical body does its work, as it should, then the whole body grows and becomes strong. That is how it is with/in the body of Christ. If the members love each other and do the work Christ has given them, then the body of Christ will grow strong and mature by Christ's power in each believer. (16)

Section.heading: Ephesians 4:17-5:20 Stop living the life that you practiced before you knew Christ and start living the life that you now have from knowing him.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the meaning (theme) of what Paul wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: Paul urged the Christians to stop doing the evil kinds of behavior that they used to do when they were pagans/people who did not know God, and to start doing the good deeds that people who know Christ should do.

Questions.Q: What did Paul urge the Ephesian Christians not to do?
Questions.A: He urged them not to act/behave like the unbelievers do. (17)

Questions.Q: What is the thinking of the unbelievers like?
Questions.A: Their thoughts are worthless. // What they think about is worthless. (17)
They do not understand about God. (18)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that unbelievers do not know about becoming God's people?
Questions.A: Unbelievers do not know that because they are ignorant of God/him,
and are stubborn/resist his ways. (18)

Questions.Q: What do those unbelieving people do?
Questions.A: They are not ashamed to do bad things and also they practice/do all kinds of immoral acts. (19)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the Ephesian Christians should behave/act differently than the way the unbelievers do?
Questions.A: They should act differently because when they became believers in Christ, they learned of a new way to live/to conduct themselves. (20-21)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that the Ephesian Christians should behave differently than the way the unbelievers do?
What is the reason that the Ephesian Christians should act differently than the way the unbelievers do?

Questions.Q: Since they have learned of a new way to live, what should they do concerning the way in which they used to live?
Questions.A: They should no longer live the way that they used to live. (22)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they should no longer live the way that they used to live?
Questions.A: They should no longer live that way because the things they used to do were bad. (22)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they used to do those bad deeds?
Questions.A: They used to do those bad deeds because they obeyed the evil desires that were in their hearts. (22)

Questions.Q: What should they now be doing, instead of the evil/bad deeds that they used to do?
Questions.A: They should continually be thinking good thoughts and doing good deeds. (23-24)
Questions.Alternative: What should they now be doing, instead of the evil deeds that they used to do?
What should they now be doing, instead of the bad deeds that they used to do?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they now have the power/ability to do deeds and think thoughts that are good?
Questions.A: They are able to do that because God has given them a new nature/character/them desires to do what he wants done. (24)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that they now have the power to do deeds and think thoughts that are good?
What is the reason that they now have the ability to do deeds and think thoughts that are good?

Questions.Q: What is this nature/character/desire like?
Questions.A: This nature/character/desire is to be like God's own good/holy character. (24)
Questions.Alternative: What is this nature like?
What is this character like?
What is this desire like?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they should stop lying?
Questions.A: They should stop lying because God has given them a new nature/character/desire. (25a)
Questions.Note: This refers back to 4:22-24.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they should tell the truth to their fellow believers?
Questions.A: They should tell the truth to their fellow believers because they are fellow members of the body of Christ/they all belong, as a group, to Christ. (25)

Questions.Q: If they become angry, what is the reason that they should be careful not to continue being angry?
Questions.A: They should not continue to be angry because it is easier for them to sin/to do bad deeds when they are angry. (26)
When they are angry it gives the Devil the opportunity to lead/tempt them to sin. (27)

Questions.Q: What do you know about the Devil?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The name "Devil" is the Greek equivalent of the Hebrew name for "Satan". Satan is the chief enemy of God. He is the supreme evil spiritual being, who leads and directs all other evil spiritual beings. (See "Devil" in KBT in the "Satan" entry.)

Questions.Q: What should the person, who used to steal, do [now that he is a believer]?
Questions.A: He should stop stealing and work to gain money for his needs/to support himself. (28)
Questions.Alternative: What should the person, who used to steal, do now that he is a believer?
What should the person, who used to steal, do?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that he should work?
Questions.A: He should work, so that he might also be able to give something to those people who are in need/poor. (28)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the believers should speak good words to other people, rather than bad words?
Questions.A: The believers encourage/help other people when they speak good words to them. (29)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they should not [sin] and make God's Holy Spirit sad?
Questions.A: They should not [sin] and make God's Holy Spirit sad because God gave them his spirit as a mark/sign that he owns them. (30)
