Questions.Note: Exegetical Helps on Ephesians states that this gives the motivation for not [sinning and] making the Holy Spirit sad. Believers have received such a great benefit through the Holy Spirit. It would be very wrong/ungrateful of them to make him sad.
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that they should not sin and make God's Holy Spirit sad?
What is the reason that they should not and make God's Holy Spirit sad?

Questions.Q: Since they have the Holy Spirit, what will happen to them in the future?
Questions.A: [God] will completely save them at some future day/time. (30)

Questions.Q: What did Paul tell them to stop doing in verse 31?
Questions.A: He told them to stop feeling bitter/resentful toward others,
to stop feeling angry toward others,
to stop shouting/brawling/fighting with others,
to stop insulting/slandering/saying bad things about others,
and to stop showing malice/hateful feelings toward others. (31)

Questions.Q: What did Paul tell them to do, instead of having all those bad feelings which are listed in verse 31?
Questions.A: He told them that they should be kind to one another.
They should be merciful/compassionate to one another.
They should forgive one another. (32)

Questions.Q: How should they forgive one another?
Questions.A: They should forgive one another as freely as God had forgiven them. (32)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that God forgave them?
Questions.A: He forgave them because of Christ. // He forgave them because of what Christ has done for them. (32)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they should try to be/behave like God?
Questions.A: They should try to be/behave like God because they are his children. (1)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that they should try to be like God?
What is the reason that they should try to behave like God?

Questions.Q: How or in what way should they live their lives?
Questions.A: They should live their lives by loving one another/loving others. (2)

Questions.Q: Whom should they follow/imitate, as they love others?
Questions.A: They should love others in the same way that Christ loved us. (2)
Questions.Alternative: Whom should they follow, as they love others?
Whom should they imitate, as they love others?

Questions.Q: How did Christ show his love for us?
Questions.A: Christ showed his love for us by giving his life/by dying for us. (2)

Questions.Q: What did God think about Christ dying for us?
Questions.A: God was pleased that Christ died for us. (2)

Questions.Q: Since they are God's people what should they not do?
Questions.A: They should not do anything that is sexually immoral.
They should not be indecent or greedy. (3)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for a person/someone to commit sexual immorality?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The word "immorality" is a general word which refers to any kind of unlawful sexual intercourse. (See "immorality" in KBT in the "sin" entry.)
Questions.Alternative: What do you think it means for a person to commit sexual immorality?
What do you think it means for someone to commit sexual immorality?

Questions.Q: How careful should they be to not do those evil/immoral deeds?
Questions.A: They should not do those evil deeds at all/at any time, so that no one can/is able to accuse them of doing evil deeds. (3)
Questions.Alternative: How careful should they be to not do those evil deeds?
How careful should they be to not do those immoral deeds?

Questions.Q: What should they do, instead of speaking bad, senseless language and speaking filthy words?
Questions.A: They should thank God [for what he has done for them]. (4)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they should not speak bad language and speak filthy words?
Questions.A: It is not proper/fitting/good for God's people to talk that way. (4)

Questions.Q: What other reason did Paul give them for not doing/committing the sins/bad deeds he mentioned in 5:3, that is, being immoral, indecent or greedy?
Questions.A: Paul stated that people, who habitually do such deeds, will not be allowed to enter/share where God and Christ rule. // Paul stated that people, who do such deeds, will not be allowed to enter the kingdom of Christ and of God and to receive the rewards/good things which God has promised. (5)
Questions.Alternative: What other reason did Paul give them for not doing the sins he mentioned in 5:3, that is, being immoral, indecent or greedy?
What other reason did Paul give them for not doing the bad deeds he mentioned in 5:3, that is, being immoral, indecent or greedy?
What other reason did Paul give them for not committing the sins he mentioned in 5:3, that is, being immoral, indecent or greedy?
What other reason did Paul give them for not committing the bad deeds he mentioned in 5:3, that is, being immoral, indecent or greedy?

Questions.Q: What do you think the kingdom of God is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The kingdom of God, rather than being a territory over which God rules, is the presence of God ruling in the lives of men.
Questions.Note: See "kingdom of God" in KBT.

Questions.Q: If a person is greedy, what is he like?
Questions.A: A greedy person is like an idolater because he worships riches/possessions /things instead of worshiping God. (5)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when someone practices idolatry?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that a person gives respect and devotion to a physical object as a god. The idol can be a representation or symbol of a deity, or any other being, or a thing made or used as an idol of worship.

Questions.Q: According to verse 6, how might they be deceived?
Questions.A: They might be deceived by believing the lies/falsehoods/untruths of people who say that the actions, which Paul mentioned in verses 3-5, are not bad/evil. (6)

Questions.Q: What will God do to people who do those bad deeds?
Questions.A: God will soon punish the people who disobey him by doing those kinds of bad deeds. (6)

Questions.Q: What should they do if they come into contact with people like that who do those bad deeds?
Questions.A: They should not participate with those people in the bad deeds that they do. (7)

Questions.Q: What was their condition before they believed in the Lord Jesus?
Questions.A: They were controlled by darkness/the dark. // Their minds were darkened. // They did not know the Lord Jesus, and they practiced doing evil deeds. (8)

Questions.Q: What happened to them when they believed in the Lord Jesus?
Questions.A: He enlightened their minds. // He showed them how evil/bad their evil deeds were before they believed in him. (8)

Questions.Q: What should they do, now that the Lord has enlightened their minds?
Questions.A: They should live like people who have been enlightened by the Lord. (8b)
They should try to learn to do the deeds that please the Lord. (10)

Questions.Q: What do people do who have been enlightened by the Lord?
Questions.A: They do what is good, right, and honest. (9)

Questions.Q: Instead of participating in the evil/bad deeds which the unbelievers do, what should they do?
Questions.A: They should cause people to know that those deeds are bad/evil. (11)
Questions.Alternative: Instead of participating in the evil deeds which the unbelievers do, what should they do?
Instead of participating in the bad deeds which the unbelievers do, what should they do?

Questions.Q: What did Paul say about the deeds that unbelievers do when other people can not see them?
Questions.A: He said that those deeds are so bad that it is shameful to even talk about what the unbelievers do when other people can not see them. // He said that those deeds are so bad that it is shameful to even talk about them. (12)

Questions.Q: What can people see when someone shines a light on something that was in darkness/the dark?
Questions.A: When someone shines a light on something that was in the dark, people can clearly see it/what it looks like. (13-14a)
Questions.Note: This is a figure of speech. It can be explained like this. In the same way when unbelievers do evil deeds in secret, and Christians tell them what God's word says about those deeds, the Christians are making known to the unbelievers that their deeds are evil in God's opinion. The Christians are like the light that shines in the darkness.
Questions.Alternative: What can people see when someone shines a light on something that was in darkness?
What can people see when someone shines a light on something that was in the dark?

Questions.Q: What did Paul tell the Christians/the believers to do?
Questions.A: He told them that they should not live/behave like foolish/unwise people, instead they should live/behave like wise people. (15)
Questions.Alternative: What did Paul tell the Christians to do?
What did Paul tell the believers to do?

Questions.Q: What should they do when they have the opportunity?
Questions.A: They should do good deeds when they have the opportunity. (16)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they should do good deeds when they have the opportunity?
Questions.A: They should do good deeds because the days are evil/people are doing many evil deeds now. (16)

Questions.Q: What did Paul tell the believers/Christians to do?
Questions.A: He told them not to be foolish. Instead, they should try to find out what the Lord wants [and do it]. (17)
Questions.Alternative: What did Paul tell the believers to do?
What did Paul tell the Christians to do?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they should be careful not to become intoxicated with wine nor any intoxicating drink?
Questions.A: They should be careful not to become drunk/intoxicated because anyone who becomes drunk does many bad deeds/deeds which are bad. (18)

Questions.Q: Instead of becoming drunk, what should they do?
Questions.A: They should allow the Holy Spirit to control them. (18)

Questions.Q: If they are controlled/filled by the Spirit, what will/should they be doing?
Questions.A: They will sing all kinds of songs of God to [encourage] each other. (19)
They will sing songs to praise the Lord with all their heart. (19)
They will thank God for everything. (20)
Questions.Alternative: If they are controlled by the Spirit, what will they be doing?
If they are controlled by the Spirit, what should they be doing?
If they are filled by the Spirit, what will they be doing?
If they are filled by the Spirit, what should they be doing?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they should thank God for everything?
Questions.A: They should thank God for everything because of what the Lord Jesus Christ has done for them. (20)

Questions.Q: When they thank God, through whom/whose name do they mention/depend on/do they pray?
Questions.A: They should pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. (20)
Questions.Alternative: When they thank God, on whom do they depend?
When they thank God, through whom do they pray?
When they thank God, whose name do they mention?
When they thank God, on whose name do they depend?

Section.heading: Ephesians 5:21-33 Wives should submit to their husbands, and husbands should love their wives in the same way that Christ loves the church.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the meaning (theme) of what Paul wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: Every husband should love his wife in the same way that Christ loves the believers. (25)
Every wife should obey and respect her husband. (22)

Questions.Q: How can believers honor/show respect for Christ?
Questions.A: Believers can honor/show respect for Christ by submitting to one another/each other/by following/by doing what the other believer wants/desires. (21)
Questions.Alternative: How can believers honor Christ?
How can believers show respect for Christ?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that a wife should submit herself to/obey her husband?
Questions.A: A wife should submit herself to her husband because this is a duty a Christian wives owes to the Lord/it is the right thing for her to do as a believer/because this is what the Lord wants her to do. (22)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that a wife should submit herself to her husband?
What is the reason that a wife should obey her husband?
What is the reason that a wife should submit herself to or obey her husband?

Questions.Q: In what way is a husband the head of his wife? // In what way does a husband have authority over his wife?
Questions.A: A husband has authority over his wife in the same way that Christ has authority over the believers/the church. (23)
Questions.Alternative: In what way is a husband the head of his wife?
In what way does a husband have authority over his wife?

Questions.Q: What else does Christ do for the believers/church?
Questions.A: He saves the believers/the church. (23)
Questions.Alternative: What else does Christ do for the believers?
What else does Christ do for the church?

Questions.Q: What are all the believers regarded as/called in their relationship to Christ?
Questions.A: They are/make up/constitute his body. // They belong to Christ as one group. (23)
Questions.Alternative: What are all the believers regarded as in their relationship to Christ?
What are all the believers called in their relationship to Christ?

Questions.Q: In what manner or how completely should each wife obey her husband?
Questions.A: Each wife should obey her husband completely, just as all believers should obey Christ completely. (24)

Questions.Q: In what way should each husband love his wife?
Questions.A: Each husband should love his wife in the same way that Christ loves the church/the believers. (25)

Questions.Q: How did Christ show his love for the church/the believers?
Questions.A: Christ showed his love when he gave his life/died for the church/the believers. (25)
Questions.Alternative: How did Christ show his love for the church?
How did Christ show his love for the believers?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Christ died for the church/the believers?
Questions.A: Christ died for the church/the believers, so that he might make them pure/sanctify them/free them from sin/good as God is good. (26)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that Christ died for the church?
What is the reason that Christ died for the believers?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to sanctify someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: According to T.N. on Ephesians, "sanctify" in this verse, means "so that he might make them pure".

Questions.Q: What did Christ do to make the church/the believers pure/sanctified?
Questions.A: He washed them with the water [of baptism] and with his word. (26)
Questions.Note: When they heard and believed God's word, trusted in him and were baptized, Christ made them pure and cleansed them from their sins.
Questions.Alternative: What did Christ do to make the church pure?
What did Christ do to make the church sanctified?
What did Christ do to make the believers pure?
What did Christ do to make the believers sanctified?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Christ did that/sanctified them/made them pure?
Questions.A: He did that so that he could make all his people beautiful as he is/(from his viewpoint) free from sins and to bring them all into his presence. (27)
He did that in order that his people will have no sins. (27)
He wanted his people to be holy and perfect. (27)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that Christ did that?
What is the reason that Christ sanctified them?
What is the reason that Christ made them pure?

Questions.Q: How or in what way should each man love his own wife?
Questions.A: Each man should love his own wife in the same way that he loves himself/his own body. (28)

Questions.Q: When a man loves his wife, whom else is he also loving at the same time?
Questions.A: A man, who loves his wife, loves himself/his own body also. (28)

Questions.Q: Instead of hating his own body, what does a man do?
Questions.A: Instead of hating his own body, a man loves and takes care of his own body. (29)

Questions.Q: In what way does a man care for his own body?
Questions.A: He cares for his own body in the same way Christ cares for the church/believers. (29)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Christ cares for the church/believers?
Questions.A: Christ cares for the church/believers because they are his body/believers/because they belong to him. (30)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that Christ cares for the church?
What is the reason that Christ cares for the believers?

Questions.Q: How does the scripture show that a husband and wife have a closer relationship than they do to/with other family members?
Questions.A: A man and his wife have a closer relationship because a man leaves his father and mother and unites with his wife. (31)
Questions.Alternative: How does the scripture show that a husband and wife have a closer relationship than they do to other family members?
How does the scripture show that a husband and wife have a closer relationship than they do with other family members?

Questions.Q: When a man has been united to his wife, how are the two of them then regarded/counted?
Questions.A: They are then counted as one. (31)
Questions.Alternative: When a man has been united to his wife, how are the two of them then regarded?
When a man has been united to his wife, how are the two of them then counted?

Questions.Q: To what else does the scripture, that Paul quoted in verse 31, refer besides a husband and wife becoming/being one?
Questions.A: It also refers to Christ and his relationship to/love for the church/the believers. (32)
Questions.Alternative: To what else does the scripture, that Paul quoted in verse 31, refer besides a husband and wife becoming one?
To what else does the scripture, that Paul quoted in verse 31, refer besides a husband and wife being one?

Questions.Q: What important deed/matter should every husband take care to do?
Questions.A: Every husband should love his wife as he loves himself. (33)
Questions.Alternative: What important deed should every husband take care to do?
What important matter should every husband take care to do?

Questions.Q: What important deed/matter should every wife do?
Questions.A: Every wife should respect her husband. (33)
Questions.Alternative: What important deed should every wife do?
What important matter should every wife do?

Section.heading: Ephesians 6:1-4 Children should obey their parents, and fathers should not provoke their children to anger.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the meaning (theme) of what Paul wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: He gave advice to children regarding their relationship with their parents. He gave advice to fathers regarding their relationship with their children.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that children should obey their parents?
Questions.A: They should obey their parents because it is the right thing for them to do. (1)

Questions.Q: What is the first commandment [which God gave] and which included a promise of something good to those who obey/follow that command?
Questions.A: His commandment to children to respect your father and mother is the first one. (2)
Questions.Alternative: What is the first commandment which God gave and which included a promise of something good to those who obey that command?
What is the first commandment which God gave and which included a promise of something good to those who follow that command?
What is the first commandment that included a promise of something good to those who obey that command?
What is the first commandment that included a promise of something good to those who follow that command?

Questions.Q: What did God promise to those who follow that/the first command?
Questions.A: God promised that everything would/will go well with them, and that they would/will live a long time on this earth/land/live many years. (3)
Questions.Alternative: What did God promise to those who follow that command?
What did God promise to those who follow the first command?

Questions.Q: What should fathers be careful not to do?
Questions.A: They should not treat their children in such a way that will make them angry. (4)

Questions.Q: How or in what way are fathers to discipline/train their children?
Questions.A: They should advise them concerning how to live as believers.
They should teach them to do what the Lord wants them to do. (4)
Questions.Alternative: How or in what way are fathers to discipline their children?
How or in what way are fathers to train their children?

Section.heading: Ephesians 6:5-9 Slaves and masters should treat each other with mutual respect because they both have the same master in heaven and he has no favorites.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the meaning (theme) of what Paul wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: Paul taught/advised/counseled slaves and masters how they should treat/regard/respect/consider each other.

Questions.Q: In what way are [Christian] slaves to obey their masters here on earth?
Questions.A: They should be anxious/solicitous/full of concern to please them and to show them respect.
They should serve them properly, as if it were Christ they were serving. (5)
Questions.Alternative: In what way are Christian slaves to obey their masters here on earth?
In what way are slaves to obey their masters here on earth?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to be a slave [of someone]?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means the person, who is a slave, is totally responsible to and dependent upon another person, or that the person has become completely subservient to a dominating influence.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think it means for someone to be a slave of someone?
What do you think it means for someone to be a slave?
What do you think it means for someone to be a slave of someone/something?
What do you think it means for someone to be a slave of something?

Questions.Q: What else should slaves keep in mind as they serve their masters?
Questions.A: They must obey their masters at all times and not only/just when their masters are watching them. (6)
It is not good if the only reason they obey their masters is in order that their masters might say good things about them. (6)
As they work for their masters, they should keep in mind that they are also serving Christ. (6-7)

Questions.Q: What does God want [Christian] slaves to do?
Questions.A: They should do the tasks/work that God has given/assigned them to do as slaves. (6)
Questions.Alternative: What does God want Christian slaves to do?
What does God want slaves to do?

Questions.Q: How or in what manner should they do that work?
Questions.A: They should do that work with all their strength. (6)
They should do that work in a willing/happy manner/way. (7)

Questions.Q: What will the Lord do for anyone who does good?
Questions.A: He will give/reward him with something good. (8)

Questions.Q: What is the proper way for [Christian] masters to treat their slaves?
Questions.A: They should treat their slaves well/do good to their slaves in the same way/manner that [Christian] slaves are required to do good to their masters.
They should not threaten them. (9)
Questions.Alternative: What is the proper way for Christian masters to treat their slaves?
What is the proper way for masters to treat their slaves?

Questions.Q: Who has the same Master in heaven?
Questions.A: Both [earthly] masters and slaves have the same Master in heaven. (9)

Questions.Q: How does the believer's Master judge people?
Questions.A: He judges them all alike/without partiality according to what they do. (9)

Section.heading: Ephesians 6:10-20 Put on all of the armor of God so that you can stand against the devil and his evil temptations.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the meaning (theme) of what Paul wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: Paul told the Ephesian Christians how to resist the Devil when he attacks them.
He reminded them to pray.

Questions.Q: What did Paul tell the Christians to do?
Questions.A: He told them to receive power from the Lord as they remain united with him, so that they may be strong because his power is very great. (10)

Questions.Q: What should they do so that they will not be deceived when the Devil tries to trick them?
Questions.A: They should use every resource/everything that God gives them/the whole armor of God for their protection. (11)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that we ought/it is necessary for us to be prepared to resist the Devil?
Questions.A: We ought to/It is necessary for us to be prepared to resist the Devil because we are not fighting against people. We are fighting against invisible spirits/demons, who have great power and authority to rule and to do evil. (12)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that we ought to be prepared to resist the Devil?
What is the reason it is necessary for us to be prepared to resist the Devil?

Questions.Q: Where are those evil spirits ruling?
Questions.A: Those evil spirits are ruling here on earth and in the skies/heavens/in the area between heaven (the dwelling place of God) and earth. (12)

Questions.Q: If believers use all the resources that God gives them to protect themselves/the whole armor of God, what will they be able to do?
Questions.A: They will be able to resist those enemies/the evil spirits/the demons (mentioned above) when they want to make the believers do evil deeds.
They will win over/defeat/not listen to/not be influenced by those enemies in the end. (13)
Questions.Alternative: If believers use all the resources that God gives them to protect themselves, what will they be able to do?
If believers use the whole armor of God, what will they be able to do?

Questions.Q: What did Paul tell the believers to do in order to face/resist those enemies/evil spirits?
Questions.A: He told them to stand firm with the belt of truth/speak the truth,
and always do what is right. (14)
He told them to keep believing in the Good News, which gives them peace. (15)
He told them to take up the shield of faith/trust in Jesus Christ. (16)
He told them to take the helmet of salvation/to be assured/to know that God has saved them. (17)
He told them to use the sword of the Spirit/the word of God. (17)
He told them to pray as the Holy Spirit leads them. (18)
Questions.Alternative: What did Paul tell the believers to do in order to face those enemies?
What did Paul tell the believers to do in order to face those evil spirits?
What did Paul tell the believers to do in order to resist those enemies?
What did Paul tell the believers to do in order to resist those evil spirits?

Questions.Q: To what did Paul compare those things which he told them to do?
Questions.A: When they speak the truth, it is like a belt which a soldier ties around his waist so he is ready to move quickly. (14)
When they do what is right, it is like a breastplate (a kind of shirt worn by soldiers) that protects a soldier in a battle. (14)
When they believe in the Good News which gives them peace, it is as though they had shoes on their feet; and they will stand firm. (15)
When they trust/have faith in Jesus Christ, it is like the shield that protects the soldier from the burning arrows that the enemy shoots at him. (16)
When they know that God has saved them, it is like the helmet that protects the soldier's head. (17)
When they use the sword of the Spirit/word of God, it is like a sword that they can use to fight against Satan. (17)

Questions.Q: If they trust/have faith in Christ, what will they be able to do?
Questions.A: They will be able to resist Satan when he wants them to do evil. (16)
Questions.Alternative: If they trust Christ, what will they be able to do?
If they have faith in Christ, what will they be able to do?

Questions.Q: To what did Paul compare Satan's attacks on them?
Questions.A: Paul wrote that it was as though Satan were shooting burning arrows at them. (16)

Questions.Q: When should they pray?
Questions.A: They should pray at all times/on every occasion. (18)

Questions.Q: For what should they pray?
Questions.A: They should ask God to help them all the time. (18)

Questions.Q: For whom should they pray?
Questions.A: They should pray for all God's people. (18)

Questions.Q: What did Paul request/ask the Ephesians to pray when he asked them to pray for him?
Questions.A: He asked them to pray that God would help him to teach boldly the Good News to people. The Good News had not been known before by all people. (19)
Questions.Alternative: What did Paul request the Ephesians to pray when he asked them to pray for him?
What did Paul ask the Ephesians to pray when he asked them to pray for him?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Paul was put in prison?
Questions.A: He was put in prison because he had been teaching the Good News about Christ. (20)
Questions.Note: Jesus chose Paul to be his ambassador to preach the Gospel. But people who hated Jesus wanted to stop Paul from preaching the Gospel, so they had Paul arrested. That is why Paul was in prison when he wrote this letter to the Ephesians.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Paul wanted to preach/teach the Good News about Christ?
Questions.A: He wanted to preach/teach the Good News about Christ because that is the work which Christ sent him to do. (20)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that Paul wanted to preach the Good News about Christ?
What is the reason that Paul wanted to teach the Good News about Christ?

Section.heading: Ephesians 6:21-24 Paul sent his final greetings to the Christians in Ephesus.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the meaning (theme) of what Paul wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: Paul said some things about Tychicus, and then he asked God to take care of the Ephesians.

Questions.Q: Whom did Paul send to the Ephesians?
Questions.A: He sent Tychicus to them. (21)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Paul sent Tychicus to the Ephesians?
Questions.A: Paul sent Tychicus to the Ephesians, so that he might tell/inform them what was happening to Paul and his companions. (21-22)
He sent Tychicus to the Ephesians, so that he might encourage them. (22)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say about Tychicus?
Questions.A: Paul said that Tychicus was a Christian brother whom they loved and that he was faithful in serving the Lord. (21)

Questions.Q: What did Paul desire for all the Christian brothers?
Questions.A: Paul desired that God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ would give them peace.
Also Paul wanted God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ to cause them to love each other and to continue to believe in Christ. (23)

Questions.Q: What do you think "God the Father" means?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that God is the father of Jesus Christ and of anyone who accepts Jesus as his or her Savior and Lord.
Questions.Note: See "God the Father" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think the title "God the Father" means?
What do you think the term "God the Father" means?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to be at peace?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: To be at peace means that a person has a mental or spiritual condition marked by freedom of disquieting or oppressive thoughts or emotions.

Questions.Q: To whom did Paul want God to be gracious?
Questions.A: He wanted God to be gracious to all those/us who love our Lord Jesus Christ very much. (24)
Questions.Alternative: On whom did Paul want God's grace to rest?
Who did Paul want to experience God's grace?
Who did Paul want to experience grace?
To whom did Paul want God to show grace?

Section.heading: Galatians 1:1-5 Paul sent greetings to the Christians in Galatia.

Questions.Q: Tell, in your own words, the basic meaning (theme) of what Paul said in these verses.
Questions.A: Paul and the brothers with him sent greetings to the churches in the [province of] Galatia. (1-2)

Questions.Q: What do you think Paul meant when he said the "brothers"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In this reference "brother" means fellow believer or fellow Christian. (See "brother" in KBT in the "disciple" entry.)

Questions.Q: What do you think the church is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It is a group of believers-in-Christ who live in one place. However, sometimes the writer talks about the believers who live in several places or towns in one larger region. That is the case in this reference, since he is writing to more than one church.
Questions.Note: See "church" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Who wrote this letter?
Questions.A: Paul wrote the letter. (1)

Questions.Q: What did he say about himself?
Questions.A: He said that he was an apostle of Jesus Christ and God the Father. (1)

Questions.Q: What do you think an apostle does?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The general meaning of the Greek word apostolos is "envoy", "appointed representative", "someone who is sent on a mission". In the New Testament, the term "apostle" has the specific sense of an appointed representative of Jesus Christ. In Acts and the rest of the New Testament, the term "apostle" is the most common term that is used to refer to those who were commissioned by Jesus Christ to be founders of the church, and who then took up that function and position.
Questions.Note: See "apostle" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think an apostle is?

Questions.Q: What do you think is the meaning of "Christ"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "Christ" is the English rendering of the Greek word Christos, which means "anointed one."
Questions.Note: See "Christ" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Who do you think God is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In English, the term "God" with a capital "G" is used to refer to the one supreme Creator. The term "god" with a small "g", as in "a god" or "many gods", can refer to any spiritual being that people worship. The Greek word theos can be used in the same two ways.
Questions.Note: In many languages the term for God is a proper name and cannot be used to refer to anyone except the one supreme creator of the world. It cannot be pluralized. (Or, if it can be pluralized, the meaning may be something very different from the English "gods". In one language, the plural form of God, meant "God and those who follow him" and was an appropriate way to translate "saints".) (See "God" in KBT.)

Questions.Q: What do you think "God the Father" means?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that God is the father of Jesus Christ and of anyone who accepts Jesus as his or her Savior and Lord.
Questions.Note: See "God the Father" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think the title "God the Father" means?
What do you think the term "God the Father" means?

Questions.Q: How can we know that Paul was really an apostle?
Questions.A: Jesus Christ and God the Father, not men, appointed him to that position. (1)

Questions.Q: What did God the Father do to Jesus?
Questions.A: The Father raised Jesus from death. (1)

Questions.Q: What did Paul desire for them?
Questions.A: His desire for them was that God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ would give them grace and peace. (3)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to have/use grace?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In this reference it means that God would show favor to them.
Questions.Note: See "grace" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think it means for someone to have grace?
What do you think it means to have grace?
What do you think it means for someone to experience grace?
What do you think it means for someone to use grace?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to be at peace?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that a person has a mental or spiritual condition marked by freedom of disquieting or oppressive thoughts or emotions.

Questions.Q: What does it mean to you to have someone as your lord?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A lord is someone who has power and exercises it responsibly. To call someone your lord means that you have given them control over your life. The Lord, in this case, is Jesus. Every Christian strives to make Jesus lord in his or her life by giving Him complete control. (See "Lord" in KBT in the "God" entry.)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say the Lord Jesus Christ has done?
Questions.A: He gave himself/died voluntarily for our sins. (4)

Questions.Q: What was the reason that Jesus did that?
Questions.A: He did it to set us free from the evil that people do. (4)
God the Father wanted him to do it. // It was God's will that he do that. (4)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to save you?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that a person will rescue someone else out of a dangerous situation. In this case, Jesus came to mankind to rescue them from an eternity in Hell.
Questions.Note: See "save" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think it means for someone to deliver you?

Questions.Q: What do you think "this present evil age" means?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: This present evil age means that it is the time in which we now live, where sin and evil are present/people do evil things. (See "age" in KBT in the "world" entry.)

Questions.Q: What does a person do when he sins?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He deliberately keeps on doing those things which please himself and which displease God.
Questions.Note: See "sin" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What [should] people give to God for doing that?
Questions.A: They should give him glory forever. (5)
Questions.Alternative: What should people give to God for doing that?
What people give to God for doing that?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when you give glory to someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: When you give glory to someone, you reveal the greatness of that person, you demonstrate or show openly that someone is worthy of receiving honor.
Questions.Note: See "glory" in KBT.

Section.heading: Galatians 1:6-10 Paul warned the Christians not to follow any other gospel than the one that he gave to them.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what Paul said in these verses.
Questions.A: Paul was concerned that the Christians [in Galatia] were leaving the true gospel and were turning to a different gospel. (6)

Questions.Q: What do you think the gospel is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The word "gospel" is a translation of the Greek noun euangelion. In the New Testament the noun euangelion is used in a restricted sense. It does not mean just any kind of good news, but specifically the good news or joyful report that God has made a way to save sinful human beings. In the New Testament it is always used with this one sense and is usually translated in the RSV and most modern English versions as "gospel".
Questions.Note: See "gospel" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What was the reason that Paul was surprised?
Questions.A: He was surprised that they were quickly deserting the one [God] who called them. (6)

Questions.Q: What was the reason that they turned from God?
Questions.A: They turned from God to accept a different gospel. (6)

Questions.Q: How did God call them?
Questions.A: He called them by means of Christ's great kindness to them. (6)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say about the different gospel?
Questions.A: He said that it was no gospel at all. (7)

Questions.Q: What were some people trying to do with this different gospel?
Questions.A: They were trying to confuse the Christians/believers
and pervert/change the gospel of Christ. (7)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say will happen to anyone, including an angel from heaven, for preaching a different gospel than the one he taught them?
Questions.A: They will be eternally condemned [by God]. (8)

Questions.Q: What do you know about angels?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Angels are spiritual messengers who either deliver a message to humans, carry out God's will, praise God, or guard God's throne.
Questions.Note: See "angel" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Where do you think heaven is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It is that part of God's creation above the earth and the waters, including "air" and "space," and serves as home for God and the spirits who serve Him.
Questions.Note: See "heaven" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think someone is doing when he preaches?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: When someone preaches, he is proclaiming the gospel to those who are listening. This also means that a person urges others to accept or reject what he is preaching.

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to condemn someone else?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that someone pronounces someone else guilty, with the clear implication that the person will be punished for what he did. (See "condemn" in KBT in the "judge, judgment" entry.)

Questions.Q: Do you think an angel from heaven could/would preach a [distorted] message [contrary to the true gospel that Paul was preaching]? // What would it tell you if an angel from heaven preached a message contrary to the truth?
Questions.A: One of God's true angels would never do this. If a being appeared as an angel and spoke false words, this would be a demon/evil spirit.
Questions.Note: Here Paul's use of this expression is essentially supposing the impossible, since a good angel "from heaven" could never do this (though a person could mistakenly suppose that he had seen an angelic messenger, rather than a demonic one).

Questions.Q: What did Paul tell them again?
Questions.A: He told them again that anyone will be eternally condemned [by God], if they preach a gospel to them other than the one they already accepted. (9)

Questions.Q: What did Paul tell them he would not be doing if he was trying to please men?
Questions.A: He said that he would not be a servant of Christ. (10)
Questions.Alternative: What did Paul tell them he would be doing if he was trying to please men?
What did Paul tell them he would not be if he was trying to please men?
If Paul were trying to please men, then what?

Questions.Q: What do you think a servant does?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A servant is a person who is required to work for another and obey him. Servants are usually paid for their work, while slaves are not paid.

Section.heading: Galatians 1:11-24 Paul told the Galatians that the gospel that he preached is from Jesus Christ not from man. God called him to preach this gospel.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what Paul said in these verses.
Questions.A: Paul told them that God chose him. (15)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say about the gospel he preached to them?
Questions.A: He said that people did not make it up. (11)

Questions.Q: What was the reason that Paul said that the gospel he preached was not made by people?
Questions.A: He said that because he did not hear it from any man and because no man taught him this gospel. (12)

Questions.Q: Who told Paul about the gospel?
Questions.A: Jesus Christ told/caused Paul to know the gospel. (12)

Questions.Q: What did Paul do to the believers when he was involved in Judaism/the Jewish religion?
Questions.A: He violently persecuted the believers and tried to destroy them. (13)
Questions.Alternative: What did Paul do to the believers when he was involved in Judaism?
What did Paul do to the believers when he was involved in the Jewish religion?

Questions.Q: What do you know about Jews [and Judaism]?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "Jews" refers to the descendants of Abraham through his son Isaac. A Jew is a member of the people of Israel. He is committed to the Jewish religious system. All male Jews were circumcised on the 8th day after their birth, and that was a mark of being a Jew. The Jewish religious tradition involved adherence to the law of Moses. (See "Jew" in KBT in the "Israel" entry.)
Questions.Alternative: What do you know about Jews?
What do you know about Jews and Judaism?
What do you know about Jews and the Jewish religious system?

Questions.Q: What did Paul say about the way he formerly followed Judaism/the Jewish religion?
Questions.A: He obeyed the rules of Judaism better than other Jews who were his own age.
Also he was very zealous for the traditions of his ancestors/the Jewish nation. (14)
Questions.Alternative: What did Paul say about the way he formerly followed Judaism?
What did Paul say about the way he formerly followed the Jewish religion?

Questions.Q: What purpose did God have for Paul, even though he was persecuting the believers?
Questions.A: God wanted Paul to serve him. (15)

Questions.Q: When did God decide to choose Paul to serve him?
Questions.A: He chose Paul before he was born. (15)

Questions.Q: What was the reason that God chose Paul?
Questions.A: God chose Paul to show his grace/favor to him. (15)

Questions.Q: What was the reason that God made known/revealed his son to Paul?
Questions.A: God revealed/made known his son to Paul so that Paul could preach to the Gentiles about his son. (16)
Questions.Alternative: What was the reason that God made known his son to Paul?
What was the reason that God revealed his son to Paul?

Questions.Q: Who do you think the Gentiles are?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "Gentiles" is usually the English translation of the Greek ta ethnê or related forms. From the viewpoint of the Jews, "Gentiles" referred to all people who were not Jews and who were, therefore, not God's chosen people and did not worship him. When used from the viewpoint of Christians (as frequently in the epistles of Paul), the term often referred to those who did not believe in Jesus Christ. It was also used in some contexts to refer to people of all nations.
Questions.Note: See "gentile" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did Paul say he did not do after God revealed his Son to him?
Questions.A: He did not consult with any person. // He did not ask any person what to do. (16)

Questions.Q: Where did Paul not go?
Questions.A: He did not go to Jerusalem to see those who were apostles before him. (17)

Questions.Q: Where did Paul go?
Questions.A: He went into [the country of] Arabia. (17)

Questions.Q: Where did Paul go after he had been to Arabia?
Questions.A: He returned to [the city of] Damascus. (17)

Questions.Q: How long was it before Paul went up to Jerusalem to visit Peter?
Questions.A: It was three years later before/when he went there. (18)

Questions.Q: How long did Paul stay with him?
Questions.A: He stayed there fifteen days. (18)

Questions.Q: Whom else did Paul see at that time?
Questions.A: He saw only James, the brother of the Lord. (19)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say to the Galatians in verse 20?
Questions.A: He told them that God knew that, what he was writing to them, was not a lie. (20)

Questions.Q: Where did Paul go after he had been to Jerusalem visiting Peter?
Questions.A: He went to [the land of] Syria, and also to [the land of] Cilicia. (21)

Questions.Q: Which believers in [the land of] Judea knew Paul?
Questions.A: None of the believers in Judea knew him. (22)
Questions.Alternative: Which believers in the land of Judea knew Paul?
Which believers in Judea knew Paul?

Questions.Q: How did the people in Judea learn about Paul?
Questions.A: They heard others say that he used to persecute them/the believers, but now he was preaching that people should trust in Christ. Before he preached about Christ, he tried to destroy those who believed in Christ. (23)

Questions.Q: When the believers in Judea heard that Paul was preaching the gospel, what did they do?
Questions.A: They praised God because of what he had done through Paul. (24)

Questions.Q: What do you think it meant for them to praise God?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: They were praising God by expressing a prayer of thanks and adoration to him for his goodness to them. (See "praise" in KBT in the "bless" entry.)

Section.heading: Galatians 2:1-10 James, Peter and John accepted Paul as an apostle.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what Paul said in these verses.
Questions.A: Paul convinced the Christian leaders in Jerusalem that God had called him to preach to the Gentiles. (9)

Questions.Q: When was the next time Paul went to Jerusalem?
Questions.A: It was fourteen years later when he went there again. (1)
Questions.Note: The T.H. suggests it was fourteen years after his last visit to Jerusalem.

Questions.Q: Who went with Paul on that trip?
Questions.A: Barnabas and Titus went with him. (1)

Questions.Q: What was the reason that Paul went to Jerusalem at that time?
Questions.A: He went there because [God] revealed to him that he should go. (2)

Questions.Q: With whom did he meet in Jerusalem?
Questions.A: He met privately with the leaders of the believers. (2)

Questions.Q: What was the purpose of that meeting?
Questions.A: The purpose was to tell them about the gospel that he preached among the Gentiles/those who were not Jews. (2)

Questions.Q: What was the reason that it was important to Paul that the church leaders know what he was preaching to the Gentiles?
Questions.A: If the leaders did not know what he was preaching, they might disapprove/hinder his work. (2)
Questions.Note: See the T.H. for comments on this verse.

Questions.Q: What was Titus not compelled/forced [by the church leaders] to do?
Questions.A: He was not compelled/forced [by the church leaders] to be circumcised. (3)
Questions.Alternative: What was Titus not compelled by the church leaders to do?
What was Titus not forced by the church leaders to do?
What was Titus not compelled to do?
What was Titus not forced to do?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to circumcise someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that someone removes the foreskin of the male genital. Traditionally the father, or someone else, would perform this on his son on the 8th day after his birth and that was a mark of being a Jew. (See "the circumcised" in KBT in the "Israel, Jew, Hebrew" entry.)

Questions.Q: Who had come into their group?
Questions.A: Some men who said they were fellow believers, but who were not believers had come into their group. (4)

Questions.Q: How had they come in?
Questions.A: They infiltrated/slipped in secretly to the group. (4)

Questions.Q: What was the reason that they came into the group?
Questions.A: They came to find out if the believers [were adhering to the Jewish system of laws]. (4)

Questions.Q: What did these men want to do to the believers?
Questions.A: They wanted to make the believers adhere to/slaves of [the Jewish system of laws]. (4)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to be a slave of someone/something?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means the person is totally responsible to and dependent upon another person or the person has become completely subservient to a dominating influence.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think it means for someone to be a slave of someone?
What do you think it means for someone to be a slave of something?
What do you think it means for someone to be a slave?

Questions.Q: How did Paul respond to those false believers?
Questions.A: He strongly resisted them. (5)

Questions.Q: What was the reason that Paul rejected what they wanted to do?
Questions.A: He rejected it so that the believers could continue to believe the true gospel. (5)

Questions.Q: What was Paul's attitude about those who seemed to be important leaders?
Questions.A: He was not influenced by their position/status, since God does not judge by external appearance. (6)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for a person to judge someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means someone/a judge will determine if a person is guilty or not of committing a crime. He does this by assessing the evidence connected to the person and what he may have done.
Questions.Note: See "judge" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did Paul say those leaders [James, Peter/Cephas and John] recognized?
Questions.A: They recognized that [God] had chosen Paul to preach the gospel to the Gentiles, just as [God] had chosen Peter to preach the gospel to the Jews. (7)
Questions.Alternative: What did Paul say those leaders James, Peter and John recognized?
What did Paul say those leaders James, Cephas and John recognized?
What did Paul say those leaders recognized?

Questions.Q: How did they realize that [God] had chosen Paul to preach to the Gentiles?
Questions.A: They realized that God, who chose Peter to be an apostle to the Jews, was also the one who chose Paul to be an apostle to the Gentiles. (8)
They saw God at work in Paul. (8)
James, Peter/Cephas, and John perceived that God had given Paul grace [for this ministry to the Gentiles]. (9)
Questions.Alternative: How did they realize that God had chosen Paul to preach to the Gentiles?
How did they realize that Paul had been chosen to preach to the Gentiles?

Questions.Q: What did Paul say about James and Peter/Cephas and John?
Questions.A: They were leaders. (9)
Questions.Alternative: What did Paul say about James and Peter and John?
What did Paul say about James and Cephas and John?

Questions.Q: What was their attitude about Paul's work?
Questions.A: They recognized that [God] had especially chosen Paul to do that work. (9)

Questions.Q: What did they do after they recognized that?
Questions.A: They accepted Paul and Barnabas as fellow-workers. (9)
They agreed that Paul and Barnabas should [preach] to the Gentiles, while they [James, Peter/Cephas and John] should [preach] to the Jews. (9)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to have fellowship with someone else?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The word "fellowship" refers to a relationship between two or more people, all of whom have something in common or all of whom participate in the same activity.
Questions.Note: The same Greek word may also be translated, in certain contexts, as "sharing", "participation", or "partnership". (See "fellowship" in KBT.)

Questions.Q: What did the leaders ask Paul and Barnabas to do?
Questions.A: They asked them to help the poor [Christians living in Jerusalem]. (10)

Questions.Q: How did Paul feel about helping the poor?
Questions.A: He was eager to do it. (10)

Section.heading: Galatians 2:11-21 Paul showed Peter that he was wrong in the way he treated the Gentile Christians.

Questions.Q: Tell, in your own words, the basic meaning (theme) of what Paul said in these verses.
Questions.A: He told them about the time he rebuked Peter for being afraid of the criticism of the Jews. (11-12)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say happened when Peter/Cephas came to [the city of] Antioch?
Questions.A: Paul opposed him. (11)
Questions.Alternative: What did Paul say happened when Peter came to the city of Antioch?
What did Paul say happened when Cephas came to the city of Antioch?
What did Paul say happened when Peter came to Antioch?
What did Paul say happened when Cephas came to Antioch?

Questions.Q: What was the reason that Paul did that?
Questions.A: Paul opposed Peter, because Peter was clearly wrong. (11)

Questions.Q: What had Peter/Cephas done that was wrong?
Questions.A: Peter had been eating with the Gentiles, until some men came from James. Then he would not eat with them any more. (12)
Questions.Alternative: What had Peter done that was wrong?
What had Cephas done that was wrong?

Questions.Q: What was the reason that Peter did that?
Questions.A: He was afraid that the [Jewish people] would criticize him for eating with people who were not circumcised. (12)

Questions.Q: When Peter/Cephas did that, what did the other Jewish believers do?
Questions.A: They, too, acted as hypocrites. (13)
Questions.Alternative: When Peter did that, what did the other Jewish believers do?
When Cephas did that, what did the other Jewish believers do?

Questions.Q: What do you think a hypocrite does?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A hypocrite is a person who acts contrary to what he knows he should do.

Questions.Q: What did Barnabas do after he saw the others do those hypocritical things?
Questions.A: He felt that he must do the same as all the others and follow them in their hypocritical actions. (13)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say the Jewish believers were doing [when they would no longer eat with the Gentiles]?
Questions.A: They were not being consistent with what they knew about the gospel. (14)
Questions.Alternative: What did Paul say the Jewish believers were doing when they would no longer eat with the Gentiles?
What did Paul say the Jewish believers were doing?

Questions.Q: What did Paul say to Peter/Cephas in front of all the others?
Questions.A: He told Peter that he was a Jew, but he lived like the Gentiles lived [who did not follow the Jewish customs]. So why was he forcing the Gentiles to live like the Jews lived? (14)
Questions.Alternative: What did Paul say to Peter in front of all the others?
What did Paul say to Cephas in front of all the others?

Questions.Q: Paul talked about Gentile sinners. What do you think he meant?
Questions.A: Jews considered the Gentiles to be sinners because they did not follow the laws of Moses. (15)
Questions.Note: The respondent would not be able to give this answer from this verse alone. See "Gentile" in KBT & the T.H. for more details.

Questions.Q: What did Paul say all Jewish believers know?
Questions.A: They know that [God] accepts a person/looks on a person as right because that person has believed in Jesus Christ. (15-16)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to be justified?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that a person is declared to be accepted by God. This restores the relationship broken by sin, especially with reference to human beings being justified by God (i.e. being declared by God to be accepted by him, to be in good standing with him) on the basis of their faith in Christ. (See "justified" in KBT in the "just" entry.)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to observe the law?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It is usually used to refer to those who are trying to become acceptable to God by doing what the laws given through Moses command.
Questions.Note: See "law" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think it means to do the works of the law?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to have faith in someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Faith is the quality of trusting someone. It is the act of wholeheartedly and steadfastly believing in the existence, power, and benevolence of a supreme being. (See "faith" in KBT in the "believe, believing, belief, faith, trust" entry.)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say may/would be realized when they strived to be accepted by God through Christ?
Questions.A: They realized that the Jews would consider them as sinners, since now, they did not follow [the Jewish laws]. (17)
Questions.Alternative: What did Paul say may be realized when they strived to be accepted by God through Christ?
What did Paul say would be realized when they strived to be accepted by God through Christ?
What did Paul say may be realized when they strove to be accepted by God through Christ?
What did Paul say would be realized when they strove to be accepted by God through Christ?

Questions.Q: What did Paul say that Christ did not promote?
Questions.A: He said that Christ did not promote sin. (17)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say would prove that he is a lawbreaker?
Questions.A: It would be proven that he is a lawbreaker, if he tried again to follow the [Jewish laws]. (18)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say about the law?
Questions.A: He was no longer controlled by the law, since he knew that the law could not save him from his sins. (19)

Questions.Q: Since Paul was no longer controlled by the law, what did he want to do?
Questions.A: Since he was no longer controlled by the law, Paul wanted to live for God. (19)

Questions.Q: What happened when Christ was crucified?
Questions.A: Paul said it was as though he died with Christ on his cross. (20)

Questions.Q: What do you think happened to someone when the soldiers crucified them?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: During this time Roman soldiers would crucify someone by either tying their arms to a crossbeam or pounding nails through their wrists. Then the person was pulled up on an upright post, which was planted in the ground, and tied or nailed to it at his ankles. (See "crucify" in KBT in the "cross" entry.)

Questions.Q: What do you know about the cross?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The cross consisted of two pieces of wood. One piece was a thick wooden post which was planted upright in the ground. The other piece was the cross-beam, which was fastened across the upright post so that it formed a + or T shape.
Questions.Note: See "cross" in KBT.

Questions.Q: How did Paul live now?
Questions.A: He wanted Christ to live in him/to control his life. (20)

Questions.Q: What do you think life means in this verse?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Life in this verse means the state of being alive physically. // The way he was living.

Questions.Q: What did Paul say about the Son of God?
Questions.A: He said that the Son of God loved him, and he died for him. (20)

Questions.Q: Who do you think the Son of God is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The Son of God is Jesus. (See "son of god" in KBT in the "Christ" entry.)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when someone loves someone else?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The person who loves another person seeks the good of that person. His attitude to the one whom he loves is an attitude of persistent and selfless goodwill.
Questions.Note: See "love" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did Paul say about what God had done for him?
Questions.A: He said that he did not set it aside/reject it. (21)

Questions.Q: What is a person actually saying when he says it is necessary to follow all the law in order to be accepted by God?
Questions.A: He is saying that Christ died for nothing. (21)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to be righteous?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that a person is in a state of having been accepted by God as right in his eyes. (See "righteous" in KBT in the "just, justify..." entry.)

Section.heading: Galatians 3:1-14 Paul asked the Galatians if they received the Spirit of God by doing the works of the law or by believing the gospel.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what Paul said in these verses.
Questions.A: Paul reminded the Galatians that all that God did for them was because they believed [in Christ], not because they followed the law. (2, 14)

Questions.Q: How did Paul describe the Galatians?
Questions.A: He called them foolish. // He said they were foolish. (1)

Questions.Q: What did Paul ask them?
Questions.A: He asked them who had deceived them/led them astray. (1)
Questions.Note: This is a rhetorical question. It may be translated as a statement in some languages.

Questions.Q: What had Paul described to them?
Questions.A: He described to them how Jesus Christ had died on the cross. (1)

Questions.Q: What did Paul ask them about receiving the Spirit?
Questions.A: He asked them if they had received the Spirit by observing the law, or if they had received the Spirit by believing what they heard [about Jesus Christ]. (2)
Questions.Note: This is a rhetorical question.

Questions.Q: Who do you think the Spirit is in this verse?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The Spirit is the Spirit of God.
Questions.Note: See "spirit" in KBT.

Questions.Q: How did their new life as believers begin?
Questions.A: They began their new life as believers with the Spirit present in them. (3)

Questions.Q: What did Paul ask about how they were living as Christians?
Questions.A: He asked them if they were trying to do good as God desires through their own efforts. (3)
Questions.Note: This is a rhetorical question.

Questions.Q: What did Paul ask them about the things they suffered as Christians?
Questions.A: He asked them if they suffered for nothing. (4)
Questions.Note: This is a rhetorical question.

Questions.Q: What did Paul ask them about the reason that God gave them his Spirit and did miracles among them?
Questions.A: He asked them if God had done this because they observed the law or because they believed what they heard [about Jesus Christ]. (5)
Questions.Note: This is a rhetorical question.

Questions.Q: What do you think a miracle is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The Greek word dunamis usually means "power." In the plural it can mean "acts of power, powerful deeds" and is used in the New Testament to refer to miracles. RSV sometimes translates this word as "mighty work" and sometimes as "miracle".
Questions.Note: See "miracle" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What was the reason that God accepted Abraham as righteous?
Questions.A: God did that because Abraham believed God. (6)

Questions.Q: What does someone do when he believes?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He puts his trust and commitment in another person.
Questions.Note: See "believe" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Who did Paul say are the real descendants of Abraham?
Questions.A: Those people who believe [in God] are his descendants. (7)

Questions.Q: What important thing can a person read in the scriptures that was predicted a long time ago?
Questions.A: A person can read in the scriptures where it was predicted that God would accept the Gentiles as right with him because they believed [in him]. (8)

Questions.Q: What do you think Paul was referring to as "scripture"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The scriptures are the contents of the Old Testament as God gave them to men to write down.
Questions.Note: See "scripture" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did the writer announce/tell in the scriptures to Abraham?
Questions.A: The writer told Abraham, in the scriptures, that he would be used [by God] to bless/to show favor to people in all nations/people everywhere. (8)
Questions.Note: The scripture is from Genesis 12:3.
Questions.Alternative: What did the writer announce in the scriptures to Abraham?
What did the writer tell in the scriptures to Abraham?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to bless someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means to make someone happy, to give good fortune or satisfaction, to confer prosperity upon someone.
Questions.Note: See "bless, blessed, blessing" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What does the word "nation" mean to you?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "Nation" refers to the people who make up that nation. This community of people possesses a more or less defined territory of land and government. (See "nation" in KBT in the "gentile" entry.)

Questions.Q: Who is blessed [by God] along with Abraham?
Questions.A: All those who have faith [in God] are blessed [by God]. (9)
Questions.Alternative: Who is blessed by God along with Abraham?
Who is blessed along with Abraham?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that everyone, who relies on observing the law, cursed [by God]?
Questions.A: They are cursed because [Moses] wrote long ago that [God] will punish anyone who does not do everything written in the book of the law. (10)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that everyone, who relies on observing the law, cursed by God?
What is the reason that everyone, who relies on observing the law, cursed?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for God to put a curse on someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that God will pronounce a punishment on someone or condemn a person to be cut off from all of God's blessings. (See "curse" in KBT in the "bless, blessed, blessing" entry.)

Questions.Q: Whom does the law justify?
Questions.A: No one is justified by the law. (11)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that this is true?
Questions.A: This is true because the one God accepts as right with him will live by believing [God]. (11)

Questions.Q: On what is the law not based?
Questions.A: It is not based on believing [God]. (12)

Questions.Q: What will a person have to do who depends on the law?
Questions.A: That person must do everything the law requires him to do. (12)

Questions.Q: From what did Christ redeem them?
Questions.A: He redeemed them from being punished by [God]. (13)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to redeem someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: With only one or two exceptions in the New Testament, the words "to redeem", "redemption", "ransom" refer to Christ's action in giving up his own life in order that God forgive the sins of those who believe in him.
Questions.Note: See "redeem" in KBT.

Questions.Q: How did Christ do that?
Questions.A: [God] punished Christ instead of punishing people. (13)

Questions.Q: What does the scripture say about anyone who is hanged/killed on a tree?
Questions.A: It states that anyone who is hanged/killed on a tree is cursed [by God]. (13)
Questions.Alternative: What does the scripture say about anyone who is hanged on a tree?
What does the scripture say about anyone who is killed on a tree?

Questions.Q: What was the reason that Christ did that?
Questions.A: He did it so that [God] might also give the same blessing to the Gentiles that he had promised to Abraham. (14)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to make a promise?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that someone will make a declaration that he will do, or refrain from doing, something specified. (See "promise" in KBT in the "covenant" entry.)

Questions.Q: What did God promise to Abraham?
Questions.A: He promised that they would receive the Spirit. (14)

Questions.Q: How would they receive what he promised?
Questions.A: They would receive the Spirit because they believed [God]. (14)

Section.heading: Galatians 3:15-25 God's promise can not be changed by a later law.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what Paul said in these verses.
Questions.A: God gave his blessing to Abraham because of the promise he had made with Abraham not because Abraham adhered to/followed the law. (18)

Questions.Q: What example did Paul give in verse 15?
Questions.A: The example he gave is that no one can set aside/break or add to a human covenant. (15)

Questions.Q: What do you think a covenant is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A covenant is a strong, binding agreement made between two people, an act in which they commit themselves to one another. In the case of the covenant which God has made with his people, God is the initiator of the covenant; it is he who makes a promise and states the terms. (It is not a negotiated agreement between two equal parties in which terms are discussed until agreed upon.)
Questions.Note: See "covenant" in KBT.

Questions.Q: With whom did God make his promise?
Questions.A: He made his promise to Abraham and to his descendant. (16)

Questions.Q: To which descendant was Paul referring?
Questions.A: He was referring to Christ. (16)

Questions.Q: God made a promise to Abraham. God also gave the law to his people, Israel. Which did he do first?
Questions.A: He gave his promise to Abraham first. (17)

Questions.Q: How many years later did [God] give the law to his people?
Questions.A: He gave it to them 430 years later. (17)
Questions.Alternative: How many years later did God give the law to his people?
How many years later did the law come?
How many years later did God's people receive the law?
How many years later did the Jews receive the law?

Questions.Q: What effect did the law have on the promise that God made with Abraham?
Questions.A: The law had no effect on the promise. // It did not set aside/break the promise. (17)

Questions.Q: What problem did Paul point out if they expected to receive what God had promised by following the law?
Questions.A: Then it no longer depended on [God's] promise. (18)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say was the purpose of the law?
Questions.A: He said the purpose was to show people what wrong doing is. (19)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to commit a transgression?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that a person disobeys a law or custom. (See "transgression" in KBT in the "sin" entry.)

Questions.Q: How long was the law to be in effect?
Questions.A: It was to be in effect until that descendant of Abraham had come. (19)

Questions.Q: How did God give the law to his people?
Questions.A: Angels gave it to a mediator/go-between. (19)

Questions.Q: When is a mediator/go-between needed?
Questions.A: He is needed when two other people are involved. (20)
Questions.Alternative: When is a mediator needed?
When is a go-between needed?

Questions.Q: What do you think a mediator does?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The word mediator (Greek mesitês) means a person who stands between two people or groups of people, who have a dispute or business with each other. The mediator works until an agreement between them is accomplished.
Questions.Note: See "mediator" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did Paul ask the Galatians about the law?
Questions.A: He asked them if the law was opposed to what God promised. (21)
Questions.Note: This is a rhetorical question.

Questions.Q: What answer did Paul give for this question?
Questions.A: He said the law was absolutely not opposed. (21)
Questions.Note: This is a rhetorical question.

Questions.Q: What did Paul say would have been the result if [God] had given a law that could give life?
Questions.A: Then everyone could be put right with God by obeying the law. (21)
Questions.Alternative: What did Paul say would have been the result if God had given a law that could give life?
What did Paul say would have been the result if a law had been given that could give life?
What did Paul say would have been the result if the law could give life?

Questions.Q: What do you think righteousness means?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It is the state of having been accepted by God as right in his eyes. (See "righteousness" in KBT in the "just" entry.)

Questions.Q: What do you think this verse means by "the whole world"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: This most likely means the whole universe.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think this verse means by "everything"?
Questions.Note: See "world" in KBT.
This could also mean all those who live on the earth. See the T.H.

Questions.Q: What controls all people/mankind?
Questions.A: All mankind is under the control of sin. (22)
Questions.Alternative: What controls all people?
What controls all mankind?

Questions.Q: What was the reason that [God] did that?
Questions.A: God wanted to give people what he had promised them because they believed in Jesus Christ. (22)
Questions.Alternative: What was the reason that God did that?
What was the reason that everyone is shut up under sin?
What was the reason that everyone is under the control of sin?
What was the reason that God shut up everyone under sin?
What was the reason that God used Scripture to shut up everyone under sin?
What was the reason that God used Scripture to bring everyone under the control sin?

Questions.Q: What was the condition of people before they believed in Jesus Christ?
Questions.A: They were held prisoners by the law. // The law controlled them. (23)

Questions.Q: How long did they have to be held prisoners by the law?
Questions.A: They were held prisoners by the law until they believed in Jesus Christ. (23)

Questions.Q: What was the reason God put his law in charge of people?
Questions.A: He wanted people to believe in Jesus Christ. // He put his law in charge of people to lead them to Christ. (24)

Questions.Q: What was the reason for that?
Questions.A: The reason was so that [God] would accept people as justified because they had believed [in Christ]. (24)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that people are no longer to follow the law/be controlled by the law?
Questions.A: Now people have believed [in Christ], and they are controlled by him. (25)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that people are no longer to follow the law?
What is the reason that people are no longer to be controlled by the law?

Section.heading: Galatians 3:26-4:7 Paul told the Galatian Christians that they were all sons of God because they had believed in Jesus Christ.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what Paul said in these verses.
Questions.A: He told them that because they believed in Christ they have become sons of God. (26)

Questions.Q: What happened when people believed in Christ and were baptized?
Questions.A: They were clothed with Christ. // They had become like Christ in the kind of lives they lived. (27)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when someone is baptized?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: If a person is baptized into a person or into the name of a person, it means that he is initiated into a new relationship with that person; he becomes united with that person. Thus to be baptized into (the name of) Christ is to be brought by baptism into spiritual relationship with him.
Questions.Note: See "baptize" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What was the reason that Paul said there was no difference in them no matter who they were?
Questions.A: [God] considers all people the same, if they have believed in Christ. (28)

Questions.Q: What benefit do they have if they belong to Christ?
Questions.A: They are Abraham's descendants, if they belong to Christ and, therefore, will receive what [God] has promised. (29)

Questions.Q: To what is an heir, who is a child, just like/similar?
Questions.A: He is just like a slave. (1)
Questions.Alternative: To what is an heir, who is a child, just like?
To what is an heir, who is a child, similar?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that is true?
Questions.A: It is true because others supervise him and manage his affairs. (2)

Questions.Q: How long will he be supervised by others?
Questions.A: Others will supervise him until the time that his father decided. (2)

Questions.Q: To what did Paul say they were slaves?
Questions.A: He said they were slaves to the basic principles/rules of this world. (3)

Questions.Q: How long did that continue?
Questions.A: It continued until the time which God had decided. (4)

Questions.Q: What did God do when that time came?
Questions.A: He sent his own son [into the world]. (4)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say about the son of God?
Questions.A: He was born to a woman,
and he was subject to the law. (4)

Questions.Q: What was the reason that God sent his son into the world?
Questions.A: He sent his son to free/redeem those people who followed/were slaves to/under the law. (5)

Questions.Q: What was the reason that God wanted to free them from the law?
Questions.A: He did that so that they could become God's sons. (5)

Questions.Q: What was the reason that God sent the Holy Spirit/the spirit of his son into their hearts/lives?
Questions.A: He did that because they are his sons. (6)
Questions.Alternative: What was the reason that God sent the Holy Spirit into their hearts?
What was the reason that God sent the Holy Spirit into their lives?
What was the reason that God sent the spirit of his son into their hearts?
What was the reason that God sent the spirit of his son into their lives?

Questions.Q: What does it mean to you to talk about the "heart"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The most common use of the word "heart" in the Bible is to refer to the spiritual center or innermost part of a human being. In Hebrew and Greek "heart" is most commonly associated with thoughts and ideas.
Questions.Note: See "heart" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think it means when it says their "hearts"?
What do you think the "heart" is in this verse?

Questions.Q: What do you think "Abba" means in this verse?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "Abba" means father in Aramaic.

Questions.Q: In what way is each of them changed?
Questions.A: Each one of them is not a slave anymore.
Each one of them is now a son of God. (7)

Questions.Q: What will God do for them, since they are sons of God?
Questions.A: He will bless them. // He will favor them much. (7)

Section.heading: Galatians 4:8-20 Paul warned the Galatians not to return to the false gods that they served before they came to know God.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what Paul said in these verses.
Questions.A: He told them that, now that they knew God, they should not go back to serve/worship/be slaves of the false gods they served before. (9)
