Questions.Q: In the past in what state were they when they did not know God?
Questions.A: They served/worshiped/were slaves to false gods. (8)

Questions.Q: About what did Paul ask them, now that they knew God?
Questions.A: He asked them why they were going back to following those false gods/false teachings.
He also asked them if they wanted to become slaves of those things again. (9)

Questions.Q: What were they doing that made Paul believe that they were becoming slaves of those things/worshiping false gods/following false teachings again?
Questions.A: They were observing special days, months, seasons and years. (10)
Questions.Alternative: What were they doing that made Paul believe that they were becoming slaves of those things/worshipping false gods/following false teachings again?
What were they doing that made Paul believe that they were becoming slaves of those things again?
What were they doing that made Paul believe that they were worshiping false gods again?
What were they doing that made Paul believe that they were worshipping false gods again?
What were they doing that made Paul believe that they were following false teachings again?

Questions.Q: What worried Paul about them?
Questions.A: He was worried that he may have wasted his time on them. (11)

Questions.Q: What did Paul strongly ask them to do?
Questions.A: He asked them to become like him/believe as he did. (12)

Questions.Q: What had Paul done?
Questions.A: He had become like [they used to be by being free from following the law]. (12)
Questions.Note: See comments on this verse in T.N.

Questions.Q: How had they treated Paul in the past?
Questions.A: They treated him well. (12)

Questions.Q: What physical condition did Paul have that caused him to preach the gospel to them the first time?
Questions.A: He had been sick at that time. (13)

Questions.Q: How did they treat him at that time, even though his sickness was a trial to them?
Questions.A: They did not despise him because of his illness.
They welcomed him in the same way they would welcome an angel of God or even Jesus Christ. (14)

Questions.Q: What had been their attitude toward Paul when he was sick?
Questions.A: He said they had been happy/joyful.
He said, that if it were possible, they would have taken out their own eyes and given them to him. (15)

Questions.Q: What was the reason that it now appeared as though they treated him differently than when he was sick?
Questions.A: That was the case, because Paul asked them what had happened to their joy/happiness. (15)

Questions.Q: About what did Paul ask them?
Questions.A: He asked them if he had become their enemy. (16)

Questions.Q: What was the reason that he asked them that question?
Questions.A: He asked them that, because he told them what was true. (16)

Questions.Q: What was the attitude of those other people/false teachers toward the Galatians?
Questions.A: They showed an interest in them, but their intentions were not good. (17)
Questions.Alternative: What was the attitude of those other people toward the Galatians?
What was the attitude of those false teachers toward the Galatians?

Questions.Q: What was the real purpose of those false teachers?
Questions.A: They wanted to alienate the Galatians from Paul, so that the Galatians would follow them/their teachings/those false teachers. (17)

Questions.Q: When did Paul say it was good to have an interest in someone?
Questions.A: It is good to have an interest in someone when the purpose is good. (18)

Questions.Q: When did Paul say they should have an interest in someone/be zealous for someone?
Questions.A: They should always be interested in someone/be zealous for someone and not just when that person is present with them. (18)
Questions.Note: The T.H. states that the object "of the interest" could be the Galatians, then the subject could be either Paul or men in general. If the object "of the interest" was Paul, then the subject would have to be the Galatians.
Questions.Alternative: When did Paul say they should have an interest in someone?
When did Paul say they should be zealous for someone?

Questions.Q: Whom did Paul call his "dear children"?
Questions.A: He called the Galatian believers his dear children. (19)

Questions.Q: How did Paul feel about the Galatians?
Questions.A: He said that he felt the same kind of pain for them as a woman has pain during childbirth. (19)

Questions.Q: What did Paul desire for them?
Questions.A: He desired that they would become like Christ. (19)

Questions.Q: What did Paul wish he could do?
Questions.A: He wished that he could be there with them. (20)

Questions.Q: What was the reason that Paul wished he could be there with them?
Questions.A: He wanted to be there with them, so that he could change his attitude toward them. (20)
Questions.Note: The T.H. states that he wanted to change his attitude from one that was severe to one that was more gentle.

Questions.Q: How was he feeling about them?
Questions.A: He was worried about them. (20)

Section.heading: Galatians 4:21-31 Hagar represented slavery and Sarah represented freedom.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what Paul said in these verses.
Questions.A: The story of Abraham and his two wives represents/illustrates two different covenants. (22-24)

Questions.Q: To whom was Paul talking in these verses?
Questions.A: He was talking to the Galatians who wanted to follow the law. (21)

Questions.Q: What did he ask them?
Questions.A: He asked them if they understood what the law really said. (21)

Questions.Q: What story from scripture did Paul tell them?
Questions.A: He told them the story of Abraham and his two sons. (22)

Questions.Q: What kind of mother did each of those sons have?
Questions.A: One son was born to a slave woman,
and the other son was born to a free woman (one who was not a slave). (22)

Questions.Q: What were the circumstances under which each son was born?
Questions.A: The son of the slave woman was born just as anyone else is born, [not as a result of God's promise].
The son of the free woman was born as the result of the promise [God had made to Abraham and Sarah]. (23)
Questions.Note: God had promised Abraham and Sarah that they would have a son in their old age, when they were physically incapable of having children.

Questions.Q: What was the reason that Paul told them this story?
Questions.A: He used it as an illustration. (24)

Questions.Q: What did the two women represent?
Questions.A: They represented two different covenants. (24)

Questions.Q: What was the name of the slave woman?
Questions.A: Hagar was the name of the slave woman. (24)

Questions.Q: What did the slave woman represent?
Questions.A: She represented the covenant [God] made at Mount Sinai. (24)

Questions.Q: What happened to her children?
Questions.A: They became slaves, because their mother was a slave. (24)

Questions.Q: What did Hagar stand for/represent?
Questions.A: Hagar represented Mount Sinai. (25)
Questions.Alternative: What did Hagar stand for?
What did Hagar represent?

Questions.Q: Where is Mount Sinai?
Questions.A: It is located in [the country of] Arabia. (25)

Questions.Q: What else did Hagar represent?
Questions.A: She represented the present city of Jerusalem, which is like a slave along with all of its people, [because they follow the laws of Moses]. (25)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say about the Jerusalem that is above/is in heaven?
Questions.A: He said that Jerusalem is free/is not a slave.
He said that Jerusalem is like a mother to the believers. (26)
Questions.Alternative: What did Paul say about the Jerusalem that is above?
What did Paul say about the Jerusalem that is in heaven?

Questions.Q: Who was [God] speaking to in this scripture?
Questions.A: God was speaking to [Sarah]/a woman who was not able to bear children. (27)
Questions.Note: This scripture is from Isaiah 54:1.
Questions.Alternative: Who was God speaking to in this scripture?
To whom was God speaking in this scripture?
Who was being addressed in this scripture?
Who was being spoken to in this scripture?
To whom was this scripture spoken?
To whom was this scripture directed?

Questions.Q: What was she told to do?
Questions.A: She was told to rejoice/be happy and shout with joy. (27)

Questions.Q: What was the reason that she should rejoice?
Questions.A: She should rejoice because she will have many children. (27)

Questions.Q: In what way are believers like Isaac?
Questions.A: Isaac [was born as a result of God's] promise; so in the same way all believers [are God's children because of his] promise. (28)

Questions.Q: How did the two sons [of Abraham] treat each other?
Questions.A: The one born in the usual/ordinary way, [Hagar's son], fought with/persecuted [Isaac], the son who was born as the result of [God's promise]/what [God's] Spirit [had promised]. (29)
Questions.Alternative: How did the two sons of Abraham treat each other?
How did the two sons treat each other?

Questions.Q: What did the scripture state about the slave woman and her son? // What was stated in the scripture about the slave woman and her son?
Questions.A: It was stated in the scripture that [Abraham] should get rid of the slave woman and her son. (30)
Questions.Note: This was a quote from Genesis 21:10 where Sarah was telling Abraham to get rid of the slave woman and her son.
Questions.Alternative: What did the scripture state about the slave woman and her son?
What was stated in the scripture about the slave woman and her son?

Questions.Q: What was the reason that it was necessary to get rid of them?
Questions.A: They had to be sent away, because the son of the slave woman could not share in the inheritance with the son of the free woman. (30)

Questions.Q: What did Paul want them to learn from that illustration/all of that?
Questions.A: He wanted them to learn that believers are not like children of the slave woman. They are like children of the free woman. (31)
Questions.Alternative: What did Paul want them to learn from that illustration?
What did Paul want them to learn from all of that?

Section.heading: Galatians 5:1-12 Paul told the Galatians not to become slaves again [of the laws of Moses], but to live in the freedom that Christ had given them.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what Paul said in these verses.
Questions.A: He told them that, since Christ had set them free, they should not let themselves become slaves again [to the law]. (1)

Questions.Q: What value would Christ be to them if they allowed others to circumcise them [because they followed the laws of Moses]?
Questions.A: Christ would be of no value/no use to them at all. (2)
Questions.Alternative: What value would Christ be to them if they allowed others to circumcise them in order to follow the laws of Moses?
What did Paul warn the Galatians would happen if they became circumcised?
What did Paul warn the Galatians would happen if they followed the laws of Moses (and became circumcised)?
What did Paul warn them would happen if they became circumcised?
What did Paul warn them would happen if they allowed others to circumcise them?
What value would Christ be to them if they allowed others to circumcise them?
What value would Christ be to them if they allowed others to circumcise them because they followed the laws of Moses?
What value would Christ be to them if they allowed those who followed the laws of Moses to circumcise them?
What value would Christ be to them, if they allowed others to circumcise them [because they followed the laws of Moses]?

Questions.Q: What will those who let others circumcise them have to do?
Questions.A: They will have to obey the whole law. (3)
Questions.Alternative: What will those who become circumcised have to do?

Questions.Q: What happens to their relationship with Christ when they try to be made right/justified [with God] by obeying the law?
Questions.A: They have alienated/separated themselves from Christ. (4)
Questions.Alternative: What happens to their relationship with Christ when they try to be made right with God by obeying the law?
What happens to their relationship with Christ when they try to be made justified with God by obeying the law?
What happens to their relationship with Christ when they try to be made right by obeying the law?
What happens to their relationship with Christ when they try to be made justified by obeying the law?

Questions.Q: What is the result when they do that?
Questions.A: They reject [God's] grace. (4)

Questions.Q: For what do those, who do not depend on the law but on Christ, hope /believe?
Questions.A: They hope/believe for the time when [God] will make them righteous/right with himself. (5)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to hope in something?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means to have a desire to see something happen or to obtain something.

Questions.Q: How does [God] make them righteous?
Questions.A: He does it/that by his Spirit who is in them, because they believe in Jesus Christ. (5)
Questions.Alternative: How does God make them righteous?
How does God make people righteous?
How will God make us righteous?
How are they made righteous?

Questions.Q: What value was there for them to be circumcised or not to be circumcised?
Questions.A: There was no value in either. (6)

Questions.Q: What is the only thing that is really important?
Questions.A: The only thing that is important is when they show that they believe [in Christ] through loving [other people]. (6)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say to them?
Questions.A: He said that they were running a good race. // He said that they were doing well [in their relationship to Christ]. (7)
Questions.Note: If the "race" metaphor is used here, use follow-up questions as needed to determine whether respondent understands the metaphor. Paul is not referring to a competitive race between two groups of Christians (e.g., the circumcised and the uncircumcised).

Questions.Q: What did Paul ask them?
Questions.A: He asked them who made them stop obeying the truth/true words about God. (7)

Questions.Q: What did [God], the one who called them, not do to them? // What did God not do to them?
Questions.A: He was not the one who made them stop obeying the truth. (8)
Questions.Alternative: What did God, the one who called them, not do to them?
What did the one who called them not do to them?
What did God, who called them, not do to them?
What did God not do to them?

Questions.Q: Who had called/invited them to become his people?
Questions.A: [God] had called them. (8)
Questions.Alternative: Who had called them to become his people?
Who had invited them to become his people?

Questions.Q: Of what did Paul remind them?
Questions.A: He told them that it only takes a little yeast to make the whole batch of dough rise. // A little false teaching deceives many people. (9)

Questions.Q: About what was Paul confident?
Questions.A: He was confident that they would not take any other view/not believe anything different. (10)
Questions.Note: He may have believed that they would agree with him. According to the T.H., many translations leave the statement ambiguous.

Questions.Q: Of what else was Paul sure?
Questions.A: He was sure that [God] would punish the person who was leading them into confusion. (10)

Questions.Q: What did Paul ask them?
Questions.A: He asked them why people were still persecuting him if he was preaching that circumcision was necessary [to be right with God/accepted by God]. (11)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say would be true, if he really were preaching that circumcision was necessary?
Questions.A: If circumcision were necessary, then the cross would no longer be a problem/stumbling block. // If circumcision were necessary, then his preaching about the death of Christ would no longer be a problem for the Jew. (11)
Questions.Note: See comments in the T.H.

Questions.Q: What did Paul wish those false teachers would do to themselves?
Questions.A: He wished they would go all the way and emasculate/castrate themselves. (12)

Section.heading: Galatians 5:13-26 Paul told the Galatians not to let their freedom be a reason to indulge in their physical desires; but they should be led by the Spirit and serve one another.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what Paul said in these verses.
Questions.A: Paul told them that they were called/invited [by God] to be free [from the law].
He said that since they had this freedom, they should not think that they could let their physical desires control them.
He told them they should serve one another, because they love one another. (13)

Questions.Q: How did Paul say the whole law was summed up/fulfilled/completed by people?
Questions.A: The whole law was fulfilled/completed by people when they loved other people as they loved themselves. (14)
Questions.Alternative: How did Paul say the whole law was summed up by people?
How did Paul say the whole law was fulfilled by people?
How did Paul say the whole law was completed by people?

Questions.Q: About what did Paul warn them?
Questions.A: He warned them that, if they kept quarreling with each other, they would destroy each other. (15)

Questions.Q: What did he tell them to do in order to avoid satisfying their bad/evil desires?
Questions.A: He told them to allow the Spirit to direct their lives. (16)
Questions.Alternative: What did he tell them to do in order to avoid satisfying their bad desires?
What did he tell them to do in order to avoid satisfying their evil desires?

Questions.Q: How do the Spirit and our human evil desires react?
Questions.A: They oppose each other/they are enemies. (17)

Questions.Q: What are they not able to do as a result of this conflict between the Spirit and their evil desires?
Questions.A: They are not able to do what they want to do. (17)

Questions.Q: What do they need to do with the law, if they allow the Spirit to lead them?
Questions.A: They are no longer under the law. // They no longer have to do what the law states [to be accepted by God]. (18)

Questions.Q: What sins did Paul mention in verses 19-21?
Questions.A: The first three are sexual sins: sexual immorality, impurity, debauchery/sensuality (indecent conduct);
The next two are religious sins: idolatry, witchcraft/sorcery;

The next eight sins have to do with their relationships with each other: hatred, strife/discord (lack of harmony or agreement between people), jealousy, fits of rage, selfish ambition, dissensions (quarrels which produce divisions between people), divisions (people separate themselves into parties, combinations or cliques), envy;
The last two specific sins are group sins characterized by a loss of self-control: drunkenness, orgies.
This is an open list, since the writer recognizes that there are many other similar sins.

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to commit sexual immorality?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: This is a general word referring to any kind of unlawful sexual intercourse. (See "immorality" in KBT in the "sin" entry.)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to do things that are impure?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that the person does sinful things that contaminate him. These things make the person unfit for God's presence. (See "impure" in KBT in the "unclean" entry.)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when someone practices idolatry?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that a person gives respect and devotion to a physical object as a god. The idol can be a representation or symbol of a deity or any other being or a thing made or used as an idol of worship.

Questions.Q: What did Paul warn them about doing those things?
Questions.A: He told them that people who practice those things will not inherit the kingdom of God. (21)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to inherit the kingdom of God?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In ordinary English the word "inherit" means "to receive something belonging to your father after he dies". But in the use of the term in this passage, where something is inherited from God, there is no thought of anyone dying. The meaning is "to receive something that God has promised to give you, provided that you fulfill certain conditions". To inherit the kingdom of God a Christian/believer enjoys having God rule over him.
Questions.Note: See "kingdom of God" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did Paul tell them the fruit of the Spirit is?
Questions.A: He told them the fruit of the Spirit is:
love/the Spirit causes people to love other people,
joy/the Spirit causes people to be very happy,
peace/the Spirit causes people to live in peace with one another,
patience/the Spirit causes people to endure troubles/remain quiet when others persecute them,
kindness/the Spirit causes people to be kind to one another,
goodness/the Spirit causes people to be good to one another,
faithfulness/the Spirit causes people to conduct themselves in such a way that people trust them,
gentleness/the Spirit causes people to not be harsh with one another,
and self-control/the Spirit causes people to be able to say "no" to one's own evil desires. (22-23)
Questions.Note: This is a list of what the Spirit produces in the life of someone who believes in Christ.

Questions.Q: What law is against the fruit of the Spirit?
Questions.A: There is no law that is against the fruit of the Spirit. (23)

Questions.Q: What have those people, who belong to Christ Jesus, done about their sinful desires?
Questions.A: They refuse to do the evil things that they desired to do. (24)

Questions.Q: What did Paul tell them they should do, since the Spirit has given them spiritual life?
Questions.A: He told them to allow the Spirit to control their lives. // They should allow the Spirit to direct and guide them. (25)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say they must not do, if the Spirit controls their lives?
Questions.A: They must not be proud,
they must not provoke/irritate one another,
and they must not envy/be jealous of one another. (26)

Section.heading: Galatians 6:1-10 All believers in Christ should help each other when they suffer or are tempted.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what Paul said in these verses.
Questions.A: Believers fulfill/obey the law of Christ, when they help each other with their problems. (2)

Questions.Q: What did Paul tell them to do, if one of the believers had sinned/had done something wrong?
Questions.A: He said those who are guided by the Spirit should help that one return to fellowship with the Lord. (1)
Questions.Alternative: What did Paul tell them to do, if one of the believers had sinned?
What did Paul tell them to do, if one of the believers had done something wrong?

Questions.Q: What warning did Paul give to the person who helps a believer who has sinned?
Questions.A: Paul said that person should be careful that he is not tempted to sin also. (1)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to be tempted [by someone/something] to do something bad/wrong?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means to try to persuade somebody to do something sinful.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think it means to be tempted by someone to do something bad?
What do you think it means to be tempted by someone to do something wrong?
What do you think it means to be tempted by something to do something bad?
What do you think it means to be tempted by something to do something wrong?
What do you think it means to be tempted to do something bad?
What do you think it means to be tempted to do something wrong?

Questions.Q: When did Paul say someone is deceiving himself?
Questions.A: He said that a person is deceiving himself, when he thinks that he is very important, but he is not very important. (3)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say each man should do?
Questions.A: He said each man should test/judge/examine his own actions. (4)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to test something?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It generally means that a person assesses something to see if it is good or bad.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think it means to test?
What do you think it means to judge something?
What do you think it means to examine something?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that this is a good thing to do?
Questions.A: If a person does this, he will be able to evaluate his own conduct more accurately than he does when he compares himself with someone else. (4)

Questions.Q: For what did Paul say each man is responsible?
Questions.A: He said each man is responsible to carry his own load. (5)
Questions.Note: The T.H. states this "load" could refer to one's own conduct or to his own share of normal duty or to his own weakness, sin, etc.

Questions.Q: To whom was Paul speaking in this verse?
Questions.A: He was talking to anyone who was being taught the word/Christian message [by someone]. (6)

Questions.Q: What did Paul tell this person to do?
Questions.A: Paul told him to share what he has with his teacher. (6)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to share?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: When a person shares something, he gives something that he has to someone else to help him in some way. This could be some kind of material item like money, food, clothing, etc. (See "sharing" in KBT in the "fellowship" entry.)

Questions.Q: What did he tell them not to do?
Questions.A: He told them not to let themselves be deceived by anyone. (7)

Questions.Q: What reason did Paul give to show that a person cannot mock God?
Questions.A: He used the figure of a farmer: Just as a farmer reaps exactly what he plants, so the actions of a person affect the outcome/affect what happens to him. (7)

Questions.Q: What will be the result, if a person keeps doing the bad things he naturally wants to do?
Questions.A: If he continues doing those bad things, God will punish him with eternal death. (8)

Questions.Q: What will be the result, if a person keeps doing the good things the Holy Spirit wants him to do?
Questions.A: If he lets the Spirit direct his life, he will have eternal life in heaven. (8)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for a person to have eternal life?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that a person will live forever with God.
Questions.Note: This eternal life is in the spiritual realm not the physical.

Questions.Q: What did Paul tell them not to do?
Questions.A: He said they should not become tired of doing good things. (9)

Questions.Q: What was the reason they should not become tired of doing good things?
Questions.A: If they continued to do good things, they would reap a harvest/God would surely reward them. (9)

Questions.Q: What should believers do?
Questions.A: They should do good things to everyone, at every opportunity. (10)

Questions.Q: To whom should believers especially do good things?
Questions.A: Paul said they should especially do good things to those who are believers. (10)

Section.heading: Galatians 6:11-18 Paul told the Galatians that the important thing was that they live as Christ desires, because Christ died for them on the cross. Whether or not a person is circumcised is not important.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what Paul said in these verses.
Questions.A: Paul said that it did not matter if a person was circumcised or not.
What was really important was that the person was created new by God/that God had created the person new. (15)

Questions.Q: What did Paul tell them in this verse?
Questions.A: He told them that he was writing this part of the letter with his own hand. (11)
Questions.Note: According to the T.H. and T.N., there is no unanimity of opinion as to what parts of the letter are written by Paul and what parts by a scribe.

Questions.Q: What was the reason that the [false teachers] wanted the Galatians to be circumcised?
Questions.A: They wanted to be able to boast [that the Galatians had followed their teaching]. (12)
Questions.Alternative: What was the reason that the false teachers wanted the Galatians to be circumcised?
What was the reason that the wanted the Galatians to be circumcised?

Questions.Q: What was the reason they wanted others to know that?
Questions.A: They wanted others to know it, so that they would not be persecuted [by the Jews] for the cross of Christ. (12)
Questions.Note: The cross of Christ refers to the fact that Christ died on the cross and all that he accomplished by doing that.

Questions.Q: What did Paul say about those who are circumcised?
Questions.A: He said they did not obey the law, but they wanted the Galatians to be circumcised, so that they could boast about it. (13)

Questions.Q: About what did Paul say he was going to boast?
Questions.A: He said he was only going to boast about the death of Jesus Christ [on the cross]. (14)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say about the cross of Jesus Christ/what Christ accomplished on the cross?
Questions.A: He said because of what Christ accomplished on the cross, he no longer had the desires to do evil as others do/live as the world lives. (14)
Questions.Alternative: What did Paul say about the cross of Jesus Christ?
What did Paul say about what Christ accomplished on the cross?

Questions.Q: What do you think "world" means in this verse?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The world in this verse means a moral system that is opposed to God and Christ.
Questions.Note: See "world" in KBT.
The T.H. states that "world" is used here to describe a way of life in which human worth is measured by external circumstances.

Questions.Q: Whom did Paul want to have peace and mercy?
Questions.A: He wanted those who followed this rule, who are God's people, to have grace and mercy. (16)

Questions.Q: Whom do you think he meant by the "Israel of God"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: After the resurrection of Jesus Christ, Christians regarded themselves as being the true people of God, because of their belief in Jesus Christ. They therefore referred to themselves as "Israel" and regarded themselves as the spiritual successors of the people of Israel. In this sense the focus is on being the people of God; racial origin is not important.
Questions.Note: See "Israel" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when someone is merciful to someone else?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "Mercy" in the New Testament is an act of kindness by God or someone else toward people who are in need. The person (God or man) acts to relieve some kind of suffering or distress.
Questions.Note: See "mercy" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did Paul tell the Galatians to stop doing to him?
Questions.A: He told them to stop giving him trouble. (17)

Questions.Q: What was his reason for saying that?
Questions.A: He said that, because he had the scars on his body [that showed he was a slave] of Jesus/[that showed that he had suffered] as Jesus had suffered. (17)

Questions.Q: What body do you think is meant here?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In this verse Paul meant his physical body.
Questions.Note: See "body" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did Paul pray for them?
Questions.A: He prayed that the Lord Jesus would keep on helping them. (18)

Section.heading: Genesis 1:1-2:3 How God made the world.

Questions.Q: About what event is this passage? // What events are recorded/written about in this passage?
Questions.A: God created the earth, and the sky, moon, and stars/the heavens. God also created mankind.
Questions.Alternative: About what event is this passage?
What events are recorded in this passage?
What events are written about in this passage?

Questions.Q: Tell [me] the main events recorded in this passage.
Questions.A: At first, the world was empty/formless/unordered and dark. Then, God spoke and made light; and he separated day from night - which was what happened on the first day. On the second day, he made the sky. Then on the third day, he separated the oceans from the land; and he made the plants. On the fourth day, he made the sun, moon, and stars. Then he made fish, sea creatures, and birds on the fifth day. On the sixth day, he made animals and man and woman. He told them to rule over his creation. With this/At this time, his (work of) creating was finished. On the seventh day, God rested.
Questions.Note: If conducting a live interview and one of the shorter versions of the question is used, be prepared to prompt if necessary to elicit an adequate response: What was the world like? What happened on each of the days?
Questions.Alternative: Tell the main events recorded in this passage.
What were the main events recorded in this passage?
Tell me the main events recorded in this passage. What was the world like? What happened on each day?
Tell me the main events recorded in this passage. What was the world like? What happened on each of the days?

Questions.Q: Since God is the one who made the world and the animals and people, then who made God?
Questions.A: Nobody made God. He has always existed - He never had a beginning.
Questions.Note: See "God" in KBT.

Questions.Q: As you read/heard this passage, did you think the author wrote it/was writing mostly for children? Or did he write it mainly for adults?
Questions.Note: The Scriptures were written mainly for/to adults. If the translation on which you are working is intended mainly for adults, then when people read/hear it, it should not seem like a children's story.
Questions.Alternative: Did this passage sound like it was written mostly for children or for adults?
As you heard this passage, did you think the author wrote it mostly for children? Or did he write it mainly for adults?
As you heard this passage, did you think the author was writing mostly for children? Or did he write it mainly for adults?
As you read this passage, did you think the author wrote it mostly for children? Or did he write it mainly for adults?
As you read this passage, did you think the author was writing mostly for children? Or did he write it mainly for adults?

Questions.Q: At what time did these events happen?
Questions.A: These events happened in the very beginning - before there was land, or sky, or any animals or people. (1)
Questions.Alternative: When did these events happen?

Questions.Q: What is meant by "the heavens"/"the sky"?
Questions.A: This refers to the sky (and to where the stars, sun and moon are). (1)
Questions.Note: Be sure/Ensure that the respondent is not thinking specifically about "Heaven" - God's dwelling place, or the eternal resting place of God's people.
Questions.Alternative: What is meant by "the heavens" sky"?
What is meant by "the "the sky"?

Questions.Q: What was the appearance of the world at that time - in the beginning?
Questions.A: The world had no form; there was nothing on the earth; it was dark. (2)

Questions.Q: What was hovering above the waters?
Questions.A: The Spirit of God/The Power of God was hovering above the waters. (2)

Key Term Check: If the translation has "Spirit of God" here (rather than "Power of God"), be sure/ensure that the one who answers does not think that this refers to a being who is different/distinct from God (as referred to in 1:1). (See "Spirit of God" under "spirit" in KBT 2.b.)

Questions.Q: What did God make on the first day?
Questions.A: He made light. (3)

Questions.Q: What did God do to make light/to cause light to appear?
Questions.A: When he spoke, it became light/light appeared. -OR- He said that there should be light. (3)
Questions.Alternative: What did God do to cause light to appear?
What did God do to make light appear?

Questions.Q: What did God think/feel about the light that he had made?
Questions.A: He was pleased. (4)
Questions.Alternative: What did God think about the light that he had made?
What did God feel about the light that he had made?

Questions.Q: After God made light, then what did he do next?
Questions.A: He separated light from darkness (and gave them names). (4-5)

Questions.Q: Then what did God do/make on the second day?
Questions.A: He separated the water above from the water below. (6-7)
Questions.Alternative: Then what did God do on the second day?
Then what did God make on the second day?

Questions.Q: What do you think is meant by "water above" and "water below"?
Questions.Note: Probably the "water above" refers to/is the clouds or something like them. The "water below" probably refers to/might be the rivers, seas, and oceans.

Questions.Q: What did God name this thing that separates the "above-waters" from the "below-waters"?
Questions.A: He named it "Sky". (8)

Questions.Q: Now what did God do on the third day?
Questions.A: He gathered together the waters that were below the sky and land appeared. (9)

Questions.Q: What did he call the dry part? What did he name the waters?
Questions.A: The dry part he called "land/earth". He named the waters, "Lake/Sea/Ocean". (10)

Questions.Q: After God made the land/earth and the lakes/seas, how did he feel about them?
Questions.A: He was pleased with them. (10)
Questions.Alternative: After God made the land and the lakes, how did he feel about them?
After God made the land and the seas, how did he feel about them?
After God made the earth and the lakes, how did he feel about them?
After God made the earth and the seas, how did he feel about them?

Questions.Q: What did God want to happen on the land?
Questions.A: He wanted the land to produce all kinds of plants, such as grains and trees. (11-12)

Questions.Q: What did God do on the next day?
Questions.A: He made the sun, moon, and the stars. (14-16)

Questions.Q: What day was that?
Questions.A: It was the fourth day. (19)

Questions.Q: What were the sun, moon, and stars to do for/on the earth?
Questions.A: They were to shine on the earth, and to separate day from night, and to mark seasons and/or special times. (14-18)
Questions.Alternative: What were the sun, moon, and stars to do for the earth?
What were the sun, moon, and stars to do on the earth?

Questions.Q: What did God do on the fifth day?
Questions.A: He made all of the creatures that live in water; and he made all creatures that fly. (20-21)
Questions.Note: Some languages may require several terms to be all inclusive.

Questions.Q: How did God feel/think about all of the sea creatures and birds?
Questions.A: He was pleased (with them). (21)
Questions.Alternative: How did God feel about all of the sea creatures and birds?
How did God think about all of the sea creatures and birds?

Questions.Q: What did God say to the birds and (sea) creatures?
Questions.A: He blessed them -OR- He said, "May it be well with you." And he told them to increase (and/or multiply). (22)

Key Term Check: The concept "bless" occurs frequently and with different meanings. In this case, it refers to God granting his approval and his desire to see the birds and sea creatures prosper or do well. And in "blessing" the birds and sea creatures, God also gave to them the power to propagate/to pass on the gift of life that they have received from God. (See "bless" in KBT A.1.)

Questions.Q: On the sixth day, what was the first thing that God made?
Questions.A: He made all the animals/land creatures. (24-25)
Questions.Note: Some languages may require several terms to be all inclusive.

Questions.Q: After he made the animals, what else did he do on that day?
Questions.A: He made humans/human beings/people. (26-27)

Questions.Q: In what way/How did God make humans/people different from (the way he made) animals and fish and birds?
Questions.A: God made humans "like himself"/"in his image". (26-27)
Questions.Alternative: In what way did God make humans different from (the way he made) animals and fish and birds?
In what way did God make people different from (the way he made) animals and fish and birds?
How did God make humans different from (the way he made) animals and fish and birds?
How did God make people different from (the way he made) animals and fish and birds?
In what way did God make humans different from animals and fish and birds?
In what way did God make people different from animals and fish and birds?
How did God make humans different from animals and fish and birds?
How did God make people different from animals and fish and birds?

Questions.Q: Over what did God say that humans/man would have authority?
Questions.A: Humans would have authority over all creatures: fish, birds, and animals. (26-28)

Key Term Check: In 1:28, God blessed the man and woman. Similar to 1:22, this refers to God granting his approval and his desire to see the humans/human beings/people/man prosper or do well. In this case, God also gave authority to humans/man to rule over the rest of the world.
Questions.Note: See "bless" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: Over what did God say that humans would have authority?
Over what did God say that man would have authority?

Questions.Q: What did God give to humans for their food?
Questions.A: He gave them seed-bearing plants and fruits. (29)

Questions.Q: At that time, what did God give to the animals and birds for their food?
Questions.A: He gave them all the grasses/grains and other plants. (30)

Questions.Q: How did God feel about all that he had made?
Questions.A: He was very pleased. (31)

Questions.Q: How many days did it take for God to create the world? // In how many days did God create the world?
Questions.A: He created the world in 6 days. (2)
Questions.Alternative: How many days did it take for God to create the world?
In how many days did God create the world?

Questions.Q: What did God do on the seventh day?
Questions.A: He stopped working/creating (things). -OR- He rested. (2)

Questions.Q: Do you think that he had to rest because he was tired/weary?
Questions.Note: No, God never becomes tired/weary.
Questions.Alternative: Do you think that he had to rest because he was tired?
Do you think that he had to rest because he was weary?

Questions.Q: What did God declare about the seventh day?
Questions.A: He made it holy/special/different. (3)
Key Term Check: God "set apart" the seventh day; he declared that it was special, and different from the other 6 days. (See "holy" in KBT 3.b.)

Section.heading: Genesis 2:4-25 How God created the first man and the first woman.

Questions.Q: What do we read about in this passage/here?
Questions.A: We read of how God created man and woman, and about the Garden/Park/Place of Eden. We read how Adam named the animals; and we read about God's command not to eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
Questions.Alternative: What is this passage about?
What do we learn about in this passage?
What do we read about in this passage?
What do we read about here?

Questions.Q: Tell me about what God did to create man.
Questions.A: He took some soil/dust and formed it into a man, and breathed into the man the breath to cause him to live/that caused him to live. (7)

Questions.Q: Tell me about what God did to create woman.
Questions.A: He made the man sleep very deeply while he removed a rib from the man. After that he made a woman from the man's rib. // Then with the man's rib he made a woman. (21-22)

Questions.Q: When we read this passage, what do we learn about what the earth/world was like before God created man?
Questions.A: There were no plants. It did not rain. The ground was kept moist/wet from water that came from underground. (5-6)
Questions.Alternative: When we read this passage, what do we learn about what the earth was like before God created man?
When we read this passage, what do we learn about what the world was like before God created man?

Questions.Q: After God formed man from the dust/soil, what did God do to cause him to live/become alive?
Questions.A: He breathed into the man the breath that caused him to live. (7)
Questions.Note: Key Term Check: The Hebrew text at Genesis 2:4 introduces the compound term, "Yahweh Elohim" in referring to God. If the translation uses a different term here than in the preceding sections, it is important to ensure that the respondents do not think that the different term refers to a different God/being. (See "God" in KBT.)
Questions.Alternative: After God formed man from the dust, what did God do to cause him to live?
After God formed man from the dust, what did God do to cause him to become alive?
After God formed man from the soil, what did God do to cause him to live?
After God formed man from the soil, what did God do to cause him to become alive?

Questions.Q: Where did God place the man?
Questions.A: He placed the man in a garden/park/pleasant place, called "Eden" (a place in the east). (8)

Questions.Q: Tell me about that garden.
Questions.A: That garden had many beautiful trees, with good fruit in the garden. In the middle of the garden/park were two special trees: one that had fruit which gave people life, and one that had fruit which would give them knowledge of good and evil. (9)

Questions.Q: What was the source of water for the many trees in that garden/Eden place?
Questions.A: There was a large river flowing through that garden/Eden place. -OR- There were four large rivers flowing through it. (10)
Questions.Alternative: What was the source of water for the many trees in the Garden of Eden?
What was the source of water for the many trees in that garden?
What was the source of water for the many trees in Eden?
What was the source of water for the many trees in the Eden place?

Questions.Q: From this passage, what do we learn about those/the four rivers of that garden?
Questions.A: This passage mentions the names of the rivers, and the lands/territories through which some of them flowed. (11-14)
Questions.Alternative: From this passage, what do we learn about those four rivers of that garden?
From this passage, what do we learn about the four rivers of that garden?

Questions.Q: Tell me about the place called Havilah.
Questions.A: Havilah was a place with good/pure gold, and also perfume/something aromatic. There were also many beautiful stones/jewels there. (11-12)

Questions.Q: For what purpose did God place the man in the Garden of Eden/Eden place?
Questions.A: God put the man there to care for/look after the place. (15)
Questions.Alternative: For what purpose did God place the man in the Garden of Eden?
For what purpose did God place the man in that garden?
For what purpose did God place the man in Eden?
For what purpose did God place the man in the Eden place?

Questions.Q: What did God command man at this time?
Questions.A: God commanded man to eat fruits from any tree in the garden, except that man was not to eat the fruit from the tree that caused a person to know good and evil. (16-17)

Questions.Q: What did God say would happen to man, if he ate from the tree that caused/causes a person to know good and evil?
Questions.A: God said that the man would certainly (begin to) die. (17)
Questions.Alternative: What did God say would happen to man, if he ate from the tree that caused a person to know good and evil?
What did God say would happen to man, if he ate from the tree that causes a person to know good and evil?

Questions.Q: After God had placed the man in Eden, what did God think/feel/say about the man being alone?
Questions.A: He thought/felt/said that it was not good for the man to be alone. (18)
Questions.Alternative: After God had placed the man in Eden, what did God think about the man being alone?
After God had placed the man in Eden, what did God feel about the man being alone?
After God had placed the man in Eden, what did God say about the man being alone?

Questions.Q: So what did God say that he would do for the man?
Questions.A: He said that he would make a helper/companion/partner for the man. (18)

Questions.Q: How were the animals and birds named?
Questions.A: First, God brought the animals and birds to the man. // First, God caused the animals and birds to come to the man. Then the man named them/named each one. (19-20)

Questions.Q: In what way did God make the woman differently from the way he made the man?
Questions.A: God made the man from the soil/dust. But he made the woman from the rib/side of the man. (21-22)

Questions.Q: Before God removed the rib from Adam, what did he do to Adam?
Questions.A: God caused him to sleep deeply. (21)

Questions.Q: After God removed the rib from Adam, what did he do to Adam?
Questions.A: God closed Adam's side/flesh/wound. (21)
Key Term Check: The translation might refer to "flesh" here. This concept has theological significance in other contexts, especially when it is used figuratively. (See "flesh" in KBT A.1.)

Questions.Q: After God had made the woman, what did he do with her?
Questions.A: He took/brought her to the man. (22)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the man called his partner "woman"?
Questions.A: The word "woman" means "from man." Because she was made from him/from part of him/from one of his ribs, he called her "woman". (23)

Questions.Q: When a man separates from his parents and unites with a wife, to what event does that refer?
Questions.A: That refers to marriage. // That event is marriage. (24)

Questions.Q: When we read verse 18 and verses 23-24, what do we learn about why a man needs a wife, and why a woman needs a husband?
Questions.A: God saw that it was not good for a man to be alone. And woman, having been made from (a part of/a rib of) a man, needs to be re-united with a man. (18, 23-24)

Questions.Q: We read that the man and the woman were naked. How did they feel about that?
Questions.A: They were not ashamed. // They did not feel ashamed. (25)
Questions.Alternative: How did the man and the woman feel about being naked?

Section.heading: Genesis 3:1-24 The first man and woman disobeyed God's command.

Questions.Q: What important event do we learn about in this passage?
Questions.A: We learn about the first time that man and woman disobeyed God. -OR- We learn about how sin first came into the world.

Questions.Q: Tell me the main events/points/happenings in this account/passage.
Questions.A: The serpent persuaded the woman to eat some fruit from the tree - the one which would enable someone to know good and evil. Then the woman also persuaded the man to eat some of the fruit from that tree. Then they were both ashamed. When God came to (visit/see) them, the man blamed the woman, and the woman blamed the serpent. Then God put a curse on the serpent, and also on the woman, and on the man. (The curse applies to all of their descendants.)
Questions.Alternative: Tell me the main events in this account.
Tell me the main events in this passage.
Tell me the main points in this account.
Tell me the main points in this passage.
Tell me the main happenings in this account.
Tell me the main happenings in this passage.

Questions.Q: What type of creature spoke to the woman?
Questions.A: The creature/It was a serpent/snake. (1)

Questions.Q: How was this serpent different from all the other creatures that God had made?
Questions.A: It/He was more crafty/clever. (1)

Questions.Q: In what way did the snake distort/change God's instructions?
Questions.A: The snake suggested that God had prohibited the man and woman from eating any fruit from any of the trees of that garden. (1)
Questions.Alternative: In what way did the snake distort God's instructions?
In what way did the snake change God's instructions?

Questions.Q: What did the woman say in response?
Questions.A: She said that God permitted them to eat the fruit from any trees in the garden, except from the one at the middle/center of the garden. (2-3)

Questions.Q: According to the woman, what did God say would happen if they ate that fruit or even touched it?
Questions.A: According to her, God said that they would die. (3)

Questions.Q: What was the serpent's answer to the woman?
Questions.A: He said that they would not die. He said that after they eat fruit from that tree, they will be like God, knowing good and evil. (4-5)

Questions.Q: As the woman looked at the fruit, what did she think about it?
Questions.A: She thought that it looked very good, and that it was probably delicious, and that it would make her wise. (6)

Questions.Q: So what did the woman do?
Questions.A: She picked some of the forbidden fruit(s), and she ate it/them. (6)

Questions.Q: What else did the woman do?
Questions.A: She gave some of that fruit to her husband, and he ate it/them, too. (6)

Questions.Q: What happened immediately after they ate the fruit(s)?
Questions.A: They felt shame about being naked/They were ashamed because they were naked, so they made coverings for themselves from leaves. (7)

Questions.Q: When the man and woman heard God walking in the garden, what did they do?
Questions.A: They hid from him among the trees. (8)

Questions.Q: Then what did God do?
Questions.A: He called (out) to the man, "Where are you?" (9)

Questions.Q: When God called (out) to the man, what did the man answer?
Questions.A: He said that he was afraid because he was naked. So he hid. // So he had hidden. (10)

Questions.Q: So then what did God ask the man?
Questions.A: He asked the man who had told him/who had told the man that he was naked. God also asked the man if he had eaten from the forbidden fruit. (11)

Questions.Q: When God asked the man if he had eaten fruit from the tree forbidden to him, what did the man answer?
Questions.A: He admitted that he had eaten the fruit, but he said that the woman had given him the fruit. He also said that God had given that woman to him. (12)

Questions.Q: Do you think that the man was taking responsibility for what he had done?
Questions.A: No, he was not. He tried to suggest that the woman was responsible. Perhaps he was even suggesting that God was responsible, since God had given the woman to him/to the man. (12)

Questions.Q: Did the woman take responsibility for what she had done?
Questions.A: No, she did not. She said that the serpent had tricked her. (13)

Questions.Q: What did God say he would do to punish the serpent?
Questions.A: God caused it to slide/slither on its stomach/on the ground, and the snake would now eat dust/the serpent's head would now be in the dust. Also, the serpent and its descendants/offspring/progeny would be enemies with the woman and her descendants/offspring/progeny. (14)
Key Term Check: In pronouncing punishment here, God had cursed the serpent. In this context, "curse" is the opposite of "bless."
Questions.Note: See "bless" in KBT.

Questions.Q: In the future, what will the serpent do to the woman's offspring/descendant(s)?
Questions.A: The snake will strike at his/their heel. (15)
Questions.Note: This might mean that Satan will tempt people to sin, or that Satan will attack the Christ. These interpretations are not clear from this passage alone.
Questions.Alternative: In the future, what will the serpent do to the woman's offspring?
In the future, what will the serpent do to the woman's descendant?
In the future, what will the serpent do to the woman's descendants?
In the future, what will the serpent do to the woman's offspring/descendent(s)?

Questions.Q: What will the woman's descendant(s) do to the snake?
Questions.A: The woman's descendant(s) will crush the snake's head. (15)
Questions.Note: This probably means that the Christ will destroy Satan. This interpretation is not clear from this passage alone.
Questions.Alternative: What will the woman's descendent(s) do to the snake?

Questions.Q: What new/different experience did God say that the woman would have from that time on?
Questions.A: God said that the woman would have/experience great pain when she gives birth to a child. He also said that she would desire her husband/that she would desire to rule over her husband, but that her husband would rule over her. (16)
Questions.Alternative: What new experience did God say that the woman would have from that time on?
What different experience did God say that the woman would have from that time on?

Questions.Q: Then what did God say he would do to punish the man?
Questions.A: He said that he (God) had cursed the ground, and that thorns and thistles would now grow. As a result, it would become difficult for the man to produce food. And finally, the man would die. As man came from the soil/dust, he will again become soil/dust. (17-19)

Questions.Q: What name did Adam give to his wife?
Questions.A: He called her "Eve." (20)

Questions.Q: For what reason did he choose that name for her?
Questions.A: That name means "life," and she would be the mother/ancestor of everyone born after that. (20)

Questions.Q: What did God do for Adam and his wife at that time?
Questions.A: He made them clothing from the skins of animals. (21)

Questions.Q: What do you think would be the situation of mankind, if people had been allowed/permitted to continue to eat fruit from the tree that gave/gives life?
Questions.A: People might have lived forever (in the state of knowing good and evil). (22)
Questions.Alternative: What do you think would be the situation of mankind, if people had been allowed to continue to eat fruit from the tree that gave life?
What do you think would be the situation of mankind, if people had been allowed to continue to eat fruit from the tree that gives life?
What do you think would be the situation of mankind, if people had been permitted to continue to eat fruit from the tree that gave life?
What do you think would be the situation of mankind, if people had been permitted to continue to eat fruit from the tree that gives life?

Questions.Q: At first, Adam and Eve were allowed to eat fruit from the tree that gives life, and they would not die. Why do you think it was no longer good for mankind to live forever?
Questions.A: It was no longer good because we/they are now spiritually dead. We/they have experienced both good and evil. (22)

Questions.Q: Therefore, what did God do so that people were no longer able to eat fruit from the tree that gave/gives life?
Questions.A: He sent them away from the Garden of Eden. He placed cherubim/watchers and a flaming sword at the east gate, so that they could not return to the Garden. (23-24)
Questions.Alternative: Therefore, what did God do so that people were no longer able to eat fruit from the tree that gave life?
Therefore, what did God do so that people were no longer able to eat fruit from the tree that gives life?

Questions.Q: Whom did God expel/send away from the Garden of Eden?
Questions.A: He sent out both Adam and Eve. -OR- He sent out Adam, and his wife accompanied him. (23)
Questions.Note: The text actually refers only to Adam in these verses, but it is quite clear from Genesis 4 that his wife accompanied him.
Questions.Alternative: Whom did God expel from the Garden of Eden?
Whom did God send away from the Garden of Eden?

Questions.Q: What was Adam to do after he left the Garden of Eden?
Questions.A: He was to work/cultivate the soil. (23)

Questions.Q: The cherubim/watchers which God placed at the gate - what do you think they were like?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The beings whom God placed to guard the gate to Eden were called "cherubim", the plural form of "cherub". A cherub is a supernatural being. It might belong to a subclass of angelic beings, or it might be something similar to an angel.
Questions.Note: We do not know about their appearance. They were probably strong and powerful. Nobody could persuade the cherubim/watchers to allow them to return to the Garden.
See "angel" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: The cherubim which God placed at the gate - what do you think they were like?
The watchers which God placed at the gate - what do you think they were like?
What do you think the cherubim, which God stationed at the edge of the garden, were like?
God placed cherubim at the edge of the garden. What do you think they were like?

Questions.Q: What was the reason that God placed the cherubim at the gate?
Questions.A: God placed the cherubim there to keep anyone from entering the Garden (and thus being able to eat fruit from the tree that gave/gives life). (24)

Questions.Q: What do you think about that serpent which tempted Eve and Adam - do you think that it was just a snake?
Questions.A: No, it was really Satan (who is the leader of evil spirits).
Questions.Note: Probably "the serpent" was really Satan. However, the author does not state this, and one who is reading/hearing this passage and is not familiar with the rest of the Bible might not be able to identify the serpent as being Satan.

Section.heading: Genesis 4:1-26 The account of the sons of Adam and Eve.

Questions.Q: Tell me the main events in this passage.
Questions.A: Eve gave birth to two sons. One of them, Cain, killed the other, Abel. Then God punished Cain. Later, Eve gave birth to another son, Seth. We also learn about some of Cain's descendants.

Questions.Q: What was the name of Adam and Eve's firstborn son?
Questions.A: His name was Cain. (1)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that his parents gave that name to him?
Questions.A: They named him "Cain" because that means, "get/obtain/acquire", and she was able to get/obtain/acquire a son. (1)

Questions.Q: According to Eve, who helped her to have/acquire a son?
Questions.A: She said that God had helped her. (1)
Questions.Alternative: According to Eve, who helped her to have a son?
According to Eve, who helped her to acquire a son?

Questions.Q: What was the name of Adam and Eve's second son?
Questions.A: His name was Abel. (2)

Questions.Q: When the sons grew up, what type of work did they do?
Questions.A: Abel became a shepherd, and Cain became a farmer of his land/of some land. (2)

Questions.Q: Do we know what Cain produced/looked after on his farm?
Questions.A: We know only that he did not produce/look after animals/livestock - he had grain or some kind of plant(s). (3)
Questions.Alternative: Do we know what Cain produced on his farm?
Do we know what Cain looked after on his farm?

Questions.Q: After a time, Cain did something with some of the produce from his farm. Abel likewise did something with some of his lambs. What did the brothers do?
Questions.A: They gave some of the increase from their work as a gift to God. (3-4)

Key Term Check: This is the first of many occasions in Scripture where someone brings an offering to God. In some languages, it may be necessary to use a different term for Cain's offering of farm produce from that used for Abel's offering of an animal.
Questions.Note: See "sacrifice, offering" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do we know about the lambs that Abel brought to God?
Questions.A: The lambs which Abel brought to God were among the firstborn (and they may have been of special quality). (4)

Questions.Q: How did God feel about these offerings of Cain and Abel?
Questions.A: He was pleased with Abel's offering, but he rejected Cain's offering. (4-5)

Questions.Q: Then how did Cain feel?
Questions.A: Cain felt angry/upset/depressed. (5)

Questions.Q: So what did God say to Cain?
Questions.A: God assured Cain that he/God would accept him, if he (Cain) responded in the proper way. God also warned Cain that he (Cain) must be careful, because the desire to rebel against God is like an enemy/a wild animal who wanted/wants to destroy him, and that Cain must seek to overcome that desire. (6-7)

Questions.Q: What do you understand is meant by "sin"? // What do you understand "sin" to be?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In this context, Cain has refused to accept God's judgment as just. The central idea of "sin" is rebellion against God.
Questions.Note: See "sin" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: What do you understand is meant by "sin"?
What do you understand "sin" to be?

Questions.Q: So then what did Cain do?
Questions.A: He suggested that Abel go with him to an uninhabited/secluded place. Then he attacked and killed Abel. (8)

Questions.Q: What happened next?
Questions.A: God asked Cain about where his brother Abel was. Cain answered that he did not know. Cain (somewhat rudely) asked God if he (Cain) was responsible to look after his brother. (9)

Questions.Q: What did God say about Abel?
Questions.A: God said that Cain had defiled/spoiled the ground with Abel's blood, and that Abel's blood was crying out to God. -OR- When God saw Abel's blood on the ground, it was as though God heard Abel calling out to him (God). (10-11)

Questions.Q: Now what did Cain experience?
Questions.A: It was more difficult for him to raise crops. He had no home. He was to/He had to wander from place to place. (12)

Questions.Q: What did Cain think about what God said?
Questions.A: Cain thought that it was excessive, and that it was more than he could endure. (13)

Questions.Q: What four things did Cain mention as he described what he would experience from then on?
Questions.A: He said that he would be banished from the land/from his place. He would be banished from God's presence. He would have to wander about without a home. People (who met him) would kill him. (14)

Questions.Q: What was God's answer to Cain?
Questions.A: God/He said that, no, people would not kill him. God/He said that, if someone did kill Cain/him, then God would punish the killer seven times more/harder than he had punished Cain. -OR- God said, "No, people will not kill you. If someone does (try to) kill you, I will punish that killer/him seven times harder than I have punished you." (15)

Questions.Q: And then what else did God do to protect Cain?
Questions.A: God/He put a mark/sign on Cain to warn anyone who might try to kill him/Cain. (15)

Questions.Q: Then what did Cain do?
Questions.A: He left God's presence and went to the land of Nod, which is east of Eden. (16)

Questions.Q: What was the name of Cain's son?
Questions.A: The name of Cain's son was "Enoch." -OR- Cain's son was named, "Enoch." (17)

Questions.Q: And what else was given the same name?
Questions.A: Cain built/founded a town/settlement, and he named it Enoch. (17)

Questions.Q: Who was Lamech?
Questions.A: He was a descendant of Cain/descendant of Enoch, Cain's son. (17-18)

Questions.Q: Whom did Lamech marry?
Questions.A: He married two women: Adah and Zillah. (19)

Questions.Q: Who were three of Lamech's sons? What did each one of them originate/begin/initiate?
Questions.A: One son was Jabal, who began the practice of living in tents and caring for livestock. Another son was Jubal, the first musician/the ancestor of those who play the harp or flute. Another son (of Lamech) was Tubal-Cain, the first one to make/who made things from metal. (20-22)
Questions.Alternative: Who were three of Lamech's sons? What did each one of them originate?
Who were three of Lamech's sons? What did each one of them begin?
Who were three of Lamech's sons? What did each one of them initiate?

Questions.Q: What did Lamech say about anyone who might try to harm him?
Questions.A: He said that such a person would be punished 77 times. (24)

Questions.Q: What was the name of the third son of Adam and Eve? For what reason was he named that?
Questions.A: He was named "Seth," because that means "give/gift/substitute"; and Eve said that God had given Seth to replace Abel. (25)

Questions.Q: What did people begin to do during the time of Seth?
Questions.A: They began to worship God. -OR- They began to call God by his name, "Yahweh". (26)

Key Term Check: There are two well-supported interpretations of this passage. One interpretation is that at this time, people began to use the name, YHWH, in calling upon God. Another possible meaning is that, at this time, people began once again to turn to God - to call upon him/call out to him and worship him.
Questions.Note: See "name" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do we read about here?
Questions.A: We read about some of Adam's descendants, up to the time of Noah and his three sons.

Questions.Q: Tell me about one/Give me an example of one of the people mentioned in this chapter.
Questions.A: Seth, Adam's third son, was very much like his father. -OR- Enoch lived so close to God throughout his life that he did not die; God took him directly to Himself. -OR- Methuselah lived [longer than anyone else has ever lived on this earth,] to the age of 969 years.
Questions.Alternative: Tell me about one of the people mentioned in this chapter.
Give me an example of one of the people mentioned in this chapter.

Questions.Q: What do you think the Scripture means, when it says that God made humans in his likeness?
Questions.A: Probably this means that people are able to enter into a relationship of love and worship toward God, and that people are able to freely choose to do good or evil/to obey or to disobey him. (1)
Questions.Note: It does not refer to a physical resemblance.

Questions.Q: After Seth was born, how many more years did Adam live?
Questions.A: Adam lived 800 more years after Seth was born. (4)

Questions.Q: For how many years did Enoch live?
Questions.A: He lived for 365 years. (23)

Questions.Q: And then what happened to Enoch?
Questions.A: God took Enoch to heaven alive. Enoch did not die. -OR- God took him. Enoch did not die, but (somehow) God took him to heaven without Enoch having to experience death. (24)

Questions.Q: For what reason did Lamech name his son Noah?
Questions.A: The name "Noah" sounds like a Hebrew term that can mean "relief" or "comfort." (29)
Questions.Note: This explanation is not in the text. Therefore if the translation has not indicated the meaning of Noah's name, the respondent/hearer will not be able to answer this question.
Questions.Alternative: Why did Lamech name his son Noah?
For what reason did Lamech name his son, "Noah"?

Questions.Q: What were people like/What was mankind like at that time?
Questions.A: People were very evil. // Mankind was very evil. (5)
Questions.Alternative: What were people like at that time?
What was mankind like at that time?

Questions.Q: How did God feel about people/mankind?
Questions.A: God/He was very sad/disappointed/heart-broken. (6)
Questions.Alternative: How did God feel about people?
How did God feel about mankind?

Questions.Q: Who were taking the beautiful women as wives?
Questions.A: The "sons of God". (2)
Questions.Note: It is not certain to whom this refers. It might be angels or other heavenly beings. Or it might refer to earthly rulers. Or it might refer to men who belonged to a clan that formerly had been strongly committed to obeying God.

Questions.Q: According to God, for what reason would his Spirit not remain with people/mankind forever/for a long time? -OR- According to God, for what reason would he not allow people/mankind to live forever/for a long time?
Questions.A: God's Spirit would not remain with people/mankind forever/for a long time. // God would not allow people/mankind to live forever/for a long time, because people chose to give in to the temptations of the flesh. (3)
Questions.Alternative: According to God, for what reason would his Spirit not remain with people forever?
According to God, for what reason would his Spirit not remain with people for a long time?
According to God, for what reason would his Spirit not remain with mankind forever?
According to God, for what reason would his Spirit not remain with mankind for a long time?
According to God, for what reason would he not allow people to live forever?
According to God, for what reason would he not allow people to live for a long time?
According to God, for what reason would he not allow mankind to live forever?
According to God, for what reason would he not allow mankind to live for a long time?

Questions.Q: For how long did God allow people to live?
Questions.A: God allowed people to live for 120 years. (3)

Questions.Q: When the "sons of God" joined in union with the human women, who/what were their offspring?
Questions.A: Their offspring were the Nephilim. The/Those Nephilim were perhaps giants, or at least they were very powerful. (4)
Questions.Alternative: When the "sons of God" joined in union with the human women, who were their offspring?
When the "sons of God" joined in union with the human women, what were their offspring?

Questions.Q: At that time, was God glad that he had created people/mankind?
Questions.A: No, God regretted that he had created people/mankind. (6)

Key Term Check: The Hebrew term used here to refer to God's regret is used elsewhere to refer to repentance; some aspects of God's "regret" are similar to aspects of a person's "repentance". But of course God did not repent of sin, as He has never sinned.
Questions.Note: See "repent" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: At that time, was God glad that he had created people?
At that time, was God glad that he had created mankind?

Questions.Q: What did God decide to do, because people/mankind had become so wicked?
Questions.A: God decided to destroy people and the birds and animals. (7)
Questions.Alternative: What did God decide to do, because people had become so wicked?
What did God decide to do, because mankind had become so wicked?

Questions.Q: Were there any people with whom God was pleased at that time?
Questions.A: Yes, God was pleased with Noah. (8)
Key Term Check: God took pleasure in the character of Noah, and thus God chose to save Noah and his family.
Questions.Note: See "grace, favor" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did God tell Noah to do?
Questions.A: God told Noah to build a large boat.

Questions.Q: What was the purpose of that boat?
Questions.A: The boat was to be a place for Noah and (some of) his family, and some of the birds and animals/some of the creatures to be saved from the flood.

Questions.Q: What was Noah's character like?
Questions.A: Noah had a close relationship/was in a close relationship with God. Noah obeyed God. (9)
Key Term Check: Noah is described as a person who lived as God desired him to live. He was not sinless, but he sought to be obedient to his God.
Questions.Note: See "just, righteous" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Who were the other members of Noah's family?
Questions.A: Noah had three sons: Ham, Shem, and Japheth. (10)

Questions.Q: What do we learn about the character of the rest of the people?
Questions.A: The rest of the people had become corrupt and violent. (11-12)

Questions.Q: What did God instruct Noah to build?
Questions.A: God told him to build a very large boat. (14-15)

Questions.Q: Describe the boat which Noah built.
Questions.A: The boat was about 150 meters long, 25 meters wide, and 15 meters high, made of wood (and perhaps reeds), and covered with tar/pitch/bitumen/asphalt. It had an opening near the top, and a door in the side. It had three decks/levels. (14-16)

Questions.Q: According to God, by what means would he destroy the people and other creatures?
Questions.A: God said that he would send a flood. (17)

Questions.Q: Whom would God save from the flood?
Questions.A: God would save Noah, Noah's wife, and their (three) sons, and their sons' wives. (18)

Questions.Q: What did God say to Noah in order that Noah would know that God was sincere?
Questions.A: God said that he was making a "covenant," or a very special promise, to Noah. (18)

Key Term Check: This is the first occurrence of the term "covenant" in Scripture. God entered/was entering into a special relationship with Noah, wherein God promised to do something very important for Noah (and God also expected certain behavior from/of Noah).
Questions.Note: See "covenant" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did God tell Noah to take with him on (board) that boat?
Questions.A: God told Noah to take a pair (male and female) of every bird and animal, and adequate food for his family and for the creatures. (19-21)

Questions.Q: What did Noah do after God had given his instructions?
Questions.A: Noah obeyed God. -OR- Noah did exactly as God told him to do. (22)

Questions.Q: Describe the events of this chapter.
Questions.A: God told Noah to take his family, and pairs of animals and birds, into the boat. Noah did so, and a week later the flood began. Water came from above and below, and covered the earth. It rained for 40 days and nights. Everything that was not in the boat/on board the boat died.

Questions.Q: Has anything like this ever occurred in your place?
Questions.Note: Major floods have occurred in many places of the world. But the flood described in this chapter appears to be a worldwide flood - or at the very least, it covered a very large portion of the earth.

Questions.Q: In what way was Noah different from the other people living at that time?
Questions.A: God said that Noah was the only one on the earth at that time who was righteous. (1)

Questions.Q: How many of each kind of animal was Noah to take into the boat/on board?
Questions.A: He was to take seven pairs of each of those animals which had been declared "clean", and also one pair of each of those animals which were not "clean". (2)
Key Term Check: God declared certain creatures to be ritually clean, and it was therefore acceptable for people to eat them or to offer them as sacrifices to God.
Questions.Note: See "clean" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: How many of each kind of animal was Noah to take into the boat?
How many of each kind of animal was Noah to take on board?

Questions.Q: How many of each kind of bird was Noah to take?
Questions.A: He was to take seven pairs of each kind of bird. (3)

Questions.Q: When would the flood begin, and how long would the rain last?
Questions.A: The flood would begin in seven days, and it would rain for forty days and nights. (4)

Questions.Q: How old was Noah when the flood began?
Questions.A: Noah was 600 years old. (6)

Questions.Q: Tell who and what were on the boat with Noah.
Questions.A: Noah's wife was there, and Noah's sons and their wives. And there were (male and female) pairs of (clean and unclean) animals, and pairs of birds. (7-9)

Questions.Q: From where did the (flood) waters come?
Questions.A: The (flood) waters came from below the earth and as rain from the sky. (11-12)

Questions.Q: For how long did it rain?
Questions.A: It rained for forty days and nights. (13)

Questions.Q: How was the door to the large boat shut? // Who shut the door?
Questions.A: God shut the door. (16)
Questions.Alternative: How was the door to the large boat shut?
Who shut the door?

Questions.Q: To what height did the floodwaters rise?
Questions.A: The water was about four fathoms/twenty-two feet/seven meters above the highest mountains. (20)

Questions.Q: What died in the flood?
Questions.A: Every living creature - humans, animals, and birds - all died, except (for) Noah and his companions in the large boat. (21-23)

Questions.Q: For how long did the floodwaters cover the earth?
Questions.A: The waters covered the earth for 150 days. (24)

Questions.Q: Tell what happened to Noah and those with him in the large boat.
Questions.A: The rain stopped falling, and the water stopped gushing out of the ground. Eventually the large boat came to rest on the earth/ground. The waters continued to go down. After some time Noah released a raven, which flew around until the earth was dry. He also released a dove, but it could not find dry land, so it returned. He sent it out again a week later, and it returned with a leaf. When he released it again, a week later, it did not return. Eventually the earth dried up, and God told Noah that he and his family and all the creatures on the large boat were to leave the boat/and God told Noah to take his family and all the creatures off/out of the large boat.

Questions.Q: In the first verse, what do we learn about God caring for those in the large boat?
Questions.A: We learn that God had not forgotten them. He thought about them, and he sent a wind to begin to dry the earth. (1)
Questions.Note: If the translation uses a word something like "remember" here, be sure/ensure that the respondent does not think that this implies that God had forgotten about everyone on the large boat, and then he suddenly remembered them.

Questions.Q: As the waters began to recede/go down, where did the large boat finally come to rest?
Questions.A: It came to rest on the mountains of Ararat. (4)
