Questions.Alternative: As the waters began to recede, where did the large boat finally come to rest?
As the waters began to go down, where did the large boat finally come to rest?

Questions.Q: What were Noah and his family able to see about two and a half months later?
Questions.A: They could see the tops of other mountains. (5)

Questions.Q: What did Noah first release from the large boat?
Questions.A: He released a raven. (7)

Questions.Q: What did he release next?
Questions.A: He then released a dove. (8)
Questions.Alternative: What was the second thing he released?
What did he release after the raven?
What was the second bird he sent out?

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that he released birds?
Questions.A: The birds could look for dry land. If there was adequate dry land, they would probably not return to the boat. (11, 12)

Questions.Q: What did the dove do after Noah released it the first time?
Questions.A: It flew around, and then returned to the boat (because the water was still too high). (9)

Questions.Q: What did the dove do after Noah released it the second time?
Questions.A: It flew around, and again it returned to the boat. But this time it had a fresh/new leaf from an olive tree. (11)

Questions.Q: What did Noah think/conclude when the dove returned with the fresh olive leaf?
Questions.A: He realized that the floodwaters were almost gone. (11)
Questions.Alternative: What did Noah think when the dove returned with the fresh olive leaf?
What did Noah conclude when the dove returned with the fresh olive leaf?

Questions.Q: How long did Noah wait before he released the dove again?
Questions.A: He waited for one/another week. (12)

Questions.Q: What did the dove do after Noah released it the next time?
Questions.A: The dove flew away, and it did not return to the boat. (12)

Questions.Q: How many times did Noah release the dove?
Questions.A: Noah released the dove three times. (8, 10, 12)

Questions.Q: After the dove flew away and did not return, and after Noah looked out and saw everything drying up, he still did not leave the large boat. Two more months passed/went by. What happened before Noah left the large boat?
Questions.A: They did not leave the boat until God told them to leave it. (16)
Questions.Alternative: After the dove flew away and did not return, and after Noah looked out and saw everything drying up, he still did not leave the large boat. Two more months passed. What happened before Noah left the large boat?

After the dove flew away and did not return, and after Noah looked out and saw everything drying up, he still did not leave the large boat. Two more months went by. What happened before Noah left the large boat?

Questions.Q: What did God tell/want the animals and birds to do after they had left the large boat?
Questions.A: God told/wanted them to reproduce. (17)
Questions.Alternative: What did God tell the animals and birds to do after they had left the large boat?
What did God want the animals and birds to do after they had left the large boat?

Questions.Q: What was the first thing that Noah did, after he and his family and all the birds and animals had left the large boat?
Questions.A: He built an altar to God, and he sacrificed some of the animals and birds. (20)

Key Term Check: That altar was probably a platform made of stones. Noah slaughtered some of the animals, placed the carcasses on the platform, and burned them as an expression of devotion to God. (See "altar" in KBT 1.a.)

Questions.Q: What did God think about the sacrifice?
Questions.A: He was pleased. (21)

Questions.Q: What did God say at that time about the character of humans?
Questions.A: God said that people wanted to do evil/are bent toward evil even from their childhood. (21)

Questions.Q: Even though the thinking of people/mankind is very bad/thoroughly corrupt, what did God declare (that he would not do again)?
Questions.A: God declared that he would never again destroy all living things.
Questions.Note: God, of course, had not destroyed all living things - he saved Noah and his family, and pairs of all the animals and birds. It seems that, what God is saying here is that, even though much of mankind will continue to choose to live apart from God, he will never again choose just a few people and animals, and destroy all the rest.
Questions.Alternative: Even though the thinking of people is very bad, what did God declare (that he would not do again)?
Even though the thinking of people is thoroughly corrupt, what did God declare (that he would not do again)?
Even though the thinking of mankind is very bad, what did God declare (that he would not do again)?
Even though the thinking of mankind is thoroughly corrupt, what did God declare (that he would not do again)?

Section.heading: Genesis 9:1-17 God made a covenant with Noah.

Questions.Q: Tell me about the commands/instructions that God gave to Noah and to his sons in this passage.
Questions.A: God told them that they were to reproduce and populate the earth. He told them that it was unlawful to murder.
Questions.Alternative: Tell me about the commands that God gave to Noah and to his sons in this passage.
Tell me about the instructions that God gave to Noah and to his sons in this passage.

Questions.Q: Tell me about God's promise in this passage.
Questions.A: God promised that he would never again send a flood to kill all living creatures. He said that the rainbow would be a reminder/sign of His promise.

Questions.Q: After the Flood, how did the animals react toward humans?
Questions.A: The animals began to fear humans/began to be afraid of humans. (2)

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that the animals began to be afraid of humans at that time?
Questions.A: Animals began to be afraid of humans, because humans began to kill and eat animals. (3)

Questions.Q: What did God say that people must not do, when eating an animal?
Questions.A: God said that people must not eat animals while the animals still have life in them/before the blood has drained from them. (4)

Questions.Q: What did God say that someone must do, if an animal kills a person, or if a person intentionally kills another person?
Questions.A: Someone must then kill/execute the person or animal which had intentionally killed a person. (5, 6)

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that it is so very wrong to kill a person?
Questions.A: It is terrible to kill a person, because God made people in his image. (6)

Questions.Q: What did God promise then/at that time?
Questions.A: God promised that he would never send another flood to destroy the earth. (11, 15)
Questions.Alternative: What did God promise then?
What did God promise at that time?

Questions.Q: To whom did God make that promise?
Questions.A: God promised that to Noah and to his sons, and to their descendants, and to all the birds and animals. (9-10, 16)
Questions.Note: In most languages, someone can make a "promise" to a person, but not to an animal. On the other hand, it might not be considered unacceptable for God himself to make a "promise" to an animal.

Questions.Q: What was the sign that God gave as a reminder of his promise?
Questions.A: God gave the rainbow as a sign of his promise. (13-17)
Key Term Check: God gave the rainbow as a sign that what he says is true.
Questions.Note: See "miracle, sign, wonder" in KBT.

Questions.Q: In this passage, who are the main people (involved in the story)?
Questions.A: The main people are: Noah, and his three sons (Shem, Ham, and Japheth) (and their descendants).

Questions.Q: Do you think that your ancestors descended from Noah?
Questions.A: Yes, all people since Noah's time/since the time of Noah have descended from his family. (19)
Questions.Note: Some respondents might choose not to believe this. If that is the case, it is important, at this time, simply to be sure/to ensure that they understand the text.

Questions.Q: What type of work did Noah do after the flood?
Questions.A: He became a farmer (and planted a vineyard). (20)

Questions.Q: What was the shameful thing that Noah did?
Questions.A: Noah became drunk, and then lay naked in his tent (and one of his sons saw him). (21)

Questions.Q: This "tent" in which Noah lay - what do you think it was like?
Questions.A: It was a (non-permanent) shelter, probably made of woven cloth or animal skins which were held up by poles.

Questions.Q: Who saw Noah like that?
Questions.A: Ham saw him. (22)
Questions.Alternative: Who saw Noah naked?

Questions.Q: What did Ham do after he saw his father?
Questions.A: Ham went and told his brothers what he had seen. (22)

Questions.Q: So now what did those two brothers of his do?
Questions.A: They covered up their father without looking at him. (23)

Questions.Q: When Ham told his brothers about his father's nakedness, do you think that Ham was careful about how he talked about his father, or do you think that Ham was disrespectful?
Questions.A: He was probably disrespectful/mocking. (24-25)

Questions.Q: Whom did God punish for what Ham had done?
Questions.A: God punished Ham's son, Canaan, and Canaan's descendants. (25-27)

Questions.Q: Who ruled over the descendants of Ham?
Questions.A: The descendants of Shem and Japheth ruled over Ham's descendants. (26, 27)
Questions.Alternative: Who ruled over the descendents of Ham?

Questions.Q: How old was Noah when he died?
Questions.A: Noah was 950 years old. (29)

Section.heading: Genesis 10:1-32 The descendants of Japheth, Ham, and Shem.

Questions.Q: What is this chapter about? // What is the theme/subject of this chapter?
Questions.A: This chapter is about the descendants of Japheth, Ham, and Shem and how they began to scatter to many parts of the earth/into the rest of the world.
Questions.Alternative: What is this chapter about?
What is the theme of this chapter?
What is the subject of this chapter?

Questions.Q: What is special about Nimrod, one of Ham's descendants?
Questions.A: He was a mighty hunter and a warrior. He established/ruled over several major places/locations. (8-12)
Questions.Alternative: What is special about Nimrod, one of Ham's descendents?

Questions.Q: Tell about this happening/incident/story. What were the people trying to do, and what caused them to stop/discontinue their work/project?
Questions.A: The people were trying to build a great city with a very tall tower, so that they would not become scattered. But God confused their languages/God caused them to begin speaking different languages, so that they were not able to understand each other. Therefore they were not able to continue building the city. Instead/As a result, they scattered to many different places.
Questions.Alternative: Tell about this happening. What were the people trying to do, and what caused them to stop their work?
Tell about this happening. What were the people trying to do, and what caused them to stop their project?
Tell about this happening. What were the people trying to do, and what caused them to discontinue their work?
Tell about this happening. What were the people trying to do, and what caused them to discontinue their project?
Tell about this incident. What were the people trying to do, and what caused them to stop their work?
Tell about this incident. What were the people trying to do, and what caused them to stop their project?
Tell about this incident. What were the people trying to do, and what caused them to discontinue their work?
Tell about this incident. What were the people trying to do, and what caused them to discontinue their project?
Tell about this story. What were the people trying to do, and what caused them to stop their work?
Tell about this story. What were the people trying to do, and what caused them to stop their project?
Tell about this story. What were the people trying to do, and what caused them to discontinue their work?
Tell about this story. What were the people trying to do, and what caused them to discontinue their project?

Questions.Q: At the beginning of this event/incident/happening, how many languages did the people speak?
Questions.A: They all spoke one/the same language. (1)
Questions.Alternative: At the beginning of this event, how many languages did the people speak?
At the beginning of this incident, how many languages did the people speak?
At the beginning of this happening, how many languages did the people speak?

Questions.Q: What did the people plan to do?
Questions.A: They planned to build a great city with a very tall tower. (3-4)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they wanted to build the city and tower?
Questions.A: They wanted the city and tower to be symbols/a symbol of their greatness, and to keep them together in one place. (4)

Questions.Q: According to God, why were those people's plans/activities evil/bad/wrong?
Questions.A: Their plans/activities were evil/bad/wrong, because the people would then think/presume/conclude that they could do anything they pleased/that nothing was impossible for them to do. (6)
Questions.Alternative: According to God, why were those people's plans evil?
According to God, why were those people's plans bad?
According to God, why were those people's plans wrong?
According to God, why were those people's activities evil?
According to God, why were those people's activities bad?
According to God, why were those people's activities wrong?

Questions.Q: Do you think that God really felt threatened or afraid of the people, or was he concerned about the character of the people?
Questions.A: He was concerned because they were not spreading out in the world, and he was probably concerned about their pride and arrogance. (6, 9)

Questions.Q: What did God do to stop/prevent those people from building the city and tower?
Questions.A: God caused them to speak different languages. Then they became confused (and could not work together). (9)
Questions.Alternative: What did God do to stop those people from building the city and tower?
What did God do to prevent those people from building the city and tower?

Questions.Q: What happened after God caused them to speak different languages?
Questions.A: The people scattered to different places. (9)

Section.heading: Genesis 11:10-26 The genealogy from Shem to Abram.

Questions.Q: This passage is about whose descendants?
Questions.A: This is about the descendants of Shem.
Questions.Alternative: This passage is about whose descendents?
Whose descendants is this passage about?

Questions.Q: Who was Shem? (Who was Shem's/his father?)
Questions.A: Shem was one of Noah's sons. (10:1)
Questions.Alternative: Who was Shem? (Who was Shem's father?)
Who was Shem's father?
Who was Shem? (Who was his father?)

Questions.Q: How long was it from the time of the Flood until the birth of Arphaxad, one of Shem's sons?
Questions.A: Arphaxad was born two years after the Flood. (10)
Questions.Note: Scholars do not agree concerning the precise meaning of "two years after the Flood" - whether this refers to after the beginning of the Flood, or after the end of the Flood. If it would be problematic to retain this ambiguity in translation, then it seems best to understand this as something like, "two years after the end of the Flood".

Questions.Q: What were the names of Abram's two brothers?
Questions.A: Abram's brothers were Nahor and Haran. (26)

Questions.Q: This passage is about whose family? // About whose family is this passage?
Questions.A: This is about the family of Terah. (27)
Questions.Note: This section is an introduction to the life of Abram/Abraham. It speaks of his origins. Thus, if a person answers that this passage is about Abram's/Abraham's family, that answer would be acceptable.
Questions.Alternative: This passage is about whose family?
About whose family is this passage?

Questions.Q: From which of the sons of Noah did Terah descend?
Questions.A: Terah was a descendant of Shem. (11:10)

Questions.Q: Who were the three sons of Terah?
Questions.A: Terah's three sons were: Abram, Nahor, and Haran. (27)

Questions.Q: Which one of Terah's sons had the same name as Terah's father?
Questions.A: Nahor had the same name as Terah's father. (11:24)

Questions.Q: What was the name of Abram's nephew?
Questions.A: Abram's nephew was Lot, the son of Haran. (27)

Questions.Q: Which of Terah's sons died while still young? // Which of Terah's sons died while he, the son, was still young?
Questions.A: Haran died while he was still young. (28)
Questions.Alternative: Which of Terah's sons died while still young?
Which of Terah's sons died while he, the son, was still young?

Questions.Q: What is the name of Abram's wife? What do we learn about her here?
Questions.A: Abram's wife was Sarai, and we learn here that she was not able to have any children. (29, 30)

Questions.Q: Whom did Terah take on a journey?
Questions.A: Terah took Abram and Sarai, and Terah's grandson, Lot. (31)

Questions.Q: What was their destination?
Questions.A: They were going to the land of Canaan. (31)

Questions.Q: Did they arrive at Canaan?
Questions.A: No, they did not arrive there. (31)

Questions.Q: Where did they settle instead?
Questions.A: They settled at a place called Haran. (31)

Questions.Q: What happened to Terah while they were at Haran?
Questions.A: Terah died at Haran. (32)

Section.heading: Genesis 12:1-9 God called Abram. // God ordered Abram to leave that/his place.

Questions.Q: Tell me about what happened to Abram here/at this time.
Questions.A: God told Abram to leave his place/that place, and go to another land. God told him/Abram that he (Abram) would have many descendants. God said that he would bless/help Abram and his descendants and many other people, because of Abram. So Abram left, with his wife and nephew and servants, and went to Canaan.
Questions.Alternative: Tell me about what happened to Abram here.
Tell me about what happened to Abram at this time.

Questions.Q: What did God tell Abram to leave?
Questions.A: God said that Abram was to leave that/the place where he was/his country, his extended family/his relatives, and his immediate family. (1)

Questions.Q: And where did God tell Abram to go?
Questions.A: God told Abram to go to a place that God was to (later) show him. (1)

Questions.Q: What were some of the things that God promised to Abram?
Questions.A: God promised that Abram would have many descendants, and that God would bless Abram/God would make Abram successful/God would do good to Abram. God also promised that Abram would have a good reputation, and that Abram would be a blessing/would bring good to others. And God promised to bless/do good to those people who bless Abram - and to curse those people who curse Abram/to curse those people who say evil about Abram. God promised that he would bless/do good to clans/people-groups from all around the world because of Abram. (2-3)

Questions.Q: Who went with Abram?
Questions.A: Sarai (his wife), Lot (his nephew), and their servants went with Abram. They took many possessions/all their possessions with them. (4, 5)

Questions.Q: How old was Abram at the time they left/departed Haran?
Questions.A: Abram was 75 years old when they left/departed Haran. (4)
Questions.Alternative: How old was Abram at the time they left Haran?
How old was Abram at the time they departed Haran?

Questions.Q: Did Abram and his group reach Canaan/arrive at Canaan?
Questions.A: Yes, they reached Canaan/arrived at Canaan. (5)
Questions.Alternative: Did Abram and his group reach Canaan?
Did Abram and his group arrive at Canaan?

Questions.Q: Where did they stop/make their first stop in Canaan?
Questions.A: They stopped at a special tree at Moreh, near Shechem place. (6)
Questions.Alternative: Where did they stop in Canaan?
Where did they make their first stop in Canaan?

Questions.Q: At that time, who was living in the region where Abram stopped?
Questions.A: The Canaanites were (living) there. (6)

Questions.Q: What did God say that he would give to Abram's descendants?
Questions.A: God would give them the land (of Canaan). (7)
Questions.Alternative: What did God say that he would give to Abram's descendents?
What did God promise to give to Abram's descendants?

Questions.Q: After God promised that land, what was Abram's response?
Questions.A: Abram built an altar (to worship God)/a platform for sacrificing animals to God. (7)

Questions.Q: After that, where did Abram go?
Questions.A: Abram went/traveled to the hills east of Bethel/hills between Bethel and Ai. (8)

Questions.Q: When Abram arrived at the hills east of Bethel, what did he do there?
Questions.A: Abram built an altar (to worship God)/a platform for sacrificing animals to God. (8)

Questions.Q: Where did Abram go after that?
Questions.A: After that, Abram continued moving south toward the Negev/Negeb. (9)

Section.heading: Genesis 12:10-20 Abram and Sarai (and their servants) traveled to/went to Egypt.

Questions.Q: Tell what Abram did at that time. What happened as a result?
Questions.A: Because of a famine, Abram and Sarai went to Egypt. Abram was afraid that people of Egypt would kill him in order to take his wife. So Abram told Sarai to say/had Sarai say that she was his sister. Pharaoh took Sarai into his harem/to be his wife; but then God sent a terrible plague upon Pharaoh's household. Pharaoh (discovered the source of the plague and) became very angry with Abram, because Abram had not been fully honest/had not told the whole truth. Therefore, Pharaoh deported/expelled Abram and his household from Egypt.

Questions.Q: What was the reason why Abram went to Egypt?
Questions.A: Abram went to Egypt [so he and his household would have food,] because there was a famine in Canaan. (10)

Questions.Q: What was Abram worried about?
Questions.A: Abram was worried that some Egyptians would see how beautiful Sarai was, and would then kill Abram in order to take her. (11-12)

Questions.Q: What did Abram tell Sarai to do?
Questions.A: Abram told Sarai to say that she was his (Abram's) sister. (13)

Questions.Q: When Pharaoh's officials saw Sarai, what happened?
Questions.A: Pharaoh's officials told Pharaoh of how beautiful Sarai was, and then Pharaoh took her into his household/Pharaoh had her taken into his household. (14-15)

Questions.Q: After that, how did Pharaoh treat Abram?
Questions.A: Pharaoh treated Abram very well, sending him many animals as gifts. (16)

Questions.Q: So then what happened to Pharaoh and his household?
Questions.A: God sent a terrible plague on Pharaoh's household. (17)

Questions.Q: For what reason did God send the plague?
Questions.A: God sent the plague because it was wrong for Pharaoh to take another man's wife into his household to be his wife/to be one of his wives. (17)

Questions.Q: So then what did Pharaoh say to Abram?
Questions.A: Pharaoh told Abram that he (Abram) should have said that Sarai was really his (Abram's) wife. (18-19)

Questions.Q: What did Pharaoh do next?
Questions.A: Pharaoh then deported Abram and all those with him from Egypt. -OR- Pharaoh told Abram to leave Egypt with all his family and servants. (19-20)

Questions.Q: In your opinion, did Abram behave in an honorable way?
Questions.A: Probably not - Abram did not speak truthfully about his wife. (18-19)

Questions.Q: What happened at this time? When Abram and his household returned from Egypt, what problem occurred? What did they do about it?
Questions.A: Abram and Lot both had many animals that needed food/feeding. The problem was, there was not enough land where they were living/staying to support all the animals. So Lot chose to go elsewhere, to a place near where very wicked people were living. God renewed his promises to Abram, and Abram built an altar to God/to worship God.

Questions.Q: When Abram and his household left Egypt, where did they stay at first?
Questions.A: They first stayed in the Negeb. (1)

Questions.Q: Who was with Abram?
Questions.A: Abram's wife, Sarai, and his nephew, Lot, were with Abram. (And probably servants, also.) (1)

Questions.Q: What else did Abram take with him from Egypt?
Questions.A: Abram also took with him many animals, and much silver and gold. (2)

Questions.Q: Did Abram and his household stop in the Negeb and stay there permanently?
Questions.A: No, they continued traveling to/toward Bethel, where they had previously been living/staying. (3)

Questions.Q: When they arrived at the place where they had camped before, what did Abram do?
Questions.A: Abram worshiped God. (4)

Questions.Q: What problem did Abram and Lot have/experience?
Questions.A: There was not enough land/food for all their animals. -OR- There was not enough land for all of their animals to be able to get enough food. (5-6)
Questions.Alternative: What problem did Abram and Lot have?
What problem did Abram and Lot experience?

Questions.Q: Who began to quarrel?
Questions.A: The people looking after/taking care of Lot's animals began to quarrel with those looking after/taking care of Abram's animals. (7)

Questions.Q: Who else was living in the land at that time?
Questions.A: The Canaanites and Perizzites were also living there. (7)

Questions.Q: According to Abram, why should his herdsmen/workers and Lot's herdsmen/workers not quarrel?
Questions.A: They should not quarrel because Abram & Lot were (close) relatives. (8)
Questions.Alternative: According to Abram, why should his herdsmen and Lot's herdsmen not quarrel?
According to Abram, why should his herdsmen and Lot's workers not quarrel?
According to Abram, why should his workers and Lot's herdsmen not quarrel?
According to Abram, why should his workers and Lot's workers not quarrel?

Questions.Q: So what did Abram suggest to Lot?
Questions.A: Abram suggested that they separate. He suggested that Lot choose which portion of land he wanted, and Abram would go somewhere else. (9)

Questions.Q: Where was the portion of land that Lot chose?
Questions.A: Lot chose (the portion of) land that was (in) the valley/plain near the Jordan River. (10)

Questions.Q: What do we learn about the land that Lot chose for himself?
Questions.A: We learn that it had lots of water, like the Garden of God or the (fertile) land of Egypt. (10)

Questions.Q: What do we learn about what would happen to that place in the future?
Questions.A: We learn that God was to later destroy (towns in) that place. (10)

Questions.Q: So Lot took his animals and servants and settled in a different place. What was the name of the town/city near to where they settled?
Questions.A: They settled near Sodom. (12)
Questions.Alternative: So Lot took his animals and servants and settled in a different place. What was the name of the town near to where they settled?
So Lot took his animals and servants and settled in a different place. What was the name of the city near to where they settled?

Questions.Q: What kind of people lived at Sodom? // What was the character of the people at Sodom?
Questions.A: The people were very evil. (13)
Questions.Alternative: What kind of people lived at Sodom?
What was the character of the people at Sodom?

Questions.Q: After Lot left, what did God say to Abram?
Questions.A: God renewed his promise to Abram. God promised to give all the land to him and his descendants, and to give Abram very many descendants. (14-17)

Questions.Q: What does it mean that Abram's descendants will be like dust?
Questions.A: It means that they will be numerous/very many. As a person cannot count dust, in the same way Abram's descendants will be so many that a person cannot count them. (16)
Questions.Alternative: What does it mean that Abram's descendents will be like dust?

Questions.Q: Where did Abram settle at that time?
Questions.A: Abram (and his household) settled in/near (some special trees at) Hebron. (18)

Questions.Q: What did Abram do there/at Hebron?
Questions.A: Abram built an altar (to offer sacrifices) to (worship) God. (18)
Questions.Alternative: What did Abram do there?
What did Abram do at Hebron?

Section.heading: Genesis 14:1-16 Abram rescued his nephew, Lot.

Questions.Q: Tell how it came to be that Abram and his men went to battle/war. What were the circumstances that led to this?
Questions.A: A war took place in which Abram's nephew, Lot, was taken captive. Abram pursued/went after the army that had captured Lot, and Abram rescued/was able to rescue his nephew.
Questions.Alternative: Tell how it came to be that Abram and his men went to battle. What were the circumstances that led to this?
Tell how it came to be that Abram and his men went to war. What were the circumstances that led to this?

Questions.Q: We read here of two groups of kings who fought each other. How many kings grouped together on one side? How many kings grouped together on the other/opposing side?
Questions.A: There were four kings fighting (on one side) against five kings (on the other side). (1-2, 9)
Questions.Alternative: We read here of two groups of kings who fought each other. How many kings grouped together on one side? How many kings grouped together on the other side?
We read here of two groups of kings who fought each other. How many kings grouped together on one side? How many kings grouped together on the opposing side?
In this battle, how many kings were allied on each side?

Questions.Q: Where did they fight?
Questions.A: They fought at the plain/valley called Siddim (that is, the Salt Sea or Dead Sea). (3)

Questions.Q: Who won the battle?
Questions.A: Kedorlaomer and his allies defeated the others/other kings. (5-7)

Questions.Q: What did the armies/soldiers from Sodom and Gomorrah do?
Questions.A: They fled. Some fell into/hid in tar pits; others escaped to the hills. (10)
Questions.Alternative: What did the armies from Sodom and Gomorrah do?
What did the soldiers from Sodom and Gomorrah do?

Questions.Q: What did Kedorlaomer take from Sodom?
Questions.A: He (and his armies) took all the people's belongings, including food - including even Lot and all he owned. (11-12)

Questions.Q: How did Abram know that Kedorlaomer had captured/taken away his nephew, Lot?
Questions.A: Someone escaped from the battle, and ran and told Abram about Lot. (13)
Questions.Alternative: How did Abram know that Kedorlaomer had captured his nephew, Lot?
How did Abram know that Kedorlaomer had taken away his nephew, Lot?

Questions.Q: When Abram found out that Lot had been carried off/taken away, what did he do?
Questions.A: Abram and his men chased after Lot's captors. When they caught up with Lot's captors in Dan, Abram's men split into groups, defeated the enemy, and chased them away. (14-15)
Questions.Alternative: When Abram found out that Lot had been carried off, what did he do?
When Abram found out that Lot had been taken away, what did he do?

Questions.Q: What did Abram bring back from his battle with Kedorlaomer's army?
Questions.A: Abram brought/was able to bring back Lot and his possessions, including the women and other people. (16)

Questions.Q: Tell what happened when Abram returned from the battle.
Questions.A: The king of Sodom, and Melchizedek (who was king of Salem, and was also a priest) came to him (Abram). Melchizedek blessed Abram, and Abram gave to Melchizedek a tenth of what he (Abram) had recovered from/in the battle. The king of Sodom then told Abram that he (Abram) could keep the rest of the property that Abram had recovered, but Abram did not accept it.

Questions.Q: After the battle, who came to Abram?
Questions.A: The king of Sodom, and also Melchizedek (who was king of Salem, and also a priest of God) came to Abram. (17, 18)

Questions.Q: Who offered Abram food and drink/bread and wine?
Questions.A: Melchizedek offered Abram food and drink. (18)
Questions.Alternative: Who offered Abram food and drink?
Who offered Abram bread and wine?

Questions.Q: What do we learn about Melchizedek?
Questions.A: He was king of Salem, and also a priest of God Most High. (18)
Questions.Alternative: Who was Melchizedek?
What was Melchizedek's position?
What was Melchizedek's title?
What does this say about Melchizedek?

Questions.Q: What do you think was the work of a priest?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: During the time of the Old Testament, people understood that they could not simply approach God on their own. A priest was a "go-between" or mediator between people and God. A priest would offer sacrifices to God on behalf of God's people. A priest would also burn incense, offer prayers, and lead the people in worshiping God.
Questions.Note: See "priest" in KBT.

Questions.Q: We learn that Melchizedek brought Abram food and drink/bread and wine. What else did Melchizedek do for Abram?
Questions.A: Melchizedek also blessed Abram/asked God to do good for Abram. (19)

Key Term Check: On several previous occasions, God has blessed people or animals (Genesis 1:22, 28; 5:2; 9:1; 12:2-3). In this passage/section the author wrote that Melchizedek blessed Abram. It was not that Melchizedek did the same thing that God had done - rather, in this passage Melchizedek asked God to do good for/bless Abram.
Questions.Note: See "bless" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: We learn that Melchizedek brought Abram food and drink. What else did Melchizedek do for Abram?
We learn that Melchizedek brought Abram bread and wine. What else did Melchizedek do for Abram?

Questions.Q: Is this one whom Melchizedek called "Most High God" someone different from the one called LORD in 13:18?
Questions.A: No, these are different titles which both refer to the one true God.
Questions.Alternative: Is this one whom Melchizedek called "Most High God" someone different from the one called LORD in Genesis 13:18?
Is this one whom Melchizedek called "Most High God" someone different from the one called LORD earlier in Genesis?

Questions.Q: After Melchizedek blessed Abram, what did Abram give to Melchizedek?
Questions.A: Abram gave to Melchizedek one tenth of what Abram and his men recovered from Kedorlaomer. (20)

Questions.Q: What suggestion did the king of Sodom make to Abram?
Questions.A: The king said that Abram should release the people of Sodom whom he/Abram had rescued, but that Abram could keep all the wealth that he had recovered. (21)

Questions.Q: And what was Abram's response?
Questions.A: Abram said that he had promised [to] God that he would not accept any wealth from the king of Sodom. (22-23)

Questions.Q: What was the reason that Abram gave for not wanting to receive anything from the king of Sodom?
Questions.A: Abram said that if he did receive something from the king of Sodom, then the king could say that he was the one who made Abram wealthy. (23)

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that Abram did not want the king of Sodom to be able to say that he was the one who made Abram wealthy?
Questions.A: Perhaps it was because the people Sodom were especially evil. (13:10, 13) Or perhaps Abram simply did not want any person to claim that they were the ones who made Abram wealthy - that it was God who had made Abram wealthy.

Questions.Q: What was Abram willing to accept from the king of Sodom?
Questions.A: Abram was willing to accept the food that his men had already eaten, and also the share of the booty/goods to which his allies were entitled. (24)

Questions.Q: Tell me about what happened here.
Questions.A: God appeared to Abram in a vision and renewed his promises to Abram. He promised to give Abram numerous/very many descendants, and to give Abram the land of Canaan. God also predicted that Abram's descendants would be slaves in a foreign place for 400 years, but that God would deliver them and return them to their homeland/land.

Questions.Q: When God spoke to Abram, to what did he compare himself?
Questions.A: He called himself "Abram's shield"/"a shield to Abram". (1)

Questions.Q: What do you think that God meant by comparing himself to a shield?
Questions.A: He meant/was saying that he would protect and help Abram.

Questions.Q: What did God promise to Abram at that time?
Questions.A: God promised to give Abram great reward. (1)

Questions.Q: But what was Abram's problem?
Questions.A: Abram had no children - no one to inherit the blessings that God would give to him. (2-3)

Questions.Q: According to Abram, who would receive all of his inheritance?
Questions.A: Eliezer, from Damascus, one of Abram's servants, would receive Abram's inheritance. (3)

Questions.Q: What did God promise to Abram about a future family?
Questions.A: God said that Abram was to have his own child, and that Abram's descendants would be too many to count. (4-5)

Questions.Q: To what did God compare Abram's descendants?
Questions.A: God compared them to stars. (5)
Questions.Alternative: To what did God compare Abram's descendents?

Questions.Q: In what way were Abram's descendants to be like stars?
Questions.A: They would be too many to count. (5)
Questions.Alternative: In what way were Abram's descendent to be like stars?

Questions.Q: What was Abram's response?
Questions.A: Abram believed God. -OR- Abram believed what God told him/what God had said. (6)

Key Term Check: At a minimum, Abram believed at that time that God would do as God said he would do: God would give to Abram numerous/very many descendants. But Abram's response here probably went beyond simply believing God's promise - Abram also believed "in God" - that is, Abram believed that God's character was beyond any kind of doubt.
Questions.Note: See "believe" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did God consider about Abram? -OR- What was God's evaluation of Abram?
Questions.A: God considered/declared Abram to be righteous/straight. -OR- God was pleased with Abram. (6)
Key Term Check: As Noah sought to obey God (6:9), likewise/in the same manner Abram sought to trust God.
Questions.Note: See "just, righteous" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: What did God consider about Abram?
What was God's evaluation of Abram?

Questions.Q: What did God promise Abram about the land (of Canaan)?
Questions.A: God promised that he would give Abram the land. (7)

Questions.Q: And then what was Abram's question to God?
Questions.A: Abram asked how he could know that God would truly give Abram the land. (8)

Questions.Q: What did God tell Abram to get?
Questions.A: God told Abram to get a (female) cow, a female goat, a male sheep. Each animal was to be 3 years old. And God also told Abram to get a dove and a young pigeon. (9)

Questions.Q: After Abram got the animals and birds, what did he do?
Questions.A: Abram then killed the three animals and the two birds. He cut each of the animals in half (down the middle), and arranged them in a line (with the halves facing each other). Then he waved away/chased/kept other birds away from the dead animals and birds. (10-11)

Questions.Q: What happened to Abram when night arrived?
Questions.A: Abram fell into a deep sleep, and saw a vision that terrified him. (12)

Questions.Q: What was to be the future for Abram's descendants?
Questions.A: Abram's descendants would live in a foreign land for 400 years. They would be slaves, and others would oppress them/would treat them harshly. (13)
Questions.Alternative: What was to be the future for Abram's descendents?

Questions.Q: And what was to happen to the nation that oppressed the descendants of Abram?
Questions.A: God would punish them. (14)
Questions.Alternative: And what was to happen to the nation that oppressed the descendents of Abram?
What was to happen to the nation that oppressed the descendants of Abram?
What was to happen to any nation that oppressed the descendants of Abram?

Questions.Q: When Abram's descendants were to leave that other land, what would they take with them?
Questions.A: They would leave with very much wealth. (14)
Questions.Alternative: When Abram's descendents were to leave that other land, what would they take with them?

Questions.Q: And what would be Abram's future? Was he to join his descendants in being enslaved and oppressed?
Questions.A: No, Abram was to die in peace. (15)
Key Term Check: God promised that when Abraham was about to die, he would not be experiencing serious problems, but rather he would be/feel deeply satisfied and fulfilled.
Questions.Note: See "peace" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: And what would be Abram's future? Was he to join his descendents in being enslaved and oppressed?
What would be Abram's future? Was he to join his descendents in being enslaved and oppressed?

Questions.Q: For how long were Abram's descendants to be slaves in the other land?
Questions.A: They were to be there for four generations, or 400 years. By that time, the Amorites/people of Amor, who were living in Canaan, would have become excessively wicked. (16)
Questions.Alternative: For how long were Abram's descendents to be slaves in the other land?

Questions.Q: When it became dark, what happened?
Questions.A: A smoking oven/firepot and a blazing torch passed between the pieces/halves of the slaughtered animals and birds. (17)

Questions.Q: What did God promise to Abram at that time?
Questions.A: God promised to give to his descendants all the land, from the river in Egypt (all the way) to the large Euphrates River. (18-21)

Section.heading: Genesis 16:1-16 Ishmael was born to (Hagar and) Abram.

Questions.Q: Tell what happened at the time of this account.
Questions.A: Sarai, Abram's wife, had so far been unable to bear Abram a child. So she gave to Abram her servant, an Egyptian woman named Hagar, to bear a child for Abram. Hagar became pregnant, and then became disrespectful to Sarai. So Sarai made life miserable for Hagar, and Hagar then fled/ran away. An angel met Hagar, and told her to return to Abram. The angel also told Hagar that she would have a son, that she should name the boy "Ishmael", and that Ishmael would quarrel continually/not be at peace/not get along with his brothers.

Questions.Q: What was Sarai's situation at that time?
Questions.A: Sarai still had no children. (1)

Questions.Q: What did she suggest to Abram?
Questions.A: She said that Abram should sleep with her servant, Hagar, and have a child with/by/through the servant. (2-3)

Questions.Q: At the time that this happened, how long had Abram and Sarai been in the land of Canaan?
Questions.A: They had been there (for) 10 years. (3)

Questions.Q: When Hagar became pregnant, what was her attitude towards Sarai?
Questions.A: She became very disrespectful/arrogant/proud. (4)

Questions.Q: What was Sarai's reaction?
Questions.A: She became very upset with Hagar. (5)

Questions.Q: According to Sarai, who was at fault?
Questions.A: She blamed Abram. // She said that Abram was at fault.

Key Term Check: Sarai said in this account/passage that God should examine her and Abram, and that God should decide/pass judgment concerning who was at fault. It is possible that Sarai was simply expressing her displeasure and was not sincerely calling on God to pass judgment. However, many translations might use here the same term that is used elsewhere to refer specifically to God's judgment.
Questions.Note: See "judge, judgment" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What was Abram's response to Sarai?
Questions.A: Abram told Sarai to do whatever she wished/wanted with Hagar. (6)

Questions.Q: In what manner did Sarai begin to treat Hagar?
Questions.A: Sarai began to treat Hagar in a harsh/cruel manner. (6)

Questions.Q: As a result/So what did Hagar do?
Questions.A: Hagar fled/ran away. (6)
Questions.Alternative: As a result what did Hagar do?
So what did Hagar do?

Questions.Q: Who approached Hagar to speak with her?
Questions.A: The Angel of God/The Angel of YHWH appeared to Hagar. (7)

Key Term Check: There are about 56 references in the NIV OT and NT to "the Angel of the LORD", "the Angel of God", and "the Angel of the Lord". In some or all of these cases, it seems that this expression is referring to God himself (and not an angel) appearing supernaturally to people.
Questions.Note: See "angel" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did The Angel command Hagar?
Questions.A: The Angel told Hagar to return home and to submit to Sarai. (9)

Questions.Q: What did The Angel promise to Hagar?
Questions.A: The Angel promised Hagar that she would have numerous/very many descendants - more than she could count. (10)

Questions.Q: What was Hagar to name her son?
Questions.A: She was to name her son Ishmael. (11)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that that name was chosen for Hagar's son?
Questions.A: The name Ishmael means, "God hears", and at that time, God "heard" that Hagar was miserable/was being mistreated. (11)

Questions.Q: What was Ishmael's character to be like? // What kind of person would Ishmael be?
Questions.A: Ishmael would always be a quarrelsome person. // He would always be in conflict with others. (12)
Questions.Alternative: What was Ishmael's character to be like?
What kind of person would Ishmael be?

Questions.Q: What did Hagar call God at this time?
Questions.A: Hagar called God, "The God who sees (me)." // She called God, "El-roi", which means, "The God who sees (me)." (13)

Questions.Q: At the time when Ishmael was born, how old was Abram?
Questions.A: Abram was 86 years old. (16)

Section.heading: Genesis 17:1-8 God's eternal promise to his people.

Questions.Q: What did God promise to Abram in this account/passage?
Questions.A: God promised to make Abram into a mighty nation - into many nations! He promised Abram that he would have many, many descendants, and he promised that some of Abram's descendants would become kings. God promised to give the land of Canaan to Abram's descendants. God would always be the God of Abram and of Abram's descendants.
Questions.Alternative: What did God promise to Abram in this account?
What did God promise to Abram in this passage?

Questions.Q: For how long are these promises of God to be in effect?
Questions.A: God's promises are eternal/forever. (7-8)

Questions.Q: What did God require of Abram?
Questions.A: God commanded Abram to serve him (God) faithfully. (1)

Questions.Q: When Abram was 99 years old, what happened to him?
Questions.A: God appeared to him, renewed his promises to Abram, and changed his name to Abraham. (1-6)

Questions.Q: What name did God use to refer to himself in this passage/here?
Questions.A: God referred to himself as "El Shaddai," which means, "God Almighty"/"God All-powerful." (1)
Questions.Alternative: What name did God use to refer to himself in this passage?
What name did God use to refer to himself here?

Questions.Q: What did Abram do when God appeared to him and began to speak to him?
Questions.A: Abram bowed down with his face to the ground. (3)

Questions.Q: What new name did God give to Abram?
Questions.A: God changed Abram's name to "Abraham". (5)

Questions.Q: What does the name "Abraham" mean?
Questions.A: The name "Abraham" means "father/ancestor of many". (5)

Questions.Q: What did God promise to Abraham concerning/about his/Abraham's descendants?
Questions.A: God promised that Abraham's descendants would be very numerous/many; some of them would become kings. (6)
Questions.Alternative: What did God promise to Abraham concerning his descendants?
What did God promise to Abraham concerning Abraham's descendants?
What did God promise to Abraham about his descendants?
What did God promise to Abraham about Abraham's descendants?
What did God promise to Abraham concerning/about his/Abraham's descendents?
What did God promise to Abraham concerning his descendents?
What did God promise to Abraham concerning Abraham's descendents?
What did God promise to Abraham about his descendents?
What did God promise to Abraham about Abraham's descendents?

Questions.Q: What did God give to Abraham and his descendants?
Questions.A: God gave Abraham and his descendants all of the land of Canaan. (8)
Questions.Alternative: What did God give to Abraham and his descendents?

Questions.Q: What else did God promise to Abraham about his (Abraham's) descendants?
Questions.A: God promised that Abraham's descendants would worship him as God (and that he, God, would care for Abraham's descendants as their God). (8)
Questions.Alternative: What else did God promise to Abraham about his (Abraham's) descendents?

Questions.Q: Did God expect Abraham and Abraham's descendants to do anything as a response to God's promises?
Questions.A: Yes, God expected Abraham and Abraham's descendants to be circumcised.
Questions.Alternative: Did God expect Abraham and Abraham's descendents to do anything as a response to God's promises?

Questions.Q: How were Abraham and his descendants to demonstrate their willingness to accept God's promises?
Questions.A: Abraham and his descendants were to circumcise themselves/be circumcised. (10-11)

Key Term Check: To circumcise a man or boy is to surgically cut off a specific piece of skin from the end of his penis. It was performed as a sign that the man or boy was included among the descendants of Abraham, who were in a special "covenant" or "promise" relationship with God.
Questions.Note: See "covenant" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: How were Abraham and his descendents to demonstrate their willingness to accept God's promises?

Questions.Q: What was the meaning of circumcision? What did it signify?
Questions.A: It was a sign of the agreement. It signified that Abraham and his descendants were accepting God's promises, and would continue to be faithful to God. (11)

Questions.Q: Who was to be circumcised?
Questions.A: All of the males were to be circumcised. This includes servants/slaves (whether the servants/slaves had been bought, or had been born among Abraham's descendants). (12)

Questions.Q: At what age were they to be circumcised?
Questions.A: They were to be circumcised when they were 8 days old. (12)

Questions.Q: But if a male refused to be circumcised, what would happen to him?
Questions.A: The people were to expel him; they would not count/they were not to count him as one of God's people. (14)

Questions.Q: After God promised to bless/to do good for Abraham, whom did he promise to bless/for whom did he promise to do good in this passage?
Questions.A: He promised to bless/to do good for Sarah. (And he also promised to bless/to do good for Ishmael.)
Questions.Alternative: After God promised to bless Abraham, whom did he promise to bless in this passage?
After God promised to bless Abraham, for whom did he promise to do good in this passage?
After God promised to do good for Abraham, whom did he promise to bless in this passage?
After God promised to do good for Abraham, for whom did he promise to do good in this passage?

Questions.Q: Earlier, God changed Abram's name. Whose name did he change in this account/passage?
Questions.A: He changed Sarai's name. (15)
Questions.Alternative: Earlier, God changed Abram's name. Whose name did he change in this account?
Earlier, God changed Abram's name. Whose name did he change in this passage?

Questions.Q: What did God say that Abraham should now call his wife, Sarai?
Questions.A: God said that her new name was "Sarah." (15)

Questions.Q: In what ways did God promise to do good to Sarah/to bless Sarah?
Questions.A: God said that he would enable Sarah to have a son, and very many descendants. He also promised that some of her descendants would become kings. (16)
Questions.Alternative: In what ways did God promise to do good to Sarah?
In what ways did God promise to bless Sarah?

Questions.Q: How did Abraham respond after God promised [to] him that Sarah would have a son?
Questions.A: Abraham bowed down, and he laughed. (17)
Questions.Alternative: How did Abraham respond after God promised to him that Sarah would have a son?
How did Abraham respond after God promised him that Sarah would have a son?

Questions.Q: In your opinion, what caused Abraham to laugh?
Questions.A: Probably the reason that he laughed was because he and his wife were very old, and Abraham did not think that they could have any children. (17)

Questions.Q: At that time, how old were Abraham and Sarah?
Questions.A: Abraham was 100, and Sarah was 90 years old. (17)

Questions.Q: What did Abraham say to God?
Questions.A: He said that God's blessing should/would go to Ishmael. (18)

Questions.Q: According to God, with/through whom would He confirm/secure/establish his eternal promise to Abraham?
Questions.A: God would confirm his eternal promise with/through Isaac. (19, 21)
Questions.Alternative: According to God, with whom would He confirm his eternal promise to Abraham?
According to God, with whom would He secure his eternal promise to Abraham?
According to God, with whom would He establish his eternal promise to Abraham?
According to God, through whom would He confirm his eternal promise to Abraham?
According to God, through whom would He secure his eternal promise to Abraham?
According to God, through whom would He establish his eternal promise to Abraham?

Questions.Q: Did that mean that God would not help/bless Ishmael?
Questions.A: No, it did not. (20)
Questions.Alternative: Did that mean that God would not help Ishmael?
Did that mean that God would not bless Ishmael?

Questions.Q: How would God help/bless Ishmael?
Questions.A: God promised Ishmael many descendants, and 12 of his sons would be kings. He promised that Ishmael would become a great people-group. (20)
Questions.Alternative: How would God help Ishmael?
How would God bless Ishmael?

Questions.Q: According to God, when would Sarah give birth?
Questions.A: God said, "You will give birth about a year from now." // God said that she would give birth about a year later. (21)

Questions.Q: How old was Abraham when he was circumcised?
Questions.A: Abraham was 99 years old (at that time). (24)

Questions.Q: And how old was Ishmael?
Questions.A: Ishmael was 13 years old (when he was circumcised). (25)

Questions.Q: Who else was circumcised that same day?
Questions.A: All of the men and boys in Abraham's household, including the servants, were circumcised. (27)

Section.heading: Genesis 18:1-15 God again promised a son to Abraham.

Questions.Q: Tell about what happened here.
Questions.A: One day, three men (angels? or two angels and God himself?) suddenly appeared where Abraham's tent was set up. He rushed around to prepare them a meal. Then one of them predicted that Sarah would certainly have a son in about a year. Sarah overheard the conversation and she laughed silently, because she and Abraham were very old/were so old. God asked why Sarah had laughed. God pointed out that nothing is too difficult for him.

Questions.Q: At that time/At the time of this incident, where was Abraham?
Questions.A: He was camping near some special trees on a piece of land owned by someone named Mamre. (1)
Questions.Alternative: At that time, where was Abraham?
At the time of this incident, where was Abraham?

Questions.Q: What did Abraham see?
Questions.A: He saw three men/three angels/two angels, and God in the form of a man, standing not far away. (2, 10, 13, 14)

Questions.Q: When Abraham saw them, what did he do?
Questions.A: He ran to them and bowed (down to greet them). (2)

Questions.Q: What did Abraham say to them?
Questions.A: He invited them to stay for a while, to rest, and to eat. (3-4)

Questions.Q: What did Abraham want to do for the three visitors?
Questions.A: Abraham wanted his servants to bring water for washing, and to prepare/bring some food (for the visitors). (4-5)

Questions.Q: How much flour did Abraham tell his wife to prepare/make ready?
Questions.A: He told her to prepare/make ready three measures - perhaps about 20 kilos or 18 liters. (6)
Questions.Alternative: How much flour did Abraham tell his wife to prepare?
How much flour did Abraham tell his wife to make ready?

Questions.Q: Was Abraham preparing a snack, or a large feast?
Questions.A: He was preparing a large feast. (6-8)

Questions.Q: Did Abraham join in eating the feast with his visitors?
Questions.A: No, he waited on them. (8)

Questions.Q: When the visitors began to speak with Abraham, what did they ask him?
Questions.A: They asked Abraham (about) where his wife, Sarah, was. (9)

Questions.Q: What did one of them, then, say about Sarah?
Questions.A: One of them said that in about a year Sarah would bear/have a son. (10)

Questions.Q: When Sarah heard what the visitor said, what did she do?
Questions.A: She laughed to herself. (12)

Questions.Q: What caused Sarah to laugh?
Questions.A: She laughed because she and Abraham were both very old. It seemed strange/peculiar/odd to think of her conceiving, and bearing a child. (11-12)

Questions.Q: What did God then ask Abraham?
Questions.A: God asked why Sarah had laughed, and why she had asked, "Can an old woman like me give birth?" (13)

Questions.Q: In your opinion, is there anything that God cannot do?
So God repeated his prediction that Sarah would have a son in about one year. What else did God mention would take place at that time?
Questions.A: God also said that he would return at that time. (14)

Questions.Q: When Sarah heard what God said to Abraham, how did she feel/what feeling did she experience?
Questions.A: She was afraid. (15)
Questions.Alternative: When Sarah heard what God said to Abraham, how did she feel?
When Sarah heard what God said to Abraham, what feeling did she experience?

Questions.Q: So then what did Sarah do?
Questions.A: She lied, saying that she had not laughed. (15)

Questions.Q: Then what did God say?
Questions.A: He said that Sarah did in fact laugh. (15)

Section.heading: Genesis 18:16-33 Abraham pleaded/appealed to God on behalf of the people of Sodom.

Questions.Q: Tell me about this conversation. Who was speaking with whom, and about what were they talking?
Questions.A: Abraham was speaking with God. God said that he was going to destroy Sodom because the people were so/very wicked. But Abraham asked God not to destroy the city if there were 50 good people. God agreed to Abraham's request. Then Abraham lowered the number to 45, then 40, then 30, 20, and finally 10. And in each case, God agreed to spare the city for the sake of a few good people. Then God went on his way, and Abraham returned to his tent.

Questions.Q: How far did Abraham go with the men? // What did Abraham do when the men started to leave [to go to Sodom]?
Questions.A: Abraham probably walked a short distance, perhaps to the edge of the area where he lived. (He was not trying to go with them on their journey. This was just a hospitable way of saying good-bye.)
Questions.Alternative: How far did Abraham go with the men?
What did Abraham do when the men started to leave?
What did Abraham do when the men started to leave to go to Sodom?

Questions.Q: For what reason did God reveal to Abraham what he (God) was planning to do?
Questions.A: God revealed it to Abraham, because Abraham was to have very many descendants. God planned to bless all the nations of the earth through Abraham, and God expected Abraham to lead his family to obey God. (18-19)
Questions.Alternative: For what reason did God reveal to Abraham what he was planning to do?
For what reason did God reveal his plan to Abraham?

Questions.Q: What did God say that he had heard about the people of Sodom and Gomorrah?
Questions.A: God had heard that they were very/excessively evil. (20)

Questions.Q: How do you think God heard about their wickedness? // Who do you think told God that the people of Sodom and Gomorrah were wicked?
Questions.A: God knows everything. He might have received a "report" from angels, but he was not getting information that was news to him.
Most likely, the "cries" are figurative. (Matthew Poole's Commentary: "Sins are said to cry when they are gross, and manifest, and impudent, and such as highly provoke God to anger.")
Questions.Alternative: How do you think God heard about their wickedness?
Who do you think told God that the people of Sodom and Gomorrah were wicked?
What do you think the "cries" were like that God says he had heard?
Questions.Note: Depending on the respondent's preconceptions regarding the nature of God, this might not be obvious. Ensure that the translation is at least ambiguous and does not suggest outright that God had just learned about the situation via a report or accusation.

Questions.Q: What was God's purpose in going to Sodom and Gomorrah?
Questions.A: He went there to find out/see for himself (or to show that he had personally witnessed the evidence) if the reports of evil were true. (20-21)
Questions.Note: Benson Commentary: "Not as if there were any thing concerning which God is in doubt; but he is pleased thus to express himself after the manner of men, and to show that he ascertains the criminal’s guilt before he passes sentence."

Questions.Q: We learn that one of Abraham's three visitors was God. At that point, what did God do? What did the other two visitors do?
Questions.A: God stayed and spoke with Abraham. The other two visitors went to Sodom. (22)

Questions.Q: What was God going to do to the people of Sodom because they were so/very wicked?
Questions.A: God was going to destroy them all.
Questions.Note: This is implied, but not stated at this point. However, Abraham is about to plead on behalf of the people of Sodom. One cannot properly understand this action of Abraham's if one does not realize that God intended to destroy the wicked people of Sodom.
Questions.Alternative: What was God going to do to the people of Sodom because they were so wicked?
What was God going to do to the people of Sodom because they were very wicked?

Questions.Q: About what did Abraham question God? // What did Abraham ask God?
Questions.A: Abraham asked if God would destroy good/innocent people along with wicked ones. (23-25)
Questions.Alternative: About what did Abraham question God?
What did Abraham ask God?

Questions.Q: Then what did Abraham request of God?
Questions.A: Abraham requested that, if there were 50 honest/good people in the city, God would not destroy it. (24-25)

Questions.Q: What was God's answer to Abraham?
Questions.A: God agreed not to destroy Sodom, if there were 50 honest/good people. (26)

Questions.Q: What other requests did Abraham make of God?
Questions.A: Abraham then asked that God not destroy Sodom, if the honest/good people numbered only 45, or 40, or 30, or 20, or 10. (28, 29, 30, 31, 32)

Questions.Q: What did Abraham say to show that he was not making demands of God?
Questions.A: He said that he was only dust and ashes (a man and that he was unworthy). He asked permission to continue speaking, and he asked God not to be angry with him. (27, 30, 31, 32)

Questions.Q: Do you think it was appropriate for Abraham to make requests of God in that manner?
Questions.A: There is no indication in the text that God was offended/that God objected to Abraham's requests.

Questions.Q: What can we learn about God from this account?
Questions.A: We learn that God is patient and forgiving, but that He does not completely overlook wickedness.

Section.heading: Genesis 19:1-29 Sodom and Gomorrah were destroyed.

Questions.Q: Tell what happened at this time.
Questions.A: The two angels went to Sodom, and Lot persuaded them to stay overnight at his house. The men of Sodom tried to take the two visitors and rape them. In order to protect themselves and Lot's family, the angels struck the rioting men blind/with blindness/caused the rioting men to become blind. The next morning, the two visitors/visiting angels grabbed Lot and his wife and two daughters and led them out of the city. Sodom and Gomorrah - and the whole plain - were destroyed.

Questions.Q: Who went/came to Sodom?
Questions.A: Two of the three visitors who had been to see/visit Abraham went/came to Sodom. They are identified in the text/in this scripture as two angels. (1)
Questions.Alternative: Who went to Sodom?
Who came to Sodom?

Questions.Q: Who met those two angels?
Questions.A: Lot met them. (2)

Questions.Q: What did Lot say to the two angels?
Questions.A: Lot invited them to come to his place and to spend the night there. (2)

Questions.Q: What did the two angels say in response to Lot's invitation?
Questions.A: The angels said that they would just spend the night in the public area/square. (2)

Questions.Q: Did the two angels spend the night in the public area/square?
Questions.A: No, Lot persuaded them to stay at his house. (3)
Questions.Alternative: Did the two angels spend the night in the public area?
Did the two angels spend the night in the public square?

Questions.Q: When they were all about to go to sleep, what happened?
Questions.A: The men and boys of Sodom came, surrounded the house, and told Lot to send out his two visitors. (4-5)

Questions.Q: What did the men of Sodom want to do with Lot's two visitors?
Questions.A: They wanted to rape/violate the visitors. (5)

Questions.Q: Instead of Lot sending out/giving his two visitors to the men of Sodom, what did he suggest to the crowd?
Questions.A: Lot said that he would give to the crowd his two maiden daughters instead. (8)
Questions.Alternative: Instead of Lot sending out his two visitors to the men of Sodom, what did he suggest to the crowd?
Instead of Lot giving his two visitors to the men of Sodom, what did he suggest to the crowd?

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason why Lot offered his two daughters to the crowd, instead of sending out/giving up his visitors?
Questions.A: It would seem that, in Lot's mind, it was worse for his visitors to be raped/violated than for the same to happen to his daughters.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think was the reason why Lot offered his two daughters to the crowd, instead of sending out his visitors?
What do you think was the reason why Lot offered his two daughters to the crowd, instead of giving up his visitors?
Why do you think Lot offered his two daughters to the crowd, instead of giving up his visitors?

Questions.Q: After Lot begged the crowd not to harm his guests, what was the crowd's response?
Questions.A: The crowd ordered Lot to stand aside/get out of the way, and they threatened to treat him worse than they would treat the visitors. They crowded in on Lot, nearly pushing the door down. (9)

Questions.Q: Then what did Lot's two visitors do?
Questions.A: They pulled Lot inside the house and locked the door. Then they made the men blind/temporarily blind. (10-11)

Questions.Q: What did Lot's two visitors instruct him to do?
Questions.A: They told Lot to warn his relatives to flee. Lot was to warn his children and anyone married to his children. (12)

Questions.Q: What was the reason that the angels would have to destroy Sodom?
Questions.A: They would have to destroy Sodom because God was aware that the people of Sodom were very/excessively evil. (13)

Questions.Q: To whom did Lot go to warn that Sodom was about to be destroyed?
Questions.A: Lot went to warn two men who were about/planning to marry his daughters. (14)

Questions.Q: Did those two men/fiancés of his daughters flee the city with Lot and his family?
Questions.A: No. They did not believe Lot. -OR- No, they thought that Lot was joking. (14)
Questions.Alternative: Did those two men flee the city with Lot and his family?
Did those two fiancés of his daughters flee the city with Lot and his family?

Questions.Q: Did Lot want to leave Sodom/leave his place?
Questions.A: No. He hesitated/delayed. (16)
Questions.Alternative: Did Lot want to leave Sodom?
Did Lot want to leave his place?

Questions.Q: What did the angels have to do in order to compel/force Lot and his family to leave Sodom?
Questions.A: The angels took them by their hands and led/took them out of the city.
Questions.Alternative: What did the angels have to do in order to compel Lot and his family to leave Sodom?
What did the angels have to do in order to force Lot and his family to leave Sodom?

Questions.Q: God was willing to save Lot, even though Lot was not willing to leave. What does this show us about God's character? // What can we see in this incident about God's character?
Questions.A: God is merciful. (16)

Key Term Check: God was not obligated to save Lot and his family (from destruction), especially since Lot was not willing to obey the angels and leave Sodom. But God showed mercy or compassion in removing Lot and thus saving him.
Questions.Note: See "mercy" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: God was willing to save Lot, even though Lot was not willing to leave. What does this show us about God's character?
What can we see in this incident about God's character?
God was willing to save Lot, even though Lot was not willing to leave. What can we see in this incident about God's character?

Questions.Q: What did the angels instruct Lot and his family?
Questions.A: The angels said that they must run, and not stop in the valley/plain. They must not look back, but must continue to the mountains. (17)

Questions.Q: If Lot and his family would not obey, what was to happen to them?
Questions.A: They were to be destroyed/consumed/burned up. -OR- They were to die. (17)

Questions.Q: Did Lot want to flee to the mountains?
Questions.A: No, he did not. (18-19)

Questions.Q: What was the reason that Lot gave to God/to the angels for not wanting to flee to the mountains?
Questions.A: Lot said that the mountains were too far away. Perhaps he feared that when Sodom was destroyed, it would be too dangerous to be exposed/caught in the open plain, before there was time to reach the mountains. (19)
Questions.Alternative: What was the reason that Lot gave to God for not wanting to flee to the mountains?
What was the reason that Lot gave to the angels for not wanting to flee to the mountains?

Questions.Q: What did Lot admit that the angels were doing for him?
Questions.A: Lot admitted that the angels were (being) kind/merciful to save him. (19)

Key Term Check: In this situation, Lot was probably not referring to being saved from eternal punishment, but rather he meant that the angels were delivering him from certain death, as Sodom was about to be destroyed. Some languages may use one term to refer to saving someone from death, and a different term to refer to saving someone from eternal punishment.
Questions.Note: See "save" in KBT.

Questions.Q: So what did Lot suggest that he and his family do, instead of fleeing all the way to the mountains?
Questions.A: Lot suggested that he and his family take shelter in a small nearby town/city. (20)

Questions.Q: What was the angel's response to Lot's suggestion/request?
Questions.A: The angel agreed. He allowed Lot and his family to stay at a small place. (21)
Questions.Alternative: What was the angel's response to Lot's suggestion?
What was the angel's response to Lot's request?

Questions.Q: What did the angel urge Lot and his family to do?
Questions.A: He urged them to hurry. (22)

Questions.Q: What did the angel say was the reason why Lot and his family must hurry?
Questions.A: Lot and his family must hurry because the angel was soon to begin to destroy Sodom and Gomorrah. But the angel could not begin (to destroy the cities/the wicked people of the cities) until Lot and his family were safe. (22)

Questions.Q: After that/From then on, what did people call that place where Lot and his family took shelter?
Questions.A: People called the place "Zoar", which means "little". (22)
Questions.Alternative: After that, what did people call that place where Lot and his family took shelter?
From then on, what did people call that place where Lot and his family took shelter?

Questions.Q: At what time of day did Lot and his family arrive at Zoar?
Questions.A: They arrived there in early morning, at the time of sunrise. (23)

Questions.Q: What happened then to Sodom and Gomorrah?
Questions.A: God rained fire on the cities. -OR- God caused fire and brimstone/sulfur to fall on the cities. He destroyed all life in those cities/there. (24)

Questions.Q: What did God destroy by the fire?
Questions.A: God destroyed all of the people, animals, and plants of Sodom and Gomorrah, including nearby cities and villages. (25)

Questions.Q: While Lot and his family were fleeing, what did Lot's wife do?
Questions.A: She looked back at Sodom. (26)

Questions.Q: When Lot's wife looked back, what happened to her?
Questions.A: She became like a statue made of salt. (26)

Questions.Q: Who now went and looked out over the land?
Questions.A: Abraham looked out over the land. (27-28)

Questions.Q: What (kinship) relationship was Abraham to Lot?
Questions.A: Abraham was Lot's uncle.

Questions.Q: What did Abraham see?
Questions.A: Abraham saw thick smoke above the land, like a huge cooking/smoking fire/like smoke from a furnace. (28)

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that God showed mercy to Lot?
Questions.A: Lot was Abraham's nephew, and Abraham had been asking God not to destroy Sodom if there were good/innocent people living there. (It is not clear whether/that Lot, his wife, and their two daughters were "righteous/innocent" people. But probably they were, at least, not as evil as the rest of the people who were destroyed.)

Questions.Q: Tell what happened after Lot and his daughters had fled the wicked city of Sodom.
Questions.A: Lot and his two daughters left Zoar and lived in a cave in the mountains. The daughters were upset because they had no husbands. Thus they could not have children to carry on the family line. They influenced/induced their father to become drunk, and each of them then had sexual relations with Lot. From each of those two children born, a nation of many people eventually came into being/eventually emerged.

Questions.Q: What was the reason that Lot left Zoar?
Questions.A: Lot was afraid to remain in Zoar. (30)

Questions.Q: Who went with Lot from Zoar?
Questions.A: Lot's two daughters went with him. (30)

Questions.Q: When they left Zoar, where did they go?
Questions.A: They went to the mountains. (30)

Questions.Q: And what was their residence/dwelling place there in the mountains?
Questions.A: They lived in a cave. (30)
Questions.Alternative: And what was their residence place there in the mountains?
And what was their dwelling place there in the mountains?

Questions.Q: What was the concern of his daughters?
Questions.A: The daughters were concerned that they and their father had no descendants. Lot had no sons, and there were no men around to marry the two daughters. (31)

Questions.Q: So what did the two daughters decide to do?
Questions.A: The daughters decided to induce/influence their father to become drunk. Then (when he did not really know what he was doing), each of them would have sexual relations with him. (32)

Questions.Q: Which of the daughters was the first to carry out the plan?
Questions.A: The elder daughter was the first. (33)

Questions.Q: At the time the daughters had sexual relations with their father, did he know about it?
Questions.A: No, because he was too drunk. (33, 35)

Questions.Q: What was the outcome of the two daughters having sexual relations with Lot?
Questions.A: Both of the daughters became pregnant. (36)

Questions.Q: What people-group descended/came into being from the child of the elder daughter?
Questions.A: The son of the elder daughter was named Moab, and from him came the Moabites. (37)
Questions.Alternative: What people-group descended from the child of the elder daughter?
What people-group came into being from the child of the elder daughter?

Questions.Q: And what people-group is named after/named from the child of the younger daughter?
Questions.A: The son of the younger daughter was named Ben-Ammi, and from him came the Ammonites/and his descendants are called the Ammonites. (38)
Questions.Alternative: And what people-group is named after the child of the younger daughter?
And what people-group is named from the child of the younger daughter?

Questions.Q: Do you think what those daughters of Lot did was good?
Questions.A: No. Their action and the outcome are described here/in this passage, but there is no indication that God approved of it in any way.
Questions.Alternative: Do you think what Lot's daughters did was good?

Section.heading: Genesis 20:1-18 Abraham and Sarah deceived King Abimelech at Gerar.

Questions.Q: Tell what Abraham and Sarah did here/at this time, and what was the outcome.
Questions.A: They went to a place called Gerar, and while they were there, they said that Sarah was Abraham's sister. King Abimelech took Sarah into his palace (to be one of his concubines). But God came to the king in a dream and told him that Sarah was Abraham's wife. God also caused Abimelech's wife and the other women of the royal household to be barren/unable to become pregnant. So the king returned Sarah to Abraham, along with a gift of sheep and oxen and servants, and much silver (money). Abraham prayed to God, and God then healed Abimelech and his household.
Questions.Alternative: Tell what Abraham and Sarah did here, and what was the outcome.
Tell what Abraham and Sarah did at this time, and what was the outcome.

Questions.Q: Where were Abraham and Sarah at this time/according to this passage?
Questions.A: They had gone to the Negeb, to a place called Gerar, between Kadesh and Shur. -OR- They first went to the Negeb, to a place between Kadesh and Shur, and then they moved on to a place called Gerar. (1)
Questions.Alternative: Where were Abraham and Sarah at this time?
Where were Abraham and Sarah according to this passage?

Questions.Q: What did Abraham say about his wife, Sarah?
Questions.A: Abraham said that she was his sister. (2)

Questions.Q: What did King Abimelech do?
Questions.A: He had someone bring Sarah to him at his palace. He already had a wife (17), so he probably intended to make Sarah one of his concubines. (2)

Questions.Q: What did God reveal to Abimelech?
Questions.A: He told Abimelech that Sarah was a married woman. (3)

Questions.Q: By what means did God reveal that to Abimelech?
Questions.A: He appeared to him/revealed it to him in a dream. (3)

Questions.Q: What did God say was going to happen to Abimelech because he had taken a married woman into his household?
Questions.A: God said that Abimelech was going to die. (3)

Questions.Q: Had Abimelech had sexual relations with Sarah?
Questions.A: No, he had not. (4)

Questions.Q: Before Abimelech had the dream, had he known that Sarah was married?
Questions.A: No, he had not known that. (5)

Questions.Q: What was the reason why Abimelech had thought that Sarah was Abraham's sister?
Questions.A: He had thought that because both Abraham and Sarah had said that. (5)

Questions.Q: What did Abimelech claim here about his character?
Questions.A: He said that he was innocent: that he had done no wrong/that his conscience was clear and his hands were "clean". (5)
Key Term Check: A person with "clean hands" is one who is not guilty. (Either they did not commit an offense, or else they did but then they repented and the offended person(s)/one(s) forgave them.)
Questions.Note: See "clean" in KBT.

Questions.Q: How did it happen that Abimelech did not commit sin with Sarah? Was it because Abimelech was wise or cautious?
Questions.A: No, it was because God prevented Abimelech from sinning. (6)

Questions.Q: What did God command [to] Abimelech?
Questions.A: God told Abimelech that he must return Sarah to Abraham. (7)
Questions.Alternative: What did God command to Abimelech?
What did God command Abimelech?

Questions.Q: If/When Abimelech returned Sarah (to Abraham), what was Abraham to do for him?
Questions.A: Abraham was to/would pray for Abimelech. (7)
Questions.Alternative: If Abimelech returned Sarah (to Abraham), what was Abraham to do for him?
When Abimelech returned Sarah (to Abraham), what was Abraham to do for him?

Questions.Q: What was special about Abraham, so that Abimelech could be assured that Abraham's prayers would be effective?
Questions.A: Abraham was a prophet of God. (7)
