Key Term Check: In this case, a prophet is a mediator between God and man - one who intercedes or makes requests to God on behalf of someone else. Abraham earlier had interceded on behalf of the people of Sodom.
Questions.Note: See "prophet" in KBT.

Questions.Q: But if Abimelech did not return Sarah to Abraham, what would happen?
Questions.A: All the people in Abimelech's palace would die. (7)

Questions.Q: After God spoke to Abimelech through the dream, what did Abimelech do?
Questions.A: He got up early/arose early the next morning and called together his officials/advisors/servants. (8)

Questions.Q: When Abimelech's officials heard about his dream, what was their response?
Questions.A: They became very fearful. (8)

Questions.Q: After Abimelech informed his officials, what did he do?
Questions.A: He summoned Abraham and demanded an explanation. (9-10)

Questions.Q: According to Abimelech, if he had had sexual relations with Sarah, who would have shared in the guilt?
Questions.A: The people of Gerar, over whom Abimelech was ruler, would have shared in his guilt. (9)

Questions.Q: When Abraham said that Sarah was his sister, was he really being truthful?
Questions.A: No. He implied that she was only his sister. In fact, she was his half-sister, but also his wife. (12)

Questions.Q: What was the reason that Abraham gave for lying about his wife?
Questions.A: Abraham said that he was afraid that someone would kill him in order to take his wife. (11)

Questions.Q: Was this the first time that Abraham lied about Sarah?
Questions.A: No, he had done the same thing when he went to Egypt several years before this time. (12:10-20)

Questions.Q: In your opinion, was it right for Abraham to say that Sarah was (only) his sister?
Questions.A: No. He was being deceitful. // He deceived Abimelech (and others). He did not tell the whole truth.

Questions.Q: Did Abimelech return Sarah to Abraham?
Questions.A: Yes, he did. (14)

Questions.Q: What else did Abimelech give to Abraham?
Questions.A: Abimelech gave to Abraham sheep, oxen/cattle, and male and female servants. (14)

Questions.Q: What did Abimelech invite Abraham to do?
Questions.A: Abimelech invited Abraham to choose wherever he wanted to live. (15)

Questions.Q: What else did Abimelech give to Abraham?
Questions.A: Abimelech also gave 1000 silver coins/1000 pieces of silver to Abraham. (16)

Questions.Q: What was the reason why Abimelech gave to Abraham such very expensive gifts?
Questions.A: Abimelech did this to repay/compensate Sarah for shame, and as a sign that she had done nothing wrong. (16)

Questions.Q: What condition had all the palace women been experiencing?
Questions.A: They had been unable to become pregnant. (18)

Questions.Q: What did Abraham do concerning the condition of the palace women?
Questions.A: Abraham prayed to God; he asked God to heal them. (17)

Questions.Q: And were the palace women then able to become pregnant?
Questions.A: Yes, they were. (17)

Questions.Q: Besides the palace women, do we learn about anybody else who needed healing?
Questions.A: Yes, Abimelech also needed healing. (17)

Questions.Q: I am listing/will list 5 events, and I ask you to place them in the order in which they happened: (a) Abimelech had a dream; (b) Abimelech returned Sarah to Abraham; (c) the women of the palace became unable to become pregnant/unable to conceive; (d) Abimelech took Sarah into his palace; (e) Abraham prayed for Abimelech and for his people.
Questions.A: First, (d) Abimelech took Sarah into his palace; then (c) the women of the palace became unable to become pregnant/conceive. After that, (a) Abimelech had a dream; then (b) Abimelech returned Sarah to Abraham. Finally, (e) Abraham prayed for Abimelech and for his people/his subjects/the people of his nation.
Questions.Alternative: Put the following 5 events in the order in which they happened: (a) Abimelech had a dream; (b) Abimelech returned Sarah to Abraham; (c) the women of the palace became unable to become pregnant; (d) Abimelech took Sarah into his palace; (e) Abraham prayed for Abimelech and for his people.

I am listing 5 events, and I ask you to place them in the order in which they happened: (a) Abimelech had a dream; (b) Abimelech returned Sarah to Abraham; (c) the women of the palace became unable to become pregnant; (d) Abimelech took Sarah into his palace; (e) Abraham prayed for Abimelech and for his people.

I am listing 5 events, and I ask you to place them in the order in which they happened: (a) Abimelech had a dream; (b) Abimelech returned Sarah to Abraham; (c) the women of the palace became unable to conceive; (d) Abimelech took Sarah into his palace; (e) Abraham prayed for Abimelech and for his people.

I will list 5 events, and I ask you to place them in the order in which they happened: (a) Abimelech had a dream; (b) Abimelech returned Sarah to Abraham; (c) the women of the palace became unable to become pregnant; (d) Abimelech took Sarah into his palace; (e) Abraham prayed for Abimelech and for his people.

I will list 5 events, and I ask you to place them in the order in which they happened: (a) Abimelech had a dream; (b) Abimelech returned Sarah to Abraham; (c) the women of the palace became unable to conceive; (d) Abimelech took Sarah into his palace; (e) Abraham prayed for Abimelech and for his people.

Section.heading: Genesis 21:1-7 Isaac was born to (Sarah and) Abraham.

Questions.Q: About whom is this passage/account/story?
Questions.A: This passage/account/story is about Isaac (and Sarah and Abraham).
Questions.Alternative: About whom is this passage?
About whom is this account?
About whom is this story?

Questions.Q: Tell me about what happened in this passage/account/story.
Questions.A: Sarah became pregnant and gave birth to a son. Abraham named the boy, "Isaac," and circumcised Isaac when he was 8 days old.
Questions.Alternative: Tell me about what happened in this passage.
Tell me about what happened in this account.
Tell me about what happened in this story.

Questions.Q: What did Sarah experience here/at this time/in this account?
Questions.A: Sarah became pregnant and gave birth to a son. (2)
Questions.Alternative: What did Sarah experience here?
What did Sarah experience at this time?
What did Sarah experience in this account?

Questions.Q: Before that happened, did Sarah have any reason to believe that she would not give birth to a child?
Questions.A: Yes, she had never born/given birth to a child before; and she and Abraham were both already very old. (2, 5)

Questions.Q: Did Sarah have any reason to believe that she was to bear a child?
Questions.A: Yes, God had promised that to Abraham (17:16, 19, 21), and Sarah knew about the promise (18:13-14).

Questions.Q: What did Abraham name his son?
Questions.A: He called him "Isaac". (3)

Questions.Q: When Isaac was/became 8 days old, what did Abraham do?
Questions.A: Abraham circumcised Isaac. (4)
Questions.Alternative: When Isaac was 8 days old, what did Abraham do?
When Isaac became 8 days old, what did Abraham do?

Questions.Q: How old was Abraham when Isaac was born?
Questions.A: Abraham was 100 years old at that time. (5)

Questions.Q: Soon after Isaac was born, what did Sarah say?
Questions.A: Sarah said that God gave her joy and made her laugh, and others would join her in laughing. She also said that nobody would have thought to tell Abraham that Sarah would yet nurse/bear a child. -OR-She also said that nobody would have imagined that Sarah would yet nurse/bear a child. She also said that she was able to bear a son by Abraham who was also very old. (6-7)

Questions.Q: When Sarah spoke about other people laughing, what do you think that she meant? (Do you think that she meant that they will make fun of her? Or did she mean that they would share (in) her joy?)
Questions.A: Probably she meant that they would share (in) her joy, and thus laugh together with her. (6)

Questions.Q: Do you remember other times when Abraham and Sarah laughed?
Questions.A: Both Abraham and Sarah laughed when they were told that they would yet have a son. (17:17; 18:12, 15)

Questions.Q: What is the meaning of the name Isaac?
Questions.A: Isaac means "laughter", or "he laughs".
Questions.Note: The idea of "laughter" in connection with Isaac is relevant in 17:17, 19 and 18:12. A footnote or similar literary device should have indicated this connection at least once.
Questions.Alternative: What is the meaning of the name, "Isaac"?

Questions.Q: Tell what happened at this time/at the time of this account.
Questions.A: Sarah was upset at the idea of Ishmael having a part of Isaac's inheritance. She insisted that Abraham send away Ishmael and his mother, Hagar. So Abraham sent them out into the wilderness. Ishmael nearly died of thirst, but suddenly Hagar heard a voice promising that Ishmael would live and that his descendants would become a great nation. Then God showed Hagar some water, and Ishmael's life was spared. He grew up in the wilderness, became an archer, and eventually married/took a woman from Egypt for his wife.
Questions.Alternative: Tell what happened at this time.
Tell what happened at the time of this account.

Questions.Q: At the beginning of this account/story, approximately how old do you think Isaac was?
Questions.A: He was probably about two or 3 years old - he was at the age when his mother would stop breastfeeding him. (8)
Questions.Alternative: At the beginning of this account, approximately how old do you think Isaac was?
At the beginning of this story, approximately how old do you think Isaac was?

Questions.Q: At that time, what did Abraham do?
Questions.A: Abraham caused a feast to be held. (8)

Questions.Q: What did Sarah see happening?
Questions.A: Sarah saw Ishmael playing with Isaac. -OR- Sarah saw Ishmael teasing Isaac. -OR- Sarah saw Ishmael pretending that he was Isaac, the heir of Abraham. (9)
Questions.Note: The Hebrew text here can apparently be interpreted as any of the above. The person who answers should answer according to the interpretation that the translator chose.

Questions.Q: Ishmael's mother was Hagar. What two details are mentioned here about Hagar?
Questions.A: The writer mentions that Hagar was Egyptian, and that she was Sarah's servant. (9)

Questions.Q: So what did Sarah tell Abraham?
Questions.A: Sarah said that she did not want Ishmael to share in the inheritance, and thus she wanted Abraham to send Ishmael away. (10)

Questions.Q: How did Abraham feel about that?
Questions.A: Abraham felt/was very sad. (11)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that that made Abraham sad?
Questions.A: It made Abraham sad because Ishmael was his son. (11)

Questions.Q: What did God say to Abraham?
Questions.A: God told Abraham not to be upset, but to do whatever Sarah wanted him (Abraham) to do. (12)

Questions.Q: What did God promise about Ishmael?
Questions.A: God promised that Ishmael would have many descendants, and that his descendants will become a nation/people-group. (13)

Questions.Q: What did Abraham do the next morning?
Questions.A: He arose/got up early, gave Hagar food and water, and he sent her and her son away. (14)

Questions.Q: What did Hagar do?
Questions.A: She (took Ishmael and) wandered around the wilderness/uninhabited place called Beersheba. (14)

Questions.Q: When Hagar and Ishmael had no more water, what did Hagar do?
Questions.A: She left Ishmael under some bushes/in the shade of some bushes, and sat about 50 fathoms/100 yards away, and cried. (15-16)
Questions.Note: It is not completely clear from the Hebrew text whether verse 16 refers to Hagar crying or to Ishmael crying. The person who answers should answer according to the translated text.

Questions.Q: What did Hagar say to herself?
Questions.A: Hagar said that she could not bear to watch her child die. (16)

Questions.Q: Then what happened?
Questions.A: God/The angel of God called to Hagar. (17)

Questions.Q: From where did the voice come?
Questions.A: The voice came from heaven/the sky.

Key Term Check: It is not clear here whether the author intended to say that the voice came from the "sky", that is, from somewhere above; or if the voice came from "heaven" (where God is said to dwell).
Questions.Note: If the translators understand this to be referring to "heaven, where God is said to dwell"; then it is possible that a different term will be used in the translation/here than in earlier passages referring to the "sky" (e.g., Gen. 1; 2; 7:11; 8:2).
See "heaven, sky" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did God/the angel of God say to Hagar?
Questions.A: He said that Hagar need not fear, that God had heard her son crying. He said that Hagar was to go to her child/bring her child and comfort him. He also promised that he would make the descendants of Ishmael a powerful people-group. (17-18)
Questions.Alternative: What did God say to Hagar?
What did the angel of God say to Hagar?

Questions.Q: Then in what way did God help Hagar?
Questions.A: He caused her to see a well (of water), and she was thus able to obtain/draw water for her son. (19)

Questions.Q: What do we learn about Ishmael from this account/passage?
Questions.A: He lived in the wilderness of Paran, and became skilled at archery/became skilled at hunting animals with a bow and arrow. (20)
Questions.Alternative: What do we learn about Ishmael from this account?
What do we learn about Ishmael from this passage?

Questions.Q: Did God forget about Ishmael while he was growing up?
Questions.A: No - God was "with" Ishmael. -OR- God was caring for/watching over Ishmael. (20)
Questions.Note: The expression, "God with" occurs at least sixteen times in Genesis (21:20, 22; 26:3, 24, 28; 28:15, 20; 31:3, 5, 42; 35:3; 39:2, 3, 21, 23; 48:21). In these various contexts, God being "with" someone means that He was providing for them, or guiding them, or protecting them - He was caring for them.

Questions.Q: When Ishmael was an adult, what did his mother do?
Questions.A: She arranged for him to marry an Egyptian woman. (21)

Section.heading: Genesis 21:22-34 Abraham made an agreement with Abimelech.

Questions.Q: Tell me what happened in this account/at this time.
Questions.A: King Abimelech came to Abraham and asked him to promise that he would deal fairly/truthfully with Abimelech. Abraham agreed, but also mentioned that there was a problem with a water well which Abimelech's men had taken from Abraham's men. Abraham gave some animals to Abimelech, and the place was called "Beersheba", which means "Well of oath" or "Well of 7". And Abraham worshiped God there.
Questions.Alternative: Tell me what happened in this account.
Tell me what happened at this time.

Questions.Q: Who visited Abraham in this account/at this time?
Questions.A: King Abimelech and the leader of his soldiers, Phicol, visited him. (22)
Questions.Alternative: Who visited Abraham in this account?
Who visited Abraham at this time?

Questions.Q: What did Abimelech say to Abraham?
Questions.A: Abimelech said that God has been with Abraham/that God has been helping Abraham. Abimelech asked Abraham to promise/swear that he would not betray Abimelech or his descendants. -OR- Abimelech asked Abraham to promise/swear that he would always deal fairly/truthfully with him (Abimelech) and his descendants. (23)

Questions.Q: According to Abimelech, for what reason should Abraham be loyal to Abimelech?
Questions.A: Abimelech had been loyal to Abraham. (23)

Questions.Q: What was Abraham's reply to Abimelech?
Questions.A: Abraham agreed. He said that he would promise him that/he would make an oath. (24)

Questions.Q: What was the problem that Abraham then mentioned to Abimelech?
Questions.A: Abraham told Abimelech about a (water) well which Abimelech's servants had taken from Abraham's servants/which Abimelech's servants were no longer allowing Abraham's servants to use. (25)

Questions.Q: And what was Abimelech's response to Abraham?
Questions.A: Abimelech said that he had not known anything about that/the situation. (26)

Questions.Q: What did Abraham give to Abimelech?
Questions.A: Abraham gave sheep and oxen/cattle to Abimelech. (27)

Questions.Q: What did Abraham set apart (from his flock of sheep)?
Questions.A: He set apart seven young female lambs/sheep. (28)

Questions.Q: What was the meaning of those seven sheep?
Questions.A: Abraham gave them to Abimelech to be a sign that Abimelech believed that Abraham had dug the well. (30)

Questions.Q: What was the reason that that place was called Beersheba?
Questions.A: The word "Beersheba" means "Well where a promise was made"/"Well of oath"/"Well of Seven".
Questions.Note: It is not certain whether the name "Beersheba" referred to the oath/treaty which Abraham and Abimelech made, or if it referred to the seven young sheep.
Questions.Alternative: Why was that place was called Beersheba?
What was the reason that that place was called, "Beersheba"?

Questions.Q: After Abimelech left, what two things did Abraham do?
Questions.A: He planted a "tamarisk" tree, and he worshiped God. (32)

Questions.Q: What quality or characteristic of God does the writer mention here?
Questions.A: The writer mentions that God is eternal - that he had no beginning and will have no end. (33)

Questions.Q: Where did Abraham stay at that time?
Questions.A: He stayed at the place of the Philistine people. (34)

Section.heading: Genesis 22:1-24 God tested Abraham's faith by commanding/requesting him to sacrifice Isaac.

Questions.Q: What did God tell Abraham to do, and what happened?
Questions.A: God told Abraham to take Isaac, his beloved son, to a mountain, where Abraham was to kill Isaac and to offer/sacrifice him as a burnt offering to God. Abraham obeyed God, and at the last minute, God told Abraham not to harm Isaac. Then God provided a ram for a sacrifice, instead of Isaac. God repeated his blessing-promise to Abraham. Finally, Abraham heard about the many sons that his brother, Nahor, had.

Questions.Q: For what purpose did God tell Abraham to sacrifice Isaac?
Questions.A: God did this to test Abraham's faith - to demonstrate that Abraham believed that whatever God said is true/right. (1)

Key Term Check: This is a key passage for understanding the Biblical teaching about "faith" or "believing". It had been many years since God first promised that Abraham's descendants would be as numerous as the stars of the sky. God had said that his promise was to be fulfilled through Isaac. At this time, God has told Abraham to sacrifice Isaac. God was asking Abraham to believe that he (God) would fulfill his promise, even though it looked absolutely/completely impossible.
Questions.Note: See "believe" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did God tell Abraham to do?
Questions.A: God told Abraham to take his beloved son, Isaac, to the land of Moriah; and at Moriah Abraham was to kill/slaughter Isaac, and to burn him as a sacrifice to God. (2)

Questions.Q: What did Abraham do in response to God's instructions?
Questions.A: He did as God had told him to do. He got up early, saddled a donkey, and got firewood for the sacrifice. He took Isaac and two of his (Abraham's) own servants, and went to the place where God had told him to go. (3)

Questions.Q: How many days did they walk, before they could see/they saw the place where they were to go?
Questions.A: They walked for three days (before they could see that place). (4)
Questions.Alternative: How many days did they walk, before they could see the place where they were to go?
How many days did they walk, before they saw the place where they were to go?

Questions.Q: When Abraham could see/saw the place to which they were going, what did he say to his servants?
Questions.A: Abraham told his servants to remain with the donkey.
Questions.Alternative: When Abraham could see the place to which they were going, what did he say to his servants?
When Abraham saw the place to which they were going, what did he say to his servants?

Questions.Q: What did Abraham say that he and Isaac would do?
Questions.A: Abraham said that he and Isaac would go a little further, and worship (God), and then return to where the servants were waiting. (5)
Questions.Note: Skip this question if the answer was already given in response to the previous question.

Questions.Q: After Abraham spoke to the servants, what did he and Isaac do?
Questions.A: Abraham loaded the firewood on Isaac's shoulders/head/back. Then Abraham took the knife and fire/coals, and he and Isaac continued walking. (6)

Questions.Q: What did Isaac ask his father?
Questions.A: He asked where the lamb was that they would use for the sacrifice. (7)

Questions.Q: What was Abraham's answer?
Questions.A: Abraham told him/said that God would provide the lamb. (8)

Questions.Q: When they arrived at the place, about which God had told Abraham, what did Abraham do?
Questions.A: He built an altar and piled the firewood on it. Then he tied up Isaac, and laid him on top of the wood. (9)

Questions.Q: Then what did Abraham do?
Questions.A: He got/picked up the knife to kill/slaughter his son. (10)

Questions.Q: As Abraham picked up the knife to kill Isaac, what happened?
Questions.A: God called/The angel of God called to him from heaven, telling Abraham not to kill the boy. (12)

Questions.Q: What else did he say to Abraham?
Questions.A: God said that he knew that Abraham truly exalts and obeys God/honors and respects God. God said that Abraham demonstrated that he was willing to obey God completely, because he (Abraham) was willing to offer/sacrifice his only/beloved son to God. (12)

Questions.Q: Was Abraham able to sacrifice a burnt offering to God?
Questions.A: Yes, because God provided a male sheep. -OR- Yes, because suddenly a male sheep appeared, caught in a nearby bush; and Abraham offered that to God. (13)

Questions.Q: For what reason did Abraham name the place "The Lord Will Provide"/"Yahweh-yireh"?
Questions.A: Abraham named it that, because God had provided him (with) an animal to sacrifice. (14)
Questions.Alternative: For what reason did Abraham name the place "The Lord Will Provide"?
For what reason did Abraham name the place "The Lord Will "Yahweh-yireh"?

Questions.Q: Had Abraham predicted, "God will provide" at an earlier point in this story?
Questions.A: Yes, when Isaac had asked Abraham, "Where is the lamb for the sacrifice?" Abraham had answered him that God would provide (an animal). (7-8)

Questions.Q: As God repeated his promises to Abraham, what did God say was a reason for blessing Abraham?
Questions.A: God said that he was blessing Abraham because Abraham obeyed/listened to him (God), even to the extent that Abraham entrusted to God his only/beloved son. (16)

Questions.Q: What did God promise to Abraham?
Questions.A: God promised to bless Abraham greatly/richly. God said that Abraham's descendants would become as numerous as the stars in the sky and as the sand on the seashores, and that his descendants would be powerful. (17)

Questions.Q: And what did God say about all people-groups in the world?
Questions.A: God said that through Abraham's descendants, all people-groups in the world would also be blessed. (18)

Questions.Q: After God spoke his promises to Abraham, what happened next?
Questions.A: Abraham and Isaac returned to the servants, and then they all went home to Beersheba. (19)

Questions.Q: What (kinship) relationship were Nahor and Abraham?
Questions.A: They were brothers. (20)
Questions.Alternative: What relationship were Nahor and Abraham?
What was the relationship between Nahor and Abraham?
How were Nahor and Abraham related?

Questions.Q: How many sons did Nahor have by his wife, Milcah?
Questions.A: He had eight sons by Milcah. (20-22)

Questions.Q: How many sons did Nahor have by Reumah?
Questions.A: He had four sons by Reumah. (24)

Questions.Q: So, how many sons did Abraham's brother have altogether?
Questions.A: He had twelve sons. (20, 24)

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason the writer mentioned about those twelve sons of Abraham's brother in this passage?
Questions.A: Perhaps this was another test of Abraham's faith. Abraham heard of all the sons that his brother had, but Abraham still had only two sons - and one of them had been sent away.

Section.heading: Genesis 23:1-20 Sarah died and was buried.

Questions.Q: Tell what happened at this time/in this passage.
Questions.A: Sarah died, and Abraham bought a piece of land to use as a burial place for her.
Questions.Alternative: Tell what happened at this time.
Tell what happened in this passage.

Questions.Q: Where was Sarah, and how old was she, when she died?
Questions.A: She was at Kiriath Arba, later called Hebron. She was 127 years old. (1, 2)

Questions.Q: What did Abraham do when Sarah died?
Questions.A: He mourned and wept. (2)

Questions.Q: What was Abraham's purpose in going to the Hittites?
Questions.A: He went to them in order to get/acquire a burial place for Sarah. (3-4)

Questions.Q: What was the reason why it might have been difficult for Abraham to get/acquire a burial place for Sarah?
Questions.A: Abraham was a foreigner, and thus the Hittites might have been unwilling to give or sell him any land. (4)
Questions.Alternative: What was the reason why it might have been difficult for Abraham to get a burial place for Sarah?
What was the reason why it might have been difficult for Abraham to acquire a burial place for Sarah?

Questions.Q: After Abraham requested some land where he could bury Sarah, what was the answer of the Hittites?
Questions.A: They said that Abraham is a powerful/honored leader, and that his wife should be/was entitled to be buried in a special grave. They told Abraham that they would allow him to bury Sarah in any of their burial places. (5-6)
Questions.Note: At this time, the Hittites did not actually offer to give or sell Abraham any land. They offered him the use of one of their burial places.

Questions.Q: After the Hittites answered him, what did Abraham do before he spoke to them again?
Questions.A: Abraham bowed to the Hittites (to show them respect/to show his respect for them). (7)

Questions.Q: Where was the place that Abraham wanted as a burial place for Sarah?
Questions.A: It was the cave of Machpelah, at the end of Ephron's land. (9)

Questions.Q: At that time, who was the owner of that piece of land?
Questions.A: The owner was Ephron, son of Zohar. (8)

Questions.Q: How much did Abraham say that he would give as payment for the cave?
Questions.A: He said that he would pay the full price - however much Ephron valued it. (9)

Questions.Q: Did Abraham want some land that he could use only temporarily?
Questions.A: No, he wanted land for a permanent burial place. (9)

Questions.Q: Where was Ephron at that time?
Questions.A: He was there sitting with the other Hittites at the gate. (10)

Questions.Q: What was Ephron's answer to Abraham?
Questions.A: Ephron said that he would give the land, including the cave, for Abraham to bury his wife. (11)

Questions.Q: What did Abraham do before he replied?
Questions.A: Abraham bowed (again). (12)

Questions.Q: What then did Abraham say?
Questions.A: Abraham offered to pay (the) full price for the land. (13)

Questions.Q: What was Ephron's response? // What did Ephron reply to Abraham?
Questions.A: He said that the value of the land was 400 pieces of silver - but what is that to friends? -OR- but that is nothing to friends -OR- but since we want to be friends, we do not need to be concerned about the price. (14-15)
Questions.Alternative: What was Ephron's response?
What did Ephron reply to Abraham?

Questions.Q: What happened next?
Questions.A: Abraham paid Ephron 400 pieces of silver. Then he buried Sarah. (16, 19)

Questions.Q: What was included in the land that Abraham bought?
Questions.A: The land included the field, the cave, and trees in the field. (17)

Questions.Q: Who witnessed this agreement?
Questions.A: The Hittites/The Hittite elders who were gathered there witnessed the agreement. (18)

Questions.Q: What was Abraham's purpose for the land that he had bought?
Questions.A: He bought the land in order to make a permanent burial place (for Sarah). (20)

Questions.Q: Tell what happened in this chapter.
Questions.A: Abraham had become very old, and his son, Isaac, still had no wife. So Abraham sent a trusted servant back to Abraham's homeland to get/find a wife for Isaac. Abraham's servant asked/requested God to lead him to the woman of God's choice. The servant asked/requested of God that if a certain woman was God's choice, that when the servant asked her for some drinking water, then she would give him some. He also asked/requested God that the woman of God's choice would offer to get/draw/bring him water for his (the servant's) camels. As soon as the servant finished praying/making that request of God, a young woman named Rebekah appeared. She was the daughter of Isaac's cousin, Bethuel. When Abraham's servant asked her for a drink, she gave him one and offered to get/draw/bring water for his camels, also. The servant watched her, and then gave her some jewelry, and asked/questioned her about her family. When the servant learned that Rebekah was from Abraham's family, he praised God. He went with Rebekah to her home, and explained everything to her family. Her family agreed that Rebekah could go with that servant to marry Isaac - but they wanted her to stay a little while longer. The servant wanted to return home to Canaan soon, and Rebekah agreed that she would go with him. As they were arriving back in Canaan, Rebekah saw a man in the field - it turned out to be Isaac. They were married, and Rebekah comforted Isaac over/in the death/loss of his mother.

Questions.Q: What did the author say about Abraham at this time/at the time of this incident?
Questions.A: Abraham was now very old, and God had blessed him in many ways. (1)
Questions.Alternative: What did the author say about Abraham at this time?
What did the author say about Abraham at the time of this incident?

Questions.Q: In verse 2, to whom was Abraham speaking?
Questions.A: He was speaking with the leader of his servants, the one entrusted with all Abraham's wealth/the one in charge of his household. (2)

Questions.Q: What was the custom at that time when making a very important vow/promise?
Questions.A: One would put his hand under the thigh/between the thighs of the person to whom he was making a promise. (2)
Questions.Alternative: What was the custom at that time when making a very important vow?
What was the custom at that time when making a very important promise?

Questions.Q: What did Abraham ask his servant to promise?
Questions.A: The servant was to promise that he would not get/find a wife for Isaac from among the Canaanite people. Rather, the servant was to go to Abraham's relatives in another land to get/find a wife for Isaac. (3-4)

Questions.Q: Among whom was the servant to seek/choose a wife for Isaac?
Questions.A: He was to seek/choose a woman from among Abraham's relatives. (4)
Questions.Alternative: Among whom was the servant to seek a wife for Isaac?
Among whom was the servant to choose a wife for Isaac?

Questions.Q: What worried/concerned Abraham's servant?
Questions.A: He was worried that a woman/the prospective wife might not want to leave her home (land), and go to Canaan to live; and that Isaac might have to leave Canaan and return to the relatives' land. (5)
Questions.Alternative: What worried Abraham's servant?
What concerned Abraham's servant?

Questions.Q: And what was Abraham's response to his servant?
Questions.A: Abraham told his servant that Isaac was not to leave Canaan and return to the land of his relatives. (6, 8)

Questions.Q: What do you think might have been the reason why Abraham did not want Isaac to go to his (Abraham's) former place?
Questions.A: God had promised the land of Canaan to Abraham and his descendants. If Isaac went back/should go back to Abraham's relatives' land/former place, then Isaac might not return again to Canaan. (7)

Questions.Q: What did Abraham say that God would do, in order that the servant would be able to find/get a wife for Isaac?
Questions.A: Abraham said that God would send his angel ahead to help the servant. (7)
Questions.Alternative: What did Abraham say that God would do, in order that the servant would be able to find a wife for Isaac?
What did Abraham say that God would do, in order that the servant would be able to get a wife for Isaac?

Questions.Q: But if there was no woman willing to go with the servant to Canaan, then what would happen?
Questions.A: The servant would not have to fulfill his promise/vow to Abraham. But regardless of what happened, the servant must not take Isaac back to Abraham's former place. (8)

Questions.Q: Was Abraham's servant willing to make the promise/vow to carry out Abraham's wishes?
Questions.A: Yes, he put his hand under Abraham's thigh/between Abraham's thighs and promised/swore to do all that Abraham had asked him to do. (9)
Questions.Alternative: Was Abraham's servant willing to make the promise to carry out Abraham's wishes?
Was Abraham's servant willing to make the vow to carry out Abraham's wishes?

Questions.Q: Upon how many animals did the servant load cargo?
Questions.A: He loaded cargo on ten animals. (10)

Questions.Q: What kind of animals was used to carry the cargo?
Questions.A: They were camels - large, strong animals that could carry heavy burdens for long distances. (10)

Questions.Q: What was the cargo of the camels?
Questions.A: They carried various gifts. (10)

Questions.Q: Where did Abraham's servant go?
Questions.A: He went to Aram Naharaim. -OR- He went to Mesopotamia. (10)

Questions.Q: Who had settled in the place to which the servant went?
Questions.A: Nahor, the brother of Abraham, had settled there. (10)

Questions.Q: When the servant arrived there, what time of day was it?
Questions.A: It was late afternoon or evening. (11)

Questions.Q: In that place, what often happened at that time of day?
Questions.A: The women came to get/draw water. (11)

Questions.Q: When he arrived in the late afternoon/evening, was that the same day on which he had begun his journey?
Questions.A: No, he had traveled many days/a great distance.
Questions.Alternative: When he arrived in the late afternoon, was that the same day on which he had begun his journey?
When he arrived in the evening, was that the same day on which he had begun his journey?

Questions.Q: What did he have the camels do?
Questions.A: He had them kneel down (to rest) near a well/spring outside the city/town/village. (11)

Questions.Q: What did the servant request from God in verse 12?
Questions.A: He asked God to show mercy/loving-kindness to Abraham by giving him (the servant) success as he sought a wife for Isaac. (12)

Questions.Q: How was the servant to know which woman God had chosen to be a wife for Isaac?
Questions.A: The servant was to ask for some water. The woman whom God had chosen to be Isaac's wife would give the servant some water. She would also offer to draw water for the camels. (14)

Questions.Q: While Abraham's servant was still praying, who arrived at the spring/well?
Questions.A: A young (unmarried) woman named Rebekah arrived. (15)
Questions.Alternative: While Abraham's servant was still praying, who arrived at the spring?
While Abraham's servant was still praying, who arrived at the well?

Questions.Q: What was Rebekah carrying?
Questions.A: She was carrying a water pot/jar. (15)

Questions.Q: In what manner was she carrying the jar?
Questions.A: She was carrying it on her shoulder. (15)

Questions.Q: Who was this Rebekah? That is, who was her father, and who were her grandparents?
Questions.A: She was the daughter of Bethuel; her grandparents were Nahor and Milcah. (Nahor was Abraham's brother.) (15)

Questions.Q: What else do we learn from this passage about Rebekah?
Questions.A: She was young, beautiful, and had never been married nor had sexual relations. (16)

Questions.Q: When the servant saw Rebekah, what did he do?
Questions.A: He asked her to give him a drink from her pot/jar of water. (17)

Questions.Q: And what was Rebekah's answer?
Questions.A: She offered him water to drink. (18)

Questions.Q: After the servant had finished drinking, what then did Rebekah say to him?
Questions.A: She offered to get/draw water for his camels, too - all the water that they would need. (19)

Questions.Q: Then what did Rebekah do?
Questions.A: She poured the water from her jar into the trough, and then drew/got water for all the camels. (20)

Questions.Q: Do you think that she had to draw/get a lot of water?
Questions.A: Yes, she had to get enough for ten camels. (Camels drink a lot of water.) (20)
Questions.Alternative: Do you think that she had to draw a lot of water?
Do you think that she had to get a lot of water?

Questions.Q: While Rebekah was drawing/getting water for the camels, what did the servant do?
Questions.A: He watched her, in order to see if she did what he had requested of God (as a sign that she was the one to be Isaac's wife). (21)
Questions.Alternative: While Rebekah was drawing water for the camels, what did the servant do?
While Rebekah was getting water for the camels, what did the servant do?

Questions.Q: After Rebekah had finished drawing/getting water for the camels, what did Abraham's servant do?
Questions.A: The servant gave her a gold nose ring and two heavy/large gold bracelets. (22)
Questions.Alternative: After Rebekah had finished drawing water for the camels, what did Abraham's servant do?
After Rebekah had finished getting water for the camels, what did Abraham's servant do?

Questions.Q: Then what did the servant ask Rebekah?
Questions.A: He asked her who her father is/who her parents are. And he asked if he and his companion(s) could stay at her father's house that night. (23)

Questions.Q: What was Rebekah's answer?
Questions.A: She said that her father was Bethuel, and her grandparents were Nahor and Milcah. And she said that there was a place for the servant and his companions to stay in their house. She told him that her (father's) household would also provide food for the servant's camels. (24-25)

Questions.Q: When the servant heard Rebekah's answer, what did he do?
Questions.A: He bowed/He prostrated himself, and thanked and praised God. (26)

Questions.Q: What did Abraham's servant say/declare about God?
Questions.A: He said/declared that God had been merciful/kind and faithful, and had fulfilled his promise to Abraham by leading him (the servant) to Abraham's relatives. (27)
Questions.Alternative: What did Abraham's servant say about God?
What did Abraham's servant declare about God?

Questions.Q: When Rebekah had finished speaking with the servant, what did she do?
Questions.A: She ran home and told her mother and other family members about what had happened. (28)

Questions.Q: Who was Laban?
Questions.A: Laban was Rebekah's brother. (29)

Questions.Q: When he heard what Rebekah said, what did he do?
Questions.A: He ran to find Abraham's servant. When he found the servant, he invited him to come and stay at their house. (30-31)

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that Laban was very eager to invite the servant to his father's house?
Questions.A: Maybe the gold jewelry (and many camels) impressed Laban. (30) -OR- Maybe he wanted to get his sister married off. -OR- Maybe he was excited about his sister being able to marry a relative.

Questions.Q: Where did Laban find Abraham's servant?
Questions.A: The servant was still at the well/spring. (30)

Questions.Q: What did Laban say to the servant?
Questions.A: He invited the servant to his house, saying that there was room for him, and also for his camels. (31)

Questions.Q: When they arrived at the house, what happened?
Questions.A: Laban unloaded the cargo from the camels, and he also fed the camels and made a place for them to rest. And Laban brought water to Abraham's servant and his companions, so that they could wash their feet. -OR- Laban had the cargo from the camels unloaded, and he had the camels fed and had a place made for the camels to rest. Laban also had water brought to Abraham's servant and his companions, so that they could wash their feet. (32)

Questions.Q: Afterwards, when someone brought food, what did Abraham's servant say?
Questions.A: He said that he could not eat until he had explained his purpose in coming to them. (33)

Questions.Q: What did the servant say about Abraham?
Questions.A: He said that God had blessed Abraham, and that Abraham was now wealthy, with many animals, such as sheep and goats/cattle, camels, and donkeys. He told them that Abraham also had silver and gold, and male and female slaves. (34-35)

Questions.Q: According to the servant, what was the reason that Abraham had become so wealthy?
Questions.A: God had blessed Abraham.
Questions.Note: The concept "bless" is a key concept throughout this chapter. See also verses 1, 27, 31.

Questions.Q: Then what did the servant say about Sarah?
Questions.A: He said that she had given birth to a son in her old age. (36)

Questions.Q: Then what did the servant say about Isaac?
Questions.A: He said that Isaac would inherit all of Abraham's wealth. (36)

Questions.Q: What did the servant talk about next?
Questions.A: The servant said that he had made a solemn promise/vow to Abraham, that he (the servant) would not get/choose a wife for Isaac from Canaan. Rather, the servant promised that he would go to the family of Abraham's father to get/choose a wife for Isaac. (37-38)

Questions.Q: Abraham had said that there was a circumstance/situation in which the servant would not have to fulfill that vow. What was that situation?
Questions.A: Abraham had said that, if the servant made the proposal/went to Abraham's relatives, but they would not allow any of their young women to become Isaac's wife, then he (the servant) would not have to fulfill the vow. (41)
Questions.Alternative: Abraham had said that there was a circumstance in which the servant would not have to fulfill that vow. What was that situation?
Abraham had said that there was a situation in which the servant would not have to fulfill that vow. What was that situation?

Questions.Q: Had Abraham been confident that his servant would find a wife for Isaac among his (Abraham's) relatives?
Questions.A: Yes, Abraham had been confident. (40)

Questions.Q: What did Abraham say would happen to make the servant's journey successful?
Questions.A: Abraham said that God would send his angel with the servant, and would thus give him (Abraham's servant) success. (40)

Questions.Q: The servant then told them what he had requested of God earlier. What had he requested of/from God?
Questions.A: He had asked God to help him succeed/achieve his purpose. He had said that if a girl came to draw/get water, he would ask her for some. Also if she was willing to give him (some) water, and also to draw/get water for his camels, he asked God that she might be the one whom God had chosen to be a wife for Isaac. (42-44)
Questions.Alternative: The servant then told them what he had requested of God earlier. What had he requested of God?
The servant then told them what he had requested of God earlier. What had he requested from God?

Questions.Q: Then he told them about Rebekah's arrival. What did he say about that?
Questions.A: He said that while he had still been praying/He said that before he had finished praying, Rebekah had arrived to draw/get water. After she had filled her jar, he asked her for a drink, and she gave him some water, and also took/gave water to the camels. He had then asked her about her father, and she had told him about her family. He had then given her a nose-ring and bracelets. (45-47)

Questions.Q: What did the servant say he did after that?
Questions.A: He said that he had worshiped and praised God. (48)

Questions.Q: According to the servant, what was the reason that he had been successful as he had sought a wife for Isaac?
Questions.A: The servant had been successful because God had led/guided him to the relatives of his master, and he was thus able to find a suitable wife for Isaac. (48)

Questions.Q: Then what did the servant request of Rebekah's family?
Questions.A: The servant requested that Rebekah's family allow her to become Isaac's wife/that Rebekah's family receive Abraham's son (as Rebekah's husband) - or else tell him otherwise. (49)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the servant needed to know whether Rebekah's family was willing to allow her to become Isaac's wife?
Questions.A: When the servant knew the intentions of Rebekah's family, then he would know what he should do next. (49)

Questions.Q: What answer did the brother and father of Rebekah give to Abraham's servant?
Questions.A: They said that it was clear that God had brought Abraham's servant to them. -OR- They said that it was clear that what had happened was God's will. Therefore, they must not choose to go/to speak against God's will. They told Abraham's servant to take Rebekah to be Isaac's wife, because this was predestined by God/because this was determined by God from beforehand. (50-51)

Questions.Q: When the servant heard their answer, what was the first thing that he did?
Questions.A: He bowed (low to the ground) and worshiped/praised God. (52)

Questions.Q: After that, what else did the servant do?
Questions.A: He brought out beautiful clothing, gold and silver jewelry, and put them on Rebekah. He also gave expensive gifts to Laban and to Rebekah's mother. (53)

Questions.Q: After Abraham's servant gave the gifts, what happened next?
Questions.A: Rebekah's family gave the servant and his companions food and drink. And the servant and his companions slept there for one night. (54)

Questions.Q: When they awoke the next morning, what did the servant do?
Questions.A: He requested permission to take Rebekah and begin the journey home. (54)

Questions.Q: But what did Rebekah's brother and mother want?
Questions.A: They wanted Rebekah to stay with them another week or 10 days. -OR- They wanted Rebekah to stay with them another year or so. (55)
Questions.Note: The meaning of the Hebrew text is not certain at this point. The one responding to these questions should provide an answer which is consistent with the translated text.

Questions.Q: After Rebekah's family suggested that she remain at home for a period of time, what was the response of Abraham's servant's?
Questions.A: He did not want to delay his return home, since God had granted success in his mission. (56)

Questions.Q: So then what did Rebekah's relatives say?
Questions.A: They said that they would ask Rebekah what she wanted to do. (57)

Questions.Q: What did Rebekah want to do?
Questions.A: She said that she would go with Abraham's servant. (58)

Questions.Q: Who accompanied Rebekah as she left home?
Questions.A: The woman who had nursed Rebekah/cared for Rebekah went with her. (59)

Questions.Q: As Rebekah was about to leave, what did her relatives do?
Questions.A: They prayed to God, asking him to bless Rebekah. (60)

Questions.Q: As they prayed to God, what did they ask him to do for Rebekah?
Questions.A: They asked God that she would have very many descendants, and that her descendants would be victorious over their enemies. (60)

Questions.Q: Who else accompanied Rebekah?
Questions.A: Other servants who had been looking after Rebekah also accompanied her. (61)

Questions.Q: What was their mode of travel?
Questions.A: They rode on camels. (61)

Questions.Q: Meanwhile, where was Isaac?
Questions.A: He was living in the Negeb, in South Canaan/south of Canaan. He had recently traveled to the Well of God Who Sees Me/traveled to Beer-lahairoi, but had now returned home. -OR Isaac had moved on to Beer-lahairoi and was living in the Negeb. (62)
Questions.Note: The meaning of the Hebrew text is not certain at this point. The one responding to these questions should provide an answer which is consistent with the translated text.

Questions.Q: When Isaac saw that some camels were arriving, about what time of the day was it?
Questions.A: It was evening. (63)

Questions.Q: And what was Isaac doing at that time?
Questions.A: He was strolling, thinking about God. -OR- He was praying/mourning/planting in the field. (63)
Questions.Note: The meaning of the Hebrew text is not certain at this point. The one responding to these questions should provide an answer which is consistent with the translated text.

Questions.Q: When Rebekah saw Isaac, what did she do?
Questions.A: She dismounted/got down from her camel, and asked the servant who that man was. (64-65)

Questions.Q: When he told her that it was Isaac, then what did she do?
Questions.A: She got/brought out a veil and covered her face. (65)

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that she covered her face?
Questions.A: Perhaps it was the custom when a young woman was about to meet her future husband. (66)

Questions.Q: When they reached Isaac, what did the servant do?
Questions.A: He told Isaac all that had happened. (66)

Questions.Q: What did Isaac do, and what did he experience?
Questions.A: He took Rebekah as his wife. He loved her, and she brought comfort to him as he had been mourning his mother's death. (67)

Key Term Check: This is probably the first time that the writer of Genesis speaks of someone loving his/her spouse. In some languages, it may be necessary to use a different term here than at Gen. 22:2, where we read of Abraham's love for Isaac.
Questions.Note: See "love" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What were the names of the three women by/through whom Abraham had sons?
Questions.A: They were Hagar, Sarah, and Keturah.
Questions.Alternative: What were the names of the three women by whom Abraham had sons?
What were the names of the three women through whom Abraham had sons?

Questions.Q: Before Abraham died, did he see the complete fulfillment of God's promises to him?
Questions.A: No. God gave Abraham several sons, including Isaac. And Abraham was able to purchase a small piece of land in Canaan. But before he died, Abraham did not have countless descendants who had become a strong nation.

Questions.Q: Does this mean that sometimes God makes promises which he does not keep? -OR- Does this mean that sometimes God's promises do not come true?
Questions.A: No, it only means that sometimes he does not fulfill them immediately.
Questions.Alternative: Does this mean that sometimes God makes promises which he does not keep?
Does this mean that sometimes God's promises do not come true?

Questions.Q: How many sons did Abraham have by Keturah?
Questions.A: He had six sons by Keturah. (2)
Questions.Note: Some translations do not specify that the children of Abraham mentioned here were all sons - that is, male children. However, the children referred to here are certainly sons, and the translation should make this clear.

Questions.Q: To whom did Abraham bequeath most of his wealth?
Questions.A: He gave most of it to Isaac. (5)

Questions.Q: What did Abraham do for his other sons?
Questions.A: He gave them gifts/portions of his wealth. (6)

Questions.Q: To what place did Abraham send his other sons?
Questions.A: He sent them away from Isaac, to a place in the east. (6)

Questions.Q: How old was Abraham at the time of his death?
Questions.A: He was 175 years old. (7)

Questions.Q: Who buried him?
Questions.A: His sons, Isaac and Ishmael buried him. (9)

Questions.Q: Where did they bury him?
Questions.A: They buried him in the cave of Machpelah, near Mamre. (9)

Questions.Q: Who was the former owner of the land where they buried Abraham?
Questions.A: The former owner was Ephron, the son of Zohar. (9)

Questions.Q: From what people-group was Ephron?
Questions.A: He was a Hittite. -OR- He was from the Hit/Hatti people-group. (9)

Questions.Q: Was Abraham the first person whom someone buried in this cave?
Questions.A: No, Abraham had earlier buried his wife Sarah there. (10)

Questions.Q: Where did Isaac live after his father died?
Questions.A: He lived near Beer-lahairoi in the Negeb. -OR- He lived in the Negeb near the Well of God Who Sees Me. (11)

Questions.Q: What had Abraham experienced which God now transferred to Isaac?
Questions.A: God had blessed Abraham. God now blessed Isaac. -OR- Abraham had experienced God's blessings. Now Isaac experienced His blessings. (11)

Questions.Q: Tell what this section is about. -OR- What is the theme/subject/topic of this section?
Questions.A: This passage is about the people who descended from Ishmael, the son of Abraham and Hagar.
Questions.Alternative: Tell what this section is about.
What is the theme of this section?
What is the subject of this section?
What is the topic of this section?

Questions.Q: Tell me about Ishmael's mother.
Questions.A: She was Hagar, an Egyptian, and she had been the slave/servant of Sarah. (12)

Questions.Q: How many sons did Ishmael have?
Questions.A: He had twelve sons. (16)

Questions.Q: How do we know that those men became well known?
Questions.A: We know this because tribes/people-groups descended from them and were named after them. (16)

Questions.Q: How old was Ishmael at the time of his death?
Questions.A: He was 137 years old. (17)

Questions.Q: Where did Ishmael's descendants live?
Questions.A: They lived between Havilah and Shur, near Egypt. (18)
Questions.Alternative: Where did Ishmael's descendents live?

Section.heading: Genesis 25:19-26 Jacob and Esau were born.

Questions.Q: Whose family (line) does the writer of Genesis describe in this section?
Questions.A: He describes the family of Isaac in this section.

Questions.Q: Tell me about Rebekah's experiences as a mother.
Questions.A: She was married to Isaac for twenty years before she finally had any children. And when she did become pregnant, she was carrying twins. And the twins fought each other while still in the womb.

Questions.Q: How old was Isaac when he married Rebekah?
Questions.A: He was 40 years old. (20)

Questions.Q: What do we know about the family that Rebekah came from?
Questions.A: Her brother was Laban, and their father was Bethuel the Aramean from Paddan-aram/Mesopotamia. (20)

Questions.Q: What problem did Rebekah have in the early years of her marriage?
Questions.A: She was unable to become pregnant. (21)

Questions.Q: Earlier in this book of Genesis, what other woman was unable to become pregnant for many years?
Questions.A: Sarah, the mother-in-law of Rebekah, was also unable to become pregnant for a long time.
Questions.Alternative: Earlier in this book, what other woman was unable to become pregnant for many years?
Earlier in Genesis, what other woman was unable to become pregnant for many years?
The author previously told about another woman who was unable to become pregnant for many years. Who was that?
Questions.Note: See Gen. 11:30.

Questions.Q: What did Isaac do about Rebekah's problem?
Questions.A: Isaac prayed to God for her. (21)

Questions.Q: What happened after Isaac prayed?
Questions.A: God granted his request, and Rebekah became pregnant with twins. (21)

Questions.Q: While Rebekah was pregnant, what was her problem?
Questions.A: The two children inside her were often fighting. (22)

Questions.Q: Because of her problem, what did she do?
Questions.A: She prayed to God about it. (22)

Questions.Q: What did God say about her offspring?
Questions.A: God told her that there were two sons in her womb, and that two opposing tribes/people-groups would descend from them. And God said that (eventually) the descendants of the older son would serve the descendants of the younger son. (23)

Questions.Q: What do we know about Rebekah's first-born son?
Questions.A: His body was very red and hairy, so they named him "Esau". (25)

Questions.Q: What does the name "Esau" mean?
Questions.A: It means "hair/hairy".

Questions.Q: And what do we know about the younger son?
Questions.A: He was grasping tightly to Esau's heel, so he/they named him "Jacob". (26)

Questions.Q: What does the name "Jacob" mean?
Questions.A: It means, "grasping the heel" (which is a figurative way of referring to someone deceiving another person).

Questions.Q: Do you have any ideas about what "grasping the heel" might symbolize about Jacob and Esau?
Questions.A: It might mean that Jacob will deceive Esau. (Perhaps it is a symbol of Jacob trying to hold Esau back, so that he (Jacob) could get ahead/succeed.)
Questions.Note: See verse 23.

Questions.Q: At the time the twins were born, how old was Isaac?
Questions.A: He was 60 years old. (26)

Questions.Q: So how long were Isaac and Rebekah married before they had children?
Questions.A: They were married [for] 20 years before they had children. (20, 26)

Section.heading: Genesis 25:27-34 Esau sold his rights as firstborn son.

Questions.Q: Tell what happened in this passage between the twins.
Questions.A: Esau became a skillful hunter, while Jacob preferred to stay home. One day Esau came in from hunting. He was tired and hungry. Jacob was cooking some stew, so Esau asked for some of it. Jacob told Esau that he could have some, but only if Esau swore/promised to give up his rights as the firstborn son to Jacob. So Esau agreed to do that, and he did not seem to regret his action.

Questions.Q: What do you think about the way the two young men behaved in this incident?
Questions.A: Probably it was not appropriate for Jacob to manipulate his brother in this way. And it was quite certainly not appropriate for Esau to care so little about his birthright.

Questions.Q: Tell me what kind of young man Esau was, and what kind of a young man Jacob was.
Questions.A: Esau became a skillful hunter, and preferred to be away from where many people lived/settled. Jacob was (steady and) quiet, preferring to stay at home. (27)

Questions.Q: What did Isaac and Rebekah think about their sons?
Questions.A: Isaac was especially fond of Esau, but Rebekah was fonder of Jacob. (28)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Isaac favored/preferred Esau?
Questions.A: Isaac favored Esau because he brought his father meat from wild animals that he had killed. (28)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that Isaac favored Esau?
What is the reason that Isaac preferred Esau?

Questions.Q: Where had Esau been before he came home?
Questions.A: He had been away in the wilderness/open countryside, probably hunting (animals). (29)

Questions.Q: How did Esau feel when he arrived home?
Questions.A: He was exhausted and hungry. (29)

Questions.Q: What did Esau tell Jacob to do?
Questions.A: He told Jacob to give him some of the stew/soup that Jacob was cooking. (30)

Questions.Q: What was Esau's nickname, what was its meaning, and how did it happen that people called him by that name?
Questions.A: He was called Edom, which means “red.” People called him that because he asked Jacob for some of his (Jacob's) red stew/soup. (30)

Questions.Q: So what did Jacob say in response to Esau's request?
Questions.A: Jacob said that he would give Esau some food, but only if Esau would give Jacob his (Esau's) birthright - that is, Esau's rights as first-born son. (31)

Questions.Q: In your opinion, what do you think Esau was entitled to as the firstborn son?
Questions.A: At that time, it meant that Esau would inherit twice as much as his younger brother, Jacob.

Questions.Q: So what did Esau answer to Jacob's request for the birthright?
Questions.A: Esau said that he was starving to death, so his birthright was not very important. (32)

Questions.Q: In your opinion, do you think Esau was really dying of hunger?
Questions.A: He probably was not.

Questions.Q: Was Jacob satisfied with a simple verbal agreement that Esau was giving him (Jacob), the rights of the firstborn?
Questions.A: No, he insisted that Esau swear to his intention to give Jacob the birthright. (33)

Questions.Q: So what did Esau do then?
Questions.A: He swore/made a solemn promise to Jacob that Esau's former rights as firstborn would, from that time on, belong to Jacob. (33)

Questions.Q: Did Esau have strong regrets for selling his birthright?
Questions.A: No, it did not seem at all important to Esau. (34)

Section.heading: Genesis 26:1-5 God renewed his promise with Isaac.

Questions.Q: Does this passage seem similar to any earlier passages?
Questions.A: Yes, it is similar to God's promises to Abraham (15:1-21; 17:1-8).

Questions.Q: What was Isaac's problem, and what did he do about it?
Questions.A: There was a famine in the land, so he went to Gerar. (1)

Questions.Q: What did God command [to] Isaac?
Questions.A: God told Isaac not to go to Egypt, but to stay in the place that God would tell him. (2-3)
Questions.Alternative: What did God command to Isaac?
What did God command Isaac?

Questions.Q: What was God's promise to Isaac?
Questions.A: God said that he would be with him/care for him, and bless him. God said that he would give all the land to Isaac and his descendants. In doing this, God was being faithful to fulfill his promise to Abraham. (4)

Questions.Q: What was God's promise concerning Isaac's descendants?
Questions.A: God promised to make them as numerous as the stars, and to give them all the land. (4)
Questions.Alternative: What was God's promise concerning Isaac's descendents?

Questions.Q: What did God promise to do through Isaac's descendants?
Questions.A: God promised to bless all the people-groups in the world. (4)
Questions.Alternative: What did God promise to do through Isaac's descendents?

Questions.Q: What did God say was the reason that he would fulfill these promises through/for Isaac?
Questions.A: God said that he would fulfill these promises because Abraham believed God. Abraham showed/demonstrated that he believed God by means of being faithful/obedient to all of God's will - all that God commanded. (5)
Questions.Alternative: What did God say was the reason that he would fulfill these promises through Isaac?
What did God say was the reason that he would fulfill these promises for Isaac?

Section.heading: Genesis 26:6-11 Isaac and Rebekah deceived Abimelech at Gerar.

Questions.Q: Tell what took place at this time.
Questions.A: Isaac and Rebekah were staying at/in Gerar. When the men of Gerar asked about Rebekah, Isaac said that she was his sister, because he was afraid that if people knew that she was his wife, then they might kill him to take her. But one day Abimelech, the king, saw Isaac embracing Rebekah, and scolded Isaac for not telling others that she was his wife. So Abimelech told everyone not to harm Isaac or Rebekah.

Questions.Q: In what country/region was Isaac staying at the time of this incident?
Questions.A: He was staying at/in Gerar. (6)
Questions.Alternative: In what country was Isaac staying at the time of this incident?
In what region was Isaac staying at the time of this incident?

Questions.Q: Do you remember that another prominent character in the book of Genesis also stayed in Gerar for a time? Who was that?
Questions.A: Abraham and Sarah also stayed in Gerar. (Gen. 20:1-18)
Questions.Alternative: Do you remember two other prominent characters in the book of Genesis also stayed in Gerar for a time? Who were they?
Do you remember another prominent character in the book of Genesis who also stayed in Gerar for a time?
Do you remember any other prominent characters in the book of Genesis who also stayed in Gerar for a time?
Do you remember who else in the book of Genesis also stayed in Gerar for a time?

Questions.Q: When the men of Gerar asked about Rebekah, what did Isaac answer?
Questions.A: He said that Rebekah was his sister. (7)

Questions.Q: What was the reason that he answered that way?
Questions.A: Isaac answered that way because Rebekah was beautiful, and he was afraid that someone would kill him and take Rebekah as a wife. (7)

Questions.Q: One day, what did King Abimelech see?
Questions.A: He saw Isaac hugging/embracing Rebekah. (8)

Questions.Q: Upon seeing that, what did Abimelech realize about Isaac and Rebekah?
Questions.A: He realized that they were not brother and sister, but rather they were husband and wife. (9)

Questions.Q: So what did Abimelech do next?
Questions.A: He summoned Isaac and questioned him about falsely claiming that Rebekah was his sister. (9)

Questions.Q: So what was Isaac's answer?
Questions.A: Isaac said that he was afraid that someone (from Gerar) might kill him because Rebekah was beautiful and they might want to take her as a wife. (9)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the king was upset with Isaac?
Questions.A: The king was upset, because he knew that men from Gerar might think that Rebekah was unmarried. One of the men might then have had sexual relations with Rebekah/might have taken her as his wife. He would then be guilty of sin. And other people of Gerar would share in that guilt. (10)

Questions.Q: So then what did Abimelech command [to] his people?
Questions.A: He said that nobody was allowed to harm Isaac or Rebekah. If a person harmed them, that person would have to die. (11)
Questions.Alternative: So then what did Abimelech command to his people?
So then what did Abimelech command his people?

Questions.Q: Tell me about the problems that Isaac and his servants experienced at the time of this incident.
Questions.A: Isaac had become very wealthy and his neighbors began to envy him, so they filled in Isaac's (water) wells. And then King Abimelech asked Isaac to move elsewhere. So Isaac moved, and he/his servants dug two new wells, but the neighbors claimed those wells, also. Finally, when they dug a third well, the neighbors no longer bothered them.

Questions.Q: While Isaac was living in Gerar, what kind of work was he doing?
Questions.A: He was farming the land. (12)

Questions.Q: In what way did God bless Isaac?
Questions.A: God caused Isaac's crops to grow very well/to multiply by 100, and thus Isaac became wealthy and powerful. (12-14)

Questions.Q: For what reason did the Philistine people envy Isaac?
Questions.A: They envied him because he had/owned so many animals (sheep, goats, and cattle), and servants. (14)

Questions.Q: So what did the Philistine people do because they were jealous?
Questions.A: They filled in the wells that Abraham's servants had dug. (15)

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that was a serious situation for Isaac?
Questions.A: That was a serious problem because Isaac needed the (well) water for his many animals.

Questions.Q: What did Abimelech tell Isaac to do?
Questions.A: He told Isaac to leave Gerar and go elsewhere. (16)

Questions.Q: What did Abimelech say was the reason that he was asking Isaac to leave?
Questions.A: Abimelech said that Isaac had become too (rich and) powerful. (16)

Questions.Q: So where did Isaac go?
Questions.A: He went to (the) Gerar Valley/Plain. (17)

Questions.Q: While he was there, what did he do?
Questions.A: There were some wells in that region which Abraham's servants had dug many years before. Someone had filled in those wells. So Isaac and his men re-opened the wells. They gave the wells the same names that Abraham had given them. (18)

Questions.Q: Did they also dig any new wells?
Questions.A: Yes, they dug a new well in the valley and found running water. (19)

Questions.Q: And then what happened?
Questions.A: The local shepherds/animal keepers of Gerar claimed that the new well/spring was theirs, and they argued with Isaac's servants about it. (20)

Questions.Q: What did Isaac name that place/well?
Questions.A: He named it "Esek", which means "quarreling/argument/contention". (20)
Questions.Alternative: What did Isaac name that place?
What did Isaac name that well?

Questions.Q: So what happened next?
Questions.A: Isaac's servants dug a new well, but the men of Gerar fought over that one also. (21)

Questions.Q: What did Isaac then name the new watering place/well?
Questions.A: He named it "Sitnah", which means "opposition/enmity". (21)
Questions.Alternative: What did Isaac then name the new watering place?
What did Isaac then name the new well?

Questions.Q: What did Isaac and his men do next?
Questions.A: They moved away and dug another/a new well. (22)

Questions.Q: So what did Isaac name the watering place/well this time?
Questions.A: He named it "Rehoboth", which means, "room enough"/"broad places". (22)
Questions.Alternative: So what did Isaac name the watering place this time?
So what did Isaac name the well this time?

Questions.Q: What did Isaac say that God had done for them?
Questions.A: Isaac said that God had given them an open/roomy place, and that from that time on, God would give them success there. (22)

Questions.Q: After that where did Isaac go?
Questions.A: He went to Beersheba. (23)

Questions.Q: While he was there, what happened?
Questions.A: God appeared to him and spoke to him. (24)

Questions.Q: What did God say to Isaac?
Questions.A: God said that he (God) was the God of Isaac's father, Abraham. And God said that Isaac need not fear, because he (God) was with him/God would guide him. God also said that he (God) would bless him and increase (the number of) his descendants. (24)

Questions.Q: What did God say was the reason that he would bless Isaac?
Questions.A: God said that it was because he (God) had made a promise to Abraham. (24)

Questions.Q: After God appeared to Isaac, what did Isaac do?
Questions.A: He built an altar and worshiped God. (25)

Questions.Q: And what did Isaac's servants do?
Questions.A: They dug/They began to dig another/a new well. (25)

Section.heading: Genesis 26:26-33 Isaac and Abimelech made an agreement.

Questions.Q: Tell what happened between Isaac and Abimelech.
Questions.A: Abimelech came/went to Isaac and asked him if they could promise each other that they and their people would live together in peace. Isaac agreed, and so they made the promise/treaty.

Questions.Q: Who visited Isaac at this time?
Questions.A: (King) Abimelech, with Ahuzzath his advisor, and Phicol the leader of his soldiers, visited Isaac. (26)

Questions.Q: When they first arrived, what did Isaac do?
Questions.A: He asked why they had come. He mentioned that previously they had asked him to leave them and go live elsewhere. (27)

Questions.Q: What had Isaac's visitors realized about Isaac?
Questions.A: They knew that God was with Isaac. -OR- They knew that God was helping Isaac. (28)

Questions.Q: So what was their purpose in going to Isaac?
Questions.A: Abimelech and his men wanted to make a treaty/agreement with Isaac. (28)

Questions.Q: What did they want Isaac to promise?
Questions.A: They wanted Isaac to promise that he would not harm them/not fight against them. (29)

Questions.Q: What did they say about what they had done when Isaac had formerly lived among them/in their place?
Questions.A: They said that they had treated Isaac well, and that they had sent him away peacefully/with an agreeable settlement. (29)
Questions.Alternative: What did they say about what they had done when Isaac had formerly lived among them?
What did they say about what they had done when Isaac had formerly lived in their place?

Questions.Q: Then what did Isaac do?
Questions.A: He had a feast prepared for Abimelech and his men, and they ate and drank together. (30)

Questions.Q: Who do you think was eating and drinking?
Questions.A: Abimelech and his men, together with Isaac and his men, were all drinking.
Questions.Note: It is virtually certain that Isaac and his men joined in the feast.

Questions.Q: What happened in the morning?
Questions.A: Isaac and Abimelech made a solemn promise/vow not to fight each other. Then Abimelech and his companions left. (31)

Questions.Q: On that day, what else happened?
Questions.A: Isaac's servants told him that they had found water (at the place where they had been digging a well). (32)

Questions.Q: What did Isaac name that well?
Questions.A: He called it Shibah, which means "oath". (33)

Questions.Q: At the time that Esau (got) married/took a wife, how old was he?
Questions.A: He was forty years old. (34)
Questions.Alternative: At the time that Esau (got) married, how old was he?
At the time that Esau took a wife, how old was he?

Questions.Q: From what people-group were Esau's wives?
Questions.A: They were Hittites/from the Hit people-group. (34)

Questions.Q: What kind of relationship did Esau's wives have with his parents?
Questions.A: It was not a pleasant relationship. Esau's wives troubled/brought trouble to Esau's parents. (35)

Questions.Q: Tell what happened in Isaac's family.
Questions.A: Isaac had become an old man, and he wanted to pass on his blessing to his firstborn son. So he called in Esau, and asked him to go and hunt for some wild meat (for a meal). Then Isaac would bless him. Meanwhile, Rebekah overheard the conversation. So she called Jacob and told him to go and bring/get two goats from the flock, in order that she could prepare them and send Jacob to his father to receive the blessing. Jacob was worried that his father would discover that he was pretending to be Esau, but Rebekah told him that she would take care of everything. So Esau went off hunting, and Jacob went out and got two goats. His mother cooked/prepared the goats, and also she put some of the goat skin on Jacob's skin/arms to make him hairy like his brother. Jacob took the meal in to his father, Isaac. Isaac was suspicious at first, but he felt the goat skins and thought/supposed that it was Esau's hairy skin. So Isaac proceeded to give the blessing to Jacob. Immediately/Right after that, Esau arrived and found out what had happened. He asked his father to bless him, too, but Isaac could no longer give Esau the blessing of the firstborn. So Isaac gave Esau (only) a lesser blessing.

Questions.Q: What was Isaac's physical condition at the time of this incident?
Questions.A: He was old and (nearly) blind. He was expecting to die very soon. (1-2)

Questions.Q: What did Isaac tell Esau to do?
Questions.A: He told Esau to (go and) hunt for a wild animal, to kill it, and to bring it home and to cook/prepare it the way Isaac liked/preferred it. (3-4)

Questions.Q: What kind of instrument did Esau use in hunting?
Questions.A: He had a bow and arrows. (3)

Questions.Q: What was Isaac's purpose when he summoned Esau (to his bedside)?
Questions.A: Isaac wanted to give Esau a blessing before he (Isaac) died. A father would usually reserve that type/kind of blessing for the firstborn son. (4)

Key Term Check: The concept of "blessing" is central to this chapter. It includes the idea of praying to God, asking God to do good for someone. But it also includes the idea of God guiding someone, enabling them to predict what another person will experience. In this chapter, Isaac was a leading person in what would become the nation of Israel; and Isaac had received special promises from God, even as his father, Abraham had. At that time, Isaac was about to pass on those special promises to his son. (See "bless" in KBT A.1.)

Questions.Q: By what means/How did Rebekah know/find out about Isaac's instructions to Esau?
Questions.A: She had been listening/She overheard as Isaac spoke to Esau. (5)
Questions.Alternative: By what means did Rebekah know about Isaac's instructions to Esau?
By what means did Rebekah find out about Isaac's instructions to Esau?
How did Rebekah know about Isaac's instructions to Esau?
How did Rebekah find out about Isaac's instructions to Esau?

Questions.Q: So what did Rebekah tell Jacob to do?
Questions.A: She told him to bring her two fine young goats, so that she could prepare the meal. When the food was prepared, Jacob could take it to Isaac in order to receive the blessing. (8-10)

Questions.Q: Where was Esau at that time?
Questions.A: He had already left to hunt a wild animal/go hunting. (5)
Questions.Note: See verse 5.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Rebekah thought that she and Jacob would be able to prepare the meal for Isaac before Esau's return?
Questions.A: Her plan was that Jacob would find/bring the goats from their own herd; he would not have to hunt (an animal) in order to get/obtain the meat. (9)

Questions.Q: What did Jacob think about his mother's plan?
Questions.A: Jacob was worried that his father would discover that it was him, Jacob, and not Esau, who was coming to him for the blessing. (11-12)

Questions.Q: According to Jacob, if his father discovered that it was Jacob (who was coming for the blessing), what would his father think about Jacob's intentions?
Questions.A: Isaac would think that Jacob was trying to deceive/trick/ridicule him. (12)

Questions.Q: What did Jacob say that Isaac would do, if he (Isaac) realized that Jacob was pretending to be Esau?
Questions.A: He would curse Jacob, rather than bless him. (12)

Questions.Q: But what did Jacob's mother suggest/say to him?
Questions.A: She suggested/said that she would take responsibility for whatever happened. And she told Jacob to just go and fetch/get the goats. (13)
Questions.Alternative: But what did Jacob's mother suggest to him?
But what did Jacob's mother say to him?

Questions.Q: So what did Jacob do, and what did his mother do?
Questions.A: Jacob got/brought the goats, and then his mother prepared a tasty meal/prepared them for his father. (14)

Questions.Q: Then what else did his mother do?
Questions.A: She had Jacob put on Esau's best clothes, and she covered Jacob's arms/hands and neck with some of the goatskins. Then she gave Jacob the tasty food she had prepared. // Then she told Jacob to take to his father the food that she had prepared. (15-17)

Questions.Q: In addition to cooking meat, what else did Rebekah prepare for Jacob to take to Isaac?
Questions.A: She also made some bread. (17)

Questions.Q: What did Jacob do next?
Questions.A: He took the food to his father. (18)

Questions.Q: When Jacob spoke to his father, what did his father say?
Questions.A: Isaac asked about who it was who had come to him. (18)

Questions.Q: So then what did Jacob say?
Questions.A: He said that he was Esau, the firstborn, and that he had followed his father's instructions. (19)

Questions.Q: And what did Jacob tell his father to do at that time?
Questions.A: Jacob told his father to sit up and eat the meal, and then to bless him. (19)

Questions.Q: Then what did Isaac ask Jacob, and what did Jacob answer him?
Questions.A: Isaac asked how he had been able to get/bring the meat so quickly, and Jacob said that God had helped him. (20)

Questions.Q: What name/expression did Jacob use here to refer to God?
Questions.A: Jacob referred to God as "the LORD your [that is, Isaac's] God". -OR- Jacob referred to God as "the LORD whom you [that is, Isaac] worship as God". (20)
Questions.Alternative: What name did Jacob use here to refer to God?
What expression did Jacob use here to refer to God?

Questions.Q: Was Isaac certain that it was Esau with whom he was speaking?
Questions.A: No, Isaac was still not certain. (21)

Questions.Q: So what did Isaac request of his son?
Questions.A: Isaac asked him to come close, so that he could touch him and be sure. (21)

Questions.Q: After Isaac touched his son, what did he say?
Questions.A: He said that the voice was Jacob's voice, but that the arms were Esau's arms. (22)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Isaac did not recognize Jacob?
Questions.A: Isaac was (nearly) blind, so he could not see the one with whom he was talking. And Jacob's arms/hands felt hairy, like Esau's arms/hands. (23)

Questions.Q: What did Isaac ask at that time?
Questions.A: He asked if this/if the person was really his son Esau. (24)

Questions.Q: And what did Jacob answer?
Questions.A: Jacob said that he was Esau. (24)

Questions.Q: What happened next?
Questions.A: Isaac asked his son to bring the food, so that he could eat it and then bless his son. (25)

Questions.Q: In addition to food, what else did Jacob give to his father?
Questions.A: Jacob also gave Isaac some wine. (25)
