Questions.Q: And then what did Isaac tell his son to do?
Questions.A: Isaac told his son to come and kiss him. (26)

Questions.Q: At that time, what caused Isaac to be more certain that it was Esau (with whom he was talking)?
Questions.A: Isaac could smell Esau's clothes (which Jacob was wearing). (27)

Questions.Q: To what did Isaac compare the smell of his son?
Questions.A: He said that his son smelled like a field/farm that God has blessed. (27)

Questions.Q: What did Isaac request to God for his son (and for his son's descendants)?
Questions.A: Isaac asked God to give his son (and his son's descendants) dew/rain and good soil, and also abundant food and drink. And Isaac also asked God to make his son (and his son's descendants) powerful, ruling over other nations. Isaac (also) asked God to enable his son (and his son's descendants) to rule over his relatives. (28-29)
Questions.Alternative: What did Isaac request to God for his son (and for his son's descendents)?

Questions.Q: If a person would curse Isaac's son, what would happen to that person?
Questions.A: The one who cursed him would experience God's wrath. (29)

Questions.Q: And if a person would bless Isaac's son, what would happen to that person?
Questions.A: God would bless the person who blessed Isaac's son. (29)

Questions.Q: What happened after Isaac finished praying?
Questions.A: Just at the time that Jacob left Isaac, Esau returned from hunting. Esau prepared the meal, and brought it to Isaac. Esau invited his father to sit up and eat, and bless him. (30-31)

Questions.Q: Then what happened?
Questions.A: Isaac asked who was bringing him a meal, so Esau told him that he was Esau. Then Isaac became very upset. Isaac said that someone had already brought him a meal, and that he (Isaac) had already prayed, asking God to bless that other person. (32-33)

Questions.Q: Could Isaac renounce/withdraw the prayer that he had prayed for Jacob?
Questions.A: No, that kind of prayer could not be taken back.
Questions.Alternative: Could Isaac renounce the prayer that he had prayed for Jacob?
Could Isaac withdraw the prayer that he had prayed for Jacob?
Could Isaac withdraw the blessing that he had given to Jacob?

Questions.Q: When Esau heard his father say that, what did Esau say?
Questions.A: He cried out and asked Isaac to pray that God would bless him also. (34)

Questions.Q: And what did Isaac answer?
Questions.A: Isaac said that he could not ask God to bless Esau as the firstborn. Isaac said that Esau's younger brother had fooled/deceived him (Isaac), and had taken that which Esau was to inherit/that which rightfully belonged to Esau. (35)

Questions.Q: What then did Esau say about his younger brother, Jacob?
Questions.A: Esau said that his brother's name, "Jacob", was appropriate, because that was the second time that Jacob had deceived him (Esau) and had taken that which (rightfully) belonged to Esau. (36)

Questions.Q: At that point what did Esau ask?
Questions.A: He asked Isaac if there was any other prayer/blessing that Isaac could request for Esau. (36)

Questions.Q: What did Isaac answer Esau?
Questions.A: Isaac said that he had already prayed, requesting very much from God for Jacob. Isaac had prayed that God would make Jacob a leader over his relatives, and that God would give Jacob abundant food and drink. (37)

Questions.Q: Then what did Esau do?
Questions.A: Esau again pleaded with Isaac, asking that somehow Isaac still bless him/pray to God for him. (38)

Questions.Q: What was Esau doing at this time that indicates that he was very upset?
Questions.A: He was crying. (38)

Questions.Q: Then what did Isaac do?
Questions.A: Isaac told Esau about what would happen to Esau (and Esau's descendants) in the future. (39-40)

Questions.Q: According to Isaac, what would the soil be like where Esau would be living?
Questions.A: The soil will be far from the fertile soil, and far from the rain. -OR- The soil would be infertile and dry. (39)

Questions.Q: What did Isaac say about the future relationship between Jacob and Esau (and their descendants)?
Questions.A: Isaac said that Jacob would rule over Esau for a period of time. -OR- Isaac said that Esau would serve his brother (Jacob) for a period of time. (40)
Questions.Alternative: What did Isaac say about the future relationship between Jacob and Esau (and their descendents)?

Questions.Q: What do you think is meant by, "You will live by your sword"?
Questions.A: Probably it means that Esau would be fighting constantly. (40)

Questions.Q: Would Esau serve his brother Jacob for the rest of his life?
Questions.A: No, Esau would oppose his brother until he could remove/free himself from under his brother's power, as/like a cow throwing/getting off its yoke. (40)

Questions.Q: What was happening at the time of this incident?
Questions.A: Esau was plotting to take revenge on Jacob by killing him, so Rebekah told Jacob that he must flee. Rebekah told Isaac that she did not want Jacob to marry a Canaanite woman. Therefore Isaac told Jacob to go to his uncle Laban and to marry one of Laban's daughters. Then Isaac prayed a blessing for/asked God to bless/help Jacob.

Questions.Q: How did Esau feel toward Jacob at that time?
Questions.A: Esau hated Jacob intensely/very much. (41)

Questions.Q: What was Esau planning to do?
Questions.A: He was planning to wait until his father (had) died, and he would then kill Jacob. (41)

Questions.Q: What had Jacob done that caused Esau to be upset?
Questions.A: Jacob had deceived Isaac and obtained the blessing that would have been Esau's. (41)

Questions.Q: What can you say about Esau's character?
Questions.A: He was willing to retaliate, even to the extent of killing his own brother. (Also, there is some question about whether or not Esau was entitled to the special blessing, since he had sold his rights as firstborn to Jacob in return for some stew.)

Questions.Q: How did Jacob's mother (come to) learn about what Esau was intending to do?
Questions.A: She heard about Esau's plan (perhaps from a friend of Esau's, or a neighbor - it is not specified). (42)

Questions.Q: When Rebekah heard of Esau's plan, what did she do?
Questions.A: She summoned Jacob, and told him to quickly flee to his uncle Laban in Haran. (42-43)

Questions.Q: Did Rebekah think that Jacob would ever be able to return to her/would be able to return to her some day?
Questions.A: Yes, she said that she would send for Jacob when Esau was no longer so angry, as though he had forgotten what Jacob did to him. (44-45)
Questions.Alternative: Did Rebekah think that Jacob would ever be able to return to her?
Did Rebekah think that Jacob would be able to return to her some day?

Questions.Q: What else was Rebekah concerned about at that time, in addition to Jacob's safety?
Questions.A: She was afraid that Esau might kill Jacob, and that someone else also might die. She might have been concerned about her husband, Isaac, as he was very old and it seemed that he might soon die. Or she might have been thinking of Esau. If Esau killed Jacob, then someone (else) might want to avenge Jacob/Jacob's death, and kill Esau also. (45)

Questions.Q: What did Rebekah say to her husband, Isaac?
Questions.A: She said that she was very upset with Esau's Hittite wives, and that she would die if Jacob took a wife from the Hittites. -OR- She said that she was very upset with Esau's Hittite wives, and that she would rather die than have Jacob take a wife from the Hittites. (46)

Questions.Q: After she told this to Isaac, what did he do?
Questions.A: He summoned Jacob. (28:1)

Questions.Q: What did Isaac say to Jacob?
Questions.A: He told Jacob not to marry a Canaanite woman. (1)
He told Jacob to go to Paddan-aram/Mesopotamia, and to get/find a wife there from the family of Laban (who was Jacob's uncle). (2)

Questions.Q: What else did Isaac do at this time with Jacob?
Questions.A: Isaac also prayed a blessing for Jacob. (1, 3-4)

Questions.Q: As Isaac asked God to bless Jacob, what did he (Isaac) request (of God)?
Questions.A: He prayed that Almighty God would give Jacob many descendants, and make him ruler over a group of nations. Isaac prayed that God would bless/do good for Jacob as he (God) had blessed Abraham. And Isaac prayed that Jacob would be able to receive/get the land that God had promised to Abraham. (3-4)

Questions.Q: So what did Jacob do next?
Questions.A: He went to Paddan-aram/Mesopotamia, to stay with his uncle Laban, his mother's brother. (5)

Questions.Q: After Jacob had left home and gone to stay with his uncle (and find/get a wife), what did Esau do?
Questions.A: Esau married a daughter of his uncle Ishmael.
Questions.Alternative: After Jacob had left home and gone to stay with his uncle (and find a wife), what did Esau do?
After Jacob had left home and gone to stay with his uncle (and get a wife), what did Esau do?

Questions.Q: What had Esau heard about his brother?
Questions.A: Esau had heard that his father had blessed Jacob/his father had passed on to Jacob the special promises of God, and his parents had sent Jacob away to find/get a wife. Esau knew that his parents had strongly commanded Jacob not to take a wife from among the Canaanites. (6)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that it was to Ishmael's family/household that Esau went in order to seek a wife?
Questions.A: He went there because he realized that his father did not approve of the Canaanite women. (6-8)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that it was to Ishmael's family that Esau went in order to seek a wife?
What is the reason that it was to Ishmael's household that Esau went in order to seek a wife?

Questions.Q: What (kinship) relation was Ishmael to Isaac? // In what way were Isaac and Ishmael related?
Questions.A: Ishmael was Isaac's (half-) brother. Both of them were Abraham's sons (though they had different mothers.) (9)
Questions.Alternative: What (kinship) relation was Ishmael to Isaac?
In what way were Isaac and Ishmael related?

Questions.Q: Jacob had gone to seek a wife from the family of his mother's brother. Can you see a similarity in what Esau has done?
Questions.A: Esau has taken a wife from the family of his father's brother. (9)

Questions.Q: So how many wives did Esau now have?
Questions.A: Esau now had (at least) three wives. (26:34, 28:9)

Section.heading: Genesis 28:10-22 God renewed his promise to/covenant with Jacob.

Questions.Q: As Jacob began his journey, what happened?
Questions.A: God caused him to have a special dream. In that dream, God revealed that the promises that he (God) had made to Abraham and to Isaac were now being passed on to Jacob.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that it was at that time that God gave such a dream to Jacob?
Questions.A: Jacob was leaving home to start his own life. His father had given him special blessings. This would seem to be an appropriate time for God to confirm to Jacob that he (God) was renewing his special promises with Jacob.

Questions.Q: From where did Jacob depart, and [to] where was he going?
Questions.A: He left Beersheba and was traveling to Haran. (10)
Questions.Alternative: From where did Jacob depart, and to where was he going?
From where did Jacob depart, and where was he going?

Questions.Q: What was the reason that Jacob stopped before he arrived at his destination?
Questions.A: He stopped to sleep because it was evening/night. (11)

Questions.Q: As he prepared to go to sleep, what did he get, and what did he do with it/them?
Questions.A: He got/found a rock/some rocks. And he used it/them as a pillow/to protect his head. (11)
Questions.Alternative: As he prepared to go to sleep, what did he get, and what did he do with it?
As he prepared to go to sleep, what did he get, and what did he do with them?

Questions.Q: About what did he dream? -OR- What did he see in his dream?
Questions.A: He saw a stairway/ladder/ramp between heaven and earth, with angels going up and down it. (12)
Questions.Alternative: About what did he dream?
What did he see in his dream?

Questions.Q: Who else appeared in his dream?
Questions.A: God also appeared to him. (13)

Questions.Q: In Jacob's dream, what did God do?
Questions.A: He spoke to Jacob. (13-15)

Questions.Q: And what did God say to Jacob?
Questions.A: God promised to give to Jacob and his descendants the land where Jacob was lying/sleeping. He also promised that Jacob's descendants would be very numerous/uncountable, spread everywhere, like the dust of the earth. And God promised that he would bless/do good to all the nations of the earth through/by means of/because of Jacob's descendants. (13-14)

Questions.Q: What else did God promise to Jacob?
Questions.A: God also promised to guide Jacob/to be with Jacob, and to watch over him everywhere. God said that he would bring Jacob back to that place, that he would never leave Jacob, but rather would fulfill all of his promises to Jacob. (15)

Questions.Q: When Jacob awoke from his sleep, what did he say?
Questions.A: He said that God was in that place, though he (Jacob) had not realized/known it. (16)

Questions.Q: What did Jacob say about that place?
Questions.A: He said that it was a very awesome/fearsome place, the house of God, and that it was the door/gate (passing through) to heaven. (17)

Questions.Q: What do you think it was about that place which made it (so) awesome/fearsome to Jacob?
Questions.A: Jacob realized that he was in the presence of Almighty God. (17)
Questions.Alternative: What do you think it was about that place which made it (so) awesome to Jacob?
What do you think it was about that place which made it (so) fearsome to Jacob?

Questions.Q: What did Jacob do the next morning?
Questions.A: He arose got up early, took the stone pillow, and (carefully) stood it upright. He then sprinkled oil on the stone, making it a special remembrance to God. (18)

Questions.Q: What did he name that place?
Questions.A: He called it "Bethel". (19)

Questions.Q: What is the meaning of its name, "Bethel"?
Questions.A: It means, "House of God". (19)

Questions.Q: What did Jacob do next?
Questions.A: He made a solemn promise to God. (20)

Questions.Q: What did Jacob promise to God?
Questions.A: Jacob promised that, if God truly guided him on his journey and guarded him from all evil, and provided all Jacob's needs, such as food and clothing, then Jacob would worship only YHWH as God. He also promised that, if God safely brought/took him (Jacob) back to his father's land, he would worship only YHWH as God. (20-21)

Questions.Q: What else did Jacob say about that rock?
Questions.A: He said that it would become a place of worship to God. (22)

Questions.Q: And what else did Jacob promise to God?
Questions.A: He also promised that, of all that God gave to him (Jacob), he would give (back) to God one-tenth. (22)

Section.heading: Genesis 29:1-14a Jacob met his uncle Laban.

Questions.Q: As Jacob came to the end of his journey, how did it happen that he was able to find out where his uncle Laban was living?
Questions.A: Jacob arrived at a well where sheep were waiting to get their drinking water. It happened that Rachel, a daughter of Laban, also arrived at the well. Jacob drew/got water for Rachel's sheep, and explained who he was. Rachel ran home and summoned/got her father. Laban went to the well to see Jacob and to take/bring him (to Laban's) home.

Questions.Q: Does this story remind you of another story that took place several years before this one?
Questions.A: This story has similarities with the story of Abraham's servant traveling a long distance to find/get a wife for Isaac, and meeting Rebekah at a well. (And after the servant had told her who he was, Rebekah had run home, and then Laban had run back to the well to bring the servant to his house.)

Questions.Q: In what direction (from Canaan) did Jacob travel?
Questions.A: He traveled east. (1)

Questions.Q: As Jacob was arriving (at his destination), what did he see?
Questions.A: He saw a well in a field. (2)

Questions.Q: Tell me about that well.
Questions.A: There were three flocks of sheep near it, and there was a large stone covering the well. (2)

Questions.Q: What was the reason for the sheep being near the well?
Questions.A: They were waiting to drink water. (2)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the sheep were not drinking water when Jacob first arrived?
Questions.A: There was a large stone covering the well. (2)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that nobody had removed the large stone?
Questions.A: The shepherds were waiting until all the sheep had gathered. (3)

Questions.Q: So after the sheep had gathered and the shepherds had given the sheep water, what did those shepherds do next/what was it their custom to do before leaving?
Questions.A: They covered up the well again. (3)
Questions.Alternative: So after the sheep had gathered and the shepherds had given the sheep water, what did those shepherds do next before leaving?
So after the sheep had gathered and the shepherds had given the sheep water, what was it their custom to do before leaving?

Questions.Q: For what reason do you think the shepherds covered up the well each day?
Questions.A: Perhaps they did that to prevent someone or something from falling into it. Or perhaps they did it to keep strangers from taking water. Or possibly to keep the water clean.
Questions.Note: The text does not explain why the shepherds covered the well each day. But the one answering these questions should be able to supply a possible reason which is similar to one of the above.

Questions.Q: What did Jacob say to the shepherds?
Questions.A: He (greeted them and) asked where they were from. (4)

Questions.Q: And then about whom did Jacob ask the shepherds?
Questions.A: He asked about one called Laban, the grandson of Nahor. (5)

Questions.Q: When Jacob asked about Laban, what did the shepherds say?
Questions.A: They said that Laban was well, and that his daughter was just arriving with his (Laban's) sheep. (6)

Questions.Q: What was Jacob's advice/suggestion to the shepherds?
Questions.A: He suggested that someone draw/get water for the sheep in order that the sheep could return to their fields to eat. (7)
Questions.Alternative: What was Jacob's advice to the shepherds?
What was Jacob's suggestion to the shepherds?

Questions.Q: What reason did the shepherds give for not following Jacob's advice?
Questions.A: They said that all the sheep (and shepherds) had to gather first, before they would roll away the large stone. (8)

Questions.Q: While Jacob was talking with the shepherds, who arrived?
Questions.A: Rachel arrived. (9)

Questions.Q: What was Rachel's purpose in coming to the well?
Questions.A: She was a shepherd, watching/caring for her father's sheep. (9)

Questions.Q: In what way was Rachel related to Jacob?
Questions.A: She was his cousin - the daughter of Jacob's mother's brother. (10)

Questions.Q: When Jacob saw Rachel, what did he do?
Questions.A: He removed the large stone from the well and drew/got water for the sheep of Rachel's father. (10)

Questions.Q: Then what else did Jacob do?
Questions.A: He kissed Rachel and cried (for joy). Then he told her that he was her cousin, the nephew of her father, and that his mother was Rebekah. (11-12)

Questions.Q: After that, what did Rachel do?
Questions.A: She immediately ran home to tell her father. (12)

Questions.Q: When Laban heard that his nephew, Jacob, had arrived, what did Laban do?
Questions.A: He immediately ran to meet Jacob, and then hugged and kissed him and took him into his home. (13)

Questions.Q: What did Laban say then?
Questions.A: He said that Jacob was really and truly his relative (and his "flesh"). (14)

Section.heading: Genesis 29:14b-30 Jacob married Leah and Rachel.

Questions.Q: Tell me about how Jacob became married.
Questions.A: He was working for his uncle, Laban, and Laban asked Jacob what he (Jacob) wanted for his wages. So Jacob offered to work for Laban for seven years in return for being able to marry Rachel, Laban's younger daughter. After seven years, Laban held a wedding feast, but on the wedding night, Laban substituted Leah, his older daughter, for Rachel. The next morning, Jacob discovered that Laban had deceived him. Laban told him that he (Jacob) could also have Rachel as his wife, if Jacob would work another seven years. So a week after Jacob married Leah, he also married Rachel, and then worked (for) another seven years.

Questions.Q: What did Laban ask Jacob at that time?
Questions.A: He asked Jacob how much he (Jacob) wanted for his wages. (15)

Questions.Q: About how long had Jacob worked for Laban, when Laban asked Jacob about wages?
Questions.A: Jacob had worked for Laban for about one month. (14b)

Questions.Q: Tell me about Laban's two daughters.
Questions.A: He had two unmarried daughters: Leah the elder, and Rachel the younger. Leah's eyes were pretty/delicate/not very pretty, but Rachel was very/especially beautiful. -OR- Leah was somewhat pretty, but Rachel was very beautiful. (16-17)
Questions.Note: The meaning of the Hebrew text is not certain at this point. The one responding to these questions should provide an answer which is consistent with the translated text.

Questions.Q: What did Jacob answer to Laban?
Questions.A: Jacob offered to work hard for seven years in return for being able to marry the younger daughter, Rachel. (18)
Questions.Alternative: What did Jacob answer to Laban regarding his question about wages?
What wages did Jacob ask Laban to give him?
What did Jacob ask for in return for working for Laban?

Questions.Q: What was the reason why Jacob chose Rachel (as the one he wanted) to marry?
Questions.A: Jacob was in love with Rachel. (18)

Questions.Q: What was Laban's response to Jacob's suggestion about marrying Rachel?
Questions.A: Laban agreed, and said that it would be better to give his daughter to Jacob rather than to an outsider. (19)

Questions.Q: How did Jacob feel about working for Laban for seven years?
Questions.A: He was content with/in his work, because he loved Rachel very much. (20)

Questions.Q: When the seven-year work period was nearly finished, what did Jacob do?
Questions.A: Jacob requested that Laban give him his wife. (21)

Questions.Q: What did Laban do?
Questions.A: Laban planned/prepared a wedding feast. (22)

Questions.Q: And then what happened on the wedding night?
Questions.A: Laban deceived Jacob. He gave Jacob his elder daughter, Leah (instead of Rachel), to be Jacob's wife. (23)

Questions.Q: Did Jacob recognize Leah immediately?
Questions.A: No, he did not realize that it was Leah until they woke up in the morning. (25)

Questions.Q: Who was Zilpah?
Questions.A: She was a servant. Laban gave her to Leah to be her servant. (24)

Questions.Q: In the morning, when Jacob realized that Leah was his wife, how did he feel?
Questions.A: He was very upset and angry. (25)

Questions.Q: What did Jacob do?
Questions.A: He confronted Laban. He demanded an explanation from Laban. (25)

Questions.Q: According to Laban, what was the reason that he gave Leah, instead of Rachel, to be Jacob's wife?
Questions.A: It was their custom for the older daughter to be married before the younger. (26)

Questions.Q: What was Laban's suggestion to Jacob?
Questions.A: Laban suggested that Jacob finish the bridal week with Leah, and then marry Rachel also. Jacob would have to work for an additional seven years to pay for Rachel. (27)

Questions.Q: Was it Laban's intention that Jacob would cease being married to Leah, when he took Rachel also as his wife?
Questions.A: No. Laban intended that Jacob would be married to both women at the same time.

Questions.Q: What was Jacob's response to Laban's suggestion?
Questions.A: Jacob agreed to it. (28)

Questions.Q: After Jacob and Laban made this agreement, how much time passed before Jacob took Rachel as his wife?
Questions.A: One week passed. (28)

Questions.Q: Who was Bilhah?
Questions.A: She was a servant. Laban gave her to Rachel to be her servant. (29)

Questions.Q: How did Jacob's feelings toward his two wives compare? -OR- How did Jacob feel about Rachel, and how did he feel about Leah?
Questions.A: He loved Rachel more than he loved Leah. (30)
Questions.Alternative: How did Jacob's feelings toward his two wives compare?
How did Jacob feel about Rachel, and how did he feel about Leah?

Questions.Q: What did Jacob do to fulfill his agreement with Laban concerning Rachel?
Questions.A: He worked (for) seven more years for Rachel. (30)

Questions.Q: How many wives did Jacob have at the beginning of this account/story?
Questions.A: He had two wives: Leah, and Rachel.
Questions.Alternative: How many wives did Jacob have at the beginning of this account?
How many wives did Jacob have at the beginning of this story?

Questions.Q: How many sons did Jacob have during the time of this account/story?
Questions.A: He had eleven sons during that time.
Questions.Alternative: How many sons did Jacob have during the time of this account?
How many sons did Jacob have during the time of this story?

Questions.Q: How many women gave birth to Jacob's sons in this story?
Questions.A: Four women had sons by Jacob.

Questions.Q: Besides Leah and Rachel, who were the other two women?
Questions.A: The other two women were Rachel's servant, Bilhah, and Leah's servant, Zilpah.

Questions.Q: At the beginning of this account/story, what do we learn about Leah and Rachel?
Questions.A: We learn that Jacob did not love Leah, so God enabled her to become pregnant. But Rachel was unable to become pregnant. (31)
Questions.Alternative: At the beginning of this account, what do we learn about Leah and Rachel?
At the beginning of this story, what do we learn about Leah and Rachel?

Questions.Q: When Leah gave birth to her firstborn son, what did she say?
Questions.A: She said that God had seen/was aware of her troubles, and that surely now her husband would really love her. (32)

Questions.Q: What did she name her first son, and what did that name mean?
Questions.A: She named him "Reuben", which probably means something like, "Look, a son!" And it sounds much like a Hebrew word which means, "God has seen my troubles". (32)

Questions.Q: What happened next?
Questions.A: Leah gave birth to another son. (33)

Questions.Q: When Leah gave birth to her second son, what did she say?
Questions.A: She said that God had given her another child, because God had heard that her husband did not love her. (33)

Questions.Q: What did she name her second son, and what did that name mean?
Questions.A: She named him "Simeon", which probably means "one who hears"/"he hears". (33)

Questions.Q: When Leah gave birth to her third child, what did she say?
Questions.A: She said that she had now given her husband three sons, so maybe now her husband would become attached (with affection) to her/her husband would become close to her. (34)

Questions.Q: What did she name her third child, and what did that name mean?
Questions.A: She named him Levi, which means, "attached". (34)

Questions.Q: And then what happened?
Questions.A: Leah became pregnant and had a fourth son. (35)

Questions.Q: When Leah gave birth to her fourth son, what did she say?
Questions.A: She said that now she would praise God. (35)

Questions.Q: What did she name that child, and what did that name mean?
Questions.A: She named him "Judah", which means, "praise". (35)

Questions.Q: After her fourth son was born, what happened?
Questions.A: She did not become pregnant again. (35)

Questions.Q: What do we learn about Rachel at that time?
Questions.A: We learn that she was not having/bearing any children, and so she became jealous of her older sister, and demanded that Jacob give her children. (1)

Questions.Q: According to Rachel, what would happen if she was not able to become pregnant/bear children?
Questions.A: Rachel said that she would die. (1)
Questions.Alternative: According to Rachel, what would happen if she was not able to become pregnant?
According to Rachel, what would happen if she was not able to bear children?

Questions.Q: How did Jacob respond to Rachel?
Questions.A: He became angry and stated that only God can give children. (2)

Questions.Q: What did Rachel say that Jacob should do?
Questions.A: She told Jacob to sleep/have sexual relations with her servant, Bilhah, and the child would be considered as Rachel's child. (3)

Questions.Q: If Bilhah conceived and later had a child, who would people consider to be the mother of the child?
Questions.A: People would consider Rachel to be the mother. (3)

Questions.Q: So then what happened?
Questions.A: Jacob slept with Bilhah. She became pregnant and gave birth to a son. (4-5)

Questions.Q: When the time came for Bilhah to give birth, what did Rachel say?
Questions.A: She said that God's judgment was correct/that God had vindicated her, that he had heard her request and had given her a son. (6)

Questions.Q: What did she name the child?
Questions.A: She named him "Dan" (which sounds like the word meaning "judge", or "vindicate"). (6)

Questions.Q: What happened next?
Questions.A: Bilhah became pregnant again and gave birth to another boy. (7)

Questions.Q: When the time came for Bilhah to give birth again, what did Rachel say?
Questions.A: She said that she had struggled hard against her elder sister, and had won/and was winning. (8)

Questions.Q: What did she name that child?
Questions.A: She named the child "Naphtali"(which means, "struggle".) (8)

Questions.Q: Meanwhile, what do we learn about Leah?
Questions.A: Leah was not having/bearing any more children. (9)

Questions.Q: So what did Leah do?
Questions.A: She gave her servant, Zilpah, to Jacob, so that Zilpah could bear him children. (9)

Questions.Q: When the time came for Zilpah to give birth, what did Leah say?
Questions.A: She said that she was very fortunate. (10)

Questions.Q: What did she name the child?
Questions.A: She named him "Gad" (which means "good fortune"). (11)

Questions.Q: Then what happened?
Questions.A: Zilpah became pregnant again and gave birth to another son. (12)

Questions.Q: When the time came for Zilpah to give birth again, what did Leah say?
Questions.A: She said that she was very happy, and that people would start calling her "Happy"/and that people would consider her to be happy. (13)

Questions.Q: And what did she name that child?
Questions.A: She named him "Asher", which means "happy". (13)

Questions.Q: What did Reuben find?
Questions.A: He found a kind of plant that people thought had power to help a woman become pregnant. (14)

Questions.Q: Where did he find this plant?
Questions.A: He found it in a field. (14)

Questions.Q: What did Reuben do with that plant?
Questions.A: He took it home and gave it to his mother, Leah. (14)

Questions.Q: What did Rachel request?
Questions.A: She asked Leah to give her some of the plant. (14)

Questions.Q: What did Leah say?
Questions.A: Leah accused Rachel of taking her (Leah's) husband, and said that she did not want Rachel to take her son's plant also. (15)

Questions.Q: Then what did Rachel say?
Questions.A: Rachel told Leah that, if she would give her (Rachel) some of the special plant, then that night Jacob could sleep with Leah. (15)

Questions.Q: Did Leah concur/agree with Rachel's suggestion?
Questions.A: Yes, she did. (16)
Questions.Alternative: Did Leah concur with Rachel's suggestion?
Did Leah agree with Rachel's suggestion?

Questions.Q: What did Leah do?
Questions.A: She went to meet Jacob coming in from the fields. She told him that he was to sleep with her that night, because she had hired him (from Rachel) with some plants that her son had found. (16)

Questions.Q: So what did Jacob do?
Questions.A: That night he slept with Leah. (16)

Questions.Q: In what way did God help Leah?
Questions.A: He granted her request by giving her another son/a fifth son. (17)

Questions.Q: At this time, what did Leah say about being pregnant?
Questions.A: She said that God had rewarded her because she had given her servant to her husband. (18)

Questions.Q: What did she name that child?
Questions.A: She named him "Issachar" (which sounds like the Hebrew word meaning "reward/payment". (18)

Questions.Q: And then what happened?
Questions.A: Leah became pregnant again. (19)

Questions.Q: When the time came for Leah to give birth, what did she say?
Questions.A: She said that God had really given her good gifts/given her a good dowry. And she said that Jacob would now honor/accept her because she had given him six sons. (20)

Questions.Q: What did she name that child?
Questions.A: She named him Zebulun, which probably means, "accept". (20)

Questions.Q: And then what happened?
Questions.A: Leah later gave birth to a daughter. (21)

Questions.Q: What did Leah name her daughter?
Questions.A: She called her Dinah. (21)

Questions.Q: In what way did God help Rachel?
Questions.A: He did not forget her/He considered her/He showed her mercy/He granted her request and enabled her to become pregnant. (22)

Questions.Q: What did Rachel say about her child?
Questions.A: She said that God had removed her shame, and that she would like to have (yet) another child. (23, 24)

Questions.Q: What did she name that child?
Questions.A: She named him Joseph (which means, "add/he adds/may he add"). (24)

Section.heading: Genesis 30:25-43 Jacob and Laban made an agreement.

Questions.Q: Tell how Jacob was able to acquire very large flocks of sheep and goats.
Questions.A: Jacob and Laban made an agreement in which certain sheep and goats would belong to Jacob, and the others would belong to Laban. The ones which would belong to Jacob were those which were dark, or spotted. And Jacob was able to vastly increase the numbers of dark or spotted animals.

Questions.Q: What did Jacob request from Laban?
Questions.A: Jacob requested that he be allowed to return to his home (in Canaan) (with his wife and children). (25)

Questions.Q: At what time did Jacob request that from Laban?
Questions.A: He made that request soon after Rachel gave birth to Joseph. (25)

Questions.Q: Whom did he want to take with him when he returned home?
Questions.A: He wanted to take his wives and children. (26)
Questions.Note: Omit this question if respondent already answered it in response to the previous question about Jacob's request.

Questions.Q: According to Jacob, for what reason could he claim the right to take his wives and children and return home (to Canaan)?
Questions.A: Jacob said that he had worked hard and had paid for his wives and children by his labor. (26)

Questions.Q: For how long had Jacob been married at that time?
Questions.A: He had been married for at least seven years in order to pay for Rachel, but probably longer since he had 7 children by Leah, followed by a son by Rachel.

Questions.Q: What did Laban answer [to] Jacob?
Questions.A: He told Jacob that he did not want Jacob to leave. (27)
Questions.Alternative: What did Laban answer to Jacob?
What did Laban answer Jacob?

Questions.Q: According to Laban, for what reason did he want Jacob to stay?
Questions.A: Laban said that God had blessed/was blessing Laban because of Jacob. (27)

Questions.Q: What did Laban offer to Jacob?
Questions.A: He offered to pay Jacob whatever he (Laban) owed Jacob. (28)

Questions.Q: According to Jacob, in what way had Laban been able to benefit from Jacob's work?
Questions.A: Laban's animals had increased greatly, and Laban had become very wealthy. God had blessed Laban because of/through Jacob. (29-30)

Questions.Q: According to Jacob, for what reason did he want to leave? What could he do if he left?
Questions.A: He wanted to provide for himself and his family. (Perhaps he thought that he could earn more to provide for his family by working for himself.) (30)

Questions.Q: What did Jacob request as payment for working for Laban?
Questions.A: He asked Laban to give him any dark sheep, and spotted sheep and goats. (32)

Questions.Q: Was Jacob asking for that/those as payment for already having worked for Laban, or as payment for continuing to work for Laban?
Questions.A: He was asking for that/those as payment for continuing to work for Laban. (31)
Questions.Alternative: Was Jacob asking for that as payment for already having worked for Laban, or as payment for continuing to work for Laban?
Was Jacob asking for those as payment for already having worked for Laban, or as payment for continuing to work for Laban?

Questions.Q: For what reason was it the dark or spotted animals which Jacob suggested that Laban should give him?
Questions.A: He suggested the dark or spotted animals, so that it would be easy to distinguish between Jacob's animals and Laban's. (33)

Questions.Q: How did Laban respond to Jacob's suggestion?
Questions.A: Laban agreed, but then he himself removed the dark sheep and spotted sheep and goats. And he had his sons take those animals away from the main flock. (34-36)

Questions.Q: How long did it take for Laban's sons to travel to the place where they would look after the animals that Laban had removed from the flock?
Questions.A: It took three days. (36)

Questions.Q: While Laban's sons removed some of the animals from the main flock, who was looking after the rest of Laban's animals?
Questions.A: Jacob was looking after them. (36)

Questions.Q: After Jacob gathered/got some branches, what did he do with those branches?
Questions.A: He peeled off some bark, and put the branches near the water troughs. (37-38)
Questions.Alternative: After Jacob gathered some branches, what did he do with those branches?
After Jacob got some branches, what did he do with those branches?

Questions.Q: What was Jacob's purpose in doing that?
Questions.A: He did that so that when the animals mated, they would see the peeled branches, and thus their offspring would also be streaked and spotted. (38-39)

Questions.Q: And when those animals gave birth, how did their offspring appear?
Questions.A: Their offspring were streaked and spotted. (39)

Questions.Q: What did Jacob do with the newborn animals?
Questions.A: He separated them from the rest of the flock. (40)

Questions.Q: When the animals were mating, what else did Jacob cause the animals to look at (besides the peeled branches)?
Questions.A: Jacob caused the animals to look at the black and striped animals. (40)

Questions.Q: Did Jacob set up the peeled branches near the water troughs all the time?
Questions.A: No, he did that only when the stronger female animals were ready to mate. (41-42)

Questions.Q: What is the reason why Jacob placed those peeled branches (by the water troughs) only when it was the strong animals that were mating?
Questions.A: He did that so that only the strong ones would give birth to the spotted or dark offspring. (42)

Questions.Q: What happened as Jacob was looking after the animals in that way?
Questions.A: Jacob's flocks multiplied - they became very large. And Jacob became very wealthy. (43)

Questions.Q: What did Jacob have which indicates that he had become very wealthy?
Questions.A: Jacob had large flocks of sheep and goats, and he also had camels, donkeys, and many servants. (43)

Questions.Q: This passage describes what Jacob was doing while he was caring for/looking after Laban's animals. What was Jacob's goal/intention at that time?
Questions.A: He was attempting to increase the number of strong dark sheep and spotted sheep and goats - the animals that would eventually belong to him. (40-43)
Questions.Alternative: This passage describes what Jacob was doing while he was caring for Laban's animals. What was Jacob's goal at that time?
This passage describes what Jacob was doing while he was caring for Laban's animals. What was Jacob's intention at that time?
This passage describes what Jacob was doing while he was looking after Laban's animals. What was Jacob's goal at that time?
This passage describes what Jacob was doing while he was looking after Laban's animals. What was Jacob's intention at that time?

Questions.Q: What did Jacob do at that time?
Questions.A: He realized that Laban was becoming more unfriendly toward him, so he decided to leave, and return to Canaan. His wives agreed with him, so while Laban was away, they all left to begin the journey to Jacob's homeland.

Questions.Q: What were Laban's sons saying?
Questions.A: They were saying that Jacob had become wealthy by taking away all of Laban's wealth. (1)

Questions.Q: According to Jacob, how was Laban's attitude concerning/towards him?
Questions.A: Jacob felt that Laban's attitude was different - maybe even hostile or jealous. (2)
Questions.Alternative: According to Jacob, how was Laban's attitude concerning him?
According to Jacob, how was Laban's attitude towards him?

Questions.Q: At this time, what did God say to Jacob?
Questions.A: God told Jacob to return to the place of his relatives, and he assured Jacob that he (God) would be with him/would care for him. (3)

Questions.Q: After God spoke to Jacob, what did Jacob do?
Questions.A: He sent word to Rachel and Leah to meet him in the fields where his animals were. (4)

Questions.Q: What did Jacob say to his two wives?
Questions.A: He told them that their father's attitude toward him had changed, though God had been with him/God had been caring for him. And Jacob said that although he had worked hard, Laban had changed his wages ten/many times. He said that in the end, God had taken Laban's wealth and had given it to Jacob. (5-9)

Questions.Q: According to Jacob, what had Laban done to him?
Questions.A: Laban had cheated Jacob by changing Jacob's wages ten/many times. (7)
Questions.Note: The Hebrew text uses the number "ten" here. However, it is not certain whether Jacob expected his wives to interpret this number literally, or if they would have understood this in a figurative way, meaning "several" or "many". The one responding to these questions should provide an answer which is consistent with the translated text.

Questions.Q: By what means had Laban tried to cheat Jacob?
Questions.A: Laban had not kept his promises. He had promised to give Jacob the offspring of certain animals, but when the offspring were born, Laban changed the arrangement. (8)

Questions.Q: What reason did Jacob give for why Laban had not been able to prosper (while, at that time, Jacob was prospering)?
Questions.A: Jacob said that it was because God did not allow Laban to prosper. God had taken away Laban's wealth and had given it to Jacob. (7-9)

Questions.Q: What do you think that Jacob was thinking when he said that God had been with him (Jacob)? In what way had God been with Jacob?
Questions.A: God had protected Jacob from Laban, and in the end had taken Laban's wealth from him and had given it to Jacob. (7, 9)

Questions.Q: What type of event did Jacob describe to his wives in this passage?
Questions.A: He told them about a dream that he had had/about something that he had dreamed. (10-13)

Questions.Q: At what time of the year did Jacob have that dream?
Questions.A: It happened during a mating season. (10)

Questions.Q: Tell me about Jacob's dream.
Questions.A: The male goats that were mating with the female ones were all multicolored (that is, streaked, spotted, or speckled). Then God/the angel of God appeared to Jacob and told him that he had seen Laban's behavior toward Jacob. That was why it was the multicolored ones which were mating (and producing multicolored offspring). He reminded Jacob that he was the God of Bethel. (10-13)

Questions.Q: What did God tell Jacob to do?
Questions.A: He told Jacob to leave that place/to leave Mesopotamia and return home. (13)

Questions.Q: What did Rachel and Leah say to Jacob?
Questions.A: They said that there was no more family inheritance for them, and that their father had treated them as foreigners. They said that Laban had sold them and had spent the money he had received (in payment for them). And they said that the wealth that God had taken from Laban belonged to them and their children. (14-16)

Questions.Q: When the women said about their father, "he regards us as foreigners", what do you think they meant?
Questions.A: They probably meant that Laban was not treating them as his daughters, but rather as though they were strangers from another place. (15)

Questions.Q: According to Jacob's wives, what should Jacob do?
Questions.A: He should do whatever God told him to do. (16)

Questions.Q: So what did Jacob do then?
Questions.A: He put his wives and children on camels, took all of his animals and possessions, and left for Canaan. (17-18)

Questions.Q: In what way did he transport his many animals?
Questions.A: He (and his servants) drove the animals in front of them. (18)

Questions.Q: Did Laban know (immediately) that they had left?
Questions.A: No, he did not know. (19-20)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Laban did not know that they had left?
Questions.A: He did not know, because he was away shearing sheep. (19)

Questions.Q: What was Rachel able to do because Laban was not there?
Questions.A: She was able to steal her father's household gods/idols. (19)

Questions.Q: The manner in which Jacob and his wives left Laban is similar to some other events that had taken place in Jacob's life. Can you remember any of those events?
Questions.A: Jacob slipped away at this time with Laban's daughters and grandchildren. This was similar to the way that Jacob deceived his father Isaac and took Esau's blessing. It is also similar to the way in which Laban gave Leah to be Jacob's wife, when Jacob was expecting Rachel to be given to him. In each of these events, someone deceived someone else.

Questions.Q: Where were Jacob and his wives and children going?
Questions.A: They were going to the hills/mountains of Gilead place. (21)

Questions.Q: In this passage, what happened to Jacob and those with him?
Questions.A: Laban discovered that Jacob had left, and had taken his wives and children and flocks. So Laban and some of his relatives chased after Jacob and his family. Just before Laban caught up with them, God appeared to Laban and told Laban to be careful (about what he said to Jacob). So Laban arrived at Jacob's camp and asked why Jacob had left secretly. Laban accused Jacob of stealing Laban's household gods/idols. Jacob insisted that he had not stolen the gods/idols, nor had anyone else in his family stolen them. Laban searched everywhere in Jacob's camp, but could not find the gods/idols. Then Jacob scolded Laban very strongly.

Questions.Q: After Jacob and his wives and children had fled, how long was it until Laban knew about it?
Questions.A: Laban learned of it after three days. (22)

Questions.Q: When he found out, what did Laban do?
Questions.A: He gathered some relatives and chased after Jacob for seven days. (23)

Questions.Q: Where were Jacob and his family when Laban found them?
Questions.A: They were camped in the hills of Gilead. (23, 25)

Questions.Q: Just before Laban found Jacob, what had happened to Laban?
Questions.A: God appeared to him in a dream, and told him not to threaten Jacob/told him to be careful (about) what he said to Jacob. (24)

Questions.Q: As Laban came close to where Jacob and his family were, what did Laban do?
Questions.A: He (and those with him) set up their tents/set up camp. (25)

Questions.Q: What was Laban's complaint to Jacob?
Questions.A: Laban complained that Jacob had deceived him by taking away his daughters secretly, like captives. (26)

Questions.Q: According to Laban, what would he have done if he had known that Jacob and his (Jacob's) wives and children were leaving?
Questions.A: Laban said that he would have held a farewell party/sent them off with music and festivities. (27)

Questions.Q: What else did Laban say he would have done if he had known that his daughters and grandchildren were leaving?
Questions.A: He said that he would have kissed his daughters and grandchildren, and said farewell to them. (28)

Questions.Q: What did Laban say about the manner in which Jacob left/departed?
Questions.A: He said that Jacob had behaved foolishly. (28)
Questions.Alternative: What did Laban say about the manner in which Jacob left?
What did Laban say about the manner in which Jacob departed?

Questions.Q: What was the reason why Laban did not harm Jacob at that time?
Questions.A: God had told Laban not to threaten Jacob/told Laban to be careful (about) what he said to Jacob. (29)

Questions.Q: What was it about Jacob's situation that Laban said he (Laban) could understand?
Questions.A: Laban said that he could understand that Jacob wanted to return to his homeland. (30)

Questions.Q: What did Laban accuse Jacob of doing?
Questions.A: Laban accused Jacob of stealing his (Laban's) household gods/idols. (30)

Questions.Q: What did Jacob say was the reason that he left without informing Laban?
Questions.A: Jacob said that he was afraid that Laban would force Jacob to leave his (Laban's) daughters behind. (31)

Questions.Q: What was Jacob's response concerning the stolen gods?
Questions.A: He said that Laban could search their camp, and that if he found the gods, then whoever had stolen them would die. (32)

Questions.Q: Did Jacob know that it was Rachel who had taken Laban's gods?
Questions.A: No, he did not know that. (32)

Questions.Q: What did Laban do?
Questions.A: He searched all/each of their tents - Jacob's, then Leah's, then Bilhah's and Zilpah's, and finally he searched Rachel's tent. (33)

Questions.Q: What had Rachel done with the gods?
Questions.A: She had put them in her camel saddle, and she was sitting on the saddle. (34)

Questions.Q: When Laban searched inside Rachel's tent, what happened?
Questions.A: Rachel said that she was having her monthly menstrual period, and so she did not stand up. As a result, Laban did not find the gods. (35)

Questions.Q: How did Jacob react after Laban had completed searching the camp?
Questions.A: He became very angry. (36)

Questions.Q: What did Jacob complain about to Laban at that time?
Questions.A: Jacob complained that Laban had chased after him, and then had searched Jacob's camp. (36-37)

Questions.Q: About what else did Jacob complain?
Questions.A: Jacob said that he had taken very good care of Laban's animals. He (Jacob) had taken responsibility for any lost animals while working for Laban, even though Laban had changed his (Jacob's) wages ten/many times. And Jacob had had to live in the fields (many times) during those twenty years. (38-41)

Questions.Q: What did Jacob say about eating Laban's animals while he (Jacob) was caring for them?
Questions.A: He said that he had never eaten one of Laban's animals. (38)

Questions.Q: If a wild animal had killed a sheep or goat while Jacob was caring for the sheep or goat, who paid for the sheep or goat?
Questions.A: Jacob paid for it. (39)

Questions.Q: If someone had stolen a sheep or goat, who paid for it?
Questions.A: Jacob paid for it. (39)

Questions.Q: (For) how long did Jacob work for Laban?
Questions.A: He worked for Laban (for) 20 years. (40)
Questions.Alternative: For how long did Jacob work for Laban?
How long did Jacob work for Laban?

Questions.Q: What were some of the hardships that Jacob had experienced during that time?
Questions.A: Often the days were very hot. And the nights were very cold, and he was unable to sleep well. (40)

Questions.Q: How many times did Laban change Jacob's wages?
Questions.A: Laban changed his wages ten times. -OR- Laban changed his wages several/many times. (41)
Questions.Note: The Hebrew text uses the number "ten" here. However, it is not certain whether Jacob expected those listening to interpret this number literally, or if they would have understood this in a figurative way, meaning "several" or "many". The one responding to these questions should provide an answer which is consistent with the translated text.

Questions.Q: If God had not been with Jacob, what would have happened to him?
Questions.A: Jacob said that Laban would have sent him away with nothing. (42)

Questions.Q: According to Jacob, what did God see?
Questions.A: Jacob said that God saw that he (Jacob) had worked hard, and that Laban had been cruel to him. (42)

Questions.Q: Because of what God saw, what did God do?
Questions.A: God appeared to Laban and told him not to threaten Jacob. (42)

Section.heading: Genesis 31:43-55 Jacob and Laban made an agreement.

Questions.Q: How was the conflict between Laban and Jacob finally resolved?
Questions.A: The two men made a peace treaty. They affirmed before God that they would not harm each other. They set up a pile of stones as a memorial of the treaty, and they shared a meal together. Then Laban said farewell to his daughters and grandchildren, and he returned home.

Questions.Q: After Jacob confronted Laban with the way that Laban had treated Jacob unjustly, how did Laban respond to Jacob?
Questions.A: Laban claimed that he still had rights over Jacob's wives and children, since the wives were his (Laban's) daughters, and Jacob's children were his (Laban's) grandchildren. Laban even claimed that the animals were his (Laban's). But then he admitted that he could not take them from Jacob. So he suggested that he and Jacob make a covenant/agreement. (43-44)

Questions.Q: How did Jacob respond to Laban's suggestion?
Questions.A: He set up a stone as a monument of their covenant/agreement. (45)

Questions.Q: What did Jacob tell his companions to do?
Questions.A: He told them to gather rocks and pile them up. (46)

Questions.Q: What happened next?
Questions.A: Jacob and Laban (and all of their companions) ate a meal together near the pile of stones. (46)

Questions.Q: What was the meaning/significance of that pile of rocks?
Questions.A: It was a visible sign/symbol of the agreement between Jacob and Laban. (48)
Questions.Alternative: What was the meaning of that pile of rocks?
What was the significance of that pile of rocks?

Questions.Q: What did Laban say to Jacob?
Questions.A: Laban prayed that God would guard over them while they were apart, in order to ensure that the two men would keep their agreement. (49)

Questions.Q: According to Laban, what was Jacob not to do?
Questions.A: Jacob was not to harm his wives. And he was also not to take any other wives. (50)

Questions.Q: Who will know whether Jacob was harming his wives or taking additional women as wives?
Questions.A: God would know. (50)

Questions.Q: What did Laban say that he would not do?
Questions.A: He would not pass the pile of rocks in order to harm Jacob. (51-52)

Questions.Q: And what else was Jacob not to do?
Questions.A: He was not to pass the pile of rocks in order to harm Laban. (52)

Questions.Q: But according to Laban, if he and Jacob did not keep their promises to each other, what would happen?
Questions.A: The God of Abraham and the God of Nahor would punish the one who broke the promise. (53)

Questions.Q: Then what did Jacob do?
Questions.A: He swore an oath to God - to the God worshiped and revered by his father Isaac. (53)

Questions.Q: And what else did Jacob do?
Questions.A: He slaughtered an animal as an offering to God, and he called his relatives to a feast. (54)

Questions.Q: What happened after the feast?
Questions.A: Everyone slept there. (54)

Questions.Q: In the morning, what did Laban do?
Questions.A: He kissed his daughters and grandchildren, and asked God to bless them, and then he left for (his) home. (55)

Section.heading: Genesis 32:1-21 Jacob sent gifts to Esau.

Questions.Q: What was Jacob worried about at that time?
Questions.A: He was worried that his brother, Esau, would still be very angry at him, and that Esau would take revenge against Jacob and his family.

Questions.Q: So what did Jacob do to prepare for meeting with Esau?
Questions.A: He sent several messengers on ahead. Each messenger had a small herd of animals to give to Esau as a gift from Jacob.

Questions.Q: Where was Jacob traveling to at that time?
Questions.A: He was traveling to his homeland in Canaan. (31:18)

Questions.Q: As Jacob continued on his journey, what happened to him?
Questions.A: He met/encountered angels of God. (1)

Questions.Q: What did he call the place where that happened?
Questions.A: He called it "Mahanaim" (which probably means something like "Two Camps"). (2)

Questions.Q: What did Jacob do next?
Questions.A: He sent servants ahead of him to meet his elder brother, Esau. (3)

Questions.Q: What did Jacob instruct his servants to say to Esau?
Questions.A: He told them to say that Esau's servant, Jacob, had been staying with (Uncle) Laban and had not been home for a long time. And the servants were to say that Jacob now has many animals and servants. They were to tell Esau that Jacob was sending word to him, so that he (Esau) would accept Jacob/be friendly to Jacob. (4-5)

Questions.Q: What did Jacob say in order to show respect toward his elder brother?
Questions.A: Jacob called himself Esau's servant. (4)
Jacob called Esau his lord [as a title of respect]. (4-5)
And he said that he wanted Esau to accept him/be friendly toward him. (5)

Questions.Q: What did Jacob say that he had now accumulated/he now owned?
Questions.A: He said that he had accumulated oxen, donkeys, sheep, goats, and male and female servants. (5)
Questions.Alternative: What did Jacob say that he had now accumulated?
What did Jacob say that he now owned?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Jacob sent word to his brother Esau?
Questions.A: He did that in order that Esau would accept him/would be friendly toward him. (5)

Questions.Q: When the servants returned to Jacob, what did they tell him?
Questions.A: They said that Esau was on his way to meet Jacob, along with 400 men. (6)

Questions.Q: What was Jacob's response?
Questions.A: He was terribly frightened, and he divided the people into two groups. (7)

Questions.Q: What was his purpose in making two separate groups?
Questions.A: He did that so that if Esau attacked one group, the other group could escape. (8)

Questions.Q: Then what did Jacob do?
Questions.A: He prayed (to God). (9-12)

Questions.Q: What did Jacob say (in his prayer) about what God had told him to do?
Questions.A: He said that God had told him to return home to his family. (9)

Questions.Q: What did Jacob say about what God had promised him?
Questions.A: Jacob said that God had promised to treat him well/to do good for him. He also said that God had promised to give him (Jacob) very many descendants. (9, 12)

Questions.Q: Did Jacob feel that God had fulfilled his promise to treat him well/to do good for him?
Questions.A: Yes, Jacob said that he was not worthy to receive God's love/kindness and faithfulness. (10)
Questions.Alternative: Did Jacob feel that God had fulfilled his promise to treat him well?
Did Jacob feel that God had fulfilled his promise to do good for him?

Questions.Q: What was the proof/evidence that God had given Jacob blessing and love?
Questions.A: Jacob had left home with just his one walking stick, and now he was returning as "two groups". (10)
Questions.Alternative: What was the proof that God had given Jacob blessing and love?
What was the evidence that God had given Jacob blessing and love?

Questions.Q: What did he request of God at that time?
Questions.A: He asked God to save him and his household from Esau. (11)

Questions.Q: About what did Jacob remind God?
Questions.A: Jacob reminded God that God had promised to bless him/to treat him kindly, and to give him innumerable descendants, like/as the sands of the seashore. (12)

Questions.Q: After Jacob had prayed to God, what did he do?
Questions.A: He prepared gifts for Esau. He chose many animals, and grouped them into herds, each with a leader. And he sent (ahead) the animals as gifts to Esau. (13-16)

Questions.Q: How many animals did Jacob choose as gifts for Esau?
Questions.A: Jacob chose 200 female goats and 200 female sheep, and 20 male goats and 20 male sheep. He also chose 30 female camels with their young, 40 cows, and 10 bulls. And he also chose 20 female donkeys and 10 male donkeys. (14-15)

Questions.Q: What did he tell his servants to do?
Questions.A: They were to keep the herds separate. Then, when each servant met Esau, and Esau asked the servant questions, the servant was to say that the animals belonged to [Esau's servant,] Jacob. Then each servant was to present the animals as gifts to (their/Jacob's) master, Esau. (16-18)

Questions.Q: What did Jacob tell his servants to say about where he (Jacob) was?
Questions.A: Each servant was to say that Jacob was following behind/was on his way. (18, 20)

Questions.Q: When the servants were speaking with Esau about Jacob, what term were they to use in referring to Jacob?
Questions.A: They were to call him Esau's slave/servant. (18, 20)

Questions.Q: But when the servants were speaking with Esau, what term were they to use in referring to Esau?
Questions.A: They were to refer to Esau as Jacob's master/lord. (18)

Questions.Q: For what purpose did Jacob send gifts to his older brother?
Questions.A: Jacob was attempting to persuade Esau to accept him/be friendly toward him. (20)

Questions.Q: Where did Jacob spend the night?
Questions.A: He stayed at the place where they had been camping. (21)

Questions.Q: What happened to Jacob during the night?
Questions.A: A "man"/Someone appeared and wrestled with Jacob. When the man realized that he could not subdue Jacob, he struck Jacob's hip. Then the man told Jacob to release him, but Jacob said that the man must first give Jacob a blessing. The man changed Jacob's name to "Israel". Jacob realized that he had been wrestling with God.

Questions.Q: That night, after Jacob had prepared gifts for Esau, what did he do?
Questions.A: He had Leah, Rachel, Bilhah, Zilpah, and his children cross to the other side of the river Jabbok. Then he sent across his possessions. (22-23)

Questions.Q: Then what happened to Jacob?
Questions.A: Someone appeared to Jacob, seeming to be in the form of a person. The two of them wrestled until near dawn/it was almost morning. (24)

Questions.Q: When Jacob's opponent realized that he was not defeating Jacob, what did he do?
Questions.A: He touched/struck Jacob's hip and dislocated/wrenched/strained it/and knocked it out of joint. (25)

Questions.Q: What did he then say to Jacob?
Questions.A: He told Jacob to let him go, because it was almost daytime. (26)

Questions.Q: What was Jacob's answer?
Questions.A: Jacob said that he would not release him until he blessed Jacob. (26)

Questions.Q: So then what happened?
Questions.A: The man asked Jacob his name, and Jacob told him. Then the man said that Jacob's name would no longer be "Jacob". Rather, it would, from that time on, be "Israel", because Jacob had struggled with God and man/struggled with divine and human beings, and Jacob had overcome/won. (27-28)

Questions.Q: Then what did Jacob ask his opponent?
Questions.A: Jacob asked his opponent to tell/reveal his (the opponent's) name. (29)

Questions.Q: What was his opponent's response?
Questions.A: He did not reveal his name, but he blessed Jacob. (29)

Questions.Q: What then did Jacob name that place?
Questions.A: He called it Peniel. (30)

Questions.Q: What is the meaning of "Peniel"?
Questions.A: "Peniel" means something like "the face of God". (30)

Questions.Q: In your opinion, what did Jacob think would happen to a person who saw God?
Questions.A: Jacob thought that such a person would die. (30)

Questions.Q: When Jacob left Peniel, in what manner was he walking?
Questions.A: He was limping, because his hip was dislocated. (31)

Questions.Q: How do the people of Israel show their respect for Jacob?
Questions.A: They do not eat meat from (near) the hip of animals. (32)

Section.heading: Genesis 33:1-20 Jacob and Esau made an agreement.

Questions.Q: What happened when Jacob and Esau finally met?
Questions.A: Jacob arranged his family in a line, and went ahead of them to meet Esau. The brothers embraced each other, and then Jacob introduced his wives and children to Esau. Jacob convinced Esau to accept his gifts. Esau offered to accompany Jacob and his family on the rest of their journey, but Jacob declined.

Questions.Q: How long was it that Jacob and Esau had not seen each other?
Questions.A: They had not seen each other for more than 20 years. (31:38)

Questions.Q: At the end of this chapter, where did Jacob and his family finally arrive?
Questions.A: They arrived in Canaan.

Questions.Q: What did Jacob see in the distance?
Questions.A: He saw Esau coming towards him, with 400 men. (1)

Questions.Q: When Jacob saw Esau coming, what did he do?
Questions.A: He arranged his family into a line/column. He put Leah's and Rachel's servants in front with their children. Then he placed Leah and her children, and at the rear/back, Rachel and Joseph. But Jacob went ahead of them all. (2-3)

Questions.Q: In your opinion, for what reason did Jacob place Rachel and Joseph at the back?
Questions.A: He did that probably because they were his favorites, and had the highest status within the family. It was probably customary for those of lower status to be the first to bow in submission to a powerful person such as Esau.
Also if Esau were to attack them, the wives and children would have an opportunity to escape. Rachel and Joseph, being at the rear, would have the clearest path to flee.

Questions.Q: As Jacob approached/came near to Esau, what did Jacob do?
Questions.A: He bowed down seven times. (3)
Questions.Alternative: As Jacob approached Esau, what did Jacob do?
As Jacob came near to Esau, what did Jacob do?

Questions.Q: When Esau saw Jacob, what did he do?
Questions.A: Esau ran to meet him, and hugged and kissed him. (4)

Questions.Q: In what way did the brothers show their emotions at that time?
Questions.A: They both cried (for joy). (4)

Questions.Q: After Jacob and Esau met and embraced each other, what happened?
Questions.A: Esau asked about the women and children who were with Jacob. (5)

Questions.Q: And what was Jacob's reply?
Questions.A: He said that they were the children whom God had graciously given to him. (5)

Questions.Q: Describe how Jacob's family presented themselves to Esau.
Questions.A: First, the two servants of Leah and Rachel (that is, Bilhah and Zilpah), brought their children to Esau, and they all bowed down to him. Then, Leah and her children did the same. Finally, Rachel and Joseph did likewise. (6-7)

Questions.Q: Then what did Esau and Jacob discuss?
Questions.A: Esau asked about all the animals that he had met as he was getting closer to Jacob. Jacob said that he wanted to give them to Esau so that Esau would accept/be friendly toward him. (8)

Questions.Q: According to Esau, why did he not want the animals?
Questions.A: He said that he already had many. (9)

Questions.Q: According to Jacob, why did he very much want his brother to accept the animals/the greeting gifts?
Questions.A: Jacob was so glad that Esau had accepted him/that Esau was being friendly toward him. Also, Jacob said that God had graciously blessed him with very much, so therefore he wanted to give some to his brother. (10-11)
Key Term Check: The idea of "grace" (generosity, kindness, favor) is a key theme in this account (see also 32:5b; 33:8, 15).
Questions.Note: See "grace" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: According to Jacob, why did he very much want his brother to accept the animals?
According to Jacob, why did he very much want his brother to accept the greeting gifts?

Questions.Q: What did Esau suggest at that time?
Questions.A: He suggested that he and his men accompany Jacob and his group. (12)

Questions.Q: What was Jacob's reply?
Questions.A: Jacob said that Esau should not wait for them, since Jacob's group included small children and young animals, and thus they were not able to travel quickly. Jacob suggested that Esau go ahead of them, saying that Jacob and his group would meet them at Seir. (13-14)

Questions.Q: What did Jacob say might/would happen, if they drove the animals too fast?
Questions.A: Jacob said that the animals might/would die. (13)
Questions.Alternative: What did Jacob say might happen, if they drove the animals too fast?
What did Jacob say would happen, if they drove the animals too fast?

Questions.Q: So what was Esau's next suggestion?
Questions.A: Esau said that he could leave some of his men to guide Jacob. (15)

Questions.Q: And what was Jacob's response?
Questions.A: He said it was not necessary, and that the important thing was that Esau was on good terms with him (Jacob). -OR- He said that if Esau did not mind [allowing Jacob and his group to proceed on their own], it was not necessary to have anyone from Esau's group accompany them. (15)

Questions.Q: Where did Esau go at that time?
Questions.A: He began to travel home to Seir. (16)

Questions.Q: Where did Jacob go?
Questions.A: He went to Succoth. (17)

Questions.Q: Did Jacob travel alone to Succoth, or did his family and animals go there also?
Questions.A: They all traveled together. (17-18)

Questions.Q: What did they do at Succoth?
Questions.A: They built temporary places to live, and shelters for their animals. (17)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that place was named "Succoth"?
Questions.A: That means, "shelters". (17)

Questions.Q: When Jacob and his group arrived at Canaan, where did they first stay?
Questions.A: They set up their camp near the town or city of Shechem. (18)

Questions.Q: By what means did Jacob obtain/get some land on which to live?
Questions.A: He bought some land from the sons/descendants/family of Hamor. (19)
Questions.Alternative: By what means did Jacob obtain some land on which to live?
By what means did Jacob get some land on which to live?

Questions.Q: How much did the land cost?
Questions.A: Jacob paid 100 pieces of silver/money for the land. (19)

Questions.Q: After that, what did he do?
Questions.A: He built an altar and called it, "El-Elohe-Israel" ("God, the God of the people of Israel"). (20)

Section.heading: Genesis 34:1-31 Jacob's sons deceived Shechem and Hamor and took revenge at Shechem.

Questions.Q: Tell what happened here to Jacob's family and what they did in response.
Questions.A: A powerful young Canaanite man named Shechem raped Dinah, a daughter of Jacob. When Dinah's brothers heard about it, they were extremely upset. Shechem and his father approached Jacob and his family, asking if Shechem could marry Dinah. Her brothers thought of a way/means to take revenge. So they told Shechem that he could marry Dinah only if he and all the men of their town would be circumcised. Shechem agreed to the condition, and he was able to persuade the other men of the town to also be circumcised. And then three days later, when all the men were recovering and unable to defend themselves, two of Dinah's brothers, Levi and Simeon, went to the town and slaughtered all the men. The other sons of Jacob took away all the women and children and wealth. Jacob was now very upset with his two violent sons, but they felt that they were justified because of how Shechem had treated their sister.

Questions.Q: Who was Dinah?
Questions.A: She was the daughter of Jacob and Leah. (1)

Questions.Q: Where did she go?
Questions.A: She left her father's household to go visit some Canaanite women/girls who lived nearby. (1)

Questions.Q: Who was Shechem?
Questions.A: He was the son of Hamor the Hivite. Hamor was the leader of the area. -OR- Shechem was the leader of the area. (2)
Questions.Note: Most scholars understand the text to read that Hamor, the father, was the leader. But some understand it to read that Shechem, the son, was the leader. The one responding to these questions should provide an answer which is consistent with the translated text.

Questions.Q: What did Shechem do to Dinah?
Questions.A: He raped her. -OR- He coerced her to have sex with him, although they were not married. (2)

Questions.Q: And then what did Shechem do?
Questions.A: He tried to win her affection, and he asked his father to arrange for Dinah to become his wife. (3-4)

Questions.Q: When Jacob first heard about what had happened, what did he do?
Questions.A: He waited until his sons came in from the fields. (5)

Questions.Q: What were Jacob's sons doing in the fields?
Questions.A: They were looking after their cattle/animals. (5)

Questions.Q: As Jacob's sons were returning home from the fields, who else arrived to speak with Jacob?
Questions.A: Shechem's father, Hamor, arrived at the same time. (7)

Questions.Q: What was Hamor's purpose/intention in going to speak with Jacob?
Questions.A: Hamor wanted to discuss with Jacob the situation between his (Hamor's) son and Jacob's daughter. (6)
Questions.Alternative: What was Hamor's purpose in going to speak with Jacob?
What was Hamor's intention in going to speak with Jacob?
Questions.Note: Though the request has not yet been stated explicitly, it will probably be evident at this point that Hamor wanted to ask Jacob to let Dinah (his daughter) marry Shechem. (See verse 4.)

Questions.Q: When Jacob's sons heard about what had happened to Dinah, what was their reaction?
Questions.A: They were extremely upset - shocked/pained and very angry. (7)

Questions.Q: What did Hamor request?
Questions.A: He asked that Jacob's family allow Shechem and Dinah to marry (each other). (8)

Questions.Q: What else did Hamor suggest?
Questions.A: He suggested that the young men and women of Jacob's family intermarry with the people of the land/intermarry with Hamor's people. (9)

Questions.Q: If Jacob would agree to do as Hamor suggested, what was Hamor's promise?
Questions.A: Hamor said that they could live freely among Hamor's people: engage in trade, buy property, and settle in their land. (10)

Questions.Q: What did Hamor's son, Shechem, offer to Jacob's family?
Questions.A: Shechem said that he would give anything that Jacob's family requested as payment/bride-price/dowry. (11-12)

Questions.Q: What does it mean that Jacob's sons deceived Shechem and Hamor?
Questions.A: Jacob's sons agreed that their family would intermarry with Hamor's family, if the men of Hamor's family would become circumcised. But Jacob's sons did not intend to keep their promise. (13-16)

Questions.Q: For what reason did Jacob's sons deceive Shechem and Hamor?
Questions.A: They did that because Shechem had violated their sister. (13)

Questions.Q: What did Jacob's sons say must happen before Shechem could take Dinah as his wife?
Questions.A: They said that all the men of Hamor's family must first be circumcised. (14-15)

Questions.Q: And what did Jacob's sons say they would do if all the men of Hamor's family would be circumcised?
Questions.A: The sons said that they would intermarry with Hamor's family and that they would all live together and become one people-group. (16)

Questions.Q: But if the men of Hamor's family did not want/were not willing to be circumcised, what would Jacob's sons do?
Questions.A: They would take Dinah and leave. (17)
Questions.Alternative: But if the men of Hamor's family did not want to be circumcised, what would Jacob's sons do?
But if the men of Hamor's family were not willing to be circumcised, what would Jacob's sons do?

Questions.Q: What did Hamor and Shechem think of the suggestion of Dinah's brothers?
Questions.A: They agreed to the suggestion. (18)
Questions.Alternative: What did Nahor and Shechem think of the suggestion of Dinah's brothers?
What did Hamor and Shechem think of Dinah's brothers' suggestion?
How did Hamor and Shechem respond to the suggestion of Dinah's brothers?
How did Hamor and Shechem respond to Dinah's brothers' suggestion?

Questions.Q: What did Hamor and Shechem do next?
Questions.A: They went to the town/city leaders in order to persuade them that all of the men of the town/city should be circumcised. (19-20)

Questions.Q: According to Hamor and Shechem, what should their people invite Jacob's people to do?
Questions.A: They should invite Jacob's people to live among Hamor's people, and intermarry and engage in trade. (21)

Questions.Q: According to Hamor and Shechem, what would be the outcome, if their people intermarried with Jacob's family/people?
Questions.A: Hamor's people would be able to acquire/take over the wealth of Jacob's people. (23)
Questions.Alternative: According to Hamor and Shechem, what would be the outcome, if their people intermarried with Jacob's family?
According to Hamor and Shechem, what would be the outcome, if their people intermarried with Jacob's people?

Questions.Q: What did Hamor and Shechem say that their people must do in order to intermarry with Jacob's people?
Questions.A: Their men would first have to be circumcised. (22)

Questions.Q: And how did Hamor's people respond?
Questions.A: They agreed to the proposal. The men became circumcised. (24)

Questions.Q: In your opinion, why do you think Hamor's people agreed to the proposal?
Questions.A: Perhaps they were interested in the economic benefits. (23) Also, Shechem was a highly respected member of Hamor's family, so his influential position might have had an effect. (19) Or perhaps Hamor's people were forced/obligated to obey him (and Shechem) (even if Hamor's people did not necessarily agree with Hamor).

Questions.Q: What happened next?
Questions.A: Three days later, while the men of the town/city were recovering from the circumcision procedure, Dinah's two brothers/full-brothers, Simeon and Levi, brutally attacked the (men of the) city and killed all the men, including Hamor and Shechem. (25-26)

Questions.Q: What was the reason that the two brothers were able to overcome all the men of the city?
Questions.A: The men were still sore and not yet fully recovered from being circumcised. (25)

Questions.Q: What weapons did the two brothers use?
Questions.A: They used swords. (25)

Questions.Q: Where was Dinah when Simeon and Levi began to attack the men of the city?
Questions.A: She was in Shechem's house. (26)

Questions.Q: What happened to Dinah? // What did Simeon and Levi do about/do for Dinah?
Questions.A: The brothers rescued her from Shechem's house and took her home. (26)
Questions.Alternative: What happened to Dinah?
What did Simeon and Levi do about Dinah?
What did Simeon and Levi do for Dinah?

Questions.Q: Then what did the other brothers do?
Questions.A: They plundered/looted the city. They took all the livestock and wealth, and even took/dragged away the women and children. (27)

Questions.Q: How did Jacob react to what his sons had done?
Questions.A: He was very upset. He said that the other people of the land were going to be against their family now, and the people might unite and destroy Jacob's whole family. (30)

Questions.Q: What was it about Jacob's family that made them vulnerable to attack from the other people of the land?
Questions.A: They were only a few people/relatively few (compared to the numbers of other people in the land). (30)

Questions.Q: How did Levi and Simeon respond to what Jacob said?
Questions.A: They said that their sister was not a prostitute, and it was wrong for Shechem to have violated her. (31)

Questions.Q: Jacob said that the other people of the land might destroy his whole family. If that happened, what would be the outcome of God's promise to make Jacob's descendants as numerous as the sands on the seashore?
Questions.A: If someone destroyed his family, then God's promise might/would not be fulfilled/God's promise might/would fail.
Questions.Alternative: Jacob said that the other people of the land might destroy his whole family. If that happened, what would be the outcome of God's promise to make Jacob's descendents as numerous as the sands on the seashore?

Questions.Q: In your opinion, do you think that the sons' behavior was appropriate, or do you think that it was excessive?
Questions.A: Jacob thought it was excessive. (30)
