Simeon and Levi felt it was just punishment for Shechem's outrageous behavior. (7, 31)
Questions.Note: It was really excessive. Respondents who are familiar with God's standards and biblical principles of retribution and vengeance will agree with Jacob. Respondents whose views on justice are shaped by experiences with community/family feuding that place a high value on revenge might side with the brothers.

Section.heading: Genesis 35:1-15 God renewed his promise with Jacob at Bethel.

Questions.Q: What are some of the things that God said to Jacob at the time of this account/at this time?
Questions.A: God told Jacob to move on (from Shechem) to Bethel, and to build an altar there to worship him. God also told Jacob that his name from now on would be "Israel," and that his descendants would increase greatly in numbers, and they would become great and powerful. And God said that he would give Jacob's descendants the land (of Canaan).
Questions.Alternative: What are some of the things that God said to Jacob at the time of this account?
What are some of the things that God said to Jacob at this time?

Questions.Q: Where did God tell Jacob to move/go at that time?
Questions.A: God told Jacob to move/go to Bethel. (1)
Questions.Alternative: Where did God tell Jacob to move at that time?
Where did God tell Jacob to go at that time?

Questions.Q: In what land or area was Bethel?
Questions.A: It was in the land of Canaan. (1)

Questions.Q: What did God tell Jacob to do at Bethel?
Questions.A: God told him to settle there, and to build an altar to worship God. (1)

Questions.Q: Of what event did God remind Jacob?
Questions.A: He reminded Jacob of the time when he (Jacob) had fled (from) Esau, and God had appeared to Jacob. (1)

Questions.Q: What were Jacob's three commands to his people?
Questions.A: The people were to discard their foreign false-gods/idols. They were to (repent and) cleanse themselves, and they were to put on clean clothes. (2)

Questions.Q: According to Jacob, how had God helped him?
Questions.A: God had helped him when he had problems, and God guided/guarded Jacob wherever he went. (3)

Questions.Q: What did Jacob's family do at that time?
Questions.A: They gave Jacob all their foreign false-gods/idols, and they also gave him their earrings. (4)

Questions.Q: What did Jacob do with the false-gods/idols and with the earrings of his family?
Questions.A: He buried everything under a large tree near Shechem. (4)
Questions.Alternative: What did Jacob do with the false-gods and with the earrings of his family?
What did Jacob do with the idols and with the earrings of his family?

Questions.Q: While Jacob and his family and servants were traveling to Bethel, how did God help them?
Questions.A: God caused all the people along the way/people around them to fear them, so that nobody attacked/chased them. (5)

Questions.Q: What did Jacob do, after they arrived?
Questions.A: He built an altar there, and named it "El-bethel"/"God of Bethel". (7)

Questions.Q: While they were there at Bethel, what else happened?
Questions.A: Deborah, Rebekah's nursemaid who was then very old, died. (8)

Questions.Q: Who was Rebekah?
Questions.A: She was Jacob's mother, the wife of Isaac.
Questions.Note: See Genesis 25:21; 28:5.

Questions.Q: What did Jacob's family do with Deborah's corpse?
Questions.A: They buried it near a tree/under the branches of a tree which was (in a valley) below Bethel. (8)

Questions.Q: When God appeared to Jacob at Bethel, what did God say to him?
Questions.A: God blessed him/God announced that he would do good for Jacob, and God said that his name was no longer Jacob, but Israel. (9-10)

Questions.Q: What did God call himself when he spoke to Jacob?
Questions.A: He called himself God Most High/God Almighty. (11)

Questions.Q: What did God promise to Jacob?
Questions.A: God promised that Jacob would have many descendants, who would become many people-groups. And some of Jacob's descendants would become kings. (11)

Questions.Q: To whom had God made similar promises before that time?
Questions.A: God had made similar promises to Abraham and Isaac.

Questions.Q: What did God promise to give to Jacob and his descendants?
Questions.A: God promised to give them land. (12)
Questions.Alternative: What did God promise to give to Jacob and his descendents?

Questions.Q: After God had spoken to him, what did Jacob do?
Questions.A: He set up a stone pillar as a remembrance/as something to remind people that God spoke to him (Jacob) at that place. And he poured on the stone pillar a drink offering and oil. Then he named that place Bethel/House of God. (14-15)

Questions.Q: What is the meaning of the name "Bethel"?
Questions.A: It means "House of God". (15)
Questions.Alternative: What does "Bethel" mean?
What is the meaning of the name, "Bethel"?

Questions.Q: Who died during that time?
Questions.A: Rachel and Isaac died.

Questions.Q: Who was Rachel?
Questions.A: She was Jacob's favorite wife.

Questions.Q: And who was Isaac?
Questions.A: He was the father of Jacob and Esau. And he was the son which God had promised to give to Abraham. // And he was the son which God had given to Abraham as fulfillment of God's promise.

Questions.Q: When Jacob and his group left Bethel, while they were traveling, what happened?
Questions.A: Rachel began to give birth. She was in very much pain. (16)

Questions.Q: What did the midwife say to Rachel?
Questions.A: She told Rachel not to fear. And she told Rachel that she was giving birth to/had given birth to a baby boy. (17)

Questions.Q: But then what happened as Rachel was giving birth? -OR- But then what happened very soon after Rachel gave birth?
Questions.A: Rachel died. (18-19)
Questions.Alternative: But then what happened as Rachel was giving birth?
But then what happened very soon after Rachel gave birth?

Questions.Q: As Rachel was about to die, what did she name her son?
Questions.A: She called him Ben-oni (which means "son of my grief/sorrow"). (18)

Questions.Q: Did Jacob like that name, "Ben-oni"?
Questions.A: No, he changed it to Benjamin (which means "son of my right hand"/"son who will be fortunate"). (18)

Questions.Q: What did Jacob do with Rachel's dead body/corpse?
Questions.A: He (and those with him) buried Rachel near the way/path going to Bethlehem, which at that time was called Ephrath/going to Bethlehem, in Ephrath. (19).
Questions.Alternative: What did Jacob do with Rachel's dead body?
What did Jacob do with Rachel's corpse?

Questions.Q: What did Jacob make at that time?
Questions.A: He made a grave marker/stone monument over her grave. (20)

Questions.Q: Where did Jacob and his group go next?
Questions.A: They went to a place near/beyond Migdal-Eder/the tower of Eder. (21)

Questions.Q: Who was Reuben, and who was Bilhah?
Questions.A: Reuben was the eldest son of Jacob, one of Leah's sons. Bilhah was the servant of the late Rachel/of Rachel, who had just died.

Questions.Q: What did Reuben do at that time?
Questions.A: He slept with his father's concubine/wife/secondary-wife, Bilhah. (22)

Questions.Q: Did Jacob know (about)/find out what Reuben had done?
Questions.A: Yes, someone told Jacob about it. (22)

Questions.Q: How many sons did Jacob have?
Questions.A: He had twelve sons. (22-26)

Questions.Q: Who was the firstborn son?
Questions.A: The firstborn was Reuben. (23)

Questions.Q: What were the names of the sons to whom Rachel gave birth?
Questions.A: They were Joseph and Benjamin. (24)

Questions.Q: Where did Jacob go at that time/at the time of this account?
Questions.A: He went to where Isaac was staying, at Mamre. (27)
Questions.Alternative: Where did Jacob go at that time?
Where did Jacob go at the time of this account?

Questions.Q: Who were Isaac and Abraham?
Questions.A: Isaac was the father of Jacob, and Abraham was Jacob's grandfather.

Questions.Q: Where was Isaac living?
Questions.A: He was living at Mamre, near Kiriath-arba. (27)

Questions.Q: What name was later used for Kiriath-arba?
Questions.A: It was later called Hebron. (27)

Questions.Q: When Isaac died, how old was he?
Questions.A: He was 180 years old when he died. (28)

Questions.Q: Who buried Isaac?
Questions.A: His two sons, Esau and Jacob, buried him. (29)

Section.heading: Genesis 36:1-8 The descendants of Esau in Canaan.

Questions.Q: Who is this section about?
Questions.A: It is about Esau's wives, and the sons born to Esau while he was in Canaan.

Questions.Q: What was another name which people used for Esau?
Questions.A: Esau was also called "Edom". (1, 8)

Questions.Q: What were the names of Esau's wives?
Questions.A: They were Adah, Oholibamah, and Basemath. (2-3)

Questions.Q: Which one of Esau's wives was his cousin?
Questions.A: Basemath was his cousin. (3)

Questions.Q: How many sons did Esau's wives give birth to in Canaan?
Questions.A: They gave birth to five sons in Canaan. (4-5)

Questions.Q: What problem did Esau and Jacob encounter?
Questions.A: When they were living near each other in Canaan, there was not enough land for their households and all of their animals. (7)

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that the land was not adequate for Esau and Jacob?
Questions.A: Probably there was not enough pasture for their large numbers of animals. // Probably there was not enough land in order for their large numbers of animals to be able to get/find sufficient food.

Questions.Q: So what did they do about the problem?
Questions.A: Esau moved away from Canaan. (6)

Questions.Q: Who, and what, did Esau take with him when he moved?
Questions.A: He took his wives, children, servants, and all of his animals. (6)

Questions.Q: Where did Esau go?
Questions.A: He went to the hills of Seir. (8)
Questions.Alternative: Where did Esau go [to]?
Where did Esau go to?

Section.heading: Genesis 36:9-19 The descendants of Esau in Edom.

Questions.Q: About whom is this section/passage of Scripture?
Questions.A: It is about Esau's grandsons, and the tribal leaders who descended from Esau.
Questions.Alternative: About whom is this section of Scripture?
About whom is this passage of Scripture?

Questions.Q: Where were Esau and his descendants at that time/the time of this account?
Questions.A: They were in the hills of Seir. (9)
Questions.Alternative: Where were Esau and his descendants at that time?
Where were Esau and his descendants at the time of this account?
Where were Esau and his descendents at that time/the time of this account?
Where were Esau and his descendents at that time?
Where were Esau and his descendents at the time of this account?

Questions.Q: How many grandsons of Esau did the writer of Genesis mention here?
Questions.A: The writer mentioned thirteen. (10-14)

Questions.Q: In your opinion, do you think that perhaps one of the grandsons had lower status than the other twelve?
Questions.A: Possibly Amalek was of lower status, since his mother was a concubine/servant/secondary-wife. (12)

Section.heading: Genesis 36:20-30 The indigenous people-groups of Edom.

Questions.Q: About whom is this section/passage of Scripture?
Questions.A: It is about people who were native to the place called Edom. They descended from a man named Seir.
Questions.Alternative: About whom is this section of Scripture?
About whom is this passage of Scripture?

Questions.Q: About whom is this section/passage?
Questions.A: It is about kings who ruled in Edom (before there were kings in Israel).
Questions.Alternative: About whom is this section?
About whom is this passage?

Questions.Q: Concerning whose family is this story/account?
Questions.A: It is about Jacob and his family/Jacob's family. (2)
Questions.Alternative: Concerning whose family is this story?
Concerning whose family is this account?

Questions.Q: Between whom was conflict developing at that time?
Questions.A: Conflict was developing between Joseph and his brothers.

Questions.Q: What are some events that added to the tension between Joseph and his brothers?
Questions.A: Joseph sometimes told his father about bad things that his brothers were doing. Also, Jacob gave to Joseph a very special robe; that made his brothers jealous. And then Joseph had two dreams which suggested that he was superior to his brothers, and even superior to his father and mother.

Questions.Q: Where was Jacob living at this time?
Questions.A: He was in the land of Canaan. (1)

Questions.Q: Who else had lived in Canaan before Jacob?
Questions.A: Jacob's parents had also lived there. (1)

Questions.Q: What do we learn about Joseph?
Questions.A: Joseph was 17 years old at that time. He looked after sheep with his half-brothers. He sometimes told his father about bad things that his half-brothers did. Joseph was his father's favorite; he was born when his father was old. His father gave him a beautiful robe. His brothers were jealous and did not speak kindly to him. (2-4)
Questions.Note: Some of the following questions can be omitted if the respondent has adequately related the information in response to this question.

Questions.Q: What relationship was Joseph to Bilhah and Zilpah?
Questions.A: Joseph was the stepson of Bilhah and Zilpah.

Questions.Q: What relationship were the children of Bilhah and Zilpah to Joseph?
Questions.A: The children of Bilhah and Zilpah were half-brothers to Joseph. (2)

Questions.Q: For what reasons did Joseph's brothers hate him?
Questions.A: Joseph (sometimes) told Jacob, their father about bad things that his half-brothers were doing. Also, he was Jacob's favorite, and Jacob had even given to Joseph a special, beautiful robe. (2-4)

Questions.Q: For what reason did Jacob love Joseph more than he loved his other sons?
Questions.A: Joseph was born when Jacob was already old. (3) (Also, Joseph was the first child born after a very long time to Jacob's favorite wife, Rachel.) (Gen. 29:16-18, 21-31; 30:22-24)

Questions.Q: In what way did Jacob show that Joseph was his favorite son?
Questions.A: Jacob made a beautiful robe/had a beautiful robe made especially for Joseph. (3)

Questions.Q: In your opinion, how do you think Joseph's robe looked?
Questions.A: Maybe it was long and beautiful, with long sleeves. Perhaps it had many colors. (3)

Questions.Q: What was the attitude of Joseph's brothers toward him?
Questions.A: They hated him and spoke unkindly to him. (4)

Questions.Q: What happened to cause Joseph's brothers to hate him even more?
Questions.A: Joseph told his brothers about two dreams that he had. In those dreams, the brothers bowed down to Joseph (as though he were a king). (5-6, 9)

Questions.Q: How many dreams did Joseph recount/relate to his brothers/tell his brothers about?
Questions.A: He told them about two of his dreams. (5-6, 9)
Questions.Alternative: How many dreams did Joseph recount?
How many dreams did Joseph relate to his brothers?
How many dreams did Joseph tell his brothers about?

Questions.Q: Do you know of someone who has had a dream that told them something about what will happen in the future?
Questions.Note: This question is about personal experience - answers will vary.

Questions.Q: What happened in Joseph's two dreams?
Questions.A: In the first dream, Joseph and his brothers were binding/bundling sheaves during harvest. Joseph's bundle stood up and all his brothers' bundles surrounded his and bowed down to it. In the second dream, the sun, moon and eleven stars bowed low to Joseph. (6-7, 9)

Questions.Q: Those two both had a (similar) meaning. What did the dreams mean?
Questions.A: They meant that Joseph's parents and his brothers would show/give special honor to Joseph. (7, 9)
Questions.Alternative: Those two dreams both had a similar meaning. What did the dreams mean?
Those two dreams both had a meaning. What did the dreams mean?
Joseph's two dreams both had a similar meaning. What did the dreams mean?
Joseph's two dreams both had a meaning. What did the dreams mean?
What did Joseph's two dreams mean?
What did those two dreams mean?

Questions.Q: What do you think caused Joseph's brothers to become angry, when he told them his dreams?
Questions.A: The dreams showed Joseph like/as a king ruling over his older brothers. They already disliked him, because he was Jacob's favorite son. They certainly did not want to bow down to him. (8, 10-11)

Questions.Q: What was meant by the "sun, moon and eleven stars"?
Questions.A: The sun was his father, the moon was his mother, and the eleven stars were his half-brothers. (10)

Questions.Q: For what reason do you think Jacob scolded Joseph when Joseph recounted/told his family about his dreams?
Questions.A: Perhaps Jacob recognized that Joseph was proud in claiming/seeming to claim that he (Joseph) would become a leader over the rest of his family. (10)
Questions.Alternative: For what reason do you think Jacob scolded Joseph when Joseph recounted his dreams?
For what reason do you think Jacob scolded Joseph when Joseph told his family about his dreams?

Questions.Q: In your opinion, what do you think caused Joseph's brothers to become very jealous of him?
Questions.A: Perhaps they believed that God spoke through dreams, and that Joseph might actually become a leader over them - and they would not have liked that. (11)

Questions.Q: How did Jacob react to Joseph's dreams?
Questions.A: Jacob thought about what they might mean. (11)
Questions.Note: This response followed his initial reaction, which was to rebuke/scold him.
Questions.Alternative: After Jacob's initial reaction to Joseph's dreams, what did he do?
After Jacob's initial negative reaction to Joseph's dreams, what did he do?

Questions.Q: In a family with many brothers, who do you think is usually the leader?
Questions.A: Probably the eldest brother is usually the leader.

Questions.Q: After Joseph's brothers were so angry about his first dream, why do you think Joseph told them about his second dream?
Questions.A: Maybe Joseph was proud, and he wanted to taunt/mock his older brothers. Or maybe he felt that God had given him the dreams and therefore it was wrong not to tell about them.

Questions.Q: What happened to Joseph?
Questions.A: His father sent him to check on his brothers (who were working) in the fields, and his brothers decided to harm him. First they were going to kill him, but Reuben persuaded them to just put Joseph in an empty pit. Later some traders came by, and the brothers sold Joseph to them as a slave. So the traders took Joseph to Egypt. Meanwhile, Joseph's brothers killed a goat, smeared some blood on Joseph's special robe, and took the bloodied robe home to Jacob. When Jacob saw it, he was extremely upset.

Questions.Q: Where did Joseph's brothers go?
Questions.A: They went to a place called Shechem/to some fields near Shechem. (12)

Questions.Q: What were they doing there?
Questions.A: They were grazing their family's sheep there. // They were looking after their father's sheep in the fields/pastures there. (12)

Questions.Q: Where was Joseph when his father summoned him?
Questions.A: Joseph was at home in Hebron with his father. (14)

Questions.Q: What did Jacob decide that Joseph should do?
Questions.A: Jacob decided that Joseph should go to see his brothers. (13-14)

Questions.Q: What was Joseph's purpose/intention in going to Shechem? // For what purpose did Jacob send Joseph to Shechem?
Questions.A: Jacob wanted Joseph to see/discover/find out if all was well with the other brothers and the sheep. And Jacob wanted Joseph to bring him news of them. (14)
Questions.Alternative: What was Joseph's purpose in going to Shechem?
What was Joseph's intention in going to Shechem?
For what purpose did Jacob send Joseph to Shechem?

Questions.Q: When Joseph arrived at/near Shechem, what happened?
Questions.A: Joseph searched/looked around but could not find his brothers. A man there asked Joseph who/what he was looking for, and Joseph told the man. Then the man told Joseph that the brothers said they were planning/going to move to Dothan. (15-17)
Questions.Alternative: When Joseph arrived at Shechem, what happened?
When Joseph arrived near Shechem, what happened?

Questions.Q: After the man spoke to Joseph, what did Joseph do?
Questions.A: He went to Dothan and there he found his brothers. (17)

Questions.Q: Where was Joseph when his brothers first saw him?
Questions.A: Joseph was still a long way/considerable distance from his brothers. (18)

Questions.Q: When Joseph's brothers saw him, what did they do?
Questions.A: They planned to kill Joseph. (18)

Questions.Q: For what reason did Joseph's brothers call him "Dreamer"/"Master of Dreams"?
Questions.A: They called him that because of the dreams that he had/that he had told to them.
Questions.Alternative: For what reason did Joseph's brothers call him "Dreamer of Dreams"?
For what reason did Joseph's brothers call him "Master of Dreams"?
Why did Joseph's brothers call him "Dreamer of Dreams"?
Why did Joseph's brothers call him "Master of Dreams"?
For what reason did Joseph's brothers call him, "Dreamer"/"Master of Dreams"?

Questions.Q: Tell me about the brothers' plan.
Questions.A: They planned to kill Joseph and throw his corpse/body into a deep cistern/pit/well. (20)

Questions.Q: For what purpose do you think the brothers wanted to kill Joseph?
Questions.A: Maybe it was so that after he was dead, his dreams would not be fulfilled/come true. (20)

Questions.Q: What did they plan to say to Jacob about Joseph?
Questions.A: They were going to tell him that a wild animal had killed and eaten Joseph. (20)

Questions.Q: Who wanted to help/rescue Joseph?
Questions.A: Reuben wanted to help/rescue him. (21)
Questions.Alternative: Who wanted to help Joseph?
Who wanted to rescue Joseph?

Questions.Q: What did Reuben suggest?
Questions.A: Reuben suggested that they not kill Joseph, but instead drop him into one of the dry cisterns/wells there, and leave him (to die). (21-22)

Questions.Q: In what way was Reuben related to the rest of the brothers? // What was Reuben's status with the rest of the brothers?
Questions.A: Reuben was the eldest of the brothers. He was the firstborn (son of Leah). (29:32)
Questions.Alternative: In what way was Reuben related to the rest of the brothers?
What was Reuben's status with the rest of the brothers?

Questions.Q: Did Reuben intend that Joseph would die in the cistern/well?
Questions.A: No, Reuben wanted to return Joseph alive to Jacob. (22)
Questions.Alternative: Did Reuben intend that Joseph would die in the cistern?
Did Reuben intend that Joseph would die in the well?

Questions.Q: When Joseph arrived where his brothers were, what happened to him?
Questions.A: The brothers grabbed him, took off his beautiful robe, and dropped him into one of the dry cisterns/wells there. (23-24)

Questions.Q: After that, what did Joseph's brothers do?
Questions.A: They sat down to eat. (25a)

Questions.Q: Do you think that Reuben was with the rest of the brothers when they sat down to eat?
Questions.A: Apparently, Reuben had gone away for a short time. (29)

Questions.Q: While the brothers were eating, what did they see?
Questions.A: They saw a group/caravan of Ishmaelites/traders with camels loaded with cargo. (25b)

Questions.Q: Where were the Ishmaelites coming from, and [to] where were they going?
Questions.A: They were coming from Gilead, and going towards Egypt to/in the south. (25b)
Questions.Alternative: Where were the Ishmaelites coming from, and to where were they going?
Where were the Ishmaelites coming from, and where were they going?

Questions.Q: What cargo did the Ishmaelites have?
Questions.A: They had spices, perfumes, and incense. (Some of it might have been medicine.) (25b)

Questions.Q: What was the livelihood/occupation of the Ishmaelites?
Questions.A: They were traders.
Questions.Alternative: What was the livelihood of the Ishmaelites?
What was the occupation of the Ishmaelites?
Questions.Note: Although the original text does not make their livelihood explicit until verse 28, if it is not obvious from the context clues in verses 25 and 27, it might be helpful to state their occupation explicitly in verse 25.

Questions.Q: When Joseph's brothers saw the Ishmaelites, what did they think about doing?
Questions.A: They planned to sell Joseph to the Ishmaelites, rather than kill him. (26-27)

Questions.Q: Who suggested that idea?
Questions.A: Judah was the one who suggested it. (26)

Questions.Q: According to Judah, why was it better that the brothers sell Joseph, rather than kill him?
Questions.A: If they were to sell Joseph, they could earn some money. And also they would not be responsible for (the guilt/shame of) killing a brother/a close relative. (26-27)

Questions.Q: How much money did the Ishmaelite/Midianite traders pay (the brothers) for Joseph?
Questions.A: They paid 20 pieces of silver. (28)
Questions.Alternative: How much money did the Ishmaelite traders pay (the brothers) for Joseph?
How much money did the Midianite traders pay (the brothers) for Joseph?

Questions.Q: Then where did the traders take Joseph [to]?
Questions.A: They took him to Egypt. (28)
Questions.Alternative: Then where did the traders take Joseph to?
Then where did the traders take Joseph?

Questions.Q: Where was Reuben at the time that the traders bought Joseph?
Questions.A: Reuben was away somewhere else. (29)
Questions.Note: Possibly he was tending the flocks while the others ate.

Questions.Q: What did Reuben do when he returned?
Questions.A: Reuben went to the cistern/pit where the brothers had put Joseph. He saw that Joseph was no longer there, and he because extremely upset. (29)

Questions.Q: What did Reuben do when he saw that Joseph was not there?
Questions.A: He tore his clothes. He went to his brothers and said that Joseph was missing. And he asked them what he could do now. // He asked them how he could go home without his (youngest) brother. (29)

Questions.Q: In your opinion, for what reason did he tear his clothes?
Questions.A: This was their custom. It was the way that they showed that they were extremely upset. (29)

Questions.Q: In your opinion, what do you think was the cause for Reuben being so much more upset than his brothers?
Questions.A: Probably Reuben felt responsible to protect his (youngest) brother, since Reuben was the oldest brother.

Questions.Q: What did Joseph's brothers do next?
Questions.A: They killed a goat and smeared some of its blood on Joseph's special robe. And then they took the robe and showed it to their father for him to identify (it). (31-32)

Questions.Q: For what purpose did they kill the goat?
Questions.A: They did that in order to have some blood to smear on Joseph's special robe. That would cause Jacob to think that a wild animal had killed Joseph.

Questions.Q: In Jacob's thinking, what happened to Joseph?
Questions.A: Jacob concluded that a wild animal had killed and eaten Joseph. (33)

Questions.Q: What did Jacob do after he concluded that Joseph was dead?
Questions.A: He tore his clothes and put sackcloth/put rough cloth around his waist. He said that he would grieve until he died. (34-35)

Questions.Q: When Jacob's children saw how upset their father was, what did they do?
Questions.A: They tried to comfort him. (35)

Questions.Q: Then what did Jacob answer to his children?
Questions.A: He said that he would grieve until he died. (35)

Questions.Q: To what place/Where did Jacob say that he would go in his grief?
Questions.A: He said that he would go to the world of the dead. (35)
Questions.Alternative: To what place did Jacob say that he would go in his grief?
Where did Jacob say that he would go in his grief?

Questions.Q: What do you think he meant by "world of the dead"?
Questions.A: He was referring to the place where the spirit/soul of a person goes when he or she dies.
Questions.Note: The Hebrew term here is "sheol". It did not refer specifically to heaven or to hell. It had a more general meaning: the place where the spirit/soul of any person goes when he or she dies.

If a literal term such as "grave" is used in the translation, ensure that it can also carry a more figurative sense (and that that sense is understood in this context) because Jacob could not have meant that he would be buried in the same grave or tomb as Joseph, since he believed that Joseph's body had been eaten.

Questions.Q: In the meantime, what had happened to Joseph?
Questions.A: The traders had taken Joseph to Egypt. There they sold him to someone else. (36)

Questions.Q: Who bought Joseph in Egypt?
Questions.A: A man named Potiphar bought him. (36)

Questions.Q: What do we know about Potiphar?
Questions.A: He was the chief leader of the palace guards of the King of Egypt. (36)

Questions.Q: Who were the two main people in this account/story?
Questions.A: Judah and Tamar were the two main people in this account/story.
Questions.Alternative: Who were the two main people in this account?
Who were the two main people in this story?

Questions.Q: Who was Judah?
Questions.A: He was one of Jacob's sons. (He was the fourth son, born to Leah.) He was one of Joseph's brothers/half-brothers.

Questions.Q: And who was Tamar?
Questions.A: She was Judah's daughter-in-law. She married Judah's eldest son, Er. After Er died, she married his brother, Onan.

Questions.Q: Do you think that the author of Genesis approved of what Judah did after Onan died?
Questions.A: The text does not indicate whether or not the author approved of it, but he probably did not.

Questions.Q: What about Tamar's behavior in seducing Judah - do you think that the author of Genesis approved of that?
Questions.A: Again, the text does not indicate whether or not the author approved of it, but he probably did not.

Questions.Q: Approximately how much time do you think passed from the beginning of this story/account/chapter until/to the end?
Questions.A: Probably at least 20 years passed. (Judah (got) married and had three sons. And the sons grew to marriageable age.)
Questions.Alternative: Approximately how much time do you think passed from the beginning of this story until the end?
Approximately how much time do you think passed from the beginning of this story to the end?
Approximately how much time do you think passed from the beginning of this account until the end?
Approximately how much time do you think passed from the beginning of this account to the end?
Approximately how much time do you think passed from the beginning of this chapter until the end?
Approximately how much time do you think passed from the beginning of this chapter to the end?

Questions.Q: Soon after Joseph's brothers sold him to the traders, what did Judah do?
Questions.A: He left his family and went to a place called Adullam. (1)

Questions.Q: With whom did he stay there?
Questions.A: He stayed with a man named Hirah. (1)

Questions.Q: Tell me about Judah's wife.
Questions.A: She was a Canaanite. Her father's name was Shua. (2)

Questions.Q: Tell me about Judah's sons.
Questions.A: His firstborn was Er. His second son was Onan, and the third was Shelah. (3-5)

Questions.Q: When Shelah was born, where were Judah and his family living?
Questions.A: They were living at Kezib. (5)

Questions.Q: What do we know about Judah's firstborn son, Er?
Questions.A: [When he became a young man,] his father arranged for him to marry a girl named Tamar. But Er was very evil, so God took his life. (6-7)

Questions.Q: What was the name of Er's wife?
Questions.A: Her name was Tamar. (6)

Questions.Q: What was the cause for which God took Er's life/for which God caused Er to die?
Questions.A: God caused Er to die because Er was very wicked. (7)
Questions.Alternative: What was the cause for which God took Er's life?
What was the cause for which God caused Er to die?

Questions.Q: After Er died, what did Judah tell Onan to do?
Questions.A: He told Onan to take Tamar as his wife, and to have a child. The first child born to Onan and Tamar would be considered as Er's child. (8)

Questions.Q: Did Onan fully obey his father?
Questions.A: No. He did seem to take Tamar as his wife, but he would not let her conceive/make her pregnant. (9)

Questions.Q: What happened to Onan?
Questions.A: God took his life, too. (10)

Questions.Q: What was the cause for which God took Onan's life/for which God caused Onan to die?
Questions.A: God did that because Onan was not willing to have a child who would be considered as Er's child. (10)
Questions.Alternative: What was the cause for which God took Onan's life?
What was the cause for which God caused Onan to die?

Questions.Q: It was God's intention that Jacob and his sons have many descendants. Did Onan cooperate with the will of God?
Questions.A: No. He prevented Tamar from having any children. (9)
Questions.Alternative: It was God's intention that Jacob and his sons have many descendents. Did Onan cooperate with the will of God?

Questions.Q: After Onan died, what did Judah tell his daughter-in-law, Tamar?
Questions.A: He told her not to remarry at that time. He told her instead to return to her father's household and wait for Shelah to become a young man. (11)

Questions.Q: Did Judah truly intend for his third son, Shelah, to marry Tamar?
Questions.A: No. Judah was afraid that his son, Shelah, would also die. (11)

Questions.Q: What happened to Judah's wife?
Questions.A: She also died. (12)

Questions.Q: After Judah had mourned his wife, what did he do?
Questions.A: He and his friend Hirah went to a place called Timnah, where people were shearing sheep. (12)

Questions.Q: At that time, what did Tamar realize/conclude about Judah's plans for her and Shelah?
Questions.A: Tamar realized/concluded that Judah was not planning to marry her to Shelah. (14)
Questions.Alternative: At that time, what did Tamar realize about Judah's plans for her and Shelah?
At that time, what did Tamar conclude about Judah's plans for her and Shelah?

Questions.Q: So what did Tamar decide to do at that time?
Questions.A: When she heard that Judah was going to Timnah, she (got) dressed in different clothes, and a veil, so that Judah would not recognize her. Then she waited for him near the road to Timnah. (14)

Questions.Q: When Judah saw Tamar, what did he suppose?
Questions.A: He did not recognize her. He thought that she was a prostitute. (15)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Judah did not recognize her as his daughter-in-law?
Questions.A: He did not recognize her because she was wearing a veil. (15)

Questions.Q: What did Judah do when he saw her?
Questions.A: He asked her to have sexual relations/sex with him. (16)

Questions.Q: How did Tamar respond?
Questions.A: She asked Judah what he would give her in payment. (16)

Questions.Q: What did Judah offer to her?
Questions.A: Judah said that he would send her a young goat from his flock/herd. (17)

Questions.Q: And how did Tamar respond to Judah's offer?
Questions.A: She requested a down payment or a pledge. She said that Judah must (temporarily) leave, with her, his personal stamp/seal and its cord, as well as his staff. (18)

Questions.Q: Did Judah agree to her request?
Questions.A: Yes, he did. (18)

Questions.Q: [Some time later,] what did Tamar discover was the result of her union with Judah?
Questions.A: She discovered that she was pregnant. (18)
Questions.Alternative: Some time later, what did Tamar discover was the result of her union with Judah?
What did Tamar discover was the result of her union with Judah?
What was the result of Tamar's union with Judah?
what did Tamar discover was the result of her union with Judah?

Questions.Q: After Judah and Tamar were finished, what did Tamar do?
Questions.A: She returned home, removed her veil, and (got) dressed again in her widow clothes. (19)

Questions.Q: After Judah arrived at the place where his goats were, what did he do?
Questions.A: He sent his friend, Hirah, with a goat to pay Tamar and to redeem/get back his pledge (the stamp/seal and its cord, and his staff). (20)

Questions.Q: What happened when Hirah arrived at the place where Judah had met Tamar?
Questions.A: Hirah was not able to find Tamar. (20)

Questions.Q: Since Hirah could not find Tamar, what did he do?
Questions.A: He asked the people there what had happened to the temple/shrine prostitute who had been at that place before. (21)

Questions.Q: What was the answer of those people?
Questions.A: They said that there had never been a temple/shrine prostitute there. (21)

Questions.Q: When Hirah told Judah that he could not find the woman, what did Judah decide to do?
Questions.A: He decided to allow/let the woman keep the pledges. (23)

Questions.Q: For what reason did Judah not want to continue to search for the woman?
Questions.A: He was afraid that people would laugh at him/make fun of him. (23)

Questions.Q: Then, about three months later, what happened?
Questions.A: Judah heard that Tamar was pregnant as a result of being a prostitute. (24)

Questions.Q: When Judah heard that, what did he do?
Questions.A: He said that the people must put her to death (by burning her). (24)

Questions.Q: But what did Tamar do?
Questions.A: She sent Judah his pledges and said that the owner of those items was the one who had caused her to become pregnant. (25)

Questions.Q: So then what did Judah think?
Questions.A: He realized that he had done wrong to Tamar by not giving her his youngest son as her husband. (26)

Questions.Q: What do we know about Judah's relations with Tamar after that?
Questions.A: He did not sleep with her again. (26)

Questions.Q: When it was time for Tamar to give birth, what happened?
Questions.A: Tamar had twin boys. As they were being born, one put his hand out first, and a midwife tied a red thread around his wrist. But then he drew his hand back into her womb. Therefore the other twin was born first. (27-29)

Questions.Q: What were the twins named?
Questions.A: The firstborn was named Perez (which means something like "insist on getting out"). The other was named Zerah (which means "red" or "brightness"). (29-30)

Questions.Q: What happened to Joseph?
Questions.A: A man named Potiphar bought Joseph to work as a household slave. While Joseph was working there, Potiphar prospered. Potiphar realized that this was because God was blessing Joseph. So Potiphar promoted Joseph and eventually placed Joseph in charge of his entire household.

Questions.Q: Joseph was able to prosper/be very successful during this time. What was the cause of that?
Questions.A: God was with/caring for/watching over/helping Joseph.
Questions.Alternative: Joseph was able to prosper during this time. What was the cause of that?
Joseph was able to be very successful during this time. What was the cause of that?

Questions.Q: At that time, where was Joseph, and what was he doing?
Questions.A: Joseph was in Egypt at that time. He was living with and working for Potiphar. (1)

Questions.Q: What do we know about Potiphar?
Questions.A: He was the chief of the King's/Pharaoh's palace guards. (1)

Questions.Q: At the beginning of this section, what position did Joseph have in Potiphar's household?
Questions.A: Joseph was a slave. (1)

Questions.Q: What do you think it was like to be a slave?
Questions.A: A slave was required to do anything that the master ordered. A slave did not receive wages, and usually did not own anything. A slave could not decide for whom he/she would work.

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to say that God was with Joseph?
Questions.A: It means that God was watching over him, protecting him, caring for him. It means that God caused him to succeed in his work. It means that God had a plan for Joseph. (2-4)

Questions.Q: What did Potiphar notice that caused him to put Joseph in charge of his (Potiphar's) household?
Questions.A: Potiphar noticed that God was helping Joseph/caring for Joseph. (3-4)

Questions.Q: For what types of activities/work do you think that Joseph was responsible?
Questions.A: He was in charge of the household servants, and also all of Potiphar's property/business affairs. It/That work probably included some farming (income). (4-5)
Questions.Alternative: For what types of activities do you think that Joseph was responsible?
For what types of work do you think that Joseph was responsible?

Questions.Q: In what way was Potiphar affected by God helping Joseph/caring for Joseph?
Questions.A: God blessed Potiphar and caused everything of Potiphar's to prosper. (5)
Questions.Alternative: In what way was Potiphar affected by God helping Joseph?
In what way was Potiphar affected by God caring for Joseph?

Questions.Q: In your opinion, what do you think Joseph's character was like at that time?
Questions.A: He was trustworthy, he probably worked hard, and he was responsible/he could carry responsibility. (6)

Questions.Q: What was the only thing that Potiphar had to do for/attend to himself?
Questions.A: Potiphar had only to eat. (6)
Questions.Alternative: What was the only thing that Potiphar had to do for himself?
What was the only thing that Potiphar had to attend to himself?

Section.heading: Genesis 39:6b-20a Potiphar put Joseph in prison.

Questions.Q: Then what happened to Joseph?
Questions.A: Potiphar's wife was trying to persuade Joseph to sleep with her, but Joseph refused. On one occasion, Potiphar's wife told Potiphar that Joseph had tried to rape her. So Potiphar had Joseph put in jail.

Questions.Q: What do we know about Joseph's appearance?
Questions.A: He was handsome/attractive. (6b)

Questions.Q: When Potiphar's wife tried to persuade Joseph to sleep with her, what did Joseph say were the reasons why he did not want to do that?
Questions.A: He said that Potiphar had given him control over almost everything. That meant that Potiphar trusted Joseph to do what was right. Therefore, if Joseph was to sleep with Potiphar's wife, Joseph would be betraying his master. (8-9)

Questions.Q: If Joseph was to sleep with Potiphar's wife, whom else, besides Potiphar, would Joseph be betraying?
Questions.A: He would also betray God. (9)

Questions.Q: When Joseph said that, did Potiphar's wife leave him alone?
Questions.A: No, she continued to try to persuade him to sleep with her. (10)

Questions.Q: And what did Joseph do then?
Questions.A: He tried to avoid her. (10)

Questions.Q: In what kind of situation was Joseph one day, when Potiphar's wife tried to persuade him to sleep with her?
Questions.A: He was working alone in the house (of Potiphar). (11)

Questions.Q: By what means was Potiphar's wife able to get/grab Joseph's robe?
Questions.A: She grabbed Joseph, and when he ran away, she was still holding (onto) his robe. (12)
Questions.Alternative: By what means was Potiphar's wife able to get Joseph's robe?
By what means was Potiphar's wife able to grab Joseph's robe?

Questions.Q: After Joseph ran away, what did Potiphar's wife do?
Questions.A: She yelled/called (out) for the other men servants. When they came to her, she said that Joseph had tried to rape her. (13-15)

Questions.Q: What did she say about Joseph's robe?
Questions.A: She said that when she began to cry/scream, he ran away, leaving it behind. (15)

Questions.Q: What did Potiphar's wife do next?
Questions.A: She waited until Potiphar came home, and then she told him the same story. (16-17)

Questions.Q: Did Potiphar's wife suggest that Potiphar himself was partly to blame?
Questions.A: Yes, she pointed out that Potiphar was the one who brought Joseph into their house. (17)

Questions.Q: What was Potiphar's response?
Questions.A: He was very angry. (19)

Questions.Q: What did Potiphar do to Joseph?
Questions.A: He had Joseph imprisoned. (20)

Questions.Q: In what jail did he have Joseph imprisoned?
Questions.A: He had Joseph imprisoned in the jail for those who did wrong against the King. (20)

Questions.Q: Tell what happened while Joseph was in prison.
Questions.A: God watched over Joseph there, also. The chief jailer thought well of Joseph and put Joseph in charge/and made Joseph a leader. And everything went well in the prison.

Questions.Q: In what way was Joseph's experience in prison similar to his experience in Potiphar's household?
Questions.A: In both situations, the person in charge appreciated Joseph, and gave Joseph more and more responsibility. Also, in both situations God gave Joseph success in everything he did.

Questions.Q: Although Joseph had done only good, Potiphar put him in jail. Did that mean that God had forgotten about Joseph and was no longer caring for him/watching over him/helping him?
Questions.A: No, God continued to love Joseph, and was always with him/helping him. (21, 23)
Questions.Alternative: Although Joseph had done only good, Potiphar put him in jail. Did that mean that God had forgotten about Joseph and was no longer caring for him?
Although Joseph had done only good, Potiphar put him in jail. Did that mean that God had forgotten about Joseph and was no longer watching over him?
Although Joseph had done only good, Potiphar put him in jail. Did that mean that God had forgotten about Joseph and was no longer helping him?

Questions.Q: Who now began to trust Joseph?
Questions.A: The chief jailer/chief prison guard began to trust Joseph. (21-22)

Questions.Q: What responsibility did the chief jailer give to Joseph?
Questions.A: The chief jailer made Joseph responsible for (taking care of) all the other prisoners. (22)

Questions.Q: Do you remember what Joseph seemed to be like before, when he was living (with his family) in Canaan? In what ways do you think his character might have changed from that time?
Questions.A: Joseph does not seem to be proud now. He has become an obedient, trustworthy worker who has grown to know and trust God. (22-23)

Questions.Q: If, for example, we experience serious problems or "misfortune" - does that mean that God has forgotten us?
Questions.A: No. We can learn from this story/account that even when we experience serious problems, God is still caring for/watching over us. (23)

Section.heading: Genesis 40:1-23 Joseph interpreted the dreams of prisoners.

Questions.Q: Tell what Joseph was able to do in prison on this occasion.
Questions.A: Pharaoh had imprisoned two of his servants in the same jail where Joseph was. While they were there, one night each of those servants had a special dream. They were upset because they did not know what their dreams meant. But when they told their dreams to Joseph, he told them the meanings of the dreams. He said that Pharaoh would release one of them from prison in three days, but that Pharaoh would execute the other one in three days. And that is (exactly) what happened. But the one whom Pharaoh released from prison forgot all about Joseph.

Questions.Q: Whom did Pharaoh put in prison with Joseph?
Questions.A: He imprisoned his chief drink-server/cup-bearer/the leader of his drink-servers, and his chief baker/the leader of his bakers. (1-2)

Questions.Q: Where did he imprison them?
Questions.A: He put them in the house of the captain/leader of those who guarded Pharaoh. (3)

Questions.Q: Who took care of the two new prisoners?
Questions.A: Joseph took care of them. (4)

Questions.Q: One morning, the two prisoners looked different than usual. What was their appearance?
Questions.A: They looked worried/upset. (6)

Questions.Q: What was the reason that the two prisoners appeared worried/upset?
Questions.A: During the night, each of them had had a dream. They knew that their dreams had meaning, but there was nobody to explain the meaning of their dreams. (5)
Questions.Alternative: What was the reason that the two prisoners appeared worried?
What was the reason that the two prisoners appeared upset?

Questions.Q: When Joseph saw that the two prisoners looked worried/upset, what did he do?
Questions.A: He asked them why they were worried/upset. (7)
Questions.Alternative: When Joseph saw that the two prisoners looked worried, what did he do?
When Joseph saw that the two prisoners looked upset, what did he do?

Questions.Q: And when they told Joseph the reason that they were worried, what did he say to them?
Questions.A: He told them to tell him (about) their dreams. (8)

Questions.Q: According to Joseph, who knows how to interpret dreams/explain the meaning of dreams?
Questions.A: Only God can interpret dreams. (8)
Questions.Alternative: According to Joseph, who knows how to interpret dreams?
According to Joseph, who knows how to explain the meaning of dreams?

Questions.Q: Tell me about the dream of the chief drink-server/cup-bearer/the leader of Pharaoh's drink-servers.
Questions.A: The chief drink-server saw a grape vine with three branches in his dream. The branches grew buds which opened into flowers, which grew into ripe grapes. He was holding Pharaoh's cup, and he squeezed some grape juice into the cup for him (Pharaoh) to drink. Then he gave it to Pharaoh. (9-11)
Questions.Alternative: Tell me about the dream of the chief drink-server.
Tell me about the dream of the chief cup-bearer.
Tell me about the dream of the cup-bearer.
Tell me about the dream of the leader of Pharaoh's drink-servers.

Questions.Q: According to Joseph, what was the meaning of that dream?
Questions.A: The three branches represented a time period of three days. After three days, Pharaoh would release the drink-server from prison, and the man would resume his work of leading those who served Pharaoh's drinks. (12-13)

Questions.Q: What request did Joseph ask of the drink-server?
Questions.A: Joseph requested that he ask Pharaoh to release him (Joseph) from jail. (14)

Questions.Q: According to Joseph, why was it right that someone release him from jail?
Questions.A: Joseph said that someone had unfairly/unjustly stolen/brought him from his own land, and then someone (else) had unfairly/unjustly put him in prison. (15)

Questions.Q: What did the chief baker/the leader of Pharaoh's bakers think about the dream of the chief drink-server/cup-bearer?
Questions.A: He thought that the meaning/interpretation of the dream of the chief drink-server was a good/favorable one. (16)
Questions.Alternative: What did the chief baker think about the dream of the chief drink-server?
What did the chief baker think about the dream of the chief cup-bearer?
What did the leader of Pharaoh's bakers think about the dream of the chief drink-server?
What did the leader of Pharaoh's bakers think about the dream of the chief cup-bearer?

Questions.Q: So what did the chief baker do (at that time)?
Questions.A: He (also) told his dream to Joseph. (16)

Questions.Q: Tell me about the dream of the chief baker/the leader of Pharaoh's bakers.
Questions.A: In his dream the chief baker saw three (flat) baskets of bread/cakes/pastries on top of his own head. (Apparently, the baskets were piled on top of each other.) Then he saw birds pecking/eating the breads/cakes from the top/uppermost basket which contained Pharaoh's (favorite) baked goods. (16-17)
Questions.Alternative: Tell me about the dream of the chief baker.
Tell me about the dream of the leader of Pharaoh's bakers.

Questions.Q: What did Joseph tell him was the meaning of that dream?
Questions.A: He said that the three baskets represented three days, after which Pharaoh/someone would take the baker from prison and cut off his (the baker's) head. And Pharaoh would have someone impale the baker on a post. Then birds would come and peck at the corpse of the baker. (18-19)

Questions.Q: After 3 days, what occasion occurred?
Questions.A: It was Pharaoh's birthday. (20)

Questions.Q: What did Pharaoh do to celebrate?
Questions.A: He held a feast/banquet for his officials/servants. (20)

Questions.Q: What else did he do at that time?
Questions.A: He had the chief drink-server/cup-bearer and the chief baker brought out from the jail. (20)

Questions.Q: What happened to the chief drink-server/cup-bearer?
Questions.A: Pharaoh restored him to his previous position. (21)
Questions.Alternative: What happened to the chief drink-server?
What happened to the chief cup-bearer?

Questions.Q: And what happened to the baker?
Questions.A: Pharaoh had him hanged/impaled on a pole. (22)

Questions.Q: God had enabled Joseph to interpret the dreams of his two fellow prisoners. What was the outcome of Joseph telling the meanings of the dreams?
Questions.A: The events happened in the way that Joseph had said they would. But then the chief drink-server/cup-bearer forgot to say anything to Pharaoh about Joseph. (23)

Section.heading: Genesis 41:1-36 Joseph interpreted the dreams of Pharaoh.

Questions.Q: At the beginning of this account, how much time had passed since Joseph interpreted the dreams of the two prisoners?
Questions.A: Two years had passed. (1)

Questions.Q: What was causing Pharaoh to be very upset?
Questions.A: He had had two dreams one night, and he was sure that they had a meaning, but he did not know what their meaning was. And none of his wise men could tell him the meaning.

Questions.Q: How was Pharaoh finally able to learn the meaning of his dreams?
Questions.A: He had Joseph brought to him, and Joseph told him the meaning.

Questions.Q: How many dreams did Pharaoh have, and how many nights did he dream?
Questions.A: He had two dreams, both in the same night. (1, 4-5, 8)

Questions.Q: Tell me about Pharaoh's first dream.
Questions.A: In his dream, he was standing near the Nile River. There he saw seven fat and healthy cows come from the river. And then seven different cows appeared - but they were all very thin and ugly. (At first) they stood near the fat cows. Then (suddenly) the thin cows ate the fat cows. (2-4)

Questions.Q: What happened to Pharaoh immediately after the first dream?
Questions.A: He woke up. (4)

Questions.Q: Tell me about Pharaoh's second dream.
Questions.A: In his second dream, he saw a stalk of grain with seven fat, healthy heads/clusters. Then on the same stalk he saw another seven heads/clusters, but they were thin and very unhealthy/withered. And then the thin ones ate the fat ones. (5-7)

Questions.Q: The seven heads/clusters that were thin and unhealthy - what do you think they looked like, and why were they like that?
Questions.A: They were thin, dry, empty/useless; the sun and/or hot wind had scorched them. (6)
Questions.Alternative: The seven heads that were thin and unhealthy - what do you think they looked like, and why were they like that?
The seven clusters that were thin and unhealthy - what do you think they looked like, and why were they like that?

Questions.Q: How did Pharaoh feel when he awoke?
Questions.A: He was worried about the dreams and wanted to know what they meant. (8)

Questions.Q: Whom did Pharaoh summon to interpret his dreams?
Questions.A: He summoned his magicians/priests and wise men. (8)
Questions.Alternative: Whom did Pharaoh call to interpret his dreams?
Whom did Pharaoh call to interpret his visions?
Whom did Pharaoh call to ask about the meaning of his dreams?

Questions.Q: What did Pharaoh's magicians/priests and wise men tell him about the meaning of his dreams?
Questions.A: They were unable to tell him the meaning. (8)
Questions.Alternative: What did Pharaoh's magicians and wise men tell him about the meaning of his dreams?
What did Pharaoh's priests and wise men tell him about the meaning of his dreams?

Questions.Q: What did Pharaoh's chief drink-server/cup-bearer do at that time?
Questions.A: He remembered Joseph and told Pharaoh about him. (9-13)
Questions.Alternative: What did Pharaoh's chief drink-server do at that time?
What did Pharaoh's chief cup-bearer do at that time?

Questions.Q: When the drink-server/cup-bearer said that he remembered his sins/failure/wrong, to what do you think he was referring?
Questions.A: He might have been referring to what he had done which resulted in Pharaoh putting him in prison. Or he might have been thinking of Joseph's request to tell Pharaoh about him (Joseph). Or he might have been thinking about both of those events. (9)
Questions.Alternative: When the drink-server said that he remembered his sins, to what do you think he was referring?
When the drink-server said that he remembered his failure, to what do you think he was referring?
When the drink-server said that he remembered his wrong, to what do you think he was referring?
When the cup-bearer said that he remembered his sins, to what do you think he was referring?
When the cup-bearer said that he remembered his failure, to what do you think he was referring?
When the cup-bearer said that he remembered his wrong, to what do you think he was referring?

Questions.Q: Tell me about what the drink-server/cup-bearer said to Pharaoh at this time.
Questions.A: He said that Pharaoh had put him in prison, along with the chief baker. And that one night, each of them had had a dream. A young Hebrew man who was in prison with them was able to tell them the meaning of their dreams. And everything had happened exactly as the young Hebrew man had said they would. (10-13)
Questions.Alternative: Tell me about what the drink-server said to Pharaoh at this time.
Tell me about what the cup-bearer said to Pharaoh at this time.

Questions.Q: What did Pharaoh do next?
Questions.A: He sent for Joseph. // He had Joseph brought from the prison. (14)

Questions.Q: What did Joseph have to do before he appeared before Pharaoh?
Questions.A: He had to shave (his face, and probably cut his hair), and dress in acceptable clothes. (14)

Questions.Q: When Pharaoh asked Joseph to tell him the meaning of his dreams, what was Joseph's first response?
Questions.A: He said that he was not able to interpret dreams himself, but that God could reveal the meaning. (16)

Questions.Q: What does this suggest about Joseph's character?
Questions.A: It shows that he trusted (in) God, and that he was humble. He did not want anyone to think that he (Joseph) had powers or abilities which he did not truly have in himself.

Questions.Q: What did Pharaoh say about the thin cows when he first saw them in his dream?
Questions.A: He said that they were thin and very ugly - that he had never seen such ugly cows in all of Egypt. (19)

Questions.Q: And after the thin cows had eaten the fat ones, how did they appear?
Questions.A: They were still thin and ugly - as though they had not eaten anything. (21)

Questions.Q: According to Joseph, what was the purpose of Pharaoh's two dreams?
Questions.A: God was showing [to] Pharaoh what he (God) would do. (25)

Questions.Q: What was the meaning of the seven fat cows and seven plump heads of grain in the dreams?
Questions.A: They represented seven years of abundance/prosperity, with very good crops. (26)

Questions.Q: What was the meaning of the seven thin cows and the seven thin/empty heads of grain?
Questions.A: They represented seven years of famine. (27)
Questions.Alternative: What was the meaning of the seven thin cows and the seven thin heads of grain?
What was the meaning of the seven thin cows and the seven empty heads of grain?

Questions.Q: Since Pharaoh had two dreams, did that mean that there would be two times of abundance, and that there would also be two times of famine?
Questions.A: No, both of the dreams referred to (the) one time of abundance followed by (the) one seven-year famine. (25-26)

Questions.Q: What did Joseph say about how serious the famine would be?
Questions.A: He said that the famine would be so severe that people would forget about the seven years of abundance. (30-31)
Questions.Alternative: What did Joseph say about how severe the famine would be?
What did Joseph say about the severity of the famine?

Questions.Q: (Then) what is the significance of Pharaoh having two dreams (rather than only one dream)?
Questions.A: God was showing that it would truly happen and that it would be soon. (32)
Questions.Alternative: Then what is the significance of Pharaoh having two dreams rather than only one dream?
What is the significance of Pharaoh having two dreams rather than only one dream?
Then what is the significance of Pharaoh having two dreams?
What is the significance of Pharaoh having two dreams?

Questions.Q: Was God revealing things about which he (God) knew, but over which he had no control? Or did God have control over those times of abundance and times of famine?
Questions.A: God not only knew about what would happen, but he also had control over all the events/happenings. (25, 28, 32)

Questions.Q: Do you remember when Joseph dreamt while he was a boy in Canaan? Can you see anything similar between Joseph's experience then and Pharaoh's experience at this time?
Questions.A: With Joseph and (also) with Pharaoh, there were two dreams, and both times the two dreams had the same meaning.

Questions.Q: What did Joseph advise Pharaoh?
Questions.A: He advised Pharaoh to choose a wise/discerning man to administer many others who would gather grain during the good years and store it to be used during the time of famine. (33-35)

Questions.Q: How much grain did Pharaoh's officials need to gather during the years of abundance?
Questions.A: They needed to gather one-fifth of the harvest (each year) (to store away for the time of famine). (34)

Questions.Q: According to Joseph, what would happen if food was not stored away during the years of abundance?
Questions.A: The people would starve. They would die from lack of food. (36)

Questions.Q: In your opinion, by what means do you think that Joseph had become knowledgeable about planning or preparing?
Questions.A: Probably he had learned that while he was in charge of Potiphar's household, and then later as the one in charge at the prison.

Section.heading: Genesis 41:37-57 Joseph ruled wisely in times of prosperity.

Questions.Q: After Joseph told Pharaoh the meaning of the dreams, what happened to Joseph?
Questions.A: Pharaoh made him the most senior official in Egypt, second only to (Pharaoh) himself.

Questions.Q: What were Joseph's responsibilities as the most senior official in Egypt?
Questions.A: He was to supervise the collection of surplus grain during the seven years of abundance, and then supervise its distribution during the famine.

Questions.Q: What did Pharaoh and his officials think of Joseph's suggestion?
Questions.A: They thought it was a good idea. (37)

Questions.Q: Whom did they choose to lead/administer the program?
Questions.A: They chose Joseph. (38-40)
Questions.Alternative: Whom did they choose to lead the program?
Whom did they choose to administer the program?

Questions.Q: According to Pharaoh, what was special about Joseph?
Questions.A: God's spirit was with/in Joseph, giving him wisdom and discernment. (38-39)

Key Term Check: Joseph had earlier stated that only God was able to interpret the meaning of dreams. When Joseph explained the meaning of Pharaoh's dreams, Pharaoh concluded that God must have given Joseph special understanding. Frequently in the Old Testament, when someone demonstrated special abilities that come from God, people said that they had God's spirit.
Questions.Note: See "spirit" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What caused Pharaoh to conclude that God's spirit was with/in Joseph?
Questions.A: God had showed/revealed to Joseph the meaning of Pharaoh's dreams. (39)
Questions.Alternative: What caused Pharaoh to conclude that God's spirit was with Joseph?
What caused Pharaoh to conclude that God's spirit was in Joseph?

Questions.Q: Tell me about Joseph's position in the government of Egypt - how high was his rank/position?
Questions.A: His position was above (the position of) everyone except Pharaoh himself. (40-44)
Questions.Alternative: Tell me about Joseph's position in the government of Egypt. How high was his rank?
Tell me about Joseph's position in the government of Egypt - how high was his rank?
Tell me about Joseph's position in the government of Egypt. How high was his position?
Tell me about Joseph's position in the government of Egypt - how high was his position?

Questions.Q: What did Pharaoh do to demonstrate that he had given so much authority to Joseph?
Questions.A: Pharaoh placed a special ring on Joseph's finger. And he gave Joseph special clothing, and a gold chain necklace. (42)

Questions.Q: What else did Pharaoh give to Joseph so that Joseph could travel and conduct his work?
Questions.A: Pharaoh had a special chariot/cart which he reserved for the one closest in power/authority to himself. He gave Joseph a very special chariot/cart. (43)

Questions.Q: When someone drove that special chariot/cart, what happened?
Questions.A: Someone announced that an important official was coming (and told people to make room for the chariot/cart to pass by). (43)
Questions.Alternative: When someone drove that special chariot, what happened?
When someone drove that special cart, what happened?

Questions.Q: What did Pharaoh mean when he said that no one would move a hand or a foot in the entire land of Egypt without Joseph's approval? Does this mean (literally) that every person must request permission from Joseph to even move a hand or foot?
Questions.A: No, it is an expression that emphasized that Pharaoh had given to Joseph power or authority above everyone else in Egypt (except for Pharaoh). (44)

Questions.Q: What else did Pharaoh change in Joseph's life?
Questions.A: He gave him an Egyptian name, and he arranged his marriage. (45)

Questions.Q: Who became Joseph's wife?
Questions.A: Asenath, the daughter of the priest of On, became Joseph's wife. (45)

Questions.Q: How old was Joseph when Pharaoh made him the chief ruler (under Pharaoh) in Egypt?
Questions.A: Joseph was 30 years old. (46)

Questions.Q: For a long period of time, Joseph was a slave or in jail. How many years had passed since his brothers had sold him to the traders?
Questions.A: It had been 13 years. (Joseph was 17 years old (Genesis 37:2), when Jacob had sent him to check on his older brothers.)

Questions.Q: From this story about Joseph, what lessons can we see about why God sometimes causes people to experience difficulty?
Questions.A: God uses suffering to test us and to change us. He is always in control of the circumstances that affect us, even though sometimes it may not appear as though God is in control.

Questions.Q: As soon as Joseph left Pharaoh's palace, what did he do?
Questions.A: He traveled throughout the land of Egypt (probably in order to become familiar with the country and its resources). (46)

Questions.Q: What were the crops like during the first seven years that Joseph was in charge?
Questions.A: The crops produced exceptionally well. They produced much more grain than they did in normal years. (47)

Questions.Q: What did Joseph do during those first seven years?
Questions.A: When the people harvested grain, he had a portion of the grain stored in barns/granaries/warehouses in each town/city. (48)

Questions.Q: Where did they store the grain?
Questions.A: They stored it in barns/granaries/warehouses in each town/city near where it grew. (48)

Questions.Q: How much grain were they able to store?
Questions.A: They had so much that it filled all the storage places (until they overflowed) - so much that they could not account for all of it. (49)

Questions.Q: What else happened during those years of abundant crops?
Questions.A: Joseph and his wife had two sons. (50)

Questions.Q: What were the names of Joseph's sons?
Questions.A: They were Manasseh and Ephraim. (51-52)

Questions.Q: As we consider the name which Joseph gave to his eldest son, Manasseh, what can we conclude about Joseph's attitudes/feelings (about his past experiences)?
Questions.A: God had helped Joseph not to feel angry or bitter regarding his brothers and his hard experiences. (51)
Questions.Alternative: As we consider the name which Joseph gave to his eldest son, Manasseh, what can we conclude about Joseph's attitudes (about his past experiences)?
As we consider the name which Joseph gave to his eldest son, Manasseh, what can we conclude about Joseph's feelings (about his past experiences)?

Questions.Q: If someone wrongs us, do you think that we should remember what they did and take revenge, or should we forgive and forget the wrong that they did against us?
Questions.A: We should follow Joseph's example and forgive/forget.

Questions.Q: What was the reason why Joseph named his second son "Ephraim"?
Questions.A: He gave him that name because it means "fruitful". And (just as a tree begins with nothing but later has fruit, so) Joseph began with nothing when he came to Egypt, but later he had achieved a high position of responsibility, and had a wife, and two sons. (52)

Questions.Q: After the seven years of abundant harvests in Egypt, what happened?
Questions.A: There was a famine. The farmers/people were not able to grow any food. (53)

Questions.Q: Where was the famine?
Questions.A: The famine was throughout Egypt and also the surrounding lands. (54, 57)

Questions.Q: What were people beginning to experience?
Questions.A: They were beginning to starve. // They were experiencing severe hunger. (55)

Questions.Q: What did the people do when they began to experience severe hunger?
Questions.A: They went to Pharaoh to get/obtain food. (55)

Questions.Q: And what did Pharaoh tell them to do?
Questions.A: He told them to go to Joseph and to do whatever Joseph said (they were to do). (55)

Questions.Q: Did Joseph give away the stored grain free of charge?
Questions.A: No, the people had to buy the grain from what he had stored in the barns.

Questions.Q: What did the people who had no food in the lands surrounding Egypt do?
Questions.A: They went to Egypt to buy grain. (57)

Section.heading: Genesis 42:1-24 Joseph's brothers traveled to Egypt.

Questions.Q: Tell what happened with Joseph's family/Joseph's father and brothers during the time of famine.
Questions.A: They, too, had no food in Canaan because of the famine, so all of Joseph's brothers, except (for) Benjamin, went to Egypt to buy food. When they arrived, they had to go to Joseph to buy/get grain. They did not recognize him, but he recognized them. He accused the brothers of being foreign spies. They insisted that they were not spies, but rather were brothers who were in need of food. They mentioned that their father and youngest brother were still back in Canaan. Joseph told them that he would not believe them unless they brought their youngest brother to him. So he kept Simeon in jail, and sent the other nine brothers home to get/bring back Benjamin. When they arrived home, they found that the money that was to have been payment for the grain was in their grain sacks. They told Jacob about all that had happened. Jacob was very upset that now he had lost Simeon too (in addition to Joseph). So he said that he would not allow his nine sons/the brothers to take Benjamin back with them to Egypt, because he feared that Benjamin, too, would not return.
Questions.Alternative: Tell what happened with Joseph's family during the time of famine.
Tell what happened with Joseph's father and brothers during the time of famine.

Questions.Q: Who went to Egypt?
Questions.A: Joseph's ten older brothers went to Egypt. (3)

Questions.Q: For what purpose did they go to Egypt?
Questions.A: There was famine in Canaan, but there was food in Egypt. Jacob's family had little or no food to eat, so Jacob sent ten of his sons to Egypt in order to buy food. (1-3)

Questions.Q: According to Jacob, what would happen to their family, if his sons did not go to Egypt to buy food?
Questions.A: They would starve (to death). (2)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Benjamin did not accompany his brothers?
Questions.A: He stayed with his father, because (Jacob thought that) he was the only child of Rachel who was still living, and Jacob feared that something bad/harmful might happen to him. (4)

Questions.Q: Were other foreigners also going to Egypt in order to buy food?
Questions.A: Yes, other foreigners were going to Egypt, because the famine had spread beyond Egypt. (5)

Questions.Q: What was Joseph's government/political position at that time?
Questions.A: He was governor/master/ruler in Egypt. Only Pharaoh had more power/authority than Joseph.
Questions.Alternative: What was Joseph's government position at that time?
What was Joseph's political position at that time?

Questions.Q: What were the circumstances which caused Joseph's brothers to go to see Joseph himself?
Questions.A: They happened to go to Joseph because he was responsible for selling grain. (6)

Questions.Q: When Joseph and his brothers met, what did his brothers do?
Questions.A: The brothers bowed to the ground in front of Joseph. (6)

Questions.Q: What did Joseph do at that time?
Questions.A: He recognized his brothers, but he pretended that he did not recognize them. And he questioned them roughly concerning where they had come from. (7)

Questions.Q: What do you think prevented Joseph's brothers from recognizing him?
Questions.A: At that time, Joseph was 30 years old, and they had not seen him since he was 17 years old. Also, he was wearing Egyptian clothes, and was using his Egyptian name, and he was a very high official. (41:14, 42, 45-46; 42:8)

Questions.Q: What do you think might have caused Joseph to remember what he had dreamt so many years ago?
Questions.A: Perhaps it was because his brothers bowed to him. (6, 9)

Questions.Q: What did Joseph say was his brothers' purpose in coming to Egypt?
Questions.A: He said that they were spies, that they wanted to see if it would be easy to conquer the land of Egypt. (9)

Questions.Q: Do you think that Joseph truly supposed that those men were spies?
Questions.A: No, he did not. (He was probably testing them.)

Questions.Q: When Joseph said that they were spies, how did they respond?
Questions.A: They said that they had come only to buy food, and that they were honest/truthful men. They added that they were all brothers, and were not spies. (10-11)

Questions.Q: What did Joseph reply?
Questions.A: He repeated his earlier claim that the men had come to see if it would be easy to conquer the land of Egypt. (12)

Questions.Q: So what did the brothers say then?
Questions.A: They explained that they were all the sons of one father, and that their father and one younger brother were still living in Canaan. (13)

Questions.Q: Who was the younger brother whom they mentioned?
Questions.A: That was Benjamin. (13)

Questions.Q: Did the brothers say anything about their brother, Joseph?
Questions.A: Yes, they said that he was no longer with them/he was lost/he had died. (13)

Questions.Q: At that time, what did Joseph demand that his brothers do in order to prove that what they said was really true?
Questions.A: Joseph said that one of the men must go home and then bring back their younger brother to him. Meanwhile, the other brothers must stay in jail in Egypt. (15)

Questions.Q: According to Joseph, if the youngest brother does not come to him (Joseph) in Egypt, what would Joseph conclude about all the brothers?
Questions.A: He said that he would know that the men were spies. (16)

Questions.Q: It seems as though Joseph did not trust his brothers. What was the reason that this might be the case?
Questions.A: His brothers had sold him as a slave, and had then lied about it to their father.

Questions.Q: How many days were the brothers in prison?
Questions.A: They were in prison for three days. (17)

Questions.Q: In your opinion, how do you think the brothers felt while they were in prison?
Questions.A: They were probably very afraid. Perhaps they considered that what was happening now was punishment/retribution for the cruel way that they had treated Joseph many years ago.
Questions.Note: See verse 21.

Questions.Q: After the brothers had been in prison for 3 days, what happened?
Questions.A: Joseph went to them and told them that instead of sending one brother home to get/to bring back the youngest brother, he (Joseph) would keep only one brother in prison. All the others could return home. (19)

Questions.Q: What did Joseph say was the reason why he showed mercy to them in that way?
Questions.A: He said that he feared/respected God. (18)

Questions.Q: If someone fears/respects God, would you expect them to show mercy to other people?
Questions.A: Yes.
Questions.Alternative: If someone fears God, would you expect them to show mercy to other people?
If someone respects God, would you expect them to show mercy to other people?

Questions.Q: What did Joseph tell the brothers to do at this time?
Questions.A: They were to take food back (to Canaan), and then they were to return to Egypt bringing their youngest brother. (19, 20)

Questions.Q: What did Joseph say that he would do if the brothers brought back their youngest brother to Egypt?
Questions.A: Joseph told them that he would free the one brother (Simeon); he said that he would not execute them as spies. (20)

Questions.Q: What did the brothers say about why they were experiencing those problems/difficulties?
Questions.A: They said that the problems/difficulties were payment/retribution/penalty for having been cruel to Joseph (many years ago). (21)
Questions.Alternative: What did the brothers say about why they were experiencing those problems?
What did the brothers say about why they were experiencing those difficulties?

Questions.Q: During that time, years ago, when they had put their brother Joseph in the pit/cistern, and then sold him to the traders, what reaction had they seen and heard from Joseph?
Questions.A: They had seen him terrified, and had heard him pleading for mercy. (21)
Questions.Alternative: During that time, years ago, when they had put their brother Joseph in the pit, and then sold him to the traders, what reaction had they seen and heard from Joseph?
During that time, years ago, when they had put their brother Joseph in the cistern, and then sold him to the traders, what reaction had they seen and heard from Joseph?

Questions.Q: And when they had seen and heard how he had reacted, what had they done?
Questions.A: They had still mistreated him. They ignored Joseph's cries for mercy and still sold him. (21)

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that the brothers still remembered something that they did so long ago?
Questions.A: It is often difficult to forget sins. When we sin, there are consequences, and God will judge and punish those who have been cruel to others. (21-22)

Questions.Q: So years later, as the brothers were in Egypt, what did Reuben say to the rest of his brothers?
Questions.A: He scolded/rebuked his brothers because they had not followed his advice/warnings years ago. (22)

Questions.Q: According to Reuben, what would happen to the ten brothers?
Questions.A: He said that they would suffer retribution/revenge for having mistreated Joseph. (22)

Questions.Q: Did Joseph understand what his brothers were saying?
Questions.A: Yes, Joseph could still understand the language that his family spoke. (23)

Questions.Q: Did the brothers realize that Joseph was able to understand them?
Questions.A: No, they did not realize that. (23)

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason the brothers supposed that Joseph did not understand what they were saying?
Questions.A: They supposed that Joseph was an Egyptian who did not know their language. When Joseph had communicated with his brothers, he had done so through an interpreter. (23)

Questions.Q: As Joseph heard the brothers express their regret for what they had done to him years ago, how did Joseph feel?
Questions.A: He was very upset. He went into another room and cried. (24)

Questions.Q: What did Joseph do next?
Questions.A: He returned to his brothers and spoke some more with them. Then he had someone tie up Simeon while the other brothers watched. (24)

Questions.Q: What would happen to Simeon? For what purpose did Joseph have him tied up?
Questions.A: Simeon would have to stay in prison while his brothers return to Canaan (to get Benjamin). (24)

Section.heading: Genesis 42:25-38 Joseph's brothers returned to Canaan.
