Questions.Q: What happened as the brothers traveled back home to Canaan?
Questions.A: On the way, one of them found that the money that he had used to buy grain was still inside his grain sack (on top of the grain). They arrived home and told Jacob about what had happened in Egypt. Then they found that the payment money was in all of their grain sacks. They did not understand what was happening and they were terrified. Meanwhile, Jacob was terribly upset because he had not only lost Joseph, but now it appeared that he had also lost Simeon. So he was not willing to risk sending Benjamin to Egypt.

Questions.Q: What did Joseph do for his brothers as they prepared to return home to Canaan?
Questions.A: Joseph had his servants fill the brothers' grain sacks, and he also gave them provisions for their journey. (25)

Questions.Q: What did Joseph tell his servants to do with the money that the brothers had brought as payment for the grain?
Questions.A: He told the servants to return the money to the brothers. The servants were to put the money inside the grain sacks, on top of the grain. (25)

Questions.Q: Did the brothers know that Joseph had instructed that their payment money be put in the grain sacks?
Questions.A: No, the brothers did not know about that. (28, 35)

Questions.Q: How did Joseph's brothers transport their wheat home?
Questions.A: They loaded it onto donkeys that they had brought from Canaan. (26)

Questions.Q: Did they journey directly home in one day, or did they have to stop and rest on the way?
Questions.A: They had to stop at nighttime. (27)

Questions.Q: When they stopped to rest, what did one of the brothers discover?
Questions.A: One of them found that the money that he had used to pay for the grain was in his grain sack. (27-28)

Questions.Q: What was the reason that he had opened his grain sack while they were still on their journey?
Questions.A: He had opened his sack to get some grain to feed the donkeys. (27)

Questions.Q: How did the brothers feel, when he discovered the money in his grain sack?
Questions.A: They were very scared/upset. (28)

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason why they were so scared/upset?
Questions.A: Maybe they thought that someone would accuse them of taking the grain without paying for it. They supposed that they might experience more trouble, and that this was payment/retribution from God. (28)
Questions.Alternative: What do you think was the reason why they were so scared?
What do you think was the reason why they were so upset?

Questions.Q: What did they do when they arrived (at) home?
Questions.A: They told their father, Jacob, about all that had happened. They said that the man in charge in Egypt had spoken roughly to them, and had accused them of being spies. When they said that they were not spies but were all brothers, then the man said that one of them had to stay behind in Egypt. He told them that the others were to take grain home, and then bring back their youngest brother, to prove that they were telling the truth. (30-34)

Questions.Q: Then, when they unloaded their grain sacks, what did they find?
Questions.A: They found that all of their money was still there. It was inside their sacks, on top of the grain. (35)

Questions.Q: When they saw all their money, how did they feel?
Questions.A: They were terrified. (35)

Questions.Q: What did Jacob say at that time?
Questions.A: He said that his sons had caused him (Jacob) to lose Joseph, and now also Simeon. And he did not want them to take Benjamin and lose him, also. Jacob said that everything was going wrong for him. (36)

Questions.Q: Who promised to be responsible for/take care of Benjamin?
Questions.A: Reuben said that he would be responsible for Benjamin. (37)
Questions.Alternative: Who promised to be responsible for Benjamin?
Who promised to take care of Benjamin?

Questions.Q: What did Reuben say to his father, as a guarantee that he (Reuben) would truly watch out for/protect Benjamin?
Questions.A: Reuben said that, if he did not return Benjamin to Jacob, then Jacob could take the lives of Reuben's two children in exchange for Benjamin. (37)
Questions.Alternative: What did Reuben say to his father, as a guarantee that he (Reuben) would truly watch out for Benjamin?
What did Reuben say to his father, as a guarantee that he (Reuben) would truly watch out protect Benjamin?

Questions.Q: What was the reason why Jacob was especially concerned that nothing harmful would happen to Benjamin?
Questions.A: Benjamin was the only son of Rachel left/remaining. Rachel had been Jacob's favorite wife. (38)

Questions.Q: According to Jacob, what would happen to him, if Benjamin went to Egypt, and then did not return home?
Questions.A: Jacob said that he would grieve and probably die. (38)

Questions.Q: So was Jacob willing at that time to allow Benjamin to go to Egypt with his older brothers?
Questions.A: No, he was not willing. (38)

Section.heading: Genesis 43:1-17 Joseph's brothers returned to Egypt.

Questions.Q: Did Joseph's brothers immediately return to Egypt with Benjamin?
Questions.A: No, because Jacob did not want to allow Benjamin to go to Egypt.

Questions.Q: Did they finally go at a later time?
Questions.A: Yes, they did.

Questions.Q: What was the reason that Jacob finally allowed the brothers to take Benjamin to Egypt?
Questions.A: That was the only way that they could get/obtain more food.

Questions.Q: In your opinion, how do you think that Simeon was feeling all that time?
Questions.A: He probably felt that his brothers had abandoned him there in prison. He may have given up hoping that they would return to get him/to have him released.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Jacob told his sons to return to Egypt?
Questions.A: The famine continued and they had used up all the food that they had brought back from Egypt on their first trip. (1-2)

Questions.Q: Which of the brothers became the spokesman/began to speak on behalf of all of the brothers?
Questions.A: Judah became the spokesman. (3)
Questions.Alternative: Which of the brothers became the spokesman?
Which of the brothers became the spokesman for the brothers?
Which of the brothers began to speak on behalf of all of the brothers?

Questions.Q: What did Judah reply when their father told them to return to Egypt for more food?
Questions.A: Judah said that they could not buy food - they could not even speak with the man in charge of the grain - unless they took Benjamin with them. (3-5)

Questions.Q: Then for what did Jacob rebuke/blame his sons?
Questions.A: He rebuked/blamed them for telling the man that they still had a younger brother at home. (6)
Questions.Alternative: Then for what did Jacob rebuke his sons?
Then for what did Jacob blame his sons?

Questions.Q: What was their answer to Jacob?
Questions.A: They said that they were only answering the questions that the man had asked them. They said that they could not have known that the man would have demanded that they bring their youngest brother to Egypt. (7)

Questions.Q: What did Judah say at that time to his father?
Questions.A: He urged Jacob to send Benjamin along and he (Judah) would ensure Benjamin's safety. Judah pointed out that they needed more food, or else they and their families would all die. (8-9)

Questions.Q: How do we know that a long time had passed since the brothers first returned home from Egypt?
Questions.A: Judah said that they could have made two more trips to and from Egypt, if they had returned immediately with Benjamin. (10)

Questions.Q: What did Jacob decide at that time?
Questions.A: Jacob decided that he must allow Benjamin to go to Egypt. So he sent expensive gifts, and double the payment for the grain. (11-14)

Questions.Q: Tell me about the gifts that Jacob had his sons take to Egypt.
Questions.A: They were probably special things that might not have been readily available in Egypt. They included types of nuts (pistachio nuts and almonds), honey, and some plant juice/sap/liquid which was probably used as medicine or perfume. (11)

Questions.Q: For what reason do you think that Jacob sent double payment?
Questions.A: Probably he intended that his sons have enough money to pay for the grain from the first trip, as well as (for that which they would buy on) this second trip. (12)

Questions.Q: What did Jacob say was possibly the reason that someone had placed the money in their (grain) sacks?
Questions.A: He said that someone might have made a mistake/oversight. (12)

Questions.Q: What did Jacob say as a blessing for/to his sons on their journey? -OR- What did Jacob request of God for his sons, as they prepared to leave for Egypt again?
Questions.A: Jacob prayed that God would show mercy to his sons, when they met with the man in charge of selling the grain in Egypt. He prayed that Simeon and Benjamin would be able to return. (14)
Questions.Alternative: What did Jacob say as a blessing for his sons on their journey?
What did Jacob say as a blessing to his sons on their journey?
What did Jacob request of God for his sons, as they prepared to leave for Egypt again?

Questions.Q: If Benjamin and Simeon do not return, what would Jacob do?
Questions.A: He would grieve deeply, but would also accept it (as God's will). (14)

Questions.Q: So on their second trip to Egypt, what did they take with them?
Questions.A: They took their youngest brother, Benjamin, and also special gifts, and double the money required to buy the grain. (15)

Questions.Q: When Joseph saw Benjamin with his brothers, what did he do?
Questions.A: He had his steward/his head servant take all the brothers to his (Joseph's) home, and he ordered his steward/head servant to kill an animal for the noon meal. (16-17)

Questions.Q: Tell me about what Joseph's brothers experienced on this occasion.
Questions.A: First, they told the man in charge of Joseph's household about the money that the brothers had found in their grain sacks. The man answered that they did not need to worry about that. Then the man released Simeon from jail and brought him to his brothers. Joseph spoke briefly with them about their father and about Benjamin, the youngest brother. Then Joseph fed them a special meal.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that the brothers were afraid to go to Joseph's home?
Questions.A: It was very unusual for someone in Joseph's high position to invite a group such as those to his home. The brothers tried to understand why this was happening. They supposed that someone might have reported that, when the brothers got grain the first time, they did not pay for it. And now Joseph might punish them as though they had stolen the grain. (18)

Questions.Q: What did the brothers suppose that Joseph might do to them if he thought that/because they had not paid for the grain?
Questions.A: They were afraid that Joseph would make them his slaves and take their donkeys. (18)
Questions.Alternative: What did the brothers suppose that Joseph might do to them if he thought that they had not paid for the grain?
What did the brothers suppose that Joseph might do to them because they had not paid for the grain?

Questions.Q: What did the brothers do in order to try to solve the problem?
Questions.A: They talked to the man in charge of Joseph's household, and tried to pay again for the grain which they had received on the first trip. (19-22)

Questions.Q: What was the steward's answer to them?
Questions.A: He told them not to be afraid. He said that the appropriate person/office had truly received the brothers' payment. And he told them that maybe God had put the money back into their grain sacks. (23)

Questions.Q: After they spoke about the grain payment, what did Joseph's household manager do?
Questions.A: He released Simeon from jail and brought him to his brothers. (23b)

Questions.Q: What did Joseph's servants do next?
Questions.A: They welcomed the brothers into Joseph's home, and gave them water to wash, and food for their donkeys. (24)

Questions.Q: What did the brothers do while they waited for Joseph to come home?
Questions.A: They prepared the gifts that they had brought for him. (25)

Questions.Q: When Joseph arrived (at) home, in what manner did the brothers greet him?
Questions.A: They brought their special gifts, and bowed low/bowed to the ground in front of him. (26)

Questions.Q: When the brothers bowed in front of Joseph, were they worshiping him as though he was God?
Questions.A: No, they were showing respect to him since he was a man of very high position.
Questions.Alternative: When the brothers bowed in front of Joseph, were they worshipping him as though he was God?

Questions.Q: What did Joseph ask them?
Questions.A: Joseph asked them how they were/if they were well. And he asked whether their father was still alive. (27)

Questions.Q: What was the brothers' response?
Questions.A: They said that their father was (still) alive and well, and then they bowed again in front of Joseph. (28)

Questions.Q: When Joseph saw Benjamin, what did Joseph say?
Questions.A: Joseph asked God to bless Benjamin - to show favor or kindness to him. (29)

Questions.Q: What happened next?
Questions.A: Joseph felt overwhelmed by his emotions, so he went quickly into his room to cry. (30)

Questions.Q: Then what did Joseph do?
Questions.A: He washed his face (so that people no one would see that he was/felt upset), came out of his room, and ordered his servants to bring the food. (31)

Questions.Q: Tell me about the seating arrangements for the meal.
Questions.A: Joseph sat alone, and his brothers ate together as a group, seated/arranged in order of their age. The Egyptians ate together, separated from Joseph and his brothers. (32)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the Egyptians did not eat/sit together with Joseph's brothers?
Questions.A: The Egyptians despised/looked down on the Hebrews. // The Egyptians considered the food of the Hebrews (as) taboo. (32)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that the Egyptians did not eat together with Joseph's brothers?
What is the reason that the Egyptians did not sit together with Joseph's brothers?

Questions.Q: What was it about the seating arrangements which caused Joseph's brothers to be very surprised?
Questions.A: Joseph/Joseph's servant had told the brothers where they were to sit. That seating arrangement was in order of age - from the eldest to the youngest. (33)

Questions.Q: Tell me about the manner in which the brothers received their food.
Questions.A: Someone brought them their food from Joseph's table. And Benjamin received five times more food/much more food than his brothers. (34)

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that Joseph gave special treatment to Benjamin?
Questions.A: Perhaps he did this to honor Benjamin, since Benjamin was Joseph's only full-brother. (The others were Joseph's half-brothers.) Also, perhaps Joseph was testing his brothers to see if they would treat Benjamin in the same manner as they had treated Joseph when their father gave Joseph special treatment.

Questions.Q: Do you think that the brothers were ashamed or afraid to eat or drink very much?
Questions.A: No, they ate and drank freely. (34)

Questions.Q: After Joseph's brothers bought their grain and left for home, what happened?
Questions.A: The man in charge of Joseph's household chased after/pursued them and accused them of stealing a special cup from Joseph. The brothers denied it. The man searched their grain sacks and found the cup in Benjamin's sack. He said that Benjamin would have to stay in Egypt as a slave. The brothers all returned to Joseph, and Joseph again said that Benjamin would have to stay as his slave. Then Judah spoke up. He told Joseph that their father, Jacob, would die if Benjamin did not return (with them) to Canaan. And Judah offered to remain in Egypt as Joseph's slave in place of Benjamin.

Questions.Q: What do you think might have been Joseph's purpose in all of this?
Questions.A: Probably he was testing his brothers. Perhaps Benjamin had taken Joseph's place as Jacob's favorite son. And if the other brothers had not changed, then they would use this opportunity to get rid of Benjamin - to cause him to become a slave in Egypt as had happened to Joseph years ago. But if the brothers were sorry for what they had done to Joseph - and to their father, Jacob - then perhaps at this time they would do anything they could to keep Benjamin from being enslaved, and to return him to his father in Canaan.

Questions.Q: How much grain/food did Joseph tell his servant to put in the sacks of his brothers?
Questions.A: Joseph said to fill the sacks with as much grain/food as the brothers could carry. (1)
Questions.Alternative: How much grain did Joseph tell his servant to put in the sacks of his brothers?
How much food did Joseph tell his servant to put in the sacks of his brothers?

Questions.Q: After Joseph's servant had filled the brothers' sacks with grain/food, what else did Joseph tell him to place in the sacks?
Questions.A: Joseph told him to place the brothers' payment money on top of the grain inside the sacks. Joseph also told the servant to place Joseph's special silver cup in Benjamin's sack. (1-2)
Questions.Alternative: After Joseph's servant had filled the brothers' sacks with grain, what else did Joseph tell him to place in the sacks?
After Joseph's servant had filled the brothers' sacks with food, what else did Joseph tell him to place in the sacks?

Questions.Q: What time of day was it when the brothers left to return home?
Questions.A: It was very early morning. (3)

Questions.Q: What did Joseph command his servant to do next?
Questions.A: He told his servant to follow them and to overtake them, and then to accuse them of stealing his silver cup. (4-5)

Questions.Q: When the servant caught up to Joseph's brothers and accused them of stealing Joseph's special silver cup, what was the brothers' response?
Questions.A: They were shocked that anybody could think that they would do such a thing. (7)

Questions.Q: What did the brothers say was proof/evidence that they were honest men?
Questions.A: They told him that they had brought back the money that they had found in their grain sacks on the first trip, even though they had made full payment for that grain. (8)
Questions.Alternative: What did the brothers say was proof that they were honest men?
What did the brothers say was evidence that they were honest men?

Questions.Q: According to Joseph's brothers, what should be the punishment, if Joseph's servant should find the special silver cup among them?
Questions.A: They said that if one of the brothers had the cup, then that man must die. And all the other brothers must become Joseph's slaves. (9)

Questions.Q: Did Joseph's servant agree with the brothers' suggestion for punishment?
Questions.A: He agreed in part. The servant said that whoever had the cup would become a slave, and the other brothers could go free. (10)

Questions.Q: What did the brothers do next?
Questions.A: They quickly unloaded their grain sacks from the donkeys. (11)

Questions.Q: Describe how the servant searched for that silver cup.
Questions.A: He searched the grain sacks of each brother, beginning with the eldest brother, and proceeding to the youngest. (12)

Questions.Q: And did the servant find the cup?
Questions.A: Yes, it was in Benjamin's sack. (12)

Questions.Q: When the servant found the silver cup in Benjamin's sack, what did his brothers do?
Questions.A: They were extremely upset - so much that they tore their clothes to show their grief/despair. Then they loaded the grain back on their donkeys, and they all returned to Joseph. (13)

Questions.Q: What did the brothers do when they arrived (back) at Joseph's home?
Questions.A: They all fell to the ground. (14)

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that they all fell to the ground?
Questions.A: That was probably their/a way of showing that they were hoping that Joseph would show them mercy/would be merciful to them.

Questions.Q: According to Joseph, by what means did he know who had his cup?
Questions.A: Joseph said that he had special knowledge and could discern who were thieves. (15)

Questions.Q: Who now spoke on behalf of all the brothers?
Questions.A: Judah spoke on their behalf. (16)

Questions.Q: According to Judah, what is the reason that the brothers were experiencing such terrible circumstances?
Questions.A: Judah said that God had seen their sin (and caught them at it), and he was punishing them. (16)

Questions.Q: What did Judah say should now happen?
Questions.A: He said that all of the brothers should become slaves, together with Benjamin. (16)

Questions.Q: Did Joseph agree with Judah's suggestion?
Questions.A: No, Joseph said that Benjamin must become his slave, but that the other brothers were to return home to their father. (17)

Questions.Q: What was Judah's response?
Questions.A: Judah approached Joseph respectfully, and told Joseph about their family, and how their father had finally agreed to send Benjamin to Egypt. Then he urged Joseph to free Benjamin, because otherwise their father would die from grief. (18-34)

Questions.Q: When Judah began to speak with Joseph, what did Judah say to demonstrate his respect for Joseph?
Questions.A: Judah asked permission to speak with Joseph, and asked Joseph to be patient with him (Judah). And Judah recognized/acknowledged that Joseph's authority/power (to kill or to pardon) was similar/was the same as Pharaoh's authority/power. (18)

Questions.Q: When the brothers had met Joseph on their first trip, what had the brothers told him about Jacob, Benjamin, and Joseph?
Questions.A: They had told him that Jacob was an old man, and that Benjamin was his youngest son, born when Jacob was already old. They had said that Jacob loved Benjamin very much, and that Benjamin's brother (Joseph) was dead. (20)

Questions.Q: According to Judah, when the brothers tried to persuade Jacob to allow them to take Benjamin to Egypt, what had Jacob said about Benjamin's brother, Joseph?
Questions.A: Jacob had said that he had gone away/he had disappeared, presumably killed by a wild animal. And Jacob had added that he had never seen Joseph since that time. (27-28)

Questions.Q: In what way did Judah show a much greater concern for his father at this time, than he did years ago, when Joseph had gone to find his brothers in the fields?
Questions.A: At this time, Judah was afraid that Jacob would die because of his grief over Benjamin. But years before, when Judah had suggested that they sell Joseph as a slave, he seemed to have no concern for how Jacob would feel. (22-31)

Questions.Q: In verse 30, according to Judah, what was the reason that he could not return to his father without Benjamin?
Questions.A: Judah said that Benjamin meant very much to Jacob - as though Benjamin's life/soul was bound to Jacob's life/soul. Jacob would not be able to go on living without Benjamin. (30-31)

Questions.Q: According to Judah, if Benjamin cannot return to Jacob, and if Jacob dies of grief, who would be responsible for that?
Questions.A: He said that he and his brothers would be responsible. (31)
Questions.Alternative: According to Judah, if Benjamin were not allowed to return to Jacob, and if Jacob were to die of grief, who would be responsible for that?

Questions.Q: Who would be even more responsible than the rest of the brothers? -OR- Who would carry more blame than the rest of the brothers?
Questions.A: Judah would carry more blame. He had made a special pledge to Jacob. He had promised to ensure that nothing harmful would happen to Benjamin. (32)
Questions.Alternative: Who would be even more responsible than the rest of the brothers?
Who would carry more blame than the rest of the brothers?

Questions.Q: What suggestion did Judah make to Joseph?
Questions.A: Judah offered to be a slave in Benjamin's place. (33)

Questions.Q: In your opinion, in what way had Joseph been able to test his brothers, in order that he might know whether their character had changed since they sold him into slavery?
Questions.A: Benjamin's situation was similar to how Joseph's was, in that Jacob had a special love for Benjamin. Joseph emphasized that when he served Benjamin more food. He was now giving the brothers an opportunity to abandon Benjamin.

Questions.Q: In your thinking/opinion, did Judah (and his brothers) pass the test?
Questions.A: Yes, this time Judah showed great care/concern for Benjamin and for his father. (33-34)
Questions.Alternative: In your thinking, did Judah (and his brothers) pass the test?
In your opinion, did Judah (and his brothers) pass the test?

Section.heading: Genesis 45:1-28 Joseph revealed himself to his brothers.

Questions.Q: What happened after Judah finished pleading with Joseph?
Questions.A: Joseph told his brothers who he really was - that he was the brother whom they had sold into slavery. He told them not to worry, because it was all a part of God's plan. And then he told them to go home and bring Jacob and all of their families to come and live in Egypt. Pharaoh was pleased to hear of Joseph's brothers and Joseph's father. Pharaoh also said that Jacob and his entire family should move to Egypt. When the brothers arrived home with the news, at first Jacob could not believe them. But they persuaded him, and Jacob agreed to go to Egypt to see Joseph.

Questions.Q: At the time when Joseph revealed/introduced himself to his brothers, who was present with them?
Questions.A: Only Joseph and his brothers were present. (1)
Questions.Alternative: At the time when Joseph revealed himself to his brothers, who was present with them?
At the time when Joseph introduced himself to his brothers, who was present with them?

Questions.Q: Just before Joseph revealed/introduced himself to his brothers, what did he do?
Questions.A: He became very emotional. He wept loudly. (2)
Questions.Alternative: Just before Joseph revealed himself to his brothers, what did he do?
Just before Joseph introduced himself to his brothers, what did he do?

Questions.Q: When Joseph's brothers realized that the man in charge of all Egypt was their brother, Joseph, how did they feel?
Questions.A: They were so shocked/overwhelmed that they could not speak. (3)

Questions.Q: What did Joseph then say to his brothers?
Questions.A: Joseph told them not to be upset or angry with themselves for selling him and causing him to be brought to Egypt as a slave. (5)

Questions.Q: According to Joseph, what was the reason why he had been brought to Egypt?
Questions.A: Joseph told them that God had sent him to Egypt ahead of the rest of his family, in order that Joseph would be able to save them and their families from death during the famine. (5, 7)

Questions.Q: At that time, how many years of famine had passed, and how many more years of famine would there be?
Questions.A: Two years of famine had passed, and there were five years left. (6)

Questions.Q: According to Joseph, if God had not brought him to Egypt, what would have happened to Joseph's relatives/Joseph's extended family/Jacob and Jacob's descendants?
Questions.A: Joseph said that they would all have died. (7)

Key Term Check: This is perhaps the first reference in the Old Testament to the concept of "remnant" - that God has acted to preserve some of his people. On this and other occasions, God acts in such a way as to preserve a "remnant" or "remainder" of his people. He will not allow anyone to completely destroy his people, even though many of them will become unfaithful to him.
Questions.Alternative: According to Joseph, if God had not brought him to Egypt, what would have happened to Joseph's relatives?
According to Joseph, if God had not brought him to Egypt, what would have happened to Joseph's extended family?
According to Joseph, if God had not brought him to Egypt, what would have happened to Jacob and Jacob's descendants?
According to Joseph, if God had not brought him to Egypt, what would have happened to Joseph's relatives/Joseph's extended family/Jacob and Jacob's descendents?
According to Joseph, if God had not brought him to Egypt, what would have happened to Jacob and Jacob's descendents?

Questions.Q: According to Joseph, who was in control of whatever happened to him?
Questions.A: God was in control. (5, 7-8)

Questions.Q: According to Joseph, what was one bad thing that God used in order to bring about/cause good?
Questions.A: God allowed Joseph's brothers to sell him into slavery in Egypt. (5, 7)
Questions.Alternative: According to Joseph, what was one bad thing that God used in order to bring about good?
According to Joseph, what was one bad thing that God used in order to cause good?

Questions.Q: Do we believe that God is in control of everything that happens to us, good or bad, even as he was in control of Joseph's life?
Questions.A: That is one lesson that we can learn from this story/account.
Questions.Alternative: Do you believe that God is in control of everything that happens to us, good or bad, even as he was in control of Joseph's life?
Do you believe that God is in control of everything that happens to you, good or bad, even as he was in control of Joseph's life?
Do you believe that God is in control of everything that happens to people, good or bad, even as he was in control of Joseph's life?
Do we believe that God is in control of everything that happens to people, good or bad, even as he was in control of Joseph's life?

Questions.Q: As Joseph was talking to his brothers, in what way did he describe the extent of his authority?
Questions.A: He said that he was the advisor to Pharaoh and chief administrator over his household and all of Egypt. (8)

Questions.Q: What did Joseph say that his brothers were to do at that time?
Questions.A: They were to return home and tell their father that Joseph was alive. They were to tell him that God had made him a ruler/leader in Egypt. And they were to say that Joseph wanted his father to come quickly to Egypt to live near him. (9-10)

Questions.Q: According to Joseph, what was the reason why Jacob should move to Egypt?
Questions.A: Joseph wanted to have his father near him. And Joseph also wanted to be able to provide food for the whole family during the famine. (10-11)

Questions.Q: According to Joseph, where was a good place for them to live in Egypt?
Questions.A: He said that they could live in Goshen. (10)

Questions.Q: What did Joseph want to give to them?
Questions.A: He wanted to give them food and whatever they needed. (11)

Questions.Q: If they did not move to Egypt, what would happen to them?
Questions.A: They would become extremely poor, lacking everything that they needed. (11)

Questions.Q: At that point, what do you think was the reason why Joseph made special mention of Benjamin? In what way were Joseph and Benjamin related?
Questions.A: Benjamin was his full brother. The others had the same father as Joseph, but they did not have the same mother as Joseph and Benjamin. (12)

Questions.Q: At this time, what did Joseph add to what his brothers were to tell their father about him/his position in Egypt?
Questions.A: They were to tell their father that Joseph has great power and authority, and much honor and wealth. (13)
Questions.Alternative: At this time, what did Joseph add to what his brothers were to tell their father about him?
At this time, what did Joseph add to what his brothers were to tell their father about his position in Egypt?

Questions.Q: After Joseph finished instructing his brothers about bringing their father to Egypt, what did they all do?
Questions.A: Joseph hugged Benjamin, and kissed and cried with all the other brothers. And they all spoke together for a time. (14-15)

Questions.Q: Who heard the news, that Joseph's brothers had arrived?
Questions.A: Pharaoh and his household heard about it. (16)

Questions.Q: How did they feel about that news?
Questions.A: They were very happy about it. (16)

Questions.Q: What did Pharaoh instruct Joseph's brothers?
Questions.A: Pharaoh told them to load their donkeys and quickly go home to Canaan, and to bring/move Joseph's father and their households to Egypt in order to live there. (17-18)

Questions.Q: What did Pharaoh say that he would give to them in Egypt?
Questions.A: Pharaoh promised to give them good land and food, and to replace anything they had to leave behind (in Canaan). (18, 20)

Questions.Q: What did Pharaoh give/loan them for their trip?
Questions.A: Pharaoh gave/loaned them wagons in which Joseph's father, and the brothers' wives and children, could ride during the long journey (from Canaan to Egypt). (19)
Questions.Alternative: What did Pharaoh give them for their trip?
What did Pharaoh loan them for their trip?

Questions.Q: What did Pharaoh say about the belongings of Jacob's family which they might have to leave behind in Canaan?
Questions.A: Jacob and his family would not have to worry about their belongings which they might have to leave behind (in Canaan), because Pharaoh would replace them with the best in Egypt. (20)

Questions.Q: What did Joseph give to the brothers for their journey to Canaan?
Questions.A: He gave them wagons, and also food and other necessities for the journey. (21)

Questions.Q: What gifts did Joseph give to his brothers?
Questions.A: Joseph gave all of them (expensive) clothes. And he gave Benjamin five robes/five sets of clothes, and also 300 pieces of silver/300 silver coins. (22)

Questions.Q: What did Joseph send as gifts for his father?
Questions.A: Joseph sent ten donkeys loaded with special products of Egypt, and ten (female) donkeys loaded with grain and other necessities for the journey. (23)

Questions.Q: As the brothers were leaving, what did Joseph say?
Questions.A: Joseph told them not to quarrel/be upset on their journey home. (24)

Questions.Q: Did the brothers arrive back safely in Canaan?
Questions.A: Yes, they were able to return safely to their father. (25)

Questions.Q: When Jacob heard about Joseph, what did he think?
Questions.A: Jacob was shocked/overwhelmed, and could hardly believe that Joseph was still alive. (26)

Questions.Q: What was it that helped Jacob to believe that Joseph was still alive?
Questions.A: He was able to believe because of the message that Joseph had sent with his (Joseph's) brothers, and also because Jacob saw the wagons (loaded with good things) which Pharaoh had sent for Jacob in which he was to ride to Egypt. (27)

Questions.Q: What did Jacob decide?
Questions.A: He decided that, before he died, he would go to Egypt to see Joseph. (28)

Section.heading: Genesis 46:1-7 Jacob and his sons traveled to Egypt.

Questions.Q: Tell what this section is about.
Questions.A: It is about the move/transfer of Jacob and all of his extended family from Canaan to Egypt.

Questions.Q: Do you think that Jacob might have been worried about moving himself and his whole family out of Canaan?
Questions.A: Yes, he probably was anxious/worried.

Questions.Q: What happened during that time to help Jacob believe that he would be doing right to move to Egypt?
Questions.A: God appeared to Jacob and assured him that Jacob was to move/take his family to Egypt.

Questions.Q: What land was Jacob's family leaving?
Questions.A: Jacob's family was leaving the land of Canaan. (1)

Questions.Q: Where did they make their first main stop?
Questions.A: They stopped at Beersheba. (1)

Questions.Q: What did Jacob do at Beersheba?
Questions.A: He offered sacrifices to God. (1)

Questions.Q: What does the author say here about the identity of the God to whom Jacob offered sacrifices?
Questions.A: He is the God whom Jacob and his father, Isaac, had worshiped. (1)

Questions.Q: What happened to Jacob during the night?
Questions.A: God spoke to him in a dream. (2)

Questions.Q: What did God tell Jacob not to fear/not to be afraid of?
Questions.A: God said that Jacob should not be afraid to go to Egypt. (3)
Questions.Alternative: What did God tell Jacob not to fear?
What did God tell Jacob not to be afraid of?

Questions.Q: What are four wonderful promises that God spoke to/promised to Jacob?
Questions.A: God said that he would be with him in Egypt. He also said that Jacob's descendants would become a great nation. God assured Jacob that Joseph would look after him when Jacob's time came to die/when it came time for Jacob to die. And God promised that he would bring Jacob/would bring Jacob's descendants back to Canaan. (3-4)
Questions.Note: It is not certain whether God's promise to bring Jacob back to Canaan is referring specifically to bringing his corpse back to Canaan, or to the Exodus, when God would bring Jacob's descendants back to Canaan. Or perhaps it refers to both Jacob's corpse and to his many descendents.
Questions.Alternative: What are four wonderful promises that God spoke to Jacob?
What are four wonderful promises that God promised to Jacob?

Questions.Q: By what means of transport did Jacob and his family travel to Egypt?
Questions.A: The wives and children of Jacob's sons rode in wagons which Pharaoh had provided. Probably Jacob also rode in a wagon. (5)

Questions.Q: What did Jacob do with all his animals and belongings?
Questions.A: He took them with him to Egypt. (6)

Questions.Q: What does this section describe?
Questions.A: This section tells of the descendants of Jacob who went to Egypt. (It includes Joseph and his family, who were already in Egypt.)

Questions.Q: Which of Jacob's sons is listed first?
Questions.A: Reuben, the eldest, is listed first. (8)

Questions.Q: How many sons did Reuben have?
Questions.A: He had four sons. (9)

Questions.Q: Who was Jacob's second son?
Questions.A: His second son was Simeon. (10)

Questions.Q: What do we know about the mother of Simeon's son, Shaul?
Questions.A: She was a Canaanite/from Canaan. (10)

Questions.Q: How many of Judah's sons died in Canaan?
Questions.A: Two died: Er and Onan. (12)

Questions.Q: Which of Judah's sons was the father of Hezron and Hamul?
Questions.A: Perez was their father. (12)

Questions.Q: After Judah, who were the next two sons listed (here)?
Questions.A: Issachar and Zebulun were the next two listed. (13-14)

Questions.Q: Who was the mother of those six sons: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar and Zebulun?
Questions.A: Leah was their mother. (15)

Questions.Q: Where were they born?
Questions.A: They were born in Paddan-aram (also called Mesopotamia). (15)

Questions.Q: Who was Leah's daughter?
Questions.A: Her daughter was Dinah. (15)

Questions.Q: How many descendants did Jacob and Leah have? -OR- How many descendants did Jacob have by Leah?
Questions.A: There were thirty-three descendants (at that time/at the time this was written). (15)
Questions.Alternative: How many descendants did Jacob and Leah have?
How many descendants did Jacob have by Leah?
How many descendents did Jacob and Leah have? -OR- How many descendents did Jacob have by Leah?
How many descendents did Jacob and Leah have?
How many descendents did Jacob have by Leah?

Questions.Q: What was the name of Leah's maid?
Questions.A: Leah's maid's name was Zilpah. (18)

Questions.Q: Who were Zilpah's two sons?
Questions.A: Her two sons were Gad and Asher. (16-17)

Questions.Q: Who was the father of Serah?
Questions.A: Asher was her father. (17)

Questions.Q: Who was the father of Zilpah's children?
Questions.A: Jacob was their father. (18)

Questions.Q: How many descendants did Jacob and Zilpah have?
Questions.A: There were sixteen descendants (at that time/at the time this was written). (18)
Questions.Alternative: How many descendents did Jacob and Zilpah have?

Questions.Q: How many sons did Rachel have?
Questions.A: She had two sons. (19)

Questions.Q: What were their names?
Questions.A: They were Joseph and Benjamin. (19)

Questions.Q: Who was Asenath?
Questions.A: She was Joseph's wife, an Egyptian, the daughter of Potiphera. (20)

Questions.Q: Who were the sons of Joseph and Asenath?
Questions.A: They were Manasseh and Ephraim. (20)

Questions.Q: How many sons did Benjamin have?
Questions.A: He had ten sons. (21)

Questions.Q: How many descendants did Jacob and Rachel have (at the time of this account)?
Questions.A: They had fourteen descendants. (22)
Questions.Alternative: How many descendents did Jacob and Rachel have (at the time of this account)?

Questions.Q: Whose maid was Bilhah?
Questions.A: She was Rachel's maid. (25)

Questions.Q: Who were Bilhah's sons?
Questions.A: Her sons were Dan and Naphtali. (23-24)

Questions.Q: How many descendants did Jacob and Bilhah have?
Questions.A: They had seven descendants. (25)
Questions.Alternative: How many descendents did Jacob and Bilhah have?

Questions.Q: In counting Jacob's 66 own offspring/66 direct descendants in this account, who was not included in the count/list?
Questions.A: The count/list did not include Jacob's daughters-in-law (the wives of Jacob's sons). (26)
Questions.Alternative: In counting Jacob's 66 own offspring in this account, who was not included in the count?
In counting Jacob's 66 own offspring in this account, who was not included in the list?
In counting Jacob's 66 direct descendants in this account, who was not included in the count?
In counting Jacob's 66 direct descendants in this account, who was not included in the list?
In counting Jacob's 66 own offspring/66 direct descendents in this account, who was not included in the count/list?
In counting Jacob's 66 direct descendents in this account, who was not included in the count?
In counting Jacob's 66 direct descendents in this account, who was not included in the list?

Questions.Q: What is the total number of Jacob's descendants who went to Egypt?
Questions.A: They were seventy. (27)
Questions.Alternative: What is the total number of Jacob's descendents who went to Egypt?

Section.heading: Genesis 46:28-47:12 Jacob and his sons settled in Egypt.

Questions.Q: Tell what happened next to Jacob and his sons.
Questions.A: They arrived in Egypt, and Joseph took some of them to meet Pharaoh. Pharaoh asked them about their work/occupation, and Pharaoh gave permission for them to settle in Goshen. So Joseph helped them to settle there, and provided everything that they needed.

Questions.Q: As Jacob and his family were traveling to Egypt, what did Jacob tell Judah to do?
Questions.A: He told Judah to go ahead in order to learn the way, and then lead them all to Goshen. (28)

Questions.Q: When Jacob and the family arrived at Goshen, what did Joseph do?
Questions.A: He traveled in his chariot/cart to Goshen (to meet his father and the rest of the family). (29)

Questions.Q: Describe Joseph's meeting with his father.
Questions.A: As soon as Joseph arrived, he embraced/hugged his father, and cried for joy (for) a long time. (29)

Questions.Q: What did Jacob say when he met Joseph?
Questions.A: Jacob said that because he had now seen his long-lost son, he could die peacefully/contentedly. // When he (Jacob) died, he would die peacefully/satisfied. (30)

Questions.Q: Do you think that Jacob meant that he wanted to die soon?
Questions.A: No. He was saying that even if he was to die soon, he would die peacefully/contented/in peace.

Questions.Q: What did Joseph say that he would go immediately to tell Pharaoh?
Questions.A: He would tell Pharaoh that his father and relatives had arrived, and that they were sheep and cattle herders/they raised sheep and cattle. And he would tell Pharaoh that his family had brought their sheep and cattle and other possessions with them. (31-32)

Questions.Q: According to Joseph, what would Pharaoh ask his brothers?
Questions.A: Pharaoh will ask them what is their work/occupation/livelihood. (33)

Questions.Q: What did Joseph instruct his brothers to say in response to Pharaoh's question?
Questions.A: The brothers were to say that they (and their ancestors) had raised livestock for very many years (and that they wished to continue to do so). (34)

Questions.Q: What did the Egyptians think about herdsmen/people who worked with livestock?
Questions.A: They despised/looked down on herdsmen/people who worked with livestock. (34)
Questions.Alternative: What did the Egyptians think about herdsmen?
What did the Egyptians think about people who worked with livestock?

Questions.Q: What did Joseph say to Pharaoh at that time?
Questions.A: Joseph told Pharaoh that his father and brothers had arrived from Canaan, along with their flocks of sheep and herds of cattle, and other possessions. (1)

Questions.Q: Whom did Joseph take to meet Pharaoh?
Questions.A: He took five of his brothers. (2)

Questions.Q: What was Pharaoh's first question to Joseph's brothers?
Questions.A: He asked them about their work/occupation/livelihood. (3)

Questions.Q: According to Joseph's brothers, what were the circumstances that caused them to move to Egypt?
Questions.A: There was a severe famine in Canaan, and there had been no food for their flocks of sheep. (4)

Questions.Q: What request did the five brothers ask of Pharaoh?
Questions.A: They asked Pharaoh to allow them to live (for a period of time) in Goshen. (4)

Questions.Q: What did Pharaoh offer Joseph and his family?
Questions.A: He told Joseph to choose the best land/place for his family to live. Pharaoh said that they could live in Goshen, if they wished. (6)

Questions.Q: Did Pharaoh make any request of Joseph or his brothers?
Questions.A: Yes, Pharaoh asked them to choose some from among their family who knew how to care for livestock/animals to care for his (Pharaoh's) cattle. (6)

Questions.Q: After that, whom did Joseph bring to Pharaoh?
Questions.A: He brought his father, Jacob, to meet Pharaoh. (7)

Questions.Q: What did Jacob do as soon as he met Pharaoh?
Questions.A: He asked God to bless Pharaoh. -OR- He (formally) greeted Pharaoh. (7)

Questions.Q: What did Pharaoh ask Jacob?
Questions.A: He asked Jacob how old he (Jacob) was. (8)

Questions.Q: What was Jacob's response?
Questions.A: Jacob said that he was 130 years old, and that he had had a difficult life. And he said that his life had been shorter than that of his ancestors. (9)

Questions.Q: What did Jacob do as he left Pharaoh?
Questions.A: He again asked God to bless Pharaoh. -OR- He (formally) bid farewell to Pharaoh. (10)

Questions.Q: In what area of Egypt did Joseph settle Jacob and his extended family?
Questions.A: He settled them in the area near/around Rameses. (11)

Questions.Q: What else did Joseph do for his father's households?
Questions.A: Joseph provided sufficient food for them all. (12)

Section.heading: Genesis 47:13-26 Joseph ruled wisely in times of famine.

Questions.Q: How was Joseph able to save very many people from starving (to death)?
Questions.A: He had ensured that grain was stored up during the seven years of abundant harvests. Then, when the (years of) famine came, he began to sell the grain. When the people had spent all their money, he exchanged grain for livestock. And when the people had exchanged all their livestock for grain, then they sold themselves as slaves to Pharaoh and gave up their land to Pharaoh.

Questions.Q: In what places did the famine affect people?
Questions.A: It affected the people of Egypt and Canaan. (13)

Questions.Q: What did Joseph do with all the money he received from the sale of the grain/from selling the grain?
Questions.A: He took it to Pharaoh. -OR- He deposited it in Pharaoh's treasury/palace. (14)
Questions.Alternative: What did Joseph do with all the money he received from the sale of the grain?
What did Joseph do with all the money he received from selling the grain?

Questions.Q: What did the people do when they had spent all their money to buy food?
Questions.A: They admitted that they had no more money, and they asked Joseph to have pity on them and give them food. (15)

Questions.Q: What did Joseph do when the people asked him to give them food?
Questions.A: He said that he would give them food in exchange for their cattle/livestock. (16)

Questions.Q: For how long were the people able to buy food by exchanging their cattle/livestock?
Questions.A: They were able to do that for one year. (17)
Questions.Alternative: For how long were the people able to buy food by exchanging their cattle?
For how long were the people able to buy food by exchanging their livestock?

Questions.Q: After they had sold all their livestock, then with what did the people offer to pay for their food?
Questions.A: The offered themselves (as slaves to Pharaoh), and they offered their land. (18)

Questions.Q: After a time, who became the owner of all the land in Egypt?
Questions.A: Pharaoh became the owner. (20)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Joseph did not buy the land of the priests in Egypt?
Questions.A: Pharaoh had been giving the priests food during the famine. As a result, they did not have to sell their land to obtain food. (22)

Questions.Q: How were the people of Egypt to obtain seed so that they could begin planting again (after the famine)?
Questions.A: Joseph said that he would give them the seed that they needed. (23)

Questions.Q: What did the people have to do as payment for the seed?
Questions.A: They had to give one-fifth of their harvest to Pharaoh. (24)

Questions.Q: What were the people to do with the rest of the grain that they harvested?
Questions.A: They were to keep some as planting-seed for the following year, and they were to feed their families. (24)

Questions.Q: How did the people feel about what Joseph had done?
Questions.A: They were thankful that he had saved their lives, and so they were willing to be Pharaoh's slaves. (25)

Questions.Q: What law did Joseph enact/establish at that time?
Questions.A: He declared that, from then on, the people must give one-fifth of the produce/of their harvest to Pharaoh. (26)

Key Term Check: The concept of "law" is a very important theme throughout the Old and New Testaments. In this particular context, it refers simply to a requirement that a ruler had declared/established and which his people must observe/obey.
Questions.Note: See "law" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: What law did Joseph enact at that time?
What law did Joseph establish at that time?

Questions.Q: Did that law apply to everyone in Egypt?
Questions.A: It did not apply to the priests, since Pharaoh had not confiscated/taken over their lands. (26)

Questions.Q: Who was approaching the time of his death?
Questions.A: Jacob was near death.

Questions.Q: Whom did Jacob summon to attend to him at his death?
Questions.A: He summoned his son, Joseph.

Questions.Q: What was the experience of Jacob and his descendants in Egypt?
Questions.A: They multiplied in number and they prospered/and they were very successful. (27)
Questions.Alternative: What was the experience of Jacob and his descendents in Egypt?

Questions.Q: How much longer did Jacob live/How long did Jacob live, after he and his family moved to Egypt?
Questions.A: He lived for seventeen (more) years. (28)
Questions.Alternative: How much longer did Jacob live, after he and his family moved to Egypt?
How long did Jacob live, after he and his family moved to Egypt?

Questions.Q: How old was Jacob when he died?
Questions.A: He was 147 years old. (28)

Questions.Q: What request did Jacob make of Joseph before he (Jacob) died?
Questions.A: He requested that Joseph bury him in Canaan, not in Egypt. (29-30)

Questions.Q: Specifically where in Canaan did Jacob want Joseph to bury him?
Questions.A: He wanted Joseph to bury him near the place where Jacob's ancestors had been buried. (30)

Questions.Q: What did Jacob ask Joseph to do in order to indicate that Joseph was sincere in carrying out the request?
Questions.A: Jacob asked Joseph to solemnly swear to carry out his (Jacob's) request. (29-31)

Section.heading: Genesis 48:1-22 Jacob pronounced his blessing/bequeathed his inheritance on Joseph and on Joseph's sons.

Questions.Q: What did Jacob do at that time?
Questions.A: He prayed that God would bless Joseph and Joseph's sons.

Questions.Q: What did Joseph hear that caused him to take his two sons and go to see his father, Jacob?
Questions.A: Joseph heard that Jacob was ill and near death. (1)

Questions.Q: When Jacob heard that Joseph had arrived, what did he do?
Questions.A: Jacob exerted/forced himself to sit up. (2)

Questions.Q: About what important memory did Jacob tell Joseph at that time?
Questions.A: Jacob said that God had appeared to him at Luz in the land of Canaan, and God had blessed him by promising that Jacob would have many descendants who would become many people-groups. And God also had promised that Jacob's descendants would inherit the land of Canaan forever. (3-4)

Questions.Q: What name did Jacob use to refer to God at that time/in this account?
Questions.A: Jacob called him "God Almighty". (3)
Questions.Alternative: What name did Jacob use to refer to God at that time?
What name did Jacob use to refer to God in this account?

Questions.Q: What did Jacob declare about Manasseh and Ephraim at that time?
Questions.A: Jacob adopted them as his children. (5)

Questions.Q: From whom would Manasseh and Ephraim receive their inheritance?
Questions.A: They would receive it from Jacob. (5)

Questions.Q: If Joseph had any more children, from whom would they inherit?
Questions.A: They would inherit from their elder brothers, Manasseh and Ephraim. (6)

Questions.Q: After Jacob spoke about Manasseh and Ephraim, about whom did he speak?
Questions.A: He spoke about his dead/late wife, Rachel. (7)

Questions.Q: Where did Rachel die?
Questions.A: She had died in Canaan, a short distance before they reached Ephrath. (7)

Questions.Q: What relationship was Rachel to Joseph?
Questions.A: She was his mother.

Questions.Q: In your opinion, why do you think that Jacob spoke of Rachel at this time?
Questions.A: Jacob had decided to adopt Manasseh and Ephraim, and that decision may have been partly a result of the fact that Rachel had died before she could give Jacob any more children. Or possibly because Jacob was thinking of his own death being near, that caused him to remember the death of his beloved wife.

Questions.Q: What change in health had Jacob experienced in his old age?
Questions.A: He had become partly blind. (8, 10)

Questions.Q: As Joseph brought his two sons close to Jacob, what did Jacob do?
Questions.A: He kissed and hugged/embraced Joseph's sons. (10)

Questions.Q: What two surprises did Jacob feel were because of God's mercy to him? -OR- For what two blessings was Jacob very grateful to God?
Questions.A: Firstly, Jacob had not expected to ever see Joseph again, but he did. And secondly, he was able to see (even) Joseph's two children. (11)
Questions.Alternative: What two surprises did Jacob feel were because of God's mercy to him?
For what two blessings was Jacob very grateful to God?

Questions.Q: Describe how Joseph positioned his sons near their grandfather.
Questions.A: He placed the elder son, Manasseh, near Jacob's right hand. And he placed the younger son, Ephraim, near Jacob's left hand. (13)

Questions.Q: What did Jacob do when he was about to place his hands on his grandsons?
Questions.A: He crossed his arms, so that his right hand was on Ephraim, and his left hand was on Manasseh. (14)

Questions.Q: When Jacob put his hands on his grandsons, what did that act signify (that he was about to do)?
Questions.A: It signified that he was about to ask God to bless his grandsons. (15-20)

Questions.Q: What are the names of Jacob's ancestors, those who also worshiped God?
Questions.A: The names of Jacob's ancestors are Isaac (Jacob's father), and Abraham (Jacob's grandfather). (15)
Questions.Alternative: What are the names of Jacob's ancestors, those who also worshipped God?
What are the names of Jacob's ancestors who also worshiped God?

Questions.Q: What did Jacob say as he looked back over his life?
Questions.A: Jacob thanked God because God had cared for him (Jacob), and God had sent an angel to help/rescue him in times of trouble. (15-16)

Questions.Q: What did Jacob request of God at this time for Ephraim and Manasseh?
Questions.A: Jacob prayed that God would give them many descendants who would carry on the names/who would continue to extend the family line of Abraham and Isaac and Jacob. (15-16)

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason why Joseph thought that Jacob's right hand should have been placed on Manasseh's head, and not on Ephraim's head?
Questions.A: In praying a blessing, the elder person generally placed his right hand on the head of the eldest son, not on the younger one. (17-18)

Questions.Q: Had Jacob mistakenly placed his right hand on the younger son?
Questions.A: No, had deliberately placed his right hand on Ephraim's head. (19)

Questions.Q: According to Jacob, which of his two grandsons would have very many descendants who would become a great number of people-groups?
Questions.A: Ephraim's descendants would become a great number of people-groups. (19)
Questions.Alternative: According to Jacob, which of his two grandsons would have very many descendents who would become a great number of people-groups?

Questions.Q: Does that mean that the descendants of Manasseh would be (very) few?
Questions.A: No, he would also have many descendants, but Ephraim would have more than Manasseh. (19)
Questions.Alternative: Does that mean that the descendents of Manasseh would be (very) few?

Questions.Q: In what way were future generations going to refer to Ephraim and Manasseh?
Questions.A: They would use the names of Ephraim and Manasseh when they pronounce a blessing on someone. That meant that they would express a hope that God would prosper someone as he had prospered Ephraim and Manasseh. (20)

Questions.Q: Finally, what did Jacob say to Joseph?
Questions.A: Jacob told Joseph that, although he (Jacob) would soon die, God would be with him (Joseph, and his sons and his brothers). And Jacob said that God will take them back to Canaan. (21)

Questions.Q: What special inheritance did Jacob give to Joseph at the same time?
Questions.A: Jacob gave/bequeathed to Joseph some land which Jacob had won in a battle. (22)

Questions.Q: How had Jacob acquired that piece of land?
Questions.A: He had won it in a battle against the Amorites. (22)

Section.heading: Genesis 49:1-28 Jacob pronounced his blessing/bequeathed his inheritance on Joseph and on Joseph's brothers.

Questions.Q: Tell what was happening in this section.
Questions.A: Jacob had gathered his sons together, in order to reveal what will happen/reveal the future for each of them, and especially for their descendants. At that time, Jacob spoke his final blessing on each of his sons.

Questions.Q: Whom did Jacob summon at that time, and for what purpose?
Questions.A: He summoned all of his (twelve) sons, in order to bless them/in order to bestow a blessing from God upon them, and to reveal what would happen to them in the future. (1-2)

Questions.Q: According to Jacob, what was good about Reuben?
Questions.A: He was an honor to Jacob's manhood/He was an honor to Jacob as a man, and he was strong. (3)

Questions.Q: And what was not good about his character?
Questions.A: He had shamed his father by sleeping with one of his father's wives. (4)

Questions.Q: What do you think that Jacob meant, when he said that Reuben was unstable as water/like a flood/unruly as the waves of the sea?
Questions.A: Probably he meant that Reuben was reckless and difficult to restrain. (4)
Questions.Alternative: What do you think that Jacob meant, when he said that Reuben was unstable as water?
What do you think that Jacob meant, when he said that Reuben was like a flood?
What do you think that Jacob meant, when he said that Reuben was unruly as the waves of the sea?

Questions.Q: What did Reuben lose because he had wronged his father?
Questions.A: Reuben would no longer be considered the number one/the greatest/the first son. (4)

Questions.Q: After speaking of Judah, of whom did Jacob speak next?
Questions.A: He spoke of Simeon and Levi. (5-7)

Questions.Q: What do you think that Jacob meant by saying that Simeon and Levi are brothers?
Questions.A: He meant that they had the same characteristics - that they did the same things, they were a pair, or "two of a kind", or "brothers in crime". (5)

Questions.Q: What kind of men were Simeon and Levi?
Questions.A: They were violent and cruel. They had killed innocent people and animals. (5-7)

Questions.Q: What did they do to some animals?
Questions.A: They hamstrung them - they sliced tendons in the animals' legs, which caused the animals to become crippled. (6)

Questions.Q: What was the reason why the brothers treated the animals in that cruel way?
Questions.A: They did it for fun/sport. -OR- They did it just because they felt like doing it. (6)

Questions.Q: To what incident/event was Jacob referring?
Questions.A: He was talking about how they had killed/slaughtered Hamor, Shechem, and others (after Shechem had violated Dinah).
Questions.Alternative: To what incident was Jacob referring?
To what event was Jacob referring?
Questions.Note: See Chapter 34.

Questions.Q: What did Jacob say about the anger and wrath of Simeon and Levi?
Questions.A: He said Simeon and Levi were very fierce and cruel. Their anger/wrath was certainly excessive. (7)

Questions.Q: What would be the retribution/outcome for the way those two brothers acted/reacted toward others?
Questions.A: They would be scattered throughout the land. (7)
Questions.Alternative: What would be the retribution for the way those two brothers acted toward others?
What would be the retribution for the way those two brothers reacted toward others?
What would be the outcome for the way those two brothers acted toward others?
What would be the outcome for the way those two brothers reacted toward others?

Questions.Q: Which of Jacob's sons did he speak about next?
Questions.A: He next spoke about Judah. (8-12)

Questions.Q: What attitude would Judah's brothers have towards him in the future?
Questions.A: They would praise and respect him. (8)

Questions.Q: What would happen to Judah's enemies?
Questions.A: Judah would always defeat them. (8)

Questions.Q: What do you think Jacob meant by comparing Judah with a lion?
Questions.A: Judah was strong, and it would be dangerous to provoke him. (9)

Questions.Q: What did Jacob say about Judah's power or authority?
Questions.A: He said that Judah and his descendants would become (military or civic) leaders. (10)

Questions.Q: Did Jacob predict that Judah and his descendants would prosper, or did he say that they would experience poverty?
Questions.A: He predicted that they would prosper. (11-12)
Questions.Alternative: Did Jacob predict that Judah and his descendents would prosper, or did he say that they would experience poverty?

Questions.Q: What kind of images did Jacob use to refer to how much Judah would prosper?
Questions.A: Jacob spoke of Judah's descendants having so many grapes that they would tie their horses to grapevines, and that they would not mind if the horses ate the grapes. They would be able to make so much wine that it would be as plentiful as water - as if they would use wine to wash their clothes/laundry. Likewise, their cattle or goats would produce an abundance of milk. (11-12)

Questions.Q: What did Jacob say about the location of the land of Zebulun's descendants?
Questions.A: It would be near the sea/ocean. (13)
Questions.Alternative: What did Jacob say about the location of the land of Zebulun's descendents?

Questions.Q: Who was compared to a strong donkey which only lies down (to rest)?
Questions.A: That is what Jacob said about Issachar. (14)

Questions.Q: What do you think that might suggest about Issachar and his descendants?
Questions.A: Probably they were not willing to work/very industrious. (14)
Questions.Alternative: What do you think that might suggest about Issachar and his descendents?

Questions.Q: Since the purpose of the letter is to persuade Jewish Christians not to go back to the old Jewish religion, why do you think he told them all this about God's Son and the angels?
Questions.A: These Hebrew Christians were thinking about leaving Christianity and their believing in Jesus Christ as God's Son and going back into their old religion, Judaism. In that religion, the Jews had come to think that God was very far away, and in order to communicate with God, the gap had to be filled with beings like angels. Angels were thought of as very important and were worshiped. But the Son is the only one between God and man, and people are to worship only him.
Questions.Note: A sharp respondent will probably say the purpose was to teach them that they were not to worship angels. That is about all you can expect them to know of this unless the information is in the introduction.
