Questions.Q: When was it said to the ancestors?
Questions.A: Long ago.

Questions.Q: How do we know that? How did the author know?
Questions.A: It is written in God's Book.

Questions.Q: Who is this about?
Questions.A: The Israelites' ancestors.

Questions.Q: What does it say about them?
Questions.A: (1) They heard God and yet rebelled.
(2) They were the ones Moses lead out of Egypt.
(3) God was angry with them for 40 years.
(4) They sinned and died in the wilderness.
(5) They would never be allowed in the place of rest he had for them.
(6) They were not able to go in because they did not believe.
Questions.Note: Reread and ask, "What else?" as necessary.

Questions.Q: Why do you think the author was telling them this?
Questions.A: If they rebel as their ancestors did, they will never make it into God's place of rest.

Questions.Q: Do you have any other comments to make about the passage just checked?
Questions.Alternative: Do you have any further comments to make about the passage just checked?
Do you have any other comments to make about the section just checked?

Questions.Q: Briefly tell in your own words what the author said.
Questions.A: God is offering his people a place of rest today and it is the same as it was for the ancestors of the Jews in that we must believe or we will not given the blessings of that rest.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words as much as you can remember.
What does this say about rest?
Questions.A: God has promised that he has provided a rest for his people that is still valid today.

Questions.Q: What else does it say about that? What does the author want them to do about it?
Questions.A: Be very sure/careful that they do not fail to receive it.

Questions.Q: What does this say about God's Message? Who has heard it?
Questions.A: They have heard it just like their ancestors had.

Questions.Q: What else does it say about the ancestors and the message?
Questions.A: It did them no good because they did not believe it.
Questions.Note: For Hebrews 4:2, use either the group A questions or the group B questions. It would be redundant to ask all 3 questions.
group A (Heb 4:2)

Questions.Q: How did the ancestors respond to the Message?
Questions.A: They did not believe it.
Questions.Note: For Hebrews 4:2, use either the group A questions or the group B questions. It would be redundant to ask all 3 questions.
group B (Heb 4:2)

Questions.Q: So what happened?
Questions.A: They did not benefit from it.
Questions.Note: group B (Heb 4:2)

Questions.Q: What does it say about the rest that God gives? // Who gets the rest?
Questions.A: Those who believe, receive it.
Questions.Alternative: What does it say about the rest that God gives?
Who gets the rest?

Questions.Q: It says "I was angry and made a solemn promise." Who is speaking?
Questions.A: God

Questions.Q: What does it say about the rest that he gives?
Questions.A: People who do not believe him do not receive it.
Questions.Note: There is more than one interpretation of the argument here. This and the following two questions are based on the view that the argument hinges on the expression "the rest that I give" having the present tense of "give," indicating that God's rest existed before his promise to the Israelites and is not limited to them.

Questions.Q: What else does he say? When is it that he gives that rest? Only in the past? Only in the future? Anytime? Why do you think that?
Questions.A: It should be clear that the rest is not limited to any time period.

Questions.Q: What does it say about God's rest and the creation of the world?
Questions.A: God had rest to give his people by the time he finished creating the world. It existed before his promise to the Israelites.

Questions.Q: What does this say about the seventh day?
Questions.A: Somewhere in Scripture it says God rested on the seventh day.

Questions.Q: Why is the author telling us that?
Questions.A: To prove that God had a rest/had established a rest by the time he finished creating the world.

Questions.Q: What does this say about rest?
Questions.A: They shall never come in and rest with me.

Questions.Q: Who is speaking?
Questions.A: God

Questions.Q: Why is the author telling them this?
Questions.A: To remind them that those who do not believe do not receive the rest God gives.

Questions.Q: What does it say about the message and those who first heard it?
Questions.A: Those who first heard it were not allowed to go into the place of rest God had for them.

Questions.Q: What does it say about others?
Questions.A: But there are others to whom God gives rest.

Questions.Q: What does this say about God speaking? // It says, "Today, if you will hear His voice, do not harden your hearts." Can you explain what that means?
Questions.A: If anyone hears God speaking, he should not refuse to obey.
Questions.Alternative: What does this say about God speaking?
It says, "Today, if you will hear His voice, do not harden your hearts." Can you explain what that means?

Questions.Q: If you hear him speaking when?
Questions.A: Today/anytime.
Questions.Alternative: If you hear God speaking when?
What does this say about when God might speak to a person?

Questions.Q: Who said that?
Questions.A: David
Or, God speaking through David.

Questions.Q: Why is the author telling them what David said? or What do these words of David tell/teach them about the rest God gives his people?
Questions.A: (To prove) it is still possible to receive rest from God today.
Questions.Alternative: Why is the author telling them what David said? or What do these words of David teach them about the rest God gives his people?
Why is the author telling them what David said? or What do these words of David tell them about the rest God gives his people?

Questions.Q: How do we know that David said, "If you hear him speaking today?"
Questions.A: It is in a song he wrote which is in God's Book.

Questions.Q: Do you have any other comments to make about the passage just checked?
Questions.Alternative: Do you have any further comments to make about the passage just checked?
Do you have any other comments to make about the section just checked?

Questions.Q: Briefly tell in your own words what the author said.
Questions.A: The rest Joshua led the Israelites into was not the final rest. There is another and we must make every effort to see that we do not fail to enter into it/obtain it.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words as much as you can remember.
What does this say about Joshua and the rest that God gives people?
Questions.A: It says that the rest Joshua led the people of God into was not the final rest.
Questions.Note: Use either this question (A) or the following question (B). It would be redundant to ask both questions.
question A (Heb 4:8)

Questions.Q: The Bible says Joshua led God's people into the place of rest God promised. Wasn't that the complete fulfillment of the promise?
Questions.A: No.
Questions.Note: Use either this question (B) or the preceding question (A). It would be redundant to ask both questions.
question B (Heb 4:8)

Questions.Q: How do we know that?
Questions.A: If it had been, God would not have spoken of another time of rest.

Questions.Q: What does this say about the rest? // So what is the author trying to tell them about rest?
Questions.A: There is still another rest for God's people.
Questions.Alternative: What does this say about the rest?
So what is the author trying to tell them about rest?

Questions.Q: What else does it say about it? // What is it like?
Questions.A: It is like the rest when God rested on the seventh or Sabbath Day when he finished his work.
Questions.Alternative: What else does it say about it?
What is it like?

Questions.Q: Why does it say this rest that God gives is like the rest when God rested on the seventh day?
Questions.A: Because those who obtain it/go in and rest with God will rest from their own work just as God rested from his.

Questions.Q: What does this tell them about the rest?
Questions.A: They must make every effort to enter/obtain it.
Questions.Note: For Hebrews 4:11, use either the group A questions or the group B questions. It would be redundant to ask all 3 questions.
group A (Heb 4:11)

Questions.Q: What else does he tell them?
Questions.A: They must not disobey as the people did long ago and fail to enter/obtain that rest.
Questions.Note: group A (Heb 4:11)

Questions.Q: What does the author want them to do?
Questions.A: (1) Make every effort to obtain this rest from God.
(2) Not to disobey as the people did long ago and fail to enter the rest.
Questions.Note: For Hebrews 4:11, use either the group A questions or the group B questions. It would be redundant to ask all 3 questions.
group B (Heb 4:11)

Questions.Q: Do you have any other comments to make about the passage just checked?
Questions.Alternative: Do you have any further comments to make about the passage just checked?
Do you have any other comments to make about the section just checked?

Questions.Q: Briefly tell in your own words what the author said.
Questions.A: God's words are extremely powerful and penetrating. He knows everything people even think and is the judge of whether they are right or wrong.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words as much as you can remember.
What does this say about God's words?
Questions.A: (1) His words are living and are very powerful.
(2) They are sharper than any two-edged sword.
(3) They cut through joints and marrow and where soul and spirit meet.

Questions.Q: What does it mean that God's words are like a two-edged sword and that they cut through joints and marrow and where soul and spirit meet?
Questions.A: God's words are powerful and go right through people's innermost thoughts and being. They show whether their thoughts and decisions are right or wrong.

Questions.Q: What does this say about God?
Questions.A: Nothing can be hid from him, everything in all creation is exposed and lies open before his eyes.

Questions.Q: What else does it say about him? or Why is the author telling them those things about God and his words?
Questions.A: It is to him that people must give an account of themselves.

Questions.Q: Do you have any other comments to make about the passage just checked?
Questions.Alternative: Do you have any further comments to make about the passage just checked?
Do you have any other comments to make about the section just checked?

Questions.Q: Briefly tell in your own words what the author said.
Questions.A: Jesus Christ is our High Priest who can help us in everything. So let us not be afraid to come near to God.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words as much as you can remember.
What does this say about Jesus?
Questions.A: He is our High Priest who has gone into heaven.
He is the Son of God.

Questions.Q: Why is the author telling us that?
Questions.A: We must never stop trusting him.

Questions.Q: What does this tell them about our High Priest?
Questions.A: He can understand and sympathize with our weaknesses/in all the situations which are hard for them/hard for them to live as God wants them to.

Questions.Q: What else does it say about him? // Why is he able to sympathize with them in the situations which are hard for them?
Questions.A: It says the reason he can sympathize is that he also was put into all kinds of situations in which it was hard for him to obey God. Yet he never disobeyed.
Questions.Alternative: What else does it say about him?
Why is he able to sympathize with them in the situations which are hard for them?

Questions.Q: What does this tell us about how we should come to God? // Why is the author telling them these things about Jesus?
Questions.A: Since we have someone like Jesus there in God's presence to help us, let us boldly come near to God so he can show us mercy and graciously/out of his goodness help us when we need help.
Questions.Alternative: What does this tell us about how we should come to God?
Why is the author telling them these things about Jesus?
Questions.Note: For Hebrews 4:16, use either the group A questions or the group B questions. It would be redundant to ask all 3 questions.
group A (Heb 4:16)

Questions.Q: What does the author tell us to do?
Questions.A: To boldly come near to God.
Questions.Note: For Hebrews 4:16, use either the group A questions or the group B questions. It would be redundant to ask all 3 questions.
group B (Heb 4:16)

Questions.Q: What will happen? // Why?
Questions.A: He will show us mercy and out of his goodness help us when we need help.
Because Jesus is there to help us, we need not fear.
Questions.Alternative: What will happen?
Why?
Questions.Note: group B (Heb 4:16)

Questions.Q: What do the things he just told us about Jesus have to do with our coming near to God without fear?
Questions.A: There is no need to fear since we know that we have someone like Jesus there to help us.

Questions.Q: It says we are to "come boldly to God." How can we come boldly to God? How would you explain that to someone?
Questions.A: Because Jesus is our High Priest and understands our weakness, we can trust Him to show us grace and mercy.

Questions.Q: The author just told us that God has a rest to give his people if they continue to believe and obey him. Then he said God's words are powerful and he is our judge. Now he is telling us that Jesus is our High Priest. Why is he telling us all these things?
Questions.A: They are all reasons why we must continue to believe and obey him.
Questions.Note: Few respondents will be able to answer this.

Questions.Q: Do you have any other comments to make about the passage just checked?
Questions.Alternative: Do you have any further comments to make about the passage just checked?
Do you have any other comments to make about the section just checked?

Questions.Q: Briefly tell in your own words what the author said.
Questions.A: It says a high priest is a man who is chosen to make sacrifices for the people. He understands them because he is weak also and has to make sacrifices for himself.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words as much as you can remember.
What does this tell them about a high priest?
Questions.A: (1) He is a man.
(2) He is selected and appointed to represent the people.
(3) His job is to offer gifts and sacrifices for their sins.
(4) He is able to be gentle with those who are ignorant and have wandered from God.
(5) Because he is weak, he has to offer sacrifices for his own sins as well as for others.
Questions.Note: Reread and ask, "What else?" as necessary.

Questions.Q: Why is he able to be gentle with those who are ignorant, etc.?
Questions.A: Because he has weaknesses of his own.
Questions.Alternative: Why is the high priest able to be gentle with those who are ignorant and are going astray?

Questions.Q: Do you have any other comments to make about the passage just checked?
Questions.Alternative: Do you have any further comments to make about the passage just checked?
Do you have any other comments to make about the section just checked?

Questions.Q: Briefly tell in your own words what the author said.
Questions.A: No one chooses to be high priest. God chooses the high priest and he chose Christ.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words as much as you can remember.
What does this tell/teach them about the high priest?
Questions.A: No one chooses that honor for himself.
Questions.Alternative: What does this tell them about the high priest?
What does this teach them about the high priest?

Questions.Q: What else? // Who chooses him?
Questions.A: God chooses the high priest.
Questions.Alternative: What else?
Who chooses him?

Questions.Q: What does it say about Aaron?
Questions.A: God chose him as high priest.

Questions.Q: What does this say about Christ?
Questions.A: God chose him to be High Priest.

Questions.Q: What else? // How did God show that he was choosing Christ?
Questions.A: God said to him, "You are my Son, today I officially acknowledge you as my own."
Questions.Alternative: What else?
How did God show that he was choosing Christ?

Questions.Q: Why is the author telling us this?
Questions.A: He is showing that God honored Christ/put him into an important position. He told everyone that Christ is his Son.

Questions.Q: What does this say about a priest?
Questions.A: You will be priest forever like Melchizedek.

Questions.Q: Who said this?
Questions.A: God

Questions.Q: To whom was he talking?
Questions.A: Christ

Questions.Q: Why is the author telling them this?
Questions.A: To show that God chose Christ as High Priest.

Questions.Q: Do you have any other comments to make about the passage just checked?
Questions.Alternative: Do you have any further comments to make about the passage just checked?
Do you have any other comments to make about the section just checked?

Questions.Q: Briefly tell in your own words what the author said.
Questions.A: Jesus learned to obey God when he had to suffer to obey him. And when God prepared him to be our High Priest in that way, he made him a priest like Melchizedek.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words as much as you can remember.
What does this say about Jesus?
Questions.A: When he was on earth, he prayed intensely to God who could have saved him from death.

Questions.Q: Did God hear him? Yes. Why?
Questions.A: Because Jesus was humble and wanted to obey God.

Questions.Q: What does this say about Jesus?
Questions.A: (1) Even though he was God's son, he learned what it meant to obey God when he had to suffer in order to obey.
(2) [After God prepared him in this way,] He made him the One who gives eternal life to people who obey God.
(3) God made him a High Priest, one like Melchizedek.
Questions.Note: Reread and ask, "What else?" as necessary.

Questions.Q: It says Jesus learned what it meant to obey when he had to suffer in order to obey. What do you think that means? Why would Jesus have to suffer in order to obey? How would you explain that to someone?
Questions.A: It was hard for him to die on the Cross and endure having God turn his back on him. Furthermore he was a man as well as God's Son. And as man's representative before God, he must go through what people go through to learn obedience. There may be other reasons, but always in contrast to our usual reason of sinfulness.
Questions.Note: These answers are primarily for the translator, as very few respondents will be able to give these reasons. The translator should just be sure that the respondent does not understand a wrong reason.

Questions.Q: According to this, if a person wants eternal life/salvation, where does he get it / to whom will he go to get it?
Questions.A: [From] Jesus.
Questions.Alternative: According to this (verse 9), if a person wants eternal life, where does he get it?
According to this (verse 9), if a person wants eternal life, to whom will he go to get it?
According to this, if a person wants eternal life, where does he get it?
According to this, if a person wants eternal life, to whom will he go to get it?
According to this, from whom does a person get eternal life?
According to this, who is the source of eternal salvation?

Questions.Q: When did God make him the One who gives eternal life to people? // What happened before God made him the One to give eternal life?
Questions.A: God made him perfect/prepared through suffering.
Questions.Alternative: When did God make him the One who gives eternal life to people?
What happened before God made him the One to give eternal life?

Questions.Q: And who does he give eternal life to?
Questions.A: To those who obey God.

Questions.Q: Why is the author telling all these things about Jesus? (The translator could give the respondent a hint by asking "Why did he write this paper?")
Questions.A: He is telling the Jews how important Jesus is because they were about to leave him and go back to their old religion.

Questions.Q: It says God made him a priest after the order of/like Melchizedek. What do you think that means?
Questions.Note: The answer is not clear in this passage so the respondent will probably say he doesn't know. That is sufficient at this point. Chapter 7 will explain this in more detail.
Questions.Alternative: It says God made him a priest after the order of Melchizedek. What do you think that means?
It says God made him a priest like Melchizedek. What do you think that means?

Questions.Q: Do you have any other comments to make about the passage just checked?
Questions.Alternative: Do you have any further comments to make about the passage just checked?
Do you have any other comments to make about the section just checked?

Questions.Q: Briefly tell in your own words what the author said.
Questions.A: The author had much to tell them, but it was too hard to explain to them because they were like children in their understanding.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words as much as you can remember.
What does the author say about "this matter" or topic he is telling them about?
Questions.A: He had much to tell them but it was complicated and especially hard to explain to them.

Questions.Q: The author says he has much to say to them about "this matter"/topic. What is the topic?
Questions.A: The priesthood of Jesus, which is like that of Melchizedek.
Questions.Alternative: The author says he has much to say to them about "this matter". What is this matter?
The author says he has much to say to them about "this topic. What is the topic?
What is the topic?
What is he trying to tell them about?

Questions.Q: Why [was it hard to explain]?
Questions.A: Because they had become slow to understand/mentally lazy and not capable of grasping complicated ideas.
Questions.Alternative: Why was it hard to explain?
Why?
Why was it difficult to explain?
Why was it hard to explain about the priesthood of Jesus?
Why was it difficult to explain about the priesthood of Jesus?
Why was it hard to explain how the priesthood of Jesus was like that of Melchizedek?
Why was it difficult to explain how the priesthood of Jesus was like that of Melchizedek?

Questions.Q: What does he say about the people he is writing to?
Questions.A: (1) They should be teaching others but instead they still have to be taught the first lessons they heard about God.
(2) They are like little children who have to drink milk and can't eat solid food.

Questions.Q: The author says they are like little children who have to drink milk, etc. What did he mean by that?
Questions.A: They can't understand anything advanced or complicated.

Questions.Q: What does this say about children/infants?
Questions.A: They don't know right from wrong.
Questions.Alternative: What does this say about children?
What does this say about infants?

Questions.Q: Again he says they are like children. What does he mean this time?
Questions.A: He is saying they do not know right from wrong like little children.

Questions.Q: What does this say about [solid] food?
Questions.A: Solid food is for adults.
Questions.Alternative: What does this say about food?
What does this say about solid food?

Questions.Q: What else does he say about adults/those who are mature?
Questions.A: They have trained themselves to know the difference in good and evil.
Questions.Alternative: What else does he say about adults?
What else does he say about those who are mature?

Questions.Q: Why is he talking about "solid food?" What does he mean by that?
Questions.A: Solid food = complicated/advanced teaching about God.
Questions.Alternative: What does he mean by "solid food" in this passage?

Questions.Q: Do you have any other comments to make about the passage just checked?
Questions.Alternative: Do you have any further comments to make about the passage just checked?
Do you have any other comments to make about the section just checked?

Questions.Q: Briefly tell in your own words what the author said.
Questions.A: Let us leave the basics/beginning doctrines and go on to more advanced doctrines and spiritual maturity.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words as much as you can remember.
What does he say about teaching/lessons? // What does the author want the readers to do?
Questions.A: Leave off going over and over the first lessons and learn to obey Christ better/more and more.
Questions.Alternative: What does he say about teaching?
What does he say about lessons?
What does the author want the readers to do?

Questions.Q: What are those first lessons?
Questions.A: (1) People must turn away from doing things that will cause them to be separated from God forever.
(2) They must trust in God (who can forgive their sins and cause them to live forever).
(3) People must be baptized in water to show they belong to Christ.
(4) When the church leaders [have a special ceremony where they] put their hands on a believer, it shows that God has given that person/believer his Spirit.
(5) Someday God will raise the dead to life.
(6) And He will judge everyone according to the way they lived on earth and will punish forever those who do not belong to Christ.
Questions.Alternative: What are those elementary teachings?
Questions.Note: Reread and ask, "What else?" as necessary.

The translator may need to have each doctrine read and ask what the respondent understands by what is said there. An unbeliever especially will not fully understand these doctrines, but the surface meaning should be clear.

Questions.Q: Now what does he say about those lessons?
Questions.A: Leave them and go on to more advanced doctrines and to spiritual maturity.

Questions.Q: What does he say about God?
Questions.A: If God allows it, that's what they will do.

Questions.Q: It says, "if God allows." Why does it say that? Why wouldn't God allow them to go on to advanced lessons?
Questions.A: This comment may only mean the usual subordinating of everything to God's will. See commentaries.
Questions.Note: In the next section, we see that God may not allow people to come back to him if they have turned their backs on him.

Questions.Q: Do you have any other comments to make about the passage just checked?
Questions.Alternative: Do you have any further comments to make about the passage just checked?
Do you have any other comments to make about the section just checked?

Questions.Q: Briefly tell in your own words what the author said.
Questions.A: It is impossible for some people to repent again and come back to God.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words as much as you can.
What kind of people is the author referring to in these verses?
Questions.A: (1) Those who have come to understand God's Message to us.
(2) They have enjoyed/received the good things God gives his people.
(3) They have experienced the Holy Spirit in their lives (or received the Holy Spirit).
(4) They know the joy of having God speak to them.
(5) They have seen God using his power as he will in the Coming Age.
Questions.Note: Reread and ask, "What else?" as necessary.

The translator may need to go back and ask what the respondent understands by "they have come to understand God's Message" and "they have received the good things God gives his people" and "experienced the Holy Spirit in their lives" and "seen God using his power as He will in the Coming Age."

Questions.Q: What does this say about those people?
Questions.A: (1) After all that, they turned away from God.
(2) And now it is impossible for them to repent again.

Questions.Q: Why [is it impossible for them to repent again]?
Questions.A: Because they have nailed the Son of God to the Cross once more and exposed him to open shame.
Questions.Alternative: Why?
Why is it impossible for them to repent again?

Questions.Q: What does that mean?
Questions.A: They have put him to shame before everyone because they have rejected him just like the people who crucified him.

Questions.Q: What does this say about God? // What does God do with a field/ground which produces well?
Questions.A: Literal answer: God blesses the ground that drinks the rain and grows useful plants for those who cultivate it.
Metaphorical answer: God blesses people who receive His gifts (enlightenment, Holy Spirit, word of God, power) and bear spiritual fruit / continue to follow Him.
Questions.Note: If respondent only gives a literal answer, subsequent questions will prompt for metaphorical significance.
Questions.Alternative: What does this say about God?
What does God do with a field which produces well?
What does God do with ground which produces well?
What does God do with a field which produces a good harvest?
What does God do with ground which produces a good harvest?

Questions.Q: What does this say about the ground?
Questions.A: If it grows thorns and weeds, it is in danger because God may curse it and destroy it with fire.

Questions.Q: Why is the author telling us about a field/ground?
Questions.A: He was telling about people who cannot repent and now he is talking about a field (as a metaphor for peoples' hearts).
Questions.Note: Use follow-up questions as needed to determine whether respondent understands the metaphor.
Questions.Alternative: Why is the author telling us about a field?
Why is the author telling us about ground?

Questions.Q: Why? // What does each part of the metaphor represent? // What does the ground/field represent? What does the rain represent? What does the useful vegetation represent? What do the thorns and thistles represent? What does burning represent?
Questions.A: It is the same with the people as it is with the ground. Their hearts are like the ground and God's Message is like the rain. When God has spoken to them they should become and live like people who are spiritually mature/adults in God's ways. When they do, God blesses them. But if they remain useless to him, they are in danger of being cursed by him and destroyed the same way useless weeds are burned.
Questions.Note: This is a follow-up to the preceding two questions. Whether this is needed and the exact question(s) to ask will depend in part on the previous response.
Questions.Alternative: Why?
What does each part of the metaphor represent?
What does the ground represent? What does the rain represent? What does the useful vegetation represent? What do the thorns and thistles represent? What does burning represent?
What does the field represent? What does the rain represent? What does the useful vegetation represent? What do the thorns and thistles represent? What does burning represent?

Questions.Q: Do you have any other comments to make about the passage just checked?
Questions.Alternative: Do you have any further comments to make about the passage just checked?
Do you have any other comments to make about the section just checked?

Questions.Q: Briefly tell in your own words what the author said.
Questions.A: The author doesn't think those he is writing to are like those people he has just described as leaving God. He just wants to be sure they don't become lax in their relationship to God.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words as much as you can remember.
What does the author say to those he is writing to?
Questions.A: He is sure they have not left Christ.

Questions.Q: Why does he think that about them?
Questions.A: Because he has seen that God is giving them the good things he gives those who live like people who are spiritually mature/useful to him (like the good ground yields good fruit and receives God's blessing).

Questions.Q: What does this say about God?
Questions.A: He is not unfair.

Questions.Q: What else? or Why does the author say that?
Questions.A: He will not forget the work those people did or how they showed God they loved him by helping their fellow Christians.

Questions.Q: What does the author say to them here?

Questions.Q: Briefly tell in your own words what the author said.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words as much as you can remember.

Questions.A: (1) They were part of a whole system of worship set up by Moses.
(2) If that system was perfect/adequate/able to make people acceptable to enter God's presence, there would have been no need for a different kind of priest.

Questions.Q: What does he mean by a different kind of priest?
Questions.A: One like Melchizedek, not like the Levites who descended from Aaron.

Questions.A: (1) No member ever served as priest.

Questions.Q: Why is the author saying all this about the Levitical priests and Melchizedek and Jesus? What is he trying to tell those people to whom he was writing?
Questions.A: Those people were about to leave Jesus and go back to their old way of worshiping with the Levitical priests. He was trying to tell them that they would be going back to an inferior system. That system could not make people acceptable to enter God's presence.

(4) In that first room was a lamp and a table with bread set there as an offering/gift for God. (2)
(5) A thick curtain separated the first and second rooms in the tent. (3)
(6) That second room was called the Most Holy Place (Place where God lived). (3)
(7) In front of the curtain was a gold table/altar where the priests burned incense. (4)
(8) Inside the second room was a chest covered with gold inside and out. (4)
(9) The chest was called the Chest of the Agreement. (4)

(10) Inside the chest was a gold jar with a sample of the manna/food with which God fed the people in the desert, Aaron's rod that sprouted, grew leaves, etc., and the two flat pieces of stone with the commandments written on them. (4)
(11) Above that chest were two images of the special angels that are always with God. (5)

(12) Those angels are attached to the lid with their wings spread out over the chest where (the high priest placed the blood of a sacrificed animal once a year to show that) God forgave people's sins. (5)

Questions.Q: Briefly tell in your own words what the author said.

Questions.Q: What else does it say about the way being open?

Questions.Q: What kind of sin was the blood supposed to pay for?

Questions.Q: It says the old way of worship showed that animal sacrifices and gifts were not sufficient to make people acceptable to God or not sufficient to make their hearts clean from sin. How did it show that?

Questions.Q: Briefly tell in your own words what the author said.
Questions.A: The Agreements God made with man were like the agreement people make to give someone something when they die (wills). The people cannot receive the things until after the person's death. (They are not valid until there is a death.) It was that way with that First Agreement God made with Moses.

Questions.A: To prove that an animal had died to pay for his sins and the sins of the people.

Questions.A: To prove that he had died for the sins of people.

Questions.Q: Why didn't he just take the blood of animals like the Jewish priests?
