Section.heading: James 1:1-8 James told the brothers/believers in Jesus that trials help their faith to grow and become mature. He also said if anyone wants wisdom, he must ask God and not doubt that God will give it to him.

Questions.Q: What did he tell them they should feel when they experience different kinds of trials/hardships?
Questions.A: He told them that they should be joyful. (2)
Questions.Alternative: What did he tell them they should feel when they experience different kinds of trials?
What did he tell them they should feel when they experience different kinds of hardships?

Questions.Q: What must a person do when he prays?
Questions.A: He must believe without any doubt [that God will answer his prayer]. (6)

Questions.Q: What does someone do when he believes?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "To believe in a person" means to trust someone, to rely on someone, to make a positive act of commitment to someone.
Questions.Note: See "believe" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Who was the writer of this letter?
Questions.A: He was James.
He was a servant of God
and of the Lord Jesus Christ. (1)

Questions.Q: What do you think a servant does?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A servant is a person who works for someone. A good servant does what that other person tells him to do. Servants receive pay for their work, while slaves do not receive pay.
Questions.Note: See "servant" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Who do you think God is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In English, the term "God" with a capital "G" is used to refer to the one supreme Creator. The term "god" with a small "g", as in "a god" or "many gods", can refer to any spiritual being that people worship. The Greek word theos can be used in the same two ways. In many languages the term for God is a proper name and cannot be used to refer to anyone except the one supreme creator of the world. It cannot be pluralized.
Questions.Note: See "God" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What does it mean to you to have someone as your lord?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A lord is someone who has authority over someone. To call someone your Lord means that you have given him control over your life. The Lord, in this case, is Jesus. Every Christian strives to make Jesus his lord, by giving Him complete control. (See "Lord" in KBT in the "God" entry.)

Questions.Q: To whom was James writing?
Questions.A: He wrote to the twelve tribes that were scattered among the nations. (1)

Questions.Q: What does the word "tribe" mean to you?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "Tribe" may refer to an extended family within a nation who are descended from a common ancestor, as in the case of the twelve tribes of Israel, who are descended from the twelve sons of Israel. (See "tribe" in KBT in the "gentile" entry and the "Levite" entry.)

Questions.Q: What does the word "nation" mean to you?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Here the term means that the 12 Jewish tribes had scattered to other countries/other groups of people who were not Jews. "Nation" is referring to the people who make up that nation. This community of people possesses a more or less defined territory of land and government. (See "nation" in KBT in the "gentile" entry.)

Questions.Q: What do you think James meant when he said "my brothers"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He meant those who were fellow-followers of Jesus. (2) (See "brother" in KBT in the "disciple" entry.)
Questions.Note: UBS states that this letter was not addressed only to male Christians.

Questions.Q: What was the reason that they should feel joyful?
Questions.A: It was that, as they experienced trials, they learned to believe that God would help them. (3)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to have faith in someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Faith is the quality of trusting someone. (See "faith" in KBT in the "believe, believing, belief, faith, trust" entry.)

Questions.Q: What will perseverance do for them?
Questions.A: If they keep on believing that God does help them, they will learn to believe him whenever anything happens to them. They will not forsake God/turn away from God in any circumstance. (4)

Questions.Q: What should they do if they lack wisdom/the wisdom that God gives?
Questions.A: They should pray to God and ask him to give them wisdom. (5)
Questions.Alternative: What should they do if they lack wisdom?
What should they do if they lack the wisdom that God gives?

Questions.Q: What will God do if they do this?
Questions.A: He will give wisdom to them. (5)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that he will give them wisdom when they ask him for it in prayer?
Questions.A: It is because he is generous and he does not find fault/shame/scold those who ask things from him. (5)

Questions.Q: What is a person like who doubts [whether or not God will answer his prayer]?
Questions.A: He is like a wave of the sea blown back and forth by the wind. (6)
Questions.Alternative: What is a person like who doubts whether or not God will answer his prayer?
What is a person like who doubts?

Questions.Q: What should a person know who doubts [that God will answer his prayer]?
Questions.A: He should not think that the Lord will give him anything. (6-7)
Questions.Alternative: What should a person know who doubts that God will answer his prayer?
What should a person know who doubts?

Questions.Q: What else is characteristic of a person who doubts God?
Questions.A: He is a person who can never make up his mind about what he thinks and is not consistent in his behavior. (8)

Section.heading: James 1:9-11 James gave some advice to the poor believers and to the rich believers. He told them how they should feel about the position in which they found themselves.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the basic meaning (theme) of what James said in these verses?
Questions.A: James gave advice to both the rich and to the poor believers concerning what their attitude toward life should be. (9-10)

Questions.Q: If a brother is poor, what should he do?
Questions.A: He should rejoice/be happy in his high position/when [God] makes him prosper. (9)

Questions.Q: If a brother is rich, what should he do?
Questions.A: He should rejoice/be happy in his low position/when [God] causes him to lose his riches. (10)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that he should rejoice?
Questions.A: He should rejoice because he will pass away like a flower. (10)

Questions.Q: What happens to a plant and its flower when the sun shines on it with its blazing heat?
Questions.A: The plant withers, its flower falls off
and its beauty is destroyed. (11)

Questions.Q: How are a flower and a rich man alike?
Questions.A: They both live for a short time and then they both die. (11)
Questions.Alternative: How are a flower and a rich person alike?

Section.heading: James 1:12-18 When a person has trials, he should continue to believe that God will help him. God does not send temptations to believers. They are tempted because of their own evil desires that lead to sin.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the basic meaning (theme) of what James said in these verses?
Questions.A: He told them that God will help them when they continue to believe him when they are tempted and tried.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that a man is blessed [by God] who perseveres when he experiences trials?
Questions.A: A man is blessed [by God] because after he has stood the test he will receive the victor's crown which is eternal life that God has promised to those who love him. (12)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that a man is blessed by God who perseveres when he experiences trials?
What is the reason that a man is blessed who perseveres when he experiences trials?
Why is a man blessed by God who perseveres when he experiences trials?
Why is a man blessed who perseveres when he experiences trials?
What is the reason that a person is blessed by God who perseveres when he experiences trials?
What is the reason that a person is blessed who perseveres when he experiences trials?
Why is a person blessed by God who perseveres when he experiences trials?
Why is a person blessed who perseveres when he experiences trials?
Why is a person blessed who perseveres under trial?
Why is a person blessed who endures temptation?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means, when someone loves someone else?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The person who loves another person seeks the good of that person. His attitude to the one whom he loves is an attitude of persistent and selfless goodwill.
Questions.Note: See "love" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to make a promise?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that someone will make a declaration that he will do or will refrain from doing something specified. (See "promise" in KBT in the "covenant" entry.)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to be blessed?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Being in a desirable state or position, fortunate.
Questions.Note: See "bless, blessed, blessing" in KBT.

Questions.Q: When a person is tempted [by someone/something], what must he be careful not to do?
Questions.A: He must not say that God is the one who tempts him. (13)
Questions.Alternative: When a person is tempted by someone, what must he be careful not to do?
When a person is tempted by something, what must he be careful not to do?
When a person is tempted, what must he be careful not to do?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that he should not say that?
Questions.A: He should not say that because God never tempts anyone and also God cannot be tempted to do evil/to do wrong. (13)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to be tempted [by someone/something] to do something bad/wrong?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: When someone/something tempts you to do something bad or evil, he may promise you some kind of pleasure or gain from doing it.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think it means to be tempted by someone to do something bad?
What do you think it means to be tempted by someone to do something wrong?
What do you think it means to be tempted by something to do something bad?
What do you think it means to be tempted by something to do something wrong?
What do you think it means to be tempted to do something bad?
What do you think it means to be tempted to do something wrong?

Questions.Q: If God never tempts anyone to do evil, then why is it that people are easily/often tempted to do what is sinful?
Questions.A: Everyone has his/her own desire to do evil. (14)
Questions.Alternative: If God never tempts anyone to do evil, then why is it that people are easily tempted to do what is sinful?
If God never tempts anyone to do evil, then why is it that people are often tempted to do what is sinful?

Questions.Q: If anyone yields to these evil desires, what will happen?
Questions.A: He will commit sin. (15)

Questions.Q: What is the final outcome/result, if anyone yields to the sinful things he wants to do?
Questions.A: If he does not repent, he will die [physically and spiritually], and he will never be with God. (15)
Questions.Alternative: What is the final outcome, if anyone yields to the sinful things he wants to do?
What is the final result, if anyone yields to the sinful things he wants to do?

Questions.Q: What does a person do when he sins?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He deliberately keeps on doing those things that displease God.
Questions.Note: See "sin" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did he tell them not to do?
Questions.A: He told them not to be deceived, that is not to think that God caused people to sin. (16)

Questions.Q: What did he say that God gives to them?
Questions.A: He told them that God/the Father gives them good and perfect gifts. (17)

Questions.Q: In what way is God different from the shifting shadows?
Questions.A: They change, but he never changes. (17)

Questions.Q: What did God choose to do?
Questions.A: He chose to cause us to be his children through the word of truth/the Christian message/the gospel. (18)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that he did this?
Questions.A: He did this because he wanted us to be a kind of first fruits of all he created. // He wanted us to occupy first place among all his creatures. // He wanted us to be the first to be redeemed of the total number of God's creatures to be redeemed. (18)

Section.heading: James 1:19-27 James told the brothers that they not only should listen to the gospel but they should also do what the gospel says.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the basic meaning (theme) of what James said in these verses?
Questions.A: Everyone not only must listen to God's word, but they must also obey it. (22)
He wrote about what the person who truly believes God should do. (27)

Questions.Q: What did he tell the brothers to remember to do?
Questions.A: They must be quick/eager to listen,
they must not be hasty in what they say,
and they must not become angry easily. (19)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that a person should not become angry easily?
Questions.A: A person should not become angry easily because the person who is angry does not do the things that God wants him to do. (20)

Questions.Q: What should they do instead?
Questions.A: They must get rid of/remove all bad/impure thoughts and stop doing the bad things they are/might be doing. (21)

Questions.Q: What should they submissively/humbly follow/obey?
Questions.A: They should obey the word [of God] that [he] has placed in their hearts/minds. (21)
Questions.Alternative: What should they submissively follow?
What should they submissively obey?
What should they humbly follow?
What should they humbly obey?

Questions.Q: What does "heart" mean to you?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The most common use of the word "heart" in the Bible is to refer to the spiritual center or innermost part of a human being. In Hebrew and Greek "heart" is most commonly associated with thoughts and ideas.
Questions.Note: See "heart" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What is God's word able to do?
Questions.A: It has the ability to save them. (21)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to save you?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that a person will rescue someone else out of a dangerous situation. In this verse Jesus came to mankind to rescue them from an eternity in Hell.
Questions.Note: See "save" in KBT.

Questions.Q: How is it possible for them to deceive themselves?
Questions.A: They will deceive themselves if they think that they will be saved just by hearing God's word.
They must also do what it tells them to do. (22)

Questions.Q: What is a person like, who listens to the word, but does not do what it says?
Questions.A: He is like a man who looks at his face in a mirror and immediately goes away from the mirror and forgets what he looks like. // He does not give attention to what he looks like, just as one who does not give attention/obey God's word. (23-24)

Questions.Q: What does this perfect law give to people?
Questions.A: It gives them freedom [from sin]. (25)

Questions.Q: What is meant by the phrase/words "perfect law"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that the gospel is the perfect rule for conduct, and is perfect in itself. (See "perfect law" in Exegetical Summary on James.)
Questions.Alternative: What is meant by the phrase "perfect law"?
What is meant by the words "perfect law"?

Questions.Q: If a person considers carefully not only what [God's] law says, but also does what it tells him to do, what will [God] do to/for him?
Questions.A: [God] will make him happy in all that he does. (25)
Questions.Alternative: If a person considers carefully not only what God's law says, but also does what it tells him to do, what will God do to him?
If a person considers carefully not only what God's law says, but also does what it tells him to do, what will God do for him?
If a person considers carefully not only what the law says, but also does what it tells him to do, what will God do to him?
If a person considers carefully not only what the law says, but also does what it tells him to do, what will God do for him?

Questions.Q: What value/use is it for a person to say/claim that he is a Christian, but he does not control what he says/speaks bad/evil things?
Questions.A: It is of no use at all. // It is worthless. (26)
Questions.Alternative: What value is it for a person to say that he is a Christian, but he does not control what he says?
What value is it for a person to say that he is a Christian, but he speaks bad things?
What value is it for a person to say that he is a Christian, but he speaks evil things?
What value is it for a person to claim that he is a Christian, but he does not control what he says?
What value is it for a person to claim that he is a Christian, but he speaks bad things?
What value is it for a person to claim that he is a Christian, but he speaks evil things?
What use is it for a person to say that he is a Christian, but he does not control what he says?
What use is it for a person to say that he is a Christian, but he speaks bad things?
What use is it for a person to say that he is a Christian, but he speaks evil things?
What use is it for a person to claim that he is a Christian, but he does not control what he says?
What use is it for a person to claim that he is a Christian, but he speaks bad things?
What use is it for a person to claim that he is a Christian, but he speaks evil things?

Questions.Q: What is a person like this doing to himself?
Questions.A: He is deceiving himself because he thinks that he really is a good Christian. (26)

Questions.Q: When does God the Father accept someone as a genuine believer [in Jesus]?
Questions.A: He regards a person as a good Christian when he is involved in taking care of widows and orphans
and does not participate in or do what unbelievers do. (27)
Questions.Alternative: When does God the Father accept someone as a genuine believer in Jesus?
When does God the Father accept someone as a genuine believer?

Questions.Q: What do you think "world" means in this verse?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It refers to all the people who are opposed to God and Christ.
Questions.Note: See "world" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think it means, when something is pure?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: This is a figure of speech, which might be paraphrased: If a person wants to follow God sincerely and in a way that is acceptable (to God), this is what he will do. (See "pure" in KBT in the "clean" entry.)

Section.heading: James 2:1-13 James told the believers that it was wrong for them to show more favor to rich people than to poor people.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the basic meaning (theme) of what James said in these verses?
Questions.A: James told the believers that it was wrong for them to treat rich people with more respect than they treated poor people. They should treat all people alike regardless of their status/position in life. (3-4)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to call our Lord Jesus Christ glorious?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that Jesus Christ is wonderful.
Questions.Note: See "glorious" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did he tell them not to do?
Questions.A: He told them not to show favoritism/treat people in different ways according to how they look. (1)

Questions.Q: In this example two people came into their meeting. Who were these two people?
Questions.A: One was a rich person and one was a poor person. (2)

Questions.Q: What was the rich person wearing?
Questions.A: The rich person was wearing expensive clothes and a gold ring. (2)

Questions.Q: What was the poor person wearing?
Questions.A: The poor person was wearing shabby clothes. (2)

Questions.Q: How did the believers treat the rich person?
Questions.A: They showed respect to him by giving him a place of honor. (3)

Questions.Q: How did the believers treat the poor person?
Questions.A: They were disrespectful to him by telling him to stand or sit on the floor. (3)

Questions.Q: If they show favoritism to the rich, what bad thing did James say that they were guilty of doing?
Questions.A: They were making distinctions between the rich people and the poor people, based on evil thoughts. (4)

Questions.Q: What do you think these evil thoughts were/are?
Questions.A: They regarded/thought that the rich people were better than the poor people. (4)
Questions.Alternative: What do you think these evil thoughts were?
What do you think these evil thoughts are?

Questions.Q: How do we know that the rich are not superior to/better than the poor?
Questions.A: God chose those who are poor. (5)
Questions.Alternative: How do we know that the rich are not superior to the poor?
How do we know that the rich are not better than the poor?

Questions.Q: What do you think the kingdom of God is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The kingdom of God consists of God's people.
Questions.Note: See "kingdom of God" in KBT.

Questions.Q: How had the people, to whom James was writing, treat the poor?
Questions.A: They insulted/dishonored/despised the poor. (6)

Questions.Q: Of what three things are the rich characteristically guilty?
Questions.A: They oppress/exploit/dominate the believers.
They sue the believers in court.
They blaspheme/speak evil of him/Jesus Christ. (6-7)
Questions.Note: Check to make sure that the respondent understands the questions in verses 6 and 7 as rhetorical questions. (I. e., It's not that James doesn't know the answer to these questions; but he is using rhetorical questions as a teaching technique to help them understand that their tendency to favor the rich over the poor is not proper nor well founded).

Questions.Q: What very important law/command [has God] given in his word?
Questions.A: [God] has given the law that states that everyone must love others just as they love themselves. (8)
Questions.Alternative: What very important law has God given in his word?
What very important command has God given in his word?

Questions.Q: What did James say about what they were doing, if they were obeying this law?
Questions.A: They were doing the right thing. (8)

Questions.Q: But what if they show favoritism/treat some people in different ways according to how they look?
Questions.A: Then they have sinned, because they have not followed [God's] royal/important law to love others as they love themselves. (9)
Questions.Alternative: But what if they show favoritism according to how they look?
But what if they treat some people in different ways according to how they look?

Questions.Q: What did James say about a person who strives to follow/obey all of God's law, but there is one command he fails to follow?
Questions.A: He is guilty of breaking all of the law. (10)
Questions.Alternative: What did James say about a person who strives to follow all of God's law, but there is one command he fails to follow?
What did James say about a person who strives to obey all of God's law, but there is one command he fails to follow?

Questions.Q: What example did James tell the people to show/prove this?
Questions.A: He told them that even if someone does not commit adultery but he kills people, he has sinned. // Even though he has obeyed [God's] command not to commit adultery, he has sinned against [God's] command which says he should not kill. (11)
Questions.Alternative: What example did James tell the people to show this?
What example did James tell the people to prove this?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to commit adultery with another person?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means to have sex with a person who is not his wife or with one who is not her husband.

Questions.Q: What did he tell them to do?
Questions.A: He told them to say and do things like people who will be judged by [God's] law that gives them freedom [from sin]. (12)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to judge someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means someone/a judge will determine if a person is guilty or not guilty of doing something wrong. He does this by assessing the evidence connected to the person and what he may have done.
Questions.Note: See "judge" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What will happen to the person who has not shown mercy to others?
Questions.A: [God] will not be merciful to him when he judges that person. (13)

Questions.Q: What will happen to the person who has been merciful to others?
Questions.A: [God] will be merciful to that person when he judges him. (13)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means, that someone is merciful to someone else?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "Mercy" in the New Testament is an act of kindness by God or someone else toward people who are in need. The person (God or man) acts to relieve some kind of suffering or distress.
Questions.Note: See "mercy" in KBT.

Section.heading: James 2:14-26 Christians not only must believe in Jesus Christ but also they must help others. That will demonstrate that they believe in Jesus Christ.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the basic meaning (theme) of what James said in these verses?
Questions.A: A person must show that he believes Christ by doing something good to/for others. If he does not do good to others, he is not doing as a Christian should do. (17, 20, 26)

Questions.Q: What did James ask the Christians in this verse?
Questions.A: He asked them what good it was for someone to say that they had faith but they did not do good to others.
He also asked them if this kind of faith can save them. (14)

Questions.Q: What did James ask the Christians in this verse?
Questions.A: He asked them what good it was if a person ignores the needs of fellow Christians like those in the example, which James wrote, and just says, "Go, keep warm and well fed." (15-16)

Questions.Q: What would James say in reply to someone who said that one person believes and another person performs good deeds?
Questions.A: He would reply to that person by saying "Prove to me, if you can, that a Christian can believe and not perform good deeds. But I, by means of my good deeds, will prove to you that I believe. (18)
Questions.Note: UBS suggests translating this verse like this.

Questions.Q: How many Gods are there?
Questions.A: There is only one God. (19)

Questions.Q: What do the demons believe?
Questions.A: They also believe that there is one God. (19)

Questions.Q: What do you think a demon is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A demon is a spiritual being that serves Satan as his agent, being under his authority. They have power to oppress a human being and even take control of him. (See "demon" in KBT in the "evil spirit, unclean spirit" entry.)

Questions.Q: What did James ask this person?
Questions.A: He asked him if he wanted evidence/proof that faith without deeds is useless. (20)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that [God] considered Abraham righteous?
Questions.A: He considered Abraham righteous because he obeyed God by offering his son, Isaac, on the altar. (21)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that God considered Abraham righteous?
What is the reason that Abraham was considered righteous?
Why did God consider Abraham righteous?
Why was Abraham considered righteous?

Questions.Q: What do you think an altar is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: An altar is a kind of table or platform where animals or other offerings are given by someone to God.
Questions.Note: See "altar" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to be righteous?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that a person is in a state of having been accepted by God as being right. (See "righteousness" in KBT in the "just, justify" entry.)

Questions.Q: How was Abraham's faith made complete?
Questions.A: It was made complete through what he did. (22)

Questions.Q: What did God do when Abraham believed [what God said to/promised him]?
Questions.A: [God] counted/accepted him as a righteous person. (23)
Questions.Alternative: What did God do when Abraham believed what God said to him?
What did God do when Abraham believed what God said promised him?
What did God do when Abraham believed?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that [God] called Abraham his friend?
Questions.A: He called Abraham his friend because Abraham believed God. (23)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that God called Abraham his friend?
What is the reason that Abraham was called God's friend?
What is the reason that Abraham was called a friend of God?
Why did God call Abraham his friend?
Why was Abraham called God's friend?
Why was Abraham called a friend of God?

Questions.Q: How is a person justified [with/before God]?
Questions.A: A person is justified [with God] through his faith and what he does with it. (24)
Questions.Alternative: How is a person justified with God?
How is a person justified before God?
How is a person justified?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means, when someone is justified with God?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It refers to the state of being accepted by God in good standing with him on the basis of one's faith in Christ.
Questions.Note: See "justify" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What good thing did Rahab do so that [God] considered her a righteous person?
Questions.A: She gave lodging to the Jewish spies and helped them to escape in a different direction. (25)
Questions.Alternative: What good thing did Rahab do so that God considered her a righteous person?
What good thing did Rahab do so that God considered her righteous?
What good thing did Rahab do so that she was considered a righteous person?
What good thing did Rahab do to be considered a righteous person?
What good thing did Rahab do to be considered righteous?

Questions.Q: What did James compare in this verse?
Questions.A: He said that a person who does not have his spirit is dead. He can not do anything. Likewise, if a person does not do anything good, his faith is useless/dead. (26)

Section.heading: James 3:1-12 Christians need to control how they talk, because some people praise God and some people curse men.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the basic meaning (theme) of what James said in these verses?
Questions.A: James told about all the harm we do when we do not control what we say. (6, 8-9)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that James warned them not to be too eager to become teachers [of God's word]?
Questions.A: He warned them because anyone who teaches [God's word] will be judged more strictly [by God]. (1)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that James warned them not to be too eager to become teachers of God's word?
What is the reason that James warned them not to be too eager to become teachers?

Questions.Q: How or in what way are all people the same?
Questions.A: Everyone makes mistakes. (2)

Questions.Q: If it were possible for someone to never make a mistake in what he says, what would this person be like?
Questions.A: He would be a perfect person who is able to control all that he does. (2)

Questions.Q: How is anyone able to control a horse?
Questions.A: Anyone can control a horse by putting a bit into the horse's mouth, and use it to turn the whole animal. (3)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that a ship would be hard for someone to steer?
Questions.A: It is hard because it is big and is blown/driven by strong winds. (4)

Questions.Q: How is the pilot able to steer the ship?
Questions.A: He can steer it by using a very small rudder. (4)

Questions.Q: Where does the ship go when the pilot steers it by using the rudder?
Questions.A: The ship will go wherever the pilot wants it to go. (4)

Questions.Q: What does a small spark have the ability to do?
Questions.A: A small spark can set a large forest on fire. (5)

Questions.Q: What four small objects did James compare in verses 3-5?
Questions.A: A bit, a ship's rudder, the tongue or the mouth of a person and a small spark. (3-5)

Questions.Q: In what way are these four the same?
Questions.A: Although they are very small, they each have great ability to control or to cause affects. (3-5)

Questions.Q: What did James say about the tongue/mouth/lips?
Questions.A: He said it is like a fire that is destructive.
It shows that we have sinned much.
It corrupts the whole person. // It affects all that a person does in his earthly life.
The evil that it says is from hell, that is, from Satan. (6)
Questions.Alternative: What did James say about the tongue?
What did James say about the mouth?
What did James say about the lips?

Questions.Q: What do you know about hell?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It is a place where those who have rejected the Lord will spend eternity. It is a place where there is constant pain and darkness.
Questions.Note: See "hell" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What is man able to tame/control?
Questions.A: He can tame/control all wild animals and birds, reptiles and creatures of the sea. (7)
Questions.Alternative: What are people able to tame?
What are people able to control?
What is man able to tame?
What is man able to control?

What is mankind able to control?
What can people tame?
What can people control?
What can man tame?
What can man control?
What can mankind tame?
What can mankind control?

Questions.Q: What has no one ever been able to tame/control?
Questions.A: No one can tame/control the tongue/mouth/lips. (8)
Questions.Alternative: What has no one ever been able to tame?
What has no one ever been able to control?

Questions.Q: What did James call the tongue/mouth/lips?
Questions.A: He called it evil, uncontrollable, and like a poison. (8)
Questions.Alternative: What did James call the tongue?
What did James call the mouth?
What did James call the lips?

Questions.Q: What good use do we sometimes make of our tongues/mouths/lips?
Questions.A: We use them to praise our Lord and Father. (9)
Questions.Alternative: What good use do we sometimes make of our tongues?
What good use do we sometimes make of our mouths?
What good use do we sometimes make of our lips?

Questions.Q: What evil/bad purpose do we use our tongues/mouths/lips for?
Questions.A: We use them to speak evil against others. (9)
Questions.Alternative: What evil purpose do we use our tongues for?
What evil purpose do we use our mouths for?
What evil purpose do we use our lips for?
What bad purpose do we use our tongues for?
What bad purpose do we use our mouths for?
What bad purpose do we use our lips for?

Questions.Q: What did James say about using the tongue/mouth/lips to speak both words of praise and to speak words of cursing?
Questions.A: This is not proper/good. // It should not happen. (10)
Questions.Alternative: What did James say about using the tongue to speak both words of praise and to speak words of cursing?
What did James say about using the mouth to speak both words of praise and to speak words of cursing?
What did James say about using the lips to speak both words of praise and to speak words of cursing?

Questions.Q: What place of water/water supply can pour out both sweet and bitter water from the same place?
Questions.A: There is no place that can do it. (11)
Questions.Note: This answer is implied.
Questions.Alternative: What place of water can pour out both sweet and bitter water from the same place?
What water supply can pour out both sweet and bitter water from the same place?

Questions.Q: What fruit can a fig tree not bear?
Questions.A: It cannot bear olives. (12)
Questions.Note: This answer is implied.

Questions.Q: What fruit can a grapevine not bear?
Questions.A: It cannot bear figs. (12)
Questions.Note: This answer is implied.

Questions.Q: What kind of water can a place of bitter water not produce?
Questions.A: It cannot produce sweet water. (12)

Section.heading: James 3:13-18 James told the Christians that there are two kinds of wisdom, earthly wisdom and heavenly wisdom. All Christians should choose the wisdom that God gives.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the basic meaning (theme) of what James said in these verses?
Questions.A: If a person is truly wise, he will prove it by doing good [deeds for others] and live humbly. (13)

However, if a person claims to be wise, but he is very jealous, bitter and selfish, that person is making a boast that is not true. Such a person is not wise. The wisdom he claims to have does not come from God but instead comes from Satan. (14-15)

Questions.Q: What should a person not do, if he is very envious and very ambitious?
Questions.A: He should not boast about it nor deny that it is true. (14)

Questions.Q: If a person claims that he is wise, but he does the things mentioned in verse 14, what did James say about the thinking/claim of a person like that?
Questions.A: His thinking/claim to be wise is not from [God] in heaven, but instead comes from demons. His thinking is characteristic of the people who do not know God. (15)
Questions.Alternative: If a person claims that he is wise, but he does the things mentioned in verse 14, what did James say about the thinking of a person like that?
If a person claims that he is wise, but he does the things mentioned in verse 14, what did James say about the claim of a person like that?

Questions.Q: Where do you think heaven is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It is that part of God's creation above the earth and the waters, including "air" and "space," and serves as home for God and the spirits who serve Him.
Questions.Note: See "heaven" in KBT.

Questions.Q: If people are jealous and selfish, what kinds of things will happen as they interact/live with others?
Questions.A: They will squabble with and disturb each other, and they will make a practice of doing evil deeds. (16)
Questions.Alternative: If people are jealous and selfish, what kinds of things will happen as they interact with others?
If people are jealous and selfish, what kinds of things will happen as they live with others?

Questions.Q: What is the character/conduct like of a person whose wisdom comes from God?
Questions.A: He does only good deeds.
He does not like to fight or quarrel.
He is gentle in his dealings with others. // He respects the desires of others.
He does not force his own way upon others. // He is submissive.
He is very merciful.
He does good to others.
He regards all people without favoritism. // He treats all people the same.
He does not tell lies or pretend to be something he is not. // He is sincere. (17)
Questions.Alternative: What is the character like of a person whose wisdom comes from God?
What is the conduct like of a person whose wisdom comes from God?

Questions.Q: What happens when those who promote peace/peacemakers give advice in a peaceful manner?
Questions.A: They cause other people to do good deeds. (18)
Questions.Alternative: What happens when those who promote peace give advice in a peaceful manner?
What happens when peacemakers give advice in a peaceful manner?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to be at peace?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: To be at peace is to have a mental or spiritual condition marked by freedom of disquieting or oppressive thoughts or emotions.

Section.heading: James 4:1-12 James told the Christians that they were quarreling and fighting because of their desire for the things of this world. They needed to stop being controlled by earthly desires, repent of their sins and submit to God.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the basic meaning (theme) of what James said in these verses?
Questions.A: He told the Christians that, if they follow their desires to just please themselves, they will join with those who are the enemies of God. (4)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they sometimes fought and quarreled?
Questions.A: They fought and quarreled because they had strong desires [to possess things and to be honored]. (1)

Questions.Q: If they wanted those things very much, but could not get them, what did they do?
Questions.A: They killed [other people] and coveted [what other people had]. (2)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to covet what someone else has?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that a person desires to have what another person has.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they do not secure/gain/obtain the things they want?
Questions.A: They do not obtain the things they want because they do not ask God for those things. (2)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that they do not secure the things they want?
What is the reason that they do not gain the things they want?
What is the reason that they do not obtain the things they want?

Questions.Q: If they were to ask God for something, why would he not give it to them?
Questions.A: He would not give it to them if they were thinking of the selfish ways in which they would use it. (3)

Questions.Q: What did James mean by calling the people adulterous?
Questions.A: He called them that because they did not want to obey God. (4)

Questions.Q: What did James say about anyone who chose to be a friend of those who are not Christians?
Questions.A: That person became an enemy of God. (4)

Questions.Q: What did he tell them that they should think about the scripture?
Questions.A: They should think that there was a reason for what the scripture stated. (5)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that we slight God and refuse to love/follow him fully?
Questions.A: We slight God because we have fierce innate desires which tend [to lead us away from him]. (5)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that we slight God and refuse to love him fully?
What is the reason that we slight God and refuse to follow him fully?

Questions.Q: Even though we people wander away from God, why can we be confident that he will help us to follow him?
Questions.A: God has told us that he will help us to do good deeds. (6)

Questions.Q: How did James show us that this is true?
Questions.A: He quotes the scripture which states that God will help those who humble themselves. (6)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to have/use grace?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that a person shows that he accepts and loves another person even when they do not deserve it.
Questions.Note: See "grace" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think it means to have grace?
What do you think it means for someone to have grace?
What do you think it means for someone to experience grace?
What do you think it means to use grace?

Questions.Q: What does God do to those who are proud?
Questions.A: He does not help them. (6)

Questions.Q: What did James say their relationship should be toward God?
Questions.A: They should submit themselves to him. (7)

Questions.Q: What did James say their relationship should be toward the devil?
Questions.A: They should resist him. (7)

Questions.Q: What will the devil do, if they resist him?
Questions.A: He will flee from them. (7)

Questions.Q: What do you know about the Devil?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "Devil" is the Greek equivalent of the Hebrew "Satan." Satan is the chief enemy of God. He is the supreme evil spiritual being who leads and directs all other evil spiritual beings. (See "Devil" in KBT in the "Satan" entry.)

Questions.Q: What else should they do in regard to their relationship to God?
Questions.A: They should fellowship with God. (8)

Questions.Q: If they come near to God, what will he do?
Questions.A: God will fellowship with them. (8)

Questions.Q: What should those people do who are sinners?
Questions.A: They should repent. (8)

Questions.Q: What should those people do who are double-minded in regard to following God?
Questions.A: They should follow God in a single-minded manner. (8)

Questions.Q: What did James tell them to do?
Questions.A: Instead of being joyful about what they were doing, they should be sad/sorrowful [because of their sins]. (9)

Questions.Q: What else did James tell them to do?
Questions.A: They should humble themselves before the Lord. (10)

Questions.Q: What will God do if they are humble before him?
Questions.A: He will honor/help/exalt them. (10)

Questions.Q: What did James tell them not to do?
Questions.A: They must not criticize one another. (11)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they should not do this?
Questions.A: They should not do this because anyone who criticizes or judges his fellow believer is not obeying what God told them to do. They are saying that God's laws do not concern them. (11)

Questions.Q: Who is the only lawgiver and judge?
Questions.A: [God] is the only one who is able to save and destroy [people]. (12)

Questions.Q: After stating the fact that [God] is the only one who can save and destroy them, what did James tell them?
Questions.A: He told them not to criticize/judge their neighbor. (12)
Questions.Alternative: After stating the fact that God is the only one who can save and destroy them, what did James tell them?
After stating that God is the only one who can save and destroy them, what did James tell them?
After stating that their is only one who can save and destroy, what did James tell them?

Section.heading: James 4:13-17 Since we can't be certain what the future will be like, we should say that we will do a certain thing, if it is the Lord's will, instead of boasting about what we will do tomorrow.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the basic meaning (theme) of what James said in these verses?
Questions.A: We should realize that we are completely dependent on God for everything. Therefore, we should not make any plans without thinking about what God wants us to do. (15)

Questions.Q: To whom was James speaking?
Questions.A: He was talking to those who said they would go to a city and earn money. (13)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that James criticized those who make plans for the future, thinking that they will become wealthy?
Questions.A: They do not realize [or admit] that life is uncertain. // They do not know what will happen in the future. (14)

Questions.Q: How did James show that life is uncertain and transient/short?
Questions.A: He compared it to vapor/fog that soon vanishes away. (14)
Questions.Alternative: How did James show that life is uncertain and transient?
How did James show that life is uncertain and short?

Questions.Q: In view of the fact that our lives are uncertain and transient, what should we say/believe?
Questions.A: We should say that, if it is the Lord's will, we will live and do a certain thing. (15)
Questions.Alternative: In view of the fact that our lives are uncertain and transient, what should we say?
In view of the fact that our lives are uncertain and transient, what should we believe?

Questions.Q: What did James say about their boasting and bragging?
Questions.A: He said it was evil. (16)

Questions.Q: What did James say about anyone who did not do the good that they knew they should do?
Questions.A: He said they were sinning. (17)

Section.heading: James 5:1-6 James told the rich people what will happen to them, because they have hoarded their wealth.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the basic meaning (theme) of what James said in these verses?
Questions.A: [God] will severely punish those who have become rich by cheating others.

Questions.Q: What did he tell them to do?
Questions.A: He told them to weep and to wail. (1)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that he told them to do that?
Questions.A: He told them to do that because of the misery that was going to come upon them. (1)

Questions.Q: What has happened to their riches and clothes?
Questions.A: Their riches have become rotted/worthless
and their clothes have been eaten by moths. (2)

Questions.Q: What has happened to their gold and silver?
Questions.A: Their gold and silver have become corroded/worthless. (3)

Questions.Q: What will this corrosion do to them?
Questions.A: It will prove to them that they are not using their wealth as they should use it. (3)

Questions.Q: What do you think he meant by flesh in this verse?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He meant their physical bodies.
Questions.Note: See "flesh" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What had the rich people been busy doing?
Questions.A: They had been busy accumulating/hoarding great wealth. (3)

Questions.Q: What were these rich people guilty of doing?
Questions.A: They had not paid the wages of those who had worked in their fields. (4)

Questions.Q: What was the response of the workers?
Questions.A: They cried out to the Lord Almighty and complained to him. (4)

Questions.Q: What did God do in response to their complaints?
Questions.A: He listened to their complaints. (4)

Questions.Q: How did the rich people live?
Questions.A: They spent their time on earth enjoying luxury and pleasure. (5)

Questions.Q: What else did James say these rich people have done?
Questions.A: They condemned and murdered innocent people. (6)

Questions.Q: What did these innocent people do against the rich?
Questions.A: They did not resist/oppose them. // They had done nothing bad against the rich. (6)

Section.heading: James 5:7-12 James encouraged the Christians to be patient and endure the trials that would happen to them.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the basic meaning (theme) of what James said in these verses?
Questions.A: They should be patient because the Lord is coming soon. (7-8)
Questions.Note: This implies that the Lord will come and deliver all those who believe in him and take them with him to heaven.

Questions.Q: For what does the farmer have to be patient?
Questions.A: He has to be patient and wait for the land to produce the crop,
and he has to be patient and wait for the rains. (7)

Questions.Q: How does the example of the farmer relate to James telling people to be patient?
Questions.A: The readers need to wait patiently for the return of the Lord as a farmer has to wait patiently for his crops. (8)

Questions.Q: What did he tell them not to do?
Questions.A: He told them not to grumble against each other. (9)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they should not do this?
Questions.A: They should not do this because if they did grumble, [God] would punish them. (9)

Questions.Q: When will [God] judge all people?
Questions.A: [God] will soon judge all people. (9)
Questions.Note: Depending on which commentary is used the judge is either God or Christ. See Exegetical Summary on James.
Questions.Alternative: When will God judge all people?
When will Christ judge all people?
When will all people be judged?
When is judgment going to occur?

Questions.Q: Whom did he tell them to consider as an example of patience?
Questions.A: He told them to consider the prophets. (10)

Questions.Q: In what way were they examples of patience?
Questions.A: They were patient and continued to speak God's message to the people, in spite of the things they suffered. (10)

Questions.Q: What do you know about prophets?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A prophet was someone who spoke on behalf of God and was sent by Him. He often foretold future events. Prophets were mainly persons who advised the people to obey God only.
Questions.Note: See "prophet" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did he say about those prophets?
Questions.A: They were blessed/happy. (11)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they were blessed/happy?
Questions.A: They were blessed/happy because they were patient even though they suffered. (11)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that they were blessed?
What is the reason that they were happy?

Questions.Q: Who was like these prophets who persevered when he suffered?
Questions.A: Job was like them. (11)

Questions.Q: What happened to Job after he had trusted God through all his sufferings/trials?
Questions.A: The Lord showed him great compassion. (11)
Questions.Alternative: What happened to Job after he had trusted God through all his sufferings?
What happened to Job after he had trusted God through all his trials?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the Lord did this?
Questions.A: He did this because the Lord is merciful and compassionate to his people. (11)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to be compassionate to someone else?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: This takes place when someone shows deep feeling for and understanding of the misery and suffering that someone else is experiencing. (See "compassion" in KBT in the "mercy" entry.)

Questions.Q: Most of the versions (English) translated what James wrote in 5:12 as "Above all." Why?
Questions.A: He wrote that so that his hearers would know that what he is about to say is very important. (12)
Questions.Note: This answer is implied.

Questions.Q: Upon/By what did he tell them not to swear?
Questions.A: He told them not to swear by heaven, earth or anything else. (12)
Questions.Alternative: Upon what did he tell them not to swear?
By what did he tell them not to swear?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to swear?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that a person makes a solemn promise or states an important truth; and to make it more certain, he will use the name of God or a substitute for the name of God.

Questions.Q: What did he tell them to do, instead of swearing?
Questions.A: They should speak the truth at all times: they should say "yes," if a thing is true and "no," if it is false. (12)

Questions.Q: What will happen to them if they fail to follow his advice?
Questions.A: [God] will punish them. (12)
Questions.Alternative: What will happen to them, if they fail to follow his advice?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means, if someone condemns someone else?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that someone pronounces someone else guilty, with the clear implication that the person will be punished for what he did. (See "condemn" in KBT in the "judge, judgment" entry.)

Section.heading: James 5:13-20 James told the Christians how important it is that they pray to God and ask him to help them with their needs. He will help them if they believe that he will help them.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the basic meaning (theme) of what James said in these verses?
Questions.A: James told the Christians that God will answer their prayers, if they believe when they pray.

Questions.Q: What should people do, when they are in trouble?
Questions.A: They should pray [to God]. (13)

Questions.Q: What should they do when they are happy?
Questions.A: They should sing praise [to God]. (13)

Questions.Q: If one of them is sick what should he do?
Questions.A: He should call for the elders of the church to pray for him. (14)

Questions.Q: What do you think an elder is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: An elder is a leader in the church.

Questions.Q: What else are the elders to do in addition to praying for the sick person?
Questions.A: They should anoint him with oil, asking the Lord to heal him. (14)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to anoint someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In this context it was done as a symbolic act when praying to God to heal a sick person. The disciples of Jesus often anointed sick people with oil when they asked God to heal them. Probably they poured or smeared oil on the forehead of the person. In this context the action seems to have been symbolic, although rubbing or massaging a person with oil was also practiced as a medical treatment in the ancient world.
Questions.Note: See "anoint" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What will happen as a result of [people] praying and believing that the sick person will be healed [by God]?
Questions.A: God will heal that person. (15)
Questions.Alternative: What will happen as a result of people praying and believing that the sick person will be healed by God?
What will happen as a result of people praying and believing that the sick person will be healed?
What will happen as a result of praying and believing that the sick person will be healed by God?
What will happen as a result of praying and believing that the sick person will be healed?

Questions.Q: What else will [God] do for the sick person?
Questions.A: [He] will forgive his sins. (15)
Questions.Alternative: What else will God do for the sick person?
What else will the Lord do for the sick person?
What else will be done for the sick person?
What else will the sick person receive?

Questions.Q: What do you think happens, when someone forgives someone else?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Forgiveness always involves two people, one of whom has done something wrong to the other and offended him. Forgiveness takes place, when the one who was offended sets aside his right to justice and decides not to punish the offender as he deserved.
Questions.Note: See "forgive" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What else should they do so that they might be healed [by God]?
Questions.A: They should confess their sins to one another and pray for one another. (16)
Questions.Alternative: What else should they do so that they might be healed by God?
What else should they do so that they might be healed?

Questions.Q: How can they be sure that praying will help their situation?
Questions.A: The prayer of a righteous person is very powerful in its effect. (16)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to be righteous?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that a person is in a state of having been accepted by God as right. (See "righteousness" in KBT in the "just, justify..." entry.)

Questions.Q: What example did James give to show them that God answers the prayers of a true believer?
Questions.A: He wrote about Elijah. (17)

Questions.Q: What kind of a man was Elijah?
Questions.A: He was a normal person like anyone. (17)

Questions.Q: What did he pray [to God]?
Questions.A: He prayed that it would not rain. (17)
Questions.Alternative: What did he pray to God?
What did he pray?

Questions.Q: What happened after he prayed?
Questions.A: It did not rain for 3 1/2 years. (17)

Questions.Q: What did he pray [to God] after that?
Questions.A: He prayed that it would rain again. (18)
Questions.Alternative: What did he pray to God after that?
What did he pray after that?

Questions.Q: What happened after he prayed?
Questions.A: It rained and the earth produced its crops once again. (18)

Questions.Q: What did James want his hearers to understand?
Questions.A: He wanted them to understand how very important it is to help other Christians who do not keep on believing God's word. (19-20)

Questions.Q: What has someone accomplished who attempted to help a brother who has not kept believing God's word, and that brother returned once more to believe God's word?
Questions.A: He has saved that person from death/being separated from God;
and [God] will forgive all his sins. (20)

Section.heading: John 1:1-5 The Word of God became a human being, Jesus.

Questions.Q: About whom was John talking in these verses?
Questions.A: He was talking about Jesus/Christ who revealed who God is. // He is called The Word. He was the one who was the expression of who God is. (1)
Questions.Note: Check to see if "Word" or "Message" can be understood as a person. Does the grammar/sentence structure at least allow for a symbolic interpretation i.e., that the Word refers to Jesus Christ and not just a literal spoken or written word? You may want to identify "The Word" as Jesus in the section heading.

Questions.Q: What are some things John said about the Word/Jesus here?
Questions.A: He already existed in the beginning before God made the world. (1)
He was with God. (1)
He was God. (1)
God made all things through/by means of him. (3)
Life was in him. (4)
Questions.Note: This may refer to spiritual life or to all senses of the word "life."
Questions.Alternative: What are some things John said about the Word here?
What are some things John said about the Jesus here?

Questions.Q: Who do you think God is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In English, the term "God" with a capital "G" is used to refer to the one supreme Creator. The term "god" with a small "g", as in "a god" or "many gods", can refer to any spiritual being that people worship. The Greek word theos can be used in the same two ways.
Questions.Note: In many languages the term for God is a proper name and cannot be used to refer to anyone except the one supreme creator of the world. It cannot be pluralized. (Or, if it can be pluralized, the meaning may be something very different from the English "gods". In one language, the plural form of God, meant "God and those who follow him" and was an appropriate way to translate "saints".) (See "God" in KBT.)

Questions.Q: Who was with God in the beginning?
Questions.A: The Word/Jesus was with God. (2)

Questions.Q: What was beginning?
Questions.A: The world was beginning.
-OR-
God was beginning to make the world. (2)

Questions.Q: Through whom did God make all things?
Questions.A: He made them through the Word. (3)

Questions.Q: What things did God not make through him?
Questions.A: He made all things through him. (3)

Questions.Q: What does the Word have to do with life?
Questions.A: The Word is the source of eternal life. // Eternal life comes from the Word. (4)

Questions.Q: What does that life give to people or do for people?
Questions.A: It/He gives light to them. (4)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when John said this life gives light to people?
Questions.A: It causes people to know the truth about God, and to know what they should do. (4)

Questions.Q: How would/do [village] people use the word "light"?
Questions.Note: (The answer should allow for new or correct understanding that someone would refer to as light or like light.)
Some languages have a problem in translating the word for light in a figurative sense.
Questions.Alternative: How would village people use the word "light"?
How do village people use the word "light"?
How would people use the word "light"?
How do people use the word "light"?

Questions.Q: What do you think "light" means in this verse?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Light refers to truth or divine truth.
-OR-
Light refers to knowledge or knowledge of God or revelation.

Questions.Q: How does light affect darkness?
Questions.A: It shines in the darkness (and some or all of the darkness ends). (5)

Questions.Q: How does the darkness affect the light?
Questions.A: It does not have any effect on it; it does not put it out.
-OR-
The darkness has not understood it. (5)

Questions.Q: What do you think that John wanted to teach us by means of this picture language about light and darkness?
Questions.A: He wanted us to learn that the truth, which God has revealed to us, cannot be hidden.
-OR-
Evil and sin could not stop the good and the truth, which Jesus did and taught. (5)

Questions.Q: What do you think "darkness" means in this verse?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Darkness refers to spiritual or moral sin.

Section.heading: John 1:6-9 God sent John to tell people about the light that was coming.

Questions.Q: About whom was John talking in these verses?
Questions.A: He wrote about another man named John. (6)
Questions.Note: The John, who wrote these things, was a disciple/follower of Jesus. The John in these verses was known as John the Baptist or John the Baptizer. He came before Jesus started working.

Questions.Q: What does the passage say about this John?
Questions.A: God sent him. (6)
He came to tell people about the light. (7-8)
He himself was not that light. (8)

Questions.Q: Who was the messenger whom God sent?
Questions.A: God sent John. (6)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that he came?
Questions.A: He came to tell people about the light. (7)
He came so that through his witness all people might believe in [the person who was] that light. (7)
Questions.Note: Check the way that "witness" is translated. Some translators tend to use a word that refers primarily to a witness in court. Check that this has not been done.

Questions.Q: What does someone do when he believes?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He puts his trust and commitment in another person.
Questions.Note: See "believe" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think the "light" represents?
Questions.Note: "I don't know" or "It is something God was going to reveal" would be acceptable here from a non-Christian; answers such as: "The light is the same as the Word" or "The light is Jesus Christ" or "The person who was coming" would be acceptable from a Christian. (7)

Questions.Q: Was John the light or was someone else the light?
Questions.A: Someone else was the light. (8)

Questions.Q: What was the real light doing?
Questions.A: It was coming into the world and shining on all men/people. (9)

Questions.Q: What do you think John was trying to teach us in this picture language about giving light to people?
Questions.A: He wanted us to know that someone was coming into the world who would reveal the truth or give a clear understanding about God to everyone. (9)

Section.heading: John 1:10-14 Jesus/The Word came into the world.

Questions.Q: What did (the people of) the world think about the Word in these verses?
Questions.A: The people of the world did not recognize/know who he [really] was. (10)
Moreover, they refused to acknowledge him, or to believe that he came from God. (11)
Nevertheless, some people did believe in him. (12)

Questions.Q: What did God do through the Word?
Questions.A: He created the world. (10)

Questions.Q: Where did the Word come/go?
Questions.A: He came/went to his own [country], to the people of Israel. (11)
Questions.Alternative: Where did the Word come?
Where did the Word go?

Questions.Q: What do you know about the name "Israel"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In the New Testament, the terms "Israel" and "Israelite" are used by Jews to refer to themselves, and also by God to refer to them as his people.
Questions.Note: See "Israel" in KBT.

Questions.Q: How did his own people respond to him?
Questions.A: They refused to accept him. (11)
Questions.Note: Check here to be sure that the understanding of "his own people" is his relatives, neighbors, his own nation.

Questions.Q: What did the Word do for people who received him and believed that he came from God?
Questions.A: He gave them all the right to become children of God, to become God's people. (12)

Questions.Q: How do they become God's children?
Questions.A: God is their Father. God causes it to be so. (13)

Questions.Q: What was the way that they did NOT become God's children?
Questions.A: They did not become God's children by natural means: it is not a physical thing, it has nothing to do with marriage, sexual intercourse, or human birth. (13)

Questions.Q: What did John say that the Word did?
Questions.A: He became a human being. (14)
He lived among human beings. (14)
He came from [God] the Father. (14)

Questions.Q: What do you think "God the Father" means?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that God is the father of Jesus Christ and of anyone who accepts Jesus as his or her Savior and Lord.
Questions.Note: See "God the Father" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think the title "God the Father" means?
What do you think the term "God the Father" means?

Questions.Q: What do you think "flesh" means, or is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that all of mankind was made of skin and bones.
Questions.Note: See "flesh" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did those, who saw the Word, see?
Questions.A: They saw the great power/authority (to do miracles, to die and be resurrected) that the Word had received from God, since he was [God] the Father's only Son. (14)

Questions.Q: What do you think this "glory" was that the people saw?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It was the shining majesty which accompanies God's presence.
Questions.Note: -OR-
It refers to Jesus's entire life and death.
-OR-
It refers to Jesus's unique relationship to the Father.
-OR-
It refers to the character of God as seen in Jesus's life.
(See "glory" in KBT.)

Questions.Q: What was the Word like?
Questions.A: He was always kind and loving
and showed people completely what was true about God. (14)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to have/use grace?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that a person shows that he accepts and loves another person, even when he or she/that person does not deserve it.
Questions.Note: See "grace" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think it means to have grace?
What do you think it means for someone to have grace?
What do you think it means for someone to experience grace?
What do you think it means to use grace?

Section.heading: John 1:15-18 John testified about the Word.

Questions.Q: What do you think that one, who was coming after John had come, has to do with all this? // What does the term "the one, who was coming after John," have to do with all this?
Questions.A: They are all referring to the same person. // All the terms/titles refer to the same person. (15)
Questions.Alternative: What do you think that one, who was coming after John had come, has to do with all this?
What does the term "the one, who was coming after John," have to do with all this?

Questions.Q: What do you think the term, "the Word," has to do with God's only Son?
Questions.A: It refers to Jesus/the same person. (15, 18)

Questions.Q: What do you think the term, "the Word," has to do with Jesus Christ?
Questions.A: They are the same person. // The Word refers to Jesus Christ. (17)

Questions.Q: What did John say about the one who was going to come after him?
Questions.A: The one, who was coming, would be greater (that is, more important) than John. (15)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that this person, who was coming, was greater than John?
Questions.A: The reason was because he existed long before John was born. (15)
Questions.Note: If the translator makes any change in the text here, he should also adjust verse 30.

Questions.Q: What did the/that Son of God, who was coming after John, give people?
Questions.A: The Son of God gave people many good things in his kindness and love, and then even more kindness and love. (16)
Questions.Alternative: What did the Son of God, who was coming after John, give people?
What did that Son of God, who was coming after John, give people?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to bless someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means to make someone happy, to give good fortune or satisfaction, to help someone. (See both "grace" and "bless, blessed, blessing" in KBT.)

Questions.Q: To whom did he give these things?
Questions.A: He gave them to all people. (This refers to all Christians, including John the author.) (16)

Questions.Q: What is the source of these blessings?
Questions.A: The loving-kindness of God's Son. // Jesus was the source. (16)

Questions.Q: What is the difference between what God did through Moses and what he did through Jesus?
Questions.A: Through Moses people received God's laws,
but through Jesus Christ, God revealed his loving-kindness and the truth about himself. (17)

Questions.Q: What law do you think Moses gave the people from God?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "The law from God that Moses gave the people was what he wrote in the first five books of the Old Testament.
Questions.Note: See "law" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Who has seen God?
Questions.A: No one has seen him. (18)

Questions.Q: Then, how do people know what God is like?
Questions.A: It is only through God's Son that people have come to know what God is like. (18)

Questions.Q: Where is God's Son?
Questions.A: He is at his Father's side, in heaven. (18)

Questions.Q: What are some of the pictures, or ways, that are used to refer to Jesus Christ in these verses from 1:1-18?
Questions.A: He is called the Word, the light, the truth, and God's Son.

Section.heading: John 1:19-28 John the Baptist prepared the way for the one whom God appointed to save us.

Questions.Q: Who was this "John" who is mentioned in these verses?
Questions.A: He was John the Baptist.
Questions.Note: See the note above at 1:6.

Questions.Q: What did John the Baptist say about himself?
Questions.A: He said that he was not the Christ (the one whom God had promised to send to save us). (20)
He was not [the prophet] Elijah (whom the people were expecting to come). (21)
He said he was the one who would tell people to get ready for the Lord [God] coming to them. (23)

Questions.Q: Whom did the Jews in Jerusalem send to meet with John the Baptist?
Questions.A: They sent [some of the] priests and Levites [who worked in the place for worshiping God]. (19)

Questions.Q: What do you know about priests and Levites?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The priests were in charge of the sacrifices and the offerings at the worship places/the temple. The Levites cared for things used in worship or for sacrifices. (See both "priest" and "Levite" in KBT.)

Questions.Q: What was the reason they sent those/these people?
Questions.A: They wanted to know who John was, especially whether he was the Christ. (19-20)
Questions.Alternative: What was the reason they sent those people?
What was the reason they sent these people?

Questions.Q: What do you think is the meaning of the Christ?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "Christ" is the English rendering of the Greek word Christos, which means "anointed one."
Questions.Note: See "Christ" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What does someone do when he confesses?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He tells the truth about who he is or what he has done.

Questions.Q: Who else did they think that John was?
Questions.A: They thought that he might be the prophet Elijah or the prophet that God had said he would send. (21)
Questions.Note: See Deuteronomy 18:15.

Questions.Q: What do you know about prophets?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A prophet is someone who speaks for God and is inspired by Him. He often foretells future events. Prophets were mainly spokespersons who called His people to obedience by appealing to Israel's past and future.
Questions.Note: See "prophet" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What was John's answer to these questions?
Questions.A: He said that he was not Elijah or that/this prophet. (21)

Questions.Q: What was their reason for asking John all those/these questions?
Questions.A: They asked John those questions because they wanted an answer to take back to those who had sent them. (22)
Questions.Alternative: What was their reason for asking John all those questions?
What was their reason for asking John all these questions?

Questions.Q: What did John say about himself?
Questions.A: He said that he was the messenger who was out in the desert telling people to prepare for the coming of the Lord. (23)

Questions.Q: What does it mean to you to have someone as your lord?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A lord is someone who has power and exercises it responsibly. To call someone your lord means that you have given him or her control over your life. The Lord, in this case, is Jesus. Every Christian strives to make Jesus lord in his or her life by giving Him complete control. (See "Lord" in KBT in the "God" entry.)

Questions.Q: Who had foretold that such a messenger would come?
Questions.A: Isaiah the prophet had foretold that. (23)

Questions.Q: What happened in the town of Bethany?
Questions.A: The priests and Levites asked John those questions. (28)
John was baptizing people there in the Jordan River. (28)

Questions.Q: Where was Bethany?
Questions.A: It was on the east side of the Jordan River, [the side furthest away from Jerusalem]. (28)

Questions.Q: Who else questioned John? // What does this say about the people who questioned John?
Questions.A: They were some messengers whom the Pharisees had sent. (24-25)
Questions.Alternative: Who else questioned John?
What does this say about the people who questioned John?

Questions.Q: What do you know about Pharisees?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The Semitic words mean "the separated ones," which was transliterated into Greek. It came to mean a certain group of Jewish people. So the idea of "separated" does not need to be included here. The name "Pharisee" means "the separated ones." They were the largest and most important of the Jewish religious groups. They controlled the synagogues and exercised great control over the general population. They taught that the way to God was through obeying the law. They opposed Jesus because He refused to accept the teachings of their oral law.
Questions.Note: See "Pharisee" in KBT.

Questions.Q: About what did they ask John?
Questions.A: They asked him why he was baptizing people, if he was not the Christ, or Elijah, or the prophet they were expecting. (25)

Questions.Q: Do you think these men thought John was doing the right thing?
Questions.A: No, they were challenging his credentials.
Questions.Note: Their question implied that only the Christ or an important prophet (such as Elijah) had the right to baptize people.
Questions.Alternative: Do you think these men thought John had the right to baptize?
Did these men think that John had the right to baptize?

Questions.Q: With what did John baptize the people?
Questions.A: He used water to baptize people. (26)

Questions.Q: What do you think John did with the people when he baptized them?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He did something so that water washed over the people, either by putting them down under the water, or by putting water over the top of them, probably the first way.
Questions.Note: See "baptize" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did he say about another person/this other person who was coming?
Questions.A: He was standing among them;
and they did not know who he was. (26)
Questions.Alternative: What did he say about another person who was coming?
What did he say about this other person who was coming?

Questions.Q: What was John's relationship to that/this other person?
Questions.A: John said that he was not worthy to untie his sandals. (27)
He was less than a slave in comparison with that person. (27)
Questions.Alternative: What was John's relationship to that other person?
What was John's relationship to this other person?

Questions.Q: What do you think is the meaning of what John said here?
Questions.A: That other person (Jesus) was so great that John felt he wasn't worthy enough to do even the lowest tasks/duties for him. (27)

Section.heading: John 1:29-34 John the Baptist called Jesus "the Lamb of God."

Questions.Q: About whom is John talking in these verses?
Questions.A: He talked about Jesus. (29)

Questions.Q: What new information is told about Jesus Christ in these verses?
Questions.A: He is the Lamb of God. (29)
He takes away the sins of the people. // He will forgive people's sins. (29)
He is more important/greater than John. (30)
John saw the Holy Spirit come down on him and stay with him. (32)
He will baptize people with the Holy Spirit. // He will give people the Holy Spirit. (33)
He is the Son of God. (34)

Questions.Q: What did John the Baptist say when he saw Jesus?
Questions.A: He said, "Look! There is the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of people/people's sin." (29)

Questions.Q: What do you think John meant when he called Jesus "the Lamb of God"?
Questions.A: God had told the Jews to sacrifice a lamb, which would die for their sins. John meant that now. God was giving his only son, Jesus, to die for all people, so that God would forgive their sins.
Questions.Note: Check for wrong implications here. In Moslem cultures, or other cultures where lambs are sacrificed, they may be able to pick up the implication that Jesus is the one who will be the sacrifice through which God will forgive sins. In such cultures, check that the appropriate word has been used for "lamb" to suggest this idea. (See "lamb of God" in KBT in the "sacrifice" entry.)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when someone sacrifices a lamb in this way?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "Sacrifice" is the religious act of making a gift to God, or to some other powerful spiritual being, in order to establish, maintain, or restore a proper relationship between the sacrificer and the deity. Something is given up in order to achieve a purpose.
Questions.Note: See "sacrifice" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think happens when someone forgives someone else?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Forgiveness always involves two people, one of whom has done something wrong to the other and offended him.
