Forgiveness takes place when the one, who was offended, sets aside his right to justice and decides not to punish the offender, as he deserved. If the one who offended repents and accepts this forgiveness, the result is that the relationship between the two, which was broken by the offense, is restored and the guilt of the offender is removed.
Questions.Note: See "forgive" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What does a person do when he sins?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He deliberately keeps on doing those things that please himself and displease God.
Questions.Note: See "sin" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did John remind the people about Jesus?
Questions.A: Jesus was the one to whom John had been referring [the day before]. He said that there was a man who was coming at a later time.
John said this man was greater, because he existed before John was born. (30)

Questions.Q: How did John himself know/recognize Jesus?
Questions.A: God had told him beforehand that the one, on whom the Spirit would come and stay, was the one who was to come and baptize people with the Holy Spirit. (33)
Questions.Alternative: How did John himself know Jesus?
How did John himself recognize Jesus?

Questions.Q: Who do you think the Holy Spirit is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He is God's spirit, through whom he acts, reveals His will, and empowers individuals. (See "Holy Spirit" in KBT in the "spirit" entry.)

Questions.Q: In what way did John say that the one who is coming will baptize?
Questions.A: He said that he will baptize with the Holy Spirit. (33)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means that Jesus was "to baptize with the Holy Spirit"?
Questions.A: He would give/was to give people the Holy Spirit in abundance.
-OR-
He would change/was to change people by sending the Holy Spirit to/into them.
-OR-
The person's spirit was to be cleansed/would be cleansed/purified by God's spirit.

Questions.Q: How did John know that all these things were true about Jesus?
Questions.A: He saw the Spirit [of God] do just as God had said. (32)
Questions.Note: (See "Spirit of God" in KBT in the "spirit" entry.)
The Greek, and most N.T. versions, use "Spirit." The Living Bible uses "Holy Spirit."

Questions.Q: From where did the spirit come; and how did John describe him?
Questions.A: He came down from heaven like a dove. (32)

Questions.Q: Where do you think Heaven is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It is that part of God's creation above the earth and the waters, including "air" and "space," and serves as home for God and the spirits who serve Him.
Questions.Note: See "heaven" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did the Spirit do?
Questions.A: He came down on/upon Jesus and stayed with him. (32)

Questions.Q: Because John had seen all that happened, what did he want the people to know about Jesus?
Questions.A: He wanted them to know that Jesus was the Son of God. (34)

Questions.Q: What was John's reason for baptizing with water?
Questions.A: In order to cause the Jews/people of Israel to know who Jesus was. (31)

Section.heading: John 1:35-42 Jesus met Andrew and Simon Peter and they became his disciples. // Andrew and Peter became disciples of Jesus. // Andrew and Peter met Jesus and became his disciples.

Questions.Q: Who started following Jesus in these verses? // In these verses who became Jesus's disciples?
Questions.A: Andrew and Simon Peter, his [older] brother became Jesus's disciples. (40, 42)
Questions.Alternative: Who started following Jesus in these verses?
In these verses who became Jesus's disciples?

Questions.Q: Where was John when he began talking about this same topic again?
Questions.A: He was at the same place that he had been (on) the day before, [that is, he was baptizing in the Jordan (River) near Bethany]. (35)

Questions.Q: Who was with John?
Questions.A: Two of his disciples were with him. (35)

Questions.Q: What do you think a disciple is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The word "disciple" means those who have attached themselves to a given teacher, i.e., "learners." A disciple is a person who receives instruction from another person. A disciple is a person who accepts the ideas/teachings of another person and assists in spreading or implementing them.
Questions.Note: See "disciple" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What name did John call Jesus?
Questions.A: He called him the Lamb of God. (36)

Questions.Q: What did John's two disciples/the two disciples of John do?
Questions.A: They followed/went with Jesus. (37)
Questions.Alternative: What did John's two disciples do?
What did the two disciples of John do?

Questions.Q: What was their reason for doing this?
Questions.A: They had heard John say that Jesus was the Lamb of God. (37)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus ask those two disciples of John?
Questions.A: He asked them: "What do you want?" (38)

Questions.Q: What did they ask him? // What did they answer him?
Questions.A: "Rabbi, where do you live/stay?" (38)
Questions.Alternative: What did they ask him?
What did they answer him?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the two men called Jesus "Rabbi"?
Questions.A: They called him "Rabbi" because they respected him as a teacher. (38)
Key Term Check: In Hebrew, the title meant "my master." It was applied to teachers and others of an exalted and revered position. (See "Rabbi" in KBT in the "Christ" entry.)

Questions.Q: How do we know that Jesus was pleased with them?
Questions.A: He told them, "Come [along] and see." (39)

Questions.Q: What time of day did they go there?
Questions.A: It was about 4:00 in the afternoon. (39)
Questions.Note: In the Greek, it is the tenth hour. Some people might think that the two men came at 10:00 in the morning.

Questions.Q: How long did they stay there with Jesus?
Questions.A: They stayed the rest of the day. (39)

Questions.Q: What did Andrew do?
Questions.A: He found his brother Simon, told him that they had found the Messiah, and took him to [meet] Jesus. (41)

Questions.Q: What do you think the term "Messiah" means?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It is the transliteration of the Hebrew word meaning "anointed one" that was translated into Greek as Christos.
Questions.Note: See "Messiah" in KBT in the "Christ, Messiah" entry.

Questions.Q: I thought that the two men had found Jesus. Who is this person called Messiah?
Questions.A: It is Jesus, not anyone else.
Questions.Alternative: It says that the two men had found Jesus. Who is this person called Messiah?
It says that the two disciples had found Jesus. Who is this person called Messiah?

Questions.Q: I thought that Jesus was called the Christ (1:17). What are we to think about these two names about which John writes?
Questions.A: The/These two names mean the same thing. They (just) come from two different languages, Hebrew & Greek.
Questions.Alternative: In verse 17, it says that Jesus was called the Christ. What are we to think about these two names about which John writes?
In verse 17, it says that Jesus was called the Christ, but here Andrew says he is the Messiah. What do you think about these two names about which John writes?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to Simon without first asking him some questions?
Questions.A: He said: "You are Simon, son of John. Your name will be Cephas." (42)

Questions.Q: How did Jesus already know about Simon? Tell me what you think about this.
Questions.A: Jesus knew all that/all about Simon, because he was God's son.
-OR-
Earlier Andrew had told Jesus about his brother, Simon.

Questions.Q: What is the meaning of the names Cephas and Peter?
Questions.A: The meaning of both names is Rock. (42)

Questions.Q: What might [village] people think about a man whose name was Rock?
Questions.A: They might think that he was strong in his words, actions, or body.
Questions.Alternative: What might village people think about a man whose name was Rock?
What might people think about a man whose name was Rock?

Section.heading: John 1:43-51 Jesus called Philip and Nathanael to follow him.

Questions.Q: Who also started to follow Jesus?
Questions.A: The men, Philip (45)
and Nathanael, became Jesus's disciples. (49)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus ask Philip to do?
Questions.A: He asked him to come with him to Galilee [Province]. (43)

Questions.Q: Who were the men whose home area was Bethsaida in Galilee Province?
Questions.A: Philip, Andrew and Peter were the ones/were from Bethsaida. (44)

Questions.Q: What did Philip tell Nathanael?
Questions.A: Philip told Nathanael that they had found the one about whom Moses and the prophets had written [hundreds of years earlier]. (45)

Questions.Q: What did this have to do with Jesus?
Questions.A: Jesus was the one about whom Moses and the prophets had written; he was the son of Joseph, from [the town of] Nazareth. (45)
Questions.Note: See comment for the following question.
Questions.Alternative: What does he mention about Jesus; who is he?

Questions.Q: What was the relationship between Jesus and Joseph?
Questions.A: Jesus was the son of Joseph. [He was not his biological son. Joseph had raised Jesus as his child. As far as most people in the society were concerned, Jesus was Joseph's son. Even if they were familiar with the account of Jesus miraculous virgin birth, they would not necessarily believe it.] (45)
Questions.Note: In the original language, there is nothing here that suggests that Jesus was not the biological son of Joseph, though we know from elsewhere in Scripture (see Matthew 1:18-20) that he was not. Depending on how this is expressed in the target language and prior knowledge the respondent might have, this could be a point of confusion.

Questions.Q: What did Nathanael think about Nazareth?
Questions.A: He thought that nothing good could come from there (i.e., it was a totally bad place). // No one who was important would/could be from that place. (46)

Questions.Q: What did Philip ask Nathanael to do, in order to prove his words were true?
Questions.A: He told Nathanael to come [along with him] to see/and see. (46)

Questions.Q: About whom was Jesus talking, when he said, "Here is a real Israelite, in whom there is nothing false" / "Here is a person who would never tell a lie" / "Here is a person who would never deceive anyone"?
Questions.A: He was talking about Nathanael. (47)
Questions.Alternative: About whom was Jesus talking, when he said, "Here is a real Israelite, in whom there is nothing false"?
About whom was Jesus talking, when he said, "Here is a person who would never tell a lie"?
About whom was Jesus talking, when he said, "Here is a person who would never deceive anyone"?

About whom was Jesus talking, when he said, "Here is a real Israelite, in whom there is nothing false."? // "Here is a person who would never tell a lie."? // "Here is a person who would never deceive anyone."?

Questions.Q: When did Jesus know Nathanael before this time?
Questions.A: He had not known him previously. (48)

Questions.Q: What else did Jesus know about Nathanael?
Questions.A: Without seeing him, Jesus had known that Nathanael was sitting/had been sitting under the fig tree before Philip called him. (48)

Questions.Q: From what Nathanael said, who did he believe was the Son of God and the King of Israel?
Questions.A: He believed that Jesus was God's Son and the King of Israel. (49)

Questions.Q: What was Nathanael's reason for believing those/these things about Jesus?
Questions.A: He believed, because Jesus told him that he had seen him under the fig tree. (50)
Questions.Alternative: What was Nathanael's reason for believing those things about Jesus?
What was Nathanael's reason for believing these things about Jesus?

Questions.Q: What was an example of something even greater that Jesus said that Nathanael would see?
Questions.A: He would see heaven open;
and the angels of God would be going up and coming down to where the Son of Man would be. (51)

Questions.Q: What do you know about angels?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Angels are spiritual messengers, who either deliver a message to humans, carry out God's will, praise God, or guard God's throne.
Questions.Note: See "angel" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Who do you think the Son of Man is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It is Jesus. "Son of Man" is the title Christ used of Himself.
Questions.Note: See "son of man" in KBT.

Section.heading: John 2:1-11 Jesus went to a wedding feast at Cana.

Questions.Q: What event occurred in the town of Cana?
Questions.A: There was a wedding. // There was a celebration for a man to take a wife. // The people celebrated the event when a man takes his wife. (1)

Questions.Q: What was the problem at this wedding?
Questions.A: There was no more wine for the wedding guests to drink. (3)

Questions.Q: Where was the town of Cana located?
Questions.A: It was located in Galilee [Province]. (1)

Questions.Q: Whom did [the hosts] invite to this wedding?
Questions.A: They invited Jesus's mother, (1)
and Jesus and his disciples. (2)
Questions.Note: Check to make sure that your rendering also strongly implies that they were already there, not that they had just been invited.
Questions.Alternative: Whom did the hosts invite to this wedding?
Whom did invite to this wedding?

Questions.Q: Who told Jesus that the wine was all gone?
Questions.A: Jesus's mother told him. (3)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell his mother?
Questions.A: He said, "Why do you involve me?" "My time has not yet come." (4)
Questions.Note: The first quote possibly means, "This matter is neither your nor my concern." In the second quote "time" possibly means, 1. It was not time for Jesus's suffering, death, and, glorification. 2. It was not the time to act as shown Him by the Father. 3. It was not the time for Jesus to intervene.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus's mother tell the servants?
Questions.A: She told them to do whatever Jesus told them to do. (5)

Questions.Q: What do you think a servant does?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A servant is a person who is required to work for another and obey him. A servant is usually paid for his/her work, while a slave is not paid.
Questions.Note: See "servant" in KBT.

Questions.Q: For what were the six stone water jars used?
Questions.A: They were used for the Jews' religious washing. (6)
Questions.Note: In order for the Jews to make themselves acceptable to God, they had to obey many rules about how to wash. The water jars were used for the purification required by Jewish law.

Questions.Q: How much water could each water jar hold?
Questions.A: 20 to 30 gallons/75 to 115 liters. (6)
Questions.Note: Any term for measurement that is the same general size of the volume of the pot is acceptable.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell the servants to do?
Questions.A: He told them to fill the jars with water. (7)

Questions.Q: What did the servants do?
Questions.A: They filled the jars to the brim. (7)

Questions.Q: Then what did Jesus tell the servants to do?
Questions.A: He told the servants to draw/dip some of the water out of the jars and take it to the man in charge of the wedding feast. (8)

Questions.Q: What did the servants do?
Questions.A: They took some of the water to the man in charge. (8)

Questions.Q: What did this man in charge do with that water?
Questions.A: He tasted the water that Jesus had turned into wine. (9)

Questions.Q: What did the servants know about the wine that this man did not know?
Questions.A: They knew from where this wine had come. (9)

Questions.Q: John wrote in verse 3 that the wine was finished. From where do you think this wine came?
Questions.A: Jesus/God had changed the water in those pots into wine. (9)
Questions.Note: The answer is not explicit in this verse, nor is it specifically mentioned in this section. Each individual must come to his own conclusion/would have to arrive at the answer by what is implied in the whole section.

Questions.Q: Whom did the man in charge of the feast call?
Questions.A: He called the bridegroom. (9)

Questions.Q: When did people usually serve the best wine?
Questions.A: They served it first. (10)

Questions.Q: When did people usually serve the ordinary wine?
Questions.A: After the guests had drunk a lot [and would not notice any change in the taste of the wine], they served the ordinary wine. (10)

Questions.Q: What did this man say the bridegroom had done that was different from other weddings?
Questions.A: He/The man in charge said that he/the bridegroom had kept the best wine until after the ordinary wine was gone/now [when the ordinary wine was gone]. (10)

Questions.Q: Who or what do you think turned the water into wine?
Questions.A: Jesus turned the water into wine. This was the first of his miraculous signs/miracles. (11)
Questions.Note: John always refers to Jesus's miracles as "signs."

Questions.Q: What do you think a miraculous sign is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It is an extraordinary event/act that Jesus performed to show that he was from God. (See "miraculous sign" in KBT in the "miracle, sign, wonder" entry.)

Questions.Q: What were the results of Jesus doing/performing this miracle/miraculous sign?
Questions.A: The disciples realized that Jesus had power from God. (11)
Jesus's disciples believed in him. (11)
Questions.Alternative: What were the results of Jesus doing this miracle?
What were the results of Jesus doing this miraculous sign?
What were the results of Jesus performing this miracle?
What were the results of Jesus performing this miraculous sign?

Section.heading: John 2:12-17 Jesus drove the traders/merchants (and the animals) out of the temple courtyard.

Questions.Q: What bad things did some men do in these verses?
Questions.A: They sold sheep, cattle, and pigeons and exchanged money in the temple courtyard [that is, they were using the area around the temple like a market]. (14)

Questions.Q: For what do you think a temple is to be used by people?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The people were supposed to use the temple as a place to worship God.
Questions.Note: See "temple" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: For what purpose do you think people used a temple?
For what do you think the temple is to be used by people?
For what purpose do you think people used the temple?
What was the purpose of the temple?

Questions.Q: Who went to Capernaum?
Questions.A: Jesus, his mother, brothers, and his disciples went. (12)

Questions.Q: How long did they stay there?
Questions.A: They stayed a few days. (12)

Questions.Q: What was Jesus's reason for going to Jerusalem?
Questions.A: He went because it was almost time for the Jewish Feast of Passover. (13)

Questions.Q: What do you know about the Feast of Passover?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: This feast was to remember how God's angel passed over the homes of the Jews when they were slaves in Egypt. The angel passed over them because they had put the blood of a perfect lamb on their door posts as a sign. The Egyptians did not do as God had said/ordered/commanded/decreed, so the angel killed the oldest son and the firstborn animal (young) in every such house. Because of that, the Egyptians allowed the Jews to leave Egypt to return to the land God had given to the Jews' ancestor, Abraham, and to his descendants. (See "Passover" in KBT in the "sacrifice" entry.)

Questions.Q: Who/what did Jesus see/find in the temple?
Questions.A: People selling oxen and sheep and pigeons
Money-changers
Questions.Alternative: Who did Jesus see in the temple?
Who did Jesus find in the temple?
What did Jesus see in the temple?
What did Jesus find in the temple?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do to stop that/the wrong activity in the temple court?
Questions.A: He made a whip from cords. (15)
He drove all the animals out of the temple area. (15)
He overturned the tables of the moneychangers. (15)
He scattered the coins [of the moneychangers]. (15)
Questions.Note: He may have also driven the traders and the moneychangers out along with the animals.
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus do to stop that wrong activity in the temple court?
What did Jesus do to stop the wrong activity in the temple court?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus command the people, who were selling the doves, to do?
Questions.A: He told them to take the doves out of the temple area. (16)

Questions.Q: How were they using the temple area?
Questions.A: They had made it a market place. (16)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say the temple really was?
Questions.A: He said that it was his Father's house. (16)

Questions.Q: What Old Testament scripture did his disciples remember after seeing what he did/had done in the temple?
Questions.A: They remembered that, in the Old Testament scriptures, someone said, "Zeal for your house will consume me." (17)
Questions.Note: This was a quotation/quote from Psalm 69:9.
Questions.Alternative: What Old Testament scripture did his disciples remember after seeing what he did in the temple?
What Old Testament scripture did his disciples remember after seeing what he had done in the temple?

Questions.Q: To what do you think the disciples were referring as "scripture"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The scriptures are the contents of the Old Testament as God gave them to men to write down.
Questions.Note: See "scripture" in KBT.

Section.heading: John 2:18-22 Jesus talked about destroying the temple and rebuilding the temple.

Questions.Q: What was it that the Jews did not believe that Jesus could do?
Questions.A: They did not believe that Jesus could rebuild the temple in only three days, since it took [the people/the Jews] 46 years to build it the first time. (20)

Questions.Q: About what temple was Jesus really talking?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Jesus was talking about his own physical body. (21)
Questions.Note: See "body" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did the Jews ask Jesus to show them?
Questions.A: They wanted him to show them a miraculous sign to prove he had the authority to do what he had done in the temple. (18)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus answer them?
Questions.A: He said: "Tear down this temple, and in three days I will build it again." (19)

Questions.Q: When did Jesus's disciples remember that he had said this?
Questions.A: [Later on,] when [God] had raised him from the dead, they remembered. (22)

Questions.Q: When they remembered what he had said, what did they do?
Questions.A: They believed the scripture and the words that Jesus had said. (22)

Section.heading: John 2:23-25 Jesus knew what people are like.

Questions.Q: What was Jesus's reason for not trusting people?
Questions.A: The reason was because he knew what people are like. (24)

Questions.Q: What did many people in Jerusalem do when they saw the miraculous signs Jesus had done?
Questions.A: They trusted in his name. // They believed in Jesus. (23)

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason for a person or place to have a name?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A name is a label that identifies a person or place.
Questions.Note: See "name" in KBT.
If the translation does not use the word "name" here, omit this question.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do toward the people who trusted in his name/believed in him?
Questions.A: He did not trust himself to them. (24)
Questions.Note: Many believed the "signs" as coming from one who could do such things. However, their belief was only an intellectual belief, lacking in trust or commitment. Jesus knew they had only a superficial faith and did not commit Himself to them.
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus do toward the people who trusted in his name?
What did Jesus do toward the people who believed in him?

Questions.Q: What does a person do when he trusts someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He has a confident dependence in the character, ability, strength or truth of someone. (See "trust" in KBT in the "believe" entry.)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that there was no need for someone to tell Jesus about people?
Questions.A: Jesus knew [and understood] what was in a person [that is, what a person was really thinking]. (25)

Section.heading: John 3:1-15 Nicodemus came to Jesus at night. // Jesus said that a person must be born again.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell Nicodemus that was very difficult for him to understand?
Questions.A: He said that no one can see the kingdom of God unless he is born again. (3)

Questions.Q: What do you think the kingdom of God is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It has the significance of God's rule in the lives of men, rather than of a territory over which God rules.
Questions.Note: See "kingdom of God" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for a person to be born again?
Questions.A: It means the Spirit of God changes a person inside. He becomes a child of God. The man's heart, life, and thinking are made new, and he can know God.

Questions.Q: Who was Nicodemus?
Questions.A: He was a Pharisee. (1)
He was a member of the Jewish council. (1)

Questions.Q: What do you think a council is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: That council was an assembly of religious representatives that assembled to consider matters of doctrine, discipline, law, and morals.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think that council was?

Questions.Q: When did Nicodemus come to Jesus?
Questions.A: He came to him at night. (2)

Questions.Q: What did Nicodemus already know about Jesus?
Questions.A: He knew that Jesus was a teacher sent by God. (2)
Questions.Note: According to the T.H., the "we" who also knew this may have been the Pharisees as a group or the leaders as a group, or the leaders and the Pharisees together. Most likely, the "we" refers back to the "many" in 2:23. They were those people who believed because of/on the basis of Jesus's miracles.

Questions.Q: How did Nicodemus know that?
Questions.A: He knew that because of the miraculous signs that Jesus did [they were a proof of God's power working through Jesus]. (2)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Nicodemus was confused about a man being born when he is old?
Questions.A: He thought this was a physical re-birth, and he knew that an adult/a person cannot go back into his/her mother's womb to be born again. (4)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell Nicodemus was the way that a person had to be born again?
Questions.A: He said that a person must be born of water and the Spirit. (5)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for a person to be born of water?
Questions.A: The act of being "born of water" is when someone is put under the water by someone else. This symbolizes the person's decision to repent of his past sins and to do those things that the Lord requires of him from now on. His old way of living is now "washed" away by the water.
-OR-
Water is used as a symbol of God's cleansing power (as described in Ezekiel 26:25-27).
Questions.Note: The answer will depend upon the interpretation used in the translation.

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for a person to be born of the Spirit?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It refers to the transforming power of God to make a person a believer. The Spirit causes a person to become one of God's people/children.
Questions.Note: See "spirit" in KBT.
It may be important to indicate that the "spirit" is the "Holy Spirit."

Questions.Q: What do people reproduce?
Questions.A: People just produce other people. (6)

Questions.Q: What does the Spirit reproduce?
Questions.A: The spirit produces that which is spiritual/one who is a child of God (as in CEV). (6)

Questions.Q: What do you think something spiritual is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Something spiritual is relating to or consisting of spirit. It is of the nature of spirit rather than material. Spiritual things can not be seen with the human eye. (See "spiritual" in KBT in the "spirit" entry.)

Questions.Q: About what did Jesus tell Nicodemus not to be surprised?
Questions.A: He told him not to be surprised that he/Jesus said, "You [all people] must be born again." (7)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell Nicodemus about the wind?
Questions.A: He said the wind blows wherever it wishes. (8)
You can hear its sound, but you cannot know where it is coming from or where it is going. (8)

Questions.Q: To what did Jesus compare the wind?
Questions.A: He compared the wind to everyone who is born of the Spirit. (8)

Questions.Q: What did Nicodemus ask Jesus?
Questions.A: He asked Jesus how this could be. (9)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Jesus expected that Nicodemus should have known this?
Questions.A: Nicodemus was a teacher of [the people of] Israel and should have known this. (10)

Questions.Q: About what did Jesus [and his followers] testify?
Questions.A: They testified about what they knew and had seen. (11)
Questions.Alternative: About what did Jesus and his followers testify?
About what did Jesus testify?

Questions.Q: What was the response of the people [the Jews] to their testimony?
Questions.A: They did not accept it. (11)
Questions.Alternative: What was the response of the people the Jews to their testimony?
What was the response of the people to their testimony?

Questions.Q: What did Nicodemus not believe about what Jesus had said?
Questions.A: He could not believe what Jesus had said about the things of this earth. (12)

Questions.Q: Because of that, what else would Nicodemus not be able to believe?
Questions.A: He would not believe the things Jesus told/would tell him about heaven. (12)

Questions.Q: Who has gone up to heaven?
Questions.A: The Son of Man, who came down from heaven, has gone up there, also. (13)

Questions.Q: What did Moses do in the desert?
Questions.A: He put [an image of] a snake [made of bronze/metal] on a pole. (14)
Questions.Note: God told Moses to make a snake of bronze in Numbers 21:8-9.

Questions.Q: Whom were [the Jews] going to lift up in a similar way?
Questions.A: It was the Son of Man/Jesus. (14)
Questions.Note: According to Exegetical Helps, this referred to the Jews lifting Jesus up on the cross.
Questions.Alternative: Whom were the Jews going to lift up in a similar way?
Whom were going to lift up in a similar way?

Questions.Q: What does a person have to do to receive eternal life?
Questions.A: He has to believe in him [The Son of Man, God's only Son]. (15)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for a person to have eternal life?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that a person will live forever with God.
Questions.Note: This eternal life is in the spiritual realm not the physical.

Section.heading: John 3:16-21 God sent his only son into the world.

Questions.Q: What was God's purpose for sending his son into the world?
Questions.A: He sent him to save people. (17)

Questions.Q: What do you think this verse means by this "world"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It refers to all the people who live on the earth.
Questions.Note: See "world" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to save you?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that a person will rescue someone else out of a dangerous situation. In this case, Jesus came to mankind to rescue them from an eternity in Hell.
Questions.Note: See "save" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did God do because of his love for the people in the world?
Questions.A: He gave his only Son [to the world]. (16)

Questions.Q: What was the result of God giving his Son [to the world]?
Questions.A: Anyone who believes in him will not perish but have eternal life. (16)
Questions.Alternative: What was the result of God giving his Son to the world?
What was the result of God giving his Son?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means if someone perishes/for someone to perish?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that the person has died. // It means that the person will not be with God eternally.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think it means if someone perishes?
What do you think it means for someone to perish?

Questions.Q: What was not the reason that God sent his Son into the world?
Questions.A: He did not send him to condemn people. (17)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means if someone condemns someone else/for someone to condemn someone else?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that someone pronounces someone else guilty, with the clear implication that the person will be punished for what he did. (See "condemn" in KBT in the "judge, judgment" entry.)
Questions.Alternative: What do you think it means if someone condemns someone else?
What do you think it means for someone to condemn someone else?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about people who believe in him [the Son of God]?
Questions.A: They are not condemned [by God]. // [God] will not condemn people who believe in him. (18)
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus say about people who believe in him, the Son of God?
What did Jesus say about people who believe in him?
What did Jesus say about people who believe in the Son of God?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about people who do not believe in God's Son?
Questions.A: They are already condemned [by God]. // [God] has already condemned people who have not believed in God's Son. (18)

Questions.Q: What has come into the world?
Questions.A: [Jesus], the one called the light, has come. // The light has come. (19)

Questions.Q: What did people love, the darkness or the light?
Questions.A: They loved the darkness, that is, they loved to do evil deeds. (19)

Questions.Q: What is the reason for this?
Questions.A: They did evil deeds/things. (19)

Questions.Q: What does a person who does evil [deeds] think about Jesus/the light?
Questions.A: He does not want his evil deeds made visible (to others) by [the message of Jesus]. // He hates the light and will not come into the light. (20)
Questions.Alternative: What does a person who does evil think about Jesus?
What does a person who does evil think about the light?
What does a person who does evil deeds think about Jesus?
What does a person who does evil deeds think about the light?

Questions.Q: What is the reason for this?
Questions.A: The reason is that he is afraid that his evil deeds will be exposed by Jesus/[by the light]. (20)

Questions.Q: What does a person do who is doing true deeds/living in truth /living truthfully?
Questions.A: He comes/goes to Jesus. // He comes into the light. (21)
Questions.Alternative: What does a person do who is doing true deeds?
What does a person do who is living in truth?
What does a person do who is living truthfully?

Questions.Q: What is his reason for doing that?
Questions.A: He does that so that Jesus/the light may show that the deeds he did were done through God. (21)

Section.heading: John 3:22-36 John the Baptist spoke about Jesus.

Questions.Q: What did John say about Jesus?
Questions.A: John said that [Jesus] must become more important than he (John). (30)
The one [Jesus], who comes from above, is above all [things and people]. (31)
Whoever puts his faith in the Son [Jesus] will have eternal life. (36)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to have faith in someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Faith is the quality of trusting someone. It is the act of wholeheartedly and steadfastly believing in the existence, power, and benevolence of a supreme being. (See "faith" in KBT in the "believe, believing, belief, faith, trust" entry.)

Questions.Q: Where did Jesus and his disciples go?
Questions.A: They went into the land of Judea [Province]. (22)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do there?
Questions.A: He spent some time with his disciples and he baptized some people. (22)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that John baptized people at Aenon (a place or town)?
Questions.A: There was plenty of water there. (23)
The people were constantly coming to him to be baptized. (23)

Questions.Q: Which happened first, John baptizing those people or [Herod] putting him into prison?
Questions.A: John baptized those people before [Herod] put him in prison. (24)
Questions.Alternative: Which happened first, John baptizing those people or Herod putting him into prison?
Which happened first, John baptizing those people or putting him into prison?

Questions.Q: With whom did some of John's disciples argue?
Questions.A: They argued with a Jew. (25)
Questions.Alternative: With who did some of John's disciples argue?

Questions.Q: What do you know about Jews?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A Jew was a member of the nation of Palestine from the 6th century B.C. to the first century A.D. It refers to the descendants of Abraham through his son Isaac. A Jew was a member of the people of Israel. He was committed to the Jewish religious system. All male Jews were circumcised on the 8th day after their birth and this was a mark of being a Jew. (See "Jew" in KBT in the "Israel" entry.)

Questions.Q: About what did they argue with him?
Questions.A: They argued with him about the ceremonial/religious washing. (25)
Questions.Note: See comments in 2:6.

Questions.Q: Who reported something to John?
Questions.A: Some of his disciples reported it. (26)
Questions.Note: According to the T.H., the "they" is probably some of John's disciples.

Questions.Q: What did they tell John?
Questions.A: They said that the man, about whom John had been testifying, was baptizing [people]. (26)
Everyone was going to him. (26)

Questions.Q: Where was that man when he was with John?
Questions.A: He was on the other side of the Jordan River. (26)

Questions.Q: What did John tell them?
Questions.A: He said that a person can do only what is given to him from heaven [from God]. (27)

Questions.Q: Of what did John remind them that he had said before? // What did John remind them of what he had said before?
Questions.A: He said that he was not the Christ. (28)
He had been sent [by God] ahead of the Christ [who was to come later]. (28)
Questions.Alternative: Of what did John remind them that he had said before?
What did John remind them of what he had said before?

Questions.Q: To whom does the bride belong?
Questions.A: She belongs to the bridegroom. (29)

Questions.Q: What makes the bridegroom's friend happy?
Questions.A: He is happy when he hears the bridegroom's voice. (29)

Questions.Q: What made John's joy complete?
Questions.A: He was joyous when he heard the bridegroom's [Jesus'] voice. (29)

Questions.Q: Who must become less important?
Questions.A: John must become less important. (30)

Questions.Q: Who tells [people] about things which happen here in this earth?
Questions.A: The one, who is from the earth, that is, a human being tells people about things which happen here in this earth. (31)
Questions.Alternative: Who tells people about things which happen here in this earth?
Who tells about things which happen here in this earth?

Questions.Q: Who tells [people] what he has seen and heard in heaven?
Questions.A: The one, who is from heaven, tells [people] about those matters. (32)
Questions.Alternative: Who tells people what he has seen and heard in heaven?
Who tells what he has seen and heard in heaven?

Questions.Q: Who accepts his testimony?
Questions.A: No one accepts his testimony. (32)

Questions.Q: Who proves/guarantees/confirms that God is true?
Questions.A: The person who confirms the testimony/accepted his testimony. (33)
Questions.Alternative: Who proves that God is true?
Who guarantees that God is true?
Who confirms that God is true?

Questions.Q: Who speaks God's words?
Questions.A: The one, whom God has sent, speaks God's words. (34)

Questions.Q: To whom did God give the Spirit?
Questions.A: He gave the Spirit to the one whom He sent. (34)

Questions.Q: Whom does the Father love?
Questions.A: He loves the Son. (35)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means, when someone loves someone else?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The person who loves another person seeks the good of that person. His attitude to the one whom he loves is an attitude of persistent and selfless goodwill.
Questions.Note: See "love" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Into whose authority has the Father put everything?
Questions.A: He gave all authority to his Son. (35)

Questions.Q: Who will never have eternal life?
Questions.A: Whoever rejects the Son will never have eternal life. (36)

Questions.Q: What will happen to a person who rejects the Son?
Questions.A: God's wrath will be on him forever. (36)

Section.heading: John 4:1-6 Jesus left Judea and headed for Galilee.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus decide to do?
Questions.A: He decided to leave Judea and go to Galilee. (3)

Questions.Q: What was Jesus's reason for leaving Judea, according to these verses?
Questions.A: When Jesus learned that the Pharisees had heard that he/Jesus was winning and baptizing more disciples than John, Jesus left Judea. (1, 3)

Questions.Q: How many people did Jesus actually baptize?
Questions.A: He did not baptize any people. (2)

Questions.Q: Who was actually baptizing people?
Questions.A: Jesus's disciples were. (2)

Questions.Q: Did he reach Samaria [Province] before he arrived at/in Galilee or afterwards?
Questions.A: He reached Samaria before he reached Galilee. (4)
Questions.Alternative: Did he reach Samaria Province before he arrived at Galilee or afterwards?
Did he reach Samaria Province before he arrived in Galilee or afterwards?
Did he reach Samaria before he arrived at Galilee or afterwards?
Did he reach Samaria before he arrived in Galilee or afterwards?

Questions.Q: To what place did Jesus come?
Questions.A: He came to a town in Samaria called Sychar. (5)

Questions.Q: What was that town near?
Questions.A: It was near a piece of land that [long ago] Jacob gave to his son, Joseph. (5)

Questions.Q: What was on this land?
Questions.A: Jacob's well was there. (6)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do, when he came to the well?
Questions.A: He sat down beside the well to rest, because he was tired. (6)

Questions.Q: What time of day was it?
Questions.A: It was the middle of the day. // It was about the sixth hour. (6)
Questions.Note: According to the T.H., this probably was 12 o'clock noon.

Section.heading: John 4:7-26 Jesus talked with a woman at Jacob's well in Samaria.

Questions.Q: Who came and met Jesus at the well?
Questions.A: A Samaritan woman came there. // A woman of Samaria came there. (7)

Questions.Q: About what kind of water did Jesus and the woman talk?
Questions.A: He spoke about Living water. (10-11)
He also spoke about water that will eliminate thirst. (14-15)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell the woman would be the way true worshipers would worship the Father?
Questions.A: He told her that true worshipers would worship the Father by God's Spirit and truth. (23)
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus tell the woman would be the way true worshippers would worship the Father?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to worship the Father?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means to give him respect and devotion. It may be regarded as the direct acknowledgment to God, of his nature, attributes, ways and claims, whether by the outgoing of the heart in praise and thanksgiving or by deeds done in such acknowledgment.
Questions.Note: According to the T.H., a person must worship Him on the spiritual level, in the true way that God has shown.

Questions.Q: For what did the Samaritan woman come to the well?
Questions.A: She came to draw up some water. (7)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus ask the woman to give to him?
Questions.A: He asked her for some water to drink. (7)

Questions.Q: Where were Jesus's disciples?
Questions.A: They had gone into the town to buy food. (8)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the woman was surprised that Jesus asked her for a drink of water?
Questions.A: She was surprised because Jesus was a Jew, and the woman was a Samaritan. (9)
Questions.Note: The Jews never used the same dishes that Samaritans used. An alternative interpretation (less likely) is this: The Jews did not usually have anything to do with the Samaritans.

According to the T.H., there was a Jewish religious regulation in force around A.D. 65 which stated that Samaritan women were in a state of perpetual ritual impurity from the time of their birth; and anyone, who had contact with them, would share that ritual impurity. For that reason the Jews did not use dishes in common with the Samaritans.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell the woman?
Questions.A: He told her that she did not know what the gift of God was. (10)
He told her that she did not know who was asking her for water. (10)
He told her that if she had known those things she would have asked him [Jesus] to give her living water. (10)

Questions.Q: To what do you think Jesus was referring, when he spoke about "the gift of God"?
Questions.Note: "I do not know" would be an acceptable answer here. The main point of this question would be to check that there are no wrong implications. The most likely explanation is that he was referring to the Holy Spirit, often symbolized by water in John's gospel. Another possibility is that he was referring to the Jewish Law, from which Jesus quoted, and which in Rabbinical literature, was sometimes referred to as "God's gift".

Questions.Q: How did the woman address Jesus?
Questions.A: She called him "Sir." (11)
Questions.Note: This should be a polite, respect form, but not a term that would be used exclusively for addressing a divine being.

Questions.Q: What did the woman think about Jesus's ability to give her water?
Questions.A: She did not think he could give her any water. (11)

Questions.Q: What were the reasons that the woman thought that Jesus could not give her water?
Questions.A: He did not have anything with which to draw water. (11)
The well was very deep. (11)

Questions.Q: Do you think Jesus and the woman were talking about the same kind of water, or different kinds?
Questions.A: They were talking about different kinds of water.

Questions.Q: What did this woman ask Jesus about himself?
Questions.A: She asked him if he was greater than their father [ancestor] Jacob was. (12)

Questions.Q: Whose father [ancestor] was Jacob?
Questions.A: He was an ancestor of the Jews and the Samaritans. (12)
Questions.Note: According to the T.H., "our" ancestor could be interpreted as inclusive or exclusive. If it is inclusive, then she and Jesus had a common ancestor in Jacob. If it is exclusive, then Jacob was an ancestor of the Samaritans and not of the Jews.
Questions.Alternative: Whose father ancestor was Jacob?
Whose father was Jacob?

Questions.Q: According to that woman, to whom had Jacob given the well?
Questions.A: According to her, Jacob gave it to the [Samaritans]. (12)
Questions.Note: See comment on "our" ancestor above.

Questions.Q: Who had drunk from this well before?
Questions.A: Jacob, his sons, his flocks and his herds drank from it. (12)

Questions.Q: According to Jesus, what would happen to a person who drank water from that well?
Questions.A: He would be thirsty again. (13)

Questions.Q: According to Jesus, what would happen to a person who drank the water he gave?
Questions.A: He would never be thirsty again. (14)

Questions.Q: What did the water that Jesus mentioned represent?
Questions.A: It represented everlasting life. (14)

Questions.Q: What else did Jesus say about that water?
Questions.A: It will become like a spring of water in a person. (14)
Questions.Note: From The Bible Knowledge Commentary, "This inner spring contrasts with the water from the well, which required hard work to acquire. Jesus was speaking of the Holy Spirit who brings salvation to a person who believes and through him offers salvation to others."

Questions.Q: What did the woman ask Jesus to give to her?
Questions.A: She asked him for the water about which he had been talking. (15)

Questions.Q: What were the reasons that she wanted this water?
Questions.A: She wanted the water so that she would never be thirsty again. (15)
She wanted this water so that she would not have to come to the well again to draw water. (15)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell the woman to do?
Questions.A: He told her to call her husband, and then come back. (16)

Questions.Q: What did the woman tell Jesus?
Questions.A: She told him that she did not have a husband. (17)

Questions.Q: Did Jesus agree or disagree with what this woman said?
Questions.A: He agreed. (17)

Questions.Q: To how many men had she been married?
Questions.A: She had been married to five different men. (18)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell her about the man she was presently living with?
Questions.A: He told her that he was not her husband. (18)

Questions.Q: What did this woman say about Jesus?
Questions.A: She said that he was a prophet. (19)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that she said that?
Questions.A: She said that because of what Jesus told her about herself in verse 18. (19)

Questions.Q: Where did this woman's fathers [ancestors] worship?
Questions.A: They worshiped on the mountain nearby. (20)
Questions.Note: According to Exegetical Helps, "our fathers" could be referring only to the Samaritans, or it could be referring to the Samaritans and the Jews.
This was probably Mt. Gerizim since Jacob's well is located at the foot of the mountain.
Questions.Alternative: Where did this woman's fathers ancestors worship?
Where did this woman's fathers worship?

Questions.Q: According to the Jews, where were people to worship?
Questions.A: The Jews said that people were to worship in Jerusalem. (20)
Questions.Note: This is a reference to the Temple in Jerusalem.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell the woman about where they [the Samaritans] were to worship the Father?
Questions.A: He said that, in the future, you [the Samaritans] will not worship the Father on the mountain or in Jerusalem. (21)
Questions.Note: According to Exegetical Helps, "you will worship" must refer to the Samaritans.
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus tell the woman about where they the Samaritans were to worship the Father?
What did Jesus tell the woman about where they were to worship the Father?

Questions.Q: According to Jesus, what was the difference between what the Samaritans worshiped, compared to what the Jews worshiped?
Questions.A: The Samaritans worshiped someone they did not know. (22)
Questions.Note: The Jews worshiped someone they did know. (22)
Questions.Alternative: According to Jesus, what was the difference between what the Samaritans worshipped, compared to what the Jews worshipped?
According to Jesus, what was the difference between who the Samaritans worshiped, compared to who the Jews worshiped?
According to Jesus, what was the difference between how the Samaritans worshiped, compared to how the Jews worshiped?

Questions.Q: According to Jesus, where is salvation from?
Questions.A: Salvation is from the Jews [through whom God promised salvation]. (22)

Questions.Q: What do you think "salvation" means?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The noun form (Greek sôtêria) and the adjective form (Greek sôtêrios) usually refer in the New Testament to eternal salvation from sin, evil and death.
Questions.Note: See "salvation" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think Jesus meant by saying that salvation is from the Jews?
Questions.Note: "I do not know" would be an acceptable answer here. Those who have some scripture knowledge might say, "Jesus was a Jew" or "God chose the Jews as his own people and promised to help all the nations of the world through them."

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say was going to happen?
Questions.A: He said: "True worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth." (23)

Questions.Q: What do you think Jesus meant by "in spirit and truth"?
Questions.Note: "I do not know" would be an acceptable answer. There are various interpretations of this verse. According to Exegetical Helps, "spirit" could mean man's spirit or the Spirit of God. The T.H. states, that wherever the word "spirit" occurs unmarked in John's Gospel, the reference is to God's spirit. According to the NIV Commentary it is not likely that "spirit" here means the Holy Spirit. The human spirit is in mind here. One must worship, not simply outwardly but, in ones spirit. For "truth" the T.H. states that, in this Gospel, "truth" refers primarily to God himself.

Questions.Q: When is this going to happen?
Questions.A: It has already started to happen. (23)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about God?
Questions.A: He said that God is spirit. He does not have a body, [as a human does]. (24)

Questions.Q: In what way must people worship God?
Questions.A: His worshipers must worship him in spirit and truth. (24)
Questions.Note: See comments on 4:23.

Questions.Q: According to this woman, who was to come?
Questions.A: The Messiah, called Christ was to come. (25)

Questions.Q: What will the Messiah do when he comes?
Questions.A: He will explain everything. (25)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell the woman?
Questions.A: He told her that he was the one [the Messiah]. (26)

Section.heading: John 4:27-30 The Samaritan woman told other people about Jesus.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the woman thought that Jesus was possibly the Christ?
Questions.A: She thought that because he had told her things about herself. (29)

Questions.Q: Who returned at this time?
Questions.A: Jesus's disciples returned. (27)

Questions.Q: What was their reason for being surprised?
Questions.A: They were surprised because Jesus was talking with a woman. (27)
Questions.Note: Jewish customs did not allow a man to talk with a woman in the street.

Questions.Q: What did the disciples ask Jesus?
Questions.A: They did not ask him anything. (27)

Questions.Q: What did the woman do next?
Questions.A: She left her water jar and went back to the town [of Sychar]. (28)
Questions.Note: Check to ensure that the word used for water jar is appropriate for a jar used for carrying water.

Questions.Q: To whom did she talk, when she arrived back at the town?
Questions.A: She talked to the people there. (28)
Questions.Alternative: With whom did she talk, when she arrived back at the town?
What did she do when she arrived back at the town?
What did the woman do when she went back to the town?
What did the woman do when she returned to her town?
To who did she talk, when she arrived back at the town?

Questions.Q: What did she say to them?
Questions.A: She urged them to come to see the man who had told her everything she had ever done. (29)

Questions.Q: What did she ask them about the man?
Questions.A: She asked them if they thought that he was the Christ. (29)

Questions.Q: What did these people do?
Questions.A: They left the town and went out to where he was. (30)

Section.heading: John 4:31-38 Jesus spoke with his disciples about doing God's work.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus use as an illustration to teach his disciples here?
Questions.A: He used the idea that someone plants the seed and another person reaps the harvest. (37)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus's disciples tell him to do?
Questions.A: They told him to eat something. (31)

Questions.Q: What was Jesus's answer to them?
Questions.A: He told them that he had food to eat about which they did not know. (32)
Questions.Alternative: How did Jesus respond?
What was Jesus' answer to them?
How did Jesus respond to them?

Questions.Q: What did the disciples think about what Jesus had said?
Questions.A: They began to think that maybe someone had brought him some food. (33)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell his disciples was his food?
Questions.A: He told them that because he did what God sent him to do, that was like food to him. (34)

Questions.Q: What were people saying?
Questions.A: They said that it was still four months until the time to harvest their grain. (35)
Questions.Note: There are two possible interpretations here. (a) that this was a proverb, and the meaning is that the time from planting to harvest is four months (i.e. there is always a set time of waiting and maturing.) In this case the "do you not say" would refer to a proverbial saying that was generally said, and "you" refers to people in general; Or (b) that from the time when Jesus was speaking, it was still four months until the harvest would be ready. In this case, the "you" would refer to the disciples. Commentators tell us that it was actually six months from planting time to harvest, so interpretation (b) is probably more likely.

Questions.Q: According to Jesus, when would the fields [crops] be ready for [someone to] harvest?
Questions.A: The fields [crops] were already ripe and ready to be harvested by someone. (35)
Questions.Alternative: According to Jesus, when would the fields crops be ready for someone to harvest?
According to Jesus, when would the fields crops be ready for harvest?
According to Jesus, when would the fields be ready for someone to harvest?
According to Jesus, when would the fields be ready for harvest?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say the reaper was doing?
Questions.A: He was drawing/receiving his wages. (36)
He was harvesting the crop for eternal life. (36)

Questions.Q: What were the results of what the reaper was doing?
Questions.A: The sower and the reaper were both glad/joyful. (36)

Questions.Q: What do you think he meant by this?
Questions.Note: He meant that if the truth is preached to the people, they will believe and will live forever with God.

Questions.Q: Who were the people that were being glad together?
Questions.A: The one who planted and the one who reaped were glad. (36)

Questions.Q: Who do you think the "planter" and the "reaper" represented?
Questions.Note: They represented those who had been preaching God's message and preparing the way (John the Baptist and others), and those who are now preaching God's message and seeing people believe in Jesus.

Questions.Q: What saying is true? // What is true about what people often say?
Questions.A: Someone plants [the seed] and another [person] reaps [the crop]. (37)
Questions.Alternative: What saying is true?
What is true about what people often say?

Questions.Q: What do you think Jesus meant by this saying?
Questions.Note: He meant that different people have different tasks to do for God. He meant that some people have already prepared the way, and now other people will see the results.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus send his disciples out to do?
Questions.A: He sent them to reap [a harvest] where they did not work [did not plant the seed]. (38)

Questions.Q: What do you think that means?
Questions.Note: It means that he sent them to preach to people who had already heard God's message from others.

Questions.Q: Who did the hard work [planted the seed]?
Questions.A: They were other people. (38)
Questions.Alternative: Who did the hard work and planted the seed?
Who did the hard work of planting the seed?
Who did the hard work, planting the seed?
Who did the hard work?
Who planted the seed?
Who planted the seed (the hard work)?

Section.heading: John 4:39-42 Many people in Samaria came to believe that Jesus is the Messiah.

Questions.Q: What were the two reasons that people in that place began to believe in Jesus?
Questions.A: They believed because of the woman's testimony. (39, 42)
They believed because they had heard Jesus for themselves, and so they knew that he was really the Savior of the world. (42)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to be a savior?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The personal noun "savior" (Greek sôtêr) is used in the New Testament to mean "one who saves from spiritual and eternal danger". It may refer to either God or Jesus Christ.
Questions.Note: See "savior" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did the Samaritans ask Jesus to do?
Questions.A: They asked him to stay with them. (40)

Questions.Q: How long did Jesus stay with them?
Questions.A: He stayed two days. (40)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that many more people began to believe in Jesus?
Questions.A: They had heard his message. // They had heard Jesus preaching. (41)

Questions.Q: What do you think someone is doing when they preach?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: When someone preaches, they are proclaiming the gospel to those who are listening. This also means a person urges others to accept or abandon an idea or course of action.

Section.heading: John 4:43-54 Jesus went to Galilee and healed the son of a government official.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the people in Galilee welcomed Jesus when he arrived there?
Questions.A: They had seen everything he had done during/at the Passover feast in Jerusalem. (45)

Questions.Q: Whom did Jesus heal in these verses?
Questions.A: He healed the son of a government official. (49-50)

Questions.Q: What do you think it meant for Jesus to heal someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It meant he cured the person of the disease or affliction.

Questions.Q: After two days in Samaria, where did Jesus go?
Questions.A: He went to Galilee. (43)

Questions.Q: What had Jesus said?
Questions.A: He said that a prophet is not honored by those in his own country. (44)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means, when you honor someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: To honor someone is to show high regard or appreciation for them.

Questions.Q: To what town did Jesus return?
Questions.A: He returned to Cana in Galilee. (46)

Questions.Q: What had happened in that town?
Questions.A: Jesus had turned water into wine. (46)

Questions.Q: Whose son was sick?
Questions.A: A government official's son was sick. (46)

Questions.Q: Where was that government official?
Questions.A: He was in Capernaum. (46)
Questions.Note: According to the T.H., the official went to Cana presumably from Capernaum.

Questions.Q: Where was his son?
Questions.A: He was in Capernaum. (46)

Questions.Q: What did that government official hear?
Questions.A: He heard that Jesus had come from Judea and had arrived in Galilee. (47)

Questions.Q: What did that government official beg Jesus to do?
Questions.A: He wanted Jesus to come to Capernaum to heal his son. (47)

Questions.Q: How sick was that official's son?
Questions.A: He was about to die. (47)

Questions.Q: According to Jesus, what would be necessary for people to believe [him]?
Questions.A: They would have to see miraculous signs and wonders. (48)
Questions.Alternative: According to Jesus, what would be necessary for people to believe him?
According to Jesus, what would be necessary for people to believe?

Questions.Q: What did the official request/urge Jesus to do?
Questions.A: He urged Jesus to come to Capernaum before his child died. (49)
Questions.Alternative: What did the official request Jesus to do?
What did the official urge Jesus to do?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus promise the official?
Questions.A: He told him that his son would live. (50)

Questions.Q: What did the official do?
Questions.A: He believed what Jesus said and left. (50)

Questions.Q: While he was on his way home, whom did the official meet?
Questions.A: He met his servants. (51)

Questions.Q: What did they tell him?
Questions.A: They told him that his boy was well. (51)

Questions.Q: What did the official ask his servants?
Questions.A: He asked them the time when his son was better. (52)

Questions.Q: What did they answer him?
Questions.A: They answered him, "The fever left him yesterday at the seventh hour." (52)
Questions.Note: This could have been one o'clock in the afternoon.

Questions.Q: At what time had Jesus told the official that his son would live?
Questions.A: He had told him that at the same time. (53)

Questions.Q: What did the official and his household [all those living in the official's house] do?
Questions.A: They all believed in Jesus. (53)
Questions.Alternative: What did the official and his household all those living in the official's house do?
What did the official and his household do?

Questions.Q: What was their reason for believing in him?
Questions.A: They realized that Jesus had healed the official's son. (53)

Questions.Q: Up to this verse, how many miraculous signs had Jesus done since coming from Judea to Galilee?
Questions.A: He had done two miraculous signs. (54)

Section.heading: John 5:1-9a Jesus healed a paralyzed man at Bethesda pool in Jerusalem.

Questions.Q: Whom did Jesus heal in these verses?
Questions.A: He healed a man who had been sick for thirty-eight years. (5)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Jesus went to Jerusalem?
Questions.A: He went to attend a feast of the Jews. (1)

Questions.Q: What was the name of that gate in Jerusalem?
Questions.A: It was the Sheep Gate. (2)

Questions.Q: What was by that gate?
Questions.A: A pool called Bethesda was by the gate. (2)

Questions.Q: How many colonnades/porches were by this pool?
Questions.A: There were five colonnades/porches. (2)
Questions.Alternative: How many colonnades were by this pool?
How many porches were by this pool?

Questions.Q: Who were the people on the porches?
Questions.A: They were sick people--blind, lame, and paralyzed. (3)
Questions.Note: This is not an exhaustive list of sickness, but a list of examples.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus know about this man?
Questions.A: He knew that he had been sick for a long time. (6)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus ask the sick man?
Questions.A: He asked him if he wanted to be well. (6)

Questions.Q: What were the reasons that this man was still sick?
Questions.A: He did not have anyone to help him into the pool, when the water was stirred up [by someone]. (7)
Someone else had always entered the pool before he did [and had been healed]. (7)
Questions.Note: The people believed that, from time to time, an angel of the Lord came down and stirred up the waters in the pool. The first person into the pool, after each disturbance, was cured of whatever disease he had.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus command this man to do?
Questions.A: He told him to stand up, pick up his mat, and walk. (8)

Questions.Q: How long did it take for the man to be cured [by Jesus]?
Questions.A: He was cured immediately [by Jesus]. (9a)
Questions.Alternative: How long did it take for the man to be cured by Jesus?
How long did it take for the man to be cured?

Questions.Q: What did the man do after Jesus healed/cured him?
Questions.A: He picked up his mat and walked away. (9a)
Questions.Alternative: What did the man do after Jesus healed him?
What did the man do after Jesus cured him?

Section.heading: John 5:9b-13 The religious leaders were angry because Jesus healed a man on the Sabbath.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the Jews wanted to know who had healed this man?
Questions.A: The man was carrying his mat on the Sabbath, and that was against their [Jewish] law. (10)

Questions.Q: What day was it, when [Jesus] healed this man?
Questions.A: It was a Sabbath day. (9b)
Questions.Alternative: What day was it, when Jesus healed this man?
What day was it, when healed this man?

Questions.Q: What do you think the Sabbath means?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The Sabbath is the name of the seventh and last day of the week. It was set aside by the Jews as a strict day of rest from the normal work that was done on the six other days of the week. The Jews continue to observe the Sabbath on Saturday.
Questions.Note: See "Sabbath" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What was the man's reason for carrying his mat?
Questions.A: Jesus, who had healed him, had told him to do it. (11)

Questions.Q: What did the Jews ask that man who had been healed?
Questions.A: They asked him who had told him to pick up his [mat] and walk. (12)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the man did not know who had healed him?
Questions.A: He did not know because Jesus had left him/slipped away in the crowd. (13)

Section.heading: John 5:14-18 The religious leaders were angry because Jesus said that God is his Father.

Questions.Q: What were the reasons that the Jews wanted to kill Jesus?
Questions.A: They said that he had broken the Sabbath. (18)
He had made himself equal with God, by saying that God was his Father. (18)

Questions.Q: Where did Jesus later find the man whom he had healed?
Questions.A: He found him in the temple. (14)

Questions.Q: Of what fact did Jesus remind the man?
Questions.A: He told him that he was well. (14)

Questions.Q: What exhortation/command did Jesus give the man?
Questions.A: He told him to stop sinning or something worse might happen to him. (14)
Questions.Alternative: What exhortation did Jesus give the man?
What command did Jesus give the man?

Questions.Q: What did the man, whom Jesus healed, tell the Jews?
Questions.A: He told them that Jesus was the one who had healed him. (15)

Questions.Q: What did the Jews do to Jesus, because of what he was doing on the Sabbath?
Questions.A: They began to persecute him. (16)

Questions.Q: What was Jesus's reason for always doing as he did/working?
Questions.A: He was always doing what he did because [he was doing what his Father wanted him to do]. // His Father was always doing what he desired to do/working. (17)
Questions.Alternative: What was Jesus's reason for always doing as he did?
What was Jesus's reason for always doing as he working?

Section.heading: John 5:19-24 The Son does whatever the Father does.

Questions.Q: Who was speaking in these verses?
Questions.A: Jesus was speaking. (19)

Questions.Q: About whom was Jesus talking, when he talked about the Son and the Father?
Questions.A: He was talking about himself and God the Father. (19)

Questions.Q: Whose example does the Son of God follow?
Questions.A: He follows the Father's example. (19)

Questions.Q: What does the Father show to the Son?
Questions.A: He shows him all that he is doing. (20)
He will show him even greater things than these [what Jesus had done up to that point]. (20)

Questions.Q: How will the people react to the things that the Father will show to the Son?
Questions.A: They will be amazed. (20)

Questions.Q: Who is able to raise the dead?
Questions.A: The Father and the Son are able to raise the dead. (21)

Questions.Q: To whom does the Son give life?
Questions.A: He gives it to those he wants to give to. (21)

Questions.Q: Who does the Father judge?
Questions.A: The Father judges no one. (22)

Questions.Q: To whom has the Father given the right to judge people?
Questions.A: He gave the right to the Son. (22)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to judge someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means someone/a judge will determine if a person is guilty or not of committing a crime. He does this by assessing the evidence connected to the person and what he may have done.
Questions.Note: See "judge" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What was the Father's reason for giving the Son the right to judge people?
Questions.A: He did that so that all [people] will honor the Son in the same way that they honor the Father. (23)

Questions.Q: Whom must a person honor, if he says that he honors the Father?
Questions.A: He must honor the Son. (23)

Questions.Q: What must a person do to receive eternal life?
Questions.A: He must hear Jesus's words. (24)
He must believe the one who sent Jesus. (24)

Questions.Q: What will happen to the person who receives eternal life?
Questions.A: He will not be condemned [by the Son], but he will have eternal life. (24)

Section.heading: John 5:25-29 The Son of God will judge those people who have died.

Questions.Q: What will happen to the people who have died?
Questions.A: They will come out of their graves and live again. (28-29)
Those who have done good [things] will live [forever with God]. (29)
Those who have done evil [things] will be condemned [by the Son of God]. (29)

Questions.Q: What do the dead people [ones who do not believe Jesus] need to do so that they will live?
Questions.A: They need to hear/listen to the voice of the Son of God. (25)
Questions.Alternative: What do the dead people ones who do not believe Jesus need to do so that they will live?
What do the dead people need to do so that they will live?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus state about the Father and the Son?
Questions.A: They are the source of [eternal] life. (26)

Questions.Q: Who has given the Son of Man the right to judge [people]?
Questions.A: The Father has given him that right. (27)
Questions.Alternative: Who has given the Son of Man the right to judge people?
Who has given the Son of Man the right to judge?

Questions.Q: What was his reason for giving this right to the Son of Man?
Questions.A: He is the Son of Man. (27)

Questions.Q: Whose voice will all the dead people hear?
Questions.A: They will hear his [the Son of Man's] voice. (28)

Section.heading: John 5:30-47 Jesus spoke about the things that show that he did indeed come from God.

Questions.Q: What is the proof that Jesus's words can be accepted as true?
Questions.A: Someone else testified on his behalf and his testimony is true. (32)
John spoke the truth [about Jesus]. (33)
The work, that the Father had given him to finish and which he was doing, showed that he was from God. (36)
The Father has testified concerning him. (37)
Moses wrote about him. (46)

Questions.Q: What method does Jesus use to judge [others]?
Questions.A: He judges [others] only by what God tells him to do. (30)
Questions.Alternative: What method does Jesus use to judge others?
What method does Jesus use to judge?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Jesus's judgment is right?
Questions.A: He does not seek to please himself, but the one who sent him [to the world]. (30)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about any testimony that he would tell about himself?
Questions.A: He said that testimony would not be valid. (31)

Questions.Q: Who do you think sent messengers to John?
Questions.A: The Jews sent messengers. (33)
Questions.Note: This is probably a reference to 1:19.

Questions.Q: What was Jesus's reason for reminding them about John's testimony?
Questions.A: He reminded them about it, so that they might be saved [by God]. (34)

Questions.Q: To what did Jesus compare John?
Questions.A: He compared him to a lamp that burned and gave light. (35)

Questions.Q: What was the people's response to him?
Questions.A: They enjoyed his light [message] for a while. (35)

Questions.Q: What was more important than what John said about Jesus?
Questions.A: The miracles that Jesus did showed that he was from God. (36)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell them they had never known about the Father?
Questions.A: Those people had never heard his voice or seen his form. (37)
Questions.Note: The Greek word for "form" refers to the "visible form" or "outward appearance."

Questions.Q: What is the reason these people did not believe [God's] message?
Questions.A: They did not believe [God's] message because they did not believe the one whom he had sent. (38)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason these people did not believe God's message?
What is the reason these people did not believe message?

Questions.Q: How did those people think they could obtain eternal life?
Questions.A: They thought they could obtain eternal life by studying the scriptures. (39)

Questions.Q: About whom do the scriptures testify?
Questions.A: They tell about Jesus. (39)

Questions.Q: What was the reason that those people did not have eternal life?
Questions.A: They were not willing to believe Jesus. (40)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus not accept from people?
Questions.A: He did not accept their praise. (41)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell those people that they did not have?
Questions.A: He told them that they did not [have the] love [of] God [in their hearts]. (42)

Questions.Q: What does it mean to you to talk about the "heart"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The most common use of the word "heart" in the Bible is to refer to the spiritual center or innermost part of a human being. In Hebrew and Greek "heart" is most commonly associated with thoughts and ideas.
Questions.Note: See "heart" in KBT.
If the translation does not use the word "heart" here, omit this question.

Questions.Q: From whom did Jesus receive his power/authority?
Questions.A: It was from his Father. (43)
Questions.Alternative: From whom did Jesus receive his power?
From whom did Jesus receive his authority?

Questions.Q: Whom did those people accept?
Questions.A: They accepted people/anyone who came in their/his own authority. (43)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they could not believe [in him]?
Questions.A: They wanted praise from one another, and not praise from God. (44)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that they could not believe in him?
What is the reason that they could not believe?

Questions.Q: Who was the one who accused them?
Questions.A: Moses. (45)
Questions.Note: Because they did not obey all the writings of Moses, they were guilty of rejecting God.

Questions.Q: In what had they hoped?
Questions.A: Moses. (45)
Questions.Note: They had hoped to follow the teachings of Moses, but they did not obey them.

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to hope in something?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means to have a desire to see something happen or to obtain something.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that those, who believed Moses's words, will believe in Jesus?
Questions.A: Moses wrote about Jesus. (46)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they did not believe Jesus's words?
Questions.A: They did not believe what Moses had written. (47)

Section.heading: John 6:1-15 Jesus fed five thousand men (plus women and children).

Questions.Q: What was the great thing that Jesus did in these verses?
Questions.A: He fed about five thousand people with only a little food. (10, 12)

Questions.Q: Where did Jesus go?
Questions.A: He went back across the Sea of Galilee. (1)

Questions.Q: Who was following him?
Questions.A: A great crowd of people followed him. (2)

Questions.Q: What was their reason for following him?
Questions.A: They had seen his miraculous signs/mighty works in healing the sick. (2)

Questions.Q: Where did Jesus go?
Questions.A: He went up and sat down on a hillside. (3)

Questions.Q: Who went with him?
Questions.A: His disciples went with him. (3)

Questions.Q: What feast were the people to observe soon?
Questions.A: The people were to observe the Passover Feast soon. (4)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus see, as he looked around?
Questions.A: He saw a large crowd [of people] coming to him. (5)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus ask Philip?
Questions.A: He asked him where they could buy bread/food to feed all the people. (5)

Questions.Q: What was Jesus's reason for asking Philip this?
Questions.A: He wanted to test him [to see whether he believed that Jesus had power to do something about the need for food]. (6)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus already know?
Questions.A: He knew what he was going to do. (6)

Questions.Q: How much did Philip think it would cost to buy enough bread to feed all the people?
Questions.A: It would cost more than two hundred dollars/two hundred day's wages. (7)
Questions.Note: In the Greek this is two hundred denarii. According to the NIV Commentary a denarius was a day's wage. In normal times 200 hundred denarii would buy 4,800 quarts of barley or 1,600 quarts of wheat.

Questions.Q: Who was Andrew?
Questions.A: He was one of Jesus's disciples. (8)
He was Simon Peter's brother. (8)

Questions.Q: What did Andrew tell Jesus that a boy had?
Questions.A: He told Jesus that a boy had five barley loaves and two fish. (9)

Questions.Q: About what was Andrew concerned?
Questions.A: He was concerned that this small amount of food would not be enough to feed so many people. (9)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell [his disciples] to do?
Questions.A: He told [his disciples] to have the people sit down/to tell the people to sit down. (10)
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus tell his disciples to do?
What did Jesus tell to do?

Questions.Q: What did the people do?
Questions.A: They sat down. (10)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do with the bread?
Questions.A: He took it. (11)
He gave thanks [to God for it]. (11)
He [and his disciples] distributed it to the people sitting down. (11)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do with the fish?
Questions.A: He did the same thing with the fish that he had done with the bread. (11)

Questions.Q: From where do you think this bread and fish came?
Questions.A: It was the boy's food/lunch. (9)
