Questions.Q: How much bread and fish did Jesus [and his disciples] give to each person?
Questions.A: They gave everyone as much bread and fish as they wanted. (11)
Questions.Alternative: How much bread and fish did Jesus and his disciples give to each person?
How much bread and fish did Jesus give to each person?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell the disciples to do after everyone had eaten as much as they wanted?
Questions.A: He told them to pick up the left over pieces. (12)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Jesus wanted them to do that?
Questions.A: He did not want any of the food to be wasted [by leaving it on the ground]. (12)

Questions.Q: What did the disciples do with the left over pieces of the bread?
Questions.A: They filled twelve baskets with the pieces. (13)

Questions.Q: What did the people say about Jesus?
Questions.A: They said that he was the prophet who was to come into the world. (14)

Questions.Q: What was their reason for saying that/this?
Questions.A: They said that because of the miraculous sign that Jesus did. (14)
Questions.Alternative: What was their reason for saying that?
What was their reason for saying this?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus know?
Questions.A: He knew the people wanted to make him king by force. (15)

Questions.Q: Where did Jesus go?
Questions.A: He went into the hills by himself. (15)

Section.heading: John 6:16-21 Jesus walked on the (surface of) the water/lake.

Questions.Q: What was the amazing thing that Jesus did in these verses?
Questions.A: He walked on the water. (19)

Questions.Q: What did his [Jesus'] disciples do in the evening?
Questions.A: They went down to the lake. (16)
They got into a boat. (17)
They started across the lake for Capernaum [a town]. (17)
Questions.Alternative: What did his Jesus' disciples do in the evening?
What did his disciples do in the evening?

Questions.Q: By the time it had gotten dark, who had not yet joined the disciples?
Questions.A: Jesus had not yet joined them. (17)

Questions.Q: What was happening on the lake?
Questions.A: There was a strong wind blowing. (18)
There were big waves in the water/lake. (18)

Questions.Q: How far had the disciples rowed [the boat]?
Questions.A: They had rowed it three or four miles/five or six kilometers. (19)
Questions.Alternative: How far had the disciples rowed the boat?
How far had the disciples rowed?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the disciples were afraid?
Questions.A: They were afraid because they saw Jesus walking on the water and coming toward the boat. (19)

Questions.Q: For what reason do you think the disciples were afraid?
Questions.A: They thought he was a ghost.
Questions.Note: This is made explicit in the same account in the book of Mark 6:49.
Questions.Alternative: For what reason do you think the disciples were afraid when they saw Jesus walking on the water?
For what reason do you think the disciples were afraid when they saw someone walking on the water?
What do you think the disciples thought they were seeing?
What do you think the disciples thought they were seeing that frightened them?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to them?
Questions.A: He told them not to be afraid, because it was he. (20)

Questions.Q: What did the disciples do?
Questions.A: They welcomed Jesus into the boat. (21)
Questions.Note: According to the T.H., it should be made clear that they didn't have to rescue him from the lake. One could say they received him into the boat or welcomed him aboard.

Questions.Q: What happened when Jesus entered/got into the boat?
Questions.A: Immediately the boat reached shore/land at the place /to which they were heading. (21)
Questions.Alternative: What happened when Jesus entered the boat?
What happened when Jesus got into the boat?

Section.heading: John 6:22-24 The people looked for Jesus.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the crowd went to Capernaum?
Questions.A: They went to Capernaum because they knew that Jesus was no longer on the other side[Eastern side of the lake], and they wanted to find him. (24)

Questions.Q: Where was the crowd that Jesus had fed?
Questions.A: They were on the other side of the lake [across from Capernaum]. (22)

Questions.Q: What did they realize?
Questions.A: They realized that only one boat had been there. (22)

Questions.Q: What did they know about Jesus?
Questions.A: They knew that he had not gone with the disciples when they left in the boat. (22)

Questions.Q: From where had other boats come?
Questions.A: Other boats had come from Tiberias. (23)

Questions.Q: What had happened near the place where those boats had come to shore?
Questions.A: The Lord/Jesus had given thanks [to God], and then the people had eaten the bread. (23)

Questions.Q: Who else, besides Jesus, did the crowd realize was not there?
Questions.A: They realized that his disciples were not there. (24)

Section.heading: John 6:25-59 Jesus told people that he is the bread/food which gives people life (from God).

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the people were looking for Jesus?
Questions.A: He had fed them when they were hungry. (26)

Questions.Q: According to Jesus, about what should they have been seeking?
Questions.A: They should have been seeking to have eternal life. (27)

Questions.Q: Where did those people find Jesus?
Questions.A: They found him on the other side of the lake. (25)

Questions.Q: What did they ask Jesus?
Questions.A: They asked him when he had arrived there. (25)

Questions.Q: What would have been a good reason for them to look for Jesus?
Questions.A: They had seen the miraculous signs [that he did]. (26)

Questions.Q: About what type of food did Jesus tell them not to be thinking?
Questions.A: He told them not to think about food that spoils. (27)

Questions.Q: What proof is there that God the Father agreed with what Jesus was doing?
Questions.A: God gave him the power/authority to do miracles. (27)

Questions.Q: What did the people ask Jesus?
Questions.A: They asked him what God wanted them to do. (28)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell them?
Questions.A: He said that God wanted people to believe in the one whom he sent [Jesus]. (29)

Questions.Q: What did those people ask Jesus to do?
Questions.A: They asked him to perform a miraculous sign. (30)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they wanted Jesus to do that?
Questions.A: They said that if he did a miracle, then they would believe him. (30)

Questions.Q: Who had eaten manna in the desert?
Questions.A: Their ancestors ate manna. (31)

Questions.Q: Who gave the manna to their ancestors?
Questions.A: They said he [Moses] gave the manna to them. (31)
Questions.Note: According to the T.H., the people believed that the "he" in the quotation "He gave them bread..." is referring to Moses.

Questions.Q: From where did the manna come?
Questions.A: It came from heaven. (31)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell them that Moses did not do?
Questions.A: Jesus told them that Moses did not give them the bread from heaven. (32)

Questions.Q: Who gave them the true/real bread from heaven?
Questions.A: Jesus's Father gave it to them. (32)
Questions.Alternative: Who gave them the true bread from heaven?
Who gave them the real bread from heaven?

Questions.Q: What is the meaning of the bread that God gave?
Questions.A: It is the one [Jesus] who came down from heaven. (33)

Questions.Q: Who gave life to the people?
Questions.A: The one [Jesus], who came down from heaven, gave life (eternal life). (33)

Questions.Q: What did the people want Jesus to give to them?
Questions.A: They wanted him to give them this bread always/from now on. (34)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about himself?
Questions.A: He said that he was the bread of life. (35)

Questions.Q: What happens to a person who comes to Jesus and believes in him?
Questions.A: That person will never be hungry or thirsty again. (35)
Questions.Note: It would be wise to check here to be sure that the respondent does understand that this is figurative, not literal hunger and thirst.

Questions.Q: What do you think Jesus meant by that?
Questions.Note: Jesus meant that he will satisfy that person's spiritual needs (the needs of his "heart").

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell those people?
Questions.A: They had seen him, but they still did not believe [in him]. (36)

Questions.Q: Who are the people who will come to Jesus?
Questions.A: Those people that the Father gives to Jesus will come to him. (37)

Questions.Q: What will Jesus do to people who come to him?
Questions.A: He will not drive those people away. (37)

Questions.Q: From where did Jesus come?
Questions.A: He came from heaven. (38)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Jesus came down from heaven?
Questions.A: He came to do the will of [the Father] the one who sent him. (38)

Questions.Q: What did [the Father] the one, who sent him, want him to do?
Questions.A: He did not want him [Jesus] to lose any of the people he gave to him. (39)
He wanted him [Jesus] to raise all of them to life on the last day. (39)
Questions.Alternative: What did the Father the one, who sent him, want him to do?
What did the one, who sent him, want him to do?

Questions.Q: What does the Father want for all people who see the Son and believe in him?
Questions.A: He wants them to have eternal life. (40)
He wants Jesus to resurrect/raise them to life on the last day. (40)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the Jews murmured/grumbled against Jesus?
Questions.A: They murmured/grumbled because Jesus said that he was the bread that came down from heaven. (41)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that the Jews murmured against Jesus?
What is the reason that the Jews grumbled against Jesus?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the people did not believe that Jesus came down from heaven?
Questions.A: They did not believe because they knew that Mary and Joseph were his parents. (42)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell the people to stop doing?
Questions.A: He told them to stop murmuring/grumbling. (43)

Questions.Q: What must happen for a person to come to Jesus?
Questions.A: The Father must draw him to Jesus. (44)

Questions.Q: What will Jesus do for that person?
Questions.A: He will raise that person to [eternal] life on the last day. (44)

Questions.Q: What had the prophets written?
Questions.A: They wrote that God will teach all people. (45)

Questions.Q: Who are the people who come to Jesus?
Questions.A: Everyone who listens to the Father and learns from him. (45)

Questions.Q: Who has seen the Father?
Questions.A: The one, who is from God, has seen him. (46)

Questions.Q: Who do you think is the one from God?
Questions.A: He is Jesus, God's Son.

Questions.Q: Who has eternal life?
Questions.A: Anyone, who believes [in Jesus], has eternal life. (47)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about himself?
Questions.A: He said that he is the bread of life. (48)

Questions.Q: What happened to the people who ate the manna?
Questions.A: Eventually they all died. (49)
Questions.Note: It was only natural causes, not the manna that caused their deaths.

Questions.Q: What is the source of the bread about which Jesus talked?
Questions.A: Heaven is the source. (50)

Questions.Q: What will happen to a person who eats this bread?
Questions.A: He will live forever [with God]. (50)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about himself?
Questions.A: He said that he is the living bread which came down from heaven. (51)

Questions.Q: What must a person do in order to live forever?
Questions.A: He must eat this bread. (51)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say this bread is?
Questions.A: He said it was his death. (51)
Literally, he said it was his flesh/body.

Questions.Q: What was Jesus's reason for dying?
Questions.A: He died so that [people] in the world might live [forever]. (51)
Questions.Alternative: What was Jesus's reason for giving his body?
What was Jesus's reason for giving his flesh by dying?
What was Jesus's reason for sacrificing his body?

Questions.Q: How do you think Jesus gave his flesh for people?
Questions.A: He did it by dying for people.
Questions.Alternative: How do you think Jesus gave his body for people?

Questions.Q: About what did the people start arguing?
Questions.A: They argued about how Jesus could give them his flesh to eat. (52)

Questions.Q: What will happen to a person who does not eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood?
Questions.A: He will not have eternal life. (53)

Questions.Q: What must a person do in order to have eternal life?
Questions.A: He must eat Jesus's flesh and drink his blood. (54)

Questions.Q: What will Jesus do for such a person?
Questions.A: He will raise/resurrect that person up on the last day. (54)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about his flesh and blood?
Questions.A: He said it is real food and drink. (55)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about a person who eats Jesus's flesh and drinks his blood?
Questions.A: He said that person lives in fellowship/union with Jesus, and Jesus lives in fellowship/union with him. (56)

Questions.Q: Who sent Jesus [to the world]?
Questions.A: The living Father sent him. (57)
Questions.Alternative: Who sent Jesus to the world?
Who sent Jesus?

Questions.Q: What is the source of Jesus's life?
Questions.A: The Father is the source. (57)

Questions.Q: From where did the bread come about which Jesus talked?
Questions.A: It came down from heaven. (58)

Questions.Q: What happened to their ancestors after they ate the manna?
Questions.A: They died. (58)
Questions.Note: (Note: This was not as a result of eating the manna).

Questions.Q: Why do you think their ancestors died after eating the manna/bread/food that came down from heaven?
Questions.A: They died. (58)
Questions.Note: The purpose of this question is to ensure that the respondent is not was not as a result of eating the manna).

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the bread that Jesus talked about better than the manna?
Questions.A: It is better because anyone, who partakes of/eats this bread, will live forever. (58)

Questions.Q: Where did Jesus teach these things?
Questions.A: He taught them in the synagogue in Capernaum. (59)

Questions.Q: What do you think a synagogue is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A synagogue is a building or place of assembly used by Jewish communities primarily for religious worship.
Questions.Note: See "synagogue" in KBT.

Section.heading: John 6:60-65 Many people left Jesus; but some recognized that he was God's chosen one (who spoke about eternal life).

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Jesus told his disciples that no one could come to him, unless the Father made it possible for him to come?
Questions.A: Jesus knew that some of them did not believe [him]; and he knew who would betray him. (64-65)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means, when someone betrays someone else?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means to deliver someone into the hands of an enemy by treachery or fraud in violation of trust.

Questions.Q: What was very hard for some of Jesus's disciples to accept?
Questions.A: The things that he had just taught [to the people in the synagogue]. (60)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus know?
Questions.A: He knew that the disciples were grumbling about the things he taught. (61)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus ask them?
Questions.A: He asked them if the things he taught offended them. (61)

Questions.Q: What else did Jesus ask them?
Questions.A: He asked them what they would think if they saw the Son of Man ascend to the place/go back to the place from where he came. (62)

Questions.Q: What is the source of life?
Questions.A: The Spirit [of God] is the source of life. (63)

Questions.Q: What can a person do by his own efforts to obtain eternal life?
Questions.A: He can not do anything. // He can not produce eternal life. (63)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about his words?
Questions.A: They are from [God's] spirit who causes eternal life. (63)

Section.heading: John 6:66-71 Many of Jesus's disciples deserted Him.

Questions.Q: What was Jesus's reason for asking his twelve disciples if they were going to leave him?
Questions.A: He asked them because many of his followers had turned away and did not travel with him anymore. (66)

Questions.Q: What was Jesus's reason for referring to Judas as a devil?
Questions.A: He knew that Judas was going to betray him. (70-71)

Questions.Q: What do you think Jesus meant by calling Judas a devil?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He meant that he belonged to Satan/was under Satan's control. Here Jesus was speaking prophetically of the time when Satan would enter Judas. It may have the implication of "an enemy who is on the side of Satan," "an enemy who is controlled by Satan" or "a person who is wicked like Satan." (See "devil" in KBT in the "evil spirit, unclean spirit, demon" entry.)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus ask the twelve disciples?
Questions.A: He asked them if they also were going to leave him. (67)

Questions.Q: What are Jesus's words able to do?
Questions.A: His words are able to give eternal life [to people]. // When [people] obeyed his words/message, they then had eternal life. (68)

Questions.Q: What did those disciples know about Jesus?
Questions.A: They knew that he was the Holy One from God. (69)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to be holy?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Someone who is "holy" is set apart [by God] and dedicated to the service or worship of God. Anything that is "holy" for God must reflect his character by being physically unblemished or reflecting, to some degree, his purity.
Questions.Note: See "holy" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Who chose the twelve disciples?
Questions.A: Jesus chose them. (70)

Section.heading: John 7:1-9 Jesus talked with his brothers about going to the Feast of Tabernacles.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus's brothers tell him to do?
Questions.A: They told him he should leave Galilee and go to Judea. (3)

Questions.Q: What was their reason for telling him to do that?
Questions.A: They wanted him to do that, so that more of his disciples could see the miracles he was doing. (3)

Questions.Q: Where was Jesus traveling at this time?
Questions.A: He traveled in Galilee. (1)

Questions.Q: What was his reason for not traveling in Judea?
Questions.A: There the Jews wanted to kill him. (1)

Questions.Q: What feast was near at hand/close/approaching/about to start?
Questions.A: The Feast of Tabernacles was about to be observed. // [The Jews] were about to observe the Feast of Tabernacles. (2)
Questions.Alternative: What feast was near at hand?
What feast was close?
What feast was approaching?
What feast was about to start?

Questions.Q: What do you think the Feast of Tabernacles was?
Questions.A: It was a special day of religious celebration for the Jews.
Questions.Note: At the Feast of Tabernacles the Jews rejoiced because the harvest had been completed. They made/constructed temporary shelters and stayed in them for one week. In that way they remembered their ancestors. Their ancestors had lived in temporary shelters when they wandered in the wilderness for forty years. This was before they entered the land of Canaan that God had promised them.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus's brothers tell him?
Questions.A: They told him he should show himself to the world, and let them know what he was doing. (4)

Questions.Q: Who were some of the people that did not believe in Jesus?
Questions.A: His brothers did not yet believe in him. (5)

Questions.Q: What was Jesus's reply to his brothers?
Questions.A: He said that the right time had not yet come for him to go there, but that any time was right for them to go there. (6)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the people of the world hated Jesus?
Questions.A: They hated him because he told them that the things they were doing were evil/bad. (7)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell his brothers to do?
Questions.A: He told them to go to the feast. (8)

Questions.Q: What was his reason for not going to the feast?
Questions.A: He said that it was not the right time for him to go there. (8)

Questions.Q: After he said that where did he stay?
Questions.A: He stayed in Galilee. (9)

Section.heading: John 7:10-13 Jesus went to the Feast of Tabernacles.

Questions.Q: In what way did Jesus attend this feast?
Questions.A: He went to the feast secretly. (10)

Questions.Q: Who went to the feast first, Jesus or his brothers?
Questions.A: His brothers went first. (10)

Questions.Q: For whom were the Jews/Jewish leaders watching/searching at the feast?
Questions.A: They watched for Jesus. (11)
Questions.Alternative: For whom were the Jews watching at the feast?
For whom were the Jews searching at the feast?
For whom were the Jewish leaders watching at the feast?
For whom were the Jewish leaders searching at the feast?

Questions.Q: What were the different things that people were saying about Jesus?
Questions.A: Some people said that he was a good man. (12)
Other people said that he deceived people. (12)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that people did not speak publicly about Jesus?
Questions.A: They did not speak publicly about Jesus because they were afraid of the Jews/Jewish leaders. (13)

Section.heading: John 7:14-24 Jesus taught the people in the temple courtyard.

Questions.Q: What was the source of the things that Jesus taught?
Questions.A: The things that he taught came from [God] who sent him. (16)

Questions.Q: When did Jesus start to teach during that feast?
Questions.A: He started to teach halfway through the feast. (14)

Questions.Q: Where did he teach [the people]?
Questions.A: He taught them in the temple. (14)
Questions.Alternative: Where did he teach the people?
Where did he teach?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the Jews were amazed?
Questions.A: They were amazed because he knew so much and yet had never studied. (15)

Questions.Q: What will a person find out if he has a desire to do God's will?
Questions.A: He will find out whether Jesus's teaching is from God or just from himself. (17)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that a person speaks from his own knowledge?
Questions.A: A person speaks from his knowledge because he wants to gain honor for himself. (18)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about someone who wants people to honor the one who sent him?
Questions.A: He said that person speaks the truth, and there is nothing false in him. (18)

Questions.Q: What had Moses given them?
Questions.A: He gave them the law. (19)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell the people concerning the law?
Questions.A: He told them that none of them were obeying the law. (19)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus ask them?
Questions.A: He asked them why they were trying to kill him. (19)

Questions.Q: What did the people say to him?
Questions.A: They told him that he had a demon. (20)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to have a demon?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that the person is troubled or controlled by the demon, i.e. the demon is exercising its evil power over him. (See "demon" in KBT in the "evil spirit, unclean spirit" entry.)

Questions.Q: What did the people say to Jesus in response to his question about them trying to kill him?
Questions.A: They denied it by asking him who was trying to kill him. (20)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the people had been surprised?
Questions.A: They were surprised because Jesus had done a miracle. (21)

Questions.Q: What did Moses command the people to do?
Questions.A: He commanded the people [through the law] to circumcise their sons. (22)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to circumcise someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that someone removes the foreskin of the male genital. Traditionally the father or someone else would perform this on his son on the 8th day after his birth, and this was a mark of being a Jew. (See "the circumcised" in KBT in the "Israel, Jew, Hebrew" entry.)

Questions.Q: Who actually started the practice of circumcision?
Questions.A: The Jews' ancestors began that practice. (22)

Questions.Q: On what day did they sometimes circumcise their [male] children?
Questions.A: They did it on the Sabbath day. (22)
Questions.Alternative: On what day did they sometimes circumcise their male children?
On what day did they sometimes circumcise their children?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they circumcised their sons?
Questions.A: They did it in order to observe/obey Moses's law. (23)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they were angry with Jesus?
Questions.A: They were angry because he had healed a man on the Sabbath day. (23)

Questions.Q: What do you think was wrong, according to the law, when Jesus healed the sick man and when the Jews circumcised children on the Sabbath day?
Questions.Note: In both situations individuals worked/were working on the Sabbath day.

Questions.Q: In what way did those people judge [what Jesus did]?
Questions.A: They judged [him] by what they saw him do. (24)
Questions.Alternative: In what way did those people judge what Jesus did?
In what way did those people judge?

Questions.Q: What is the right way to judge someone else?
Questions.A: The right way to judge someone else is to obtain the true facts about what happened. (24)

Section.heading: John 7:25-31 People asked one another if Jesus was the Messiah.

Questions.Q: What did the people discuss in these verses?
Questions.A: They talked about whether or not Jesus was the Messiah. (26)

Questions.Q: Who was the man that the [Jewish leaders] wanted to kill?
Questions.A: They wanted to kill Jesus. (25)
Questions.Note: The answer here would have to be understood from the context of the passage.
Questions.Alternative: Who was the man that the Jewish leaders wanted to kill?
Who was the man that the wanted to kill?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that those people thought that Jesus was not the Messiah?
Questions.A: They thought they knew from where this man [Jesus] came. (27)
They believed that no one would know from where the Messiah came. (27)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to them?
Questions.A: He asked them whether/if they really knew him and knew from where he came. (28)

Questions.Q: By whose authority did Jesus come?
Questions.A: He came by the authority of the one who sent him. (28)

Questions.Q: What did he say about the one who sent him?
Questions.A: He said that he is true/speaks the truth. (28)
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus say about the one who sent him?
What did he say about that one?

Questions.Q: Who is it that does not know that one?
Questions.A: The people to whom Jesus was talking did not know him. (28)
Questions.Alternative: Who did not know the one who sent Jesus?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Jesus knew that one?
Questions.A: He knew that one because he came from him. (29)
He knew that one because he sent Jesus. (29)

Questions.Q: Who do you think is that one about whom Jesus was talking?
Questions.A: God the Father was the one about whom he talked.
Questions.Alternative: Who do you think is the one about whom Jesus was talking?

Questions.Q: What did the people try to do to Jesus?
Questions.A: They tried to seize/arrest him. (30)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they were not able to do that?
Questions.A: They could not arrest him, because his hour/time for this to happen had not yet come. (30)

Questions.Q: What were many of the people in that crowd thinking?
Questions.A: They believed in Jesus. (31)

Questions.Q: What did they say about the Messiah?
Questions.A: He will not do more miraculous signs than this man has done. (31)

Section.heading: John 7:32-36 Jesus told the people that he was going away.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about himself that confused the Jews?
Questions.A: He said, "You will look for me, but you will not find me," and "Where I am, you cannot come." (36)

Questions.Q: What did the chief priests and the Pharisees send the guards to do?
Questions.A: They sent the guards to arrest him [Jesus]. (32)

Questions.Q: What do you know about the chief priests?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Arndt and Gingrich say the following: "The plural is used to denote members of the Sanhedrin who belonged to high-priestly families: ruling high priests, those who had been deposed, and adult male members of the most prominent priestly families." Jeremiah argues that the last of these categories should rather be the leading priests who held the chief executive posts in the Temple. They were, in any case, an influential group of the most important priests.
Questions.Note: See "chief priest" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell the people?
Questions.A: He told them he would be with them for a short time and then he was going to the one who sent him. (33)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell them?
Questions.A: He said that they would not be able to find him. (34)
He said that they would not be able to come to where he was. (34)

Questions.Q: What were the Jews trying to conclude/deduce?
Questions.A: They wanted to know where Jesus was going that they could not find him. (35)
Questions.Alternative: What were the Jews trying to conclude?
What were the Jews trying to deduce?

Questions.Q: Where did the Jews think that Jesus might go?
Questions.A: They thought he might go to the Greek cities where the Jews lived, to teach the non-Jews/Greeks. (35)

Section.heading: John 7:37-39 Jesus talked about God's Spirit/the Holy Spirit.

Questions.Q: To what did Jesus compare the Spirit?
Questions.A: He compared him/the Spirit to streams of living water. (38-39)

Questions.Q: Which day of the feast was the most important?
Questions.A: The last day was the most important. (37)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus invite the people to do on the last day of the feast?
Questions.A: He invited anyone, who was thirsty, to come to him and drink. (37)

Questions.Q: What will happen to a person who believes in Jesus?
Questions.A: Streams of living water will flow from within him [He will have God's Spirit within him]. (38)

Questions.Q: Who was going to receive this Spirit [from God]?
Questions.A: Those people, who believed in Jesus, would receive Him. (39)
Questions.Alternative: Who was going to receive this Spirit from God?
Who was going to receive this Spirit?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that [God] had not given the Spirit [to those who believed in Jesus] before/in the past?
Questions.A: God had not yet glorified Jesus. // God had not yet raised Jesus to glory/heaven. (39)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that God had not given the Spirit before?
What is the reason that God had not given the Spirit in the past?
What is the reason that God had not given the Spirit to those who believed in Jesus before?
What is the reason that God had not given the Spirit to those who believed in Jesus in the past?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means that God glorified/for God to glorify Jesus?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that God honored Jesus. (See "glorify" in KBT in the "glory, glorious" entry.)
Questions.Alternative: What do you think it means that God glorified Jesus?
What do you think it means for God to glorify Jesus?

Section.heading: John 7:40-44 The people argued about who Jesus was.

Questions.Q: What is the reason for the division among the people in the crowd?
Questions.A: Different people believed differently about who Jesus was. (43)

Questions.Q: What did many people in the crowd say about Jesus?
Questions.A: They said that he was the Prophet. (40)

Questions.Q: What did other people say about him?
Questions.A: They said that he was the Messiah. (41)

Questions.Q: What is the reason some people said that he was not the Messiah?
Questions.A: They believed that the Messiah could not come from Galilee. (41)

Questions.Q: What did the scriptures say about the Messiah?
Questions.A: He would be a descendant of David. (42)
He would come from Bethlehem, the town where David had lived. (42)

Questions.Q: What did some of the people want to do?
Questions.A: They wanted to seize/arrest him. (44)

Section.heading: John 7:45-53 The religious leaders refused to believe that Jesus was the Messiah.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the chief priests and Pharisees were concerned?
Questions.A: The guards, whom they had sent, had not arrested Jesus and brought him back. (45)
They suspected that the guards were beginning to believe in Jesus. (47)

Questions.Q: What reply did the guards give to the chief priests and to the Pharisees?
Questions.A: They said, "No one has ever talked as this man does." (46)

Questions.Q: For what reason did those Pharisees say that those guards should not believe in Jesus?
Questions.A: They said that because none of the Jewish leaders or Pharisees had believed in him. (48)

Questions.Q: What did the Pharisees say about those people?
Questions.A: They said that they did not know the law [of Moses], so they were under a curse [from God]. (49)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for God to put a curse on someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that God will pronounce a punishment on someone or condemn a person to be cut off from all of God's blessings. (See "curse" in KBT in the "bless, blessed, blessing" entry.)

Questions.Q: Who was Nicodemus?
Questions.A: He was the one who had gone to see Jesus before. (50)
He was one of them [the Pharisees]. (50)

Questions.Q: What did Nicodemus ask the Pharisees about the law?
Questions.A: He asked them, "Does the law condemn a person before hearing him, to find out what he had been doing?" (51)

Questions.Q: What did they ask Nicodemus about himself?
Questions.A: They asked him if he was also from Galilee. (52)
Questions.Note: According to Exegetical Helps this question was rhetorical, since they knew that Nicodemus was not from Galilee. They were angry at him for apparently siding with the despised Galilean. To accuse someone of being a Galilean was a term of the highest reproach.

Questions.Q: What did the Pharisees tell Nicodemus he would discover, if he looked into the matter?
Questions.A: He would discover that a prophet does not come out of Galilee. (52)
Questions.Note: According to The New International Commentary on the New Testament, the Pharisees were angry men at this point and were not thinking clearly. They overlooked Jonah, who was a Galilean, and other prophets who may have come from Galilee.

Questions.Q: After that, what did everyone do?
Questions.A: They went home. (53)

Section.heading: John 8:1-11 The religious leaders brought a woman caught in adultery to Jesus.

Questions.Q: What did the teachers of the law and the Pharisees do to try to trap Jesus?
Questions.A: They brought a woman to him, who was caught in adultery, and asked Jesus what they should do/should be done with her. (3-6)

Questions.Q: What do you know about the teachers of the law?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The TEV and NIV translate "scribe" as "teacher of the law." The scribes were important people in the Jewish religious system. They were experts in knowing and interpreting the laws of Moses and in applying them to everyday life. (See "teacher of the law" in KBT in the "scribe" entry.)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to commit adultery with another person?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Adultery is the act of unfaithfulness in marriage that occurs when one of the marriage partners voluntarily engages in sexual intercourse with a person of the opposite sex other than his or her marriage partner.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do at the temple court?
Questions.A: He sat down and began teaching the people who gathered around him. (2)

Questions.Q: What did the law of Moses command the Jews to do to a woman who had committed adultery?
Questions.A: The law commanded them to stone to death any woman who committed adultery. (5)
Questions.Note: The law commanded both the man and the woman to be stoned, but in this passage, the teachers of the law and the Pharisees are focusing only on the woman.
Questions.Alternative: What did the law of Moses command the Jews to do to someone who had committed adultery?
What did the law of Moses command the Jews to do to women who had committed adultery?
What did the law of Moses command the Jews to do to people who had committed adultery?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do?
Questions.A: He bent over and wrote on the ground with his finger. (6)

Questions.Q: Why do you think Jesus wrote on the ground?
Questions.Note: There is no certain answer to this. Some possible answers could be: This indicated that he did not want to pass judgment. It showed that he was embarrassed. It showed that he was considering his answer. It showed that he was acting the part of a Roman judge who was recording his answer before announcing it. It indicated contempt for the accusers. He wrote passages from the law to support his verdict, or he wrote the sins of the accusers to shame them.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell those people to do?
Questions.A: He said that anyone, who had not committed sin, could start stoning the woman. (7)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do then?
Questions.A: He bent over again and wrote on the ground. (8)

Questions.Q: What did the people do?
Questions.A: They began to leave, the older ones leaving first. (9)

Questions.Q: Who was still there?
Questions.A: Jesus and the woman were left there. (9)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus ask the woman?
Questions.A: He asked her if anyone condemned her. (10)

Questions.Q: What did the woman tell Jesus?
Questions.A: She said no one [had condemned her]. (11)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to her?
Questions.A: He said that neither did he condemn her. // He said he was not condemning her either. (11)

Questions.Q: What did he command her to do?
Questions.A: He told her to go and leave/stop her life of sin. (11)

Questions.Q: Who are the two that say Jesus's words are true?
Questions.A: Jesus and the Father say his words are true. (18)

Questions.Q: What will people, who follow Jesus, experience?
Questions.A: They will never walk in darkness. (12)
They will have the light of life. (12)

Questions.Q: For what reason did the Pharisees believe that Jesus's testimony was not valid/true?
Questions.A: They did not believe his testimony was valid because he was testifying on his own behalf. (13)
Questions.Alternative: For what reason did the Pharisees believe that Jesus's testimony was not valid?
For what reason did the Pharisees believe that Jesus's testimony was not true?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that what Jesus said about himself was valid/true?
Questions.A: He knew from where he had come and where he was going. (14)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that what Jesus said about himself was valid?
What is the reason that what Jesus said about himself was true?

Questions.Q: What did the people not know about Jesus?
Questions.A: They did not know from where he had come or where he was going. (14)

Questions.Q: In what way did those people judge others?
Questions.A: They judged others in a human way/by human standards. (15)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about his judgment of others?
Questions.A: He did not judge anyone. (15)

Questions.Q: What else did Jesus say about his judgment of others?
Questions.A: He said if he did judge anyone, his decision would be right. (16)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the way Jesus judges others would be right?
Questions.A: He was not alone in the decision, since his Father, who sent him, stood/agreed with him. (16)

Questions.Q: What did their law state?
Questions.A: It stated that the testimony of two witnesses was valid/true. (17)

Questions.Q: What did they/the Pharisees ask Jesus?
Questions.A: They asked him where his father was. (19)
Questions.Alternative: What did they ask Jesus?
What did the Pharisees ask Jesus?

Questions.Q: Whom did those people/the Pharisees not know?
Questions.A: They did not know Jesus nor his Father. (19)
Questions.Alternative: Whom did those people not know?
Whom did the Pharisees not know?

Questions.Q: If those people had known Jesus who else would they have known?
Questions.A: They would have known his Father. (19)

Questions.Q: Where did Jesus teach these things to the people?
Questions.A: He taught in the temple area near where the offerings were put. (20).

Questions.Q: What is the reason that no one seized/arrested him?
Questions.A: No one seized/arrested him because his time for this to happen had not yet come. (20)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that no one seized him?
What is the reason that no one arrested him?

Section.heading: John 8:21-30 Jesus told the people what happens to those who do not believe in him.

Questions.Q: What did he say would happen to those people [who did not believe in him]?
Questions.A: He said they would die without God forgiving their sins/in their sins. (21)
Questions.Alternative: What did he say would happen to those people who did not believe in him?
What did he say would happen to those people?

Questions.Q: What could they do so that God forgave their sins/they would not die in their sins?
Questions.A: They needed to believe that Jesus was the one whom he claimed to be. (24)
Questions.Alternative: What could they do so that God forgave their sins?
What could they do so they would not die in their sins?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say he was going to do?
Questions.A: He said he was going to go away. (21)

Questions.Q: Where could they not go?
Questions.A: They could not go where Jesus was going. (21)

Questions.Q: What did they think Jesus meant when he said that they could not go where he was going?
Questions.A: They thought he was going to kill himself. (22)

Questions.Q: What was the difference between Jesus and those people/the Pharisees?
Questions.A: Jesus came from heaven. They belonged to the earth. (23)
Questions.Alternative: What was the difference between Jesus and those people?
What was the difference between Jesus and the Pharisees?

Questions.Q: What did those people ask Jesus?
Questions.A: They asked him who he was. (25)

Questions.Q: What did he tell them?
Questions.A: He said that he was the one whom he claimed to be from the beginning. (25)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus have to say about them?
Questions.A: He had much to tell them about the bad/evil things they did. (26)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about the one who had sent him?
Questions.A: Jesus said that he was true/reliable. (26)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell the people?
Questions.A: He told the people only what he heard from the one who sent him. (26)

Questions.Q: What did those people not understand?
Questions.A: They did not understand the fact that he was talking to them about his Father. (27)

Questions.Q: According to Jesus what would they know after the people crucified him/put him on a cross?
Questions.A: They would know who he really was. (28)
They would know that he does nothing on his own. (28)
They would know that he only tells [the people] what the Father has taught him. (28)
Questions.Alternative: According to Jesus what would they know after the people crucified him?
According to Jesus what would they know after the people put him on a cross?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about the one who sent him?
Questions.A: He said that he/his Father was with Jesus. (29)
He had not left him alone. (29)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus always do?
Questions.A: He always did what pleased him [his Father]. (29)

Questions.Q: What was the response of many of the people who heard Jesus?
Questions.A: They believed in him. (30)

Section.heading: John 8:31-41 Jesus told the Jews that if they obeyed his teachings they would be free from sin.

Questions.Q: What could have made them free?
Questions.A: If they knew the truth [about God], then they would be free. (32)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that those people thought they were free?
Questions.A: They thought they were free because they were descendants of Abraham and they said that they had never been slaves to anyone. (33)

Questions.Q: To whom was Jesus talking?
Questions.A: He talked to the Jews who believed in him. (31)

Questions.Q: What did he tell them?
Questions.A: He told them that, if they obeyed his teaching, they would really be his disciples. (31)

Questions.Q: What did they ask Jesus?
Questions.A: They asked him how they would be set free. (33)

Questions.Q: According to Jesus what is the condition of anyone who sins?
Questions.A: That person is a slave of sin. (34)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to be a slave of someone/something?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that the person is totally responsible to and dependent upon another person, or the person has become completely subservient to a dominating influence. (See "slave" in KBT in the "servant, slave" entry.)
Questions.Alternative: What do you think it means to be a slave of someone?
What do you think it means to be a slave of something?

Questions.Q: What is the difference between a son and a slave?
Questions.A: A son belongs to a family forever, but a slave does not always belong to the family. (35)

Questions.Q: For what reason did the people want to kill Jesus?
Questions.A: They did not accept what he said. (37)

Questions.Q: About what did Jesus tell them?
Questions.A: He told them about the things that he had seen in the Father's presence. (38)

Questions.Q: What did those people do?
Questions.A: They did what they heard from their/had been taught by their fathers. (38)

Questions.Q: According to those people, who was their father?
Questions.A: Abraham was their father/ancestor. (39)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they were wrong in saying that Abraham was their father?
Questions.A: They were wrong because they did not do the things their father, Abraham, did. (39)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do for those people?
Questions.A: He told them the truth from God. (40)

Questions.Q: What was the difference between what Abraham had done and what those people wanted to do?
Questions.A: Those people wanted to kill Jesus, but Abraham never tried to do anything like that. (40)

Questions.Q: According to Jesus, whom were they imitating?
Questions.A: They imitated their father. (41)
Questions.Note: Jesus implied that their father was not Abraham, since they did not do the same as Abraham had done.

Questions.Q: What did they tell Jesus?
Questions.A: They said that they were not illegitimate children, but that God was their Father. (41)

Section.heading: John 8:42-47 Jesus told the Jews that, if God were their Father, they would love him. // Jesus told the Jews that they were children of the Devil, not children of God.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell the Jews/them?
Questions.A: He said that, if God were their father, they would love him. (42)
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus tell the Jews?
What did Jesus tell them?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell them?
Questions.A: He came from God. (42)
He did not come on his own. (42)
God sent him. (42)

Questions.Q: What was the reason that they did not understand what Jesus had said?
Questions.A: They did not understand what Jesus had said because they refused to accept his message. (43)

Questions.Q: According to Jesus, who was the father of those people?
Questions.A: The Devil was their father. (44)

Questions.Q: What do you know about the Devil?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "Devil" is the Greek equivalent of the Hebrew "Satan." Satan is the chief enemy of God. He is the supreme evil spiritual being, who leads and directs all other evil spiritual beings (See "Devil" in KBT in the "Satan" entry.)

Questions.Q: Whose desires did they obey? // Whom did they obey?
Questions.A: They obeyed the Devil. // They obeyed the Devil's desires/orders. (44)
Questions.Alternative: Whose desires did they obey?
Whom did they obey?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about the devil?
Questions.A: He was a murderer from the beginning. (44)
There is no truth in him. (44)
He naturally lies. // It is his habit to lie. (44)
He is a liar. (44)
He is the father of lies. (44)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that those people did not believe Jesus?
Questions.A: He was telling the truth, and they did not want to believe the truth. (45)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus challenge those people to do?
Questions.A: He challenged them to prove that he was guilty of sin. (46)

Questions.Q: Who hears what God says?
Questions.A: He who belongs to God hears God. (47)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that those people/Jews did not hear?
Questions.A: They did not belong to God. (47)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that those people did not hear?
What is the reason that those Jews did not hear?

Section.heading: John 8:48-59 Jesus made some claims about himself to the Jews. // Jesus told the Jews what kind of person he is.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about himself?
Questions.A: Anyone who kept/believed his word would never die [that is, they will live forever with God]. (51)
Abraham rejoiced because he knew about the future coming of the Messiah. (56)
Before Abraham was born, he existed. (58)

Questions.Q: Of what did the Jews accuse Jesus?
Questions.A: They said that he was a Samaritan
and demon possessed. (48)

Questions.Q: What was his answer to them?
Questions.A: He said that he was not possessed by a demon. (49)

Questions.Q: Whom did he honor?
Questions.A: He honored his Father. (49)

Questions.Q: What did those people/Jews do to Jesus?
Questions.A: They dishonored him. (49)
Questions.Alternative: What did those people do to Jesus?
What did those Jews do to Jesus?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about being glorified/honored [by men]?
Questions.A: He was not seeking men's honor/it, but that there was one who was seeking it for him. (50)
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus say about being glorified by men?
What did Jesus say about being honored by men?
What did Jesus say about being glorified?
What did Jesus say about being honored?

Questions.Q: What did he say about the one who was seeking glory/honor for him?
Questions.A: He was the one to decide in Jesus's favor/judge. (50)
Questions.Alternative: What did he say about the one who was seeking glory for him?
What did he say about the one who was seeking honor for him?

Questions.Q: Of what did the Jews accuse Jesus?
Questions.A: They said he was demon possessed. (52)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they said that?
Questions.A: They said that because he had said that anyone, who kept/obeyed his word, would never die; and yet Abraham and the prophets had died. (52)

Questions.Q: What did they think that Jesus was saying?
Questions.A: They thought he believed that he was greater than Abraham and the prophets. (53)

Questions.Q: Who was Abraham?
Questions.A: He was the father/ancestor of the Jews. (53)

Questions.Q: What would Jesus's honor mean, if he honored himself?
Questions.A: His honor would mean nothing. (54)

Questions.Q: Who honored Jesus?
Questions.A: His Father honored him. (54)

Questions.Q: Whom did the Jews claim to be their Father?
Questions.A: They claimed that their Father was God. (54)

Questions.Q: Who knows God?
Questions.A: Jesus knows/knew him. (55)

Questions.Q: What else does Jesus do?
Questions.A: He keeps his [God's] word. (55)

Questions.Q: Who does not know God?
Questions.A: The people, to whom Jesus was talking, did not know him. (55)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say he would be, if he said he did not know God?
Questions.A: He would be a liar like the people to whom he was talking. (55)

Questions.Q: About what did Abraham know?
Questions.A: He knew about the future coming of Jesus. (56)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the Jews did not believe that Jesus had seen Abraham?
Questions.A: They did not believe that Jesus had seen Abraham because Jesus was less than fifty years old. (57)

Questions.Q: What did the Jews do after they heard Jesus say, "Before Abraham was born, I am"?
Questions.A: They picked up stones to throw at him. (59)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do?
Questions.A: He hid himself and left the temple grounds. (59)

Section.heading: John 9:1-12 Jesus healed a man who was born blind.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do in these verses?
Questions.A: He caused a blind man to see. (11)

Questions.Q: Whom did Jesus see?
Questions.A: He saw a man who had been born blind. (1)

Questions.Q: What did his disciples ask Jesus/him?
Questions.A: They asked him: "Whose sin had caused him to be blind, his or his parents?" (2)
Questions.Alternative: What did his disciples ask Jesus?
What did his disciples ask him?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell them?
Questions.A: He told them that neither the man nor his parents had sinned. (3)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that this man was born blind?
Questions.A: He was born blind so that God might demonstrate his power to heal the man. (3)

Questions.Q: What does God want people to do?
Questions.A: People are to do what the one, who sent Jesus, wants done/them to do. // God wants people to obey him/do what he has told them to do. (4)

Questions.Q: When are people to do what God wants them to do?
Questions.A: They are to do what God wants them to do whenever they have the opportunity (to do them). (4)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say he was?
Questions.A: He said that he was the light of the world. [He was to continue to tell God's message to people to cause them to believe God.] (5)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do?
Questions.A: He spit/spat on the ground,
made some mud with the saliva,
and put it on the man's eyes. (6)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell the blind man to do?
Questions.A: He told him to go wash [his face] in the pool of Siloam. (7)

Questions.Q: What is the meaning of Siloam?
Questions.A: The word Siloam means "sent." (7)

Questions.Q: What happened after the man went and washed [his face]?
Questions.A: He was able to see. // He came back seeing. (7)
Questions.Alternative: What happened after the man went and washed his face?
What happened after the man went and washed?

Questions.Q: About what were the people talking?
Questions.A: They were wondering if that man was the same man who used to sit and beg. (8)

Questions.Q: What did people say about that man?
Questions.A: Some people said he was [the one who had been blind]. (9)
Other people said he just looked like that man. (9)

Questions.Q: What did the man say about himself?
Questions.A: He said that he was the man [who had been blind]. (9)

Questions.Q: What did the people/they ask him?
Questions.A: They asked him how he was able to see now. (10)
Questions.Alternative: What did the people ask him?
What did they ask him?

Questions.Q: What did he tell them?
Questions.A: He said that the man they called Jesus had made some mud and put it on my eyes. (11)
Then he told me to go to Siloam and wash [my face]. (11)

Questions.Q: When did the blind man start to see?
Questions.A: He could see after he had washed [his face]. (11)

Questions.Q: What else did they ask the man who had been blind?
Questions.A: They asked him where this man [Jesus] was. (12)

Questions.Q: What was the former blind man's answer?
Questions.A: He said he did not know [where Jesus was]. (12)

Section.heading: John 9:13-34 The Pharisees questioned the blind man to find out how he had been healed.

Questions.Q: What did the Pharisees ask the man who had been blind?
Questions.A: They asked him how he was now able to see. (15)

Questions.Q: What was his answer?
Questions.A: He said that he [Jesus] had put mud on his eyes,
then he said that he had washed [his face],
and then he could see. (15)

Questions.Q: Whom did they take to the Pharisees?
Questions.A: They took the man, who had been blind, to the Pharisees. (13)

Questions.Q: On what day was it that Jesus healed the blind man's eyes?
Questions.A: He healed him on a Sabbath day. (14)

Questions.Q: What did some of the Pharisees say [about Jesus]?
Questions.A: They said that Jesus/he was not from God. (16)
Questions.Alternative: What did some of the Pharisees say about Jesus?
What did some of the Pharisees say?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they said that?
Questions.A: They said that because he had not kept/obeyed the Sabbath [law]. (16)

Questions.Q: What did others say about Jesus?
Questions.A: They asked/wondered how one, whom the leaders considered bad, could do such miraculous signs. (16)

Questions.Q: Whom did the Pharisees question again?
Questions.A: They questioned the man, who had been born blind, again. (17)

Questions.Q: What did they ask him?
Questions.A: They asked the former blind man/him what he had to say about him [Jesus]. (17)

Questions.Q: What was his answer?
Questions.A: He said that he was a prophet. (17)

Questions.Q: What did the Jews still not believe?
Questions.A: They did not believe the man had been blind and could now see. (18)

Questions.Q: For whom did they send?
Questions.A: The called for/sent for his parents. (18)

Questions.Q: What did they ask his parents?
Questions.A: They asked: "Is this your son?" (19)
"Is this the one whom you say was born blind?" (19)
"How is it that now he can see?" (19)

Questions.Q: What did they know about their son?
Questions.A: They knew that he was their son,
and that he had been born blind. (20)

Questions.Q: What did they not know about their son?
Questions.A: They did not know how he was now able to see
or who opened his eyes. (21)

Questions.Q: What did his parents tell the Jews to do?
Questions.A: They told the Jews to ask him, since he was old enough to answer for himself. (21)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that his parents had said this?
Questions.A: They were afraid of the Jews/Jewish leaders. (22-23)

Questions.Q: What had the Jews decided?
Questions.A: They had decided that anyone, who acknowledged/confessed that Jesus was the Messiah, should/would be put out of the synagogue. (22)

Questions.Q: Whom did they [the Pharisees] call back again?
Questions.A: They called back the man who had been blind. (24)
Questions.Alternative: Whom did they the Pharisees call back again?
Whom did they call back again?

Questions.Q: What did they tell him to promise to do?
Questions.A: They wanted him to promise to tell them the truth. (24)
Questions.Note: The phrase "Give glory to God" is an oath formula binding a man to tell the truth before God.

Questions.Q: What did they believe about Jesus?
Questions.A: They believed that he was a sinner [as he did not observe the Sabbath]. (24)

Questions.Q: What did the blind man not know about Jesus?
Questions.A: He did not know whether/if he was a sinner or not. (25)

Questions.Q: What did he know?
Questions.A: He knew that he had been blind, but now he could see. (25)

Questions.Q: What did they ask the blind man?
Questions.A: They asked: "What did he do to you?" (26)
"How did he open your eyes?" // "How did he cause you to see?" (26)

Questions.Q: What was the blind man's/his answer?
Questions.A: "I have already told you and you would not listen." (27)
"Why do you want to hear it again?" (27)
"Do you want to become his disciples too?" (27)
Questions.Alternative: What was the blind man's answer?
What was his answer?

Questions.Q: What was their reaction?
Questions.A: They insulted him. (28)

Questions.Q: According to those Pharisees, whose disciple was this man?
Questions.A: He was Jesus's disciple. (28)

Questions.Q: Whose disciples were they?
Questions.A: They were Moses's disciples. (28)

Questions.Q: What did they know about Moses?
Questions.A: They knew that God had spoken to him. (29)

Questions.Q: What did they not know about Jesus?
Questions.A: They did not know from where he had come. (29)

Questions.Q: What was amazing to the man who had been blind?
Questions.A: They did not know from where Jesus had come, and yet he had healed his eyes/caused him to see. (30)

Questions.Q: What did they [all] know?
Questions.A: God does not listen to sinners. (31)
God listens to the godly man who does his will. (31)
Questions.Alternative: What did they all know?
What did they know?

Questions.Q: Of what had they never heard?
Questions.A: They had never heard that [someone] caused a man, who was born blind, to be able to see. (32)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Jesus would not have been able to do anything?
Questions.A: If he had not come from God, he would not be able/would not have been able to heal a blind person/do miracles. (33)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the Pharisees were angry with the man, who had been blind, for lecturing them?
Questions.A: They were angry with him because they believed that he had lived a life of sin/practicing sin. Therefore, he could not possibly teach the Pharisees who thought that they were very good people. (34)

Questions.Q: What did they do to the man who had been blind?
Questions.A: They threw him out [of the synagogue]. (34)

Section.heading: John 9:35-41 Jesus said that he came to heal the blind (spiritually) [to save those who knew that they were sinners], and to show those who think they can see (spiritually) [know God, but really do not know God, that they are sinners] that they are blind. // Jesus said that he came to open the eyes of blind people and to cause people who can see to become blind.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Jesus came to judge [the world]?
Questions.A: He came so that the blind will see,
and those who see will prove to be/turn out to be blind. (39)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that Jesus came to judge the world?
What is the reason that Jesus came to judge?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus hear?
Questions.A: He heard that they had thrown the man, who had been blind, out [of the synagogue]. (35)

Questions.Q: What did he ask this man?
Questions.A: He asked him if he believed in the Son of Man. (35)

Questions.Q: What did the man ask Jesus to do?
Questions.A: He asked Jesus to tell him who the Son of Man was. (36)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that he asked Jesus to do that?
Questions.A: He wanted to know so that he could believe in him. (36)

Questions.Q: According to Jesus, who was the Son of Man?
Questions.A: He was the one whom the man had seen, and the one who was talking to him.
It was Jesus. // Jesus was the Son of Man. (37)

Questions.Q: When Jesus said this, what did the man do?
Questions.A: He believed in him and he worshiped him. (38)

Questions.Q: What did the Pharisees understand Jesus to be saying about them?
Questions.A: They believed he was saying that they were blind [that they did not really know God]. (40)

Questions.Q: In what case would they have not been guilty of their sins?
Questions.A: They would not have been guilty, if they had been blind [had admitted their sins and had believed in Jesus]. (41)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they were guilty?
Questions.A: They were guilty because they said they could see. // [They did not admit that they were sinners.] (41)

Section.heading: John 10:1-21 Jesus said that he is the good shepherd.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about himself as the good shepherd?
Questions.A: He is like the gate. (9)
Anyone who comes in by him will be saved. (9)
He is willing to [die] lay down his life for the sheep. (11, 15)
He knows his sheep. (14)
His sheep know him. (14)

Questions.Q: What is the truth about a person who goes into the sheep pen/fold by a way other than the gate?
Questions.A: He is a thief and a robber. (1)
Questions.Alternative: What is the truth about a person who goes into the sheep pen by a way other than the gate?
What is the truth about a person who goes into the sheep fold by a way other than the gate?

Questions.Q: Who enters by the gate?
Questions.A: The shepherd of the sheep enters by the gate. (2)

Questions.Q: Who opens the gate for the shepherd?
Questions.A: The watchman/gatekeeper opens the gate. (3)

Questions.Q: To whose voice do the sheep listen?
Questions.A: They listen to the shepherd's voice. (3)

Questions.Q: In what way does the shepherd call his sheep?
Questions.A: He calls them by their names. (3)

Questions.Q: Then, what does he do with them?
Questions.A: He leads them out. (3)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the sheep follow that shepherd?
Questions.A: They follow that shepherd because they know his voice. (4)

Questions.Q: What will those sheep do with someone else?
Questions.A: They will not follow him, but will run away from him. (5)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they do that?
Questions.A: They do that because they do not recognize/know his voice. (5)

Questions.Q: What type of story is this?
Questions.A: This is a figure of speech/parable. (6)

Questions.Q: What do you think a figure of speech is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A figure of speech is similar to a parable in which one thing represents another. For example, the shepherd represents Jesus and the sheep represent Jesus's followers. It is a short fictitious story that illustrates a moral attitude or religious principle. (See "figure" in KBT in the "parable" entry.)

Questions.Q: How well did the people understand this story?
Questions.A: They did not understand it. (6)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say he was?
Questions.A: He said that he was the gate for the sheep. (7)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about others who came before him?
Questions.A: He said that they were thieves and robbers. (8)

Questions.Q: What was the response of the sheep toward them?
Questions.A: The sheep did not listen to them. (8)

Questions.Q: What will a person, who comes in by him, be able to do?
Questions.A: He will go in and out and find pasture. [He will be kept safe. His daily needs will be provided by Jesus.] (9)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the thief comes to the sheepfold?
Questions.A: He comes to steal, kill, and destroy [the sheep]. (10)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Jesus came?
Questions.A: He came so that people may have a full life [all that they need]. (10)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about the hired man?
Questions.A: He is not the shepherd,
and he does not own the sheep. (12)

Questions.Q: What does the hired man do?
Questions.A: He abandons the sheep and runs away when he sees a wolf coming. (12)

Questions.Q: What does the wolf do?
Questions.A: He attacks the flock [of sheep] and scatters it. (12)

Questions.Q: What was the reason that the hired man ran away?
Questions.A: He was only a hired man and did not care for the sheep. (13)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about himself and his Father?
Questions.A: His Father knows him, and he knows his Father. (15)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about those other sheep?
Questions.A: They were not of his/this flock, but he must bring them in too. (16)
They will listen to his voice. (16)

Questions.Q: What relationship will all the sheep have with each other?
Questions.A: They will all be part of one flock and have one shepherd. (16)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Jesus's Father loves him?
Questions.A: Jesus's Father loves him because Jesus was willing to die. (17)

Questions.Q: What was his purpose for dying/laying down his life?
Questions.A: He died that so that he could be raised to life [by God]. (17)
Questions.Alternative: What was his purpose for dying?
What was his purpose for laying down his life?

Questions.Q: Who was able to take Jesus's life from him/kill him?
Questions.A: No one could kill him. He was willing to die. (18)
Questions.Alternative: Who was able to take Jesus's life from him him?
Who was able to take Jesus's life from kill him?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus have the authority to do?
Questions.A: He had the authority to die,
and the authority to become alive again. (18)

Questions.Q: Who gave him the command to die and to become alive again?
Questions.A: His Father gave the command. (18)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the Jews were divided concerning who he was?
Questions.A: They were divided because of the things that Jesus had said. (19)

Questions.Q: What did some of the Jews say about Jesus?
Questions.A: They said that he was demon possessed and that he was raving mad. (20)

Questions.Q: What did other Jews say about him?
Questions.A: They said that he said things that a demon possessed man would not say. (21)
A demon possessed man could not heal the blind [people]. (21)

Section.heading: John 10:22-42 The Jewish leaders said that Jesus was blaspheming, and they refused to believe in him.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the Jews accused Jesus of blaspheming?
Questions.A: They accused him because he claimed to be God. (33)

Questions.Q: What feast were the people celebrating?
Questions.A: They celebrated the Feast of Dedication. (22)

Questions.Q: What do you know about the Feast of Dedication?
Questions.Note: This feast was also known as Hanukkah and the Feast of Lights. The people celebrated this feast to commemorate the purification and rededication of the temple by Judas Maccabaeus in 165 BC.

Questions.Q: What time of the year did they celebrate this feast?
Questions.A: The feast took place in the winter. (22)

Questions.Q: What was Jesus doing?
Questions.A: He was walking in Solomon's Colonnade/Porch. (23)

Questions.Q: Where was this place located?
Questions.A: It was in the temple area. (23)

Questions.Q: What did the Jews want Jesus to tell them?
Questions.A: They wanted him to tell them if he were/was the Messiah. (24)

Questions.Q: What had Jesus already told those Jews?
Questions.A: He had told them [that he was the Messiah]. (25)

Questions.Q: What did the Jews think about his answer?
Questions.A: They did not believe him. (25)

Questions.Q: What was proof that he was the Messiah?
Questions.A: The miracles he did in his Father's name proved that he was the Messiah. (25)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that those people did not believe Jesus?
Questions.A: They did not believe Jesus because they did not belong to his flock. (26)

Questions.Q: Who listens to Jesus's voice?
Questions.A: Those who are his sheep listen to him. (27)

Questions.Q: Whom does he know?
Questions.A: He knows those who are his sheep. (27)

Questions.Q: What do Jesus's sheep do?
Questions.A: They follow him. (27)

Questions.Q: What does Jesus do for his sheep?
Questions.A: He gives them eternal life. // He causes them to have eternal life. (28)

Questions.Q: Who is able to take Jesus's sheep from him?
Questions.A: No one can do it. (28)

Questions.Q: Who is greater than all?
Questions.A: His Father is greater. (29)

Questions.Q: Who gave these sheep to Jesus?
Questions.A: His Father gave them to Jesus. (29)

Questions.Q: Who is able to take the sheep from his Father?
Questions.A: No one can do it. (29)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about himself and the Father?
Questions.A: He said that they are one. (30)

Questions.Q: What were the Jews about to do?
Questions.A: They picked up stones to stone Jesus. (31)

Questions.Q: Who had given Jesus the power/authority to do the miracles?
Questions.A: His Father gave him the power/authority to do the miracles. (32)
Questions.Alternative: Who had given Jesus the power to do the miracles?
Who had given Jesus the authority to do the miracles?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus ask those Jews?
Questions.A: He asked them for which of the miracles [that he did] were they wanting to stone him? (32)

Questions.Q: What was their answer to his question?
Questions.A: They said they did not want to stone him for any of the miracles he did, but because he committed blasphemy. (33)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to commit blasphemy?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It is an attitude of disrespect that finds expression in an act directed against the character of God. Jesus claimed that he was God's Son.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell them that [someone] had written in their law?
Questions.A: [Someone] had written that "I have said you are gods." (34)
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus tell them that someone had written in their law?
What did Jesus tell them had been written in their law?

Questions.Q: Whom did he [God] call gods?
Questions.A: He said that about the people who heard his message. (35)
Questions.Alternative: Whom did he call gods?
Whom did God call gods?

Questions.Q: What was the reason that Jesus was not blaspheming God when he said that he was the Son of God?
Questions.A: It was true that God had chosen and sent him [to the world]. (36)

Questions.Q: Since he was doing the things that the Father had given him to do, what should the people have believed?
Questions.A: They should have believed in him because of the things he did. (38)

Questions.Q: If they believed in him because of the things he did, what would they learn about Jesus?
Questions.A: They would know that the Father was in him, and that he was in the Father. (38)

Questions.Q: What did the people try to do again?
Questions.A: They tried to seize/arrest him. (39)

Questions.Q: What happened?
Questions.A: Jesus escaped out of their hands. (39)

Questions.Q: Where did Jesus go?
Questions.A: He went back across the Jordan [River]. (40)

Questions.Q: What had John done in that place before?
Questions.A: He had baptized some [people]. (40)

Questions.Q: Who stayed there?
Questions.A: Jesus stayed there. (40)

Questions.Q: Who came to Jesus?
Questions.A: Many people came to him. (41)

Questions.Q: What had John not done?
Questions.A: He had not done any miraculous signs. (41)

Questions.Q: What had John told people?
Questions.A: He told them the truth about Jesus. (41)

Questions.Q: What was the result of that?
Questions.A: Many of the people there believed in Jesus. (42)

Section.heading: John 11:1-16 Lazarus became sick and died.

Questions.Q: Who was Lazarus?
Questions.A: He was a man who lived in Bethany [a town]. (1)
He had two sisters, Mary and Martha. (1-2)
He was a dear friend of Jesus. (3)

Questions.Q: What happened to him?
Questions.A: He became sick and died. (3, 14)

Questions.Q: Who else lived in Bethany?
Questions.A: Mary and her sister Martha lived there. (1)

Questions.Q: What had Mary done before?
Questions.A: She had poured perfume on the Lord's feet, and wiped them with her hair. (2)

Questions.Q: What did Mary and Martha do?
Questions.A: They sent a message to Jesus to tell him that the one he loved was sick. (3)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about Lazarus's sickness?
Questions.A: He said that his sickness would not end in death,
but that it was to bring honor to God;
and it was the means by which the Son of God would receive honor. (4)

Questions.Q: Whom did Jesus love?
Questions.A: He loved Mary, Martha, and Lazarus. (5)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do when he heard that Lazarus was sick?
Questions.A: He stayed where he was for two more days. (6)

Questions.Q: Whom did Jesus tell to go with him to Judea?
Questions.A: He told his disciples to go with him. (7)

Questions.Q: Of what did his disciples remind Jesus?
Questions.A: They reminded him that, just recently, the Jews [in Judea] had tried to stone him. (8)

Questions.Q: What did his disciples ask Jesus?
Questions.A: They asked him if he were going back there. (8)

Questions.Q: According to Jesus, when will a person walk if he does not want to stumble?
Questions.A: He will walk in the daylight. (9)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that a person will not stumble at that time?
Questions.A: He will not stumble because it is daylight/he sees by this world's light [the sun]. (9)

Questions.Q: What will happen when a person walks during the night?
Questions.A: He will stumble because it is dark/he can not see well. (10)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell his disciples about Lazarus?
Questions.A: He told them that he had fallen asleep. (11)

Questions.Q: What was Jesus going to do?
Questions.A: He was going to awake him/wake him up. (11)

Questions.Q: What did his disciples think would happen, if Lazarus was just sleeping?
Questions.A: They thought that he would improve/be better/be well. (12)

Questions.Q: What was the difference between what Jesus meant, and what the disciples understood?
Questions.A: Jesus meant that Lazarus had died, but the disciples thought that Jesus meant that he was just asleep. (13)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus then tell his disciples?
Questions.A: He told them that Lazarus had died/was dead. (14)

Questions.Q: What was the reason that Jesus was glad that he had not been/was not there [with Lazarus]?
Questions.A: He wanted his disciples to believe [in him]. (15)
Questions.Alternative: What was the reason that Jesus was glad that he had not been there?
What was the reason that Jesus was glad that he was not there?
What was the reason that Jesus was glad that he had not been there with Lazarus?
What was the reason that Jesus was glad that he was not there with Lazarus?

Questions.Q: Where did Jesus want to go?
Questions.A: He wanted to go to Lazarus. (15)

Questions.Q: Why do you think Thomas was called "Didymus"?
Questions.A: "Thomas" is derived from the Hebrew word "Te'oma" which means "twin." The word "twin" translates the Greek word "Didymus" which has the same meaning.

Questions.Q: What did Thomas say to the other disciples?
Questions.A: He told them that they [including himself] should go too, so that they could die with Lazarus/him. (16)

Section.heading: John 11:17-37 Jesus comforted Martha and Mary in the death of their brother, Lazarus. // Jesus went to the (older) sisters of Lazarus and comforted them.

Questions.Q: Where did Jesus go?
Questions.A: He went to Bethany to comfort Martha and Mary. (20, 23, 29)

Questions.Q: When Jesus arrived in Bethany, what did he find out about Lazarus?
Questions.A: He discovered that Lazarus had already been in the tomb for four days. (17)

Questions.Q: What was the distance between Bethany and Jerusalem?
Questions.A: It was about two miles distance. (18)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that those Jews were comforting Mary and Martha?
Questions.A: They were comforting them because their brother [Lazarus] had died. (19)

Questions.Q: What did Martha do when she heard that Jesus was coming?
Questions.A: She went out to meet him. (20)

Questions.Q: What did Mary do?
Questions.A: She stayed at home. (20)

Questions.Q: According to Martha, who could have prevented the death of Lazarus?
Questions.A: If Jesus had been there before Lazarus died, [he could have healed him]. (21)

Questions.Q: What did Martha say about God?
Questions.A: He would do whatever Jesus asked him to do. (22)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus promise Martha?
Questions.A: He said that her brother [Lazarus] would rise to life/live again. (23)

Questions.Q: What did Martha know?
Questions.A: She knew that Lazarus would rise again at the resurrection on the last day [of the world]. (24)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about himself?
Questions.A: He said that he was the one who had power to raise the dead and the one to cause people to have eternal life. (25)

Questions.Q: What will happen to a person who believes in Jesus?
Questions.A: He will live [eternally with God] even though he dies. (25)

Questions.Q: What will happen to a person who lives and believes in Jesus?
Questions.A: He will never die. (26)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus ask Martha?
Questions.A: He asked her, if she believed what he had told her. (26)

Questions.Q: What was Martha's answer?
Questions.A: She said that she believed what he had said,
and also that he was the Messiah, the Son of God, who was to come into the world. (27)

Questions.Q: What did Martha say to Mary?
Questions.A: She told her that the Teacher was there/had arrived and was asking for her. (28)

Questions.Q: For what reason do you think she called him "Teacher"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: To call someone "teacher" implied respect, but not necessarily affection or commitment. (See "teacher" in KBT in the "Christ, Messiah" entry.)

Questions.Q: What did Mary do after she heard what Martha said to her?
Questions.A: She arose/stood up/got up quickly and went to him. (29)

Questions.Q: Where was Jesus?
Questions.A: He was outside the village where Martha had met him. (30)

Questions.Q: Who followed Mary?
