Questions.A: Key Term Check: The cross was constructed of two pieces of wood. One piece was a thick wooden post, which was placed/planted upright into a hole in the ground. The other piece was the crossbeam , which was fastened across the upright post so that it formed a + or T shape.
Questions.Note: See "cross" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What was that place called in Aramaic?
Questions.A: It was called Golgotha. (17)
Questions.Alternative: What was that place called in Hebrew?
What was the other name of that place?
What was the The Place of the Skull called in Aramaic?
What was the The Place of the Skull called in Hebrew?

What was the The Place of the Skull called in the language of the Jews?
What was that place called by the Judean people?

Questions.Q: Whom did [the soldiers] crucify with Jesus?

Questions.Alternative: Whom did the soldiers crucify with Jesus?
Whom did crucify with Jesus?

Questions.Alternative: What did the notice read that Pilate told someone to write?

What did the notice read that Pilate wrote?

Questions.Q: Who read that notice?
Questions.A: Many of the Jews read the notice. (20)

Questions.A: Many of the Jews read that notice because the place was close to the city,

Questions.Q: What did Pilate tell them?

Questions.Q: What kind of undergarment was Jesus wearing?

What is the reason that the soldiers cast lots to divide Jesus' clothing among themselves?

Why did the soldiers divide Jesus' clothing among themselves?
Why did the soldiers cast lots among themselves for Jesus' clothing?
Why did the soldiers cast lots to divide Jesus' clothing among themselves?
Why did the soldiers cast lots to decide which of them would get to take parts of Jesus' clothing?

Questions.Q: What did he say to the disciple whom he loved?
Questions.A: He said, "Here is your mother." (27)

What did Jesus do after he drank some wine vinegar?
What did Jesus do after he drank some sour wine?

Questions.Q: What do you think the Jews did on that day?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Preparation day was Friday, and it was also the day before the Sabbath. They had to prepare everything in advance, before the Sabbath when no work was permitted/could be done. (See "day of Preparation" in KBT in the "Sabbath" entry.)

Questions.Q: What was the next day going to be?
Questions.A: The next day was going to be a special Sabbath. (31)

Questions.A: They asked him to [tell the soldiers to] break the legs of the men on the crosses and take the men's bodies down. (31)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they wanted the men's bodies taken down from the crosses?
Questions.A: They wanted the men's bodies taken down from the crosses because they did not want the bodies left on the crosses during the Sabbath day. (31)

Questions.Q: Whose legs did the soldiers break?
Questions.A: They broke the legs of the two men who had been crucified with Jesus. (32)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the soldiers did not break Jesus's legs?
Questions.A: The did not break Jesus's legs because he was already dead. (33)

Questions.Q: What did one of the soldiers do to Jesus?
Questions.A: He pierced Jesus's side with a spear. (34)

Questions.Q: What happened after he did that?
Questions.A: Blood and water poured out of Jesus's side. (34)

Questions.Q: Who spoke about that?
Questions.A: The man who saw it happen spoke about it. (35)

Questions.Q: What is true about that man?
Questions.A: His testimony is true. (35)

Questions.Q: What did that person know?
Questions.A: He knew that he told the truth. (35)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that he testified about that happening/event/incident?
Questions.A: He testified so that people would believe. (35)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that he testified about that happening?
What is the reason that he testified about that event?
What is the reason that he testified about that incident?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that those things happened?
Questions.A: Those things happened so that two scriptures would be fulfilled: "Not one of his bones will be broken." (36)
and "They will look on the one they have pierced." (37)

Section.heading: John 19:38-42 Joseph of Arimathea and Nicodemus buried Jesus's body in a tomb. // Joseph of Arimathea and Nicodemus took Jesus's body (from the cross) and buried him in a tomb.

Questions.Q: What did Joseph and Nicodemus do with Jesus's body?
Questions.A: They wrapped it, along with the spices, in strips of linen cloth. (40)
They laid it in the tomb. (42)

Questions.Q: For what did Joseph of Arimathea ask Pilate? // What did Joseph of Arimathea request of Pilate?
Questions.A: He asked Pilate to give him the body of Jesus to bury it. (38)
Questions.Alternative: For what did Joseph of Arimathea ask Pilate?
What did Joseph of Arimathea request of Pilate?

Questions.Q: Who was Joseph?
Questions.A: He was a secret disciple of Jesus. (38)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that he was a secret disciple of Jesus?
Questions.A: He was a secret disciple of Jesus because he was afraid of the Jews/Jewish leaders. (38)

Questions.Q: What did Joseph do after he received Pilate's permission?
Questions.A: He [went to the cross] and took the body [of Jesus]. (38)

Questions.Q: What did Nicodemus do?
Questions.A: He went with Joseph to take Jesus's body. (39)

Questions.Q: What had Nicodemus done in the past?
Questions.A: He had gone to see Jesus at night. (39)

Questions.Q: What did Nicodemus bring with him at that time?
Questions.A: He brought about seventy-five pounds of a mixture of myrrh and aloes. (39)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they wrapped the body, along with the spices, in strips of linen cloth?
Questions.A: They did that because it was the Jews' custom for burial. (40)

Questions.Q: Where was the garden located?
Questions.A: The garden was near the place where Jesus had been crucified [by the soldiers]. (41)

Questions.Q: Where was the tomb located?
Questions.A: The tomb was located in the garden. (41)

Questions.Q: Whom had they buried in that tomb up to that time?
Questions.A: No one had buried anyone in that tomb yet. (41)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they laid Jesus there?
Questions.A: They laid Jesus there because it was the Jewish day of Preparation,
and the tomb was close by. (42)

Section.heading: John 20:1-9 Mary Magdalene, Peter and another disciple discovered that Jesus's body was missing from the tomb.

Questions.Q: Who were the three people who went to Jesus's tomb, according to these verses?
Questions.A: Mary Magdalene. (1)
Simon Peter and the other disciple whom Jesus loved were the three people who went. (3)

Questions.Q: When did Mary Magdalene go to the tomb?
Questions.A: She went early [in the morning], while it was still dark, on the first day of the week. (1)

Questions.Q: What did she see there?
Questions.A: She saw that someone had removed the stone from the entrance to the tomb. (1)

Questions.Q: Then where did she go?
Questions.A: She went running to Simon Peter and the disciple whom Jesus loved. (2)

Questions.Q: What did Mary Magdalene tell them?
Questions.A: She told them, "They have taken the Lord out of the tomb, and we do not know where they have put him." (2)

Questions.Q: Of the two disciples, which of them reached the tomb first?
Questions.A: The other disciple [whom Jesus loved] arrived first. (4)

Questions.Q: What did that disciple do?
Questions.A: He bent over and saw the strips of linen lying [in the tomb]. (5)

Questions.Q: What did Simon Peter do, when he reached the tomb?
Questions.A: He went inside/into the tomb. (6)

Questions.Q: What did he see?
Questions.A: He saw the strips of linen lying there. (6)

Questions.Q: What else did he see?
Questions.A: He saw the burial cloth which had been around Jesus's head. (7)

Questions.Q: Where was the burial cloth?
Questions.A: [Someone] had folded it up and placed it by itself, separate from the linen. (7)

Questions.Q: Who went inside/into the tomb next?
Questions.A: The other disciple [whom Jesus loved] went inside next. (8)
Questions.Alternative: Who went inside the tomb next?
Who went into the tomb next?

Questions.Q: What happened to him when he went inside?
Questions.A: He saw [what was inside] and believed [that Jesus had risen from the dead]. (8)

Questions.Q: What did they not understand?
Questions.A: They did not understand the scripture [in which someone had written] that Jesus must rise from the dead. (9)

Section.heading: John 20:10-18 Jesus appeared to Mary Magdalene (at the tomb).

Questions.Q: Whom did Mary Magdalene see, after she talked with the angels?
Questions.A: She saw Jesus. (16)

Questions.Q: Whom did she tell about seeing Jesus?
Questions.A: She told the disciples. (18)

Questions.Q: Where did the disciples go then?
Questions.A: They went back to their homes. (10)

Questions.Q: What did Mary do outside the tomb?
Questions.A: She cried, and she bent over and looked into the Tomb [again]. (11)

Questions.Q: What did she see inside the tomb?
Questions.A: She saw two angels, dressed in white. (12)

Questions.Q: Where were they seated?
Questions.A: They were seated where the body of Jesus had been. One was sitting where Jesus's head had been, and the other was sitting where Jesus's feet had been. (12)

Questions.Q: What did they ask her?
Questions.A: They asked her why she was crying. (13)

Questions.Q: What did she tell them?
Questions.A: She said, "They have taken away my Lord, and I do not know where they have put him." (13)

Questions.Q: What did she not realize as she turned around?
Questions.A: She did not realize that it was Jesus at whom she was looking. (14)

Questions.Q: What did he ask her?
Questions.A: He asked her why she was crying,
and for whom was she looking. (15)

Questions.Q: Who did she think he was?
Questions.A: She thought he was the gardener. (15)

Questions.Q: What did she tell him to do?
Questions.A: She told him to tell her where he had put the Lord's body, if he had carried it away. (15)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that she said that to him?
Questions.A: She said that to him because she wanted to go and retrieve/recover/reclaim the body. (15)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to Mary?
Questions.A: He spoke her name, "Mary." (16)

Questions.Q: What did she say to Jesus?
Questions.A: She answered, "Rabboni!" (16)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell Mary not to do?
Questions.A: He told her not to hold onto him. (17)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that he said that?
Questions.A: He said that because he had not yet returned to the Father. (17)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell Mary to do?
Questions.A: He told her to go to his brothers/disciples, and to tell them that he was going to return to his Father and their Father, his God and their God. (17)

Questions.Q: What do you think Jesus meant when he said "his brothers"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He meant those who were fellow-followers of Jesus. (See "brothers" in KBT in the "disciple" entry.)

Questions.Q: What did Mary tell the disciples?
Questions.A: She told them that she had seen the Lord,
and that he had told her that he was going back to the Father. (18)

Section.heading: John 20:19-23 Jesus appeared to his disciples. // Jesus showed his disciples that he was alive.

Questions.Q: To whom did Jesus appear?
Questions.A: He appeared to his disciples. (19)

Questions.Q: When did Jesus come and stand among his disciples?
Questions.A: He came on the evening of the first day of the week. (19)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the disciples kept the doors locked?
Questions.A: They kept the doors locked because they were afraid of the Jews/Jewish leaders. (19)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to the disciples?
Questions.A: He said, "Peace be with you!" (19)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus show to them?
Questions.A: He showed them his hands and side. (20)

Questions.Q: What did the disciples feel, when they saw the Lord?
Questions.A: They were overjoyed/very happy. (20)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to them?
Questions.A: He said, "Peace be with you! As the Father has sent me, I am sending you." (21)

Questions.Q: What did he do to them?
Questions.A: He breathed on them. (22)

Questions.Q: What did he tell them then?
Questions.A: He said, "Receive the Holy Spirit." // "Accept the Holy Spirit in your lives." (22)

Questions.Q: What would happen, if they forgave anyone his sins?
Questions.A: They are forgiven [by God]. (23)

Questions.Q: What would happen, if they did not forgive anyone his sins?
Questions.A: God will/would not forgive that man's sins. // They would not be forgiven [by God]. (23)

Section.heading: John 20:24-31 Jesus appeared to Thomas. // Thomas refused to believe that Jesus was alive, until he saw him for himself.

Questions.Q: To whom did Jesus show himself according to these verses?
Questions.A: Jesus showed himself to all the disciples including Thomas. (26)

Questions.Q: Who was Thomas?
Questions.A: He was one of the twelve disciples. (24)

Questions.Q: Where was Thomas, when Jesus appeared to the disciples before?
Questions.A: He was not with the disciples. (24)

Questions.Q: What did the other disciples tell Thomas?
Questions.A: They told him that they had seen the Lord. (25)

Questions.Q: What did Thomas tell the other disciples that he had to see and do, before he would believe?
Questions.A: He told them that he had to see the nail marks in Jesus's hands,
and put his finger where the nails were,
and put his hand into Jesus's side. (25)

Questions.Q: Where were the disciples a week later?
Questions.A: They were in the house again. (26)

Questions.Q: Where was Thomas?
Questions.A: He was with the other disciples. (26)

Questions.Q: What did they do with the doors this time?
Questions.A: They locked them again. (26)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to them this time?
Questions.A: He said again, "Peace be with you!" (26)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell Thomas to do?
Questions.A: He told him to put his finger there and to look at Jesus's hands,
and then to stretch out his hand and to put it in Jesus's side,
and to stop doubting and to believe. (27)

Questions.Q: What did Thomas then say to Jesus?
Questions.A: He said, "My Lord and my God." (28)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Thomas believed [in Jesus] at that time?
Questions.A: He believed [in Jesus] because he had seen Jesus. (29)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that Thomas believed in Jesus at that time?
What is the reason that Thomas believed at that time?

Questions.Q: Who will be blessed [by God]?
Questions.A: Those who will believe [in Jesus] without seeing Jesus will be blessed [by God]. (29)
Questions.Alternative: Who will be blessed by God?
Who will be blessed?

Questions.Q: What other things did Jesus do?
Questions.A: He did many other miraculous signs in the presence of his disciples. (30)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that [someone] wrote those things/about those events?
Questions.A: They were written so that we may believe that Jesus is the Messiah, the Son of God,
and that by believing, we may have [eternal] life. (31)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that someone wrote those things?
What is the reason that someone wrote about those events?

Section.heading: John 21:1-14 Jesus appeared to some of his disciples at the sea of Tiberias, while they were fishing.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell the disciples to do, in order to catch some fish?
Questions.A: He told them to throw their net out on the right side of the boat. (6)

Questions.Q: What happened after they had thrown the net out on the right side?
Questions.A: They could not pull it back in, because the net was so full of fish. (6)

Questions.Q: To whom did Jesus appear at the Sea of Tiberias?
Questions.A: He appeared to his disciples. (1)

Questions.Q: How many disciples were there?
Questions.A: Seven were there. (2)

Questions.Q: Where was Simon Peter going?
Questions.A: He was going fishing. (3)

Questions.Q: Who went with him?
Questions.A: The other disciples went with him. (3)

Questions.Q: How long did they fish?
Questions.A: They fished all night. (3)

Questions.Q: How many fish did they catch?
Questions.A: They did not catch even one/any fish. (3)

Questions.Q: Where was Jesus standing early in the morning?
Questions.A: He was standing on the shore. (4)

Questions.Q: What did the disciples not realize?
Questions.A: They did not realize that it was Jesus who was standing there. (4)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus ask them?
Questions.A: He asked them if they had caught any fish. (5)

Questions.Q: What did they tell him?
Questions.A: They told him, "No, we have not caught any fish." (5)

Questions.Q: Who recognized that it was Jesus?
Questions.A: The disciple, whom Jesus loved, recognized that it was Jesus. (7)

Questions.Q: What did he say to Peter when he recognized Jesus?
Questions.A: He said, "It is the Lord!" (7)

Questions.Q: What did Simon Peter do when he heard that?
Questions.A: He wrapped his outer garment around him and jumped into the water. (7)

Questions.Q: What did the rest of the disciples do?
Questions.A: They followed him/Peter in the boat, dragging the net full of fish. (8)

Questions.Q: How far from shore had they been?
Questions.A: They were about a hundred yards/60 meters from shore. (8)

Questions.Q: When they landed [at the shore,] what did they see?
Questions.A: They saw a charcoal fire with fish and bread being cooked on it. (9)
Questions.Alternative: When they landed at the shore, what did they see?
When they landed what did they see?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell them to do?
Questions.A: He told them to bring some of the fish they had just caught. (10)

Questions.Q: What did Simon Peter do?
Questions.A: He climbed aboard [the boat] and dragged the net ashore. (11)

Questions.Q: How many fish had they caught?
Questions.A: They had caught one hundred and fifty-three fish. (11)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell them to do?
Questions.A: He told them to come and have breakfast. (12)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the disciples did not ask Jesus who he was?
Questions.A: They did not ask him, because they knew that he was the Lord. (12)

Questions.Q: To whom did Jesus give the bread and the fish?
Questions.A: He gave it to the disciples. (13)

Questions.Q: How many times had Jesus appeared/shown himself to his disciples?
Questions.A: He showed himself to them three times. (14)
Questions.Alternative: How many times had Jesus appeared to his disciples?
How many times had Jesus shown himself to his disciples?

Section.heading: John 21:15-25 Jesus restored Peter so that he could continue to follow him.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus ask Simon Peter three times?
Questions.A: He asked Simon if he loved him. (15-17)

Questions.Q: What did Simon say?
Questions.A: He said, "Yes, Lord, you know that I love you." (15)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell him to do?
Questions.A: He told him to feed his lambs/his followers/those who believed him. (15)

Questions.Q: What did Simon tell him?
Questions.A: He said, "Yes, Lord, you know that I love you." (16)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell him to do that time?
Questions.A: He told him to take care of his sheep/his followers/those who believed in him. (16)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Peter was feeling hurt?
Questions.A: He was feeling hurt because Jesus had asked him three times if he loved him. (17)

Questions.Q: What did Peter tell Jesus?
Questions.A: He said, "Lord you know all things; you know that I love you." (17)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell him to do then/that time?
Questions.A: He told him to feed his sheep/his followers/those who believed in him. (17)
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus tell him to do then?
What did Jesus tell him to do that time?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell Simon that he used to do when he was young?
Questions.A: He told Simon that, when he was young, he used to dress himself and go anywhere he wanted to go. (18)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell Simon would happen to him when he became old?
Questions.A: He told him that when he became old he will stretch out his hands, and someone else will dress him, and lead him where he did not want to go. (18)

Questions.Q: What was Jesus telling Simon Peter by telling him those things?
Questions.A: He was telling him the way in which he would die and bring honor to God. (19)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus then tell Simon Peter to do?
Questions.A: He told him to/keep believing him/follow him. (19)

Questions.Q: When Peter turned around whom did he see?
Questions.A: He saw the disciple whom Jesus loved. (20)

Questions.Q: What was that disciple doing?
Questions.A: He was following Jesus and Simon Peter. (20)

Questions.Q: What had that disciple, whom Jesus loved, done at another time/in the past?
Questions.A: He had leaned back against Jesus at the supper and said, "Lord, who is going to betray you?" (20)
Questions.Alternative: What had that disciple, whom Jesus loved, done at another time?
What had that disciple, whom Jesus loved, done in the past?

Questions.Q: About whom did Peter ask Jesus?
Questions.A: He asked him about the disciple whom Jesus loved. (21)

Questions.Q: According to Jesus's answer, about what was Peter to think?
Questions.A: He was to think about obeying/following Jesus. (22)

Questions.Q: About what was Peter not to think?
Questions.A: He was not supposed to think about what was going to happen to the other disciple. (22)

Questions.Q: What was the report that someone had spread among the brothers/followers of Jesus?
Questions.A: Someone started a rumor among the brothers that the disciple, whom Jesus loved, would not die. (23)
Questions.Alternative: What was the report that someone had spread among the brothers of Jesus?
What was the report that someone had spread among the followers of Jesus?

Questions.Q: What is the difference between, what Jesus had said, and what the followers were reporting?
Questions.A: Jesus had said, "If I want him to live until I come, what is that to you?" But the followers had been reporting that that disciple/the disciple, whom Jesus loved, was not going to die. (23)

Questions.Q: Who testified and wrote about these things?
Questions.A: The other disciple, whom Jesus loved, testified about these things. (24)

Questions.Q: What do we know about what he testified/his testimony?
Questions.A: We know that it is true. (24)
Questions.Alternative: What do we know about what he testified?
What do we know about his testimony?

Questions.Q: If all of the things that Jesus did while on earth were written down, how much would it be?
Questions.A: The whole world would not be able to hold the books that would be written. (25)

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what Jude said in these verses.
Questions.A: Jude told who he was
and addressed his letter to those whom [God] had called [to be Christians/believers/his people]. (1)
Jude desired/asked that [God] continue to show favor to them. (2)

Questions.Q: Who was Jude?
Questions.A: He was a servant of Jesus Christ
and the brother of James. (1)

Questions.Q: What do you think Jude meant when he said the "brother"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In this reference "brother" means someone born of the same father and/or mother. (See "brother" in KBT in the "disciple" entry.)

Questions.Q: What do you think a servant does?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A servant is a person who is required to work for another and obey him. Servants are usually paid for their work, while slaves are not paid.
Questions.Note: See "servant" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the meaning of "Christ"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "Christ" is the English rendering of the Greek word Christos, which means "anointed one."
Questions.Note: See "Christ" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did Jude say how God the Father felt about those people?
Questions.A: He said that God loved them. (1)

Questions.Q: Who do you think God is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In English, the term "God" with a capital "G" is used to refer to the one supreme Creator. The term "god" with a small "g", as in "a god" or "many gods", can refer to any spiritual being that people worship. The Greek word theos can be used in the same two ways.
Questions.Note: In many languages the term for God is a proper name and cannot be used to refer to anyone except the one supreme creator of the world. It cannot be pluralized. (Or, if it can be pluralized, the meaning may be something very different from the English "gods". In one language, the plural form of God, meant "God and those who follow him" and was an appropriate way to translate "saints".) (See "God" in KBT.)

Questions.Q: What do you think "God the Father" means?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that God is the father of Jesus Christ and of anyone who accepts Jesus as their Savior and Lord.
Questions.Note: See "God the Father" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think the title "God the Father" means?
What do you think the term "God the Father" means?

Questions.Q: What was Jesus Christ doing for those people?
Questions.A: He was protecting/caring for them. (1)

Questions.Q: What did Jude desire for those to whom he wrote?
Questions.A: He desired that [God] would favor them with mercy, peace and love. (2)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when someone shows mercy to someone else?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "Mercy" in the New Testament is an act of kindness by God or someone else toward people who are in need. The person (God or man) acts to relieve some kind of suffering or distress.
Questions.Note: See "mercy" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to be at peace?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that a person has a mental or spiritual condition marked by freedom of disquieting or oppressive thoughts or emotions.
Questions.Note: See "peace" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when someone loves someone else?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The person who loves another person seeks the good of that person. His attitude to the one whom he loves is an attitude of persistent and selfless goodwill.
Questions.Note: See "love" in KBT.

Section.heading: Jude 3-16 Jude warned the Christians about some false teachers that had gotten into the church and were spreading false ideas about how the Christians should live that were not according to the true gospel of the Lord. They did not believe that Jesus is the son of God or that he is the only Lord and Savior.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what Jude said in these verses.
Questions.A: Jude warned them about false teachers who distort the true teaching about the grace of God/the way he shows grace to us/the way he deals with us in grace. (4)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to have/use grace?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that a person shows that he accepts and loves another person even when they do not deserve it.
Questions.Note: See "grace" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think it means to have grace?
What do you think it means for someone to have grace?
What do you think it means for someone to experience grace?
What do you think it means to use grace?

Questions.Q: What was Jude going to write about originally?
Questions.A: He intended to write about the salvation/Christian faith/Christian religion that they shared. (3)
Questions.Note: UBS states that salvation here is synonymous with the Christian faith or Christian religion.

Questions.Q: What do you think "salvation" means?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The noun form (Greek sôtêria) and the adjective form (Greek sôtêrios) usually refer in the New Testament to eternal salvation from sin, evil and death.
Questions.Note: See "salvation" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did Jude feel that he needed to do, instead of writing about this salvation?
Questions.A: He felt he needed to write to them and urge them to fight for the faith/the gospel (a body of doctrines that all Christians accept and proclaim) that God has entrusted/given to all the saints/Christians/his people. (3)

Questions.Q: What do you think he meant by "the faith"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "Faith" in this reference is the true things that Christians believe in and practise, Christian doctrine, Christianity, the way of Jesus Christ. (See "faith" in KBT in the "believe" entry.)

Questions.Q: Who do you think the saints are?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: They are those people who belong to God, God's people, those who believed in Christ. It does not refer to a special group of people who were particularly good people. In the New Testament it is used to refer to believers-in-Christ in general. (See "saint" in KBT in the "disciple" entry.)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Jude believed it was necessary to write to them to take a firm stand against those who contradict their belief/faith in God?
Questions.A: He believed this because some ungodly men had joined the fellowship of Christians and these men distorted the message/teaching about the grace of God. (4)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that Jude believed it was necessary to write to them to take a firm stand against those who contradict their belief in God?
What is the reason that Jude believed it was necessary to write to them to take a firm stand against those who contradict their faith in God?

Questions.Q: In what ways did they distort this message about the grace of God?
Questions.A: They changed the grace of God in such a way that it gave them a license to do immoral acts.
They denied/rejected Jesus Christ as our only Sovereign/Master and Lord. (4)

Questions.Q: What does it mean to you to have someone as your lord?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A lord is someone who has power and exercises it responsibly. To call someone your lord means that you have given them control over your life. The Lord in this case is Jesus. Every Christian strives to make Jesus lord in his or her life by giving Him complete control. (See "Lord" in KBT in the "God" entry.)

Questions.Q: How did those men get into the fellowship of the Christians?
Questions.A: They got into the fellowship secretly. (4)

Questions.Q: What will the fate/end of those men be?
Questions.A: They will be condemned [by God] just as the scriptures stated. (4)
Questions.Alternative: What will the fate of those men be?
What will the end of those men be?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means if someone condemns someone else?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that someone pronounces someone else guilty with the clear implication that the person will be punished for what he did. (See "condemn" in KBT in the "judge, judgment" entry.)

Questions.Q: Even though the readers knew how the Lord had dealt with/punished those who acted wickedly in the past, what did Jude want to do?
Questions.A: He wanted to remind them of it. (5)
Questions.Alternative: Even though the readers knew how the Lord had dealt with those who acted wickedly in the past, what did Jude want to do?
Even though the readers knew how the Lord had punished those who acted wickedly in the past, what did Jude want to do?

Questions.Q: In the case of the people of Israel, even though the Lord delivered them out of Egypt what did he later do to some of them?
Questions.A: He destroyed those who did not believe [in him]. (5)

Questions.Q: What does someone do when he believes?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He puts his trust and commitment in another person.
Questions.Note: See "believe" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What other example did Jude give of those who acted wickedly in the past?
Questions.A: He gave the example of the angels who did not keep their positions of authority [that God had given to them] but instead abandoned their own home/dwelling place. (6)

Questions.Q: What do you know about these kind of angels/fallen angels?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A fallen angel, one of the angels who sided with Satan against God, who fell with Satan from heaven, and who now serve him.
Questions.Note: See "angel" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: What do you know about these kind of angels?
What do you know about fallen angels?

Questions.Q: What did God do to those angels because they rebelled against him?
Questions.A: He has kept them securely bound with everlasting/eternal chains in the darkness [below]. (6)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for something to be eternal?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that it will last forever/it will never end.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that God is keeping them bound in this way?
Questions.A: He is keeping these angels bound there until the day when [he] will judge them [for the sins they have committed]. (6)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to judge someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means someone/a judge will determine if a person is guilty or not of committing a crime. He does this by assessing the evidence connected to the person and what he may have done.
Questions.Note: See "judge" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What other example did Jude give of those who acted wickedly in the past?
Questions.A: Jude gave the example of the people living in the towns/cities of Sodom and Gomorrah and in the towns nearby. (7)

Questions.Q: What did those people do that caused [God] to punish them?
Questions.A: They committed acts of sexual immorality
and perversion. (7)
Questions.Alternative: What did those people do that caused God to punish them?
What did those people do that caused them to be punished?
What did those people do to earn punishment?
What did those people do that caused them to undergo punishment?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to commit sexual immorality?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: This is a general word referring to any kind of unlawful sexual intercourse. (See "immorality" in KBT in the "sin" entry.)

Questions.Q: How did [God] punish those people for the sinful acts they committed?
Questions.A: He completely destroyed them and their cities with fire. (7)
Questions.Alternative: How were those people punished for the sinful acts they committed?
What punishment did those people receive for the sinful acts they committed?

Questions.Q: What lesson did Jude intend to teach through mentioning the destruction of these people and their cities?
Questions.A: This example was a warning to others of the way in which God will punish all who commit sinful deeds. (7)

Questions.Q: Who were the men spoken of/mentioned here who practiced the same kinds of sins that are mentioned above in verses 5-7?
Questions.A: They were the false teachers mentioned previously in verse 4. (8)
Questions.Alternative: Who were the men spoken of here who practiced the same kinds of sins that are mentioned above in verses 5-7?
Who were the men mentioned here who practiced the same kinds of sins that are mentioned above in verses 5-7?

Questions.Q: Of what three types of sins were those false teachers guilty?
Questions.A: They indulged in shameful physical acts,
rejected the authority of [God],
and reviled/said bad things about the angels. (8)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to call something glorious?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "The glorious ones" in Greek is literally "the glories". The angels are referred to in this way because they are closely associated with God, living in his presence and reflecting his glory. (See "glorious" in KBT in the "glory" entry.)

Questions.Q: What do you know about angels who have not fallen like those in verse 6?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Angels are spiritual messengers who either deliver a message to humans, carry out God's will, praise God, or guard God's throne.
Questions.Note: See "angel" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Who is Michael?
Questions.A: He is the archangel/the chief angel. (9)

Questions.Q: What did Michael refuse to do?
Questions.A: Michael did not condemn the Devil with insulting words when he and the Devil argued about [who was to have] the body of Moses. (9)

Questions.Q: Who do you think the Devil is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The form diabolos "the Devil" is the Greek equivalent of the Hebrew word "Satan". Satan is the chief enemy of God. He is the supreme evil spiritual being who leads and directs all other evil spiritual beings. (See "devil" in KBT in the "Satan" entry.)

Questions.Q: What body do you think is meant here?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In this reference it is Moses's physical body.
Questions.Note: See "body" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Instead of insulting the Devil, what did Michael do?
Questions.A: He simply said "The Lord rebuke you!" (9)

Questions.Q: Unlike Michael, what did those men/false teachers do?
Questions.A: They insulted things they did not understand. (10)
Questions.Alternative: Unlike Michael, what did those men do?
Unlike Michael, what did those false teachers do?

Questions.Q: In what way were those false teachers/men like wild animals?
Questions.A: They did what they did by instinct without thinking. (10)
Questions.Alternative: In what way were those false teachers like wild animals?
In what way were those men like wild animals?

Questions.Q: What will happen to them because of those evil things they did by instinct?
Questions.A: They will be destroyed by those things. (10)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that those false teachers are destined to suffer a terrible fate?
Questions.A: They will suffer a terrible fate because they followed the evil examples of Cain, Balaam and Korah. (11)
Questions.Note: (Note: UBS states that in late Judaism and early Christianity, Cain was a symbol of treachery and greed.
Balaam was covetous. Out of love for money he led the people of Israel to worship false gods. Korah led a rebellion against Moses and Aaron.)

Questions.Q: When the believers, to whom Jude wrote, met together to share in their love feasts what did those false teachers do?
Questions.A: They joined the believers in eating with them. (12)

Questions.Q: What did those false teachers do at the love feasts?
Questions.A: Those false teachers disrupted the meal with their shameless carousing. (12)

Questions.Q: With whose welfare were those false teachers concerned?
Questions.A: They were concerned only for themselves. (12)

Questions.Q: What did Jude say those false teachers were like?
Questions.A: They were like clouds which bring no rain, but instead are just blown off by the wind.
They were like trees at harvest time which bear no fruit.
They were also like dead and uprooted trees. (12)

Questions.Q: To what else did Jude compare those false teachers?
Questions.A: They were like wild/huge/crashing waves of the sea which spray foam and refuse all around because of the shameful deeds they did.
They were like wandering/falling stars. (13)

Questions.Q: What will their ultimate fate be?
Questions.A: [God] has reserved a place of blackest darkness for them. (13)

Questions.Q: Who prophesied about those false teachers?
Questions.A: Enoch, who was the sixth direct descendant from Adam, prophesied about them. (14)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when someone prophesies?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that a person will speak out a direct message from God or proclaim a message inspired by God. (See "prophesy" in KBT in the "prophet" entry.)

Questions.Q: What did Enoch prophesy?
Questions.A: He said that the Lord will come with thousands of his holy angels. (14)
He said that they will come to judge everyone,
to convict all the ungodly people of all the ungodly things they have done
and to convict all the ungodly sinners of all the terrible things they have said against the Lord/God. (15)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to be holy?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Someone who is "holy" is set apart [by God] and dedicated to the service or worship of God. Anything that is "holy" for God must reflect his character by being physically unblemished or reflecting, to some degree, his purity.
Questions.Note: See "holy" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What does a person do when he sins?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He deliberately keeps on doing those things that please himself and displease God.
Questions.Note: See "sin" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did those false teachers make a practice of doing?
Questions.A: They were always grumbling/complaining and finding fault [with others].
They followed their own evil desires.
They bragged/boasted about themselves.
They flattered others to get what they wanted. (16)

Section.heading: Jude 17-23 Jude told the Christians that, since they have been warned that there are false teachers among them, they should help one another to grow and mature in their faith in God so that they won't be led astray by those false teachers.

Questions.Q: What did the apostles warn the Christians will happen in the last days/when the world is about to end?
Questions.A: Men will appear who will make fun of/ridicule/scoff at the Christians. (18)
Questions.Alternative: What did the apostles warn the Christians will happen in the last days?
What did the apostles warn the Christians will happen when the world is about to end?

Questions.Q: What did Jude tell his friends to do?
Questions.A: He told them to make their faith/believing in Christ strong/firm
and to pray in/with the power/ability the Holy Spirit gave them. (20)

Questions.Q: What did Jude tell his friends to remember?
Questions.A: He told them to remember the words of the apostles of the Lord Jesus Christ. (17)

Questions.Q: What do you think an apostle does?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The general meaning of the Greek word apostolos is "envoy", "appointed representative", "someone who is sent on a mission". In the New Testament it develops the specific sense of an appointed representative of Jesus Christ. In Acts and the rest of the New Testament, the term "apostle" is the most common term that is used to refer to those who were commissioned by Jesus Christ to be founders of the church, and who then took up that function and position.
Questions.Note: See "apostle" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What will be characteristic of those men?
Questions.A: They will follow their own ungodly desires. (18)
They will cause divisions among the believers.
They will follow/will do the evil things they naturally desire.
They will not have the Holy Spirit. (19)

Questions.Q: Who do you think the Holy Spirit is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He is God's spirit, through whom he acts, reveals His will, and empowers individuals. (See "Holy Spirit" in KBT in the "spirit" entry.)

Questions.Q: What else did he tell them to do?
Questions.A: He told them to keep on being conscious of/depending on the love which God had for them as they waited for the Lord Jesus Christ to give them eternal life. (21)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for a person to have eternal life?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that a person will never die, he will live forever.
Questions.Note: This eternal life is in the spiritual realm not the physical.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Christ will give them this eternal life?
Questions.A: He will do this because he is merciful to them. (21)

Questions.Q: How did Jude say they are to treat those people who doubt?
Questions.A: They are to show mercy to those who doubt. (22)

Questions.Q: What are they to do in order to save others who are in danger of destruction/hell?
Questions.A: They are to warn/help/convince them so that they might be rescued/saved. (23)
Questions.Alternative: What are they to do in order to save others who are in danger of destruction?
What are they to do in order to save others who are in danger of hell?

Questions.Q: To whom else are they to show mercy?
Questions.A: They are to show mercy to those who have been contaminated by the evil things they desire to do. (23)

Questions.Q: When they show mercy to them and try to help them what are they to do?
Questions.A: They are to be on guard/avoid being contaminated by their sinful ways lest they also become involved with them in their sinful ways. (23)

Section.heading: Jude 24-25 Jude praised God because he is the only one who can keep the Christians from falling away from him.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what Jude said in these verses.
Questions.A: Jude ended his letter with praise to God. (25)

Questions.Q: What did Jude say that [God] is able to do for them?
Questions.A: He is able to keep them from falling/sinning/abandoning the Christian faith.
He is able to bring them into his presence without fault and with great joy. (24)
Questions.Alternative: What did Jude say that God is able to do for them?
What did Jude say that God is able to do for you?
What did Jude say that God is able to do for us?
What did Jude say that God is able to do for Christians?
What is God is able to do for them?
What is God is able to do for you?
What is God is able to do for us?
What is God is able to do for Christians?

Questions.Q: What did Jude want God to receive?
Questions.A: He wanted God to receive/be acknowledged [by all people] as having glory, majesty, power and authority. (25)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when you give glory to someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: When you give glory to someone you reveal the greatness of someone, you demonstrate or show openly that someone is worthy of receiving honor.
Questions.Note: See "glory" in KBT.

Questions.Q: How did Jude say that God will be acknowledged as having these attributes?
Questions.A: These attributes of God will be seen because of/through Jesus Christ our Lord. (25)

Questions.Q: When did Jude say that God will be acknowledged/honored in this way?
Questions.A: God was acknowledged from the past, and is now in the present, and will be acknowledged forever. (25)
Questions.Alternative: When did Jude say that God will be acknowledged in this way?
When did Jude say that God will be honored in this way?

Section.heading: Luke 1:1-4 Luke told about the purpose of his writing these words.

Questions.Q: What do you think was Luke's purpose in writing this first passage?
Questions.A: Luke wanted to tell Theophilus the reason why he wrote all the rest of this book.

Questions.Q: To whom did Luke write these words?
Questions.A: He wrote to an important man named Theophilus. (3)
Questions.Note: If it is possible in your language, show that Theophilus was more important than Luke. Luke spoke with respect to Theophilus.

Questions.Q: Many people had been writing about the same things. What were those things?
Questions.A: They had been writing about the events that had taken place among them. (1)
Questions.Note: Luke used the words "among us". If your language uses one pronoun to include the listener within the group and another pronoun to exclude the listener, the pronoun used here should exclude Theophilus. The events happened among people whom Luke knew. They were groups of Jews and others who believed in Jesus. We do not know whether Theophilus was either a Jew or a believer when Luke wrote to him.

Questions.Q: What do you think those events were telling about?
Questions.A: They told about Jesus.
-OR-
They told about the things Jesus had said and done.

Questions.Q: How did those people know the things about which they had written?
Questions.A: They had seen those things happen (from when they first began). (2)

Questions.Q: How did Luke know about those events?
Questions.A: He carefully checked into all those matters which were related to Jesus's life and work, beginning with the first things that happened. (3)

Questions.Q: What was Luke's purpose for writing about these same things?
Questions.A: He wrote so that Theophilus would know that the information he had been told was true and reliable. (4)

Section.heading: Luke 1:5-25 An angel told Zechariah that his wife would bear his son, John the Baptizer.

Questions.Q: Tell me about the things that happened to Zechariah.
Questions.A: An angel appeared to Zechariah while he was working in the temple as a priest. The angel told him that his wife, Elizabeth, would have a baby son and that he must name him John. Because Zechariah and Elizabeth were very old and she had never been able to have a baby before, Zechariah did not believe the angel. Because he did not believe, the angel made him unable to speak until the baby was born. After Zechariah returned home, Elizabeth became pregnant.

Questions.Q: What was so important about Elizabeth conceiving and bearing a son that Luke wrote about it to Theophilus?
Questions.A: An old, barren couple conceiving and bearing a child (7) would show that God was doing this. People would know that God had important work for John to do when he grew up (15-17).
John would prepare people for Jesus's coming (17).

Questions.Q: At what time did Zechariah and Elizabeth live?
Questions.A: They lived during the time when Herod was king of Judea. (5)

Questions.Q: What work did Zechariah's do?
Questions.A: He was a priest. (5)

Questions.Q: What do you think a priest did when he worked?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He represented the people who came to worship God. He acted in their place by offering their sacrifices, prayers and gifts to God. He also represented God to those people when he announced that God had accepted their offerings and had forgiven their sins.
Questions.Note: See "priest" in KBT.

Questions.Q: How did Zechariah and Elizabeth act and live?
Questions.A: They lived in a way which God had said was right, obeying all his commands/commandments. No one could say they had broken God's laws. (6)
Questions.Note: Because Luke explained here what "righteous" living is, a question about this Key Term will not be asked until it is used again at verse 17.

Questions.Q: What commands/commandments do you think that the Lord expects people to follow/obey?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The answer should focus on actions like those named in the Ten Commandments (Exod. 20:1-17; Deut. 5:1-21), but may include other instructions God gave to his people as well.
Questions.Alternative: What commands do you think that the Lord expects people to follow?
What commands do you think that the Lord expects people to obey?
What commandments do you think that the Lord expects people to follow?
What commandments do you think that the Lord expects people to obey?

Questions.Q: To whom did Luke refer in the words "the Lord's commandments" (6), "the Lord's temple" (9) and "the Lord's angel" (11)?
Questions.A: He referred to God himself.

Key Term Check: The word "lord" refers to a person who has authority over another person. God has supernatural authority over all of mankind because he created everyone and everything in the world. See "Lord" in KBT in the "God" entry.

Questions.Q: Why did Elizabeth have no children?
Questions.A: She was not able to bear any children
and now both she and her husband were old. (7)

Questions.Q: What happened to Zechariah when the men of his clan were serving God as priests?
Questions.A: The men chose him to burn incense [on the altar] inside the temple building [in Jerusalem]. (8-9)

Questions.Q: How did the men choose which man would do this important work?
Questions.A: They followed the usual custom of the priests, which was to cast lots. (9)

Questions.Q: How do the people who speak your language choose someone when everyone, or no one, wants to be chosen?
Questions.Note: Listen for whether the words used in the translation are used, or not used, to describe the culture's customs.

Questions.Q: If the people who speak your language do something like the priests did in order to help them decide things, tell me what they do.
Questions.Note: The words used in the translation should not refer to actions that are illegal or that are opposed by the Christian churches present in the language area.

Questions.Q: What kind of a building do you think a temple is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A temple is a place where people gather to worship/sing/pray/offer sacrifices to a spirit being. This one was for worshiping God.
Questions.Note: See "temple" in KBT. (9)
Questions.Alternative: What do you think a temple is?
What do you think a temple was?
What is a temple?
For what purpose do you think people used the temple?
What was the purpose of the temple?

Questions.Q: What were the people who were worshiping doing at the time Zechariah went inside the temple to burn incense for God?
Questions.A: They were praying. (10)
Questions.Alternative: What were the people who were worshipping doing at the time Zechariah went inside the temple to burn incense for God?

Questions.Q: Where were they praying?
Questions.A: They were outside (the temple building, but not outside the temple grounds). (10)
Questions.Note: This referred to the main building, which Zechariah had entered. The worshipers had not left the temple grounds.

A footnote may be necessary to clarify that the temple was regarded as so holy that only the priests were permitted to enter into it (see Lev. 9 and 16). All the worshipers stayed outside the front of the building.

Questions.Q: What do you think that people do when they pray?
Questions.A: They ask someone, usually a spirit being, for help with their problems and needs or the problems and needs of other people. They thank and praise the spirit for his past help and blessings.
Questions.Note: In the GNT, this talking is only with God.

Questions.Q: What happened while Zechariah was inside the temple?
Questions.A: An angel (of the Lord) appeared to him. (11)

Questions.Q: Who do you think an angel is and what does he do?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: An angel is a good spirit being whom God created. He stays where God is and does whatever work God tells him to do. Often he carries a message from God to someone.
Questions.Note: See "angel" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think an altar is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It is a table-like structure usually made of wood or piled stones. Gifts of incense, food, animals or other valuable things are set on its flat top to give to God or to other spirits. Often those gifts are burned up on the top of the altar. The altar of incense in the temple was made of wood and then covered with gold (Exod. 30:1-10; 37:25-29; 1 Chron. 28:18).
Questions.Note: See "altar" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Pretend you are the angel and this table/chair/bench/tree is the altar. Show me where the angel was standing according to this verse.
Questions.A: (Because many languages describe "right" and "left" by referring to a person's or animal's "hands", an object like an altar cannot have a "right side" or a "left side", even though the Greek and English languages allow it. The object that the person is using to represent the altar should be at that person's left side as he/she faces you, the checker.

If the person is not standing in the correct place, you should go and stand in the correct position. Then ask the person to tell you the correct way to describe where you are now standing. That may be by saying that the altar was at the angel's left-hand side.)
Questions.Note: A few writers say that the "right side" referred to Zechariah's right side, but the grammar here parallels other examples that are not disputed, such as Mark 10:37 and John 21:6.
Questions.Alternative: Pretend you are the angel and this table is the altar. Show me where the angel was standing according to this verse.
Pretend you are the angel and this chair is the altar. Show me where the angel was standing according to this verse.
Pretend you are the angel and this bench is the altar. Show me where the angel was standing according to this verse.
Pretend you are the angel and this tree is the altar. Show me where the angel was standing according to this verse.

Questions.Q: How did Zechariah feel when he saw the angel?
Questions.A: He was alarmed and afraid. (12)

Questions.Q: What did the angel say to Zechariah about that?
Questions.A: Zechariah should not be afraid because God had heard [and was ready to answer] his prayer (about having a son). (13)

Questions.Q: What else did the angel say about God answering Zechariah's prayer?
Questions.A: Zechariah's wife, Elizabeth, would give birth to his son and he must name the boy John. (13)
Key Term Check: Choosing the right name for a person or a place was extremely important to the Jews. See "name" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Whom did the angel say would be happy that John was born?
Questions.A: He said that Zechariah himself and many other people, too, would rejoice. (14)

Questions.Q: For what reason would they be so happy?
Questions.A: John would be important and honored in God's sight, that is, according to what God considers important. (14-15)
Questions.Note: The person who answers may include things in his/her answer from the items in the answer below the next question. You may then skip over the next question.

Questions.Q: How would John's life show that he was an important worker for God?
Questions.A: He would never drink wine or any other drink that could make him drunk. (15)
He would be filled with the Holy Spirit right from his birth or even before that. // He would have the Holy Spirit in his life right from his birth or even before that. (15)

Key Term Check: The Holy Spirit is the spirit of the holy God. He works in people's hearts/spirits/lives on God's behalf, revealing God's will to us and guiding us to please God. See "Holy Spirit" in KBT in the "advocate, counselor" entry and also in the "spirit" entry.
He would cause many Israelites/Jews to turn [their hearts/lives away from sin] to obeying God. (16)
Key Term Check: See "Israel" and "Jew" in KBT in the "Israel, Jew, Hebrew" entry.
He would work with the same kind of power and spirit as [the prophet] Elijah had done. (17)
Questions.Note: A footnote may be needed to indicate that God required this of priests while they were on duty (see Lev. 10:8-9). He also required those who took the Nazirite vow to live like this (see Num. 6:1-4).
(Note: This may be translated:
"having the same determination and attitude as Elijah had",
-OR-
"having God's power and spirit the same as Elijah had.")

Questions.Q: Who do you think Elijah was?
Questions.A: He was a prophet in Old Testament times (1Kng. 17-2Kng. 2).
He did many miracles and spoke God's messages to many people, including many kings.
He never died, but God took him up to heaven alive (2Kng. 2).
Questions.Note: Luke did not use the word "prophet" here, but this question checks the respondent's understanding of who Elijah was and what he had done.

You may want to make a footnote or reference that in the last two verses of the Old Testament God said that he would send Elijah back to earth just before the savior would come. More than four hundred years later the angel Gabriel used those very same words when he told Zechariah what his son John would do. Jesus later said that John had done the same work in the same way as Elijah had done earlier (see Matt. 11:14; Mark 9:11-13).

Questions.Q: What do you think a prophet does?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A prophet tells people messages that come from the spirit world. In the Bible only the men who spoke messages from God were called prophets. They spoke for God about what he had done in the past or would do in the future. They told how that would affect the people who were listening to them.
Questions.Note: See "prophet" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What was this important work that John would do when he grew up?
Questions.A: He would help many Israelites/Jews to turn their hearts to God (16) by turning their hearts to [love] their fellowmen/children, and by turning away from disobeying God to following the way of people who acted rightly. (17),
-OR-
He would go ahead of the Lord (their God) and get many people ready for him to come into their lives (physically and spiritually/to rule and reign).
Questions.Note: The words "the Lord" as found here in some English translations is the word "him" in the Greek text. "Him" clearly refers back five words earlier to "the Lord their God" (vs. 16). The Jews referred to only one spirit being as "the Lord" (see Deut. 6, especially vs. 4). Any words used in a translation that only allow for Jesus, the Messiah, to be understood in this verse need adjusting.

Questions.Q: What do you think a righteous person is like?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A righteous person is one who wants to please God by living the way God says is the right way.
Questions.Note: See verse 6 again. Also see "righteous" in KBT in the "just, justify" entry.

Questions.Q: What did Zechariah say when he heard that his wife would bear a son for him?
Questions.A: "I myself and my wife are too old. How will I know this will really happen?" (18)

Questions.Q: Do you think that Zechariah's response showed that he believed the angel or that he did not believe him?
Questions.A: His words showed that he did not believe the angel/did not have strong faith.
Questions.Note: The key terms of "believe" and "faith" are discussed in verse 20, below.

Questions.Q: How did the words of Zechariah show that he did not believe the angel?
Questions.A: He asked the angel to do something to prove that he had the power to do what he had said. (18)

Questions.Q: What authority did the angel have to tell this message to Zechariah?
Questions.A: He, Gabriel, stood in the very presence of God, (that is, he was a special angel to whom God gave the important work to do). God had sent him to Zechariah to tell him this good news. (19)

Questions.Q: What was the angel's good news?
Questions.A: God had heard Zechariah's prayers to have a child. He was going to give Zechariah a son (13).
Questions.Note: The Greek word Luke used here means "tell good news". It is the same word he used regularly elsewhere in this book to indicate that God's plan to send the Messiah to save people was happening right then. That meaning is also in the words of the angel here (17), but it is not what a person would think of immediately. Zechariah's son would be preparing people for the Lord God's coming into the world in the person of his son, Jesus, to save them. That was "good news". If the respondent includes this point in his/her answer, give him/her special praise.

Questions.Q: What sign did the angel give to Zechariah to prove that he was telling him the truth?
Questions.A: Zechariah would not be able to speak until the day those things happened, that is, the day that child was born. (20)

Questions.Q: Why did Zechariah have this problem/difficulty?
Questions.A: He did not believe what the angel had said. (20)
Questions.Alternative: Why did Zechariah have this problem?
Why did Zechariah have this difficulty?

Questions.Q: What does it mean that a person believes (or does not believe) what another person has said?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: That person is convinced/sure in his mind, he completely trusts, that the speaker told the truth. (See "believe" in KBT. "Faith" is also discussed in that entry.)

Questions.Q: What were the people who were standing outside the temple thinking?
Questions.A: They were amazed that Zechariah was staying such a long time in the temple. (21) (They did not know any normal reason why this should be happening, so it seemed very strange.)

Questions.Q: What happened when Zechariah did come back out to them?
Questions.A: Zechariah was not able to speak to them, so he used his hands to make signs. (22)

Questions.Q: What did the people think that Zechariah's actions meant?
Questions.A: The people then knew that he had seen a vision inside the temple. (22)

Questions.Q: What do you think happens when a person sees a vision?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It is like a person having a dream when he is wide awake and his eyes are wide open. The person often can see spirit beings and see or hear things he did not know about before. God helped Zechariah to see and hear the angel.

Questions.Q: When did Zechariah return home?
Questions.A: He returned home when his time of serving in the temple was finished. (23)

Questions.Q: What happened after he was back home?
Questions.A: His wife Elizabeth became pregnant. (24)

Questions.Q: What did Elizabeth do then?
Questions.A: She just stayed in and around her house. She did not want a lot of people to see her. (24)

Questions.Q: How long did she do like that?
Questions.A: She did that for five months. (24)

Questions.Q: What did she say/think about being pregnant?
Questions.A: She said that this was the way the Lord had helped her. He was now taking away the disgrace/humiliation/shame she felt/had in the eyes of other people. (25)
Questions.Alternative: What did she say about being pregnant?
What did she think about being pregnant?

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that people humiliated Elizabeth or caused her to feel shame?
Questions.A: She had never borne a child, especially no son.

Section.heading: Luke 1:26-38 An angel told Mary that she would bear God's son, Jesus.

Questions.Q: Tell me about the things that happened to Mary.
Questions.A: God sent an angel to tell Mary that she would have a baby son and that his name would be Jesus. Mary was surprised and frightened by this. She asked the angel how this could happen because she was not married yet. The angel said that God himself would cause her to become pregnant. Therefore, the child would be the son of God. Mary accepted that this was what God wanted for her, so she was willing for this to happen to her.

Questions.Q: What was so important about Mary conceiving and bearing a son that Luke wrote about it to Theophilus?
Questions.A: A virgin conceiving and bearing a child would show that God was doing this. (27, 31, 34, 35)
This child, Jesus, would be referred to as (or called) the Son of God. (32, 35)
God would give him authority over Israel forever. (32)

Questions.Q: At what time did God send an angel to speak to Mary?
Questions.A: He sent the angel during the sixth month of Elizabeth's pregnancy. (26)

Questions.Q: Was this the same angel whom God had sent to speak to Zechariah or was this another angel?
Questions.A: He was the same angel, Gabriel. (19, 26)

Questions.Q: What did Luke tell us about Mary?
Questions.A: She lived in the town of Nazareth in the district/province/state of Galilee. (26)
She was a virgin. (27)
She was promised in marriage to Joseph. (27)

Questions.Q: What did Luke tell us about Joseph?
Questions.A: He was a descendant of [Israel's great king,] David. (27)

Questions.Q: What did the angel say to Mary?
Questions.A: "Hello/Good Day, you to whom the Lord has shown great kindness. He is with you." (28)

Questions.Q: What did Mary think after hearing him say that?
Questions.A: She was thoroughly confused/mixed up/in turmoil. (29)
She wondered what these unusual words of greeting really meant.

Questions.Q: What did the angel say was the reason that Mary was not to be afraid?
Questions.A: God had decided to show special kindness to her. (30)

Questions.Q: What was going to happen which would show God's kindness to Mary?
Questions.A: She would become pregnant and bear a [special] son. (31)

Questions.Q: What did the angel say to show Mary that her son would be a special/important person?
Questions.A: The angel told her the name God had chosen for the child, the name Jesus. (31)
-OR-
The angel told her what name she must give to the child. (31)
Jesus would do important work for God, and people/God would call him the Son of the Most High/Supreme God. (32)
The Lord [who is] God would make him a king, as his ancestor David had been. (32)
-OR-
The Lord [who is] God would give him authority to rule like his ancestor [King] David had done. (32)
Jesus's reign over the descendants of Jacob [Israel/God's people] would never end. (33)
Questions.Alternative: What did the angel say to show Mary that her son would be a special person?
What did the angel say to show Mary that her son would be a important person?

Questions.Q: After hearing that she would bear a child, what did Mary ask?
Questions.A: She asked how this could happen since she had never had sexual relations with a man. (34)

Questions.Q: What did the angel say about how Mary would become pregnant?
Questions.A: The Holy Spirit would do it supernaturally./The Holy Spirit would make it happen. (35)

Questions.Q: What did the angel say would show that it was true that God made it happen?
Questions.A: The child would be holy and would be called the son of God. (35)

Questions.Q: What do you think makes someone holy?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: God declares that person to be set apart from the way people live to please themselves. He sets them apart in order to totally serve him. That person would be morally pure, acting in all ways like God would act.
Questions.Note: If you discuss how God is holy, see the question at verses 49b-50 below.

Questions.Q: Why did the angel tell Mary that Elizabeth was pregnant?
Questions.A: Elizabeth, who had been unable to have children and now was very old, was already into her sixth month of pregnancy. Since that seemed impossible, but was true, then nothing would be too difficult for God to do. [Mary, too, would have the baby the angel was telling her about.] // Whatever God says will happen, he will use his great power to make happen. He had already helped old Elizabeth become pregnant. [Therefore, Mary should believe what the angel was telling her also.] (36-37)

Questions.Q: When the angel talked earlier with Zechariah, Zechariah did not believe that what the angel said would really be able to happen. How did Mary respond to the angel's message to her?
Questions.A: She did believe him.

Questions.Q: What did Mary say that showed that she believed him?
Questions.A: She said that she was ready to serve God, to allow him to use her in the way the angel had said. // Because she thought of herself as God's servant/slave, she would be happy for him to use her in the way the angel had said.

Questions.Q: What do you think a slave is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A slave is a person who must do whatever his/her master wants because the master owns the person as a possession. The slave is not free to do what he likes or go where he likes.
Questions.Note: See "servant, slave" in KBT.

Questions.Q: When Mary visited Elizabeth, what happened that showed that God was there with the two women?
Questions.A: The Holy Spirit filled/inspired/caused Elizabeth to speak like a prophet about Mary and the child she would bear. (41-42)
-OR-
Before Mary said anything more than a greeting to Elizabeth, God's Spirit had already revealed to Elizabeth what was happening to Mary and that Mary had believed that it would happen. (41-45)

Questions.Q: What did Mary do in the days following the angel's visit to her?
Questions.A: She got ready and went quickly to the town where Elizabeth lived. (39)

Questions.Q: How long a time does it sound like Mary traveled to go to Elizabeth?
Questions.Note: Because the distance Mary traveled would have been more than 70 miles (115 km.), the translation of "went quickly" should allow for 3-4 days of travel.

Questions.Q: Where was the town where Zechariah and Elizabeth lived?
Questions.A: It was in the hilly/mountainous region of Judah (Judea). (39)
Questions.Note: Luke wrote the name as "Judah", the Jews' traditional name for the area, the name used in the Old Testament. It referred to the descendants of Judah, whom God had told to live there. At the time Zechariah and Elizabeth lived there, the Roman government called the area the province of "Judea". That name is used elsewhere in the New Testament. Whichever name is in your translation, it should be clear to the target audience as to what the name refers, whether to a tribal/clan territory or to a government name.

Questions.Q: What happened when Elizabeth heard Mary's greeting?
Questions.A: The baby in Elizabeth's womb leaped/jerked/moved excitedly for joy. (41, 44)
The Holy Spirit filled/inspired Elizabeth to speak out with a loud voice/excitedly. (41)

Questions.Q: What did Elizabeth say about God's kindness towards Mary?
Questions.A: God was blessing her more than he had blessed any other woman. (He was also blessing the child she would bear.) (42)

Questions.Q: What does it mean to bless someone and to be blessed?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: One person praises/says good things about the other person or asks God to do good things for that person.
Questions.Note: See "bless, blessed, blessing" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think this special blessing from God was which Elizabeth was talking about?
Questions.A: Mary would give birth to God's son. No other woman would have that privilege and honor.

Questions.Q: What had the Holy Spirit revealed to Elizabeth about Mary's baby?
Questions.A: He would be Elizabeth's Lord. (43)
Questions.Note: What Elizabeth said shows us that she already knew the baby in Mary's womb was the savior God had promised, even God himself.

Questions.Q: How did Elizabeth feel about such an important person coming into her home?
Questions.A: She felt unworthy/undeserving of such an honor. (43)

Questions.Q: How did she know that Mary was pregnant and that Mary's baby would be her own Lord?
Questions.A: At the same time that she heard Mary greet her, the baby in her own womb leaped/jerked/moved excitedly for joy. That confirmed to her that what she had learned from the Holy Spirit was true. (41, 44)

Questions.Q: What did Elizabeth feel was the reason that Mary was so blessed/fortunate/in such a happy state?
Questions.A: Mary believed that what the Lord had said to her [through the angel] really would happen. (45)
Questions.Alternative: What did Elizabeth feel was the reason that Mary was so blessed?
What did Elizabeth feel was the reason that Mary was so fortunate?
What did Elizabeth feel was the reason that Mary was in such a happy state?

Questions.Q: Why did Mary want to talk about these things?
Questions.A: She wanted to express her joy and praise to God for what he had done. (46-47, 49)

Questions.Q: What did Mary say that God had done?
Questions.A: He thought about/remembered his people, her in particular (48), but also all of the Israelites (54).
He saved them from bad kings [and other dangers]. (47, 52)
He helped her (48) and all of the Israelite people (53-54).
He was merciful to them as he had promised [her forefathers, such as Abraham and his descendants,] long ago (50, 54, 55).

Questions.Q: What did Mary say it was that made her very joyful?
Questions.A: God [cared about her and] had taken notice of her, even though she thought of herself as only a servant/slave of God/only a very ordinary, unimportant person. (48)
Key Term Check: See "servant/slave" above at 1:38. Also see "servant, slave" in KBT.

Key Term Check: See "soul" and "spirit" in KBT. The Jews used sets of synonyms to create parallel lines in their Hebrew poetry. Thus, a person can understand "soul" and "spirit" in verses 46 and 47 as synonyms for Mary herself. However, elsewhere in the Bible "soul" refers to a person's inner self, that part we call "life" itself. It refers more to the humanness of a person, that is, his physical aspects rather than his spiritual aspects. "Spirit", on the other hand, refers to a person's relationship with the supernatural world, especially God. Both the physical and the spiritual aspects of Mary, that is, her whole self, was very joyful.

Questions.Q: What would show that God had truly taken special notice of her?
Questions.A: From that time onward all generations would refer to Mary as having a special blessing from God. (48)

Questions.Q: Why would everyone think and speak like that about her?
Questions.A: The mighty God had done great/important things for her [in making her the mother of the Savior]. (49)

Questions.Q: Because God had chosen Mary to be the mother of the Savior, what did she understand better about God?
Questions.A: He is always holy and very merciful to all those people who are in awe of him/those who revere and respect him as God.

Questions.Q: What do you think it means that God is holy?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He is perfectly good and right in everything he is and does. There is nothing bad, wrong or evil in him or in what he does. No one else is like him. We honor and worship him because he is like that.

Questions.Q: What do you think it means that God is very merciful?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He has deep feelings of genuine compassion/loving concern for people and, because of that, he does not punish their sin/wrongdoing as they deserve.
Questions.Note: See "mercy" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What are some of the ways in which God has used his power/strength to help his people?
Questions.A: He has scattered those people who think proud thoughts about themselves. (51)
He has brought the reign and high status of [some] kings to an end (52a),
but given increased status to the humble people/and made humble people important (52b).
He has generously given those people with [spiritual] needs everything they needed, even more,
but has taken away the good things [of this world] from those who trusted in them [instead of trusting God]. (51-53)
Questions.Alternative: What are some of the ways in which God has used his power to help his people?
What are some of the ways in which God has used his strength to help his people?

Questions.Q: What did Mary say about God's interacting with his people Israel?
Questions.A: He had come to help them and all Abraham's descendants forever.
By doing that, God was keeping the promise he made to the Israelites' ancestors, such as Abraham, to be merciful to them.

Questions.Q: How long did Mary stay at Elizabeth's house?
Questions.A: She stayed about three months.

Section.heading: Luke 1:57-66 Elizabeth bore John the Baptizer.

Questions.Q: What did neighbors and relatives recognize as unusual about the birth of this baby?
Questions.A: An elderly woman bore a healthy son. (57)
The parents did not want the boy to be named after his father or any other relative, but to be named John. (59-63)
Zechariah was able to speak again just as the angel had foretold. (20, 64)

Questions.Q: What were the neighbors' and relatives' responses to these things?
Questions.A: The people rejoiced with Elizabeth. (58)
They were amazed that Zechariah also wanted to name the baby John. (63)
People all over that (hilly/mountainous) area talked much about all these things (65)
and thought seriously about what this boy would be [or what he would do] in the future. (66)

Questions.Q: What happened to show that the Lord had been very merciful/kind towards Elizabeth?
Questions.A: She was pregnant the usual amount of time.
and then she gave birth to a son [even though she was elderly]. (57)
Questions.Alternative: What happened to show that the Lord had been very merciful towards Elizabeth?
What happened to show that the Lord had been very kind towards Elizabeth?

Questions.Q: How did her neighbors and relatives respond?
Questions.A: They rejoiced with her concerning the Lord's great kindness to her [in giving her a son]. (58)

Questions.Q: What happened on the child's eighth day?
Questions.A: People came to circumcise and name the baby. (59)

Questions.Q: What do you think that the people did to this new baby boy when they circumcised him?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: They cut off the ring of foreskin from around the boy's penis. (See peritemnw in L&N in entry 53.51.)
Questions.Note: If the translator is using the name of a cultural ceremony, ask about all its implications physically, culturally and spiritually. The Jews did the ceremony as a religious rite which dedicated the child to God and physically marked him as a Jew. If the translator's culture does not practice circumcision, describing the action may sound offensive and vulgar to any mixed group of men and women or children. The translator may need to use a more general word or phrase in the translation and refer to a footnote or glossary item.
