In that note the translator can explain clearly what is done to a male's body and tell why it was customary to do it on a Jewish baby's eighth day (see Gen. 17:9-14; Lev. 12:1-3).

Questions.Q: What problem came up among the people at Zechariah's house that day?
Questions.A: The friends and relatives wanted to call/name the boy [his father's name,] Zechariah. (59, 61)
But Elizabeth strongly told them, "No", and said that he would be named/called John. (60)

Questions.Q: How did the visitors and Zechariah communicate with each other?
Questions.A: They used [hand] signs/sign language. (62-63)

Questions.Q: How did Zechariah show what he thought about the boy's name?
Questions.A: He asked for something on which to write and he wrote the name John. (63)

Questions.Q: Why were all the people amazed at Zechariah's answer?
Questions.A: They did not know any reason for his answer because neither the boy's father nor any other relative was being honored by giving him that name. (61)
Also, both the father and mother agreed that the child's name was to be John. (60, 63)

Questions.Q: Why did Zechariah and Elizabeth name the boy John?
Questions.A: They named him John because that was the name the angel had told Zechariah to name him even before Elizabeth was pregnant. (1:13)

Questions.Q: What happened to Zechariah at the moment he wrote the name?
Questions.A: He was able to speak again. (64)

Questions.Q: What did Zechariah first talk about after he could speak?
Questions.A: He blessed/praised God. (64)

Questions.Q: What did people do after they had seen or heard about the events surrounding John's birth?
Questions.A: They were all fearful/in reverential awe and talked very much about these events. (65)
They thought much/seriously about what it all meant (66a)
and they said, "What will this child be [when he grows up]?" (66b)

Questions.Q: What did those people recognize was happening in these unusual events?
Questions.A: They recognized that God was actively overseeing all that happened to John. (66c)

Section.heading: Luke 1:67-80 Zechariah praised God and prophesied.

Questions.Q: What was Zechariah's purpose in talking about these things?
Questions.A: He wanted to praise God because God was about to send the savior to help his people (68) as he had promised long ago. (69-70, 72, 78-79)
He also wanted to speak the message that God's Spirit had given him about how John would fit into God's plans to send a savior to them. (76-77)

Questions.Q: How did Zechariah know about all these things?
Questions.A: The Holy Spirit was in him, guiding his thinking as he spoke. (67)

Questions.Q: What do you think that Zechariah did when he prophesied?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He spoke the message that God's spirit guided him to say about the past and the future. He reminded the people that, with the birth of John, God was beginning to do what he had said in the past that he would do.

Questions.Q: What kind of help had God given to his people Israel?
Questions.A: God had come to set his people free (68) from their enemies (71). // God had come to release his people (68) from the control of their enemies (71).
Key Term Check: See "redeem, redemption, ransom" in KBT.
Questions.Note: The translation of "enemies" should allow for spiritual enemies as well as human enemies.

Questions.Q: How was God going to set his people free?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: For understanding the time frame which Zechariah used, see "age" in KBT in the "world, age" entry.
Questions.Note: He was sending a powerful savior (69), just as he had promised through his prophets long ago (70).

Questions.Q: What does a savior do?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He rescues/saves another person who is in danger of being hurt or even dying, if someone does not help him quickly.
Questions.Note: See "save, salvation, savior" in KBT.

Questions.Q: From which well-known family would this savior come?
Questions.A: He would be a descendant of [former king] David who had served God. (69)

Questions.Q: What kind of a relationship do you think that David had with God?
Questions.A: David wanted to help/please God, so he did what God asked him to do. God was pleased with David. (69)
Questions.Note: Although English translations use the word "servant", the Greek word is not the same one normally translated "servant" or "slave". The word used here is normally translated "child", and in the context here the focus is on the kind of loving help a child gives his father.

Questions.Q: Zechariah said that God was sending a savior. What did that show to Zechariah?
Questions.A: It showed him that God was being merciful to Abraham and the other [Israelite] forefathers. He (God) was doing what he had promised/said he would do in the covenant he had made with them. (72-73)
-OR-
God was being merciful to the [Israelites'] ancestors by continuing to keep his part of the covenant promise that he had made to Abraham and the other forefathers. (72-73)
-OR-
God was being merciful just as he had firmly promised to Abraham and the other forefathers. (72-73)

Questions.Q: What is a covenant?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It is an agreement, an especially binding promise, usually made by two people who are of equal status. If the person on one side of the covenant does not do as both have agreed, there usually is a strong punishment for him or he pays compensation to the other person. Today it would be called a contract. But the Greek word that is used in the Bible for covenants strongly implies that the terms of the agreement were stated by the person on only one side of the discussion, not both sides. Usually God is the one who says what will happen, that is, what he will do and what people must do. He binds himself to the other party.
Questions.Note: See "covenant" in KBT.

If the language has a special name to refer to these kinds of agreements, ask the respondent(s) to tell you the kinds of situations in which the people make these special agreements, these firm promises. Listen for any points where it would not be appropriate to state that God made that kind of an agreement. If there are some questionable areas, the translator may need to re-think how he used that term in the translation.

Questions.Q: What do you think made this covenant a holy one?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It was holy because God, who made it, is holy. It came from God, he spoke it, so it had the same characteristics that God has. (72)

Questions.Q: What does a person do when he swears an oath?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He uses strong, positive words to show that he will truly do as he has just promised. He also calls on God (Mark 14:71) or another spirit being (Josh. 23:10; Jer. 13:16; Amos 8:14) to punish him very badly if anything he has just said is not completely true. (See 2 Sam. 3:35.)

Questions.Q: What do you think will assure a person that God will do what he promises?
Questions.A: God is holy [Amos 4:2] and has all the power necessary to do anything he says. When he makes a promise, the other person will know for sure that God will do it.
Questions.Note: Sometimes God says he swears by himself. (See Gen. 22:16, where you will find the covenant and oath Zechariah was talking about here.) He also swears by his name, that is, his reputation (Isa. 45:23). Since God has never failed to keep his promises in the past and has never done any other bad action, he surely will not lie now, either (Ps. 89:34-35).

Questions.Q: What had God promised to Israel's ancestors?
Questions.A: He had promised to rescue them/save their people from being under the control of people who hated them/who were their enemies. (71, 74)
He would make them able to serve him without fearing (him).
-OR-
… without fearing (that their enemies would persecute or attack them). (74)

Questions.Q: How will they serve God without being afraid?
Questions.A: They will serve him by doing what is right in the sight of God and man the rest of their lives.
-OR-
They will serve him by being pure in their hearts and in their actions the rest of their lives.
-OR-
They will serve him by not doing what is wrong, but by doing what is right the rest of their lives.
Questions.Note: The three choices for verse 75 are the main interpretations of how the words "holiness" and "righteousness" relate to each other when they are found in the same sentence.

Questions.Q: In what way will John be a part of God's plan to send a savior?
Questions.A: He will go ahead of the Lord/savior to prepare the way for people (to accept him). (76)
-OR-
He will go ahead of the Lord/savior to tell people to prepare their lives for his coming. (76)

Questions.Q: What will people say about him because he does that work?
Questions.A: They will say he is a prophet of the Most High God/the Supreme God. (76)
Questions.Note: If you already discussed the term "prophet" above in 1:17, skip over the next question.

Questions.Q: What work do you think that a prophet does?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A prophet tells people messages which come from the spirit world. In the Bible only the men who spoke messages from God were called prophets. They spoke for God about what he had done in the past or would do in the future. They told how that would affect
the people who were listening to them.
Questions.Note: See "prophet" in KBT.

Questions.Q: How will John prepare the people to be ready for the savior?
Questions.A: He will tell them that God will save them when they ask him to forgive/remove their sins. (77)

Questions.Q: What is sin?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Because God made all people and told us how to live to please him, every time a person's thoughts, words or actions do not follow what God has said is right, that is sin. It is a turning away from being like God wants us to be.
Questions.Note: See "sin, sinner" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What does God do when he forgives sins?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He removes any record of a person's wrong action. That means that there is no need for the person to compensate God in any way, such as by being punished or by giving him good things or doing extra actions which would please him. God does not think of that person as being a bad person any longer, but as a person who is ready to do good.
Questions.Note: See "forgive" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Why does God forgive people's sins?
Questions.A: It is because God has deep feelings of wanting to be merciful towards them. (78)

Questions.Q: Tell me what the picture language about the sun/darkness/shadows means to you.
Questions.A: [THE SUN:] The sun is a picture of the savior coming from heaven to start a new day, a new period in our lives. He makes it clear to us how he saves us. Now we are encouraged about what is going to happen to us.
[DARKNESS/SHADOWS:] The time of not knowing about the true God and of being afraid that something, perhaps God or evil spirits, might soon make us die, ends. (78-79)
Questions.Note: This question is only relevant if the translation of verses 78-79 has picture language about the sun or darkness or shadows.
Questions.Alternative: Tell me what the picture language about the sun means to you.
Tell me what the picture language about the darkness means to you.
Tell me what the picture language about the shadows means to you.

Questions.Q: Where is this place that Zechariah said the savior would come from?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He said that the savior would come from heaven, that is, from the place where God and other spirit beings live. (78)
Questions.Note: See "heaven, sky" in KBT.

The word needed here may be different from the word for the physical sky, even though Greek and English use the same word for both meanings. Use what is correct for the culture and language of the translation.

Questions.Q: What do you think this peace is to which Zechariah referred?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: This peace is a calm heart/spirit which does not worry when we face God because he has already forgiven our sins.
-OR-

Long, long ago God promised mankind that he would send someone to save them from the punishment they deserved. Later, God sent Jesus into this world as that savior. When we see clearly that God already has done what he promised to do, we have peace in our hearts. Peace is a calm heart/spirit and being free from worry.
Questions.Note: See "peace" in KBT.
See "peace" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did Luke tell us about John growing to be a man?
Questions.A: He matured physically and mentally.
Then he lived in an uninhabited area/the wilderness/desert until the time he began his work publicly among the people of Israel.

Questions.Q: What did Luke tell about in these verses?
Questions.A: He told about the birth of Jesus and why Joseph and Mary were in the town of Bethlehem at that time.

Questions.Q: What new order/command/decree did Augustus make?
Questions.A: He commanded that everyone whom the Roman government ruled should have his/her name recorded in the government records. (1)
Questions.Alternative: What new order did Augustus make?
What new command did Augustus make?
What new decree did Augustus make?

Questions.Q: Why was Augustus able to command all the people to do that?
Questions.A: He was the Caesar, the very highest government official in all the area which the Roman government ruled. (1) (He even ruled over the kings.)

Questions.Q: Where were the people to go to record their names?
Questions.A: They were to go to the area/village where their ancestors had been born/had lived. (3)

Questions.Q: Read the last verse of chapter 1 and the first verse of this chapter again. Will people think that Augustus commanded this when John was still a baby or after John had grown to be a man?
Questions.A: Augustus commanded this when John was still a baby.
Questions.Note: According to the difference in the times when Elizabeth and Mary became pregnant (see Luke 1:26-36), John would have been about six months old when this next event happened.

Questions.Q: What did Joseph do when he heard about the command to register/record his name?
Questions.A: He also obeyed the government's command to have their officials record his name in their book. (4, 5)
He left the town/village of Nazareth in [the province of] Galilee (4a)
and traveled to the town/village of Bethlehem in [the province of] Judea. (4b)
He traveled with Mary, the young woman who was promised in marriage to him. (5)
Questions.Alternative: What did Joseph do when he heard about the command to register his name?
What did Joseph do when he heard about the command to record his name?

Questions.Q: Why did Joseph go to the village of Bethlehem?
Questions.A: That was the village where Joseph's ancestor, (the famous king) David, had lived. (4b)

Questions.Q: What do we learn about Mary from hearing/reading these verses?
Questions.A: She had been promised to Joseph to be his wife. (5)
She was pregnant. (5)
She went with Joseph to have the officials record their names in the government book. (4, 5)
She delivered a baby boy, her first child, while she and Joseph were at Bethlehem. (6-7)
Questions.Alternative: What do we learn about Mary from hearing these verses?
What do we learn about Mary from reading these verses?

Questions.Q: How did Mary care for her baby son?
Questions.A: She wrapped him in pieces of cloth (according to the Jewish custom of that time) and laid him in a manger/an animal's food trough/box. (7)

Questions.Q: Why did she have to use an animal's food box as the baby's bed?
Questions.A: Because all the places for travelers to stay (the inns/hotels) were already full of people, Joseph and Mary had to stay in the place where people usually fed their animals. (7)

Section.heading: Luke 2:8-20 An angel told some shepherds about the baby and they went to see him.

Questions.Q: God sent an angel at night with a message for some shepherds. What had happened that was so important for the shepherds to know?
Questions.A: The angel brought them the good news that the savior, Christ the Lord, had been born. (11)

Questions.Q: What were some shepherds doing the night when Mary bore her baby?
Questions.A: They were staying out in the open countryside guarding their flocks of sheep/goats at night. (8)

Questions.Q: What caused the shepherds to be very much afraid?
Questions.A: They suddenly saw an angel standing in front of them (9a)
and the bright light of God's glory/presence was shining all around them. (9b)
Questions.Note: (Key Term Check: The Greek word translated "glory" has many variations in meaning and use. Each meaning tries to describe a characteristic of God which people do not have. God is totally without sin. He is so different from sinful mankind that people find it hard to explain or describe what they see or experience when God makes his presence known.

You probably will not find a word in your language which includes every aspect of the Greek word for glory and would be correct for every use. You will probably find that the use of "glory" in verse 14 below is already different from its usage here. As much as you are able, translate any one aspect of "glory" consistently. See "glory" in KBT.)

Questions.Q: Why did the angel tell the shepherds they should not be afraid?
Questions.A: They were not to be afraid because he had come to tell them some good news which would cause all people to rejoice greatly. (10)

Questions.Q: What was that good news?
Questions.A: The good news was that the savior had been born that same night. (11)

Key Term Check: Luke used the Greek word which means "tell good news." It is the same word he used in 1:19 and we will see it again at 3:18 and 4:18, among many other places. Luke always used it to refer to the good news that God's plan to send the Messiah to save people was already happening. That is also the meaning of the angel's words here [10-11.)

Questions.Q: What did the angel say to indicate that this savior was someone very special?
Questions.A: He said that this savior was the Christ (the anointed one sent by God) and Lord (the one with authority to rule and reign over people [See Mic. 5:2]). (11)
Questions.Note: Key Term Check: Make sure that the title "Christ" is understood to be just that, a title, not a personal name. You may wish to make a footnote or glossary entry which indicates that this is the Greek equivalent to the Hebrew title "Messiah". See "Christ, Messiah" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Where did the angel say the savior was born?
Questions.A: In the village where [their ancestor, King] David had lived (that is, in Bethlehem). (11)

Questions.Q: What would the shepherds see which would prove to them that what the angel said was true? -OR- How would the shepherds know if they had found the baby which the angel was talking about?
Questions.A: They would find the baby wrapped in pieces of cloth (according to their Jewish custom) (12b)
and lying in a manger, that is, an animal's food trough/box. (12c)
Questions.Alternative: What would the shepherds see which would prove to them that what the angel said was true?
How would the shepherds know if they had found the baby which the angel was talking about?

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason this would be a sign to them?
Questions.A: People do not customarily put their babies into any animal's food box.
-OR-
The Jews would not expect to find the savior, whom they expected God to send to earth, in such a humble place as a manger.
Key Term Check: See "sign" in KBT in the "miracle, sign, wonder, mighty work" entry.

Questions.Q: What suddenly happened near that angel?
Questions.A: A great number of other spirit beings from heaven (angels) appeared. (13)

Questions.Q: What were those angels doing?
Questions.A: They were praising God. (13)
Questions.Note: The Greek word used here is not one of the eight words used in the rest of the GNT text to refer to songs and singing. It does not tell us whether the angels sang or not. The focus of this verb is on the content and purpose of the action, not the manner.

Questions.Q: What did their words of praise say about God?
Questions.A: There is glory for God in highest [heaven]. (14)
Questions.Note: "Highest" may refer to either the place where God is, or the place where the praising is occurring. Either way is acceptable, but if it can refer to both, that is even better.

Questions.Q: What do you think this glory is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It is the best praise, honor, and giving of thanks which can be given to God because of his perfect goodness to them.

Questions.Q: What did the angels say about people?
Questions.A: They said that there is peace among the people on the earth whom God has favored/with whom he is pleased. (14)
Key Term Check: See "peace" discussed above at 1:79.

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that the angels said these things in their praising God?
Questions.A: They were happy that the Savior was born. He would bring that kind of glory to God and peace to mankind. (They recognized that, because the savior had been born, there now was this glory and peace in heaven and on the earth, and they were excited about it.)

Questions.Q: When the angels finished praising God, what did they do?
Questions.A: They went back to heaven. (15)

Questions.Q: What did the shepherds decide to do then?
Questions.A: They decided to go to Bethlehem and see this thing that [the angel of] the Lord had just told them about had happened there, [the savior had been born that day]. (15)
-OR-
They decided to go to Bethlehem and see the savior whom [the angel of] the Lord had just told them had been born there that day. (15)

Questions.Q: How do we know the men were very excited to go find this savior who had just been born?
Questions.A: They went hurriedly on their way. (16)

Questions.Q: What did they find when they looked around the village of Bethlehem?
Questions.A: They located Mary and Joseph and saw the baby lying in the manger/an animal's food trough/box. (16)

Questions.Q: After they had seen the baby, what did they do?
Questions.A: They told people[, including Mary and Joseph,] what [the angel] had said to them about this child. (17)

Questions.Q: When the people heard the shepherds' story of what had happened, what did they think?
Questions.A: All of them were amazed. (18) (This kind of thing did not normally happen, so it seemed very strange.)

Questions.Q: How did Mary respond to all that had happened regarding her baby?
Questions.A: She kept thinking about them, wondering very much about what they meant. (19)

Questions.Q: After the shepherds had told people about these things, what did they do?
Questions.A: They returned [to where they had left their sheep flock outside the town]. (20)

Questions.Q: As they went back there, what were they saying or doing?
Questions.A: They were honoring God and saying wonderful things about him./They were talking about the unsurpassed greatness and the goodness of God. (20)

Questions.Q: What did Luke say was the reason for their joy?
Questions.A: Everything they had seen and heard was just as the angel had said that it would be. (20)

Section.heading: Luke 2:21 Mary and Joseph name the baby Jesus.

Questions.Q: What happened on the eighth day of Jesus's life?
Questions.A: He was circumcised,
and [his parents] named him Jesus.

Questions.Q: Why did Mary and Joseph name their baby boy Jesus?
Questions.A: It was the name the angel had told Mary to name him even before she was pregnant (1:31).
Questions.Note: An angel had also told Joseph to name the baby that name. (See Matt. 1:21)

Section.heading: Luke 2:22-24 Mary and Joseph presented Jesus to God at the temple.

Questions.Q: Why did Mary and Joseph take the baby Jesus to the temple at that particular time?
Questions.A: The Lord [God] had said that parents must present/dedicate every firstborn male child to him (Exod. 13:2, 12, 15). (22-23)
They also were to bring a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons [and give them to a priest] to offer as a sacrifice. (22, 24)
Questions.Note: The Law of Moses and the Law of the Lord are discussed below.

Questions.Q: Why did Mary and Joseph wait some weeks before they went to the temple to present the baby Jesus to God?
Questions.A: They waited for the days/time to end for Mary to be ritually pure/clean again. (22)
Questions.Note: The Law of Moses said that for 40 days after a Jewish woman had delivered a baby, she was not ritually clean/pure, so they waited for that time to end. The woman had to bring a special offering (see Lev. 12:2-8) in order to become ritually clean/pure again. After she did that, she would again be allowed to go to the temple and participate in religious activities.

Questions.Q: What do you think that Luke was talking about when he referred to being made pure/clean?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The words "made clean" here refer to being clean ritually, thus being allowed again into the public worship and the presence of God.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think that Luke was talking about when he referred to being made pure?
What do you think that Luke was talking about when he referred to being made clean?
Questions.Note: If the translator used a very general word like "clean," check to make sure it does not mean only to remove external things, such as dried blood or dirt from the skin. If the translator is using a cultural term for a ceremony which must be performed by local women when they wish to return to normal activities after childbirth, ask about all its implications physically, culturally and spiritually.
See "clean, pure" and "unclean, defiled, impure" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What is the Law of Moses?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The Law of Moses is the laws and instructions which God had revealed to Moses. Although Moses wrote them down, they were God's laws for his people/the Jews/the Israelites to follow. That is why Luke referred to the same laws both as "the Law of Moses" (22) and as "the Law of the Lord" (23, 24).
Questions.Note: See "law" in KBT.
The Jews collected what Moses wrote, and those writings now are the first five books of the Old Testament.

Questions.Q: What kind of sacrifice did Mary bring?
Questions.A: She brought two doves or two young pigeons. (24)

Questions.Q: What happened to those two birds when they were sacrificed?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The priest killed them in a way that God had told them to use for such animals. Then they were given to God by burning them up (see Lev. 3, 6:24-30, and 12:6-8).
Questions.Note: See "sacrifice" in KBT.

Section.heading: Luke 2:25-35 Simeon saw the baby Jesus and prophesied.

Questions.Q: Tell me about Simeon going to the temple.
Questions.A: (The answer should include the basic facts and activities of the event. Those items not mentioned can be checked on in the detail questions below.)

Questions.Q: What do you think that we are to learn from what Luke wrote about Simeon being at the temple?
Questions.A: Simeon was one of the Israelites who was waiting for the savior (Messiah) whom God had promised to send to them. The Holy Spirit showed Simeon that the baby, Jesus, was that savior (25, 26, 30).
-OR-
We can learn that Jesus is the savior of all the other ethnic groups of the world, as well (31-32).

Questions.Q: Tell me some of the things you heard/read about Simeon in this section.
Questions.A: He lived in Jerusalem.
He loved and honored God and did what was right in God's sight.
The Holy Spirit was in him. (25)
[He probably was quite old. (26)]
Questions.Alternative: Tell me some of the things you heard about Simeon in this section.
Tell me some of the things you read about Simeon in this section.

Questions.Q: Who was Simeon waiting to see before he died?
Questions.A: He was waiting to see the one who would console/encourage/help Israel in the midst of/out of its troubles, that is the Christ/Messiah/savior whom God would send. (25-26)

Questions.Q: How did Simeon know he would not die before he saw the Christ/(the Messiah)?
Questions.A: The Holy Spirit had revealed that to him. (26)
Questions.Alternative: How did Simeon know he would not die before he saw the Christ?
How did Simeon know he would not die before he saw the Messiah?

Questions.Q: Why did Simeon go to the temple grounds that particular day?
Questions.A: The Holy Spirit caused him to go there. (27)

Questions.Q: What did Simeon see there?
Questions.A: He saw the parents (Joseph and Mary) bring their baby, Jesus, into the temple grounds [to do what the Law of Moses said that they must do]. (27)

Questions.Q: When Simeon saw the family, what did he do?
Questions.A: He received/held the baby Jesus in his arms and blessed/praised God [for sending him]. (28)

Questions.Q: Simeon had not died before seeing the savior, just as God had revealed to him. What did Simeon say about how he felt now?
Questions.A: His was ready to die, because he had peace in his heart./God could allow him to die because he had peace in his heart. (29)

Questions.Q: What did Simeon say caused him to have a peaceful heart?
Questions.A: He had seen the one through whom God would save his people, Israel, and all [other] ethnic groups./He had seen the one whom God had sent to save people from all ethnic groups. (30-32)

Questions.Q: In what way, do you think, is Jesus like a light for the Israelites/Jews and for all the people who are not Jews?
Questions.A: In the same way that light allows us to see what is in a dark place, when a person learns about Jesus's work as his savior, that person knows clearly what must happen in order for him to be saved from his sins.
The people of Israel already knew much about God, but now they would understand even more about him.

The people who were/are not Jews would really see the contrast between the way they lived before they knew about God and the life the savior made possible for them. It would be as if Jesus had turned on a light for them to see better.
Key Term Check: See "the nations" in KBT in the "Gentiles, pagans" entry.
Questions.Alternative: In what way, do you think, is Jesus like a light for the Israelites and for all the people who are not Jews?
In what way, do you think, is Jesus like a light for the Jews and for all the people who are not Jews?

Questions.Q: What did Mary and Joseph think about what Simeon said about the baby?
Questions.A: They were amazed that he knew so much about the work Jesus would do. (33)
-OR-
They were amazed that God had revealed some of the same things to Simeon about their baby that the angel had told them. (33)
Questions.Note: They did not know any normal reason why Simeon should know these things without God showing them to him. It seemed very strange to them.

Questions.Q: What did Simeon do then?
Questions.A: He asked God to bless them and then spoke to Mary. (34)
Questions.Note: The Greek text literally says "Simeon blessed them", but that means that he asked God to bless them. There are many other blessings which people spoke in the Bible which make this custom of giving a blessing clear to us.

Questions.Q: What, do you think, is the meaning of this picture language about many Israelite people falling and others rising because of Jesus?
Questions.A: Those Israelites who do not accept Jesus as their savior sent by God will fall away. That means that they will be separated from God and be a part of those people whose bad actions will lead to God destroying them (for all time to come).

Those others who do accept Jesus as their savior will rise above the sin of this world. That means that they will be separated from the bad things in this world and will be joined with God (for all time to come). (34)

Questions.Q: What kind of a sign do you think that Jesus was to be?
Questions.A: People would see and realize that God's promises about sending a savior were being fulfilled in what Jesus said and did. (34)
He is the one through whom God shows the way for a person to be saved.
In Jesus, people would see God beginning to rule and reign in people's lives and they would also see how they were to live.
Questions.Note: Any of these answers is good.

Questions.Q: How would people respond to seeing this sign of Jesus in the world?
Questions.A: Many (people) would say bad things about Jesus (and things he would teach). (34)

Questions.Q: What will happen to the many people who say or think bad things about this sign from God?
Questions.A: Their real thoughts would be clearly seen and would show that they were rejecting God and his plan to save them. (35a)

Questions.Q: How will the action of people rejecting Jesus's life and work affect his mother, Mary?
Questions.A: She would feel great sorrow/anguish in her heart like the pain she would feel if someone pierced it with a sword. (35b)

Section.heading: Luke 2:36-38 Anna spoke about the baby Jesus.

Questions.Q: What happened while Simeon was holding the baby Jesus and speaking to his parents?
Questions.A: [The woman/widow] Anna came up to them and thanked God for [sending] the child [to be the savior/Messiah].
She also told about this child to people who were waiting for God to set free the people [of Israel, represented here by those] living in Jerusalem. (38)

Questions.Q: What do you think that we are to learn from what Luke wrote about Anna being at the temple?
Questions.A: God's Spirit showed her also (36a) that the baby Jesus was the one God had sent to set free the people [of Israel]. (38).
-OR-
It was not just the man Simeon who realized that baby Jesus was the savior [that God had promised to send].
-OR-
Anna was another person who spread the good news that Jesus was the savior, starting already when he was only a few weeks old. (38)

Questions.Q: Tell me some of the things you heard/read about Anna in this section.
Questions.A: She was a prophetess.
Her father was Phanuel and they had descended from Asher [one of Jacob's/Israel's sons].
She had married and then lived with her husband for 7 years [until he died]. (36)
After that, she was a widow and was now 84 years old.
She served/worshiped God by means of fasting and praying at the temple grounds from morning until night/all day long. (37)
(She, too, seems to have been waiting for God to send the one who would free his people.) (38)
Questions.Alternative: Tell me some of the things you heard about Anna in this section.
Tell me some of the things you read about Anna in this section.

Questions.Q: What do you think that Anna did when she fasted?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: She chose to not eat food for certain periods of time so that she could focus her thoughts better on God and not on her bodily needs. She especially used that time to pray and show that she was sorry for her sins.

Section.heading: Luke 2:39-40 The family returned to Nazareth.

Questions.Q: What do you think that we are to learn from what Luke wrote about the family returning to Nazareth?
Questions.A: Luke told Theophilus at the beginning of this book (1:1-4) that he wanted to present a true account of Jesus's life. Since Mary and Joseph had come to Bethlehem for having their names recorded, it would be natural for them to return home to Nazareth.
-OR-

Jesus did not grow up in his forefather King David's village of Bethlehem, nor in Jerusalem, where the temple of God was. He appeared to be an ordinary child in an ordinary family in an ordinary village.
Questions.Note: People would have to accept him based on the way he lived and what he taught, not on his social status, which would be based on who his ancestors were or on his religious education.

Questions.Q: When were Joseph and Mary ready to return to their home in Nazareth?
Questions.A: They were ready when they had finished doing everything that the Law of the Lord commanded them to do [after having a baby boy]. (39)

Questions.Q: What was happening to Jesus while the family lived in Nazareth?
Questions.A: He grew bigger and stronger and very wise. God also showed special kindness to him. (40)
Key Term Check: See "grace" in KBT.

Section.heading: Luke 2:41-52 The boy Jesus went with his parents to the temple in Jerusalem.

Questions.Q: What do you think that we are to learn from what Luke wrote about the boy Jesus going to the temple in Jerusalem?
Questions.A: Luke wanted the reader to know that Jesus was very wise, even at that early age. He knew the work God had given him [to be the savior]. (49)
Everyone who heard Jesus speak realized that he was very wise and that he wanted to please God. (47, 52)

Questions.Q: What was the reason that Jesus's parents went again to Jerusalem?
Questions.A: It was their custom to go there every year to celebrate the Feast of the Passover. (41-42)
Questions.Note: Every Jew was to go to the temple in Jerusalem once a year. Many people chose to go at the time for this feast.

Questions.Q: What do you know about this Jewish feast?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: This feast was to remember how God's angel passed over the homes of the Jews when they were slaves in Egypt. The angel passed over them because they had put the blood of a perfect lamb on their doorposts as a sign. The Egyptians did not do as God had said, so the angel killed the oldest son and the firstborn animal young in every such house. Because of that, the Egyptian ruler allowed the Jews to leave Egypt and return to the land God had promised to them. (See "The Passover sacrifice" in KBT in the "sacrifice, offering, blood" entry.)

Questions.Q: How old was Jesus when he went with his parents?
Questions.A: 12 years old. (42)
Questions.Note: A footnote may be good here to indicate that this was the age at which Jewish boys and girls began to be considered/called adult men and women. As adults they had to do all the religious activities that God told the Jews to do, such as to worship in Jerusalem during the Feast of the Passover.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus and his parents do when the Feast days were finished?
Questions.A: While his parents started to return home to Nazareth, Jesus stayed in Jerusalem. (43-44)

Questions.Q: Why were Mary and Joseph not worried about Jesus staying by himself in the big city?
Questions.A: They did not know that Jesus had stayed there. (43) They thought that he was with other people in the [large] group who were traveling together [towards Nazareth]. (44)

Questions.Q: How much time passed before they really started to look for him?
Questions.A: They traveled one whole day and then started to look for him. (44)

Questions.Q: Where did his parents look for him?
Questions.A: They looked for him among their relatives and friends [who also were traveling that direction]. (44)

Questions.Q: What did they do when they did not find Jesus among those people?
Questions.A: They returned to Jerusalem to look for him there. (45)

Questions.Q: On which day of their searching did his parents find him?
Questions.A: On the third day. (46)

Questions.Q: Where was Jesus when they found him?
Questions.A: He was in the temple grounds sitting among the teachers [of the Jewish Law]. (46)

Questions.Q: What was he doing there?
Questions.A: He was listening to them and asking them questions. (46)

Questions.Q: What was the reason that everyone there was so astounded?
Questions.A: They were astounded at his good understanding and wise answers, [because he was only twelve years old]. (47)

Questions.Q: What did his parents think of all this?
Questions.A: They were greatly astounded. (48)

Questions.Q: What did his mother say to him about all this?
Questions.A: "Son, why have you done this to us? Your father and I have been very worried as we have been searching for you!" (48)
Questions.Note: When you translate the words "your father" to refer to Joseph, follow the custom of the people who will use this translation. Use the words normally used by a mother when she speaks to her children about her husband. Because Joseph was not the true physical father of Jesus, some languages may require a translator to use a word similar to "stepfather".

Questions.Q: Do the words of her question show that she was upset and frustrated, or do they show that she wanted Jesus to answer her question?
Questions.A: (Note: Her words should show that she was upset and frustrated. They should show or imply disapproval and finding fault with him.)

Questions.Q: Jesus had not been with his parents for three days. What do you think was the reason that he asked his mother, "Why did you have to look for me?"
Questions.A: If they had thought about the reason that God had sent him into the world to do his (God's) work, they would have known that he would be in God's house, the temple. (49)

Questions.Q: Did his answer help them understand the reason that he had stayed there in Jerusalem?
Questions.A: No, it did not. (50)

Questions.Q: Now that Mary and Joseph were there with him, what did Jesus do?
Questions.A: He went home with them to Nazareth and obeyed them. (51)

Questions.Q: How did Mary respond to all that had happened regarding her son?
Questions.A: She kept thinking about all these things and wondering very much about their meaning. (51)

Questions.Q: What did Luke tell us about Jesus growing to be a man?
Questions.A: He matured physically and mentally./He grew taller and wiser. (52a)
He pleased both God and the people around him more and more by the way he lived. (52b)

Section.heading: Luke 3:1-6 John the Baptizer prepared the way for Jesus.

Questions.Q: What do you think that we are to learn from what Luke wrote about John the Baptizer's work?
Questions.A: Luke wanted to show us that John began the work of getting people's hearts ready to hear and obey Jesus's message, just as the angel (1:16-17) and the Holy Spirit (1:76-79) had told Zechariah that John would do.

Questions.Q: What kind of work did the men Tiberius (Caesar), Pontius Pilate, his brother Philip and Lysanias all do?
Questions.A: They were all high government officials [in areas where the Romans had authority]. (1)
Questions.Note: Tiberius was the highest Roman official and lived in Rome. The other men were officials under him in the regions around Jerusalem.

Questions.Q: What kind of work did the men Annas and Caiaphas do?
Questions.A: They were high priests [in Jerusalem]. (2)

Questions.Q: What happened to John during the time when all those men were the leaders of the people?
Questions.A: God told John to start his work. (2)

Questions.Q: Where was John living when God told him to start his special work?
Questions.A: He was living in an uninhabited area/the wilderness/desert. (2)

Questions.Q: What did John do in all the area around the Jordan River?
Questions.Note: He preached that people were to repent and then be baptized. (3)
The key terms "preach" and "repent" are discussed here, but "baptize" will be checked below in vs. 7.

Questions.Q: If a person preaches in your/a village, what does he do?
Questions.A: (Accept any answer. Probable answers:
He teaches more of the parts of the Bible to the people who believe the talk about Jesus.
-OR-
He harangues the believers to behave better than they have been doing.)
Questions.Note: Neither of these two actions is what the Bible called preaching. When one of the above answers is given, if at all possible, the translator should use other words appropriate to the action found in the verse in the GNT and not automatically use the church word for "preach".
Questions.Alternative: If a person preaches in your village, what does he do?
If a person preaches in a village, what does he do?

Questions.Q: What do you think that John actually did in those places when he "preached"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: John spoke out with authority to tell some news (that God had sent the savior he had promised to them). In this verse, he also was telling the people how they could respond appropriately to that news.
Questions.Note: In the GNT, preaching was always done to people who had not yet heard the message. In English translations, three different Greek words are all translated "preach". In this verse the Greek word focuses on the aspect of telling with authority.

Questions.Q: What does a person do when he repents?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He deliberately stops doing the sinful ways that please himself and changes to doing those ways which please God and are right in God's sight.
Questions.Note: See "repent" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Why did people repent?
Questions.A: They wanted God to forgive/remove their sins. (3)

Questions.Q: What had the prophet Isaiah written about this many years before John and Luke were born?
Questions.A: He had written that someone would preach in the wilderness that people were to get ready to accept the one whom God would send to save them. (4-6)

Questions.Q: How were those people to get ready for this?
Questions.A: They were to correct/change their lives from living in bad ways to living in ways that pleased God. (They were to do whatever was necessary to get rid of their bad ways, like men straighten and level bad places in a path/road.) (4-5)

Questions.Q: Why did Luke quote these words which the prophet Isaiah had written?
Questions.A: He wanted to show the readers that John was doing what Isaiah said that someone would do before the savior arrived. (2b-4)

Section.heading: Luke 3:7-20 John the Baptizer preached his message to the people.

Questions.Q: What did Luke write about in these verses?
Questions.A: He wrote about what John said to different groups of people, especially to those who came to him in order for him to baptize them.

Questions.Q: How many people came to where John was staying in that uninhabited area/wilderness/desert?
Questions.A: Crowds of people. (7)
Questions.Alternative: How many people came to where John was staying in that uninhabited area?
How many people came to where John was staying in that wilderness?
How many people came to where John was staying in that desert?

Questions.Q: Why did so many people go to see John?
Questions.A: They wanted John to baptize them. (7)

Questions.Q: What do you think that John did with the people when he baptized them?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He did something so that water washed over the people either by putting them down under the water or by putting water over the top of them, probably the first way (Mark 1:9-10).
Questions.Note: See "baptize, baptism" in KBT.

Questions.Q: With what did John compare these people?
Questions.A: He said they were [like] a group of poisonous snakes. (7)

Questions.Q: What does it mean in your language if one person calls another person a (poisonous) snake?
Questions.Note: The translation should reflect an insulting put-down by John. Some bad characteristic of poisonous snakes should be implied, such as their being sly, deceiving, or deadly. It should not be anything that is regarded as speaking well of a person.

Questions.Q: What were those people doing which reminded John of snakes?
Questions.A: [By coming to be baptized, they thought that they were tricking John/God. They wanted him to think that they had already repented of their sins, but they had not repented.] They hoped that in this way they could escape God being angry about their sins and ready to punish them as they deserved. (7)

Questions.Q: John called the people a bunch of young snakes who had descended from other snakes. Who do you think those people were, who showed/taught them to act like they were doing?
Questions.A: They were their parents, -OR-
the leaders of the Jews, -OR-
even the devil, who is the chief evil spirit. (7)
Questions.Note: In other places in the Bible, the devil used the form of a snake to deceive people (see Gen. 3 and 2 Cor. 11:3). Jesus later said that the devil was their father, and called him the Father of Lies (see John 8:44).
Questions.Alternative: John called the people a bunch of young snakes who had descended from other snakes. Who do you think those people were, who showed them to act like they were doing?
John called the people a bunch of young snakes who had descended from other snakes. Who do you think those people were, who taught them to act like they were doing?

Questions.Q: If those people did not want God to punish them for their sins, John told them one thing they must do and one thing they must not do. What were those two things?
Questions.A: He said that their actions must show that they really had repented/changed. (8a)
Also, they must not think that, because they were descendants of Abraham, God would not punish them for their sins. (8b)

Questions.Q: Why did John say that they must not trust in their being descendants of Abraham to keep God from punishing them?
Questions.A: He said that, if God only wanted a large number of descendants from Abraham, he could change ordinary stones into more descendants. [That meant that God did not need those particular people for any reason.] (8)

Questions.Q: In verse 9 John used the picture language of a tree and its fruit, an ax at the tree's roots and a fire. What do you think these things represent?
Questions.A: The tree represents a person.
The tree's good fruit represents activities the person does which please God.

People use an ax to cut down fruit trees which do not produce good fruit. John said the ax was already close to the tree roots. When roots are cut, the tree's life is totally ended. Likewise, God is ready to punish/destroy a person because he/she is bad. That will be the end of that person's life.
The fire represents how that unproductive tree will be destroyed, which suggests the fire of hell for such a person.

Questions.Q: Which type of people did John picture as being ready to burn in hell?
Questions.A: They were the people who had not repented,
and/or they were trusting in their ancestry (who their ancestors were) to save them. (See 3:8.)

Questions.Q: What did John tell the people they should do to show that they had truly repented?
Questions.A: They should be ready to share their clothing and food with those who have [little or] none. (11)

Questions.Q: What did John tell the men who collected taxes that they should do to show that they had truly repented?
Questions.A: They should not collect more money from people than the true amount of tax the people owed [to the Roman government]. (13)

Questions.Q: What did John tell the soldiers they should do?
Questions.A: They should be satisfied with their pay. That is, they should not physically force anyone to give them money. (14)
They also should not say that if the person would not give them money, they would falsely accuse that person in court [so that person would get into trouble or be put in the jail]. (14)

Questions.Q: What do you think that the Jewish people were waiting for and thinking might be happening?
Questions.A: They were waiting for the Christ/Messiah to come and set them free from their troubles. (15)

Questions.Q: What were all the people thinking about John in this regard?
Questions.A: They were seriously wondering if John himself was the Christ. (15)

Questions.Q: How did John answer them concerning whether or not he was the Christ/Messiah?
Questions.A: He himself was not the Christ/Messiah. The Christ/Messiah would have much greater power and authority than he himself had. (16-17)
Questions.Alternative: How did John answer them concerning whether or not he was the Christ?
How did John answer them concerning whether or not he was the Messiah?

Questions.Q: How did John show that the Christ would do greater work than he himself was doing?
Questions.A: The Christ would baptize people with the Holy Spirit and fire, not just with water as John did.
John did not feel he even was important enough to be the servant who might assist Christ by untying his sandals. (16)
John pictured the Christ as having authority to save and to punish people. (He himself did not have such authority.) (17)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means that Christ will baptize people with the Holy Spirit and with fire?
Questions.A: Those whom Christ causes to repent will receive his Holy Spirit into their hearts,
but Christ will throw those who do not repent into the fires of hell to destroy them. (17)
-OR-

The Christ would cause people who repent to come under the influence of God's Holy Spirit. The Spirit would get rid of all that was not good in their lives just as a fire does with grass and sticks. (17)
-OR-

Baptism with water is only an outward, ritual cleaning to show what we want to happen in our inner being. The Christ will truly clean/cleanse one's inner being by means of his Holy Spirit and remove impurities as fire does. (16-17)

Questions.Q: What is the work of the winnowing fork in the picture language John used?
Questions.A: People use it to separate all the rubbish from the good grain. (17)

Questions.Q: What, do you think, are the good things and the bad things that the Christ will be separating?
Questions.A: Christ will separate the good people from the bad people. Those people who repent and believe in him are good. Christ will separate them from those people who do not repent.

Questions.Q: What do you think will happen to those people whom he calls good?
Questions.A: He will gather them [into heaven] where he wants to keep them, as a farmer gathers the wheat and stores it in a safe place. (17)

Questions.Q: What do you think will happen to those people whom he calls bad?
Questions.A: They will be burned up/destroyed in the never-ending fires [of hell], as a farmer burns the rubbish parts of the wheat and grass. (17)

Questions.Q: In verse 18 Luke wrote that John kept on urging/strongly requesting [the people to repent of their sins] and that he preached the Good News to them. If people will be punished in the fires of hell, that does not sound like good news. What was the good news that John preached?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The Good News was that the Christ, the one whom God had promised would come to save his people, was already among them. If they repented and prepared their hearts to accept the savior, God would not throw them into the fires of hell.

Key Term Check: The words "preached the Good News" in English translations are actually only one word in Greek. The word literally means, "he Good News-ed". The focus is on what he preached, not how he did it. See the discussion above at 3:3.
Questions.Note: See "gospel" in KBT.

If the language of the translation allows for it, try to use the terminology you have here for "good news" back in 1:19 and 2:10 also. Those two references are a bit more general, but they do still apply to the Good News of the savior having come.
Questions.Alternative: In verse 18 Luke wrote that John kept on urging the people to repent of their sins and that he preached the Good News to them. If people will be punished in the fires of hell, that does not sound like good news. What was the good news that John preached?

In verse 18 Luke wrote that John kept on strongly requesting the people to repent of their sins and that he preached the Good News to them. If people will be punished in the fires of hell, that does not sound like good news. What was the good news that John preached?

In verse 18 Luke wrote that John kept on urging and that he preached the Good News to them. If people will be punished in the fires of hell, that does not sound like good news. What was the good news that John preached?

In verse 18 Luke wrote that John kept on strongly requesting and that he preached the Good News to them. If people will be punished in the fires of hell, that does not sound like good news. What was the good news that John preached?

Questions.Q: Why did John rebuke Herod, the king?
Questions.A: Herod had married his brother's wife, Herodias, as well as having done other bad actions. (19)

Questions.Q: What other bad action did Herod do then?
Questions.A: He [sent men and had them] put John into prison. (20)

Questions.Q: What do you think that we are to learn from what Luke wrote about Jesus being baptized?
Questions.A: The special things which happened at that time show us that Jesus was/is God's son.

Questions.Q: Who do you think baptized Jesus?
Questions.A: John the Baptizer did (Matt. 3:13-15; Mark 1:9).

Questions.Q: Did John baptize Jesus before he was in the prison, or after being there?
Questions.A: John did it before he was in the prison.
Questions.Note: John died while he was in the prison (see Mark 6:14-29). Try to show in either verse 20 or 21 that the activities in 3:21-22 happened before the activities in vs. 20.

You may want to put verses 19-20 into a "verse bridge" along with verses 21-22. Number these verses together as 19-22, and mention Jesus's baptism (from 21-22) first, followed by Herod putting John in prison (19-20).

Questions.Q: What happened while John baptized Jesus and then Jesus was praying?
Questions.A: [God] opened heaven/the sky (21) and the Holy Spirit came down upon him in a bodily form like a dove. Also, God spoke [to Jesus] from heaven. (22)

Questions.Q: Do Luke's words sound as though this was a vision Jesus saw, or do the words sound as though this really happened?
Questions.A: The words, "in a bodily form," show that it really happened. (22) (See John 1:32-34.)

Section.heading: Luke 3:23-38 These were the ancestors of Jesus.

Questions.Q: What do you think that we are to learn from what Luke wrote about Jesus's ancestors?
Questions.A: He showed the Jews (and us) that Jesus was the Messiah that the prophets had said would come, because he had the same ancestors, such as David and Abraham, as the prophets had said the Messiah would have.
He showed us that Jesus was a true human being like us.

Questions.Q: Does this listing sound like the way other people who speak your language would tell you about their own list of ancestors?
Questions.Note: It should. This listing should follow the traditional way of listing one's ancestors.

Questions.Q: How old was Jesus when he began his work of preaching the Good News?
Questions.A: He was about 30 years old. (23)

Questions.Q: Whom did people think was the father of Jesus?
Questions.A: Joseph. (23)

Questions.Q: Whom did Luke name as the true/original ancestor of Jesus?
Questions.Alternative: Whom did Luke name as the true ancestor of Jesus?
Whom did Luke name as the original ancestor of Jesus?

Questions.Q: Which names in the list do you remember from other parts of the Bible?
Questions.A: Believers most likely will know Old Testament events about:
Jacob and his father Isaac (34)
Isaac and his father Abraham (34)
Shem and his father Noah (36)
Seth and his father Adam [might even mention that God had created Adam] (38)
(King) David and his father Jesse (31-32)
Questions.Note: The respondent (especially if an unbeliever or new Christian) may not remember any of the names.
The point is to check whether the respondent understands these names to be names of real people or assumes them to be mythological characters or spirit beings.

Section.heading: Luke 4:1-13 The devil tried to make Jesus disobey God.

Questions.Q: Luke wrote about the time when the devil came to Jesus. What do you think that we are to learn from that?
Questions.A: The devil tried to make Jesus disobey God, but Jesus would not disobey.
If Jesus had obeyed the devil, he would have been as sinful as we are. Then he could not have been the one to save all of us who sin.
-OR-
Jesus had human feelings just as we do. When he had not eaten for forty days, he was very hungry. The devil tried to make Jesus obey him instead of obeying God, but Jesus did not obey the devil.

Questions.Q: Why did Jesus go into an uninhabited area/into the wilderness/desert?
Questions.A: The Holy Spirit caused him to go there. (1)
Questions.Alternative: Why did Jesus go into an uninhabited area?
Why did Jesus go into the wilderness?
Why did Jesus go into the desert?

Questions.Q: Who is the devil whom Luke wrote about here?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He is the chief of the evil spirits, the enemy of God and God's people.
Questions.Note: See "Satan" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did the devil try to do with Jesus there?
Questions.A: He tempted Jesus [to sin]./He tried to make Jesus obey him and disobey God. (2)

Questions.Q: What does it mean to tempt another person?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that one person tries to make the other obey him to do something which disobeys higher authorities, such as parents, the government, or God. (2)

Questions.Q: Why was Jesus hungry?
Questions.A: He had not eaten during the forty days he had been staying there. (2)

Questions.Q: How did the devil try to use this hunger of Jesus to make Jesus obey him?
Questions.A: He told Jesus to prove that he was the son of God by changing a stone into food. (3)

Questions.Q: How did Jesus respond to him?
Questions.A: He spoke words which were written [by Moses in the book of God's Words].
He said that eating food is not the only or most important thing in life. (4)
[He did not obey the devil.]

Questions.Q: What did the devil show to Jesus from a high place?
Questions.A: He showed him all the nations of the world at one time. (5)

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that the devil took Jesus to a high place?
Questions.A: He wanted to show Jesus how much authority/power he had over the whole world.
He hoped to entice Jesus to follow him.

Questions.Q: How did the devil tempt Jesus when they looked at all those kingdoms/nations all over the world?
Questions.A: He said that if Jesus would worship him, he would give Jesus all authority [to rule] over the kingdoms/nations/people.
He would also give Jesus all the glory/honor that a person would receive because he had that authority. (5-7)
Questions.Alternative: How did the devil tempt Jesus when they looked at all those kingdoms all over the world?
How did the devil tempt Jesus when they looked at all those nations all over the world?

Questions.Q: What do you think that a person does when he worships another person?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He shows great honor and deep respect for the other person. He acts as though that person has more authority or strength or wisdom or goodness or beauty than any other human, and so is like God. (See L&N entry 53.14 and those at 53.53-64.)

Questions.Q: Who do you think gave the devil the authority over the kingdoms/nations/people?
Questions.A: God did before the devil disobeyed God and God made him leave heaven.
-OR-
God had given that authority to the first people, Adam and his wife, Eve. But they obeyed the devil, rather than what God had told them to do. In that way they gave that authority to the devil.
-OR-
No one had given that authority to the devil. He lied about it to Jesus.
Questions.Alternative: Who do you think gave the devil the authority over the kingdoms?
Who do you think gave the devil the authority over the nations?
Who do you think gave the devil the authority over the people?

Questions.Q: How did Jesus respond to the devil this time?
Questions.A: He spoke words which were written [by Moses in the book of God's Words].
He said that everyone is to worship and serve only the Lord [who is] God. (8)
[He did not obey the devil.]

Questions.Q: How did the devil tempt Jesus the third time?
Questions.A: He said that Jesus should prove that he was the son of God by jumping off the highest point of the temple and falling to the ground. (He even partially quoted Psalm 91:11-12 to back up his dare.) (9)

Questions.Q: How would this prove that Jesus was God's son?
Questions.A: Because God would tell his angels to watch over him, he would not hurt himself. (9)

Questions.Q: How did Jesus respond to him this time?
Questions.A: He spoke words which were written [by Moses in the book of God's Words].
He said that no one is to tempt/test God. (12)
[He did not obey the devil.]

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to test God?
Questions.A: A person tries to cause God to do what that person wants to happen. The person wants God to feel as though he (God) must do this action in order to show that he is more powerful than the problem the person created.

Questions.Q: Jesus's answers stopped the devil from tempting him more. Where did Jesus always get his answers?
Questions.A: The answers were all in God's Word [which men had written down long ago]. (4, 8, 12)
Questions.Alternative: What was the source of the answers Jesus used to stop the devil from tempting him more?
What was the source of the answers Jesus used to stop the devil from continuing to tempt him?
What was the source of the answers Jesus used to answer the devil and stop his temptations?
What was the source of the answers Jesus used to answer the devil?
What was the source of the answers Jesus used to defeat the devil's temptations?

Questions.Q: What did the devil do after Jesus would not obey him those three times?
Questions.A: He left Jesus and waited for another time to try again later. (13)
Questions.Alternative: What did the devil do after Jesus would not succumb to his three attempts to make Jesus sin?
What did the devil do after he failed to get Jesus to sin those three times?
What did the devil do when Jesus would not give in to his repeated temptations?
What did the devil do when he saw that he was unsuccessful in getting Jesus to sin?
What did the devil do when he saw that he was unsuccessful in his three attempts to cause Jesus to sin?

Section.heading: Luke 4:14-30 The people of Nazareth rejected Jesus.

Questions.Q: What can we learn from what Luke wrote about the ways that people responded to Jesus's preaching?
Questions.A: People who lived all over Galilee [province] heard about him (14) and praised him (15). From the words of Isaiah (21), the people could see that Jesus was that person whom God had promised to send [as the savior]. However, the people of his hometown would not accept him as sent by God (24). This was because they thought of him as being only a local man whom they had seen grow up (22).

Questions.Q: Back in verse 1 when Jesus went into the wilderness/desert, he was led by the Holy Spirit and had all the power of the Holy Spirit. What did Luke write about this at the time Jesus left that uninhabited area?
Questions.A: He returned to Galilee [province] completely guided by the Holy Spirit's power (just as when he went into the desert). (14)
Questions.Alternative: Back in verse 1 when Jesus went into the wilderness, he was led by the Holy Spirit and had all the power of the Holy Spirit. What did Luke write about this at the time Jesus left that uninhabited area?
Back in verse 1 when Jesus went into the desert, he was led by the Holy Spirit and had all the power of the Holy Spirit. What did Luke write about this at the time Jesus left that uninhabited area?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do there in Galilee [province]?
Questions.A: He taught in the people's synagogues around the area. (15)
Questions.Note: There is a strong implication that Jesus also had been doing miracles, such as healing people. That is implied from the words "power of the Spirit" and "news about him spread", as well as Jesus later stating that the prophecy of Isaiah was fulfilled in the work he was doing.
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus do there in Galilee province?
What did Jesus do there in Galilee?

Questions.Q: What do you think a synagogue was?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A synagogue was a building which the Jews built in order to gather for hearing someone read and teach from the Word of God and where they could worship him. Many Jews lived too far away from the temple in Jerusalem to walk there regularly for worship, so they built a synagogue in each village for that purpose.
Questions.Note: See "synagogue" in KBT.

Questions.Q: How did the people around Galilee [province] respond to Jesus?
Questions.A: The news about him spread all around (14).
All those who heard him teach praised him (15).
Questions.Alternative: How did the people around Galilee province respond to Jesus?
How did the people around Galilee respond to Jesus?

Questions.Q: Why did Jesus go into the synagogue in Nazareth?
Questions.A: That was the village where [Mary and Joseph] had raised him.
He customarily went there every Sabbath Day [to worship God]. (16)

Questions.Q: What do you think makes a particular day be the Sabbath Day?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It is the seventh day of the week, Saturday, the day on which God rested from his work of creating the world. He told people to honor him on that day by resting from their work/by not working. The Jews used that day to meet together to worship God.
Questions.Note: See "Sabbath" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Why did Jesus stand up in the synagogue?
Questions.A: It was the customary way for a person to show that he wanted to read [God's Word]. (16)

Questions.Q: Take a piece of paper and show me what Jesus did in order to get ready to read.
Questions.A: (The person who is answering these questions may have to roll up the piece of paper first before unrolling it and holding it at a proper distance for reading from it. Jewish Scripture writings happen to be rolled side-to-side, not top-to-bottom, but that is not the key part of the action you want to see happen.)
Questions.Note: A footnote or glossary entry may be needed to indicate that long ago people wrote on long pieces of paper or thin animal skin which they kept safe by rolling each one around a wooden rod. In order to read the words, the paper or skin had to be unrolled to find the place where one was to begin reading.

Questions.Q: Which part of God's Word did Jesus open?
Questions.A: He opened/unrolled the part that the prophet Isaiah had written. (17)

Questions.Q: After Jesus had opened the scroll/book/papers, what did he do?
Questions.A: He read part of what Isaiah had written there.
Questions.Alternative: After Jesus had opened the scroll, what did he do?
After Jesus had opened the book, what did he do?
After Jesus had opened the papers, what did he do?

Questions.Q: To whom, do you think, was Isaiah referring when he wrote "me" in these two verses?
Questions.A: Isaiah was not speaking about himself. He was referring to a special Servant of the Lord whom God would send to the Jews. That special person would say these words to the Jews. The Jews already understood that servant would be the Messiah whom God had promised to send to them. We know from verse 21 that this special person was Jesus himself, but Isaiah did not know Jesus's name when he wrote these words.
Questions.Note: The translator may need make this explicit at the end of verse 17 in the introduction to the quote, such as, "... where it is written about the special Servant of the Lord, ..."

Questions.Q: What did Isaiah say this special person would do?
Questions.A: He was to tell/preach the Good News [that God's plan to save them was taking place right then] to the poor people. (18b)
He was to proclaim [with authority]/preach to the people whose lives were as if they had been captured [by the devil and their own sins] that they could be free [of those things]. (18c)
He was to proclaim [with authority]/preach to the blind people that they could see again. (18c)
He was to free those who had been treated unfairly. (18d)
He was to proclaim [with authority]/preach that the time when the Lord would show kindness to his people [had come]. (19)
Questions.Note: Has the reference to the Good News been translated in the same way here (4:18b) as it was in 3:18? It should be clearly referring to the same thing both there and here.

Questions.Q: How would that special person know he was supposed to do that work?
Questions.A: God's Spirit had or would anoint him by coming on/to him in a special way (18a).

Questions.Q: What does it mean to anoint someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Someone having great authority appoints another person to do a special kind of work on his behalf. That person with authority usually shows this by pouring or rubbing an oil or ointment onto the other person's head. In the Bible times people most often used olive oil to appoint and dedicate a new prophet, priest or king. The focus here is on the appointing function, not on the pouring on of oil.
Questions.Note: See "anoint" in KBT.

Questions.Q: How would that person be able to do all those difficult things?
Questions.A: God's Spirit would make him able to do those things. (18)

Questions.Q: When Jesus had finished reading part of Isaiah's words written on the paper/scroll, what did he do with that scroll?
Questions.A: He rolled it up and gave it back to the man who looked after the writings. (20)
Questions.Alternative: When Jesus had finished reading part of Isaiah's words written on the paper, what did he do with that scroll?
When Jesus had finished reading part of Isaiah's words written on the scroll, what did he do with that scroll?

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that everyone there was watching him?
Questions.A: Because he sat down (as was the custom for a teacher to do), they now expected him to teach them about that text [or even to do some of those things he had read about]. (20)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about those words which he had read from the book by Isaiah?
Questions.A: They were now coming true as they heard him speak them [because he was the one about whom Isaiah had written, the one whom God had anointed/chosen to do these things]. (21)
Questions.Note: See "Scripture" in KBT.

Questions.Q: How did the people think of him at first?
Questions.A: They thought and spoke well of him and were amazed at his very good way of speaking/the wonderful things he said. (22)

Questions.Q: Why were they amazed by his speaking ability?
Questions.A: They knew him as [the carpenter] Joseph's son, [just a local boy with no special schooling]. (22) (They did not know any normal reason why he should know so much about God's Word.)

Questions.Q: What does this proverb, "Doctor, first make yourself well!", mean in regard to Jesus?
Questions.A: Since he had done miracles in Capernaum [and other places in the general area], he must do the same things right there in his hometown. This would show everyone that he really was the person about whom the prophet Isaiah had written.
-OR-

If a person who claimed to be a doctor was able to cure himself, then what he claimed would be true. In the same way, if Jesus could do miracles, then what he claimed [as being sent by God] would also be true. (23)

Questions.Q: What do you think that Jesus's response to them means?
Questions.A: A prophet is not accepted by the people in his hometown because they know him and think of him as the same kind of person as themselves. They think he is not able to teach them anything they do not already know about God.

Jesus knew that these people did not accept that he was a prophet. He also knew that they did not accept that he was the Christ. Therefore, they would not be able to accept or believe what he said or did right there in front of them.

Questions.Q: What caused the Jews to suffer long ago when Elijah lived in Israel?
Questions.A: There was no rain for 3 1/2 years. That caused a severe famine. (25)

Questions.Q: There were many widows in Israel at that time who had great trouble finding food. To whom did God send Elijah?
Questions.A: He sent Elijah to a widow who lived in the town of Zarephath. Zarephath was near the city of Sidon [outside the land of Israel]. (26)

Questions.Q: There were many people sick with leprosy/bad skin disease in Israel when Elisha lived. Whom did God bring to Elisha to be made well?
Questions.A: Naaman, a man from the country of Syria. (27)
Questions.Alternative: There were many people sick with leprosy in Israel when Elisha lived. Whom did God bring to Elisha to be made well?
There were many people sick with a bad skin disease in Israel when Elisha lived. Whom did God bring to Elisha to be made well?

Questions.Q: What do you think that Jesus was talking about when he said that Naaman was made "clean"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He was talking about Naaman having clear skin again after he was well.
He was also talking about the kind of cleanness God required before a person could be allowed into the public worship or allowed to live with his family again.
Questions.Note: See "clean" in KBT.
If a very general word like "clean" is being used in the translation, make sure it does not refer only to removing external things like dirt or general illness from the body.

This is the same Greek word which was used in 2:22 when Mary needed to become "clean" again following childbirth. However, the language of the translation may have separate names for each of these situations due to the male-female distinction or due to blood being involved in one case and not in the other. The words in the translation must be appropriate to each of these references.

Questions.Q: How do the two examples from the Old Testament scripture show that what Jesus was saying about prophets was true?
Questions.A: The people of Israel did not accept/believe two of their greatest prophets, Elijah and Elisha. Their own people did not accept them as men who spoke for God, so God used them to do his work among other people, some non-Jews who did believe them. (25-27)

Questions.Q: Thinking about these two examples, if the Nazareth people would not accept Jesus as the Christ, what do you think that he would do?
Questions.A: He would go to other places, [as Elijah and Elisha had done,] where the people would accept him as a prophet/the Christ.

Questions.Q: What was the people's response when they heard Jesus say those things in verses 23-27?
Questions.A: They were full of anger/furious. (28)

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that they were so angry about what Jesus had said?
Questions.A: They knew that he was implying that they were not believing, just as the Jews had done in the time when Elijah and Elisha were prophets.

They felt that he was rejecting them and would go to other places to teach God's word and do great things [by God's power] among people who would accept him. He might even go to people who were not Jews.

Questions.Q: What did those people do to Jesus?
Questions.A: They [angrily] removed him [from the synagogue and on] out of their town. They took/led him to an edge of the hill on which their town was built, intending to throw him over that edge/cliff [to kill him]. (29)
Questions.Note: The town was not on the top of the hill. It was on the side of a hill which has some steep edges at the top. People think that is where the townspeople took Jesus.

Questions.Q: Why were they not able to do what they intended to do?
Questions.A: Because Jesus walked through the middle of the crowd and went on his way, the people did not get to push him over the edge.(30)

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that he was able to do that?
Questions.A: God's Spirit and power helped him.

Section.heading: Luke 4:31-37 Jesus made an evil spirit leave a man.

Questions.Q: What did the people in the Capernaum synagogue think when they heard and saw what Jesus did there?
Questions.A: They were greatly astounded/astonished. (32, 36)
They talked about it among themselves (36) and with others (37).

Questions.Q: What happened that caused them to think like that?
Questions.A: Jesus spoke with so much authority and power that even demons/evil spirits obeyed what he told them to do. (They realized that God must be helping him do those things.) (32, 36)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do on the Sabbath Day when he was in the town of Capernaum?
Questions.A: He was teaching [God's Word to] the people in the synagogue. (31)

Questions.Q: Why did a man in the synagogue shout loudly at Jesus?
Questions.A: He had a demon, that is, an unclean/evil spirit, in him. (33)

Questions.Q: What do the people who speak your language say are the characteristics/signs to know a spirit is a demon/an evil spirit?
