Questions.A: Key Term Check: A demon is a spirit that only does evil things and tries to cause trouble for people, especially those who want to obey God's Word. The demon obeys Satan and opposes what God has said.
Questions.Note: Notice that Luke called the same spirit by both names in this verse.
See "evil spirit, unclean spirit, demon" and "unclean, defiled, impure, uncleanness" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: What do the people who speak your language say are the characteristics to know a spirit is a demon?
What do the people who speak your language say are the characteristics to know a spirit is an evil spirit?
What do the people who speak your language say are the signs to know a spirit is a demon?
What do the people who speak your language say are the signs to know a spirit is an evil spirit?

Questions.Q: What did the demon in this man know about Jesus?
Questions.A: He knew that Jesus was a man from the town of Nazareth. (34)
He knew that Jesus had power and authority to destroy/get rid of him [and other spirits who were in the man]. (34)
He knew that Jesus was the holy one who had come from God. (34)

Questions.Q: How did Jesus make the demon leave the man?
Questions.A: He sternly commanded/rebuked the spirit that it must stop what it was saying and doing, and now leave, and it did. (35)

Questions.Q: Why were the people so astonished?
Questions.A: Jesus not only taught with authority, but even evil spirits obeyed his commands. (36)

Questions.Q: Who heard about these things which Jesus had done there in Capernaum?
Questions.A: People who lived in all the areas around Capernaum heard about these things. (37)

Section.heading: Luke 4:38-44 The main work of Jesus was to preach the Good News, not to heal the sick people.

Questions.Q: Why did Luke write about Jesus leaving Capernaum to go to other cities?
Questions.A: Jesus said that the real reason he came down to earth was to preach the Good News that God wanted to rule and reign in each person's life. (43)

Questions.Q: What did the people at Simon's house ask Jesus to do?
Questions.A: Someone asked him to help [by healing] Simon's mother-in-law who was suffering with a high fever. (38)

Questions.Q: How did Jesus make her well?
Questions.A: Standing/Bending over her, he sternly commanded the sickness to leave her. (39)

Questions.Q: How do we know that she was well quickly?
Questions.A: She immediately got up and served [food to] the people there. (39)

Questions.Q: What happened later in that day as the sun was setting?
Questions.A: People brought everyone who was sick in some way to Jesus. [They wanted Jesus to heal the sick people.] (40)

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that the people waited until the sun was setting?
Questions.A: The Jewish laws did not permit people to travel or carry things on the Sabbath Day. A day ended when the sun set, and the new day began. Being a new day, people could then come and bring those who were sick.
Questions.Note: The translator may want to create a footnote or glossary entry to explain this.

Questions.Q: How did Jesus make them well again?
Questions.A: He laid his hands on each one of them and healed them. (40)

Questions.Q: What did the demons do when they came out of many people?
Questions.A: They cried out that Jesus was the son of God. (41a)

Questions.Q: What else did they know about Jesus?
Questions.A: They knew that he was the Christ/Messiah. (41b)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus strongly warn/sternly command those demons/evil spirits not to do?
Questions.A: He strongly warned/sternly commanded them not to speak about this again. (41)
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus strongly warn those demons not to do?
What did Jesus strongly warn those evil spirits not to do?
What did Jesus sternly command those demons not to do?
What did Jesus sternly command those evil spirits not to do?

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that Jesus forbid them to speak anything more?
Questions.A: He did not want people to think that he (Jesus) was associated with the evil spirits.
-OR-
He wanted people to recognize God's power and authority in his words and actions
and then realize that he was the Christ, just as God had promised them.
-OR-
Many Jews thought that the Messiah would set them free from the Roman government, not from sin, so they would misunderstand such words from the spirits.)
-OR-
He did not want the Jewish leaders to turn against him and end his ministry before he had done everything that God had sent him to do.

Questions.Q: Where did Jesus go the next day at daybreak?
Questions.A: He went out [from the town] to a place where he could be alone. (42)

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that the people were looking for him?
Questions.A: They wanted him to stay there, [perhaps to heal people when they were sick or to do other miracles]. (They may have thought that he had already left their town.) (42)

Questions.Q: Why did Jesus not stay there, but went to other towns, even as far away as the synagogues in Judea province?
Questions.A: God had sent him [down to earth] to tell/preach the Good News about the kingdom of God. (43, 44)

Key Term Check: The two words which are often translated "preach" in English translations are both here in one context. Verse 43 refers to the content of Jesus's message. Verse 44 refers to how he presented that Good News message, doing it "with authority".

Questions.Q: What is the kingdom of God?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: God wants to rule over every person and reign in each one's heart and life as a king rules over the people who live in his country. The people in a kingdom submit to the king's rule, obeying his laws. God was establishing his kingship through his son, Jesus, whom he sent to the earth as the Messiah/the Christ he had promised to send.
Questions.Note: See "kingdom of God" in KBT.

Section.heading: Luke 5:1-11 Jesus called Simon and his companions to follow him.

Questions.Q: How did Simon and his companions respond to Jesus's words and actions?
Questions.A: They obeyed his requests (3, 4-5),
saw that he had great power (9)
and then followed him (11).

Questions.Q: Why were many people crowding around Jesus at the lakeside?
Questions.A: They all wanted to hear God's message which Jesus spoke. (1)

Questions.Q: Why did Jesus get into a fishing boat?
Questions.A: He got into the boat in order to be out in front of the people and better teach them. (1, 3)

Questions.Q: Who owned the boat in which Jesus sat?
Questions.A: Simon did. // Simon owned it. (3)

Questions.Q: What were Simon and the other fishermen doing when Jesus asked to use Simon's boat?
Questions.A: They were washing out their [large] fishing nets. (2)

Questions.Q: When Jesus had finished teaching the crowd, what did he tell Simon?
Questions.A: He told Simon to go catch fish out in the deep water of the lake. (4)

Questions.Q: Why did Simon not want to go fishing at that time?
Questions.A: He and the other men had fished all night, but had caught nothing. (5)

Questions.Q: Why would Simon try again to catch fish?
Questions.A: He respected Jesus, who had told him to do it. (5)

Questions.Q: What happened when they obeyed Jesus's words?
Questions.A: They caught so many fish that their nets began to tear/break [from the weight]. (6)

Questions.Q: How were they able to pull in those nets full of fish?
Questions.A: They motioned to their partners in the other boat to come and help them. (7)

Questions.Q: Why were both the boats about to sink?
Questions.A: The many fish filled both boats and were so heavy that the boats sat very low in the water. (7)

Questions.Q: Who is this man named Peter?
Questions.A: He is Simon. It is another name for him. (8)
Questions.Note: You may wish to have a footnote or glossary entry which indicates that Simon was also called Peter in the Greek language (see John 1:40-42). Simon was his Hebrew name.

Questions.Q: Show me what you think that Simon did when he "fell down at Jesus's knees".
Questions.A: (The respondent should kneel in front of someone or something which represents Jesus's legs. We do not know if Simon bowed his head or not, but that was a sign of honor to the person who was standing or sitting.)

Questions.Q: Why did Simon fall down at Jesus's knees and tell him to go away from him?
Questions.A: He had seen Jesus use God's power and was astonished by it. Now he shows his submission to Jesus. He knew that he was a person who sinned [and that Jesus did not sin]. Simon probably felt unworthy to have one sent by God right there helping him. (8-9)

Questions.Q: Other people also were astonished by this large number of fish they had caught. Who were they?
Questions.A: They included Simon's companions as well as his partners, James and John (who were sons of the man named Zebedee). (9-10)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say in response to Simon's words?
Questions.A: "Do not be afraid. From now on you will catch men." (10)

Questions.Q: What do you think that Simon would do to "catch men"?
Questions.A: He would not grab people with his hands or his fishing net. This is picture/figurative language. Simon would gather people, both men and women, by encouraging them to become believers in/followers of Jesus in God's kingdom.

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that Jesus said that Simon should not have been afraid of him or his power?
Questions.A: They would be working together for the same purpose, not as enemies. Jesus had used his power to help, not to hurt or frighten anyone. (10)

Questions.Q: How did those men get ready to "catch men"?
Questions.A: They pulled their boats up on the shore, left everything there and followed Jesus. (11)
Questions.Note: The meaning of "to follow Jesus" here includes both walking behind Jesus away from the boats at the lake and learning from him as they went everywhere together.

Questions.Q: How did the men catching so many fish helped them decide to follow Jesus? What do you think?
Questions.A: Simon saw that Jesus had real power and authority when he spoke or did something.
He recognized that it was power from God that he, as a normal, sinful human being, did not have. (8)
The men would learn more about that power and authority [and about Jesus's message] as they went around with him and listened to him teach.

Section.heading: Luke 5:12-16 Jesus healed a man who was sick with leprosy/a bad skin disease.

Questions.Q: After Jesus healed the man who had leprosy/a bad skin disease, how did people respond?
Questions.A: The man having leprosy believed in Jesus and Jesus healed him. (13)
New crowds of people came to hear him [teach God's Word] and to have him heal them of their sicknesses. (15)
Questions.Alternative: After Jesus healed the man who had leprosy, how did people respond?
After Jesus healed the man who had a bad skin disease, how did people respond?

Questions.Q: How did Jesus and the man sick with leprosy/the bad skin disease meet?
Questions.A: Jesus was in the same town as the man. The man saw him there. (12)
Questions.Alternative: How did Jesus and the man sick with leprosy meet?
How did Jesus and the man sick with the bad skin disease meet?

Questions.Q: What did the man do when he saw Jesus?
Questions.A: He quickly bowed low, putting his [knees and his] face to the ground [in front of Jesus] and pleaded with/appealed to Jesus to heal him so he would be [physically and ritually] clean. (12)

Questions.Q: This man talked to Jesus as if he was not sure about something. Was he not sure that Jesus wanted to heal him or was he not sure that Jesus had enough power to heal him?
Questions.A: He was not sure that Jesus wanted to heal him. He knew Jesus had enough power. (12)

Questions.Q: What do you think that the man was thinking about when he said, "Make me clean"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He was talking both about having clear skin again after he became well and about becoming ritually clean. That means that the priests would allow him to once again be in the public worship and in the presence of God and to live with his family.
Questions.Note: See 4:27, above.

Questions.Q: How did Jesus make the man well again?
Questions.A: He reached out and touched/put his hand on the sick man and told him he was healed. (13)
Questions.Note: If a person allowed another who was sick with leprosy to be near him or to touch him, that was a culturally bad thing. It meant that the new person also was ritually unclean for a set amount of time. Therefore, no one wanted to touch a person with leprosy, but Jesus felt compassion for the man. The translator may want to have a glossary entry about the Jews' laws and taboos concerning leprosy (see Lev. 13-14).

Questions.Q: What was the man to do after Jesus healed him?
Questions.A: He was to go show his healed skin to a priest and then offer the sacrifices which Moses had commanded for a person who was healed of leprosy. (14)

Questions.Q: What result did Jesus intend when he told the man to go to the priest?
Questions.A: He wanted the people/the priests to know for sure that the man was totally healed [and safe to be near]. (14)
(It would also show that Jesus followed/obeyed the Laws of Moses and told others to do the same.)

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that Jesus commanded the man not to tell anyone about this?
Questions.A: He did not want people to become excited only about the things he did to help people.
-OR-
He did not want the man to interact with other people before a priest declared him [ritually] clean.
-OR-
He did not want the priests to hear of the miracle before the man arrived. If they were hostile toward Jesus, they might decide not to say that the man was cured or ritually clean.
Questions.Note: If the person who is answering these questions already knows a lot about events in the four gospels, he may give one of the answers below. These answers are still true and acceptable, but they are not found in Luke's gospel up to this point.
He did not want the people or the priests to think that he disregarded the Laws of Moses.

Questions.Q: Jesus commanded the man not to say anything to anyone else. What happened anyway?
Questions.A: News about Jesus's teaching and miracles spread even more than before.
Crowds of people came to hear him [teach God's Word].
Many people wanted him to heal them of their sicknesses. (15)

Questions.Q: Why did Jesus go to an uninhabited area/into the wilderness/desert?
Questions.A: He wanted to get away from people and pray [alone to God]. (16)
Questions.Alternative: Why did Jesus go to an uninhabited area?
Why did Jesus go into the wilderness?
Why did Jesus go into the desert?

Section.heading: Luke 5:17-26 Jesus forgave the sins of a paralyzed man and healed him.

Questions.Q: Why did Jesus heal the paralyzed man?
Questions.A: He wanted everyone who was there to know that he had authority from God to forgive sins. Because they could not see that, he healed the sick man to show that God had given power to him. (24)

Questions.Q: After Jesus healed that man, how did people respond?
Questions.A: Those people who believed in Jesus were helped (20, 25) and many praised God (25-26).
The Pharisees and the teachers of the Law/scribes criticized him (21).

Questions.Q: Who had come to hear Jesus teach?
Questions.A: Pharisees and teachers of the Law had come from many places. (17)

Questions.Q: What do you know about these two groups of men called the Pharisees and the teachers of the Law?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The Pharisees were a group of Jewish religious leaders who also were very much like a political party. They followed the teaching of the experts in interpreting the Scriptures (who are often called scribes, or teachers of the Law). After those teachers of the Law had decided how a Jew was to live in order to please God, the Pharisees tried to live that way. They were very proud of themselves and thought that they were better than all the other people who did not live as they did.

The teachers of the Law were men who had authority to copy the writings of the Old Testament writers. They became the teachers and interpreters of the Old Testament Scriptures, especially the laws of God written down by Moses. Because of that work of writing, those men were called scribes.
Questions.Note: See "Pharisee" and "scribe, teacher of the law" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did Luke write about the power of God?
Questions.A: It was there with/in Jesus and available for him to heal [the sick people]. (17)

Questions.Q: Why were some men coming, carrying another man on a mat/stretcher?
Questions.A: The man on the mat was paralyzed, and they believed that Jesus could heal him. (18, 20)
Questions.Alternative: Why were some men coming, carrying another man on a mat?
Why were some men coming, carrying another man on a stretcher?

Questions.Q: Tell me about the sickness of the man on the mat/stretcher.
Questions.A: The sick man could not move his legs and, perhaps, not his arms. It was as if those parts were dead. He could not walk or stand, so his friends carried him to Jesus.
Questions.Alternative: Tell me about the sickness of the man on the mat.
Tell me about the sickness of the man on the stretcher.

Questions.Q: When they came to the house, what did they try hard to do?
Questions.A: They tried hard to carry the sick man inside and lay him in front of Jesus. (18)

Questions.Q: Why were they not able to do that?
Questions.A: There were many people in the house/in their way. (19)

Questions.Q: What did they do in order to put the sick man in front of Jesus?
Questions.A: They went up onto the [flat] roof,
[removed some roofing material/tiles from] over the place where Jesus was
and lowered the mat on which the sick man lay. (19)

Questions.Q: Why did Jesus decide to forgive the sick man's sins?
Questions.A: He saw [all the hard work the men had done to put the sick man in front of him, and knew] that they believed/had faith that he could heal the man. (20)

Questions.Q: What was that faith which the men had?
Questions.A: The men trusted and were confident that something was true, even when it could not be seen. They trusted and were confident that, by the power of God, Jesus was able to heal their friend. (See "faith" in KBT in the "believe" entry.)

Questions.Q: Why were the Pharisees and the teachers of the Law/scribes upset when Jesus said that he had forgiven the sick man's sins?
Questions.A: They did not believe that Jesus was God's son. Because only God can forgive sins, when Jesus forgave the man's sins, they wrongly thought that he was blaspheming God/pretending to be like God. Anyone who claimed to be God or to have God's authority was blaspheming God. (21)
Questions.Alternative: Why were the Pharisees and teachers of the Law upset when Jesus said that he had forgiven the sick man's sins?
Why were the Pharisees and scribes upset when Jesus said that he had forgiven the sick man's sins?

Questions.Q: What do you think that a person does when he blasphemes God?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He claims to be equal with God in some way.
-OR-
He speaks evil against God. He insults God and defames his name and character so that others will not honor or respect him.
(God had said that people should kill such a person [Lev. 24:16]).

Questions.Q: How is it, do you think, that Jesus knew their thoughts?
Questions.A: He was God's son and the Lord God's power was present with him.
Questions.Note: See verse 17.

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that Jesus implied that they should not have thought such things?
Questions.A: The things that he had already taught and done should have proven to them that he had come from God and that God had given him authority both to forgive sins and to heal the sick.
-OR-
They came expecting to hear Jesus teach God's Word clearly and do some miracles. Since he could only do those things by God's power, he could forgive sins by that same power, too.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the answer to Jesus's question about whether it is easier to forgive sins or to heal a person who is paralyzed?
Questions.A: Neither action is possible unless you are God. If Jesus could do one, he must be God, so he could do the other by using that same power.
-OR-

If you say you have power to forgive someone's sins, it may be just empty words, because no one can see whether it is true or not. However, if you say you have power to heal someone, everyone will see whether that happens or not. In that way, healing someone is harder to do, because everyone will see whether you are lying or not.

Questions.Q: Whom was Jesus talking about when he spoke about the Son of Man?
Questions.A: He was speaking about himself. (24)

Key Term Check: This is a title used in the Old Testament in Dan. 7:13-14. Daniel was referring to a human figure who, nevertheless, is a being in heaven. God gave him authority to be the leader of God's people on earth. The teachers of the Law knew that this title referred to the Messiah. Jesus applied this title to himself. See "Son of Man" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Why did Jesus tell the sick man to get up and leave?
Questions.A: He said that to the sick man in order that the Pharisees and the teachers of the Law would know that he had power from God to heal the man. Then they would know that he also had authority (from God/as God's son) to forgive sins. (24)

Questions.Q: How did the people there know that Jesus had healed the man?
Questions.A: He stood up in front of them, took up his mat/bedding and went home praising God. (25)

Questions.Q: What did those people think and do when they saw the man do that?
Questions.A: They all could hardly believe what they were seeing, and it caused them to have great respect for God and to praise him. They realized that they had seen unusual things happen right there in front of them. (26)

Section.heading: Luke 5:27-32 Jesus called Levi to follow him.

Questions.Q: When Jesus called Levi to follow him, how did Levi respond?
Questions.A: He left everything [related to his government work] and followed Jesus. He even hosted a banquet/feast in Jesus's honor. (27-29)

Questions.Q: When Jesus ate food with many other people at Levi's house, how did the Pharisees and teachers of the Law/scribes respond?
Questions.A: They complained to his disciples. (30)
Questions.Alternative: When Jesus ate food with many other people at Levi's house, how did the Pharisees and teachers of the Law respond?
When Jesus ate food with many other people at Levi's house, how did the Pharisees and scribes respond?

Questions.Q: Why did Jesus come to this earth?
Questions.A: He came to call/invite people who know they sin to repent [of their sins]. (32)

Questions.Q: What work did Levi do?
Questions.A: He collected tax money [for the Roman government]. (27)
Questions.Note: You may wish to have a footnote or glossary entry which indicates Levi was also called Matthew in the Greek language (see Matt. 9:9-13). Levi was his Hebrew name.

Questions.Q: Where was Levi when Jesus spoke to him?
Questions.A: He was sitting in a government office collecting taxes. (27)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus ask Levi to do?
Questions.A: He asked Levi to follow him [and learn from him as they went everywhere together]. (27)

Questions.Q: What did Levi do to show that he already believed in Jesus?
Questions.A: He got up, left everything [related to his work] and went with Jesus. (28)

Questions.Q: How did Levi honor Jesus?
Questions.A: He made a great banquet/feast for Jesus. (29)

Questions.Q: What other groups of people were also at this feast?
Questions.A: There was a large crowd of other men who collected taxes (29), some Pharisees and teachers of the Law/scribes (30), Jesus's disciples (30) and others (29) [whom the Pharisees and teachers of the Law regarded as sinners (30) ].

Questions.Q: What kind of a person is a disciple?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A disciple is a person who spends much time learning from someone who is wise. Usually the student follows the teacher everywhere he goes, listening to and discussing with the teacher everything he or she says. The disciple is like an apprentice, but is not learning craft skills.
Questions.Note: See "disciple" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Who were Jesus's disciples at this time?
Questions.A: Luke has only written about Simon Peter, James, John (verse 11) and now Levi.
Questions.Note: There probably were many other people who followed Jesus and may be included here. However, we only know the names of those twelve whom he called his apostles (see Luke 6:12-16), and two others who were later considered to replace Judas as an apostle (see Acts 1:21-23).

Questions.Q: Why did the Pharisees and teachers of the Law/scribes complain to the disciples?
Questions.A: Jesus and his disciples were eating with the tax collectors and other people whom the Pharisees regarded as sinners. They were people who did not follow all the ways Pharisees said that were necessary to fully please God. (30)
Questions.Alternative: Why did the Pharisees and teachers of the Law complain to the disciples?
Why did the Pharisees and scribes complain to the disciples?

Questions.Q: What do you think is the meaning of Jesus's illustration about people who need a doctor?
Questions.A: Sick people know they need help, so they do whatever the doctor tells them to do to get well again. In the same way, people who know they are sinners, know they need someone to help them become right in God's sight again.
Jesus said that he came to help the people who [know they] sin to repent. The people who already think they are well or righteous do not look for, and do not want, any help. (31-32)

Questions.Q: Jesus used the picture language of people who know they are sick and people who think they are well. To whom, do you think, was he referring?
Questions.A: The tax collectors, disciples and those whom the Pharisees called sinners knew that they needed Jesus to help them.
Generally, the Pharisees and teachers of the Law/scribes were the ones who thought that they were good/righteous. Therefore, they thought that they did not need Jesus to forgive them.

Section.heading: Luke 5:33-39 Some people asked Jesus about the reason that his disciples did not fast.

Questions.Q: Jesus's disciples treated fasting and praying differently than John's disciples and the followers of the Pharisees did. How did Jesus show the reason for that difference?
Questions.A: He told them stories to explain/illustrate the reason. (34-35, 36, 37-39)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus show in his picture language was the reason for this difference?
Questions.A: Jesus was saying that his disciples were celebrating something new, that is, the son of God was among them. This meant having new ways of responding to God and his Word.
The old ways were no longer adequate, [even though they had been right and good in their time and had served well].
These new ways, however, would not just blend in and match the old, but must totally replace them.
Questions.Note: The more parts of the answer which someone gives, the better the answer, but even one part will be an acceptable answer. Not every part must be understood from this one reading.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus imply that the response of some people would be to him? -OR- How did Jesus expect some people to respond to him?
Questions.A: They would reject the new ways [of relating to God which he, Jesus, lived and taught,] and stay with their old ways [as explained by the Pharisees and teachers of the Law]. (39)
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus imply that the response of some people would be to him?
How did Jesus expect some people to respond to him?

Questions.Q: How were Jesus's disciples different from the disciples of John and the Pharisees?
Questions.A: The disciples of John and of the Pharisees often fasted and prayed. Jesus's disciples did not. (33)
Key Term Check: See "fasting" discussed at 2:37.

Questions.Q: What comparisons did Jesus make when he used the picture language about a wedding?
Questions.A: He compared his disciples to the friends of the bridegroom and compared himself to the bridegroom. (34-35)

Questions.Q: In what way, do you think, did Jesus's comparison answer their question about why his disciples did not fast?
Questions.A: Jesus's disciples did not fast at that time because they were happy that Jesus was with them (34). Later, when he had been taken away from them [by his enemies], they would fast [because they would be sad] (35).

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say was the reason that it is not good to patch/mend an old piece of clothing with a piece cut from a new piece of clothing?
Questions.A: The new one is ruined and the old one looks strange and mismatched.
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus say was the reason that it is not good to patch an old piece of clothing with a piece cut from a new piece of clothing?
What did Jesus say was the reason that it is not good to mend an old piece of clothing with a piece cut from a new piece of clothing?

Questions.Q: What comparison, do you think, was Jesus making when he used the picture language/parable about the new clothing and the old clothing and a patch?
Questions.A: The new clothing represented what Jesus was teaching about a person's relationship with God.
The old clothing represented the ways the religious teachers had taught the people to relate to God in the past.
The patch was only a small piece of the new way. It did not really make things better.
Questions.Alternative: What comparison, do you think, was Jesus making when he used the picture language about the new clothing and the old clothing and a patch?
What comparison, do you think, was Jesus making when he used the parable about the new clothing and the old clothing and a patch?

Questions.Q: What do you think were ways that Jesus wanted the people to change?
Questions.A: If the people wanted to be in a right relationship with God, they must follow what Jesus taught, and not just try to improve what they were already trying to do.

Questions.Q: If the people who speak your language use picture language/parables, tell me one of those stories and then tell me its meaning.
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A parable shows its meaning indirectly by using picture language to make a comparison. The parts of the comparison are generally not explained. The listeners themselves must think much about the meaning hidden in each part of the picture language. Jesus taught spiritual truths in this story form.
Questions.Note: See "parable" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: If the people who speak your language use picture language, tell me one of those stories and then tell me its meaning.
If the people who speak your language use parables, tell me one of those stories and then tell me its meaning.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say was the reason that it is not good to put new wine into old wineskins?
Questions.A: New wine will [ferment and swell and] burst the old wineskin [which is no longer flexible] and will spill out onto the ground. That will ruin both the wine and the wineskin. Neither one will have any value. (37)

Questions.Q: What comparison, do you think, was Jesus making when he used the picture language about the new wine and the old wineskin?
Questions.A: The new wine represented Jesus's new teaching [about a person's relationship with God].
The old wineskin represented the way the people had been relating to God in the past.

If people tried to fit the new ways into the old patterns [as taught by the Pharisees and traditions], that would not work. The old way, then, was no longer useful and the value of the new way would be lost, too.

Questions.Q: What do you think were ways that Jesus wanted the people to change?
Questions.A: (He wanted them to change in the same ways as he had talked about in the parable with the old and the new clothes.) If the people wanted to be in a right relationship with God, they must follow what Jesus taught, and not just try to improve what they were already trying to do, such as fasting.

Section.heading: Luke 6:1-11 Jesus's authority was greater than the laws about the Sabbath Day.

Questions.Q: Why did the Pharisees criticize Jesus and his disciples for picking grain?
Questions.A: They thought that Jesus and his disciples were disobeying the Laws [of Moses] about [not working on] the Sabbath Day. (2, 7)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell them about the Sabbath Day?
Questions.A: He said that he, the Son of Man, was Lord over it, that is, he had authority [from God] to say what could be done on the Sabbath Day. (5)
Also, he implied [with the example from God's Word about David and his companions] that God permitted people to do good, helpful things on the Sabbath Day when there was a special need. (3-4, 9)

Questions.Q: Where was Jesus walking one Sabbath Day?
Questions.A: He was going through grain fields. (1)

Questions.Q: What kind of a place do you think a grain field is?
Questions.A: It is a field/garden where grass crops like wheat or barley are planted to raise the seeds for food.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus's disciples do as they walked there?
Questions.A: They picked some heads of the grain, rubbed them around in their hands [to remove the husks] and ate the kernels. (1)

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that they did that?
Questions.A: They were probably hungry. (3-4)
Questions.Note: They were not stealing the grain. The Law of Moses allowed them to take some grain to eat as they walked along (see Deut. 23:25).

Questions.Q: What do you think that the Pharisees were thinking about when they criticized Jesus and his disciples?
Questions.A: They regarded what the disciples did as being work, [like harvesting grain or gathering food]. People were not permitted by the Law [of Moses] to do any kind of work activity on the Sabbath Day. (2)

Questions.Q: What did David and his companions once do when they were hungry and had no food?
Questions.A: They entered [the grounds of] the house of God,
received [from a priest] the bread which only the priests were permitted to eat [after they had offered a new set of fresh bread to God],
and ate it [even though they were not priests]. (4)

Questions.Q: Why was that food/bread special and only for the priests to eat?
Questions.A: The priests previously had given it to God, setting it out [on a special table] for him. (4)
Questions.Alternative: Why was that food special and only for the priests to eat?
Why was that bread special and only for the priests to eat?

Questions.Q: Does it sound to you as though Jesus was saying that David and his men had done something wrong?
Questions.A: (It should not sound that way. Rather, Jesus was using this story about David as an example that it is more important to meet a need than to obey the rules of religion.)

Questions.Q: Who was this "Son of Man" whom Jesus said had authority to decide what was permitted on the Sabbath Day?
Questions.A: Jesus himself was the Son of Man. (See 5:24.)

Questions.Q: What was wrong with one man in the synagogue where Jesus was teaching?
Questions.A: He had a shriveled/atrophied right hand. (6)

Questions.Q: Why were the Pharisees and the teachers of the Law/scribes carefully watching Jesus?
Questions.A: If Jesus healed that man on the Sabbath Day, they would have a good reason to accuse him of working. The Law [of Moses] did not permit anyone to work on the Sabbath Day. (7) (Then they could punish him or, at least, tell people that he was not a good teacher of God's Word.)
Questions.Alternative: Why were the Pharisees and teachers of the Law carefully watching Jesus?
Why were the Pharisees and scribes carefully watching Jesus?

Questions.Q: Why did Jesus tell the man with the shriveled hand to stand up in front of everyone else?
Questions.A: He knew what those men were thinking, so he wanted everyone to clearly see him heal the man. (8)

Questions.Q: The Pharisees did not answer Jesus's question about which choice should be made. Which of those choices do you think that people should choose?
Questions.A: People should choose to do good, which may save someone's life. (9)

Questions.Q: How did the man's hand become perfect again?
Questions.A: Jesus told him to stretch it out straight. When the man obeyed Jesus, his bad hand became completely well. (10)

Questions.Q: How did the Pharisees respond when Jesus told them these things and then he healed the man?
Questions.A: They were furiously mad/full of anger at him and began discussing what they could do to [kill] him. (11)
Questions.Note: See Matt. 12:14 and Mark 3:6, where the Pharisees stated clearly what they intended to do.

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that the Pharisees and the teachers of the Law were so angry at Jesus?
Questions.A: He neither interpreted the rules, nor obeyed them in the way that they had taught people to obey them.
He implied that, if people followed their rules, they might do something evil or even destroy someone's life. (9)
He was making them appear to be foolish in front of many people.

Section.heading: Luke 6:12-16 Jesus chose twelve men and appointed them as his apostles.

Questions.Q: Why did Jesus spend a whole night praying to God?
Questions.A: A large group of disciples followed Jesus. He wanted [God to help him] to carefully choose a few men out of that large group to become his apostles. (12-13)

Questions.Q: Do you think that Jesus went alone to pray or that other men went with him?
Questions.A: He probably went alone. Luke wrote that Jesus went into the hills to pray and that he wanted to choose some special workers. (He probably would not have asked any other person to join him at that time.) (12)

Questions.Q: How do you know God had helped him choose the right men?
Questions.A: He immediately chose them in front of the other people who followed him. (13)

Questions.Q: How many men did he choose for this special work?
Questions.A: Twelve men. (13)

Questions.Q: What was the special name Jesus gave this group of twelve men?
Questions.A: He designated them as his apostles. // He named them apostles. (13)

Questions.Q: What do you think the difference was between the work an apostle would do and the work a disciple would do?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: An apostle was sent with full authority from the one who had sent him to speak or act in his place. A disciple was really only a student who followed his teacher around. He had no authority to represent the teacher.
Questions.Note: See "apostle" and "disciple" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Tell me about the two men named Simon.
Questions.A: Jesus gave the name Peter to one Simon. He was the brother of Andrew. (14)
The other Simon was known as the Zealot. (15)

Questions.Q: What do you think a "Zealot" was?
Questions.A: Jews who really wanted their people and their country to be free from the control and rules of the Roman government were called Zealots. They felt strongly that they should be independent.
Questions.Note: If the word is not already translated by a descriptive phrase, the translator may want to explain the word in a footnote or glossary item.

Questions.Q: Tell me about the two men named James.
Questions.A: One was a son of Zebedee and the brother of John (see 5:10). They were partners with Simon in the fishing business. (14)
The other James was the son of a man named Alphaeus. (15)

Questions.Q: Tell me about the two men named Judas.
Questions.A: One was the son of a man named James. (15)
The other Judas was Judas Iscariot, who [later] became a traitor [to Jesus]/a betrayer [of Jesus]. (16)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for a person to be a traitor/betrayer?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He acts like a good friend to you or your group, but then he helps your enemies do something bad to hurt you/your group.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think it means for a person to be a traitor?
What do you think it means for a person to be a betrayer?

Section.heading: Luke 6:17-26 Jesus explained what kind of people are truly happy.

Questions.Q: What will happen to those who want to know God better and want to please him?
Questions.A: They will be happy/feel blessed [by God]. They will receive a great reward in heaven. (20-23)

Questions.Q: What will happen to those who want to have the things which are part of this world and want to please themselves?
Questions.A: They will be punished [by God]. They have already received whatever happiness they will ever have. (24-26)

Questions.Q: Who was waiting for Jesus when he came down the mountain?
Questions.A: There was a large crowd of disciples/followers
and a great many other people from all over the area where Jews lived, [including] Jerusalem,
as well as people from the region beside the sea where the towns of Tyre and Sidon were. (17)

Questions.Q: Why were those people waiting for Jesus?
Questions.A: They had come to hear him [teach God's Word]
and to have him heal them of their diseases. (18)

Questions.Q: What happened to some of those people?
Questions.A: Those people who were troubled by evil spirits were healed. (18)
Those people who touched Jesus were all healed by his power [flowing out from him,] [into them]. (19)

Questions.Q: What are some of the characteristics of those whom Jesus says are happy/feel blessed by God?
Questions.A: They are poor (20), hungry, weeping (21) and hated (that is, excluded, insulted and defamed) by others because they associate with Jesus (22). (That is, they focus on God.)
Questions.Note: The Greek word which is translated in these verses as "blessed" is not the same word which Luke used back in 1:42, 1:64, and 2:28 when Elizabeth, Zechariah, and Simeon each blessed someone. The word Luke used here refers to inner happiness, not outward happiness.
Questions.Alternative: What are some of the characteristics of those whom Jesus says are happy?
What are some of the characteristics of those whom Jesus says are feel blessed by God?

Questions.Q: Why would the disciples know they should expect this kind of trouble/bad treatment?
Questions.A: The [peoples'] forefathers had treated the prophets, [who also had focused their lives on God,] the same way. (23)
Questions.Alternative: Why would the disciples know they should expect this kind of trouble?
Why would the disciples know they should expect this kind of bad treatment?

Questions.Q: Why are the people who have these troubles called happy/blessed by God?
Questions.A: God rules and reigns in their lives, that is, they live under God's authority and direction. (20)
Their hunger/needs/desires [to know God better and to please him] will be met. (21a)
Their crying will become laughter. (21b)
They will receive a great reward [from God] in heaven because [people will treat them] the same way as the [peoples'] forefathers treated the prophets [whom God had sent out with his message]. (23)
Questions.Alternative: Why are the people who have these troubles called happy?
Why are the people who have these troubles called blessed by God?

Questions.Q: What are some of the characteristics of those people who should expect God to cause horrible things to happen to them?
Questions.A: They are rich (24), well fed, enjoying this present life (25) and ones about whom people say good things (26).

Questions.Q: Why will they suffer punishment from God, and not blessings?
Questions.A: They have focused their lives on becoming rich and have already enjoyed many pleasures in this life. (24)
They have focused their lives on eating well, but will still hunger/have a need [for real satisfaction]. That hunger will not be met. (25a)
They have focused their lives on entertaining themselves, [not on what pleased God]. (25b)
They have focused their lives on being praised by everyone else, [but not by God]. (26)

Questions.Q: What do you think happened to the false prophets and the [peoples'] forefathers who always praised them?
Questions.A: God punished them.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think happened to the false prophets and the peoples' forefathers who always praised them?
What do you think happened to the false prophets and the forefathers who always praised them?

Section.heading: Luke 6:27-36 People who follow Jesus's teaching should love their enemies.

Questions.Q: Why should people who want to follow what Jesus taught do/be good to everyone?
Questions.A: Because their Father [in heaven] is compassionate towards them, they should be compassionate in the same way to all others, including their enemies. (31, 35-36)
Also, they should do/be good to them because God will greatly reward them and call them his children. (35)
Questions.Alternative: Why should people who want to follow what Jesus taught do good to everyone?
Why should people who want to follow what Jesus taught be good to everyone?

Questions.Q: To whom was Jesus telling these words?
Questions.A: He was speaking to those people who heard what he taught them [and desired to obey him]. (27) (Those people were referred to as his disciples in verse 20.)

Questions.Q: How should a person who follows Jesus treat his enemies?
Questions.A: He should love his enemies. (27)
Questions.Note: Key Term Check: The Greek language has several words which are translated "love" in English. The word used here means a gracious, outgoing, active interest in the welfare of another person. John used the same word to explain how much God loves us [John 3:16; 1 John 4:9-11. Jesus used the word to talk about loving God and loving one's neighbor as one loves himself [Mark 12:30-31]. Paul used the word to tell how a husband should act toward his wife [Eph. 5:25]. We should love our enemies the same as God loves us and the same as we love anyone else, including our wives and God. The translator must have good reasons if he/she has used a different word for love in this verse than he/she would use in those other contexts. See "love" in KBT.

The person who answers may also talk about doing good to them (27), blessing them and praying for them (28). If he included all these, you should skip the next question. If he did not include these things, please ask the next question.

Questions.Q: How should one show love for his enemies?
Questions.A: Do good to those who hate you (27),
ask God to bless those who curse you (28a)
and pray for those who are cruel to you (28b).
If someone slaps you on one cheek, turn [so he can hit] the other one also (29a)
If someone takes something of yours, such as your coat, do not stop him from taking [other things, such as] your shirt. (29b)
If someone asks you to give him something, give it and don't ask for it back. (30)

Questions.Q: What do you think that a person will say or do if he is cursing you?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He wants evil and suffering to come into your life, so he asks spirit beings, either God or an evil spirit, to cause you injury or trouble. This is the exact opposite of the meaning of "blessing".
Questions.Note: See "curse" in KBT in the "bless, blessed, blessing" entry.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say is a good way to remember how we are to show love to such people?
Questions.A: We should do for other people what we want them to do for us. (31)

Questions.Q: Why did Jesus not praise people who show love or do good only to those who have already done the same for them?
Questions.A: Even people who do not try to obey God, do that. (32-33)

Questions.Q: What if you lend something to another person knowing that he will repay you?
Questions.A: That, too, is not any different from what any non-Christian would do. You will not receive any special credit from God for doing that. (34)

Questions.Q: Jesus said that we are to love our enemies, do good to them (27) and lend things to them without expecting to get anything back (30). If we do like that, what will be the result?
Questions.A: [God] will greatly reward us
and [people will know that] we are children of the Most High [God]. (35)

Questions.Q: Why will we be regarded as his children for doing like that?
Questions.A: We will be doing as our heavenly Father, God, does. He is kind and compassionate, even to the people who are ungrateful and wicked. (35-36)

Section.heading: Luke 6:37-42 People should not judge others.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about people who judge the actions and motives of others?
Questions.A: He said that they are like blind people trying to show other blind people the right way (39).
They are hypocrites because they have the same problems in even greater amounts, but do not pay attention to them (42). (They are no help to anyone.)

Questions.Q: What does it mean to judge someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A person sees or hears something about that other person, evaluates it, and decides how he will act towards that other person. Usually the person who judges assumes a position of authority [and superiority] over the one he is judging.
Questions.Note: See "judge, judgment" in KBT.

Questions.Q: In what ways can one show God's mercy to another person?
Questions.A: Jesus said that we are not to judge the other person['s motives] or condemn him/her, that is, we are not to decide what is an appropriate punishment for that person. We should forgive that person (37) and be generous to them (38). That will show God's mercy.

Questions.Q: If we do not judge others, but forgive them, how will God act toward us?
Questions.A: He will not judge or condemn us, but will forgive us (37). He will be generous to us (to the same degree that we have been generous to others). He will give us even more, in return, than we might have expected (38).

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say that tells you that God will be generous to us?
Questions.A: He spoke about a good/full measure, about pressing the things down [in the container], about shaking the things together and about extra things spilling over [the edge of the container]. (38)

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that the person selling the grain (6:38) would pour it into the buyer's lap/onto the buyer's clothing?
Questions.A: The seller did that in order that the buyer could carry the grain away. (Also, the grain would be too much to carry in cupped hands.)
Questions.Note: In the Jewish culture of Jesus's time the people wore loose-fitting clothing. Some folds of extra cloth were spread wide at times to be used to carry such things as grain. See TN for Luke 6:38.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think was the reason that the person selling the grain (6:38) would pour it into the buyer's lap?
What do you think was the reason that the person selling the grain (6:38) would pour it onto the buyer's clothing?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say will happen if a blind man/person follows another blind man/person?
Questions.A: Neither man will see a hole, so they both will fall into it. (39)
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus say will happen if a blind man follows another blind man?
What did Jesus say will happen if a blind man follows another blind person?
What did Jesus say will happen if a blind person follows another blind man?
What did Jesus say will happen if a blind person follows another blind person?

Questions.Q: What other picture language did Jesus use to show us how we are to know what to do?
Questions.A: He talked about a student learning all that he is able to learn from his teacher. Then he would be like his teacher. (40)

Questions.Q: To whom, do you think, was Jesus referring when he talked about a blind man [in verse 39]?
Questions.A: The blind man represents any one who does not know what is the right thing to do. If we follow such a person, we will be just like them. That is, we will not know what is right and will probably get hurt, besides.
Questions.Note: Jesus may have been referring to Jewish leaders who did not accept that God had sent him to be the savior. Whoever followed their leading would also not believe in him.
Questions.Alternative: To whom, do you think, was Jesus referring when he talked about a blind man in verse 39?
To whom, do you think, was Jesus referring when he talked about a blind man?

Questions.Q: To what teacher and students, do you think, might Jesus have been referring [in verse 40]?
Questions.A: He was referring to himself as the good teacher. People who do what he teaches are his students, his disciples. Those people will be like him.
Questions.Alternative: To what teacher and students, do you think, might Jesus have been referring in verse 40?
To what teacher and students, do you think, might Jesus have been referring?

Questions.Q: First look at what Jesus taught his disciples in verses 20-40. Then tell me four or more ways which Jesus said that his disciples could be like him.
Questions.A: The disciple/student will want to know God better. (21a)
He will be hated, insulted, and rejected [by people who oppose God]. (22)
He will love his enemies [as well as his friends]. (27a, 35)
He will do good to those who hate him. (27b, 35)
He will bless those who curse him. (28a)
He will pray for those who treat him badly. (28b)
He will be generous and lend, even to those who are ungrateful. (30, 34, 35, 38)
He will act toward others the same as he would want them to act toward him. (31)
He will be kind to those who are ungrateful or wicked. (35)
He will be merciful [to those having needs]. (36)
He will not judge or condemn others. (37a)
He will forgive others. (37b)
Questions.Note: All of these items should be clear in the translation, but do not expect anyone to find more than six quickly. Four items will be adequate.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say in his picture language about a speck of sawdust and an entire plank?
Questions.A: A person with a plank in his own eye sees a speck of sawdust/wheat chaff in another person's eye and offers help, not even noticing his own bigger problem. (41)

Key Term Check: Jesus said that the man with the small thing in his eye was the other man's "brother". If the translation uses the kin term for brother, ask about whom one calls his "brother" in that culture. If that word refers only to people who are one's blood relatives, suggest using a term with a wider meaning. The Greek word for "brother" included a wider sense of referring to other men with whom one interacted regularly, such as one's neighbor. See "the brothers" in KBT in the "disciple" entry.

Questions.Q: What do you think that Jesus wanted us to learn from this picture language?
Questions.A: We do not notice, or try to correct, our own big problems or very bad actions. Instead, we are quick to see other people's small problems and wrong actions and tell them what to do, as though we are better than they are.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus call a person who acts like that?
Questions.A: He called that person a hypocrite. (42)

Questions.Q: What might a [village] person have done that would cause other people to call him/her a hypocrite?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Such a person pretends to believe or do what other people will approve or for which they would praise him. He does not act because he really believes it is right or good.
Questions.Alternative: What might a village person have done that would cause other people to call him a hypocrite?
What might a village person have done that would cause other people to call her a hypocrite?
What might a person have done that would cause other people to call him a hypocrite?
What might a person have done that would cause other people to call her a hypocrite?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say one must do before he is able to help another person with his problem?
Questions.A: He must get rid of his own big problem before he can help another person with his/her small problem. (42)

Section.heading: Luke 6:43-45 Jesus told a parable about recognizing a tree by its fruit.

Questions.Q: How did Jesus compare trees and their fruit to people?
Questions.A: We can know the true inner character of a person by his/her words and actions (45), just as we can tell the quality of a tree by looking at its fruit (43-44). // In the same way that fruit can only be as good as the tree which produces it (43-44), a person's words and actions will reflect what is in his/her heart (45).

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about trees and their fruit in this parable?
Questions.A: He said that good trees produce good fruit and bad trees have bad fruit. Therefore, one can know whether a tree is good or bad just by looking at its fruit. (43-44)
Also, the specific kind of fruit depends on the kind of tree on which it is growing. (44)

Questions.Q: What did he say about people and their character and behavior/actions?
Questions.A: He said that good people have good qualities in their hearts and those are seen in their behavior. Evil people have evil thoughts in their hearts and those are seen in their evil behavior. A person's words show the kind of thoughts which are in his/her heart. (45)
Questions.Alternative: What did he say about people and their character and behavior?
What did he say about people and their character and actions?

Section.heading: Luke 6:46-49 Jesus told a parable about the way in which two men built houses.

Questions.Q: How did Jesus use the example of the base/foundation for a house to show us how people ought to respond to Jesus's teaching?
Questions.A: Those who set their way of living [and their faith] on a good, firm basis which will last, do so when they not only hear the words of Jesus, but also obey them.
Questions.Alternative: How did Jesus use the example of the base for a house to show us how people ought to respond to Jesus's teaching?
How did Jesus use the example of the foundation for a house to show us how people ought to respond to Jesus's teaching?

Questions.Q: Why was Jesus upset by people calling him by the respectful title "Lord"?
Questions.A: They talked as though they respected him as their teacher, but they did not show it by obeying what he taught. (46)

Questions.Q: Who did Jesus say is like a man/person who builds his house on a firm/strong base/foundation?
Questions.A: He is the person who comes to Jesus, hears his teaching, and then does what Jesus said. (47)
Questions.Alternative: Who did Jesus say is like a man who builds his house on a firm base?
Who did Jesus say is like a man who builds his house on a firm foundation?
Who did Jesus say is like a man who builds his house on a strong base?
Who did Jesus say is like a man who builds his house on a strong foundation?
Who did Jesus say is like a person who builds his house on a firm base?
Who did Jesus say is like a person who builds his house on a firm foundation?
Who did Jesus say is like a person who builds his house on a strong base?
Who did Jesus say is like a person who builds his house on a strong foundation?

Questions.Q: What happens when troubles come to a person who has that strong base/foundation for his life?
Questions.A: He stands firm [in his faith]. // He is not moved [from his strong belief in Jesus]. (48)
Questions.Alternative: What happens when troubles come to a person who has that strong base for his life?
What happens when troubles come to a person who has that strong foundation for his life?

Questions.Q: Who did Jesus say is like a man who does not build his house on a firm/strong base/foundation?
Questions.A: He is the person who hears Jesus's teaching, but does not do what he said. (49)
Questions.Alternative: Who did Jesus say is like a man who does not build his house on a firm base?
Who did Jesus say is like a man who does not build his house on a firm foundation?
Who did Jesus say is like a man who does not build his house on a strong base?
Who did Jesus say is like a man who does not build his house on a strong foundation?

Questions.Q: What happens when troubles come to such a house or such a person?
Questions.A: The house does not stand firm. It collapses and is totally destroyed. [Likewise, the troubles destroy a person who does not base his life on Jesus. He will suffer in hell forever].(49)

Section.heading: Luke 7:1-10 Jesus healed the sick and dying slave of a Roman army officer.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do to help a Roman army officer?
Questions.A: He healed his servant/slave who was sick and dying [without going directly to the man]. (6, 10)

Questions.Q: Why did the Jewish elders want Jesus to help the Roman army officer?
Questions.A: They said that the officer loved their Jewish people
and that he even had helped much to build a synagogue for them. (4-5)

Questions.Q: What was the real reason that Jesus helped the army officer, even though he was not a Jew?
Questions.A: Jesus knew that the officer had great faith in him [to heal his servant]. (9)

Questions.Q: What happened that caused a Roman army officer to send a message to Jesus?
Questions.A: The servant/slave of the army officer was sick and about to die (2), and the officer heard about Jesus [either that he healed the sick, or that he had returned to Capernaum] (3).
Key Term Check: See 1:38 above for the meaning of "servant" and "slave".

Questions.Q: Why was this important man in the army even thinking about a servant/slave?
Questions.A: He loved/respected/valued this young man. (2)
Questions.Alternative: Why was this important man in the army even thinking about a servant?
Why was this important man in the army even thinking about a slave?

Questions.Q: Whom did this army officer send with his message to Jesus?
Questions.A: He sent some elders of the Jews. (3)

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that the Roman army officer sent those men and not other Romans or himself?
Questions.A: Perhaps he thought that Jesus would listen to elders of his own Jewish people more than to someone who was not a Jew.

Questions.Q: What message did this army officer send to Jesus?
Questions.A: He wanted Jesus to come and heal his servant. (3)

Questions.Q: How do you know that those Jewish leaders also wanted Jesus to help this Roman man?
Questions.A: The words "kept on urging"/"earnestly asked"/"strongly requested" mean that those Jewish leaders wanted Jesus to help the man. They said that he was worthy [in their thinking] to have Jesus help him. (4)

Questions.Q: Whom did this army officer send with another message to Jesus?
Questions.A: He sent some of his friends. (6b)

Questions.Q: Why did the army officer himself not want to inconvenience/cause any problem for Jesus?
Questions.A: He did not feel worthy/good enough to either speak with Jesus or to have Jesus come inside his home. (6b-7)
Questions.Note: He also may not have wanted to cause a cultural problem for Jesus, because he knew that it was taboo for a Jew to enter the house of a non-Jew.
Questions.Alternative: Why did the army officer himself not want to inconvenience for Jesus?
Why did the army officer himself not want to cause any problem for Jesus?

Questions.Q: How did the army officer expect Jesus to heal the servant/slave if Jesus did not go inside the house where that sick man was?
Questions.A: He believed that Jesus needed only to speak [the words of healing from wherever he was] and the sick man would be well again. (7)
Questions.Alternative: How did the army officer expect Jesus to heal the servant if Jesus did not go inside the house where that sick man was?
How did the army officer expect Jesus to heal the slave if Jesus did not go inside the house where that sick man was?

Questions.Q: How did the army officer know that Jesus could heal his servant just by saying that the man was to become well?
Questions.A: He knew how authority worked. // He was under some higher authority and others were under his authority. When someone with authority spoke, that command was carried out. (8)
Questions.Note: By saying this, he showed that he believed that Jesus had been given authority by God over sickness. When Jesus spoke, the sickness would have to end/leave.

Questions.Q: How did Jesus react to the words of the Roman army officer?
Questions.A: He was amazed and told the crowd of people that he had not found [any other person with] great faith like that, not even among the people of Israel. (9) (He knew that this kind of strong faith did not normally happen even among the Jews who had God's Word and who had Jesus himself in their midst.)

Questions.Q: What does it mean that someone believes/has faith in another person?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that he believes what that person told him and that he trusts that person to do just as he said that he would do. (See "faith" in KBT in the "believe" entry. Also see 5:22, above.)
Questions.Alternative: What does it mean that someone believes in another person?
What does it mean that someone has faith in another person?

Questions.Q: How do we know that Jesus healed the army officer's servant/slave?
Questions.A: We read in verse 10 that when the friends of the army officer returned to his house, they found that the servant/slave was already well. (10)
Questions.Alternative: How do we know that Jesus healed the army officer's servant?
How do we know that Jesus healed the army officer's slave?

Section.heading: Luke 7:11-17 Jesus raised a widow's son who had died.

Questions.Q: What did all the people realize after they saw Jesus raise the dead young man to be alive again?
Questions.A: They realized that Jesus was a great prophet whom God had sent,
and that God was helping his people through the things which Jesus did. (16)

Questions.Q: Who was with Jesus when he approached the town of Nain?
Questions.A: His disciples and a large crowd of other people were with him. (11)

Questions.Q: What did they all see happening as they came near the gate/entranceway in the town wall?
Questions.A: Men were carrying out a dead person [on a stretcher], and many townspeople were with them. (12)
Questions.Note: If the language requires that the manner of carrying a dead person be named, use the appropriate cultural name for such a stretcher or platform. The translation must not imply that the men carried the corpse in their bare hands, even if it was wrapped in cloth. That was taboo for a Jew.
Questions.Alternative: What did they all see happening as they came near the gate in the town wall?
What did they all see happening as they came near the entranceway in the town wall?

Questions.Q: Where do you think that the men were taking the corpse?
Questions.A: They were going to bury it away from where the people lived. (12)

Questions.Q: Who was the dead person?
Questions.A: He was the only son of a widow. (12)

Questions.Q: What do you think made this especially sad for the woman?
Questions.A: Being a widow, she needed a son to care for/support her.
Also, a son was needed to carry on the family lineage and name.

Questions.Q: Why did Jesus tell the widow, "Do not cry"?
Questions.A: He felt compassion for her [and would take away the problem that was causing her to cry]. (13)

Questions.Q: What happened that caused the men carrying the coffin/bier to stop walking and stand still?
Questions.A: Jesus had come up to them and put his hand on the coffin/bier. (14)
Questions.Alternative: What happened that caused the men carrying the coffin to stop walking and stand still?
What happened that caused the men carrying the bier to stop walking and stand still?

Questions.Q: To whom did Jesus then speak?
Questions.A: He spoke to the [dead] young man. (14)

Questions.Q: The young man was dead. How, do you think, was he able to hear Jesus speak to him?
Questions.A: Jesus first made him alive again, then the young man heard Jesus's words.
-OR-
Jesus's power made the young man alive again through speaking the words.

Questions.Q: How did the widow and the others with her know her son was alive again?
Questions.A: He sat up, as Jesus had told him to do, and he began talking. (15)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means in 7:15 that "Jesus gave him back to his mother"?
Questions.A: Jesus put him back under his mother's care.
Questions.Note: The young man owed his life to Jesus. In wanting to show his never-ending thankfulness to Jesus, the young man might have followed the cultural practice of being like a slave to the one who had saved him. Jesus released the young man from that sense of debt and "gave him back to his mother."
-OR-
When the woman's son died, he "left" his mother. When Jesus made the young man alive again, it was as if Jesus was giving a gift to the mother.

Questions.Q: What was the people's response when they saw what had happened?
Questions.A: They all were overcome with awe/fear and praised God. (16)

Questions.Q: How did they now regard Jesus?
Questions.A: They realized that Jesus was a great prophet now living among them
and that God [had come and] was helping his people [Israel] through the things which Jesus did. (16)
Questions.Note: If the translation refers to God "visiting" his people, ask what that means when someone who speaks that language does that action in the village. If the primary meaning is to stay with someone you have not seen for a while, suggest a change in terms. The original Greek word had much more focus on coming to care for or look after someone else. The word strongly implies that the visitor takes a continuous responsibility for the one/ones being visited.

Questions.Q: How do you know that the people liked what Jesus had done?
Questions.A: They praised God/gave glory to God [for causing it] (16)
and told people all over the land of the Jews about Jesus
[that is, about what he had done, -OR- about his being a great prophet from God] (17)
Questions.Note: Key Term Check: Please look at 2:14 where this use of "glory" was already discussed. Other comments are in the note at 2:9.

Section.heading: Luke 7:18-35 Jesus described his ministry in relation to that of John the Baptizer.

Questions.Q: How did Jesus's ministry relate to/compare with John's ministry?
Questions.A: John prepared the way for Jesus and now Jesus had arrived. John had done his part, just as [the prophet Malachi] had written [Mal. 3:1] (27).
Now Jesus was ministering to needy people [just as the prophet Isaiah had said that the one sent from God would do], adding to, and finishing, [in unexpected ways] what John had started (21-23).
Questions.Alternative: How did Jesus's ministry relate to with John's ministry?
How did Jesus's ministry relate compare with John's ministry?

Questions.Q: How did people respond to what Jesus said about himself and John? His answer appeared to be different from what John and others had expected.
Questions.A: Some people [had repented and] had John baptize them. They were the same ones who now were recognizing that God was working through Jesus [and were ready to obey him]. (29) (They believed that God was doing through Jesus's ministry what they had expected through John's ministry.)
The Pharisees and the experts in the Law [of Moses] had rejected what John had told them, so they were not ready/able to accept what Jesus now taught them, either. (30)

Questions.Q: John [the Baptizer] learned about Jesus's ministry through his own disciples and had not gone to see for himself. What do you think was the reason for that?
Questions.A: King Herod had put John in prison earlier (see 3:20), so he could not go see for himself.
Questions.Alternative: John the Baptizer learned about Jesus's ministry through his own disciples and had not gone to see for himself. What do you think was the reason for that?
John learned about Jesus's ministry through his own disciples and had not gone to see for himself. What do you think was the reason for that?

Questions.Q: What was the important question that John wanted to ask Jesus?
Questions.A: Was Jesus the person whom God had said would come [as the Messiah], or were they to wait for someone else [to be the Messiah]? (19, 20)

Questions.Q: What had John's disciples seen and heard that should be a clear answer to him?
Questions.A: They had seen Jesus heal many who were sick or had evil spirits in them. (21)
He also had made the people who were blind to see (21, 22);
[he had made] those who were lame to walk (22);
[he had] healed those who had leprosy/bad skin disease, making [them] ritually clean; (22)
[he had made] those who were deaf to hear (22)
[he had] raised those who were dead [ to be alive again] (22)
and he was telling/preaching the Good News to the poor people (22). (The Good News was that God had sent the Messiah to save them and that God wanted to rule and reign in their hearts.)
Questions.Note: The meaning of the Greek verb katharizw includes both physical cleanness and ritual cleanness (see L&N entry 23.137). A different word is used in verse 21 to refer only to being healed. The translation may need to use two verbs to cover all the meaning here. (See the discussion at 5:12-16 about leprosy and people being made clean.)

Questions.Q: In what way, do you think, were all these things a clear answer to John's question?
Questions.A: They all showed that Jesus was God who had come among the people to help them (as people had been saying all over the country). (17)
-OR-
They all showed that Jesus had power from God [just as Jesus had read in the Nazareth synagogue from the prophet Isaiah's writings (See Luke 4:17-21) ].

Questions.Q: What kind of person did Jesus say would be truly happy when he thought about all the things that Jesus was doing?
Questions.A: That person is one who does not stop believing that Jesus was the Messiah whom God had sent into the world. (23)
Questions.Note: Although verse 23 is worded as a general truth and applies to everyone, Jesus was specifically directing this statement to John, just the same as verse 22. If the person answering these questions has not heard or read much about John's ministry in his/her own language, he will probably not realize that John expected the Messiah to do things differently from the way Jesus was doing them. John expected that Jesus would talk more of God's judgment, as John had done, not of God's love. That is the reason that John sent his disciples to ask the important question in verse 19.

Questions.Q: Why had people gone into the uninhabited area/wilderness/desert to see John?
Questions.A: They went because he was a prophet, even more than an ordinary prophet. (24-26)
Questions.Note: There had not been any prophet from God for over 400 years, so many people went to see John out of curiosity, as well.
Questions.Alternative: Why had people gone into the uninhabited area to see John?
Why had people gone into the wilderness to see John?
Why had people gone into the desert to see John?

Questions.Q: In what ways was John not like a reed in the wind?
Questions.A: Reeds are very ordinary plants like stiff grass, which people commonly see as the wind blows them back and forth.
-OR-

Wind blows and pushes reeds back and forth in various directions, but John always was strong to preach the same message about repenting. He did not change his message because someone, such as King Herod, did not like to hear it (see 3:19-20).

Questions.Q: In what ways was John not like a man in fine clothes?
Questions.A: People who wear expensive clothes live in large, beautiful, expensive homes, such as a king does. John lived in the desert (see Luke 1:80b).
Questions.Note: We also know that John wore clothes made from rough camel hair and ate things which he found in the wilderness/desert (see Mark 1:6).

Questions.Q: What was the purpose of John's ministry?
Questions.A: God had sent him as a messenger. John was to tell people to prepare their hearts/thoughts [to accept Jesus as the one whom God had sent to save them]. (27)

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that Jesus said that John was greater than anyone else ever born?
Questions.A: He had the important work of preparing the way for Jesus, the savior of all mankind.

Questions.Q: What do you think is a way in which whoever is least important in the kingdom of God is greater than John?
Questions.A: John, the greatest one to announce that the kingdom of God had began, was not as great as the least important person who experiences the joy and blessings of Jesus having saved him and who now obeys God as he rules and reigns in that kingdom.
-OR-
John regarded himself as a very unworthy servant (see 3:16), but every one who believes that Jesus has saved him/her is a child of God. That is greater than being a servant.
-OR-

John was in the prison and did not live to see Jesus die for mankind's sins and be raised by God to live again. The least important person who knows that those things did take place and believes that is greater (that is, blessed more) than John.
-OR-

John understood the kingdom of God as focusing on God's final, great judgment of all the world and on the circumstances which surrounded the Jews. Jesus knew that the kingdom was something inside a person, something spiritual and eternal. The least important person who understands that as Jesus did is, therefore, greater than John.

Questions.Q: How did the people, including those who collected taxes, respond when they heard Jesus speak about John like this? -OR- How did the people, including those who collected taxes, respond when they heard John preach?
Questions.A: Since John had baptized them, they all acknowledged that God's plan was right. [Part of that plan had been that John had helped them to prepare their hearts for the ministry and teaching of Jesus.] (29)
-OR-
They all agreed that God was just [in his judging their sins and in his claim on their lives], as they had previously shown by their having had John baptize them. (29)
Questions.Alternative: How did the people, including those who collected taxes, respond when they heard Jesus speak about John like this?
How did the people, including those who collected taxes, respond when they heard John preach?

Questions.Q: How did the Pharisees and the experts in the Law of Moses respond when they heard Jesus speak of John like this/when they heard John speak like this?
Questions.A: They rejected/refused to accept God's purposes/plans for themselves [in Jesus's message], as they had already shown by refusing to have John baptize them. (30)
Questions.Alternative: How did the Pharisees and the experts in the Law of Moses respond when they heard Jesus speak of John like this?
How did the Pharisees and the experts in the Law of Moses respond when they heard John speak like this?

Questions.Q: Whom did Jesus compare to little children?
Questions.A: The people alive at that time [who had seen and heard both John and Jesus]. (31)

Questions.Q: In what ways had those people acted like little children?
Questions.A: They did not like it when someone was serious and did not join in their lighthearted fun,
Neither did they like it when someone was joyous, but they felt he should be more serious. (32)

Questions.Q: To whom did Jesus refer as the one who had been serious, but the people had rejected him?
Questions.A: He referred to John the Baptizer. (33)

Questions.Q: What did some people see John do that they did not like?
Questions.A: They did not like him because he did not eat [food] and drink [wine] as they did. (33)

Questions.Q: What do you think those people meant when they said that John had a demon [in him]?
Questions.A: The way John lived (his clothes, food, home and appearance) caused people to think a demon was living in him and telling him things. (That was not true, but if it were true, the people would be right to not obey John's message, even though he said that it was from God).
Questions.Alternative: What do you think those people meant when they said that John had a demon in him?
What do you think those people meant when they said that John had a demon?

Questions.Q: To whom did Jesus refer as the one who had been joyous, but the people had rejected him also?
Questions.A: He referred to the Son of Man, (that is, he referred to himself). (34)

Questions.Q: What did some people see Jesus do that they did not like?
