Questions.A: They did not like him because he ate and drank with tax collectors and others whom they regarded as sinners [that is, people whom they thought were socially and religiously unacceptable]. (34)

Questions.Q: How could anyone know whether John's and Jesus's ministries were really part of God's wise plan or not?
Questions.A: Those people who obeyed what John and Jesus taught were the ones who lived according to God's will/wise plan for them, [not those people who rejected both John and Jesus]. (35)
-OR-
The lives of those who followed the teaching of John and Jesus showed that this was the right/correct way to be in the will of God. (35)
-OR-

People prove that God's will/wise plan is right when they live according to what John and Jesus taught, and God accepts them, [while he does not accept those people who reject what John and Jesus taught]. (35)

Section.heading: Luke 7:36-50 A sinful woman anointed Jesus with perfume.

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that Jesus allowed this woman, whom other people regarded as bad, to touch him and put perfume on him?
Questions.A: Jesus allowed her to do what she did in order to teach Simon that God forgives anyone who repents.
-OR-

She responded with great love for Jesus because she realized that she had sinned much and God had forgiven her. (The more people realize that they have sinned, the happier they are when God forgives them.) (47)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say was the reason that he had forgiven this woman?
Questions.A: She believed/had faith [in Jesus as the one who saved her from sin]. (50)
Questions.Note: If the person answers that she loved Jesus/God very much, so he forgave her, that is the wrong answer. The translator has misunderstood the meaning of verse 47. Adjust that verse when you discuss it below (see 7:44-47), then read the adjusted section of the translation and ask this Overview question again.

Questions.Q: What did Luke write about the woman who came to the Pharisee's house?
Questions.A: She was [regarded by the other people as] a sinner, that is, a person who had done many things which were obviously against the Law of Moses. (37)

Questions.Q: Why did she come to the Pharisee's house?
Questions.A: She knew that Jesus was there to eat with the Pharisee. (36-37)

Questions.Q: Knowing that, what did she do?
Questions.A: She brought a stone bottle of perfume. (37)
She stood weeping near Jesus's feet [which were stretched out behind him, as he reclined] (38),
wetting his feet with her tears (38).
Then she wiped his feet with her [long] hair (38),
repeatedly kissed them (38),
and then poured the perfume on them (38).
Questions.Note: Key Term Check: The Greek word which is translated "poured on" in verses 38 of the NIV is translated "anointed" twice in verse 46. It is the same Greek word that Luke used in 4:18, but here the focus is on the literal pouring, not the figurative use for appointing. See "anoint" in KBT.

Questions.Q: In verses 38 and 45 we heard the words "she kissed his feet". What, do you think, was the woman actually doing?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: She touched or pressed her pursed lips on his feet as a sign of her affection and reverence/respect for him.
Questions.Note: If the culture of the translation does not show affection or reverence with the kissing action, it is more important to keep that purpose clear, rather than worry about describing the exact action of the woman. In verse 45, Jesus referred to the kissing action as a sign of greeting, though not done to the feet. It would be best if one action could stand for both, as in Jesus's time, but that may not be possible.

Questions.Q: What did the Pharisee think about this woman?
Questions.A: He thought of her as a person who had sinned much [and everyone knew it]. (39)

Questions.Q: What did the Pharisee think about Jesus because he did not forbid the woman to do this?
Questions.A: He thought that Jesus was not a prophet because he allowed a sinful person to do this for him. (The Pharisee expected that a true prophet would have knowledge from God about the woman's bad actions in the past.) (39)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do to help the Pharisee Simon understand the meaning of the woman's actions?
Questions.A: He told a parable about two men who owed another person money. (41-42)

Questions.Q: Tell me the parable.
Questions.A: Two men owed money to another person. One owed much more than the other. However, neither man could repay that money, so the moneylender forgave each man his debt. (41-42)

Questions.Q: Which man did Simon say would love the moneylender more than the other man did?
Questions.A: He said that it probably was the one who had the bigger debt canceled. (43)

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that would be true?
Questions.A: The one who had been forgiven much would show it more than the person who had been forgiven less.

Questions.Q: If Simon had been a good Jewish host, he would have done certain things when Jesus arrived. What things did Jesus say that Simon had not done for him?
Questions.A: Simon had not given any water to Jesus for [washing] his feet. (44)
He had not given Jesus a kiss [of traditional greeting]. (45)
He had not anointed Jesus's head with [olive] oil [to show hospitality]. (46)

Questions.Q: Which person showed the greater love for Jesus, Simon or the woman?
Questions.A: Jesus indicated that the woman did.

Questions.Q: On what basis could anyone know that the woman's many sins had already been forgiven by Jesus?
Questions.A: They could see that she loved [Jesus] very much, [as such a person might do]. (47)

Questions.Q: What do you think that Jesus meant when he implied that Simon had been forgiven few sins?
Questions.A: Simon may have thought that he did not sin much, so he had not ask God to forgive him much. (Simon had not realized how much God had forgiven him, so his response of love was less than the woman's response.)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell the woman about her sins?
Questions.A: They all had been forgiven [by him]. (48)

Questions.Q: What was the reason that Jesus had forgiven her many sins?
Questions.A: She believed/had faith [that Jesus could save her and cause her to have a right relationship with God]. (50)

Questions.Q: What do you think this peace is that Jesus said would be in/with the woman as she left him?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It is peace which God gives to a person who has trusted Him/who has believed in His Son. This peace is a calm heart/spirit free from worry when we face God because he has already forgiven our sins.
Questions.Note: See "peace" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think this peace is that Jesus said would be in the woman as she left him?
What do you think this peace is that Jesus said would be with the woman as she left him?

Questions.Q: When Jesus told the woman that her sins had been forgiven, what did the other people there think?
Questions.A: They knew that only God could forgive sins, so they thought that Jesus was taking the place of God [and should be punished (see 5:21) ]. (49)

Section.heading: Luke 8:1-3 Some women traveled with Jesus and his disciples to help them.

Questions.Q: Tell me what Jesus was doing at that time.
Questions.A: He traveled to many towns and villages preaching the Good News that the Kingdom of God [had already come/begun]. (1)
Questions.Note: See 7:22 above, where "Good News" was last mentioned.

Questions.Q: Who traveled with him?
Questions.A: His twelve apostles/disciples traveled with him. (1)
Also with him were some women from whom Jesus had made evil spirits leave or whom he had healed of other diseases. (2)

Questions.Q: How did Jesus and his disciples have enough money for the things they needed?
Questions.A: The women used some of their own money to help them. (3)

Section.heading: Luke 8:4-15 Jesus told a parable about a man sowing seed in his field.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus teach the people by means of this story about seeds and different types of ground?
Questions.A: Different people believe God's message [about the savior] in differing amounts. Some do not want to believe it, others only believe a little bit, and others are ready to believe everything God has said. Only those people whose hearts are ready [to receive and obey Jesus's teaching] will experience the fruit/benefits/good things that will come from believing. (12-15)

Questions.Q: Tell me what happened to the seeds in the story Jesus told.
Questions.A: Some seeds fell on the path. [People and animals] walked on them and then birds ate them. (5)
Some seeds fell on rock. It came up, but withered because there was not enough water. (6)
Some seeds fell where thorns grew. The thorns grew [big] and choked the plants. (7)
Some seeds fell on good ground and produced very much/a hundred times as much new seed. (8)

Questions.Q: How did the man plant that seed?
Questions.A: He scattered the seed over the top of the ground. (5)
Questions.Note: If the people who will use this translation do not plant seed in this way, a footnote may be helpful to explain that scattering seed is appropriate in many cultures. The man was not being foolish when he scattered the seed.

Questions.Q: When Jesus finished telling the story he said that the people with ears should listen. Every person has ears. What do you think that he meant?
Questions.A: He meant that everyone should pay attention [and think carefully about the hidden meaning].

Questions.Q: Why did the disciples ask Jesus to explain the parable?
Questions.A: They did not understand the meaning of the picture language. (9)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say was hidden in this parable?
Questions.A: The secrets about the kingdom of God, that is, how God planned to save people and then rule and reign as the one who is most important in their lives. (10)

Questions.Q: To whom would Jesus explain the meaning of the parable, and to whom would he not explain it?
Questions.A: He would explain it to the disciples, but not to the other people. (10)
Questions.Note: The Greek word order shows that Jesus emphasized the contrast between the two groups of people. The pronoun which refers to the disciples was put first in its part of the sentence and the pronoun which refers to the other people was put first in the second part of the sentence. It says, "To you [God] has given ..., but to the rest [it is] in parables." If the translator is able to show a strong contrast between the two groups in the wording of his translation, it would be good to do that here.

Questions.Q: Why were Jesus's disciples able to understand the meaning after he explained it, but the other people did not understand?
Questions.A: Because the disciples believed that Jesus was God and they were following him and learning more about God, he caused/allowed them to understand. (10)

Questions.Q: Other people also saw Jesus do miracles and heard him tell the good news from God. What do you think was the reason that they not understand what they saw and heard?
Questions.A: They did not believe that God had sent Jesus to be their savior. Therefore, God did not allow them to understand. They would not have followed God better, even if they had understood the meaning.
-OR-

Jesus quoted what the prophet Isaiah had written. He implied that the same situation was happening again. The Jews living at the time of Jesus did not want to pay attention to God's message just like their forefathers in the time of Isaiah had not paid attention to Isaiah's message from God. (Jesus also implied that the end result for those who did not believe that God had sent him would be the same as it had been for their unbelieving forefathers. Their cities would be destroyed and their people would be scattered. [See Isa. 6:9-12.])

Questions.Q: What did the seed in the parable represent?
Questions.A: It was the Word of God/God's message [about saving us by means of Jesus]. (11)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say that the different types of ground represented?
Questions.A: They were the people who heard/listened/paid attention [to God's message].
-AND/OR-
They are the people who hear/listen/pay attention [to God's message]. (12-15)

Questions.Q: What happened to the different listeners?
Questions.A: Some heard God's message, but the people did not pay attention. Then the devil took what they had heard away, that is, he made them forget all about it. (12)
Some heard it, received it excitedly and believed it for a while. But when troubles came to them, they stopped believing it. (13)

Some heard it, but the good things of this world became more important to them than God's message and took over its place in their lives. They thought about the things in this world more and more and they thought about God less and less. Before very long, other people could tell by their words and actions that they did not believe in God any more. (14)

Some who were honest and good heard it and kept it in their hearts and minds. Even through troubles, they continued to believe it. Finally, other people saw many good things that pleased God in their lives. (15)

Section.heading: Luke 8:16-18 Jesus used a lamp to explain that he would not hide the truth about the kingdom of God.

Questions.Q: What do you think that Jesus wanted to teach the people by means of this story about a lamp and its light?
Questions.A: The purpose of a lamp is to help people by making light for them to see clearly. Jesus was like the lamp that God had put on earth to make the truths about the kingdom of God clear to those who listened carefully.

Questions.Q: Why do people light lamps?
Questions.A: People light lamps to give light when they cannot see otherwise. (16)

Questions.Q: What does a person do with a lamp after he lights it?
Questions.A: He puts/places it out where it can be useful, as on a lamp holder. He does not hide it under anything. (16)

Questions.Q: When the lamp is lit, what will happen to things that a person could not see in the dark?
Questions.A: The person (and others who are nearby) will see them clearly. They will not be hidden any more. (17)

Questions.Q: Why should a person listen well to what Jesus taught us about the kingdom of God?
Questions.A: The person who understands/believes [even a small amount] will receive [help from God] to understand/believe more. (18)

Questions.Q: What will happen to a person who does not have any understanding/faith?
Questions.A: [God] will even take away what little understanding/faith he thought that he had. (18)
Questions.Alternative: What will happen to a person who does not have any understanding?
What will happen to a person who does not have any faith?

Section.heading: Luke 8:19-21 Jesus's mother and brothers come to see him.

Questions.Q: Who came to see Jesus?
Questions.A: His mother and brothers came to see him. (19)

Questions.Q: Why did someone need to tell Jesus about them?
Questions.A: The crowd of people was so large that they could not get near Jesus. (19)

Questions.Q: Whom did Jesus say he regarded the same as his mother and brothers?
Questions.A: Those [people] who hear God's word and do [what it says] are as important to him as his blood relatives.
-OR-
Those [people] who hear God's word and do [what it says] are more important to him than if they were his blood relatives. (21)

Section.heading: Luke 8:22-25 Jesus commanded a storm on the sea to be calm, and it obeyed him.

Questions.Q: Tell me what happened to Jesus and his disciples in their boat.
Questions.A: (The answer should cover the basic outline of the story, including Jesus rebuking the storm and the lake as well as rebuking his disciples. Any part which the person does not mention can be reviewed by using a specific question from below.)

Questions.Q: What can we learn about Jesus from what Luke wrote about the men in the boat?
Questions.A: Jesus showed that he had authority over all [the forces] of nature, [such as the wind/storm/waves].

Questions.Q: Where were Jesus and his disciples going in a boat?
Questions.A: They were going to the other side of the lake. (22)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do while they sailed their boat on that lake?
Questions.A: He fell asleep. (23)

Questions.Q: What happened while Jesus slept?
Questions.A: A terrible windstorm blew down [from the surrounding mountains] onto the lake. (23)
The boat began to fill [with water] and the men were in danger [of drowning/dying]. (23)

Questions.Q: What did the disciples do and say to Jesus?
Questions.A: They woke Jesus and told him they were about to be destroyed [by the storm]. (24a)

Questions.Q: What did the disciples think would be the final outcome of this storm?
Questions.A: They thought that they would violently die [by drowning]. (23-24a)

Key Term Check: The Greek word that describes what the disciples thought would happen to them focuses on the destruction and total ruin of people or objects. It is the same word that was used in 5:37 to describe what happened to the wineskins. See "destroy, perish, (be lost" in KBT.)

Questions.Q: After the disciples woke Jesus, what did he do?
Questions.A: He sternly commanded/rebuked the wind and the violent, tossing waves (and the storm stopped, and all was calm again). (24)

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that Jesus asked/talked about the disciples' faith?
Questions.A: They had acted just as though they did not believe that he had God's power to do whatever he wanted to do. // They had seen Jesus do great things by God's power, but they did not trust him to save himself and them now. // Their reaction to the storm was the same as the reaction of people who had no faith in God. (25) (See "faith" in KBT in the "believe" entry.)
Questions.Alternative: What do you think was the reason that Jesus asked about the disciples' faith?
What do you think was the reason that Jesus talked about the disciples' faith?

Questions.Q: Why were the disciples amazed at what had happened?
Questions.A: They had seen Jesus use [God's/his] authority over the winds and the water, and they did what he told them to do. (25) (They knew that ordinary people did not have any control over the natural elements.)

Questions.Q: The storm had ended. Why were the disciples still afraid?
Questions.A: They realized that they were in the presence of one who had supernatural power to command even the winds and the water to obey him. He was not an ordinary person, as they were. (25)

Section.heading: Luke 8:26-39 Jesus made many demons/evil spirits leave a man.

Questions.Q: Jesus cast many demons out of one particular man. What can we learn about Jesus from that?
Questions.A: Jesus showed that he had authority over all the fierce demons, [even those outside of Jewish territory].
-OR-
Jesus wanted to help all people, even those who were not Jews and who did not live among the Jews.
Questions.Note: These people had the same response to Jesus doing a miracle among them as his disciples had on the lake a short time earlier. Both groups were afraid of Jesus's great power being present among them. These Gerasene/Gadarene/Gergesene people rejected Jesus, but the man who was healed, and the disciples earlier, believed that God had sent Jesus.

Questions.Q: Where is the area where Jesus [and his disciples] went ashore?
Questions.A: It is on the other side of the lake across from Galilee [province], in the land of the Gerasene/Gadarene/Gergesene [people]. (26)
Questions.Note: You may want to note in a reference to a map or in a footnote that Jesus was now outside the area the Jews regarded as their own land. The people to whom he talked there were not Jews and they did not worship the true God.
Questions.Alternative: Where is the area where Jesus and his disciples went ashore?
Where is the area where Jesus went ashore?

Questions.Q: Whom did Jesus meet when he went ashore?
Questions.A: He met a demon-possessed man from the [nearby] town. (27)

Questions.Q: What did Luke tell us about this man?
Questions.A: The man was from the town [of Gerasa nearby]. (27)
He had not worn clothes for a long time. (27)
He did not live in a house, but stayed among the tombs. (27)
When he saw Jesus [coming], he cried out, (28)
dropped to the ground, lying flat in front of Jesus [as a sign that he submitted himself to Jesus] (28)
and shouted out in a loud voice. (28)
Many times the demons had seized/controlled the man. (29)
[People] tried to restrain the man by tying his hands and feet with chains (29)
and then guarded him, (29)
but many times the man had broken the chains (29)
and the demon had driven him into a region with no inhabitants/into the wilderness. (29)

Questions.Q: What did the man shout in the loud voice to Jesus?
Questions.A: He shouted, "What do you want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I plead with/appeal to you, do not torture me!" (28)
Questions.Note: The question is a rhetorical one. The man was not asking Jesus for an answer. He was implying that, because Jesus was so different from himself in a spiritual sense, Jesus should leave the man and the spirits in him alone.

Questions.Q: Why did the man say this?
Questions.A: Jesus had already commanded the evil spirit/demon to come out of the man. (29)
Questions.Note: It is also implied that the demon was saying that he and Jesus had nothing in common, so he did not want anything to do with Jesus, who might punish him.

Questions.Q: How was it, do you think, that the man already knew Jesus's name and that he was the son of God?
Questions.A: Demons know who God is, and who God's son is, [because God has authority over them].

Questions.Q: What did the demon say his name was?
Questions.A: His name was Legion/Thousands/A great many. (30)

Questions.Q: Why did the demon say his name was that?
Questions.A: He said that because many demons had entered the man. (30)

Questions.Q: What did the demons keep on urging/earnestly ask/strongly request Jesus not to do to them?
Questions.A: They did not want him to command them to go to the Abyss, the deep hole with no bottom. (31)
Questions.Note: Key Term Check: See "abyss" in KBT in the "hell, Hades, abyss" entry. It is the place where God imprisoned evil spirits and they suffer torment ever since he expelled them from heaven (see Rev. 20:3). They will not leave there until the Judgment (see Matt. 8:29). If the term is not clear in the text, use a footnote or glossary item to explain about this place.
Questions.Alternative: What did the demons keep on urging Jesus not to do to them?
What did the demons earnestly ask Jesus not to do to them?
What did the demons strongly request Jesus not to do to them?

Questions.Q: Where did those demons want Jesus to send them instead?
Questions.A: They wanted to go into the herd of [a great] many pigs which was feeding on the mountainside. (32)

Questions.Q: What happened after Jesus permitted those demons to go into that herd of pigs?
Questions.A: The herd of pigs then rushed/charged/stampeded down the steep bank/slope into the lake and drowned. (33)

Questions.Q: What did the men who looked after those pigs do?
Questions.A: When they saw what happened [to the pigs], they ran away through the countryside and town telling the news [about the pigs drowning]. (34)

Questions.Q: What did the people who heard the men's report do?
Questions.A: They went out to see what had happened. (35)

Questions.Q: What did those people see when they came to where Jesus was?
Questions.A: They found the man who had earlier had demons in him now sitting near Jesus's feet. (35)
He was dressed and he was thinking clearly. (35)

Questions.Q: How did they feel after seeing the man act so differently than before?
Questions.A: They were afraid. (35)

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that they were afraid?
Questions.A: They were afraid because they knew it meant that Jesus had great power to drive out those demons from the man.

Questions.Q: How did those people learn about what had happened to the man who had demons in him?
Questions.A: The people who had seen [Jesus] heal him told them. (36)

Questions.Q: Why did all the people who lived in that area ask Jesus to leave?
Questions.A: They were completely afraid [of Jesus's great power which they thought might do more harm than good]. (37)

Questions.Q: How did Jesus respond to their request?
Questions.A: He got into the boat and left. (37)

Questions.Q: What did the man who earlier had demons in him want to do?
Questions.A: He pleaded with/appealed to Jesus to allow him to go with Jesus [in the boat]. (38)

Questions.Q: When the man was asking to go with Jesus, where do you think Jesus was?
Questions.A: Jesus was still there in the man's country, walking to the boat or even getting into the boat.
Questions.Note: The last word of 8:37 in the Greek is "he-returned", and in the NIV, "... and left." But what happened in 8:38-39a took place before Jesus actually left the man. To help respondents avoid becoming confused about the order of events, combine the numbering for verses 37-39 and describe the events in the order of verse 38, 39a, 37, and then 39b.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell the man to do?
Questions.A: He told him to return home and tell [people] what God had done for him. (39)

Questions.Q: What did that man do after Jesus left?
Questions.A: He did what Jesus had told him to do, that is, he left there, [went home,] and proclaimed [to people] all over the town what Jesus had done for him. (39)

Section.heading: Luke 8:40-56 Jesus healed a sick woman and raised a dead girl to live again.

Questions.Q: What can we learn about Jesus from his helping the sick woman and the dead girl?
Questions.A: Jesus showed that he had authority to heal people who were very sick. He could cause people who had died to live again, [both things that no one else had power to do]. (43-44, 49 and 54-55)

Questions.Q: From where did Jesus and his disciples return?
Questions.A: They had been across the lake with the Gerasene/Gadarene/Gergesene people. (26, 37)

Questions.Q: To where, do you think, did Jesus and his disciples return?
Questions.A: They returned to Galilee province, as both of the towns which were last named by Luke were in Galilee. (See the reference in 7:1 to Capernaum and in 7:11 to Nain.)

Questions.Q: How did people greet Jesus when he arrived back in Galilee?
Questions.A: They welcomed him./They were happy he had returned./They were waiting eagerly for him. (40)

Questions.Q: What did the man Jairus do when he came to Jesus?
Questions.A: He dropped to the ground, lying flat at Jesus's feet and earnestly asked for help.
He kept on urging/strongly requested Jesus to go to his house. (41)

Questions.Q: Why did Jairus want Jesus to do that?
Questions.A: His only daughter was dying. (42a)

Questions.Q: Where was Jesus going?
Questions.A: He was on his way to Jairus's house just as Jairus had asked him to do in verse 41.

Questions.Q: What happened on the way to Jairus's house?
Questions.A: The crowd of people was pressing up against him (42b),
and a woman came up behind him (44),
touched the edge of his outer clothing (44),
and was healed (44).

Questions.Q: What was the woman's sickness?
Questions.A: For twelve years she had suffered from excessive [menstrual] bleeding. (43)

Questions.Q: What had the woman done to try to be healed?
Questions.A: She had paid all her [money] to doctors [to help her], but no one had been able to heal her/stop the bleeding. (43)
Questions.Note: Many Bible scholars do not believe that Luke wrote the words that we find in some manuscripts about paying doctors. Therefore, the translator may not have included it in this translation, or it may be set apart by special use of punctuation. If those words are not in the translation, then skip this question.

Questions.Q: Why did Jesus ask, "Who touched me?"
Questions.A: He knew that [healing] power had gone out from him. (46)

Questions.Q: Why did Peter object?
Questions.A: The crowd of people was surrounding and bumping into Jesus. [He did not think that it was possible to distinguish one accidental touch from another.] (45)

Questions.Q: Why did the woman finally come to Jesus and tell the reason for touching him?
Questions.A: She realized that she could not remain anonymous, that Jesus was not going to ignore this. (47)

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that she trembled as she came to Jesus?
Questions.A: She had to tell her story in front of all those people. (47)
-OR-
She feared that Jesus would be upset with her or even take away her healing [because she had not asked, and then she had hesitated to speak when Jesus asked his question].
Questions.Note: The woman was also ritually unclean, so she was not to touch any man (see Lev. 15:19, 25 and 19:22).

Questions.Q: Jesus was not a father, but he called this woman by the title "Daughter". What do you think that he meant by calling her "Daughter"?
Questions.A: Though she was not his real daughter, he wanted to show her that he cared about her and was not angry with her.
Questions.Note: "Daughter" may not be the term used by the culture of the translation to show this same meaning. Use a culturally appropriate kin term or title for Jesus to address this woman. He wanted to show that he was friendly and caring as a father would be when helping his daughter.
Questions.Alternative: Jesus was not a father, but he called this woman by the title, "Daughter". What do you think that he meant by calling her "Daughter"?

Questions.Q: What had the woman shown by wanting to touch Jesus's clothing?
Questions.A: She had faith/She believed that Jesus could save/heal her [by God's power]. (48)

Questions.Q: What happened while Jesus was still speaking to the woman?
Questions.A: Someone came from Jairus's [house/family] with a message [for Jairus]. (49)

Questions.Q: What was the message the person brought?
Questions.A: "Your daughter is dead. Don't inconvenience/cause any problem for the teacher any more." (49)

Questions.Q: Who was the teacher whom the messenger was talking about?
Questions.A: The teacher was Jesus.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus encourage Jairus to do after he heard the messenger?
Questions.A: He wanted Jairus not to be afraid, but to believe that [he/God] could still help his daughter be well again. (50)

Questions.Q: Who went with Jesus into Jairus's house/the room where the girl was?
Questions.A: Peter, James, John and the child's parents entered with Jesus. (51)
Questions.Alternative: Who went with Jesus into Jairus's house room where the girl was?
Who went with Jesus into Jairus's the room where the girl was?

Questions.Q: What were other people at Jairus's house doing?
Questions.A: They were wailing and mourning/showing their sorrow for the [dead] girl. (52)
Questions.Note: One of the Greek words for what the people were doing describes their cultural practice of showing sorrow by beating on one's own chest. If the culture of the translation has words for both the crying about a person's death and for a cultural practice always associated with showing one's sadness, both of those terms should be used here.

Questions.Q: Why did Jesus tell those people to stop wailing?
Questions.A: He said that the child was not dead, but sleeping. (52)

Questions.Q: Why did the people laugh at/make fun of Jesus?
Questions.A: They knew that the child was dead [so they assumed that Jesus was joking or did not know the truth]. (53)
Questions.Alternative: Why did the people laugh at Jesus?
Why did the people make fun of Jesus?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do with the girl?
Questions.A: Holding her hand, he spoke loudly and told her to get up. (54)

Questions.Q: What happened then?
Questions.A: The child's spirit/breath returned into her body and she immediately stood up. (55)

Questions.Q: What did the girl's parents think about what had just happened?
Questions.A: They were greatly astounded. (56)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell the girl's parents to do?
Questions.A: He ordered them not to tell anyone what had happened. (56)
(He also had told someone to give the girl some food to eat. We assume it was her parents who did it.) (55)

Section.heading: Luke 9:1-6 Jesus sent out the twelve apostles.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus send the twelve apostles to do on his behalf?
Questions.A: They were to preach/proclaim [that] God was restoring his kingdom [in the words and work of Jesus].
They were also to heal the sick. (2)
Questions.Note: This "healing of the sick" probably included casting out demons from people who were bothered/controlled by them.

Questions.Q: How were the twelve apostles going to be able to do the great things that Jesus had been doing?
Questions.A: He gave them power and authority to drive/cast out all demons and to cure diseases. (1)

Questions.Q: What did the apostles do when they went around to villages?
Questions.A: They announced the Good News and healed people everywhere. (6)
Questions.Note: The NIV uses the words "preaching the gospel" in this verse. This translates the Greek word which means "tell good news". The translator should use the same wording here that he used in 3:18 and 4:18 to talk about this message. It was the same message which John and Jesus had preached. (See "gospel" in KBT.)

Questions.Q: What were the apostles to take with them on their travels?
Questions.A: They were to take nothing; no walking stick, no bag, no money, no food and no extra clothes. (3)

Questions.Q: Those are all things people take with them when they go on a long walk to another place, even today. In what way, do you think, would the disciples get the things they might need?
Questions.A: Jesus expected them to trust God to provide for their needs. (They really would have to begin allowing God to rule in their lives.)

Questions.Q: Where were the disciples to stay when they visited a village?
Questions.A: They should stay the whole time they were at that village in the first house where they were welcomed. (4)

Questions.Q: What were they to do if the town's people did not welcome them?
Questions.A: They were to leave that town. As they were leaving, they were to shake off the dust from their feet. (5)

Questions.Q: What would that action do besides help clean their feet?
Questions.A: It would show the town's people that the apostles were separating themselves from them. (5)
It would show that the apostles didn't want even dust from that place to go with them [in the work Jesus had given them]. (5)
It would show that the one who had sent the apostles, Jesus/God, would be angry with those people because of their unbelief. (5)
Questions.Note: This custom was practiced by the Jews when they left a non-Jewish/Gentile town because just being there would make the Jews ritually unclean. Then they could not worship at the temple. If the apostles did this in Jewish villages and towns, townspeople would know that they were being treated as people who rejected God.

Section.heading: Luke 9:7-9 King Herod was confused about who Jesus was.

Questions.Q: Why was King Herod confused about who Jesus was?
Questions.A: He had heard about all that had happened [regarding Jesus's preaching and miracles]. (7)
Some [people] were saying that Jesus might be John [the Baptizer] whom [God] had raised from the dead. (7)
But Herod had seen John's head after [he (Herod) had ordered someone] to cut it off/sever it from his body, so he did not know who Jesus really was. (9)

Questions.Q: What were other people saying about who Jesus was?
Questions.A: Some said that he was [the prophet] Elijah who had reappeared, while still others said that [God] had raised from the dead one of the [other] prophets of long ago. (8)
Questions.Note: Elijah had not died, but God had taken him straight up to heaven (see 2 Kings 2). Be sure the translation does not say that Elijah had "come back to life again".

Questions.Q: What did King Herod want to do to end his confusion?
Questions.A: He tried to meet/see Jesus. (9)

Section.heading: Luke 9:10-17 Jesus fed more than five thousand people.

Questions.Q: Often many people sit down together to eat at a banquet/feast. What did you hear in this story that would cause you to say that a miracle happened when those 5,000 people ate together with Jesus?
Questions.A: Jesus had only five bread rolls and two fish, but he, being the son of God, caused them to multiply/increase into enough pieces to satisfy all those people. (16)
Even more, they still had twelve basketfuls left over [uneaten]. (The leftover food was more than they had at the beginning [13], before Jesus blessed the food [16].) (13-17)
Questions.Alternative: Often many people sit down together to eat at a banquet. What did you hear in this story that would cause you to say that a miracle happened when those 5,000 people ate together with Jesus?
Often many people sit down together to eat at a feast. What did you hear in this story that would cause you to say that a miracle happened when those 5,000 people ate together with Jesus?

Questions.Q: What did the apostles do when they returned from the work Jesus had sent them to do?
Questions.A: They reported to Jesus what they had done [in their time away from him]. (10)

Questions.Q: Why did Jesus take the apostles to an area near the town of Bethsaida?
Questions.A: He wanted to go somewhere away from all the people and only be with these twelve men. (10)

Questions.Q: What happened while they were at that place?
Questions.A: When people found out where Jesus was, they followed him [to that place]. (11)

Questions.Q: How did Jesus treat the crowd that followed him there?
Questions.A: He welcomed them, spoke to them about the kingdom of God and healed those who needed to be healed. (11)

Questions.Q: Why did the twelve apostles want Jesus to send the people away?
Questions.A: The people needed to go where others lived (in surrounding villages or on farms) in order to have a place to stay [for the night] and in order to find enough food to eat. This was necessary because they were in an uninhabited place and it was getting late in the day. (12)

Questions.Q: Did Jesus send all those people away like his disciples suggested to him?
Questions.A: No, he did not.

Questions.Q: What did he do?
Questions.A: He told his disciples to give food to the people. (13)

Questions.Q: How much food did the disciples have altogether?
Questions.A: They had five bread rolls and two [smoked/cooked] fish. (13)
Questions.Note: The "bread" of the Middle Eastern cultures is not the size or shape of the loaf of bread common among Westerners. The word used for "fish" either should imply small ones that one person could easily eat at one meal, or it should not imply anything about size. The same story in John 6:9 makes it clear they were small fish or only portions of fish that were ready to be eaten with the bread. (See L&N entry 5.16.)

Questions.Q: How many people were there with the disciples?
Questions.Note: 5,000 people were there, counting only the men. (14a)

There were probably much fewer women and children present than men because it was far from where people normally lived. Also remember that the Jews began calling a boy a man after he had been through the ritual at the temple at the age of 12 or 13, as Jesus had done. Each culture begins to use the term "man" after different events and different ages. The terms used here should cover all the males aged 13 and older. For example, the Hewa translation in Papua New Guinea used the words "5,000 married-men and mature-boys".

Questions.Q: Do you think that the disciples wanted to go somewhere to get enough food for all those people?
Questions.A: No, they did not. They said earlier that no one lived nearby. It was an impossible option. (Besides, they would need a lot of money and more than 12 men to carry enough food back to that place. See Mark 6:35-37.)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell the disciples to do about this problem?
Questions.A: They were to have the people get ready to eat by siting/relaxing [on the ground] in groups of fifty. (14b)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do about food for all those people?
Questions.A: He took the five bread rolls and two fish, and (16)
while looking up towards heaven, he blessed the food, (16)
then broke it [into pieces] (16)
and gave [the pieces] to his disciples to distribute to the crowd. (16)

Questions.Q: How do we know there was enough food for all those people?
Questions.A: Luke wrote that all the people ate enough to be satisfied, and
[the disciples] carried away twelve basketfuls of leftover food pieces. (17)

Section.heading: Luke 9:18-20 Peter said that Jesus was the Christ sent by God.

Questions.Q: What do you think that Peter's answer to Jesus showed about the disciples?
Questions.A: They now recognized/believed that he was the Christ, the one whom God had sent to save his people as he had promised. (20)

Questions.Q: What was Jesus doing before he asked his disciples these questions?
Questions.A: He was praying alone/by himself. (18)

Questions.Q: What were his questions about?
Questions.A: His questions were about what the crowds of people and the disciples were saying about Jesus. (18, 20)

Questions.Q: What were other people saying about Jesus?
Questions.A: They said that he was John the Baptizer, or Elijah or one of the [other] prophets of long ago who had risen from the dead. (19)

Questions.Q: Who did the disciples say that Jesus was?
Questions.A: Peter said that Jesus was God's Christ, (the person God had set apart for coming to this earth to save his people). (20)
Questions.Note: See "Christ, Messiah" in KBT.

The Greek word order shows us that Jesus was making a strong contrast between the crowd's thinking and the disciples' thinking. It would be good if the translation could show that contrast. In English, it might be like this: "And you? Who do you say that I am?"

Questions.Q: Jesus strongly warned/sternly commanded his disciples not to tell anyone what they knew about him. What did they know?
Questions.A: They knew that he was the Christ/Messiah. (20)
Questions.Alternative: Jesus strongly warned his disciples not to tell anyone what they knew about him. What did they know?
Jesus sternly commanded his disciples not to tell anyone what they knew about him. What did they know?

Section.heading: Luke 9:21-27 Jesus said that he would die, but God would raise him to live again.

Questions.Q: How would people treat Jesus?
Questions.A: People would make him suffer; they would reject him [and his claim to be the Christ] and kill him. (22)

Questions.Q: How would God treat Jesus?
Questions.A: God would raise him back to life again (three days after that). (22)

Questions.Q: How should a person act who truly wants to follow Jesus?
Questions.A: He must do as Jesus did, being committed each day to God, even when the things of this world look like they will make that person very happy or when people might make fun of him because he believes in Jesus as the savior. Each day that person must deny his human desire to take good care of himself by focusing on getting more and more possessions. Owning all the things in the world will not keep him from dying or being killed. He must do as Jesus did, even if it leads to suffering, rejection or being killed. That will lead him to the kind of life God wants him to have. (23-25)

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that Jesus told the disciples not to tell anyone yet about this?
Questions.A: He didn't want them to tell other people yet because the Jews had wrongly understood what kind of a savior the Messiah would be. He needed more time to teach more Jews the truth about the savior whom God had now sent.

Questions.Q: Whom was Jesus talking about when he spoke about the Son of Man?
Questions.A: He was talking about himself.
Questions.Note: See comments at 5:24.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say would happen to him?
Questions.A: He must suffer many things/in many ways/much. (22)
The elders [of the Jews] and the chief priests and the teachers of the Law/scribes would reject him/his claim to be the Messiah. (22)
People would kill him. (22)
[God] would raise him [from the dead/to live again] on the third day [of his being dead]. (22)

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that Jesus named those three specific groups of people who would reject him and what he had to say about himself?
Questions.A: Those three groups were the leaders who together decided what was right or wrong for the Jews to do or think. They would influence all the other people as to what they should think about Jesus or do to him.
Key Term Check:
Questions.Note: The elders (of the Jews) were the older and wiser Jewish men who met to discuss problems in their Jewish society and culture.

The chief priests were the leaders among the priests at the temple in Jerusalem. They decided everything that had to do with worship of God and use of the temple grounds. (See "Chief Priest, High Priest" in KBT.)
The teachers of the Law/scribes were the ones who knew best how to apply the laws God had told to Moses in everyday Jewish life. (See the answer back at 5:17.)

Questions.Q: What must one do if he wants to follow Jesus?
Questions.A: He should deny himself,
take up his cross each day and
follow Jesus. (23)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to deny oneself?
Questions.A: It means that a person does not think only about himself and those things which make him happy. (Jesus wanted people to think about how to please God and be totally committed to him first.)

Questions.Q: At the time Jesus lived, when a person carried a cross, what do you think it meant?
Questions.A: It meant that person was on his way to die (by being nailed on crossed timbers until he could not breathe anymore).
Key Term Check: See "cross, crucify" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for people today to take up/carry one's cross?
Questions.A: It means that a person must accept whatever suffering comes because he is one who follows Jesus. He must be willing to die in order to remain faithful to God, even die in a humiliating way like those who died on a cross.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think it means for people today to take up one's cross?
What do you think it means for people today to carry one's cross?

Questions.Q: How often must the person who follows Jesus put his focus on God, not himself?
Questions.A: He must do it every day. Every day he must be willing to suffer whatever happens to him because he has put God first in his life. (This is not an action that a person does once and then forgets about it.)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say would happen to the person who wanted to save his own life?
Questions.A: He said that person would lose it. (24)

Questions.Q: That sounds like a contradiction in the way that people understand life and death. What do you think that Jesus meant by that?
Questions.A: The person who does not do as Jesus just said in verse 23 will lose his chance to have the eternal life that Jesus promised elsewhere in the gospels.
He may also die physically just as Jesus said that he would in verse 22.
Questions.Note: Luke had not written anything about eternal life up to this point in his gospel. Therefore, if the respondent has not been a worshiping Christian for a long time, he will find that this question is impossible to answer. He has no background to fit it into, and the words are a paradox. Do not be critical of anyone's answer to this question.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say would happen when a person loses his life because he follows Jesus?
Questions.A: He said that person would save it. (24)

Questions.Q: This, too, sounds like a contradiction in terms. What do you think that Jesus meant by saying that?
Questions.A: He was not talking about a person's physical life, so he must have been referring again to spiritual life that is eternal. The person who does as Jesus said in verse 23 will receive the eternal life that Jesus promised.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about a person who gains control or becomes the owner of everything in the world?
Questions.A: He has gained nothing important if it means that he loses or gives up his own spirit [for all of eternity]. // He has given up the most important, eternal thing in order to have pleasure in this short life. The trade is not worth it, Jesus said. (25)

Questions.Q: What will happen to the person who is ashamed when other people know he follows Jesus and obeys what he taught?
Questions.A: The Son of Man, Jesus, will be ashamed of him/her when he comes [back to this earth from heaven, not from the grave,] surrounded by his [own] glory and the glory of the Father and the holy angels. (26)
Key Term Check: See the discussion about "glory" at 2:9 and 2:14.

Questions.Q: Who is this "Father" Jesus was talking about?
Questions.A: He is Jesus's father, God, who is also our spiritual father. (See 6:35-36.)

Questions.Q: Luke has not written anything in the earlier parts of this book about Jesus going away and coming back. To what, do you think, was he referring?
Questions.A: Jesus told us elsewhere in the gospels that one day he will come back from heaven to judge all the people on the earth. (See Matt. 16:27; 25:31-47; Mark 13:32-37; Luke 21:8-28.)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say would happen before some of the people who were standing there would die?
Questions.A: Some of them would see/experience/give their attention to the kingdom of God.
Questions.Note: The Greek word translated "see" is used in many contexts, from ordinary seeing with one's eyes to meanings which include more and more mental understanding which becomes clearer. These would include meanings such as, "pay attention to", "take notice of" and "be concerned about". It also is used figuratively to mean "experience" (see John 3:36 and Heb. 11:5). The exact meaning to which Jesus referred when using this word in this verse is not altogether clear. Some of the possibilities are listed below.
Some of the people would see the brightness of Jesus's glory on a mountain eight days later (9:28-36). (Note: See the discussion about "glory" at 2:9 and 2:14.)
-OR-
Some would see Jesus die, rise from the dead to live again and then see him go up to heaven (23:26-24:53).
-OR-
Some would see the Holy Spirit come on Pentecost. Those who believed that Jesus was the Christ would grow into large numbers of people (Acts 2; 4:23-35).

Section.heading: Luke 9:28-36 Some disciples saw Jesus in his glory with Moses and Elijah.

Questions.Q: Tell me what happened to Jesus and three of his disciples on a mountain.
Questions.A: (The answer should cover the basic outline of the story, including:
Jesus's appearance changing, [that is, his face and his clothing looked different],
Moses and Elijah appearing and talking with Jesus,
the bright light,
the disciples' sleepiness and Peter's suggestion about building temporary shelters for
the three,
hearing God's voice speaking from the cloud which surrounded them
and their not telling anyone about the incident until later on.
Any part which is not mentioned can be asked about from a specific question below.)

Questions.Q: What do you think that Jesus wanted to teach or show these disciples by having them see these things happen on the mountain?
Questions.A: God was confirming that everything Jesus had taught them just the week before, as Luke recorded it in 9:22-27, really was true. They must listen to Jesus and know that the glory about which he had spoken would still come.

(He wanted these few disciples to have a brief look at the glory he had been talking about which would come in the kingdom of God. The glory would first be Jesus's and, later on, every believers'. The glory existed already, but God had not yet fully revealed it to all the people. Not even all the believers had experienced it yet.

They also heard the voice of God telling them that they must listen to Jesus. This was another witness confirming what they had heard Jesus himself already say. He was the one the disciples must follow, regardless of what the religious leaders told them. God had said so directly to them. What Jesus had just taught them in verses 22-27 was that he had insisted on suffering as the way to glory. He also had called on them to give up their own physical lives to gain eternal life, even to bear their own suffering because of their faith in him and follow him through his suffering.)

Questions.Q: Where did Jesus take Peter, James, and John?
Questions.A: He took them up onto a mountain. (28)

Questions.Q: Why did they go there?
Questions.A: They went there to pray. (28)

Questions.Q: What happened to Jesus while he prayed?
Questions.A: The way that his face looked changed and
his clothing became sparkling/dazzling/radiant white. (29)

Questions.Q: What did Luke write about Moses and Elijah?
Questions.A: They appeared in their heavenly glory/brightness and talked with Jesus. (31)

Questions.Q: What did they talk about with Jesus?
Questions.A: They talked with him about his leaving [this world] while he was at Jerusalem. (31)

Questions.Q: What do you think they meant by saying that Jesus would be leaving this world?
Questions.A: They meant that the events that would happen to Jesus at Jerusalem, namely, his dying, rising again would lead to his ascending into heaven.

Questions.Q: What were the disciples doing?
Questions.A: They were asleep/kept falling asleep. (They were not praying.) (32)

Questions.Q: What did the disciples see when they were fully awake?
Questions.A: They saw [the brightness of] his glory and the two men standing with him. (32)

Questions.Q: When Peter saw all that, what did he suggest to Jesus that they (the three disciples) should do?
Questions.A: He felt good about being there, so he wanted to build three shelters, one each for Jesus, Moses, and Elijah. (33)

Questions.Q: In what way, do you think, did Peter not know what he was really saying?
Questions.A: He did not think about the meaning or implications of his words. He seems to have wanted to do something to keep Moses and Elijah there for a longer time. Spirit beings from heaven did not need physical shelters for protection or comfort.

Questions.Q: What happened while Peter was speaking?
Questions.A: A bright cloud appeared and it surrounded/covered/enveloped them all. (34)

Questions.Q: How did the disciples feel about that?
Questions.A: They were afraid [of all that was happening to them so suddenly/mysteriously]. (34)

Questions.Q: Whose voice was it which spoke in that cloud?
Questions.A: God's voice spoke.

Questions.Q: How do you know it was God who spoke?
Questions.A: He called Jesus his son whom he had chosen [to come into the world to die for mankind's sins]. (35)
Questions.Note: The cloud and the brightness were also signs in the Old Testament that God was present. Any voice which people heard in that context was always God's voice. God had already spoken once from heaven when Jesus had been baptized by John (see Luke 3:22).

Questions.Q: What did God say about Jesus?
Questions.A: He said that Jesus was God's son and God had chosen him [to be the Christ/Messiah/savior]. (35)

Questions.Q: What did God say that the disciples should do?
Questions.A: They must listen to what Jesus taught them. (35)
Questions.Note: The Greek wording emphasizes that Jesus is the one they must listen to and obey. When the religious leaders would later openly oppose Jesus concerning the writings of Moses and the prophets, the disciples knew that God had already told them directly whom they must obey. When those same leaders would order the disciples to stop talking about Jesus, the disciples could show from the Old Testament that they must follow God's instructions, not men's.

Questions.Q: What did the disciples see when the voice and the cloud had left?
Questions.A: Only Jesus was there [with them, not Moses and Elijah or God]. (36)

Questions.Q: To whom did the disciples tell what they had seen and heard?
Questions.A: They told no one, but kept silent for the time being. (36)

Section.heading: Luke 9:37-43a Jesus ordered an evil spirit to leave a boy, and it did.

Questions.Q: What happened when Jesus and the three disciples came down from the mountain?
Questions.A: A crowd met them.
A man in that crowd had a son whom a spirit seized, caused him to have convulsions and would not leave him alone.
The boy also foamed at the mouth.
The other disciples had not been able to heal him, so the father pleaded with/appealed to Jesus to do it.
Jesus was upset with the disciples/all the crowd for not believing strongly that God could free this boy.
Jesus rebuked the demon, healed the boy, and gave him back into his father's care.
Everyone was amazed at the power of God.

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that Jesus was so upset?
Questions.A: He had given all twelve disciples power and authority over these things earlier (9:1). He had told them that the religious officials would reject his teachings and cause him to suffer and die because of it (9:22). They needed to believe completely in Jesus. However, they did not believe as completely as Peter had implied they did when he confessed his belief in who Jesus really was (9:20). Most of the other people also had followed Jesus regularly and heard what he had taught. He knew he was going to leave them all soon and did not have a lot of time to keep on teaching them. They should already have believed completely. This made him upset.

Questions.Q: One man in the crowd was shouting to Jesus. About what was he shouting?
Questions.A: He wanted Jesus to take a look at his son, (who was his only child). (38)
He begged Jesus to drive out the [evil] spirit that seized him (40), making the boy scream, have convulsions, and foam at the mouth. (It left the boy battered and bruised.) (39-40)

Questions.Q: Had anyone else tried to help this man and his boy?
Questions.A: Yes, the other [nine] disciples had tried, but they had not been able to cast out the spirit. (40)

Questions.Q: What does it mean to "cast out a spirit/demon" from a person?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means ordering the demon to immediately leave the person alone and go away.
Questions.Alternative: What does it mean to "cast out a spirit from a person?
What does it mean to "cast out a demon" from a person?

Questions.Q: How often had that spirit bothered the boy?
Questions.A: The spirit hardly ever left the boy alone. Because it attacked the boy so often, that [evil] spirit was destroying/killing the boy. (39)
-OR-
The spirit had never left the boy easily. Whenever it had gone away, the boy was left badly injured from the wild thrashing of his body. (39)

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that the father was so worried that he now pleaded for help?
Questions.A: He loved his son very much. Also, he probably needed the son to carry on the family lineage and family name and to care for/support him when he became old.

Questions.Q: What kind of people did Jesus say these people were?
Questions.A: He said that they were unbelieving and morally wrong/crooked/wicked. (41)

Questions.Q: How long did Jesus sound as though he wanted to stay and put up with their slow learning?
Questions.A: He did not want to stay any extra time. He had told them everything that was important for them to believe and to live as members of God's kingdom. Jesus knew that his remaining time on earth was short. God would not delay his plan for Jesus to take away mankind's sin.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do about the boy?
Questions.A: He told the boy's father to bring his son to him (Jesus). (41)
He sternly commanded the demon [to leave the boy], (42)
healed the boy, (42)
and returned him to his father's care. (42)

Questions.Q: What did all the crowd think about this?
Questions.A: They were all astounded/amazed at the great power of God to cast out such a powerful demon. (43a) (They knew that ordinary people did not have any control over the spirit world.)

Section.heading: Luke 9:43b-45 Jesus says someone will betray him to his enemies.

Questions.Q: What new information did Jesus tell his disciples?
Questions.A: He told them that someone would betray [him,] the Son of Man, into the hands/control of other men. (44)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to betray someone into other people's hands/control?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means to deliver that person into the control of someone whom that person regards as an enemy. The person who betrays another pretends to be a friend or of the same mind as the person who is being betrayed, and then tricks him into making himself vulnerable/accessible to the enemy.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think it means to betray someone into other people's hands?
What do you think it means to betray someone into other people's control?

Questions.Q: What were all the other people doing while Jesus talked to his disciples?
Questions.A: All the other people were [still] talking about being amazed at what Jesus had done. (43b)

Questions.Q: How did the disciples respond to what Jesus told them?
Questions.A: Even though Jesus had told them to let the words really get set in their minds (that is, listen carefully and not forget), they did not understand what he meant. (45)

Questions.Q: Why did they not understand?
Questions.A: The clear meaning had been hidden [by God]. As a result, they did not understand it yet. (45)
-OR-
The clear meaning had been hidden [by God] in order that they not understand it yet. (45)
Questions.Note: The Greek word hina relates parts of a sentence to each other. In this sentence it could be understood to either make the second part of the sentence be the result of the actions in the first part, or it could make the second part be the purpose of the actions in the first part. The choices above show these two acceptable ways to understand the verse.

Questions.Q: Why did they not ask Jesus to explain it more clearly?
Questions.A: They were afraid to ask him about it.

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that the disciples were afraid to ask Jesus to explain his words?
Questions.A: They may have been afraid he would actually tell them about some terrible thing that was going to happen to him, that is, that he would be more specific about how he was going to die at the hand of others.
-OR-
They thought that all he had said on this matter was too mysterious to want to know more about it.
-OR-

Jesus just had been angry with the people because they did not believe him. The disciples did not understand his teaching, so they did not want him to know that they did not understand this, either. He might really be angry with them then.
-OR-

Jesus just had shown everyone that he had God's power over evil spirits. It did not seem possible that anyone could trick/fool/betray Jesus into his enemies' hands/control. Therefore, they were afraid to ask about this.
Questions.Note: There are several possible reasons that they were afraid to ask. Any one of these would be an adequate answer:

Section.heading: Luke 9:46-48 Jesus's disciples argued about who would be the greatest in the kingdom of God.

Questions.Q: Who did Jesus say would be the greatest/most important disciple? -OR- Who did Jesus say would be the greatest/most important person in the kingdom of God?
Questions.A: He said that the person who is willing to serve in the lowest position of honor is really the one who is the greatest/most important [in God's sight]. (48) (That person has given up all desire for personal greatness.)
Questions.Alternative: Who did Jesus say would be the greatest disciple?
Who did Jesus say would be the most important disciple?
Who did Jesus say would be the greatest person in the kingdom of God?
Who did Jesus say would be the most important person in the kingdom of God?

Questions.Q: What were the disciples arguing about among themselves?
Questions.A: They argued about which of them would be the greatest/most important person [in their group of 12/in the kingdom of God]. (46)

Questions.Q: How did Jesus know about their discussion?
Questions.A: He knew because he was the son of God. No one told him about it. (47)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do with a small child?
Questions.A: He got a small child and had him stand beside Jesus. (47)
Then Jesus used that child as a focal point for what he told the disciples about being great/important. (48)

Questions.Q: How did Jesus use this child to teach a lesson to the disciples?
Questions.A: When a person accepts/welcomes and cares for a child like that one in Jesus's name, it is the same as though that person is accepting/welcoming Jesus. And whoever welcomes Jesus is also welcoming/accepting [God] who sent him [into this world]. (48)

(A person whom God considers great/important is one who accepts the work of serving unimportant, ordinary people, as represented by this child. That person's attitude shows that he wants to serve Jesus, and God, who sent Jesus to this earth.)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to do something "in the name of Jesus"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means doing something as Jesus's representative, in his place, or because we love him. It is doing something on the basis of who Jesus was and what he did, that he was holy and that he perfectly reflected God's love to all who would accept him. He did not do it for great honor, but because he loved God, he served him by doing what God wanted him to do among the people here on earth. (See "in the name of" in KBT in the "name" entry.)

Section.heading: Luke 9:49-50 Whoever is not against you is for you.

Questions.Q: Why did John and the other disciples try to stop a man from casting out demons in Jesus's name?
Questions.A: They tried to stop him because that man was not a member of their group (of Jesus's followers). (49) (John may have been thinking that Jesus had only given that power and authority to the twelve apostles [9:1].)

Questions.Q: What do you think that it means here to do that work "in Jesus's name"?
Questions.A: The power and authority of Jesus are in his name. Calling on the name of Jesus and doing something in his name means that you are doing it with the power and authority of Jesus himself.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think that it means here to do that work "in Jesus's name"? Note: Only use this question if the translation does not make the meaning clear.
Questions.Note: Use this question only if the translation does not make the meaning clear.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say that John and the other disciples should do about that man who was not one of the twelve apostles?
Questions.A: They should not stop him [from doing that work in Jesus's name]. (50)

Questions.Q: What reason did Jesus give for his saying that?
Questions.A: The man was not working against Jesus, but for him, with the same goal Jesus had to free people from a demon's control. (50)

Section.heading: Luke 9:51-56 People in a Samaritan village did not allow Jesus to stay in their village.

Questions.Q: How was Jesus's response to those people who opposed him different from his disciples' response to them?
Questions.A: James and John wanted to punish those Samaritans, but Jesus quietly accepted their being opposed to him and refused to retaliate against/pay back those who insulted him [and God]. (54-56)

Questions.Q: For what event in his life was Jesus preparing?
Questions.A: He was preparing for the time when he would be going up [to heaven]. (51)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do as that time came closer?
Questions.A: He started to go determinedly towards Jerusalem. (51)
Questions.Note: This statement by Luke marks a very important change in the way that he wanted us readers to look at the following events and teaching of Jesus. Each one is not just one more separate story, but each is part of how he was preparing himself and his disciples for what would happen to him in Jerusalem. Jesus knew these were his last opportunities to prepare his disciples.

Questions.Q: What were the messengers supposed to do for him?
Questions.A: They went ahead of him to a Samaritan village to get things ready for him [to eat there and stay overnight]. (52)

Questions.Q: Who do you think that the Samaritans were?
Questions.A: They were the people who lived in the province of Samaria which lay between the Jews' provinces of Judea and Galilee.
Questions.Note: Hundreds of years earlier, the king of Assyria had taken most of the Jews away as captives (see 2 Kings 17:24-41). He had then sent people from other lands to live in that area. They married with the few Jews whom the king had left behind. The Samaritans were the descendants of those people. They had to be taught about God, but since the Assyrian king had destroyed the temple in Jerusalem, the Samaritans developed their own worship places and ways to worship. When the Jews returned from being captives, they rebuilt the temple in Jerusalem and stayed separate from the Samaritans, having nothing to do with them.

Questions.Q: What did the Samaritan people decide about Jesus and his disciples staying in their village?
Questions.A: They did not welcome/accept him, that is they refused to allow him to stay. (53)

Questions.Q: Why did they refuse to have him stay there?
Questions.A: Because he was headed towards Jerusalem [to worship in the Jewish temple there]. (53)
Questions.Note: Because Jesus was headed to Jerusalem to worship, it meant that he did not regard the Samaritans' temple on Mt. Gerazim nearby as a proper place in which to worship the true God. This offended the Samaritans.

Questions.Q: What did the disciples James and John want to do to the Samaritans?
Questions.A: They asked Jesus if he wanted them to call fire down from heaven to destroy those people. (54)

Questions.Q: How did Jesus respond to them?
Questions.A: He turned towards them and sternly rebuked them/commanded them [to stop thinking that way]. (55)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus and the disciples do when they were not allowed to stay in that particular place?
Questions.A: They went on to another [Samaritan] village. (56)

Section.heading: Luke 9:57-62 People who want to follow Jesus must let go of everything else they think is important.

Questions.Q: What do you think that Jesus would want us to learn from these examples about following him?
Questions.A: To follow Jesus means putting his desires for us as more important in our lives than our desires for our own well-being. We must come to him with no conditions, just as he followed his father's will in his own life. He had no desire for his own well-being, but his only desire was to do his father's will.

Questions.Q: Where were Jesus and his disciples going?
Questions.A: They were still headed towards Jerusalem. (9:51)

Questions.Q: A man approached Jesus along the road. What did this man say to Jesus?
Questions.A: He said that he would follow Jesus wherever Jesus went. (57)

Questions.Q: What do you think the man meant that he wanted to do?
Questions.A: He wanted to be a [close] disciple of Jesus and learn from him while traveling around.

Questions.Q: What do foxes and birds have that Jesus said he did not have?
Questions.A: Foxes have their [own] dens/holes/homes in the ground and birds have their [own] nests [for rest, safety, and shelter], but he had no such place [of his own] where he could rest/sleep. (58)

Questions.Q: What do you think that Jesus wanted that man to learn from his answer?
Questions.A: If the Son of Man, Jesus, had to live without the comfort of knowing he had his own safe home in which to rest, then his followers should not expect to have that, either. Knowing that other people [like those in the one Samaritan village] would not welcome him into their homes, then anyone who follows Jesus must expect the same thing to happen to him or her.

Questions.Q: What was the response of another person to Jesus's call to follow him [and be his disciple]?
Questions.A: He wanted first to go [home] and care for his elderly father until the father [died and] was buried. (59)
Questions.Alternative: What was the response of another person to Jesus's call to follow him and be his disciple?
What was the response of another person to Jesus's call to follow him?

Questions.Q: Who did Jesus say should care for those who died?
Questions.A: Those who are [already] dead should care for the dead. (60)

Questions.Q: That sounds impossible. What do you think that Jesus wanted the man to learn from that part of his answer?
Questions.A: Since dead people cannot do anything, Jesus must have meant that the people who have not repented from their sins (that is, those who are spiritually dead) and are not ruled by God (that is, those who are not in the kingdom of God), should care for those parents who need help and might die.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say was more important for that man to do than care for his father?
Questions.A: He must go and speak out about/proclaim the kingdom of God. (60)

Questions.Q: What did another person want to do before following Jesus?
Questions.A: He wanted first to go back home and say good-bye to those who lived there/to his loved ones. (61)

Questions.Q: What happens when a person wants to make straight lines for planting food (or, building a fence), but he/she regularly looks all around?
Questions.A: He will have crooked rows for planting, so some plants will be too close together and other space will be useless. (62)
Questions.Alternative: What happens when a person wants to make straight lines for planting food (or, building a fence), but he regularly looks all around?
What happens when a person wants to make straight lines for planting food (or, building a fence), but she regularly looks all around?

Questions.Q: What do you think is the way that this picture language of a man preparing his field/garden applies to serving in the kingdom of God?
Questions.A: The person who wants to be a disciple in the kingdom of God must keep his mind centered on God. In that way his work for God will be useful. Thinking about what he may have left behind, and longing for it, will slow him down and he will not be a useful worker (Luke 10:1-16).
Questions.Alternative: What do you think is the way that this picture language of a man preparing his field applies to serving in the kingdom of God?
What do you think is the way that this picture language of a man preparing his garden applies to serving in the kingdom of God?

Section.heading: Luke 10:1-16 Jesus sent out 72 more disciples.

Questions.Q: What work did Jesus tell these 72 other disciples to do?
Questions.A: They were to go ahead of him to every town and place where he was about to go (1) and decide which places would welcome him and which would not welcome him (based on how well they had been received) (8, 10, 16).

They were to speak a blessing of peace wherever they were welcomed (5-6, 8), and to shake off the dust from their feet wherever they were not welcomed [in order to show that God did not approve of what the people who lived at that place had done] (10-12).
They were to heal the sick in the places which welcomed them (9), and in every place tell the people that the kingdom of God had come (9, 11).
They were to ask God to send out more workers [to those people who were ready to hear the Good News]. (2)
Questions.Note: Some Greek manuscripts refer to only 70 disciples, but the editors of the United Bible Societies' The Greek New Testament, 4th revised edition, 1993, give a slight preference for the number "72" as the original number which Luke wrote here. You may have either number in the translation.

Questions.Q: How were these many disciples to divide into groups when they went to do this work?
Questions.A: They were to go two by two. (1)

Questions.Q: Where were they supposed to go?
Questions.A: They were to go to every town and place where he was planning to go. (1)

Questions.Q: Tell me about workers and fields which are ready to be harvested.
Questions.A: Often when a very big harvest is ready to be gathered, there is a need for more workers than are available. The food or grain must be gathered quickly before it falls, rots, spoils, or is ruined by bad weather. The workday is usually long and the work hard.
Questions.Note: In many places, as in Israel, food/seed is planted in all the fields/gardens at the same time because of the times of rain and sun. Therefore, all the food and grain is ready to harvest at about the same time, too. If the culture of the translation has no understanding of this kind of seasonal planting and harvesting, probably a glossary item needs to be prepared for this text.

Questions.Q: What do you think that Jesus meant when he talked about workers and fields?
Questions.A: He was not talking about real fields with food or grain that was ready to be harvested. This was picture language about the many people who were ready to believe in him when those disciples would tell them about the kingdom of God being present/the Good News that Jesus had come to save them.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about the number of workers compared to the number of people ready to hear and believe the good news about the kingdom of God?
Questions.A: The workers were few, but the number of people who were ready to hear was plentiful/very many. (2)

Questions.Q: Who, do you think, was the Lord of the harvest, the owner of the field of ripe food/grain?
Questions.A: God was.
Questions.Alternative: Who, do you think, was the Lord of the harvest, the owner of the field of ripe food?
Who, do you think, was the Lord of the harvest, the owner of the field of ripe grain?

Questions.Q: Do you think that there are now enough workers in the world, or are there still more people who need to hear about the kingdom of God?
Questions.A: There are still many more people today who have not heard about God's love, so many more workers are needed to go and tell them.

Questions.Q: Tell me what kind of animals wolves and lambs are.
Questions.A: Wolves are a variety of fierce, wild dogs which like to eat meat. Lambs are baby sheep which have a gentle nature and eat grass. They have no way to protect themselves from a fierce animal like a wolf.

Questions.Q: What do you think that Jesus meant when he talked about lambs and wolves?
Questions.A: He was not talking about real animals. This is picture language about the disciples going out among people who would reject their message and might try to harm them. The disciples were not to be fierce, but gentle and harmless in their actions and words. (They were to depend on God to protect them.)

Questions.Q: How were these disciples to get ready for going from place to place?
Questions.A: Jesus told them not to carry a money holder/purse/wallet, a bag [for extra things] or [extra] sandals/shoes. (4)

Questions.Q: What were they to do if they met people as they walked from one place to another?
Questions.A: They were not to become involved in long conversations on the road, [but move on to do the work Jesus had sent them to do]. (4)

Questions.Q: What were the disciples to do when they entered a house?
Questions.A: They were to bless [the people who lived in] that house with words of peace. (5)

Questions.Q: What kind of peace do you think that was?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: This peace is a calm heart/spirit which is free from worry and quarreling because God's representative was in that house and brought Good News.
Questions.Note: See "peace" in KBT.

Questions.Q: How, do you think, would a "man of peace" who lived in that house act towards Jesus's disciples?
Questions.A: He probably would welcome them as the representatives of Jesus. He would be willing to listen to what the disciples said about the kingdom of God.
He would also offer them [long-term] hospitality, giving them a place to stay and food to eat.

Questions.Q: What will happen if the man of that house was not a man of peace?
