Questions.A: The blessing of peace would not stay with that man, but it would return to the disciples [either to give them peace or to be as if they had never spoken it]. (6)

Questions.Q: How were they to act when they stayed in someone's house?
Questions.A: They were to stay there during their whole time in that place, eating [and drinking] whatever the people gave them. (7)

Questions.Q: What reason did Jesus give the disciples to make them feel comfortable about taking nothing along with them, and about staying in only one house and eating the food there?
Questions.A: He said that the worker was worthy to receive his pay. (7)

Questions.Q: What were they to do in the places where they were welcomed?
Questions.A: They should eat what was given to them [by the people] (8),
heal the sick [people] who lived there,
and tell them, "The kingdom of God is near." (9)

Questions.Q: What were they to do in the places where they were not welcomed?
Questions.A: They should go out into the streets [where many people would see them] (10)
and tell [the people there] why they were shaking the dust of that place off their feet [in protest] (11).
They should also tell those people that they should be fully aware that the kingdom of God was near [and they were not part of it yet]. (11)

Questions.Q: What do you think was the purpose of telling those people once more that the kingdom of God was near?
Questions.A: The people would know that by rejecting the disciples and their message they were also rejecting their chance/the opportunity to become part of the kingdom of God. As the disciples left, so did the people's chance/opportunity.
-OR-

The people would know that if they repented/changed their minds quickly, there was still one last chance while the disciples were in their town to tell them more, or they could arrange for Jesus to come and teach them.

Questions.Q: With what did Jesus compare people who did not welcome the disciples whom he had sent?
Questions.A: He said that [the people of the town of] Sodom would bear/endure better the punishment God had for them on The Day [when he would judge all people] than [the people of] that town would be able to bear/endure the [even greater] punishment God had for them. (12)
-OR-
He said that on The Day [when God would judge all people] [the people of] that town would have more/greater punishment [from God] than [the people of the town of] Sodom would suffer.
Questions.Note: There is much implied information in this verse which Jesus, the disciples, and Luke all understood, but which the people who will read this translation may not know. Depending on the level of general Bible knowledge among the people, it may be necessary to have a glossary item which explains that the people who lived in the town of Sodom many years earlier had sinned greatly and God would severely punish them (see Gen. 19). The people of Sodom did not know God's plan to send a savior, so they did not trust God for being saved. By comparison, the people of a town which rejected the disciples and their message about the savior would be punished even more than the people of Sodom.

Questions.Q: What judgment, do you think, was Jesus talking about in verse 14?
Questions.A: Jesus referred to the day/time when God will judge all the people of the world, dead or alive. They will either live with him forever or be punished in Hell forever. (See Matt. 25:31-46.)
Key Term Check: See "judge, judgment" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Why should the people from the towns of Chorazin and Bethsaida expect God to severely punish them when he judges all people?
Questions.A: The people in those towns saw [Jesus do] miracles [besides teach them about the kingdom of God], but they did not believe him and repent. (13)

Questions.Q: Jesus probably did the same things in those two towns that he had done in Capernaum and other cities of the Jews. What kinds of miracles do you think those people saw Jesus do? (Any two or three of these items will make an adequate answer.)
Questions.A: He cast demons out of people (4:33-36),
he cured any illness or disease (4:38-40), even leprosy (5:13),
he healed physical problems (5:17, 26 and 6:6, 10),
he raised dead people to be alive again (7:14-16),
he calmed a storm (8:23-25),
and he fed thousands of people with a very small amount of food (9:16-17).

Questions.Q: What do you understand it is that makes something be called "a miracle"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A miracle is something which happens in our physical world that is different from the way that people know that the processes of nature take place. Spirit beings, such as God, use their great power to do these things.
Questions.Note: See "miracle, sign, wonder, mighty work" in KBT. Also see the note in L&N, following entry 76.8.
In the NT, all the miracles occurred so that the individual or the group of people who saw it happen would desire a stronger relationship with God.
Questions.Alternative: According to your understanding, what makes something be called "a miracle"?
What makes something be called "a miracle"?
What is a "miracle"?
What do you think a "miracle" is?

Questions.Q: How did Jesus compare these two towns, Chorazin and Bethsaida with other cities?
Questions.A: If the people who lived in the [Gentile/non-Jewish] towns of Tyre and Sidon had seen those miracles, they would have sat in sackcloth and ashes to show that they had repented; but the people in these two Jewish towns had not repented. (13)

The people of Tyre and Sidon would bear/endure better [the punishment God had for them] when he would judge [all people on The Last Day] than these people would be able to bear/endure the [even greater] punishment God had for them. // When [God] judges [everyone on The Last Day], he will not punish the people of Tyre and Sidon as severely as he will punish the people of Chorazin and Bethsaida. (14)

Questions.Q: What do you think it would have meant if the people of Chorazin and Bethsaida had sat in sackcloth and ashes?
Questions.A: It was the cultural way to show great sorrow and mourning when a great tragedy had occurred. In this case, they would have been showing great sorrow for their sins against God and their desire to obey him from then onward.
Questions.Note: If this is not the custom for showing sorrow and repentance in the language area, it would be good to make the purpose clear in the text.

Questions.Q: What should people in the town of Capernaum expect to happen to them in the time when God will judge all people?
Questions.A: They should expect to be sent down to the place of the dead [where God would punish them]. They would not be taken up [by God/God's angels] to heaven where God lives. (15)

Key Term Check: If the language of the translation has a traditional name for the place of the dead, that name can be used. Here it refers to a place which is the opposite of heaven and all for which it stands. See "Hades" in KBT in the "hell, Hades, abyss" entry.

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason those people might have expected that God would take them to heaven?
Questions.A: Jesus had indicated that he had done miracles in Capernaum (4:23).
He had taught in the synagogue there and driven out the evil spirit from a man (4:31-44).
He had healed the Roman army officer's servant there (see Luke 7:1-10).
Questions.Note: We know from the other gospel writers that Jesus lived there (see Matt. 4:13; John 2:12),
taught about the Kingdom of God there (see Matt. 4:17; John 6:24, 59-64),
and healed the paralytic man there (see Mark 2:1-12; Luke 5:17-26).
The people of Capernaum may have thought that God would give them special treatment because Jesus had done all these things in their town, but they had not believed Jesus's message.

Questions.Q: To whom was Jesus talking in verse 16?
Questions.A: He was speaking to the 72 disciples he was sending out, not to the people of Capernaum.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say was the reason why the people who did not accept his disciples would receive great punishment?
Questions.A: The disciples were preaching the same message as Jesus, so when the people accepted them, it was the same as though they were receiving the one who sent them, Jesus. When they rejected what the disciples' said, they were rejecting Jesus and his Father who had sent him. [By rejecting Jesus's disciples they were rejecting God's plan for them, so God would reject them. They could not be saved any other way.] (16)

Section.heading: Luke 10:17-24 The 72 disciples returned in joy and Jesus also rejoiced.

Questions.Q: What were the 72 disciples rejoicing about?
Questions.A: When they used Jesus's name, even the demons obeyed them [to leave people]./God had given them power even over demons. (17)

Questions.Q: What was the real reason that they should rejoice?
Questions.A: It was that their names were recorded [by God] in heaven where he lives. (20)

Questions.Q: About what was Jesus rejoicing?
Questions.A: God had chosen to give his wisdom and power to these unschooled, unsophisticated, but obedient, men. (21)

Questions.Q: What did the 72 disciples say when they returned to Jesus?
Questions.A: They said that even the demons obeyed them [to leave people] when they (the disciples) used the authority of Jesus's name. (17)

Questions.Q: What other work had they done besides casting out demons from people?
Questions.A: They had healed the sick and preached the Good News about the kingdom of God. (10:9)
Questions.Note: The words of the disciples implied that the power over demons was more than what they had expected. Luke recorded only that Jesus had given them power over sickness and authority to preach. Jesus had not explained the full range of the authority he had given them until after they had returned (see vs. 19). Their sensing that demons obeyed them was more than they had expected. That sensing of the disciples should be expressed appropriately in the translation.

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that it was important that the disciples used Jesus's name when they did that work?
Questions.A: The name of Jesus had/held all the power and authority that Jesus had given to them. They had no personal power or authority greater than the demons' power. The power and authority was only theirs because Jesus had given it to them. (Because Jesus was the son of God, the demons also had to obey what his representatives said that Jesus wanted them to do.)

Questions.Q: How did Jesus respond to the disciples' excitement?
Questions.A: He said that he had seen Satan fall from heaven [where spirit beings live] just as a bolt of lightning flashes [instantly] from the sky to the earth. (18)

Questions.Q: Who is Satan?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He is a spirit being who is the chief enemy of God and of those who believe in God's Son, Jesus.
Questions.Note: See "Satan" in KBT.
It is more important to use a term which gives the right understanding of who Satan is, rather than imply that "Satan" is only a personal name.

Questions.Q: What do you think that Jesus meant by his response to the disciples?
Questions.A: [In his spirit] he had seen Satan's control of people end each time the disciples [preached, healed, or] cast out a demon in Jesus's name. Satan truly was defeated.
-OR-
Jesus had actually seen God cast Satan out of heaven before the world began, so the disciples' comments only confirmed that truth and were a sign of it.
Questions.Note: Any answer that does not contradict what men wrote in the rest of the Bible is acceptable. The Greek words do not clearly indicate whether Jesus was referring to the time when the disciples had been casting out demons or to a time before the world began. The disciples had seen Satan's demons obey their commands in Jesus's name. Jesus told them that he had seen Satan himself have to leave heaven immediately at God's command.

Questions.Q: What other examples did Jesus give to the disciples of how they might use the authority he had given to them?
Questions.A: They would be able to walk on snakes and scorpions
and to overcome all the power of the enemy.
Nothing would hurt them [when they were serving as Jesus's representatives].

Questions.Q: Who do you think was the enemy to whom Jesus referred [in verse 19]?
Questions.A: Satan was that enemy.
Questions.Alternative: Who do you think was the enemy to whom Jesus referred in verse 19?
Who do you think was the enemy to whom Jesus referred?

Questions.Q: What was a more important reason for the disciples to rejoice than that demons obeyed them?
Questions.A: It was more important that [God] had recorded their names in heaven. (20)
Questions.Note: The Greek word that introduces verse 20 shows clearly that Jesus was going to say something different from what the disciples expected him to say. The translation should also show that change in the way that the speakers of that language usually show that.

Questions.Q: What do you think this picture language about writing names down means?
Questions.A: It means that God knew that those disciples believed in Jesus as the savior he had sent. He knew that they were members in his kingdom and that he would allow them to enter heaven. They belonged there. (20)

Questions.Q: Who caused Jesus to be joyful?
Questions.A: The Holy Spirit did. (21)

Questions.Q: For what did Jesus thank his father, God?
Questions.A: He thanked God that he (God) had hidden these things from those people who [thought that they] were wise and had learned much. He had done that in order that those people would not understand those things. (21)

Questions.Q: What do you think those things were that God had hidden from the people who thought that they were wise and had learned much?
Questions.A: They were the things the disciples had learned about having authority as a follower of Jesus.
-OR-
It was the knowledge the disciples had that their names were recorded already by God in heaven.
-OR-
When they had seen God's power at work as they served Jesus, they knew that the kingdom of God had already come.
-OR-
Satan truly was defeated and his workers had to obey Jesus's followers. God's plan for sending a savior had happened already.
Questions.Note: The Greek text does not point back clearly to any one particular thing when it says, "these things".

Questions.Q: To whom, do you think, was Jesus referring when he said that little children had seen/understood things that God had hidden from others?
Questions.A: He was referring to his disciples who were ordinary, working people, not religious scholars. They were humble and willing to believe what he told them, not proud of their learning or stubborn.
Questions.Alternative: To whom, do you think, was Jesus referring when he said that little children had seen things that God had hidden from others?
To whom, do you think, was Jesus referring when he said that little children had understood things that God had hidden from others?

Questions.Q: What do you think it was that God had been pleased to do?
Questions.A: He had hidden his plan from those who thought that they were wise and now had revealed it to those who were like little children in comparison [and they had believed it]. (21)

Questions.Q: Listen to verse 22 again and then tell me to whom Jesus was speaking. Do you think that he was speaking at this point to his father or to all the people around him?
Questions.A: He was speaking then to those people who were around him, not to God.
Questions.Note: The translation may need to make that change of hearer clear for the respondent.

Questions.Q: God had given some understanding, power and authority to those 72 disciples. What did Jesus say God had given to him?
Questions.A: All knowledge, power and authority had been given to him by [God] his father. (22)

Questions.Q: Who did Jesus say will really know who God is and who his son is?
Questions.A: Only [God] the Father really knows who his son really is,
and only [Jesus] the son and those [people] to whom he chooses to reveal him know who [God] the Father really is, that is, what his true nature is like. (22)

Questions.Q: To whom, do you think, does Jesus choose to reveal more understanding about who God is and what he is like?
Questions.A: He chooses to reveal more understanding to all those who believe in Jesus as God's son who came into the world to save us as God had promised.

Questions.Q: To whom was Jesus speaking in verse 23?
Questions.A: He was speaking only to his disciples.

Questions.Q: Whom did Jesus say should feel happy/blessed by God?
Questions.A: [God] had blessed those [people] who had seen what those disciples had seen. (23)
Questions.Alternative: Whom did Jesus say should feel happy?
Whom did Jesus say should feel blessed by God?

Questions.Q: What had the disciples seen?
Questions.A: They had seen Jesus, the Messiah, God's son, bring the Good News that they could be in the kingdom of God. They had also seen Jesus use his authority and power to help people. Now as Jesus's representatives to different places, they had been able to do the same as Jesus had done.

Questions.Q: Who had wanted to see these things which the disciples had seen, and hear what they had heard, but had not been able to do so?
Questions.A: Many prophets and kings had wished that they could have seen and heard what the disciples experienced [while Jesus taught them]. (24)

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that those prophets and kings had not seen or heard the things that the disciples had?
Questions.A: Those prophets and kings had died many, many years before Jesus was born on the earth.

Section.heading: Luke 10:25-37 Jesus told a parable about a Samaritan man who showed mercy.

Questions.Q: How did what Jesus believed and taught about receiving the eternal life compare with what the Jewish expert in the Law understood about it from the Law of Moses?
Questions.A: Jesus told the man to do the very same thing that the man had said that Moses had written in the books of the Law. [He had to do what the Law said, not just know what it said.] (26-28)

Questions.Q: How does a person get eternal life?
Questions.A: Jesus said that we are to love and obey God [perfectly], according to his commands that Moses wrote down. This included loving our neighbor perfectly, too. (26-27)
Questions.Note: Every person who tries to do as Jesus said soon finds that he cannot do it all perfectly and will never get eternal life by his own efforts. The only way left is to trust in Jesus's perfect life and in his death so that God could forgive our sins. Thus, eternal life is a gift from God.

Questions.Q: What is the answer to the expert's second question, "Who is my neighbor?"
Questions.A: A person's neighbor is anyone/everyone who needs our help in any way. (36-37)

Questions.Q: What did the expert in the Law want to know about eternal life?
Questions.A: He wanted to know what he had to do so that he could receive/inherit that life. (25)

Questions.Q: What kind of life do you think that eternal life is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Eternal life is a life that is not affected by time limits, such as whether a person is still alive physically or not. That kind of living can begin now while we are still alive and will go on forever, even after our bodies die. Jesus, in his dying and rising on our behalf, made it possible for us to have that eternal life. God graciously and freely allows us to have that new life. It is a life of having a close relationship with God, obeying him as he rules over us.
Questions.Note: See "life" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Why was that expert in the Law asking that question?
Questions.A: He wanted to test Jesus, [whether he really knew about God's laws and how to interpret them or not. He may have hoped to make Jesus appear wrong in front of the other people]. (25)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus ask the man to tell him?
Questions.A: He asked the man to tell him what [Moses] had written [about eternal life] in the Law. (26)

Questions.Q: What had Moses said that people should do to receive eternal life?
Questions.A: A person should love God with every part of him and then love his neighbor as [much as, or in the same way as, he loves] himself. (27)

Key Term Check: The Greek word for "heart" referred to the physical organ in the chest which pumps blood around the body. The word also referred to the center of a person's feelings, desires, and emotions. This verse refers to the heart as the center of emotions. The translation should use the term for whatever body part the culture says is that center of emotions, not necessarily the word for the heart. See "heart" in KBT.
Key Term Check: See 1:46-48, above, for comments on "soul". Also see "soul" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about the expert's answer?
Questions.A: He had answered correctly. If he did that, he would have [eternal] life. (28)

Questions.Q: Jesus had answered the expert's first question completely. Why did the expert in the Law ask Jesus another question about this topic?
Questions.A: He wanted to justify himself, that is, he wanted to show that he was doing the right thing by his wanting to clearly understand how to get eternal life. (29)
-OR-
He wanted to show that he was right in the way that he had been living and treating people. (29)
Key Term Check: See "justify" in KBT in the "just, justify, justification" entry.
Questions.Note: He may have felt embarrassed in front of the other people because Jesus had him answer his own question with Scripture verses that every Jew knew. These verses did not have hidden meaning so that a person needed to be an expert in the Law of Moses in order to understand them.

Questions.Q: What was the man's next question?
Questions.A: "Who is my neighbor?"/"To whom does [that word] 'neighbor' [really] refer"? (29)

Questions.Q: How did Jesus answer the expert's question about whom a person should regard as his neighbor?
Questions.A: He told the man a parable. (30-35)

Questions.Q: What happened to the Jewish man in Jesus's story who was traveling from Jerusalem to the town of Jericho?
Questions.A: Robbers attacked him. (30)
They took all his clothes. (30)
They beat him. (30)
They left him [lying there on the road] like a dead man/nearly dead. (30)

Questions.Q: Did anyone else walk along that road?
Questions.A: Yes, a priest and, later, a man from the tribe/clan of Levi [who worked in the temple] [and even later, a Samaritan man,] each came along that road. (31-32)
Key Term Check: See "Levite" in KBT.
Questions.Note: The first words in the Greek text in 10:31 indicate that the priest (and other people) did not often come along that road, so the injured man could have died there before another person found him and helped him. It would be good if the translation indicated that another person might not come along that part of the road until a long time after the robbers had beaten the man. See other translations for ideas.

Questions.Q: What did the priest do when he saw the injured man?
Questions.A: He passed by on the other/the far side of the road [and did not help the man]. (31)

Questions.Q: What did the man from the tribe of Levi do when he saw that man?
Questions.A: He did the same as the priest had done, that is, he walked along the other side of the road as he passed the man without helping him. (32)

Questions.Q: Who else came along that road to Jericho?
Questions.A: A Samaritan man came. (33)

Questions.Q: What did the Samaritan man do when he saw the injured man?
Questions.A: He felt very sorry for the man [and wanted to help him]. (33)
He went up to the injured man, (34)
poured [olive] oil and wine on his wounds (34)
and bandaged them. (34)
Then he put/placed the man on his own donkey (34)
and took him to an inn/hotel. (34)
There he took care of the [injured] man. (34)

Questions.Q: What kind of oil do you think it was that the Samaritan man put on the other man's wounds?
Questions.A: It was juice from the fruit of the olive tree.

Questions.Q: What did that Samaritan man do the next day when he left that inn?
Questions.A: He took out some money (two coins made of silver) and gave it to the owner of the inn to pay for whatever that injured man needed. (35)

Questions.Q: Which man did the expert in the Law say was acting like a neighbor to the man who had been robbed?
Questions.A: The man who had mercy on him was the one who acted like a neighbor. (37)
Questions.Note: If the respondent answers with, "The Samaritan", skip over the next question.

Because of the bad feelings between the Jews and the Samaritans, this very religious Jew who was asking Jesus the question about eternal life and one's neighbor would not give credit out loud even to a Samaritan in a story by saying his nationality by name. He only described him by the good thing he did. If the language of the translation has a way to refer to a socially ostracized person or group, such as traditional enemies, see if that is an appropriate term for this expert to use here.

Questions.Q: Which man was that? The priest or the man from the tribe of Levi or the Samaritan?
Questions.A: The Samaritan was the one who had mercy.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell the expert in the Law to do since he understood correctly which man had been the best neighbor?
Questions.A: He was to do just the same [as the Samaritan had done in showing mercy]. (37)

Section.heading: Luke 10:38-42 Jesus visited the home of Martha and Mary.

Questions.Q: What do you think that we should learn for ourselves from this incident?
Questions.A: We should be like Mary and choose to do what is most important in life. That is, we should stop being too busy with good activities which we think are important, and learn about God and how he wants us to live.

Questions.Q: Luke wrote that these things happened "while Jesus and his disciples were on their way." Where were they headed?
Questions.A: They were going to Jerusalem.
Questions.Note: See the answers and Note back at 9:51.

Questions.Q: Where did they stop along the way?
Questions.A: They stopped at the home of Martha [and her sister Mary]. (38-39)

Questions.Q: What did Mary do while Jesus was at their house?
Questions.A: She sat at his feet listening to what he said. (39)

Questions.Q: What did Martha do while Jesus was there?
Questions.A: She was very busy/upset with getting everything ready to feed and care for Jesus. (40)

Questions.Q: While Martha was very busy, how did she feel about her sister Mary only sitting down?
Questions.A: She was upset. She asked Jesus if it didn't bother him that Mary was not helping her get things ready. (40)
Questions.Note: The Greek words clearly show that Martha was upset and frustrated. The translation should show that, too in an appropriate way.

Questions.Q: What did Martha want Jesus to do about this problem?
Questions.A: She wanted him to tell Mary to help her. (40)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about Martha?
Questions.A: He said that she was worried about many things, but only one thing was really needed/important. (42)

Questions.Q: What was that one important thing?
Questions.A: What Mary had chosen to do was the more important thing. She had chosen to learn from Jesus. (42)
Questions.Note: Some Bible scholars say that the "one thing" referred to Martha preparing less food and thus having less work. Then it would have been easy enough for one person to get ready quickly and also have time to hear what Jesus had to say.
Questions.Alternative: What was the one important thing, which Mary had chosen?
What was the one important thing?
What was the one necessary thing, which Mary had chosen?
What was the one necessary thing?

Questions.Q: Do the words of Jesus in verses 41-42 sound like he was angry with Martha?
Questions.Note: It should not sound like he was angry. He was chiding/correcting her, but he was gentle and sympathetic to Martha's desire to show her love to him.

Questions.Q: Do you think that Jesus told Mary to stop listening and to go help Martha?

Section.heading: Luke 11:1-13 Jesus taught his disciples how they should pray.

Questions.Q: Who was the example whom the disciples wanted to follow in the way that they prayed?
Questions.A: Jesus was their example. (1)

Questions.Q: Who do you think is the best example for us to follow when we want to know how to pray?
Questions.A: Jesus is. (All that is recorded in the Bible about Jesus praying and what he taught about praying is the starting point for how, when, and where we are to pray meaningfully to God.)

Questions.Q: What do you think that Jesus wanted his disciples to learn about praying from the story he told about a man asking a neighbor for some food?
Questions.A: They must come with their needs at any time and persevere/be persistent in praying.
-OR-
If even an unwilling human friend can be moved to act by a person who is persistent in his request for a need, how much more will God be moved by the persistence of one who prays to him for a need.

Questions.Q: What do you think that Jesus wanted his disciples to learn about praying from the examples he gave about a human father responding to his son's request for help?
Questions.A: God, our Father in heaven, is ready to hear our prayers and answer them even more than a human father would respond to his children's requests.

Questions.Q: What did one of Jesus's disciples ask him to do for them?
Questions.A: He asked Jesus to teach them [how/what] to pray. (1)

Questions.Q: How should a person who is praying address the one to whom he is praying, that is, God?
Questions.A: He should address him as/call him "Father". (2)

Questions.Q: What was the first thing Jesus said to God in this prayer?
Questions.A: He said that he wanted to honor/revere God's name more as being holy.
-AND/OR-
He said that he wanted God's name to be honored/revered as being holy [by more and more people]. (2)

Questions.Q: How is it possible, do you think, that a name can be holy?
Questions.A: It is holy because it is part of the person who is holy./A person's name reflects what that person is like.

Questions.Q: What should a person pray about God ruling in people's lives?
Questions.A: One should pray that the time for God to rule over his people should come [soon/quickly].
-AND/OR-
God's rule should come/happen to all people. // All people should submit to God ruling over them. // May all people know/acknowledge God as their king.
Questions.Note: The language of the translation may not allow an abstract object, such as a kingdom, to "come". Ask about this if the text appears to be a literal translation.

Questions.Q: If God is not ruling over some people, who do you think is ruling over them?
Questions.A: The devil is ruling them./Satan is ruling them.
Questions.Note: A person may think that he is ruling/guiding himself, but that is not true. If God is not ruling, then that person has allowed himself to be under Satan's control.

Questions.Q: How/What should a person pray about his food?
Questions.A: He should ask God to help him get what he needs for that day. (3)
Questions.Note: See the Note at 9:13 about "bread".
Questions.Alternative: How should a person pray about his food?
What should a person pray about his food?

Questions.Q: What should a person pray about God forgiving his sins?
Questions.A: He should tell God that, because he is ready to forgive all other people who are indebted to him [in some way], he is ready to ask God to forgive him his sins. (4)

Questions.Q: How does a person forgive another person who is indebted to him/who has sinned against him?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He stops thinking about that person as having done something wrong against him. That means that there is no need for that person to compensate him in any way, such as by being punished or by giving him good things or by doing extra actions which would please him. The one who forgives does not think of that other person as being a bad person any longer.
Questions.Note: See "forgive" in KBT.

This is the same thing that God does when he forgives a person (see 1:77). If the speakers of the language used in the translation use a term for God forgiving people which is different from the term the people use for forgiving others, check what the people's reasons may be. This can be checked by switching the verbs for forgiveness and asking what makes each one acceptable or unacceptable in the people's minds. The Greek text uses the same word in both references. God expects us to do the same as he has done for us (see Luke 6:37; Matt. 6:14-15; 18:32-35; Mark 11:25).
Questions.Alternative: How does a person forgive another person who has sinned against him?
How does a person forgive another person who is indebted to him?

Questions.Q: What should a person pray about his being tempted to disobey God?
Questions.A: He should ask God to lead him in ways where Satan is not waiting to tempt him. // God should not permit him to enter into situations where Satan will tempt him to sin.
-OR-

He should ask God not to allow him to do anything that day which would cause God to stop protecting him and, thus, leave him open to the devil's temptations. // He wants God to keep him living according to/submitting to God's perfect will/desires so that Satan has no way to control him.

Questions.Q: In the story that Jesus told, what happened in the middle of the night?
Questions.A: A man went to his friend's house to borrow some food/three loaves of bread. (5)

Questions.Q: Why did the man go there at that time of night?
Questions.A: Another friend who had traveled to visit him had arrived, and there was no food [in the house] to serve him. (6)

Questions.Q: Why did the neighbor friend not want to open the door and give this man some food?
Questions.A: The door was locked/secured [and would be difficult or noisy to open and close again]. (7)
The man's children were in the [same] bed with him [and would wake up if the father got up and moved around]. (7)

Questions.Q: Why did he finally get up and give the man who was standing outside all the food he needed?
Questions.A: Because the man who was outside was persistent/kept on asking him for the food, the neighbor gave him all that he needed. (8)

Questions.Q: Whom, do you think, the man inside the house and the man who was standing outside represented in Jesus's story?
Questions.A: The man inside the house represented God,
and the man standing outside represented the disciples or anyone who requests God's help.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say that a person is to do if he needs something?
Questions.A: He is to keep on asking [God for it], seeking [for it] and knocking on God's door [because of it]. (9)
Questions.Note: Most writers of commentaries mention that the three phrases convey a sense of increasing intensity to get whatever is needed, knocking on a door being the most intense. However, knocking may not be the normal way in the culture of the target audience to show one's desire to interact with the people inside a neighbor's house. For help in adjusting the translation to be culturally appropriate, see TN, Luke 11:9c.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say was the reason that he told the disciples to pray in that manner?
Questions.A: Everyone who prays in that way receives or finds what they needed, or [God] opens his door, [and gives it to them]. (10)

Questions.Q: What two examples did Jesus give of how a father would not treat a request from his son?
Questions.A: If his son asked for a fish, the father would not give him a snake instead. (11)
If his son asked for an egg, he would not give him a scorpion. (12)

Questions.Q: How did Jesus compare his disciples with God?
Questions.A: He said that they were bad in contrast to God who is perfect. Even so, they gave good things to their children when they asked. God wants [and is ready] more than they to give perfect gifts, even his own Holy Spirit, to those people who will ask him. (13)

Section.heading: Luke 11:14-23 Some people said that Jesus's power came from Satan.

Questions.Q: Jesus implied that what he had done by the power of God was to show/reveal something to the people. What should the people have understood?
Questions.A: Casting out the demon from a man was a sign that the kingdom of God had come to them/was happening among them [because Jesus was the one whom God had sent to save them]. (20)
Questions.Alternative: Jesus implied that what he had done by the power of God was to show something to the people. What should the people have understood?
Jesus implied that what he had done by the power of God was to reveal something to the people. What should the people have understood?

Questions.Q: How did Jesus's statements about the parts of a divided kingdom being against each other apply to what had just happened?
Questions.A: He was referring to what the people had been thinking when he cast out the demon. (18b) If he was one of Satan's workers, he would not cast another of Satan's workers out of a man. That would only weaken Satan's kingdom. Their thinking did not make sense.

Questions.Q: People had responded to Jesus and his message in different ways. What did Jesus say about those different responses?
Questions.A: The people were either for him or against him. There was no middle/neutral choice. (23)

Questions.Q: What happened which started many people talking about Jesus's power?
Questions.A: Jesus was casting out a demon that made a man unable to talk/mute/dumb.
As the demon went out, the man [who had been] mute/dumb began to speak. (14)

Questions.Q: How did most of the people who saw that react?
Questions.A: They were amazed. (14)
Questions.Note: Luke already has used this same Greek word "thaumazw" eight times to describe people's reactions to things they saw or heard. Check again at 8:25 and 9:43 to see whether the translation has described this action consistently. Luke wrote that the same thing happened each time, so the translation should reflect that, too.

Questions.Q: How did some people react?
Questions.A: Some of them said that Jesus was using Beelzebub's/Beelzebul's power. (15)

Questions.Q: Who is Beelzebub/Beelzebul?
Questions.A: He is the leader/ruler of the demons. (15)
Questions.Alternative: Who is Beelzebub?
Who is Beelzeboul?
Who is Beelzebul?
Who is Beelzebub/Beelzeboul?

Questions.Q: What other name did Jesus use for this leader of the demons?
Questions.A: He used the name Satan. (18)

Questions.Q: How did other people react?
Questions.A: They asked Jesus to show them a sign/miracle from [God in] heaven. They wanted to test him, [that is, to prove that his power and authority really were from God and not from Satan]. (16)
-OR-
They asked Jesus to cause a sign/miracle to happen in the sky or to come from the sky. [Then they would know that God had sent him to do what he was doing.] (16)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say happens when the people in a kingdom or a house divide into groups and argue or fight against each other?
Questions.A: That kingdom or household loses its power and its unity and will be ruined/its power and influence will decrease greatly. (17)

Questions.Q: How were the people, including Pharisees, to judge whether Jesus had used Satan's power or God's power to cast out that demon?
Questions.A: Since some of the Pharisees' own followers cast out the same kind of demons, the people should ask them if they used Satan's power to do that. (19) (Their own people would quickly show them that such an opinion about anyone, even Jesus, was wrong.)
Key Term Check: See "judge, judgment" in KBT.

Questions.Q: To what do these words, "God's finger/hand/arm" refer in verse 20?
Questions.A: They refer to casting out the demon by God's power.
Questions.Note: If the translation does not use a figure of speech here (e.g., "God's finger", "God's hand", "God's arm"), omit or rewrite this question.
Questions.Alternative: To what do these words, "God's finger refer in verse 20?
To what do these words, "God's hand refer in verse 20?
To what do these words, "God's arm" refer in verse 20?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus mean when he said "the kingdom of God has come upon you"?
Questions.A: God's power was being displayed as far superior to their power, as a victorious force which they could not stand against.
Jesus' effective use of divine power demonstrated that God's kingdom was being established in their midst.
Questions.Note: If the text is a literal translation of the Greek "kingdom comes", see how the same wording was adjusted at 11:2.

Questions.Q: Jesus used picture language again to try to make his point clear to everyone. Tell me the example you just heard.
Questions.A: A strong man guards his possessions so they are safe. (21)
When someone stronger attacks and overpowers him, [the stronger man] takes everything which had protected that man and divides that man's possessions [among his own friends]. (22)

Questions.Q: To whom, do you think, was Jesus referring when he talked about those two strong men?
Questions.A: Jesus was referring to Satan as the strong man.
He was referring to himself as the stronger man who attacked.

Questions.Q: To what, do you think, did the picture of Satan's possessions refer?
Questions.A: Satan's possessions were the people whom his demons controlled.

Questions.Q: To what, do you think, did the weapons which Satan used refer?
Questions.A: Satan's weapons were the demons.

Questions.Q: Jesus had just cast out a demon which had made a man unable to talk. What do you think was the way that relates to what Jesus said about robbing another person?
Questions.A: A robber must be stronger than the person he robs. Since Jesus had sent Satan's demons out of the man, then Jesus is clearly stronger than Satan. He overpowered Satan and won the victory.
Questions.Note: Jesus had defeated Satan in the desert earlier (see Luke 4:1-13). Now he was taking away from Satan the people he had controlled. This was like taking away the things that Satan had owned. Jesus was giving out the benefits of his victory to the members of his own kingdom by freeing them from any demon's control.

Questions.Q: To what, do you think, did Jesus refer when he spoke about gathering and scattering something?
Questions.A: Jesus referred to gathering people [to follow him] into the kingdom of God. Satan does not want that to happen, so he does things to keep people out of God's kingdom.

Questions.Q: Jesus had cast out the demon which had made a man unable to talk. What do you think was the way that relates to what Jesus said about gathering and scattering?
Questions.A: The people who had thought that Jesus had used Satan's power to cast out the demon were not helping Jesus [or encouraging others to come to him], but causing other people to stay away.

Section.heading: Luke 11:24-26 Jesus told about an evil spirit which left a person, but later returned.

Questions.Q: What could happen to a person from whom God casts out an evil spirit?
Questions.A: [If he does not replace that evil spirit with God's Spirit in his life,] he could be worse off at the end than he had been at first [before God cast out the spirit from him]. (26)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say that an evil spirit does when it leaves a person?
Questions.A: It goes through the desert looking for a place to rest. (24)

Questions.Q: What does the spirit do when it finds no place to rest there?
Questions.A: It decides to return to the place from which it had left [in the person]. (24)

Questions.Q: What does it do when it returns to that person?
Questions.A: It finds that place/person empty and clean, [ready for someone to move in and stay there]. (25)
It brings (seven) other spirits worse than itself to come and live there with it. (26)

Section.heading: Luke 11:27-28 Jesus told which people are truly happy.

Questions.Q: Who did the woman say was blessed/truly happy?
Questions.A: [Jesus's mother, being] the woman who had borne and breast-fed him was blessed/happy. (27)
Key Term Check: See the explanation of "blessed" at 6:20.
Questions.Note: The words which the woman spoke literally mean that the womb and the breasts were the things which were "blessed". She used the poetic pattern of her Hebrew/Aramaic language to express her meaning by using two parallel statements. The two statements together help us understand that the woman's focus was not on the body parts, but on the person to whom they belonged, Jesus's mother. The translation should reflect that focus, regardless whether it is culturally appropriate or not to speak about wombs and breast-feeding in a public gathering, such as a church service.
Questions.Alternative: Who did the woman say was blessed?
Who did the woman say was truly happy?

Questions.Q: Who did Jesus say were even more blessed/happier than his mother?
Questions.A: Those [people] who hear the word of God [and do what it says] are even happier. (28)
Questions.Note: Jesus did not say that his mother was not blessed, but that these people would be even more blessed than his own mother. Actually, his mother's great happiness/blessing was because she had listened and obeyed God's word which the angel had spoken to her (see Luke 1:38, 45; 2:51).
Questions.Alternative: Who did Jesus say were even more blessed than his mother?
Who did Jesus say were even happier than his mother?

Section.heading: Luke 11:29-32 Some people asked Jesus to do a sign/miracle for them.

Questions.Q: What sign did Jesus talk about?
Questions.A: He told them that the only sign about which he would do anything for them was [what they already knew had happened in the prophet] Jonah's life and his preaching (29). [He, Jesus,] the Son of Man would be like Jonah for them (30), and even greater than Jonah (32).
Questions.Note: The things which the people of Nineveh had seen in Jonah's life are named in Matthew's account of this event (see Matt. 12:38-42). Jonah's message was that the people had to repent or be punished. This was the same message which Jesus now preached. Also, Jonah had spent three days and three nights in the stomach of a great fish. It seemed that he had died when he had been thrown into the sea, but then it was as though he rose from the dead when that fish spit him up on the shore. Jesus implied that something similar would happen to him. Because his wisdom was greater than Solomon's and his message greater than Jonah's, the people already had enough reason to believe in him.

Questions.Q: Who did Jesus say were wicked people?
Questions.A: He said that those people who were alive then as he spoke were wicked.
-OR-
He said that the people to whom he was speaking were wicked. (29)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say was a sign to him that they were wicked?
Questions.A: They [kept on] asking for a sign (which they would say proved that he had been sent by God and had God's power in him). (29)

Questions.Q: Who would condemn/accuse those people?
Questions.A: Jesus referred to the time/Last Day when God will judge all the people of the world. (See 10:14.)
Questions.Alternative: Who would condemn those people?
Who would accuse those people?

Questions.Q: How could people who were not Jews have anything to say against the Jews who lived at Jesus's time?
Questions.A: The Queen who came from the South had wanted to hear [King] Solomon's wise words/teaching, so she traveled from very far away just to hear him. Now, someone [much] greater than [King] Solomon was there, [Jesus, but the Jews who lived nearby and heard him had not believed what he taught]. (31)
The people of Nineveh had repented when Jonah preached [to them] (32), [but these people had not repented when Jesus preached to them]. (32)

Questions.Q: What judgment do you think Jesus was talking about in verses 31 and 32?
Questions.A: Jesus referred to the time/Last Day when God will judge all the people of the world. (See 10:14.)

Questions.Q: What will the Queen who came from the South and the people of Nineveh do when God later judges all the people of the world?
Questions.A: They will be raised [from the dead by God] and condemn/accuse [the people who lived at Jesus's time] because those people did not repent [of their sins]. (32)
-OR-
They will stand up [as witnesses] and condemn/accuse [the people who heard Jesus preach] for not repenting [of their sins]. (32)

Questions.Q: The people would see the same kind of sign as the people of Nineveh had seen when Jonah preached to them long ago. But how had the way that the Nineveh people responded to Jonah been different from the way that the people were now responding to Jesus?
Questions.A: The people of Nineveh had repented when Jonah preached [to them] (32), [but these people had not repented when Jesus preached to them].

Section.heading: Luke 11:33-36 When a person recognizes that Jesus's words and work were from God, it is like a lamp sending light into all parts of that person's life.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus try to teach the people by using this story about a lamp and its light and people's eyes?
Questions.A: The purpose of a lamp is to help people to see clearly when it is dark. God put Jesus on the earth to make the truths about [the kingdom of] God clear to those who believe the signs that God had sent him. Those clear truths will affect all areas of those believers' lives. The people who don't believe that about Jesus will not have a clear understanding even of the small amount of truth that they think they have.

Questions.Q: What do you think those people should have realized right then in order that their whole lives would have God's truth in them?
Questions.A: They should have realized that Jesus's words and work were showing God's truths to them. Only in believing and accepting that in their lives would they have clear understanding and direction in all that they thought and did.

Questions.Q: Why do people light lamps?
Questions.A: People light lamps to give light so people can see when it is too dark otherwise. (33)

Questions.Q: What does a person do with a lamp after he lights it?
Questions.A: He puts/places it where it can be useful, such as on a lamp holder. He does not hide it under anything. (33)

Questions.Q: What part of our bodies did Jesus say is like a lamp?
Questions.A: He said that our eyes work as a lamp for our bodies. (34)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say was the way that a person's eyes work like a lamp?
Questions.A: Good eyes let in lots of light, so the person sees well.
But when eyes are bad, the person sees nothing/only darkness. (34)
-AND/OR-
Good eyes let in light and the whole body functions well.
When the eyes are bad, the whole body does not function well. (34)
Questions.Note: The Greek words which Luke used for "good" and "bad" have two ways to be understood. One way is to understand them as evaluating physical things, like real eyes. The other way is to understand them as evaluating what God said about who Jesus was and how he wants us to live. Because this cannot all be included, generally, in the translated text, small footnotes or a glossary item may be needed to make both aspects of the meaning clear. The people who were listening to Jesus understood what he meant.
Also see "darkness" described above at 1:79.

Questions.Q: What hidden meaning, do you think, did Jesus want the people to understand from this?
Questions.A: Those people thought that they already had a clear understanding about God, but it really was not clear.
Actually, since they had not believed in Jesus, they real did not know God.
Questions.Note: Using the figurative language of Jesus about light and darkness, we could say that because they did not have the light of Jesus in them, their lives were still in darkness.

Section.heading: Luke 11:37-54 Jesus warned the religious leaders that God would punish their hypocrisy.

Questions.Q: The Pharisees pretended to please God, but they were really only pleasing themselves. What should the Pharisees have expected to happen to them because of what they were doing?
Questions.A: They should expect [that God would punish them by causing] horrible things to happen to them. (42, 43, 44, 46, 47, 50-51, 52)

Questions.Q: What were the reasons that the experts in the Law should expect God to cause horrible things to happen to them also?
Questions.A: They made so many rules for the people, it was almost impossible to obey them all. The experts never helped/made it easier for the people to obey them, not even a little bit. (46)

They built tombs/special burial places for the prophets their own forefathers/ancestors had killed, and in that way showed that they approved of what their forefathers had done. Those experts in the Law were not honoring/obeying the prophets God sent them, [meaning John the Baptizer and Jesus,] any more than their forefathers had honored/obeyed God's prophets in their time. (47-51) (Note: It was as if they were honoring their forefathers for having killed the prophets, not that they were honoring the prophets. It was as if the only good prophet was a dead one.)

They had not shared with the people how to really know [God or God's plan for the Messiah to save them nor how to understand the Scriptures which pointed to the Messiah]. This kept those who [wanted to] enter [the kingdom of God/a proper relationship with God] from doing so, and even they themselves were not entering. (52)

Questions.Q: What happened when Jesus had finished speaking about those things?
Questions.A: A Pharisee invited Jesus to eat with him. (37)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do that surprised the Pharisee?
Questions.A: Jesus did not first [ritually] wash before eating the [midday] meal. (38)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about the Pharisees' concern about cleaning things?
Questions.A: They worried about [pleasing God by ritually] cleaning the outsides of [physical] things like plates and cups.
But at the same time, [they did not get rid of] their own bad thoughts and attitudes inside themselves [that did not please God]. (39)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say was inside those Pharisees that did not please God?
Questions.A: They were very greedy and very wicked. (39)
Questions.Note: Jesus explained in Mark 7:15-23 about what should be regarded as clean or unclean in God's eyes. Both of the Greek words which name bad things here in verse 39 are also included in Mark's passage in a longer list of bad actions which come out of a person's heart and make him unclean.

Questions.Q: To whom, do you think, was Jesus referring when he talked about the one who made the outside and the inside of people?
Questions.A: He was referring to God.

Questions.Q: Since God made all parts of a person, which parts, do you think, does God want that person to be most concerned about?
Questions.A: Probably he wants people to be concerned about all parts, but especially the inside, [because that is where bad actions start].
Questions.Note: The person who answers this question will probably name the specific part of the body which he regards as the place of emotions, thoughts or belief. That is a good answer. The translation should not be so general that hearers will think that Jesus contrasted the physical outside with the physical organs inside the abdomen.

Questions.Q: In verse 39 Jesus said that the Pharisees' (centers of emotions, thoughts or belief) were very greedy/full of greedy actions. What does he say that they should do to show that they were clean inside (that is, they were free from sin)?
Questions.A: They should give the things which will be in their hearts, [such as love and a desire to help] to the poor people. (They could do that by sharing their food or possessions with them.) (41)
Questions.Alternative: In verse 39 Jesus said that the Pharisees' (centers of emotions, thoughts or belief) were very greedy. What does he say that they should do to show that they were clean inside (that is, they were free from sin)?

In verse 39 Jesus said that the Pharisees' (centers of emotions, thoughts or belief) were full of greedy actions. What does he say that they should do to show that they were clean inside (that is, they were free from sin)?

In verse 39 Jesus said that the Pharisees' hearts (centers of emotions, thoughts or belief) were very greedy. What does he say that they should do to show that they were clean inside (that is, they were free from sin)?
In verse 39 Jesus said that the Pharisees' hearts were full of greedy actions. What does he say that they should do to show that they were clean inside (that is, they were free from sin)?
In verse 39 Jesus said that the Pharisees' (centers of emotions, thoughts or belief) were very greedy. What does he say that they should do to show that they were free from sin?
In verse 39 Jesus said that the Pharisees' (centers of emotions, thoughts or belief) were full of greedy actions. What does he say that they should do to show that they were free from sin?
In verse 39 Jesus said that the Pharisees' hearts (centers of emotions, thoughts or belief) were very greedy. What does he say that they should do to show that they were free from sin?
In verse 39 Jesus said that the Pharisees' hearts were full of greedy actions. What does he say that they should do to show that they were free from sin?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say that the Pharisees should do about the tithes they had been giving?
Questions.A: He said that they should not stop tithing when they began to judge people fairly and to love God. (42b)

Questions.Q: How, do you think, were the Pharisees like unmarked graves?
Questions.A: [They appeared to obey God, but they were hiding their bad attitudes and actions. In a spiritual sense] they were like dead bodies rotting inside graves of which people were not aware. The people around the Pharisees did not know that they were like that [in their hearts].
Questions.Note: The Pharisees were contaminating those people by teaching them to follow the Pharisees' own bad example. See Num. 19:16 to read how a person became contaminated by stepping on a grave. (44)

Questions.Q: What were the reasons that the Pharisees should expect [that God will punish them by causing] horrible things to happen to them?
Questions.A: They were careful to give God one-tenth of every kind of little plant in their gardens, but they did not care at all about judging [others] fairly or loving God. (42a)
They loved to have [people] honor them when they were in public places, like the synagogue and marketplace. (43)

People [who thought that the Pharisees were good examples to follow in order to obey God] did not realize how bad/evil the Pharisees were on the inside, (that is, in their attitudes and actions). [In a spiritual sense] the Pharisees were dead and rotting. [That caused all the people who followed the Pharisees to become contaminated/unclean in God's eyes just as the Pharisees were.] (44)
Questions.Note: See 10:25-28 where these two things are agreed upon as being the two most important things God wants in a person's life.
Questions.Alternative: What were the reasons that the Pharisees should expect that God will punish them by causing horrible things to happen to them?
What were the reasons that the Pharisees should expect horrible things to happen to them?

Questions.Q: How did one man respond to that powerful/strong talk of Jesus?
Questions.A: He told Jesus that he (Jesus) was insulting even his own group, who were the teachers of the Law [of Moses]. (45)
Questions.Note: Those teachers said that they knew the most about what Moses wrote that God wanted in a person's life. The Pharisees made their own rules to help them live according to what these experts had said.
Questions.Alternative: How did one man respond to that powerful talk of Jesus?
How did one man respond to that strong talk of Jesus?

Questions.Q: Jesus used a word picture about "loading people down with burdens". Of what do you think that heavy load was a picture?
Questions.A: The experts in the Law [of Moses] taught the people many of their own rules, thinking those rules would help people to obey God's rules.
Questions.Note: Do not use this question (or re-write it) if the translation does not contain this word picture.

Questions.Q: Jesus also used a word picture about "lifting a finger" to do work. How much work do you think a person can do by using only one finger?
Questions.A: A person cannot do any useful work by using only one finger.

Questions.Q: How did Jesus apply that meaning to what the experts in the Law of Moses were doing?
Questions.A: They told the people to obey their many rules, but they did not help the people even a small amount [to obey them]. (46)

Questions.Q: Even before God sent out his prophets and apostles, what did he know/say about how they would be treated by the Jews?
Questions.A: He knew that the Jews would kill some and persecute others.
-OR-
He knew that the Jews would kill and persecute some of them.
Questions.Alternative: Even before God sent out his prophets and apostles, what did he know about how they would be treated by the Jews?
Even before God sent out his prophets and apostles, what did he say about how they would be treated by the Jews?

Questions.Q: What, do you think, did the Jews do when they persecuted some of God's prophets and apostles?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: They oppressed and harassed the prophets and apostles on a regular basis for the purpose of having them suffer pain and frustration.
Questions.Note: See L&N 39.45.

Questions.Q: Whom will God hold responsible for the prophets who had been killed by the Jews?
Questions.A: The generation of Jews who were living at the time that Jesus was living would be responsible. (50-51)

Questions.Q: For which prophets will those Jews be punished by God?
Questions.A: God will punish them for all the prophets whom they and their forefathers had killed since the world was first made. (50-51)

Questions.Q: Jesus used a word picture about a key. To what do you think Jesus referred when he spoke of "the key of knowledge"?
Questions.A: He referred to a correct understanding of their [Old Testament] scriptures, which would show the people that Jesus was the Messiah whom God had promised to send to them.
They would also see that they could then enter into a direct relationship with God, accepting his ruling and reigning over them [in the kingdom of God].
Questions.Note: Do not use this question (or re-write it) if the translation does not contain this word picture.

Questions.Q: What happened after Jesus finished talking and left that place?
Questions.A: The Pharisees and the teachers of the Law/scribes began to oppose Jesus fiercely/to be hostile towards him. (53a)
They raised a lot of questions/They mentioned many topics, just waiting until he said something [which they considered wrong. Then the Jewish leaders could punish him] (53-54).

Section.heading: Luke 12:1-12 Jesus warned and encouraged his disciples to revere God and not fear men.

Questions.Q: Who do you think will be the one who will make known all the things which hypocrites have hidden from other people? (See verses 1-3)
Questions.A: God will [on the day he judges all the world, if not before then].

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell his disciples they should not do when people might try to kill them or take them to court?
Questions.A: They should not be afraid.
They should not worry about how to defend themselves or what they will say (11)

Questions.Q: While the Pharisees and teachers of the Law/scribes were opposing Jesus, what was happening with the people who came to listen to Jesus?
Questions.A: They had become a crowd of thousands [of people] who were stepping on each other's feet, [there were so many people so close together]. (1)
Questions.Alternative: While the Pharisees and teachers of the Law were opposing Jesus, what was happening with the people who came to listen to Jesus?
While the Pharisees and scribes were opposing Jesus, what was happening with the people who came to listen to Jesus?

Questions.Q: About what did Jesus warn his disciples?
Questions.A: He warned them about the hypocritical [actions and attitudes of the] Pharisees, which [would affect things like] yeast does. (1)

Questions.Q: Tell me about yeast.
Questions.A: Key Term Check: If yeast is mixed with water and honey or sugar it grows and ferments, causing air bubbles. If a person makes dough by adding flour to that mixture, the yeast will make that dough swell and increase in size.

Questions.Q: What is hypocrisy?/What does a person do who is a hypocrite?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A hypocritical person pretends to believe or do that which other people will approve or that for which other people praise him. He does not do it because he really believes that what he does is right or good.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say would happen to the things the Pharisees or others had covered up or hidden?
Questions.A: Their secrets would be uncovered/disclosed and made known [to others]. // [God] would uncover/disclose them, making [it possible for other people] to know about them. (2)

Questions.Q: How did Jesus explain this further to his disciples?
Questions.A: What they had said in some dark [place or time] would be heard out in the daylight, [that is, out in the open for all to hear]. (3)
What they had whispered into [someone's] ear inside a room would be proclaimed/spoken loudly from the rooftops/housetops. (3)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say was the reason that the disciples were not to fear other men?
Questions.A: People could only kill their bodies, but then could do nothing more [to hurt them]. (4)

Questions.Q: Whom should the disciples fear?
Questions.A: They should fear him who could kill their bodies and who also has authority to throw them into hell. (5)

Questions.Q: What kind of a place is hell?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Hell is a place of punishment for all people who disobey God. It is pictured as a place where fire always burns and it is separated from where God lives. (See "hell" in KBT in the "hell, Hades, abyss" entry.)

Questions.Q: Who do you think the person is whom they should fear?
Questions.A: He is God. Only God has that power and authority.

Questions.Q: What two examples did Jesus tell the disciples in order to show that God cared for them?
Questions.A: God does not forget about each [little] sparrow which, when it is sold, it is worth only a very, very small amount of money. (6)
God even knows each and every hair on a person's head. (7)

Questions.Q: What will Jesus, the Son of Man, do when a person acknowledges/openly says to people that he believes that Jesus is the savior?
Questions.A: Jesus will acknowledge/openly say before God's angels [that that person belongs to him]. (8)
Questions.Alternative: What will Jesus, the Son of Man, do when a person acknowledges that he believes that Jesus is the savior?
What will Jesus, the Son of Man, do when a person openly says to people that he believes that Jesus is the savior?

Questions.Q: What will Jesus do when a person denies to people that he has any association with Jesus?
Questions.A: Jesus will disown/deny him before God's angels [that that person belongs to him]. (9)

Questions.Q: Jesus said that there was a serious sin which could be forgiven and one which could not be forgiven. What were those two sins?
Questions.A: Everyone who says something disrespectful/evil/bad about the Son of Man, Jesus, can be forgiven [by God],
but a person who blasphemes the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven [by God]. (10)
Key Term Check: See the comments on "blaspheme" at 5:21.

Questions.Q: Why should the disciples not worry about what they would say when they needed to defend themselves before people in the synagogue or in the government?
Questions.A: The Holy Spirit would teach them at that time what they should say. (12)

Section.heading: Luke 12:13-21 Jesus told a parable about a foolish man who stored up wealth for himself.

Questions.Q: Jesus warned the people who were listening to him to be on their guard against something. What was it?
Questions.A: They must protect themselves from all the ways of being greedy, that is, desiring to possess more and more money and things. They should not become like that. (15)

Questions.Q: Tell me the parable that Jesus told about a greedy man.
Questions.A: A rich man's land produced a good crop of grain/wheat.
He wanted to keep all of it, but his storage buildings were too small.
He decided to take down the old buildings and put up larger ones.
He boasted to himself that his many good things would take care of him for many years.
Therefore, now he could have feasts and enjoy himself and not worry about working hard any more.
But God said that man was foolish to think only about himself and his future when he did not know that he was about to die that night.
Others would use all those things he had saved for himself. (16-20)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say would happen to anyone who is selfish and greedy?
Questions.A: God will judge those people who are selfish, holding on to the things they possess [and do not share them].

He may make them die to show how foolish all their selfish work was. [Anyone who thinks only of his many possessions and does not think how to please God, will perish/will not have eternal life.] (21)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say a person should do instead of being greedy/selfish with the things he has?
Questions.A: Instead of trying to become rich with the things that make him happy, a person should greatly enjoy using his money and abilities to do what pleases God. (21)
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus say a person should do instead of being greedy with the things he has?
What did Jesus say a person should do instead of being selfish with the things he has?

Questions.Q: What do you think are ways that a person could greatly enjoy using his money and abilities to do what pleases God?
Questions.A: He should first obey God and then use his material wealth in Christian love and compassion. He should try to relieve the needs of others in his family, in the family of believers, and among others. He should do it for God's glory, not his own.

Questions.Q: What did one person in the crowd want Jesus to do for him?
Questions.A: He wanted Jesus to tell his (the man's) brother to divide [properly/fairly] what they had inherited [from their father]. (13)

Questions.Q: How did Jesus respond to this man?
Questions.A: He said that [no one] had appointed him to judge how those brothers were to divide what they had inherited [from their father]. (14)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about how a person should think about the things he possesses?
Questions.A: He said that possessing many things will not make a person's life better/happier nor will it make him live longer. // Having a good life is not based on how many things a person possesses. (15)

Questions.Q: What made the rich man in the parable very happy?
Questions.A: His land had produced a good crop. (16)

Questions.Q: What problem was that man thinking about?
Questions.A: He did not have [enough] place to store all the crops. (17)

Questions.Q: What did he decide to do?
Questions.A: He decided to tear down/take apart his [small/old] buildings and build larger ones in which to store his grain. (18)

Questions.Q: How would he then feel about all those things he was saving?
Questions.A: He would feel satisfied. He also felt that he could relax and enjoy life, thinking that those things would take care of him for many years to come. (19)

Questions.Q: How did God feel about that man's thinking and his actions?
Questions.A: God called him a fool for not realizing he might/would die that same night and never enjoy all the things he had saved for himself. (20)

Section.heading: Luke 12:22-34 Do not worry about the things you need.

Questions.Q: Why were Jesus's disciples not to worry about eating to stay alive and covering their bodies with clothing?
Questions.A: Being alive has more important aspects than worrying about [having enough] food.
Their bodies were also more important than what clothes they would wear on them. (23)

Questions.Q: From all that Jesus had just said about the foolish rich man in verses 16-20, what do you think makes such worrying about one's food and clothes bad?
Questions.A: When a person worries, he thinks about only himself and what he wants, not about God and what he wants for us (28b, 34). It also has no lasting value (26, 33).

Questions.Q: About what should a disciple or follower of Jesus be thinking and on what should he focus his life instead of worrying about food and clothing?
Questions.A: He should seek ways for God to rule and reign in his life and in the lives of others. Then [God] will provide those things [as the person needs them]. (31)
-OR-
When he allows God to rule in his life, God will provide whatever he needs to live, so he should not worry about those things. (31)

Questions.Q: Since God has been pleased already to give blessings related to his kingdom/his ruling over us and providing for us, what should the people who are in God's kingdom do?
Questions.A: They should think more about using their possessions to help people who are in need, and think less about keeping things safe for themselves. When they help others, it is as though they are putting treasure in heaven to use and enjoy later. Their focus will be on pleasing God, not themselves. (33-34)
Questions.Alternative: Since God has been pleased already to give blessings related to his kingdom, what should the people who are in God's kingdom do?
Since God has been pleased already to give blessings related to his ruling over us and providing for us, what should the people who are in God's kingdom do?

Questions.Q: How were the ravens to be an example for Jesus's disciples?
Questions.A: They do not sow/plant [seeds] or reap/harvest [what they had sown/planted], and they do not have special places in which to store [extra food so they could use it later]. Even so, God provides food for them. (24a)

Questions.Q: Since God does that for birds, which do not get ready for the dry time/cold time when no new food will grow, what should that show to the disciples?
Questions.A: It shows that God will provide them with at least all their basic needs. (24b)
-OR-
It shows that God will do more for them because they are worth much more [to him] than the birds. (24b)
Questions.Alternative: Since God does that for birds, which do not get ready for the dry time when no new food will grow, what should that show to the disciples?
Since God does that for birds, which do not get ready for the cold time when no new food will grow, what should that show to the disciples?

Questions.Q: How much longer did Jesus say that a person can make himself live just by worrying about it?
Questions.A: He said that a person cannot make himself live even one hour longer. (25)

Questions.Q: Which part of a person's life can worrying about it help?/How does it help a person to worry?
Questions.A: No part of a person's life is helped./Worrying does not help in any way. (26)

Questions.Q: What example did Jesus use next to teach his disciples not to worry?
Questions.A: He told about the wild flowers/lilies. (27)

Questions.Q: How are the wild flowers to be an example for them?
Questions.A: They do not do any kind of work, but God makes them very beautiful anyway. Not even [ancient King] Solomon in all his beautiful clothes ever dressed as beautifully as one wild flower (27).
Questions.Note: The two kinds of work which Jesus named referred specifically to general physical labor, such as Jewish men did, and to the twisting of fibers into thread/yarn/string, which Jewish women did. If the culture of the translation has similar roles which divide the work of men and women, or if it has two other work roles to which they traditionally refer as indicating men and women, do try to use one of those divisions here.

Questions.Q: If God does that for the wild flowers which are alive only a very short time, what should that have shown to the disciples?
Questions.A: It should have shown that God would provide them with at least all their basic needs. (28)
-OR-
It should have shown that God would do even more for them because they would have a longer, lasting purpose than the flowers (28).

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that Jesus compared the beauty of the wild flowers to Solomon?
Questions.A: Solomon had been king of Israel a long time before Jesus lived. God made him the richest man in all the world. He could buy any beautiful clothing or jewelry that he wanted. Even so, God made the wild flowers more beautiful than King Solomon had ever been.

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that Jesus called his disciples "men of little faith" [in verse 28b]?
Questions.A: Since God is so caring and generous with insignificant [birds and] flowers, his own followers' worries must show their lack of faith/trust in God's ability or interest to provide for them. (28)
-OR-
The heathen/pagan people [who do not have a relationship with God] worry about/focus their lives on all such things. (30)
Questions.Note: (Key Term Check: See "heathen" in KBT in the "Gentiles, pagans, the nations" entry.)
Questions.Alternative: What do you think was the reason that Jesus called his disciples "men of little faith" in verse 28b?
What do you think was the reason that Jesus called his disciples "men of little faith"?

Questions.Q: Who or what, do you think, is this "little flock [of sheep]" to which Jesus spoke? (32a)
Questions.A: Jesus called his disciples a little flock of sheep.
Questions.Alternative: Who or what, do you think, is this "little flock of sheep" to which Jesus spoke? (32a)
Who or what, do you think, is this "little flock" to which Jesus spoke? (32a)

Questions.Q: How might the disciples be like a little flock of sheep which did not need to worry?
Questions.A: By themselves they could become lost and in danger without a shepherd, but [God,] their Father, was watching out for them and had been pleased to provide [them with his] kingdom/what they needed spiritually. He would provide their physical needs, as well. (32)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell his disciples to do which would show that they were not worrying about the things they needed every day?
Questions.A: They should sell what they possessed and give [the money] to the poor [people]. (33a)

Questions.Q: Instead of a person who follows Jesus valuing and gathering earthly possessions/treasures, what should he be valuing and gathering?
Questions.A: He should gather things having great value in heaven where they will never lose their value. He should not gather things like money which falls out of a purse when it wears out and has holes in it. No thief will steal those things in heaven and no moth will destroy those things by eating holes in them. They will last forever. (33)
Questions.Alternative: Instead of a person who follows Jesus valuing and gathering earthly possessions, what should he be valuing and gathering?
Instead of a person who follows Jesus valuing and gathering earthly treasures, what should he be valuing and gathering?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say made this matter so very important to God?
Questions.A: What a person regards as very important will be the thing on which he focuses his thoughts and desires. If the focus of a person's heart is on earthly things, God will know that person is not focusing on him. A person should value pleasing God, not pleasing himself. (34)

Section.heading: Luke 12:35-48 Jesus's disciples were to be faithful servants, ready for their Master's return at any time.

Questions.Q: How did Jesus apply the two stories to his disciples?
Questions.A: The disciples must be ready because [he,] the Son of Man, will return when they do not expect him. (40)

Questions.Q: What will the master do for that servant/slave whom he found was ready for his return, doing the work the master had told him to do?
