Questions.A: The master will reward him/make him happy by putting him in charge of (that is, giving him authority over) all that he owns. (44)
Questions.Alternative: What will the master do for that servant whom he found was ready for his return, doing the work the master had told him to do?
What will the master do for that slave whom he found was ready for his return, doing the work the master had told him to do?

Questions.Q: What will the master do for that servant/slave whom he found was not ready for his return because the servant/slave was not doing the work the master had told him to do?
Questions.A: The master will return at a time when that servant/slave is not expecting him. (46)
He will cut him into pieces/punish him severely. (46)
He will place him with those who were unfaithful/did not believe [him]. (46)
He will beat him with many blows. (47)
Questions.Alternative: What will the master do for that servant whom he found was not ready for his return because the servant was not doing the work the master had told him to do?
What will the master do for that servant whom he found was not ready for his return because the slave was not doing the work the master had told him to do?
What will the master do for that slave whom he found was not ready for his return because the servant was not doing the work the master had told him to do?
What will the master do for that slave whom he found was not ready for his return because the slave was not doing the work the master had told him to do?

Questions.Q: How would a servant/slave wait for his master who is expected to return from a wedding feast?
Questions.A: He would be dressed [to work] (35),
with lamps burning (35),
watching/alert/ready (37) when the master returns and knocks [on the door] to open it immediately for him (36).
Questions.Alternative: How would a servant wait for his master who is expected to return from a wedding feast?
How would a slave wait for his master who is expected to return from a wedding feast?

Questions.Q: How will those servants/slaves whom the master finds ready and waiting for him be fortunate/made very happy?
Questions.A: The master will dress to serve them, (37)
have them rest/relax at the table [in order to eat], (37)
and then he will bring them what they wish [to eat]. (37)
Questions.Alternative: How will those servants whom the master finds ready and waiting for him be fortunate?
How will those servants whom the master finds ready and waiting for him be made very happy?
How will those slaves whom the master finds ready and waiting for him be fortunate?
How will those slaves whom the master finds ready and waiting for him be made very happy?

Questions.Q: If the master does not return until the middle of the night or just before daylight, what should he find his servants/slaves doing then?
Questions.A: They should be alert/watching/ready [for his return]. (38)
Questions.Alternative: If the master does not return until the middle of the night or just before daylight, what should he find his servants doing then?
If the master does not return until the middle of the night or just before daylight, what should he find his slaves doing then?

Questions.Q: What would a house owner do if he knew when a thief would come?
Questions.A: He would not have allowed his house to be broken into. (39)

Questions.Q: What did Peter ask about those two earlier stories?
Questions.A: He wanted to know if they, [the 12 apostles,] were to apply them to themselves or whether the stories were for everyone to apply. (41)

Questions.Q: How did Jesus answer Peter's question?
Questions.A: He answered Peter with another question and a parable. (42-48)

Questions.Q: What kind of servant manager did Jesus say would be happy, and rewarded, when his master returns unexpectedly?
Questions.A: He is one who is faithful/trustworthy and wise (42),
because he does what he was told to do, which was to care for and nourish the other workers at the right times (43).

Questions.Q: What kind of servant manager will be punished when his master returns unexpectedly?
Questions.A: He is one who beats the [other] servants, both men and women, (45)
and [enjoys himself] both eating and drinking and getting drunk. (45)

Questions.Q: How will the master decide which bad servant deserves many blows of punishment and which one deserves only a few blows?
Questions.A: The one who knew what his master wanted, but did not get ready or do what he had been told will be beaten with many blows (47);
but the one who did not know [what the master wanted] will be beaten with few blows (48a).

Questions.Q: What will God expect/require from his servants to whom he has given many blessings and abilities?
Questions.A: He will expect/require those people to do much with those gifts, to give him a full/equal amount of use/service. (48b)
Questions.Alternative: What will God expect from his servants to whom he has given many blessings and abilities?
What will God require from his servants to whom he has given many blessings and abilities?

Questions.Q: What will God expect/require from his servants to whom he has entrusted much responsibility/authority?
Questions.A: He will expect/require those servants/people to do even more than others may do, extra service for him. (48c)
Questions.Alternative: What will God expect from his servants to whom he has entrusted much responsibility?
What will God expect from his servants to whom he has entrusted much authority?
What will God require from his servants to whom he has entrusted much responsibility?
What will God require from his servants to whom he has entrusted much authority?

Section.heading: Luke 12:49-53 Families will split and oppose each other over believing in Jesus.

Questions.Q: What do you think will be the cause of the Jews separating into two groups, even within families?
Questions.A: Some will believe that Jesus came to save them from their sins and other people will not believe.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say was a purpose in his coming to the earth?
Questions.A: He came to cast/throw/put fire on [the people of] the earth. (49)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus wish concerning that fire?
Questions.A: He wished that it had already been lit/kindled. (49)

Questions.Q: It is not written anywhere in the Bible that Jesus actually lit something on fire and threw it onto the ground or onto people. What do you think he meant by those words?
Questions.A: He meant that he had come to announce that God would judge people's sin and punish them for it.
-OR-
He meant that his message would cause people to divide into groups, some who believed him and some who did not believe him.
-OR-
He meant that his message would destroy/remove all evil and sin from those people whom he found faithful at his return.
Questions.Note: This would be like burning off the bad things in metal ores in order to make them pure and very valuable.

Questions.Q: Jesus had already been baptized by John (see 3:21-22). What do you think this baptism was which Jesus said that he needed to have happen to him?
Questions.A: His suffering and his dying on the cross. (50)

Questions.Q: How was his thinking about this affecting him?
Questions.A: He was very distressed over it./He felt as though he was carrying a great mental burden and kept on thinking about it. (50)

Questions.Q: How long would he be thinking like that?
Questions.A: Jesus would suffer like that until he died/until the [whole] thing was completed/accomplished. (50)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say was the reason that he had come to the earth? Was it to cause people to come together in peace or to cause people to separate/divide into groups?
Questions.A: He said that he came to cause people to separate/divide into groups. (51)
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus say was the reason that he had come to the earth? Was it to cause people to come together in peace or to cause people to separate into groups?
What did Jesus say was the reason that he had come to the earth? Was it to cause people to come together in peace or to cause people to divide into groups?

Questions.Q: What will happen in some families?
Questions.A: Families will be split, three people in one group, two in another. (52)
A father will be against [his] son and a son against [his] father, (53)
a mother will be against [her] daughter and a daughter against [her] mother, (53)
a mother-in-law will be against her daughter-in-law and a daughter-in-law against [her] mother-in-law. (53)

Section.heading: Luke 12:54-56 People must look at what is happening in the world and understand that those are signs that God is ready to judge them.

Questions.Q: To whom was Jesus speaking here?
Questions.A: Jesus was speaking to the crowd [of people who had been listening to him]. (54)

Questions.Q: Tell me about one way that the speakers of your language recognize that a change in the weather is coming.
Questions.Note: (This is to build rapport with the respondent and to introduce the following questions.)

Questions.Q: How did the Jews know when it was going to rain?
Questions.A: They saw clouds coming from the west. (54)

Questions.Q: How did they know it was going to be hot?
Questions.A: They knew it would be hot when the south wind blew. (55)

Questions.Q: What were they saying about what was happening at that time [when Jesus was] among them?
Questions.A: They said nothing. They did not recognize that anything special was happening. (56)
Questions.Alternative: What were they saying about what was happening at that time when Jesus was among them?
What were they saying about what was happening at that time among them?

Questions.Q: What was happening among them that they should have recognized as a sign of things to come?
Questions.A: Jesus had been preaching that the kingdom of God had come and about a time of judging all people. He had also been doing miracles by the power of God.

Questions.Q: What name did Jesus call the people who did not recognize the meaning of those signs he had been doing?
Questions.A: He called them hypocrites. (56)

Questions.Q: In what way were those people being hypocrites?
Questions.A: They thought of themselves as very wise and clever to interpret the signs of the earth and sky, but could not interpret what was happening right around/among them. (56)

Section.heading: Luke 12:57-59 People must make peace with others quickly.

Questions.Q: What lesson did Jesus try to teach the people in these verses?
Questions.A: He urged people to make peace with other people and with God before they must pay the penalty for their doing wrong. If they do not make peace, they might be punished and never be free again. (58-59)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus advise his listeners to do?
Questions.A: They should decide what is right on their own. (57)

Questions.Q: What picture language did Jesus use here?
Questions.A: He used the picture of one person taking another to the court to settle a dispute, apparently over money. If the person who has/owes the debt does not straighten the problem quickly, he may be thrown into the jail and be forced to stay there. (58-59)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus imply was the right thing to do?
Questions.A: The person being taken to the judge/court should admit that he did wrong to his accuser/opponent and work hard to settle the problem quickly. (58)

Questions.Q: What if the problem is not settled before facing a leader/ruler/judge?
Questions.A: What the judge decides will be final, and that probably will mean that the person would be confined somewhere, like a jail. (58)
Questions.Alternative: What if the problem is not settled before facing a leader?
What if the problem is not settled before facing a ruler?
What if the problem is not settled before facing a judge?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say was the only way for that person to get out of the jail?
Questions.A: He could get out only if he paid back everything, including the last small part [of the debt] which he owed. (59)

Questions.Q: Does it sound to you as though it is possible to pay the money back while you are in jail, if you did not have it to pay back before you went into jail?
Questions.A: No, it probably is not possible.
Questions.Note: Debtors held in Roman prisons could be imprisoned until their friends or family paid the debt.

Questions.Q: If this picture language is referring to God as our judge, and we stand before him and have not repented, what did Jesus imply would happen to us?
Questions.A: [God] will put us into Hell and we will never get/come out.

Section.heading: Luke 13:1-5 If a person does not repent, God will destroy him/his soul.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus warn the people who were listening to him?
Questions.A: He warned them that unless they repented, they would perish/die/be destroyed [by the Roman soldiers] in the same way as those men from Galilee. (1, 3, 5)
-OR-
He warned them that unless they repented, they also would perish/die/be destroyed [by God]. (3, 5)

Key Term Check: See "destroy, perish, (be lost" in KBT. Although the same Greek word was used in 5:37, 8:24 and 11:51 in non-spiritual contexts, the language of the translation may not allow that earlier translation to be used here to mean the total destruction of spiritual things.)

Questions.Q: What did some people in the crowd with Jesus tell him?
Questions.A: Some [Jews] from Galilee [province] had been killed by [the Roman governor] Pilate['s soldiers] while they were offering sacrifices [to God within the temple grounds], and their blood mixed with [the blood of] their sacrifices. (1)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus imply as to how the people seemed to regard that terrible act?
Questions.A: They seemed to have thought that God had punished those people because they had sinned more [than the rest of the people]. (2)

Questions.Q: What was the similar example which Jesus himself wanted the people to think about?
Questions.A: Eighteen people had been killed/had died when a tower at Siloam [in Jerusalem] fell on them. Jesus did not want the people to also think that those people had died because they were greater/worse sinners than the other people who lived in Jerusalem. (4)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about that as being the reason that all those people had died in each of those troubles?
Questions.A: He said strongly, "No, [that is not right]." (3, 5)

Section.heading: Luke 13:6-9 Jesus told a parable about a fig tree that produced no fruit.

Questions.Q: (Read 13:5 again.) What do you think was the way that Jesus wanted the people to understand the meaning of this parable after just having talked to them about repenting?
Questions.A: The way that a man judges a fruit tree is the same way that God will judge a person's life.
If people do not repent and begin doing what pleases God, then they also are of no value to him and he will destroy them.

Questions.Q: Where had the man planted this fig tree?
Questions.A: He planted it in his vineyard/grape garden. (6)

Questions.Q: What did the man see when he went to find fruit on that tree?
Questions.A: He did not find any [fruit there]. (6)

Questions.Q: How many years had that man come to check on that tree, but had never found any fruit?
Questions.A: He had come for three years. (7)

Questions.Q: Why did he tell the man who took care of his garden to cut down that tree?
Questions.A: The tree was using [valuable] space and/or plant food/nourishment which were/was in the ground. (7)

Questions.Q: What did the gardener suggest that he should do first before the owner cut down that tree?
Questions.A: He said that over the next year he would dig around it and put manure/fertilizer [into the dirt]. (8)

Questions.Q: How would the owner know whether he should allow that tree to stay or cut it down?
Questions.A: If it bore fruit the next year, [it could stay], if not, [the owner] should cut it down. (9)

Section.heading: Luke 13:10-17 Jesus healed a crippled woman on the Sabbath Day.

Questions.Q: What does this event happening in the synagogue on a Sabbath Day show us about Jesus?
Questions.A: He used God's power over Satan (13, 16) and [other] spirits (11-12).
He had compassion on people who needed help, regardless of which day it was. (11-12, 14)
-AND/OR-
He had power from God which showed his authority over rules and regulations made by men. (16)

Questions.Q: What does this event show us about some of the Jews' religious leaders?
Questions.A: They did not believe that Jesus's power and teaching showed that he was the one God had sent to be the Messiah or savior. Because they did not believe that he had any authority from God over spiritual things, they also did not believe that he had any authority to disobey their rules about the Sabbath Day.

Questions.Q: What was wrong with one woman who was in the synagogue?
Questions.A: She had been crippled for eighteen years./She was bent over and could not straighten up. (11)

Questions.Q: What had caused that problem?
Questions.A: A[n evil] spirit had caused it. (11)
Questions.Note: In verse 16, Jesus said that spirit was Satan.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell that woman?
Questions.A: He called her [to come] and told her that she had been set free from/healed of her problem. (12)

Questions.Q: How was she able to stand up straight again?
Questions.A: Jesus touched her and she was normal/standing straight again [by God's power]. (13)

Questions.Q: What did the woman do after she was standing straight again?
Questions.A: She praised God. (13)

Questions.Q: What made the ruler of the synagogue angry?
Questions.A: It was the Sabbath Day, but Jesus had healed [the woman anyway]. (14)

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that made him angry?
Questions.A: The Jewish leaders had said that was work, and God had said that no one was to work on the Sabbath Day. (See Exod. 20:9 and Deut. 5:13.)

Questions.Q: What did the ruler say to the people?
Questions.A: He said that they should come on one of the other six days [of the week when it was right to work] and be healed then. (14)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus call this man and the others who felt the same way?
Questions.A: He called them hypocrites. (15)

Questions.Q: What reason did Jesus give for calling the synagogue leaders hypocrites?
Questions.A: They untied their oxen and donkeys [which had been tied only a short time] on the Sabbath to walk around and get water to drink, but they did not want [Jesus on the Sabbath] to set free this woman who had been bound (i.e., controlled) by the devil for 18 years. (15-16)
Questions.Note: If the leaders thought that God cared about how they treated their animals on the Sabbath Day, then he surely cared much more about one of his chosen people. The synagogue leaders considered healing to be work. Jesus pointed out that caring for their animals also was work! Therefore they were hypocrites regarding not working on the Sabbath.

Questions.Q: What was the woman's relationship to Abraham?
Questions.A: Jesus called her Abraham's daughter. That meant she was a descendant of the Jew's ancestor Abraham.

Questions.Q: How did the different groups of people react to what Jesus had said and done?
Questions.A: Those men who had opposed Jesus were humiliated/shamed.
The [other] people rejoiced at all the wonderful/splendid things Jesus was doing. (17)

Section.heading: Luke 13:18-21 Jesus told two parables to show how the kingdom of God would increase.

Questions.Q: What, do you think, was Jesus trying to teach the people about the kingdom of God in these two parables?
Questions.A: The kingdom of God may appear to be very small and insignificant [at the time of Jesus], but it would increase in size and influence. // He was teaching that those who were in God's kingdom were few [in number] then, but there would be a large group in the future.
In the end, the kingdom of God would affect everyone and be a place of rest for many people. (19b, 21b)

Questions.Q: To what did Jesus compare the kingdom of God?
Questions.A: To a seed of the mustard tree/plant. (19)
Questions.Note: (Note: If the mustard tree/plant is not part of the local culture, the translation does not have to say that the seed is from that specific plant. It should, however, definitely refer to some very small seed that the people know will grow into a strong plant.
If the mustard tree/plant is used in the translation, deciding whether to call it a "tree" or a "plant" will depend on the way that the culture classifies all the growing things.)

Questions.Q: Tell me about that seed.
Questions.A: The seed is very tiny, but it grows into a large, strong tree/plant with branches. Birds make nests/places to rest in it. (19)

Questions.Q: What happened to the tiny seed in Jesus's story?/What did that tiny seed do?
Questions.A: A man threw it into his garden and it grew there, became a tree/a plant as tall as a tree, and birds made nests/places to rest in its branches. (19)

Questions.Q: To what else did Jesus compare the kingdom of God?
Questions.A: He compared the kingdom of God to yeast. (21)
Questions.Note: See 12:1 above.

Questions.Q: What happened to the yeast in Jesus's story?
Questions.A: A woman added the yeast to a mixture of much flour [and a smaller amount of liquid]. (21)

Questions.Q: What do you think the yeast did to the dough when it was mixed in well?
Questions.A: It caused all the dough to swell/increase in size.

Section.heading: Luke 13:22-30 There is only one right way to enter the kingdom of God.

Questions.Q: How did the house owner in the parable decide which people were allowed to enter and which people were told to leave?
Questions.A: Only those people who had come through the narrow door/the correct way (24) before the door was shut (25) were allowed to enter. The others were told to leave. (27)

Questions.Q: What do you think that the narrow door is a picture of?
Questions.A: Jesus meant that there is only one small way to enter the kingdom of God. (Perhaps it referred to repenting of one's sins as being the only way to enter the kingdom of God). (24)
-OR-
Jesus meant that there are not many opportunities left to enter the kingdom of God, so they must do so quickly. (25)

Questions.Q: What was Jesus doing as he traveled on his way to Jerusalem?
Questions.A: He went through cities and villages teaching [the people]. (22)

Questions.Q: What did someone ask Jesus about the people whom God was saving?
Questions.A: He asked if only a few people were to be saved. (23)

Questions.Q: To what, do you think, was Jesus referring when he spoke about entering a narrow door into a house?
Questions.A: He was talking about entering the kingdom of God.

Questions.Q: To what, do you think, was Jesus referring when he told the people to work hard at entering the kingdom of God?
Questions.A: He meant that it is not easy/simple for anyone to get in.

Questions.Q: How many people did he say will try to enter the kingdom of God?
Questions.A: Many [people] will try to enter. (24)

Questions.Q: How many people will enter?
Questions.A: Not many will enter./Not nearly as many will enter as tried to enter. (24)

Questions.Q: To whom, do you think, did the owner of the house in the parable really refer?
Questions.A: He referred to Jesus.
Questions.Note: Jesus is understood to be the owner, rather than God, his father. That comes from other times when Jesus spoke of the banquet/feast as a wedding feast in which he is the bridegroom. It can also be implied from verse 25 in the passive verb "has been raised/has risen".

Questions.Q: What will people do after Jesus closes the door of the kingdom?
Questions.A: People will stand on the outside knocking and asking the Lord to open the door for them. (25)

Questions.Q: What will Jesus answer them?
Questions.A: He will say he did not know them or where they had come from. (He had no close association or relationship with them.) (25)

Questions.Q: How will those people who are outside the kingdom try to show that they thought that they had a relationship with Jesus?
Questions.A: They will say they ate [meals] with him and that he had taught in their streets/towns. (26)

Questions.Q: What will Jesus then tell them?
Questions.A: He will tell them the same thing as before. He had no personal relationship with them. (27)
He also will tell them to go away from him, (27)
and he will call them all [people who] do evil things. (27)

Questions.Q: What will those people who did not enter the kingdom do when they see Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all the prophets in the kingdom, but they themselves are not in it?
Questions.A: They will weep and grind their teeth [in rage and frustration]. (28)

Questions.Q: Where will the people who are at the feast in the kingdom of God come from?
Questions.A: They will come from all the directions/parts of the world, (east, west, north, and south) [where the Gentiles/the non-Jews live]. (29)

Questions.Q: Who do you think are the people whom Jesus said were last, but will be first in the kingdom of God?
Questions.A: Some of the people from all over the world [who are not Jews, or who are not important in ways that the world thinks is important, or who hear last about Jesus as their savior].

Questions.Q: Who do you think are the people whom Jesus said were first, but would be last in the kingdom of God?
Questions.A: Some of the Jews [who thought that God would automatically allow them to enter because they were descendants of Abraham]. (God had said that they were his special people. They also had been the first culture to hear the Good News about being saved.)

Questions.Q: What is the reason, do you think, that those people will be as angry and frustrated as the people in this parable?
Questions.A: They will see some of their ancestors and other Jews there in the kingdom and will feel they, too, should be there because they are also Jews. But Jesus does not choose people on that basis, so they are left outside the kingdom (and the blessings people will receive there).

Section.heading: Luke 13:31-35 Jesus was not concerned about how King Herod would treat him, but how the people of Jerusalem treated God's messengers.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus's words about King Herod imply to you about changing his plans to continue going towards Jerusalem?
Questions.A: Jesus talked as though he was not worried about King Herod, but would continue doing just as he had already planned to do./Jesus indicated he did not intend to change his plans.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say were the reasons that he spoke so sadly about Jerusalem?
Questions.A: Jesus spoke sadly because [the people of] Jerusalem had often killed the prophets and other messengers God had sent to them, (34)
and they had been refusing his (Jesus') attempts to protect them from dangers. (34)

Questions.Q: Why did some Pharisees tell Jesus to go to another place?
Questions.A: They said that [King] Herod wanted to kill him. (31)

Questions.Q: What name did Jesus call King Herod?
Questions.A: He called him a fox (or some other culturally appropriate comparison). (32)

Questions.Q: Tell me how a person can be like that.
Questions.A: The person is sly and crafty.
-AND/OR-
The person is not really of any importance.
-AND/OR-
The person is cruel.
Questions.Note: The above three sentences give the Jews' reasons for calling a person a fox. Some, or all, of those reasons should apply to whatever comparison is used in the translation.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about his plans and King Herod?
Questions.A: He said that he would continue for a [short] time to cast out demons [from people] and heal [their] diseases and then would reach his goal/the end of his work just as he had planned. He said that the Pharisees could tell King Herod that. (32)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus imply about who he was and where he would die?
Questions.A: He implied that he was a prophet and that he would die in Jerusalem. (33)

Questions.Q: Jesus was not near Jerusalem or in that city. What do you think were the reasons that Jesus called out to Jerusalem?
Questions.A: He was thinking so much about the people who lived there that he spoke to them as if they were right there with him.
-OR-
The Pharisees who had come to him [from Jerusalem] could take his words/message back to the other people when they returned there.

Questions.Q: What had the people who lived in Jerusalem done to prophets and other messengers whom God had sent to them?
Questions.A: They had [often] killed the prophets and stoned [to their death] others [God had] sent to them. (34)

Questions.Q: Tell me about stoning people.
Questions.A: Stoning refers to throwing stones, big or small, at a person for the purpose of killing him. Usually many people joined in the throwing.
Questions.Note: Stoning was a way that God had said the Jews were to punish a person who blasphemed him. When the people of Jerusalem had stoned God's messengers, it was because the people or leaders had not accepted those prophets' messages as having come from God. They said that the messenger had made fun of God and had been disrespectful to him. The punishment for that was to die by stoning. (See Lev. 24:13-16.)
Use this question only if the translation does not already make the meaning clear.

Questions.Q: Whom do you think that Jesus meant when he spoke about the children of Jerusalem?
Questions.A: He meant all the people who lived there, not just the children.
-OR-
He meant all the people who depended on the religious leaders there to show them how to have a right relationship with God.
-OR-
He meant all the Jews.

Questions.Q: Jesus had compared King Herod to a fox. To what does he compare the people of Jerusalem?
Questions.A: He compared them to chicks which the mother hen wants to gather together [in order to hide/protect them] under her wings. (34)

Questions.Q: Who wanted to protect those people as a mother hen does her chicks?
Questions.A: Jesus himself wanted to protect them.. (34)

Questions.Q: How had the people of Jerusalem responded to Jesus?
Questions.A: They were not willing to listen to/do what he had told them. (34)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus want them to realize?
Questions.A: Their city/temple/country was no longer protected [by God]. It would be destroyed. (35)
Questions.Note: The Roman army did destroy Jerusalem and the temple and sent all the Jews away from there while the disciple John was still living. See Matt. 27:25.

Questions.Q: To what time, do you think, was Jesus referring when the people of Jerusalem/the Jews would finally ask the Lord God to bless him?
Questions.A: He referred to the time when Jews would believe that he was the Messiah whom God had sent.
-OR-
He referred to the time while he was still alive when he would arrive in Jerusalem for the last time (now called Palm Sunday), when the crowds of people at Jerusalem would welcome him. (See 19:38.)
-OR-
He referred to the time when he would come back to earth from heaven as God's representative.
Questions.Alternative: To what time, do you think, was Jesus referring when the people of Jerusalem Jews would finally ask the Lord God to bless him?
To what time, do you think, was Jesus referring when the people of the Jews would finally ask the Lord God to bless him?

Questions.Q: What would the Jews say at that time about Jesus?
Questions.A: They would say that God should bless him who was the one who had come in God's name [as he had said about himself all the time he was here on the earth]. (35)

Section.heading: Luke 14:1-6 On a Sabbath Day, Jesus healed a man who had swollen arms and legs.

Questions.Q: This event happening on a Sabbath Day. What does that show us about Jesus?
Questions.A: When people needed [God's] help, it did not matter which day it happened to be. Jesus had compassion on them. (1-4)

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that the Pharisees and the experts in the Law did not answer Jesus either time he asked them a question/made a strong statement to them?
Questions.A: The way that Jesus had asked/said what he did implied that everyone would agree with him.
What he had said was what each of them knew they should do or wanted to do, even on the Sabbath Day.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think was the reason that the Pharisees and the experts in the Law did not answer Jesus either time he asked them a question?
What do you think was the reason that the Pharisees and the experts in the Law did not answer Jesus either time he made a strong statement to them?

Questions.Q: Where was Jesus when he healed the man?
Questions.A: He was at the house of a leader/ruler of the Pharisees. (1)

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that the people/Pharisees who were there were watching Jesus carefully?
Questions.A: There was a man with swollen arms and legs there in front of Jesus (2). They probably wanted to see if Jesus would heal him on the Sabbath Day.
Questions.Note: The experts in the Law were right there to be witnesses who later could accuse Jesus of breaking God's Law and, thusly, deserved to die (see Exod. 20: 8-11; Num. 15:32-36).
Questions.Alternative: What do you think was the reason that the people who were there were watching Jesus carefully?
What do you think was the reason that the Pharisees who were there were watching Jesus carefully?

Questions.Q: How did the Pharisees and the experts in the Law answer Jesus's question to them?
Questions.A: They were silent./They did not answer him. (4)

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that the Pharisees and experts in the Law did not answer Jesus?
Questions.A: They did not want to answer Jesus's questions because they knew they had not been doing what God wanted them to do. [Moses's Law was their guide, and they knew that they were not following it as they should.]

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do with the sick man?
Questions.A: Jesus took hold of the man and healed him, then sent him away. (4)

Questions.Q: What examples did Jesus give of things that those people who were watching him would immediately try to get out of a well, even on the Sabbath Day?
Questions.A: He talked about a person's son (or donkey) and his ox. (5)

Questions.Q: Tell me about wells.
Questions.A: A well is a hole men dig for the purpose of bringing some liquid up from under the ground. In Jesus's example, the people would have understood it to be a well for water.
Questions.Note: Use this question only if the translation does not already make the meaning clear.

Questions.Q: How did the Pharisees and the experts in the Law respond to Jesus?
Questions.A: There was nothing they could say in response to that. (6)

Section.heading: Luke 14:7-14 God honors people who are humble.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell the people at the Pharisee's feast about receiving great honor and not great shame?
Questions.A: People who seek honor for themselves will be shamed/embarrassed/humiliated. It is the person who is humble whom [God] will honor. (11) (A person should not expect to be honored. Others should decide if, or how, a person is to be honored.)

Questions.Q: What did he tell them about being a good host?
Questions.A: The host should honor the poor [people] and those who have physical problems by inviting them to special meals. (12-14)

Questions.Q: How should people decide when they should be honored and when other people should be honored?
Questions.A: We should always be humble (11) and allow others, or God, to honor us when they decide it is appropriate (14).

Questions.Q: What did Jesus see that prompted/caused him to tell this parable/story?
Questions.A: He noticed how they were choosing the best/most honored places to sit for themselves. (7)
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus see that prompted him to tell this parable?
What did Jesus see that prompted him to tell this story?
What did Jesus see that caused him to tell this parable?
What did Jesus see that caused him to tell this story?

Questions.Q: Tell me how the people in your language area know/mark/designate the place/places of honor at a feast.
Questions.A: (The translation may use whatever term best shows what is the place/those places of honor.)
Questions.Alternative: Tell me how the people in your language area know the place of honor at a feast.
Tell me how the people in your language area know the places of honor at a feast.
Tell me how the people in your language area mark the place of honor at a feast.
Tell me how the people in your language area mark the places of honor at a feast.
Tell me how the people in your language area designate the place of honor at a feast.
Tell me how the people in your language area designate the places of honor at a feast.
Tell me how your people designate the place of honor at a feast.
Tell me how your people know the place of honor at a feast.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say might happen if a guest sat in/chose the most honored place at a wedding feast?
Questions.A: The host might come with someone else who has greater honor than he does.
The host might tell him to move to some other place because the host wants to honor the other guest more. (8-9)
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus say might happen if a guest sat in the most honored place at a wedding feast?
What did Jesus say might happen if a guest chose the most honored place at a wedding feast?

Questions.Q: How would that first guest feel? What would he have to do?
Questions.A: The first guest would be embarrassed to have to move to the place of least honor. (9)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say a guest should do instead of taking the place of most honor?
Questions.A: He said that the guest should choose the place of least honor. (10)

Questions.Q: What might the host of the feast say to that guest?
Questions.A: He might say, "[My] Friend, move to a better (more honored) place." (10)
Questions.Note: Many of the English language translations refer to the places of honor in this story with words such as "move up/higher/forward" or "move down/lower/backward" to reflect greater or lesser honor. That is culturally appropriate for English, but may not be the appropriate way to express greater or lesser honor in the language of the translation. Use what is correct for the language of the translation.

Questions.Q: What will be the result of that?
Questions.A: All the other guests will see him being honored by the host. [And they, too, will honor him.] (10)

Questions.Q: Whom would you say that people usually invite to come and eat food with them?
Questions.A: They invite only their friends, relatives, or people whom they want to impress/influence, such as those who are rich neighbors. (12a)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say is the reason that we should not do that?
Questions.A: Those people are all able to invite us in return and pay us back. (12b)
Questions.Note: He implied that there is no long term benefit in doing that. We have already received whatever good might come back to us (see 14:14b).

Questions.Q: Whom should people also invite to come and eat a feast with them?
Questions.A: We should invite [people who are] poor, crippled, lame, or blind. (13)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say is the reason that we should do that?
Questions.A: We truly will be happy/feel good about it. (14a)
God will repay us in some way when he raises all the righteous people back to life. (14c)
Questions.Note: See the explanation of "blessed" at 6:20.

Section.heading: Luke 14:15-24 Jesus told a parable about people who refused to come to a great feast.

Questions.Q: Of what do you think this great feast/banquet is a picture?
Questions.A: The feast is a picture of God inviting many people to enjoy all the blessings of being in his kingdom. (15)
Questions.Alternative: Of what do you think this great feast is a picture?
Of what do you think this banquet is a picture?

Questions.Q: What do you think will happen to all those people who are invited by God's servants/messengers and then do come to the feast?
Questions.A: They will enjoy all the blessings God has made ready for them.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think will happen to all those people who are invited by God's servants and then do come to the feast?
What do you think will happen to all those people who are invited by God's messengers and then do come to the feast?

Questions.Q: Some people had been invited first, but refused to come when the servant/slave told them everything for the feast was ready. Who do you think that the people who were listening to Jesus understood those people to be?
Questions.A: They understood those people to be the Jews, [their own people].
Questions.Alternative: Some people had been invited first, but refused to come when the servant told them everything for the feast was ready. Who do you think that the people who were listening to Jesus understood those people to be?

Some people had been invited first, but refused to come when the slave told them everything for the feast was ready. Who do you think that the people who were listening to Jesus understood those people to be?

Questions.Q: What will happen to those people who had been invited first, but did not want to come to that feast?
Questions.A: Not one of them will be able to have even a small idea (or, figuratively, even a taste,) of how good God's feast/blessing is. (24)
Questions.Note: Jesus implied that those people would not have another opportunity to come. God will not send his messengers to ask/invite them again.

Questions.Q: Read verse 15 again. Do you think that Jesus's parable showed that the man who spoke in verse 15 was right in what he said, or that he was wrong?
Questions.A: He was right about the blessings for those people who come to the feast,

but Jesus also made it clear that many who had first been invited had refused to come when everything was ready (17b-20). They would not receive another opportunity to enjoy the blessings, even though, earlier, they once had been invited (24).

Questions.Q: Who responded to what Jesus had been saying about inviting people to feasts?
Questions.A: One of the people who was [eating] at the table with Jesus responded. (15)

Questions.Q: Of whom do you think that the man who prepared a great feast is a picture?
Questions.A: He is a picture of God.

Questions.Q: A servant/slave went and told the people who had been invited that they should come immediately to the feast. Of whom do you think that the servant/slave is a picture?
Questions.A: The servant is a picture of Jesus.
Questions.Alternative: A servant went and told the people who had been invited that they should come immediately to the feast. Of whom do you think that the servant is a picture?
A servant went and told the people who had been invited that they should come immediately to the feast. Of whom do you think that the slave is a picture?
A slave went and told the people who had been invited that they should come immediately to the feast. Of whom do you think that the servant is a picture?
A slave went and told the people who had been invited that they should come immediately to the feast. Of whom do you think that the slave is a picture?

Questions.Q: What do you think was the way that the people had been told earlier about the feast that God would have?
Questions.A: They had been invited long before by God's prophets. (Jesus had come at that time to tell those people that everything was ready.)

Questions.Q: What did those people who had been invited earlier then say to the servant/slave?
Questions.A: Everyone had some kind of excuse [for not coming]. (18)
Questions.Alternative: What did those people who had been invited earlier then say to the servant?
What did those people who had been invited earlier then say to the slave?

Questions.Q: Tell me some of their excuses.
Questions.A: One person said that he had bought a field/garden/farm and had to go to see it. (18)
Another [person] said that he had bought five yoke/pair of oxen and was going to try them out/see if they did good work/see how well they plowed together. (19)
Another [person] said that he had just married [and needed to spend time with his wife]. (20)

Questions.Q: What made the owner of the house angry?
Questions.A: He was angry that all those people whom he had invited earlier refused to come after he had made everything ready.

Questions.Q: What did he then tell his servant/slave to do?
Questions.A: He told the servant/slave to go quickly to the city's streets and alleys
and bring the poor, or crippled, or blind, or lame [people whom he found there] to his feast. (21)
Questions.Alternative: What did he then tell his servant to do?
What did he then tell his slave to do?

Questions.Q: Do you think that the servant/slave went, did that and returned, or do you think that he had done it already, before the house owner told him to do it?
Questions.A: A servant/slave probably would not have done it before his lord/master told him to do so. He probably did go quickly and bring back those people he had found.
Questions.Note: It may be that the brief wording here indicates just how quickly the servant went and did what his master had told him to do. If the translation seems to imply wrongly that he had already done this, suggest ways to avoid that wrong implication. One way may be to say very briefly at the end of verse 21 or at the beginning of verse 22, “The servant went quickly, did that and returned.” A different way might be to say in verse 22, “The servant some time later said, ‘...’”
Questions.Alternative: Do you think that the servant went, did that and returned, or do you think that he had done it already, before the house owner told him to do it?
Do you think that the slave went, did that and returned, or do you think that he had done it already, before the house owner told him to do it?

Questions.Q: What did that servant/slave report to his lord/master?
Questions.A: He reported that what the master had commanded/ordered [him to do] had been done,
and still there was room/space [for more people]. (22)
Questions.Alternative: What did that servant report to his lord?
What did that servant report to his master?
What did that slave report to his lord?
What did that slave report to his master?

Questions.Q: What did the lord/master of the house then tell his servant/slave to do?
Questions.A: The servant/slave was to go to the roads and paths [outside the city] and strongly urge those people to come in [to the house and the feast which was ready there]. (23)
Questions.Alternative: What did the lord of the house then tell his servant to do?
What did the lord of the house then tell his slave to do?
What did the master of the house then tell his servant to do?
What did the master of the house then tell his slave to do?

Questions.Q: How many more people was the servant/slave to bring?
Questions.A: He should bring enough people to fill the master's house. (23)
Questions.Alternative: How many more people was the servant to bring?
How many more people was the slave to bring?

Section.heading: Luke 14:25-35 A person who wants to be Jesus's disciple must be ready to let go of everything else he has and expect to be treated the same as Jesus was.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say would prevent a person from becoming his disciple?
Questions.A: If that person did not hate his family members and even his own life, he could not be Jesus's disciple. (A disciple must be ready to let go of anything else that might prevent him from following Jesus completely.) (26)

Questions.Q: What do you think is the way that a person getting ready to build something is like someone getting ready to be Jesus's disciple?
Questions.A: When a person wants to build something, he must first evaluate the cost.
If he tries to be a disciple, but does not first evaluate everything, he may fail and other people may make fun of him. (28-30)

Questions.Q: How is the way that a king prepares to fight a battle like someone getting ready to be Jesus's disciple?
Questions.A: When a king prepares to fight in a battle, he first evaluates whether or not he has a large enough army to defeat the enemy (31). If he does not, he [submits to the other leader and] seeks to settle the conflict peacefully.

If a person tries to be a disciple by his own resources, and does not first realize that he never will be able to do so on his own, he is sure to fail. He must first be willing to give up his claim on all the things he has/owns [and submit to God]. (33)

Questions.Q: What do you think is the way that salt which loses its flavor could be like a disciple of Jesus?
Questions.A: If a person tries to be a disciple, it is a very good thing, but if he does not first evaluate everything that might be required of him (26, 27, 28, 33), his life will be as useless/worthless as salt which has lost its flavor (34-35).

Questions.Q: When a person is serious about following Jesus, how must he regard/think about his family?
Questions.A: Jesus said that he must hate his family, (that is, he must love Jesus more than he loves his family). (26)
Questions.Alternative: When a person is serious about following Jesus, how must he regard his family?
When a person is serious about following Jesus, how must he think about his family?

Questions.Q: God tells us in other verses in the Bible to love and obey our parents and to love our wives and children. What do you think that Jesus meant here when he said that a disciple must hate the people in his family?
Questions.A: Jesus did not mean that we should literally hate our family. He was comparing a person's love for his family with a true disciple's love for him/God. Compared to how great a disciple is to love Jesus, his love for his family is like hate.
Questions.Note: Jesus again was speaking extremely strong words/speaking in exaggerations to shock the people into paying close attention to what he meant. This was a way of teaching which Jewish teachers used then, and it was not meant for people to obey literally.

Questions.Q: How must that person regard/think about his own life and the things he hopes will happen to him?
Questions.A: He must hate that, too, [compared to how much he is to love Jesus]. (26)
Questions.Note: See Luke 9:23
Questions.Alternative: How must that person regard his own life and the things he hopes will happen to him?
How must that person think about his own life and the things he hopes will happen to him?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to hate oneself?
Questions.A: It means that a person does not think only about staying alive at all costs. He also does not think only about gathering more of the things which make him happy. (Jesus wanted people to think about God and be totally committed to him first.)

Questions.Q: What do you think it meant at the time Jesus lived when a person carried his cross?
Questions.A: It meant that person was on his way to die (by being nailed on crossed timbers until he could not breath anymore).
Questions.Note: Key Term Check: See "cross, crucify" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for people today to carry/bear one's cross and follow Jesus?
Questions.A: It means that a person must be willing to suffer whatever happens to him because he is one who follows Jesus. He must be willing to die, even die on a cross, as criminals used to die, in order to remain faithful to God. That person's focus must be on Jesus, not himself.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think it means for people today to carry one's cross and follow Jesus?
What do you think it means for people today to bear one's cross and follow Jesus?

Questions.Q: What does a person do before he starts to build any building?
Questions.A: He decides whether he can gather enough resources (such as himself or the help of friends or money) to complete the building once he starts. (28)

Questions.Q: What is one result that the builder does not want to happen?
Questions.A: If he makes the foundation/base and then does not have enough resources to finish the building, the people who see that will mock/make fun of him (29) because he was not able to finish what he started (30).

Questions.Q: What will a king do before he goes out to fight an enemy and defeat him?
Questions.A: He decides whether he has enough men/soldiers to fight and win over the enemy. (31)

Questions.Q: What will that king do if he decides his group of men is not large enough or strong enough to win such a fight?
Questions.A: He will send a group quickly to represent him to the other king and ask what they must do to have peace. (32)

Questions.Q: After salt loses its salty flavor, for what can it be used?
Questions.A: Nothing. It is not even useful [to mix in] with dirt or manure/dung [for later use as fertilizer]. (35)

Questions.Q: What happens to that kind of salt?
Questions.A: It is thrown out [on the ground as being useless]. (35)

Questions.Q: When Jesus finished telling these three comparisons about a person being his disciple, he said that the people with ears should listen. Every person has ears. What do you think he meant?
Questions.A: He meant that everyone should pay attention [and think carefully about the hidden meaning behind each illustration].

Section.heading: Luke 15:1-7 Jesus told a parable about a man who looked for a lost sheep until he found it.

Questions.Q: How did Jesus relate the lost sheep to those people whom the Pharisees referred to as "sinners"?
Questions.A: He said that there is more rejoicing in heaven [by God] over one sinner who repents than over the 99 [people] who are/who think they are righteous [already] and do not need to repent. (7)

Questions.Q: The last group of people to whom Jesus spoke had been a large crowd (14:25). Who made up the people listening to Jesus now?
Questions.A: Men who collected taxes and other people whom the religious leaders regarded as sinners. Those were people who did not follow all the ways Pharisees said that were necessary to fully please God. (1)
There also were Pharisees and teachers of the Law there. (2)

Questions.Q: What was the Pharisees' concern?
Questions.A: They did not like it that Jesus welcomed the "sinners" and ate with them. (2)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say a person does when he loses one sheep out of his flock of 100?
Questions.A: He leaves the 99 [sheep] out in the open countryside and goes after the lost [sheep] until he finds it. (4)

Questions.Q: What does that person do when he finds that sheep?
Questions.A: He joyfully puts it on his shoulders (5), and goes home (6).
Going into the house, he calls together [his] friends and neighbors to rejoice with him. (6)

Section.heading: Luke 15:8-10 Jesus told a parable about a woman who looked for her lost coin until she found it.

Questions.Q: How did Jesus relate the lost coin to those people whom the Pharisees referred to as "sinners"?
Questions.A: He said that there is rejoicing in the presence of God's angels over one sinner who repents. (10)
Questions.Note: This probably means that God rejoices and his "friends and neighbors", the angels, rejoice with him. God's joy over a sinner who repents and turns back to him is the theme of all of this chapter.

Questions.Q: How many coins did the woman first have and how many did she lose?
Questions.A: She first had 10 (silver) coins, but lost one. (8)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say that woman did about the lost coin?
Questions.A: She lighted a lamp and swept the house and searched carefully until she found it. (8)

Questions.Q: What did that woman do when she found that coin?
Questions.A: She called together [her] friends and neighbors to rejoice with her. (9)

Section.heading: Luke 15:11-32 Jesus told a parable about a son who came back to his father.

Questions.Q: What people are in this parable which Jesus told?
Questions.A: There is a father and his two sons (11),
the citizen/national of a far away country (15),
and the father's servants/slaves (22, 26).

Questions.Q: How is the parable about the father and his two sons similar to the stories of the lost sheep (see 15:6-7) and the lost coin (see 15:9-10)?
Questions.A: The father said that his younger son had been lost and now was found. (24b, 32c)
He also told others to celebrate with him about this. (23b, 24c, 32a)
He was rejoicing more over one sinning son who repented than over the faithful son who had stayed with him and thought that he always acted rightly (29) and did not need to repent. (7)

Questions.Q: How is the father in the story a picture of God?
Questions.A: God is ready to forgive any sinner who truly repents and comes back to him. (17-24)
God and those who belong to him are happy when each sinner does repent and return to God. (23b, 24c, 32)

God wants all those people who feel they are better children of God's than some other people who come back to God later on (29) to recognize the true reason for rejoicing (32). The faithfulness of that long-term, continuous service to God will be adequately rewarded later (31), but that should not stop them from rejoicing every time a lost "brother" or "sister" returns to the family of God.

Questions.Q: A variety of people were listening to Jesus tell these stories, the Pharisees, the teachers of the Law, the tax collectors and the "sinners" (15:1-2). In what ways, do you think, was Jesus talking about them in this parable?
Questions.A: The older son thought of his younger brother in the same way that the Pharisees and teachers of the Law thought of those people whom they referred to as "sinners". (29-30)

The younger son had done things which did not please his father, but he had finally repented and come back to ask his father to forgive him. He wanted to please his father now, just as the tax collectors and "sinners" were doing.

Questions.Q: What did the younger son want from his father?
Questions.A: He wanted his share of the father's possessions, that part which would be his when the father died. (12)

Questions.Q: What did the father decide to do about that?
Questions.A: He did divide his property/possessions between the [two sons]. (12)

Questions.Q: In what way, do you think, was it divided between the two sons?
Questions.A: (The translation should not say or imply that it was divided equally. The Law of Moses [Deut. 21:17] had said that the oldest son would get an extra portion, or double what any other individual son might receive.)

Questions.Q: What did the younger son do with his part?
Questions.A: He took it and went to a distant country/region and there he wasted his money in wild/extravagant/careless ways. (13)

Questions.Q: What happened after his money was all spent/finished?
Questions.A: A severe/serious/great famine occurred all across that country/region
and he began to not have any [food]. (14)
Questions.Alternative: What happened after his money was all spent?
What happened after his money was all finished?

Questions.Q: How did he find enough things to eat?
Questions.A: He got himself attached to/joined up with a citizen/national of that country/region who sent him into his fields to feed pigs. (15)
Questions.Note: The Greek word does not indicate whether this son now received any pay, but only that he was closely associated with a landowner there. If he was paid, it was a minimal amount, and not enough to buy an adequate amount of food.

Questions.Q: Do you think that this was good work or bad work for this boy/son?
Questions.A: It was bad work for a Jew to work for or live with a non-Jew. It was even worse to work with pigs, which were regarded as ritually unclean and unfit to be eaten. (See Lev. 11:7-8 and 24-26.)
Questions.Alternative: Do you think that this was good work or bad work for this boy?
Do you think that this was good work or bad work for this son?

Questions.Q: How bad was his hunger?
Questions.A: Very bad. He was even willing to eat the pigs' food, but no one even gave him [that much to eat]. (16)

Questions.Q: What finally happened to this son when he was starving and the pigs may have been eating more than he was?
Questions.A: He came to his senses./His thinking became clear again. (17)

Questions.Q: What did he realize when he began to think clearly about his situation?
Questions.A: His father's hired workers had more than enough food to eat, but he was starving to death. (17)

Questions.Q: Did he think that, if he stayed where he was, he really would die?
Questions.A: Yes, he did.
Questions.Note: Luke's use of the Key Term "destroy, perish" shows us how serious the famine was. The word used here is the same one Luke used in 8:24.

Questions.Q: What did he decide to do?
Questions.A: He decided to start out for home, (18)
admit to his father that he had sinned against [God in] heaven and against [his father] (18),
and ask his father to make him one of his hired workers, and not think of/call him his son (19).

Questions.Q: What did his father do when he saw his younger son coming?
Questions.A: His father saw him while he was still a long distance away, (20b)
[his heart] was moved with pity/felt compassion [for him], (20b)
and running [to his son], he hugged him around the neck and kissed him. (20b)
Questions.Note: The words used for the action of kissing as part of the Jewish cultural way for the father to greet his son here should be the same as was used at 7:45. Here, however, much more emotion can be included, as appropriate.

Questions.Q: What did the son say to his father?
Questions.A: He said, "Father, I have sinned against [God in] heaven and against you. I am no longer worthy to be called your son." (21)
Questions.Note: These words are exactly the same words and word order as in verse 18-19a. The translation should also have exactly the same wording in both places for these sentences. What the son said in verse 19b does not seem to have been said again to the father before he interrupted his son. Although the words of 19b are repeated in some Greek manuscripts, the most reliable ones do not have that sentence included here. If the translator wishes to have it in a footnote, then the wording should be exactly the same as in 19b.

Questions.Q: How do you know that the father did not do like his younger son had said?
Questions.A: The father wanted to dress his son in special clothes and jewelry (22)
and celebrate his return with special food for a feast (23).
He called the young man his son when he talked to his servants/slaves. (22-24)

Questions.Q: What special clothes did the father tell the servants/slaves to dress his son in?
Questions.A: The best robe, a ring on his finger and sandals on his feet. (22)
Questions.Note: See TN for a description of what was culturally implied in the father's actions (20b) and words (22-23).
Questions.Alternative: What special clothes did the father tell the servants to dress his son in?
What special clothes did the father tell the slaves to dress his son in?

Questions.Q: What special food did the father tell the servants/slaves to get ready to eat?
Questions.A: The calf they had fattened. (23)
Questions.Alternative: What special food did the father tell the servants to get ready to eat?
What special food did the father tell the slaves to get ready to eat?

Questions.Q: What did the father say was the reason that he wanted to feast and celebrate?
Questions.A: He said that this son of his had been [the same as] dead and [now] was alive again. (24)
The son had been [the same as] lost and [now] was found. (24)

Questions.Q: Why did the older son ask a servant about what was going on in the house?
Questions.A: He had been in the field. (25)
When he came near the house he heard music and dancing. (25)

Questions.Q: What did that servant tell him?
Questions.A: He told him that his [younger] brother had come [back] (27)
and his father had [ordered servants to] kill the fattened calf [and roast/cook it]. (27)

Questions.Q: How did the older brother feel about that?
Questions.A: He became angry and did not want/he refused to enter [the house]. (28a)

Questions.Q: What did the father do about his older son?
Questions.A: He came out[side] and kept on urging/earnestly asked for/strongly requested him [to go into the house and join in the celebrating]. (28b)

Questions.Q: What did the older brother tell his father were the reasons that he was angry?
Questions.A: He had worked like a slave for his father for so many years and had never disobeyed his orders, but the father had never given him [even] a young goat in order that he might have a party with his friends. (29)
But for his brother who had used up [the money from] their father's property with prostitutes, and [just now] come home, the father had [servants] kill the fattened calf! (30)
Questions.Note: The older son's choice of words shows that he felt as if his father had slighted him, that the father was rewarding the younger son's foolishness and disobedience and not rewarding the older son's hard work and obedience. If the translation can convey that feeling of anger and disappointment, it would reflect Luke's text well.

Questions.Q: What did the father say to show that he was not treating his older son badly?
Questions.A: He said that the older son had always been with him and everything the father owned now belonged to the older son. (They had been together enjoying life and those possessions all along and still had them!) (31)

Questions.Q: What did the father say to show that he was not celebrating the younger son's past foolish actions?
Questions.A: He said that he had to celebrate because the younger brother had returned from [foolish actions which were like] being dead or lost. Now he was alive again and found. (32)

Section.heading: Luke 16:1-13 Jesus told a parable about a shrewd/clever servant manager.

Questions.Q: On what point did Jesus want his disciples to focus their attention from this parable? (See 16:8.)
Questions.A: The servant manager had thought shrewdly about his situation and had prepared for his future life. This was typical of people who deal with each other in worldly things. They do that better than the people who focus on spiritual things do. (8)

Questions.Q: If a person cannot be trusted with the things God has given him on this earth, how will that affect spiritual things which God would like to give him?
Questions.A: God will not reward that person with things of great spiritual/eternal value. [They belong only to those who are faithful.] (11-12)

Questions.Q: To whom was Jesus telling this new parable?
Questions.A: He told his disciples. (1)

Questions.Q: What problem did the rich man have with the servant manager of his belongings/property?
Questions.A: The servant manager had been accused [by someone] of wasting the rich man's belongings. (1)
Questions.Alternative: What problem did the rich man have with the servant manager of his belongings?
What problem did the rich man have with the servant manager of his property?

Questions.Q: What did the rich man say about this to the servant manager?
Questions.A: He told him to prepare a report of his [past] work with the owner's belongings (2)
because he could no longer be the servant manager. (2)

Questions.Q: What was the servant manager worried about when he heard the rich man's instructions?
Questions.A: He was worried that he now had no work [to earn his living]. (3)

Questions.Q: Why did he not want to get work digging gardens or begging for money from other people?
Questions.A: He said that he was not strong enough to dig and too ashamed to beg. (3)

Questions.Q: What did he do to make sure he would have friends who would help him after the rich man put him out of the servant manager work?
Questions.A: He allowed each one of the people who owed debts to the rich man to make their debt much smaller than the servant manager had said it was earlier. (5-7)

Questions.Q: What kind of things did some people owe the rich man?
Questions.A: [Olive] oil (6)
Wheat (7)

Questions.Q: How many people did the servant manager help?
Questions.A: Each [and every] one. (5)
Questions.Note: The translation should be clear that he spoke to, and helped, each person with a debt, not just the two people mentioned specifically.

Questions.Q: What did the rich man think about the servant manager doing like that?
Questions.A: He commended/spoke well of the (dishonest) servant manager because he had been so shrewd/clever [to take care of himself in his business dealings]. (8)

Questions.Q: Which people did Jesus say are the more shrewd/clever when dealing with others who are like them?
Questions.A: He said that they were the people of this world. (8)
Questions.Alternative: Which people did Jesus say are the more shrewd when dealing with others who are like them?
Which people did Jesus say are the more clever when dealing with others who are like them?

Questions.Q: To which people, do you think, did Jesus refer [in verse 8] as being "the sons/children/people of this age/world" and "the sons/children/people of the light"?
Questions.A: The people of this age/world do not think about God or believe that he sent Jesus to save them.
The people of the light do think about God and do believe that he sent Jesus to save them.
Questions.Alternative: To which people, do you think, did Jesus refer in verse 8 as being "the sons of this age and "the sons of the light"?
To which people, do you think, did Jesus refer in verse 8 as being "the sons of this age and "the children of the light"?
To which people, do you think, did Jesus refer in verse 8 as being "the sons of this age and "the people of the light"?
To which people, do you think, did Jesus refer in verse 8 as being "the sons of this world" and "the sons of the light"?
To which people, do you think, did Jesus refer in verse 8 as being "the sons of this world" and "the children of the light"?
To which people, do you think, did Jesus refer in verse 8 as being "the sons of this world" and "the people of the light"?
To which people, do you think, did Jesus refer in verse 8 as being "the children of this age and "the sons of the light"?
To which people, do you think, did Jesus refer in verse 8 as being "the children of this age and "the children of the light"?
To which people, do you think, did Jesus refer in verse 8 as being "the children of this age and "the people of the light"?
To which people, do you think, did Jesus refer in verse 8 as being "the children of this world" and "the sons of the light"?
To which people, do you think, did Jesus refer in verse 8 as being "the children of this world" and "the children of the light"?
To which people, do you think, did Jesus refer in verse 8 as being "the children of this world" and "the people of the light"?
To which people, do you think, did Jesus refer in verse 8 as being "the people of this age and "the sons of the light"?
To which people, do you think, did Jesus refer in verse 8 as being "the people of this age and "the children of the light"?
To which people, do you think, did Jesus refer in verse 8 as being "the people of this age and "the people of the light"?
To which people, do you think, did Jesus refer in verse 8 as being "the people of this world" and "the sons of the light"?
To which people, do you think, did Jesus refer in verse 8 as being "the people of this world" and "the children of the light"?
To which people, do you think, did Jesus refer in verse 8 as being "the people of this world" and "the people of the light"?
To which people, do you think, did Jesus refer as being "the sons of this age and "the sons of the light"?
To which people, do you think, did Jesus refer as being "the sons of this age and "the children of the light"?

To which people, do you think, did Jesus refer as being "the sons of this world" and "the children of the light"?

To which people, do you think, did Jesus refer as being "the people of this world" and "the people of the light"?

Questions.Q: How should the children of the light be like the people who are focused on the things of this world?
Questions.A: They should use wealth to make friends for themselves, so that when the wealth fails [to be able to take care of them, the new friends, or, the friends already in heaven, namely God and the angels] will welcome them into eternal homes. (9)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about a person who can be trusted with very small amounts of money or goods?
Questions.A: People can trust him with large amounts of money or goods. (10)

Questions.Q: What did he say about a person who cannot be trusted with very small amounts of money or goods?
Questions.A: People cannot trust him with large amounts either. (10)

Questions.Q: How did Jesus apply those thoughts to something which has small value and something else having true value?
Questions.A: He spoke about worldly wealth as something which has very little value (11),
and implied that true wealth and riches was made up of spiritual things.
Questions.Note: Jesus spoke about this already in 12:32-34.

Questions.Q: Who do you think it is that wants to trust us with true riches?
Questions.A: God
Questions.Alternative: Who do you think wants to trust us with true riches?

Questions.Q: What kind of person will be entrusted by God with true riches and possessions of his own?
Questions.A: The one who has been trustworthy with someone else's wealth. (11-12)

Questions.Q: Who do you think has already given us things in this world to look after for him?
Questions.A: God. (He gives us food, strength to work, family, possessions, etc.)
Questions.Alternative: Who do you think has made us his caretakers over things in this life?

Questions.Q: How many masters can a person truly serve/obey all the time?
Questions.A: Only one.
Questions.Alternative: How many masters can a person truly serve all the time?
How many masters can a person truly obey all the time?

Questions.Q: If a person's desire for money controls all his thinking and actions, then money is his master and he is a slave to it. What will that person's thoughts/attitudes be toward God?
Questions.A: That person will hate him or despise him/think of him with contempt.
Questions.Note: The opposite will also be true, if God is a person's master.
Questions.Alternative: If a person's desire for money controls all his thinking and actions, then money is his master and he is a slave to it. What will that person's thoughts be toward God?
If a person's desire for money controls all his thinking and actions, then money is his master and he is a slave to it. What will that person's attitudes be toward God?

Section.heading: Luke 16:14-18 God knows when a person pretends to obey him, but is really just pleasing himself.

Questions.Q: What was the sin of the Pharisees which Jesus described in verses 14 and 15?
Questions.A: They wanted people to think of them as doing the right thing/having a right relationship with God, but God knew their hearts [were not focused on him, but on money or themselves]. (14-15)

Questions.Q: What two topics did Jesus talk about in which the Pharisees did not obey God in a way that pleased him?
Questions.A: He talked about [their] love of money (14-15),
and about divorce and adultery (18).
Questions.Note: The Pharisees said that they obeyed all the Law as God had commanded them to do, but Jesus was telling them that in the way they regarded money and divorce they were not obeying God's laws, but only pleasing themselves.

Questions.Q: How did the Pharisees who were also listening to Jesus react to what he had been saying?
Questions.A: They were sneering/scoffing/laughing at Jesus and at what he was saying. (14)

Questions.Q: Why did they not like what Jesus had said?
Questions.A: They loved money. (14)

Questions.Q: To what, do you think, was Jesus referring when he talked about something which has a high value in the thinking of people, but which is disgusting/revolting/nauseating to God? (15b)
Questions.A: Money, or the love for money.
Questions.Alternative: To what, do you think, was Jesus referring when he talked about something which has a high value in the thinking of people, but which is disgusting to God? (15b)
To what, do you think, was Jesus referring when he talked about something which has a high value in the thinking of people, but which is revolting to God? (15b)
To what, do you think, was Jesus referring when he talked about something which has a high value in the thinking of people, but which is nauseating to God? (15b)

Questions.Q: Before John the Baptizer had come, how did the people know about the way that God wanted them to live?
Questions.A: The Law [of Moses] and [the writings of] the Prophets [had been read and taught to them as their guide for living]. (16)

Questions.Q: What changed after John began to preach?
Questions.A: Since then the Good News about the kingdom of God was being proclaimed/preached [first by John, then by Jesus and his disciples]. (16)

Questions.Q: What was that Good News?
Questions.A: It was that God wanted to rule over every person and reign in each one's heart and life like a king rules over the people who live in his country. That time had arrived when John and Jesus began to tell about the need for people to repent and believe that Jesus had been sent by God to save them from their sins.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say had been the result of that preaching?
Questions.A: He said that everyone was forcing/pressing/charging/trying hard to make his way into it. (16)
Questions.Note: If the translation must make a specific interpretation of this sentence and not remain general, then any one of the following three choices is possible, but the first choice has the most support by Bible scholars:
1) This refers to those who believed the Good News and wanted very much to be in God's kingdom (see NLT).
2) This refers to those who did not believe the Good News, but were trying to be included some other way.
3) This refers to the those who did not believe the Good News, but were working hard to keep others out of the kingdom, such as the Pharisees or the devil were trying to do.

Questions.Q: Did what Jesus said here mean that the Law of Moses [and the writings of the Prophets] was no longer important or had no authority after he and John began to preach that the kingdom of God had arrived?
Questions.A: No. He said that it would be easier for the sky and earth to end/disappear than for one of the smallest parts of God's law to be gotten rid of. (17)
Questions.Alternative: Did what Jesus said here mean that the Law of Moses and the writings of the Prophets was no longer important or had no authority after he and John began to preach that the kingdom of God had arrived?
Did what Jesus said here mean that the Law of Moses was no longer important or had no authority after he and John began to preach that the kingdom of God had arrived?

Questions.Q: What example did Jesus talk about in order to show that he had not gotten rid of the Law?
Questions.A: He talked about divorce and adultery. (18)

Questions.Q: What does a person do when he or she commits adultery?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A married person has sexual intercourse with someone who is not that married person's spouse.

Questions.Q: According to Jesus's explanation of the Law, who will also be guilty of committing adultery?
Questions.A: It is the one who divorces his wife and marries another,
and it is the one who marries a woman whose husband has divorced her. (18)
Questions.Note: God's view of marriage, divorce, and adultery can be found in Gen. 2:24, Exod. 20:14, and Mal. 2:14-16. Jesus's explained what that meant in the kingdom of God in Matt. 19:3-9, and Mark 10:9, as well as here.

Section.heading: Luke 16:19-31 Jesus told a parable about a rich man and a beggar.

Questions.Q: This complete chapter has focused on wealth and one's relationship to God. How do you see this parable doing that?
Questions.A: This parable emphasizes obeying God's word as they know it and the importance of having the right attitude toward money and possessions.
