If people refuse to listen to and obey God's message which was in the Old Testament, then they will refuse the message about the kingdom of God which Jesus brought, even after seeing the miracles he did or seeing him after he rose from the dead.

Questions.Q: How did Jesus describe the rich man's way of life?
Questions.A: He wore [expensive clothes like] purple robes and fine linen (19)
and lived in luxury/wonderfully every day. (19)

Questions.Q: How did Jesus describe Lazarus's way of life?
Questions.A: He was a beggar [whose body] was covered with sores. (20)
He wanted very much to be able to eat what fell off/was thrown away from the rich man's table. (21)
[He was so sick and weak that] even the dogs came and licked his sores. (21)

Questions.Q: How did Lazarus get to the rich man's house?
Questions.A: [Someone, probably friends,] laid him at the gate[way]. (20)

Questions.Q: What happened to the rich man and Lazarus when they died?
Questions.A: Lazarus was carried to Abraham's side [in heaven] by angels. (22)
The rich man was buried. (22)

Questions.Q: Where was the spirit of the rich man after he had died?
Questions.A: It was in the place of the dead. (23)
Key Term Check: The description or name of the place used here should be the same as the one used at 10:15. See "Hades" in the "hell, Hades, abyss" entry in KBT.

Questions.Q: What was the rich man's way of life there in Hades?
Questions.A: He was in great pain/torture/agony. (23, 24)
He was very hot and thirsty in the middle of flames. (24)
[He implied that there was no way to relieve his suffering without outside help.]

Questions.Q: The rich man called Abraham his father in verse 24. Then Abraham called the rich man his son. What was the real relationship between the two?
Questions.A: Abraham was the ancestor of all the Jews, so the rich man was being respectful of the man who started his entire group of people. Abraham replied with the appropriate response [in the Jewish culture].
Questions.Note: The translation may use whatever terms from the culture would show respect for such a forefather and from that forefather back to his descendant.

Questions.Q: How did he want Abraham to relieve some of his pain?
Questions.A: He asked Abraham to have mercy/pity on him and send Lazarus to dip a finger in water and place it on the rich man's tongue in order to cool him off [a little bit]. (24)

Questions.Q: What two reasons did Abraham give for not doing as the rich man had asked?
Questions.A: 1) He said that the rich man should remember that when he was alive, he had received his good things, but Lazarus had received bad [things]. Now in this place Lazarus was comforted/comfortable, and the rich man was in great pain/torture/agony. (25)
2) He said that there was a great chasm/deep space/ravine which [God] had placed there so that persons on either side could not go over to the other side. (26)

Questions.Q: Why did the rich man want Abraham to send Lazarus to his father's house/descendants?
Questions.A: He had five brothers whom Lazarus should warn [about changing/repenting] in order that they not also come to that place of great pain/torture/agony. (28)
Questions.Alternative: Why did the rich man want Abraham to send Lazarus to his father's house?
Why did the rich man want Abraham to send Lazarus to his father's descendants?

Questions.Q: What did Abraham say was God's way of warning them already?
Questions.A: They had [the writings of] Moses and the Prophets. They should listen to them [tell why they should repent]. (29)

Questions.Q: Why did the rich man think that Lazarus would be able to convince them better than the Scriptures?
Questions.A: If someone [rose] from the dead, he thought that they would [definitely] listen. (30)

Questions.Q: What did Abraham say about that?
Questions.A: He said that if [those brothers] would not listen to [the writings of] Moses and the Prophets, neither would they be convinced by someone who rose from the dead. (31)

Section.heading: Luke 17:1-4 Expect God to punish you horribly if you cause another person to sin, but forgive others when they sin against you.

Questions.Q: To drown is a terrible way to die. What do you think that means about how God looks at one person tempting another to sin?
Questions.A: He must hate it because Jesus said that God would punish that person even worse than if he had drowned.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think that means about how God looks at one person tempting another to sin?
How does God view one person tempting another to sin?
How does God consider one person tempting another to sin?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say his disciples should do about these things?
Questions.A: He said that they should watch out for/beware of [this problem] among themselves. (3a)

Questions.Q: What kinds of things did Jesus say are sure to happen?
Questions.A: Things that will cause people to sin. (1)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about God punishing a person who tempts/causes another person to sin?
Questions.A: It would be better for that person to drown in the sea than to suffer the horrible things which God will do to punish him. (2)
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus say about God punishing a person who tempts another person to sin?
What did Jesus say about God punishing a person who causes another person to sin?

Questions.Q: To whom, do you think, was Jesus referring when he spoke of "these little ones"?
Questions.A: He was referring to children.
-OR-
… to those people who are new/young believers in Jesus.
-OR-
… to any believers who need God's help and protection.
-OR-
… to persons having low status, such as the poor people in the culture.

Questions.Q: To whom, do you think, was Jesus referring when he spoke about "your brother"?
Questions.A: He was referring to any close companion or fellow believer, and not directly to one's sibling. For the disciples, it would have especially meant any of the other disciples. (3b)

Questions.Q: What are we to do if our companion sins?
Questions.A: We are to strongly warn/rebuke him. (3b)

Questions.Q: What are we to do if that rebuke causes him to realize his sin and he repents?
Questions.A: If he repents, we are to forgive him. (3b)

Questions.Q: What if he sins many times against us in one day, then repents each time?
Questions.A: If he repents, we are to forgive him every time. (4)

Questions.Q: How many times did Jesus want the disciples to forgive others?
Questions.A: He said that the number "seven" in his example as representing as many times as that person repents.
Questions.Note: The number "seven" in the language of the Jews, Hebrew, sounded like the word "vow, oath". This made the number have a strong sense of being fulfilled, of being complete. Thus, "seven" here stands for all the times that this situation might happen. In English, that sense is present when a person says something happened "a dozen times" or "a hundred times". The number's absolute value as "12" or "100" is not in focus so much as that a set of a large number of occurrences of that action has taken place.

Section.heading: Luke 17:5-6 The apostles asked Jesus to increase their faith.

Questions.Q: How much faith, or what kind of faith, did Jesus say the apostles needed to do great things for God?
Questions.A: They only needed to have a tiny amount of faith, like a mustard seed is tiny, for God to work through them.
-OR-

Their faith only needed to be active, to grow and develop, like the tiny mustard seed does, into something firm and able to believe that God could do anything through them [to advance his rule and reign in people's lives]. (6) (See 13:18-19 or Matt. 13:31-32.)

Questions.Q: What did the apostles ask Jesus to do for them?
Questions.A: They asked him to add to/increase their faith [in him]. (5) (See "faith" in KBT in the "believe" entry.)

Questions.Q: What example did Jesus use to show what a small amount of faith could eventually do?
Questions.A: It could cause a (mulberry) tree to come out [of the ground] by its roots and be [re-]planted in the sea. (6)

Section.heading: Luke 17:7-10 Servants are to humbly do their duties.

Questions.Q: Who do you think was the apostles' master whom they were to serve?
Questions.A: Jesus/God.

Questions.Q: Who do you think is the master whom Christian people today are to serve?
Questions.A: God

Questions.Q: Should a person who serves God expect great honor, thanks, or rewards for obeying him? Why?
Questions.A: No. He is only doing his duty/what he should do. He should be humble about it. (10)

Questions.Q: When a servant/slave comes back from working in a field all day, what does he not expect his master to say to him?
Questions.A: "Come sit down/relax [and eat]." (7)
Questions.Alternative: When a servant comes back from working in a field all day, what does he not expect his master to say to him?
When a slave comes back from working in a field all day, what does he not expect his master to say to him?

Questions.Q: What does he expect his master to say?
Questions.A: "Prepare something for me to eat, (8)
and [then] having dressed [appropriately], serve me while I eat and drink. (8)
After that, you may eat and drink." (8)

Questions.Q: Should that servant/slave expect the master to thank him because he did what he was commanded to do? Why?
Questions.A: No. He only did what he was told to do. (9)
Questions.Note: Luke wrote Jesus's question as beginning with a negative. That made the question clearly imply that an answer of "No" was expected.
Questions.Alternative: Should that servant expect the master to thank him because he did what he was commanded to do? Why?
Should that slave expect the master to thank him because he did what he was commanded to do? Why?

Section.heading: Luke 17:11-19 Jesus healed ten men who had leprosy, but only one thanked him.

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that the one man returned to Jesus?
Questions.A: He recognized that God['s power] was at work in and through Jesus. (15)

Questions.Q: Based on what happened in this story, what does Jesus seem to expect from any person who asks him to help them?
Questions.A: That person is not merely to ask for help or believe the word of God and enjoy the blessings, but also to be thankful. (17)

Questions.Q: In which part of Israel was Jesus traveling at this time?
Questions.A: He was on his way to Jerusalem, traveling along the border between Samaria [province] and Galilee [province]. (11)

Questions.Q: Who met up with Jesus as he entered a village there?
Questions.A: Ten men who had leprosy/a bad skin disease. (12)
Questions.Note: See comments at 5:12-16.

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason those men asked Jesus to have mercy/pity on them?
Questions.A: They wanted Jesus to heal them. (12-13)
Questions.Alternative: What do you think was the reason those men asked Jesus to have mercy on them?
What do you think was the reason those men asked Jesus to have pity on them?

Questions.Q: Many sick people had come right in front of Jesus in order to be healed by him. What do you think was the reason these men called out to him from a distance?
Questions.A: God had told Moses not to permit people with leprosy/bad skin diseases to come close to others without letting the others know a person with leprosy was there. (See Lev. 13:9-17, 45-46 and Num. 5:1-5.)
Questions.Note: If these Scripture-related cultural items are not known to the respondent (or not likely to be known by the target audience), consider making a footnote or glossary item.

Questions.Q: God had told Moses that a person who had been healed of leprosy/bad skin disease should show his skin to a priest (see Lev. 13:9, 16-17, and 14:1-9). What happened to those ten men when they obeyed Jesus and started to go to a priest while they were still sick?
Questions.A: As they went, they were healed [and] made ritually clean again. (14)
Questions.Note: See the note at 7:22 about the same Greek verb as Luke used here.
Questions.Alternative: God had told Moses that a person who had been healed of leprosy should show his skin to a priest (see Lev. 13:9, 16-17, and 14:1-9). What happened to those ten men when they obeyed Jesus and started to go to a priest while they were still sick?

God had told Moses that a person who had been healed of bad skin disease should show his skin to a priest (see Lev. 13:9, 16-17, and 14:1-9). What happened to those ten men when they obeyed Jesus and started to go to a priest while they were still sick?

Questions.Q: What did the men do when they saw that they were healed?
Questions.A: Only one of them returned, praising God in a loud voice (15).
He quickly lowered his body, putting [his knees and] his face to the ground [in front of] Jesus's feet, and thanked him (16). [The rest went to see a priest, we assume.]
Questions.Note: The Greek text emphasizes that this man was not a Jew, but a Samaritan. If that element of surprise can be included in the translation, it would reflect Luke's writing better.

Questions.Q: How do we know Jesus was surprised and disappointed at all this?
Questions.A: He asked [rhetorical questions] about where the other nine men were who had also been healed/made ritually clean. (17).

Questions.Q: Why did he become so surprised and disappointed?
Questions.A: Because they had not returned to give praise to God, but only the non-Jew [Samaritan] had. (18)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say was the cause of the Samaritan man being healed/being saved?
Questions.A: He had faith/believed that Jesus could heal/save him [by God's power when no other way was possible]. (19)
Questions.Note: The Greek verb used in this sentence means both things in this case. It can also be translated as "rescued". Jesus had healed all ten men. He may have meant here that this one man also had his sins forgiven because he had recognized the power of God at work in Jesus (see Luke 7:50).
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus say was the cause of the Samaritan man being healed?
What did Jesus say was the cause of the Samaritan man being saved?

Questions.Q: Jesus told this man to get up and go. Where was he going when he stopped and came back to Jesus?
Questions.A: He had been on his way, also, to show himself to a priest. (14)

Section.heading: Luke 17:20-37 Jesus spoke about the way in which God would establish his kingdom on earth.

Questions.Q: Jesus talked much about the Son of Man returning/coming again. To whom, do you think, was he referring?
Questions.A: He was referring to himself. (22, 24, 26, 30)
Questions.Note: See comments at 5:24.
Questions.Alternative: Jesus talked much about the Son of Man coming again. To whom, do you think, was he referring?
Jesus talked much about the Son of Man returning. To whom, do you think, was he referring?

Questions.Q: Jesus clearly implied that there would be a difference between the kingdom of God coming and the Son of Man coming again/returning. What was different in the way he talked about those two things?
Questions.A: The kingdom of God would not come visibly (21),
but the return of the Son of Man, Jesus himself, would be very visible (24).
Questions.Alternative: Jesus clearly implied that there would be a difference between the kingdom of God coming and the Son of Man coming again. What was different in the way he talked about those two things?
Jesus clearly implied that there would be a difference between the kingdom of God coming and the Son of Man returning. What was different in the way he talked about those two things?

Questions.Q: What will people be doing when the Son of Man returns?
Questions.A: They will be doing their normal/ordinary activities, such as eating, sleeping, and working. (27, 28, 30, 34, 35)

Questions.Q: After hearing about the flood and the fire from heaven in earlier times, what do you think that Jesus wanted his disciples to understand about what would happen suddenly one ordinary day when most people were not expecting it?
Questions.A: He will return and save some [people, those who believe in him], but leave [all] the others [to be punished].

Questions.Q: What did the Pharisees ask Jesus about?
Questions.A: They wanted to know when the kingdom of God would come. (20)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say was the reason that people would not recognize the kingdom of God when it came?
Questions.A: There would not be visible signs beforehand to signal the kingdom of God was about to come. (20)
-OR-
It would not be visible because it was inside people['s hearts]. (21)
-OR-
It would not be recognized because it was [already] among them [in the person and work of Jesus, but they had not yet realized it]. (21-22)

Questions.Q: How were the disciples going to feel before long?
Questions.A: They would feel they wanted very much to see even one day of the Son of Man [in all his glory, or, ruling and reigning as king]. (22)
Questions.Note: Time may be one of those things in the language of the translation which cannot "come". Ask about it if the translation text literally says the time "comes".

Questions.Q: Would they see that happen soon?
What should the disciples do when someone would tell them where they could go to see the Son of Man?
Questions.A: They should not hurry to follow such people. (23)

Questions.Q: Why should they not believe such reports that the Son of Man was in one place or another?
Questions.A: Because his coming would be [as dramatic and public] as lightning flashing from one part of the sky to another. (24)
-OR-
Because his coming would be [as dramatic and public] as lightning flashes in one part of the sky and lights up [all] the other parts, or lights up [everywhere] on the ground. (24)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say must first happen before the Son of Man would come in his glory?
Questions.A: He must suffer many things/in many ways/much.
The people alive at that time [who had seen his miracles and heard him teach] would reject him/his claim to be the Messiah. (25)

Questions.Q: Jesus compared the way that the world would be like at the time he returns as the Son of Man with another time. To what other time did he compare it?
Questions.A: He compared it to the time [long, long before] when Noah lived. (26) (See Gen. 6 and 7.)

Questions.Q: What were people doing in that time when Noah lived?
Questions.A: People [did their normal activities, such as, they] were eating and drinking, (27a)
and getting married. (27a)
Questions.Note: If the culture of the translation has separate ways to refer to a man or a woman getting married, use both ways here. The Greek text does that, too. Only one term is used in the answer here because English just has one term, "get married", for both men and women.

Questions.Q: How long did people do those ordinary activities?
Questions.A: Right up to the day Noah [and his family] entered the ark/boat [he had built]. (27b)

Questions.Q: What happened suddenly which changed what those people were doing?
Questions.A: [God sent] a flood which destroyed all [those people]. (27c)

Questions.Q: What about Noah and his family?
Questions.A: They had already gone into the ark/boat [and were safe]. (27)

Questions.Q: To what time did Jesus also compare the way that the world would be at the time he returns? -OR- To what time did Jesus also compare the way that the world was at the time of Noah?
Questions.A: He compared it to the time [long, long before] when Lot lived. (28) (See Gen. 18:17-19:29.)
Questions.Alternative: To what time did Jesus also compare the way that the world would be at the time he returns?
To what time did Jesus also compare the way that the world was at the time of Noah?

Questions.Q: What were people doing in that time when Lot lived?
Questions.A: People [did their normal activities, such as, they] were eating and drinking, (28)
buying and selling, (28)
planting [food in gardens] and building [houses/buildings]. (28)

Questions.Q: How long did people do those ordinary activities?
Questions.A: [Right up to] the day Lot [and his family] left [the city of] Sodom. (29)

Questions.Q: What happened suddenly which changed what those people were doing?
Questions.A: That day fire and sulfur/burning hot stones came/[God sent] down from the sky like rain and destroyed all [those people]. (29)

Questions.Q: What about Lot and his family?
Questions.A: They had already left [the city of] Sodom [and were safe]. (29)

Questions.Q: To which "day" was Jesus referring in verse 31?
Questions.A: He was referring to the day when the Son of Man would be revealed/seen by all. (30)

Questions.Q: What will people be doing on that day when he returns?
Questions.A: People [will be doing their normal activities, such as, some] will be [resting] on their [house] roofs, others [will be working] in their fields. (31)
Questions.Note: These activities of people resting and working are also in verses 34 and 35. See 5:19 and 12:3 for how Jewish roofs were described.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about people stopping what they are doing when he arrives and then getting ready for him?
Questions.A: He said that no one was to go where his belongings were [in order to save them from the disaster which was coming]. (31)

Questions.Q: What example did Jesus give to show what would happen if someone did that?
Questions.A: He told them to remember [what happened to] Lot's wife. (32)
Questions.Note: All the Jews who were listening to Jesus knew what had happened to Lot's wife. She had thought more about her possessions which she was leaving behind than about obeying God and him saving her. She died the same as all the other people who had not obeyed God. This may need to be in a footnote or glossary item. See Gen. 19:15, 17, and 26.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say would happen to the person who wanted to save his own life/keep on living the way he was?
Questions.A: He said that person would lose [his life]. (33a)
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus say would happen to the person who wanted to save his own life?
What did Jesus say would happen to the person who wanted to keep on living the way he was?

Questions.Q: That sounds like a contradiction in the way that people understand life and death. What do you think that Jesus meant by that?
Questions.A: The person who does not do as Jesus just said in verse 31 will lose his chance to have the spiritual, eternal life Jesus promised elsewhere in the gospels.
He may also die physically just like Jesus implied in verse 32 that Lot's wife died.
Questions.Note: If the respondent has not been a worshiping Christian for some time, he will find this question is impossible to answer. He has no context to fit it into, and the words are a paradox. Do not be critical of anyone's answer to this question.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say would happen when a person loses his life because of his following Jesus?
Questions.A: He will save it/keep on living [eternally]. (33b)

Questions.Q: This, too, sounds like a contradiction in terms. What do you think that Jesus meant by that?
Questions.A: He cannot be talking about a person's physical life, so he must be referring again to spiritual life. The person who does as Jesus just said in verse 31 will receive the spiritual, eternal life which he promised to give him.

Questions.Q: Will it be night or day when the Son of Man returns?
Questions.A: Both. Some people will be sleeping at night [on one side of the world], others will be working in the daylight [on the other side of the earth]. [Which one it will be at any one place we do not know.] (34-35)

Questions.Q: What will happen to people at that time?
Questions.A: Some will be taken along, some left behind, [even within families or among friends]. (34, 35)
Questions.Note: Jesus had not said where he would be taking those people, but it would be somewhere safe. From what he said in 16:19-23, he implied they would be taken to heaven like the man Lazarus had been.

Questions.Q: What did the disciples want to know about this return of the Son of Man?
Questions.A: They asked Jesus where [his return would take place]. (30)
-OR-
They asked Jesus where [the things he just talked about in verses 30-35 would take place]. (37)

Questions.Q: In what way, do you think, did Jesus's words about vultures and dead bodies answer their question?
Questions.A: Just like [it is obvious to people even far away when] vultures gather and circle over a dead body, Jesus's return will be obvious [as he already said in 17:24].
-OR-
When the Jews/mankind was totally dead spiritually, he would return to punish those people. (37)

Section.heading: Luke 18:1-8 God will listen to the prayers of those who continue to ask him to help them and do not give up.

Questions.Q: Tell me the parable about the widow and the judge.
Questions.A: (The answer should cover the basic outline of the story, including the judge's attitudes toward people, the widow being persistent, and the judge's reasons to finally answer her repeated requests.)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus want his disciples to learn from this parable?
Questions.A: They should always pray [to God] and not get tired of it/give up/be discouraged doing it. (1)

Questions.Q: How can we compare the judge and God?
Questions.A: The judge did not care about God or people (4), but God cares about the ones he has chosen (7).
The judge kept putting off helping the widow, even though she was persistent (3, 4), but God will not do like that; he will help quickly [when he decides to act] (8).

Questions.Q: In what way did Jesus describe the judge?
Questions.A: The judge did not respect/revere God [and God's standard of right and wrong]
and he was not concerned about what people might think about the way that he decided court cases.
-OR-
The judge did not respect/revere God [and God's standard of right and wrong]
and he did not care about the people involved in the cases he decided. (2, 4)
Questions.Note: The same Greek word was used to describe a judge in 11:19 and 12:58. The translation here should describe the judge and his role in as much the same way as it was in those verses.

Questions.Q: What do you think that Jesus meant when he said that the disciples should always pray to God?
Questions.A: He meant that they should pray very often and regularly to God and depend on him for all their needs. He did not mean they must only pray and do nothing else.

Questions.Q: In what way did Jesus describe the widow?
Questions.A: She was persistent/kept on coming to the judge to do what was right. (3)

Questions.Q: What did the widow want from that judge?
Questions.A: She wanted him to listen to her problem (3),
decide that another person was taking advantage of her (3),
and correct it [in her favor] (3).

Questions.Q: Why did the widow keep on coming to that judge?
Questions.A: Because he would not take the time to listen to, and settle, the woman's complaint. (4)

Questions.Q: Why did he finally do what the woman had wanted for a long time?
Questions.A: Because she was bothering him/wearing him out with her repeated requests. (5)

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that Jesus said that his disciples were to pay attention to what the corrupt judge had said/thought?
Questions.A: The judge said that he would help the woman because of her being persistent (5). Jesus then made a comparison to God answering our prayers to him (7-8).
Questions.Alternative: What do you think was the reason that Jesus said that his disciples were to pay attention to what the corrupt judge had said?
What do you think was the reason that Jesus said that his disciples were to pay attention to what the corrupt judge had thought?

Questions.Q: If the people God has chosen as his have a need and are serious to have him help them, what are they to do?
Questions.A: They are to pray day and night/very regularly each day for that need. (8)

Questions.Q: Who do you think these people are whom God has chosen?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: They are the people who believe that God sent Jesus as the Messiah/Christ to earth to save them from their sins. God knows who will believe that and he will save them. He also knows who will not believe that and he will punish them. (See Deut. 7:6-8a, 9:4-6; Matt. 22:14; John 15:16; and Rom. 8:28-33.)

Questions.Q: When Jesus returns to earth as the Son of Man, for what will he be looking/wanting to find?
Questions.A: He will be looking for/wanting to find if there is anyone who still believes/has faith that he is the savior. (8)
Questions.Alternative: When Jesus returns to earth as the Son of Man, for what will he be looking?
When Jesus returns to earth as the Son of Man, what will he be wanting to find?

Section.heading: Luke 18:9-14 Jesus told a parable about a Pharisee and a tax collector.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus explain/teach by means of this parable to those who were listening to him?
Questions.A: A person who sins and humbly pleads for God to remove his sin/to be merciful to him [and forgive him] is declared right/acceptable by God.

Those who believe that they can depend of their own good actions [to make them right with God] and who think that they are better than all other people will not be declared right/acceptable by God. They will be humiliated/shamed/embarrassed [by him] (14).
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus explain by means of this parable to those who were listening to him?
What did Jesus teach by means of this parable to those who were listening to him?

Questions.Q: What kind of person is it whom God will greatly honor?
Questions.A: It is the person who humbles himself [before God and other people]. (14c)

Questions.Q: What kind of person is it whom God will greatly shame/humiliate/embarrass?
Questions.A: It is the person who greatly honors himself. (14b)
Questions.Alternative: What kind of person is it whom God will greatly shame?
What kind of person is it whom God will greatly humiliate?
What kind of person is it whom God will greatly embarrass?

Questions.Q: To whom did Jesus tell this parable?
Questions.A: He told it to some [people who were] relying on themselves/their own [actions] to be declared right [in God's sight]. They also were people who looked down on all others/who despised all others/who treated all others with contempt. (9)

Questions.Q: Where did the two men go to pray (to God)?
Questions.A: They went to the temple [grounds]. (10)
Questions.Note: See the comments at 1:10 about the temple area.

Questions.Q: To whom did the Pharisee compare himself when he prayed (to God)?
Questions.A: He compared himself to all other people [and made them look bad while he made himself look good]. (11-12)

Questions.Q: What did the Pharisee say were reasons that he thought that God should honor or help him?
Questions.A: He said that he was not like all the other people, whom he said robbed people, cheated people/did evil things, committed adultery or collected [more money than they should for] taxes. (11)
[He implied he was better than others when] he said that he fasted two times each week and gave one-tenth of all that he got. (12) (See 11:42a.)

Questions.Q: To whom or what did the man who collected tax money compare himself?
Questions.A: He compared himself with God/with the things God had commanded people to do. (13)

Questions.Q: What did that man say were reasons that he thought that God should help him?
Questions.A: He asked God to have mercy on him and remove/forgive his sin. (13)
Questions.Note: The Greek verb Luke used here includes more than the one English language action of "have mercy". Both of the actions in the answer above should be included in the translation (see L&N entries 40.9 and 88.75).

Questions.Q: What did that man do which shows us that he was humble?
Questions.A: He stood at a distance [apart from others] (13),
he would not even look up toward [God in] heaven (13),
but was beating on/thumping his chest [as a sign of his sorrow over sins] (13).
The words of his prayer show that he did not think of himself as worthy of anything good from God. (13)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say was the result of those two men's prayers?
Questions.A: God declared/made this tax collector right in his sight, that is, he forgave him,
but that Pharisee was not forgiven/made right with God. (14a)
Questions.Note: The last half of verse 14 is exactly the same Greek wording as Luke wrote in 14:11. Try to make the translation here as much the same as you did there.

Section.heading: Luke 18:15-17 Jesus blessed some little children.

Questions.Q: How did Jesus regard the small/young children?
Questions.A: They were an example of how people should accept God's ruling over them like a king. (16)
Questions.Alternative: How did Jesus regard the small children?
How did Jesus regard the young children?

Questions.Q: Whom did Jesus say would be the people who would not enter God's kingdom?
Questions.A: They would be the people who would not [humbly] accept his authority over them, like young children [accept authority over them]. (17)
Questions.Note: Luke wrote a strong negative word here in order to show Jesus's strong feelings about this. The translation should try to reflect a strong feeling, whether it states this verse in a positive or a negative way.

Questions.Q: What did the disciples see that they did not like?
Questions.A: They saw that people were bringing infants/babies to Jesus to have him touch/put his hand on them [to bless them]. (15)

Questions.Q: What did the disciples do when they saw that?
Questions.A: They sternly commanded/rebuked the people. (15)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do about those children?
Questions.A: He called for them [to come to him] (16)
and told [the disciples] not to stop/hinder the young ones from coming to him. (16)

Section.heading: Luke 18:18-30 Jesus warned a rich man that he must let go of his wealth if he wanted to become one of the people ruled by God.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus imply was the way to receive eternal life?
Questions.A: He implied that the man must obey [all] the commandments [which God had given to Moses] (20),
sell everything he had and distribute [that money] to the poor [people] (22),
and then follow Jesus (22). (A person must get rid of everything that makes him feel secure and safe which is based upon what he possesses.)

Questions.Q: What people will have a hard time entering the kingdom of God?
Questions.A: People who have wealth. (24-25)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus promise for those who leave their family and possessions for the sake of the kingdom of God?
Questions.A: He said that they will receive [a reward of] many times more things than what they gave up. (29-30)

Questions.Q: What did the leader/ruler ask Jesus about?
Questions.A: He wanted to know what he had to do so that he would receive/inherit eternal life. (18)
Questions.Note: The man's question is exactly the same Greek wording as Luke wrote in 10:25. Try to make the translation here as much the same as you did there.
Questions.Alternative: What did the leader ask Jesus about?
What did the ruler ask Jesus about?

Questions.Q: What kind of life do you think eternal life is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It is a life that is not affected by time limits, such as whether a person is still alive physically or not. It can begin now while we still are alive and will go on forever, even after our bodies die. Jesus in his dying and rising on our behalf made it possible for us to have that eternal life. God graciously and freely allows us to have that new life. It is a life of having a close relationship with God, obeying him as he rules over us.
Questions.Note: See "life" in KBT.

If all the same people have continued to check Luke's gospel from 10:25 right through to this point, you may skip this question. But, if the consultant, translator, key assistants, or respondents have changed, or if there has been a time break of a week or more, please ask the question again.

Questions.Q: Why did Jesus question the man about calling him a good teacher?
Questions.A: Jesus said that the term was used only to refer to God. (19)

Questions.Q: Tell me the commands from God which Jesus spoke to the man about.
Questions.A: Do not commit adultery.
Do not murder.
Do not steal.
Do not lie when you testify in court.
Show honor to your father and mother.

Questions.Q: What did the man say about those commands from God?
Questions.A: He said that he had done [what they said to do] since he had been a child. (21)
Questions.Note: The Greek verb Luke used here is the same one he used in 11:28. Because the context in both places is the same, it would be best to translate it the same way in both verses.

Questions.Q: According to Jesus, what more did the man have to do?
Questions.A: He must sell everything he had (22)
and distribute [that money] to the poor [people who did not have the things they needed] (22),
and then follow Jesus (22).
Questions.Note: The translator may want to have a footnote or glossary item which indicates that Jesus was showing the man that there was still one more command which he had not obeyed in his dealings with other people. In the list of ten commands which God had spoken to Moses, the last one spoke about coveting, that is, wrongly desiring to have things. That sin was preventing this man from receiving the eternal life which he wanted. His desire for things got in the way of his desire for God.

Questions.Q: If the man did do that, where would he have anything of great value any more?
Questions.A: Jesus said that he would have [spiritual] things of great value in heaven. (22)

Questions.Q: Why did the man become very sad/grieved?
Questions.A: He was very/extremely rich [and loved the things he possessed]. (23)
Questions.Alternative: Why did the man become very sad?
Why did the man become very grieved?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say when he saw the man's sadness?
Questions.A: He said that it is [very] difficult for those who are rich to enter the kingdom of God. (24)

Questions.Q: To what did Jesus compare a rich person entering the kingdom of God?
Questions.A: He compared it to a camel going through/entering the eye of a needle. (25)

Questions.Q: Which one of those two things did Jesus say would probably happen more easily?
Questions.A: It would [almost] be easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle (than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God). (25)

Questions.Q: We know that no animal can go through the small eye of a needle. What do you think that means for the rich person and entering the kingdom of God?
Questions.A: It is also impossible for people who depend on their earthly riches instead of only trusting God. (25)

Questions.Q: After Jesus made that comparison, how did the people who were listening respond?
Questions.A: They asked who could [possibly] be saved [from God's punishment, if what Jesus had said was true]. (26)

Questions.Q: What was Jesus's answer?
Questions.A: The things [which are] impossible for man are possible for God. (27) (God can do what people cannot do. God saves a person. The person cannot save himself by possessing many things.)

Questions.Q: What did Peter say about the disciples and the things they had possessed?
Questions.A: He reminded Jesus that they had left [all] their own things/family to follow him. (28)

Questions.Q: What reward will a person have for having left home and family for the sake of the kingdom of God?
Questions.A: He will receive many times the amount he left behind, both in this time [of physical life] and in eternal life. (29-30)
Key Term Check: See "age" in KBT in the "world, age" entry.

Section.heading: Luke 18:31-34 Jesus told his disciples again that he would die and rise to live again.

Questions.Q: Jesus has spoken several times to his disciples about these things. What do they now understand from hearing him all those times?
Questions.A: Nothing. They still do not understand what, or how, all this could happen to Jesus. It is as if the clear meaning was hidden [by God] from them [until after the events]. (34)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do with his apostles?
Questions.A: He took them [aside from the larger group of disciples or others] and told them what would happen to him after they reached Jerusalem. (31)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say would happen to him?
Questions.A: Everything that the prophets had written [in the Old Testament] about the Son of Man would be accomplished/take place. (31)

Questions.Q: What things did Jesus specifically say would happen?
Questions.A: [Someone] would betray him to the Gentile/non-Jewish people. (32)
They would mock/make fun of him (32),
insult him (32),
spit on him (32),
and flogging/whipping him, they would kill him (33).

Questions.Q: Tell me what the people in your village would think if someone spit on them or at them.
Questions.A: In that time, spitting on someone, especially in that person's face, was an extreme insult.
Questions.Alternative: Tell me what your people would think if someone spit on them or at them.
Tell me what you would think if someone spit at you.
What you would think if someone spit at you?
Tell me what the people in your language area would think if someone spit on them or at them.
Questions.Note: The answer should show the translator or consultant whether the intent of those who would spit on Jesus was also understood correctly or not.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say would happen after that?
Questions.A: On the third day he would rise again [to life]. (33)

Questions.Q: What did the disciples think about all this?
Questions.A: They understood nothing about it, that is, they did not know what he was talking about. (34)
-OR-
The meaning of what [Jesus] had said had been hidden from them [by God/by their own misunderstanding]. (34)

Section.heading: Luke 18:35-43 Jesus healed a blind beggar who persisted in asking for help.

Questions.Q: What special name did the blind man call Jesus?
Questions.A: He called him the Son of David. (39)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say was the cause of the blind man being able to see again/being saved?
Questions.A: He had faith/believed that Jesus could heal/save him [by God's power when no other way was possible]. (42)
Questions.Note: These are the same Greek words as Luke wrote at 7:50 and 17:19. Try to make the translation here as much the same wording as was used in those other verses.
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus say was the cause of the blind man being able to see again?
What did Jesus say was the cause of the blind man being saved?

Questions.Q: Where did Jesus meet the blind man?
Questions.A: Jesus was approaching Jericho and the blind man was sitting by the side of that road begging [for money from the people who walked past him]. (35)

Questions.Q: Why did the blind man ask others what was happening?
Questions.A: He heard a crowd going past [him]. (36)
Questions.Note: This implied that something important was happening, or that someone important was passing by. An important person with a crowd of people following him might be generous to the blind man when all those other people were watching.

Questions.Q: Who do you think that crowd of people was?
Questions.A: It was Jesus's 12 apostles and other disciples, at the least; maybe even other people who were also going to Jerusalem [for the Passover festival]. (36)

Questions.Q: What did people tell him was happening?
Questions.A: They told him that Jesus from [the town of] Nazareth was passing by. (37)

Questions.Q: When the blind man heard it was Jesus, what did he do?
Questions.A: He shouted out to Jesus to have mercy/pity on him. (38)

Questions.Q: How did those people who were coming along at the front of that crowd respond to his calling out?
Questions.A: They sternly commanded/rebuked him to be quiet. (39)

Questions.Q: How did that man respond when the others commanded him to be quiet?
Questions.A: He cried out/screamed to Jesus even more [loudly] for Jesus to have mercy/pity on him. (39)

Questions.Q: David had been a king of the Jews many hundreds of years earlier. What do you think was the reason that the blind man called Jesus the Son of David?
Questions.A: The man had heard about Jesus being the Messiah whom God had promised to send, so now the man called him by a common Jewish title for the Messiah. (39)

Questions.Q: How did Jesus react to the blind man's shouting?
Questions.A: Jesus stopped [walking] and commanded that [someone] bring the man to him. (40)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus ask the blind man?
Questions.A: He asked, "What do you want me to do for you?" (41)

Questions.Q: What did the man want Jesus to do for him?
Questions.A: He said that he wanted to see [again]./He said that he wanted [Jesus to do something] in order that he might see [again]. (41)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do to make the man see again?
Questions.A: He only spoke the words, "See again." (42a, 43a)

Questions.Q: How did the man respond to his being able to see?
Questions.A: He followed Jesus, praising God. (43b)

Questions.Q: How did all the other people who were walking with Jesus respond to this?
Questions.A: All the people [who] saw what happened were [also] praising God. (43c)

Section.heading: Luke 19:1-10 A tax collector named Zacchaeus met Jesus and repented.

Questions.Q: Where did Jesus and the man Zacchaeus meet and talk?
Questions.A: In the town of Jericho when Jesus stopped under the tree in which Zacchaeus had climbed. (1, 4, 5)
Later they talked at Zacchaeus's house. (6-9)

Questions.Q: How did Jesus's visit with Zacchaeus change Zacchaeus's way of living?
Questions.A: He gave half of his possessions to the poor [people] (8)
and, if he had cheated anyone of anything, he promised to pay back four times as much. (8)
Questions.Note: Although the Greek words are translated "If …," and leave the point unclear in English, the Greek grammar shows that Zacchaeus was admitting that he had sometimes cheated people concerning their taxes. He said, in effect, "To those people whom I have cheated, I now offer four times the amount back."

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say was the real purpose of him stopping to talk to Zacchaeus and staying at his house?
Questions.A: [He], the Son of Man, had come [to this earth] to search out and save those [people like Zacchaeus] who knew they were [spiritually] lost/without hope. (10)

Questions.Q: Tell me about Zacchaeus.
Questions.A: He was a chief/a superintendent/a highly ranked collector of taxes [for the Roman government], (2)
He was rich, (2)
He was a short man, (3)
but he wanted to see who Jesus was. (3)

Questions.Q: What did he do in order to see Jesus pass by?
Questions.A: He ran ahead [of where Jesus was or would pass by]
and climbed a (sycamore) tree. (4)

Questions.Q: What happened when Jesus came up the place where Zacchaeus was in the tree?
Questions.A: He looked up and spoke to Zacchaeus (about coming down because Jesus wanted to stay overnight at Zacchaeus's house with him). (5)

Questions.Q: How did Zacchaeus respond to Jesus?
Questions.A: He came down hurriedly and happily welcomed him [to stay at his home overnight]. (6)

Questions.Q: Many people saw Jesus and Zacchaeus talking and walking together. What did they all think?
Questions.A: They were muttering/grumbling [among themselves] that Jesus had entered the house to stay overnight with a [man they assumed to be a blatant] sinner. (7)

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that Zacchaeus spoke about giving away his money?
Questions.A: His work was with tax money and giving those taxes to the [enemy] Roman government. People thought, or knew, that Zacchaeus had gotten rich by keeping more of that tax money than was right.
-OR-
He changed because being with Jesus made him sorry for his past wrong actions.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about Zacchaeus's promises?
Questions.A: He said that people [who lived] in that house, [that is Zacchaeus and, maybe, all those who lived there,] had that day been saved [by God from the punishment they deserved because of their sins]. (9)

Questions.Q: What was Zacchaeus's relationship to Abraham?
Questions.A: Jesus called him Abraham's son, but that meant he was a descendant of the Jews' ancestor Abraham. (See 13:16.)
-OR-
Jesus referred to Zacchaeus's believing and trusting in God as being just like [ancestor] Abraham had done.

Section.heading: Luke 19:11-27 Jesus told a parable about a man who trusted each of ten of his servants with a valuable gold coin/a large amount of money while he went away to be made a king.

Questions.Q: What were Jesus's reasons for telling this parable to the people?
Questions.A: He was [relatively] near Jerusalem [on his way there] (11)
and the [people] thought that the kingdom of God was about to appear at any moment [especially when he would reach Jerusalem]. (11)
Questions.Note: The respondent may answer with the words from verse 26, discussed below. That is all right, but do point out the wording in verse 11 again, as well.

Questions.Q: How might Jesus have wanted the listeners to understand his parable?
Questions.A: Jesus would be going away and would not return until God made him to be king over all the people. In the meantime, other Jews would oppose him being the king over them. They should only expect to receive punishment when he returns.
-OR-
While he would be gone, his disciples must serve him faithfully and use the abilities he had given them for his overall good. Any disciple who was not faithful would be judged.

Questions.Q: Whom do you think the important man who was to become king was a picture of/represented?
Questions.A: He represented Jesus. (12)
Questions.Alternative: Whom do you think the important man who was to become king was a picture of?
Whom do you think the important man who was to become king was a picture represented?

Questions.Q: Why could going to the far away place/country not be a picture of Jesus now going to Jerusalem?
Questions.A: Because Luke wrote that they were near Jerusalem. (11)
Questions.Alternative: Why could going to the far away place not be a picture of Jesus now going to Jerusalem?
Why could going to the far away country not be a picture of Jesus now going to Jerusalem?

Questions.Q: What did that important man say and do to ten of his servants?
Questions.A: He gave them each a valuable gold coin and told them, "Do business [with this money] until I come back." (13)

Questions.Q: How long would a man from your village have to work to earn that much money?
Questions.A: (The answer should be closely equal to the pay for 100 days of work.)
Questions.Alternative: How long would a man have to work to earn that much money?
Questions.Note: If the translation uses a reference to "coin" or to the Greek name of that coin, "mina", a footnote or glossary entry would be helpful to explain the value of it. Each servant received money equal to the pay for 100 days of work.

Questions.Q: What did the important man's fellow citizens/countrymen think and do about him going off to be made a king?
Questions.A: They hated him (14)
and sent a group to represent them and say, "We do not want this man to be our king." (14)
Questions.Alternative: What did the important man's fellow citizens think and do about him going off to be made a king?
What did the important man's fellow countrymen think and do about him going off to be made a king?

Questions.Q: What happened when that important man did reach that far away place?
Questions.A: He was made a king/given a kingdom [to rule over]. (15)

Questions.Q: When he returned home, why did he call for the servants to whom he had given the money?
Questions.A: He wanted to know what any of them had earned by using [his] money. (15)

Questions.Q: What did the first two men report?
Questions.A: The first man had gained ten more coins/minas (16).
The second man had gained five more coins/minas. (18)

Questions.Q: What did the master/king say to each of them?
Questions.A: Because they had been faithful [to him by doing the work he had given them], he gave them authority over ten cities and five cities, respectively. (17, 19)
Questions.Alternative: What did the master say to each of them?
What did the king say to each of them?

Questions.Q: Why did another of the servants hide the coin/mina/money given to him by the master?
Questions.A: He was afraid of the master, knowing he was a difficult man to please. (21)
Questions.Alternative: Why did another of the servants hide the coin given to him by the master?
Why did another of the servants hide the mina given to him by the master?
Why did another of the servants hide the money given to him by the master?

Questions.Q: What did the master/king say to this servant?
Questions.A: He said he would judge the servant by the same words the servant had just used to describe the master, that is, by being very tough on him for not at least investing/loaning it out and collecting interest for the master. (22-23)
Questions.Alternative: What did the master say to this servant?
What did the king say to this servant?

Questions.Q: How do those words of the important man in your language sound to you? Do the words make you think that he was happy or frustrated or sad or angry?
Questions.A: He was frustrated and angry.
Questions.Note: If conducting the check orally, read verses 22-23 again before asking this question.
The question form in Greek is rhetorical and shows these feelings. The translation should use its own appropriate grammar or choice of words to convey the same feelings.
Questions.Alternative: How do the king's words sound to you? Do you think that he was happy or frustrated or sad or angry?
How do the master's words sound to you? Do you think that he was happy or frustrated or sad or angry?
Do the words of the king make you think that he was happy, frustrated, sad or angry?
Do the words of the master make you think that he was happy, frustrated, sad or angry?

Questions.Q: What did the master/king do about this servant who had done nothing with the money?
Questions.A: He told other [servants] who were standing nearby to take the man's coin/mina and give it to the one who had [gained] ten. (24)
Questions.Alternative: What did the master do about this servant who had done nothing with the money?
What did the king do about this servant who had done nothing with the money?

Questions.Q: What was the people's reply?
Questions.A: They sound like they thought that the master's/king's command was not fair because that servant already had many coins. (25)
Questions.Alternative: How did the people reply?

Questions.Q: What did the master/king/Jesus say that the people were to learn from the way that the king treated the servants in the parable?
Questions.A: For the person who has faithfully served [God], [God] will reward/give even more to him. (26a)
For the person who has not faithfully served [God] with [the little bit] which [God] gave him, [God] will even take that away. (26b)
Questions.Alternative: What did the master say that the people were to learn from the way that the king treated the servants in the parable?
What did the king say that the people were to learn from the way that the king treated the servants in the parable?
What did Jesus say that the people were to learn from the way that the king treated the servants in the parable?

Questions.Q: What happened to those people from verse 14 who said they did not want the important man to be their king and rule over them?
Questions.A: The master/king told [his servants to] bring those enemies [to the king] and kill them in front of him/in his presence. (27)
Questions.Alternative: What happened to those people who said they did not want the important man to be their king and rule over them?
What happened to those people who said they did not want the king to rule over them?
What happened to those people who said they no longer wanted this man to be their king?
What happened to those people in verse 14 who said they no longer wanted this man to be their king?
What happened to those people who said they no longer wanted this man to be their ruler?

Section.heading: Luke 19:28-44 Jesus arrived at Jerusalem and his many disciples honored him like a king.

Questions.Q: How did people react as Jesus rode towards Jerusalem?
Questions.A: His disciples shouted happily, welcoming him as their king. (37-38)
Some of the Pharisees from the crowd [were very upset and] told Jesus to make the disciples stop. (39)

Questions.Q: How did Jesus react as he came closer to the city?
Questions.A: He cried over [the people of] the city (because they had not recognized that God was among them). (41c, 42a, 44c)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do after he spent time with Zacchaeus in Jericho?
Questions.A: He walked on in front [of his disciples] on their way up to Jerusalem.
Questions.Note: They did go "up". The road from Jericho goes up 3,500 feet (1,050 m.) in elevation by the time it reaches Jerusalem.

Questions.Q: Where were the villages of Bethphage and Bethany?
Questions.A: They were on the hill called "The Hill of Olive [Trees]". (29)

Questions.Q: What instructions did Jesus give two of his disciples?
Questions.A: He told them to go to the village across the way/across from them, enter it, (30a)
and find a young donkey tied/tethered there. (30b)
They were to untie it and bring it back [to him]. (30c)

Questions.Q: What should they say if anyone asked them why they were untying it?
Questions.A: They were to say that the Lord needed it. (31)

Questions.Q: What happened when the disciples reached that village?
Questions.A: They found [the donkey] just as [Jesus] had told them [they would]. (32)
The owners of the young donkey asked them why they were untying it. (33)
They told [them] that the Lord needed it. (34)

Questions.Q: Are you able to tell if the owners of that donkey said it was all right for the disciples to lead the donkey away or if they said it was not all right?
Questions.Note: The respondent may answer either "Yes" or "No" because they are looking at the wording of the translation.

Questions.Q: What words give you that idea?
Questions.A: The owners did approve, or say, "Yes," because we read in verse 35 that the disciples led it to Jesus.
Questions.Note: If the respondent answered, "No," to the question above, the translator may need to add some words in verse 34 to make the owners' approval clear.

Questions.Q: What happened after the two disciples brought the young donkey back to Jesus?
Questions.A: They threw their outer clothing over the young donkey's back
and helped Jesus to get up onto that donkey and sit there. (35)

Questions.Q: What did people do as the donkey walked along with Jesus sitting on its back?
Questions.A: Some people spread out their own outer clothing on the road. (36)

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that they were doing like that?
Questions.A: They did it to prepare the path in a special way to honor Jesus [as if he were a king].

Questions.Q: Where were Jesus and the disciples when people began to shout about Jesus?
Questions.A: They were just starting down the side of The Hill of Olive [Trees] [from the top] [where they could now see the city of Jerusalem across the valley]. (37a)

Questions.Q: What did the crowd of disciples shout about as Jesus went along on the young donkey?
Questions.A: (They began to joyfully praise God with loud voices) about all the mighty deeds/miracles they had seen [him do]. (37b)

Questions.Q: What did the people say in their shouting?
Questions.A: They said God should bless this one who had come [to earth] in the Lord [God]'s name. (38)
-OR-
They said God should bless this one who was coming [towards Jerusalem] like a king/as a [new] king representing the Lord [God]. (38)
They also said that in heaven [with God] there was peace,
and glory [for God] in highest [heaven].
Questions.Note: Try to make the wording of this part the same as it is in the translation back at 13:35. Jesus had prophesied there that these very words would be spoken about him, and now they are.
See the similar wording at 2:14 and make the wording here be as much the same as it is there as is possible.

Questions.Q: How did some Pharisees react to hearing the disciples say those things?
Questions.A: They [were very upset, and] told Jesus, "Teacher, sternly command/rebuke your disciples [to stop doing like this]!" (39)

Questions.Q: When Jesus answered them, he talked about stones crying out. Stones have no mouth. What do you think he meant by that?
Questions.A: [This was such important good news,] if the disciples kept silent [about it], the stones would have to cry out/shout out [about the mighty acts of God and the coming of the Messiah/Christ]. (40)

Questions.Q: Jesus's disciples were full of joy and were praising God, but Jesus cried about the people living in Jerusalem. What did he say was the reason that he cried for them?
Questions.A: If only they, too, had known that day [how to have spiritual] peace (42a),
[they would be saved from their sins],
-OR-
[God would give that peace to them],
but that was now hidden [by God/by their own unbelief] from their eyes/understanding. (42b)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say would be the consequences of their not knowing that peace?
Questions.A: Later it would happen that their enemies would build thick walls/strong fences [to protect themselves while they attacked Jerusalem] (43a-b)
and they would surround [the city] (43c),
restraining the people of Jerusalem on all sides [of the city] (43d).
They would violently tear down the city[’s wall and buildings] to the ground and [violently kill] the people [still] inside the city (44a),
not leaving one stone [to still be] attached to/on top of another (44b).

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say was the reason that their city would be destroyed?
Questions.A: The people did not recognize the time [right then] of God having visited them/been among them [in Jesus's ministry to save them]. (44c)

Section.heading: Luke 19:45-48 Jesus drove men who were selling things out of the temple grounds.

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that Jesus was so angry at the businessmen at the temple?
Questions.A: Because those people were not thinking about God and praying to him, but only about doing business and getting a profit, maybe cheating people, just like a group of robbers would do.
-OR-
In the noise of doing business, they were hindering the other people who really had come there to pray, which was the purpose of the temple. (46)

Questions.Q: Are you able to tell if Jesus entered Jerusalem or if he stayed outside of the city because he was sad?
Questions.Note: The respondent may answer either "Yes" or "No" because they are looking at the wording of the translation.

Questions.Q: What words give you that idea?
Questions.A: We know he did because we read in verse 45 that Jesus entered the temple grounds which were inside the city.
Questions.Note: If the respondent answered, "No," to the question above, the translator may need to add some words in verse 45 to make it clear that Jesus continued riding the donkey into the city.

Questions.Q: What were some of the people in the temple grounds doing?
Questions.A: They were selling things. (45)

Questions.Q: How do you know that Jesus did not like what he saw?
Questions.A: He began driving them out [of the temple grounds] (45),
telling them what had been written [by the prophet Isaiah] about the purpose of God's house. (46a)

Questions.Q: What had God said to the prophet about the temple?
Questions.A: He had said that his house was to be a place where people would pray [to him]. (46a)

Questions.Q: How did Jesus describe what the buyers and sellers had done?
Questions.A: He said they had made the temple grounds like a hiding place for people who steal from and cheat others. (46b)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus himself do in the temple grounds/area each day?
Questions.A: He taught [the people about the kingdom of God]. (47)
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus himself do in the temple grounds each day?
What did Jesus himself do in the temple area each day?

Questions.Q: What did the chief priests, the teachers of the Law, and leaders of the people want to do about Jesus?
Questions.A: They tried to find a way to kill him. (47)

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that they were angry enough to want Jesus to die?
Questions.A: Because they felt that they were the important religious leaders.
They felt they were the ones who had authority to decide what could happen inside the temple grounds, not Jesus.
They felt they were the ones to teach the people about God, not Jesus.

Questions.Q: Why did they not just kill Jesus immediately?
Questions.A: [They were afraid the crowd would turn against them] because all the people were listening closely to what he taught them. (48)

Section.heading: Luke 20:1-8 The religious leaders asked Jesus about where his authority came from.

Questions.Q: What did the groups of leaders of the Jews want to know from Jesus?
Questions.A: They wanted to know who had given him authority to do the things he had been doing. (2)

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that Jesus did not give those men an answer?
Questions.A: Since they did not believe that God had given authority to John to baptize, then they also would not believe that God had given him (Jesus) authority to do what he had been doing. Therefore, it would be useless to say that God had sent him. They would not believe him anyway. (4-8)

Questions.Q: What was Jesus doing when the groups of leaders of the Jews came to talk to him?
Questions.A: He was in the temple area teaching the people [who believed in him] and preaching the Good News [to others] [that God's plan to send the Messiah to save people was happening right then]. (1)

Questions.Q: What question did they ask him?
Questions.A: They asked him who had given him the authority to do what he was doing at the temple. (2)

Questions.Q: How did Jesus answer them?
Questions.A: He asked them a question whether it was God who had given authority to John to baptize [people] or whether only other people had given that authority to John. (3-4)

Questions.Q: Why did those groups of leaders of the Jews first talk about this among themselves before they answered Jesus?
Questions.A: They knew that if they said [God in] heaven had given authority to John [to baptize people], then Jesus would ask them, "Why did you not believe him/believe what he said?" (5)
However, if they said it was [not God, but some other] people, then all the people who believed that John was a prophet [sent by God] would kill those leaders with large stones. (6)

Questions.Q: How did they answer Jesus?
Questions.A: They said, "We do not know [who gave authority to John]." (7)

Questions.Q: How did Jesus then answer their question?
Questions.A: He said that, since they would not tell him [who had authorized John to baptize people], he would also not tell them who had authorized him to do what he was doing. (8)

Section.heading: Luke 20:9-19 Jesus told a parable about a landowner who rented his vineyard to some tenants.

Questions.Q: Tell me the different groups of people who are in Jesus's parable.
Questions.A: There was a man who planted a vineyard/grape garden (9b),
some farmers who rented/leased the vineyard (9c),
some servants whom the owner sent to get his share of the fruit which had grown (10-12),
and the owner's son (13-15).

Questions.Q: What were the farmers/tenants who were supposed to watch over the vineyard wanting to do?
Questions.A: They wanted to have all the fruit from the vineyard and even own the vineyard themselves. (10b-15a)
Questions.Alternative: What were the farmers who were supposed to watch over the vineyard wanting to do?
What were the tenants who were supposed to watch over the vineyard wanting to do?

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason those who listened to Jesus's parable did not want such a terrible thing to ever happen to them? (16b)
Questions.A: They recognized that Jesus was using picture language to tell them their leaders had rejected the many servants, that is, prophets, whom God had sent to the Jews.
Jesus was also telling them with this picture language that God had sent Jesus, his much-loved son, also, but the leaders had rejected him and would kill him outside the city.
The picture language also showed them that God would punish the leaders for all they had done,
and he would give his people to others to care for, which those listeners understood to be non-Jews. The listeners did not like any of this.

Questions.Q: Who were the people to whom Jesus told this parable?
Questions.A: These were the same Jewish leaders who asked him that last question,
namely, the chief priests, the teachers of the Law, and the elders (20:1),
but the other people to whom Jesus had been teaching or preaching were also there.

Questions.Q: Why did the owner of the vineyard/grape garden rent it out to some farmers/tenants?
Questions.A: He was going away for a long time [and wanted them to take care of it for him]. (9)
Questions.Alternative: Why did the owner of the vineyard rent it out to some farmers?
Why did the owner of the vineyard rent it out to some tenants?
Why did the owner of the grape garden rent it out to some farmers?
Why did the owner of the grape garden rent it out to some tenants?

Questions.Q: Why did the owner send a servant/slave back to those farmers?
Questions.A: So that the farmers would give the servant/slave some of the fruit [which had grown] in the vineyard [to take back to the owner]. (10)
Questions.Note: It is also all right if the translation says that the servants came to get some of the money from selling the fruit, instead of saying they came to get some of the actual fruit.
Questions.Alternative: Why did the owner send a servant back to those farmers?
Why did the owner send a slave back to those farmers?

Questions.Q: When a person in your language group uses the garden/land area of another person, how does that one give a payment to the owner of the land?
Questions.A: (Answers may vary, but expect many answers to include the giving of some of the harvested crop to the owner of the land.)
Questions.Note: This is to highlight the purpose of the owner in the parable sending his servant to that vineyard, if such a practice is not common in the language area of the translation.
Questions.Alternative: When a person in your language group uses the garden of another person, how does that one give a payment to the owner of the land?
When a person in your village uses the garden of another person, how does that one give a payment to the owner of the land?
When a person in your language group uses the land of another person, how does that one give a payment to the owner of the land?
When a person in your village uses the land of another person, how does that one give a payment to the owner of the land?
When a person in your language group uses the land area of another person, how does that one give a payment to the owner of the land?

Questions.Q: What did the farmers do when a servant came to them?
Questions.A: They beat one servant/slave and sent him back with nothing. (10)
They beat another, did shameful things/gave shame to him and sent him back with nothing. (11)
They wounded a third servant and threw him out [of the vineyard]. (12)

Questions.Q: Why did the owner of the vineyard send his much-loved son to the farmers?
Questions.A: He thought that they would respect/honor his son. (13)

Questions.Q: What did the farmers say when they saw the owner's son coming?
Questions.A: They decided they should kill him so that they could get the vineyard for themselves. (14)

Questions.Q: What did those farmers do to the owner's son?
Questions.A: They threw him outside the vineyard and killed him. (15a)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say the owner of the vineyard would do when the farmers had killed his son?
Questions.A: He said the owner would come and destroy those people and give the vineyard to others [to care for]. (16a)

Questions.Q: What did the listeners to Jesus's parable think about that result?
Questions.A: They said that should never happen. (16b)

Questions.Q: Someone had written picture language about builders and a building stone, and now Jesus reminded the people of those words. Where were those words written?
Questions.A: Someone wrote them in God's Word/in the part of the Bible we call the Old Testament. (17)
Questions.Note: The original words can be found in Ps. 118:22.

Questions.Q: What did those words say about a building stone?
Questions.A: Builders rejected a stone for their building,
but that stone is now the most important one to hold up the house.
-OR-
but that stone is now the most important one to hold everything else in its proper place. (17b)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say in his own picture language about that stone?
Questions.A: Everyone who falls over that stone will be broken into pieces
and everyone on whom the stone falls will be crushed (to fine powder). (18)

Questions.Q: Who do you think that Jesus wanted the people to think were represented by the various parts of this picture language?
Questions.A: They were to think that the builders were a picture of the leaders of the Jews, (17b)
the stone which they rejected was Jesus, (17b)
the people who fall over that stone are those who do not believe that God sent Jesus (18a)
and the people on whom the stone falls are those who are punished forever because they do not believe in Jesus (18b).

Questions.Q: Did those who were listening to Jesus understand that he was talking about them in those word pictures?
Questions.A: Yes, they did understand.

Questions.Q: How do you know that they understood what Jesus meant?
Questions.A: The teachers of the Law/scribes and the chief priests tried to find a way to arrest Jesus right then. (19a)

Questions.Q: Why did they not do it right then?
Questions.A: They were afraid of the people [who were right there and believed that God had sent both John and Jesus]. (19b)

Section.heading: Luke 20:20-26 The religious leaders tried to cause Jesus to say something against the Jewish or Roman laws.

Questions.Q: Some men told Jesus that they wanted to know about paying taxes to the enemy Roman government, but what did they really want?
Questions.A: They wanted to make Jesus say something against the Roman government so they could arrest him and put him under the authority and control of the Roman government. (20)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about obeying the government's laws, such as paying taxes?
Questions.A: He said that people should do whatever the king/government says they all must do, such as pay their taxes,
(and they should also do whatever God says they all must do). (25)

Questions.Q: Who were sending men to spy on Jesus and catch him saying something wrong?
Questions.A: They were the teachers of the Law and the chief priests mentioned in verse 19.

Questions.Q: How did those spies get near to Jesus in order to listen and ask him questions?
Questions.A: They pretended to be concerned about doing the right thing. (20a)

Questions.Q: What would those men do if Jesus said something wrong?
Questions.A: They wanted to turn him over to the [Roman] governor's authority and control. (20b)

Questions.Q: What did the spies tell Jesus that they knew about him?
Questions.A: They said that they knew he spoke and taught correctly
and that he was not influenced by who people were,
but that he truthfully taught the way that God [wanted people to live]. (21)

Questions.Q: What did they want to know about taxes?
Questions.A: They wanted to know if it was proper [for a Jew] to pay taxes to [the Roman Emperor/king] Caesar. (22)

Questions.Q: What words tell you that Jesus was not fooled by those men trying to make trouble for him?
Questions.A: Luke says that Jesus clearly understood their attempt to trick him. (23)

Questions.Q: When they showed Jesus a [Roman] denarius/coin, what did he ask them about it?
Questions.A: He asked them whose picture/shape and words were on the coin. (24)
Questions.Alternative: When they showed Jesus a Roman denarius, what did he ask them about it?
When they showed Jesus a Roman coin, what did he ask them about it?
When they showed Jesus a denarius, what did he ask them about it?
When they showed Jesus a coin, what did he ask them about it?

Questions.Q: Whose were they?
Questions.A: [The Roman emperor/king] Caesar's. (25a)

Questions.Q: Jesus said they should do whatever was a part of the government work, such as pay their taxes. What, then, were the people to do about the things God said they should do?
Questions.A: Jesus said they should do both things, those which the government said were necessary
and those which God had said were necessary. (25b)

Questions.Q: How well did those men's plan work, their plan to catch Jesus saying something wrong in front of many people?
Questions.A: It did not work. The men were unable to catch him in what he said.
They were so amazed at his answer that they were silent/they had nothing more to say. (26)

Section.heading: Luke 20:27-40 Some Sadducees asked Jesus about people being married after they died and rose to live again.

Questions.Q: Tell me the little story about seven brothers which the Sadducees told to Jesus.
Questions.A: The first brother of seven married a woman, but died without children. (29)
The second [brother], then the third married her, but they also died childless. (30-31a)
The [rest of the] seven [brothers] were the same, [marrying her, but] leaving no children [when they each] died. (31b)
Lastly, the woman died. (32)
Questions.Note: The translation should not imply that the woman caused the men to die. This is not a true story about real men. The Sadducees created the story to try to trick Jesus. Its focus is on the idea of rising again after dying.

Questions.Q: What was the [trick] question the Sadducees asked Jesus?
Questions.A: "When people are raised by God to live again after dying, whose wife will she be, having been the wife of each of the seven?" (33)
Questions.Alternative: What was the trick question the Sadducees asked Jesus?
What was the question the Sadducees asked Jesus?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about people and their rising after being dead?
Questions.A: He said that people [whom God] declared worthy would rise to live again after being dead (35, 37),
but they would not marry (35),
they cannot die again [because they are like the angels] (36).
[Those people] are children of God, because they have been raised [by God] to live again [with him] (36c-d).

Even Moses showed that the [people who are] dead will be raised [by God] to live again when he referred to [God when he spoke to Moses out of] the burning bush as the God of Abraham, of Isaac and of Jacob, [ancestors who no longer were living on the earth] (37).

Questions.Q: The Sadducees told Jesus that they wanted to know about people being married after they rose from being dead, but what do you think they really wanted?
Questions.A: Because they did not believe that people would rise again after being dead (27), they wanted to make Jesus look foolish as he tried to make an answer for something which they thought would never happen.

Questions.Q: What did Luke tell us about the group called the Sadducees?
Questions.A: He said that they did not believe that people would rise after being dead. (27)

Key Term Check: The Sadducees were a group, like a political party. They were rich, important Jewish families. Most of the members were priests who regarded the Laws of Moses as the most important part of God's Word. They did not believe that angels or Satan were real. See "Sadducee" in KBT in the "Pharisee, Sadducee" entry.

Questions.Q: What did the Sadducees say was the rule about marriage which Moses had written down and taught to the Jews?
