Questions.A: If a man's brother died, leaving his widow, but no children, that man should marry the [dead brother's] widow and have some children for his brother. (28)

Questions.Q: How do people get to be one of those whom God will raise to live again after dying?
Questions.A: They are the people whom [God] has called/considered/regarded as worthy. (35)

Questions.Q: Not every person whom we know who has believed in Jesus as his or her savior is still alive today. Some are dead. What do you think is the way, then, that they are all alive to God?
Questions.A: We think about the bodies of those people and say they are dead, but God looks at their spirit and says they all live on. (38)
Questions.Note: God also knows that on the Last Day he will raise up the bodies of those who believe in Jesus (see John 6:39-40, 11:24 and 1 Thess. 4:13-18).

Questions.Q: Who praised Jesus for his good answer?
Questions.A: Some of the teachers of the Law/scribes. (39)

Questions.Q: Why did they praise Jesus?
Questions.A: They believed that his answer was correct (that is, it fit with their understanding of the Scriptures).
Perhaps also, they were happy to see that he had silenced the Sadducees [by showing their ideas to be wrong]. (40)
Questions.Note: We assume that these teachers of the Law were not part of the Sadducees, but were part of the Pharisees, who did believe that God raised people to be alive again after dying. They also believed in angels. They often disagreed with the Sadducees about these things (see Acts 23:6-9).

Section.heading: Luke 20:41-44 Jesus showed that the Messiah was greater than King David.

Questions.Q: Whom did Jesus indicate was the greater person, King David or the Christ?
Questions.A: He was indicating that the Christ was greater than even King David had been. (41-44)
Questions.Note: See the discussion in Translator's Notes on this section.

Questions.Q: How did the people of Jesus's time describe the Christ whom God said he would send to this earth?
Questions.A: They called him the [Special] Descendant of [King] David. (41)

Questions.Q: How had David himself described the Christ?
Questions.A: David had called him his Lord. (42, 44)

Questions.Q: Who were the two Lords whom David wrote about in the Psalm which Jesus quoted?
Questions.A: The one who spoke was Yahweh, the supreme, eternal God of the Jews.
The one whom David called "my Lord" was the Messiah, the Christ, whom God had promised to send to save God's people.
Questions.Note: Although the two persons are both called by the same name in the Greek and in the English bibles, in the original Hebrew writing, the words are clearly different and would not have been confusing.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the answer to Jesus's last question about the Christ being both a descendant of King David and his Lord at the same time?
Questions.A: The Christ [Jesus] was physically a human descendant in the family line of King David.
He also was a far greater person than King David because he was God's own son, who had been sent to this earth from heaven.

Section.heading: Luke 20:45-47 Jesus told people to not do as the teachers of the Law did.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that God would punish the kind of people Jesus talked about here even more than other people?
Questions.A: They pretended to be blessed because they obeyed God so well, but their example was teaching people to think mostly about themselves. (47)

Questions.Q: Jesus warned the people about the way that the teachers of the Law acted. What kind of things did they do?
Questions.A: They walked around in fancy clothes in market/public places in order to enjoy [people] greeting them [with great respect]. (46)
They enjoyed [people] honoring [them] by having them sit in special places both in synagogues and at feasts. (46)
They did wrong things [in order to become rich], such as becoming the owners of widows' homes [and possessions]. (47)
They showed off by saying long prayers [in public places] (that is, they pretended to be very religious). (47)

Section.heading: Luke 21:1-4 A widow gave everything she had to God.

Questions.Q: Why did Jesus regard the widow's money as more than the rich people's money?
Questions.A: She gave God everything she had to live on. The rich people only gave part of the large amount of money which they had. (It was money they did not really need in order to stay alive.) (4)

Questions.Q: Where were the people putting their gifts for God?
Questions.A: They put their gifts into a box/boxes for that purpose in the temple area. (1)

Questions.Q: How much money did the widow put into the box?
Questions.A: She put in two coins of the smallest value that there was. (2)

Questions.Q: How much money did the rich people put into that box?
Questions.A: They only gave part of the wealth which they had. (4)

Section.heading: Luke 21:5-24 Jesus warned that enemies would destroy the temple and all of Jerusalem.

Questions.Q: What major troubles did Jesus say his followers should watch for?
Questions.A: Enemies would destroy the temple. (5-7)
There would be wars, earthquakes, famines, and other disasters on the earth
and strange signs in the sky. (8-11)
People, even family members, would persecute believers and cause some to die. (12-19)
Enemies would destroy Jerusalem. (20-24)

Questions.Q: Why were those who followed Jesus not to worry when those things happened?
Questions.A: Those things would not be marks that time/the world was about to end. (9)
Jesus would give them the right wise words to say as a testimony to their faith in him. (13-15)
By continuing [to have faith] in the midst of the difficult circumstances, they would save their lives. (19)

Questions.Q: Why was the city of Jerusalem going to be totally destroyed?
Questions.A: It would be time for [God] to punish the people there just like [prophets] had written it would be. (22)
Questions.Note: Some of the things which prophets had said would happen you can read in these Old Testament books: Dan. 9:26; 1 Kings 9:6-9; Mic. 3:5-12; Mal. 4:1-2.

Questions.Q: What do you think the people had done which showed that it was time for God to punish them?
Questions.A: The people had rejected Jesus as the one whom God had sent to them to save them from their sins.

Questions.Q: What were some of the people/disciples talking about while they were in the temple grounds with Jesus?
Questions.A: They were talking about the temple and how it was decorated with beautiful stones and gifts which people had offered to God. (5)
Questions.Alternative: What were some of the people talking about while they were in the temple grounds with Jesus?
What were some of the disciples talking about while they were in the temple grounds with Jesus?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about the stones?
Questions.A: He said that at a later time not one stone would be left on top of another, [that is, someone would break those walls down into a pile of rocks]. (6)

Questions.Q: What was their response to Jesus's statement?
Questions.A: They wanted to know when that would happen
and what signs would warn them that it was about to happen. (7)

Questions.Q: Why must the people/disciples be very careful about this matter?
Questions.A: They could be deceived by [one of the] many [men] who would claim that he was the real Christ whom God had sent to save all the people in the world. (8)
They may also become frightened when hearing [people talk] about wars and civil unrest. (9)
Questions.Alternative: Why must the people be very careful about this matter?
Why must the disciples be very careful about this matter?

Questions.Q: What kinds of things would happen later which could also cause people to think that the world was about to end?
Questions.A: Some countries would fight against other countries; (10)
there would be severe earthquakes, and famine and horrible diseases in place after place. (11)
People will see strange/unusual things happen in the sky which would make them be terribly afraid and wonder [if the world was about to end]. (11)

Questions.Q: Why are people not to worry at that time?
Questions.A: Those things would happen, but that would not yet be the end of the world/time. (9)

Questions.Q: What would happen even before those wars and earthquakes and other terrible things?
Questions.A: Other people would seize the disciples/those who believed in Jesus and persecute them. (12)
Those people would turn the believers over to [the leaders of] the synagogues and prisons. (12)
They would take the believers in front of kings and governors [to be tried in court]. (12)
Questions.Note: Check whether any changes which you may have made to the Key Term "persecute" back at 11:49 should be applied to verse 12 as well.

Questions.Q: Why would those people do like that?
Questions.A: They would do that because the disciples/believers were associated with Jesus (and his name). (12, 17)

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that people would do like that to the disciples/believers?
Questions.A: Those people wanted to make the disciples/believers stop believing in, and speaking about, Jesus.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think was the reason that people would do like that to the disciples?
What do you think was the reason that people would do like that to the believers?

Questions.Q: What would be the result of these things happening to the disciples/believers?
Questions.A: Those experiences would be opportunities for them to testify [about who Jesus really was]. (13)
Questions.Alternative: What would be the result of these things happening to the disciples?
What would be the result of these things happening to the believers?

Questions.Q: How would they know what they should say [about Jesus] to those synagogue or government leaders?
Questions.A: Jesus himself would give them wise words to say. (15a)
They should not carefully plan out in their own minds what they think would be good arguments. (14)
Questions.Alternative: How would they know what they should say about Jesus to those synagogue or government leaders?
How would they know what they should say to those synagogue or government leaders?

Questions.Q: Tell me how their testimony in court would affect the ones who accused them of doing wrongly.
Questions.A: None of those [people] who opposed the disciples/believers would be able to be against or contradict what they just said. (15b)

Questions.Q: Who will some of the people be who betray the disciples/believers?
Questions.A: Some of them will be one's parents, brothers, relatives and friends. (16)
Questions.Alternative: Who will some of the people be who betray the disciples?
Who will some of the people be who betray the believers?

Questions.Q: How strongly would these people cause trouble for the disciples/believers?
Questions.A: [By their testimony in court] they would cause [some] of the disciples/believers to die (16),
and all [those people] would hate the disciples/believers (17).
Questions.Alternative: How strongly would these people cause trouble for the disciples?
How strongly would these people cause trouble for the believers?

Questions.Q: Would they all be destroyed by those who hate them so much?
Questions.A: No, they would not! (18)

Questions.Q: How would they save their lives/souls?
Questions.A: By continuing [to have faith] in the midst of the difficult circumstances, they would save their lives. (19)
Questions.Alternative: How would they save their lives?
How would they save their souls?

Questions.Q: How would people know that Jerusalem was about to be totally destroyed?
Questions.A: They would see [enemy] armies surround the city. (20)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus suggest that the people do then?
Questions.A: Those [people who lived] in Judea [province] should flee to the mountains
and those in the city should get out of it. Others should not go into the city. (21)

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that it would be so dreadful a time for pregnant women and those having infants?
Questions.A: They would not be able to flee quickly.
-OR-
They would be less able to handle extreme hardships in those situations.

Questions.Q: What would happen to the entire area?
Questions.A: There would be great suffering/calamity/misery all over the region. (23)

Questions.Q: What would happen to the people?
Questions.A: [The enemies] would kill them by means of swords,
and capture others and take them away to many other nations/countries. (24)

Questions.Q: What would happen to Jerusalem?
Questions.A: It would be destroyed and treated with contempt by people from nations which did not honor God. (24)

Questions.Q: How long would those other nations do that to Jerusalem?
Questions.A: It would continue until the end of the time [which God had set] for it to end. (24)

Section.heading: Luke 21:25-28 Jesus told about signs which people will see when the Son of Man will return to earth.

Questions.Q: When the time of trouble and suffering is over, what will happen?
Questions.A: The Son of Man (Jesus) will come back to this world. (27-28)

Questions.Q: Why should those who believe in Jesus be so excited and happy about seeing him return to earth?
Questions.A: He will be coming to release them/get them back [from the troubles and disasters taking place in the world due to sin and Satan]. (28)

Questions.Q: What unusual things will people see or experience that will make them worry and be afraid?
Questions.A: They will see signs in the sun, moon, and stars. (25)
Their thinking will be confused and fearful because of the sea roaring and the waves tossing wildly. (25)
They will faint from fear, not knowing what will happen to the world, because stars [and other things we see in the sky] will waver/totter/move as if someone shook them around. (26)

Questions.Q: What will people see when the Son of Man returns?
Questions.A: He will come in a cloud in a powerful and majestic manner. (27)

Questions.Q: What should those who believe in Jesus do when these things begin to happen?
Questions.A: They should stand up and lift up their heads [in joyous expectation]. (28)

Section.heading: Luke 21:29-33 Jesus's words will last forever.

Questions.Q: How would the people know that what Jesus was teaching them really would happen?
Questions.A: Just like new sprouts on a fig tree help people to know that summer is near, even so, when people see certain things happen [in nature], they should realize that other things which Jesus also predicted will naturally follow soon after that. (30-31)
When Jesus said something will happen, it will happen, even if the sky and the earth and the things we see there cease to exist. (33)

Questions.Q: What do people know when they see sprouts appear on a fig tree?
Questions.A: They know that the time for summer is near. (30)
Questions.Note: See possible cultural alternatives to use instead of "summer" in TN.

Questions.Q: What were people to learn from seeing the unusual things Jesus said would happen in the sky, earth and sea?
Questions.A: The kingdom of God (his fully ruling and reigning over his people) was about to happen. (31)

Questions.Q: When would those things happen?
Questions.A: They would happen before the people who were living then at Jesus's time would die. (32)
Questions.Note: Although some people interpret the words "this generation" in several other ways, when one looks at the other places where Luke used these words, they clearly refer to the people living in Jesus's time. See Luke 7:31; 11:29, 30, 31, 32, 50, 51; and Acts 2:40.

Section.heading: Luke 21:34-38 Be ready for Jesus' return.

Questions.Q: What are the important points that Luke is telling about in this section?
Questions.A: Don't let drunkenness or worry weight your heart down.
It is important to be ready for Jesus' coming.
We should pray for strength.
Jesus was attracting a crowd of people who wanted to listen to him.

Questions.Q: What can cause your heart to become dull / weighed down?
Questions.A: dissipation / carousing
drunkenness
worries / anxiety

Questions.Q: When/How did Jesus say the day of his coming / the coming of the kingdom of God would be?
Questions.A: Suddenly/Unexpectedly, like a trap
Questions.Note: Respondents might give answers from previous section. (See similar questions there.)
Questions.Alternative: When did Jesus say the day of his coming / the coming of the kingdom of God would be?
How did Jesus say the day of his coming / the coming of the kingdom of God would be?

Questions.Q: Who will experience the events Jesus describes? // Who will experience the coming of Jesus? // Who will experience the coming of God's kingdom?
Questions.A: All people who live on earth. (35)
Questions.Alternative: Who will experience the events Jesus describes?
Who will experience the coming of Jesus?
Who will experience the coming of God's kingdom?

Questions.Q: What did he say should be done during these bad incidents?
Questions.A: Be on the alert
Pray (to escape them)

Questions.Q: Before whom are we to stand?
Questions.A: The Son of Man (Jesus)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell them to do while they are alert? // Why did Jesus tell them to keep alert?
Questions.A: Pray for strength to escape all these things and to stand before the Son of Man.
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus tell them to do while they are alert?
Why did Jesus tell them to keep alert?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do every day in the temple?
Questions.A: He taught the people

Questions.Q: Where did Jesus spend the nights?
Questions.A: The mount of Olives / Olivet (37)

Questions.Q: For what purpose/reason did people used to come to the temple early in the morning?
Questions.A: To listen to Jesus (38)
Questions.Alternative: For what purpose did people used to come to the temple early in the morning?
For what reason did people used to come to the temple early in the morning?

Section.heading: Luke 22:1-6 Judas Agrees to Betray Jesus

Questions.Q: About which important incidents is Luke telling in this section?
Questions.A: In this section, Luke is telling about Judas agreeing to betray Jesus. Satan entered Judas and went to the chief priests to turn Jesus in for money.

Questions.Q: Which festival was approaching?
Questions.A: The festival of Unleavened Bread was approaching.

Questions.Q: What do they call that festival?
Questions.A: They call the festival Passover.

Questions.Q: Who were looking for a chance to kill Jesus?
Questions.A: The chief priests and the teachers of the law were looking for a chance to kill Jesus.

Questions.Q: What were the chief priests and teachers of the law afraid of?
Questions.A: The chief priests and teachers of law were afraid of the people.
Questions.Note: Although the text does not specify what exactly they were afraid of, if respondent attempts to explain why they were afraid, ensure that the translation does not imply anything incorrect.

Questions.Q: Who did Satan possess?
Questions.A: Satan entered Judas Iscariot.

Questions.Q: What makes it surprising that Judas would betray Jesus?
Questions.A: Judas was one of the twelve disciples.
Questions.Alternative: What makes it unexpected that Judas would betray Jesus?
Why might it be unexpected that Judas would betray Jesus?

Questions.Q: How can you tell/know someone is possessed by an evil spirit?
Questions.A: The person possessed by an evil spirit will act or speak against God/His children.
Questions.Alternative: How can you tell someone is possessed by an evil spirit?
How can you know someone is possessed by an evil spirit?

Questions.Q: To whom did Judas go, and tell about being able to hand Jesus over?
Questions.A: Judas went to the chief priests and the officers of the temple guard.

Questions.Q: What did they happily agree to give Judas?
Questions.A: They happily agreed to give Judas money.

Questions.Q: When was he looking for a chance to catch Jesus in order to hand him over to them?
Questions.A: Judas was looking for a chance to catch Jesus when no crowd was present.

Questions.Q: Why do you think Judas wanted to hand Jesus over to them when no one else was present?
Questions.A: If Judas handed Jesus over when a crowd was present, the crowd might have been resentful and angry towards him.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus instruct his disciples about?
Questions.A: Jesus instructed them about the details of preparing for the Passover meal.

Questions.Q: What did they used to do on that festival day?
Questions.A: The Jews used to sacrifice a lamb for the Passover meal [in remembrance of their ancestors deliverance from slavery in Egypt].

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell Peter and John to do?
Questions.A: Jesus told Peter and John to go make preparations for the Passover meal.

Questions.Q: What did Peter and John ask Jesus?
Questions.A: They asked, "Where do you want us to prepare for it?"

Questions.Q: Who did Jesus say would meet them?
Questions.A: Jesus said that they would meet a man carrying a jar of water.

Questions.Q: How do you think Jesus knew about the man coming from another village carrying the water pot while the disciples were going?
Questions.A: Jesus is God. He knows everything.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell them to ask the landlord of that house?
Questions.A: Jesus told them to say, "The Teacher asks: Where is the guest room, where I may eat the Passover with my disciples."
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus tell them to ask the owner of that house?

Questions.Q: What were the disciples to do in that [upper] room?
Questions.A: The disciples were to make preparations for the Passover meal.
Questions.Alternative: What were the disciples to do in that upper room?
What were the disciples to do in that room?
What did Jesus want the disciples to do in that upper room?
What did Jesus ask the disciples to do in that upper room?
What did Jesus want the disciples to do in that room?
What did Jesus ask the disciples to do in that room?

Questions.Q: How do you think the upper room of the house was [to be] decorated?
Questions.A: There probably would have been low lying tables and seats or mats.
Questions.Alternative: How do you think the upper room of the house was decorated?
How do you think the upper room of the house was to be decorated?
How do you think the upper room of the house was furnished?

Questions.Q: After those disciples went, what did they find there?
Questions.A: They found things just as Jesus had told them.

Questions.Q: What new covenant was Jesus telling his disciples about?
Questions.A: The new covenant Jesus was telling about is his body being broken and his blood shed for the bad things we have done.

Questions.Q: What new practice/ordinance was Jesus establishing?
Questions.A: Jesus was establishing the breaking of bread and drinking of the cup as a way to remember him/his death.
Questions.Alternative: What new practice was Jesus establishing?
What new ordinance was Jesus establishing?
What new way of celebrating the Passover was Jesus establishing?
What new tradition was Jesus establishing?
How was Jesus changing the way the Passover was celebrated?
How was Jesus changing the normal Passover celebration?

Questions.Q: How do you think Jesus was able to tell about things that would happen in the future: who would betray him, how he would die and what would happen to him who betrayed him?
Questions.A: Jesus knew his purpose to come to earth. He knew what he was going to go through. Jesus is God.

Questions.Q: Where did Jesus and his disciples to go [and sit/recline]?
Questions.A: Jesus and his disciples reclined at the table.
Questions.Alternative: Where did Jesus and his disciples to go and sit?
Where did Jesus and his disciples to go and recline?

Questions.Q: About which hope [that he had] did Jesus tell his disciples?
Questions.A: Jesus told his disciples he had hoped to eat the Passover meal before he suffered.
Questions.Alternative: About which hope that he had did Jesus tell his disciples?
About which hope did Jesus tell his disciples?

Questions.Q: Until when did Jesus say that he would not eat [the Passover]?
Questions.A: Jesus said He would not eat the Passover until it finds fulfillment in the kingdom of God.
Questions.Alternative: Until when did Jesus say that he would not eat the Passover?
Until when did Jesus say that he would not eat the Passover meal?
Until when did Jesus say that he would not eat?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus mean by that?
Questions.A: When Jesus said this, he referred to the Passover festival. He was going to be the [true] sacrificial lamb. After that, he would not celebrate the Passover anymore [on earth], but he would celebrate the final rescue of God's people in heaven.
Questions.Note: There is a lot of deep significance contained in Jesus' statement. Many respondents will probably only be able to understand a small part of what Jesus meant.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do with the cup [filled with grape juice]?
Questions.A: Jesus gave thanks and divided it among the disciples.
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus do with the cup filled with grape juice?
What did Jesus do with the cup?
What did Jesus do with the cup filled with wine?

Questions.Q: Having broken the bread, what did he tell them while giving it to them?
Questions.A: Jesus said, "This is my body given for you; do this in remembrance of me."

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say would be the witness of the cup [filled with grape juice]?
Questions.A: Jesus said the cup signified a new covenant in his blood.
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus say would be the witness of the grape juice?
What did Jesus say would be the witness of the cup filled with grape juice?
What did Jesus say would be the witness of the cup?
What did Jesus say would be the witness of the cup filled with wine?
What did Jesus say would be the witness of the wine?
What did Jesus the grape juice signified?
What did Jesus the grape juice represented?
What did Jesus say the cup filled with grape juice signified?
What did Jesus say the cup signified?
What did Jesus say the cup filled with wine signified?
What did Jesus say the wine signified?
What did Jesus say the wine represented?

Questions.Q: Where was Judas at this time? // What was Judas doing at this time?
Questions.A: Judas was there at the table, eating with Jesus and the disciples.
Questions.Alternative: Where was Judas at this time?
What was Judas doing at this time?

Questions.Q: What was Judas about to do?
Questions.A: Judas was going to betray Jesus.

Questions.Q: What was the promise given by God? // What had God promised?
Questions.A: The promise given by God was that the Son of Man would be [betrayed and] sacrificed.
Questions.Alternative: What was the promise given by God?
What had God promised?

Questions.Q: What was about to happen to Jesus? // What was Jesus about to do?
Questions.A: Jesus was going to die.
Questions.Alternative: What was about to happen to Jesus?
What was Jesus about to do?

Questions.Q: To whom will trouble come?
Questions.A: Trouble will come to the man who betrays Jesus.

Questions.Q: What did the disciples ask one another?
Questions.A: The disciples asked who would do this.

Questions.Q: About what did the disciples quarrel?
Questions.A: The disciples quarreled about who is considered to be the greatest.
Questions.Alternative: About what did the disciples argue?
What dispute did the disciples have?
About what did a quarrel break out among the disciples?
About what are the disciples quarreling?

Questions.Q: How do the kings of this earth/the Gentiles rule?
Questions.A: The kings of this earth/the Gentiles rule over the people and burden them.
Questions.Alternative: How do the kings of this earth rule?
How do the kings of the Gentiles rule?
What attitude do the authorities have?

Questions.Q: What do those kings/authorities call themselves?
Questions.A: The kings call themselves Benefactors.
Questions.Alternative: What do those kings call themselves?
What do those authorities call themselves?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell his disciples about how they should live?
Questions.A: Jesus told his disciples to be humble and serve others.

Questions.Q: Jesus asks "Who is greater, the one who is at the table or the one who serves?" What do you think is the answer to that question?
Questions.A: In the world, it is considered that the one who is at the table is greater but in God's view, the one who serves is greater.
Questions.Alternative: Who is greater, the one who sits and eats at the table or the one who serves?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about his behavior among the disciples?
Questions.A: Jesus said that he was behaved as a servant.

Questions.Q: What are the trials Jesus is referring to?
Questions.A: The trials Jesus is referring to are the hatred that was given by the leaders/rulers/teachers of law. Jesus was not welcomed in many places.

Questions.Q: Who do you think Jesus’ father could be?
Questions.A: Jesus’ father is God.
Questions.Note: Although his earthly father was Joseph, he was not referring to him.
Questions.Alternative: Who do you think Jesus’ father is?
Who do you think Jesus’ father was?
Who is Jesus’ father?
Who was Jesus’ father?
When Jesus spoke of his Father, who was he talking about?

Questions.Q: What kind of authority did Jesus say he was going to give the disciples?
Questions.A: Jesus said he would give the disciples authority to judge the twelve tribes of Israel.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell his disciples they would do [in His kingdom]?
Questions.A: Jesus said that they would eat and drink at his table in his kingdom.
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus tell his disciples they would do in His kingdom?
What did Jesus tell his disciples they would do?

Questions.Q: Jesus says that in his kingdom his disciples would eat and drink with him. Where do you think his kingdom is?
Questions.A: His kingdom is in heaven.
Questions.Alternative: He says that in my kingdom you will eat and drink along with me. Where do you think Jesus’ kingdom really is?
What does Jesus mean when he says "in my kingdom?" Where or what is Jesus’ kingdom?

Questions.Q: Who is Jesus talking to in this passage?
Questions.A: Jesus is talking to Peter.

Questions.Q: What does Jesus say will happen?
Questions.A: Jesus says that Peter will deny him three times and the rooster will crow.

Questions.Q: How is the spirit world related to the world in which we live?
Questions.A: Both worlds are active. There is a constant spiritual battle that happens. For everything that we see in the physical world, there will be equivalent battles in the spiritual world.

Questions.Q: What was Satan trying to do to Simon Peter and the other disciples?
Questions.A: Satan was trying to tempt and test Simon Peter and the disciples.
Questions.Alternative: What was Satan trying to do to the disciples?
What was Satan trying to do with Simon Peter and the other disciples?
What was Satan trying to do with the disciples?
What was Satan trying to do to them?
What was Satan trying to do with them?
What did Satan want to do?

Questions.Q: Who do you think Satan is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Satan is the chief enemy of God. He is the supreme evil spiritual being who leads and directs all other evil spiritual beings.
Questions.Note: See "Satan" in KBT.

Questions.Q: To whom did Jesus pray when he prayed for Simon Peter?
Questions.A: Jesus prayed to his Father [God] for Simon Peter.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus pray for on behalf of Simon Peter?
Questions.A: On Peters' behalf, Jesus prayed for his faith not to fail.

Questions.Q: To whom did Jesus say would be given courage?
Questions.A: Jesus said courage would be given to the disciples.
Questions.Alternative: To whom did Jesus say would be given strength?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus want Simon Peter to do?
Questions.A: Jesus wanted Simon Peter to strengthen brothers.

Questions.Q: Then what did Simon Peter tell Jesus?
Questions.A: Peter said, "Lord, I am ready to go with you to prison and to death."
Questions.Alternative: What did Simon Peter tell Jesus next?
How did Simon Peter respond to Jesus?
How did Simon Peter answer Jesus?

Questions.Q: Do you think Simon Peter was telling the truth?
Questions.A: Peter gave an impulsive answer.
Questions.Note: Peter was not intending to lie, but he was not able to judge correctly how he would respond when Jesus was arrested.

Questions.Q: Do you think Simon Peter understood what was about to happen to Jesus? Why?
Questions.A: Peter probably didn't understand what was going to happen to Jesus because if he did he wouldn't have denied Jesus three times.

Questions.Q: Jesus told Simon Peter, "Before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times." But how did Jesus know when the rooster would crow and how many times he would tell lies?
Questions.A: Jesus is God, so he is omniscient.
Questions.Alternative: Jesus told Simon Peter, "Before the rooster crows, three times you will lie about me saying that you don’t know me." But how did Jesus know when the rooster would crow and how many times he would tell lies?
How did Jesus know when the rooster would crow and how many times Simon Peter would deny him?

Questions.Q: According to this, do you think that Jesus knows about what the birds, animals and people will do, and when?
Questions.A: Yes, Jesus knows about the birds, animals and people. He knows the future, past and present.

Section.heading: Luke 22:35-38 Scripture Must Be Fulfilled in Jesus

Questions.Q: What are the incidents written about in this section?
Questions.A: Jesus reminded them about the time when he sent them out to every town and place without a purse, bag or sandals.

Questions.Q: What instructions is Jesus giving his disciples?
Questions.A: Jesus' instructions were to take their purse, bags and sword. (referring to preparedness)

Questions.Q: What do you think Jesus wants his disciples to understand now?
Questions.A: Jesus wanted his disciples not to get worried or anxious (referring to the previous experience they had).
Jesus wanted his disciples to know that important prophecies concerning him were about to be fulfilled.
Jesus wanted his disciples to be ready for some big changes.

Questions.Q: Then what did Jesus ask?
Questions.A: Jesus asked, "When I sent you without purse, bag or sandals, did you lack anything?"
Questions.Alternative: Then what did Jesus ask his disciples?
What did Jesus ask next?
After speaking to Simon Peter, what did Jesus ask his disciples?
After speaking, what did Jesus ask?

Questions.Q: What incident is Jesus asking them to remember?
Questions.A: Jesus is asking them to remember the event of sending them two by two to different towns.
Questions.Alternative: What incident is Jesus asking them about?
Questions.Note: See Luke 9:1-3 and Luke 10:1-4

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say that they should take along with them?
Questions.A: Jesus told them to take a purse/bag and a sword.

Questions.Q: Why do you think Jesus told them to take these things?
Questions.A: Jesus told them to take these things to get prepared for tough situations.

Questions.Q: Did Jesus want them to go out and buy swords right then?
Questions.A: No.

Questions.Q: In speaking of swords, what do you think Jesus meant? Do you think the disciples understood him?
Questions.A: No, the disciples did not understand. Jesus was asking them to be prepared [spiritually].

Questions.Q: Jesus told them that these things would happen in fulfillment of what [prophecy]?
Questions.A: The prophecy was that the Son of Man would be betrayed.
Questions.Alternative: Jesus told them that these things would happen in fulfillment of what prophecy?
Jesus told them that these things would happen in fulfillment of what?
What was about to be fulfilled?
Jesus told them that these things would happen according to which prophecy?
Jesus told them that these things would happen according to which word?

Questions.Q: Who do you think originally said the words: "And he was numbered with the transgressors?"
Questions.A: Isaiah said these words (Isaiah 53:12)
Questions.Note: Unless the translation (or a footnote) makes it clear or the respondent has a good knowledge of the Old Testament, it is unlikely that they would know this was written by Isaiah. However, it should be clear from the text that this is a prophecy and not words being spoken for the first time by Jesus.

Questions.Q: Then what did the disciples tell Jesus?
Questions.A: The disciples said, "See Lord, here are two swords."

Questions.Q: Then what did Jesus say?
Questions.A: Jesus replied "That's enough!"

Questions.Q: What do you think Jesus meant when he said that was enough?
Questions.A: Jesus said "That's enough" because the disciples did not understand his point. He was referring to the spiritual aspect and not the worldly aspect.

Section.heading: Luke 22:39-46 Jesus Prays on the Mount of Olives

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do in this passage?
Questions.A: In this passage, Jesus prays on the Mount of Olives.

Questions.Q: What did the disciples do?
Questions.A: The disciples fell asleep.

Questions.Q: Jesus was facing suffering and sorrow. Do you think that these difficulties, hardships and troubles will come to those who believe in God, or not?
Questions.A: Hardships and troubles will come to those who believe in God.

Questions.Q: Where did Jesus [and the disciples] go [according to his/their custom]?
Questions.A: Jesus and his disciples went to the Mount of Olives.
Questions.Alternative: Where did Jesus go?
Where did Jesus go according to his custom?
Where did Jesus and the disciples go?
Where did Jesus and the disciples go according to their custom?

Questions.Q: After arriving there, what did Jesus tell his disciples?
Questions.A: Jesus told the disciples, "Pray that you will not fall into temptation.

Questions.Q: What temptation do you think Jesus meant?
Questions.A: Jesus had already told the disciples that they would abandon him, so he was probably referring to the temptation to be afraid and fall away.
He might also have meant the temptation to act improperly during his arrest.
He was also perhaps giving general teaching about using prayer to avoid any kind of temptation to sin.

Questions.Q: How far away was Jesus from his disciples when he prayed?
Questions.A: He was about a stone's throw beyond them.

Questions.Q: Why do you think Jesus went away from his to pray?
Questions.A: Jesus went away for privacy. He wanted to be alone.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus pray to his father?
Questions.A: Jesus prayed for the cup of suffering to be taken away from him.

Questions.Q: What Jesus spoke of "this cup," what did he mean?
Questions.A: The cup signified suffering and the death he was going to experience.
Questions.Note: See Matthew 20:22. This question is only needed if the expression is translated literally.

Questions.Q: How did the angel from heaven help Jesus?
Questions.A: The angel from heaven strengthened him.

Questions.Q: [An angel appeared from heaven to give courage to/strengthen Jesus.] Do you think God sends angels in order to give courage to/strengthen those who believe in him while they are suffering?
Questions.A: Yes, God sometimes sends angels to minister to people in need.
Questions.Alternative: Do you think God sends angels in order to give courage to those who believe in him while they are suffering?
Do you think God sends angels in order to strengthen those who believe in him while they are suffering?
An angel appeared from heaven to give courage to Jesus. Do you think God sends angels in order to give courage to those who believe in him while they are suffering?
An angel appeared from heaven to strengthen Jesus. Do you think God sends angels in order to strengthen those who believe in him while they are suffering?
How do you think God helps those who believe in him when they are suffering?

Questions.Q: [God is invisible. So,] do you think [heaven’s] angels can be seen or not?
Questions.A: Heaven's angels are invisible.
Questions.Alternative: God is invisible. So, do you think heaven’s angels can be seen or not?
Do you think angels can be seen or not?
Do you think angels can be seen?
Do you think heavenly angels can be seen or not?
Do you think heaven’s angels can be seen or not?
God is invisible. Do you think angels can be seen?

Questions.Q: What drops were/was falling like blood? // How was Jesus sweating?
Questions.A: Jesus’ sweat was falling like drops of blood.
Questions.Alternative: What drops were falling like blood?
What was falling like blood?
How was Jesus sweating?

Questions.Q: How does Luke show/describe the intensity of Jesus' anguish?
Questions.A: Luke describes Jesus' emotions and says that sweat fell like blood.
Questions.Alternative: How does Luke show the intensity of Jesus' anguish?
How does Luke describe the intensity of Jesus' anguish?
How do we know that Jesus was in great anguish?

Questions.Q: What were his disciples doing at that time? Why?
Questions.A: The disciples fell asleep because they were exhausted from sorrow.

Questions.Q: How did Jesus feel about his disciples sleeping while he was praying in anguish?
Questions.A: Jesus felt upset that his disciples were sleeping while he was praying in anguish.

Questions.Q: What is Luke is telling about in this section?
Questions.A: In this section, Luke is telling about Jesus getting arrested.

Questions.Q: After reading/hearing this passage, how do you understand what Jesus told his disciples about carrying a sword?
Questions.A: Jesus was not talking about a physical sword but rather the mindset to be ready [for spiritual battle].

Questions.Q: Who arrived while Jesus was talking to his disciples?
Questions.A: While Jesus was talking to his disciples, Judas arrived.
Questions.Alternative: While talking like that, who was coming to them?

Questions.Q: How do you think Judas knew where to find Jesus?
Questions.A: The Mount of Olives was his usual place to pray.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus ask Judas?
Questions.A: Jesus asked Judas, "Judas, are you betraying the Son of Man with a kiss?"

Questions.Q: How do you think Jesus felt when he asked Judas this question?
Questions.A: Jesus probably felt hurt and betrayed.

Questions.Q: What did the disciples understand was about to happen?
Questions.A: The disciples understood that Jesus was going to be arrested.

Questions.Q: What did the disciples ask Jesus?
Questions.A: The disciples asked, "Lord, should we strike with our swords?"

Questions.Q: Did the disciples wait for Jesus to answer?
Questions.A: No.

Questions.Q: Why did one of disciples cut off a man's ear?
Questions.A: They were trying to defend Jesus.
Jesus had talked about buying a sword, so they thought he was calling them to engage in a physical fight.
Most likely the disciple intended to cut off the man's head but only managed to cut off his ear.

Questions.Q: Was Jesus in favor of his disciples attacking that man?
Questions.A: Jesus was not in favor of his disciples attacking that man.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do [for that man]?
Questions.A: Jesus touched the man's ear and healed him.
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus do for that man?
What did Jesus do?

Questions.Q: To whom did Jesus ask, "Did you have to come with swords and clubs as if I was an outlaw?"
Questions.A: Jesus asked this to the chief priests, the officers of the temple guard and the elders who had come to arrest him.

Questions.Q: Where did Jesus think/imply they should have arrested him?
Questions.A: Jesus thought they should have arrested him in the temple courts.
Questions.Alternative: Where did Jesus think they should have arrested him?
Where did Jesus imply they should have arrested him?

Questions.Q: To whom and into whose hands did he say God handed over this situation?
Questions.A: He said this in reference to the chief priests and the officers of the temple guard who came to arrest him as Satan was given authority for reigning that hour.

Questions.Q: When Jesus spoke of "darkness," was he speaking of the lack of light because it was night time, or something else?
Questions.A: He was speaking of spiritual darkness.

Questions.Q: Before this incident [happened], Jesus had told Simon Peter about this matter/what would happen. How do you say this thing came true? // Did it happen as Jesus had predicted? Give details.
Questions.A: Yes, Jesus predicted everything that would happen. It came true just as Jesus had predicted.
Questions.Alternative: Before this incident, Jesus had told Simon Peter what would happen. How do you say this thing came true?
Before this incident happened, Jesus had told Simon Peter about this matter. How do you see his prediction coming true?
Before this incident, Jesus had told Simon Peter about this matter. Did it happen as Jesus had predicted? Give details.
Before this incident, Jesus had told Simon Peter about this matter. Did it happen as Jesus had predicted?
Tell how this things happened as Jesus had predicted.
Tell how this things happened as Jesus had predicted to Simon Peter.
Questions.Note: See Luke 22:31-34

Questions.Q: Where did they take Jesus?
Questions.A: They took Jesus to the house of the high priest.

Questions.Q: How did Simon Peter go/follow?
Questions.A: Peter followed at a distance.
Questions.Alternative: How did Simon Peter follow?
How did Simon Peter go?

Questions.Q: Why do you think Simon Peter did not stay with the group of men who were taking Jesus?
Questions.A: He was afraid.

Questions.Q: What were they/the people doing in the courtyard?
Questions.A: The people kindled a fire in the middle of the courtyard and sat together.
Questions.Alternative: What were they doing in the courtyard?
What were the people doing in the courtyard?

Questions.Q: Why did Simon Peter sit down with the others? Were they friends?
Questions.A: They were not friends. He wanted to see Jesus at a distance.
It was probably cold, so Peter wanted to be close to the fire.
Questions.Alternative: What were they doing in the courtyard?
What were the people doing in the courtyard?

Questions.Q: What did three different people say about Simon Peter?
Questions.A: The three different people said that Peter had been with Jesus.

Questions.Q: Who were the people who said that Simon Peter had been with Jesus and his disciples?
Questions.A: The first person was a servant girl seated there in the firelight. The other two people aren't described specifically.

Questions.Q: How did Simon Peter respond to them?
Questions.A: Peter responded to them by denying everything they said.

Questions.Q: What caused these people to conclude that Simon Peter was one of the disciples?
Questions.A: They saw Peter with Jesus.
They recognized that Peter was a Galilean.

Questions.Q: Did these people reach this conclusion together or independently?
Questions.A: These people concluded this independently.

Questions.Q: When did the rooster crow?
Questions.A: As Peter was denying the third accusation, the rooster crowed.

Questions.Q: What happened when the rooster crowed?
Questions.A: When the rooster crowed, Jesus turned and looked straight at Peter.

Questions.Q: What was Simon Peter reminded of?
Questions.A: Simon Peter was reminded of Jesus’ words to him: "Before the rooster crows today, you will disown me three times."

Questions.Q: Then what did Simon Peter do?
Questions.A: Simon Peter went outside and wept bitterly.

Questions.Q: Why did Simon Peter weep?
Questions.A: Simon Peter did not keep his word (standing with Jesus till the end). He felt guilty for denying his best friend to escape pain.

Section.heading: Luke 22:63-65 Jesus is Mocked and Beaten

Questions.Q: What did the guards do while beating Jesus?
Questions.A: The guards began to mock and beat him up.

Questions.Q: What did they ask Jesus?
Questions.A: They blindfolded him and asked, "Prophesy! Who hit you?"

Questions.Q: What were they implying by asking that question?
Questions.A: They did not believe that Jesus had the power to prophesy or know who was hitting him.

Questions.Q: Did Jesus answer their question?
Questions.A: No.

Questions.Q: Do you think Jesus was able to answer?
Questions.A: Yes he was able to answer. He chose not to answer.

Questions.Q: What type of words did they say to Jesus?
Questions.A: They said many insulting things to him.

Questions.Q: What type of assembly/meeting is being described?
Questions.A: This was a [religious] trial held before the council of elders.
Questions.Alternative: What type of assembly is being described?
What type of meeting is being described?

Questions.Q: Who is the Son of Man?
Questions.A: The Son of Man is Jesus.

Questions.Q: What claim did Jesus make about his relationship to God in this section?
Questions.A: Jesus said that He will be seated at the right hand of God.

Questions.Q: What legal charge were these men bringing against Jesus?
Questions.A: The legal charge against Jesus is him claiming that he is the Messiah/Son of God.

Questions.Q: Tell who participated in to this meeting.
Questions.A: The people who participated in this meeting are the council of the elders of the people, chief priests and teachers of the law.

Questions.Q: What did they ask Jesus?
Questions.A: They asked him, "If you are the Messiah, tell us."

Questions.Q: What do you think the term "Messiah" means?
Questions.A: Messiah means deliverer and anointed.
Key Term Check: It is the transliteration of the Hebrew word meaning "anointed one" that was translated into Greek as Christos.
Questions.Note: See "Messiah" in KBT in the "Christ, Messiah" entry.

Questions.Q: What answer did Jesus give to them?
Questions.A: Jesus answered, "If I tell you, you will not believe me, and if I asked you, you would not answer. But from now on, the Son of Man will be seated at the right hand of the mighty God."

Questions.Q: What did these men understand from Jesus' answer?
Questions.A: These men understood that Jesus was claiming to have a special relationship to God [as the Christ/the Son of God].
They also thought that Jesus was blaspheming.

Questions.Q: Was their understanding of Jesus' answer correct? (Did he really say what they thought?)
Questions.A: They were correct in understanding that Jesus was claiming to be the Christ.
They incorrectly believed his words to be blasphemy [because he really was the Christ].

Questions.Q: How did Jesus' answer their second question?
Questions.A: Jesus answered, "You say that I am."

Questions.Q: What did Jesus mean when he said that?
Questions.A: Jesus was affirming that he was the Son of God.

Questions.Q: What did they say about [being] witnesses?
Questions.A: They said they themselves were witnesses because they heard what Jesus said.
Questions.Alternative: What did they say about being witnesses?
What did they say about witnesses?

Questions.Q: What legal conclusion did they reach based on Jesus' words?
Questions.A: They said that Jesus was blaspheming because he claimed to be the Son of God.

Questions.Q: Do you think their conclusion was correct?
Questions.A: No. Their conclusion was incorrect.

Questions.Q: What type of assembly/meeting is being described?
Questions.A: This was a trial/legal hearing [held before Pilate, the Roman governor].
Questions.Alternative: What type of assembly is being described?
What type of meeting is being described?

Questions.Q: In the trial told about in the previous section, the men found Jesus guilty. How is this trial different?
Questions.A: This trial was a secular trial to determine if Jesus had broken any Roman laws.
This trial was different because only a Roman governor could give a punishment/sentence someone to death.

Questions.Q: Why do you think Pilate was not able to find any fault in Jesus?
Questions.A: Pilate couldn't find any fault in Jesus because he couldn't find any basis for a charge.
Jesus had not broken any Roman laws.
Questions.Note: Although Pilate might have accused Jesus of leading an insurrection because he did claim to be the king of the Jews, probably seeing Jesus demeanor and poor estate he did not take the charge or the claim very seriously.
John's gospel reveals that there was more to this conversation, so Pilate might well have understood that Jesus' claim to be the king posed no credible threat to the Roman government.

Questions.Q: Where did they take Jesus after that?
Questions.A: They took Jesus to Pilate.

Questions.Q: Who was Pilate?
Questions.A: Pilate was a Roman governor.
Questions.Note: Unless the translation (or a footnote) makes it clear or the respondent has independent knowledge of the characters in this account, they might have to guess. If guesses reveal an inaccurate understanding, it might be worth considering how to improve clarity.

Questions.Q: What accusations did they bring against Jesus?
Questions.A: They claimed Jesus was undermining the government by opposing payment of taxes to Caesar.
They said Jesus claimed to be the Messiah, a king [implying that he was opposing Caesar's throne].

Questions.Q: Why do you think their accusations would be of concern to Pilate?
Questions.A: It would be a threat to the Roman Empire [if Jesus really were trying to establish a kingdom to seize power from the Roman government].

Questions.Q: What did Pilate ask Jesus?
Questions.A: Pilate asked Jesus "Are you the king of the Jews?"

Questions.Q: How did Jesus respond?
Questions.A: Jesus replied "You have said so."

Questions.Q: What did Jesus mean when he said that?
Questions.A: When Jesus said that, he implied/affirmed that he is the king of the Jews.

Questions.Q: What did Pilate understand from Jesus' answer?
Questions.A: Pilate understood that Jesus was agreeing that he was indeed the king of the Jews.
Questions.Note: The text here does not necessarily make this clear, nor does it offer any explanation about how Pilate interpreted this claim, but since Pilate goes on to say that Jesus was innocent, he apparently did not interpret that claim as an act of treason or insurrection.

Questions.Q: What legal conclusion did Pilate reach?
Questions.A: Pilate's conclusion was that Jesus was innocent.

Questions.Q: What did those people continue to say about Jesus?
Questions.A: The people said that Jesus was stirring up people all over Judea by his teaching.

Questions.Q: Where did they say Jesus began teaching?
Questions.A: They said that Jesus began teaching in Galilee.

Questions.Q: Where do you think Galilee was?
Questions.A: Galilee is in the north of Israel.
Questions.Note: Galilee is about 126 km from Jerusalem.
Questions.Alternative: Do you think Galilee was close to where they were now?
Do you think Galilee was close to Jerusalem?
Do you think Galilee was close to where Pilate was?

Questions.Q: What type of assembly/meeting is being described?
Questions.A: This was a trial/legal hearing [held before Herod].
Questions.Alternative: What type of assembly is being described?
What type of meeting is being described?

Questions.Q: How was Herod’s interaction with Jesus different form Pilate's?
Questions.A: At first, Herod was pleased to see Jesus but when Jesus did not answer his questions, he started to mock Jesus with the other teachers of law and soldiers. Pilate was more considerate to Jesus. He found no basis for a charge and he did not mock Jesus.

Questions.Q: If any of the world’s authorities question Jesus, do you think he needs to answer them?
Questions.A: Jesus is a very powerful king, so he is not obligated to answer anyone's questions.
Questions.Alternative: If any of the world’s authorities question Jesus, do you think he needs to answer them or not?
If any of the world’s authorities question God’s son, Jesus, do you think he needs to answer them or not?

Questions.Q: [Raising the dead, calming the storm, healing all sicknesses, dying and coming back to life — we call these kinds of things miracles.] Who do you think is able to do these kinds of miracles?
Questions.A: Jesus [because he is God] is able to do these kinds of miracles.
God can also empower Jesus' followers to perform miracles.
Questions.Alternative: Raising the dead, calming the storm, healing all sicknesses, dying and coming back to life — we call these kinds of things miracles. Who do you think is able to do these kinds of miracles?
Raising the dead, calming a storm, healing sicknesses, and coming back to life after dying are examples of miracles. Who do you think is able to do these kinds of miracles?
Miracles are things like raising the dead, calming a storm, healing sicknesses, and dying and coming back to life. Who do you think is able to do these kinds of miracles?
Who do you think is able to perform miracles?

Questions.Q: Where was Jesus from [while he lived on the earth]?
Questions.A: Jesus was from Galilee.
Questions.Note: Respondents familiar with the gospel might note that Jesus was actually born in Bethlehem, but this passage refers to his having started in Galilee, which is where he grew up.
Questions.Alternative: Where was Jesus from?
Where was Jesus from while he lived on the earth?
Where was Jesus from during his earthly life?
What region of Israel was Jesus from?
What was Jesus home region?

Questions.Q: Why did Pilate send Jesus to Herod?
Questions.A: Pilate sent Jesus to Herod because Jesus was under Herod’s jurisdiction.
Questions.Note: An astute respondent might also point out that this was easy to do since Herod was in Jerusalem (rather than up in Galilee).

Questions.Q: How did Herod feel when he first saw Jesus?
Questions.A: When Herod saw Jesus, he was greatly pleased.

Questions.Q: Why did Herod want to see Jesus?
Questions.A: Herod wanted to see Jesus because he hoped that Jesus would perform a miracle.

Questions.Q: How did Jesus respond to Herod's questions?
Questions.A: Jesus gave no answer to Herod’s questions.

Questions.Q: Why do you think Jesus did not answer Herod?
Questions.A: Perhaps if Jesus answered Herod, he might have been set free, but because he came to earth to be a sacrifice for us, his purpose would have defeated if he said anything to Herod.
Jesus knew Herod's motives and he did not want to give Herod the satisfaction of a reply.
It had been prophesied that Jesus would be silent before his accusers, so this fulfilled that prophecy.

Questions.Q: What kinds of things do you think the chief priests and teachers of the law were saying?
Questions.A: The chief priests and teachers of the law were probably accusing and mocking Jesus.

Questions.Q: How were Herod’s soldiers treating Jesus?
Questions.A: Herod’s soldiers ridiculed and mocked Jesus.

Questions.Q: Why did Herod and the soldiers dress Jesus in an elegant robe?
Questions.A: They dressed Jesus in an elegant/royal robe as a way of mocking Jesus.

Questions.Q: How do you think Herod felt after seeing Jesus?
Questions.A: Herod would probably have been angry after seeing Jesus because Jesus wasn't answering any of his questions.
He would have been disappointed because he expected Jesus to perform a sign, but Jesus did not do that.
Questions.Alternative: How did Herod feel after seeing Jesus?

Questions.Q: How did Herod and Pilate become friends?
Questions.A: Herod and Pilate became friends through the trials of Jesus.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what happened in this section.
Questions.A: In this section, Pilate and Herod found Jesus innocent. However the crowd wanted Jesus to be crucified instead of Barabbas (a man thrown into prison for insurrection in the city and for murder). Pilate appealed to them but they kept shouting and Pilate gave up. He released Barabbas and ordered Jesus to be crucified.

Questions.Q: If any of these events surprised you, explain why.
Questions.A: The surprising event in this section is the crowd wanting Jesus dead. A few days before this event, the crowd called Jesus the king of kings and welcomed him with palm leaves. A few days later, they wanted him dead.

Questions.Q: Why were people shouting that Jesus should be crucified after all the good things he had done to help people? // [All the people continued to scream out that Jesus should be crucified on the cross.] Why were those people — [some of] whom he/Jesus may have healed, raised from the dead, and fed when they were hungry — now screaming/shouting that Jesus should be crucified?
Questions.A: A few people did not follow Jesus with a whole heart. When Jesus performed miracles, they were happy but then they did not believe that he was the Son of God.
Questions.Alternative: Why were people shouting that Jesus should be crucified after all the good things he had done to help people?
Why were the people — some of whom Jesus may have healed, raised from the dead, and fed when they were hungry — now shouting that Jesus should be crucified?
Why were the people — many of whom Jesus had healed, raised from the dead, and fed when they were hungry — now screaming that Jesus should be crucified?

All the people continued to scream out that Jesus should be crucified on the cross. Why were those people — whom he had healed, raised from the dead, and fed when they were hungry — now screaming that Jesus should be crucified?
Why were these people shouting that Jesus should be crucified?

Questions.Q: Why do you think Pilate wanted to release Jesus [and not Barabbas]?
Questions.A: Pilate wanted to release Jesus and not Barabbas because he found no evidence for their charges against him. Barabbas was a bad person who was thrown into prison for insurrection in the city and for murder.
Questions.Alternative: Why do you think Pilate wanted to release Jesus and not Barabbas?
Why do you think Pilate wanted to release Jesus?

Questions.Q: Who did Pilate call [together]?
Questions.A: Pilate called the chief priests, the rulers and the people.
Questions.Alternative: Who did Pilate call together?
Who did Pilate call?

Questions.Q: Why did Pilate gather the chief priests, the rulers and the people?
Questions.A: Pilate wanted to gather the chief priests, the rulers and the people to tell them that Jesus was innocent and that he had done nothing to deserve death.

Questions.Q: What did Pilate say to them?
Questions.A: Pilate told them that Jesus had done nothing wrong and there was no basis for their charges against him.

Questions.Q: What was the legal verdict that Pilate and Herod agreed on?
Questions.A: The legal verdict that Pilate and Herod agreed on was that Jesus was innocent.

Questions.Q: Why was Pilate going to punish Jesus [if he had not found him guilty]?
Questions.A: Pilate was going to punish Jesus because the crowd wanted Jesus dead.
Most likely this was Pilate's attempt to appease the accusers.
Questions.Alternative: Why was Pilate going to punish Jesus if he had not found him guilty?
Why was Pilate going to punish Jesus?
Why was Pilate going to punish Jesus since he had not found him guilty?
Since Pilate had not found Jesus guilty, why do you think he was going to punish him?
Questions.Note: Respondent might rely on personal or cultural biases about government corruption or the tendency of people in power to be cruel to explain this. Or they might try to relate an understanding about the Roman government and its attitude toward the Jews. Nothing in the text should lead a respondent to conclude that Pilate had found Jesus guilty of something (i.e., a lesser crime) that was worthy of punishment but not death.

Questions.Q: What were [the] people shouting?
Questions.A: The people shouted "Away with this man! Release Barabbas to us" and "Crucify him!"
Questions.Alternative: What were the people shouting?
What were people screaming?

Questions.Q: [The people were asking for a criminal/Barabbas to be released.] What was the [Jewish/Roman] custom that was being followed [at that time]?
Questions.A: The Jewish/Roman custom at that time was that a criminal would be released during a festival.
Questions.Alternative: Do you know what custom was being followed that caused them to argue about which prisoner to release?
Why were the people arguing with Pilate about which prisoner to release?
What was the custom that was being followed?
What was the Jewish custom that was being followed at that time?
What was the Roman custom that was being followed?
The people were asking for a criminal to be released. What was the custom that was being followed?
The people were asking for Barabbas to be released. What was the custom that was being followed?
The people were asking for Barabbas, who was a criminal, to be released. What was the custom that was being followed?

Questions.Q: What crimes had Barabbas committed?
Questions.A: Barabbas committed murder and insurrection in the city.

Questions.Q: Who won in the end?
Questions.A: The religious leaders [and the people calling for Jesus to be crucified]
Barabbas also won his freedom.

Questions.Q: Why did Pilate grant their demand?
Questions.A: Pilate granted their demand because he experienced lots of pressure from the crowd and wanted to please them.
Pilate was afraid of a riot.

Questions.Q: Who did Pilate set free, and who did he hand over to be killed/crucified?
Questions.A: Pilate set free Barabbas and handed Jesus to be killed/crucified.
Questions.Alternative: Who did Pilate set free, and who did he hand over to be crucified?
Who did Pilate set free, and who did he hand over to be killed?

Questions.Q: Where were the soldiers taking Jesus?
Questions.A: The soldiers took Jesus [out of the city] to the place where he was to be crucified.
Questions.Note: A respondent who is familiar with the gospel might also mention that he was going to Calvary to the placed called the Skull

Questions.Q: Explain what you think Jesus words in this section mean.
Questions.A: Jesus’ words in this section mean not to cry for him but for our children and ourselves so that we won't perish.

Questions.Q: While the soldiers were leading Jesus, who was coming into the city?
Questions.A: Simon of Cyrene was coming into the city.
Questions.Alternative: While the soldiers were leading Jesus, who was coming toward the city?

Questions.Q: Where was [this man named] Simon from?
Questions.A: Simon was [originally] from Cyrene.
Simon was coming in from the country.
Questions.Alternative: Where was this man named Simon from?
Where was Simon from?
From what place was Simon?

Questions.Q: Do you think Simon knew Jesus?
Questions.A: No, Simon probably did not know Jesus.
Questions.Note: Since he has the same name as Simon Peter, be sure that the respondent understands that this is not the same person.

Questions.Q: Why did they/the soldiers make Simon follow him/Jesus?
Questions.A: The soldiers made Simon follow Jesus with the cross because it probably would have been hard for Jesus to carry the cross by himself.
Questions.Alternative: Why did they make Simon follow Jesus, carrying the cross for him?
Why did the soldiers make Simon follow Jesus, carrying the cross for him?
Why did they make Simon follow him, carrying the cross for him?
Why did the soldiers make Simon follow him, carrying the cross for him?
Why did they make Simon carry the cross for Jesus?
Why did the soldiers make Simon carry the cross for Jesus?
Why did they make Simon carry the cross for him?
Why did the soldiers make Simon carry the cross for him?
Why did they make Simon follow Jesus?
Why did the soldiers make Simon follow Jesus?
Why did they make Simon follow him?
Why did the soldiers make Simon follow him?

Questions.Q: Who else followed Jesus?
Questions.A: A large number of people followed him, including women [who were mourning].

Questions.Q: What did the women do while following Jesus?
Questions.A: The women mourned and wailed while following Jesus.
Questions.Alternative: What did those ladies do while following Jesus?
What were the women doing?
Why were the women following Jesus?
Why were some of those women following Jesus?

Questions.Q: Why did Jesus tell those women not to cry for him?
Questions.A: Jesus told those women not to cry for him because he is going to come back to life.
Jesus implied that the injustice being done to him was not as bad as the judgment that would come on the people later [if they did not trust him for salvation].
Questions.Note: The exact reason may be difficult to determine from the text, but ensure that the translation is not implying any ideas that as incorrect.
Questions.Alternative: Why did Jesus say that the women should not cry for him?
Why did Jesus say to the women of Jerusalem that they should not cry for him?
Why did Jesus say to the ladies of Jerusalem that they should not cry for him?
Why did Jesus say to the daughters of Jerusalem that they should not cry for him?
Why did Jesus tell the women who were following him not to cry for him?
Why did Jesus tell them not to cry for him?

Questions.Q: For whom did Jesus say those women should cry [instead]?
Questions.A: Jesus told them to cry for themselves and their children.
Questions.Alternative: For whom did Jesus say those women should cry?
For whom did Jesus say those women should cry instead?
For whom did Jesus say those ladies should cry?

Questions.Q: Which days/time did Jesus say are/is coming?
Questions.A: Jesus said the time will come when women will say "Blessed are the childless women, the wombs that never bore and the breasts that never nursed!" Then they will say to the mountains, "Fall on us!" and to the hills, "Cover us!"
Jesus said a time of dryness [or death] was coming.
Jesus predicted a time of judgment or tribulation, when people would wish to be dead or hidden [from God].
Questions.Alternative: Which time did Jesus say is coming?
Which days did Jesus say are coming?

Questions.Q: Do you think Jesus was speaking of events that are still in the future, or of something that has already happened?
Questions.A: Jesus was probably speaking [primarily] of the literal destruction of Jerusalem.
Jesus words also could apply to future tribulation and judgment.
Questions.Note: Most commentators agree that Jesus' word foretold the Roman siege of Jerusalem, which happened about 40 years later in A.D. 70.

Questions.Q: What is the meaning of the tree being green or dry?
Questions.A: The green tree is a representation of Jesus, and the dry tree is the [evil] people. If Jesus is being crucified, despite being found innocent, the people should expect even greater persecution.
OR The green tree represents of the time when Jesus was alive, speaking words of life to the people. Later, when Jesus was gone, people would behave even worse [and suffer for their evil actions].

Questions.Q: What was the main event that happened in this section?
Questions.A: The main event in this section is Jesus' crucifixion.
OR The main event in this section is Jesus asking God to forgive the people.

Questions.Q: Why do you think it is difficult for an ordinary person to ask God to forgive people who are beating him or taking his life?
Questions.A: It is difficult because people want to live. Most people would prefer life over death. People would probably do anything to escape death and it's hard to forgive someone who takes away a life.
Questions.Alternative: Jesus said, "Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing." Why do you think it is difficult for an ordinary person to pray like that when people are beating him or taking his life?
Do you think it would be difficult for you to ask God to forgive people who are beating you or taking your life? Why?

Questions.Q: How was Jesus executed?
Questions.A: Jesus was executed by being crucified.

Questions.Q: Who [else] did the soldiers execute/crucify/bring along with Jesus?
Questions.A: Two criminals were also led along with Jesus to be executed/crucified.
Questions.Alternative: Who else did the soldiers crucify along with Jesus?
Who else did the soldiers execute along with Jesus?
Who else did the soldiers bring along with Jesus?
Who did the soldiers bring along with Jesus?

Questions.Q: Where was Jesus executed?
Questions.A: Jesus was executed in a place called the Skull.
Questions.Alternative: What was the name of the place where Jesus was executed?
What was the place called where Jesus was executed?
At which place was Jesus executed?
Where was Jesus killed?
Where was Jesus crucified?

Questions.Q: On what were Jesus and the other men hung/nailed?
Questions.A: Jesus and the other men hung on crosses/poles [made of wood].
Questions.Note: See Luke 23:26.

Although centuries of Christian tradition suppose that the "cross" was formed with a horizontal beam attached to a vertical pole, neither the Greek word nor historical or archaeological evidence confirm that there was a horizontal piece. Translations may or may not imply this.
Questions.Alternative: On what were Jesus and the other men hung?
On what were Jesus and the other men nailed?

Questions.Q: Where was Jesus crucified, relative to the two criminals?
Questions.A: Jesus was crucified in the middle. One criminal on his right, the other on his left.
Questions.Alternative: Where was Jesus' cross located?
Where was Jesus' cross positioned?

Questions.Q: Who do you think Jesus’ father is?
Questions.A: Jesus’ father is God.
Questions.Alternative: Who is Jesus’ father?
When Jesus prayed to his Father, who was he talking to?

Questions.Q: What did the soldiers do after crucifying Jesus?
Questions.A: The soldiers divided up his clothes.

Questions.Q: How did the soldiers decide who would get the various articles of Jesus' clothing?
Questions.A: The soldiers cast lots/gambled.
Questions.Note: Cultures have different ways of "fairly" distributing limited items up among numerous persons. Although "casting lots" was sometimes used by believers who understood God to be in control of everything, the translation here should not imply that the soldiers here attached any religious significance to their game.

Section.heading: Luke 23:35-43 Jesus is Mocked on the Cross

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what happened in this section.
Questions.A: In this section, the rulers, the people, the soldiers and even one of the criminals mocked Jesus on the cross. The other criminal rebuked the criminal and believed Jesus. Jesus told him that he would be in paradise.

Questions.Q: Since Jesus raised the dead to life, do you think he had the power to save his own life?
Questions.A: Yes, Jesus had the power to save his own life.

Questions.Q: Why do you think Jesus did not try to come off the cross and save his life [to prove that he had the power/he was the Messiah]?
Questions.A: Jesus did not try to come off the cross (to save his life) because his purpose wouldn't have been completed. He also needed to fulfill the scriptures.
Questions.Alternative: Why do you think Jesus did not try to come off the cross and save his life?
Why do you think Jesus did not try to come off the cross and save his life to prove that he had the power?
Why do you think Jesus did not try to come off the cross and save his life to prove that he was the Messiah]?
Why do you think Jesus did not come off the cross and save his life?
Why do you think Jesus did not come off the cross and save his life to prove that he had the power?
Why do you think Jesus did not come off the cross and save his life to prove that he was the Messiah]?

Questions.Q: What were the people doing?
Questions.A: The people stood watching, and the rulers sneered and mocked him.

Questions.Q: By saying what kinds of things did the authorities mock Jesus?
Questions.A: The authorities told Jesus to save himself if he really is God's Messiah.

Questions.Q: Which people there did not believe that Jesus was the Messiah or a true king?
Questions.A: The soldiers, rulers and one of the criminals who hung there did not believe that Jesus was the Messiah.

Questions.Q: Why do you think the soldiers offered Jesus wine vinegar?
Questions.A: The soldiers offered Jesus wine vinegar because Jesus was probably thirsty but they were mocking him.

Questions.Q: What do you think was the meaning of the sign which was [nailed] [on the cross] above Jesus’ head?
Questions.A: The sign above Jesus' head was intended as a form of mockery. It read: "This is the king of the Jews". It's true, but many people did not believe it.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think was the meaning of the sign which was above Jesus?
What do you think was the meaning of the sign which was above Jesus’ head?
What do you think was the meaning of the sign which was on the cross above Jesus’ head?
What do you think was the meaning of the sign which was nailed on the cross above Jesus’ head?
What do you think was the meaning of the sign which was nailed above Jesus’ head?

Questions.Q: Do you think the person who made that sign believed that Jesus was a true king?
Questions.A: No.

Questions.Q: What did one of the criminals/crucified men say [to mock Jesus]?
Questions.A: He said, "Aren't you the Messiah? Save yourself and us!"
Questions.Alternative: What did one of the crucified men say?
What did one of the criminals say?
What did the first criminal say?
What did one of the crucified men say to mock Jesus?
What did one of the criminals say to mock Jesus?
What did the first criminal say to mock Jesus?

Questions.Q: Did that [first] criminal think that Jesus could save them?
Questions.A: No he did not think that Jesus could save them.
Questions.Alternative: Did that criminal think that Jesus could save them?
Did that first criminal think that Jesus could save them?

Questions.Q: Tell about the differences you see between the two criminals.
Questions.A: The first criminal (insulting Jesus) had no respect, faith or humility. However the second criminal rebuked him and accepted responsibility for the crimes that he had done. He feared God and believed that Jesus is the Messiah.

Questions.Q: How did the second criminal show that he believed that Jesus was the Messiah? // What did the second one/criminal say to the first one/criminal [while scolding him]?
Questions.A: He said, "Don't you fear God since you are under the same sentence?"
Questions.Alternative: How did the second criminal show that he believed that Jesus was the Messiah?
What did the second one say to the first one?
What did the second criminal say to the first criminal?
What did the second one say to the first one while scolding him?
What did the second criminal say to the first criminal to scold him?
How did the second criminal scold the first criminal?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell him/the second criminal?
Questions.A: Jesus said, "Truly I tell you, today you will be with me in paradise."
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus tell him?
What did Jesus tell the second criminal?
How did Jesus respond to the second criminal?

Questions.Q: What do you think happened to the second criminal [after he died]?
Questions.A: After the second criminal died, he went to paradise/heaven.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think happened to the second criminal after he died?
What do you think happened to the second criminal?

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what happened in this section.
Questions.A: In this section, the sun stopped shining and darkness came over the land. The temple curtain tore in two and the Jesus committed his spirit and died. Many people witnessed this and were in anguish. A centurion believed that Jesus was a righteous man.

Questions.Q: Who has authority over the earth, sky, sun and stars?
Questions.A: God has authority over the earth, sky, sun and stars.

Questions.Q: What were the different reactions people had to Jesus' death?
Questions.A: A centurion praised God and said that Jesus is a righteous man. The witnesses beat their breasts and went away. The women who had followed him watched from a distance.

Questions.Q: What unusual or miraculous things happened that afternoon as Jesus was being crucified?
Questions.A: When Jesus was being crucified, at noon, darkness came over the whole land and the sun stopped shining.

Questions.Q: How do you think it happened that from midday until three in the afternoon the sun stopped shining and the whole land was dark?
