Questions.A: God stopped the sun from shining.

Questions.Q: How was the curtain/veil of the temple torn?
Questions.A: God tore the curtain/veil of the temple.
Questions.Alternative: How was the curtain of the temple torn?
How was the veil of the temple torn?
At that time, what happened in the temple?

Questions.Q: What was the meaning of the words Jesus shouted just as he was dying?
Questions.A: Jesus' words meant that he was dying and surrendering his spirit into God’s hands.

Questions.Q: What do you think happens to our spirit after our bodily life is over?
Questions.A: I think the spirit goes to God after our bodily life is over.
Questions.Alternative: Having shouted, "Father I entrust my spirit into your hands", he gave up his life. What do you say about where and why our spirit must go after our bodily life is over?
Having shouted, "Father I entrust my spirit into your hands", he gave up his life. What do you say about where and why our life must go after our bodily life is over?
What do you think happens after our bodily life is over?

Questions.Q: When did Jesus give up his spirit?
Questions.A: Jesus gave up his spirit when the curtain of the temple tore in two.
This happened in the afternoon, sometime between noon and 3:00.
Questions.Alternative: When did Jesus release his life?

Questions.Q: Having seen this, what did the centurion/commander accept/declare?
Questions.A: The centurion declared that Jesus was a righteous man.
Questions.Alternative: Having seen this, what did the centurion accept?
Having seen this, what did the commander accept?
Having seen this, what did the centurion declare?
Having seen this, what did the commander declare?

Questions.Q: What do you think made the centurion/commander reach this conclusion?
Questions.A: I think the sun stopping and darkness covering the land made the centurion reach his conclusion.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think made the centurion reach this conclusion?
What do you think made the commander reach this conclusion?

Questions.Q: What were those people [who had come there to see the incident/crucifixion] doing as they went back?
Questions.A: As they went back, they beat their breasts [as a sign of lament or sorrow].
Questions.Alternative: What were those people who had come there to see the incident doing as they went back?
What were those people who had come there to see the crucifixion doing as they went back?
What were the people doing as they went away?
What were the people who had witnessed this doing as they went away?

Questions.Q: How do you think those people felt?
Questions.A: Those people probably felt really angry and upset.

Questions.Q: Who else was standing at a distance and watching?
Questions.A: The women were at a distance watching.

Questions.Q: Why do you think Luke mentions that some of Jesus' followers were watching these events?
Questions.A: Luke wanted to give an account with very specific details that could only come from eye witnesses.
Luke wanted his readers to believe that his account was true and authoritative.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what happened in this section.
Questions.A: This section is about Joseph (from the Judean town of Arimathea) burying Jesus’ body in a tomb. This section also mentions the women from Galilee preparing spices for his body.

Questions.Q: If someone in your community dies, where do you take the corpse and what do you do with it?
Who was this man named Joseph?
Questions.A: Joseph was a member of the Council. He was a good and upright man.
Questions.Note: Ensure that respondent understands that this is not Jesus' earthly father.

Questions.Q: Why might it be surprising that Joseph offered to take Jesus' body [to prepare it] [for burial]?
Questions.A: He was a member of the Council that had condemned Jesus to death.
Questions.Alternative: Why might it be surprising that Joseph offered to take Jesus' body to prepare it for burial?
Why might it be surprising that Joseph offered to take Jesus' body for burial?
Why might it be surprising that Joseph offered to take Jesus' body?
Why might it be surprising that Joseph wanted to take Jesus' body to prepare it for burial?

Questions.Q: What does Luke tell us about Joseph to help us understand why Joseph wanted to do this?
Questions.A: Luke tells us that Joseph was a good man who had not agreed to the decision to have Jesus crucified.

Questions.Q: Where was Joseph from?
Questions.A: Joseph was from the Judean town of Arimathea.

Questions.Q: What did he ask Pilate for? // Having gone to Pilate, what did he ask for?
Questions.A: He asked Pilate for Jesus’ body.
Questions.Alternative: What did he ask Pilate for?
Having gone to Pilate, what did he ask for?
What did he want Pilate to allow him to do?

Questions.Q: What did he/Joseph [of Arimathea] do after getting Jesus body down from the cross?
Questions.A: After getting Jesus’ body down from the cross, he wrapped it in linen cloth and placed it in a tomb.
Questions.Alternative: What did he do after getting Jesus body down from the cross?
What did Joseph do after getting Jesus body down from the cross?
What did Joseph of Arimathea do after getting Jesus body down from the cross?

Questions.Q: Describe the place where he put Jesus' body/corpse.
Questions.A: The place where he put Jesus’ body was in a tomb cut in a rock, one in which no one had yet been laid.
Questions.Alternative: Describe the place where he put Jesus' body.
Describe the place where he put Jesus' corpse.

Questions.Q: What is the difference between a tomb carved from rock, and a grave dug in the ground?
Questions.A: One is in the ground and the other above the ground (in a rock)

Questions.Q: Why did Joseph need to hurry to finish that work?
Questions.A: Joseph needed to hurry to finish that work because the Sabbath was about to begin.

Questions.Q: Who else saw that he had put the body/corpse inside the [carved rock] tomb?
Questions.A: The women who had come with Jesus from Galilee followed Joseph and saw that he put the body/corpse in the tomb.
Questions.Alternative: Who else saw that he had put the body inside the tomb?
Who else saw that he had put the corpse inside the tomb?
Who else saw that he had put the body inside the carved rock tomb?
Who else saw that he had put the corpse inside the carved rock tomb?

Questions.Q: What did those women do after they went home?
Questions.A: After they went home, they prepared spices and perfumes.
Questions.Alternative: What did those ladies do after they went home?

Questions.Q: What do you think they planned to do with these things/spices and perfumes?
Questions.A: The spices and perfumes were to preserve the body and help cover up bad smells as the body decomposed.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think they planned to do with these things?
What do you think they planned to do with these spices and perfumes?

Questions.Q: What do you think the Sabbath means? (Why did they need to rest?)
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The Sabbath is the name of the seventh and last day of the week. It was set aside by the Jews as a strict day of rest from the normal work that was done on the six other days of the week. The Jews continue to observe the Sabbath on Saturday.
Questions.Note: See "Sabbath" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What was the surprise that the women witnessed?
Questions.A: Jesus was no longer in the tomb. He had risen from the dead.

Questions.Q: What change did these women have as a result of this experience?
Questions.A: The women remembered what Jesus had said about coming back to life, and they believed.
The women thought that they lost their teacher but they were hopeful and happy after this experience.

Questions.Q: Since only God has authority over life to be able to raise a dead person back to life, who do you think Jesus is? // Seeing Jesus power to come back to life, what does this tell us about who he is?
Questions.A: Jesus is powerful, all knowing and he is the Messiah. He has so much power that he can raise a dead person back to life.
Questions.Alternative: Seeing Jesus power to come back to life, what does this tell us about who he is?
Since only God has authority over life to be able to raise a dead person back to life, who do you think Jesus is?

Questions.Q: Now what day was it?
Questions.A: It was a Sunday [the first day of the week].

Questions.Q: Where did those women go that morning?
Questions.A: That morning, the women went to the tomb.
Questions.Alternative: Where did those ladies go on the Sunday morning?

Questions.Q: What do you think they were planning to do?
Questions.A: They were planning to apply the perfumes/spices to Jesus’ body.

Questions.Q: What was the first thing they noticed when they approached the tomb?
Questions.A: The first thing they noticed was that the stone was rolled away.

Questions.Q: What do you think they thought when they saw that?
Questions.A: They probably thought that someone stole Jesus’ body.

Questions.Q: Why were they unable to do what they had planned?
Questions.A: They were unable to do what they had planned because they did not have the body/corpse.

Questions.Q: Who appeared to those women?
Questions.A: Two men/angels appeared to those women.
Questions.Alternative: What appeared to those ladies?

Questions.Q: What did those men appear like? // How was their appearance?
Questions.A: The clothes of the men gleamed like lightning.
Questions.Alternative: What did those men appear like?
How was their appearance?

Questions.Q: Why did the women bow down [with their faces to the ground]?
Questions.A: The women bowed down because they were frightened.
Questions.Alternative: Why did the women bow down with their faces to the ground?
Why did the women bow down?

Questions.Q: Why do you think the women were afraid?
Questions.A: The women were probably afraid because they did not see the body and then suddenly two men appeared beside them.
The two men had clothes that gleamed like lightning, so the women probably knew they were angels.

Questions.Q: Why did the men/angels ask the women why they were looking for Jesus [the living] in the tomb [among the dead]?
Questions.A: The angels asked because the women were supposed to know that Jesus was alive since he told them that on the third day he would rise.
Questions.Alternative: Why did the men ask the women why they were looking for Jesus in the tomb?
Why did the men ask the women why they were looking for the living among the dead?
Why did the men ask the women why they were looking for Jesus among the dead?
Why did the angels ask the women why they were looking for Jesus in the tomb?
Why did the angels ask the women why they were looking for the living among the dead?
Why did the angels ask the women why they were looking for Jesus among the dead?
Questions.Note: This is a rhetorical question. If the target language does not use rhetorical questions, or this is not phrased as a question in this passage, exclude this question.

Questions.Q: What did those men/angels tell the women?
Questions.A: The men/angels told the women that Jesus has risen! They reminded the women about Jesus’ words: "The Son of Man must be delivered over to the hands of sinners, be crucified and on the third day be raised again."
Questions.Alternative: What did those men tell the women?
What did those angels tell the women?
What did those men tell the ladies?

Questions.Q: What had the women forgotten?
Questions.A: The women forgot Jesus’ words [predicting his resurrection] when they were in Galilee.

Questions.Q: Where did the women go when they left the tomb? // Who did the women go to see after they left the tomb?
Questions.A: The women went to the Eleven and to all the other followers of Jesus.
Questions.Alternative: Where did the women go when they left the tomb?
Who did the women go to see after they left the tomb?

Questions.Q: What were the names of those women?
Questions.A: The names of the women were Mary Magdalene, Joanna and Mary the mother of James.
Questions.Alternative: What were the names of those ladies?

Questions.Q: What did the disciples think when they heard the women's report?
Questions.A: The disciples did not believe the women after hearing the women's report.
Questions.Alternative: What did the disciples think about those ladies?

Questions.Q: Why did the disciples not believe the women?
Questions.A: The disciples did not believe the women because their words seemed like nonsense.

Questions.Q: What did Peter go and do?
Questions.A: Peter ran to the tomb. He saw the strips of linen lying by themselves and he went away wondering what happened.

Questions.Q: Why do you think Peter came home surprised?
Questions.A: I think Peter found it hard to believe that Jesus was alive.

Questions.Q: After Peter saw inside the tomb, do you think he believed the women?
Questions.A: Peter apparently believed the women's report about Jesus body being gone, but he still had doubts or questions about what had happened.

Questions.Q: At this point, who believed that Jesus was alive, and who still doubted or had questions about what had happened?
Questions.A: At this point, the women believed that Jesus was alive. The others (including Peter) had questions or doubted.

Questions.Q: Who were going to [the village called] Emmaus?
Questions.A: Two men were going to Emmaus.
Questions.Alternative: Who were going to the village called Emmaus?
Who were going to Emmaus?
Who all were going to the village called Emmaus?

Questions.Q: How long do you think it took to reach Emmaus?
Questions.A: It was seven miles from Jerusalem to Emmaus, so it was probably normally a journey of two hours or more on foot.
Questions.Alternative: Do you think the trip to Emmaus took a long time?
How far was it for the men to go to Emmaus?
Was it very far to Emmaus?

Questions.Q: What were they talking about while they were walking?
Questions.A: They were talking about the things that happened with Jesus’ death.
Questions.Alternative: What were they talking about?
What were they talking about on the way?
What were these men talking about while they were walking?
What were they discussing while they were walking?
What were they discussing about while they were walking?

Questions.Q: Who came up and started walking with them?
Questions.A: Jesus came up and started walking with them.
Questions.Alternative: Who joined those two disciples?
Who came up and joined those two disciples?
Who joined those two disciples as the walked?
Who was walking along with those two disciples?

Questions.Q: Do you think these two men knew what Jesus looked like?
Questions.A: Yes, these two men had been followers of Jesus, so they knew what he looked like.

Questions.Q: What was unusual about this meeting with Jesus?
Questions.A: The unusual thing about this meeting with Jesus is that they did not recognize him.

Questions.Q: Why do you think they couldn't recognize Jesus now?
Questions.A: Jesus kept them from recognizing him on purpose.
OR Because they were sad and didn't think Jesus could be alive, their confusion prevented them from recognizing him.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus ask them?
Questions.A: Jesus asked them what they were discussing.

Questions.Q: Do you think Jesus already knew the answer to his own question?
Questions.A: Yes, Jesus knew the answer to his own question.

Questions.Q: Why do you think Jesus asked this question?
Questions.A: Jesus wanted to join in the discussion, and it would seem strange to them if he appeared to know already what they were talking about.

Questions.Q: How were these two disciples feeling?
Questions.A: The two disciples felt upset. Their faces were downcast.

Questions.Q: How did the disciples respond to Jesus question?
Questions.A: One of the disciples, Cleopas responded to Jesus’ question. He asked, "Are you the only one visiting Jerusalem who does not know the things that have happened there in these days?"

Questions.Q: How widely was the news of Jesus death known?
Questions.A: The news of Jesus’ death was widely known. The men thought everyone in Jerusalem knew about it.

Questions.Q: Did Jesus understand what Cleopas was asking about?
Questions.A: Yes, Jesus understood what Cleopas was asking about [but he pretended not to know].

Questions.Q: What did they say about how Jesus lived?
Questions.A: They said that Jesus was a prophet who was powerful in his words and actions.

Questions.Q: Who condemned Jesus to be killed?
Questions.A: The chief priests and the rulers condemned Jesus to be killed.

Questions.Q: What had they hoped for?
Questions.A: They hoped that Jesus was going to redeem Israel.

Questions.Q: Why did it now seem impossible to realize that hope?
Questions.A: It seemed impossible to realize that hope because Jesus had been dead for three days. No one expected a person to revive after three days in the tomb.

Questions.Q: How many days earlier had these events taken place?
Questions.A: These events took place three days earlier.

Questions.Q: What additional (amazing or confusing) information did they tell Jesus?
Questions.A: The additional information they told Jesus is that the women didn't find his body in the tomb and that they saw angels saying that he was alive.

Questions.Q: What had the women told the disciples?
Questions.A: The women told the disciples that Jesus is alive.
Questions.Alternative: What did the ladies say who were following along with the disciples?

Questions.Q: What did the disciples who went to the tomb find?
Questions.A: The disciples who went to the tomb found no sign of Jesus.
Questions.Alternative: What did some of the disciples who went to the tomb see?
What else did some of the disciples who went there to see find out?

Questions.Q: Had Cleopas and his companion been to the tomb?
Questions.A: No.

Questions.Q: At the start of this section, were Cleopas and his companion thinking that Jesus was alive or dead?
Questions.A: Cleopas and his companion thought Jesus was dead.

Questions.Q: Why do you think there are writings about Jesus from long before he was born? // Normally if anyone wants to write about someone, they would write about how he lived and what he did within his lifetime. That would be normal. But even before he was born, [from 1500BC onwards,] there are writings about Jesus. What kind of person do you think Jesus is?
Questions.A: God loved his people and promised his people that a Savior would come and rescue everyone. Jesus is God. He loves everybody and he sacrificed himself for us.
Questions.Alternative: Normally if anyone wants to write about someone, they write about how he lived and what he did within his lifetime. But long before he was born, there are writings about Jesus. What kind of person do you think Jesus is?
Why do you think there are writings about Jesus from long before he was born?

Normally if anyone wants to write about someone, they would write about how he lived and what he did within his lifetime. That would be normal. But even before he was born, from 1500BC onwards, there are writings about Jesus. What kind of person do you think Jesus is?

Questions.Q: What do you think the term "Messiah" means?
Questions.A: Messiah means promised deliverer.
Key Term Check: It is the transliteration of the Hebrew word meaning "anointed one" that was translated into Greek as Christos.
Questions.Note: See "Messiah" in KBT in the "Christ, Messiah" entry.

Questions.Q: How did Jesus feel about these two disciples? (Was he angry, upset, etc.?)
Questions.A: I think Jesus understood that these two disciples didn't understand the message so he explained the Scriptures to them.
Questions.Alternative: How did Jesus feel about these two disciples?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to those [two] disciples/men?
Questions.A: Jesus told the disciples that the events were supposed to happen. He said, "How foolish you are, and how slow to believe all that the prophets have spoken. Did not the Messiah have to suffer these things and then enter his glory?"
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus say to those disciples?
What did Jesus say to these two disciples?
What did Jesus say to the two men?

Questions.Q: Having suffered/faced all those difficulties/things, what must happen to Christ?
Questions.A: After suffering, Christ would be victorious and glorious.
Questions.Alternative: Having suffered these things, what had to happen to Christ?
Having suffered, what had to happen to Christ?
What had to happen to Christ?
What had to happen to the Messiah?
Having faced all those difficulties, what must happen to Christ?

Questions.Q: Who was Jesus talking about?
Questions.A: Jesus was talking about the prophets and what they said would happen to him.
Questions.Alternative: Who was Jesus talking about when he explained these things?
Who was Jesus explaining about?

Questions.Q: Who wrote about Jesus in [the Old Testament] Scriptures?
Questions.A: Moses and all the prophets wrote about Jesus in the Old Testament
Questions.Alternative: Who wrote about Jesus in the Old Testament Scriptures?
Who wrote about Jesus in scripture?

Questions.Q: How did he teach them after that?
Questions.A: Jesus explained the Old Testament prophecies about the Messiah suffering.
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus explain to them after that?
What did Jesus explain to them?

Questions.Q: What specific things do you think Jesus might have explained?
Questions.Note: Respondents with a more extensive knowledge of the Old Testament (or who remember some of the details of prophetic fulfillment mentioned in Luke or the other gospels) might be able to give details about specific prophecies and how Jesus fulfilled them. Others might have difficulty with this question, but some may be able to draw on verse 26 for an answer.

Questions.Q: Where do the events in this section take place?
Questions.A: In the village of Emmaus.
Questions.Alternative: Where did these events happen?

Questions.Q: Where did Jesus seem to be going?
Questions.A: Jesus seemed to going on further [past Emmaus].
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus act like he planned to do?
Then where did Jesus want to go?

Questions.Q: What did those disciples request of Jesus?
Questions.A: The disciples requested Jesus to stay with them since it was getting late.

Questions.Q: Where did Jesus enter?
Questions.A: Jesus entered the village where the two disciples asked Jesus to stay with him.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus give thanks for?
Questions.A: Jesus gave thanks for the bread.

Questions.Q: When did they recognize Jesus?
Questions.A: They recognized Jesus after he broke the bread and gave it to them.

Questions.Q: Why didn't they finish their meal with Jesus?
Questions.A: They didn't finish their meal with Jesus because he disappeared from their sight.

Questions.Q: What happened to Jesus so that they could no longer see him?
Questions.A: Jesus disappeared so that they could no longer see him.

Questions.Q: Where do you think Jesus went, or what happened to his body?
Questions.Note: Eventually, we find out that Jesus went to Jerusalem to see the disciples. At this point, the text just says he disappeared. The translation should not imply that this was a ghostly apparition.

Section.heading: Luke 24:32-49 Jesus Appears to His Disciples

Questions.Q: Since Jesus has a [physical] body like us, what [kinds of work] do you think he is able to do?
Questions.A: Jesus can do all sorts of things with his body (just like us). He can eat, sleep, touch objects, smell, hear, taste, etc.
Questions.Alternative: Since Jesus has a body like us, what do you think he is able to do?
Since Jesus has a physical body (like us), what kinds of things do you think he is able to do?
Jesus said, "I have body and bones which an evil-spirit does not." Due to Jesus having a body like us, what kinds of work do you think he is able to do?

Questions.Q: Why do you think it was important for Jesus to show his disciples that he had a real body?
Questions.A: Jesus wanted the disciples to know he was really alive and not a ghost.

Questions.Q: Since evil spirits do not have a body, what kinds of things do you think they [evil spirits] cannot do?
Questions.A: Evil spirits cannot eat or drink or physically attack us.
Questions.Alternative: Since evil spirits do not have a body, what kinds of things do you think they cannot do?
Since evil spirits do not have a body, what kinds of things do you think evil spirits cannot do?

Questions.Q: What did those two disciples talk about after Jesus disappeared?
Questions.A: After Jesus disappeared, they talked about their hearts burning within them while they were talking to Jesus.
Questions.Alternative: What did those two disciples think about how they had felt when Jesus was talking to them?
What did those two disciples say about how they had felt when Jesus was talking to them?
What did those two disciples say to one another?

Questions.Q: What did those two disciples do next?
Questions.A: The two disciples got up and went to Jerusalem.

Questions.Q: Was this their original plan?
Questions.A: No, this wasn't their original plan.

Questions.Q: How do you know?
Questions.A: They were planning to stay because it was getting late.

Questions.Q: Why did they want to go back such a long way after just arriving at Emmaus?
Questions.A: They wanted to go back to tell the Eleven that it was true that Jesus had risen.

Questions.Q: Who all were gathered in Jerusalem?
Questions.A: The Eleven and those with them were gathered in Jerusalem.

Questions.Q: Who spoke first?
Questions.A: The Eleven [apostles]

Questions.Q: What did the [Eleven] apostles say to these two disciples?
Questions.A: The apostles told the disciples "It is true. The Lord has risen and appeared to Simon." And they told everything that happened on the way.
Questions.Alternative: What did the Eleven say to these two disciples?
What did the apostles say to these two disciples?
What did the eleven apostles say to these two disciples?
What did the eleven apostles say to the two disciples who had arrived?
What did the eleven apostles say to the two disciples who had come back to Jerusalem?

Questions.Q: What event had changed the apostles' thoughts about what the women had told them earlier?
Questions.A: Jesus had appeared to Simon Peter.
Questions.Alternative: What event had changed the eleven apostles' thoughts about what the women had told them earlier?
What event had changed the disciples' thoughts about what the women had told them earlier?

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what the two disciples [who had returned] from Emmaus said to the other disciples [in Jerusalem].
Questions.A: They told them that Jesus is alive and had talked to them on the way to Emmaus.
They told them that they recognized Jesus when he broke bread with them at dinner.
Questions.Alternative: Tell in your own words what the two disciples who had returned from Emmaus said to the other disciples in Jerusalem.
Tell in your own words what the two disciples who had returned from Emmaus said to the other disciples.
Tell in your own words what the two disciples from Emmaus said to the other disciples in Jerusalem.
Tell in your own words what the two disciples from Emmaus said to the other disciples.
Tell in your own words what the two disciples from Emmaus said to the eleven apostles.

Questions.Q: What happened while they were discussing all these events?
Questions.A: While they were discussing about these events, Jesus stood among them.
Questions.Alternative: What happened while they were talking?
What happened while they were talking about this?

Questions.Q: [Having stood among them,] what did Jesus say?
Questions.A: Jesus said, "Peace be with you."
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus say?
Having stood among them, what did Jesus say?
What was Jesus' greeting?
How did Jesus speak to them?

Questions.Q: [Having seen Jesus,] how did they feel? // What did they think when they saw Jesus?
Questions.A: They were startled and frightened.
They thought they were seeing a ghost.
Questions.Alternative: How did they feel?
How did they feel when they saw Jesus?
Having seen Jesus, how did they feel?
How did seeing Jesus make them feel?
How did they react to seeing Jesus?
What did they think when they saw Jesus?

Questions.Q: Jesus said that having seen certain things, they should recognize him/see that he was not a ghost. What were those things?
Questions.A: Jesus showed them his hands and his feet.
Jesus invited them to touch his body to see that he was real.
Questions.Alternative: Jesus said that having seen certain things, they should see that he was not a ghost. What were those things?
Jesus said that having seen certain things, they should recognize him. What were those things?
What things did Jesus say they could see to know that he was not a ghost?
What things did Jesus say they could see to understand that he was not a ghost?
What things did Jesus show to prove that he was really Jesus and not a ghost?

Questions.Q: Why did [all those] disciples become/remain confused/troubled?
Questions.A: They still remained confused/troubled because of their joy and amazement.
Questions.Alternative: Why did the disciples remain confused?
Why did the disciples remain troubled?
Why did the disciples still have difficulty believing?
Why did all those disciples become troubled?

Questions.Q: Then what did Jesus request?
Questions.A: Jesus requested food.
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus request?
Then what did Jesus ask them for?
What did Jesus ask them at that time?

Questions.Q: Why did Jesus ask them for food?
Questions.A: Jesus asked for food to prove to them that he was alive and was not a ghost.

Questions.Q: What did they pass to Jesus?
Questions.A: They gave him a piece of broiled fish.

Questions.Q: After eating the fish, what did Jesus tell them?
Questions.A: Jesus told them, "This is what I told you while I was with you: Everything must be fulfilled that is written about me in the Law of Moses, the Prophets and the Psalms."
Questions.Alternative: After eating the fish, what did he tell them?

Questions.Q: Who were hearing these things explained for the second time?
Questions.A: Cleopas and his companion were hearing these things for the second time.

Questions.Q: Describe how you think Jesus helped the disciples.
Questions.A: Jesus helped the disciples by opening their minds/explaining so that they could understand the Scriptures.

Questions.Q: How were the disciples to have known that Jesus would rise from the dead?
Questions.A: The disciples could have read the Scriptures (Old Testament) that prophesied about his death and resurrection.

Questions.Q: About what/which gospel/good news did Jesus say they should share/preach?
Questions.A: Jesus told them to preach that people could have their sins forgiven.
Jesus told them to tell about his life in the world: his ministry, death and resurrection.
Questions.Alternative: About what did Jesus tell them to preach?
About which gospel did Jesus say they should share?
About which good news did Jesus say they should share?
What was the good news Jesus told them to preach?

Questions.Q: What do you think the term "witness" means?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: One who has seen or heard or knows something (usually by first-hand experience) and can testify about it.

Questions.Q: What had the disciples witnessed?
Questions.A: The disciples witnessed his entire life. His ministry, death and resurrection.

Questions.Q: Why were the disciples to stay in Jerusalem?
Questions.A: The disciples were to stay in Jerusalem because Jesus commanded them to. They were to wait until the Holy Spirit comes.
Questions.Alternative: Why do you think the disciples were supposed to wait in Jerusalem?
Why were the disciples not to leave Jerusalem?
Why do you think the disciples should not leave Jerusalem?

Questions.Q: What kind of power do you think the disciples were going to receive?
Questions.A: The disciples were going to receive spiritual power from the Holy Spirit.

Questions.Q: Where do you think Jesus is now?
Questions.A: Jesus is in heaven with God.

Questions.Q: [Jesus was raised up towards heaven.] So we can’t see him now with our eyes. Do you think Jesus knows about all the things happening in the world?
Questions.A: Yes, Jesus knows what's happening in the world.
Questions.Alternative: Since we can’t see Jesus now with our eyes, do you think Jesus knows about all the things happening in the world?
Jesus was raised up into heaven, so we can’t see him now with our eyes. Do you think Jesus knows about all the things happening in the world?
Jesus was raised up towards heaven. So we can’t see him now with our eyes. Do you think Jesus knows about all the things happening in the world?

Questions.Q: Where did Jesus lead the disciples [to bless them]?
Questions.A: Jesus lead the disciples out to the vicinity of Bethany to bless them.
Questions.Alternative: Where did Jesus lead the disciples?
Where did Jesus take the disciples?
Where did Jesus take the disciples to bless them?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means that Jesus "blessed" them?
Questions.A: Jesus gave them words of encouragement and consecration.

Key Term Check: The word "bless" here probably refers to speaking words of consecration and encouragement (as we see in Matthew 28:18-20 and in Acts 1:8). (See "blessing" in KBT in the "bless" entry.)

Questions.Q: How were the disciples feeling?
Questions.A: The disciples felt great joy. They were happy and praised God.

Questions.Q: After that [when Jesus went up into heaven], where did those disciples go?
Questions.A: After Jesus went up into heaven, the disciples went to Jerusalem and stayed at the temple.
Questions.Alternative: After Jesus ascended into heaven, where did the disciples go?
After Jesus went up into heaven, where did those disciples go?
After that, where did the disciples go?
After seeing Jesus raised up into heaven, where did the disciples go?
After that event, where did those disciples go?

Questions.Q: What were the disciples doing at the temple?
Questions.A: The disciples were praising God in the temple.
Questions.Alternative: What were the disciples doing in the temple area?

Section.heading: Mark 1:1-8 John the Baptist prepared the way for Jesus.

Questions.Q: Who wrote this book?
Questions.A: Mark wrote it.
Questions.Note: Sometimes they called him John Mark. See Acts 12:12-13:13, 15:37, and Col. 4:10.

Questions.Q: What did Mark write about?
Questions.A: Mark wrote the good news about Jesus Christ, God's son. // Mark wrote the good news about what Jesus Christ did for all people.

Questions.Q: Why do you think they called this "Good News"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: See "Good News" in KBT in the "gospel" entry.

Questions.Q: Who first wrote the words that Mark put down here?
Questions.A: Isaiah, the prophet [of long ago], wrote the words that Mark quoted here. (2)
Key Term Check: See "prophet" in KBT.

Questions.Q: When the prophet Isaiah wrote this quotation, who do you think it was who had said, "I will send my messenger ahead of you?"
Questions.A: God said that. (2)
Questions.Note: Most of the people to whom Mark wrote would have understood that Isaiah was quoting God. You may need to state clearly that Isaiah was writing what God said.

Questions.Q: To whom was God talking when he said those words which Isaiah wrote down?
Questions.A: God was speaking to his son, Jesus. (2-3)
Questions.Note: This is implied, but it may need to be stated clearly if people do not realize that.

Questions.Q: Who do you think was the messenger that Isaiah spoke about?
Questions.A: He was John [the Baptist]. (4)

Questions.Q: Did the messenger really want the people to improve a road for the Lord to use as he came to them?
Questions.A: No.

Questions.Q: What did he want them to do?
Questions.A: He wanted them to get ready in their hearts/thinking for the Lord's coming by repenting so that God could forgive them. We can tell this when we learn more about the messenger, that is, John, in verses 4-8.
Key Term Checks: See "repent" and "forgive" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Tell me what a "lord" is.
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The word "lord" refers to a person who has authority over another person. God has supernatural authority over people because he created everyone and everything in the world. Sometimes he is called "the LORD God". (See "Lord" in KBT in both the "Christ" entry and the "God" entry.)

Questions.Q: Who was that lord who was coming?
Questions.A: The lord who was coming was Jesus.

Questions.Q: Where did John appear and start his public ministry?
Questions.A: He appeared in the desert/wilderness. (4)

Questions.Q: If a person preaches in a village, what does he do?
Questions.A: Herald, publish, or proclaim something (e.g., the gospel) openly.
Questions.Note: Other answers you are likely to hear are:
1) He teaches more of the parts of the Bible to the people who believe the talk about Jesus.
2) He harangues the believers to behave better than they have been doing.

Neither of these two actions is what the Bible refers to as preaching. When one of the above answers is given, if at all possible, the translator should use other words that are appropriate to the action found in the Greek NT text. He should not automatically use the church word for "preach." Please ask the next question below before making any word changes.

Questions.Q: What do you think that John actually did in those places when he "preached"?
Questions.A: John spoke out with authority to tell some news (that God had sent the Savior he had promised to send). In this verse, he also was telling people what they should do because of that news. (4)
Questions.Note: Key term check: See "preach" in KBT in the "gospel" entry.
In English translations, three different Greek words are all translated "preach". The Greek word used in this verse means to speak with authority.

Questions.Q: What did he tell the people to do?
Questions.A: He told them to repent and be baptized. (4)
Key Term Check: See "baptize" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What would happen if they did this?
Questions.A: [God] would forgive their sins. (4)
Key Term Check: See "sin" in KBT.

Questions.Q: When people read this, will they think that all the people of Judea, including everyone from Jerusalem went and had John baptize them?
Questions.Note: The word "all" does not mean everyone here. In Greek, and in English as well, "all" can be used as a way of saying "many". See the TEV.

Questions.Q: What did John do to the people?
Questions.A: He baptized them.

Questions.Q: How does a person "baptize" another?
Questions.A: [Keep the person's answer in mind.]

Questions.Q: Is there any other way to baptize people?
Questions.Note: The idea here is to try to find a term for "baptize" that has a meaning broad enough to cover the different ways of baptism used by the different Christian groups in the area.

Questions.Q: What did the people do before John baptized them?
Questions.A: They admitted [to others/to God] how they had sinned. (5)

Questions.Q: What did John wear?
Questions.A: John wore rough clothing that was locally made. (6)

Questions.Q: What was John's main food?
Questions.A: John ate mainly locusts and honey. (6)

Questions.Q: Why do you think that he ate like that?
Questions.A: It was simple food he could find in the wilderness.
Questions.Note: Mark may have told us about John's food and clothing because it was similar to that of the Old Testament prophets, especially Elijah (see 2 Kings 1:8).

Questions.Q: What did John tell the people about someone whom they would see later on?
Questions.A: He told them that the one who came after him would be a much greater person than he. (7)

Questions.Q: Why would John not want to do (or, hesitate to do) even very simple work for such a person, like untying his shoes?
Questions.A: John understood how great that person was.
He felt that he himself was not really good enough to be even a servant to him. (7)
Questions.Alternative: Why would John not want to do even very simple work for such a person, like untying his shoes?
Why would John hesitate to do even very simple work for such a person, like untying his shoes?

Questions.Q: What was the difference between the way John baptized, and the way the person who would come after him would baptize?
Questions.A: John baptized people who repented with water. The one who would come later would cause people who repented to come under the influence of the Holy Spirit. (8)
-OR-
John used water baptism to show their change of heart toward God; the one who came later would use the Holy Spirit. (8)
Key Term Check: See "Holy Spirit" in KBT in the "advocate" entry.

Questions.Q: Who was the person that John the Baptist said would come?
Questions.A: He was Jesus. (9)

Questions.Q: And who do these verses show Jesus to be?
Questions.A: He is the Son of God. (11)
Key Term Check: See "Son of God" in KBT in the "Christ" entry.

Questions.Q: Who was baptizing, and whom did he baptize?
Questions.A: John baptized Jesus. (9)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus see as he came up out of the water?
Questions.A: He saw the/a Spirit come to him from the sky like a dove. (10)

Questions.Q: What spirit and whose voice was it that came down from the sky? What do you think?
Questions.A: It was God's spirit and God's voice. [Key Term Check: See "heaven" in KBT.]

Questions.Q: What do we learn about Jesus from what God said?
Questions.A: We learn that Jesus is God's son.
Also, God loves him and is pleased with him. (11)

Key Term Check: The Greek language has several words which are translated "love" in English. The word used here means that a person has a gracious, outgoing, active interest in the welfare of another person. Jesus used the same word to talk about loving God and loving one's neighbor as one loves himself (Mark 12:30-31. Some cultures have a special term for a father's love for his oldest son or his only child. (See "beloved" in KBT in the "love" entry.) ]

Section.heading: Mark 1:12-13 Satan tested Jesus to see if he could get Jesus to obey him instead of God.

Questions.Q: Why do you think that Satan would want to tempt Jesus?
Questions.A: He wanted to try to get Jesus to obey him rather than God. [Key Term Check: tempt]

Questions.Q: Why did Jesus go out into the desert/wilderness?
Questions.A: God's Spirit caused him to go there. (12)
Questions.Alternative: Why did Jesus go out into the desert?
Why did Jesus go out into the wilderness?

Questions.Q: Mark mentions Satan here. Who is he?
Questions.A: [He is chief of the evil spirits.] [Key Term Check: See "Satan" in KBT.]

Questions.Q: What did Satan try to do?
Questions.A: He tried to make Jesus sin (that is, to disobey God), but Jesus would not do that. (13)
Key Term Check: See "sin" in KBT.

Questions.Q: When people read this, what will they think was Mark's reason for mentioning the animals here?
Questions.A: Mark probably only wanted to show that it was out in a lonely place where there were no people, just animals.
Questions.Alternative: Why do you think Mark mentions the animals here?

Questions.Q: Who came to Jesus there?
Questions.A: Angels came from God. (13)
Questions.Note: (Key Term Check: See "angel" in KBT.)
Questions.Alternative: Who came to Jesus in the wilderness?

Questions.Q: What did they do?
Questions.A: They came and helped him. (13)

Section.heading: Mark 1:14-20 Jesus called His first four disciples to follow him.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus ask the fishermen to do?
Questions.A: He asked them to leave their work of fishing and follow him, that is, become his disciples. (17, 20)
Questions.Note: (Key Term Check: If the term "disciple" is introduced here, see its entry in KBT.)
In Israel at that time, different teacher's disciples, that is, their apprentice-type students, would continually go around with their teacher in order to learn from them.

Questions.Q: Where did Jesus go after King Herod [sent his men and had them] put John in prison, and what did Jesus do there?
Questions.A: Jesus went to Galilee [province] and traveled around, preaching the Good News from God. (14)
Questions.Alternative: Where did Jesus go after King Herod sent his men and had them put John in prison, and what did Jesus do there?
Where did Jesus go after King Herod put John in prison, and what did Jesus do there?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus preach?
Questions.A: He told the people that the time for God's new way of ruling over people was very near and that they must repent of their sins and believe the Good News. (15)
Key Term Checks: kingdom of God, repent, believe. Each term is a separate entry in KBT.

Questions.Q: What kind of work did Simon and his brother Andrew do before Jesus came to them?
Questions.A: They worked at catching fish [with a net.] (16)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say he would cause them to become if they followed him?
Questions.A: He said that he would cause them, who had caught fish, to become those who would encourage people to trust and follow God. (17)

Questions.Q: How do we know that Simon and Andrew agreed to that?
Questions.A: They left their fishing nets and went around with him. (18)

Questions.Q: What were James and John doing when Jesus saw them?
Questions.A: They were in a boat, mending their fishing nets. (19)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means that Jesus "called" them?
Questions.A: He asked them to be his followers/disciples. (20)

Questions.Q: How do we know that they agreed to do that?
Questions.A: They left their fishing business and followed him. (20)

Questions.Q: Who else had been in the boat with James and John?
Questions.A: Their father Zebedee and some other men who worked for pay had been with them. (20)

Section.heading: Mark 1:21-28 Jesus commanded an evil spirit to come out of a man.

Questions.Q: What did the people think when they heard and saw what Jesus did?
Questions.A: They were amazed. (27)

Questions.Q: Why were the people so amazed?
Questions.A: They saw that Jesus taught with authority (22),
and that when he commanded the evil spirits to do something they had to obey him, so those people were impressed (25-27).

Questions.Q: Who, if anyone, did Jesus take with him when he went to Capernaum?
Questions.A: He took along the men he had called to follow him (his disciples).

Questions.Q: Why do you think that Jesus would go to the synagogue on the Sabbath day?
Questions.A: The Sabbath day was a special day of the week to rest and worship God. (21)
Questions.Note: Key Term Checks: See "Sabbath" and "synagogue" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did the people think when they heard Jesus teach?
Questions.A: They were amazed. (22)

Questions.Q: Why were they so amazed?
Questions.A: They were amazed because he taught like someone to whom God had given authority. (22)
Key Term Check: See "teacher of the law" in KBT in the "scribe" entry.
Questions.Note: The teachers of their Jewish law never taught like that. They mostly repeated what other people had said or written about the various laws.

Questions.Q: Why did a man shout out when Jesus was teaching?
Questions.A: The man shouted because an evil spirit possessed him. (23)
The evil spirits were afraid that Jesus was going to destroy them (cause their complete downfall). (24)
Key Term Check: See "evil spirit" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Why did the man say "us" part of the time?
Questions.A: The evil spirit spoke through the man's voice and knew that all of the evil spirits were in danger. That is why he said "us". (23-24)

Questions.Q: What did the evil spirit in this man know about Jesus?
Questions.A: He knew that Jesus was a man from the town of Nazareth. (24)
He knew that Jesus had power and authority to destroy/get rid of him [and the other spirits who were in the man]. (24)
He knew that Jesus was the holy one who had come from God. (24)
Questions.Note: (Key Term Check: See "destroy" in KBT.)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when it says that Jesus was God's holy one?
Questions.A: Jesus was set apart from the way people lived to please themselves. God set him apart to totally serve him. Jesus was morally pure, acting in all ways like God would act. (24)
Questions.Note: Key Term: See "holy" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What can you tell about Jesus's power from verses 25 and 26?
Questions.A: He was able to cause the evil spirits to leave the man by commanding them to leave.

Questions.Q: What did the people think when they saw that the evil spirit obeyed Jesus?
Questions.A: They were amazed at what they called "this new teaching."
They were amazed that the evil spirits had to obey Jesus. (27)

Questions.Q: What did the people do after they left the synagogue?
Questions.A: They talked about what Jesus had done until people in all of the surrounding area knew about it. (28)

Section.heading: Mark 1:29-34 Jesus healed many sick people.

Questions.Q: What else did Jesus do that showed that God had sent him?
Questions.A: He healed many sick people and cast out demons (that is, evil spirits). (31-34)

Questions.Q: Where did Jesus and his followers/disciples go when they left the synagogue?
Questions.A: They went to Simon and Andrew's house. (29)
Questions.Alternative: Where did Jesus and his followers go when they left the synagogue?
Where did Jesus and his disciples go when they left the synagogue?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do at their house?
Questions.A: He healed Simon's mother-in-law. (31)

Questions.Q: How do we know that she was healed at once?
Questions.A: She began to serve food to the people who were there. (31)

Questions.Q: What happened that evening?
Questions.A: Many of the local people came to the door. (33)
They brought their relatives who were sick and those whom demons/evil spirits possessed. (32)

Questions.Q: What do people who speak your language say are the signs that a spirit is a demon?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A demon is a spirit that only does evil things and tries to cause trouble for people, especially people who want to obey God's Word. (See "demon" in KBT in the "evil spirit" entry.)
Questions.Note: In the Bible, demons and evil spirits are names for the same thing.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do?
Questions.A: He healed all the people who were sick and cast out all the evil spirits. (34)

Questions.Q: What does it mean to "cast out a spirit" from a person?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A person with authority from God does something or says something that shows a demon in another person that it must obey him and leave that person.. The person with God's authority usually tells the spirit that it must immediately leave the person alone and go away.
Questions.Note: If a cultural term is in the translation here, ask where the power comes from which makes the evil spirit obey the speaker's words. If that power is not from God, that term must be modified or changed altogether.

Questions.Q: What did he tell the evil spirits not to do?
Questions.A: He told them not to talk about him [being the Son of God]. (34)

Questions.Q: Why do you think that Jesus did not want them to speak?
Questions.A: An evil spirit's testimony is not necessarily helpful.
-OR-
Jesus did not want the scribes and other religious leaders to become angry with him at that time.
Questions.Note: The text does not have an answer for us. This question is a check for any misunderstanding.

Section.heading: Mark 1:35-39 Jesus traveled around Galilee [province] preaching the Good News.

Questions.Q: Why did Jesus come to the earth?
Questions.A: He came in order to tell people God's message. (38)
Questions.Note: (See 1:14-15 again.)

Questions.Q: Why did Jesus get up early in the morning and go off by himself?
Questions.A: He wanted to have time to pray alone. (35)

Questions.Q: Why did Simon Peter and the others go looking for him?
Questions.A: They wanted to tell him that many people were looking for him. (36-37)

Questions.Q: Why do you think that the people were looking for him?
Questions.A: They probably wanted him to heal and cast demons out of more of their people.

Questions.Q: Did Jesus go back, or what did he do?
Questions.A: No. He went away from there so that he could go throughout Galilee [province]. (38-39)

Questions.Q: Why did he do that?
Questions.A: He did that because he had come into the world to tell people God's message. (38)

Section.heading: Mark 1:40-45 Jesus healed a man with leprosy.

Questions.Q: What happened after Jesus healed a man?
Questions.A: Many people heard about it and wanted to come to him for healing. (45)

Questions.Q: What was wrong with the man who came to Jesus?
Questions.A: He had a disease called leprosy. [Key Term Check: leprosy]
Questions.Note: You may want a glossary entry about the cultural taboos in Bible times about leprosy.

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that the man with leprosy knelt down in front of Jesus?
Questions.A: In that way he showed that he knew that Jesus was much greater than he.
Questions.Note: In Matthew's account (Matt. 8:2), he makes it clear that this was an act of worship, not merely a posture of humility, so while that would be an acceptable answer, it is not clear from Mark's account.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think was the reason that the man with leprosy kneeled down in front of Jesus?
Why do you think the man with leprosy knelt down in front of Jesus?

Questions.Q: What do you think that the man meant when he said, "Make me clean"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He was talking both about having clear skin again after he became well and about becoming ritually clean. That means that the priests would allow him to again be in the public worship and to live with his family.
Questions.Note: See "clean" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Did this man believe that Jesus would heal him?
Questions.A: He believed that Jesus had the power to heal him, but did not know if he wanted to or not.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do with the man?
Questions.A: He touched the man who had leprosy and healed him. (41-42)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell the man?
Questions.A: Jesus told him that he should not tell anyone about what Jesus had done for him,
but he should go to the priest [at the temple in Jerusalem] and show him that he was healed of leprosy.
Then he should offer [a sacrifice to God]. (43-44)
Key Term Check: See "offering" in KBT in the "sacrifice" entry.

Questions.Q: Why do you think that Jesus told him to offer a sacrifice?
Questions.A: Moses had written in the Old Testament that Jewish people who were healed of leprosy must offer such a gift to God. (44)
(Also, the people around there would then know that the man was cured, and they would not need to avoid being near him or avoid touching him any more.)

Questions.Q: What do you think a priest did when he worked?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A priest represented the people who came to worship God. He acted in their place by offering their sacrifices, prayers and gifts to God. He also represented God to those people when he announced that God had accepted their offerings and had forgiven their sins.
Questions.Note: See "priest" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Did the man obey all that Jesus had said to him?
Questions.A: No, he did not. (45)

Questions.Q: What did he do?
Questions.A: He went and told many people what Jesus had done for him. (45)

Questions.Q: Why could Jesus not enter any town in an open/public way?
Questions.A: People would crowd around him so that he could not do anything. They all wanted to see him and have him heal their sick people. (45)
Questions.Alternative: Why could Jesus not enter any town in an open way?
Why could Jesus not enter any town in an public way?

Section.heading: Mark 2:1-12 Jesus healed a paralyzed man.

Questions.Q: Why did the scribes think that Jesus should not say he forgave the paralyzed man's sins?
Questions.A: They did not believe that God had sent him, therefore, they thought that he was offending God by acting as if he could take God's place and forgive sin. (7)

Questions.Q: What happened when Jesus went to the town of Capernaum?
Questions.A: A large crowd gathered in, and around, the house where he was
and he taught them God's message.

Questions.Q: Who came looking for Jesus there?
Questions.A: Some people who were bringing a paralyzed man came to him. (3)

Questions.Q: What problem did they have when they got there?
Questions.A: They could not get near Jesus because there were so many people in the house. (4)

Questions.Q: What did they do about that?
Questions.A: They climbed [by outside stairs] to the [flat] roof,
removed some of the roof material,
attached ropes to the man's mat,
and lowered him to the place where Jesus was standing. (4)

Questions.Q: When they did that, what did Jesus realize about them?
Questions.A: He realized that they had faith (that is, they really believed) that he was able to heal the man. (5)
Questions.Note: (Key Term Check: See "faith" in KBT in the "believe" entry.)

Questions.Q: How do you think that he knew that?
Questions.A: He knew that because they had worked so hard to get to him. (5)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to the paralyzed man?
Questions.A: He said, "I forgive your sins." (5)

Questions.Q: What does a person do when they forgive another person?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: They stop thinking about that person as having done something wrong against them. There is no need for the person who did wrong to compensate them, either by receiving punishment or by giving good things in return.
Questions.Note: See "forgive" in KBT.

If the translation has a term for God forgiving people that is different from the term ordinarily used for people forgiving others, check into the reason for this difference. Try switching the verbs for forgiveness and ask what makes each one unacceptable in the people's minds. The Greek text uses the same word in both cases. God expects us to forgive others the same as he has done for us (see Mark 11:25; Matt. 6:14-15; 18:32-3; Luke 6:37).

Questions.Q: Who else was there in the house at that time?
Questions.A: Some of the teachers of the Jewish law also were there. (6)

Questions.Q: What do you think that a person does when he blasphemes God?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He claims to be equal with God in some way.
-OR-
He speaks rudely to insult God and defame his name and character so that others will not honor or respect him.

Questions.Q: What did they think about what Jesus said to the man?
Questions.A: They were angry. They thought that Jesus had no right to say he forgave the man's sin, since only God can forgive people's sin. (They were not willing to believe that Jesus was God's son, nor even that God had sent him.) (9)

Questions.Q: How do you think that Jesus knew what the teachers of the law were thinking?
Questions.A: Since he is God, he knows everything.
He could also see the expression on their faces as he talked.

Questions.Q: After he said that he forgave the paralyzed man's sins, Jesus indicated to the teachers of the law that they could learn from what he was about to do. What did he expect them to learn?
Questions.A: He told them that when he forgave the paralyzed man, they did not believe that he really had done that. Now he would heal the man. Then they could know that he was from God, and therefore able both to heal and to forgive sin. (9-10)

Questions.Q: Who was Jesus talking about when he mentioned the "Son of Man"?
Questions.A: He was speaking of himself.

Key Term Check: "Son of Man" is a title that the prophet Daniel used in Dan. 7:13-14. Daniel was referring to a human figure who is, nevertheless, a heavenly being. God gave him authority to be the leader of God's people on earth. The teachers of the law knew that this title referred to the Messiah. Jesus applied this title to himself.
Questions.Note: See "Son of Man" in KBT.

Questions.Q: How did the people know that the man was healed?
Questions.A: They saw him get up and walk away, carrying his mat. (12)

Questions.Q: What did the people think when they saw the man get up and walk away?
Questions.A: They were amazed and praised (glorified/gave glory to) God. (12)
Questions.Note: Key Term Check: The Greek word translated here as "praised" is the Key Term "glory/glorify". Each meaning of that Greek word tries to describe a characteristic of God that people do not have. In this verse it refers to the best praise, honor, and giving of thanks that anyone can give to God because of his perfect goodness to them.
See "glorify" in KBT in the "glory" entry.

Section.heading: Mark 2:13-17 Jesus called Levi to be a disciple.

Questions.Q: Who was the person whom Jesus called to become one of his followers?
Questions.A: Jesus called Levi (who was a tax collector) to become his follower. (13)

Questions.Q: What sort of people does Jesus call to come to him?
Questions.A: He calls sinners
-OR-
He calls those who need his help, especially those who know they need his help. (17)

Questions.Q: Where did Jesus go at that time?
Questions.A: Jesus went to beside the Sea of Galilee. (13)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do after he arrived there?
Questions.A: He taught the people. (13)

Questions.Q: What was Levi's regular work?
Questions.A: He was a tax collector. (14)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to Levi?
Questions.A: He told Levi to leave his work and became a follower him. (14)

Questions.Q: How do we know that Levi was willing to follow Jesus?
Questions.A: We know he was willing because he left his work and became a follower of Jesus. (14)

Questions.Q: Where did Jesus go on a later day?
Questions.A: He went to Levi's house and was eating there. (15)

Questions.Q: What other people were there?
Questions.A: Besides Jesus and his disciples, many tax collectors and others [that the religious leaders] called sinners were there. (15)
Key Term Check: If "disciple" has not already been discussed above, see its entry in KBT.

Questions.Q: Did Jesus walk around, sit and talk with such people?
Questions.A: Yes, he often did. (Many of those people became his followers). (15)

Questions.Q: When people read this who will they think that the Pharisees and the teachers of the law were?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Pharisees were people of the Pharisee party. The teachers of the law were usually Pharisees they taught God's laws and the Jewish rules passed down for generations that they also called laws.
Questions.Note: See "Pharisee" in KBT.
(Note: You may want glossary entries on the Pharisees and the teachers of the law).

Questions.Q: What caused them to become unhappy?
Questions.A: They saw Jesus eating with people who did not follow all of the Jewish rules and regulations that the Pharisees though Jewish people should follow. (16)

Questions.Q: Why do you think that the Pharisees thought that it was not good for Jesus to be with such people?
Questions.A: They thought that good people should not mix with sinful people (lest the sinful people make the righteous people unclean in God's sight). (16-17)
Key Term Check: See "righteous" in KBT under "just, justify" entry.

Questions.Q: Why do you think that Jesus talked about sick people and a doctor?
Questions.A: He compared himself to a doctor and sinners to sick people. (17)

Questions.Q: Why did Jesus go to where sinners were?
Questions.A: He went to where they were because his work was to call the sinners to repent and follow God. (17)

Section.heading: Mark 2:18-22 People asked Jesus why his disciples did not fast.

Questions.Q: What was the most important thing that Jesus was trying to show people in these verses?
Questions.A: He was trying to show them that his teaching involved a whole new approach. If they tried to follow their traditions and just add some of his new teaching, it would not work. (19-22)

Questions.Q: What was it that the disciples of John and the Pharisees did?
Questions.A: They fasted, that is, they went without food for a period of time (to help them think about God). (18)

Key Term Check: When they fasted, they avoided eating food for certain periods of time according to the Jewish traditions and teaching of their religious leaders. The purpose was to focus their thoughts better on God.

Questions.Q: Did the followers of Jesus do the same thing?
Questions.A: No. (implied in 18-19)

Questions.Q: What did the people ask Jesus?
Questions.A: They asked him why his disciples did not fast when the disciples of John and those of the Pharisees fasted regularly. (18)

Questions.Q: How did Jesus answer them?
Questions.A: He answered them by using picture language (that is, he told a story with a hidden meaning). He said that during a wedding festival, friends of the honored man (that is, the bridegroom) would not fast. (19)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say would happen one day?
Questions.A: He said that the honored man (bridegroom) would be taken away from them (killed). That is the time when his friends would fast. (19)

Questions.Q: Who do you think that Jesus was talking about when he spoke of the bridegroom, and his friends?
Questions.A: He was talking about himself and his disciples being together and later being separated.
Questions.Note: Both the near and the distant context suggests this meaning.

Questions.Q: What answer did Jesus's picture language give them about why Jesus's followers did not fast?
Questions.A: Jesus showed them that his disciples were right to rejoice and not fast (a sign of sorrow) while he was with them.

Questions.Q: Do you think Jesus would care if his disciples fasted if they decided to do that?
Questions.A: No.

Questions.Q: How can we tell that?
Questions.A: He said in his picture talk that later, when people took him away from them, his disciples would have a real reason to fast.

Questions.Q: What was one thing that Jesus said people do not do?
Questions.A: They do not mend an old garment with a piece of new cloth. (21)

Questions.Q: Do people in your village ever mend an old garment with a piece of new cloth?
Questions.Note: Check for possible mismatching contrast with local cultural practice here.
Questions.Alternative: Do your people ever mend an old garment with a piece of new cloth?

Questions.Q: What was the second thing that Jesus said people do not do?
Questions.A: They do not put new wine in an old goatskin [bag/bottle]. (22)
Questions.Note: When people seal new wine in a leather container, it will ferment and swell up. An old leather bag is no longer pliable and will break. Both the wine and the bag are ruined.

Questions.Q: When Jesus spoke about cloth and about the wine and bottle, what was he teaching the people?
Questions.A: CLOTH-Jesus was teaching that his new teachings cannot be like a patch on the peoples' old system of beliefs. They needed to change their whole approach to God and their belief system.
Questions.Note: WINE BOTTLE-Pouring some of his teaching into their old non-pliable system was not going to work. They needed to realize that his teaching was new and they needed to follow it all. (Note: Watch carefully for people understanding the meaning wrongly because they are living in a different time and place than Jesus and his listeners.)

Section.heading: Mark 2:23-28 Jesus showed the Pharisees that he had authority over the Sabbath day.

Questions.Q: Why did the Pharisees say that the disciples were doing something wrong?
Questions.A: The Pharisees felt it was wrong to do anything like work because it was the Sabbath day. (23)
Questions.Note: According to the Jewish rules (traditions), that they had added to the Old Testament laws, people were not supposed to do anything that was even a bit like work on the Sabbath day.

Questions.Q: What were the disciples doing as they walked along a path?
Questions.A: They were breaking off some of the grain and eating it. (23)

Questions.Q: Why do you think that they did that?
Questions.A: Because they were hungry. (implied from verse 25)

Questions.Q: What did the Pharisees say was wrong about that?
Questions.A: The Pharisees said that the disciples were breaking the law by working on the day of rest. (24)
Key Term Check: See "law" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What work did they accuse them of doing?
Questions.A: They implied that picking some grain and taking the husks off to eat it, was the same as harvesting grain on the Sabbath. (24)

Questions.Q: Why did Jesus remind them about what their honored ancestor David had done?
Questions.A: That situation was similar to the disciples picking a bit of food on the rest day. In David's case, he had gone against the law concerning special bread that was kept in the temple. Only priests were allowed to eat that bread. When he and his men arrived at the temple hungry, he had asked the priest, and received from him, some of that special bread. He ate part of it. Then he also gave some to his men to eat(and God did not punish him.) (25-26)

Questions.Q: What do you think that Jesus was implying about what David and his men had done?
Questions.A: He was showing that it was all right for them to do that when they were hungry and the special bread was all they could get to eat.

Questions.Q: What was Jesus teaching the Pharisees?
Questions.A: He was teaching them that the rest day was not meant to make people suffer, like going without food. The rest day is to help people. (27)

Questions.Q: The Pharisees had asked why the followers of Jesus were doing work on the Sabbath day and therefore were breaking the laws. How did Jesus answer that question?
Questions.A: Jesus said that he, the Son of Man, is the boss over the Sabbath day, and therefore knows how to apply the Sabbath day laws. (28)

Section.heading: Mark 3:1-6 Jesus healed a man with a crippled hand.

Questions.Q: Why did the Pharisees watch Jesus intently after he entered the synagogue?
Questions.A: They watched to see if he would heal a man who had a withered hand on the Jewish Sabbath day. If he did that, then they would have something about which they could accuse him [to try to stop him from preaching his message]. (2)

Questions.Q: When Jesus went into the synagogue on a Sabbath day who was there?
Questions.A: A man with a shriveled hand was there
and some other people who were watching Jesus closely were there. (1-2)

Questions.Q: Why were those people watching him closely?
Questions.A: They wanted to see if he would heal the man so they could accuse him of working on the rest day. (2)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to the man with the shriveled hand?
Questions.A: He told him to stand up in order that everyone could see him. (3)

Questions.Q: Do you think that the man stood up?
Questions.A: Yes. (Jesus continued talking to the man, so we assume that the man had obeyed him.) (3)

Questions.Q: What question did Jesus ask the people who were there?
Questions.A: He asked them if it was all right to do bad things or to do good things on the rest day. He also asked if it was all right to kill people or to save them from dying on the rest day. (4)
Key Term Check: See "save" in KBT.

Questions.Q: How did they answer him?
Questions.A: They did not say anything. (4)

Questions.Q: Why do you think that they did not say anything?
Questions.A: They knew that they could never say it was all right to do bad or to kill people. They did not want to say it was all right to do good on the Sabbath day, since it would then be all right for Jesus to heal the man that day. They must have thought it best not to say anything.

Questions.Q: Why do you think that Jesus was so angry and upset as he looked at them?
Questions.A: It seems clear that they did not feel sorry for the man with the shriveled hand.
They did not want to learn more about God nor to change. (2-5)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to the man?
Questions.A: He told him to stretch out his hand. (5)

Questions.Q: Then what happened?
Questions.A: As the man stretched out his hand, [God] healed him. (5)

Questions.Q: What did the Pharisees do then?
Questions.A: They went and started planning how they could destroy Jesus (that is, how they could ruin all that Jesus was doing, probably by killing him). (6)

Section.heading: Mark 3:7-12 Some people asked Jesus why his disciples did not fast.

Questions.Q: What can we learn from this passage about the way that most of the people felt about Jesus?
Questions.A: We can determine that people were pleased with him. Everybody was talking about the amazing things he was doing and huge crowds were following him wherever he went.

Questions.Q: What happened when Jesus went off to a place near the lake with his disciples to be alone with them?
Questions.A: Many people from Galilee [province] and surrounding areas came.

Questions.Q: Why did Jesus tell his disciples to prepare a small boat?
Questions.A: He asked them to do that so that he would not be bumped around by the crowd.
(Also, he probably needed to get a bit of space between him and them so they could see him and hear him speak). (9)

Questions.Q: Why were the people pushing around him?
Questions.A: He had healed many people, with the results that others who needed healing were coming to touch him. (10)

Questions.Q: What were the evil spirits saying?
Questions.A: They said that Jesus was the Son of God. (11)

Questions.Q: Why do you think that Jesus would tell the evil spirits to be quiet?
Questions.A: He wanted to carry on his teaching and work so that people could see who he was and then believe in him.
-OR-
He did not want to start an argument with the Jewish leaders about his being the Son of God.
-OR-
He did not want people to think that evil spirits were helping him to do his teaching.
(It does not tell us why. There may be other possible answers.)

Section.heading: Mark 3:13-19 Jesus chose twelve apostles from among his many disciples.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do at this time?
Questions.A: He picked out 12 men to be his apostles/sent-ones from among a larger number of his followers. (14)

Questions.Q: Where did Jesus go?
Questions.A: He went up into the hills. (13)

Questions.Q: Whom did Jesus call to come up there with him?
Questions.A: He invited a large number of people he had already chosen. (13)

Questions.Q: What did he do then?
Questions.A: He chose twelve men from among them to be extra near him. That way he could teach them more and then send them out to represent him as they preached and drove demons/evil spirits out of people. (14-15)
Questions.Note: (Key Term Check: See "apostle" in KBT.)

Questions.Q: What special name did Jesus give to Simon?
Questions.A: He gave Simon the name, Peter. (16)

Questions.Q: What special name did Jesus give to James and John, and what does that name mean?
Questions.A: He called them Boanerges. That means "sons of thunder" or, "the thunder ones". (17)

Questions.Q: Why do you think that he called them that?
Questions.A: We are not sure why he called them that. This may describe some trait of theirs like a fiery nature.
Questions.Note: These questions are to check for any obviously wrong understanding of the names.

Questions.Q: What do we know about the other disciple also named Simon?
Questions.A: He was probably a patriot, that is, one who wanted to be free from foreigners ruling his people. He even may have been ready to fight to free his country.
Questions.Note: The Romans ruled over the Jews at that time.

Questions.Q: What does Mark say here about Judas Iscariot?
Questions.A: Judas was the one who would later betray Jesus by turning him over to his enemies. (19)
Questions.Note: Check that the way these verses are written does not imply that Judas had already betrayed Jesus. Mark wrote these verses after Judas betrayed Jesus, but that had not yet happened at this point in Jesus's life.

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to betray someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Betraying someone means to act like their friend while turning them over to their enemies.

Section.heading: Mark 3:20-30 The teachers of the law said that the chief of evil spirits controlled Jesus.

Questions.Q: What were some people saying about Jesus?
Questions.A: Some people said that his power to cast out evil spirits came from Beelzebub/Satan. (22-23)

Questions.Q: What was Jesus teaching by means of his parables?
Questions.A: He was teaching that Satan would not drive the other evil spirits out of a person. (23-26)

Questions.Q: How did Jesus show that his power did not come from Satan?
Questions.A: He told the men that if his power came from Satan, he would not then fight against Satan by driving evil spirits out of people. Satan would always be on the same side as his own spirits who work against what God wants. (23-27)

Questions.Q: What happened when Jesus went into someone's house to eat with them?
Questions.A: So many people pushed in wanting his attention that he and his disciples had no chance to even eat. (20)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus's family think about this?
Questions.A: They thought that he was going becoming insane.
They wanted to go [to him] and take him away from there. (21)

Questions.Q: What did the teachers of the Jewish law say about Jesus?
Questions.A: They said that Beelzebub possessed him. (22)

Questions.Q: Who is Beelzebub?
Questions.A: He is the chief of demons/evil spirits. (22)

Questions.Q: What is the difference between Beelzebub and Satan?
Questions.A: They are not two different people. They are just two different names for the same spirit being.

Questions.Q: If the people who speak your language use picture language/parables, tell me one of those stories and then tell me its meaning.
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A parable shows its meaning indirectly by using picture language to make a comparison. The storyteller generally does not explain the parts of the comparison. The listeners themselves must think about the meaning that the storyteller has hidden in the different parts of his picture language. Jesus taught spiritual truths in this story form.
Questions.Note: See "parable" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: If the people who speak your language use picture language, tell me one of those stories and then tell me its meaning.
If the people who speak your language use parables, tell me one of those stories and then tell me its meaning.

Questions.Q: Why would Satan not drive out evil spirits?
Questions.A: Groups like families, clans, and governments, do not fight with each other otherwise they would break up. Likewise, Satan would not oppose his own evil spirits and cast them out, or soon he would no longer have any evil spirits to follow him that he could rule over. (26)

Questions.Q: Who is the "strong man" that Jesus spoke about here?
Questions.A: He was speaking about Satan. (27)

Questions.Q: What was Jesus saying about himself and Satan here?
Questions.A: Jesus was pointing out that he had more power than Satan. That is, Jesus had God's power and could control Satan and cast out Satan's evil spirits. Otherwise, Satan would not let Jesus take from him those who had been his subjects. (27)

Questions.Q: Why did Jesus begin talking about people who speak against the Holy Spirit?
Questions.A: When those people saw Jesus use the power of the Holy Spirit, but said that Jesus was using the power of Satan, they were speaking (that is, blaspheming) against the Holy Spirit. (29-30)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about the punishment for anyone who speaks against the Holy Spirit?
Questions.A: He said that (God) will never forgive people that do like that. Their punishment will last forever. (29)

Section.heading: Mark 3:31-35 Those who follow Jesus are the same as being his mother or his brothers and sisters.

Questions.Q: What do you think was the important point Jesus was teaching in these verses?
Questions.A: Jesus was teaching that everyone who does what pleases God is special to Jesus. They are like his own family. (31-34)

Questions.Q: Who came to look for Jesus?
Questions.A: His mother and [younger] brothers came to look for him. (31-32)

Questions.Q: How did Jesus know that his mother and brothers were there?
