Questions.A: People in the crowd around him told him. (32)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus want to teach to those people that day?
Questions.A: He wanted them to learn that all who do what God wants are like family members to him. (34-35)

Questions.Q: Do you think that Jesus refused to go and talk to his own family?
Questions.A: Mark did not tell us about that, but only about what Jesus wanted to teach from that situation.
Questions.Note: Jewish teachers used to start with something that was happening and then teach something else from it. When the crowd mentioned family, Jesus similarly started from that thought and taught about his close relationship to people who obey God. This was the important part that Mark wanted us to know. He did not bother to go back and tell us more about his introduction to this incident and whether Jesus talked with his mother and brothers afterward or not.

Section.heading: Mark 4:1-9 Jesus told a parable about a farmer sowing seed.

Questions.Q: In this parable, what did Jesus say about the different soils where the farmer sowed the seed?
Questions.A: There was great variety in the ground on which that seed fell. (3-8)
Some seed did not get a chance to sprout.
Some sprouted, but did not grow well.
Other seed sprouted and grew. The new seed these seeds produced varied from an acceptable crop to a very good crop.
Questions.Alternative: In this parable, what did Jesus say about the different types of soil where the seed was sown?
What did Jesus say about the different types of soil where the seed was sown?
Tell me about the different types of soil where the seed was sown.
What did Jesus say about the different soils where the farmer sowed the seed?
Tell me about the different soils where the farmer sowed the seed.
What did Jesus say about the different soils and the resulting growth?
Tell me about the different soils and the resulting growth.
Tell me about the different places where the seed was sown and what happened as a result.
In this parable, what did Jesus say about the different seed that the farmer sowed?

Questions.Q: What was Jesus teaching the people about listening carefully to him?
Questions.A: He was teaching them to be sure to listen and follow the good message God caused them to hear.

Questions.Q: How many people were there that day?
Questions.A: There was a large crowd there. (1)

Questions.Q: So what did Jesus do?
Questions.A: He got into the boat. (1)

Questions.Q: Why did he get into the boat?
Questions.A: He got into the boat so that he could move away from the crowd a bit (so everyone could see and hear him better). (1-2)

Questions.Q: How did Jesus teach them?
Questions.A: He used parables to teach them various things. (2)

Questions.Q: What was this main parable about?
Questions.A: This story was about a man who sowed seed in his field/garden. (3)

Questions.Q: How did the man place/sow the seed for growing in his field?
Questions.Note: Check whether the manner of sowing is clearly tossing/scattering, since some fell where people would not ordinarily plant seed.
Questions.Alternative: How did the man place the seed for growing in his field?
How did the man sow the seed for growing in his field?

Questions.Q: What happened to some of the seed?
Questions.A: Some seed fell on the path at the edge of the field
and the birds came and ate it. (4)

Questions.Q: What happened to other seed?
Questions.A: Some seed fell on soil with rock underneath.
It came up quickly, but its roots did not develop, so it wilted from the heat of the sun and dried up. (5-6)

Questions.Q: Where did other seed fall?
Questions.A: Some seed fell where thorny plant/weeds grew.
These weeds kept the good seed from growing well, so it did not bear anything. (7)

Questions.Q: What happened to the other seed?
Questions.A: Other seed fell on good soil, grew well, and produced a crop all the way from an acceptable amount of food to others having an abundant amount of food. (8)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus mean by what he said here?
Questions.A: People need to think seriously about this parable so that they will understand and learn from its warning.

Section.heading: Mark 4:10-20 Jesus explained the parable about the sower.

Questions.Q: What was Jesus teaching with this parable?
Questions.A: Jesus was teaching that God causes all kinds of people to hear his message. (14-20)
On some people, his message has no effect or no lasting effect.
On other people, it produces a real lasting effect, making them fruitful, very fruitful or truly very fruitful.

Questions.Q: How do we know that Jesus's disciples and the others with them did not understand the meaning of the story about the seed?
Questions.A: The disciples asked him to tell them the meaning. (10)

Questions.Q: What previously untaught truths did Jesus say that God was now causing them to understand?
Questions.A: God wanted them to understand the truth about God's kingdom, (that is, about God's plan of how he would rule in peoples' lives/hearts). (11)

Questions.Q: When Jesus said that God had revealed this truth to them, to whom was he talking?
Questions.A: He was talking to those who were his followers (that is, those who believed in him). (11)

Questions.Q: What happened to the others, those who were not Jesus's followers?
Questions.A: They were like some of the Israelite people of Isaiah's time. Isaiah wrote of them that they saw and heard what God was doing, but they did not understand the meaning of it. They did not want to change, and were not seeking God's forgiveness.
Questions.Note: In what Isaiah had written, it was the people's own choice that they did not respond. They were the ones thinking "lest at any time we should turn and be converted." Here in these verses some of the hearers were hostile, so Jesus used parables to help him proclaim the message without causing them to reject it.

Questions.Q: How do we know that Jesus was surprised that his followers had not understood the parable?
Questions.A: He gently rebuked them.

Questions.Q: In the parable, what did the seed that the man sowed represent?
Questions.A: The seed represented God's message, the gospel, as God caused people to hear it. (14)

Questions.Q: What does the seed that fell on the path and was eaten by the birds represent?
Questions.A: That seed represents the people who hear the message, but Satan influences them to forget it so that the message has no effect on the way they live. (15)

Questions.Q: What does the seed that fell in the rocky place represent?
Questions.A: The seed that fell on the rocky place represents people who hear the message and at first respond to it happily. (16)
But when others oppress and harass them, causing them to suffer pain and be frustrated for following God's Word, they soon give up and stop obeying the message. (17)
Key Term Check: persecute

Questions.Q: What does the seed that fell among the thorny weeds represent?
Questions.A: The seed that fell among the weed represents people who obey the message at first, but who do not continue to follow its teaching. Their concerns about life in this world (or, in these times) and a desire for money and other things take all their attention away from God's Word.
Key Term Check: See "world, age" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What kind of people are represented by the seed that fell in good soil?
Questions.A: The seed that fell on good soil represents those who hear the word of God, believe it, and allow it to change their lives so that they do what is pleasing to God.

Section.heading: Mark 4:21-25 Jesus told a proverb about a lamp.

Questions.Q: What do you think that Jesus was teaching here?
Questions.A: He was teaching that whoever understands the truth must make it clear to others by the way they live. People must be active in applying what they know of God, then God will help them to understand more. If, on the other hand, they do not come up to a minimum amount of understanding and doing what God says, the little bit they understand and do God will not count in their favor. (That is, they do not become part of his kingdom.)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say is the purpose of a lamp?
Questions.A: It's purpose is to give light to everyone. People are to put a lamp where it's light can shine out. They never (light it and then) put it under a box or bed.

Questions.Q: What do you think he meant by talking about the lamp here?
Questions.A: He was talking of the good news.

Questions.Q: What do you think that Jesus was saying about this good news?
Questions.A: God's purpose was to make clear to people how he wants to receive them through what Jesus did in dying for them.

Questions.Q: What do you think that God had hidden which he was then making clear to people?
Questions.A: He was only then making his plan clear about Jesus dying for us. Jesus's dying for us was so that God can rule in our lives. That is the good news!

Questions.Q: What warning did Jesus give here?
Questions.A: Jesus warned people that they must pay attention to what they hear, so that God will help them to understand more. (23-24)

Questions.Q: What further warning is there in verse 25?
Questions.A: He warned that people are to understand that if their response to God's good news (of providing forgiveness for their sin and so forth) is inadequate, the little bit they know will not help them any. (25)

Section.heading: Mark 4:26-29 Jesus explained that the kingdom of God is like seed that grows.

Questions.Q: To what did Jesus compare the kingdom of God?
Questions.A: He compared the kingdom of God to seed that someone sowed and he talked of how it grows gradually. It continues to grow until the harvest time comes, although no one can see a cause for it to grow.

Questions.Q: What do you think Jesus meant by this illustration?
Questions.A: The effect of God's word on a person goes on growing (progressing) until God's full purpose in that person is completed.
-OR-
The effect of God's word in the world is something that goes on growing until God's full purpose in the world is completed.

Questions.Q: What was Jesus really talking about in this parable of the seed growing?
Questions.A: He was talking about the way in which God is bringing about his rule in people's lives and/or in the world. (26)

Questions.Q: What illustration did he use?
Questions.A: He used the illustration of seed that a man sowed on a farm. (26)

Questions.Q: What happened to the seed?
Questions.A: It grew slowly/gradually all of the time. (27)

Questions.Q: What caused it to grow?
Questions.A: No one knows. An unseen source of energy caused it. (28)

Questions.Q: What happened at the end of the growing season?
Questions.A: At the end of the growing season the crop was ready, so the owner harvested it.

Questions.Q: Who do you think the owner really is and what did Jesus mean when he talked about the owner harvesting his crop?
Questions.A: The owner is God. Jesus meant that God will take those people who become his very own to be with him when the time is right. (29)

Section.heading: Mark 4:30-34 Jesus explained that the kingdom of God is like a tiny seed that grows into a large shrub.

Questions.Q: What illustration did Jesus use to show what God was doing?
Questions.A: He used the illustration of a tiny seed that grew into a tree-size plant. (30-36)

Questions.Q: What do you think is the important thing he was teaching from the tree/shrub?
Questions.A: He was teaching that at first a small number of people believe Jesus and become God's people. He will rule over them. Gradually God will rule over more and more people as more believe on Jesus.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think is the important thing he was teaching from the tree?
What do you think is the important thing he was teaching from the shrub?

Questions.Q: Why did Jesus ask these (rhetorical questions)? Did he not know how to describe the Kingdom of God?
Questions.A: He knew but he was introducing the topic of the kingdom of God by making people think about it.

Questions.Q: About what subject was Jesus teaching here?
Questions.A: He was still teaching about what would happen when God began his new way of ruling over people. (See verse 26.)

Questions.Q: What is special about a mustard seed that would make Jesus's comparison a good way for him to teach about the kingdom of God?
Questions.A: A mustard seed is very small when it is planted. (31)

Questions.Q: What happens to mustard seed when it grows?
Questions.A: It becomes a large plant with branches big enough for shade for birds.
-OR-
It becomes a large plant with branches big enough for birds to make their nests there. (32)
Questions.Note: The translator may want a glossary note to explain that Jesus spoke about the tallest plant in the gardens of Israel, a very dry land. The mustard tree does not compare to the much taller or thicker trees that grow in forests in wetter lands.

Questions.Q: What else did Mark tell us about the way that Jesus was teaching people?
Questions.A: Jesus used only parables. (33-34)

Questions.Q: With whom did Jesus use the parables?
Questions.A: He used the parables with the crowds of people who came to hear him.
Questions.Note: Verse 34 shows that these are other people, not his disciples. Other men besides Mark who wrote about this show that Jesus did this with the crowds.

Questions.Q: Why did he use only parables with them?
Questions.A: He used parables because he only taught people as much as they would understand/accept. (33)
Questions.Note: They could listen to his parables without being offended. Thinking about these or discussing them with others they could gradually learn more. With their view being so different from what Jesus knew about the kingdom of God and the Messiah his using parables helped to keep them from rejecting him completely and not listening anymore.

Questions.Q: To whom did he explain all of the parables?
Questions.A: He explained them to his followers. (They really wanted to know and follow his teaching.) (34)

Section.heading: Mark 4:35-41 Jesus commanded a storm to stop.

Questions.Q: What new amazing thing did Jesus do?
Questions.A: He caused a storm to stop.
-OR-
He showed his disciples that he had power over the wind. (39)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to his disciples?
Questions.A: He said that they should cross over to the other side of the lake. (35)

Questions.Q: Where was Jesus at that time?
Questions.A: He was in the boat. (4:1, 36)

Questions.Q: What did the disciples do after Jesus said that they should cross over the lake?
Questions.A: They started out with him in the boat. (36)

Questions.Q: What about the crowd of people that was there?
Questions.A: Jesus and his disciples left them behind on the shore of the lake. (36)

Questions.Q: What happened as Jesus and his men were crossing the lake?
Questions.A: The wind became very strong and the waves started filling up the boat. (37)

Questions.Q: What was Jesus doing at that time?
Questions.A: He was asleep in the back part of the boat. (38)

Questions.Q: How did the disciples feel about the storm?
Questions.A: They were very afraid. They thought that they were about to die. (38)

Questions.Q: What did they do then?
Questions.A: They woke Jesus and complained. They were thinking that he did not care that the storm was about to cause them all to drown/die. (38)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do?
Questions.A: He awoke and told the wind to stop and the waves to be calm. (39)

Questions.Q: What happened then?
Questions.A: The storm immediately stopped. (39)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus have to say to his disciples?
Questions.A: He rebuked them. (40)

Questions.Q: Why did He rebuke them?
Questions.A: He rebuked them because they were afraid, which showed that they did not yet really trust him yet nor realize his power. (40)

Questions.Q: What new thing did the disciples realize about Jesus?
Questions.A: Since he could stop the wind and waves by just speaking, they realized that he must be more than an ordinary person. (41)

Section.heading: Mark 5:1-20 Jesus sent many evil spirits out of a man.

Questions.Q: How did Jesus show God's power in this story?
Questions.A: He sent out many evil spirits from a man (and allowed them to go into a herd of pigs). (2-13)

Questions.Q: Where did Jesus and his disciples go in the boat?
Questions.A: They went to the Gerasa area. (1)

Questions.Q: Who came to meet Jesus as he got out of the boat?
Questions.A: A man who was possessed by an evil spirit met Jesus. (2)

Questions.Q: What does the text say about this man?
Questions.A: He lived in tombs (that is, caves where people were buried). (3)
Whenever people had tried to tie him up, he had broken the chains or ropes they used. (3-4)
He cried out loudly and cut himself with stones. (5)

Questions.Q: What did the man do when he saw Jesus?
Questions.A: He ran to Jesus, knelt in front of him and worshiped him. (6)

Questions.Q: What do you think that a person does when he worships another person?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He shows great honor and deep respect for the other person. He acts as though that person has more authority or strength or wisdom or goodness or beauty than any other human, and so is like God. (See Louw & Nida entry 53.14 and those at 53.53-64.)

Questions.Q: How do we know that the man knew who Jesus was?
Questions.A: He called Jesus the Son of God. (7)

Questions.Q: How do we know that the man believed that Jesus had power?
Questions.A: He was afraid of what Jesus might do to him. (7)
Questions.Note: Actually, it was the evil spirits within him who were afraid of what Jesus might do to them.

Questions.Q: What had Jesus said that caused the man (and the evil spirit in him) to say, "Do not torture me"?
Questions.A: Jesus already had commanded the evil spirit to come out of the man. (8)
Questions.Note: In verse 8, Mark was telling what happened even before the events in verse 7. If the translation here causes confusion, the translator could move verse 8 and its events to first position and then put those of verse 7 following that. The verse number should then be combined as 7-8.

Questions.Q: What question did Jesus ask the evil spirit in the man?
Questions.A: Jesus asked him what his name was. (9)

Questions.Q: What did the evil spirit say?
Questions.A: The evil spirit said that his name was legion (that is, many), because there were many evil spirits in the man. (9)

Questions.Q: Since these evil spirits knew that they had to leave the man, where did they want to go?
Questions.A: They did not want to go far away. They asked that Jesus allow them to go into some pigs that were nearby. (12)

Questions.Q: What happened then?
Questions.A: Jesus agreed that the evil spirits could go into the pigs, and they did so.
Then the whole herd of pigs ran down a steep incline into the sea, where they drowned. (13)

Questions.Q: What did the people who looked after the pigs do?
Questions.A: They went and told the people around there what had happened.

Questions.Q: What did those people do when they heard about it?
Questions.A: Many (of those) people went out to see what had happened. (14)

Questions.Q: What did they notice about the man that the evil spirits had continually tormented?
Questions.A: They could see that the demons/evil spirits had left him and he was dressed and completely well. (15)

Questions.Q: Why do you think that the people were afraid when they saw this?
Questions.A: They knew how strong the evil spirits had been in the man and realized that Jesus was very powerful.
Questions.Note: There may be other reasonable answers besides this one.

Questions.Q: How did the people who came later learn more about what had happened?
Questions.A: Those who had seen it happen told them about it. (16)

Questions.Q: What did the people want Jesus to do?
Questions.A: They begged him to go away. (17)

Questions.Q: How do we know that Jesus agreed to leave there?
Questions.A: He got into the boat. (18)

Questions.Q: What did the man whom evil spirits had possessed ask of Jesus?
Questions.A: He asked Jesus to allow him to go with Jesus. (18)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell him?
Questions.A: Jesus told him to go home and tell his own people about God having had compassion on him and helping him. (19)
Questions.Note: Jesus had deep feelings of genuine compassion and loving concern for the man, and thus helped him out of his situation. (See "mercy" in KBT.)

Questions.Q: What did the man do?
Questions.A: He went around that whole area telling people what Jesus had done for him. (20)

Section.heading: Mark 5:21-43 Jesus healed a sick woman and raised a dead girl back to life.

Questions.Q: In what two ways did Jesus show God's power?
Questions.A: He healed a woman (whom doctors had not made better in 12 years) (25-34),
and raised a dead girl back to life (21-24a, 35-43).

Questions.Q: Where did Jesus go next?
Questions.A: He went across the lake. (21)

Questions.Q: What happened when he arrived?
Questions.A: A crowd gathered around him. (21)

Questions.Q: Then who came to Jesus?
Questions.A: Jairus, a leader of a synagogue came to Jesus. (22)

Questions.Q: What did Jairus ask Jesus to do?
Questions.A: Jairus asked Jesus to go with him to his house to touch and heal his daughter who was about to die. (23)

Questions.Q: How was Jairus feeling at that time?
Questions.A: He was very concerned and begged Jesus to help him. (23)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do?
Questions.A: He started to go to Jairus's house. (24)

Questions.Q: Did anyone else go with them?
Questions.A: Yes. There was a large crowd of people pushing all around them. (24)

Questions.Q: What was wrong with the woman in the crowd?
Questions.A: She had not stopped bleeding for twelve years. (25)

Questions.Q: Had she been to doctors?
Questions.A: Yes, and she had spent all her money on them, but they did not help her. (26)

Questions.Q: What did the woman do?
Questions.A: She came up behind Jesus and touched his clothes. (27)

Questions.Q: Why did she do that?
Questions.A: She did that because she thought if she did that, she would be healed. (28)

Questions.Q: Was she healed?
How did she know it?
Questions.A: She felt a change in her body. (29)

Questions.Q: Did Jesus know that something had happened?
Questions.A: Yes. Jesus felt healing power going to someone. (30)
(Check that "power passing from him" does not seem to indicate that his healing of her left him with less power than before.)

Questions.Q: How did his disciples answer Jesus's question about who had touched him?
Questions.A: They were surprised that he had asked such a question. They said that many were pushing around him. Therefore some would touch him. (31)

Questions.Q: What did the woman do?
Questions.A: She was very worried but came and told Jesus what she had done. (33)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to the woman?
Questions.A: He assured her of God's peacefulness in her life and told her that her believing in him had enabled him to heal her. (34)
Questions.Note: (See "peace" in KBT.)

Questions.Q: What message did the men from Jairus's house bring?
Questions.A: They brought the news that Jairus's daughter had already died. (35)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to Jairus then?
Questions.A: Jesus said, "Do not fear, just believe (that is, keep on trusting in me)." (36)

Questions.Q: Whom did Jesus allow to go with them to Jairus's house?
Questions.A: Jesus allowed only Peter, James and John to go with them. (37)

Questions.Q: What was happening at Jairus's house?
Questions.A: People there were crying and mourning. (38)

Questions.Q: Why did the people laugh at Jesus?
Questions.A: He had said that Jairus's daughter was asleep. They knew that she was really dead not just sleeping, so they ridiculed him. (39)

Questions.Q: Do you think that Jesus thought that she had not died?
Questions.A: No. He knew she had died.

Questions.Q: Why do you think that he said she was sleeping?
Questions.A: He probably said that because he knew that she would soon be alive again.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do then?
Questions.A: He sent most of the people out of the room. He then took the girl by the hand and commanded her to wake up. (40-41)

Questions.Q: Then what happened?
Questions.A: The girl came to life and stood up. (42)

Questions.Q: Was the girl big enough to stand up by herself?
Questions.A: Yes. She was twelve years old. (42)

Questions.Q: What was the reaction of her parents?
Questions.A: Her parents were amazed. (42)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell her parents to do then?
Questions.A: They were not to tell anyone, but to give her something to eat. (43)

Section.heading: Mark 6:1-6 Jesus went to his own town but the people rejected him.

Questions.Q: How did the people of Jesus's home town feel about him?
Questions.A: Many people were impressed with him, but then they rejected him anyway. (2-3)

Questions.Q: What caused them to decide to reject him?
Questions.A: They knew that the members of his family were just ordinary people. Therefore they did not believe that he could be anyone special. (2-3)

Questions.Q: Where did Jesus go?
Questions.A: He went to his hometown where his family lived and where he had grown up.
Questions.Note: This was not the place where he was born.

Questions.Q: What did the people of Jesus's home town think about him, his teaching, and his miracles?
Questions.A: They were amazed by his teaching and miracles;
but they knew that he and his family were some of their own village people.
Therefore they thought that he could not be an important person with important teaching. (2-3)

Questions.Q: Did Jesus know how they felt?
Questions.A: Yes, he knew.

Questions.Q: What did he say?
Questions.A: He quoted a saying his people had saying, "Prophets are honored everywhere except in their own home town and among their own people." (4)

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that Jesus did not do many miracles there in his home town?
Questions.A: The people refused to believe that God had sent him. (5)
-OR-
The people knew him when he was a small boy, so they did not honor him as God's prophet. (5)

Questions.Q: What had he been able to do?
Questions.A: He did heal a few sick people. (5)

Questions.Q: How did Jesus feel about the people's reaction to him?
Questions.A: He was really surprised that they did not believe in him. (6)

Section.heading: Mark 6:7-13 Jesus sent out his twelve disciples to preach the gospel and do his work.

Questions.Q: What does this section tell us about Jesus's work and his influencing people?
Questions.A: He had taught and given power/authority to his disciples so that they could teach and help others much as he did. In that way, many more people became aware of what he was doing.

Questions.Q: Whom did Jesus call to come to him at that time?
Questions.A: He called together his twelve disciples whom he had chosen.

Questions.Q: Why did Jesus send them away?
Questions.A: He sent them to do his work.
Questions.Note: We will ask about more specific information later, but check here that the respondents understand that Jesus was sending them to work for him, not just sending them away.

Questions.Q: Did Jesus say that the twelve disciples should travel together?
Questions.A: No. He said that they should go in groups of two. (7)

Questions.Q: What special authority did Jesus give his disciples?
Questions.A: He gave them authority to use God's power to send evil spirits out of people. (7)

Questions.Q: What are some of the things Jesus told the disciples they could and could not take with them on their journey?
Questions.A: They were not to carry food or money or extra clothes with them, only their walking stick. They could wear sandals on their feet. (8-9)

Questions.Q: If the disciples did not take food or money or extra clothing with them, who would take care of that?
Questions.Note: Wherever they went and taught, their hosts were to provide their food and other things.
If they refused to do that, then the disciples should go to another place.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell them about moving around to different homes within the various villages they visited?
Questions.A: He told them to stay only with the people who first invited them until they left that village. (They were not to move out just because they would rather stay some place else.) (10)

Questions.Q: If the people of any town would not listen to them, what were the disciples to do?
Questions.A: They were to shake the dust off their feet as they left the village. That would be a sign of warning to those people. (11)
Questions.Note: This was a cultural way to show clearly that they had given the people of that village a chance to hear God's message, but the people had refused to listen.

Questions.Q: After they had heard Jesus's instructions, what did the disciples do?
Questions.A: They went out and preached the message that everyone should repent and stop sinning. (12)
They also healed many people, and sent demons/evil spirits out of many people. (13)

Questions.Q: What did the disciples do to the sick people before they became well again?
Questions.A: They anointed them with [olive] oil. (13)
Questions.Note: (Key Term Check: Anointed. A person with authority pours or rubs an oil or ointment onto the other person's head or the body part which was hurting. See "anoint" in KBT.)

Section.heading: Mark 6:14-29 Herod ordered his men to behead John the Baptist.

Questions.Q: How did it happen that Herod ordered a soldier to kill John the Baptist?
Questions.A: Herodias and her daughter persuaded Herod to have someone kill John. (21-26)

Questions.Q: What was it that King Herod heard?
Questions.A: He heard about all that Jesus and his disciples were doing. (14)

Questions.Q: What were some people saying about Jesus?
Questions.A: Some people were saying that Jesus was really John the Baptist and that God had raised him back to life. (15)

Questions.Q: What were other people saying about Jesus?
Questions.A: Some said that he was the prophet Elijah.
Others said that he was a prophet like Elijah and other prophets who had spoken for God many years earlier. (15)

Questions.Q: Who did Herod think that Jesus was?
Questions.A: He thought that Jesus was John (the Baptist) whose head he (Herod) had ordered his men to cut off. Herod thought that (God) caused John to become alive again. (16)

Questions.Q: Why had Herod given orders for John the Baptist to be put in prison?
Questions.A: Herod order his men to put John in prison because John had been telling Herod that it was wrong for him (Herod) to have Herodias as his wife. Herodias was Herod's brother's wife (not widow). (18)

Questions.Q: What did Herodias want to happen to John?
Questions.A: She (was very angry and) wanted Herod to order someone to kill John. (19)

Questions.Q: Why was Herodias not able to have John killed?
Questions.A: She was unsuccessful because Herod would not let her do that. (19-20)

Questions.Q: Why would Herod not let her kill John?
Questions.A: Herod knew that John was really a man whom God had set apart to serve him. Therefore, Herod was afraid to kill him.
He also liked to listen to John talk about God, even though it made him quite upset. (20)

Questions.Q: How did Herodias get an opportunity to have someone kill John?
Questions.A: On Herod's birthday her daughter danced for Herod's guests.
Herod was very pleased and made a strong promise to give the girl anything she wanted.
Her mother told her to ask for John the Baptist's head. Therefore that is what she did.(21-24)

Questions.Q: When Herodias's daughter went and asked Herod for John's head, was he happy to give it to her?
Questions.A: No. He was very upset; he did not want to kill John. (25)

Questions.Q: Why did Herod go ahead and order a soldier to kill John?
Questions.A: He was ashamed to break the strong promise he had made in front of his guests. (26)
(Ordering people to be killed was a common practice of some kings in those times.)
Key Term Check: See "oath" in KBT in the "covenant" entry.

Questions.Q: What order did Herod give?
Questions.A: He ordered one of his men to go and cut off John's head and bring it back to him. (27)

Questions.Q: What will people who read the translation think was the reason that someone carried John's head on a plate/tray?
Questions.A: That was the kind of container they thought was best for everyone to see that John was dead. (28)
Questions.Note: Check whether people in the target culture use the item named in the translation for carrying or holding food. No one was intending to eat John's head, so that is not what should be inferred here. The name of a relatively flat, stiff item to carry the head on should be used in the translation instead.
Questions.Alternative: What will people who read the translation think was the reason that someone carried John's head on a plate?
What will people who read the translation think was the reason that someone carried John's head on a tray?

Questions.Q: Why do you think that the girl took John the Baptist's head to her mother?
Questions.A: Her mother could then see for herself that the man she hated so much was truly dead.

Questions.Q: What happened to the body of John the Baptist?
Questions.A: John's disciples came and took it and buried it. (29)

Section.heading: Mark 6:30-44 Jesus fed five thousand men (plus women and children).

Questions.Q: What miracle did Jesus do?
Questions.A: Jesus fed a huge crowd from five loaves of bread and two (cooked) fish.

Questions.Q: What was it that the disciples of Jesus told him?
Questions.A: They told him all about what had happened while they were out preaching and healing people. (30)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to them?
Questions.A: He said that they should all go to a quiet place and rest for a while. (31)

Questions.Q: Why could they not rest right there where they were?
Questions.A: They could not rest there because many people were coming, wanting their attention. (31)

Questions.Q: So what did Jesus and the disciples do?
Questions.A: They got into a boat to go to a quiet place. (32)

Questions.Q: Why were they not able to find a quiet place?
Questions.A: People saw them leaving, so they ran along the shore and arrived at the place where the disciples were going before they did! (33)

Questions.Q: When Jesus saw all the people waiting for them, how did he feel?
Questions.A: He was sorry for them because they were like sheep without anyone to guide and take care of them. (34)

Questions.Q: So what did Jesus do?
Questions.A: He taught them. (34)

Questions.Q: What time of day was it by then?
Questions.A: It was late afternoon. (35)
Questions.Note: Also see 6:47, which must mean "when it became dark".

Questions.Q: Why were the disciples concerned?
Questions.A: They were concerned because the people were hungry and there was no food nearby. (35-36)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to the disciples?
Questions.A: He told them to give the people food to eat. (37)

Questions.Q: Why were the disciples surprised when Jesus told them to do that?
Questions.A: It would have cost them very much to feed all of those people. (37)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus then ask the disciples?
Questions.A: He asked them how many loaves of bread they had. (38)

Questions.Q: What did they answer?
Questions.A: They said that they had five loaves and two (cooked) fish. (38)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus have the disciples do?
Questions.A: He told the disciples to have the people sit down on the grass in groups. (39)

Questions.Q: How were the people arranged on the grass?
Questions.A: They sat down in groups of fifty people and one hundred people. (40)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do then?
Questions.A: He took the five loaves of bread and the two fish and thanked God for them.
Then he broke them in pieces and gave them to his disciples to give to the people. (41)

Questions.Q: How do we know that there was enough food for all of those people to eat all they wanted?
Questions.A: We know there was plenty because it says that they ate and were satisfied, and there was some food left. (42-43)

Questions.Q: How much food was left after everyone had eaten?
Questions.A: There was enough food to fill twelve baskets with the leftover pieces (not crumbs). (43)

Questions.Q: How many people were there in the crowd?
Questions.A: There were five thousand men (plus their wives and children).

Questions.Q: How could all of those people be fed like that?
Questions.A: God caused the food to increase, that is, God did a miracle.

Section.heading: Mark 6:45-52 Jesus walked on the top of the water.

Questions.Q: What was this new miraculous thing that Jesus did?
Questions.A: He walked on top of the sea [lake]. (48)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell his disciples to do?
Questions.A: He told them to get into their boat and go on ahead of him to Bethsaida. (45)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do after they left in the boat?
Questions.A: He stayed on the shore and said goodbye to the many people as they departed. (45)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do after he said good-by to the crowd?
Questions.A: He went up into the hills to pray. (46)

Questions.Q: When it got dark, where was Jesus, and where were his disciples?
Questions.A: He was alone on the land, and the disciples were in the boat in the middle of the lake. (47)

Questions.Q: What trouble were the disciples having?
Questions.A: They were having to row the boat against a strong wind. (48)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do?
Questions.A: He walked on the water to them and started to go past them. (48)

Questions.Q: What happened when the disciples saw Jesus?
Questions.A: They became scared and screamed. (49)

Questions.Q: Why were they so afraid?
Questions.A: They thought that he was a ghost. (49-50)

Questions.Q: Why do you think that they thought he was a ghost?
Questions.A: They thought he was a ghost because ordinarily people cannot walk on water.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to the disciples?
Questions.A: He told them that it was only he, they did not need to be afraid. (50)

Questions.Q: What happened as soon as Jesus got into the boat?
Questions.A: The strong wind ceased. (51)

Questions.Q: Why were the disciples so astonished?
Questions.A: They were surprised because they did not yet understand that Jesus had power to do miracles, such as making food increase, (and walking on water). (52)

Questions.Q: Why do you think that Jesus could do those things?
Questions.A: He is God./He had God's power.

Section.heading: Mark 6:53-56 Jesus healed people at Gennesaret.

Questions.Q: Where did Jesus and his disciples come to land?
Questions.A: They came to land at Gennesaret. (53)

Questions.Q: What happened at Gennesaret as soon as they got out of the boat?
Questions.A: People recognized Jesus, so they ran through the whole region and brought back their sick people for him to heal. (54-55)

Questions.Q: What happened wherever Jesus went?
Questions.A: People brought their sick people to where he was going to pass by in order that they could touch him and be healed. All who even touched the edge of his clothes were healed. (56)

Section.heading: Mark 7:1-23 Jesus explained what causes people to become unclean in God's sight.

Questions.Q: What did some of Jesus's disciples do that the Pharisees saw and became upset?
Questions.A: His disciples ate food without first washing their hands in the proper ritual as their ancestors had said that all Jewish people should do to please God. (2-5)

Questions.Q: What is it that really makes people unclean?
Questions.A: It is the evil things that they think and do, coming from their own evil nature/desires. (23)

Questions.Q: What did some Pharisees and teachers of the law see some of the disciples doing?
Questions.A: They saw them eat without first washing their hands in a special way for ceremonial cleaning. (1-4)

Questions.Q: What did the Pharisees want the disciples to do?
Questions.A: The Pharisees wanted them to clean their hands from a religious uncleanness as their ancestors used to do. (5)
Questions.Note: (Key Term Check: unclean/defiled)

Questions.Q: Why do you think that the Pharisees kept thinking that their custom of special washings was so important?
Questions.A: They believed that people who did not follow this custom, were doing bad in God's sight. They thought that people had to follow certain rituals to stay clean in order to show that they wanted to obey God's laws.

Questions.Q: What did the Pharisees do that caused Jesus to become angry?
Questions.A: They insisted that people must obey their Jewish customs that their ancestors had made,
but were not concerned about obeying what God had commanded. (6-8)

Questions.Q: What might a person that speaks this language do that would cause other of his people to call him a hypocrite?
Questions.A: (Listen for any possible wrong understanding of what Jesus meant here.)

Key Term Check: hypocrite. Such a person pretends to believe or do what other people will approve of or praise him for. He does not do it because he really believes that what he does is right or good.

Questions.Q: What commands/commandments do you think that the Lord expects people to obey?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: commandment. The answer should focus on actions like those God named in the Ten Commandments (Exod. 20:1-17; Deut. 5:1-21. It also may include other instructions God gave to his people, as well.]
Questions.Alternative: What commands do you think that the Lord expects people to obey?
What commandments do you think that the Lord expects people to obey?

Questions.Q: Why did Jesus talk about Isaiah?
Questions.A: Isaiah had written (in the Old Testament) about Jewish people of that time who were just like these Pharisees. Those people acted like they cared for and worked for God, but they really were only concerned with themselves. (6-9)

Questions.Q: Will people who read verse 9 think that Jesus was praising the Pharisees?
Questions.A: He was not praising them. He was angry at what they were doing.
Questions.Note: Jesus was using a figure of speech called irony. That is, he was saying the very opposite of what he meant. When he said, "You have a great way of setting aside God's commandments...," he meant, "You have a very bad way of acting. You ignore God's commands and make up your own rules that do not agree with what God has said."

Questions.Q: Jesus gave an example to show how the Pharisees were teaching the people wrongly. They were not following God and his teaching like they pretended they were. What were they doing?
Questions.A: They said that they were teaching God's laws, while they were actually teaching their Jewish traditions. (9)
Questions.Note: For Mark 7:9-13, use either the group A questions or the group B questions. It would be redundant to ask all 4 questions.
group A (Mrk 7:9-13)

Questions.Q: What was the difference between the command that Moses gave them from God and what the Pharisees were saying and doing?
Questions.A: Moses had given them a firm command that people should respect and help their parents.

The Pharisees were now telling people that if they ever dedicated things to God as an offering, they could not later change their minds and use those things to help their parents, even though their parents may have no other goods or money. (10-12)
-OR-
The Pharisees were now saying that people could avoid giving to their needy parents by making an oath that set aside what they owned as being already dedicated for future offerings to God. (10-12)
Questions.Note: group A (Mrk 7:9-13)

Questions.Q: What did the law say that a man should do to his parents?
Questions.A: Moses wrote in the law that people should honor their father and mother. (10)
People should not speak disrespectfully against their parents. (10)
Jesus implied that this meant that a man should help take care of his parents' needs. (11)
Questions.Note: For Mark 7:9-13, use either the group A questions or the group B questions. It would be redundant to ask all 4 questions.
group B (Mrk 7:9-13)
Questions.Alternative: What did the Law say that a person should do to his parents?
What did the Law say that a person should do for his parents?
How did the Law say that a person should treat his parents?
According to the Law, how were people supposed to treat their parents?
What did the Law say that a person should do to his father and mother?
What did the Law say that a person should do for his father and mother?
How did the Law say that a person should treat his father and mother?
According to the Law, how were people supposed to treat their father and mother?
What did the Law that Moses wrote say that a person should do to his parents?
What did the Law that Moses wrote say that a person should do for his parents?
How did the Law that Moses wrote say that a person should treat his parents?
According to the Law that Moses wrote, how were people supposed to treat their parents?
What did the Law that Moses wrote say that a person should do to his father and mother?
What did the Law that Moses wrote say that a person should do for his father and mother?
How did the Law that Moses wrote say that a person should treat his father and mother?
According to the Law that Moses wrote, how were people supposed to treat their father and mother?

Questions.Q: What did the Pharisees say that a man could do to his parents?
Questions.A: The Pharisees were now telling people that if they ever dedicated things to God as an offering, they could not later change their minds and use those things to help their parents, even though their parents may have no other goods or money. (10-12)
-OR-
The Pharisees were now saying that people could avoid giving to their needy parents by making an oath that set aside what they owned as being already dedicated for future offerings to God. (10-12)
Questions.Note: group B (Mrk 7:9-13)
Questions.Alternative: What did the Pharisees say that a person could do to his parents?
What did the Pharisees say that people could do to avoid helping their parents?
What did the Pharisees say that people could do to avoid this requirement of the Law?
What did the Pharisees say that a person could do instead?

Questions.Q: Why was what the Pharisees were doing so bad?
Questions.A: They were using their own customs and traditions to avoid having to follow God's commandments. (13)
Questions.Alternative: What made the Pharisees' behavior so bad?
What made the Pharisees' behavior so evil?
Why was what the Pharisees were doing so evil?
Why was Jesus so critical of the Pharisees?
Why was Jesus so critical of the Pharisees' behavior?
Why was Jesus so critical of what the Pharisees were doing?
Why was Jesus so angry with the Pharisees?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to all the people?
Questions.A: He said that we can not be made unacceptable to God by what we eat (like wrong food or some uncleanness) coming into our bodies. Rather, it is the evil actions that start in our own inner thoughts that make us unacceptable to God. (15-16)

Questions.Q: Did the other people there that day and the disciples understand easily what Jesus was teaching them?
According to Jesus's explanation to the disciples, what was he talking about when he mentioned, "the things which are outside of people which enter them"?
Questions.A: He was talking about food (and any physical or ritual uncleanness) which goes into people's bodies. (18-19)

Questions.Q: What do you think may have made it difficult for the disciples and the others who heard Jesus teach that day to understand that what people eat does not offend God?
Questions.A: The Jewish religious leaders emphasized a lot of food and touching restrictions. Jesus's teaching was quite different and they had difficulty understanding that he was actually saying that breaking the many of food and pollution restrictions was not what would offend God. They needed to make a decision as to whether they would follow Jesus or their tradition. He said that their slowness to understand was caused by their hardness of heart. (6:52; 8:14-21)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus mean when he spoke of "the things that come out from a person"?
Questions.A: He was talking about the bad things we do because of bad desires that come from within us. (20-23)

Questions.Q: Can you name three of the bad actions which Jesus said start in our own thoughts.
Questions.A: Evil thoughts, sexual immorality, theft/stealing, murder, adultery, (21)
coveting/greed, malice/meanness/wickedness, deceit, lewdness/sensuality, envy, slander/insults, arrogance/pride, folly/foolishness (22)

Section.heading: Mark 7:24-30 A woman from a non-Jewish nation begged Jesus to heal her daughter.

Questions.Q: What did the woman who came to Jesus want him to do for her?
Questions.A: She wanted him to send an evil spirit out of her daughter. (25)

Questions.Q: Why do you think Mark wanted to be sure we knew where this woman came from?
Questions.A: We need to know that to understand what she and Jesus were talking about. Also people need to know that Jesus helps and receives both Jews and non-Jews.

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that Jesus did not want people to know where he was?
Questions.A: He was trying to have a time of quietness away from the many people. (24)

Questions.Q: Where did Jesus go to get away from all those people?
Questions.A: He went to the area near [the city of] Tyre [in the Syrian province of Phoenicia]. (24)

Questions.Q: Why do you think that he was not able to stop people from knowing where he was?
Questions.A: He was not able to remain hidden because he had become well known and people were talking about him [even outside the regions of the Jews]. (24)

Questions.Q: Does Jesus's reply [in verse 27] sound as if he was agreeing to do what the woman had asked?
Questions.A: No, he was not agreeing with her. [He implied that she was like a dog compared to the Jews.]
Questions.Alternative: Does Jesus's reply in verse 27 sound as if he was agreeing to do what the woman had asked?
Does Jesus's reply sound as if he was agreeing to do what the woman had asked?

Questions.Q: What do you think Jesus meant when he talked about children and bread and dogs?
Questions.A: Jesus was saying that he had come to help the "children", the Jews, and that they should be helped first before he helped the "dogs" (which is what Jews sometimes called non-Jews).
Questions.Note: The meaning of what Jesus said here probably will not be easy for people to understood.

Points to check: Is it clear that Jesus was using a "proverb" with figurative meaning? If not, is it possible to include some clue to indicate that? Is the fact that the woman was not a Jew shown plainly enough (vv. 24 & 26)? It may be possible to put that in the section heading.

Questions.Q: How did the woman reply to Jesus?
Questions.A: She said that even the dogs under the table get some of the crumbs. (28)

Questions.Q: What do you think she meant?
Questions.A: She meant that maybe there could be some small amount of help that Jesus could use for a non-Jew, such as her, too. (28)

Questions.Q: Does Jesus's answer to the woman sound as if he was angry with her or pleased about her reply?
Questions.A: He was pleased with her.

Questions.Q: How can you tell that Jesus was pleased with the woman's reply?
Questions.A: He told her that she could go [because he had answered her request and had sent the demon out of her daughter]. (29)

Questions.Q: Why do you think that Jesus was pleased with the woman's reply?
Questions.A: It may have been because she persisted in asking for what she wanted.
-OR-… because she clearly believed that he was able to do it.
-OR-…just because it is in God's plan that his gracious blessings should reach to all people groups.
Questions.Note: This question is a check for any obvious misunderstanding.

Questions.Q: What did the woman find out when she arrived home?
Questions.A: She found out that the demon/evil spirit had left her daughter and she had recovered. (30)

Section.heading: Mark 7:31-37 Jesus healed a man who was deaf and could not speak clearly.

Questions.Q: What miracle did Jesus do next?
Questions.A: He healed a man who was unable to hear and could not speak clearly. (33-35)

Questions.Q: Whom did people bring to Jesus?
Questions.A: They brought a man who was deaf and could not speak properly. (32)

Questions.Q: Why do you think that the people asked Jesus to put his hands on the man?
Questions.A: They wanted Jesus to heal him, to make him able to hear and to speak clearly.

Questions.Q: Where did Jesus take the man?
Questions.A: He took him aside/away from the crowd. (33)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do?
Questions.A: He put his fingers in the man's ears.

Questions.Q: What else did Jesus do after that?
Questions.A: Then he took spit and touched the man's tongue with it. (33)

Questions.Q: Why do you think that Jesus looked toward heaven?
Questions.A: He looked toward heaven because he was praying to God who is in heaven.
-OR-
He looked toward heaven because he wanted the people to know that he was asking God's help as he commanded the man's ears to open.

Questions.Q: What did the word "Ephphatha" from the language the Jews spoke mean?
Questions.A: It means, "Be open!".
-OR- "May these ears be opened!" (33-34)

Questions.Q: How do we know that the man was able to hear and speak?
Questions.A: Mark told us that the man could hear and he began to speak plainly. (The talk in Greek about his tongue being loosened is most likely just a way of saying that he had no more speech problem.) (35)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus command the people who were present?
Questions.A: He said that they should not tell others about what he had done. (36)

Questions.Q: How do we know that the people did not obey Jesus?
Questions.A: Mark told us that they began talking more and more about what Jesus did. (37)

Questions.Q: What did most of the people think when they heard about the man who could now hear and speak?
Questions.A: They said, "Jesus does everything well/just right, even making the deaf people hear and the mute to speak." They were overwhelmed. (37)
Questions.Note: Their statement may have meant that what Jesus did fit well with everything that was predicted about the Messiah for whom they had been waiting. See Isa. 35:3-6.

Section.heading: Mark 8:1-10 Jesus fed four thousand men, plus women and children.

Questions.Q: What miracle did Jesus do?
Questions.A: He fed four thousand men [plus the women and children] from seven loaves of bread and a few small fish. (6-9)

Questions.Q: Why was Jesus feeling sorry for the people?
Questions.A: They were hungry; they had been there with him for three days and had eaten all their food. (2)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus think might happen if they sent the hungry people home?
Questions.A: He thought that some who had come a long way might collapse before reaching home. (3)
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus think might happen if they sent the people home without feeding them?
What did Jesus think might happen if they sent the people home without giving them food?
What did Jesus think might happen if they sent the people home hungry?
What did Jesus think might happen if they sent the hungry people away?
What did Jesus think might happen if they sent the people away without feeding them?
What did Jesus think might happen if they sent the people away without giving them food?
What did Jesus think might happen if they sent the people away hungry?

Questions.Q: What did the disciples think about themselves being able to feed the people?
Questions.A: They thought that it would be impossible to find enough food to feed all those people in that place where few people lived. (4)

Questions.Q: How much bread did the disciples have?
Questions.A: They had seven loaves of bread. (5)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do?
Questions.A: He told the crowd of people to sit down.
Taking the seven loaves of bread and then thanking God for them,
he broke them (in pieces) and gave them to his disciples to pass out to the people. (6)

Questions.Q: What else did they have to eat besides the loaves of bread?
Questions.A: They had a few small fish. (7)
Questions.Alternative: What else did the disciples have to eat besides the loaves of bread?
What else did they have besides the loaves of bread?
What else did the disciples have besides the loaves of bread?

Questions.Q: How much food was left when everyone had eaten enough?
Questions.Note: After they all had eaten, there was enough food left to fill seven baskets with broken pieces. (8)
These pieces were not crumbs.

Questions.Q: How many people were there in the crowd?
Questions.A: There were four thousand [men, plus the women and children]. (9)
Questions.Note: In Matthew's account, it clearly indicates that only men were included in the count. In Mark 6.44, it specifically states "five thousand men", but here in Mark 8:9, it says only "four thousand." Even though the Greek numeral has a masculine declensional ending, this does not necessarily mean that only males are to be considered. If leaving it ambiguous in the translation is an option in the target language, it is fine to do so and thereby reflect the ambiguity of the text in Mark's account. However, in the light of the parrallel account by Matthew, if the target language requires a gender-specific noun here, it would be better to say "men."
Questions.Alternative: How big was the crowd?
How big was the crowd who ate the food?
How big was the crowd of people who ate the food?
How big was the crowd who were served?
How big was the crowd of people who were served?
How big was the crowd that ate the food?
How many people ate the food?
How many ate the food?
How many people were served?
How many were served?

Questions.Q: When the crowd had left, what did Jesus and his disciples do?
Questions.A: They left in a boat and crossed over the lake to the region of Dalmanutha. (10)

Section.heading: Mark 8:11-13 The Pharisees asked Jesus for a miraculous sign to prove that God had sent him.

Questions.Q: When those Pharisees came to Jesus, what do you think that they wanted to do?
Questions.A: They apparently wanted to trick him into making some mistake.
Then they could use that mistake as a reason to say that God had not sent him.

Questions.Q: Did Jesus agree to cause a miraculous sign for them?
Questions.A: No, he refused.
Questions.Note: Key Term Check: See "sign" in KBT in the "miracle" entry.

Questions.Q: Why do you think that Jesus sighed deeply?
Questions.A: He probably sighed deeply because the Pharisees continually rejected him and God's plan for people.

Questions.Q: When Jesus left the Pharisees, where did he go?
Questions.A: To the other side of the Sea of Galillee.
Questions.Note: The name of the body of water is not mentioned explicitly here, but the respondent should understand that he crossed a body of water in the boat.

Section.heading: Mark 8:14-21 Jesus told his disciples to beware of the Pharisees' wrong teaching.

Questions.Q: After reading/hearing these verses do you think Jesus was pleased with his disciples at that time, or not?
Questions.A: He was displeased with them. (17-21)
Questions.Alternative: After reading these verses do you think Jesus was pleased with his disciples at that time, or not?
After hearing these verses do you think Jesus was pleased with his disciples at that time, or not?

Questions.Q: Why did he rebuke them?
Questions.A: He rebuked them because they were so slow to understand what his teaching meant and the true meaning of what he was doing. (17-21)

Questions.Q: What had the disciples forgotten to bring with them?
Questions.A: The disciples had forgotten to bring [an adequate amount of] food. (They had just one loaf of bread with them.) (14)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to them at that time?
Questions.A: He warned them to be careful to avoid "the yeast of the Pharisees and of Herod." (15)

Questions.Q: Tell me about yeast.
Questions.A: Key Term Check: If yeast is mixed with water and honey or sugar, it grows and ferments causing air bubbles. If a person makes dough by adding flour to that mixture, the yeast will spread through to lump of dough and cause it to increase in size.

Questions.Q: What did the disciples think that Jesus was talking about?
Questions.A: The disciples thought that Jesus was talking about (making more) bread.
-OR- They thought that he was pointing out that he was aware of their having forgotten to bring enough food. (16)

Questions.Q: How do we know that Jesus was not talking about the food we call bread?
Questions.A: He compared it to the miracles he had done, not the actual food.

Questions.Q: What do you think that Jesus was meaning when he spoke about yeast?
Questions.A: He was talking about the bad influence of the Pharisees and of Herod. (He was using a common Jewish figurative meaning of yeast as something that people mixed in and it affected all it touched.)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus think about the way that the disciples were reasoning?
Questions.A: He was not pleased. He rebuked them firmly for being so slow to understand that he did not need to be concerned about a shortage of food. (17-21)
Questions.Note: Check that there is strong emotional feeling here. The Greek text shows strong feeling here by a number of rhetorical questions, one after the other.

Section.heading: Mark 8:22-26 Jesus healed a blind man at Bethsaida.

Questions.Q: What miracle did Jesus do?
Questions.A: He healed a blind man. (22-25)

Questions.Q: Why did people bring the blind man to Jesus?
Questions.A: They brought him so that Jesus could touch and heal him. (23-25)

Questions.Q: Why do you think that Jesus led the man out of the village?
Questions.A: He led him away from the crowd of people.
Questions.Note: Check for any misunderstanding.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do to the man?
Questions.A: He spit on his eyes and put his hands on him.
Then he asked the man whether he could see anything. (23)

Questions.Q: How much could the man see immediately?
Questions.A: He could see people walking around, but they looked like trees to him. (24)

Questions.Q: Then what did Jesus do?
Questions.A: He put his hands on the man's eyes a second time. (25)

Questions.Q: Then could he see plainly?
Questions.A: Yes, he could see everything plainly. (25)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to the man when he sent him home?
Questions.A: He told him not to go back into the village. (26)

Section.heading: Mark 8:27-30 Peter stated clearly that Jesus is the Christ/Messiah.

Questions.Q: Who did Peter say that Jesus was?
Questions.A: Peter said to Jesus, "You are the Christ/the Messiah/the anointed one." (29)

Questions.Q: What question did Jesus ask his disciples?
Questions.A: He asked them who people were saying that he was. (27)

Questions.Q: What was their reply?
Questions.A: His disciples said that some people were saying that he was John the Baptist. Some were saying that he was Elijah. Some said that he was one of the Old Testament prophets. (28)

Questions.Q: Who was Elijah?
Questions.A: Elijah was one of the prophets who lived in the time of their ancestors.
Questions.Note: Check that the translation does not contrast Elijah with the prophets in such a way as to imply that Elijah was not one of the prophets.

Questions.Q: Who, or what, do you think that a Christ is?
Questions.A: [Key Term Check: The name "Christ" is a title, not a personal name. The meaning of the word refers to anointing God's special representatives with olive oil. The Christ was the one whom God had sent especially to save God's people. (See "Christ" and "Messiah" in KBT in the "Christ" entry.) ]
Questions.Note: You may wish to make a footnote or glossary entry which indicates that this is the Greek equivalent to the Hebrew title "Messiah".

Questions.Q: Did Jesus say that what Peter said was not true?
Questions.A: No.

Questions.Q: Why do you think that Jesus told his disciples not to tell people who he was?
Questions.A: He may have told them that because at that time he wanted people to believe in him for what he himself did and said, rather than what others said.
-OR-
He may have told them that because Jewish leaders and others might immediately reject him before they personally saw him and heard him speak.

Section.heading: Mark 8:31-9:1 Jesus told his disciples that people would kill him and that he would rise to life again on the third day after that.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say was going to happen to him?
Questions.A: He said that the leaders of the people would reject and kill him,
and that he would rise to live again on the third day after that. (31)

Questions.Q: What must everyone who wants to be a follower of Jesus do?
Questions.A: They must put their own desires second to what Jesus wants,
and be ready to suffer, even die, if it becomes necessary. (34-35)

Questions.Q: About whom was Jesus speaking when he talked about the "Son of Man"?
Questions.A: He was speaking of himself.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say would happen to him as time went on?
Questions.A: He said that he would experience great difficulties.
The Jewish leaders (that is, the elders, the chief priests, and the teachers of the law) would reject him,
and people would kill him,
but after three days he would rise to live again. (31)

Questions.Q: How do we know that the disciples did not understand what Jesus was talking about?
Questions.A: Peter was not happy with what Jesus said.
He tried to tell Jesus that it must not happen like that. (32)

Questions.Q: How did Jesus reply to Peter?
Questions.A: He rebuked him. (33)

Questions.Q: Why do you think that Jesus called Peter "Satan"?
Questions.A: Jesus referred to Peter as Satan because he knew that Satan was trying to use Peter's words to persuade Jesus to not be willing to die to save people. (33)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to Peter about Peter's way of thinking?
Questions.A: He told Peter that he was thinking about things that were important to humans [such as staying alive].
He was not thinking about things that were important to God. (33)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus mean when he said that they must "take up their cross"?
Questions.A: He meant that they must be ready to be criticized, to suffer and even to die so that they could identify themselves as his followers no matter what happened to them as a result. (34)

Questions.Q: What was Jesus teaching here?
Questions.A: He was teaching that a person who wants to have a good life in this world, [and gain things for his own pleasure] will lose his true (eternal) life.

On the other hand, God will give eternal life to people who are willing to serve Jesus and tell the Good News, even if it means that they will suffer or that someone will kill them because of their serving him. (35)
Key Term Check: See "save" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think that a person can do in order that he may experience eternal life?
Questions.A: There is nothing that a person can trade for eternal life. It is impossible to buy back your own soul/life. [Key Term Check: See "soul" in KBT.]
Questions.Note: This is implied by Jesus using rhetorical questions (that is, questions that do not expect an answer), as he did in verses 36 and 37.

Questions.Q: What warning did Jesus give?
Questions.A: Jesus warned against people being ashamed of openly being associated with him. He said that if anyone is ashamed in this world now to say that they follow Jesus and what he teaches, then Jesus will reject them when he (Jesus) comes back to this world again. (38)

Questions.Q: What will people see when Jesus returns to earth as the Son of Man?
Questions.A: They will see his father's glory and the holy angels will be with him. (38)

Questions.Q: What do you think that glory is which people will see?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: As mentioned above (see 2:12), glory has many aspects of meaning. Here the meaning focuses on God's goodness and greatness shown by a bright, beautiful light surrounding Jesus and the angels.
Questions.Note: See "glory" in KBT. (Also see "holy" at 1:24, above.)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell the people that they were going to see?
Questions.A: He said that they would see God ruling in a new way. (1)

Questions.Q: When were people going to see this?
Questions.A: They would see this soon, within the lifetime of some of the people who were standing there. (1)

Section.heading: Mark 9:2-13 Jesus changed in his appearance and three of his disciples saw his glory.

Questions.Q: What happened to Jesus on the mountain?
Questions.A: The way Jesus looked changed, and, for a while, the disciples saw him in a dazzling white brightness (that is, God's glory). They were able to see him more clearly as the pure and powerful person he really is. (2-3)

Questions.Q: Whom did Jesus take up the hill with him?
Questions.A: He took three of his disciples: Peter, James, and John. (2)

Questions.Q: When they first arrived on the mountain, who else was there with them?
Questions.A: No one; they were all alone. (2)

Questions.Q: Who else then appeared, and what did they do?
Questions.A: Elijah and Moses appeared and talked with Jesus. (4)

Questions.Q: What did Peter say to Jesus about what he was seeing?
Questions.A: He said that it was good that he and the other two disciples were there.
They should put up three shelters: one for Jesus, one for Moses, and one for Elijah. (5)

Questions.Q: Why did Peter say that?
Questions.A: He was so very afraid because of what he was seeing, that he apparently thought that he would feel better if he said something. (6)

Questions.Q: Whose voice do you think it was that they heard speaking?
Questions.A: They heard God speak.

Questions.Q: How do you know that God spoke?
Questions.A: Mark wrote that the voice came from heaven [where God lives]
and that he called Jesus his son. (7)

Questions.Q: What did he say about Jesus, his son?
Questions.A: He said that he loves Jesus, and that [the disciples] should listen to him. (7)

Questions.Q: What did the disciples notice then?
Questions.A: They noticed that they could no longer see Moses and Elijah; [they had gone]. (8)

Questions.Q: What instructions did Jesus give the disciples as they were coming down from the hilltop?
Questions.A: He told them not to tell people what they had seen until later when he had risen from the dead. (9)

Questions.Q: How do you know that the disciples did not understand what he meant?
Questions.A: Mark wrote that they did not tell others, but discussed among themselves what he meant by "rising from being dead." (10)

Questions.Q: What question did the disciples ask Jesus?
Questions.A: They asked him why the teachers of the law said that Elijah must come before the Christ/Messiah would come. (11)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus reply?
Questions.A: He said that it was true that Elijah had to come first [before the Messiah/Christ]. (12)

He also said that Elijah had come already. When he came, however, people had treated him badly, doing whatever they liked to him, just like [the prophets long ago had predicted] in what they had written. (13)

Questions.Q: Of what fact about himself did Jesus remind them again?
Questions.A: He reminded them again that [the prophets long ago] had written in God's Book that he, the Son of Man, would have to suffer much [pain] and be rejected [by the people]. (12)

Section.heading: Mark 9:14-29 Jesus sent an evil spirit out of a boy.

Questions.Q: What miracle did Jesus do?
Questions.A: He sent an evil spirit out of a boy. (25-26)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus and the three disciples see when they came down from the hill?
Questions.A: They saw a large crowd of people gathered together where some teachers of the law were arguing with the other disciples. (14)

Questions.Q: What did the people do when they saw Jesus?
Questions.A: They were amazed and they ran to greet him. (15)

Questions.Q: Why do you think that they were so amazed?
Questions.A: Probably they were amazed because he was coming just when they needed him. (15)
Questions.Note: There could be other reasons. Mark did not tell us.

Questions.Q: What question did Jesus ask his disciples?
Questions.A: He asked them what they were discussing so much. (16)

Questions.Q: Who replied to Jesus's question, and what did he say?
Questions.A: A man in the crowd replied. He said that he brought his son who was possessed by an evil spirit that made him unable to speak. He said that he had asked the disciples to send the spirit out of the boy, but they had not been able to do so. (17-18)

Questions.Q: What did the man say that the spirit had caused the boy to do?
Questions.A: The spirit caused the boy to be unable to speak.
At times it would also throw him on the ground and cause him to foam at the mouth,
grind his teeth, and become rigid. (18)

Questions.Q: How do we know that Jesus was upset about what had been happening there?
Questions.A: He showed that he was disappointed that they still did not believe in his power after all he had done and said to them.
He told them [in a sharp manner] to bring the boy to him. (19)
Questions.Note: Check that there is strong emotional feeling here. The Greek text shows strong feeling here by a number of rhetorical questions, one after the other.

Questions.Q: What happened when the spirit saw Jesus?
Questions.A: It immediately threw the boy to the ground and caused him to convulse violently. (20)

Questions.Q: How long had the boy been like that?
Questions.A: The father said that the boy had been like that since he was a small child. (21)

Questions.Q: Did the man believe that Jesus could heal his son?
Questions.A: He was not sure. (22)

Questions.Q: How often did that spirit bother the boy?
Questions.A: The evil spirit attacked the boy so often that it was destroying/killing the boy. (22)

Questions.Q: What words did the man say that surprised Jesus?
Questions.A: Jesus was surprised that the man said, "If you can, …." (23)
Questions.Alternative: What words did the man say that Jesus challenged?
What words did the man say that caught Jesus' attention?
What did the man say that Jesus challenged?
What did the man say that caught Jesus' attention?
What words did the father say that Jesus challenged?
What words did the father say that caught Jesus' attention?
What did the father say that Jesus challenged?
What did the father say that caught Jesus' attention?
What did the father say that surprised Jesus?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about the man's words "If you can, …"?
Questions.A: He gently rebuked the man, saying that it was not a problem of Jesus's ability, but rather a problem of whether the man would believe (that is, keep on trusting) in Jesus. (23)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell the man about believing that he (Jesus) could help the boy?
Questions.A: He told him that, if a person believes when he asks [God] to do something, then [God] will do what he asks of him. (23)
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus tell the man about believing?
What did Jesus say about the importance of believing?

Questions.Q: What did the man say about believing?
Questions.A: He told Jesus that he did believe [that Jesus could do it for him].
He begged Jesus to help his tendency to not believe [enough that Jesus was able to help him].
-OR-
He begged Jesus to help his son, even though he himself had a tendency to not believe well. (24)
Questions.Alternative: What did the man say about his belief?
What did the man say about his ability to believe fully?

Questions.Q: Why did Jesus speak to the spirit to send it out of the boy at that particular time?
Questions.A: He began to send the spirit out of the boy right then because a crowd of (curious) people was running together (around him). (25)

Questions.Q: When Jesus spoke to the spirit, what happened to the boy?
Questions.A: The spirit shrieked/screamed, shook the boy violently, and came out of him.
The boy lay still, like a dead person. (26)
Questions.Alternative: When Jesus spoke to the spirit, what happened?
When Jesus rebuked the spirit, what happened to the boy?
When Jesus rebuked the spirit, what happened?
When Jesus commanded the spirit to come out, what happened to the boy?
When Jesus commanded the spirit to come out, what happened?
When Jesus commanded the spirit to leave the boy, what happened?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do to him then?
Questions.A: Jesus took his hand and helped him to stand up. (27)

Questions.Q: What did the disciples ask Jesus about that event?
Questions.A: They asked him why they were not able to send out that evil spirit from the boy. (28)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus reply?
Questions.A: He replied that one can send out such a spirit only through praying. (29)

Section.heading: Mark 9:30-32 Jesus again told his disciples that someone would betray him and kill him.

Questions.Q: What was Jesus encouraging his disciples to understand?.
Questions.A: He wanted them to realize that he would be killed and would rise to live again. (31)

Questions.Q: Why did Jesus not want people to know where he was at that time?
Questions.A: Jesus did not want people to know where he was right then because he wanted to be able to teach his disciples privately. (30-31)

Questions.Q: What was he teaching them?
Questions.A: He was teaching them that (someone) was going to betray him to other men who would kill him, the Son of Man, but after three days he would rise to life again. (31)

Questions.Q: What do you think about the disciples having so much difficulty understanding what Jesus said about dying and rising again?
Questions.A: They expected him to become their king soon and dying did not seem to them like it could be related to what they expected the Christ/Messiah to do.
Questions.Alternative: Why do you think the disciples had so much difficulty understanding what Jesus said about dying and rising again?

Questions.Q: What kept the disciples from asking Jesus to explain what he meant about dying and rising to live again?
Questions.A: They were afraid to ask him.. (32)

Section.heading: Mark 9:33-37 Jesus told his disciples that, if they wanted to be great in God's kingdom, they must be servants to all people.

Questions.Q: What was Jesus trying to make his disciples understand?
Questions.A: He wanted them to understand that anyone who wants to be ranked as first (most important) in the kingdom of God must have the attitude of being the least important person and serve others. (35)
Questions.Note: (Key Term Check: See "servant" in KBT.)

Questions.Q: What were the disciples arguing about as they traveled along?
Questions.A: They were arguing about which of them was the most important [among them]. (34)

Questions.Q: How do we know that Jesus knew what they had been arguing about?
Questions.A: Mark wrote that Jesus began to talk about people being first (most important) and last (least important). (35)

Questions.Q: Why did Jesus take a small child in his arms?
Questions.A: He wanted to show the disciples that they should not worry about how important they were relative to others. They should be helpful to everyone, including those who appear less important, such as a child. (36-37)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to do something "in the name of Jesus"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Doing something in the name of Jesus means doing it as Jesus's representative, (that is, in his place, or because of love for him). Jesus was holy and he perfectly reflected God's love to all who would accept him. Jesus did not work in order to gain honor for himself. He served God because of is love for him. When a person does like that because of Jesus, he does it "in Jesus's name". (See "in the name of" in KBT in the "name" entry.)

Section.heading: Mark 9:38-41 Jesus said that whoever is not opposing him and his people is on his side.
