Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about people who do good things in his name, even though they are not in association with his other followers?
Questions.A: He said that we should allow them to keep on doing good things in his name. (39)

Questions.Q: What was it that the disciples had seen which they did not like?
Questions.A: They had seen a person who was not one of their group driving out demons/evil spirits in the Jesus's name. (38)

Questions.Q: What had they said to the person?
Questions.A: They had told him to stop using Jesus's name when he wanted to expel demons from people. (38)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to his disciples about telling that person to stop?
Questions.A: He said that they should allow such a person to continue. (39)

Questions.Q: Why should he continue?
Questions.A: If people do miracles in Jesus's name, they will only speak well of him. They are really on his side. (39-40)

Questions.Q: What else did Jesus say?
Questions.A: He said that God will be sure to reward anyone who gives even a cup of cold water to a follower of his because of their being his follower. (41)

Section.heading: Mark 9:42-50 Jesus warned his disciples to be careful not to do anything that would cause people who believe in him to fall away.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus teach here?
Questions.A: He taught that it is a serious thing for a person to do anything that would cause one of his "little ones" to sin.
Also, we must be serious enough to do what ever it takes to stop sinning.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about any person who would cause an immature follower of his to sin?
Questions.A: He said that it would have been better for that person if someone had caused him to (sink to the bottom of deep water and) drown first so that he would not have lived to cause the other person to fall away from Christ. (The punishment from God will be worse than drowning.) (42)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus teach in these verses?
Questions.A: When people sin it is very serious matter. We must stop sinning, no matter what we lose because of stopping. (43-47)

Questions.Q: What will happen to people who continue in sin?
Questions.A: God will have his angels throw them into hell because of it. (46-47)

Questions.Q: What kind of a place is the place where they will throw the sinners?
Questions.A: Hell is a very undesirable place of torment. It is described as being like a rubbish heap, where the fire keeps burning and the maggots keep chewing. (47-48)
Questions.Note: (Key Term Check: hell)

Questions.Q: Do you think that God wants people to cut off part of their body or gouge out an eye if it causes them to sin?
Questions.A: No. He does not want that. Jesus was teaching how very serious sin is so people would understand that and not sin. By not sinning, they would avoid God's serious punishment for disobeying him, that punishment being even worse than cutting off part of one's body. (48)

Questions.Q: Why is it necessary for people to go through difficulties (like being "sprinkled with fire")?
Questions.A: In this way they will become more serious and more pure like God wants them to be.
(Just as intense heat purifies metal as it is being made, so a sprinkling of difficulties in our lives tends to cause us to allow God to cleanse us and make us useful to him.)
Questions.Note: There are different possible interpretations of verse 49. Check which interpretation the translators used in the translation. See if it fits with what Mark wrote before and after this verse.

Questions.Q: What was Jesus encouraging the disciples to do?
Questions.A: Jesus was encouraging the disciples to live the kind of lives God wanted them to live
and to have peace among themselves.
Questions.Note: There are different possible interpretations of this section on salt and fire. The figurative use of salt here could refer to the flavoring quality or the preserving quality of salt. Watch especially for wrong meaning that does not fit general Biblical teaching. Check the meaning understood by those who hear or read this to see if it fits this context.

Section.heading: Mark 10:1-12 Jesus said that when anyone divorces their wife or husband they break God's command.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus teach about divorce?
Questions.A: He taught that God joined husbands and wives and they should never divorce. (5-8)

Questions.Q: What question did the Pharisees ask Jesus?
Questions.A: They asked Jesus whether it was against the law [of God] for a man to divorce his wife. (2)

Questions.Q: Why did they ask Jesus that question?
Questions.A: They were testing him, (trying to get him to say something that they could use against him.) (2)

Questions.Q: How did Jesus answer them?
Questions.A: He asked them what Moses had commanded about divorce [when he wrote God's laws]. (3)

Questions.Q: What did the Pharisees reply?
Questions.A: The Pharisees said that Moses did allow a man to write a paper/certificate of divorce and to send his wife away with it. (4)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about why Moses made a rule about men writing out a notice of divorce when divorcing their wives?
Questions.A: Jesus said that Moses made that rule about writing a divorce notice because of people stubbornly resisting God's [true] way for them. (5)
Questions.Note: Moses did not start the divorcing. He knew that men were divorcing their wives and he insisted that if they were doing that, they must give the wife an official notice. In that way people would know that the man and woman had divorced.

Questions.Q: What was God's plan for married couples?
Questions.A: God intended that a man should leave his parents and have a very strong tie with his wife—their special relationship makes them one unit, so people should not separate them. (6-9)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus teach about divorced people marrying again?
Questions.A: He said that, if a man divorces his wife or a woman her husband and then marries again, he/she commits adultery. (11-12)

Questions.Q: What does a person do when he or she commits adultery?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Adultery. A married person has sexual intercourse with someone who is not that married person's spouse. This term is also used in the cases where an unmarried person has sexual intercourse with someone who is married.

Section.heading: Mark 10:13-16 People brought small children to Jesus and he blessed them.

Questions.Q: How did Jesus feel about children coming to him?
Questions.A: He was happy for the children to come to him. (14)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about the only way that a person can come under God's rule and authority?
Questions.A: He said that a person must submit to God as a child does. (15)

Questions.Q: What was happening that the disciples did not like?
Questions.A: People were bringing small children to Jesus. (13)

Questions.Q: What did the people want Jesus to do?
Questions.A: The people wanted Jesus to touch the children. (13)

Questions.Q: Why [did the people want Jesus to touch the children]?
Questions.A: They wanted him to bless them. (16)
Questions.Alternative: Why?
Why did the people want Jesus to touch the children?

Questions.Q: What did the disciples do?
Questions.A: They rebuked the people and tried to stop them from bringing their children to Jesus. (13)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say?
Questions.A: Jesus said that they should permit the children to come to him. (14)

Questions.Q: What else did he say about that?
Questions.A: He also said that the citizens of God's kingdom are people who will accept God's rule over them as children do. A person can only become one of God's people by becoming like a child. (15)

Questions.Q: What do you think that the people who read this translation will think Jesus meant when he said that they must become like a child?
Questions.A: It should mean that people must be humble and simple enough to believe what God says
and then follow through by obeying him.
Questions.Note: This is a check for any misunderstanding from what "like a child" may mean in a different culture from where Jesus said it.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think that the people who read this will think Jesus meant when he said that they must become like a child?
What do you think that the people who hear this will think Jesus meant when he said that they must become like a child?
What do you think Jesus meant when he said that they must become like a child?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do with the children?
Questions.A: He took them up in his arms, put his hands on them, and blessed them. (16)

Questions.Q: When people read that Jesus "blessed" them, what will they think that he did?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He probably said, "May God bless you." That was how the Jewish religious teachers used to do at that time. (See "bless" in KBT.

Section.heading: Mark 10:17-22 Jesus talked to a rich young man about eternal life.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell the rich man that he would have to do in order to receive eternal life?
Questions.A: He told him that he needed to sell all his possessions, give the money to the poor, and then be one of Jesus's followers. (21)

Questions.Q: As Jesus was leaving that place, what did one man do?
Questions.A: He ran to Jesus and knelt down in front of him.

Questions.Q: What question did he ask Jesus?
Questions.A: He asked Jesus what he must do in order to have eternal life.

Questions.Q: What kind of life do you think eternal life is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Eternal life is not affected by time. God can cause it to begin now while we are still alive and it will go on forever, even after our bodies die.
Questions.Note: See "life" in KBT.

Questions.Q: How did the man address Jesus?
Questions.A: He called Jesus "Good teacher/master."

Questions.Q: When Jesus replied to the man, did he mean that the man should not call him "good"?
Questions.A: No.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus want the man to think about when he asked him why he called him good, and then said that only God is good?
Questions.A: Jesus wanted the man to realize that Jesus was good because he is God's anointed one (the Christ). (18)

Questions.Q: In Jesus reply to the man, what did he indicate that a person needs to do in order to have eternal life?
Questions.A: Jesus showed that people need to obey God's commandments. (19)

Questions.Q: What kind of life had the man lived?
Questions.A: He had been obeying God's commandments all his life. (20)

Questions.Q: How did Jesus feel as he looked at the man?
Questions.A: He loved him. (He knew that the man was sincerely asking these questions, not just "testing" him as others often did.) (21)

Questions.Q: What else did Jesus tell the man to do?
Questions.A: Jesus said that he must sell all his possessions and give the money to the poor.
Then he would receive his reward in heaven.
He also told him that when he had done that, he should come and follow Jesus. (21)

Questions.Q: How did the young man respond to what Jesus said?
Questions.A: He was sad, and went away. (22)

Questions.Q: Why did the man feel sad?
Questions.A: He owned many things [and did not want to sell them]. (22)

Section.heading: Mark 10:23-27 Jesus said that it is difficult for a rich person to come under God's rule.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell his disciples?
Questions.A: He told them that it is hard for a rich person to become one that God rules over. (23)

Questions.Q: Why do you think that Jesus said that it is hard for a rich person to become one of God's people?
Questions.A: He said that because their possessions can be more important to them than doing what God wants them to do.
Questions.Note: This is a check for misunderstanding. Jesus did not say that rich people cannot come under God's rule. He only said that possessing many things makes it harder to submit to God.

Questions.Q: What illustration did Jesus use to show how hard it is for a rich person to become a citizen of God's kingdom?
Questions.A: Jesus said that it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to become one that God truly rules over. (24-25)

Questions.Q: What did the disciples think when they heard what Jesus said?
Questions.A: They could hardly believe what he said. (26)

Questions.Q: Why were they so amazed?
Questions.A: They thought [if it was difficult for people whom God had favored to be under God's rule] how could ordinary people [like them] be accepted by God? (27)
Questions.Note: The Jews thought that if a person was rich, that was a sign that God was very pleased with him.

Questions.Q: Did Jesus say it was impossible for a rich person to become a citizen of God's kingdom?
Questions.A: No, he said that the love of riches makes it almost impossible for a person to stop trusting the riches and only trust God. (God, of course, can do all kinds of things, including help a rich person understand that God's plan for him is more important than all kinds of riches.) (27)

Section.heading: Mark 10:28-31 Jesus talked about people who give up a lot to be a follower of Christ.

Questions.Q: What was Jesus promising to those who leave things behind in order to obey and serve him?
Questions.A: In this world they will receive more good things than they have to leave behind in order to follow God.
Also, [people will] persecute them, causing them to suffer, but later they will live with God forever. (29-30)

Questions.Q: What did Peter say to Jesus?
Questions.A: He said that he and the other disciples had left everything in order to follow him. (28)

Questions.Q: (Ask, if not already clear.) What did Jesus say will happen to those who leave their homes and the people in their families for the sake of Jesus and telling the Good News?
Questions.A: They will receive much more than they have left in this world,
though at the same time [other people] will persecute them and cause them to suffer. (29-30)

Questions.Q: What will happen to them after this present life ends?
Questions.A: They will live on forever [with God]. (30)

Questions.Q: What do you think Jesus meant by the saying, "Many who are first will be last"?
Questions.A: He meant that many of those people whom the society or culture honors the most in this life will be honored the least in the next life.

Section.heading: Mark 10:32-34 Jesus again predicted his death to his disciples.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell his disciples would happen to him when they reached Jerusalem?
Questions.A: He told them that someone would betray him,
others would condemn him to die and then put him under the control of non-Jews (33),
who would mock him, beat him, kill him,
and after three days he would rise again from being dead. (34)

Questions.Q: Where were Jesus and his disciples going?
Questions.A: They were going to Jerusalem.

Questions.Q: As Jesus walked on ahead of the disciples and others following them, what were their feelings?
Questions.A: They were bewildered and afraid. (32)

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that they were afraid to go to Jerusalem?
Questions.A: They knew that the Jewish leaders there did not like Jesus
and wanted to cause him to stop teaching and doing miracles.

Questions.Q: Jesus said that someone was going to betray him. To whom would that person betray him?
Questions.A: He said that that person would betray him to the chief priests and the teachers of the law. (33)

Questions.Q: What would those leaders do to him?
Questions.A: Those leaders would decide that he should be killed,
and then they would hand him over to non-Jewish people. (33)
Key Term Check: See "Gentiles" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say that the non-Jews would do to him?
Questions.A: They would mock him, spit on him, beat him and kill him. (34)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say would happen to him after he died?
Questions.A: He said that after three days he would rise to live again. (34)

Section.heading: Mark 10:35-45 James and John asked Jesus to do something for them.

Questions.Q: What did James and John ask of Jesus?
Questions.A: They asked that when Jesus had the honor of being king in God's kingdom he would allow one of them to sit at his right side and the other at his left side (that is, in the seats for the most-honored people, one on each side of him). (37)
Questions.Note: In Jewish custom the right hand side of important people was the most honored position anyone could ever have. The left hand side was the next most honored position.

Questions.Q: Who do you think would decide about the people who will be honored in the kingdom of God?
Questions.A: God [the Father] has already decided who will have that honor. (40)

Questions.Q: What was Jesus trying to make his disciples understand?
Questions.A: Anyone who wants to be first in importance in the kingdom of God must have the attitude of a slave (that is, he must regard himself as the least important person of all, and serve all the others). (44)
Questions.Note: (Key Term Check: See "slave" in KBT in the "servant" entry.)

Questions.Q: How did Jesus answer James and John's request?
Questions.A: He told them that they did not know what they were [really] asking.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus then ask them?
Questions.A: He asked them whether they would be able to drink [what was in] the cup that he would have to drink.
And he asked them if they would be able to endure being baptized in the way that he would be baptized. (38)

Questions.Q: What do you think Jesus meant when he said [in verse 38], "Can you drink the cup that I drink?"
Questions.A: He was asking if they could endure the kind of suffering that he would experience.
Questions.Note: The figure of speech in Greek referring to drinking from a cup came from comparing a difficult experience to drinking a bitter fluid, possibly even a poison which would cause people to die.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think Jesus meant when he said in verse 38, "Can you drink the cup that I drink?"
What do you think Jesus meant when he said, "Can you drink the cup that I drink?"

Questions.Q: What do you think Jesus meant by his question asking if they would be able to endure being baptized the same as he would endure being baptized?
Questions.A: In this second figure of speech he was not talking about his being baptized. He had already been baptized by John the Baptist a couple of years before this time. He was comparing having many troubles to being totally surrounded by water as when people are baptized. His meaning here was something like, "You want the glory of this leadership position, but have you thought it through? Can you endure the deep sufferings like I will have to endure before taking that position?"

Questions.Q: What did James and John reply?
Questions.A: They told Jesus that they were ready [to do whatever was necessary]. (39)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to them then?
Questions.A: He agreed that they would experience some of the same suffering,
but he said that he was not the one to decide who would get what position [of honor]. (39-40)

Questions.Q: What did the other ten disciples think when they heard what James and John had asked?
Questions.A: They were angry with them. (41)

Questions.Q: Why do you think that they were angry with James and John?
Questions.A: They probably were angry because they thought that James and John were trying to get ahead of them in the kingdom of God.

Questions.Q: Among those who are not God's people, how do rulers and leaders behave?
Questions.A: They like to get important positions and use their authority to give orders to others. (42)

Questions.Q: How should the followers of Jesus be different than those leaders?
Questions.A: Anyone who wants to be great among the followers of Jesus must become a servant to all the others, whether they are of high or low social position. (43)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about himself?
Questions.A: He said that he came to serve others, not for them to serve him,
and he came to exchange his life as a ransom for the lives of the many people.
(That is he, one person, came in order to die so that the many people [on earth] could be free to live forever.) (45)
Key Term Check: See "ransom" in KBT in the "redeem" entry.

Section.heading: Mark 10:46-52 Jesus healed a blind man named Bartimaeus/Son of Timaeus.

Questions.Q: What miracle did Jesus do?
Questions.A: He caused a blind man (named Bartimaeus/Son of Timaeus) to see again. (52)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus then say was the cause of that man being able to see again?
Questions.A: Jesus said that the reason was that he believed that Jesus would heal him [with power from God]. (52)

Questions.Q: Who was with Jesus at that time?
Questions.A: His disciples and a big crowd of people were with him. (46)

Questions.Q: What were they all doing with Jesus?
Questions.A: They were approaching [the town of] Jericho (46) as they walked to Jerusalem (see verse 32).

Questions.Q: Who was sitting beside the road there?
Questions.A: A blind man named Bartimaeus was sitting beside the road begging [for money]. (46)

Questions.Q: What did this blind man do when he heard that Jesus was passing by?
Questions.A: He started to shout out, begging Jesus to help him. (47)
Questions.Note: (Key Term Check: mercy. See 5:19.)

Questions.Q: Do you think that the blind man had heard about Jesus before?
Questions.A: He seemed to know that Jesus could heal people, and he called him "Son of [King] David," implying that he knew who Jesus was. (47)

Questions.Q: In what way, do you think, was Jesus the "Son of David"?
Questions.A: He was the descendant of King David.
Questions.Note: God had said a descendant of King David would be the one to save God's people. (Key Term Check: See "Son of David" in KBT in the "Christ" entry.)

Questions.Q: What did the people near the blind man try to do?
Questions.A: They tried to stop him from calling out to Jesus. (48)

Questions.Q: How do we know that he did not follow their advice?
Questions.A: He went on shouting more and more. (48)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do when he heard the blind man shouting?
Questions.A: He stopped and had the people there call the blind man [to come] over [to him]. (49)

Questions.Q: What did the blind man do?
Questions.A: The blind man threw aside his cloak [in order to move faster], jumped up quickly, and went to Jesus. (50)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus ask the blind man?
Questions.A: Jesus asked him what he wanted Jesus to do for him. (51)
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus say to the blind man?

Questions.Q: What did the man want Jesus to do for him?
Questions.A: He wanted to see [again]. (51)

Questions.Q: What do you think was the blind man's attitude to Jesus?
Questions.A: He was very respectful. He called Jesus "Rabbi" (that is, "Teacher"). (51)
Key Term Check: See "Rabbi" in KBT in the "Christ" entry.

Questions.Q: What happened then?
Questions.A: The man could see, and he followed Jesus along the road. (52)

Section.heading: Mark 11:1-11 Jesus entered Jerusalem like a king.

Questions.Q: How did the people receive Jesus when he reached Jerusalem?
Questions.A: They shouted happily, welcoming him as their king. (8-10)

Questions.Q: Where were the villages of Bethphage and Bethany?
Questions.A: They were on the hill called "the mountain of Olives," quite near to Jerusalem. (1)

Questions.Q: What instructions did Jesus give to two of his disciples?
Questions.A: He told them to go to the village [that they could see] ahead of them, enter it,
and they would find a young donkey tied there, one that no one had ever ridden.
He said that they were to untie it and bring it [to him]. (2)

Questions.Q: What should they say if anyone asked them what they were doing?
Questions.A: They were to say that the Lord needed [the donkey] and would send it back soon. (3)

Questions.Q: What happened when the disciples reached the village?
Questions.A: They found the donkey just as Jesus had said that they would. (4)
People asked them why they were untying it. (5)
They told [them] that Jesus had told them to [do it]. -OR-
They told [them] what Jesus had told them to say. (6)
The people allowed them to take it [to Jesus]. (4-6)

Questions.Q: What happened after the two disciples brought the young donkey to Jesus?
Questions.A: Some disciples threw their outer clothing over the donkey's back for Jesus to sit on. (7)
Many people spread their outer clothing on the road,
and other people spread [palm] branches on the road. (8)

Questions.Q: Why do you think that they were doing like that?
Questions.A: They did it to prepare the path in a special way to honor Jesus like they did their kings.

Questions.Q: What did the people shout?
Questions.A: They shouted praises for Jesus, saying that God had blessed him by giving him power to save them. (9)

Questions.Q: Whom did they say Jesus was representing?
Questions.A: They said that Jesus was representing God. (9)

Questions.Q: What do you think that they thought was going to happen?
Questions.A: They apparently thought that Jesus would immediately fulfill the Old Testament prophesies about the Messiah/Christ setting up his kingdom on earth. (They probably thought that Jesus would become king over their land, perhaps even the world, and cause the Romans to leave their country.) (10)

Questions.Q: After entering Jerusalem, where did Jesus go?
Questions.A: He went to the temple area. (11)
Questions.Note: (Key Term Check: See "temple" in KBT.)

Questions.Q: What did he do when he reached the temple?
Questions.A: He looked around and then went back to Bethany, since it was late [in the day]. (11)

Section.heading: Mark 11:12-19 Jesus drove the traders out of the temple courtyard.

Questions.Q: What happened the next morning as Jesus and his disciples were walking along?
Questions.A: Jesus saw a fig tree. He went and checked it for fruit,
and finding it had none, said that it would never bear fruit again. (12-14)

Questions.Q: Why do you think that Jesus was so angry at the businessmen in the temple courtyard?
Questions.A: He was angry because those people were not thinking about God and praying to him there at the temple, but were using the temple area for getting a profit, just like a group of robbers would do.
-OR-
In the noise of doing their business, they were making it hard for other people who really had come there to pray. (17)

Questions.Q: Why did Jesus go to look at the fig tree?
Questions.A: He went and looked because he was hungry. He wanted to see if it had anything to eat on it. (12)

Questions.Q: Why did the tree not have any figs on it?
Questions.Note: It did not have figs because it was not the time for figs. (13)

Some people say that in March poorer people ate small buds that would later drop off as the fruit formed. It was probably April at this time, and this tree did not have the edible buds on it. Therefore it may be that the tree would not have had any figs that year anyway, even when it became time for the fruit.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to the tree?
Questions.Note: He said that the tree would never bear fruit again. (14)

Questions.Q: When Jesus reached Jerusalem, where did he go?
Questions.A: He went to the temple area (that is, the courtyard around the temple building). (15)

Questions.Q: What were some of the people in the temple area doing?
Questions.A: They were buying and selling things and changing money. (15)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do?
Questions.A: He told them that they were doing wrong and he drove them out of the temple area. (15-17)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do that showed how angry he was about the peoples' actions?
Questions.A: He turned over the tables of those who were changing money and the benches of those who were selling doves. (15)
He would not allow anyone to carry things for their business across the temple courtyard. (16)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say?
Questions.A: Jesus said that [the prophets long ago] had written that God said his house was to be a place where all cultural groups would pray. These traders, however, had made it into a robbers' den (that is, like a place for robbers to gather and then go out to harm people). (17)

Questions.Q: What did the chief priests and teachers of the law do when they heard what Jesus had done?
Questions.A: They were very angry and began to plan how they could destroy Jesus (that is, how they could ruin all that Jesus was doing, probably by killing him). (18)

Questions.Q: Why do you think that they were so angry?
Questions.A: They were angry because they thought that Jesus had no authority to run those people out. They felt they were the bosses of the temple and the area around it.

Questions.Q: Why did they not just kill Jesus immediately?
Questions.A: They were afraid that the crowd would turn against them because the people were amazed by what he taught them. (18)

Section.heading: Mark 11:20-26 Jesus taught the disciples that if a person prays believing that God will do something for him, God will do it.

Questions.Q: What was Jesus teaching his disciples?
Questions.A: He was teaching that when a person prays, he must believe that God will answer his prayer, and then God will do what they ask of him. (22-24)

Questions.Q: As the disciples walked along the next morning, what did they see?
Questions.A: They saw that the fig tree on which Jesus had put a curse the day before had withered. (20-21)

Questions.Q: Tell me some examples of people putting a curse on something.
Questions.Note: This is a check whether or not the respondent assumes that Jesus used power from Satan to make the curse happen. If so a different expression will probably need to be used.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say that they must do to have their prayers answered?
Questions.A: As they pray, they must believe that God will do what they ask. (22)

Questions.Q: What illustration did Jesus give to show what sorts of things are possible if we trust God?
Questions.A: He said that if they would say to a mountain that it should move and fall into the sea, God would cause it to happen. (23)

Questions.Q: What must people do so that God will cause what they pray for to happen?
Questions.A: They must believe that God has already done it for them. (24)

Questions.Q: What else must a person do as he prays?
Questions.A: He must forgive everyone for anything they have done against him. (25)

Questions.Q: What happens when a person who belongs to God forgives others?
Questions.A: They make the way clear for God to forgive (or keep on forgiving) them.

Section.heading: Mark 11:27-33 The religious leaders asked Jesus who had given him authority to do the things he did.

Questions.Q: What were the chief priests and teachers of the law asking Jesus?
Questions.A: They were asking who had given him the authority to do the things he was doing [in the temple area]. (28)

Questions.Q: Where was Jesus when the chief priests and teachers of the law were asking where he got his authority?
Questions.A: He was walking in the temple area. (27)

Questions.Q: How did Jesus answer them?
Questions.A: He asked them a question. (29)

Questions.Q: What was Jesus's question to them?
Questions.A: He asked them whether it was God who had given authority to John to baptize people, or whether John had done it on his own authority. (29-30)

Questions.Q: Why did the chief priests and teachers of the law find it difficult to answer that question?
Questions.A: They knew that if they said that God had sent John to preach and baptize, then Jesus would ask why they did not believe John the Baptist's message. If, however, they said that it was not God who sent John the Baptist, then the people would turn against them because the people believed that God had chosen John to be one of his prophets. (31-32)

Questions.Q: How did they answer Jesus?
Questions.A: They said that they did not know whether John the Baptist had God's authority to do what he did or not. (33)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to them?
Questions.A: He said that, since they would not answer his question about who sent John to preach and baptize, he would not answer their question about who gave him authority to do what he was doing. (33)

Section.heading: Mark 12:1-12 Jesus told a parable about a man who rented his grapevine garden to wicked tenants.

Questions.Q: In the story which Jesus told, what were the vine growers wanting to do?
Questions.A: They were wanting to obtain all of the fruit from the vineyard, and even the vineyard itself, for themselves by stealing and killing. (2-7)

Questions.Q: What do you think they were supposed to be doing?
Questions.A: They were supposed to grow much fruit
and give some of the [first] fruit [probably ¼ to ½ of the harvest] to the owner of the garden. (2)

Questions.Q: To whom was Jesus speaking at this time?
Questions.A: He was speaking to the Jewish leaders-the chief priests, teachers of the law, and elders.
Questions.Note: This information should be clear from 11:27, but it may be good to say it again here in 12:1. It is important for a correct understanding of the meaning of the parable.

Questions.Q: What kind of speaking was Jesus using here? (That is, was he telling a history, a story, a parable, or what?)
Questions.A: Jesus was using a parable, a story with a deeper meaning.

Questions.Q: Jesus began his parable speaking of a certain man. What did this man do?
Questions.A: He planted a vineyard.

Questions.Q: Why do you think that the man made a fence around the vineyard?
Questions.A: He made a fence to show that it was his and to protect it.

Questions.Q: Why do you think that the man dug a pit?
Questions.A: He dug a pit so that he would have a place to put the grapes in order to tramp the juice out of them.

Questions.Q: Why do you think that he built a tower?
Questions.A: He made a tower so that he could go there and watch for wild animals or birds that might eat or ruin the grapes.(The tower probably provided a place to stay and to store grain as well as a good placed above the vines from which to watch the field.)

Questions.Q: What did the man do when he had finished preparing the vineyard?
Questions.A: He put it in the care of some people who would rent it,
and then he went away to another country. (1)

Questions.Q: What happened when the harvest time came?
Questions.A: The owner sent a servant/slave to collect some of the harvest from the vineyard. (2)

Questions.Q: Do you think that the people who took care of the vineyard should have to give some of their harvest to the servant?
Questions.A: That was part of their agreement. The owner of the vineyard was supposed to receive [the first] part of the harvest as payment for them using his vineyard.
Questions.Note: This is a check for any misunderstanding.

Questions.Q: How do we know that those people did not give a part of the harvest to the servant whom the owner sent?
Questions.A: Mark wrote that they beat him and sent him away with nothing. (3)

Questions.Q: What did the owner of the vineyard do then?
Questions.A: He sent other servants/slaves, but the people looking after the vineyard rejected them all, beating some and killing some. (4-5)

Questions.Q: Whom did the owner of the vineyard send last?
Questions.A: He sent his own son. (6)

Questions.Q: What did the people looking after the vineyard do when they saw the son of the owner come near?
Questions.A: They decided that they should kill him so that they could take over the vineyard for themselves. (7-8)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say that the owner of the vineyard would do after they had killed his son?
Questions.A: He said that the owner would come and kill those people
and find others to care for his vineyard. (9)

Questions.Q: When Jesus said, "Surely you have read in Scripture ...", to what did he refer?
Questions.A: He was talking about the part of the Bible we now call Old Testament. [Key Term Check: See "Scripture" in KBT.]

Questions.Q: To whom was Jesus speaking when he said that?
Questions.A: He was speaking to the chief priests and other Jewish leaders who were there. (10)

Questions.Q: What is the saying which Jesus then quoted from God's book?
Questions.A: He said, "The stone which the builders had refused to use, has become the most important stone in [supporting] the [whole] house." (10)
Questions.Note: Check whether it is clear to the respondent that this is a proverb. It should be clear, at least, that it has a meaning other than being about building a real house.

Questions.Q: What was the reaction of the chief priests and teachers of the law to what Jesus said?
Questions.A: They were very angry and began planning to arrest him. (12)

Questions.Q: Why were they so angry?
Questions.A: They knew that Jesus's story was about them. (12)

Questions.Q: In what way do you think that the parts of the story were about the Jewish leaders?
Questions.A: They knew that God often used a vineyard to represent Israel in the Old Testament scriptures. They also knew that they were the ones whom God had put in charge of his people, but they and their ancestors had rejected the prophets whom God had sent, and treated them badly. Jesus was warning that as the owner of his vineyard God would punish those leaders and get others to watch over his vineyard (his people).
Questions.Note: The person who is answering these questions may not know that God used the picture of a vineyard often to refer to the Jews.

Check that at least the following is communicated: (a) Jesus was speaking with hidden meaning in the illustrations about the vineyard and the stone that the builders rejected. (b) The story was told as a warning to the Jewish leaders, and they had reacted strongly to it.
(The translator could explain in a footnote that the Old Testament writers commonly referred to Israel as God's vineyard.)

Questions.Q: Why were the Jewish leaders afraid of the crowd?
Questions.A: The Jewish leaders were afraid because they knew that the ordinary people believed that God was with Jesus.
They knew that the people might rebel against them if they tried to arrest and kill him. (12)

Section.heading: Mark 12:13-17 Some Pharisees asked Jesus if they should pay taxes to Caesar, the king of the Roman people.

Questions.Q: Were the Pharisees and the followers of Herod able to trick Jesus into saying something that was wrong and to show that he therefore was not sent by God?
Questions.A: No. They were not able to trick him.

Questions.Q: What were the Pharisees and the followers of Herod who came to Jesus trying to do?
Questions.A: They were trying to trick Jesus into saying something for which they could accuse him [of breaking God's laws or the Roman laws] or in any way cause him trouble. (13)

Questions.Q: What did they tell him that they knew about him?
Questions.A: They said that they knew that he was an honest man who would not change his message to please people no matter who they might be. He only taught God's message. (14)

Questions.Q: What question did they then ask Jesus?
Questions.A: They asked him whether it was right to pay taxes to Caesar, or not. (14-15a)
Questions.Note: Check that it is clear who Caesar was, if "Emperor" or "King" is not mentioned in the translated text. The word "Caesar" is a title, not a man's personal name.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus know about what the Pharisees were thinking?
Questions.A: He knew they were only acting nice to him so they could get him to say something about which they could accuse him. (15b)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell them to bring him?
Questions.A: He told them to bring [a Roman coin called] a denarius to him. (15b)

Questions.Q: After they brought the coin to him, what question did Jesus ask them?
Questions.A: He asked them about the person whose picture and name they saw on the coin. (16)

Questions.Q: What did they answer?
Questions.A: They answered that it was Caesar (the emperor/king of Rome) whose picture and name was on the coin. (16)

Questions.Q: Then what did Jesus say?
Questions.A: He said that they should go ahead and serve Caesar with things like that money that were related to him, but at the same time they should serve God (as he requires). (17)

Questions.Q: Why do you think amazed them so much when they heard his answer to their trick question?
Questions.A: They were amazed because he made such a wise answer that fit the situation and stopped their trick from working.

Section.heading: Mark 12:18-27 Some Sadducees questioned Jesus about people rising to live again after dying.

Questions.Q: How did Jesus show that people live on after dying?
Questions.A: He showed that God refers to some who died as being alive. He said that even after Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob were dead God had said, "I am their God." (So Jesus showed that God knows that when his people's bodies die, their spirits continue to live on with him.) (26-27)

Questions.Q: Who were the Sadducees?
Questions.A: The Sadducees were a Jewish group [like a political party who were mostly (rich) priests]
[They had their own views on certain spiritual things, such as,] they believed that people would not live again after dying. (18)
Key Term Check: See "Sadducee" in KBT in the "Pharisee" entry.
Questions.Note: It may be good to have a glossary entry on the Sadducees.

Questions.Q: What Jewish marriage rule that Moses had written down did the Sadducees quote?
Questions.A: They quoted the rule that if a man died without any children, his brother should marry his widow [and have some children to inherit the dead brother's land and possessions.] (19)

Questions.Q: Tell me the main part of the story that the Sadducees told to Jesus.
Questions.A: They said that there were seven brothers, and the first married and died without having any children. (20)

Then the second brother married that widow and later died, also without having any children. All seven brothers, one after the other, in the same way each married that same woman and each died without having any children. (21-22)

Questions.Q: What did they want Jesus to decide from their story?
Questions.A: They wanted him to tell them whose wife she would be, when all seven of her husbands were alive again after the resurrection. (23)

Questions.Q: Why do you think that the Sadducees asked that question?
Questions.A: It was a trick question. They thought that in order to answer it Jesus would have to choose to disagree with God's law that Moses wrote or else agree with them that his own teaching that people live after dying was wrong.

Questions.Q: What was Jesus's attitude toward the Sadducees?
Questions.A: He rebuked them for not knowing the scriptures and not understanding how powerful God really is. (24)

Questions.Q: How did Jesus answer their question?
Questions.A: He said that after people have risen from death, they will not be marrying each other. (25)

Questions.Q: In what way, do you think, did Jesus mean that people will be like the angels in heaven?
Questions.A: Just as angels are not married now, people will not be married then. (25)

Questions.Q: How did Jesus show that people will rise again from death?
Questions.A: Jesus pointed out from the Old Testament that after the Jewish ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob had died, God said, "I am the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob." So since God spoke of himself being their God after they had died, he knew that they were still living. (26-27)

Questions.Q: What were the Sadducees mistaken about?
Questions.A: They were mistaken when they said that no one lives again after death. (26-27)

Section.heading: Mark 12:28-34 Jesus told a teacher of the law which of God's commandments are the most important.

Questions.Q: Which did Jesus say were the two most important commandments of God?
Questions.A: Jesus said that to love God with all your being, and to love other people as you love yourself are the two most important commandments. (31-32)

Questions.Q: What question did one of the teachers of the law ask Jesus?
Questions.A: One of them asked, "Which is the most important commandment that God gave?" (28)

Questions.Q: Why did he ask Jesus that question?
Questions.A: He asked that question because he knew Jesus had given a very good answer to the Sadducees' trick question and he had this real question of his own that he wanted Jesus to answer. (28)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about God?
Questions.A: Jesus said that there is only one God. The LORD (that is, Yahweh) is the only God. (29)

Questions.Q: To whom do the words "O Israel" refer?
Questions.A: Those words refer to the Jews, [God's chosen people]. (29)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say is the most important commandment?
Questions.A: He said that most important commandment is that we must love God with every part of our being and with all of our ability. (30)

Questions.Q: What is the second most important commandment?
Questions.A: The second most important commandment is that we are to love other people in the same way that we love ourselves. (31)
Key Term Check: The Greek word for "love" that is used here means that a person has a gracious, outgoing, active interest in the welfare of another person.
Questions.Note: See "love" in KBT.
John used the same word to explain how much God loves us (John 3:16; 1 John 4:9-11). The translator must explain his reasons if he did not use the same word for love in each of verses 30 and 31.

Questions.Q: What did the teacher of the law say about Jesus's reply?
Questions.A: He said that Jesus had spoken the truth. (32-33)

Questions.Q: Then what did Jesus say to the man?
Questions.A: Jesus said that the man was very near to entering God's kingdom (that is, ready to put himself under God's authority and allow God to rule over him). (34)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means here when it says that from then on no one dared to question Jesus any more?
Questions.A: What Mark means is that they gave up using trick questions to try to cause Jesus to say something that would make him look foolish to the people. At this time they gave up because each time they questioned him he would give such good answers that the people would trust him more instead of less.

Section.heading: Mark 12:35-37 Jesus explained from scripture that the Messiah they were expecting to come had to be greater than their ancestor King David.

Questions.Q: Was Jesus teaching that King David or the Messiah (the one God appointed to come as savior and king) was greater?
Questions.A: He was teaching that the Messiah (the Christ) was to be greater than David. Jesus said that David himself had called him "Lord." (35-37)

Questions.Q: Did Jesus say that the Messiah would be a descendant of David when he came, or not?
Questions.A: He allowed for that. Here he was causing the people to think it through and realize that the Christ they often talked about and were expecting was more than what just being David's offspring would make him. (35-37)
Questions.Note: The Jerusalem Bible translates verse 37 as: "… in what way then can he be his [that is, David's] son?" Translating it something like that should make the real meaning of Jesus's question easier to understand.

Questions.Q: Why do you think the crowd of people was delighted with what Jesus had said?
Questions.A: Jesus had shown clearly that the teachers of the law did not follow their own teaching about the Messiah (the Christ). (35-37)

Questions.Q: What did the teachers of the law say about the Messiah?
Questions.A: They said that the Messiah was to be born as a descendant of David. (35)

Questions.Q: Do you think that Jesus agreed with that?
Questions.A: Yes, he would have since that is also scripture. (But here he is making a point about a more important relationship, that is: that the Messiah (the Christ) is the son of God. The religious teachers should have also understood that, but they did not.)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say that David himself had said about the Christ?
Questions.A: David had referred to the Christ as his (David's) Lord. (36)

Questions.Q: Did David think that Christ was more important or less important than himself?
Questions.A: By calling Christ his Lord, David honored Christ. By doing that, he showed that Christ was greater than he himself.

Questions.Q: What would the Lord God do while Jesus sat in the place of honor beside him?
Questions.A: God would make Jesus's enemies be submitted to him (that is, make them have to obey whatever he said. (36)

Section.heading: Mark 12:38-40 Jesus told people to not do as the teachers of the law did.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that God would punish the kind of people Jesus talked about here [in verse 40] even more than other people?
Questions.A: They worked at making people think that they were obeying God especially well, but by their own example they were teaching people be selfish.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think is the reason that God would punish the kind of people Jesus talked about here in verse 40 even more than other people?
What do you think is the reason that God would punish the kind of people Jesus talked about here even more than other people?

Questions.Q: Jesus warned the people about the way that the teachers of the Law acted. What kind of things did they do?
Questions.A: They walked around in fancy clothes in public places in order to enjoy [people] greeting them. (38)
They enjoyed [people] honoring [them] by having them sit in places set aside for honored people, both in synagogues and at feasts. (39)
They cheated people [in order to become rich], such as becoming the owners of widows' homes [and possessions]. (40)
They showed off by saying long prayers [in public places] (that is, they pretended to be very religious). (40)

Questions.Q: Why do you think that Jesus said that God would punish the teachers of the law severely?
Questions.A: God would punish them because they not only did evil, but covered it up by acting like they were really serving God. (38-40)

Section.heading: Mark 12:41-44 A widow gave everything she had to God.

Questions.Q: For what did Jesus praise the widow?
Questions.A: Jesus praised the widow for being willing to give her last bit of money to God, which was all she had left for staying alive. (43-44)

Questions.Q: Where in the temple area was Jesus sitting?
Questions.A: Jesus was sitting near the box where people used to put their gifts for God. (41)

Questions.Q: What did he see as he sat there?
Questions.A: He saw many rich people who gave large amounts [of money]. (41)
Then he saw one poor widow who put in two coins of the smallest value that there was. (42)

Questions.Q: Why did Jesus regard the widow's money as more than the rich people's money?
Questions.A: She gave God everything she had to live on. The rich people only gave part of the large amount of money that they had. (It was money they did not really need in order to stay alive.) (44)

Section.heading: Mark 13:1-27 Jesus told his disciples about the signs that will show that he is about to return to this world.

Questions.Q: Mention some of the things that Jesus said would happen before the end of the world.
Questions.A: He said that there will be many people who will claim to be the Christ who has returned. (6 and 21-22)
There will be wars, earthquakes, and much trouble. (7-8)
People will arrest those who believe in Jesus, take them into court, and beat them. (9)
People would preach the Good News to all the nations. (10)
People will hate those who follow Jesus, even if they are their own relatives. (12-13)
Something/Someone will try to dishonor God (or, take his honor for itself) in a very shocking/disgusting way. (14)
The sun and moon will no longer give light, the stars will fall from the sky, and everything in the universe will be shaken. (24-25)
Questions.Note: If the respondent does not read the text themselves but only hears someone read it, do not expect them to remember more than about three of these items. Otherwise, a respondent should probably be able to recall about five items.
Questions.Alternative: Mention some of the things that Jesus said would happen before the end of the world?

Questions.Q: When all those troubles happen, how will there be any believers who are still alive in the world?
Questions.A: God will allow those troubles to happen only for a short time. (20)

Questions.Q: What will happen to those believers when the Son of Man returns?
Questions.A: He will send his angels to gather them from every part of the world. (27)

Questions.Q: What did one of Jesus's disciples say about the buildings in the temple area?
Questions.A: His disciple said that the temple was a wonderful building made of great stones. (1)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say would happen to the temple?
Questions.A: Jesus said that people would completely break down the temple. (2)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus's disciples later ask him?
Questions.A: They ask him when the things he had told about would take place [when would people destroy the temple]. (3-4)

Questions.Q: As Jesus answered them, what warning did he give?
Questions.A: He said that they should be careful not to let people trick them [about when people would destroy the temple]. (5)

Questions.Q: What did he say many people would come and claim?
Questions.A: He said that many would come and claim that they were the Christ, and in that way deceive many people. (6)

Questions.Q: What troubles did he say there would be?
Questions.A: He said that there would be wars nearby and far away. There would be earthquakes and famines in various places. (7-8)

Questions.Q: To what time do you think these earthly troubles (here compared to first birth-pains) would show movement?
Questions.A: Those troubles would show progress toward the end of this present age (that is, toward the finalizing of the "these things" his disciples spoke about in verse 4 and Christ's coming to earth a second time). (7-8)

Questions.Q: Who was it that Jesus said people would arrest and take to court?
Questions.A: Jesus was speaking to his followers here, so he was referring to his followers.

Questions.Q: According to Jesus's words, why would people arrest them?
Questions.A: They would arrest them because they followed Jesus.

Questions.Q: What would his followers have opportunity to do when people took them to trial?
Questions.A: They would have opportunities to tell kings and officials about Jesus.

Questions.Q: What else did Jesus say would happen to his followers?
Questions.A: He said people would turn then over to the council [of Jewish leaders] who would whip them in the synagogues.

Questions.Q: Why would they do like that to them?
Questions.A: They would do that to them his followers because they were identified with Jesus (and with his name).

Questions.Q: What must people do first concerning the gospel?
Questions.A: Christ's followers must first preach the gospel to all nations. (10)

Questions.Q: What do you think it is that will happen, once people have preached the gospel to all nations?
Questions.Note: "The end" will arrive, as stated in verse 7, that is, the end of this time which we are in now. (Note: This time will end with Christ's return. See verses 26-37.)
-OR-
All "these things" which Andrew had mentioned in his question in verse 4 will happen.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think will happen once people have preached the gospel to all nations?
What do you think will happen once people have preached the Good News to all nations?
What will happen once people have preached the gospel to all nations?
What will happen once all nations have heard the gospel?
What will happen once all nations have heard the Good News about Jesus?
What will happen once all nations have heard the Good News?

Questions.Q: How will the followers of Jesus know what they should say when people take them to court?
Questions.A: God's Spirit will help them to say the right things at the time, so they should not worry about what they will say. (11)

Questions.Q: What terrible things will happen within some families?
Questions.A: Family members will betray other family members, handing them over to be killed. (12)

Questions.Q: Why will many people hate the followers of Jesus?
Questions.A: They will hate them because they follow him. (13)

Questions.Q: Whom did Jesus say God would accept?
Questions.A: He will accept those who firmly remain faithful to him. (13)

Questions.Q: What do you think Mark meant when he wrote about an "abomination of desolation"?
Questions.A: (The meaning in the Greek text is not very clear. It should be clear from the translation, though, that something shocking enough to cause people to draw back in horror will be in a (holy) place where it should never be. Because of this shocking thing, God will withdraw from that place leaving it desolate.)

Questions.Q: When people see this shocking thing (or person) taking over where it (or he) should never be, what are they to do?
Questions.A: They are not to hesitate, thinking of getting anything from their houses.
They must flee for their lives to a safe place, such as the mountains. (14-16)

Questions.Q: What do you think will make it so dreadful for pregnant women and those with small children?
Questions.A: It would be difficult for them to run, and therefore they would be in danger of being caught before they could get away. (17)

Questions.Q: Why did Jesus say to pray that this would not happen in the winter?
Questions.A: He said that because he knew it would be a time of much suffering, and would be worse still if the weather was bad, such as cold and rainy. (18)

Questions.Q: Would the suffering of that time be very serious?
Questions.A: Yes, it would be the worst suffering that had ever happened or would ever happen. (19)

Questions.Q: What has God done for the sake of his chosen people?
Questions.A: He has planned it to last only a short time. (20)

Questions.Q: Who do you think these people are whom God has chosen?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The "elect" (or "chosen ones") are the people who believe that God sent Jesus as the Christ to earth to save them from their sins. God knows who will believe that and he has chosen to save them.

Questions.Q: What else did Jesus warn his followers about?
Questions.A: He warned them that many different men would come and falsely claim to be prophets or claim to be the Christ/Messiah. (21-23)

Questions.Q: When this time of trouble and suffering is over, what is going to happen?
Questions.A: Jesus will come back to this world. (26)

Questions.Q: What signs will people see happening at the end of this time of suffering?
Questions.A: The sun and moon will no longer give light,
the stars will fall from the sky,
and everything in the universe will be shaken. (24-25)
Questions.Note: These verses could be either figurative language or could be understood literally. In comparing this with Isaiah 24:21-23 and 34:4 and Rev. 6:13-14, it seems that this could be figurative language for great disruption in or complete loss of leadership when the Jews are scattered, or when Christ sets up his final reign, or both.

Questions.Q: Who will return then to this world?
Questions.A: The Son of Man, (that is, Jesus Christ Jesus) will return. (26)

Questions.Q: In what way will he come back?
Questions.A: He will return in a manner that will clearly show that he has great power. (26)

Questions.Q: Who will come with him?
Questions.A: His angels will come with him. (27)

Questions.Q: What will he send his messengers to do?
Questions.A: He will send them to gather the people he has chosen from every part of the world, wherever they may be. (27)

Section.heading: Mark 13:28-31 Jesus said that people can know about the time of his coming back to this world if they take note of earlier events that he told them would happen before his return.

Questions.Q: What is it that we can learn from the fig tree?
Questions.A: There are predictable patterns, such as, when fig tree leaves appear, we know that summer is near. [The same is true about knowing when Christ will return to this world.] (28-29)

Questions.Q: How do the people in your culture know that the "summer" or rainy time is near?
Questions.A: (Check that the illustration as used in these verses has meaning in the receptor language.)

Questions.Q: Can you explain the meaning of Jesus's words, "When you see these things happen, you know that it/he is near?"
Questions.A: He meant that when they saw wars, earthquakes, famines, suffering, persecution, and the "abomination of desolation" take place they would know that the end time was near.
Questions.Alternative: Can you explain the meaning of Jesus's words, "When you see these things happen, you know that it is near?"
Can you explain the meaning of Jesus's words, "When you see these things happen, you know that he is near?"

Questions.Q: When were "these things" going to happen?
Questions.A: These things would happen while some of the people living then were still alive.
-OR-
These things would happen while some of the Jewish race were still alive. (30)
Questions.Note: If the translation can be ambiguous as to which of the above two choices is to be made that would be good since it appears he may have left it that way because it refers to both. That is, there was a time of trouble and destruction of the temple in the year 70, but there will be another time of trouble as well.

Questions.Q: What is it that will never cease to exist (that is, it will always remain)?
Questions.A: What Jesus taught will always remain (will never be destroyed). (31)

Section.heading: Mark 13:32-37 Jesus said that no one knows the time when he will return to this world.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell his followers they must continually be doing?
Questions.A: They should be watching and ready for him when he comes back. (32-33)

Questions.Q: Why is it necessary to be constantly watching out?
Questions.A: No one knows the exact time when he will come back. (32)

Questions.Q: Who knows the time when Jesus Christ will return to the world?
Questions.A: God the Father is the only one who knows. (32-33)

Questions.Q: What comparison did Jesus use to teach what his return will be like?
Questions.A: He used an illustration about a man who assigned work to his servants/slaves
and then left on a trip without telling them when he would come back. (32-35)

Questions.Q: What was Jesus's instruction to his followers?
Questions.A: They must always be ready for his return. (36-37)

Section.heading: Mark 14:1-11 The religious leaders plotted how they might kill Jesus.

Questions.Q: What were the chief priests and teachers of the law trying to do?
Questions.A: They were trying to find a way to arrest Jesus secretly and kill him. (1-2)

Questions.Q: What reason did Jesus give for saying that the woman had done well to pour the ointment on him, rather than to sell it and to give the money to the poor?
Questions.A: He said that the poor people would always be there with them. They could help them any time, but he would not always be there. (He also said that the woman was preparing his body beforehand for when people would bury it.) (7-8)

Questions.Q: What was it that was going to happen after two more days?
Questions.A: Two Jewish festivals would start. They called the one the Passover and the other the Festival of Eating Bread Made with No Yeast. (1)
Key Term Check: See "The Passover sacrifice" in KBT in the "sacrifice" entry.

Questions.Q: What did the chief priests and teachers decide not to do during the festivals?
Questions.A: They decided not to arrest and kill Jesus. (1-2)

Questions.Q: Why did they say that they should not do it during the festivals?
Questions.A: They said that they should not do it then because the crowds of people who came to the festival might riot [and the Roman soldiers would punish all the Jews for that]. (2)

Questions.Q: Where was Jesus at that time?
Questions.A: Jesus was at Bethany, in the house of Simon [who had been] a leper. (3)

Questions.Q: What happened while Jesus was still eating in Simon's house?
Questions.A: A woman came in, bringing some very expensive perfume (made of a plant called nard). It was in a beautiful jar made of an alabaster stone. (3)

Questions.Q: What did the woman do?
Questions.A: She broke open the jar and poured the perfume on Jesus's head. (3)
Questions.Note: The only way to open that type of container was to break the thin neck of the jar. Breaking the jar was not an accident, they did that on purpose to get the liquid out.

Questions.Q: How did some of the people there feel about her doing that?
Questions.A: They complained that she had wasted the perfume.
They said that someone should have sold it for a lot of money,
and given that money to the poor people. (4-5)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to the people who were rebuking the woman?
Questions.A: He said that they should leave her alone. She had done a very good thing to him. (6)

Questions.Q: Did Jesus say that it was not good to help the poor?
Questions.A: No. He wanted people to help the poor, but he said that it was good that the woman had used this perfume on him as she did. (7)

Questions.Q: Jesus's words show that he knew something was about to happen to him. What was it?
Questions.A: He knew that people were going to kill him and bury him. (7-8)

Questions.Q: What did Judas Iscariot do?
Questions.A: He went to the chief priests and told them that he would help them to capture Jesus. (10-11)

Questions.Q: What did the chief priests promise they would do for Judas in return?
Questions.A: They promised that if he would betray Jesus to them, they would give him money. (11)

Section.heading: Mark 14:12-26 Jesus ate the Passover meal with his disciples.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell his disciples about the bread and the wine that he gave them during the Passover meal?
Questions.A: He said that the bread was his body and the wine was his blood. (22, 24)

Questions.Q: What was to be the purpose of Jesus's blood spilling out?
Questions.A: By letting his blood spill out he would establish a covenant [between God and] many people.

Questions.Q: In the custom of the Jews, what did they do on the first day of the festival?
Questions.A: They sacrificed a lamb, called the Passover lamb. (12)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus's disciples ask him?
Questions.A: They asked him where they should go to prepare things so that he and they could eat this special Passover meal together. (12)

Questions.Q: How many disciples did Jesus send to prepare for him?
Where did he say that they should go?
Questions.A: He said that they should go into the town. (13)

Questions.Q: What did he say they should do next?
Questions.A: He said that they would see a man coming towards them carrying a jar of water.
They should follow him to the house where he went. (13-14)

Questions.Q: In what way, do you think, would they know which man carrying water to follow home?
Questions.A: Jesus knew there would only be one such man. (Besides, in Jewish culture, women were the ones to carry water, not men. A man carrying water would be unusual.)

Questions.Q: What would they find at that house?
Questions.A: They would find that the owner had a large room upstairs which he had already made ready for them. They were to prepare for the meal there. (14-15)

Questions.Q: How did things work out for those two disciples when they went to town?
Questions.A: Everything happened just as Jesus had said it would be. (16)

Questions.Q: As the sun had set, where were Jesus and his other disciples?
Questions.A: They arrived at the room where the two disciples had prepared the meal for them. (17)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell his disciples as they all were eating?
Questions.A: He said that one of those who was there eating with him was going to betray him. (18)

Questions.Q: What did the disciples say when they heard this?
Questions.A: They were sad, and each one said, "Surely it is not I?" (19)

Questions.Q: What else did Jesus say?
Questions.A: Jesus said that it was one of the twelve [disciples], one who was dipping bread in the same bowl (of soup/sauce) with him. (20)

Questions.Q: To what was Jesus referring when he said what happened would be "just as it had been written"?
Questions.A: The prophets long ago had written in God's what would happen to the savior whom God would send. Now what they had written was about to come true as those things happened to Jesus.
Questions.Note: Jesus and the men who wrote the various parts of the New Testament often quoted statements that the prophets had written long before Jesus's lifetime. The speakers were not simply illustrating a point, but were showing that God was causing things to happen just as he had predicted through his prophets in the Old Testament writings.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about the person who would betray him?
Questions.A: Jesus said that it would have been better for that man if he had never been born. (21)

Questions.Q: Why do you think that it would have been better for that man if he had not been born?
Questions.Note: If he had not been born, he could not have sinned by betraying the savior whom God had sent into the world. Then he would not have had to receive the punishment for that great sin. (implied 21)

Questions.Q: What was it that Jesus gave to his disciples?
Questions.A: He gave them bread (that he had broken into pieces for them.)

Questions.Q: What else did Jesus do concerning the bread before he gave it to his disciples?
Questions.A: He thanked God for it.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about that bread?
Questions.A: He said that the bread he handed to them was his body.
-OR-

He said that the bread [represented] his body, (just as all the foods and other items on Passover meal table represented other items and events which God had used in earlier times to provide for his people.)
Questions.Note: (Some people understand this to mean that God made a miraculous or spiritual change in the bread.)

In many situations when there is more than one possible meaning, it is sufficient to follow one of them. Here it is good if you translate with a broad enough meaning to allow people to interpret these words of Jesus either of the ways above. The Greek can be interpreted either way.

Questions.Q: What was in the cup Jesus gave his disciples to drink?
Questions.A: There was wine in the cup.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about the wine?
Questions.A: He said that the wine was his blood.
-OR-
He said that the wine [represented] his blood. (24)
Questions.Note: The comments about translating verse 22, above, apply here also.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about his blood?
Questions.A: He said that he would let his blood flow out in order to help many people. (24)

Questions.Q: What else did Jesus say concerning his blood?
Questions.A: He said that because his blood would spill out, God could make a covenant with people. (24)

Questions.Q: What is a covenant?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A covenant is an agreement, an especially binding promise. If a person on one side of the covenant does not do as both have agreed, there usually is a strong punishment for him or he pays compensation to the other person. Similar agreements now are called contracts. When God makes an agreement with people, however, he makes a firm promise of what he will do and says what they must do. [See "covenant" in KBT.]
Questions.Note: If the language has a special name to refer to these kinds of agreements, ask the respondent to tell you the kinds of situations in which the people make the agreements. Listen for any points where it would not be appropriate to state that God made that kind of an agreement. Then adjust the translation as necessary.

Questions.Q: When did Jesus say that he would drink wine the next time?
Questions.A: He said that he would not drink wine again until the time when God would be ruling on earth. (25)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus and his disciples do then?
Questions.A: They sang a hymn (that is, a song from God's Book), and then left [the house (and the town)] and went to the hill called Mountain of Olives. (26)

Section.heading: Mark 14:27-31 Jesus said that Peter would deny that he even knew Jesus.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell the disciples that they were going to do?
Questions.A: He said that they were going to deny ever having associated with him. (27)

Questions.Q: What did Peter say about that?
Questions.A: He insisted that, even if the other disciples acted like that, he would never act like that regarding Jesus. (29)

Questions.Q: Jesus quoted some words that a prophet had written in God's Book a long time before. Who was it who told the prophet, "I will strike the shepherd..."?
Questions.A: It was God who said that. (27)
Questions.Alternative: Jesus quoted some words that a prophet had written a long time before. Who was it who told the prophet, "I will strike the shepherd..."?
Jesus quoted some words that a prophet had written in God's Book a long time before. Who had told the prophet, "I will strike the shepherd..."?
Jesus quoted some words that a prophet had written a long time before. Who had told the prophet, "I will strike the shepherd..."?

Questions.Q: What do you think these words mean: "I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered"?
Questions.A: It means that God would cause others to strike down the leader, and his followers would scatter. (27)
Questions.Note: Here it means specifically that Jesus's disciples would scatter when the Jews would arrest, try, and crucify Jesus.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say was going to happen after he died?
Questions.A: He would rise to live again, and go ahead of the disciples to Galilee [province]. (28)

Questions.Q: What was Peter so sure about that he said it twice?
Questions.A: He said twice that he would never say that he was not a follower of Jesus. (29, 31)
Questions.Alternative: What was Peter so certain about that he repeated it?
What did Peter emphasize by stating it twice?
What assertion did Peter make two times to show his conviction?
What statement did Peter make twice to show his certainty?
What did Peter declare twice out of confidence?
What did Peter insist upon by saying it two times?
What conviction led Peter to repeat himself?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell Peter?
Questions.A: Jesus told him that during that same night, before the rooster crowed twice, he (Peter) would say three times that he was not a follower of Jesus. (30)

Section.heading: Mark 14:32-42 Jesus went to the garden called Gethsemane and prayed.

Questions.Q: What sort of feelings was Jesus having at that time?
Questions.A: He was very concerned for himself; he knew that something very terrible was about to happen to him. (33)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus ask God in his prayer?
Questions.A: He asked God to change his plan in some way so that he (Jesus) would not have to experience the suffering that he was about to experience. (35-36)

Questions.Q: For what reason did Jesus go aside in the place called Gethsemane?
Questions.A: He wanted to pray. (32)

Questions.Q: Why was it, do you think, that that he wanted to pray at that time?
Questions.A: He wanted to pray then because he was very troubled about what was about to happen. (32-34)

Questions.Q: What were the disciples to do while he prayed?
Questions.A: They were to sit [and wait for him]. (32)

Questions.Q: Whom did Jesus take with him and go apart from the other disciples?
Questions.A: He took Peter and James and John with him. (33)

Questions.Q: What did he tell Peter, James and John to do?
Questions.A: He told them to stay there and watch/be alert. (34)

Questions.Q: How did Jesus say God was to decide what he should do?
Questions.A: Jesus said that God should do what pleased himself rather than what Jesus wanted. (36)

Questions.Q: How did Jesus address God?
Questions.A: He addressed him as "Abba" (that is, "Daddy"). (36)
Questions.Note: "Abba" is the actual word Jesus used in his Aramaic language to address his father. In the translation, use the appropriate word for when a son addresses his own father. If it sounds very similar to "Abba," only use the vernacular word. If the two words sound somewhat different from each other, transliterate Jesus's own word "Abba" and use the local word in addition as the translation of the Greek word for "[My] Father".

Questions.Q: When Jesus returned to his three disciples, what did he find?
Questions.A: He found them asleep. (37)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to those disciples?
Questions.A: He rebuked them for sleeping. (37)
He told them to keep alert and to pray so that [Satan] would not tempt them to sin. (38)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about why the disciples did not obey what he asked them to do?
Questions.A: He said, "The spirit is willing, but the body is weak." (He knew that they wanted to obey him, but they were not able by themselves and needed to pray for God's help.) (38)

Questions.Q: What happened next?
Questions.A: Jesus went away and prayed again as he had prayed before.
Then he came back and found the disciples asleep again. (39-40)

Questions.Q: What answer did the disciples have to explain their actions?
Questions.A: They did not know what to say to him. Their eyes kept falling shut [in the dark, quiet night]. (40)

Questions.Q: What happened when Jesus came back the third time?
Questions.A: He found that the disciples were sleeping, as before. (41)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus then tell his disciples?
Questions.A: He told them that the time for praying and sleeping was over.
The time had come to go forward to meet those who were coming.
Someone had betrayed him, the Son of Man, to sinful men.
Questions.Note: Check carefully that when Jesus said, "Let us go," the translation does not imply that Jesus was saying they should leave in order to avoid the betrayer or the bad situation. He was going forward to meet the betrayer; he was not talking of running in the opposite direction.

Section.heading: Mark 14:43-52 Judas betrayed Jesus by helping his enemies to find him.

Questions.Q: What did the people who came with Judas do to Jesus?
Questions.A: They arrested him. (44-46)

Questions.Q: Why do you think that Jesus did not try to prevent them from arresting him?
Questions.A: He knew that the [writers of the] scriptures had foretold [God's plan] that he would suffer for us, and so it had to happen that way. (49)

Questions.Q: Who was it who came there?
Questions.A: Judas, one of Jesus's twelve disciples, came.
Also, a crowd of people was with him, people whom the chief priests, the teachers of the law, and the [Jewish] elders had sent. (43)

Questions.Q: What were those people carrying?
Questions.A: They were carrying swords and clubs. (43)

Questions.Q: Why did Judas kiss Jesus?
Questions.A: It was a sign to the men who came with Judas. He had told them that the person he would kiss was the man whom they were to arrest. (44)

Key Term Check: kiss. In Jewish culture it was proper for one person to press his pursed lips on the side of another person's face. That was a sign of affection and reverence/respect for that other person. (See "kiss" in KBT in the "love" entry.)
Questions.Note: If the culture of the translation does not show affection or reverence with the kissing action, it is more important to keep that purpose clear, rather than worry about describing the exact action of Judas.

Questions.Q: How did Judas address Jesus?
Questions.A: Judas called him Rabbi, (that is, Teacher). (45)

Questions.Q: When the men arrested Jesus, how did his disciples try to stop them?
Questions.A: One of them drew his sword and cut off the ear of one of the servants/slaves of the High Priest. (47)

Questions.Q: Did Jesus try to resist or stop the men from arresting/capturing him?
Questions.A: No.
Questions.Alternative: Did Jesus try to resist or stop the men from arresting him?
Did Jesus try to resist or stop the men from capturing him?
