Questions.Q: Why did Jesus act surprised that they had come armed with swords and clubs?
Questions.A: He had not been resisting them or even avoiding them, like a robber/rebel would do.
He pointed out to them that they could have arrested him easily any time when he was teaching in the temple area (that is, in a very public place). (48)

Questions.Q: What did his disciples do when those people arrested/captured Jesus?
Questions.A: They all left him and ran away. (50)
Questions.Alternative: What did his disciples do when those people arrested Jesus?
What did his disciples do when those people captured Jesus?

Questions.Q: What did Mark write about a certain young man who also was there?
Questions.A: One young man who was following Jesus was wearing just a cloth tied around him. When the men tried to hold on to him, [they grabbed his clothing, so] he left the cloth [in their hands] and ran away naked. (51-52)

Section.heading: Mark 14:53-65 The council of religious leaders tried Jesus and decided that he must die.

Questions.Q: Why did the leaders of the Jews gather in the night at the High Priest's house?
Questions.A: They met for a court session and tried Jesus, deciding that he must die. (55-64)

Questions.Q: What was the reason that the Jewish council members said that Jesus must die?
Questions.A: They all agreed with the High Priest that Jesus had blasphemed God by claiming that he was the Christ, the Son of God. (61b-64)

Questions.Q: Where did the men who had arrested Jesus take him?
Questions.A: They took him to the High Priest. The chief priests and other Jewish leaders were gathering together there. (53)

Questions.Q: Why do you think that Peter followed Jesus at a distance?
Questions.A: He wanted to see what would happen to Jesus,
but he was afraid they might arrest him too. (54)

Questions.Q: How close did Peter come to the place where the Jewish leaders were trying Jesus?
Questions.A: He went right into the courtyard (that is, the open yard area) of the high priest's home
and sat there with the guards, getting warm by their fire. (54)

Questions.Q: What were the leaders of the Jews trying to do?
Questions.A: They were trying to find evidence to prove that Jesus was guilty of something for which they might condemn him to die. (55)

Questions.Q: Why do you think they could not find proof that Jesus had done something wrong?
Questions.A: They could not find proof because Jesus had not done anything wrong.
Also, the people who came as witnesses and lied [about Jesus] had conflicting stories. (56)

Questions.Q: Why were they having conflicting stories?
Questions.A: Some or all of them were lying about him. (56)

Questions.Q: What was it that some witnesses said about Jesus?
Questions.A: They said that Jesus had said that he would destroy the temple and build another one in just three days without humans working. (58)

Questions.Q: What was wrong with their testimony about this one topic?
Questions.A: Even in that one thing the witnesses did not agree. (59)

Questions.Q: What did the High Priest say to Jesus?
Questions.A: He said that Jesus should answer the accusations. (60)

Questions.Q: What surprised him?
Questions.A: He was surprised that Jesus did not defend himself. (60)

Questions.Q: What will people who read/hear this think the reason was that Jesus did not answer the High Priest's questions?
Questions.A: The High Priest already knew Jesus had not done anything wrong,
and Jesus was ready to die for us, so there was no need for him to say anything.
Questions.Note: In some places, if someone accuses another person, but that person does not answer any questions, people assume that he is guilty. This question is a check for such possible misunderstanding of Jesus's not replying.
Questions.Alternative: What will people who read this think the reason was that Jesus did not answer the High Priest's questions?
What will people who hear this think the reason was that Jesus did not answer the High Priest's questions?

Questions.Q: What question did the High Priest then ask Jesus?
Questions.A: He asked Jesus whether he was the Christ, the Son of God, or not. (61b)

Questions.Q: How did Jesus answer?
Questions.A: He said that he was. He also said that one day they would see him, the Son of Man, sitting at God's right hand and coming back to this world. (62)

Questions.Q: What will the people who read this think it means when Jesus said he would be "sitting at the right hand of God"?
Questions.A: This refers to him being equal to or next in authority with God. (62)
Questions.Note: In Jewish custom the right hand side of important people was the most honored position anyone could ever have. Therefore, this figure fits well and shows that Jesus now is there next to God, sharing in what God does.

Questions.Q: Why do you think that the High Priest tore his clothes?
Questions.A: He tore his clothes as a sign to show his very strong concern about what Jesus had said. (63)
Questions.Note: This was a Jewish custom to show extreme sorrow.

Questions.Q: Why did the High Priest say that they did not need to find any more witnesses?
Questions.A: Jesus had openly claimed that he was the Son of God, and they all had heard him say it. (62)
Questions.Note: By the Jewish law and by the scriptures no ordinary person could claim that he was equal to or greater than God. So, since they would not admit that he was God's son, they thought that they had enough evidence to condemn him to die.

Questions.Q: What did the court officials say that Jesus's punishment would be?
Questions.A: They said that he would have to die. (64)

Questions.Q: What are some of the things people then did to Jesus?
Questions.A: They began to spit on him.
They tied a cloth around his eyes and, while he could not see, they hit him and mockingly told him to tell them who it was who struck him.
Those who were guards for the High Priest's house and the temple beat him.

Section.heading: Mark 14:66-72 Peter said that he did not know Jesus.

Questions.Q: What was it that Peter said three times?
Questions.A: He said that he did not know Jesus. (68, 70, 71)

Questions.Q: Where was Peter?
Questions.A: He was in the courtyard, the open space in the compound of the High Priest. (54, 66)

Questions.Q: What was he doing?
Questions.A: He was sitting by the fire, warming himself. (54, 67)

Questions.Q: What did the servant girl say to Peter?
Questions.A: She said that he had been in the group who followed Jesus. (67)

Questions.Q: What did Peter say to her?
Questions.A: Peter said that he did not know or understand anything about what she was saying. (68)

Questions.Q: How do we know that the servant girl did not believe what Peter had said?
Questions.A: When the girl saw him again near the entrance of the compound, she said again that he was one of [the followers of Jesus]. (69)

Questions.Q: How did Peter respond to her this second time that she accused him?
Questions.A: He denied that what she said was true. (70a)

Questions.Q: Then another person said that Peter was one of the followers of Jesus. What reason did he give?
Questions.A: He said that Peter came from Galilee [province], the same as Jesus. (Probably the man could tell where Peter came from by the way he talked.) (70b)

Questions.Q: How did Peter respond to that person?
Questions.A: He spoke very strongly, binding himself by an oath that God should punish him if he was lying. Doing that, he said that he did not know Jesus at all. (71)
Questions.Note: (Key Term Check: See "curse" in KBT in the "bless" entry.)

Questions.Q: What was it that made Peter weep?
Questions.A: Peter heard the rooster crow the second time. Hearing the rooster crow reminded him that Jesus had told him that he (Peter) would say three times that he did not know Jesus before the rooster crowed the second time. (72)

Section.heading: Mark 15:1-15 They took Jesus to Pilate so that Pilate could try him in his court.

Questions.Q: What did the leaders of the Jews do with Jesus?
Questions.A: They took him to Pilate, the Roman governor, to stand trial there. (1)

Questions.Q: Did Pilate think that Jesus had done evil?
Questions.A: No, he knew that the chief priests only wanted to kill Jesus because they were jealous of him. (10)

Questions.Q: What did Pilate want to do to Jesus?
Questions.A: He wanted to set Jesus free. (9, 14)

Questions.Q: What did he do with Jesus?
Questions.A: He ordered that [some of his men] beat Jesus, and then he handed him over [to the soldiers for them] to nail him to a cross. (15)

Questions.Q: What time was it by then?
Questions.A: It was very early in the morning. (1)

Questions.Q: Why do you think that the leaders of the Jews tied Jesus before they took him to Pilate?
Questions.A: They may have wanted to convince Pilate that Jesus was a bad man.
-OR-
They may have been afraid that he would try to escape.
-OR-
They may have been afraid that his followers would try to rescue him.

Questions.Q: What question did Pilate ask Jesus?
Questions.A: He asked whether Jesus was the king of the Jews or not. (2)

Questions.Q: Did Jesus agree that he was the king of the Jews?
Questions.A: Yes. He said that it was as Pilate stated. (2)

Questions.Q: What did the chief priests say to Pilate about Jesus?
Questions.A: They accused him of having done many [evil] things. (3)

Questions.Q: What surprised Pilate?
Questions.A: Pilate was surprised that Jesus did not answer or defend himself against the accusations. (4-5)

Questions.Q: What did the Roman governor usually do at the time of the annual Jewish festival?
Questions.A: He would release one Jewish prisoner to the Jewish people.

Questions.Q: How did the Roman governor decide whom they would release?
Questions.A: They allowed the Jewish people pick the prisoner they wanted him to release. (6)

Questions.Q: Who was Barabbas?
Questions.A: He was a [Jewish] prisoner that the Romans had put in prison for leading a rebellion against the Roman government, the and for murdering someone during that rebellion. (7)

Questions.Q: What did the people ask Pilate concerning Barabbas?
Questions.A: They asked that Pilate would follow the usual custom and release a prisoner to them. They requested that he release one called Barabbas. (8, 11)

Questions.Q: Whom did Pilate want to release to them?
Questions.A: He wanted to release Jesus. (9-10)

Questions.Q: Why was it that Pilate wanted to release Jesus?
Questions.A: He knew that Jesus had not done anything wrong, and he knew that the chief priests had arrested him because they were jealous of him. (9-10, 14)

Questions.Q: Why did the people not ask for Jesus?
Questions.A: They did not ask for Jesus because the chief priests urged them to ask for Barabbas. (11)

Questions.Q: What did the people say should happen with Jesus?
Questions.A: They said that Pilate should [have some of his men] nail Jesus to a cross [to suffer there until he died]. (13-14)
Questions.Note: (Key Term Check: See "crucify" in KBT in the "cross" entry.)

Questions.Q: Why did Pilate finally agree to release Barabbas?
Questions.A: Pilate agreed only because he wanted to please the people. (15)

Questions.Q: Why did the soldiers do what they did to Jesus?
Questions.A: He had said that he was a king. They did not believe him, so they were mocking him by pretending that he was their king. (17-20)

Questions.Q: Where did the soldiers take Jesus?
Questions.A: They took him to an inner part of the compound of Pilate's palace as the Roman governor. (16)

Questions.Q: Why do you think that the soldiers chose a purple robe to put on Jesus?
Questions.A: That is the kind of robe which kings wore; they were dressing him up as a king. (17)

Questions.Q: What did they put on Jesus's head?
Questions.A: They put on him a crown made of thorny branches, shaped like the crown which kings wore. (17)

Questions.Q: How did they greet Jesus?
Questions.A: They greeted him as if he were a king. (18)

Questions.Q: Why did they honor Jesus?
Questions.A: They were not really worshiping him, but mocking him. (18-20)

Questions.Q: When the soldiers had finished mocking Jesus, what did they do?
Questions.A: They put his own clothes on him again.
Then they led him out in order to nail him to a cross. (20)

Section.heading: Mark 15:21-32 The Roman soldiers took Jesus and nailed him to a cross.

Questions.Q: What did the soldiers do to Jesus?
Questions.A: They nailed him to a cross [to suffer there until he died]. (25)

Questions.Q: Who mocked/ridiculed Jesus while he hung on the cross?
Questions.A: The people who passed by that place mocked him. (29)
The chief priests and the teachers of the law mocked him among themselves. (31)
The men who were hanging there on the other crosses also insulted him. (32)
Questions.Alternative: Who mocked Jesus while he hung on the cross?
Who ridiculed Jesus while he hung on the cross?

Questions.Q: How do we know that Jesus did not carry his cross all the way to the place where they nailed him to it?
Questions.A: Mark wrote that the soldiers forced the man Simon (from Cyrene, whom they met on the way) to carry it for him. (21)

Questions.Q: What was the name of the place where they nailed Jesus to the cross?
Questions.A: The place was called Golgotha (which means "The place of a skull"). (22)

Questions.Q: What did they offer Jesus to drink?
Questions.A: They offered him wine with some medicine in it. (23)

Questions.Q: Why do you think that they offered it to him?
Questions.A: They offered it probably to help him not feel the pain so much.
Questions.Note: This is a check for any wrong meaning.

Questions.Q: Why do you think that Jesus refused to drink it?
Questions.A: He probably refused because he had decided to suffer the full pain for mankind's sins.

Questions.Q: What did the soldiers do with Jesus's clothes?
Questions.Note: They threw "lots" to see which of them would get the different pieces of Jesus's clothing. (24)
What the men did was something like people now sometimes throw dice to choose a winner.

Questions.Q: If the people who speak your language do something like the soldiers did in order to help them decide things, tell me what they do.
Questions.Note: The translator should not use words that refer to actions that are illegal or that the Christian churches in the language area oppose. People in the Bible who believed in God sometimes used this same method to find out God's will for them (Luke 1:9; Act 1:26).

Questions.Q: What time was it when they nailed Jesus to the cross?
Questions.A: It was the third hour of daylight (that is, about nine o'clock in the morning). (25)
Questions.Note: It may be important to explain in a footnote or glossary item how the Jews determined the beginning of a day and how they counted time during a day.

Questions.Q: What did they write and put on the cross that Jesus was hanging on?
Questions.A: [A sign saying] "King of the Jews" [on a board or paper].
Questions.Note: In determining how best to word this question (and the next one, if both are used), consider both the wording in the translated text and whatever additional knowledge you might expect a respondent to have based on the other gospel accounts, pictures they have seen, or other sources.
Questions.Alternative: What was the official notice of the charge against Jesus?
What was the written charge against Jesus?
What did they put on the cross that Jesus was hanging on?
What did they nail to the cross that Jesus was hanging on?
What did they write and nail to the cross that Jesus was hanging on?
What did they put on the cross above Jesus' head?
What did they nail to the cross above Jesus' head?
What did they write and nail to the cross above Jesus' head?
What did they write?
What did someone write?
What sign did they write?
What sign did someone write?

Questions.Q: Why did someone write "King of the Jews" [on a board or paper] and put it above Jesus?
Questions.A: The Jewish leaders had accused Jesus in front of Pilate saying that he (Jesus) claimed to be a king.
Questions.Note: This is implied in 15:2. It is the reason for Pilate's question, and Jesus's answer there.
Questions.Alternative: Why did someone write "King of the Jews" on a board or paper and put it above Jesus?
Why did someone write "King of the Jews" on a board and put it above Jesus?
Why did someone write "King of the Jews" on a paper and put it above Jesus?
Why did someone write "King of the Jews" and put it above Jesus?
What was Jesus officially accused of?
For what purported crime was Jesus crucified?

Questions.Q: Whom else did they crucify at the same time as Jesus?
Questions.A: They crucified two robbers at the same time. (27)

Questions.Q: What was the attitude of those who passed by?
Questions.A: They insulted and mocked Jesus. (29)

Questions.Q: Why do you think that those people shook their heads at him?
Questions.A: Shaking their heads was a cultural way to show that they were ridiculing him.

Questions.Q: What did those people say was the reason that they ridiculed him?
Questions.A: They said that since he was the one who said that he would destroy and rebuild the temple in three days, he should be able to get down off the cross and save his own life. (29-30)

Questions.Q: Why do you think that Jesus did not use his power and come down from the cross?
Questions.A: He did not come down from the cross because he knew that we all needed to have him take our place and die for our sin. By his suffering in our place, God then could receive us into the group of those who are his very own.

Questions.Q: What did the chief priests and teachers of the law say to mock Jesus?
Questions.A: They said that he had saved other people, but he could not save himself. (31)
They said that if he would come down from the cross, they would believe that he was the Christ, the king of the Jews. (32)

Questions.Q: What happened to Jesus while he hung on the cross?
Questions.A: He cried out to God (34) and then he died (37).

Questions.Q: What unusual things happened while Jesus hung on the cross and then died?
Questions.A: It became dark everywhere for three hours in the middle of the day. (33)
The curtain that hung in the temple tore from the top down. (38)

Questions.Q: What happened at the sixth hour of daylight (that is, about midday)?
Questions.A: It became dark. (33)

Questions.Q: How long did it remain dark?
Questions.A: It remained dark for about three hours. (33)

Questions.Q: How do we know that Jesus did not feel that God was near to him at that time?
Questions.A: Jesus cried out (in a loud voice), asking God why he had left him all alone. (34)

Questions.Q: What was it that Jesus cried out loudly?
Questions.A: He cried out, "My God, My God, why have you left me all by myself?" (34)

Questions.Q: What did some of the people nearby think that he was saying?
Questions.A: They thought that he was calling out to [the prophet] Elijah. (35)

Questions.Q: Why do you think that they thought that?
Questions.A: They thought that because the word "Eloi" (that is, "My God") sounds rather like "Elijah" in the Aramaic language which Jesus was speaking.

Questions.Q: What did one man do then?
Questions.A: One of them dipped a sponge in some ordinary wine, put it on a stick, and held it up to Jesus's mouth for him to drink. (36)

Questions.Q: Do you think that Jesus drank what the man offered him?
Questions.A: Yes
Questions.Note: Mark does not tell us, but John wrote in his gospel that Jesus had asked for something to drink and then did drink from the sponge (John 19:28-30).

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do at the moment when he died?
Questions.A: He cried out loudly. (37)

Questions.Q: How do we know that Jesus died and was not just unconscious?
Questions.A: Mark wrote that Jesus stopped breathing (that is, he died). (37)

Questions.Q: What happened in the temple at the time when Jesus died?
Questions.A: The [heavy] curtain [which closed off the entrance to the holy place] in the temple was torn apart from the top to the bottom. (38)
-OR-
God caused the curtain in the temple to tare apart from the top to the bottom. (38)

Questions.Q: Who do you think caused that curtain to tear from the top part down to the bottom of it?
Questions.A: God caused it to tear like that; no person would be able to do that, especially from the top down.

Questions.Q: Who was one of the people watching Jesus?
Questions.A: A Roman centurion (that is, an officer over other soldiers) stood there opposite Jesus. (39)

Questions.Q: What did he say about Jesus?
Questions.A: He said that Jesus was certainly the Son of God. (39)
-OR-
He said that Jesus was certainly a son of a god (that is, someone superior to any human). (39)

Questions.Q: Why did that officer of the Roman soldiers say that?
Questions.A: He saw the darkness, heard what Jesus cried out, and he saw how he died. (39)

Questions.Q: Who else was standing a little distance away and watching?
Questions.A: Some of the women who had followed Jesus were watching [what happened to him]. They included (a) Mary Magdalene, (b) Mary the mother of James and Joses, and (c) Salome (40), plus many others (41).

Questions.Q: What had these women been doing for Jesus as they traveled with him and his disciples?
Questions.A: They had followed Jesus and looked after him. (41)
Questions.Note: This implies cooking, providing food, etc. They would have been looking after his disciples too, although it does not specifically say so here.

Section.heading: Mark 15:42-47 Joseph of Arimathea took the body of Jesus down from the cross and laid him in a tomb.

Questions.Q: What happened to the body of Jesus?
Questions.A: Joseph put it in a tomb (that is, in a burial cave). (46)

Questions.Q: What day was it when Jesus died?
Questions.A: It was the day for the Jews to get [food and other things] ready for the Sabbath day. (42)

Questions.Q: Who was Joseph?
Questions.A: Joseph was a man from [the town of] Arimathea.
He was an important member of the council [of Jewish leaders].
He was waiting for the time when God would rule his people. (43)

Questions.Q: Do you think that he was the Joseph who was the husband of Mary?
Questions.A: No, he was not. That was another person called Joseph.

Questions.Q: What did this Joseph do?
Questions.A: He went to Pilate and asked [Pilate to permit him] to take away Jesus's body. (43)

Questions.Q: Do you think that he was afraid to go to Pilate to ask this?
Questions.A: Perhaps, but he went boldly, without showing any fear. (43)

Questions.Q: What did Mark write that tells us why Joseph may have been so bold?
Questions.A: Mark wrote that it was nearing the evening time (42).
Questions.Note: The Jewish people considered that the Sabbath day began when the sun had set on what we call Friday, so no Jewish person would be allowed to do anything to bury Jesus's body after about six o'clock. Darkness was not the main problem.

Questions.Q: What was it that surprised Pilate?
Questions.A: He was surprised to hear that Jesus had already died. (44)

Questions.Q: How did Pilate check that Jesus really was dead?
Questions.A: He called the officer of the Roman soldiers [who had been at the cross],
and asked him if it was true that Jesus had already died. (45)

Questions.Q: What did the officer reply?
Questions.A: The officer said that Jesus was dead. (45)

Questions.Q: What did Pilate do then?
Questions.A: He permitted Joseph to take Jesus's body. (45)

Questions.Q: What did Joseph do with the Jesus's body?
Questions.A: He took it down from the cross, wrapped it in a linen cloth and put it in a tomb. (46)

Questions.Q: What did Mark write about the tomb where Joseph laid the body of Jesus?
Questions.A: He wrote that the tomb (that is, the burial cave) had been dug out of rock. (46)

Questions.Q: How did Joseph close the opening to the tomb?
Questions.A: [Others helped him] roll a large stone across the opening. (46)

Questions.Q: Who saw the place where Joseph put the body of Jesus?
Questions.A: Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses saw where his body was. (47)

Section.heading: Mark 16:1-20 God raised Jesus back to life.

Questions.Q: Why were the women not able to find the body of Jesus?
Questions.A: They could not find his body because he [was alive again and] had risen and left the tomb. (6)

Questions.Q: To whom did Jesus show himself?
Questions.A: He showed himself to Mary Magdalene (9),
to two of his other followers (12),
and to all eleven of his disciples (14).

Questions.Q: What happened to Jesus after he told his disciples what they should then do?
Questions.A: [God] took him up to heaven (and he sat at the right hand side of God). (19)

Questions.Q: What did the women do?
Questions.A: They bought some spices/ointments to anoint (that is, rub on) the body of Jesus. (1)

Questions.Q: When was it that the women bought those spices?
Questions.A: They bought them after sunset, when the Sabbath day had ended. (1)

Questions.Q: What time was it when the women went to the tomb?
Questions.A: It was very early in the morning on [the day after the Sabbath day,] the first day of the Jewish week [which in English we call, "Sunday."] (2)

Questions.Q: What caused the women to be anxious?
Questions.A: They knew that they would not be strong enough to roll aside the very large stone that covered the opening of the tomb, so they wondered who would do it [for them]. (3)

Questions.Q: What did the women find when they reached the tomb?
Questions.A: They found that [someone] already had rolled aside the (very large) stone. (4)

Questions.Q: What did they see when they went into the tomb?
Questions.A: They saw a young man dressed in white clothes, sitting on [their] right hand side. (5)

Questions.Q: What did they feel when they saw this person sitting there?
Questions.A: They were frightened/alarmed. (6)

Questions.Q: Why do you think that they were frightened/alarmed?
Questions.A: They did not know who this man was, and he probably appeared unusual.
Questions.Alternative: Why do you think that they were frightened?
Why do you think that they were alarmed?

Questions.Q: What did the young man say about Jesus?
Questions.A: He said that Jesus was not there because he had risen after being dead. (6)

Questions.Q: What message from Jesus did the young man have for them?
Questions.A: He told them that Jesus said that they were to go and tell Peter and the other disciples that he (Jesus) had gone ahead of them to Galilee [province].
Jesus also had said that they would see him when they arrived there, just like he had told them before. (7)

Questions.Q: How did the women respond to those things happening at the tomb?
Questions.A: Because they were afraid and confused about all that was happening, they hurried away from the tomb. They also did not tell anyone [along the way] what they had seen and heard. (8)

Questions.Q: What day was it when Jesus rose from being dead?
Questions.A: He rose on the first day of the [Jewish] week, the day after the Sabbath day. (9)

Questions.Q: What had Jesus previously done for Mary Magdalene?
Questions.A: He had cast out seven demons/evil spirits from her. (9)

Questions.Q: What did Mary do after she had seen Jesus?
Questions.A: She went and told [the news] to those who had been with him and [now] were mourning. (10)

Questions.Q: What did Mary tell them?
Questions.A: She told them that Jesus was alive again and that she had seen him [herself]. (11)

Questions.Q: What did the disciples do when they heard what Mary said?
Questions.A: They did not believe her report. (11)

Questions.Q: To whom else did Jesus show himself?
Questions.A: He showed himself to two of his other followers as they were walking out in the country. (12)

Questions.Q: What did Mark write about the way that Jesus looked when the two followers saw him?
Questions.A: He looked different somehow, but it does not say in what way he looked different. (12)

Questions.Q: What did these two disciples do after they realized that they had seen Jesus?
Questions.A: They went back to Jerusalem and told the other disciples. (13)

Questions.Q: What did the other disciples do when they heard what these two said?
Questions.A: They did not believe what they told them either. (13)

Questions.Q: To whom did Jesus then show himself?
Questions.A: He showed himself to all of the eleven disciples (as they were eating). (14)

Questions.Q: Why did he rebuke them?
Questions.A: He rebuked them because they had refused to believe the people who told them that they had seen him after he had risen [from being dead]. (14)

Questions.Q: To whom did Jesus say that the disciples should tell the Good News?
Questions.A: He said that they should tell the Good News to all people everywhere in the world. (15)

Questions.Q: What message/news do you think it was that Jesus said they should tell?
Questions.A: They should tell the message about how God's son, Jesus, has provided a way for God to forgive and receive people, even though they have sinned.
Questions.Alternative: What message do you think it was that Jesus said they should tell?
What news do you think it was that Jesus said they should tell?

Questions.Q: What must people do in order that God will not condemn them to eternal punishment?
Questions.A: They must believe [the gospel] and be baptized. (16)

Questions.Q: What will happen to people who do not believe the gospel?
Questions.A: God will condemn them [to eternal punishment]. (16)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say that God would enable those who believed in him to do?
Questions.A: They would be able to send/cast out demons/evil spirits from people;
they would speak new languages [in the power of the Holy Spirit];
they would pick up snakes in their hands [without being harmed]; (17)
if they drink poisonous things that could kill them, they would not be harmed;
and they would lay their hands on sick people, and they would become well. (18)

Questions.Q: Why would God give them power to do these things?
Questions.A: These actions would be signs to show people that God is with his followers and that their message is truly from him. (17)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when it says that Jesus sat down at the right hand side of God?
Questions.A: In Jewish custom the right hand side of important people was the most honored position anyone could ever have. His position there also shows his great authority along with God over the universe.

Questions.Q: What did the disciples do after Jesus had left them?
Questions.A: They went (out from Jerusalem) and preached the gospel everywhere. (20)

Questions.Q: How did the people know that the disciples' message was truly from God?
Questions.A: The Lord [Jesus] did many amazing things through them as they proclaimed his message. (20)
Questions.Note: Those "amazing things" in Greek clearly refer to those things Mark described in verses 17-18.

Section.heading: Matthew 1:1-17 Here is the genealogy of Jesus.

Questions.Q: What did Matthew write about in this first seventeen verse section?
Questions.A: This section lists the ancestors of Jesus, beginning with Abraham and continuing to Joseph, Mary's husband.

Questions.Q: What does verse one tell us about the way in which Jesus Christ was related to Abraham?
Questions.A: Jesus, counting through Joseph's ancestors, was a descendant/descendant of David; and David was a descendant of Abraham. (1)
Questions.Note: With this question, the checker/consultant can find out whether the translation suggests that Jesus was the immediate son of David and that David was the immediate son of Abraham.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the meaning of "Christ" in this verse?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In this verse "Christ" is used as a name.
Questions.Note: See "Christ" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Who was Isaac's father?
Questions.A: Isaac's father was Abraham. (2)

Questions.Q: Who was Isaac's son?
Questions.A: Isaac's son was Jacob. (2)

Questions.Q: If you were writing or explaining about different generations of people, which of these two explanations would you be more likely to use in order to make it sound more natural? 1. Would you explain/write about Isaac being the father of Jacob, and Jacob the father of Judah? or 2. Would you explain the difference by writing/saying Isaac bore Jacob, and Jacob bore Judah?
Questions.Note: This is a test for naturalness.
Questions.Alternative: If you were writing or explaining about different generations of people, which of these two explanations would you be more likely to use in order to make it sound more natural? 1. Would you explain about Isaac being the father of Jacob, and Jacob the father of Judah? or 2. Would you explain the difference by writing Isaac bore Jacob, and Jacob bore Judah?

If you were writing or explaining about different generations of people, which of these two explanations would you be more likely to use in order to make it sound more natural? 1. Would you explain about Isaac being the father of Jacob, and Jacob the father of Judah? or 2. Would you explain the difference by saying Isaac bore Jacob, and Jacob bore Judah?

If you were writing or explaining about different generations of people, which of these two explanations would you be more likely to use in order to make it sound more natural? 1. Would you write about Isaac being the father of Jacob, and Jacob the father of Judah? or 2. Would you explain the difference by writing Isaac bore Jacob, and Jacob bore Judah?

If you were writing or explaining about different generations of people, which of these two explanations would you be more likely to use in order to make it sound more natural? 1. Would you write about Isaac being the father of Jacob, and Jacob the father of Judah? or 2. Would you explain the difference by saying Isaac bore Jacob, and Jacob bore Judah?

Questions.Q: When people read verse 16, is it clear to them/can they tell who was Jesus's mother?
Questions.A: Yes. It was Mary who gave birth to him. (16)
Questions.Alternative: When people read verse 16, is it clear to them who was Jesus's mother?
When people read verse 16, can they tell who was Jesus's mother?
From verse 16, is it clear who Jesus' mother was?

Questions.Q: When people read verse 16, what will they understand about Joseph?
Questions.A: They will understand that he was Mary's husband. (16)
Questions.Note: Matthew was careful not to imply that Joseph was the true father of Jesus.

Questions.Q: What does the linking word or words that join verse 17 to the earlier verses mean?
Questions.A: The link back to the earlier verses should show that all the ancestors/generations, mentioned in this account, are fourteen in each section/case. That is, between Abraham and David, between David and the deportation to Babylon, and again between the deportation and the birth of the Christ/Messiah, there are fourteen generations listed.
Questions.Note: Genealogies did not have to mention every generation/all of the actual generations to be a valid proof of a person's lineage; and this one does not show all of the generations in each set. Some had more than the fourteen listed here.
Questions.Alternative: What does the linking word that joins verse 17 to the earlier verses mean?
What do the linking words that join verse 17 to the earlier verses mean?

Questions.Q: What do you think is the meaning of "the Christ" in 1:17?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "Christ" is the English rendering of the Greek word Christos, which means "God's anointed one."
Questions.Note: See "Christ" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think is the meaning of "the Christ"?

Section.heading: Matthew 1:18-25 Jesus, the Messiah, was born.

Questions.Q: How did Mary become pregnant? The text reveals that she did not have [sexual] union with Joseph, until after Jesus was born.
Questions.A: The Holy Spirit, by a miracle, caused her to become pregnant. (18)
Questions.Alternative: How did Mary become pregnant? The text reveals that she did not have sexual union with Joseph, until after Jesus was born.
How did Mary become pregnant? The text reveals that she did not have union with Joseph, until after Jesus was born.

Questions.Q: Who do you think the Holy Spirit is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He is God's spirit, through whom he acts, reveals His will, and empowers individuals. (See "Holy Spirit" in KBT in the "spirit" entry.)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Joseph decided not to take Mary as his wife?
Questions.A: He decided not to take Mary as his wife because he found out that she had become pregnant. (18)

Questions.Q: What sort of person does the text/the Scripture say Joseph was?
Questions.A: He was a righteous person—one who did what was right. (19)
Questions.Alternative: What sort of person does the text say Joseph was?
What sort of person does the Scripture say Joseph was?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Joseph wanted to break off the planned marriage privately?
Questions.A: He wanted to break off the planned marriage so that he would not cause problems for Mary, such as causing her to be embarrassed. (19)

Questions.Q: In his dream what did an/the angel tell Joseph?
Questions.A: The angel told Joseph not to be concerned, but to go ahead and take Mary home as his wife because she was pregnant by/from the Holy Spirit. She had not been unfaithful to Joseph. (20)
Questions.Alternative: In his dream what did an angel tell Joseph?
In his dream what did the angel tell Joseph?

Questions.Q: What do you know about angels?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Angels are spiritual messengers, who either deliver a message to humans, carry out God's will, praise God, or guard God's throne.
Questions.Note: See "angel" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did the angel tell Joseph about the child that Mary was carrying?
Questions.A: The angel told him that it would be a boy, and that Joseph should name him Jesus, (which meant "Savior"). He was to name him that because he would save his people from their sins. (21)

Questions.Q: What does it mean to "save people from their sin"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that Jesus/He saves people from remaining guilty in God's sight, and so from receiving the punishment they would otherwise receive because of their sin.
Questions.Note: See "save" in KBT.
This is a check for any wrong meaning.

Questions.Q: What does a person do when he sins?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He deliberately keeps on doing those things that please himself and displease God.
Questions.Note: See "sin" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Who had said that a virgin would be/become pregnant and would have/bear a son whom people would call Emmanuel?
Questions.A: An Old Testament prophet had said/written that. (22-23)
Questions.Alternative: Who had said that a virgin would be pregnant and would have a son whom people would call Emmanuel?
Who had said that a virgin would be pregnant and would bear a son whom people would call Emmanuel?
Who had said that a virgin would become pregnant and would have a son whom people would call Emmanuel?
Who had said that a virgin would become pregnant and would bear a son whom people would call Emmanuel?

Questions.Q: What do you know about prophets?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A prophet is someone who speaks for God because God inspires him. He often foretells future events. Prophets were mainly spokespersons who called/challenged His people to obey/obedience by appealing to Israel's past and future.
Questions.Note: See "prophet" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What does the name Emmanuel mean?
Questions.A: Emmanuel means "God is with us". (23)

Questions.Q: When Matthew wrote this name, Emmanuel, and its meaning, what do you think he wanted us to understand about Jesus?
Questions.A: Matthew wanted us to understand that, because Jesus was/is the Son of God, he is/was not an ordinary man. He is himself God.

Questions.Q: Who do you think God is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He is the supreme being whom people should worship. In English, the term "God" with a capital "G" is used to refer to the one supreme Creator. The term "god" with a small "g", as in "a god" or "many gods", can refer to any spiritual being whom people worship. The Greek word theos can be used in the same two ways.
Questions.Note: In many languages the term for God is a proper name and cannot be used to refer to anyone except the one supreme creator of the world. It cannot be pluralized. (Or, if it can be pluralized, the meaning may be something very different from the English "gods".) (See "God" in KBT.)

Questions.Q: What did Joseph do after the angel told him that Mary had been faithful to him, and explained how she had become/it was that she was pregnant?
Questions.A: He proceeded to take Mary home to be his wife. (24)
Questions.Alternative: What did Joseph do after the angel told him that Mary had been faithful to him, and explained how she had become pregnant?
What did Joseph do after the angel told him that Mary had been faithful to him, and explained how it was that she was pregnant?

Questions.Q: Did they have sexual relations as married couples usually would?
Questions.A: No. They did not have sexual relations before Jesus was born. (25)

Section.heading: Matthew 2:1-12 Wise men from the east came to see Jesus.

Questions.Q: Who came to Jerusalem from far away in/to the east and asked where the king of the Jews was born? They asked so that they could go to worship him.
Questions.A: The Magi, [astrologers], [learned men from the east] came. (1)
Questions.Alternative: Who came to Jerusalem from far away in the east and asked where the king of the Jews was born? They asked so that they could go to worship him.
Who came to Jerusalem from far away to the east and asked where the king of the Jews was born? They asked so that they could go to worship him.

Questions.Q: What happened at Bethlehem at that time/at the time of this passage?
Questions.A: Jesus was born there. (1)
Questions.Alternative: What happened at Bethlehem at that time?
What happened at Bethlehem at the time of this passage?

Questions.Q: To what do you think the name Judea referred?
Questions.A: Judea was the name of a province governed by the Romans where the Jewish people lived.

Questions.Q: In what province was Jesus born?
Questions.A: Jesus was born in the Roman province of Judea. (1)

Questions.Q: How did those men know that the Jewish king had been born?
Questions.A: We do not know what else they may have known from hearing about predictions of a promised messiah, but Matthew wrote/it says that they had seen his star and then had come to worship him. (2)

Questions.Q: What do you think those men wanted to do when they said that they wanted to worship Jesus/the newborn king?
Questions.Note: Those men wanted to give respect and devotion to Jesus/the newborn king.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think those men wanted to do when they said that they wanted to worship Jesus?
What do you think those men wanted to do when they said that they wanted to worship the newborn king?

Questions.Q: What do you know about Jews?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A Jew was a member of the nation of Palestine from the 6th century B.C. to the first century A.D. The term "Jews" refers to the descendants of Abraham through his son Isaac. A Jew was a member of the people of Israel. He was committed to the Jewish religious system. All male Jews were circumcised on the 8th day after their birth, and this was a mark of being a Jew. (See "Jew" in KBT in the "Israel" entry.)

Questions.Q: What caused Herod to be worried?
Questions.A: When Herod heard that the king of the Jews had been born, he was worried that this Jewish boy might cause the Jews to reject him, since he was a Roman king who was ruling over them. (3)

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that the people of Jerusalem were also disturbed?
Questions.A: They also were afraid because they knew that, if the Roman government leaders began thinking that the Jews were preparing to choose/have their own king, the Romans would send their soldiers to punish the Jews.
Questions.Note: This is a check for wrong meaning.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Herod called together the chief priests and scribes?
Questions.A: He called them together in order to ask them where that/this important leader, who was referred to as Messiah by the prophets in the Old Testament, was to be born. (4)

Questions.Q: What do you know about the chief priests?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The chief priests were the leaders among the priests at the temple in Jerusalem. They decided everything that had to do with the worship of God and with the use of the temple grounds.
Questions.Note: See "chief priest" in KBT.

Questions.Q: How would those people know where the Messiah was to be born?
Questions.Note: They would know from reading what the prophets had written in (Old Testament) scripture. (5)
(See Micah 5:2.)

Questions.Q: What had one of the prophets written?
Questions.A: He had prophesied saying that Bethlehem village, though a small place, was actually an important place in the land of Judah, since a ruler from that village would lead Israel someday. (6)

Questions.Q: What do you know about the name "Israel"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In the New Testament, the terms "Israel" and "Israelite" are used by Jews to refer to themselves. Those terms were also used by God to refer to them as his people.
Questions.Note: See "Israel" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did Herod find out secretly from the Magi?
Questions.A: He asked them just when the star had first appeared, [and they would have told him]. (7)

Questions.Q: What did he tell them to do?
Questions.A: He told them to go and find the child and then to report back to him. He told them that he wanted to go and worship the new ruler when they found him. (8)

Questions.Q: When the Magi left Herod, how did they find their way to where the child Jesus was?
Questions.A: The same star, that they had seen previously/before, guided them to where the child was. (9-10)

Questions.Q: What did they do when they found the child?
Questions.A: They bowed down and worshiped him and then they gave him costly gifts/presents which/that they had brought with them. (11)

Questions.Q: What did the wise men do about telling king Herod that they had found the child?
Questions.A: God spoke to them by a dream telling them that they were not to return to Herod; so they left by a different route and returned to their own country. (12)

Questions.A: He took them to Egypt. (14)

Questions.A: He took them to Egypt because an angel had appeared to him in a dream and told him to do that, before Herod's soldiers/men could find and kill Jesus. (13-14)

Questions.A: This was the time that God's son went to Egypt, so that later he could be called out of Egypt.

Questions.Q: What did Herod do when he realized that the Magi had not come back to report where they found the child, as he had asked them to do?
Questions.A: He sent his men/soldiers to Bethlehem to kill all of the boys two years old and younger that lived anywhere near Bethlehem. (16)

Questions.Q: How did killing the Bethlehem children like that fulfill what the prophet Jeremiah had said/written [in a kind of poetry which is quoted here] [in verse 18]?
Questions.A: Ramah refers to a place near Bethlehem.
Rachel refers to Isaac's wife who is/was viewed as the ancestral mother of the nation of Israel.
Questions.Note: The introduction to the Old Testament quote/quotation in the translation here may need to state that the prophet said/wrote this about a place in the Bethlehem area. The original readers would have known that Ramah and Bethlehem were (located in) the same area.

Questions.A: Joseph returned to his homeland because Herod had died. An angel from God came, spoke to Joseph/him in a dream and told him to return to Israel. (19-21)

Questions.Q: What did Joseph do when he realized that Archelaus was the new king over Judea district?
Questions.A: He took his family and went to live at/in Nazareth in the Galilee district. (22-23)

Questions.Q: How did that move, which Joseph and Mary made, help fulfill what had been predicted about the Messiah?
Questions.A: Since Jesus lived at Nazareth, people would tend to call him a "Nazarene". By doing that, they fulfilled what one of the prophets had foretold, saying/writing that the Messiah would be called a Nazarene. (23)

Section.heading: Matthew 3:1-12 John the Baptist told people to repent.

Questions.Q: What sort of person do you think was the man John the Baptist?
Questions.A: He was one who lived simply and he proclaimed God's message. (He was much like the Old Testament prophets.)

Questions.Q: What did John the Baptist do?
Questions.A: He told the people that there was a much more important person among them, whom they should follow, namely Jesus. He told them all to repent and obey God, since the time when God would rule them was near. (1-12)

Questions.Q: What do you think Matthew meant when he wrote that John the Baptist "came" or "appeared"?
Questions.A: He did not mean that John came to a certain place, but that he came into the public view, that is, he appeared on the scene, doing a public ministry. (1)

Questions.Q: From what Matthew wrote, when do you think he "came"/"appeared"?
Questions.A: The words of verse 1, "In those days", refers to the time while Jesus still lived at Nazareth. (1)
Questions.Note: We know that these events mentioned here in this text occurred many years after Jesus started living at Nazareth. At that time Jesus and John would have both been about 30 years old.
Questions.Alternative: From what Matthew wrote, when do you think he "came"?

Questions.Q: John the Baptist told people to repent in verse 2. What do you think it means when someone repents?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that the person regrets his sins and unbelief, turns from them and follows God.
Questions.Note: See "repent" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think John meant when he said that the kingdom of heaven was near?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The English word kingdom is used here in its nearly obsolete meaning of kingship. It refers to the fact of God's ruling in people's lives rather than referring to the area of the earth over which he rules. The meaning here is that the King [that is, Jesus,] was near, that the time when God will rule over people (in a special way) was to occur soon.
Questions.Note: See "kingdom of heaven" in KBT.

Questions.Q: About whom was Isaiah talking/writing when he predicted many years before, that someone in a sparsely populated place would be calling out for people to prepare the road [or way] for the Lord's coming?

Questions.Q: What do you think Matthew wanted the people to learn by his telling them about the type of clothing and food that John used?
Questions.Note: He probably wanted them to learn that John was like the Old Testament prophets and not like the city religious leaders of his time. He was like Elijah. (4)
See 2 Kings 1:8.

Questions.Q: Were the people whom John taught willing to follow his teaching?
Questions.A: Yes, they were. (4-6)

Questions.Q: How can we tell?
Questions.A: Matthew wrote that people from the whole surrounding area went to hear/and heard John's teaching. They confessed their sins, and he baptized them. (5-6)

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that John was not glad that the Pharisees and Sadducees came to him to be baptized?
Questions.A: He was not glad because he knew that they did not come wanting/in pursuit of a right relationship with God. They were just acting as though they agreed with John's teaching about repenting and worshiping God so that others would think well of them. (7-10)

Questions.Q: What do you know about Pharisees?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The Pharisees were the largest and most important of the Jewish religious groups. They controlled the synagogues and exercised great control over the general population. They taught that the way to God was through obeying the law. They opposed Jesus because He refused to accept the teachings of their oral law.
Questions.Note: See "Pharisee" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Who do you think the Sadducees were?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The Sadducees were another religious party of the Jews.
Questions.Note: See "Sadducee" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think John meant when he said they needed to produce the kind of fruit that comes from people who truly repent?
Questions.A: He meant that they needed to really change their attitude toward God and show it by their actions. (8)

Questions.Q: What was wrong with considering themselves the descendants of Abraham when they really were his descendants?
Questions.A: They mistakenly hoped that God would have to accept them no matter what they did, since they were Abraham's descendants. (This can be understood from the immediate as well as the broader context.)

Questions.Q: What do you think John meant when he said that God could make stones into children for/of Abraham if he wanted?
Questions.A: He was saying that, if God needed children for/of Abraham, he could easily do it by making them from stones. (9)
Questions.Alternative: What do you think John meant when he said that God could make stones into children for Abraham if he wanted?
What do you think John meant when he said that God could make stones into children of Abraham if he wanted?

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that John talked about cutting down trees that did not bear good fruit?
Questions.A: John was showing that God wanted people who will truly serve him. He will treat those who will not serve him as/in the same manner that men do their fruit trees that do not produce good fruit. They cut them down and burn them. (Context of 7-10 and broader NT context.)

Questions.Q: Who do you think was the one who would soon appear?
Questions.A: Jesus was the one who would soon appear. (11)

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that John might have felt that he was unfit to even carry (or untie) Jesus's sandals?
Questions.A: He might have felt that way because he knew who Jesus was. He felt unworthy to do anything for Jesus. (11)

Questions.Q: What did John think about his water baptism as compared to Jesus's kind of baptism?
Questions.A: John showed that he knew Jesus's baptism was more important/much greater. (11)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when someone is baptized?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "Baptism" is the outward sign by which a person's commitment to and union with Jesus Christ are publicly demonstrated.
Questions.Note: See "baptize" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think John was talking about when he mentioned that Jesus would baptize people with the Holy Spirit?
Questions.A: He was talking about Jesus sending the Holy Spirit to be with his people. (11)
Questions.Note: The change that the Holy Spirit would bring in people's lives would, like water baptism, be a sign to other people that they were now following God.

Questions.Q: When John said that Jesus would "baptize with the Holy Spirit and fire", what do you think he meant by "fire"? (This is a check for any obviously wrong meaning.)
Questions.A: There are different possible interpretations of what John meant.
In the Bible:

1) Fire is used figuratively to indicate purification, since fire is sometimes used to burn up less costly and less permanent elements, while leaving the valuable elements unharmed. This purification figure is commonly applied/used to apply to Christians in the New Testament.
2) Fire is used to indicate punishment/judgment from God by association with the pain of burning. Such punishment/judgment would usually apply to non-believers in the New Testament.
Questions.Note: From John's concern that, at least some of them, might depend on their status of being descendants of Abraham and miss God's blessing, he could be referring to some of them as being baptized with the Holy Spirit and others being baptized with fire. This would then make fire here mean about the same as in verses 10 and 12, where it means judgment/punishment.

Questions.Q: While he was speaking to the Pharisees and Sadducees, what do you think is the reason that John talked about God winnowing everything on his threshing floor—saving the wheat and burning the chaff?
Questions.Note: He was telling them to truly repent and to change their actions, so that they would not be punished.

Questions.Q: What kind of fire did John say God would use to burn up the chaff/unusable part?
Questions.A: God would use fire that could not be extinguished/put out. (12)
Questions.Alternative: What kind of fire did John say God would use to burn up the chaff?
What kind of fire did John say God would use to burn up the unusable part?

Questions.Q: In these verses what did Jesus ask/want John to do?
Questions.A: Jesus wanted John to baptize him. (13)
Questions.Alternative: In these verses what did Jesus ask John to do?
In these verses what did Jesus want John to do?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that John did not want to baptize Jesus?
Questions.A: John knew that Jesus did not need to repent of any sin or be forgiven for any sin, as he himself and other people did. (14)

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that Jesus wanted John to go ahead and baptize him?
Questions.Note: He apparently wanted to set an example to show what God required people to do. Also when John baptized Jesus, it would show everyone that he approved of John's work. (15)

Questions.Q: What happened when Jesus was baptized?
Questions.A: Jesus saw God's Spirit descend onto him like a dove. The people who were there heard a voice that said, "This is my son, listen to him." (16-17)

Section.heading: Matthew 4:1-11 The Devil tried to tempt Jesus.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the Spirit/Holy Spirit led Jesus into the desert?
Questions.A: The Spirit led Jesus into the desert to be tempted by the Devil. (1)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that the Spirit led Jesus into the desert?
What is the reason that the Holy Spirit led Jesus into the desert?

Questions.Q: What does it mean for the Devil to tempt someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that the Devil tries to make the person obey him or to do something to disobey higher authorities, such as parents, the government, or God.

Questions.Q: What do you know about the Devil?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The term/word "Devil" is the Greek equivalent of the Hebrew word "Satan." Satan is the chief enemy of God. He is the supreme evil spiritual being, who leads and directs all other evil spiritual beings. (See "Devil" in KBT in the "Satan" entry.)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Jesus might have wanted to turn stones into bread?
Questions.A: He was hungry. He had not eaten for 40 days. (2-3)

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that Jesus did not want to turn the stones into bread?
Questions.A: Jesus wanted to do His Father's will rather than follow Satan's demands. (4)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to "live on (or by) every word that God speaks"?
Questions.A: It means to follow all of God's instructions. (4)

Questions.Q: To what city did Satan take Jesus?
Questions.A: Satan took Jesus to Jerusalem. (5)

Questions.Q: To what building did Satan take Jesus/him?
Questions.A: Satan took him to the temple. (5)
Questions.Alternative: To what building did Satan take Jesus?
To what building did Satan take him?

Questions.Q: What was the purpose of the temple?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The people used the temple as a place to worship God. // The people worshiped God in the temple.
Questions.Note: See "temple" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: For what purpose do you think people used the temple?
How do you think people used the temple?

Questions.Q: After Satan took Jesus to the very top of the temple, what did he ask him to do?
Questions.A: Satan asked Jesus to jump (down) to the ground. (6)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Jesus would not jump down?
Questions.A: Jesus would not jump down because he did not want to test God by following anything Satan said/by doing what Satan asked him to do. (7)

Questions.Q: What do you think that Jesus meant when he said that he did not want to "test" God?
Questions.Note: Jesus meant that He did not need to know if God would protect him, if he jumped (down) off of the temple.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the devil took Jesus to the top of a high hill?
Questions.A: The devil took Jesus to a high hill, so that he would be able to see a very large area. (8)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Jesus would not bow down and worship Satan?
Questions.A: Jesus would not worship Satan because he knew that God wanted him to worship and serve only him. (10)

Questions.Q: Who is Satan?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Satan is a spirit being, who is the chief enemy of God and of those who believe in God's Son, Jesus.
Questions.Note: See "Satan" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think people who read this will/would think the angels had probably done for Jesus when they helped him?
Questions.Note: They could have given him food or just strengthened him. Their help probably met whatever need he had at that/the time. (11)

Questions.Q: How did that move fulfill what had been predicted by the prophet Isaiah in the Old Testament?
Questions.A: After he moved/After he made that move, Jesus was in the area of Zebulun and Naphtali near the Sea of Galilee, where many non-Jewish people lived. Isaiah had predicted in the Old Testament that the Gentiles (non-Jewish people) would hear about a great light (salvation), after having been in [spiritual] darkness [without a relationship to God]. This move by Jesus caused those Gentiles near those places/there to hear about/have the light of Jesus teaching to guide them to become right with God. (14-16)

Questions.Q: Who do you think the Gentiles are?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In this verse, they are those people who are not Jews.
Questions.Note: See "Gentiles" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What reason did Jesus give that people should repent?
Questions.A: He said that people should repent because the kingdom of heaven (the time of God's ruling on earth in a special way) was to occur now. (17)

Questions.Q: When people hear or read this scripture passage, what do you think they will understand about what Jesus said?
Questions.A: The king whom God sent [that is, Christ,] had arrived and it was time for them/people to repent and submit to his authority. (17)

Section.heading: Matthew 4:18-22 Jesus called the first four men to become his disciples.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do that Matthew told us about in these verses?
Questions.A: He called four men to become his disciples.

Questions.Q: Whom did Jesus first call to be his disciples?
Questions.A: He called Simon and Andrew first. (18)

Questions.Q: What was Simon's other name?
Questions.A: Simon's other name was Peter. (18)

Questions.Q: What work did Simon and Andrew do before Jesus called them to follow him?
Questions.A: They were fishermen. (18)

Questions.Q: Were they willing to leave their work?
Questions.A: Yes, they left their fishing work and they went with Jesus. (20)

Questions.Q: Whom else did Jesus call to become his disciples that day?
Questions.A: He called James and John, sons of Zebedee. (21)

Section.heading: Matthew 4:23-25 Jesus taught the good news of the kingdom and healed the sick.

Questions.Q: How did people feel about Jesus at that time/at the time of this incident?
Questions.A: People were happy with Jesus at that time.
Questions.Alternative: How did people feel about Jesus at that time?
How did people feel about Jesus at the time of this incident?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do as he traveled around in Galilee?
Questions.A: He taught in the synagogues, preached/told the good news about God's way of ruling over people and he healed the sick people. (23)

Questions.Q: What do you think a synagogue is/was?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A synagogue is/was a building or place of assembly used by Jewish communities primarily for religious worship.
Questions.Note: See "synagogue" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think a synagogue is?
What do you think a synagogue was?

Questions.Q: What do you think someone is doing when he preaches?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: When someone preaches, he is proclaiming the gospel to those who are listening. This also means that the one who preaches/a person urges others to accept or abandon an idea or course of action.

Questions.Q: What happened then?
Questions.A: People from all over Syria heard of Jesus and began bringing their sick and demon possessed people to him and he healed them. So people heard about him and large crowds from several of the surrounding areas followed him. (24-25)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to have a demon/be demon possessed?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that the person is troubled or controlled by the demon, i.e. the demon is exercising its evil power over him. (See "demon" in KBT in the "evil spirit, unclean spirit" entry.)
Questions.Alternative: What do you think it means for someone to have a demon?
What do you think it means for someone to be demon possessed?

Section.heading: Matthew 5:1-12 Jesus taught while sitting on the mountainside.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do when he saw the crowds?
Questions.A: He went and sat down on a mountainside and he began to teach his disciples and the other people there. (1-2)

Questions.Q: What do you think a disciple is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The word "disciple" means one who has attached himself to a given teacher, i.e., a "learner." A disciple is a person who receives instruction from another person. A disciple is a person who accepts the ideas/teachings of another person and assists in spreading or implementing them.
Questions.Note: See "disciple" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Who do you think would cause the different types of people, of whom Jesus speaks, to be "blessed" in the various ways that he said they would be blessed?
Questions.A: God would bless them. // God blesses them. // God does the blessing. (1)
Questions.Note: Jesus was speaking to Jewish people so he did not need to mention who would do the blessing. It may need to be made clear in some translations.

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to bless someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: One person praises/says good things about the other person or asks God to do good things for that person.
Questions.Note: See "bless, blessed, blessing" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think Jesus wanted his hearers to do in order that they could receive that kind of blessing from God?
Questions.A: He wanted them to be, or to become, his followers who would be "poor in spirit," "sorry," "meek," "hungry for righteousness" and so forth as he mentioned. (3-12)

Questions.Q: Who was there on the mountainside as Jesus began to teach?
Questions.A: His twelve disciples (1-2)
Possibly a large number of other disciples were near him.
Other people may have been on the outskirts/further away/beyond them.
Questions.Note: There are different views about this/about who else was there. (See also 7:28-29)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to be "poor in spirit"?
Questions.A: This refers to one who knows that he needs/those who know that they need help. (That is, they needed God's help to have a good relationship with him.) (3)

Questions.Q: About what sort of "mourning" do you think Jesus was talking when he said, "Blessed are those who mourn"?
Questions.A: Any grief could be in focus. Especially fitting would be grief from knowing how much they needed God's help to be free from their sins. (4)

Questions.Q: What sort of people are those who are/these meek people?
Questions.A: Meek people/They are mild mannered. They do not go about demanding all their rights. (5)
Questions.Alternative: What sort of people are those who are meek people?
What sort of people are these meek people?

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that Jesus spoke of people hungering and thirsting for righteousness?
Questions.A: He was speaking about/talking about/of people who feel a real need to be right with God, much like people who feel the need/feeling a real need to have food to eat and water to drink. (6)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to be righteous?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: If someone is righteous it means that he or she has been cleansed from his or her sin and they have a/are in a right relationship with God. (See "righteous" in KBT in the "just, justify" entry.)

Questions.Q: What kind of people will see God according to verse 8?
Questions.A: Those who have the same desires which God has will see God. (8)

Questions.Q: What do peacemakers do?
Questions.A: Peacemakers help/cause people to be reconciled. Here it probably refers to causing people to be reconciled with God. (9)

Questions.Q: What do you think might be the reason that some people would do evil/bad to righteous people, that is, those who have a right/are in a right relationship with God?
Questions.A: The reason may be that they are jealous of the righteous people,
-OR- they hate God,
-OR- they do not want righteous people around them, since that reminds them of their own sin,
-OR- they become/are upset because the righteous ones will not worship their gods. (10)
Questions.Alternative: What do you think might be the reason that some people would do evil to righteous people, that is, those who have a right relationship with God?
What do you think might be the reason that some people would do evil to righteous people, that is, those who are in a right relationship with God?
What do you think might be the reason that some people would do bad to righteous people, that is, those who have a right relationship with God?
What do you think might be the reason that some people would do bad to righteous people, that is, those who are in a right relationship with God?

Questions.Q: In verses 11 and 12 Jesus said that it is a good sign if people insult you and do evil/bad to you because you obey him. What does that good sign show?
Questions.A: It shows that you must be obeying the Lord, just as people mistreated the prophets long ago when the prophets obeyed the Lord. (11-12)
Questions.Alternative: In verses 11 and 12 Jesus said that it is a good sign if people insult you and do evil to you because you obey him. What does that good sign show?
In verses 11 and 12 Jesus said that it is a good sign if people insult you and do bad to you because you obey him. What does that good sign show?

Section.heading: Matthew 5:13-16 Believers in Jesus are like salt and are like light.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell his followers in these verses?
Questions.A: He told them that they were the salt of the earth and the light of the world. (13-14)

Questions.Q: What do you think Jesus meant when he said that his followers were "the salt of the earth"?
Questions.A: He may have been saying that his followers help to keep individuals or society from being destroyed, like salt helps to keep food from spoiling.
-OR-
He may have been saying that his followers add a pleasant quality to the people of earth, like salt adds pleasantness to the taste of food. (13)
Questions.Note: It is difficult to understand exactly what Jesus meant by salt in this verse. This question is here to check for any obviously wrong meaning from the translation of his statement (after it is translated).

Questions.Q: What do you think Jesus meant when he said that his followers were "the light of the world"?
Questions.A: He meant that they were the ones who could show others the way [to a good relationship with God]. (14)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Jesus talked about putting a light under a container?
Questions.A: Jesus wanted those who have experienced God's mercy to tell others about their experience of receiving God's mercy/how to experience his mercy. (15-16)

Section.heading: Matthew 5:17-20 Jesus explained that he came to this world in order to fulfill the laws that God gave Moses for the people of Israel.

Questions.Q: What reason did Jesus give for his coming to/say that he had come to this world?
Questions.A: He said that he had come to this world to fulfill what was taught in the Mosaic law and what was taught by the prophets in the Old Testament. (17)
Questions.Alternative: What reason did Jesus give for his coming to this world?
What reason did Jesus say that he had come to this world?

Questions.Q: What do you think Jesus meant when he said that he had come to this world?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Jesus meant that he had come to all the people who live on the earth.
Questions.Note: See "world" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think the law was?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Here the law refers to the first five books of the Old Testament, written by Moses, which contained the laws God gave to Moses for the Israelites to obey.
Questions.Note: See "law" in KBT.

Questions.Q: About what was Jesus talking when he spoke of "the law or the prophets"?
Questions.A: He was talking about the teaching found in what we now call the Old Testament. (17)

Questions.Q: Did Jesus say that people should follow his teaching and stop paying attention to the teaching found in the Old Testament?
Questions.A: No, he did not. (18)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus mean when he said that he had come to fulfill "the law and the prophets"?
Questions.A: He meant that he would fulfill the laws by obeying them.
He also meant that he would fulfill the Old Testament predictions about the promised ruler (the Messiah) by doing everything that God had predicted about him. (17)

Questions.Q: What did he say about how long the Old Testament's teaching would be important?
Questions.A: He said that the teaching of the Old Testament/teaching would be important until everything written in the Old Testament had happened. (18)

Questions.Q: Who used to teach the people of Israel about spiritual things?
Questions.A: The Pharisees and scribes taught them.
Questions.Note: This is implied in 19-20.

Questions.Q: Did Jesus think that the way the Pharisees and scribes lived was acceptable to God?
Questions.A: No, he did not. (20)

Section.heading: Matthew 5:21-26 Jesus taught about people being angry with others.

Questions.Q: About what did Jesus teach the people in these verses?
Questions.A: He taught them about being angry with others.

Questions.Q: What was the usual teaching about murder that everyone had heard before Jesus talked to them that day?
Questions.A: The people had heard that a person must not murder another person. If anyone murdered someone, then others would have to judge them guilty of killing and punish them. (21)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say was also part of God's standard for how we should treat other people?
Questions.A: He said that we should not be angry with a brother nor should we call him bad/evil names like "Wicked fool." (22)

Questions.Q: What do you think Jesus meant when he mentioned/said brother in verse 22?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In this verse Jesus meant that a brother was anyone who was a fellow-believer in Jesus. (See "brother" in KBT in the "disciple" entry.) (Also see comments from the UBS handbook on "brother" in this verse.)
Questions.Alternative: What do you think Jesus meant when he mentioned brother in verse 22?
What do you think Jesus meant when he said brother in verse 22?
What do you think Jesus meant when he said "brother"?

Questions.Q: What should a person do who was/is angry with someone?
Questions.A: Jesus said that he should first be reunited with people. Then God could forgive him when he presented his (burnt) offering to him. (23-24)
Questions.Alternative: What should a person do who was angry with someone?
What should a person do who is angry with someone?

Questions.Q: What do you think happens when two people are reconciled to each other?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Two people are reconciled to each other, when one individual or the other takes the initiative to settle the quarrel between them, so that they are no longer enemies, but friends.
Questions.Note: See "reconcile" in KBT.

Questions.Q: In verse 25, Jesus did not say to whom he was referring when he spoke of their opponent. Whom do you think he meant?
Questions.A: Here their opponent could be anyone who had something against them and might/could take them to court. Here the opponent is pictured as the local (Jewish Sanhedrin) court. (25-26)

Questions.Q: Who else could this opponent be?
Questions.Note: This opponent could be God himself.

Jesus was teaching about our relationship with God, so he was not suddenly switching to speaking of/talking about avoiding people in the local court here at the end of this section. Rather, he is using figurative language to make a strong rhetorical point. He is saying, "Do not be in a wrong relationship with God, lest you find yourself in court with him and not be able to satisfy the penalty for your wrong doing." Emphasizing the inability to pay the penalty may help to make this point clearer in the translation.

Section.heading: Matthew 5:27-30 Jesus taught about the "Do not commit adultery" law.

Questions.Q: About what did Jesus teach the people in these verses?
Questions.A: He taught them about not committing adultery.

Questions.Q: What was the usual understanding of the law about adultery in the days when Jesus was teaching?
Questions.A: The people understood that law to mean that people must not commit adultery. (27)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to commit adultery with another person?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Adultery is the act of unfaithfulness in marriage that occurs when one of the marriage partners voluntarily engages in sexual intercourse with a person of the opposite sex other than his or her marriage partner.

Questions.Q: What more did Jesus teach about this?
Questions.A: He taught that this also means that a person/we must not look at someone/people of the opposite sex to lust after them, because that is committing adultery with that person/them in our thoughts. (28)

Questions.Q: Did Jesus mean in verses 29 & 30 for someone/a person to gouge out his or her/their eye, or to cut off his or her/their arm, if he or she/they had used those parts of their bodies to sin?
Questions.A: No, he did not mean that.
Questions.Alternative: Did Jesus mean in verses 29 & 30 for someone to gouge out his or her eye, or to cut off his or her arm, if he or she had used those parts of his or her body to sin?
Did Jesus mean in verses 29 & 30 for someone to gouge out his eye, or to cut off his arm, if he had used those parts of his body to sin?
Did Jesus mean in verses 29 & 30 for people to gouge out their eyes, or to cut off their arms, if they had used those parts of their bodies to sin?
Did Jesus mean in verses 29 & 30 for a person to gouge out his or her eye, or to cut off his or her arm, if he or she had used those parts of his or her body to sin?
Did Jesus mean in verses 29 & 30 for a person to gouge out his eye, or to cut off his arm, if he had used those parts of his body to sin?

Questions.Q: What did he mean?
Questions.A: Jesus again is using rhetoric that his hearers would have understood. He meant for us to think how very serious sin is and to stop doing it. (In fact, gouging out one eye would not help much, since there would still be an eye left. The same is true of cutting off an arm.) Thinking how serious sin really is, though, should help a person to obey God, so that he can help that person.

Questions.Q: About what did Jesus teach the people in these verses?
Questions.A: He taught them that a man should not divorce his wife.

Questions.Q: What did the Jews commonly teach about divorcing one's spouse?
Questions.A: They taught that, if a man divorced his wife, he had to make it clear to her and to everyone else that he had divorced her by writing a statement saying that he had divorced her. (31)
