Questions.Q: Did Jesus say that giving her the written divorce paper made the divorce legal/all right with God?
Questions.A: No, he did not say that.
Questions.Alternative: Did Jesus say that giving her the written divorce paper made the divorce legal?
Did Jesus say that giving her the written divorce paper made the divorce all right with God?

Questions.Q: What did he say?
Questions.A: He said that, if a man divorced his wife and she remarried, he was causing her to sin/commit adultery and also causing whoever then married her to sin. (32)

Section.heading: Matthew 5:33-37 Jesus taught about their custom of making promises.

Questions.Q: About what did Jesus teach the people in these verses?
Questions.A: He taught them not to make promises and then making them firm by swearing by heaven or by earth or by Jerusalem or by one's head.

Questions.Q: What was it that the Jewish people often taught about promises?
Questions.A: They taught that, if one had made a promise, he or she had to do as he or she had promised, no matter what happened to them or others. (33)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about that?
Questions.A: He said that people should not make those promises such as saying, "As sure as heaven…", or, "As sure as God's throne, … I will do such and such." If a person is honest, he should be able to just say "yes" or "no" and let that be enough for his hearers, without adding other promises. (34-37)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Jesus did not want them to make those kinds of promises?
Questions.A: Jesus said that they should tell the truth. Lies are caused by Satan. (37)

Section.heading: Matthew 5:38-42 Jesus taught that people should not try to get revenge against others.

Questions.Q: About what did Jesus teach the people in these verses?
Questions.A: He taught them not to take revenge on/retaliate against others.

Questions.Q: What did people mean by the words "An eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth"?
Questions.A: They meant that, if someone puts out a person's eye, he was to put out their eye.
Or, if they knock out a person's tooth, then he was permitted to knock out one of theirs. (38)
Questions.Note: In the Old Testament it was the leaders who were to give this punishment to keep people from carelessly or purposefully hurting others in the future.

Questions.Q: Did Jesus think that people should insist on punishing another person when that person did wrong to them?
Questions.A: No. He said we should be willing not to react against people who make unfair demands of us. We should be willing to give more than people request of us, rather than being so concerned about their request being fair. (39-42)

Section.heading: Matthew 5:43-48 Jesus taught that people should love their enemies.

Questions.Q: About what did Jesus teach the people in these verses?
Questions.A: He taught them that they should love their enemies.

Questions.Q: What did the Jewish leaders teach the people?
Questions.A: They taught that people should love their neighbors and hate their enemies. (43)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when someone loves someone else?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The person, who loves another person, seeks the good of that person. His attitude to the one whom he loves is an attitude of persistent and selfless goodwill.
Questions.Note: See "love" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say that his disciples should do?
Questions.A: He said that they should love their enemies and pray for the ones who persecuted them. (44)

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that Jesus said that loving their enemies would make them sons of their father in heaven?
Questions.A: Loving their enemies would not make them into children of God, but it would demonstrate to others that they were children of God. The people to whom he was talking here were already related to God, as we can tell by the fact that he called God their Father. The terms "son of" and "daughters of," in that culture, were often used to mean "a typical representative of." Compare the term "daughters of Jerusalem" which they used to talk about typical women of Jerusalem. (45)
Questions.Note: The Jewish people used "sons" here in a different sense than some languages can use such words. Implied information may need to be made explicit in the translation.

Questions.Q: Where do you think heaven is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It is that part of God's creation above the earth and the waters, including "air" and "space," and serves as home for God and the spirits who serve Him.
Questions.Note: See "heaven" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus expect his disciples to do that others, who did not follow God, would likely not do?
Questions.A: Jesus expected his disciples to greet people who were not of their group, and love people other than those who loved them. (46-47)

Questions.Q: In verse 48, what is it that Jesus wants believers/his followers to do?
Questions.A: He wants his followers to accept God's way as perfect and act the way God acts. (48)
Questions.Alternative: In verse 48, what is it that Jesus wants believers to do?
In verse 48, what is it that Jesus wants his followers to do?

Section.heading: Matthew 6:1-4 Jesus taught about giving to needy people.

Questions.Q: About what did Jesus teach the people in these verses?
Questions.A: He taught them about giving to those who have needs.

Questions.Q: To what was Jesus referring when he talked about people doing "acts of righteousness"?
Questions.A: He was talking about giving to the needy, praying, and fasting. (2-18)
Questions.Note: Since this section only talks about giving to the needy, it might be necessary to read all the way through v. 18 or come back to this question again after looking at the following sections.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say would happen if a person seeks praise from others when he gives to needy people?
Questions.A: If a person, who gives to needy people, does it to impress people rather than to please God, he will not please God. God will not count such giving as a good deed. (2)
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus say would happen if a person wants others to speak well of him when he gives to needy people?
What did Jesus say would happen if a person wants others to think well of him when he gives to needy people?
What did Jesus say would happen if a person wants others to give him recognition when he gives to needy people?
What did Jesus say would happen, if a person seeks praise from others when he gives to needy people?

Questions.Q: What is a proper way to give?
Questions.A: A good way is to give without letting others know that you have given. (3-4)

Questions.Q: About what did Jesus teach the people in these verses?
Questions.A: He taught them about praying.

Questions.Q: What does a hypocrite do?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In this verse a hypocrite is one who tries to make others think he is (really) following God when he is really trying to draw attention to himself. (5)

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that Jesus mentioned hypocrites?
Questions.A: He wanted to warn his hearers not to be like hypocrites. (5-8)

Questions.Q: What do you think Jesus meant when he said that the hypocrites had already received all of their reward for praying?
Questions.A: He meant that, since they were not really praying to God, God would not send them blessing/would not help them because of those prayers. The only help they receive is when people praise them. // The only advantage they would receive for having said the prayers publicly, would be the praises of people. (5-6)

Questions.Q: Should our prayers be long, short, or what, according to verses 7 and 8?
Questions.A: We should not try to make our prayers long with meaningless words and phrases or a lot of repetition. Our prayers do not need to be long, since God already knows what we need before we ask. (7-8)

Questions.Q: Do you think Jesus meant that the prayer he suggested/suggested prayer he gave is the only way to pray?
Questions.A: No. He showed/taught them an example.
Questions.Alternative: Do you think Jesus meant that the prayer he suggested is the only way to pray?
Do you think Jesus meant that the suggested prayer he gave is the only way to pray?

Questions.Q: What did he pray concerning God himself?
Questions.A: Jesus said that they should pray that people would agree that God is holy and therefore worship him. (9)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say they should pray concerning God ruling over people?
Questions.A: He said that they should pray that the time of his ruling over people on earth would soon happen. (10)

Questions.Q: What did he want his disciples' goal to be as they prayed concerning God ruling on earth?
Questions.A: Their goal should be for people here on earth to obey God fully, as the heavenly beings/angels already obey him. (10)

Questions.Q: What did he recommend that his disciples ask concerning their own needs?
Questions.A: They should ask that God would supply their need for each day as it approached. (11)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus show in his prayer as an appropriate way for his disciples to ask God to forgive them?
Questions.A: They could ask God to forgive the wrong they did as they themselves were forgiving the wrong others did to them. (12)

Questions.Q: What do you think happens when a person/someone forgives someone else?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Forgiveness always involves two people, one of whom has done something wrong to the other and offended him. Forgiveness takes place when the one, who was offended, sets aside his right to justice and decides not to punish the offender, as he deserved. If the one who offended repents and accepts this forgiveness, the result is that the relationship between the two, which was broken by the offense, is restored and the guilt of the offender is removed.
Questions.Note: See "forgive" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think happens when a person forgives someone else?
What do you think happens when someone forgives someone else?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus suggest as one appropriate way to pray so that God would keep them from sinning?
Questions.A: They could ask God to protect them from being tempted (beyond what they could withstand) and thus God would rescue them from evil/the evil one. (13)

Questions.Q: Who do you think the evil one is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The "evil one" is another name for Satan. (See "evil one" in KBT in the "Satan" entry.)

Section.heading: Matthew 6:16-18 Jesus taught his disciples about fasting.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus teach the people in these verses?
Questions.A: He taught them about fasting.

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to fast?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: When someone fasts he chooses not to eat food for certain periods of time, so that he could focus his thoughts better on God and not on his bodily needs.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that some people would try to go around looking sad when they fasted?
Questions.A: Some people went around looking sad in order to show/to demonstrate to others that they were fasting. They wanted other people to think that they were good/religious/holy people. (16)

Questions.Q: Would God be pleased with people who fasted just to make other people think that they were seriously worshiping God?
Questions.A: No. That would not make God happy.
Questions.Alternative: Would God be pleased with people who fasted just to make other people think that they were seriously worshipping God?
Would God be pleased with people who fasted just to make other people think that they were seriously worshiping him?
Would God be pleased with people who fasted just to make other people think that they were sincerely worshiping him?
Would God be pleased with people who fasted just to impress other people?

Questions.Q: What gain did Jesus say such people earn/achieve from fasting like that?
Questions.A: He said that the only thing they would gain from such fasting would be the attention of those other people. (16)
Questions.Alternative: What gain did Jesus say such people earn from fasting like that?
What gain did Jesus say such people achieve from fasting like that?

Questions.Q: What should we do then, if we decide to fast?
Questions.A: We should dress and wash ourselves as usual, so that only God knows that we are fasting.
Since God knows everything, he will know what we are doing and can bless us. (17-18)

Section.heading: Matthew 6:19-24 Jesus taught that people should value what they will receive in heaven more than what they have while on earth.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus teach the people in these verses?
Questions.A: He taught them that they should store up treasures in heaven.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say we should store up for ourselves in heaven?
Questions.A: We should store up heavenly treasure. (20)

Questions.Q: What do you think Jesus meant when he said we should store up our treasure in heaven?
Questions.A: He meant that we need to put the highest value on our relationship to God and the good that he does for us/spiritual blessings he sends to us.

Questions.Q: What do you think Jesus meant by earthly treasure?
Questions.A: He meant anything on earth that people value and which might distract them from maintaining/continuing their relationship with God.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Jesus does not want us to spend much time and great effort in accumulating/to accumulate many possessions here on earth?
Questions.A: The things that people/we value here on earth are not long lasting, and they will tend to distract people/us from the/our lifetime goal of loving and serving God. (20-21)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that Jesus does not want us to spend much time and great effort in accumulating many possessions here on earth?
What is the reason that Jesus does not want us to spend much time and great effort to accumulate many possessions here on earth?

Questions.Q: What is the purpose of our eyes?
Questions.A: We see with our eyes and they show the rest of the body the way we want/the person wants to go. (22)

Questions.Q: What, then, is the difference between a good eye and a bad eye for the body?
Questions.A: With a good eye the person can see where he wants to go. If our/a person's eye is bad, we/he cannot see where he wants/we want to go. (22-23)

Questions.Q: What do you think Jesus meant when he spoke of a person having a "good eye" and when he spoke of a person having a "bad eye"?
Questions.A: A person who can see is like a person who has a heart to know God. A person who can not see is like a person who has a heart not to know God and not to do his will.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about a person trying to serve two masters?
Questions.A: Jesus said that if a person tries to serve two masters, he will always have more devotion for one master than for the other. Therefore, by neglecting one of the two masters, he will not be serving that one at all. (24)

Questions.Q: Should becoming wealthy or should serving God be our main desire in life?
Questions.A: Serving God should always be of more value to us than becoming wealthy. (23-24)

Section.heading: Matthew 6:25-34 Jesus taught that people/his followers/believers should not worry.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Jesus did not want his followers/believers/people to be overly concerned/worry about their future needs for food and clothing?
Questions.A: He wanted their first concern to be that of having a good relationship with God rather than being concerned/worrying about food and clothing. (25, 32-33)
-AND/OR-
He did not want them to be overly concerned/worried about their future needs. Rather, he wanted them to trust God to supply their daily needs/needs day by day. (33-34)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that Jesus did not want his followers to be overly concerned about their future needs for food and clothing?
What is the reason that Jesus did not want his followers to worry about their future needs for food and clothing?
What is the reason that Jesus did not want believers to be overly concerned about their future needs for food and clothing?
What is the reason that Jesus did not want believers to worry about their future needs for food and clothing?
What is the reason that Jesus did not want people to be overly concerned about their future needs for food and clothing?
What is the reason that Jesus did not want people to worry about their future needs for food and clothing?

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that Jesus talked about life being more important than food and clothing?
Questions.A: Having a body and being alive we have the opportunity to have a true/proper/genuine relationship with God.
Having and continuing/maintaining a true/proper/genuine right relationship with God is more important than having food and clothing. (26-27, 33)

Questions.Q: Who values us as more important than birds?
Questions.A: God values us as more important than the birds. (26)

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that Jesus asked them the question about who could live longer/add more days to their life by worrying?
Questions.A: He was not asking in order to learn something from them. He was using a question to emphasize to them that worrying does not help anyone/does no good.
Questions.Note: Ask this question only if verse 27 is in a question form after being translated.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think is the reason that Jesus asked them the question about who could live longer more days to their life by worrying?
What do you think is the reason that Jesus asked them the question about who could live add more days to their life by worrying?

Questions.Q: What do you think is the meaning of the word "life" in verse 27?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In this verse the word "life" refers to physical life/the earthly existence of a human being.

Questions.Q: If verse 28 is translated with a question form then ask: In verse 28, did Jesus want them to tell him why they still worried about their clothing?
Questions.A: No. He was telling them/saying in an emphatic way that they should not worry about their clothing/about having clothes to wear. (28)

Questions.Q: What can we learn from the way that God decorates some of the wild plants?
Questions.A: We can learn that he can also provide clothes to decorate us too. (28-30)

Questions.Q: Who was the person named Solomon mentioned in verse 29?
Questions.A: Solomon was a rich king of Israel who lived many years before Jesus made this statement.
Questions.Note: This is general knowledge known to the/Jesus's original audience/the people who were listening to Jesus speak.

Questions.Q: Who made satisfying their bodily needs for food, drink and clothing the first goal of their lives?
Questions.A: The people, who had made satisfying their bodily needs the first goal of their lives, were those people who had not trusted/followed/learned about God. (32)

Questions.Q: In verse 33, how will people have their needs met when they focus on pleasing God?
Questions.A: God will take care of them. (33)
Questions.Note: This is implied.

Questions.Q: If the translation still says so, then ask: How can a day actually be able to think enough to worry?
Questions.A: Of course, a day cannot think or worry. The meaning is that there will be a certain amount of concern for us each day [also God will provide daily for us]. So we/people should not worry ahead of time. (34)

Section.heading: Matthew 7:1-6 Do not judge others unless you are ready to be scrutinized yourself.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus teach the people in these verses?
Questions.A: He taught them that they should not judge other people.

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to judge someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In 7:1 to judge someone means to assume authority over that person/someone, to take the position of a judge towards that person/someone.
Questions.Note: See "judge" in KBT.

Questions.Q: If we scrutinize others with the idea of judging them what will happen to us?
Questions.A: If we continually judge others, God will (have to) judge us. (1-2)

Questions.Q: What do you think judgment means?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that someone decides that something is either good or bad. He considers the facts and reaches a conclusion. (See "judgment" in KBT in the "judge" entry.)

Questions.Q: What should the Pharisee have done, or anyone else do before they could guide others?
Questions.A: They needed to repent and obey God before they could guide others. (3-5)

Questions.Q: What do you think that Jesus meant when he mentioned dogs and pigs in verse 6?
Questions.A: He meant that people who did not appreciate the good news that Jesus preached/brought were like dogs and pigs. (6)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about people who react strongly against those who preach the good news?
Questions.A: Those people will reject it and also will seek to harm the ones who proclaim the good news to them. (6)

Section.heading: Matthew 7:7-12 Ask God for whatever you need.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus teach the people in these verses?
Questions.A: He taught them to ask God for everything that they need.

Questions.Q: Who did Jesus say/imply would give us what is good/what we need, if we ask?
Questions.A: He was talking about our praying to God and about God answering our prayers. (11)
Questions.Alternative: Who did Jesus say would give us what is good if we ask?
Who did Jesus imply would give us what is good, if we ask?
Who did Jesus say would give us what we need if we ask?
Who did Jesus imply would give us what we need, if we ask?

Questions.Q: Did Jesus truly/really want to know who would give a stone instead of bread to his son? And did he truly want to know who would give a snake instead of a fish to his son?
Questions.A: No, he did not truly want to know that. He was not asking a real question.
Questions.Note: Only ask this question if verses 9 and 10 still have a question form after being translated.
Rhetorical questions are used for emphasis; not to obtain/elicit/receive an answer from the hearers.
Questions.Alternative: Did Jesus truly want to know who would give a stone instead of bread to his son? And did he truly want to know who would give a snake instead of a fish to his son?
Did Jesus really want to know who would give a stone instead of bread to his son? And did he truly want to know who would give a snake instead of a fish to his son?

Questions.Q: What else did Jesus say that earthly fathers would not do to their sons?
Questions.A: Jesus said that earthly fathers would certainly not trick their children by giving them a stone when they ask for an egg. (9-10)

Questions.Q: What else did Jesus say to make us know for sure/feel sure that God will only do what is good for us?
Questions.A: He said that if people who are his children/followers, who tend to do bad/evil deeds, give only good things to their children; then people should understand how God deals with his children. If people/his children/those who follow him pray to him/to God/to their heavenly father, he will do only what is good for them. (11)
Questions.Alternative: What else did Jesus say to make us know for sure that God will only do what is good for us?
What else did Jesus say to make us feel sure that God will only do what is good for us?

Section.heading: Matthew 7:13-14 Jesus taught the people/his disciples/his followers about the narrow gate and the wide gate.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that Jesus spoke of a narrow gate and a wide gate, and also a wide road?
Questions.A: He was warning them not to do what large groups of people do because that would not help them to live forever with God. Relatively few people accept God's way to have eternal life; so just following the crowd is not a good plan. (13-14)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for a person to have eternal life?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that a person will live forever with God.
Questions.Note: This eternal life is in the spiritual realm, not in the physical.

Section.heading: Matthew 7:15-23 Jesus taught his followers to guard against/be aware of the teaching of false prophets.

Questions.Q: Of what kind of people did Jesus teach his disciples to be aware?
Questions.A: He told them to beware of false prophets.

Questions.Q: In what way are false prophets like sheep, and how are they like wolves?
Questions.A: False prophets are not harmless like sheep are harmless. They are like wolves, but they try to appear as harmless as/like harmless sheep, so that they can enter and mingle among the sheep in order to harm them. (15)

Questions.Q: What do you think a false prophet did?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A false prophet was a person who claimed to be a prophet of God, but he was not. His messages were deceptive and led to confusion. (See "false prophet" in KBT in the "prophet" entry.)

Questions.Q: What do you think Jesus meant when he talked about sheep?
Questions.A: He meant that his people were like sheep, whom the false prophets tried/try to harm by teaching them false ideas. (15)

Questions.Q: How can we recognize/discern which ones are false prophets from those who are really teaching what God wants them to teach?
Questions.A: Jesus said that we can recognize them by the results of their teaching in their own lives and in the lives of those who follow them. (16-20)
Questions.Alternative: How can we recognize which ones are false prophets from those who are really teaching what God wants them to teach?
How can we discern which ones are false prophets from those who are really teaching what God wants them to teach?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say happens to trees that do not produce good fruit?
Questions.A: Their owners cut them down and burn them. (19)

Questions.Q: If calling Jesus Lord is not enough to cause Jesus to accept us what is enough?
Questions.A: Acknowledging him as Lord and obeying his father will cause him to accept us. (21)

Questions.Q: If people say Jesus sent them to preach, and they even claim to do miracles and cast out demons, will that prove that they belong to Jesus?
Questions.A: No. They must truly obey him from their hearts, not just claim to serve him. (21-23)

Questions.Q: What do you think a demon is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The terms "evil spirit", "unclean spirit", and "demon" are used interchangeably in the New Testament. All of these terms refer to spiritual beings who serve as Satan's agents/Satan as his agents, being under his authority. These spiritual beings have power to oppress a human being and even to take control of him. (See "demon" in KBT in the "evil spirit, unclean spirit" entry.)

Section.heading: Matthew 7:24-29 Jesus taught about the wise and foolish builders.

Questions.Q: About whom did Jesus teach the people in these verses?
Questions.A: He told them about the wise builder and the foolish builder.

Questions.Q: Who did Jesus say would be like someone who builds his house on a strong rock base?
Questions.A: They would be those who did what Jesus taught. (24-25)

Questions.Q: Who would be like the man who built his house on sand?
Questions.A: They would be those who heard Jesus speak, but they did not do what he said. (26-27)

Questions.Q: What do you think Jesus meant would happen to the foolish people who would not obey him/his teaching?
Questions.A: He meant that they would lose/not have eternal life. (27)
Questions.Alternative: What do you think Jesus meant would happen to the foolish people who would not obey him?
What do you think Jesus meant would happen to the foolish people who would not obey his teaching?

Questions.Q: What amazed the people so much when they heard what Jesus taught?
Questions.A: They were amazed because he was so different from the Scribes and Pharisees. He taught with God's authority. (28-29)

Section.heading: Matthew 8:1-4 Jesus healed a man who had leprosy.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do to the man who had leprosy?
Questions.A: Jesus healed the man. (3)

Questions.Q: As the crowds followed Jesus, who came to him?
Questions.A: A man who had the disease of leprosy came to him. (2)

Questions.Q: What did the leper/man want Jesus to do for him?
Questions.A: He wanted Jesus to heal him. (2)
Questions.Alternative: What did the leper want Jesus to do for him?
What did the man want Jesus to do for him?

Questions.Q: Did he believe that Jesus could heal him?
Questions.A: Yes, he did believe. (2)

Questions.Q: How can you discern whether/tell if Jesus was willing to heal him?
Questions.A: Jesus said that he was willing and then he healed him. (3)
Questions.Alternative: How can you discern whether Jesus was willing to heal him?
How can you tell if Jesus was willing to heal him?

Questions.Q: Then what did Jesus say to the leper/man?
Questions.A: Jesus told the leper/man not to tell others that he had healed him/what he had done for him, but he told him to go to the priests and show them that he was healed. He also told him to make the special (animal) sacrifice which/that Moses had said was proper for those healed of leprosy to make/do. (4)
Questions.Alternative: Then what did Jesus say to the leper?
Then what did Jesus say to the man?

Section.heading: Matthew 8:5-13 Jesus healed a centurion's servant.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do for a centurion?
Questions.A: He healed the centurion's servant. (13)

Questions.Q: What sort of person do you think of when you hear of a "centurion"?
Questions.A: A centurion was a leader over a number of men in the Roman army. This man would not have been a Jew. (5)

Questions.Q: When he approached Jesus, what did the centurion want?
Questions.A: He wanted Jesus to heal his servant. (5-6)

Questions.Q: What do you think a servant does?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A servant is a person who is required to work for another person and to obey him. A servant is one who is (usually) paid for his/her work. A slave is owned by his master, so he is not paid for working.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that the centurion told Jesus that he obeyed his superiors and also that those whom he commanded obeyed his orders?
Questions.A: He believed that Jesus had similar power to just speak and what he said would happen to the centurion's servant. He believed that Jesus did not need to walk to his house in order to heal his servant. He believed that Jesus could speak and cause his servant to be healed without first going near him. He believed that Jesus had power and authority to heal people. (7-9)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Jesus was so surprised?
Questions.A: Jesus was surprised because this Gentile man/non-Jew had demonstrated/shown that he believed in Jesus's power more than the Jews who had been taught about God all their lives. (10-11)

Questions.Q: Who do you think Abraham, Isaac and Jacob were?
Questions.A: They were important ancestors of the Jews, who had lived many years/a long time before Jesus was on earth.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that Jesus spoke of a feast with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob?
Questions.A: The Jews used to refer to/talk about the time of going to be with God and meeting with all of his people, who had previously died, as a great feast (time of fellowship). (See Isaiah 25:6.)

Questions.Q: What do you think that Jesus meant by people coming from the east and the west to the feast in God's kingdom?
Questions.A: He was talking about many non-Jews from different parts of the world (also) being part of God's chosen ones and being a part of his kingdom. (11)

Questions.Q: To whom did Jesus refer when he said "the sons of (—Or—subjects of) the kingdom"?
Questions.A: He was referring to/talking of the Jews, who were the ones generally supposed to be God's people, though not all of them were. (12)

Questions.Q: While Jesus and the centurion were talking, what happened to the centurion's servant?
Questions.A: Jesus healed the man's servant, even though the servant was a long distance from there/where they were. (13)

Questions.Q: What does someone do when he believes?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He puts his trust and commitment in another person.
Questions.Note: See "believe" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What happened/event occurred in these verses?
Questions.A: Jesus healed many people.
Questions.Alternative: What happened in these verses?
What event occurred in these verses?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do to heal Peter's mother-in-law's fever?
Questions.A: He touched her hand. (14-15)

Questions.Q: What happened that evening?
Questions.A: People brought those who were demon possessed and others who were sick. Jesus healed the sick and sent bad spirits out of those who had them. (16)

Questions.Q: What did that have to do with the prophecy Isaiah had written in the Old Testament?
Questions.A: The healings that Jesus performed fulfilled these words which God had told Isaiah to write, "He (the Messiah) carried our weaknesses and carried away our diseases." (17)

Section.heading: Matthew 8:18-22 Jesus talked to people who wanted to become his disciples.

Questions.Q: About what did Jesus talk to people in these verses?
Questions.A: He talked to them about becoming his disciples.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that Jesus wanted to cross to the other side of the lake?
Questions.A: Jesus probably wanted to cross to the other side of the lake because people had been with him for some time and he needed to get away from the crowd for a time of rest.
Questions.Alternative: Why do you think Jesus wanted to cross to the other side of the lake?

Questions.Q: About whom do you think Jesus was speaking when he spoke of "the Son of Man" in verse 20?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Jesus was speaking about himself. "Son of Man" is a title/one of the titles Christ used of Himself.
Questions.Note: See "son of man" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus mean when he said that he had no place to lay his head?
Questions.A: He meant that the man, who asked, might not be happy staying with him, since he had no home of his own, but/and moved from place to place. (20)

Questions.Q: What do you think about the other man who was one of Jesus disciples? How long do you think it might have been before he returned to follow Jesus, if Jesus had said it was all right for him to go first and do what he wanted to do? Then he could return to become Jesus's disciple.
Questions.A: It seems quite clear that the man wanted to stay close to/around home until after his father died and was buried, not just stay home to bury someone who had already died. That could have delayed his following Jesus for a very long time. (21)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus mean when he said to let dead people bury their own dead people?
Questions.A: He meant that people who did not truly follow God, could attend to their parents and eventually bury them when they died. The person to whom Jesus was speaking was united/devoted/loyal/faithful to God and could serve by following Jesus. His/That service was more important than his staying home. (22)

Section.heading: Matthew 8:23-27 Jesus spoke and caused the storm to become calm.

Questions.Q: How did Jesus cause the storm to become calm?
Questions.A: Jesus caused the storm to become calm by telling the wind and waves to stop. (26)

Questions.Q: Where do you think the boat was when the storm came up?
Questions.A: Jesus and his disciples were in the boat crossing the lake to the other side.
Questions.Note: See Mark 4:36.

Questions.Q: What was Jesus doing when the storm came?
Questions.A: He was sleeping. (24)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the disciples were so concerned/worried?
Questions.A: They were concerned/worried because the boat could sink and they could be drowned. (25)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that the disciples were so concerned?
What is the reason that the disciples were so worried?

Questions.Q: Did Jesus think it was a time to be afraid?
Questions.A: No, he did not.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Jesus did not think it was a time to be afraid?
Questions.A: Jesus knew that they were afraid because they did not trust him nor God his father/and God the Father. (26)

Questions.Q: What do you think the disciples began to realize when the wind stopped and the sea became calm just as Jesus had said it would?
Questions.A: They must have realized then that he was more than an ordinary man. (27)

Section.heading: Matthew 8:28-34 Jesus spoke and caused evil spirits to leave two men.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do for two men who were demon-possessed?
Questions.A: He commanded the demons to come out of the two men. (32)

Questions.Q: Who met Jesus when he arrived at the other side of the lake?
Questions.A: Two violent, demon-possessed men met him. (28)

Questions.Q: About what were those two men concerned?
Questions.A: (Actually it was the demons in the men speaking through them.) They were concerned that Jesus had come to disturb them before the time set for demons to be punished. (29)

Questions.Q: When Jesus was going to drive the demons out of those two men, where did the demons ask to go?
Questions.A: The demons asked him to allow them to go out among a herd of pigs that was a short distance from there. (30-31)

Questions.Q: Did Jesus give them permission to go among the pigs?
Questions.A: Yes, he did. (32)

Questions.Q: Then what happened?
Questions.A: The demons caused the pigs to run down a steep bank into the Sea of Galilee and drown. (32)

Questions.Q: What happened after the pigs drowned?
Questions.A: The people, who took care of the pigs, ran to the town and told the people there what had happened. Many people came from the town and pleaded with Jesus to leave their area. (33-34)

Section.heading: Matthew 9:1-8 Jesus healed a paralyzed man.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do for a paralyzed man in these verses?
Questions.A: He healed the man. (6-7)

Questions.Q: Then where did Jesus go?
Questions.A: Jesus went to his home town. (1)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus notice about the man and his companions before he healed him?
Questions.A: Jesus noticed that the man and his companions believed that Jesus could and would heal/forgive and heal the man. (2)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to the paralyzed man?
Questions.A: Jesus said, "Be encouraged. I forgive your sins." (2)

Questions.Q: What did the teachers of the law think when Jesus said that?
Questions.A: They thought that Jesus was acting wrongly and sinfully, as though he could take God's place and forgive sin. (3)

Questions.Q: How could Jesus know their thoughts?
Questions.A: Being God's son, Jesus knew everything. (4)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about their refusing to realize that he could rightfully forgive the man sins?
Questions.A: He said that they had evil thoughts in their hearts. (4)

Questions.Q: What does it mean to you to talk about the "heart"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The most common use of the word "heart" in the Bible is to refer to the spiritual center or innermost part of a human being. In Hebrew and Greek, "heart" is most commonly associated with thoughts and ideas.
Questions.Note: See "heart" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What evil do you think those teachers of the law did?
Questions.A: They refused to believe God's son when he was right there with them.
They were accusing Jesus of wrongfully claiming divine authority to forgive.

Questions.Q: Do you think Jesus expected the people to answer his question(s)?
Questions.A: No, he did not.
Questions.Note: Use this question only if the translated text uses a question for what Jesus says in verse 4 and/or verse 5.

He asked those question(s) to make them start thinking. In verse 4 he was simply saying, with emphasis, that they should not think as they were. They should be willing to accept Jesus as one sent from God.
Questions.Alternative: Do you think Jesus expected the people to answer him?

Questions.Q: What do you think about verse 5? What was Jesus telling them by asking which was easier to say, "I forgive your sins," or "Get up and walk"?
Questions.A: In verse 5 he was teaching/informing/advising/showing them that to forgive sins or to heal were equally easy for him because he was the Son of God.
Questions.Alternative: What was Jesus telling them by asking which was easier to say, "I forgive your sins," or "Get up and walk"?
Questions.Note: It wasn't that one phrase was easier to say than the other phrase. Jesus demonstrated that he had power from God to heal the man. Therefore he had power to forgive sin.

Questions.Q: How did Jesus prove that he could forgive people's sins?
Questions.A: He proved to them that he could forgive sins because he had power from God/God's power to heal the man. (6-7)

Questions.Q: What do you think the crowd thought once Jesus had healed the man?
Questions.A: It sounds as though/as if they assumed that Jesus had power from God. But they did not understand that Jesus was also God. (8)

Section.heading: Matthew 9:9-13 Jesus called Matthew to follow him.

Questions.Q: What kind of work did Matthew do before Jesus called him to follow him?
Questions.A: He was a tax collector. (9)
Questions.Note: The Jews thought that tax collectors were dishonest people because many of them charged/collected/took more tax than the government required, then kept the extra money for themselves. Also, people did not like them because they collected for the Roman government, which had occupied/taken over Israel by force.

Questions.Q: What did the Pharisees think about Jesus eating with tax collectors and others, whom the Pharisees called sinners?
Questions.A: They thought that Jesus should not eat with them. (10-11)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Jesus thought it was all right for him to mix with such people?
Questions.A: Jesus's idea was that, if people were bad, they needed help from God. (He referred to them as sick people needing a doctor.) (12)

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that, right in the middle of this/his talk/teaching about his eating with sinners, Jesus talked about mercy being better than making sacrifices?
Questions.A: Jesus talked about the/our need to be merciful to others, at that time, because the Pharisees were proud of doing all of the culturally right religious acts; but they were not kind to other people, including the sinners in their midst. Also they were trying to stop Jesus from being kind to those sinners. (Their religious acts included sacrificing animals.) (13)
Questions.Alternative: What do you think is the reason that, right in the middle of this, Jesus talked about mercy being better than making sacrifices?
What do you think is the reason that, right in the middle of his talk, Jesus talked about mercy being better than making sacrifices?
What do you think is the reason that, right in the middle of his talk about his eating with sinners, Jesus talked about mercy being better than making sacrifices?
What do you think is the reason that, right in the middle of his teaching about his eating with sinners, Jesus talked about mercy being better than making sacrifices?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to show mercy to someone else?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "Mercy" in the New Testament is an act of kindness by God or someone else toward people who are in need. The person (God or man) acts to relieve some kind of suffering or distress.
Questions.Note: See "mercy" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when someone makes a sacrifice?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "Sacrifice" is the religious act of making a gift to God, or to some other powerful spiritual being. The gift is given in order to establish, maintain, or restore a proper relationship between the sacrificer and the deity. Something is given up in order to achieve a purpose.
Questions.Note: See "sacrifice" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that Jesus told them that he came to call sinners and not righteous people?
Questions.A: He said that because he came to help people who were not in/did not have a right relationship with God. (Also probably because the scribes and Pharisees (who were talking to him) called themselves "righteous people." They would not admit their need or come to ask him to forgive their sins.) (13)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus want the scribes and Pharisees to learn?
Questions.A: He wanted them to learn that God wants them to have compassion on others, rather than giving gifts to him. (13)

Section.heading: Matthew 9:14-17 John's disciples asked Jesus about fasting.

Questions.Q: Whose disciples came to Jesus?
Questions.A: The disciples of John the Baptist came to Jesus. (14)

Questions.Q: What did John the Baptist's disciples want when they came to Jesus?
Questions.A: John's disciples wanted/were wanting to know why Jesus and his disciples were not fasting/going without food on certain days to observe religious fasting times as they and the Pharisees were doing. (14)

Questions.Q: When Jesus answered their question, what do you think is the reason that Jesus told them about/talked about what friends of a bridegroom would do?
Questions.A: Jesus compared his disciples to the friends of a bridegroom who are happy to be with the bridegroom. They would not refuse to eat (which was a sign of sorrow), when the bridegroom was there with them. (15)
Questions.Alternative: When Jesus answered their question, what do you think is the reason that Jesus told them about what friends of a bridegroom would do?
When Jesus answered their question, what do you think is the reason that Jesus talked about what friends of a bridegroom would do?
When Jesus answered their question, why do you think Jesus told them about what friends of a bridegroom would do?
When Jesus answered their question, why do you think Jesus talked about what friends of a bridegroom would do?

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that Jesus mentioned the bridegroom being taken away from his friends?
Questions.A: He was telling them what would happen to him. He used the figure of a bridegroom to refer to himself. Then he explained to/told them that there would be a reason for his disciples to fast when he was taken away from them. (15)

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that Jesus had taught his disciples about when to fast and when not to fast?
Questions.A: Probably he had taught them not to just follow traditions without thinking about what they were doing. They should fast when there was a reason to fast. (15)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say is one thing that people do not do?
Questions.A: He said that people do not repair an old garment with a piece of new cloth. (16)

Questions.Q: Do people you know sometimes repair an old garment with a piece of new cloth?
Questions.Note: Check for possible mismatch with local practice. At least Jesus and his hearers did not usually patch new cloth onto old cloth.

Questions.Q: What was the second thing Jesus said people do not do?
Questions.A: He said that they did not put new wine in an old goatskin (old leather bottle). (17)
Questions.Note: Check that the point of the illustration itself is clear. When someone seals new wine in a non-pliable leather container, the wine will swell while fermenting. That will cause the container to break and result in a total loss of the contents/wine.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that Jesus spoke here about cloth, and about the wine and about hardened leather containers/bottles? What was he teaching the people?
Questions.A: He taught them that his teachings could not be a part of their old teachings/traditions/traditional system. They needed to change what they believed and also to change their way of worshiping God. (16-17)
Questions.Alternative: What do you think is the reason that Jesus spoke here about cloth, and about the wine and about hardened leather containers? What was he teaching the people?
What do you think is the reason that Jesus spoke here about cloth, and about the wine and about hardened leather bottles? What was he teaching the people?

Section.heading: Matthew 9:18-26 Jesus healed a sick woman and brought a dead girl back to life.

Questions.Q: What is the theme/topic of these verses?
Questions.Note: See if the translation checker can tell you the details of this section. Then question him about anything that was confusing to him or anything he did not remember to tell you.
Questions.Alternative: What is the theme of these verses?
What is the topic of these verses?

Questions.Q: What two miracles did Jesus perform/do?
Questions.A: He healed a woman and raised a dead girl back to life.
Questions.Alternative: What two miracles did Jesus perform?
What two miracles did Jesus do?

Questions.Q: What did the ruler (of the synagogue) want?
Questions.A: He wanted Jesus to bring his daughter back to life. (18)

Questions.Q: Did he believe that Jesus could do that?
Questions.A: Yes. We know that he did because he said, "Put your hand on her and she will live." (18)

Questions.Q: What happened as Jesus and his disciples were walking along the road to the ruler's house?
Questions.A: A woman, who had a bleeding problem for twelve years, came up behind Jesus and touched him. (20)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that she touched him?
Questions.A: She touched him because she thought that, if she could just touch him, he would make her well again. (21)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to her when she touched him?
Questions.A: He told her to be encouraged. Because she believed in him, he had made her well. (22)

Questions.Q: Did she have any more (medical/health) problems after that?
Questions.A: No. She was healed right away/immediately/at once. (22)
Questions.Alternative: Did she have any more (medical) problems after that?
Did she have any more (health) problems after that?

Questions.Q: When Jesus arrived at the ruler's house, who was there?
Questions.A: Flute players and a noisy crowd of people were there. (23)

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that they were there?
Questions.A: They were there because they had come to mourn the death of the little girl. (This is implied by the Jewish/Jews' cultural practice of having flute players come to play their flutes as a part of the/their mourning (ceremony) for a dead relative.) (23)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the crowd laughed at Jesus?
Questions.A: They laughed because he said that the girl was not dead, but (only) asleep. They knew she was dead. (24)

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that Jesus (might have) said that the girl was sleeping when she was (really/already) dead?
Questions.A: He knew her condition was temporary, since he was at the point of bringing/about to bring her back to life. (24)
Questions.Alternative: What do you think is the reason that Jesus (might have) said that the girl was sleeping when she was (really) dead?
What do you think is the reason that Jesus (might have) said that the girl was sleeping when she was (already) dead?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do then?
Questions.A: He went inside/in the house/to her bedside and took her hand; and she came back to life. (25)

Section.heading: Matthew 9:27-34 Jesus healed two blind men and he also healed a man who could not talk so that he could speak.

Questions.Q: What miracles did Jesus do in this section?
Questions.A: He made two blind men able to see and he made a man, who was unable to speak, able to speak.

Questions.Q: Who followed Jesus as he walked along the road?
Questions.A: Two blind men followed him. (27)

Questions.Q: What did they want?
Questions.A: The two blind men wanted Jesus to take pity on them and heal them (of their blindness). (27)

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that they called him "Son of David"?
Questions.A: They were identifying him as the descendant of King David, the one who would be the Anointed one (the Messiah) promised in the Old Testament. (27)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus ask them?
Questions.A: He asked them if they believed that he was able to heal them. (28)

Questions.Q: Did they believe that he was able to heal them?
Questions.A: Yes. They believed that Jesus would/could heal them. (28)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do to make them able to see?
Questions.A: He touched their eyes. (29-30)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell them after he healed them?
Questions.A: He told them not to let anyone know what he had done for them. (30)

Questions.Q: Did they obey what he said?
Questions.A: No. They told people around the whole area. (31)

Questions.Q: What was wrong with the man they brought to Jesus?
Questions.A: He was demon possessed and could not speak. (32)

Questions.Q: Who made the demon leave the man so that he was able to speak again?
Questions.A: Jesus did. (This is implied from the reason they gave for bringing the man to Jesus. It is also implied by/as the cause of the Pharisees false complaint against Jesus in verse 34.)

Questions.Q: What did the crowd of people think when Jesus did that?
Questions.A: They were amazed at the miracles Jesus was doing in their land. (33)

Questions.Q: By the miracles that Jesus did, were the Pharisees convinced that Jesus was the Messiah?
Questions.A: No. They said that Satan was helping him to drive out Satan's own demons. That was not true. (34)

Section.heading: Matthew 9:35-38 Jesus had pity for the people.

Questions.Q: What was it about the crowds of people that caused Jesus to have extra compassion/pity/feel sorry for them?
Questions.A: They were worried and confused and lacked leaders to guide them to God. They were like sheep without a shepherd, not able to do well nor/or even to survive by themselves. (36)
Questions.Alternative: What was it about the crowds of people that caused Jesus to have extra compassion for them?
What was it about the crowds of people that caused Jesus to have extra pity for them?
What was it about the crowds of people that caused Jesus to have pity on them?
What was it about the crowds of people that caused Jesus to feel sorry for them?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do as he traveled around to all of the towns and villages of Galilee?
Questions.A: He went to the synagogues and proclaimed the good news about God's new way of ruling over people. Also he healed all kinds of sicknesses which the people had. (35)

Questions.Q: What do you think Jesus meant when he said that the harvest was plentiful, but there was a shortage of workers?
Questions.A: He meant that there were many people ready to come under God's authority (enter Christ's messianic kingdom); but there were (far) too few people to instruct and lead them. (37)

Questions.Q: To whom did Jesus mention this shortage of workers? What did he ask them to do about the shortage?
Questions.A: He mentioned the need to his disciples (probably many more than just the twelve); and he told them to pray to God (the overseer of the harvest) and ask him to send (out) the needed workers. (38)

Section.heading: Matthew 10:1-42 Jesus sent out his twelve disciples to preach the gospel.

Questions.Q: What is the subject/theme of this chapter?
Questions.A: This chapter is about Jesus instructing his disciples before he sent them out to teach and to heal people. (1-8)
Questions.Alternative: What is the subject of this chapter?
What is the theme of this chapter?

Questions.Q: When Jesus called his disciples to follow him, what do you think he told them that they would have power to do as they traveled around from village to village?
Questions.A: He told them that he was giving them the power to cast out demons and to cure all of the various kinds of sicknesses that people have. (1)

Questions.Q: What was the other name of Jesus's disciple, Simon?
Questions.A: His other name was Peter. (2)

Questions.Q: The text mentions Judas Iscariot and says he betrayed Jesus. When do you think he did that, before or after this time when Jesus was sending them out?
Questions.A: He betrayed Jesus at a later time. (It may need to read something like, "the one who later betrayed him".) (4)

Questions.Q: When Jesus sent his disciples out to preach and to heal people, to what group of people did he want them to go?
Questions.A: He said that they should not go to the non-Jews/non-Jewish people nor to the Samaritans. At that time they were to go only to the people of Israel (the Jewish people). (5-6)

Questions.Q: What were they supposed to preach as they traveled around?
Questions.A: They were supposed to tell people that the time of God's ruling in a new way was near (or actually present). (7)

Questions.Q: What else were they to do?
Questions.A: They were to heal people, including those with leprosy. They were to raise people back to life, who had died, and to cast out the demons from people who were possessed by them. (8)

Questions.Q: What are some of the things the disciples were not to take with them?
Questions.A: They were not to take money, no bag [for carrying food], nor were they to take/carry an extra outer garment or sandals or walking stick. (9-10)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they were not to take such things with them?
Questions.A: They were not to take such things with them because his disciples were going out to help/serve others, and those to whom they went to help/serve were to supply their needs. (10)

Questions.Q: What sort of household were they to find to stay while they taught and healed in a particular area?
Questions.A: They were to find a household where the people were worthy to have them stay with them. They/Those would be people who realized the true value of the message the disciples were bringing. (11)

Questions.Q: What sort of greeting (salute) were they to give to home owners when they entered their homes?
Questions.A: They were to greet the home owners with "[May God give you] peace." (12-13)
Questions.Note: It may be necessary to add the implied "may God give you" in the translation here.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say that they were to do if the household or village rejected them after they had greeted them with the proper greeting?
Questions.A: They were to realize that the greeting of God's peace, or "God will help you live well," was not the correct message for those people. Then they were to proceed to treat them as the Jews usually treated outsiders who did not follow God. They were to shake the dust of that home or village from their feet to demonstrate to those people that they were acting in a way that would not allow them to receive anything from God. (12-14)
Questions.Note: In the Jewish manner of speaking/way of talking about this they would speak/talk of the disciples "taking the peace back to themselves." In English we could say, "In that case, take back your greeting." We could demonstrate the seriousness of what they have done by shaking their dust off of our feet.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that Jesus mentioned the towns of Sodom and Gomorrah here?
Questions.A: He mentioned those towns because his hearers knew, from the Old Testament, that the people of those two towns had rejected God's ways; and God had destroyed them. (15)
Questions.Note: You may need to add implied information here so that it is more clearly understood what Jesus meant by speaking of Sodom and Gomorrah.

Questions.Q: What do you think Jesus meant when he talked about sheep and wolves and about the disciples needing to be, in some ways, like snakes and doves?
Questions.A: He meant that some of the people, that they would see, would be (just) waiting to harm them. So for that reason they needed to have a good plan of action to escape danger. Snakes were viewed as having that ability, but they were not to harm anyone, just as doves do not harm anyone. (16)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that he told the disciples to watch out/be careful, and to have only good motives?
Questions.A: They were to be careful because people would bring them before the local Jewish council meeting in the synagogue and have them beaten. (17)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that he told the disciples to watch out and to have only good motives?
What is the reason that he told the disciples to be careful and to have only good motives?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that people would take them to the courts of kings and governors?
Questions.A: They would be representing Jesus, so people who were hostile to Jesus would take them to court. (18)

Questions.Q: What would happen when they were in court before the Kings?
Questions.A: Kings, governors and people of the various nations would hear their testimony about Jesus as they spoke in court. (18)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they should not worry about what to say if they were (being) brought to court for serving Jesus?
Questions.A: They were not to be worried about what to say in the court session because God's spirit would help them to know what to say to the leaders/officials as they were in the act of speaking. (19-20)

Questions.Q: After reading verses 21-25, can you think why some men would turn their own brothers over to the authorities to be killed? Or why some parents would take their own children and have them put to death? Or why some children would take their own parents and have them put to death?
Questions.A: Because family members, who did not love or believe/follow Jesus, would be so very much against those who believed/followed him that they would accuse them before leaders to have them killed. Local leaders had called Jesus, Beelzebub, that is Satan, so of course they would not like his believers/people/followers either. The believers/his people/followers needed to be ready to be rejected. (21-25)
Questions.Alternative: After reading verses 2l-25, can you think why some men would turn their own brothers over to the authorities to be killed? Or why some parents would take their own children and have them put to death? Or why some children would take their own parents and have them put to death?

Questions.Q: What do you think that Jesus meant when he said "brother" in verse 21?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In this verse, Jesus meant brother to be someone who is a biological brother.

Questions.Q: Although/Even though some of Jesus's believers/followers might be killed, what did Jesus say would happen to all those who remained faithful to him?
Questions.A: They would be rescued [from having to suffer and be/being separated from God]. (22)
Questions.Alternative: Although though some of Jesus's believers might be killed, what did Jesus say would happen to all those who remained faithful to him?
Although though some of Jesus's followers might be killed, what did Jesus say would happen to all those who remained faithful to him?
Even though some of Jesus's believers might be killed, what did Jesus say would happen to all those who remained faithful to him?
Even though some of Jesus's followers might be killed, what did Jesus say would happen to all those who remained faithful to him?

Questions.Q: Since the persecution of Jesus's believers/people/followers would sometimes be severe, what were they to do?
Questions.A: They were to go away to another town. Then if they had to leave that one, they were to flee to another. (23)
Questions.Alternative: Since the persecution of Jesus's believers would sometimes be severe, what were they to do?
Since the persecution of Jesus's people would sometimes be severe, what were they to do?
Since the persecution of Jesus's followers would sometimes be severe, what were they to do?

Questions.Q: How long was their ministry to last?
Questions.A: Their ministry would last until the Messiah/Christ came back. (23)

Questions.Q: To whom does Jesus refer with the title "the head of the household,"? And to whom does he refer as "members of his household"?
Questions.A: He was referring to himself and to those who follow him. (25)
Questions.Note: This was not a difficult saying for the disciples to understand. It would have been very clear to them.

Questions.Q: Whom were they not to fear?
Questions.A: They were not to fear those who called Jesus, Beelzebub, in verse 25. That is, they were not to fear the Jewish religious leaders.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they should not fear?
Questions.A: They were not to fear because God would judge those leaders for whatever they did to them, when/at the time he judges all people. He might even judge them before that final judgment day. (26)

Questions.Q: About what was Jesus talking when he mentioned his speaking to them "in the dark" and "whispering in their ears"?
Questions.A: He was referring to what he said to them privately. (27)

Questions.Q: About what was he talking when he referred to their "speaking in the daylight" and "proclaiming from the house tops"?
Questions.A: He was saying that they needed to proclaim the message, that/which he had taught them privately, to the people publicly/out among the people so that everyone would hear it. (27)

Questions.Q: Do you think Jesus thought that would be a dangerous/frightening thing for them to do?
Questions.A: Yes, he did.
Questions.Alternative: Do you think Jesus thought that would be a dangerous thing for them to do?
Do you think Jesus thought that would be a frightening thing for them to do?

Questions.Q: Why? // How do you know that [Jesus thought it would be dangerous/frightening]?
Questions.A: Because after he told them to proclaim the message, he told them again not to fear people who could only kill a person's body. (27-28)
Questions.Alternative: Why??
How do you know that?
How do you know that Jesus thought it would be dangerous?
How do you know that Jesus thought it would be frightening?

Questions.Q: Whom did he say they should fear?
Questions.A: They should rather be afraid to forsake/offend the one who can cause people to die, as well as cause them to be punished in hell. (28)

Questions.Q: Who do you think that is?
Questions.A: He was speaking/talking about God. (The one who can send people to hell for punishment/to be punished.)

Questions.Q: What do you know about hell?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It is a place where those who have rejected the Lord will spend eternity. It is a place where there is constant pain and darkness.
Questions.Note: See "hell" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that Jesus started speaking of/talking about sparrows?
Questions.A: He mentioned sparrows because he wanted them to know that God, who watches over rather insignificant parts of his creation, like sparrows, will certainly watch over his people. (29-31)
Questions.Alternative: What do you think is the reason that Jesus started speaking of sparrows?
What do you think is the reason that Jesus started talking about sparrows?

Questions.Q: Who knows the number of the hair on our heads?
Questions.A: God does/knows. (This is implied.) (30)

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that Jesus mentioned that fact here?
Questions.A: He was showing that, if God knows these details, then he can take care of/protect us even down to each hair. We do not need to be afraid. (30-31)

Questions.Q: After talking about how they should not be afraid of people, what was Jesus trying to make plain to his disciples in verses 32 and 33?
Questions.A: They needed to acknowledge/confess/admit to being his people, so that he could state to the Father that they were his people. (32-33)

Questions.Q: People who lived at the time Jesus was here on earth were thinking that the Messiah's (Christ's) kingdom would bring peace on the earth. Did Jesus say that would happen since he had come?
Questions.A: No. He said that his having come would cause strife. (34)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to be at peace?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: To be at peace is to have a mental or spiritual condition marked by freedom from disquieting or oppressive thoughts or emotions.

Questions.Q: About what sort of strife was Jesus talking?
Questions.A: He said that people who were of the same household would be against one another [because some would choose to believe/follow him and the others would hate them]. (35-36)

Questions.Q: In such a case will it be all right with Jesus for people to do as their relatives do, who will have nothing to do with Jesus, to keep peace in the family?
Questions.A: No, it will not be all right.

Questions.Q: Why will it not be all right?
Questions.A: It will not be all right because Jesus said that, if people cared more for their family than for him, then they were not worthy of being one of his people/counted as his. (37)

Questions.Q: What do you think Jesus meant in verse 38, when he said people needed to carry their cross and follow him?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Jesus meant that people, who wanted to follow him, needed to be willing to die in order to be a faithful follower of his/him.
Questions.Note: See "cross" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus mean by what he said in verse 39?
Questions.A: People who try to save themselves from any troubles or from death by not obeying him will lose their chance to have life eternal. Those who are willing to die on earth in order to follow him will have life eternal. (39)

Questions.Q: What do you think Jesus meant by the word "receive" when he said, "whoever receives you receives me"?
Questions.A: It is a bit difficult to know if the first reference here is to receiving them into their homes, or if Jesus is now referring mostly to people receiving rather than rejecting them and their message. However, those who would receive them because they are Jesus's disciples, would almost certainly receive them in all the above manners/ways. (40-42)

Questions.Q: Jesus said that when they receive his disciples, they are at the same time receiving him and also the one who sent him. Whom do you think people, who read the translation, will think Jesus meant when he said, "the one who sent me"?
Questions.A: They should understand that Jesus meant God his father. (Implied) (40)

Questions.Q: How will Jesus reward those who are good to people who serve God?
Questions.A: He will reward them in the same manner that he will reward those servants of his whom they help. (41)

Questions.Q: Will God notice even rather insignificant help to his newest followers by rewarding the one who helped them?
Questions.A: Yes, he will notice. Even down to a drink of water. (42)

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that God rewards such people?
Questions.A: He will reward them because they are the ones who truly follow him. (40)
Questions.Note: This answer comes from the context and draws the passage together somewhat, but would be difficult to elicit/obtain from a respondent to these questions, who was reading the passage for the first time (the ideal kind). See especially verses 13 and 14 and verse 40. Jesus's coming caused people to make a choice for or against him as seen in verse 34 and following/and subsequent verses/onward.

Section.heading: Matthew 11:1-19 John the Baptist asked Jesus if he were the Savior/Messiah for whom they have been waiting.

Questions.Q: What did John the Baptist, who was now in prison, want to know/determine/find out from Jesus?
Questions.A: He wanted to know whether/find out if Jesus was truly the Messiah for whom they had been waiting. (2-3)
Questions.Alternative: What did John the Baptist, who was now in prison, want to know from Jesus?
What did John the Baptist, who was now in prison, want to determine from Jesus?
What did John the Baptist, who was now in prison, want to find out from Jesus?

Questions.Q: Where did Jesus go, after he had instructed his disciples [and sent them out]?
Questions.A: He went through the nearby towns (in Galilee) teaching the people. (1)
Questions.Alternative: Where did Jesus go, after he had instructed his disciples and sent them out?
Where did Jesus go, after he had instructed his disciples?

Questions.Q: What reply did he send (with them) back to John the Baptist?
Questions.A: He sent back a reply/replied saying that he did all kinds of miracles, including raising dead people back to life, and that he also preached the good news to the poor (as predicted of the Messiah in the Old Testament in Isaiah 19:18-21 and 35:5-6). (4-5)

Questions.Q: How did Jesus answer John's question when he sent his reply?
Questions.A: Jesus gave evidence that he was sent by God. That is, he was doing the various types of miracles predicted of the Messiah who was to come, including raising dead people back to life. (4-6)

Questions.Q: When John's disciples left, where do you think they went?
Questions.A: They went back to where John was in prison to give him their report concerning whether Jesus was the Messiah or not. (2-7)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus start talking about to the people after John the Baptist's disciples left?
Questions.A: Jesus began to talk to them about John the Baptist. (7)

Questions.Q: To what occasion do you suppose Jesus was referring when he spoke to the people there about their going out into the desert at a previous time?
Questions.A: Jesus was talking about the time when they went out from the towns to the sparsely settled area in order to hear John the Baptist teach and to be baptized by him. (9-11)

Questions.Q: What do you think most people, who read verse 7, would think Jesus meant when he asked if they had gone out to see a reed bent back and forth by the wind?
Questions.A: In Jesus's question he was asking them if they had found John to be an easily influenced person who was like a tall thin reed that bends different ways according to which way the wind was blowing/coming. (7)

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that Jesus asked if they had gone out to see someone in fine clothes?
Questions.A: He probably asked that because their other religious leaders wore fine clothes, but John was different. (8)

Questions.Q: In verse 9, what do you think Jesus meant when he said that John was a prophet and more than a prophet?
Questions.A: He meant that John was truly a prophet; but he was not just a prophet, he was a special prophet. (9)

Questions.Q: In verse 10, who do you think spoke, and to whom was he speaking?
Questions.A: It is clear from the Old Testament and the way the Old Testament quotation/quote is used here that it was God speaking to his son, the Messiah. (10)

Questions.Q: What can we learn from that Old Testament quotation given here in verse 10? What was so special about John that Jesus said he was "more than a prophet"?
Questions.A: From the Old Testament/this quotation we learn that John was the messenger whom God sent to precede the Messiah in order to prepare the people to receive the Messiah. (10)

Questions.Q: In verse 11 Jesus continued talking about how important John was. To whom did Jesus compare John when he said that John was the greatest among them?
Questions.A: He compared John to everyone who had been born before/up until that time. (Except Jesus himself. Since he was the speaker, he could omit himself from the comparison.) (11)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say had been happening since the time John preached his message?
Questions.A: There are several interpretations:
1. The kingdom of heaven has been forcefully advancing and people of power have been trying to use it for their own personal advantage.
-OR-
2. From the time John the Baptist began preaching and baptizing, eager multitudes have been pressing/thronging into the kingdom. (12)
Questions.Note: There doesn't seem to be a conclusive interpretation of this verse. NIV favors the second one.

Questions.Q: Before John the baptizer had come, how did the people know how God wanted them to live?
Questions.A: They knew by the Law [of Moses] and [the writings of] the Prophets [which had been read and taught to them as their guide for living]. (13)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to them in this verse?
Questions.A: He said that, if they were willing to accept/believe it, John the Baptist was the Elijah who was to come. (14)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell them to do?
Questions.A: He told them that, since they could hear, they should pay attention to what he was saying. (15)

Questions.Q: To whom do you think Jesus was referring in his comparison by the words "this generation"?
Questions.A: He was referring to the people there of that time who would not accept either John's nor Jesus's teachings. (16)
Questions.Note: See UBS handbook on Matthew for this verse.

Questions.Q: How did Jesus compare the people of that time with the children who would not respond to the other children who were playing their flutes and singing songs?
Questions.A: Jesus said that the people of that time were like the children who would not dance, when other children tried to interact with them by playing [wedding songs] on their flutes.
Jesus said that the people of that time were like the children who would not mourn/cry, when other children tried to interact with them by singing [funeral] songs. (16-17)

Questions.Q: How was that comparison in verses 16 and 17 like the way many of the people of John's and Jesus's time acted?
Questions.A: Many of the people would not respond to John nor to Jesus. No matter what John and Jesus did those people were not satisfied. John did not eat or drink/fasted and the people said that he had a demon.
Jesus ate and drank/did not fast and the people said that he was a glutton and a drunkard. The people also said that Jesus was a friend of tax collectors and sinners. (18-19)

Questions.Q: What do you think Jesus meant would show that what John and he did was the right thing to do in each case?
Questions.A: Jesus meant that eventually the end result of what they did would prove that they did what God wanted them to do. That is, they acted with [God's] wisdom. (19)

Section.heading: Matthew 11:20-24 Jesus warned the people of Chorazin, Bethsaida and Capernaum.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to the people of Chorazin, Bethsaida and Capernaum?
Questions.A: He condemned/accused those people because, although/even though they saw the miracles that he did, they would not repent. (20)

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that Jesus expressed anger and said there would be suffering for the people of Chorazin and the people of Bethsaida?
Questions.A: The people from those two areas saw his miracles, but they did not repent as the non-Jews of that time, who lived in Tyre and Sidon, would have repented completely. (21)
The people to whom Jesus was speaking knew that God had destroyed the people of Sodom because of their great wickedness.
Questions.Note: It may be necessary to make reference to their wickedness in the translation by a footnote to make Jesus's meaning clear here if the fact of their wickedness is not known/understood by people in the target community.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say would have happened if the miracles that had been done in Capernaum would have been done in Sodom?
Questions.A: Jesus said that if those miracles had been done in Sodom, it would still be in existence today. (23)

Section.heading: Matthew 11:25-30 Jesus invited people to come to him for rest.

Questions.Q: Whom did Jesus invite to come to him?
Questions.A: Jesus invited those who were over burdened and weary of sin to come to him. (28)

Questions.Q: What would he do for them?
Questions.A: He would cause them to have rest from their burdens/heavy concerns of sin. (28)

Questions.Q: For what did Jesus praise his Father?
Questions.A: He praised God because he had given understanding concerning "these things" to humble people, but not to the wise people. (25-26)

Questions.Q: What do you think were some of the important values/teachings the "ordinary ones" understood more than the "wise"?
