Questions.A: The ordinary people understood that John was God's prophet to prepare people for the Messiah's coming; and that Jesus was the Messiah sent from God. With this kind of understanding they could repent and become people of God's kingdom. (1-25)
Questions.Note: Don't expect new hearers of the text to necessarily produce all of the parts of this answer; but if they do, great. For some difficult questions, part of the questioning process is to eliminate any far out, wrong answers that do not agree with scripture. Here the "these things" refers back to general discussion in the context concerning the Kingdom of God and the introduction of the Messiah king. It is difficult to know exactly what all is covered by "these things" here. The context in that sentence helps by showing that it takes a simple humble spirited person, helped by God, to understand. This indicates that "these things" are spiritual matters. Then we look for spiritual matters which individuals need to understand in this context. This searching back is going to be difficult for anyone with only a rather quick going over of the text. Rereading verses 1-25, after the question is read, may help. The meaning may need to be made more explicit.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think were some of the important values the "ordinary ones" understood more than the "wise"?
What do you think were some of the important teachings the "ordinary ones" understood more than the "wise"?

Questions.Q: From verses 25 and 26, what do think Jesus said that pleased God the Father?
Questions.A: It says that it pleased the Father to give special understanding concerning who Jesus really was to the humble, less educated people than to the supposedly wise highly educated people. (25-26)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about his part in causing people to know who God the Father really was?
Questions.A: He said that God had turned all of that responsibility over to him and that he could decide whom he should help to know the father. (27)

Questions.Q: What did he tell them to do to have/experience/possess that rest for themselves?
Questions.A: They were to become his disciples/people and to learn from him, so he could cause them to have the peace they wanted. (29)
Questions.Alternative: What did he tell them to do to have that rest for themselves?
What did he tell them to do to experience that rest for themselves?
What did he tell them to do to possess that rest for themselves?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about the responsibility he would give to them, compared to what they had been experiencing/having?
Questions.A: He said it would be relatively easy for them. (30)
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus say about the responsibility he would give to them, compared to what they had been experiencing?
What did Jesus say about the responsibility he would give to them, compared to what they had been having?

Questions.Q: What responsibility do you think the people, to whom Jesus was speaking, had been feeling/experiencing?
Questions.Note: They had the burden of trying to satisfy the requirements of the Old Testament law — the Ten Commandments, as well as all of the ceremonies of the Old Testament system. Then they often had to meet the demands of the "wise and learned" religious leaders of that time who did not have compassion on them or try to help them.
Questions.Alternative: What responsibility do you think the people, to whom Jesus was speaking, had been feeling?
What responsibility do you think the people, to whom Jesus was speaking, had been experiencing?

Section.heading: Matthew 12:1-14 The Pharisees accused Jesus of breaking God's law concerning the Sabbath.

Questions.Q: What did the Pharisees accuse Jesus and the disciples of doing in these verses?
Questions.A: They accused them of harvesting the grain on the Sabbath day. They said that this was work. They accused them of eating on the Sabbath day. They said that this was work. (2)
They accused Jesus of healing someone on the Sabbath day, which they said was work. (10)

Questions.Q: What do you think the term "the Sabbath" means?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The Sabbath is the name of the seventh and last day of the week. The Jews observed a strict day of rest from the normal work that they did on the other six days of the week.
Questions.Note: See "Sabbath" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Where were Jesus and his disciples walking?
Questions.A: They were walking through the grain fields. (1)

Questions.Q: What were the disciples doing as they walked along?
Questions.A: They were breaking off the grain and eating it. (1)

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that they did that?
Questions.A: They did that because they were hungry. (1)

Questions.Q: What did the Pharisees say about what they were doing?
Questions.A: They said that the disciples were breaking the law by working on the day of rest. (2)

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that Jesus reminded them about what David did?
Questions.A: What David did was against God's/the laws given by Moses for carrying out the Jewish ceremonies. Thus, what David did was somewhat like the disciples/a lot like this situation with the disciples harvesting a bit of food on the rest day.

Questions.Q: What had David done that was somewhat like/a bit like what the disciples were doing?
Questions.A: David had gone against the law concerning special bread that was kept in the temple. Only the priests were allowed to eat that bread. When he and his men had arrived at the temple hungry, he had asked the priest and received from him some of the special bread and ate it. He gave some of the bread to his men and they, too, ate some of it. (3-4)
Questions.Alternative: What had David done that was somewhat like what the disciples were doing?
What had David done that was a bit like what the disciples were doing?

Questions.Q: Do you think it was justifiable/lawful/acceptable to God for David and his men to eat that special bread at that time?
Questions.A: Yes, it was.
Questions.Alternative: Do you think it was justifiable to God for David and his men to eat that special bread at that time?
Do you think it was lawful to God for David and his men to eat that special bread at that time?
Do you think it was acceptable to God for David and his men to eat that special bread at that time?

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that it was lawful/acceptable to God/permissible?
Questions.A: David and his men were truly hungry and there was no other food. (3)
Questions.Alternative: What do you think is the reason that it was lawful?
What do you think is the reason that it was acceptable to God?
What do you think is the reason that it was permissible?
Why do you think it was lawful?
Why do you think it was acceptable to God?
Why do you think it was permissible?

Questions.Q: From reading verse 5, do you think Jesus thought the Pharisees had or had not read the part in the Old Testament law that said that the priests could work in the temple area on the Sabbath? Or did he think that they had not read that part, since that portion of the Old Testament said that they could work on the Sabbath, and it would not be sin for them?
Questions.A: He assumed that they had read it. He was just reminding them of another case when it was all right for people to do some work on the Sabbath. (5)

Questions.Q: Who or what did Jesus say was more important than the temple?
Questions.A: He himself was more important than the temple.
-OR-
The kingdom of God for which he and his disciples were working was greater than the temple.
-OR-

He and the kingdom of God were greater than the temple. If work could be carried out on the Sabbath for the temple service, how much more it could be done for him and/or for God's kingdom which they were promoting. (6)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say the Pharisees did not understand?
Questions.A: Jesus said that the Pharisees did not understand what God meant when he said that he desired that people have mercy on others. But rather they were ruthless to others; and then later they sought God's forgiveness when they had not been merciful to others. (7)

Questions.Q: What people would the Pharisees not have condemned, if they had understood and obeyed the way God wanted them to be merciful?
Questions.A: They would have been merciful and not spoken out against Jesus's disciples for picking grains of wheat/harvesting food when they were hungry. (7)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when a person condemns someone else?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: When a person condemns someone else he pronounces the other person guilty of committing a crime and declares that the person will be punished for what he has done. (See "condemn" in KBT in the "judge, judgment" entry.)

Questions.Q: About whom was Jesus talking when he mentioned the Son of Man?
Questions.A: He was talking about himself. (8)

Questions.Q: What did he say about himself then?
Questions.A: He said that he is the one who made/preordained/predetermined/sets the rules for the Sabbath. (8)

Questions.Q: When Jesus went into the synagogue who was there?
Questions.A: A man with a withered hand was there. (9-10)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the Pharisees asked Jesus if it was lawful/all right to heal on the Sabbath day?
Questions.A: They wanted to see if they could dare/provoke him to say or do something that would give them a reason to accuse him of working on the Sabbath. (10)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that the Pharisees asked Jesus if it was lawful to heal on the Sabbath day?
What is the reason that the Pharisees asked Jesus if it was all right to heal on the Sabbath day?

Questions.Q: How did Jesus answer them?
Questions.A: He said that if any of them had a sheep which fell into a large/big hole on the Sabbath, they would pull it out, which was work (as the Old Testament said they could do on the Sabbath). Then he said that people are much more valuable than sheep, so it is lawful to/all right by God's law to do good to people on the Sabbath day as well. (11-12)

Questions.Q: Then what did Jesus say to the man?
Questions.A: He told him to stretch out his hand. (13)

Questions.Q: Then what happened?
Questions.A: While he was stretching out his hand Jesus healed it. (13)

Questions.Q: What did the Pharisees do after that/then?
Questions.A: They went from there and began/started planning together how they could kill Jesus. (14)
Questions.Alternative: What did the Pharisees do after that?
What did the Pharisees do then?

Section.heading: Matthew 12:15-21 God had chosen Jesus as his servant. // Jesus is God's chosen servant.

Questions.Q: What part of the quotation from Isaiah (verses 17-21) did Jesus fulfill in the verses 15-16 of this chapter (the paragraph preceding the quotation)?
Questions.A: Jesus did just as Isaiah had said God's faithful servant (the Messiah king) would do. He did not promote himself loudly in the streets. Rather he left the area where the Pharisees were and he even asked those, whom he had helped, not to make him known [to others].

Questions.Q: Jesus knew that they wanted to kill him. What did he do?
Questions.A: He went somewhere/someplace else. (15)

Questions.Q: Did he stop helping people?
Questions.A: No, he did not. (15)

Questions.Q: What happened then?
Questions.A: Many people followed him and he healed their sick ones. (15)

Questions.Q: What did he ask them not to do?
Questions.A: He asked them not to tell people about him/who he was. (16)

Questions.Q: By using the Old Testament quotation/quote from Isaiah's writings, what was Matthew teaching/making clear about Jesus?
Questions.A: Matthew was teaching/revealing to/showing his readers that the promise which/that God had made through Isaiah was being fulfilled in/by Jesus. That promise was that God's chosen Servant, the Messiah, would be revealed to them; and Matthew wanted to emphasize that Jesus must truly be the predicted Christ for whom they had been waiting. (17-21)
Questions.Alternative: By using the Old Testament quotation from Isaiah's writings, what was Matthew teaching about Jesus?
By using the Old Testament quotation from Isaiah's writings, what was Matthew making clear about Jesus?
By using the quote from Isaiah's writings, what was Matthew teaching about Jesus?
By using the quote from Isaiah's writings, what was Matthew making clear about Jesus?

Questions.Q: What are some of the characteristics/attributes that God mentioned about his chosen servant which Matthew quoted in verses 18-21?
Questions.A: The attributes which God mentioned about his chosen servant include the following:
1. God loved his chosen servant. (18)
2. His servant pleased him. (18)
3. God said that he would give his Spirit to him. (18)
4. His servant would bring justice to non-Jewish people as well as to the Jews. (18)
5. He will not argue back and forth in the streets. (19)
6. He will not talk loudly in such places. (19)
7. He will be gentle with needy people. (20)
8. He would not discourage those who needed encouragement. (20)
9. But he will, eventually cause people to do what is right. (20)
10. All the people of the earth will trust in him. (21)
Questions.Alternative: What are some of the characteristics that God mentioned about his chosen servant which Matthew quoted in verses 18-21?
What are some of the attributes that God mentioned about his chosen servant which Matthew quoted in verses 18-21?
What are some of the characteristics/attributes that God mentioned about his chosen servant which Matthew quoted in verses l8-2l?

Section.heading: Matthew 12:22-37 The Pharisees said that Jesus was using the power of Beelzebub, the chief of evil spirits, to drive evil spirits out of people.

Questions.Q: Did Jesus agree with the Pharisees when they thought that he had an agreement with Beelzebub? They said/thought that he had an agreement with Beelzebub/that Beelzebub gave him power to cast out demons like the one that kept the man from seeing and not being able to speak.
Questions.A: No, he did not agree with them.
Questions.Alternative: Did Jesus agree with the Pharisees when they thought that he had an agreement with Beelzebub? They said that he had an agreement with Beelzebub Beelzebub gave him power to cast out demons like the one that kept the man from seeing and not being able to speak.

Did Jesus agree with the Pharisees when they thought that he had an agreement with Beelzebub? They said that he had an agreement with that Beelzebub gave him power to cast out demons like the one that kept the man from seeing and not being able to speak.

Did Jesus agree with the Pharisees when they thought that he had an agreement with Beelzebub? They thought that he had an agreement with Beelzebub Beelzebub gave him power to cast out demons like the one that kept the man from seeing and not being able to speak.

Did Jesus agree with the Pharisees when they thought that he had an agreement with Beelzebub? They thought that he had an agreement with that Beelzebub gave him power to cast out demons like the one that kept the man from seeing and not being able to speak.

Questions.Q: What were some of the details/incidents/points Jesus used to show that he did not have an agreement with Beelzebub to cast out demons?
Questions.A: He told them that any group that divides into two sides, and those sides start working against each other, will not last very long. Therefore, Beelzebub would not do that against his own demons. (25-26)
He said that, if it takes an agreement with Satan to cast out demons, then how was it that some of their own people claimed to cast out demons. (27)
Questions.Alternative: What were some of the details Jesus used to show that he did not have an agreement with Beelzebub to cast out demons?
What were some of the incidents Jesus used to show that he did not have an agreement with Beelzebub to cast out demons?
What were some of the points Jesus used to show that he did not have an agreement with Beelzebub to cast out demons?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say it would prove to people if they realized that he really had cast out demons?
Questions.A: It would show that he truly was the offspring of king David. Therefore they could know that God was ruling over them. (28)

Questions.Q: What was wrong with the man whom the people brought to Jesus?
Questions.A: He was blind and could not speak. (22)

Questions.Q: What do you think Jesus did to heal the man?
Questions.A: Jesus must have cast one or more demons out of the man. (22)

Questions.Q: What did the people, who were watching, think when he caused the man to be able to see and speak?
Questions.A: They were amazed that he could do that. (23)

Questions.Q: What did they think was the reason that Jesus could do such things?
Questions.A: They were thinking that he must be the offspring of David, that is the Messiah, whom the prophets had said God would send to them someday. (23)

Questions.Q: Did the leaders of the Pharisees agree with the people that Jesus must be the Messiah for whom they had been waiting?
Questions.A: No, they did not agree. (24)

Questions.Q: What did the Pharisees say about the miracles that Jesus performed/did?
Questions.A: They said that Jesus could only cure such a demon possessed man by making an agreement with Beelzebub, the leader of the demons, who then permitted/gave authority to him/allowed him to cast out the demons. (24)
Questions.Alternative: What did the Pharisees say about the miracles that Jesus performed?
What did the Pharisees say about the miracles that Jesus did?

Questions.Q: Who is this Beelzebub?
Questions.A: That is what they called the leader of the demons, who is usually called Satan. (24)

Questions.Q: How do you think Jesus knew what the Pharisees were thinking?
Questions.A: He had often heard them talking and probably he could tell from the looks on their faces, something about their attitude toward him at that time. Also he is God so he knows everything.

Questions.Q: Who was the strong man Jesus was really talking about in these verses?
Questions.A: Jesus was referring to Satan. (29)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus mean when he said that you have to tie up a strong man well before you can rob from his house?
Questions.A: He was saying/teaching them that Satan would not allow just anyone to cast out the demons that are controlled by him. That is, Jesus is more powerful than Satan. (29)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus want people to understand by what he said in verse 30?
Questions.A: People either decide for Jesus and help him gather people to himself; or else, they are helping Satan by discouraging people from following Jesus. (30)

Questions.Q: Can you think of something which/that the Pharisees did that would have caused Jesus to talk in that manner/like that?
Questions.A: The response of the Pharisees was that he could only do that because he had a connection with Satan. By being against Jesus, the Pharisees were discouraging people from following Jesus. (24, 30)
Questions.Alternative: Can you think of something which the Pharisees did that would have caused Jesus to talk in that manner?
Can you think of something which the Pharisees did that would have caused Jesus to talk like that?
Can you think of something that the Pharisees did that would have caused Jesus to talk in that manner?
Can you think of something that the Pharisees did that would have caused Jesus to talk like that?

Questions.Q: When they/people read this, what kind of sins do you think they/people should expect that God will forgive, or will not forgive?
Questions.A: They should expect that God will forgive all kinds of sin, but deliberately defaming the Holy Spirit is very dangerous. It is possible to sin in such a way/commit a sin which/do something that God can never forgive. (32)
Questions.Alternative: When they read this, what kind of sins do you think they should expect that God will forgive, or will not forgive?
When they read this, what kind of sins do you think people should expect that God will forgive, or will not forgive?
When people read this, what kind of sins do you think they should expect that God will forgive, or will not forgive?
When people read this, what kind of sins do you think people should expect that God will forgive, or will not forgive?

Questions.Q: Will God forgive people who defame other people?
Questions.A: Yes, God will forgive people who defame other people, according to verse 31.

Questions.Q: What sin will God forgive according to verse 32?
Questions.A: Verse 32 states/relates/says that God/he will forgive people who defame the Son of Man. (This phrase "son of man" can be understood as parallel to verse 31 with the same meaning as the word "man" in that verse. But probably it is better to understand Jesus to be referring to a specific man, that is, himself, Jesus the Messiah (in his human form) here in verse 32.

Questions.Q: What does it say in verse 31 and 32 about those who defame the Holy Spirit?
Questions.A: It says that God will not forgive those who defame/speak against the Holy Spirit. (31-32)

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that Jesus talked about a good tree bearing good fruit and a bad tree bearing bad fruit?
Questions.A: It is our experience that a good tree will have good fruit and that a bad tree will have bad fruit. It just does not happen the other way around. Of course Jesus was pointing out that the same is true with people. (33)

Questions.Q: Whom did Jesus call the offspring of vipers?
Questions.A: He was talking to the Pharisees or to the Pharisees plus any others who were there who thought as/in the same manner as they did. (34)

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that Jesus called them the offspring of vipers/poisonous snakes?
Questions.A: He called them that because they were evil. (34)
Questions.Alternative: What do you think was the reason that Jesus called them the offspring of vipers?
What do you think was the reason that Jesus called them the offspring of poisonous snakes?

Questions.Q: What do you think Jesus meant by "careless words"?
Questions.A: He meant anything a person/people might say without first considering if what he/they said would result in good being done rather than bad being done. (36)

Questions.Q: To what was Jesus referring when he talked about people being acquitted and about them being condemned?
Questions.A: He warned them to prepare themselves for God's final judgment. He said what a person says will make a great difference in whether God can accept that person or not accept them. (37)

Section.heading: Matthew 12:38-45 The Pharisees and Teachers of the Law asked Jesus to do a sign/miracle for them.

Questions.Q: What did some of the Pharisees say that they wanted Jesus to do in verse 38?
Questions.A: They said that they wanted him to do something supernatural which they could see. That might prove to them that he had power from God. (38)

Questions.Q: Since Jesus had just cured a man who had been blind and could not speak, what do you think was the reason that those Pharisees asked Jesus to do something miraculous?
Questions.A: They wanted him to prove that he had power from God. But also they asked that because they did not believe that he was the one sent from God (and they did not want to believe).

Questions.Q: About whom was Jesus probably talking when he said, "this generation"?
Questions.A: The scribes and Pharisees were the ones who asked to see a sign/miracle. So he was talking about them, and probably also everyone else living at that time who had not believed in him, but who would hear of people killing him and of his coming to life again after three days. (38-41)

Questions.Q: What do you think a sign/miracle is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A miracle/sign is an unusual event, which can only be explained as a special action by God (or, in some contexts, of some other supernatural power).
Questions.Note: See "miracle, sign" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think a sign is?
What do you think a miracle is?

Questions.Q: What do you think Jesus meant when he called them an "adulterous" group of people?
Questions.A: He meant that they were breaking their covenant with God as/in the same manner as some people break their marriage promise or covenant. He meant that they were unfaithful to God and that they were doing evil. (39)

Questions.Q: The "sign of Jonah" is mentioned in verses 39-41. What sort of sign was that?
Questions.A: Jonah was saved from drowning in the sea by God, who sent a sea monster to swallow him. After three days and nights the sea monster spewed/vomited/spit him out onto the land. Likewise he/Jesus would be resurrected from death after three days. (39-41) (See the OT text concerning Jonah.)

Questions.Q: Whom did Jesus mean when he said that, 1. Something or, 2. Someone greater than Jonah was there?
Questions.A: 1. If we understand/consider what he said to mean "something greater than Jonah," then Jesus meant the message about the kingdom of God, a message greater than the one proclaimed by Jonah.
-OR-
2. If we understand/consider what Jesus said to mean "someone greater than Jonah," then, of course, he would be referring to himself—the Messiah as being greater than the prophet Jonah. (41)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus mean by his statement that, at the time of judgment, the people of Nineveh would be a witness against the Jewish people of Jesus's time?
Questions.A: He meant that the Nineveh people had repented when they were warned by Jonah, but the Jewish people of Jesus time refused to repent although/even though Jesus was greater than Jonah, the one who told the Ninevites to repent. (41)

Questions.Q: If the translated text has "Queen of the South," without mentioning her country, Sheba, then ask: From where did the queen come?
Questions.A: The queen came from a country far south of where the Jews lived. (42)
Questions.Note: It will probably be best to mention Sheba in the text or in a footnote so it will be understood that she was not from Israel. (42)

Questions.Q: How will what the queen did testify against/convict the people of Jesus's generation, at the time when God judges the people of earth?
Questions.A: The Queen of Sheba came all the way to Israel in order to hear some of King Solomon's wisdom. The Jews of Jesus day refused to listen to the Messiah, who had much greater wisdom than Solomon had. Therefore, God will judge/punish them. (42)
Questions.Alternative: How will what the queen did testify against the people of Jesus's generation, at the time when God judges the people of earth?
How will what the queen did testify convict the people of Jesus's generation, at the time when God judges the people of earth?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus mean when he talked about a number of unclean spirits coming and taking up residence where only one of them had been living previously?
Questions.A: He was warning the Jewish nation that it was about to happen to them, since they did not repent and did not truly turn to God. (43-45)

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that Jesus talked about the evil spirit going through dry places/uninhabited places, as the evil spirit wandered around when it had no place to stay?
Questions.A: By speaking of dry places/uninhabited places, Jesus disclosed/revealed/showed that the evil spirit expected to find another person in whom he could live again. (43)
Questions.Alternative: What do you think is the reason that Jesus talked about the evil spirit going through dry places, as the evil spirit wandered around when it had no place to stay?
What do you think is the reason that Jesus talked about the evil spirit going through uninhabited places, as the evil spirit wandered around when it had no place to stay?

Questions.Q: What do you think an evil spirit is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The terms "evil spirit", "unclean spirit", and "demon" are used interchangeably in the New Testament. They all refer to spiritual beings who serve Satan as his agents, being under his authority. These spiritual beings have power to oppress a human being and even to take control of him.
Questions.Note: See "evil spirit" in KBT.

Questions.Q: In this account/his little story, Jesus said that the evil spirit left the person and later came back to that person, but whom was he really warning?
Questions.A: He was warning the people of Israel including the scribes and Pharisees of verse 38, who refused to believe Jesus. (45)
Questions.Alternative: In this account, Jesus said that the evil spirit left the person and later came back to that person, but whom was he really warning?
In his little story, Jesus said that the evil spirit left the person and later came back to that person, but whom was he really warning?

Section.heading: Matthew 12:46-50 Those who believe Jesus are like a family to him.

Questions.Q: From these verses what do you think was the important point Matthew wanted us to understand?
Questions.A: Matthew wanted us to know that those, who please God, are special to Jesus like his own family.

Questions.Q: Who came looking/to look for Jesus?
Questions.A: His mother and [younger] brothers came looking/to look for him. (46)
Questions.Alternative: Who came looking for Jesus?
Who came to look for Jesus?

Questions.Q: How did Jesus know that his mother and brothers were there?
Questions.A: People in the crowd around him told him. (47)

Questions.Q: Was Jesus asking the people a question that he wanted them to answer?
Questions.A: No, he was not. (48)
Questions.Note: If there is not a question in the translation at the beginning of verse 48, omit this question and the following one.

Questions.Q: What do you think he was doing?
Questions.A: He was gaining their attention, so that he could teach them. (48)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus mean when he pointed to his disciples and said, "Here are my mother and my brothers"?
Questions.A: He meant that those, who do according to what God wants, are in close relationship to him, just like brothers, and sisters and a mother. (49-50)

Questions.Q: Do you think that Jesus refused to go and talk to his own family?
Questions.Note: Matthew did not tell us about that, but only about what Jesus was able to teach the people because of their coming to see him.

Jewish teachers used to begin/start with something that was happening and then teach something else from it. When the crowd mentioned family, Jesus started from that thought and taught about his close relationship to people who obey God. This was the important part/component of the teaching which Matthew wanted to emphasize. He did not bother to go back and tell us more about this incident and whether Jesus talked with his mother and brothers afterward or not. He probably did.

Section.heading: Matthew 13:1-9 Jesus told a parable about a farmer sowing seed.

Questions.Q: In this parable, what did Jesus say about the different seed that fell to the ground as the farmer was sowing his crop?
Questions.A: There was great variation in the soil on which that seed fell and the results were different with each kind of soil:
Some seed did not have a chance to sprout.
Some sprouted, but did not grow well.

Other seed sprouted and grew. Some of these plants produced one hundred grains of seed, some of these plants produced sixty grains of seed and some of these plants produced thirty grains of seed. (3-8)

Questions.Q: What do you think a parable is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A parable is a story which shows its meaning indirectly by using picture language to make a comparison. The parts of the comparison are generally not explained. The listeners themselves must think much about the meaning hidden in each part of the picture language. Jesus taught spiritual truths in this story form.
Questions.Note: See "parable" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus teach the people about listening carefully to him?
Questions.A: He taught them to listen carefully and to follow the good message that they heard. (9)

Questions.Q: How many people do you think might have been there that day?
Questions.A: Verse 2 states/indicates that there were large groups of people gathered around him. (2)

Questions.Q: So what did Jesus do?
Questions.A: He got into the boat. (2)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that he went into the boat?
Questions.A: He went into the boat, so that he could move away from the crowd, so everyone could see and hear him better, [as he taught them]. (2)

Questions.Q: How did Jesus teach them?
Questions.A: He used parables to teach them various things. (3)

Questions.Q: What was the topic of the main/most important parable?
Questions.A: This story was about a man who sowed seed in his field. (3)
Questions.Alternative: What was the topic of the main important parable?
What was the topic of the most important parable?

Questions.Q: How did the man plant/place/sow the seed for growing in his field?
Questions.Note: Check whether the manner of sowing is clearly tossing/scattering, since some fell where people would not ordinarily plant seed if they were to dig, plant and then cover it up.
Questions.Alternative: How did the man plant the seed for growing in his field?
How did the man place the seed for growing in his field?
How did the man sow the seed for growing in his field?

Questions.Q: What happened to some of the seed?
Questions.A: Some seed fell on the path at the edge of the field and the birds came and ate it. (4)

Questions.Q: What happened to other seed?
Questions.A: Some seed fell on soil with rock underneath. It came up quickly, but its roots did not develop, so it wilted from the heat of the sun and dried up. (5-6)

Questions.Q: Where did other seed fall?
Questions.A: Some seed fell where thorny weeds grew. Those weeds prevented the good seed from growing well, so it did not produce/bear anything. (7)

Questions.Q: What happened to the other seed?
Questions.A: Other seed fell on good soil, grew well and produced a crop. Of those seeds that grew on the good soil, some produced thirty times more seed than was sown, some produced sixty times more seed than was sown and some produced one hundred times more seed than was sown. (8)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus mean by what he said in verse 9?
Questions.A: He meant that they needed to think seriously about this parable so that they would understand it and be able to learn from its warning. (9)

Section.heading: Matthew 13:10-17 Jesus explained the reason why he spoke in parables to those who were not his disciples.

Questions.Q: To whom did Jesus always tend to speak in parables?
Questions.A: Jesus always tended to speak in parables to the crowds of people. (10)

Questions.Q: What do you think was the reason that he spoke to them mostly in parables?
Questions.A: He spoke to them mostly in parables because they did not want to hear what he taught them/would teach them nor did they want to accept/receive it and turn to God. (They would probably have rejected his message immediately and stopped coming to hear him, if he had talked to them in plain speech.) (11-15)

Questions.Q: What did the disciples want to know about the way Jesus taught?
Questions.A: They wanted to know why he always spoke in parables to the crowds of people. (10)

Questions.Q: What was Jesus's first reply to their question?
Questions.A: He said that God had given them an understanding of what previously had been unknown about God's kingdom/the way God would rule over people, but he had not given that understanding to other people. (11)

Questions.Q: Verse 12 sounds like an often-repeated saying; and we know that Jesus used it on at least one other occasion, applied to something else. What do you think he meant in this verse?
Questions.A: Jesus was saying that God will give much more understanding of him and his kingdom to the people who already have some understanding. As for those who have almost no understanding of him and his kingdom, he will take way even the little that they do know. (12)
Questions.Note: (Note: Check for any far out misunderstanding of this verse. Some possible meanings suggested by various sources are:
1) They have so little understanding of God, that at the time of God's judging of people, their understanding will be counted as nothing.
—OR—
2) When he teaches in parables they will realize/see that their original views do not fit, but will still not understand nor be forgiven by God.
—OR—
3) They will lose the Old Testament law, but they will not gain understanding of the new covenant nor be forgiven by God.)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that he spoke to them in parables?
Questions.A: He spoke to them in parables because they saw him doing miracles, but they did not understand what they were seeing. And even though they heard Jesus's message, it did not mean anything to them. So he used parables, which was the right thing to do when speaking to a rather hostile audience who were not really trying to learn from him. (13)

Questions.Q: How did what the prophet Isaiah said about the people of Israel fit what Jesus said about the crowds following him?
Questions.A: The people to whom Jesus spoke/The people about whom Isaiah wrote were set in their ways/calloused in heart and would not listen to the message Jesus wanted to tell them, nor learn from what he was doing among them. (14-15)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the people about whom Isaiah wrote and the people whom Jesus was teaching did not want to respond to God's message?
Questions.A: If they had listened, they would have learned from the message and understood in their hearts what he was teaching them. Then they would have turned to him and he would have placed/put them in a right relationship with God. (15)

Questions.Q: What was it that the disciples saw and heard that other people before them had longed to see and hear?
Questions.A: Other people, who had lived before them, had longed to see the Messiah and to hear more about how God would rule over people after he/the Messiah came. (16-17)

Section.heading: Matthew 13:18-23 Jesus explained the parable about the farmer who sowed seed.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus explain to his disciples in these verses?
Questions.A: He explained the meaning of the parable of the farmer. (18)

Questions.Q: By what he said in verse 18, what did Jesus want the disciples to do?
Questions.A: He wanted the disciples to listen so that they would understand what the parable about the sower meant. (18)

Questions.Q: What does the seed which fell on the pathway represent?
Questions.A: It represents the people who hear the message about the kingdom, but do not understand it. (19)

Questions.Q: What do you think Jesus meant by "the evil one"?
Questions.A: The evil one refers to Satan. (19)

Questions.Q: How do you think rock in the soil would cause seed not to grow well?
Questions.A: Some of the soil had patches where only a bit of soil covered rock underneath. The roots of the new seedlings could go down only to the rock and could not draw enough moisture to stay alive. (20)

Questions.Q: To what sort of people did Jesus say this part of his parable was to be applied?
Questions.A: The seed on rocky soil represents people who hear God's truth and enjoy it, but they discontinue/quit following God just a short time later. (20-21)

Questions.Q: What causes them to stop following God?
Questions.A: Any difficulties related to their following God, including their being persecuted by others will cause them to stop following him. (21)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about the people who are represented in the parable by the seed that fell among the thorny weeds?
Questions.A: The seed which fell among the thorny weeds represents people who hear God's message and accept it. However, they become so concerned about this life and about having money that the message can not have any good influence on them. (22)

Questions.Q: What happened to the seed that fell on good soil?
Questions.A: It grew up and produced thirty, sixty or even one hundred times more than what was sown. (23)

Questions.Q: What do you think people, who read this, will understand about the thirty, sixty and one hundred fold increase to mean?
Questions.A: This increase means that the message did what was expected of it. That is, the message was received by a person who took it seriously. That person not only started, but also continued to serve God as expected. (23)

Section.heading: Matthew 13:24-30 Jesus told the parable about weeds.

Questions.Q: What plan of action did the farmer take when he realized there were weeds mixed with the wheat in his field?
Questions.A: He told his workers to allow the weeds to grow there until harvest time when his harvesters could easily tell the difference between the weeds and the wheat (because of the seed heads being quite different). They could then gather the weeds to burn them; and they would store the wheat in his storehouse. (30)

Questions.Q: To whom was Jesus referring when he talked about a man who sowed good seed, planned how to care for it and then would have his servants harvest the wheat?
Questions.A: Jesus was talking about God, who is the owner of the field and he is the one who will be in charge of/supervising the "harvest". (24)
He was talking about people who truly belong to God as his "harvest". (24-30)

Questions.Q: What is the kingdom of heaven like?
Questions.A: It is like the story of a man who sowed good seed. (24)

Questions.Q: Do you think that the weeds started to grow about the same time as the wheat?
Questions.A: Both started to grow about the same time, (but the servants did not realize it until the seed heads formed). (26)

Questions.Q: How had the weed seeds come into the garden?
Questions.A: An enemy of the owner had secretly planted them there. (26-28)

Questions.Q: What was the owner's plan to separate/for separating the weeds from the real wheat?
Questions.A: His plan was to allow both to grow together until the time of harvest. Then he would have his servants cut the weeds first and bundle them for burning. After that they would harvest the wheat to keep for him. (29-30)
Questions.Alternative: What was the owner's plan to separate the weeds from the real wheat?
What was the owner's plan for separating the weeds from the real wheat?

Section.heading: Matthew 13:31-35 Jesus taught a parable about a mustard seed and a parable about yeast.

Questions.Q: What do these two parables show about the kingdom of heaven?
Questions.A: Those who believed Jesus were a small group now. Many would believe Jesus in the future. (31-33)

Questions.Q: What did Matthew say about Jesus in verses 34-35?
Questions.A: Matthew made/makes it clear that it was to be expected that Jesus would teach in parables, since that had been predicted in the Old Testament. Then the fact that he spoke in parables was a proof of his being the Messiah. (34-35)

Questions.Q: What do you think might be the reason that Jesus mentioned the birds resting in or nesting in the branches of the mustard plant?
Questions.A: It showed that the plant was large. Therefore, God will rule over many people.
Also it may or may not indicate that Jesus meant that religious sects, or others like them, would try to take advantage of the great size and influence of God's kingdom on earth. (32)

Questions.Q: How much bread do you think the flour, that the woman used, might make?
Questions.A: There would have been about 55 lbs or 25 kilos of flour. So she could have made many loaves of bread. The main point to understand is that it was a huge batch of bread which shows the potential/capability of yeast to increase the volume of the batch. Therefore, the kingdom of God will spread and have great influence. (33)

Questions.Q: Was it right for Jesus to teach in parables?
Questions.A: Yes, it had been predicted in the Old Testament that the Messiah would speak in parables. (34-35)

Section.heading: Matthew 13:36-43 Jesus explained the parable about the weeds in the wheat field.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus explain to his disciples in these verses?
Questions.A: He explained the meaning of the parable about the weeds in the wheat field.

Questions.Q: What happened after Jesus returned/went home?
Questions.A: His disciples came to him and asked him to explain the meaning of his parable about weeds in the wheat field. (36)
Questions.Alternative: What happened after Jesus returned?
What happened after Jesus went home?

Questions.Q: Who did Jesus say was the one who sowed the good seed?
Questions.A: He said that the Son of Man, that is he himself, sowed the good seed. (37)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus mean in his parable when he referred to the field?
Questions.A: When he talked of the field, he meant the people. (38)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say that he meant when he talked of the good seed?
Questions.A: He told them that, when he spoke of the good seed, he was referring to the people whom God ruled. (38)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell them that he was really saying when he mentioned weeds in his parable?
Questions.A: He told them that the weeds stood for those who were not his people, but they were people who belonged to the evil one. (38)

Questions.Q: What will people think that "the evil one" means?
Questions.A: The evil one is/means the devil-as also in the next verse. (38)

Questions.Q: When Jesus mentioned the harvest time, what did he mean?
Questions.A: He meant the end of this time on earth [when he returns]. (39)

Questions.Q: What will happen at that time?
Questions.A: Just as people gathered/would gather up the weeds and burned/would burn them at harvest time, God will send his angels to gather all those who do evil and all those who cause other people to do evil. He will have them thrown into the place of fire. (40-41)

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that they will gnash their teeth?
Questions.A: They will gnash their teeth because God will severely punish them. (42)

Questions.Q: What do you think verse 43 means when it refers to God's people shining like the sun?
Questions.A: It means that they will be pure and very pleasing to God. They will reflect his glory/show how great God is. (43)

Questions.Q: When or where do you think that will happen?
Questions.A: That will happen in the age/future time to come in God's eternal kingdom. (43)

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that Jesus said that people who have ears need to listen?
Questions.A: He said that they needed to listen because it/that/this is a very important matter. If people choose to be those who do evil, they will experience a terrible end, being put in the fire; but if they follow God they will experience God's glory forever. (40-43)

Section.heading: Matthew 13:44-46 Jesus told a parable about hidden treasure.

Questions.Q: What will people learn from the two parables Jesus told in verses 44-46?
Questions.A: When people realize the value of being part of the kingdom of heaven they will gladly give up all their possessions/they have in order to be included in that kingdom. (44-46)

Questions.Q: What will people who read this parable learn about the kingdom of heaven?
Questions.A: This parable shows how very valuable being a part of the kingdom is. They begin to value everything else less important than their relationship to God. (44)

Questions.Q: How is the kingdom of heaven like a merchant's search for fine pearls?
Questions.A: The people, who discover the kingdom of heaven for what it truly is, are like a merchant who searched for and found a most valued pearl. People, who understand the kingdom of heaven, change the whole focus of their lives by becoming a part of the kingdom of heaven. (45-46)

Section.heading: Matthew 13:47-52 Jesus told a parable about people using nets to catch fish.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus explain to his disciples in these verses?
Questions.A: He explained the meaning of the parable about people using nets to catch fish.

Questions.Q: In these verses how did the people catch the fish?
Questions.A: They threw a net into the water and pulled out whatever fish were caught by the net. (47-48)

Questions.Q: What did the fishermen do after they caught the fish?
Questions.A: They separated the good, that is, the edible ones from the bad or useless ones. They kept the edible ones and threw away the rejected ones. (48)

Questions.Q: When did Jesus say that people would be separated, as the fish were?
Questions.A: At the end of this present age, that is, the end of this present time. (49)

Questions.Q: At the end of this present time, who will separate people into the two groups, that is, those who are acceptable to God and those who are not?
Questions.A: God's angels will do that work. (49)

Questions.Q: What will the angels do with those who are wicked?
Questions.A: The angels will throw the wicked into hell to be punished. (50)

Questions.Q: How can we know from verse 50 that those people will receive severe punishment?
Questions.A: They will receive severe punishment in the place of fire because Jesus declared that they will cry and clamp their teeth together. (50)

Questions.Q: To whom do you think Jesus was talking in verse 51, when he asked them if they understood what he had been teaching/telling them?
Questions.A: He was talking to his disciples.
Questions.Note: See verse 36.
Questions.Alternative: To whom do you think Jesus was talking in verse 51, when he asked them if they understood what he had been teaching them?
To whom do you think Jesus was talking in verse 51, when he asked them if they understood what he had been telling them?
To whom do you think Jesus was talking in verse 51, when he asked them, if they understood what he had been teaching/telling them?

Questions.Q: Did the disciples understand what Jesus was teaching them with these parables?
Questions.A: Yes they did. (51)

Questions.Q: Whom do you think Jesus meant when he spoke of "the teachers of the law" in verse 52?
Questions.A: He meant the disciples. They were the ones whom he was teaching about the kingdom [and almost all Jewish people were taught the Old Testament scriptures from the time they were small. The Jews often called those scriptures "the law."] (52)

Questions.Q: To whom did Jesus compare a teacher of the law?
Questions.A: He compared a teacher of the law with the owner of a house. (52)

Questions.Q: In what way did Jesus say that a teacher of the law was like the owner of a house?
Questions.A: He said that a teacher of the law, who had been taught about the kingdom of heaven, was like the owner of a house who brought new treasures and old treasures out of his storeroom. (52)

Questions.Q: What do you know about the teachers of the law?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The TEV and NIV translate "scribe" as "teacher of the law." The scribes were important people in the Jewish religious system. They were experts in knowing and interpreting the laws of Moses and in applying them to everyday life. (See "teacher of the law" in KBT in the "scribe" entry.)

Section.heading: Matthew 13:53-58 The people of Nazareth rejected Jesus.

Questions.Q: What did the people of Nazareth do concerning Jesus?
Questions.A: They rejected him. (57)

Questions.Q: Where did Jesus go after he finished teaching about the parables?
Questions.A: He went to his hometown [which was Nazareth]. (53-54)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do there?
Questions.A: He taught the people in the synagogue. (54)

Questions.Q: How did the people respond to what Jesus taught to them?
Questions.A: They were amazed/surprised about what he taught to them. (54)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the people of Nazareth rejected Jesus?
Questions.A: They rejected him because they knew him and his family.
They knew that he was [only] the carpenter's son.
They knew his mother, Mary.
They knew his brothers and sisters.
Therefore, they did not understand how he could know anything about what he taught to them. (54-57)

Questions.Q: Where did Jesus say that people do not honor a prophet?
Questions.A: Jesus said that people do not honor a prophet in his own hometown and in his own family. (57)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Jesus did not do many miracles there?
Questions.A: He did not do many miracles there because the people did not believe in him. (58)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to have faith in someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Faith is the quality of trusting someone. It is the act of wholeheartedly and steadfastly believing in the existence, power, and benevolence of a supreme being. (See "faith" in KBT in the "believe, believing, belief, faith, trust" entry.)

Section.heading: Matthew 14:1-12 The account of how King Herod caused John the Baptist to be beheaded/executed.

Questions.Q: What happened to John the Baptist in these verses?
Questions.A: Herod [ordered his soldiers to] put John in prison.
Herod then ordered [his soldiers] to cut off John's head because of a promise he had made. (3, 7, 10)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Herod [ordered his soldiers to] put John in prison?
Questions.A: Herod [ordered his soldiers to] put John in prison because John had said that it was against the [Mosaic] law for Herod to be married to Herodias, since [she also had been married to Herod's brother, Philip]. (3-4)
Questions.Note: The Mosaic law forbade a man to marry his brother's wife while the brother was still alive.
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that Herod ordered his soldiers to put John in prison?
What is the reason that Herod put John in prison?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Herod did not kill John?
Questions.A: He did not kill John because the Jews believed that he was a prophet. (5)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Herod promised to give the daughter of Herodias whatever she wanted?
Questions.A: Herod promised to give her whatever she wanted because she had danced in front of Herod and his guests on his birthday and that had pleased him very much. (6-7)

Questions.Q: What did she ask Herod to give to her?
Questions.A: She asked him to give her the head of John the Baptist on a platter. (8)

Questions.Q: How did Herod feel then about the promise that he had made to the girl?
Questions.A: He was sorry that he had made that promise. (9)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Herod gave the order to [his soldiers] to cut off John's head and bring it to the girl?
Questions.A: He gave the order to do that because he had made the promise to the girl in the presence of all his guests. (9-11)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that Herod gave the order to his soldiers to cut off John's head and bring it to the girl?
What is the reason that Herod gave the order to to cut off John's head and bring it to the girl?

Questions.Q: What did John's disciples do with his body?
Questions.A: They took his body and buried it. (12)

Questions.Q: What did John's disciples do after they had buried his body?
Questions.A: They went and told Jesus [what had happened to John]. (12)

Section.heading: Matthew 14:13-21 Jesus fed five thousand men plus women and children.

Questions.Q: What is the main thing that happened in these verses?
Questions.A: Jesus fed five thousand men, plus women and children. (21)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do after he heard the news about John from his disciples?
Questions.A: He went by boat to a place where there were no people. (13)

Questions.Q: What did the people do when they heard that Jesus had left in a boat?
Questions.A: They walked to the place where he was. (13)

Questions.Q: How did Jesus feel about the large crowd of people that he saw coming to him?
Questions.A: He felt compassion for them/sorry for them.
He healed all the people who were sick. (14)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the disciples wanted Jesus to send the crowds away?
Questions.A: They wanted Jesus to send the crowds away so the people could buy some food for themselves. (15)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus reply to the disciples?
Questions.A: He told the disciples that the people did not need to go away.
He also told the disciples to give the people something to eat. (16)

Questions.Q: How much food did the disciples have to feed the people?
Questions.A: They had five loaves of bread and two fish. (17)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do?
Questions.A: He told the people to sit on the grass.
Then he took the five loaves and two fish.
He thanked [God] for the loaves and the fish.
He broke the loaves of bread [into pieces] and gave the pieces of bread to the disciples who then gave them to the people. (19)

Questions.Q: How did the people feel after they ate?
Questions.A: They all ate as much as they wanted. // They were all satisfied. (20)

Questions.Q: How much food was left over?
Questions.A: The disciples gathered/picked up twelve baskets full of broken pieces. (20)

Section.heading: Matthew 14:22-36 Jesus walked on top of the water.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do during the fourth watch/between 3:00am and 6:00am of the night?
Questions.A: Jesus went out to the disciples by walking on the water/lake. (25)
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus do during the fourth watch of the night?
What did Jesus do between 3:00am and 6:00am?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell his disciples to do?
Questions.A: He told them to get into the boat and go to the other side [of Lake Galilee]. (22)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Jesus went up on a mountainside?
Questions.A: He went up on a mountainside to pray. (23)

Questions.Q: What happened to the boat that the disciples were using?
Questions.A: The boat was tossed/beaten by the waves because the wind was blowing against the boat. (24)

Questions.Q: How did the disciples react when they saw Jesus walking on top of the water?
Questions.A: They were all terribly afraid because they thought they were seeing a spirit/ghost. (26)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to the disciples?
Questions.A: He told them who he was so that they would not be afraid. (27)

Questions.Q: What did Peter tell Jesus to do?
Questions.A: Peter told Jesus that he should command Peter to come to him on the water. (28)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to Peter?
Questions.A: Jesus told Peter to come [to him]. (29)

Questions.Q: What did Peter do after Jesus told him to come to him?
Questions.A: Peter got out of the boat and walked on the water toward Jesus. (29)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Peter became afraid?
Questions.A: He became afraid because he saw how the strong wind [was causing large/high waves]. (30)

Questions.Q: What happened to Peter after he became afraid?
Questions.A: He started to sink [into the water]. (30)

Questions.Q: How was Peter rescued from drowning?
Questions.A: Jesus reached out his hand and caught Peter. (31)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus ask Peter?
Questions.A: Jesus asked Peter why he had not believed [that he could walk on the water/that Jesus could make him walk on the water]. (31)

Questions.Q: What happened after Jesus and Peter climbed into the boat?
Questions.A: The wind stopped blowing after they climbed into the boat. (32)

Questions.Q: What did the people in the place/region of Gennesaret do when they recognized Jesus?
Questions.A: They told other/the people to bring all those who were sick to Jesus. (34-35)
Questions.Alternative: What did the people in the place of Gennesaret do when they recognized Jesus?
What did the people in the region of Gennesaret do when they recognized Jesus?

Questions.Q: What did the people beg Jesus to let them do?
Questions.A: They begged him to let the sick people touch the edge of his cloak/garment. (36)

Questions.Q: What happened to all of the sick people who had touched Jesus's cloak/garment?
Questions.A: They were all healed [by Jesus]. (36)
Questions.Alternative: What happened to all of the sick people who had touched Jesus's cloak?
What happened to all of the sick people who had touched Jesus's garment?

Section.heading: Matthew 15:1-20 Jesus explained what caused a person to be unacceptable to God. // Jesus explained the reason people sin.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell the disciples made a person sinful/unacceptable to God?
Questions.A: He said it is what comes out of a person's mouth that makes him sinful since those deeds/actions come from the heart. (18)
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus tell the disciples made a person sinful?
What did Jesus tell the disciples made a person unacceptable to God?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the thoughts/ideas that come from the heart make a person sinful/unacceptable to God?
Questions.A: Those thoughts/ideas make a person sinful/unacceptable because evil deeds, such as murder, adultery, sexual immorality, theft, false testimony and slander come from the evil thoughts/ideas that originate in the heart. (19)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that the thoughts that come from the heart make a person sinful?
What is the reason that the thoughts that come from the heart make a person unacceptable to God?
What is the reason that the ideas that come from the heart make a person sinful?
What is the reason that the ideas that come from the heart make a person unacceptable to God?

Questions.Q: What did some Pharisees and teachers of the law ask Jesus about his disciples?
Questions.A: They asked Jesus why his disciples broke the tradition of the elders by not washing their hands before they ate. (1-2)

Questions.Q: What do you think an elder is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The elders were the ancestors of the people. // An elder was an ancestor of the Jewish people.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus reply to them?
Questions.A: He replied by asking them why they broke the command of God in order to do what they taught. (3)

Questions.Q: Which command/commandment did Jesus use as an example to show that the Pharisees and the teachers of the law broke a command/commandment of God?
Questions.A: He used the command/commandment of God that people should honor their father and mother. (4)
Questions.Alternative: Which command did Jesus use as an example to show that the Pharisees and the teachers of the law broke a command of God?
Which command did Jesus use as an example to show that the Pharisees and the teachers of the law broke a commandment of God?
Which commandment did Jesus use as an example to show that the Pharisees and the teachers of the law broke a command of God?
Which commandment did Jesus use as an example to show that the Pharisees and the teachers of the law broke a commandment of God?

Questions.Q: How did the Pharisees and the teachers of the law break that command of God?
Questions.A: They broke that command by not giving something to their father or mother that would have helped them because they had already dedicated that item/object to God. According to their teaching, anything dedicated to God could not be used for any other purpose. (5-6)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell the people made a person sinful?
Questions.A: Jesus told them that what goes into a person's mouth does not make him sinful, but what comes out of his mouth makes him sinful/unacceptable to God. (10-11)

Questions.Q: How did the Pharisees feel about what Jesus had said to them?
Questions.A: They were offended by what he had said to them. (12)

Questions.Q: What did Peter want Jesus to explain to the disciples?
Questions.A: He wanted Jesus to explain the parable in verse 11. (15)

Questions.Q: In what way did a person make himself sinful/unacceptable to God when he ate without washing his hands?
Questions.A: Jesus said that a person would not make himself sinful/unacceptable to God when he ate without washing his hands. (20)
Questions.Alternative: In what way did a person make himself sinful when he ate without washing his hands?
In what way did a person make himself unacceptable to God when he ate without washing his hands?

Section.heading: Matthew 15:21-28 A woman from another nation/Canaan begged Jesus to heal her daughter.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that a woman from Canaan came to Jesus?
Questions.A: She came to him because her daughter was demon-possessed. She asked him to help her. (22, 25)

Questions.Q: What did his disciples tell Jesus to do?
Questions.A: They told him to send the woman away because she continually shouted at them as she followed them. (23)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to the woman?
Questions.A: He told her that he was sent only to the people of Israel, who are like lost sheep. (24)
He told her that it was not right to take the children's bread and toss it to their dogs. (26)
Questions.Note: A popular attitude of the Jews toward the Gentiles, at that time, was that the Gentiles were like dogs. See comments in UBS Translator's guide for this verse.

Questions.Q: What did the woman reply to Jesus?
Questions.A: She told him that even the dogs eat the crumbs that fall from their masters' table. (27)
Questions.Note: She was saying that even dogs have some rights. They are allowed to eat the scraps from their masters' table. She meant that he could help her a little just as dogs were/are fed. See comments in UBS Translator's guide for this verse.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Jesus did what she had requested?
Questions.A: He did what she requested because she had great faith [in him]. (28)

Questions.Q: What happened to the woman's daughter?
Questions.A: Her daughter was healed [by Jesus]. (28)

Section.heading: Matthew 15:29-39 Jesus fed four thousand men, plus women and children.

Questions.Q: What were the main deeds that Jesus did in these verses?
Questions.A: He healed many people. (30)
He fed four thousand men, plus women and children. (38)

Questions.Q: Whom did the people bring to Jesus?
Questions.A: They brought people who could not walk, people who could not see, people whose hands and/or feet had been injured, people who could not talk and many other sick people. (30)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do for all of those sick people?
Questions.A: He healed them all. (30)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the people praised God?
Questions.A: They praised God because they saw people who had been mute, speaking. They saw people who had been crippled, healed. They saw people who had been lame, walking. And they saw people who had been blind, able to see. (31)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Jesus felt compassion for those people?
Questions.A: He felt compassion for them because they had been with him for three days and they had nothing to eat. Jesus did not want to send them away hungry. (32)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Jesus did not want to send the people away hungry?
Questions.A: He did not want to send the people away hungry because he was concerned that they might collapse/faint on their way home. (32)

Questions.Q: How much food did the disciples have?
Questions.A: They had seven loaves and a few small fish. (34)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do with the loaves and the fish after he had told the crowd to sit on the ground?
Questions.A: He took the loaves and the fish and thanked [God] for them.
Then he broke the loaves and the fish into pieces and gave the pieces of bread and fish to the disciples, who then gave them to the people. (35-36)

Questions.Q: How did the people feel after they ate?
Questions.A: They all ate as much as they wanted. // They were all satisfied. (37)

Questions.Q: How much food remained/was left over?
Questions.A: The disciples gathered/picked up seven baskets full of broken pieces. (37)
Questions.Alternative: How much food remained?
How much food was left over?

Questions.Q: Where did Jesus go after he had sent the crowd away?
Questions.A: He entered/got into the boat and went to the area/region of Magadan. (39)

Section.heading: Matthew 16:1-4 The Pharisees and Sadducees asked Jesus to show them a sign/miracle (to prove that he came from God).

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the Pharisees and Sadducees came to Jesus?
Questions.A: They came to him so that they could test him. (1)

Questions.Q: What did the Pharisees and the Sadducees ask Jesus to do, in order to test him?
Questions.A: They asked Jesus to show them a sign from heaven. (1)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they wanted Jesus to show them a sign from heaven?
Questions.A: They wanted him to show them a sign from heaven [to prove that he came from God]. (1)
Questions.Note: Also See Matthew 12:38.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to the Pharisees and the Sadducees?
Questions.A: He told them that they were able to predict the weather by looking at the sky, but they were not able to explain the signs/events that were happening at that time. (2-3)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say would be given to a wicked and adulterous/unfaithful generation?
Questions.A: He said that the only sign that would be given to it was the sign of Jonah. (4)
Questions.Note: Also See Matthew 12:39.
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus say would be given to a wicked and adulterous generation?
What did Jesus say would be given to a wicked and unfaithful generation?

Section.heading: Matthew 16:5-12 Jesus told his disciples to beware of the wrong teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.

Questions.Q: About what did Jesus warn his disciples in these verses?
Questions.A: He warned them about what the Pharisees and the Sadducees taught. (12)

Questions.Q: What did the disciples forget to bring with them?
Questions.A: They had forgotten to bring bread. (5)

Questions.Q: About what did Jesus warn the disciples?
Questions.A: He warned them about the yeast [that is, the teachings] of the Pharisees and Sadducees. (6)

Questions.Q: What had the disciples thought when Jesus warned them about the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees?
Questions.A: They thought Jesus had warned them because they had forgotten to bring bread. (7)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to the disciples after he heard them talking about not having any bread?
Questions.A: He told them that they did not believe [in him] very much. (8)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus ask the disciples?
Questions.A: He asked them why they were talking about not having any bread. (8)

Questions.Q: About what did Jesus remind them?
Questions.A: He reminded them about the baskets full of leftover food that they had gathered/picked up after [Jesus] fed the crowd of five thousand people and the crowd of four thousand people. (9-10)

Questions.Q: About what did Jesus ask the disciples?
Questions.A: He asked them why they did not understand that he was not teaching/talking to them about bread. (11)

Questions.Q: About what Jesus was warning them did the disciples finally understand?
Questions.A: They understood that Jesus was not warning them about the yeast used in bread, but about what the Pharisees and Sadducees taught. (12)

Section.heading: Matthew 16:13-20 Peter declared that Jesus is the Messiah/the Savior whom God had sent.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus ask his disciples?
Questions.A: Jesus asked them who people said the Son of Man was. (13)

Questions.Q: What did his disciples reply to him?
Questions.A: They told him that some people said that he was John the Baptist, some people said he was Elijah and some people said that he was Jeremiah or one of the prophets. (14)

Questions.Q: Then what did Jesus ask his disciples?
Questions.A: He asked them who they said that he was. (15)

Questions.Q: What did Simon Peter answer to Jesus's question?
Questions.A: Simon Peter said that Jesus was the Messiah, the Son of the living God. (16)

Questions.Q: According to what Jesus said, how was the information from verse 16 revealed to Peter?
Questions.A: Jesus said that his Father in heaven had revealed that information to Peter. (17)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to Peter?
Questions.A: Jesus told Peter that he was like a rock that one or a builder uses to make the foundation of a building. Jesus said that Peter would be like the foundation of the church. (18)
Questions.Note: See comments in UBS handbook on Matthew for this verse.

Questions.Q: What do you think the church is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In this verse, it is all those who believe in Jesus.
Questions.Note: See "church" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say that the power/gates of Hades/death will not be able to do against the church?
Questions.A: Jesus said that the power of death/Hades will not be able to overcome/destroy/resist the church. (18)
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus say that the power of Hades will not be able to do against the church?
What did Jesus say that the power of death will not be able to do against the church?
What did Jesus say that the gates of Hades will not be able to do against the church?
What did Jesus say that the gates of death will not be able to do against the church?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell Peter that he was going to give to him?
Questions.A: Jesus told Peter that he was going to give him the keys to/authority over the kingdom of heaven. (19)

Questions.Q: What could Peter do with the keys to/authority over the kingdom of heaven?
Questions.A: He had the authority to decide what to prohibit or what to permit [for the citizens of heaven]. (19)
Questions.Alternative: What could Peter do with the keys to the kingdom of heaven?
What could Peter do with the authority over the kingdom of heaven?

Questions.Q: How would [God] respond to whatever Peter prohibited or permitted on earth?
Questions.A: [God] would approve of whatever Peter prohibited or permitted on earth. (19)
Questions.Alternative: How would God respond to whatever Peter prohibited or permitted on earth?
What would happen in response to Peter prohibiting or permitting something on earth?
What would be the result of Peter prohibiting or permitting something on earth?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus warn his disciples not to do?
Questions.A: He warned them not to tell anyone that he was the Messiah. (20)

Section.heading: Matthew 16:21-28 Jesus told his disciples that he will be killed and that he will rise again to life on the third day.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus explain to his disciples?
Questions.A: He explained to them that he had to go to Jerusalem where the elders, chief priests and teachers of the law would cause him to suffer very much.
Then the elders, chief priests and teachers of the law would have him put to death/executed/killed.
On the third day [God] would raise him to life. (21)

Questions.Q: How did Peter react to what Jesus had said in verse 21?
Questions.A: Peter told Jesus that it would never happen to him. // Peter told Jesus that such a thing must not happen to him. (22)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus reply to Peter?
Questions.A: Jesus told Peter that he was acting like Satan.
Jesus told Peter that he was being a stumbling block to him.
Jesus told Peter that he was not thinking as/in the same manner that God does, but he was thinking as people think/do. (23)

Questions.Q: What must anyone do who wants to follow Jesus/be a disciple of Jesus?
Questions.A: Any person who wants to follow Jesus must deny himself/give up his own plans and be willing to suffer for Christ. (24)
Questions.Alternative: What must anyone do who wants to follow Jesus?
What must anyone do who wants to be a disciple of Jesus?

Questions.Q: What will happen to a person, who wants to save his own life?
Questions.A: Jesus said that a person, who wants to save his life, will lose it/eternal life. (25)

Questions.Q: What will happen to a person, who loses his life for Jesus/to follow Jesus/to be a disciple of Jesus?
Questions.A: Jesus said that a person, who loses his life for Jesus, will find it/have eternal life. (25)
Questions.Alternative: What will happen to a person, who loses his life for Jesus?
What will happen to a person, who loses his life to follow Jesus?
What will happen to a person, who loses his life to be a disciple of Jesus?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus ask his disciples in verse 26?
Questions.A: He asked them, "What good would it be if a man owns everything in the world/everything that he wants, but lost his own soul/eternal life?"
He also asked them what can a man give in exchange for his own soul/eternal life? (26)
Questions.Note: This is a rhetorical question for which Jesus did not expect an answer.

Questions.Q: What do you think the answer is to both of his questions?
Questions.A: There is nothing that anyone can give in such an exchange.

Questions.Q: How did Jesus say that the Son of Man was going to come [again]?
Questions.A: He said that the Son of Man was going to come in his Father's glory/power/authority and with his angels. (27)
Questions.Alternative: How did Jesus say that the Son of Man was going to come again?
How did Jesus say that the Son of Man was going to come?

Questions.Q: What will the Son of Man do after he has come?
Questions.A: He will reward each person according to what he has done. (27)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say was going to happen to some of those, who were standing there with him?
Questions.A: He said that some of them would not die before they saw the Son of Man coming in his kingdom/as King. (28)

Section.heading: Matthew 17:1-13 The appearance of Jesus was changed and three disciples saw his glory/him shining.

Questions.Q: What happened to Jesus on the mountain?
Questions.A: He was transfigured on the mountain. // The appearance of Jesus was changed. (2)

Questions.Q: In what way did Jesus change?
Questions.A: His face shone like the sun. His clothes became as white as the sunlight. (2)

Questions.Q: Where did Peter, James and John go with Jesus?
Questions.A: They went with him to the top of a high mountain where they could be alone. (1)

Questions.Q: What happened after Jesus was changed/transfigured?
Questions.A: The three disciples saw Moses and Elijah talking with Jesus. (3)
Questions.Alternative: What happened after Jesus was changed?
What happened after Jesus was transfigured?

Questions.Q: What did Peter volunteer to do?
Questions.A: He volunteered to make three shelters, one for Jesus, one for Moses and one for Elijah. (4)

Questions.Q: What happened while Peter was still talking?
Questions.A: A bright cloud covered all six of them/people.
A voice spoke from the cloud and said, "This is my Son, whom I love; with him I am well pleased. Listen to him." (5)

Questions.Q: How did the disciples react to hearing the voice?
Questions.A: They were very afraid. They fell face down to the ground. (6)

Questions.Q: Where did Moses and Elijah go?
Questions.A: They disappeared/vanished. (8)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell the three disciples to do?
Questions.A: Jesus told them not to tell anyone what they had seen until [God] raised the Son of Man from the dead. (9)

Questions.Q: About whom was Jesus (really) talking in verses 11-13?
Questions.A: He was talking about John the Baptist. (13)

Section.heading: Matthew 17:14-23 Jesus commanded a demon to leave the body of a boy.

Questions.Q: What miracle did Jesus do in these verses?
Questions.A: He commanded a demon to leave the body of a boy and he healed the boy. (18)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that a man came to Jesus?
Questions.A: He came to Jesus because his son suffered from having seizures.
His son often fell into the fire or into the water.
He came to ask the Lord to have mercy on his son [and to heal him]. (14-15)

Questions.Q: How had the man already tried to have someone heal his son?
Questions.A: He had taken his son to Jesus's disciples, but they could not heal him. (16)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do to heal the boy?
Questions.A: Jesus rebuked the demon and it came out of the boy. The boy was healed at that moment. (18)

Questions.Q: What had the disciples asked Jesus?
Questions.A: They asked him why they had not been able to command the demon to leave the boy. (19)

Questions.Q: What answer did Jesus give to the disciples?
Questions.A: Jesus told them that (the reason) they could not command the demon to leave the boy was because they had not believed more in God. (20)
