Questions.Q: What did Jesus say they could do if they had faith [in God] as small as a mustard seed?
Questions.A: He told them that they could tell a mountain to move and it would move.
He told them that nothing would be impossible for them. (20)
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus say they could do if they had faith in God as small as a mustard seed?
What did Jesus say they could do if they had faith as small as a mustard seed?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell his disciples was going to happen to him?
Questions.A: He told them that [men] would deliver him to other men who would kill him.
He told them that [God] would raise him to life three days later. (22-23)

Questions.Q: How did the disciples react to what Jesus had just told them?
Questions.A: They were very sad. (23)

Section.heading: Matthew 17:24-27 Jesus talked about the temple tax.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the basic theme of these verses?
Questions.A: Jesus spoke/talked about the temple tax and those who were required to pay it.

Questions.Q: What did the collectors of the temple tax ask Peter?
Questions.A: They asked him if Jesus paid the temple tax. (24)

Questions.Q: What did Peter reply to their question?
Questions.A: Peter told them that Jesus paid the temple tax. (25)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus ask Peter about taxes and duties?
Questions.A: Jesus asked Peter if kings/rulers collected the taxes and duties from their own sons or from others. (25)

Questions.Q: What did Peter reply to Jesus?
Questions.A: Peter said that kings/rulers collected the taxes and duties from others. (26)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Jesus said that Peter should pay the temple tax for himself and for Jesus?
Questions.A: Jesus said that Peter should pay the tax for himself and for Jesus so that they would not offend the tax collectors. (27)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell Peter to do in order to have/obtain the money for the temple tax?
Questions.A: Jesus told Peter to go to the lake and catch a fish.
Then he said that Peter would find the money for the tax in the mouth of the first fish that he caught.
Jesus told Peter to take that money and give it to the temple tax collectors. (27)
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus tell Peter to do in order to have the money for the temple tax?
What did Jesus tell Peter to do in order to obtain the money for the temple tax?

Section.heading: Matthew 18:1-9 Jesus told his disciples how to be great in the kingdom of God.

Questions.Q: What did the disciples ask Jesus?
Questions.A: They asked him who is the greatest/most important in the kingdom of heaven. (1)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus reply to the disciples?
Questions.A: He told them that whoever humbles himself like a little child is the greatest/most important in the kingdom of heaven. (2-4)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about anyone who welcomed/accepted a little child in his name/for his sake/because of him?
Questions.A: He said that such a/that person also welcomed/accepted Jesus. (5)
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus say about anyone who welcomed a little child in his name?
What did Jesus say about anyone who welcomed a little child for his sake?
What did Jesus say about anyone who welcomed a little child because of him?
What did Jesus say about anyone who accepted a little child in his name?
What did Jesus say about anyone who accepted a little child for his sake?
What did Jesus say about anyone who accepted a little child because of him?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say would be better for anyone than to cause a little child, who believed in him, to sin?
Questions.A: Jesus said it would be better if that person had a millstone hung around his neck and be drowned in the sea. (6)

Questions.Q: What do you think Jesus was talking about in verses 7-9?
Questions.A: He was teaching/saying that people should quit what is causing them to sin. (7-9)

Section.heading: Matthew 18:10-14 Jesus told the parable about the lost sheep.

Questions.Q: About what parable did Jesus tell to the disciples in these verses?
Questions.A: Jesus told the parable about a man who had a sheep that wandered away.

Questions.Q: In what way are little children important to God?
Questions.A: Jesus said that an angel of God is watching over each one of them. (10)

Questions.Q: What will a man, who owns a hundred sheep, do if one of the sheep wanders away?
Questions.A: He will go and search/look for that sheep. (12)

Questions.Q: How will that man feel if he finds that sheep?
Questions.A: He will be happier about that one sheep than about the others that did not wander away. (13)

Questions.Q: How did Jesus compare the way that man felt about his one sheep to the way the Father in heaven feels about his children?
Questions.A: Jesus said that the Father in heaven does not want to lose any of the little children who believe in him. (14)

Section.heading: Matthew 18:15-20 Jesus told/taught what to do if a fellow-believer does something wrong against you.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the basic theme of these verses?
Questions.A: Jesus told the disciples what they should do/say if one of their fellow-believers did something wrong to them.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell the disciples that they should do if their fellow-believer sinned against them?
Questions.A: He told them that they should go to that person and tell him what he has done against them. This should be done just between the two of them. (15)

Questions.Q: What should they do if the offending person will not listen/admit that he was wrong?
Questions.A: They should go to the offending person with one or two other persons/believers, so that everything that is said can be/is heard by two or three witnesses. (16)
Questions.Alternative: What should they do if the offending person will not listen?
What should they do if the offending person will not admit that he was wrong?

Questions.Q: What should they do if the offending person will not listen to them?
Questions.A: They should tell the whole matter/trouble to the local church/local group of believers. (17)

Questions.Q: What should they do if the offending person will not listen to the church?
Questions.A: They should treat him as though he were a pagan/non-believer or a tax collector. (17)

Questions.Q: How would [God] respond to whatever the disciples prohibited or permitted on earth?
Questions.A: [God] would approve of whatever they prohibited or permitted on earth. (18)
Questions.Alternative: How would God respond to whatever the disciples prohibited or permitted on earth?
What would happen in response to the disciples prohibiting or permitting something on earth?
What would be the result of the disciples prohibiting or permitting something on earth?

Questions.Q: How will the Father respond to requests from the disciples in which two or three of them had agreed?
Questions.A: Jesus said that his Father would do whatever they asked for them. (19)

Questions.Q: Where did Jesus say he would be whenever two or three or more of them gathered together?
Questions.A: Jesus said that he would be there with them. (20)

Section.heading: Matthew 18:21-35 Jesus told the disciples a parable about a man who refused to forgive his fellow servant.

Questions.Q: About what parable did Jesus tell to the disciples in these verses?
Questions.A: Jesus told the disciples a parable about a servant who refused to forgive a fellow servant for what he owed to him.

Questions.Q: What did Peter ask Jesus?
Questions.A: Peter asked Jesus how many times he should forgive his brother when he sins against him. He asked Jesus whether/if he should forgive his brother seven times. (21)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus answer Peter?
Questions.A: Jesus told Peter that he should forgive his brother every time. (22)

Questions.Q: To what did Jesus compare the kingdom of heaven?
Questions.A: He compared the kingdom of heaven to a king who wanted to find out/determine how much money each of his servants owed to him. (23)

Questions.Q: What did the king decide to do with a servant who owed him much money/ten thousand talents/millions of dollars?
Questions.A: The king decided that the servant, his wife, his children and all that he owned should be sold to pay the debt. (24-25)
Questions.Alternative: What did the king decide to do with a servant who owed him much money?
What did the king decide to do with a servant who owed him ten thousand talents?
What did the king decide to do with a servant who owed him millions of dollars?

Questions.Q: What did the servant beg the king to allow him to do?
Questions.A: The servant begged the king to be patient with him and he would pay back all that he owed to the king. (26)

Questions.Q: What did the king do in response to the request of his servant?
Questions.A: The king pitied his servant, so he canceled the debt and let him go. (27)

Questions.Q: What did that servant do after he was set free?
Questions.A: He found a fellow servant, who owed him a small amount of money/a few dollars. He demanded that the fellow servant pay back what he owed. (28)

Questions.Q: What did the fellow servant beg the other servant to allow him to do?
Questions.A: The fellow servant begged the other servant to be patient with him and he would repay/pay back everything that he owed to him. (29)

Questions.Q: What did the servant do in response to the request of the fellow servant?
Questions.A: He refused to be patient with him. Instead he ordered that the fellow servant be put in prison until he could repay/pay back the debt. (30)

Questions.Q: What did the other servants tell the king?
Questions.A: They told him everything that had happened between the other two servants. (31)

Questions.Q: After he heard what the other servants told him, what did the king do to the servant, whose debt he had cancelled?
Questions.A: He was very angry with the servant for what he had done to his fellow servant. The king had that first servant put in prison and tortured until he could repay/pay back all that he owed to the king. (32-34)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell the disciples would happen to them if they did not forgive their brother?
Questions.A: Jesus said that his heavenly Father would treat them in the same manner/the same way that the king treated his servant for not forgiving his fellow servant. (35)

Section.heading: Matthew 19:1-12 Jesus taught the people that anyone who divorced his wife was breaking God's commandment.

Questions.Q: About what did Jesus teach the people in these verses?
Questions.A: Jesus taught the people about what he/God thought about divorce.

Questions.Q: Where did Jesus go?
Questions.A: He left Galilee and went into the region of Judea on the east side of the Jordan River. (1)

Questions.Q: Who followed Jesus?
Questions.A: Many people followed him. (2)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do in Judea?
Questions.A: He healed many sick people. (2)

Questions.Q: What did the Pharisees ask Jesus at that time/in that place?
Questions.A: They asked Jesus if the law allowed a man to divorce his wife for any reason. (3)
Questions.Alternative: What did the Pharisees ask Jesus at that time?
What did the Pharisees ask Jesus in that place?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the Pharisees asked Jesus that question?
Questions.A: They asked Jesus that question because they wanted to test him. (3)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus reply to the Pharisees?
Questions.A: He reminded them that, in the beginning, the Creator made man and woman. (4)
God said it was for that reason that a man would leave his father and mother and be united to his wife and the two would become as one person. (5)
Therefore, they are no longer two, but as one.
Therefore, what God has joined together no man should separate [by divorce]. (6)

Questions.Q: What did the Pharisees ask Jesus next?
Questions.A: They asked Jesus why Moses had written a law that allowed a man to divorce his wife and send her away. (7)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus reply to the Pharisees?
Questions.A: Jesus told the Pharisees that Moses allowed them to divorce their wives because their [the Jews'] hearts were very hard/they were so hard to teach/they were so stubborn.
Jesus also told them that [God] had not intended, from the beginning [of creation], that a man should divorce his wife. (8)

Questions.Q: For what reason did Jesus say that a man could divorce his wife?
Questions.A: He said that a man could divorce his wife if she had been unfaithful/committed adultery in the marriage. (9)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say a man was committing/doing if he divorced his wife, when she had been faithful to him, and he married another woman?
Questions.A: Jesus said that a man, who divorced his wife when she had been faithful to him and married another woman, was committing adultery. (9)
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus say a man was committing if he divorced his wife, when she had been faithful to him, and he married another woman?
What did Jesus say a man was doing if he divorced his wife, when she had been faithful to him, and he married another woman?

Questions.Q: What did the disciples say to Jesus in response to what he had just said about divorce?
Questions.A: The disciples told Jesus that it would be better for a man not to marry a woman if that is the only situation in which a man may divorce his wife. (10)

Questions.Q: Who did Jesus say would be able to accept/understand the meaning of what he had said/this word/this teaching?
Questions.A: Jesus said that only the people, to whom God has given the understanding, will be able to grasp the meaning of this word. (11)
Questions.Alternative: Who did Jesus say would be able to accept what he had said?
Who did Jesus say would be able to accept this word?
Who did Jesus say would be able to accept this teaching?
Who did Jesus say would be able to understand the meaning of what he had said?
Who did Jesus say would be able to understand this word?
Who did Jesus say would be able to understand this teaching?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say were the reasons that some men do not marry?
Questions.A: He said that some men are eunuchs/not capable of marriage because they were born that way.
He said that some men were forced to be eunuchs by other men.
He said that some men decided not to marry because they wanted to spend all of their time serving God. (12)

Section.heading: Matthew 19:13-15 People brought small children to Jesus, and he blessed them.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that people brought little children to Jesus?
Questions.A: They brought little children to Jesus because they wanted him to place his hands on them and pray for them/ask God to bless them. (13)

Questions.Q: What did the disciples say to the people who brought the children to Jesus?
Questions.A: The disciples rebuked/scolded the people for bringing the children. (13)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to the disciples?
Questions.A: Jesus told the disciples that they should allow/permit the little children to come to him. (14)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Jesus told the disciples to allow/permit the little children to come to him?
Questions.A: Jesus said that the little children should come to him because the kingdom of heaven belongs to people like them. (14)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that Jesus told the disciples to allow the little children to come to him?
What is the reason that Jesus told the disciples to permit the little children to come to him?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do for the little children?
Questions.A: He placed his hands on them and prayed for them/asked God to bless them. (15)

Section.heading: Matthew 19:16-30 Jesus taught that it is very difficult for a rich person to receive eternal life.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the basic theme of these verses?
Questions.A: Jesus talked with a rich man about what he would have to do in order to receive eternal life.

Questions.Q: What did the man ask Jesus?
Questions.A: He asked Jesus what good deed he needed to do to have/receive eternal life. (16)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell the man to do to receive eternal life?
Questions.A: He told him to obey God's/the commandments. (17)

Questions.Q: Which commandments did Jesus tell the man to obey?
Questions.A: Jesus told the man to obey the following commandments:
Do not murder.
Do not commit adultery.
Do not steal.
Do not give false testimony/accuse anyone falsely. (18)
Honor your father and mother.
Love your neighbor as yourself. (19)

Questions.Q: Which commandments did the man tell Jesus that he had obeyed?
Questions.A: He told Jesus that he had obeyed all of them. (20)

Questions.Q: Then what did the man ask Jesus?
Questions.A: He asked him what else he needed to do [to receive eternal life]. (20)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell him to do?
Questions.A: Jesus told the man that, if he wanted to be perfect/the way God wanted him to be, he should sell his possessions and give [the money] to the poor. Then he should follow Jesus/become a disciple of Jesus. (21)

Questions.Q: What would the man have had as a result of selling his possessions and giving the money to the poor?
Questions.A: Jesus told the man that he would have treasure/a reward in heaven. (21)

Questions.Q: How did the man respond after Jesus told him what he needed to do [to receive eternal life]?
Questions.A: The man went away feeling very sad. (22)
Questions.Alternative: How did the man respond after Jesus told him what he needed to do to receive eternal life?
How did the man respond after Jesus told him what he needed to do?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that he felt very sad?
Questions.A: He felt very sad because he was very rich/had many possessions [and he did not want to give them away]. (22)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say would be easier than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God?
Questions.A: Jesus said that it would be easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God/become one of God's people/receive eternal life. (24)

Questions.Q: What do you think the kingdom of God is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The kingdom of God has the significance of God's rule in the lives of men, rather than of a territory over which God rules.
Questions.Note: See "kingdom of God" in KBT.

Questions.Q: How did the disciples react when they heard what Jesus had just said?
Questions.A: They were very amazed/surprised.
They asked Jesus, who could be saved/receive eternal life? (25)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus reply to the disciples?
Questions.A: Jesus told them that it is impossible for men to save themselves, but he said that God can save them because he can do anything. (26)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Peter asked Jesus the question in verse 27?
Questions.A: He wanted to know what they (he and the other disciples) would receive [from God] because they had given up/for giving up everything they owned/possessed to follow him/be his disciples. (27)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell the disciples to answer Peter's question?
Questions.A: Jesus told the disciples that, when the Son of Man sits on his glorious throne [to rule everyone], they would sit on twelve thrones to rule the twelve tribes of Israel. (28)

Jesus also told them that anyone who has left houses, or brothers, or sisters, or father, or mother, or children, or fields/land for his sake/in order to serve him, would receive a hundred times as much [from God]. They will also inherit/receive eternal life [from God]. (29)

Questions.Q: What do you think "glorious" means?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Glorious in this verse means magnificent, amazing, splendid, wonderful, associated with God and his presence. (See "glorious" in KBT in the "glory" entry.)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about those people, who are first/most important now, and those who are last/least important now?
Questions.A: Jesus said that those people, who are most important now, will be least important later/in the future kingdom of God. Those people, who are least important now, will be most important later/in the future kingdom of God. (30)
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus say about those people, who are first now, and those who are last now?
What did Jesus say about those people, who are most important now, and those who are least important now?

Section.heading: Matthew 20:1-16 Jesus told a parable about a man who hired men to work in his vineyard.

Questions.Q: To what did Jesus compare the kingdom of heaven?
Questions.A: He compared it to a landowner who went out early in the morning to hire men to work in his vineyard. (1)

Questions.Q: What did the landowner agree to pay each man for working in his vineyard?
Questions.A: He agreed to pay each man a denarius (the usual daily wage). (2)

Questions.Q: What did the landowner do at about 9:00 am?
Questions.A: He went to the marketplace and hired more men to work in his vineyard. (3-4)

Questions.Q: How much money did the landowner agree to pay those new workers?
Questions.A: He agreed to pay them whatever was right/a fair wage. (4)

Questions.Q: What did the landowner do at about Noon, 3:00 p.m. and 5:00 p.m.?
Questions.A: He hired more men to work in his vineyard. (5-7)

Questions.Q: What did the landowner tell his foreman to do, when the evening came/at 6:00 p.m.?
Questions.A: He told his foreman to pay all the workers beginning/starting with those who were hired last. (8)
Questions.Alternative: What did the landowner tell his foreman to do, when the evening came?
What did the landowner tell his foreman to do, at 6:00 p.m.?

Questions.Q: How much did the foreman pay each worker?
Questions.A: He paid each worker a denarius. (9-10)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that those, who were hired first, expected to receive more than a denarius?
Questions.A: They expected to receive more than a denarius because that is what the foreman paid the workers who were hired later in the day. (10)

Questions.Q: How did the workers, who were hired first, react to receiving the same pay as those workers who were hired last?
Questions.A: They complained to the landowner. (11)
They told the landowner that he paid the workers, who were hired last, the same amount that he paid them; and the last ones, whom he hired, had worked only one hour. (12)

Questions.Q: What did the landowner reply to one of the disgruntled/displeased/disappointed workers?
Questions.A: The landowner told that worker that he was not being unfair to him.
He reminded the worker that he had agreed to work for a denarius. (13)
He told the worker that he wanted to pay the man/men, who was/were hired last, the same amount that he had paid him. (14)
The landowner told the worker that he had the right to do what he wanted to do with his own money. (15)
Questions.Alternative: What did the landowner reply to one of the disgruntled workers?
What did the landowner reply to one of the displeased workers?
What did the landowner reply to one of the disappointed workers?

Questions.Q: Of what did the landowner accuse the worker?
Questions.A: He accused the worker of being envious/jealous because the landowner was generous with his money. (15)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell his disciples?
Questions.A: Jesus told his disciples that those people, who are least important now, will be the most important later. Those people, who are most important now, will be the least important later. (16)

Section.heading: Matthew 20:17-19 Jesus again told his disciples that he would be killed and would rise again to life.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the basic theme of these verses?
Questions.A: Jesus told his disciples what was going to happen to him.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell his disciples was going to happen to him?
Questions.A: He told his disciples, that in Jerusalem, he/the Son of Man would be handed over/betrayed [by someone] to the chief priests and to the teachers of the law. (18)

Questions.Q: What were the chief priests and the teachers of the law [planning] to do to him/the Son of Man?
Questions.A: They were [planning] to condemn/sentence him to death/die. (18)
They were [planning] to hand him over to the Gentiles/non-Jews/Romans who would mock/make fun of, flog/whip him and who would crucify him. (19)
Questions.Alternative: What were the chief priests and the teachers of the law planning to do to him?
What were the chief priests and the teachers of the law planning to do to the Son of Man?

Questions.Q: What do you think happened to a person whom the soldiers crucified?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: During that time/those years Roman soldiers crucified people by either tying their arms to a crossbeam or pounding nails through their wrists. Then they pulled the person up on an upright post, which was planted in the ground. Then they tied or nailed the person to the post at his ankles. (See "crucify" in KBT in the "cross" entry.)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell his disciples would happen to him on the third day after he was crucified?
Questions.A: Jesus told them that [God] would raise him back to life. (19)

Section.heading: Matthew 20:20-28 The mother of [James and John] asked Jesus to do something for her sons.

Questions.Q: What did the mother of Zebedee's sons/wife of Zebedee ask Jesus to do for her sons?
Questions.A: She asked Jesus to let one of her sons sit on his right side and the other son to sit on his left side in his kingdom/when he rules mankind. (20-21)
Questions.Alternative: What did the mother of Zebedee's sons ask Jesus to do for her sons?
What did the wife of Zebedee ask Jesus to do for her sons?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to her two sons?
Questions.A: He told them that they did not know/understand what they were asking. (22)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus ask her two sons?
Questions.A: Jesus asked them if they were able to drink the cup that he was going to drink. // Jesus asked them if they were willing to suffer in the same way that he would suffer. (22)

Questions.Q: What did her two sons answer Jesus?
Questions.A: They said that they were able to/could drink the cup that he would drink. // They said that they were willing to suffer in the same way that he would be suffering. (22)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to them next?
Questions.A: He told them that they surely would drink from his cup/suffer in the same way that he would be suffering. (23)

Questions.Q: Whom did Jesus say would decide who would sit on his right side and who would sit on his left side?
Questions.A: Jesus said that his Father/God would decide who would sit on his right side and who would sit on his left side. (23)

Questions.Q: How did the other ten disciples react when they heard what the two brothers had requested of Jesus?
Questions.A: They were angry with the two brothers. (24)

Questions.Q: About what did Jesus remind the disciples?
Questions.A: Jesus reminded the disciples that the rulers of the Gentiles exercised complete control over them and the officials of the Gentiles ruled harshly over them. (25)

Questions.Q: In what way did Jesus tell the disciples that they must not be like the rulers of the Gentiles?
Questions.A: Jesus told the disciples that whoever wanted to be great/important among them must be their servant. (26)
Jesus told the disciples that whoever wanted to be first/important among them must be their slave. (27)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to be a slave of someone/something?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that the person is totally responsible to and dependent upon another person, or the person has become completely subservient to a dominating influence. (See "slave" in KBT in the "servant, slave" entry.)
Questions.Alternative: What do you think it means to be a slave of someone?
What do you think it means to be a slave of something?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the Son of Man came to the earth/the world?
Questions.A: The Son of Man came to the earth to serve others and to give his life to set many people free [from their sins]. (28)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that the Son of Man came to the earth?
What is the reason that the Son of Man came to the world?

Section.heading: Matthew 20:29-34 Jesus healed two blind men.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do for two blind men in these verses?
Questions.A: Jesus healed two blind men in these verses.

Questions.Q: Who followed Jesus as he and his disciples were leaving Jericho?
Questions.A: A large crowd of people followed him. (29)

Questions.Q: What did two blind men, who were sitting by the roadside, do when they heard that Jesus was passing by them?
Questions.A: They shouted, "Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us!" (30)

Questions.Q: What did the crowd tell the two blind men to do?
Questions.A: The crowd rebuked/scolded the two blind men and told them to be quiet. (31)

Questions.Q: What did the two blind men do after the crowd rebuked them?
Questions.A: The two blind men shouted even louder, "Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us!" (31)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus ask the two blind men?
Questions.A: Jesus asked the two blind men what they wanted him to do for them. (32)

Questions.Q: What did the two blind men want Jesus to do for them?
Questions.A: They wanted Jesus to heal their eyes so that they could see. (33)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do for the two blind men?
Questions.A: He felt compassion/pity for them. He touched their eyes and immediately they could see. (34)

Questions.Q: What did the two men do after they were able to see again?
Questions.A: They followed Jesus/became disciples of Jesus. (34)

Section.heading: Matthew 21:1-11 Jesus entered Jerusalem (as a king).

Questions.Q: What do you think is the basic theme of these verses?
Questions.A: The author wrote about what happened as Jesus was entering Jerusalem.

Questions.Q: As Jesus and his disciples approached Jerusalem and came to the (village of) Bethphage what did Jesus tell two of his disciples to do?
Questions.A: Jesus told them to go to the (village of) Bethphage and there they would find a donkey and her colt that were tied [to a post].
Jesus told them to untie the donkey and her colt and to bring them to him. (1-2)

Questions.Q: What were the two disciples supposed to say if anyone asked them what they were doing/why they were taking the donkey and the colt?
Questions.A: The two disciples were supposed to tell that person that the Lord needed the donkey and the colt. (3)
Questions.Alternative: What were the two disciples supposed to say if anyone asked them what they were doing?
What were the two disciples supposed to say if anyone asked them why they were taking the donkey and the colt?

Questions.Q: What would that person do after the two disciples told him that the Lord needed the donkey and the colt?
Questions.A: That person would immediately permit/allow them to take the donkey and the colt. (3)

Questions.Q: What would be fulfilled by all of those events taking place?
Questions.A: The occurring/occurrence of all those events were the fulfillment of prophecies written by Isaiah and Zechariah many years before that time. (4-5)
Questions.Note: See Isaiah 62:11 and Zechariah 9:9.

Questions.Q: What did those two disciples do with the donkey and the colt?
Questions.A: They brought the donkey and the colt [to Jesus] and placed their cloaks/outer garments on the donkey and the colt. (7)

Questions.Q: Then what did Jesus do?
Questions.A: He sat on the colt. (7)
Questions.Note: See Mark 11:2 and Luke 19:30.

Questions.Q: What did the large crowd of people do?
Questions.A: Some of the people in the crowd spread their cloaks/outer garments on the road.
Other people in the crowd cut branches from the trees and spread them on the road.

The crowd of people who were walking [on the road] ahead of Jesus and behind Jesus shouted, "Hosanna to the Son of David!" "Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!" "Hosanna in the highest!" (8-9)

Questions.Q: What happened when Jesus entered Jerusalem [riding on that/the colt]?
Questions.A: The crowd of people in the city became very excited and asked the crowd of people, who were with Jesus, who he was.
The crowd of people, who were with Jesus, answered that he was Jesus, the prophet from Nazareth in Galilee. (10-11)
Questions.Alternative: What happened when Jesus entered Jerusalem riding on that colt?
What happened when Jesus entered Jerusalem riding on the colt?
What happened when Jesus entered Jerusalem?

Section.heading: Matthew 21:12-17 Jesus drove out the traders from the temple courtyard.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do when he entered the temple area?
Questions.A: He drove everyone out of the temple courtyard who were buying and selling [animals and other items to be used for sacrifices].
He overturned the tables of the moneychangers and the benches of those who were selling doves. (12)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to the moneychangers and to the people who were buying and selling?
Questions.A: He told them that it is written [in the scriptures] that [God] said, "My house will be called a house of prayer." (13)

Questions.Q: Of what did Jesus accuse the moneychangers and the people who were buying and selling [animals and other items]?
Questions.A: He accused them of making the temple area into a den of robbers/cave of thieves. (13)
Questions.Alternative: Of what did Jesus accuse the moneychangers and the people who were buying and selling animals and other items?
Of what did Jesus accuse the moneychangers and the people who were buying and selling?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do for the blind people and the lame people who came to him at the temple?
Questions.A: Jesus healed all of them. (14)

Questions.Q: How did the chief priests and the teachers of the law react when they saw the miracles that Jesus did and heard the children shouting in the temple area, "Hosanna to the Son of David"?
Questions.A: They were very angry. (15)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do then?
Questions.A: He left them/the people in the temple courts and went to the village of Bethany.
He spent the night/stayed for the night in Bethany. (17)

Section.heading: Matthew 21:18-22 Jesus cursed/condemned a fig tree and taught about faith in God.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Jesus went over to the fig tree that was beside/by the road?
Questions.A: He was hungry so he went over to the fig tree [expecting to pick some figs to eat]. (18-19)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that Jesus went over to the fig tree that was beside the road?
What is the reason that Jesus went over to the fig tree that was by the road?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus find on the fig tree?
Questions.A: All that Jesus found on the fig tree were leaves. (19)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to the fig tree?
Questions.A: He commanded the fig tree to never have/bear fruit again. (19)

Questions.Q: What happened to the fig tree?
Questions.A: The tree immediately withered/dried up. (20)

Questions.Q: How did the disciples react, when they saw that the fig tree had withered/dried up?
Questions.A: They were amazed/surprised. (20)
Questions.Alternative: How did the disciples react, when they saw that the fig tree had withered?
How did the disciples react, when they saw that the fig tree had dried up?

Questions.Q: What did the disciples ask Jesus about the fig tree?
Questions.A: They asked him how the fig tree withered/dried up so quickly. (20)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus reply to the disciples?
Questions.A: He told them that, if they had faith [in God] and did not doubt [what he could/can do], they also could do what he had done to the fig tree.
He told them that they could also command/order that mountain to throw itself into the sea and it would happen. (21)
He told them that, if they believed [in God], they would receive whatever they asked of him in prayer. (22)

Section.heading: Matthew 21:23-27 The religious leaders asked Jesus who had given him authority to do what he was doing.

Questions.Q: What did the chief priests and the elders ask Jesus while he was teaching [the people] in the temple courts?
Questions.A: They asked Jesus what right/authority did he have to do what he was doing.
They asked Jesus who gave him the right/authority to do what he was doing. (23)
Questions.Alternative: What did the chief priests and the elders ask Jesus while he was teaching the people in the temple courts?
What did the chief priests and the elders ask Jesus while he was teaching in the temple courts?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell the chief priests and the elders that they would have to do before he would answer their question?
Questions.A: Jesus told them that, if they answered his question [correctly], he would answer their question. (24)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus ask the chief priests and the elders?
Questions.A: He asked them if John's baptism/John's authority to baptize came from heaven/God or from men. (25)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the chief priests and the elders did not want to answer that John's/say that John's baptism/authority to baptize was from heaven/God?
Questions.A: They did not want to answer that John's baptism/authority to baptize was from heaven because they knew/thought that Jesus would ask them why they had not believed him/John. (25)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that the chief priests and the elders did not want to answer that John's baptism was from heaven?
What is the reason that the chief priests and the elders did not want to answer that John's baptism was from God?
What is the reason that the chief priests and the elders did not want to answer that John's authority to baptize was from heaven?
What is the reason that the chief priests and the elders did not want to answer that John's authority to baptize was from God?
What is the reason that the chief priests and the elders did not want to say that John's baptism was from heaven?
What is the reason that the chief priests and the elders did not want to say that John's baptism was from God?
What is the reason that the chief priests and the elders did not want to say that John's authority to baptize was from heaven?
What is the reason that the chief priests and the elders did not want to say that John's authority to baptize was from God?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the chief priests and the elders did not want to answer that/say that John's baptism/authority to baptize was from men?
Questions.A: They did not want to answer/say that John's baptism/authority to baptize was from men because the people believed that John/he was a prophet. (26)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that the chief priests and the elders did not want to answer that John's baptism was from men?
What is the reason that the chief priests and the elders did not want to answer that John's authority to baptize was from men?
What is the reason that the chief priests and the elders did not want to say that John's baptism was from men?
What is the reason that the chief priests and the elders did not want to say that John's authority to baptize was from men?

Questions.Q: What did the chief priests and the elders answer Jesus?
Questions.A: They told him that they did not know [the answer to his question]. (27)

Questions.Q: Then what did Jesus say to them?
Questions.A: He told them that he would not tell them what right/authority he had to do what he was doing. (27)

Section.heading: Matthew 21:28-32 Jesus told a parable about a man and his two sons.

Questions.Q: About what parable did Jesus tell to the chief priests and the elders?
Questions.A: Jesus told a parable to the chief priests and the elders about a man and his two sons.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus ask the chief priests and the elders?
Questions.A: Jesus asked them to think about the parable he was about to tell to them. (28)

Questions.Q: What did the man say to his first son?
Questions.A: He told his first son to go and work in his vineyard. (28)

Questions.Q: What did his first son answer him/say to him?
Questions.A: His first son told him that he would not go and work in the vineyard. (29)
Questions.Alternative: What did his first son answer him?
What did his first son say to him?

Questions.Q: What did the first son do after he had told his father that he would not work in the vineyard?
Questions.A: He changed his mind and went to work in the vineyard. (29)

Questions.Q: What did the man say to his second son?
Questions.A: He told his second son to go and work in his vineyard. (30)

Questions.Q: What did the second son answer him/say to him?
Questions.A: His second son told him that he would go and work in the vineyard. (30)
Questions.Alternative: What did the second son answer him?
What did the second son say to him?

Questions.Q: What did the second son do after he had told his father that he would work in the vineyard?
Questions.A: He did not go to the vineyard and work. (30)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus ask the chief priests and the elders?
Questions.A: Jesus asked them which of the two sons did what their father told them to do. (31)

Questions.Q: What did the chief priests and the elders answer Jesus?
Questions.A: They answered him that the first son had done what his father had told him to do. (31)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell the chief priests and the elders?
Questions.A: He told them that the tax collectors and the prostitutes were entering the kingdom of God in their place/in place of them. (31)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Jesus told the chief priests and the elders that the tax collectors and the prostitutes were entering the kingdom of God instead of them?
Questions.A: Jesus said that to them because John [the Baptist] came to them to teach them the way of righteousness/how to live the way that God wants them to live.
Jesus told the chief priest and the elders that they did not believe what John taught to them, but the tax collectors and the prostitutes believed him.
Jesus told the chief priests and the elders that they refused to repent/change their minds even after they saw/knew that the tax collectors and the prostitutes believed John. (32)

Section.heading: Matthew 21:33-46 Jesus told a parable about a man who rented his vineyard to wicked tenants.

Questions.Q: About what parable did Jesus tell to the chief priests and the elders?
Questions.A: Jesus told a parable to the chief priests and the elders about a man who rented his vineyard to some farmers/renters/tenants.

Questions.Q: What did the landowner do after he rented his vineyard to some farmers/tenants?
Questions.A: He went away on a journey. (33)
Questions.Alternative: What did the landowner do after he rented his vineyard to some farmers?
What did the landowner do after he rented his vineyard to some tenants?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the landowner sent his servants to the tenants when it was time to harvest the grapes?
Questions.A: He sent his servants to the tenants to collect his [share of the] fruit from the tenants. (34)

Questions.Q: What did the tenants do to the servants?
Questions.A: The tenants beat one of the servants, they killed another one, and they stoned another servant [to death]. (35)

Questions.Q: What did the tenants do to the next group of servants that the landowner sent to them?
Questions.A: The tenants treated them the same way that they had treated the first three servants. (36)

Questions.Q: Whom did the landowner send to the tenants last?
Questions.A: He sent his son to them. (37)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the landowner sent his son to the tenants?
Questions.A: He sent his son to the tenants because he believed that the tenants would respect his son. (37)

Questions.Q: What did the tenants believe they would obtain/secure if they killed the landowner's son?
Questions.A: They believed that they would obtain/secure/acquire the son's inheritance/property/vineyard. (38)
Questions.Alternative: What did the tenants believe they would obtain if they killed the landowner's son?
What did the tenants believe they would secure if they killed the landowner's son?

Questions.Q: What did the tenants do to the landowner's son?
Questions.A: They killed him. (39)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus ask the chief priests and the elders?
Questions.A: He asked them what they thought the landowner would do to the tenants when he returned/came to his vineyard. (40)

Questions.Q: What did the chief priests and the elders answer Jesus?
Questions.A: They answered him that the landowner would kill those tenants violently/brutally/cruelly/in a painful way. (41)

Questions.Q: Then what did they say the landowner would do after he had killed those tenants?
Questions.A: They said that he would rent his vineyard to other tenants who would give him his share of the crop/grapes at harvest time. (41)

Questions.Q: About what did Jesus remind the chief priests and the elders?
Questions.A: He asked them if they had never read the passage of scripture that he quoted from Psalm 118:22-23. (42)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell the chief priests and the elders was going to happen to them?
Questions.A: Jesus told them that [God] would take away from them [the privilege of belonging to] the kingdom of God; and he will give it to people who will obey his will. // God will stop ruling you evil/disobedient/rebellious people/Jews. He will rule people who will do/obey His will. (43)

Questions.Q: About whom did the chief priests and the Pharisees know Jesus was talking in his parables?
Questions.A: They knew he was talking about them. (45)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the chief priests and the Pharisees did not arrest Jesus?
Questions.A: They did not arrest Jesus because they were afraid of the crowd/people. The people believed that Jesus was a prophet. (46)

Section.heading: Matthew 22:1-14 Jesus told a parable about a wedding feast.

Questions.Q: About what parable did Jesus tell to the chief priests and the elders?
Questions.A: Jesus told the chief priests and the elders a parable about a king who prepared a wedding banquet for his son. (2)

Questions.Q: To what did Jesus compare the kingdom of heaven?
Questions.A: Jesus compared the kingdom of heaven to a king who prepared a wedding banquet for his son. (2)

Questions.Q: How did the people, whom the king had invited to the wedding banquet, respond when the servants of the king invited/told them to come to the banquet?
Questions.A: Those people refused to come to the banquet. (3)
Questions.Alternative: How did the people, whom the king had invited to the wedding banquet, respond when the servants of the king invited them to come to the banquet?
How did the people, whom the king had invited to the wedding banquet, respond when the servants of the king told them to come to the banquet?

Questions.Q: How did the people, whom the king had invited to the wedding banquet, respond when other servants of the king invited/told them to come to the banquet?
Questions.A: One person went to his field/farm/Some people went to their fields/farms, one person went to his business/some people went to their businesses. The rest of the people beat the servants and killed them. (4-6)
Questions.Alternative: How did the people, whom the king had invited to the wedding banquet, respond when other servants of the king invited them to come to the banquet?
How did the people, whom the king had invited to the wedding banquet, respond when other servants of the king told them to come to the banquet?

Questions.Q: Then what did the king do when he heard what had happened to his servants?
Questions.A: He sent his army/soldiers and they killed those people who had killed his servants. His soldiers also burned their city. (7)

Questions.Q: Then whom did the king tell his servants to invite to the banquet?
Questions.A: The king told his servants to go out into the streets and to invite anyone they found to the banquet. (9)

Questions.Q: What did the king's servants do?
Questions.A: His servants went into the streets and invited all the people, including the bad people and the good people, they found to the banquet. They invited so many people to the banquet that the place where they were celebrating the wedding was filled with people. (10)

Questions.Q: What did the king notice that concerned him about one man at the banquet?
Questions.A: The king noticed that one man at the banquet was not wearing wedding clothes. (11)

Questions.Q: What did the king ask the man?
Questions.A: The king asked the man how he entered/was admitted to the banquet without wearing wedding clothes. (12)

Questions.Q: What did the man answer/say to the king?
Questions.A: He did not answer/say anything. (12)
Questions.Alternative: What did the man answer to the king?
What did the man say to the king?

Questions.Q: What did the king tell his servants to do to the man?
Questions.A: The king told his servants to tie the man's hands and feet and to throw him outside into the darkness. In that darkness [people are punished]. [Those people] will weep and gnash their teeth/They will cry bitterly and gnash/grit their teeth in pain. (13)

Section.heading: Matthew 22:15-22 Some Pharisees asked Jesus if they should pay taxes to Caesar/the king of Rome.

Questions.Q: What did the Pharisees make plans to do?
Questions.A: They made plans to try to tempt/lure/trick Jesus to say something wrong [so that they could criticize him]. (15)

Questions.Q: What did some of the Pharisees' disciples and the Herodians ask Jesus?
Questions.A: They asked him if it was right to pay taxes to Caesar or not. (17)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus answer them?
Questions.A: He told them to give to Caesar what belongs to Caesar and to God what belongs to God. (21)

Questions.Q: How did the Pharisees and the Herodians react to the answer that Jesus gave to them?
Questions.A: They were amazed [that he had answered their question without being trapped by them]. Then they went away from him. (22)

Section.heading: Matthew 22:23-33 Some Sadducees asked/questioned Jesus about people rising back to life after having been dead.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the basic theme of these verses?
Questions.A: Some Sadducees came to Jesus and told him about seven brothers who, one after the other, had married the same widow according to the law of Moses. They had done that because the law said that, if a man died without having any children, his brother must marry the widow and have children for him. (24-26)

Questions.Q: What did the Sadducees ask Jesus?
Questions.A: They asked him, of the seven brothers, whose wife would the woman be at the resurrection/when God raises people from the dead. (28)
Questions.Note: The Sadducees believed that God did not raise people back to life after they died.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus answer them?
Questions.A: He told them that at the resurrection people will not be marrying each other nor be given in marriage. He said that people will be like the angels in heaven. (30)

Questions.Q: How did the people react to what Jesus said to them?
Questions.A: They were amazed/impressed by what he said to them. (33)

Section.heading: Matthew 22:34-40 A Pharisee asked Jesus which of God's commandments is greatest/most important.

Questions.Q: What did one of the Pharisees ask Jesus?
Questions.A: He asked Jesus which commandment is the greatest/most important in the law. (36)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the Pharisee asked Jesus that question?
Questions.A: The Pharisee asked Jesus that question to test/trap/trick him. (35)

Questions.Q: What answer did Jesus give to the Pharisee?
Questions.A: Jesus told the Pharisee that the greatest commandment is to love the Lord your God with all your being/heart and with all your soul and with all your mind. Jesus also told him that the second greatest commandment is to love your neighbor as you love yourself. (37-39)

Section.heading: Matthew 22:41-46 Jesus asked the Pharisees who the Messiah was.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the basic theme of these verses?
Questions.A: Jesus asked the Pharisees several questions about who they thought the Messiah was.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus ask the Pharisees?
Questions.A: He asked them whose son was the Messiah. (42)

Questions.Q: What did the Pharisees answer Jesus?
Questions.A: They told Jesus that the Messiah was the son of David. (42)

Questions.Q: Then what did Jesus ask the Pharisees?
Questions.A: He asked the Pharisees why David called Messiah "Lord." (43)
He also asked the Pharisees: How could the Messiah be the son of David, since David called him "Lord"? (45)

Questions.Q: What did the Pharisees answer Jesus?
Questions.A: None of the Pharisees could answer Jesus. From that moment on none of them was brave enough to ask Jesus any more questions. (46)

Section.heading: Matthew 23:1-39 Jesus warned the Pharisees and Teachers of the Law that God will judge/condemn them because of their hypocrisy.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the basic theme of these verses?
Questions.A: Jesus warned the Pharisees and the teachers of the law about all the hypocritical deeds they were doing.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to his disciples and the crowds about obeying the teachers of the law and the Pharisees?
Questions.A: Jesus told them that they must obey what the teachers of the law and the Pharisees taught/said. Jesus also told the people that they should not do what the teachers of the law and the Pharisees did because they did not do/practice what they taught. (3)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus accuse the teachers of the law and the Pharisees of doing?
Questions.A: Jesus said that they imposed heavy obligations that were difficult to obey and they did/would not do anything to make it easier for the people to obey those laws. (4)
Jesus said that they did everything/their religious acts in public so that other people would see them. (5)
Jesus said that they loved the place of honor at banquets and the most important seats in the synagogues. (6)
Jesus said that they loved to be greeted by people in the marketplaces and to be called "Rabbi" by other people. (7)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Jesus told his disciples and the crowds that they should not let anyone call them "Rabbi"?
Questions.A: Jesus said that they should not let anyone call them "Rabbi" because they had only one Master and they were all brothers/fellow believers. (8)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Jesus told his disciples and the crowds that they should not call anyone on earth "father" [who was not their biological father]?
Questions.A: Jesus said that they should not call anyone on earth "father" [who was not their biological father] because they had one Father, who is in heaven. (9)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that Jesus told his disciples and the crowds that they should not call anyone on earth "father" who was not their biological father?
What is the reason that Jesus told his disciples and the crowds that they should not call anyone on earth "father"?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Jesus told his disciples and the crowds that they should not allow/permit anyone to call them "teacher"?
Questions.A: Jesus said that they should not allow/permit anyone to call them "teacher" because they had one Teacher who is Christ. (10)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that Jesus told his disciples and the crowds that they should not allow anyone to call them "teacher"?
What is the reason that Jesus told his disciples and the crowds that they should not permit anyone to call them "teacher"?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say they had to do to be important/great?
Questions.A: Jesus said that they had to be a servant to be great. (11)
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus say they had to do to be important?
What did Jesus say they had to do to be great?

Questions.Q: What will [God] do to the person who exalts himself?
Questions.A: [God] will humble the/that person who exalts himself/acts as though/as if he is great/important. (12)
Questions.Alternative: What will God do to the person who exalts himself?
What will happen to the person who exalts himself?
What will be done to the person who exalts himself?

Questions.Q: What will [God] do to the person who humbles himself?
Questions.A: [God] will exalt that/the person. // [God] will make that/the person great/important who humbles himself. (12)
Questions.Alternative: What will God do to the person who humbles himself?
What will happen to the person who humbles himself?
What will be done to the person who humbles himself?

Questions.Q: What were the seven warnings that Jesus gave to the teachers of the law and to the Pharisees?
Questions.A: 1. Jesus warned them that they were preventing others from entering the kingdom of heaven/God. (13)

2. Jesus warned them that they did everything that they could to persuade one person to believe like a Jew, and after he believed as they did, they made him twice as much a son/child of Hell/twice as much a worker for the devil/much more deserving of punishment in Hell/twice as evil as they were. (15)

3. Jesus warned them that they were wrong in saying that the gold in the temple was more important than the temple (itself). And that the gift a person brought was more important than the altar when they made an oath. (16-22)

4. Jesus warned them that they put too much emphasis/more importance on tithing on everything that they owned. They included very small items such as mint, dill and cumin, while they ignored the more important requirements of the law such as justice, mercy and faithfulness. (23-24)

5. Jesus warned them that they did deeds to make others/people think that they were good/righteous, but inside their hearts/thoughts they were full of extortion/force/violence and self-indulgence/self-centeredness. (25-26)
6. Jesus warned them that from/on the outside they appeared to be righteous/good to people, but on the inside/in their hearts/minds they were full of hypocrisy and wickedness. (27-28)

7. Jesus warned them that to cover up their evil and to make others/people think that they were good/righteous, they built monuments to mark the graves of/for the/God's prophets/spokesmen whom their ancestors killed long ago. They even decorated the graves/monuments of the righteous to honor them. They said that, if they had lived during the time of their ancestors, they would not have killed the prophets. But Jesus told them that, since they had tried so hard to cover up their evil intentions, they were just like their ancestors who had killed the prophets. He told them to go ahead and finish what their ancestors had started. (29-32)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell the teachers of the law and the Pharisees he was going to do?
Questions.A: Jesus told them that he was going to send prophets, wise men and teachers to them. (34)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say that the teachers of the law and the Pharisees would do to those/these prophets, wise men and teachers?
Questions.A: Jesus said that they would kill and crucify some of them. They would flog some of them and they would pursue/chase others from town to town [in order to kill them]. (34)
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus say that the teachers of the law and the Pharisees would do to those prophets, wise men and teachers?
What did Jesus say that the teachers of the law and the Pharisees would do to these prophets, wise men and teachers?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say would happen to the teachers of the law and the Pharisees because of all the righteous people whom they would kill/whom they have killed?
Questions.A: Jesus said that they would be punished for all the righteous people whom they had killed/whom they would kill. (35-36)
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus say would happen to the teachers of the law and the Pharisees because of all the righteous people whom they would kill?
What did Jesus say would happen to the teachers of the law and the Pharisees because of all the righteous people whom they have killed?

Questions.Q: What do you think an altar is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: An altar is a kind of table or platform where sacrifices of animals or other offerings are made to God. Several different kinds of altars are mentioned in the New Testament.
Questions.Note: See "altar" in KBT.

Questions.Q: When did Jesus say they would see him again?
Questions.A: He said that they would not see him again until they said, "Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord." (39)

Section.heading: Matthew 24:1-35 Jesus told his disciples about the signs that will show that he is about to return to this world.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the basic theme of these verses?
Questions.A: Jesus told his disciples what would happen at the end of the world/age and after his death when he would return to this world from heaven.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell his disciples would happen to the temple?
Questions.A: Jesus told them that all the buildings of the temple would be knocked down [by enemies of the Jews]. (1-2)

Questions.Q: What did the disciples ask Jesus?
Questions.A: They asked him when the temple would be destroyed, what would be the sign of his return to this world and what would be the clue to/indication of/sign of the end of the age/world. (3)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus answer the disciples?
Questions.A: Jesus told them to be careful that no one deceived them because many people will say, "I am the Messiah."
Jesus told them that there would be wars, famines and earthquakes which are all the beginning of birth pains/difficult times. (4-8)

Questions.Q: What will happen to the disciples?
Questions.A: Jesus told the disciples that [his enemies] would persecute and kill them. They would be hated by people of all nations because of Jesus/because they believe in Jesus. (9)

Questions.Q: What will some of the believers do at that time?
Questions.A: Some of the believers will turn away from believing in Jesus. (10)

Questions.Q: When will the end of the world come?
Questions.A: The end of the world will come when the gospel of the kingdom has been preached to the people of all nations, so that people of/in every people group will have the opportunity to believe in Jesus/it. (14)

Questions.Q: What do you think the gospel is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The word "gospel" is a translation of the Greek noun euangelion. In the New Testament the noun euangelion is used in a restricted sense. It does not mean just any kind of good news, but specifically the good news or joyful report that God has made a way of salvation for sinful human beings. In the New Testament it is used always with this one sense and is usually translated in the RSV and most modern English versions as "gospel".
Questions.Note: See "gospel" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say that people should do when they see the abomination that causes desolation/the shameful/forbidden thing that makes God's altar impure which the prophet Daniel spoke about long ago?
Questions.A: Jesus said that anyone who is in Judea should run to the mountains. (16)
Jesus said that anyone who is on his rooftop should [run to the mountains also and] not go down to take anything out of his house. (17)
Jesus said that anyone who is in the field should [run to the mountains also and] not go back to get his coat/clothes. (18)
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus say that people should do when they see the abomination that causes desolation which the prophet Daniel spoke about long ago?
What did Jesus say that people should do when they see the shameful thing that makes God's altar impure which the prophet Daniel spoke about long ago?
What did Jesus say that people should do when they see the forbidden thing that makes God's altar impure which the prophet Daniel spoke about long ago?

Questions.Q: During what time should they pray that they will not have to flee/run [to the mountains]?
Questions.A: They should pray that they will not have to flee/run in the winter/during bad weather or on the Sabbath day. (20)
Questions.Alternative: During what time should they pray that they will not have to flee to the mountains?
During what time should they pray that they will not have to run to the mountains?
During what time should they pray that they will not have to flee?
During what time should they pray that they will not have to run?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they should pray that they will not have to flee/run in the winter or on the Sabbath day?
Questions.A: They should pray that they will not have to flee/run during those times because people will suffer more than anyone else has ever suffered since the beginning of the world until now. People will never suffer that much again. (20-21)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that they should pray that they will not have to flee in the winter or on the Sabbath day?
What is the reason that they should pray that they will not have to run in the winter or on the Sabbath day?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that [God] will shorten the number of days that the tribulation/the time when people will suffer will last?
Questions.A: He will shorten the number of days that people will suffer so that he can rescue the people he chose. If he does not shorten the number of days, no one will survive the terrible tribulation/time of suffering. (22)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that God will shorten the number of days that the tribulation will last?
What is the reason that God will shorten the time when people will suffer?

Questions.Q: What should they believe if at the time of the tribulation/great suffering someone says to them: "Here is the Messiah"?
Questions.A: They should not believe it/them. (23-26)
Questions.Alternative: What should they believe if at the time of the tribulation someone says to them: "Here is the Messiah"?
What should they believe if at the time of the great suffering someone says to them: "Here is the Messiah"?
What should they believe if at the time when people suffer someone says to them: "Here is the Messiah"?

Questions.Q: What will happen after the tribulation/the time when people suffer?
Questions.A: [God] will make the sun turn dark.
The moon will not shine.
The stars will fall from the sky.
[God] shall shake the heavenly bodies. // The heavenly bodies will be shaken [by God]. (29)
Questions.Alternative: What will happen after the tribulation?
What will happen after the time of the great suffering?
What will happen after the time when people suffer?

Questions.Q: Then what will happen?
Questions.A: Jesus said the sign of the Son of Man will appear in the sky and all the people on the earth will mourn/cry out in fear.
The people on the earth will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of the sky.
The people on the earth will see the power and the great glory that the Son of Man has [from God]. (30)

Questions.Q: What will the Son of Man send his angels out to do?
Questions.A: The Son of Man will send his angels out to gather/bring together all those people from all over the earth whom he has chosen to be his people. (31)

Questions.Q: What lesson did Jesus want his disciples to learn from the fig tree?
Questions.A: He told them that they know that summer is near when the twigs of the fig tree become tender and the leaves come out. In the same way they will know that the time, when this age/world will end, is near when they see all the things happening about which he has told them. (32-33)

Questions.Q: When did Jesus say that this generation/age/world will pass away?
Questions.A: Jesus said that this generation/age/world will not pass away until all the events about which [he spoke] have happened. (34)
Questions.Alternative: When did Jesus say that this generation will pass away?
When did Jesus say that this age will pass away?
When did Jesus say that this world will pass away?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say will never pass away?
Questions.A: He said that his words will never pass away/cease to exist. (35)

Section.heading: Matthew 24:36-51 Jesus said that no one knows the time when he/Jesus will return to this world.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the basic theme of these verses?
Questions.A: Jesus told the disciples about the time when he will return to this world.

Questions.Q: Who knows when Jesus/the Son of Man will return to this world?
Questions.A: Only the Father/God knows when Jesus/the Son of Man will return to this world. (36)
Questions.Alternative: Who knows when Jesus will return to this world?
Who knows when the Son of Man will return to this world?

Questions.Q: To what period of time did Jesus compare the coming/return of the Son of Man?
Questions.A: He compared it to the days/time of Noah/time when Noah lived. (37-39)
Questions.Alternative: To what period of time did Jesus compare the coming of the Son of Man?
To what period of time did Jesus compare the return of the Son of Man?

Questions.Q: For what did Jesus tell the disciples to keep watching/be prepared?
Questions.A: Jesus told them to keep watching/be prepared for the time when he will return. (42)
Questions.Alternative: For what did Jesus tell the disciples to keep watching?
For what did Jesus tell the disciples to be prepared?

Questions.Q: To what did Jesus compare his return to the world?
Questions.A: He compared his return to the world to a thief coming to break into a house. (43)

Questions.Q: What would the owner of the house have done if he had known when the thief was coming?
Questions.A: He would have kept watch/been prepared and would not have allowed/permitted the thief to break into his house. (43)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Jesus told the disciples that they must be ready/prepared for his return?
Questions.A: Jesus told the disciples that they must be ready/prepared for his return because they did not know when he will return. (44)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that Jesus told the disciples that they must be ready for his return?
What is the reason that Jesus told the disciples that they must be prepared for his return?

Questions.Q: What does a faithful and wise servant do for his master who has put him in charge of his servants?
Questions.A: A faithful and wise servant gives the other servants their food at the proper/right time. (45)

Questions.Q: What will the master do for the faithful servant when he returns?
Questions.A: The master will entrust the faithful servant with all of his possessions/property. (47)

Questions.Q: What will the master do to his servant, whom he has put in charge of his servants, if that servant has been wicked and has beaten his fellow servants? And if he has eaten and has drunk with people who are drunkards?
Questions.A: The master will punish that servant. He will put him in a place with the other people, who only pretended to obey him. In that place [they will be punished so badly that] they will cry bitterly and gnash/grit their teeth [in pain]. (48-51)

Section.heading: Matthew 25:1-13 Jesus told a parable about ten virgins.

Questions.Q: To what did Jesus compare the kingdom of heaven?
Questions.A: Jesus compared the kingdom of heaven to ten virgins who took their lamps and went to meet the bridegroom. (1)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about the ten virgins?
Questions.A: Jesus said that five of them were wise and that five of them were foolish. (2)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Jesus said five of the virgins were foolish?
Questions.A: Jesus said that five of the virgins were foolish because they did not take any oil with their lamps. (3)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Jesus said that five of the virgins were wise?
Questions.A: Jesus said that five of the virgins were wise because they took oil in jars along with their lamps. (4)

Questions.Q: What did the foolish virgins want from the wise virgins when the bridegroom was about to arrive?
Questions.A: The foolish virgins wanted the wise virgins to give them some of their oil because the flame of each of their lamps was about to go out. (6-8)

Questions.Q: What did the wise virgins tell the foolish virgins to do?
Questions.A: The wise virgins told the foolish virgins that they would not give them any of their oil since they might not have enough oil for all of them. The wise virgins told the foolish virgins to go and buy some oil for their lamps. (9)

Questions.Q: What happened while the foolish virgins were on their way to buy oil?
Questions.A: The bridegroom arrived and the five wise virgins went in with him to the wedding banquet. Then [the servants] closed the door. (10)

Questions.Q: What did the bridegroom say to the foolish virgins when they arrived at the wedding banquet later and asked him to open the door?
Questions.A: The bridegroom told them that he did not know them [therefore/so he would not allow/permit them to come inside to the banquet]. (11-12)

Section.heading: Matthew 25:14-30 Jesus told a parable about a master who entrusted money to his three servants.

Questions.Q: To what did Jesus compare the kingdom of heaven in these verses?
Questions.A: Jesus compared the kingdom of heaven to a man who, when he went on a journey, entrusted [some of] his property/money to his servants. (14)

Questions.Q: What did the man/master entrust to each of his three servants?
Questions.A: The man gave five talents/bags of money to one servant. He gave two talents/bags of money to another servant. He gave one talent/bag of money to another servant. (15)
Questions.Alternative: What did the man entrust to each of his three servants?
What did the master entrust to each of his three servants?

Questions.Q: What did the servant do with the five talents/bags of money?
Questions.A: He immediately went and invested the money and gained/earned five more bags of money. (16)
Questions.Alternative: What did the servant do with the five talents of money?
What did the servant do with the five bags of money?

Questions.Q: What did the servant do with the two talents/bags of money?
Questions.A: He went and invested the money and gained/earned two more bags of money. (17)
Questions.Alternative: What did the servant do with the two talents of money?
What did the servant do with the two bags of money?

Questions.Q: What did the servant do with the one talent/bag of money?
Questions.A: He went and dug a hole in the ground and hid the bag of money in the hole. (18)
Questions.Alternative: What did the servant do with the one talent of money?
What did the servant do with the one bag of money?

Questions.Q: What did the master of the three servants do when he returned?
Questions.A: The master of the three servants met with each one of them to determine/find out how much they had earned with his money. (19)

Questions.Q: How did the master reward the servant who had earned five more bags of money?
Questions.A: The master rewarded him by telling him that he would promote him to a higher position/put him in charge of many matters/promote him to more important responsibilities. (20-21)

Questions.Q: How did the master reward the servant who had earned two more bags of money?
Questions.A: The master rewarded him by telling him that he would put him in charge of many matters/more important responsibilities. (22-23)

Questions.Q: What did the master do to the servant who hid the one talent/bag of money in the ground and returned it to his master?
Questions.A: The master [told other servants] to take the one talent/bag of money away from that servant and give it to the servant who had ten talents/bags of money. (28)

Then the master [told other servants] to throw that servant outside into the darkness (away from him), where [he would be punished, so that] he would cry bitterly and gnash/grit his teeth [in pain]. (30)
Questions.Alternative: What did the master do to the servant who hid the one talent of money in the ground and returned it to his master?
What did the master do to the servant who hid the one bag of money in the ground and returned it to his master?

Section.heading: Matthew 25:31-46 When Jesus comes back to this world he will judge everyone and separate those, who are righteous/good in God's sight, from those who are not righteous.

Questions.Q: What will the Son of Man do when he returns to the earth?
Questions.A: He will sit on his throne in heavenly glory. (31)
When all the nations/people are gathered [by his angels] to stand in front of him he will separate the people. He will separate them as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats. (32)
He will put/send the sheep/the righteous people on/to his right and the goats/the wicked people on/to his left. (33)

Questions.Q: What will the King/the Son of Man say to those people who are on his right?
Questions.A: He will tell them to come and receive/take their inheritance which is the kingdom. (34)
Questions.Alternative: What will the King say to those people who are on his right?
What will the Son of Man say to those people who are on his right?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the King will reward those people with the kingdom?
Questions.A: He will reward them with the kingdom because:
When he was hungry, they gave him something to eat.
When he was thirsty, they gave him something to drink.
When he was a stranger, they invited him in [to their homes]. (35)
When he needed clothes, they gave him clothes.
When he was sick, they cared for him/they took care of him/looked after him.
When he was in prison, they came and visited him. (36)

Questions.Q: What will the righteous people ask the Lord?
Questions.A: They will ask him, "When did we see you hungry and fed you? When did we see you thirsty and we gave you something to drink?" (37)
They will ask him, "When did we see you as a stranger and we invited you in [to our homes]; or saw you needing clothes, and we gave you clothes?" (38)
They will ask him, "When did we see you sick or in prison, and we went to visit you?" (39)

Questions.Q: What will the King answer them?
Questions.A: He will answer them that whenever they did any of those good deeds for the least [important] of those people who belong to him, they also were doing/did those good deeds for him. (40)

Questions.Q: What will the King say to those people who are on his left/whom he sent to his left?
Questions.A: He will tell them to leave/depart from his presence and go into the eternal fire that is prepared for the devil and his angels. (41)
Questions.Alternative: What will the King say to those people who are on his left?
What will the King say to those people whom he sent to his left?
What will the Son of Man say to those people who are on his left?
What will the Son of Man say to those people whom he sent to his left?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the King will say that to those people on his left?
Questions.A: The King will say that to those people on his left because:
When he was hungry and thirsty, they did not give him anything to eat and drink. (42)
When he was a stranger, they did not invite him in [to their homes].
When he needed clothes, they did not give him any clothes.
When he was sick and in prison, they did not care for/visit/look after him. (43)

Questions.Q: What will those people ask the King?
Questions.A: They will ask him, "When did we see you hungry or thirsty, or a stranger, or needing clothes, or sick, or in prison and we did not help you?" (44)

Questions.Q: What will the King answer them?
Questions.A: He will answer, "What you did not do for those who were the least [important] people, you did not do it for me." (45)

Section.heading: Matthew 26:1-5 The religious leaders plotted privately/secretly to kill Jesus.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the chief priests and the elders assembled in the palace of Caiaphas, the high priest?
Questions.A: They assembled there to plot how they would arrest Jesus and kill him. (3-4)

Questions.Q: What do you know about the high priest?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He was the one supreme priest, that is, the chief of all the priests, who was chosen for a special function.
