Questions.Note: See "high priest" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell his disciples was going to happen to the Son of Man?
Questions.A: He told them that in two days the Passover feast would begin. He told them that it was during that time that [someone] would hand the Son of Man over [to his enemies] to be crucified. (1-2)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the chief priests and the elders decided not to arrest Jesus during the Passover feast?
Questions.A: They decided not to arrest Jesus during the Passover feast because, if they arrested him at that time, they thought the people might riot. (5)

Section.heading: Matthew 26:6-13 A woman took perfume and poured it on Jesus.

Questions.Q: What did a woman do with an alabaster jar of expensive perfume?
Questions.A: She poured the perfume on Jesus's head while he was reclining/eating at the table. (7)

Questions.Q: Where was Jesus staying?
Questions.A: He was staying in Bethany at the house of Simon the Leper. (Simon used to be a leper.) (6)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the disciples were upset at the woman for pouring the perfume on Jesus's head?
Questions.A: They were upset because they said that the perfume could have been sold at a high price and the money could have been given to the poor people. (8-9)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to the disciples?
Questions.A: Jesus told them to stop criticizing the woman since she had done a wonderful thing to him. (10)
He told them that they would always have poor people with them, but that they would not always have him. (11)
He told them that when the woman poured the perfume on him she was preparing his body/him for burial. (12)
He told them that wherever people preach the gospel in the world they will also tell what this woman has done in memory of her. (13)

Section.heading: Matthew 26:14-16 Judas agreed with the chief priests to betray Jesus.

Questions.Q: About what plans of Judas did the author write in these verses?
Questions.A: The author wrote about the decision Judas made to betray Jesus.

Questions.Q: What did Judas ask the chief priests?
Questions.A: He asked them how much money they would give to him if he betrayed Jesus to them/turned Jesus over to them. (14-15)

Questions.Q: How much money did the chief priests give to Judas?
Questions.A: They gave him thirty silver coins. (15)

Questions.Q: What did Judas do after he had received the thirty silver coins?
Questions.A: He watched for an opportunity to hand Jesus over to the chief priests. (16)

Section.heading: Matthew 26:17-30 Jesus ate the Passover meal with his disciples.

Questions.Q: About what event did the author write in these verses?
Questions.A: The author wrote about Jesus eating the Passover meal with his disciples.

Questions.Q: What did the disciples ask Jesus?
Questions.A: They asked Jesus where they should prepare to eat the Passover meal together. (17)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell the disciples to do?
Questions.A: He told them to go into the city/Jerusalem and tell a certain man that the Teacher was going to celebrate the Passover with his disciples in his house. (18)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell his disciples while/when he was reclining/eating with them?
Questions.A: Jesus told them that one of them was going to betray him. (20-21)
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus tell his disciples while he was reclining with them?
What did Jesus tell his disciples while he was eating with them?
What did Jesus tell his disciples when he was reclining with them?
What did Jesus tell his disciples when he was eating with them?

Questions.Q: Whom did Jesus say was going to betray him?
Questions.A: He said that the disciple who dipped his hand into the bowl with him would betray him. (23)

Questions.Q: What did Judas ask Jesus?
Questions.A: Judas asked Jesus if he was the one who would betray him. (25)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus answer Judas?
Questions.A: Jesus answered Judas that he was the one who would betray him. (25)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell his disciples about the bread he had given to them?
Questions.A: Jesus told his disciples that the bread was his body. (26)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell his disciples about the cup [of wine] that he had given to them?
Questions.A: Jesus told his disciples that the cup [of wine] was his blood that would seal/establish the covenant of [God] with mankind. That would happen when his blood was poured out/shed for many people when he died so that [God] would forgive their sins. (27-28)
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus tell his disciples about the cup of wine that he had given to them?
What did Jesus tell his disciples about the cup that he had given to them?

Questions.Q: What is a covenant?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It is an agreement, a binding promise, usually made by two people who are of equal status. If the person on one side of the covenant does not do as both have agreed, there usually is a strong punishment for him or he pays compensation to the other person. Today it would be called a contract. But the Greek word that is used in the Bible for covenants strongly implies that the terms of the agreement were stated by the person on only one side of the discussion, not both sides. Usually God is the one who states/decides/says what will happen, that is, what he will do and what people must do. He binds himself to the other party.
Questions.Note: See "covenant" in KBT.

Section.heading: Matthew 26:31-35 Jesus said that Peter would tell people that he did not know him/Jesus.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell his disciples that they would do that very night?
Questions.A: Jesus told them that they would all forsake him because of what would happen to him. (31)

Questions.Q: What did Peter say to Jesus about that?
Questions.A: Peter told Jesus that he would never forsake him/deny Jesus/lose his faith in Jesus even if all the other disciples forsook him/denied him/lost their faith in him. (33)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell Peter that he would do that night?
Questions.A: Jesus told Peter that he would deny that he knew Jesus three times before a rooster crowd that night. (34)

Questions.Q: What did Peter reply to Jesus?
Questions.A: Peter replied to Jesus that he would never deny that he knew Jesus even if he had to die with him. (35)

Section.heading: Matthew 26:36-46 Jesus went to the place called Gethsemane and prayed to God/his Father.

Questions.Q: About what event did the author write in these verses?
Questions.A: The author wrote about the time when Jesus went with his disciples to pray at the place called Gethsemane.

Questions.Q: Where did Jesus and his eleven disciples go?
Questions.A: They went to a place called Gethsemane. (36)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they went to Gethsemane?
Questions.A: They went there to pray. (36)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell his disciples to do?
Questions.A: Jesus told most/eight of them to sit down. (36)
Jesus took Peter and the two sons of Zebedee [further into Gethsemane] and told them to keep watch/pray with him. (37-38)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do then?
Questions.A: He went a little further [into Gethsemane] and prayed to his Father with his face to the ground. He prayed that he would not have to go through the experience of great suffering/punishment. He also prayed that his Father would do whatever was his will. (39)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do after he had prayed for a while?
Questions.A: He returned to the three disciples and found them sleeping. (40)
He told them to stay awake and pray. (41)

Questions.Q: Then what did Jesus do?
Questions.A: Jesus went away and prayed again to his Father and said that, if it was necessary for him to go through this suffering, then his Father should do what he wanted to do with him. (42)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do after he had prayed for a while?
Questions.A: He returned to the three disciples and found them sleeping again. (43)

Questions.Q: Then what did Jesus do?
Questions.A: He went away and prayed again to his Father. (44)

Questions.Q: Then what did Jesus do?
Questions.A: He returned to the three disciples. He then told them that they needed to arise/wake up because he was about to be betrayed [by someone] into the hands of sinners/his enemies. (45-46)

Section.heading: Matthew 26:47-56 The religious leaders sent people to arrest Jesus and Judas betrayed Jesus to his enemies.

Questions.Q: About what event did the author write in these verses?
Questions.A: The author wrote about the time when Judas betrayed Jesus into the hands of his enemies.

Questions.Q: Who came with Judas?
Questions.A: A large crowd came with Judas. The chief priests and the elders of the people had sent them. // They had been sent by the chief priests and the elders of the people. They were armed with swords and clubs. (47)

Questions.Q: How did Judas inform/tell them which man was Jesus?
Questions.A: Judas had told them that the man whom he would kiss would be/was Jesus. (48)
Questions.Alternative: How did Judas inform them which man was Jesus?
How did Judas tell them which man was Jesus?

Questions.Q: What did Judas do to Jesus?
Questions.A: He went up to him and he kissed him. (49)

Questions.Q: Then what did the crowd/men do?
Questions.A: They came forward, grabbed Jesus and then they arrested him. (50)
Questions.Alternative: Then what did the crowd do?
Then what did the men do?

Questions.Q: What did one of the companions/disciples of Jesus do to the servant of the high priest?
Questions.A: His companion/disciple struck the servant with his sword cutting off his ear. (51)
Questions.Alternative: What did one of the companions of Jesus do to the servant of the high priest?
What did one of the disciples of Jesus do to the servant of the high priest?

Questions.Q: What did the disciples of Jesus do after the men arrested Jesus?
Questions.A: All of his disciples deserted him and ran away. (56)

Section.heading: Matthew 26:57-68 The Council of religious leaders tried Jesus and condemned him to die.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the basic theme of these verses?
Questions.A: The author wrote, in these verses, that the chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin tried/decided to condemn Jesus.

Questions.Q: Where did the men, who had arrested Jesus, take him?
Questions.A: They took Jesus to [the palace of] Caiaphas, the high priest. (57)

Questions.Q: Who else had come to [the palace of] Caiaphas?
Questions.A: The teachers of the law and the elders had come there also. (57)
Questions.Alternative: Who else had come to the palace of Caiaphas?
Who else had come to Caiaphas?

Questions.Q: What did Peter do?
Questions.A: Peter followed Jesus at a distance up to the courtyard of the high priest. He sat down with the guards inside the courtyard to learn/find out what would happen to Jesus. (58)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin were looking for false evidence against Jesus?
Questions.A: They were looking for false evidence against Jesus/people who would lie about what Jesus had done so that they could have him killed. (59)

Questions.Q: How much evidence could they find against Jesus?
Questions.A: They could not find any evidence from false witnesses whose testimonies/accusations/stories agreed so that they could use those stories to have Jesus killed. (60)

Questions.Q: What did the high priest ask Jesus?
Questions.A: He asked Jesus if he was the Christ, the Son of God. (63)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus answer the high priest?
Questions.A: Jesus told the high priest that what he said was true/it was true what he said. (64)

Questions.Q: How did the high priest react to what Jesus said to him?
Questions.A: The high priest tore his clothes and said that Jesus was blaspheming [God]. (65)

Questions.Q: What do you think that a person does when he blasphemes God?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He claims to be equal with God in some way.
Questions.Note: -OR-
He speaks evil against God. He insults God and defames him and his character so that others will not honor nor respect him.

Questions.Q: What did the high priest ask the chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin?
Questions.A: He asked them what they thought about Jesus saying that he was the Son of God. (66)

Questions.Q: What did the chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin answer the high priest?
Questions.A: They answered him that Jesus was [guilty of blaspheming] and so he was worthy of death/deserved to die. (66)

Questions.Q: What did some members of the Sanhedrin do to Jesus?
Questions.A: Some members of the Sanhedrin spit in his face and hit him with their fists. Other members of the Sanhedrin slapped him. They asked him [sarcastically], "Prophesy to us, Christ. Who hit you?" (67-68)

Section.heading: Matthew 26:69-75 Peter declared/said that he did not know Jesus.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the basic theme of these verses?
Questions.A: The author wrote that three times Peter had denied that he knew Jesus.

Questions.Q: What did Peter say to a servant girl when she came to him and said that he had been with Jesus?
Questions.A: Peter told the servant girl, in front of all the people there, that he had not been with Jesus. (69-70)

Questions.Q: What did Peter say to the people when another girl told the people that he had been with Jesus of Nazareth?
Questions.A: Peter told the people that he did not know Jesus. This time he denied knowing Jesus with an oath/by declaring before God that what he said was true. (71-72)

Questions.Q: What did Peter say to those people, who had been standing near him, when they said to him that he surely was one of the disciples of Jesus?
Questions.A: Peter called down/invoked curses on himself and told them that he did not know the man/Jesus. (73-74)

Questions.Q: What happened after Peter denied that he knew Jesus the third time?
Questions.A: A rooster crowed after Peter denied that he knew Jesus the third time. (74)

Questions.Q: What did Peter remember after the rooster crowed?
Questions.A: He remembered that Jesus had told him that he would disown/deny Jesus three times before the rooster crowed. (75)

Questions.Q: Then what did Peter do?
Questions.A: He went outside and wept/cried bitterly/in great sorrow. (75)

Questions.Q: What did Judas do after he threw the thirty silver coins into the temple?
Questions.A: After Judas threw the thirty silver coins into the temple he left/went out and hanged himself [to death]. (5)

Questions.Q: What did the chief priests and the elders decide to do with Jesus?
Questions.A: They decided to have Jesus put to death/have someone kill/execute him. (1)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Judas returned the thirty pieces of silver/silver coins to the chief priests and the elders?
Questions.A: Judas returned the thirty silver coins to them because he had heard that Jesus had been condemned to die by the chief priests and the elders. He grieved/regretted/felt bad about what he had done to Jesus. (3)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that Judas returned the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and the elders?
What is the reason that Judas returned the thirty silver coins to the chief priests and the elders?

Questions.Q: What did Judas say to the chief priests and the elders?
Questions.A: He told them that he had sinned by betraying innocent blood/an innocent man. (4)

Questions.Q: How concerned were the chief priests and the elders about Judas?
Questions.A: They were not concerned about him. They told him that what he had done was his business/own problem. (4)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the chief priests and the elders could not put the money back into the temple treasury?
Questions.A: They could not put the money back into the temple treasury because [Moses'] law would not allow them to put money into the treasury that was blood money/money that had been used to have someone killed. (6)

Questions.Q: What did the chief priests and the elders do with the thirty silver coins?
Questions.A: They used the thirty silver coins to buy the potter's field that would be used as a place to bury foreigners. (7)

Section.heading: Matthew 27:11-26 They/The guards/soldiers took Jesus to be questioned by Pilate.

Questions.Q: What did the governor/Pilate ask Jesus?
Questions.A: The governor asked Jesus if he was the king of the Jews. (11)
Questions.Alternative: What did the governor ask Jesus?
What did Pilate ask Jesus?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus answer the governor?
Questions.A: Jesus answered him, "Yes, it is as you say." (11)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to the chief priests and the elders when they accused him [of committing many crimes]?
Questions.A: Jesus did not say anything to them. (12)
Questions.Alternative: What did Jesus say to the chief priests and the elders when they accused him of committing many crimes?
What did Jesus say to the chief priests and the elders when they accused him?

Questions.Q: What custom/tradition did the governor practice at the Feast [of the Passover]?
Questions.A: During the Feast [of the Passover] the governor practiced the custom/tradition of releasing a prisoner whom the crowd had chosen. (15)
Questions.Alternative: What custom did the governor practice at the Feast of the Passover?
What tradition did the governor practice at the Feast of the Passover?
What custom did the governor practice at the Feast?
What tradition did the governor practice at the Feast?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the governor asked the crowd if he should release Barabbas or Jesus?
Questions.A: The governor asked the crowd if he should release Barabbas or Jesus because he knew that [the leaders of the Jews] had handed Jesus over to him because they were jealous/envious of Jesus. (17-18)

Questions.Q: What did the crowd tell the governor when he asked them if he should release Barabbas or Jesus?
Questions.A: The crowd told him to release Barabbas. (17, 21)

Questions.Q: What did the crowd tell the governor when he asked them what he should do with Jesus?
Questions.A: The crowd told him to crucify Jesus. (22)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the crowd told the governor to release Barabbas and to crucify Jesus?
Questions.A: The crowd told the governor to release Barabbas and to crucify Jesus because the chief priests and the elders had persuaded/convinced/caused them to make that decision. (20)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Pilate's wife sent him a message and told him not to have anything to do with Jesus?
Questions.A: She told Pilate not to have anything to do with Jesus because she had suffered much in a dream/a nightmare/a bad dream because of him. (19)

Questions.Q: What did Pilate finally do when the crowd insisted that Jesus be crucified and they were beginning to riot?
Questions.A: When Pilate realized that he could not change the people's minds he took water and washed his hands in front of the crowd (to show that he was not guilty). He told them that he was innocent of this man's blood/death. He told them that they were to blame for his death. (23-24)

Questions.Q: What did the people/crowd answer/tell Pilate that they were willing to accept?
Questions.A: They told Pilate that they were willing to accept, for themselves and for their descendants, the blame for having Jesus killed. (25)
Questions.Alternative: What did the people answer Pilate that they were willing to accept?
What did the people tell Pilate that they were willing to accept?
What did the crowd answer Pilate that they were willing to accept?
What did the crowd tell Pilate that they were willing to accept?

Questions.Q: Then what did Pilate do with Barabbas and Jesus?
Questions.A: Pilate released Barabbas. Pilate had his soldiers whip/scourge Jesus. Then he ordered his soldiers to crucify him. (26)

Section.heading: Matthew 27:27-31 The soldiers mocked/made fun of Jesus.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the basic theme of these verses?
Questions.A: In these verses the author wrote about what the soldiers did to Jesus before they crucified him.

Questions.Q: What did the soldiers do to Jesus?
Questions.A: They stripped his clothes off of him and put a scarlet/red robe on him. (28)
They twisted together a crown of thorns and put it on his head. (29)
They put a staff/reed/stick in his right hand and then they knelt in front of him and mocked/made fun of him. (29)
They spit on him and then they took the staff/reed/stick and hit him on the head again and again with it. (30)
After they had mocked/made fun of him they took the scarlet/red robe off of him and put his own clothes back on him. Then they led/took Jesus away to crucify him. (31)

Section.heading: Matthew 27:32-44 The Roman soldiers took Jesus and nailed him to a cross.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the basic theme of these verses?
Questions.A: The author wrote about the soldiers crucifying Jesus.

Questions.Q: What did [the soldiers] force a man named Simon to do?
Questions.A: They forced him to carry the cross of Jesus. (32)
Questions.Alternative: What did the soldiers force a man named Simon to do?
What did force a man named Simon to do?

Questions.Q: What do you know about the cross?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The Romans constructed the cross of two pieces of wood. One piece was a thick wooden post, which was placed/planted upright into a hole in the ground. The other piece was the crossbeam, which was fastened across the upright post so that it formed a + or T shape.
Questions.Note: See "cross" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did [the soldiers] offer to Jesus when they came to a place called Golgotha?
Questions.A: They offered Jesus a drink of wine mixed with gall/a bitter substance. (33-34)
Questions.Alternative: What did the soldiers offer to Jesus when they came to a place called Golgotha?
What did offer to Jesus when they came to a place called Golgotha?

Questions.Q: What did the soldiers do with Jesus's clothes after they had crucified him?
Questions.A: They divided up his clothes among them by throwing lots/dice to determine which one obtained each piece of clothing. (35)

Questions.Q: Whom did the soldiers crucify at the same time that they crucified Jesus?
Questions.A: The soldiers crucified two robbers at the same time that they crucified Jesus. (38)

Questions.Q: What did those people, who passed by Jesus, the chief priests, the teachers of the law, the elders and the robbers, who were crucified with Jesus, do to him?
Questions.A: They all insulted/mocked/made fun of him. (39-44)

Section.heading: Matthew 27:45-56 Jesus died on the cross.

Questions.Q: What happened, after Jesus gave up his spirit/died?
Questions.A: [God] tore the curtain of the temple in two from top to bottom.
The earth shook and the rocks split apart. (51)
The tombs broke open and [God] raised to life the bodies of many holy people/God's people. (52)
Questions.Alternative: What happened, after Jesus gave up his spirit?
What happened, after Jesus died?

Questions.Q: What happened on the earth/land from the sixth hour/twelve o'clock noon until the ninth hour/three o'clock?
Questions.A: The whole earth/land became dark. (45)
Questions.Alternative: What happened on the earth from the sixth hour until the ninth hour?
What happened on the earth from twelve o'clock noon until three o'clock?
What happened on the land from the sixth hour until the ninth hour?
What happened on the land from twelve o'clock noon until three o'clock?

Questions.Q: What did some of the people think when they heard Jesus cry out and say, "My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?"
Questions.A: They thought that he was calling for Elijah. (46-47)

Questions.Q: What did the people whom [God] had raised to life do after [God] had raised Jesus to life?
Questions.A: They went into the holy city/Jerusalem and appeared to many people/many people saw them. (53)
Questions.Alternative: What did the people whom God had raised to life do after God had raised Jesus to life?
What did the people who had been had raised to life do after Jesus had been raised to life?
What did the people whom God had raised to life do after Jesus' resurrection?
What did the saints whom God had raised to life do after God had raised Jesus to life?
What did the saints who had been had raised to life do after Jesus had been raised to life?
What did the saints whom God had raised to life do after Jesus' resurrection?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the centurion and the soldiers with him, who were guarding Jesus, said, "Surely he was the Son of God"?
Questions.A: They said that because they had felt the earthquake and they saw everything else that had happened. (54)

Section.heading: Matthew 27:57-61 Joseph of Arimathea took the body of Jesus and laid/buried it in a tomb/cave.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Joseph went to Pilate?
Questions.A: Joseph went to Pilate to ask for the body of Jesus. (58)

Questions.Q: What did Joseph do with the body of Jesus after Pilate had ordered [his soldiers] to give it to him?
Questions.A: Joseph took the body and wrapped it in a clean linen cloth. Then he laid it in his own new tomb that he had cut out of the rock. (58-60)
Questions.Alternative: What did Joseph do with the body of Jesus after Pilate had ordered his soldiers to give it to him?
What did Joseph do with the body of Jesus after Pilate had ordered to give it to him?

Questions.Q: Who was Joseph?
Questions.A: He was a rich man from (the town of) Arimathea.
He was a disciple of Jesus. (57)

Questions.Q: What did Joseph do after he had laid the body of Jesus in his own new tomb?
Questions.A: After Joseph had laid the body of Jesus in his own new tomb, he rolled a large/big stone in front of the entrance to the tomb. Then he went away. (60)

Questions.Q: What were Mary Magdalene and the other Mary doing?
Questions.A: They were sitting opposite/across from the tomb. (61)

Section.heading: Matthew 27:62-66 Pilate sent soldiers to guard the tomb of Jesus/the cave where Jesus had been buried.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the basic theme of these verses?
Questions.A: The author wrote about the chief priests and the Pharisees asking Pilate to make Jesus's tomb more secure.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the chief priests and the Pharisees asked Pilate to order his soldiers to secure/guard the tomb until the third day after Jesus had died?
Questions.A: They wanted Pilate to order his soldiers to guard the tomb until the third day after Jesus had died because they remembered that Jesus had said that, after three days, he would rise again to life. They thought that, if the soldiers did not guard the tomb, the disciples of Jesus would come and steal the body and then they would declare/proclaim/say that [God] had raised Jesus from the dead. (62-64)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that the chief priests and the Pharisees asked Pilate to order his soldiers to secure the tomb until the third day after Jesus had died?
What is the reason that the chief priests and the Pharisees asked Pilate to order his soldiers to guard the tomb until the third day after Jesus had died?

Questions.Q: What did Pilate tell the chief priests and the Pharisees to do?
Questions.A: Pilate told them to take some of his soldiers and make the tomb as secure as they possibly could/knew how. (65)

Questions.Q: Then what did the chief priests and the Pharisees do?
Questions.A: They went to the tomb and made it secure by putting a seal/mark on the stone; and they left the soldiers there to guard the tomb. (66)
Questions.Note: They put a seal/mark on the stone so that they would know whether/if anyone had moved it.

Section.heading: Matthew 28:1-10 God raised Jesus from death. // Jesus awakened/rose from death and lives again.

Questions.Q: Where did the angel tell the women that Jesus was?
Questions.A: The angel told the women that Jesus was not in the tomb because he had risen from the dead. (6)

Questions.Q: Where did Mary Magdalene and the other Mary go the day after the Sabbath day?
Questions.A: They went to look at the tomb [where the body of Jesus lay]. (1)

Questions.Q: What happened very suddenly?
Questions.A: Suddenly there was a violent earthquake because an angel had come down from heaven. (2)

Questions.Q: What did the angel do?
Questions.A: He went to the tomb, rolled back the stone [from the entrance] and sat on it. (2)

Questions.Q: What did the angel look like?
Questions.A: The angel was bright like lightning and his clothes were white as snow/very white. (3)

Questions.Q: How did the guards react when they saw the angel?
Questions.A: The guards were so afraid of the angel that they shook and fell to the ground and lay motionless/still like dead men. (4)

Questions.Q: What did the angel tell the women to tell to the disciples of Jesus?
Questions.A: The angel told the women to go and tell the disciples of Jesus that Jesus had risen from the dead and he was going ahead of them into Galilee. That is where they would see him. (7)

Questions.Q: What happened while the women were running to tell Jesus's disciples/the disciples of Jesus what the angel had told them?
Questions.A: While the women were running to tell the disciples of Jesus, Jesus appeared to them. (8-9)
Questions.Alternative: What happened while the women were running to tell Jesus's disciples disciples of Jesus what the angel had told them?
What happened while the women were running to tell Jesus's the disciples of Jesus what the angel had told them?

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say to the women?
Questions.A: He greeted them. Then he told them not to be afraid. He told them to go and tell his brothers/disciples to go to Galilee where they would see him. (9-10)

Section.heading: Matthew 28:11-15 The guards told the chief priests what had happened.

Questions.Q: What did some of the guards tell to the chief priests?
Questions.A: Some of the guards told the chief priests everything that had happened [at the tomb]. (11)

Questions.Q: What did the chief priests and the elders decide to do?
Questions.A: They decided to give the guards/soldiers a large amount of money. Then they told them that, [if anyone asked them what had happened at the tomb], they were to say that the disciples of Jesus came during the night and stole/took his body while they were asleep. (12-13)

Questions.Q: What did the chief priests tell the soldiers that they would do, if the governor heard [that the disciples of Jesus had come and stolen the body of Jesus, while the soldiers were sleeping]?
Questions.A: The chief priests assured/told the soldiers that they would talk to the governor and convince him that the soldiers were innocent so that they would stay out of trouble. (14)
Questions.Alternative: What did the chief priests tell the soldiers that they would do, if the governor heard that the disciples of Jesus had come and stolen the body of Jesus, while the soldiers were sleeping?
What did the chief priests tell the soldiers that they would do, if the governor heard?

Questions.Q: What did the soldiers do?
Questions.A: The soldiers took the money and did as the chief priests told them to do. (15)

Section.heading: Matthew 28:16-20 Jesus told his disciples what they must do from now on.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the basic theme of these verses?
Questions.A: Jesus told his disciples to go and make disciples from every nation/people group. (19)

Questions.Q: Where did the eleven disciples go?
Questions.A: They went to Galilee to a mountain, where Jesus had told them to go. (16)

Questions.Q: What did the disciples do, when they saw Jesus?
Questions.A: When the disciples saw Jesus they worshiped him, but some of them doubted [that it was Jesus]. (17)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus tell the disciples to do?
Questions.A: Jesus told the disciples to go everywhere and teach people from every people group to be [his] disciples/followers.
Jesus told the disciples to baptize the new disciples in the name of/authority of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit. (19)
Jesus told the disciples to teach the new disciples to obey everything that he had taught to them. (20)

Questions.Q: How long did Jesus say that he would be with the disciples?
Questions.A: Jesus told the disciples that he would be with them always, until this age/world ends. (20)

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul is writing a letter to Philemon.

Questions.Q: Who is writing this letter?
Questions.A: Paul. Timothy is not a co-author, but joined Paul in sending the greeting.

Questions.Q: Where is Paul when he is writing this letter?
Questions.A: In prison.

Questions.Q: Why is he in prison?
Questions.A: Because he had been preaching about Christ Jesus.

Questions.Q: Why do you think the authorities put Paul in prison because he preached about Christ?
Questions.A: They were opposed to what he was saying and did not want him to continue telling it to others.

Questions.Q: To whom is Paul writing?
Questions.A: To Philemon. Other believers who meet in Philemon's house are also included.

Questions.Q: What does Paul want God to do for these people?
Questions.A: He wants God to bless them and give them inner peace.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: He thanks God for Philemon.

Questions.Q: Why does Paul thank God?
Questions.A: Because of what he has heard about Philemon.

Questions.Q: What has he heard about him?
Questions.A: That Philemon loves all believers.
That Philemon believes strongly in the Lord Jesus.
(Alternate interpretation: That Philemon loves the Lord Jesus and all the believers and is faithful to them.)

Questions.Q: What does Paul pray for in this verse?
Questions.A: That the fellowship he and the believers have with one another will result in knowing more about all the privileges/blessings they have in Christ.

Questions.Q: What gives Paul much joy?
Questions.A: The love that Philemon shows to others.

Questions.Q: What was the evidence of that love?
Questions.A: The help and encouragement he has given to the believers.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: He is making a request concerning Onesimus.
Onesimus was formerly Philemon's slave.
Onesimus is very useful to Paul.

Questions.Q: There was something Paul wanted Philemon to do. Did Paul have the right to issue a command to Philemon?
Questions.A: Yes.

Questions.Q: Why did Paul have that right?
Questions.A: Because he was an apostle, and so had authority among the believers.

Questions.Q: Rather than command/order, what did Paul do?
Questions.A: He made a request in a gentle, loving manner.
Questions.Alternative: Rather than command, what did Paul do?
Rather than order, what did Paul do?

Questions.Q: Of what does he remind Philemon as he makes his request?
Questions.A: That he (Paul) is an ambassador/representative of Jesus Christ.
That he is in prison.

Questions.Q: For whom is Paul making this request?
Questions.A: For Onesimus.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say about Onesimus?
Questions.A: He regards him as his son.

Questions.Q: Where did Paul meet Onesimus?
Questions.A: In prison.

Questions.Q: What happened during the time Paul and Onesimus were together in prison?
Questions.A: Paul led Onesimus to believe in the Lord.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say here about Onesimus's former conduct?
Questions.A: He was useless as a servant/slave to Philemon.

Questions.Q: What does he say about Onesimus's present conduct?
Questions.A: He is very useful to Paul, and will also be to Philemon.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul tells Philemon that he is sending Onesimus back to him.
Onesimus is a great help to Paul.
He hopes Philemon will receive Onesimus as a fellow believer.

Questions.Q: Where is Paul going to send Onesimus?
Questions.A: Back to Philemon.

Questions.Q: How does Paul feel about Onesimus?
Questions.A: He loves him very much.

Questions.Q: Would Paul like to keep Onesimus with him?
Questions.A: Yes.

Questions.Q: Why [would Paul like to keep Onesimus with him]?
Questions.A: Onesimus was helping Paul very much while he was in prison.
Questions.Alternative: Why?
Why would Paul like to keep Onesimus with him?

Questions.Q: Why, then, is Paul sending Onesimus back to Philemon?
Questions.A: He does not want to use his authority to force Philemon to let him have Onesimus to help him; he would rather have Philemon do it on his own.

Questions.Q: Onesimus had been Philemon's slave, but had run away. Why does Paul think it was a good thing that Onesimus did that?
Questions.A: He became a believer.

Questions.Q: How does Paul hope that Philemon will receive Onesimus when he returns?
Questions.A: As a brother in the Lord.

Questions.Q: How do you think Philemon might act toward Onesimus when he returned?
Questions.A: As a master whose slave had run away, he had the right to act very harshly toward him.

Questions.Q: So what is Paul really trying to persuade Philemon to do in this letter?
Questions.A: To forgive Onesimus, and receive him as a fellow believer.
To consider Paul's need for the help Onesimus could give him.

Questions.Q: On what basis is Paul asking Philemon to receive Onesimus?
Questions.A: Philemon is to remember his relationship to Paul.
Philemon is to receive Onesimus as he would receive Paul.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul will pay Philemon whatever Onesimus stole from him.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say he will pay to Philemon?
Questions.A: Whatever Onesimus stole or owes Philemon.

Questions.Q: Paul reaffirms, emphatically, that he will repay Philemon anything he lost because of Onesimus. Do you think Paul expects to have to pay anything?
Questions.A: No.

Questions.Q: Why not?
Questions.A: Because Philemon owes Paul a great deal more than what Onesimus owes Philemon; Philemon owes Paul his spiritual life.

Questions.Q: Why is Paul confident that he can ask Philemon to receive Onesimus as a fellow believer?
Questions.A: Because of the union Philemon and Paul have in the Lord.
Because of Philemon's reputation as one who refreshes/encourages other believers (7).

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul is confident that Philemon will respond to his request.

Questions.Q: What does Paul think Philemon will do when he reads the letter Paul is writing to him?
Questions.A: He is sure that Philemon will do what he (Paul) is asking him to do, and even more.

Questions.Q: Does Paul think that he will be able to visit Philemon?
Questions.A: Yes.

Questions.Q: Why does he think so?
Questions.A: Philemon and the believers who are with him are praying that he will come. Paul is sure God will answer their prayers.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul sends greetings.

Questions.Q: To whom does Paul send greetings?
Questions.A: To Philemon and the believers with him (2).

Questions.Q: Who are included in sending the greetings?
Questions.A: Paul's companions/fellow workers.

Questions.Q: What does Paul want the Lord Jesus Christ to do for them?
Questions.A: Paul wants the Lord Jesus Christ to bless them.

Section.heading: Philippians 1:1-2 Paul sent greetings from himself and Timothy to the Philippian Christians.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what Paul wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: Paul and Timothy sent greetings to the saints/believers living in [the city of] Philippi, including the church leaders and helpers/including the bishops and deacons. (1)

Questions.Q: What do you think a saint is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A saint is someone who belongs to God/a believer in Jesus. (See "saint" in KBT in the "disciple" entry.)

Questions.Q: Who wrote this letter?
Questions.A: Paul wrote the letter. (1)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say about himself and Timothy?
Questions.A: He said that they were servants of Christ Jesus. (1)

Questions.Q: What do you think a servant does?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A servant is a person who is required to work for another person and obey him. Servants are usually paid for their work, while slaves are not paid.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the meaning of "Christ"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "Christ" in this verse is used as a name.
Questions.Note: See "Christ" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did Paul want God and Christ to do for the Philippian believers?
Questions.A: He wanted both God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ to [continue to] give them grace and peace. (2)

Questions.Q: Who do you think God is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In English, the term "God" with a capital "G" is used to refer to the one supreme Creator. The term "god" with a lower case "g", as in "a god" or "many gods", can refer to any spiritual being that people worship. The Greek word theos can be used in the same two ways. In many languages the term for God is a proper name and cannot be used to refer to anyone except the one supreme creator of the world. It cannot be pluralized.
Questions.Note: See "God" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What does it mean to you to have someone as your lord?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A lord is someone who has authority over someone. To call someone your Lord means that you have given him control over your life. The Lord, in this case, is Jesus. Every Christian strives to make Jesus his lord, by giving Him complete control. (See "Lord" in KBT in the "God" entry.)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to have/use grace in this verse?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that God would show favor towards those people.
Questions.Note: See "grace" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think it means to have grace in this verse?
What do you think it means to use grace in this verse?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to be at peace?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: To be at peace is to have a mental or spiritual condition marked by freedom of disquieting or oppressive thoughts or emotions.

Section.heading: Philippians 1:3-11 Paul prayed for the Christians in Philippi.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what Paul wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: He told the Philippian Christians that he thanked God for them. (3)
He told them that he was very happy when he prayed for them. (4)
He told them that he loved them. (7)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when someone loves someone else?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The person who loves another person seeks the good of that person. His attitude to the one whom he loves is an attitude of persistent and selfless goodwill.
Questions.Note: See "love" in KBT.

Questions.Q: How often did Paul thank God for them?
Questions.A: He thanked God for them every time he thought about them. (3)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Paul was happy every time he prayed for them?
Questions.A: He was happy every time because of how they helped him to tell people the Good News [about Jesus Christ]. (5)

Questions.Q: How long did they help Paul?
Questions.A: They helped Paul from the first day [they believed this Good News], and they continued to help him at the time he wrote this letter. (5)

Questions.Q: About what was Paul sure?
Questions.A: He was sure that God would complete the good he began to do in their hearts. (6)

Questions.Q: When will God finish this good he began to do in their hearts?
Questions.A: God will finish this good in their hearts by, or on, the day Christ Jesus [returns to the earth from heaven]. (6)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that he loved them?
Questions.A: He loved them because they were his partners in [telling the Good News], which God had given him the privilege of doing. (7)

Questions.Q: When did they help him?
Questions.A: They helped him while he was in prison, and also before, when he was not in prison. (7)

Questions.Q: When Paul was not in prison, what was he doing?
Questions.A: He was defending the work of telling people the gospel/Good News.
He was proving that the gospel/Good News [about Jesus Christ] is true. (7)

Questions.Q: What do you think the gospel is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The word "gospel" is a translation of the Greek noun euangelion. In the New Testament the noun euangelion is used in a restricted sense. It does not mean just any kind of good news, but specifically the good news, or joyful report, that God has made a way of salvation for sinful human beings. In the New Testament it is always used with this one sense and is usually translated in the RSV, and most modern English versions, as "gospel".
Questions.Note: See "gospel" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did Paul say about his feelings for them?
Questions.A: He said that he longed to be with them because he loved them as Christ Jesus does. (8)

Questions.Q: What did Paul pray for them in verse 9?
Questions.A: He prayed that they will love [one another] more and more. (9)
He prayed that they will know more of what God is really like, and will be able to tell the difference between what is right and what is wrong. (9)
Questions.Note: See comments on this verse in T.N. on Philippians.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Paul wanted them to do those things in verse 9?
Questions.A: He wanted them to do those things, so that they will be able to choose what is the good/right thing to do in every situation. (10)
He wanted them to do those things, so that they will be genuinely good as God wants them to be and not to do anything wrong from now until Christ [returns to the earth from heaven]. (10)

Questions.Q: Paul prayed that they will do righteous deeds. How would they be able to do righteous deeds?
Questions.A: They would be able to do righteous deeds with Jesus Christ helping them. (11)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to be righteous?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means to live as God desires a person to live. It means that a person does what is right in the sight of God, consistent with God's laws, and what is upright. A person is in a state of having been accepted by God as right in his eyes. (See "righteousness" in KBT in the "just, justify" entry.)

Questions.Q: What will other people do when they see them doing righteous deeds?
Questions.A: Other people will honor and praise God. (11)
Questions.Note: See comments on this verse in T.N. on Philippians.

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when you honor someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: When you honor someone you show high regard or appreciation for them.

Section.heading: Philippians 1:12-30 Paul told the Philippians that the gospel was being preached much more boldly by the Christian brothers, since he was put in prison.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what Paul wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: Paul said that, because he was in prison, most of the Christian brothers had more courage to speak the word of God [to people]. (14)

Questions.Q: What do you think Paul meant when he said "the brothers"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He meant those who were fellow-believers in Jesus. (See "brothers" in KBT in the "disciple" entry.)

Questions.Q: Where was Paul?
Questions.A: Paul was in prison. (12-13)

Questions.Q: What did Paul want the believers to know?
Questions.A: He wanted them to know that more people had heard the gospel because he was in prison. (12)

Questions.Q: What did the soldiers, who were guarding the palace, and all the other people know?
Questions.A: They knew that Paul was in prison because he served Jesus Christ/was a servant of Jesus Christ. (13)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that most of the brothers/fellow-believers were not afraid to tell the word of God to people?
Questions.A: They were not afraid to tell the word of God because [they had seen how the Lord had helped Paul] while he was in prison. (14)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that most of the brothers were not afraid to tell the word of God to people?
What is the reason that most of the fellow-believers were not afraid to tell the word of God to people?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that some people preached about Christ?
Questions.A: Some people preached about Christ because they envied Paul/were jealous of Paul and were competing against him. (15)

Questions.Q: What do you think someone is doing when they preach?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: When someone preaches, they are proclaiming the gospel to those who are listening. This also means that a person/preacher urges others to accept or abandon an idea or course of action.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that other people preached about Christ?
Questions.A: Other people preached about Christ because they wanted to do what is right/good deeds. (15)

Questions.Q: What did those people, who loved Paul, know?
Questions.A: They knew that Paul was in prison to show people that the message about Christ is true. (16)

Questions.Q: What motivated those people, who envied Paul, to preach about Christ?
Questions.A: They were motivated by selfish ambition.
They wanted more people to follow them.
They thought that they could make more trouble for him in prison. (17)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Paul said he rejoiced?
Questions.A: He rejoiced because people were preaching about Christ, no matter what their motives were. (18)

Questions.Q: What did Paul rejoice about in verse 19?
Questions.A: He rejoiced that [God will say that he had done the right thing]. (19)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Paul thought that [God will say that he had done the right thing]?
Questions.A: He thought that God will say this because they/the believers were praying for him.
He thought that God will say this because the Holy Spirit will help him. (19)
Questions.Note: See comments on this verse in T.N. on Philippians.
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that Paul thought that God will say that he had done the right thing?
What is the reason that Paul thought that?

Questions.Q: Who do you think the Holy Spirit is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He is God's spirit, through whom he acts, reveals His will, and empowers individuals. (See "Holy Spirit" in KBT in the "spirit" entry.)

Questions.Q: For what did Paul eagerly expect and hope?
Questions.A: He eagerly expected that he would not do anything that would cause [God] to make him ashamed.
He expected that he would act courageously. (20)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Paul needed to have courage?
Questions.A: He needed to have courage, so that he would honor Christ by the way he acted, no matter what happened to him. (20)

Questions.Q: If Paul continued to live, what did he expect to do?
Questions.A: He expected to live to honor Christ. (21)

Questions.Q: How did he feel about dying?
Questions.A: He felt that it would be even better for him to die than to continue living. (21)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that it would be good for him to continue to live?
Questions.A: It would be good for him to live, so that he could continue to do some useful work for Christ/help more people to know Christ. (22)
It would be good for him to live, so that he could continue to help the believers. (24)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that he said it would be better for him to die than to live?
Questions.A: He said it would be better to die because then he would go to live with Christ. (23)

Questions.Q: What did Paul think would happen?
Questions.A: He thought that he would continue to live. (25)

Questions.Q: How would it help the believers if Paul continued to live?
Questions.A: He could help them to trust God more. Because they trust him/God, they would rejoice. (25)
Questions.Note: See comments in T.N. on Philippians for this verse.

Questions.Q: How did Paul think the believers would react, when he came to see them again?
Questions.A: He said they would praise Christ Jesus very much when they saw that he had brought Paul back to them again. (26)

Questions.Q: How did Paul want them to live?
Questions.A: He wanted them to live as people should live who believe the gospel of Christ. (27)

Questions.Q: When should they live like that?
Questions.A: Paul told them to live like that no matter what happened/whether or not he was able to come and see them. (27)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Paul wanted them to live as people who believe the gospel of Christ?
Questions.A: He wanted them to live like that, so that he would hear/know that they were standing firm and united together to promote trust in Christ which people do who believe the gospel/Good News. (27)

Questions.Q: What do you think is the meaning of "the faith" in this verse?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "The faith" in this verse means the truth in which Christians believe and practice. It is a/the life of following Jesus Christ. (See "the faith" in KBT in the "believe" entry.)

Questions.Q: How did Paul say believers should react to those who oppose them?
Questions.A: He said that they should not be afraid of those people who oppose them. (28)

Questions.Q: What will happen if the believers are not afraid of those who oppose them?
Questions.A: Their opponents will realize that God will destroy them.
Their opponents will realize that God will save the believers. (28)

Questions.Q: What privileges did God give to the believers?
Questions.A: He gave them the privilege of believing in Christ.
He gave them the privilege of suffering for Christ. (29)

Questions.Q: What does someone do when he believes?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He puts his trust and commitment in another person.
Questions.Note: See "believe" in KBT.

Questions.Q: How did the believers know that Paul suffered for Christ?
Questions.A: They saw him suffer [when he was with them in Philippi].
They heard how he suffered [in prison]. (30)

Section.heading: Philippians 2:1-11 Paul encouraged the Christians to practice the same kind of attitude and humility that Christ had.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what Paul wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: Paul told the believers that they should think and act the way Christ Jesus did. (5)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the believers were encouraged?
Questions.A: They were encouraged because they were united with Christ. (1)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the believers were comforted?
Questions.A: They were comforted because Christ loved them. (1)

Questions.Q: With whom did they have fellowship?
Questions.A: They had fellowship with the Holy Spirit and with one another. (1)

Questions.Q: What was their attitude toward one another?
Questions.A: They loved one another and were kind to one another. (1)

Questions.Q: What did Paul tell the believers to do to make him completely happy?
Questions.A: He told the believers to agree with one another.
He told the believers to love one another equally.
He told the believers to be united in their hearts. (2)

Questions.Q: What else did Paul tell them to do?
Questions.A: They should never try to make themselves more important than other people.
They should never do anything just to boast about it.
They should be humble and think of others/other people as more important than themselves. (3)
They should not be concerned only with what is best for themselves. They should also think about what is good for others/other people. (4)

Questions.Q: What was Christ like [in heaven]?
Questions.A: He was the same as God. (6)
Questions.Alternative: What was Christ like in heaven?
What was Christ like?

Questions.Q: What was Christ's attitude about his place/position with God [in heaven]?
Questions.A: He did not think that he should hold on to his equal place or position with God. (6)
Questions.Alternative: What was Christ's attitude about his place with God in heaven?
What was Christ's attitude about his position with God in heaven?
What was Christ's attitude about his place with God?
What was Christ's attitude about his position with God?

Questions.Q: What did Christ do instead of holding on to his equal place with God?
Questions.A: He willingly gave up his power and the privileges that came with being equal with God.
He became the same as a servant.
He became a human being. (7)

Questions.Q: After Christ appeared as a human being, what did he do?
Questions.A: He humbled himself [even more]. (8)

Questions.Q: How did he humble himself [more]?
Questions.A: He humbled himself [more]by obeying God and by allowing people to kill him when they nailed him on a cross. (8)
Questions.Alternative: How did he humble himself more?
How did he humble himself?

Questions.Q: Because Christ was willing to allow people to kill him, what did God do for him?
Questions.A: God [caused him to live again] and gave him the highest position of honor. (9)

Questions.Q: What name did God give to Jesus?
Questions.A: He gave him the name that is above every other name/has more honor and authority than every other name/the title/rank of lordship that is greater than any other title/rank. (9)

Questions.Q: Who will bow in submission to Jesus and confess that Jesus Christ is Lord?
Questions.A: Every person in heaven will bow.
Every person on the earth will bow.
Every person in the place of the dead will bow. (10-11)

Questions.Q: When people confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, whom will they be honoring?
Questions.A: They will be honoring God the Father. (11)

Questions.Q: What do you think "God the Father" means?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that God is the father of Jesus Christ and of anyone who accepts Jesus as their Savior and Lord.
Questions.Note: See "God the Father" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think the title "God the Father" means?
What do you think the term "God the Father" means?

Section.heading: Philippians 2:12-18 Continue to work out how God wants you to live with fear and trembling by obeying God.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what Paul wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: He told them that they should continue to obey God, and that they should very seriously/reverently strive to completely do those deeds which are appropriate for people whom God has saved. (12)

Questions.Q: What do you think "salvation" means in this verse?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In this verse, "salvation" refers to the restoration of the spiritual well-being of their community. (See comments on "salvation" in T.N. on Philippians, T.H. on Philippians and Exegetical Summaries on Philippians.)

Questions.Q: How can the believers do what God wants them to do?
Questions.A: They can do what God wants them to do because God causes them to want to do it.
They can do what God wants them to do because God helps them to do it. (13)

Questions.Q: How did Paul say they should do the deeds that God wants them to do?
Questions.A: He told them that they should do those deeds/what God wants them to do without complaining or arguing about it. (14)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they should do what God wants them to do without complaining?
Questions.A: They should do what God wants them to do/good deeds without complaining, so that they will be blameless/no one can criticize them for doing wrong, and so that they will be pure/sincere. (15)

Questions.Q: What kind of deeds do people do who are not God's children?
Questions.A: They continually do wicked/sinful deeds. (15)

Questions.Q: What illustration did Paul use to describe what believers are like, as they live among the wicked people in the world?
Questions.A: He said that believers are like stars that shine in the dark sky. (15)

Questions.Q: What did Paul tell them to do?
Questions.A: He told them to faithfully tell the message that gives [eternal] life [so that others too can understand and believe]. (16)

Questions.Q: How did Paul say he would feel on the day Christ [returns to the earth from heaven], if the believers had been/were faithful to God?
Questions.A: He said that he would be proud of them. (16)
Questions.Alternative: How did Paul say he would feel on the day Christ returns to the earth from heaven, if the believers had been faithful to God?
How did Paul say he would feel on the day Christ returns to the earth, if the believers had been faithful to God?
How did Paul say he would feel on the day Christ returns, if the believers had been faithful to God?
How did Paul say he would feel on the day of Christ, if the believers had been faithful to God?
How did Paul say he would feel on the day Christ returns to the earth from heaven, if the believers were faithful to God?
How did Paul say he would feel on the day Christ returns to the earth, if the believers were faithful to God?
How did Paul say he would feel on the day of Christ, if the believers were faithful to God?
How did Paul say he would feel on the day Christ returns, if the believers were faithful to God?

Questions.Q: What will the way the believers lived show/prove?
Questions.A: The way they lived will show that all of Paul's work [among them] was not wasted/brought good results. (16)
Questions.Alternative: What will the way the believers lived show?
What will the way the believers lived prove?

Questions.Q: What illustration did Paul use here to describe his suffering?
Questions.A: He said that he was like a cup of wine that is poured over a sacrifice. (17)

Questions.Q: What is the meaning of this illustration?
Questions.A: The meaning is that Paul was willing to suffer/to die for preaching the Good News to them, in order that they might believe in Jesus Christ. (17)

Questions.Q: How did Paul feel, even though he was suffering [in prison]?
Questions.A: He was glad.
He was rejoicing with the Philippian believers. (17)
Questions.Alternative: How did Paul feel, even though he was suffering in prison?
How did Paul feel, even though he was suffering?

Questions.Q: What did Paul say the attitude of the Philippian believers should be in all this?
Questions.A: They should rejoice about what had happened and was happening to them.
They should rejoice with Paul about what was happening to him. (18)

Section.heading: Philippians 2:19-30 Paul sent Timothy and Epaphroditus to Philippi.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what Paul wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: Paul hoped to send Timothy to [visit] the Philippian believers soon. (19)
Paul wanted to send Epaphroditus to the Philippian believers first. (25)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to hope in something?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means to have a desire to see something happen or to obtain something.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Paul wanted to send Timothy to the Philippian believers?
Questions.A: Paul wanted to send Timothy to [visit] them to bring back news about them. (19)

Questions.Q: What did Paul hope he would feel when he heard that news?
Questions.A: He hoped that he would be encouraged by the news. (19)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Paul chose Timothy as the one to send to them?
Questions.A: Paul chose Timothy because he was the only one among Paul's companions there, who was genuinely concerned about the Philippian believers. (20)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say about the others who worked with him?
Questions.A: Paul said the others were concerned only about what they wanted, instead of what Jesus Christ wants. (21)

Questions.Q: What was Timothy's relationship to Paul like?
Questions.A: His relationship was like a son helping his father. (22)

Questions.Q: What else did Paul say about Timothy?
Questions.A: Paul said that Timothy proved that he was faithful by the way he helped Paul preach the gospel [about Jesus Christ]. (22)

Questions.Q: When did Paul hope to send Timothy to them?
Questions.A: He wanted to send Timothy to them as soon as Paul knew what would happen to himself. (23)

Questions.Q: What did Paul think/believe was going to happen to him/himself?
Questions.A: He thought/believed that he [would be released from prison] and would come to see them. (24)
Questions.Alternative: What did Paul think was going to happen to him?
What did Paul think was going to happen to himself?
What did Paul believe was going to happen to him?
What did Paul believe was going to happen to himself?

Questions.Q: What did Paul say about Epaphroditus?
Questions.A: Paul said that Epaphroditus was his companion/fellow-worker [in telling the Good News].
Paul said that Epaphroditus was his fellow-soldier [in defending the Good News against those who opposed it].
He said that the Philippians had sent Epaphroditus to help Paul. (25)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Paul wanted to send Epaphroditus back to the Philippians?
Questions.A: Paul wanted to send him back to the Philippians because Epaphroditus was very concerned about them.
Paul also wanted to send him back to the Philippians because Epaphroditus was upset, since [he knew] that they had heard he was sick [and he knew that they were worrying about him]. (26)

Questions.Q: How sick had Epaphroditus been?
Questions.A: He had been so sick that he almost died. (27)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that he did not die?
Questions.A: He did not die because God was merciful to him [and healed him]. (27)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when someone shows mercy to someone else?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "Mercy" in the New Testament is an act of kindness by God or someone else toward people who are in need. The person (God or man) acts to relieve some kind of suffering or distress.
Questions.Note: See "mercy" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that God was merciful to Paul?
Questions.A: God was merciful to him, so that Paul would not have another reason to be sad in addition to the reason he already had to be sad. (27)
Questions.Note: T.N. on Philippians states that some commentators think that the first sorrow refers to Paul being sad because Epaphroditus was sick. Others think Paul was sad because he was in prison. They agree that the second sorrow would have been Paul's added sorrow if Epaphroditus had died.

Questions.Q: How did Paul say he would feel if Epaphroditus went back to the Philippians?
Questions.A: He said that he would feel relieved because then the Philippians would no longer worry about Epaphroditus. (28)

Questions.Q: How did Paul tell them to welcome Epaphroditus?
Questions.A: He told them that they should welcome/receive him [back] joyfully as a brother in the Lord/those who belong to the Lord should receive a Christian worker. (29)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they should honor Epaphroditus?
Questions.A: They should honor him because he almost died doing the work of Christ, and even risked his life to help Paul. (30)

Section.heading: Philippians 3:1-11 God has put us right with himself because we trusted him.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what Paul wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: Paul told the believers to rejoice because they belonged to/were in union with the Lord. (1)
He warned them about those people who believed that all [males] must be circumcised to become [Christians/believers]. (2)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to circumcise someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that someone removes the foreskin of the male genital.

Questions.Q: About what people did Paul warn them?
Questions.A: He warned them about those people, who do evil deeds. (2)

Questions.Q: What do you think was the danger in obeying what those people told them to do?
Questions.A: It would mean that they believed that circumcision would save them, rather than what Jesus Christ did for them. (3)

Questions.Q: How do believers show that they belong to God?
Questions.A: They worship God as the Holy Spirit helps them.
They rejoice because of what Christ Jesus [did to save them].
They do not rely on what they do to save themselves. (3)

Questions.Q: What reasons did Paul give to show that he could rely on/put confidence in what he had done and what he was?
Questions.A: He was circumcised when he was seven days/a week old.
He belonged to the tribe of Benjamin which was one of the tribes of the people of Israel.
He was a Hebrew and his ancestors were all Hebrews.
He carefully obeyed the laws as strictly as the Pharisees did. (4-5)
He persecuted the believers [because he felt strongly that God wanted him to do that]. (6)
He was as righteous as any person could become by obeying the laws because he obeyed them all. (6)
Questions.Alternative: What reasons did Paul give to show that he could rely on what he had done and what he was?
What reasons did Paul give to show that he could put confidence in what he had done and what he was?

Questions.Q: What do you know about the name "Israel"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In the New Testament, the terms "Israel" and "Israelite" are used by Jews to refer to themselves, and also by God to refer to them as his people.
Questions.Note: See "Israel" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think Paul meant when he said that he was a Hebrew?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In this reference, "Hebrew" is used when the Jewish character (Jewishness) of a person is particularly in focus. (See "Hebrew" in KBT in the "Israel" entry.)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to obey the law?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It is usually used to refer to those who are trying to become acceptable to God by doing what the laws, given through Moses, command.
Questions.Note: See "law" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you know about the Pharisees?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The Pharisees were the largest and most important of the Jewish religious groups. They controlled the synagogues and exercised great control over the general population. They taught that the way to God was through obeying the law. They opposed Jesus because He refused to accept the teachings of their oral law.
Questions.Note: See "Pharisee" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did Paul think about those things which were important to him/he depended on [for God to consider him to be good]?
Questions.A: He said that those things were no longer important to him. (7)
Questions.Alternative: What did Paul think about those things which were important to him?
What did Paul think about those things which he depended on?
What did Paul think about those things which were important to him for God to consider him to be good?
What did Paul think about those things which he depended on for God to consider him to be good?

Questions.Q: What did Paul say was important to him now?
Questions.A: He said that the only thing that was important to him was what Christ has done [for him]/his relationship with Christ. (7)

Questions.Q: What did Paul feel now about all the things he did [to please God]?
Questions.A: He said that those things were all worthless, that they were like garbage. (8)
Questions.Alternative: What did Paul feel now about all the things he did to please God?
What did Paul feel now about all the things he did?

Questions.Q: What was really important to him?
Questions.A: The thing that was really important to him was knowing Christ Jesus as his Lord. (8)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Paul said/considered that all that [he did before to please God] as worthless/like garbage?
Questions.A: He considered those deeds to be worthless so that he might belong to Christ. (8)
He considered those deeds to be worthless so that he might be completely united with Christ. (9)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that Paul said that all that as worthless?
What is the reason that Paul said that all that like garbage?
What is the reason that Paul said that all that he did before to please God as worthless?
What is the reason that Paul said that all that he did before to please God like garbage?
What is the reason that Paul considered that all that as worthless?
What is the reason that Paul considered that all that like garbage?
What is the reason that Paul considered that all that he did before to please God as worthless?
What is the reason that Paul considered that all that he did before to please God like garbage?

Questions.Q: How did [God] consider Paul, after Paul had done all that the [Jewish] laws required him to do?
Questions.A: [God] did not consider Paul to be good/righteous as a result of obeying all the [Jewish] laws. (9)
Questions.Alternative: How did God consider Paul, after Paul had done all that the Jewish laws required him to do?
How did God consider Paul, after Paul had done all that the Law required him to do?
What was the source of Paul's righteousness?
What was the basis of Paul's righteousness?
How did Paul think God would evaluate him?
How did Paul think God would evaluate him after Paul had done all that the Law required him to do?

Questions.Q: What was the reason that [God] considered Paul to be good/righteous?
Questions.A: [God] considered Paul good/righteous only because Paul believed in Christ. (9)
Questions.Alternative: What was the reason that God considered Paul to be good?
What was the reason that God considered Paul to be righteous?
What was the reason that considered Paul to be good?
What was the reason that considered Paul to be righteous?

Questions.Q: What did Paul say he wanted?
Questions.A: He wanted to know Christ.
He wanted to experience the power that God gave Christ/Christ received from God when he became alive again after he had died.
He wanted to suffer and even to die for Christ. (10)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Paul wanted the experiences he mentioned in verse 10?
Questions.A: He wanted those experiences, so that when he died, [God] would raise him to life again/cause him to live again. (11)

Section.heading: Philippians 3:12-4:1 Paul wrote to the Christians about continuing to serve the Lord and, as a result, reaching the goal of eternal life in heaven.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what Paul wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: Paul said that he was earnestly striving to know Christ perfectly. (12)
Paul told the believers that they should live the way he was living. (17)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say had not happened yet in his life?
Questions.A: He said that he did not [know Christ completely].
He said that [God] had not finished making him like he wanted him to be. (12)

Questions.Q: What had Paul tried very hard to do?
Questions.A: He had tried very hard to become like Christ. (12)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say he was going to do?
Questions.A: He said that he was going to stop thinking about the past and concentrate on the future. (13)

Questions.Q: To what did Paul compare his efforts?
Questions.A: He compared his efforts to an athlete who is striving to win a prize. (14)

Questions.Q: What prize was Paul trying to win?
Questions.A: He was trying hard to win that great prize, which was God calling him to heaven [because he trusted] in Christ Jesus. (14)

Questions.Q: To whom was Paul speaking in verse 15?
Questions.A: He was speaking to himself and to those Philippian believers who were [spiritually] mature/believers whose faith was strong. (15)

Questions.Q: What did he tell them?
Questions.A: He told them that they should all have the same attitude/agree with him about the things he had talked about in verses 12-14. (15)

Questions.Q: What did he say to those who did not agree with him in this?
Questions.A: He told them that God would reveal to them how they should think/God would cause them to understand clearly how they should think. (15)

Questions.Q: Whether they agree with him or not, what did Paul say they should all do?
Questions.A: He told them that they should live according to [the Good News] that they already understood/knew. (16)

Questions.Q: To whom did Paul speak in verse 17?
Questions.A: He was speaking to his brothers/fellow-believers. (17)

Questions.Q: What did Paul tell them to do in order to live good lives?
Questions.A: He told them that they should imitate his own conduct/way of thinking and acting and that of others/other Christians like him. (17)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the believers should act/behave the way that Paul did?
Questions.A: Paul said that they should behave as he did because there are many people who act/behave in a way that shows that they are against what Christ died for on the cross. (18)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that the believers should act the way that Paul did?
What is the reason that the believers should behave the way that Paul did?

Questions.Q: What do you know about the cross?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The cross was constructed of two pieces of wood. One piece was a thick wooden post, which was placed/planted upright into a hole in the ground. The other piece was the crossbeam, which was fastened across the upright post so that it formed a + or T shape.
Questions.Note: See "cross" in KBT.

Questions.Q: How many times had Paul told the believers about such people?
Questions.A: He had told them many times before. (18)

Questions.Q: How did Paul feel about having to say what he did about those people?
Questions.A: He felt very sad to the point of crying. (18)

Questions.Q: How does Paul describe those people?
Questions.A: They do whatever their bodies want.
They are proud of the bad things they do.
They think only about things on earth. (19)

Questions.Q: What will happen to those people?
Questions.A: God will destroy them. (19)

Questions.Q: How are believers different from those people whom he described in verses 18-19?
Questions.A: All believers are citizens of heaven. // All believers' real home is in heaven.
All believers are eagerly waiting for the Lord Jesus Christ to come from heaven. (20)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to be citizens of heaven?
Questions.A: All believers consider heaven to be their true homeland/native country.

Questions.Q: Where do you think heaven is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It is that part of God's creation above the earth and the waters, including "air" and "space," and serves as home for God and the spirits who serve Him.
Questions.Note: See "heaven" in KBT.

Questions.Q: When the Lord Jesus returns, what will he do for all believers?
Questions.A: He will change their physical bodies and make them like his own. (21)

Questions.Q: How will the Lord change their bodies?
Questions.A: He will use the great power that he has to change their bodies. (21)

Questions.Q: How did Paul say the believers can continue trusting and obeying the Lord?
Questions.A: He said they can do that by following the instructions he had given them in this letter. (1)

Questions.Q: How did Paul feel about the Philippian believers?
Questions.A: He loved them very much. (1)

Section.heading: Philippians 4:2-9 Paul encouraged the Christians to be joyful in the Lord, not to worry about anything and to think on things that are good.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what Paul wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: He told the believers that they should rejoice continually because of what the Lord [has done for them]. (4)
He told the believers that they should pray about difficult situations rather than worry about them. (6)
He told them that they should think about things that are good. (8)

Questions.Q: What did Paul want the two women, Euodia and Syntyche, to do?
Questions.A: He wanted them to agree with each other. // He wanted them to settle their disagreements. (2)

Questions.Q: What did he ask his faithful companion to do?
Questions.A: He asked him to help those two women [to agree with each other]. (3)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say about those two women?
Questions.A: He said that they had worked hard to help him tell people the Good News about Jesus Christ. (3)

Questions.Q: Where did Paul say [God] had written the names of all those fellow-workers?
Questions.A: He said [God had written] their names in his book which lists who will live [forever]. (3)
Questions.Alternative: Where did Paul say God had written the names of all those fellow-workers?
Where did Paul say the names of all those fellow-workers had been written?
