Where did Paul say the names of all those fellow-workers were written?
Where did Paul say God had written the names of all his fellow-workers?
Where did Paul say the names of all his fellow-workers had been written?
Where did Paul say the names of all his fellow-workers were written?

Questions.Q: What did Paul tell the believers to do?
Questions.A: He told them that they should be kind to others. (5)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they should act that way?
Questions.A: They should act that way because the Lord will return soon. (5)

Questions.Q: What else did he tell them to do?
Questions.A: He told them that they should not worry about anything. (6)

Questions.Q: What should they do when they have problems?
Questions.A: They should pray to God about the problems and ask him to help them. (6)

Questions.Q: What else should they do when they pray?
Questions.A: They should thank God for his help. (6)

Questions.Q: What will God do when they pray to him?
Questions.A: He will give them peace in their hearts. // He will give them peace in how they feel and think. (7)

Questions.Q: How did Paul describe this peace that God gives?
Questions.A: He said that people cannot understand this peace. (7)

Questions.Q: About what things did Paul tell them to think?
Questions.A: He told them to think about things that are true/that which is true,
things that people respect/what people respect,
things that [God] considers right/that which [God] considers to be right,
things that are not sin/that which is not sinful,
lovely/things that are easy for people to love/that which is lovely and easy for people to love,
and admirable/things that have a good name or reputation./that which is admirable and has a good name. (8)

Questions.Q: What did Paul tell them to think about that which is very good and about that which people say good/speak well?
Questions.A: He said that they should think about/concentrate on what is good. (8)
Questions.Alternative: What did Paul tell them to think about?
How did Paul tell them to think about that which is very good and about that which people say good?
How did Paul tell them to think about that which is very good and about that which people speak well?
On what did Paul tell them to concentrate?

Questions.Q: What did he say that they should continue to do?
Questions.A: He said that they should continue to do what they had learned from him. (9)

Questions.Q: What will happen, if they do what Paul taught them?
Questions.A: God will fellowship with them and give them peace. (9)

Section.heading: Philippians 4:10-20 Paul thanked the Philippian Christians for the financial gifts they gave to him.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what Paul wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: Paul thanked the Philippian believers for sending gifts to him. That made him very happy. (10)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Paul said he rejoiced?
Questions.A: He rejoiced because the Philippian believers had [sent a gift] to him, which showed that they were concerned about him. (10)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that it had been a long time, since they had [sent a gift] to Paul?
Questions.A: It had been a long time because they had not had an opportunity to [send a gift] to him. (10)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that it had been a long time, since they had sent a gift to Paul?
What is the reason that it had been a long time, since they had to Paul?

Questions.Q: What did Paul tell them that he had learned?
Questions.A: He told them that he had learned to be content with what he had. (11)
He knew how to be content when he did not have what he needed.
He knew how to be content when he had more than he needed.
He knew how to be content whether or not he had enough food. (12)

Questions.Q: How was he able to be content in every situation?
Questions.A: [Christ] gave him the strength to be content in every situation. (13)

Questions.Q: What had the Philippian believers done for Paul?
Questions.A: They had sent gifts to him to help him in his work. (15)

Questions.Q: How long had they been helping him by sending gifts to him?
Questions.A: They had been helping him ever since they first heard the Good News [about Jesus Christ that he preached] when he left Macedonia [a province]. (15)

Questions.Q: What other churches sent gifts to help Paul?
Questions.A: No other churches helped him. (15)

Questions.Q: How did the Philippian believers help Paul when he was in [the town of] Thessalonica?
Questions.A: They sent gifts to him two times. (16)
Questions.Alternative: How did the Philippian believers help Paul when he was in the town of Thessalonica?
How did the Philippian believers help Paul when he was in Thessalonica?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Paul was so happy about their gifts?
Questions.A: He was happy about their gifts because [God would bless them] for giving those gifts. (17)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say about the gifts they sent to him?
Questions.A: He said that he received everything they sent.
He said that he had all he needed. (18)

Questions.Q: Who brought the gifts to him?
Questions.A: Epaphroditus brought the gifts to him. (18)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say those gifts were like?
Questions.A: He said those gifts were like a fragrant/sweet smelling offering to God. God accepted those gifts, and he was pleased with them. (18)

Questions.Q: Who will provide what the Philippians need?
Questions.A: God will provide all that they need out of his unlimited riches because of [what] Christ Jesus [has done]. (19)

Questions.Q: What did Paul say that they should always do?
Questions.A: He said that they should always glorify/honor/praise God the Father. (20)

Section.heading: Philippians 4:21-23 Paul sent his final greetings to the Philippian Christians/believers.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what Paul wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: Paul and his companions/the believers, who worked with him, sent greetings to the believers in [the city of]Philippi. (20-21)

Questions.Q: Who else sent greetings to the believers?
Questions.A: The believers who were servants of Emperor Caesar also sent greetings to them. (22)

Questions.Q: What did Paul want the Lord Jesus Christ to do for the Philippian believers?
Questions.A: He wanted the Lord Jesus Christ to continue to be kind and loving to them. (23)

Section.heading: Revelation 1:1-3 This book is about the things that will happen soon that Jesus Christ showed to John.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that God revealed the events of this book to Jesus?
Questions.A: He revealed these events to Jesus to show his servants/all Christians what will happen very soon. (1)

Questions.Q: What do you think a servant does?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A servant is a person who serves the needs or purposes of another person or deity. A servant is a person who is required to work for another and obey him. Servants are usually paid for their work, while slaves are not paid.
Questions.Note: See "servant" in KBT.

Questions.Q: How did God make this news known about future events?
Questions.A: He made it known to Jesus Christ, who sent an angel to John. (1)

Questions.Q: Who do you think God is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In English, the term "God" with a capital "G" is used to refer to the one supreme Creator. The term "god" with a small "g", as in "a god" or "many gods", can refer to any spiritual being that people worship. The Greek word theos can be used in the same two ways.
Questions.Note: In many languages the term for God is a proper name and cannot be used to refer to anyone except the one supreme creator of the world. It cannot be pluralized. (Or, if it can be pluralized, the meaning may be something very different from the English "gods". In one language, the plural form of God, meant "God and those who follow him" and was an appropriate way to translate "saints".) (See "God" in KBT.)

Questions.Q: What do you think is the meaning of "Christ"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "Christ" is the English rendering of the Greek word Christos, which means "anointed one."
Questions.Note: See "Christ" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you know about angels?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Angels are spiritual messengers who either deliver a message to humans, carry out God's will, praise God, or guard God's throne.
Questions.Note: See "angel" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Who is the one who testified about everything that he saw?
Questions.A: John was the one. (2)
Questions.Note: UBS suggests that everything that John saw has to do with the message from God and with the truth proclaimed by Jesus Christ.

Questions.Q: When anyone reads the words of this prophecy and pays attention to what it says, what benefit will he receive?
Questions.A: Anyone who reads this book and pays attention to what it says will be helped [by God]. (3)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to bless someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that God will look well on him, will help him. It means to make someone happy, to give good fortune or satisfaction, to confer prosperity upon someone.
Questions.Note: See "bless" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think a prophecy is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In this verse it refers to future events. A prophecy is a message from God given through the mouth of a prophet, an inspired message. (See "prophecy" in KBT in the "prophet" entry.)

Section.heading: Revelation 1:4-8 John sent his greetings to the seven churches in Asia.

Questions.Q: Who wrote this letter?
Questions.A: John wrote the letter. (4)

Questions.Q: To whom did he write the letter?
Questions.A: He wrote the letter to the seven churches in Asia (a Roman province). (4)

Questions.Q: What do you think the church is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It is a group of Christians who live in one place.
Questions.Note: See "church" in KBT.

Questions.Q: To whom was John referring when he said that he is, and he was, and he is to come?
Questions.A: He was talking about God. (4)
Questions.Note: The answer is implied in this verse.

Questions.Q: What did John desire for them?
Questions.A: He wanted them to know that God has compassion for them, and that God wants them to be at peace with him. (4)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to show grace toward another person?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that a person shows that he accepts and loves another person, even when he or she does not deserve it.
Questions.Note: See "grace" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to be at peace?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: To be at peace is to have a mental or spiritual condition marked by freedom of disquieting or oppressive thoughts or emotions.
Questions.Note: See "peace" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Who was before [God's] throne?
Questions.A: The Holy Spirit was/seven spirits were before his throne. (4)
Questions.Alternative: Who was before God's throne?
Who was before throne?

Questions.Q: What do you think he meant by "spirit" in this verse?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The seven spirits are generally understood as a way of talking about the Holy Spirit. The imagery seems to be derived from Zechariah 4. Some commentators think they refer to the seven chief angels or archangels, who are known also from Jewish tradition. But the fact that the seven spirits are grouped with the eternal God and Jesus Christ suggests that the Holy Spirit is meant, not angelic beings. He is God's spirit, through whom he acts, reveals His will, and empowers individuals.
Questions.Note: See "spirit" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What things did John say about Jesus Christ?
Questions.A: He said he is the one who faithfully proclaimed God's message.
He was the first to rise from the dead [to live forever].
He is the ruler of the kings of the earth. (5)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when someone is faithful?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that he is worthy of being believed/trusted by someone else. He is trustworthy, reliable. (See "faithful" in KBT in the "believe" entry.)

Questions.Q: What has Jesus Christ done for us/all Christians?
Questions.A: He loves us
and he has freed us from our sins by shedding his blood/by his death. (5)
Questions.Alternative: What has Jesus Christ done for us?
What has Jesus Christ done for all Christians?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when someone loves someone else?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The person who loves another person seeks the good of that person. His attitude to the one whom he loves is an attitude of persistent and selfless goodwill.
Questions.Note: See "love" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What does a person do when he sins?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He disobeys God. He deliberately keeps on doing those things that please himself and displease God.
Questions.Note: See "sin" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What has Jesus Christ caused us to be?
Questions.A: He has caused us to be a kingdom of priests to serve his God and Father. (6)

Questions.Q: What do you think he meant by "kingdom" in this verse?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In the book of Revelation, the word "kingdom" is sometimes used to refer to the group of people whom God rules, those who recognize God as their king.
Questions.Note: See "kingdom" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think a priest does?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The particular part of meaning in focus in this verse seems to be the idea of entering into God's presence, becoming his servants and offering "spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ". Another intermediary apart from Jesus Christ is not needed; the believer can enter into God's presence directly through him.
Questions.Note: See "priest" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What should all believers do because of all that Jesus has done for them?
Questions.A: They should praise him and acknowledge his power forever and ever. (6)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when you give glory to someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: When you give glory to someone you reveal their greatness/the greatness of someone, you demonstrate or show openly that they are worthy of receiving honor.
Questions.Note: See "glory" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Who is coming with the clouds?
Questions.A: Jesus Christ is coming with the clouds. (7)

Questions.Q: Who will see him when he comes?
Questions.A: Everyone will see him. (7)

Questions.Q: How will all the people feel when Jesus Christ comes again?
Questions.A: Everyone will mourn when they see him. (7)

Questions.Q: What did God say about himself?
Questions.A: He said he is the one who began all things, and the one who will complete all things.
He always existed and will always exist.
He is all-powerful. (8)

Section.heading: Revelation 1:9-20 Christ appeared to John, and told him to write down what he saw and to send it to the seven churches.

Questions.Q: What did the voice that John heard tell him to do?
Questions.A: The voice told him to write on a scroll/book everything he saw and to send it to the churches located in seven cities. (11)

Questions.Q: What did John say about himself?
Questions.A: He said that he was their brother and companion. (9)

Questions.Q: What do you think John meant when he said their "brother"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In this reference "brother" means fellow believer or fellow Christian.
Questions.Note: See "brother" in KBT in the "disciple" entry.

Questions.Q: What did John say he was sharing with them?
Questions.A: He said he was sharing the same difficulties they were experiencing.
He was part of the people [of Christ].
He was patiently enduring his sufferings/troubles. (9)

Questions.Q: What was the reason that John was on the island of Patmos?
Questions.A: He had been sent there as a punishment for preaching the word/message of God about Jesus Christ. (9)

Questions.Q: What day of the week was it?
Questions.A: It was on the Lord's day/Sunday. (10)

Questions.Q: What did he experience on the Lord's day?
Questions.A: He was completely controlled by the Holy Spirit. (10)
Questions.Note: UBS states that this expression means to have an abnormal experience in which supernatural events happen. The spirit is God's spirit. Also see 4:2, 17:3, and 21:10.

Questions.Q: What did John hear on this day?
Questions.A: He heard a voice that sounded like a trumpet. (10)

Questions.Q: Which cities were the ones to which he was to send letters?
Questions.A: The cities were Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia, and Laodicea. (11)

Questions.Q: What did John see when he turned around to see who was speaking to him?
Questions.A: He saw seven golden lampstands. (12)

Questions.Q: What did he see among the lampstands?
Questions.A: He saw someone "like a son of man." // He saw Jesus, the one who became a man. (13)

Questions.Q: Who do you think the Son of Man is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It is Jesus. "Son of Man" is the title Christ used of Himself.
Questions.Note: See "son of man" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Describe how this person was dressed.
Questions.A: He wore a long robe that reached down to his feet
and he had a golden sash around his chest. (13)

Questions.Q: Describe what this person looked like.
Questions.A: His head and hair were very white.
His eyes were like a blazing fire. (14)
His feet glowed like brass glows.
His voice was like the sound of rushing waters. (15)
He held seven stars in his right hand.
A sharp double-edged sword came out of his mouth.
His face shone like the sun. (16)

Questions.Q: What did John do when he saw that person?
Questions.A: He fell at his feet as though he were a dead man. (17)

Questions.Q: What did that person do to comfort/reassure/calm John?
Questions.A: He put his right hand on him and told him not to be afraid. (17)
He told John that he is the first and the last, that is, that he is eternal. (17)
Questions.Alternative: What did that person do to comfort John?
What did that person do to reassure John?
What did that person do to calm John?

Questions.Q: What did that person tell John about himself?
Questions.A: He is living,
he had been dead
and now was alive forever and ever.
He had the keys of death and Hades, that is, he had the authority over the final destiny of people when they die. (18)

Questions.Q: What do you think Hades is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Hades is the temporary resting place until the final judgment for all dead people. (See "Hades" in KBT in the "Hell" entry.)

Questions.Q: What did that person tell John to do?
Questions.A: He told John to write about what he had seen and about the things that were going to happen. (19)

Questions.Q: What did that person tell John that the seven stars and the seven lampstands represented?
Questions.A: He said the stars represented the angels of the seven churches,
and the lampstands represented the seven churches. (20)

Section.heading: Revelation 2:1-7 The letter that John wrote and sent to the church at Ephesus.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what John wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: John wrote a letter to the angel of the church in Ephesus. (1)
He wrote about the good things and bad things that the Christians were doing. (2-4)

Questions.Q: Whose words did that person tell John to write in the letter?
Questions.A: He told John to write the words of the one who holds the seven stars in his right hand and walks among the seven golden lampstands. (1)

Questions.Q: What were the good things that the people in the church at Ephesus did?
Questions.A: They worked hard.
They endured persecutions with patience.
They did not tolerate evil people.
They tested those who said they were apostles but they were false. (2)
They endured hardships because they belonged to /Jesus.
They did not grow weary. (3)

Questions.Q: What do you think a false apostle does?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: False apostles were those who falsely claimed to be commissioned by Jesus Christ; they said that they spoke on behalf of Jesus Christ, but in fact they taught lies and led people astray. The apostles were responsible for guarding the truth of the gospel; false apostles introduce lies and deceptions. (See "false apostle" in KBT in the "apostle" entry.)

Questions.Q: What were the bad things the people there did?
Questions.A: They were not loving Christ and other Christians as they did when they first became Christians. (4)

Questions.Q: What did he tell them to do?
Questions.A: He told them to repent and do the things they did at first. (5)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when someone repents?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The verb "to repent" (Greek metanoeô) and the noun "repentance" (metanoia) refer to the act of deliberately turning away from sin, expressing sorrow for past sins, and determining not to sin any more.
Questions.Note: See "repent" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did he say would happen to them, if they did not repent?
Questions.A: He said he would come and remove their lampstand from its place, that is, they would cease to exist as a church. (5)

Questions.Q: What did they have in their favor?
Questions.A: He said that the fact that they hated the practices of the Nicolaitans, which he also hated. (6)

Questions.Q: What did he tell them to do?
Questions.A: He said that since they had ears they should listen to what the [Holy] Spirit was saying to them. (7)

Questions.Q: What will people be allowed [by Jesus] to do who overcome [the forces of evil]?
Questions.A: They will be allowed [by Jesus] to eat the fruit of the tree of life that grows in paradise/the garden of God. (7)
Questions.Alternative: What will people be allowed by Jesus to do who overcome the forces of evil?
What will people be allowed by Jesus to do who overcome?
What will people be allowed to do who overcome the forces of evil?
What will people be allowed to do who overcome?

Questions.Q: Where do you think paradise is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It is heaven where God is. This word was used by the Jews as a name for the place where righteous people go, either when they die or when they rise from the dead and have been vindicated on the day of Judgment. It was located in the "third heaven" in Jewish thought of the time. (See "paradise" in KBT in the "heaven" entry.)

Section.heading: Revelation 2:8-11 The letter that John wrote and sent to the church at Smyrna.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what John wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: John wrote a letter to the angel of the church in Smyrna. (8)
He told them not to be afraid of what they were going to suffer. (10)

Questions.Q: Whose words did that person tell John to write in the letter?
Questions.A: He told John to write the words of him who is eternal/the first and the last, who died and came back to life again. (8)

Questions.Q: What did he say that he knew about the people of Smyrna?
Questions.A: He knew about their persecutions/afflictions and that they were poor but yet were rich! (9)

Questions.Q: What else did he say that he knew?
Questions.A: He knew about the slander of those who said they were Jews, but they were not. They were really controlled by Satan. (9)

Questions.Q: What do you think a synagogue is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In this verse it is a group of people who opposed Christianity and who were under the power of Satan.
Questions.Note: See "synagogue" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Who do you think Satan is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Satan is the chief enemy of God. He is the supreme evil spiritual being who leads and directs all other evil spiritual beings.
Questions.Note: See "Satan" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What was going to happen to the people/Christians of Smyrna?
Questions.A: The devil was going to put some of them in prison. (10)
Questions.Alternative: What was going to happen to the people of Smyrna?
What was going to happen to the Christians of Smyrna?

Questions.Q: What do you know about the Devil?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "Devil" is the Greek equivalent of the Hebrew "Satan." Satan is the chief enemy of God. He is the supreme evil spiritual being who leads and directs all other evil spiritual beings (See "Devil" in KBT in the "Satan" entry.)

Questions.Q: For what reason was the devil going to do that?
Questions.A: He was going to do it to test them/cause them to deny Christ/cause them to deny that they believed Jesus. (10)

Questions.Q: How long would they suffer persecution?
Questions.A: They would suffer for ten days. (10)

Questions.Q: What will be their reward if they continue to be faithful?
Questions.A: They will be given the crown of life/eternal life [by Jesus]. (10)

Questions.Q: What did he tell them to do?
Questions.A: He said that since they had ears they should listen to what the [Holy] Spirit was saying to them. (11)

Questions.Q: What will happen to those who overcome [the forces of evil]?
Questions.A: They will not be hurt by the second death. (11)
Questions.Alternative: What will happen to those who overcome the forces of evil?
What will happen to those who overcome?

Section.heading: Revelation 2:12-17 The letter that John wrote and sent to the church at Pergamum.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what John wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: John wrote a letter to the angel of the church in Pergamum. (12)
He wrote about the good things and bad things they were doing. (13-14)

Questions.Q: Whose words did that person tell John to write in the letter?
Questions.A: He told John to write the words of him who has the sharp, double-edged sword. (12)

Questions.Q: What did he say about them?
Questions.A: He said that he knew that many people were under Satan's control where they lived. (13)

Questions.Q: What good things did he say they did?
Questions.A: They remained true to him/Jesus.
They did not renounce/abandon their faith in him, even when they were persecuted. (13)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to have faith in someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Faith is the quality of trusting someone. It is the act of wholeheartedly and steadfastly believing in the existence, power, and benevolence of a supreme being. (See "faith" in KBT in the "believe, believing, belief, faith, trust" entry.)

Questions.Q: Who was Antipas?
Questions.A: He was a man whom people killed, because he faithfully witnessed [about Jesus]. (13)

Questions.Q: What did Balaam teach Balaak to do that was wrong/sin?
Questions.A: He taught him to entice the Israelites to eat food that had been sacrificed to idols.
He also taught him to entice the Israelites to commit sexual immorality. (14)
Questions.Alternative: What did Balaam teach Balaak to do that was wrong?
What did Balaam teach Balaak to do that was sin?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when someone sacrifices food to an idol?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The sacrifice of food to an idol is a religious act of making a gift to some powerful spiritual being in order to establish, maintain, or restore a proper relationship between the sacrificer and the deity. Something is given up in order to achieve a purpose.
Questions.Note: See "sacrifice" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think an idol is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: An idol is a representation or symbol of a deity or any other being or thing made or used as an object of worship. (See "idol" in KBT in the "God" entry.)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to commit sexual immorality?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: This is a general word referring to any kind of unlawful sexual intercourse. (See "immorality" in KBT in the "sin" entry.)

Questions.Q: What were some of the people doing about this teaching of Balaam?
Questions.A: They were following/obeying it. (14)

Questions.Q: What other teachings were some people following?
Questions.A: They were following the things that the Nicolaitans taught. (15)

Questions.Q: What did he tell those Christians/people at Pergamum to do?
Questions.A: He told them to repent. (16)
Questions.Alternative: What did he tell those Christians at Pergamum to do?
What did he tell those people at Pergamum to do?

Questions.Q: What was he going to do to them if they did not repent?
Questions.A: He was going to come to them and fight them with the sword in his mouth. (16)

Questions.Q: What did he tell them to do?
Questions.A: He said that since they had ears they should listen to what the [Holy] Spirit was saying to them. (17)

Questions.Q: What will be the reward for anyone who overcomes [the forces of evil]?
Questions.A: [Jesus] will give him some of the hidden manna/heavenly food.
He will also give him a white stone with a new name on it which will only be known by the one who receives it. (17)
Questions.Alternative: What will be the reward for anyone who overcomes the forces of evil?
What will be the reward for anyone who overcomes?

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason for a person or place to have a name?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A name is a label which identifies a person or place.
Questions.Note: See "name" in KBT.

Section.heading: Revelation 2:18-29 The letter that John wrote and sent to the church at Thyatira.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what John wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: John wrote a letter to the angel of the church in Thyatira. (18)
He wrote about the good things and bad things they were doing. (19-20)

Questions.Q: Whose words did that person tell John to write in the letter?
Questions.A: He told him to write the words of the Son of God. (18)

Questions.Q: Who do you think the Son of God is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The Son of God is Jesus.

Questions.Q: What did the Son of God look like?
Questions.A: He had eyes like blazing fire and feet like polished brass. (18)

Questions.Q: What good things had they been doing?
Questions.A: They practiced love [for one another or for Christ].
They had faith/trusted [in Christ].
They helped others.
They patiently endured their sufferings/troubles. (19)

Questions.Q: What did he have against them?
Questions.A: They tolerated the woman Jezebel. (20)

Questions.Q: What did Jezebel call herself?
Questions.A: She called herself a prophetess. (20)

Questions.Q: What do you know about prophets?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A prophet is someone who speaks for God and is inspired by Him. He often foretells future events. Prophets were mainly spokespersons who called His people to obedience by appealing to Israel's past and future. A false prophet was a person who claimed to be a prophet of God but was not. His messages were deceptive and led to confusion. "Jezebel, who calls herself a prophetess". Apparently, this was a code name for a prominent woman in the church who taught false teachings while claiming to speak messages from God.
Questions.Note: See "prophet" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did he say that was bad about Jezebel?
Questions.A: He said she taught his people to commit immoral sexual acts
and to eat food that had been offered to idols. (20)

Questions.Q: What did he give her time to do?
Questions.A: He gave her time to repent of her immorality. (21)

Questions.Q: What did she do?
Questions.A: She was not willing to repent. (21)

Questions.Q: What will he do to her since she will not repent?
Questions.A: He will make her sick. (22)
He will kill her children. (23)

Questions.Q: What will he do to those people who commit adultery with her?
Questions.A: He will make them suffer intensely. (22)

Questions.Q: What did they need to do to keep him from making them suffer?
Questions.A: They needed to repent. (22)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to commit adultery with another person?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Adultery is the act of unfaithfulness in marriage that occurs when one of the marriage partners voluntarily engages in sexual intercourse with a person of the opposite sex other than the marriage partner.

Questions.Q: What will the people in the churches know after this?
Questions.A: They will know that he knows what the people are doing and what they are thinking.
He will repay each of them according to what they have done. (23)

Questions.Q: What does it mean to you to talk about the "heart"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The most common use of the word "heart" in the Bible is to refer to the spiritual center or innermost part of a human being. In Hebrew and Greek "heart" is most commonly associated with thoughts and ideas.
Questions.Note: See "heart" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What does the "mind" mean to you?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The word "mind" refers primarily to the thinking and understanding functions of a human being. (See "mind" in KBT in the "heart" entry.)

Questions.Q: What did he tell those people in Thyatira, who did not follow the ways of Jezebel and did not learn Satan's deep secrets, to do?
Questions.A: He told them to continue to obey him as they have been, until he comes. (24-25)

Questions.Q: What did he promise to anyone who overcomes [the forces of evil] and who does his will to the end [of the age]?
Questions.A: He will give them authority to rule over the nations. (26)
Questions.Alternative: What did he promise to anyone who overcomes the forces of evil and who does his will to the end of the age?
What did he promise to anyone who overcomes the forces of evil and who does his will to the end?
What did he promise to anyone who overcomes and who does his will to the end of the age?
What did he promise to anyone who overcomes and who does his will to the end?

Questions.Q: What does the word "nation" mean to you?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "Nation" refers to the people who make up that nation. This community of people possesses a more or less defined territory of land and government. (See "nation" in KBT in the "gentile" entry.)

Questions.Q: How will he rule others?
Questions.A: He will rule them with a rod of iron, that is, he will punish those who disobey him,
and destroy them as a person dashes pottery to pieces. (27)

Questions.Q: What authority will he give to anyone who overcomes [the forces of evil]?
Questions.A: He will give a person like this the same authority to rule over other people that his Father had given to him. (27)
Questions.Alternative: What authority will he give to anyone who overcomes the forces of evil?
What authority will he give to anyone who overcomes?

Questions.Q: What else will he give to someone who overcomes [the forces of evil]?
Questions.A: He will give him the morning star. (28)
Questions.Alternative: What else will he give to someone who overcomes the forces of evil?
What else will he give to someone who overcomes?

Questions.Q: What did he tell them to do?
Questions.A: He said that since they had ears they should listen to what the [Holy] Spirit was saying to them. (29)

Section.heading: Revelation 3:1-6 The letter that John wrote and sent to the church at Sardis.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what John wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: John wrote a letter to the angel of the church in Sardis. (1)
He wrote about the good things and bad things they were doing. (1-2)

Questions.Q: Whose words did that person tell John to write in the letter?
Questions.A: He told him to write the words of him who holds the seven spirits of God and the seven stars. (1)

Questions.Q: What did he know about them?
Questions.A: He knew their deeds.
They had a reputation of believing Christ well/doing what Christ wanted.
They were not believing Christ well/not doing what Christ wanted. (1)

Questions.Q: What did he tell them to do?
Questions.A: He told them to begin to really obey him.
He told them to start doing as they should do as Christians. (2)
Questions.Note: UBS states this is referring to Christian qualities or virtues.

Questions.Q: What caused him to speak that way to them?
Questions.A: He said that because he did not find their deeds complete in the sight of his God. // Their Christian lives were not up to the standard that his God had set. (2)

Questions.Q: What did he tell them to do?
Questions.A: He told them to remember what they have received and heard, and obey it
and to repent. (3)

Questions.Q: What will he do, if they do not repent?
Questions.A: He will come to them like a thief. (3)

Questions.Q: How will they know when he will come?
Questions.A: They will not know when he will come. (3)

Questions.Q: What will those people do that have not been doing sinful deeds/soiled their clothes?
Questions.A: They will fellowship/walk with him/[Christ], dressed in white [clothes]. (4)
Questions.Alternative: What will those people do that have not been doing sinful deeds?
What will those people do that have not soiled their clothes?

Questions.Q: For what reason will they be allowed to fellowship/walk with him?
Questions.A: They will be allowed to do this because they have faithfully done as Christ desired them to do. (4)
Questions.Alternative: For what reason will they be allowed to fellowship with him?
For what reason will they be allowed to walk with him?

Questions.Q: What will be the reward of anyone who overcomes/is victorious?
Questions.A: He will be dressed in white.
He will have his name in the book of life.
Jesus will acknowledge his name before his Father and his angels. (5)
Questions.Alternative: What will be the reward of anyone who overcomes?
What will be the reward of anyone who is victorious?

Questions.Q: What did he tell them to do?
Questions.A: He said that since they had ears they should listen to what the [Holy] Spirit was saying to them. (6)

Section.heading: Revelation 3:7-13 The letter that John wrote and sent to the church at Philadelphia.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what John wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: John wrote a letter to the angel of the church in Philadelphia. (7)
He wrote about the good things they had done. (8, 10)

Questions.Q: Whose words did that person tell John to write in the letter?
Questions.A: He told him to write the words of him who is holy and true and who holds the key of David. (7)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to be holy?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Someone who is "holy" is set apart [by God] and dedicated to the service or worship of God. Anything that is "holy" for God must reflect his character by being physically unblemished or reflecting, to some degree, his purity.
Questions.Note: See "holy" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What great power does this man have who holds the key of David?
Questions.A: He has the authority to allow people into God's kingdom and the power to exclude people from God's kingdom. // When he opens something, no one can shut it and when he shuts something, no one can open it. (7)

Questions.Q: What did he do for them?
Questions.A: He invited them to be a part of God's kingdom. No one can exclude them from the kingdom. // He placed an open door before them that no one can shut. (8)

Questions.Q: What good things did they do?
Questions.A: They kept his word/obeyed his commands.
They did not deny his name/were not unfaithful to him. (8)

Questions.Q: What did he say about those who are controlled by Satan?
Questions.A: He said they claim to be Jews but they are not. They are liars. (9)

Questions.Q: What will he make those people do?
Questions.A: He will make them come and fall down at the believers' feet
and make them acknowledge that he has loved them/the believers. (9)

Questions.Q: What will he do for them because they have kept his command to endure patiently?
Questions.A: He will keep them from the great trials/troubles that will come upon the entire world to test everyone. (10)

Questions.Q: What do you think "world" means in this verse?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means the inhabitants of the earth, all human beings.
Questions.Note: See "world" in KBT.

Questions.Q: When did he say he was coming?
Questions.A: He told them he was coming soon. (11)

Questions.Q: What did he tell them they should do?
Questions.A: He told them to keep on trusting him/Christ. (11)

Questions.Q: Why should they do this?
Questions.A: They should do this so that no one would take/steal their crown/reward. (11)

Questions.Q: What will he give as a reward to anyone who overcomes [the forces of evil]?
Questions.A: He will give them the privilege to be in the presence of God forever/the eternal kingdom of God, which they will never leave.
He will write on them the name of God, the name of the city of God, which is the new Jerusalem, and his new name. (12)
Questions.Alternative: What will he give as a reward to anyone who overcomes the forces of evil?
What will he give as a reward to anyone who overcomes?

Questions.Q: From where will the new Jerusalem come?
Questions.A: It will come down out of heaven from God. (12)

Questions.Q: For what purpose do you think people used a temple?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The people used the temple as a place to worship God.
Questions.Note: See "temple" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: For what do you think a temple is to be used by people?
For what do you think the temple is to be used by people?
For what purpose do you think people used the temple?
What was the purpose of the temple?
How do you think people used the temple?
What do you think a temple is?

Questions.Q: Where do you think heaven is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It is that part of God's creation above the earth and the waters, including "air" and "space," and serves as home for God and the spirits who serve Him.
Questions.Note: See "heaven" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did he tell them to do?
Questions.A: He said that since they had ears they should listen to what the [Holy] Spirit was saying to them. (13)

Section.heading: Revelation 3:14-22 The letter that John wrote and sent to the church at Laodicea.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what John wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: John wrote a letter to the angel of the church in Laodicea. (14)
He wrote about the fact that they were neither hot nor cold toward him/Jesus. (15)

Questions.Q: Whose words did that person tell John to write in the letter?
Questions.A: He told him to write the words of the ruler of God's creation, who did as he said he would do and who faithfully told God's word. (14)

Questions.Q: What did he wish they were, instead of not being hot or cold?
Questions.A: He wished that they were either ones who did completely as he desired or that they were ones who did not do anything that he desired them to do. (15)

Questions.Q: What was he about to do to them?
Questions.A: He was about to reject them. (16)

Questions.Q: Why did he want to do that?
Questions.A: He wanted to do that because they were not obeying him completely. (16)

Questions.Q: Why did those people say they didn't need anything?
Questions.A: They said that because they had acquired wealth and were rich. (17)

Questions.Q: What did he say about them?
Questions.A: He said they were wretched, pitiful, poor, blind and naked people, [because they were not obeying him/not living as Christians should live]. (17)

Questions.Q: What did he tell them to obtain from him?
Questions.A: He told them to obtain gold from him that had been refined by the fire,
white clothing,
and salve to put on/anoint their eyes. (18)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to anoint someone with salve or oil?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In this context it means to put oil or some similar substance on a person/a person's body/skin in a symbolic act for healing.
Questions.Note: See "anoint" in KBT.

Questions.Q: For what reason did they need to obtain those items from him?
Questions.A: He was the only source to help them live as Christians should live. (18)

Questions.Q: What does he do to those he loves?
Questions.A: He rebukes and disciplines them. (19)

Questions.Q: What did he tell them to do?
Questions.A: He told them to be earnest/zealous and repent. (19)

Questions.Q: What did he say he was doing?
Questions.A: He said that it was as though he were standing at the door and knocking, wanting to enter to help them. (20)

Questions.Q: What will he do if anyone hears his voice and allows him to help them?
Questions.A: He will go in and eat with that person, and that person will eat with him, that is, they will fellowship together. (20)

Questions.Q: What will he give to any person who overcomes [the forces of evil]?
Questions.A: He will give that person the right to sit with him on his throne as a ruler/chief. (21)
Questions.Alternative: What will he give to any person who overcomes the forces of evil?
What will he give to any person who overcomes?

Questions.Q: What did he receive from his Father after he overcame?
Questions.A: He received the right to sit with his Father on his throne as a ruler/chief. (21)

Questions.Q: What did he tell them to do?
Questions.A: He said that since they had ears they should listen to what the [Holy] Spirit was saying to them. (22)

Section.heading: Revelation 4:1-11 John saw a vision of God on his throne in heaven.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what John wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: He wrote about what he saw around the throne in heaven.

Questions.Q: What did John see?
Questions.A: He saw a door standing open in heaven. (1)

Questions.Q: What did John hear a voice saying?
Questions.A: John heard a voice say, "Come up here and I will show you what must take place after this." (1)

Questions.Q: What happened to John?
Questions.A: He was at once/immediately in the Spirit. (2)
Questions.Note: UBS states that "in the spirit" implies that John was transported by the Spirit to heaven.

Questions.Q: What did he see in heaven?
Questions.A: He saw a throne with someone sitting on it. (2)

Questions.Q: What did the person look like?
Questions.A: He had the appearance of jasper and carnelian. // His face gleamed like jasper and carnelian. (3)

Questions.Q: What else did John see?
Questions.A: He saw a rainbow, that looked like an emerald, in a circle around the throne. (3)

Questions.Q: What else was around the throne?
Questions.A: There were 24 other thrones around the throne. (4)

Questions.Q: Who were seated on the 24 thrones?
Questions.A: There were 24 elders sitting on the 24 thrones. (4)

Questions.Q: What do you think an elder is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In this verse an elder is a leader among God's people in heaven. (See "elder" in the check list of KBT in the RSV.)

Questions.Q: What were the 24 elders wearing?
Questions.A: They were wearing white clothes and had gold crowns on their heads. (4)

Questions.Q: What was coming from the throne?
Questions.A: John saw flashes of lightning.
He also heard rumblings and peals/noise of thunder coming from the throne. (5)

Questions.Q: What was in front of the throne?
Questions.A: There were seven lamps blazing in front of the throne. (5)

Questions.Q: What are those seven lamps?
Questions.A: They are the seven spirits that belong to God. (5)

Questions.Q: What else was in front of the throne?
Questions.A: There was something that looked like a sea of glass that was as clear as crystal. (6)

Questions.Q: What was in the center around the throne?
Questions.A: There were four living creatures that were covered with eyes in front and back. (6)

Questions.Q: What did those four living creatures look like?
Questions.A: The first creature looked like a lion.
The second creature looked like an ox.
The third creature had a face like a man.
The fourth creature looked like a flying eagle. (7)

Questions.Q: What did each of these four creatures have?
Questions.A: They each had six wings;
and they were covered with eyes all over, even under their wings. (8)

Questions.Q: How often did the creatures say, "Holy, holy, holy is the Lord God Almighty, who was, and is, and is to come"?
Questions.A: They said it continually. (8)

Questions.Q: What does it mean to you to have someone as your lord?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A lord is someone who has power and exercises it responsibly. To call someone your lord means that you have given them control over your life. Every Christian strives to make Jesus lord in his or her life by giving Him complete control. (See "Lord" in KBT in the "God" entry.)

Questions.Q: What happened whenever the living creatures praised him who sits on the throne?
Questions.A: The 24 elders fell down before him who sits on the throne and worshiped him,
and they laid their crowns before the throne. (10)
They said, "You are worthy, our Lord and God, for us to praise you. You are powerful, for you created all things; and by your will they were created and exist." (11)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to worship God?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means to give him respect and devotion. It may be regarded as the direct acknowledgment to God, of his nature, attributes, ways and claims, whether by the outgoing of the heart in praise and thanksgiving or by deed done in such acknowledgment.

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when you honor someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: When you honor someone you show high regard or appreciation for them.

Section.heading: Revelation 5:1-14 John saw a Lamb take a scroll from God.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what John wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: He wrote about seeing the Lamb take the scroll that was sealed. (7)
He also wrote about all those who sang praises to God and the Lamb. (9)

Questions.Q: What did John see?
Questions.A: He saw a scroll with writing on both sides and sealed with seven seals. (1)

Questions.Q: Where was the scroll?
Questions.A: It was in the right hand of the one who sat on the throne. (1)

Questions.Q: What else did John see?
Questions.A: He saw a mighty angel. (2)

Questions.Q: What was the angel doing?
Questions.A: He asked, "Who is worthy to break the seals and open the scroll?" (2)

Questions.Q: Who could open the scroll and look inside it?
Questions.A: No one could do it. (3)

Questions.Q: For what reason did John cry?
Questions.A: He cried because no one could be found who was worthy to open the scroll or look inside it. (4)

Questions.Q: What did one of the elders say to him?
Questions.A: The elder told John not to cry. (5)

Questions.Q: Who did the elder say was able to open the scroll and its seven seals?
Questions.A: He said that the Lion of the tribe of Judah was able to do this. (5)

Questions.Q: For what reason was he able to open the scroll?
Questions.A: He could do this because he had triumphed over/defeated his enemies. (5)

Questions.Q: From whose family is the Lion of the tribe of Judah?
Questions.A: He is a descendant of King David. (5)

Questions.Q: What did John see next?
Questions.A: He saw a Lamb that looked as though [someone] had killed him. (6)

Questions.Q: Where was the Lamb standing?
Questions.A: He was standing in the center of the throne area. (6)

Questions.Q: Who was in a circle around the Lamb?
Questions.A: The four living creatures and the elders were around the Lamb. (6)

Questions.Q: What did the Lamb have on his head?
Questions.A: He had seven horns and seven eyes. (6)

Questions.Q: What are the seven eyes?
Questions.A: They are the seven spirits of God, which God sent out to the whole world. (6)

Questions.Q: What did the Lamb do?
Questions.A: He took the scroll from the right hand of the one who sat on the throne. (7)

Questions.Q: What happened after the Lamb took the scroll?
Questions.A: The four living creatures and the 24 elders fell down before the Lamb. (8)

Questions.Q: What did each one of them have?
Questions.A: Each one of them had a harp,
and they were holding golden bowls full of incense. (8)

Questions.Q: What are the golden bowls of incense?
Questions.A: They are the prayers of the saints. (8)

Questions.Q: Who do you think the saints are?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: They are those people who belong to God, God's people, those who believed in Christ. It does not refer to a special group of people who were particularly good people. In the New Testament it is used to refer to believers-in-Christ in general. (See "saint" in KBT in the "disciple" entry.)

Questions.Q: What did they sing in their song?
Questions.A: They sang that the Lamb was worthy to take the scroll and open its seals. (9)

Questions.Q: For what reason was the Lamb worthy to take the scroll?
Questions.A: He was worthy because [people] had killed him,
and he had purchased men with his blood/by his death for God from every tribe and language and people and nation. (9)
Questions.Note: UBS states that the four nouns are used to include all human groupings in the world, by common ancestry, by common language, by common nationality, and by common race. It is not necessary to use all four nouns if it is unnatural in the language. To simplify, only "every race and every country" would be needed.

Questions.Q: What did the Lamb make all of those people to become?
Questions.A: He made them to become a kingdom and priests to serve our God. (10)
Questions.Note: Also see 1:6.

Questions.Q: What will those people do on the earth?
Questions.A: They will reign on the earth. (10)

Questions.Q: What did John see and hear?
Questions.A: He saw and heard the voice of millions of angels. (11)

Questions.Q: Where were the angels standing?
Questions.A: They were standing in a circle around the throne, the living creatures, and the elders. (11)

Questions.Q: What did the angels sing?
Questions.A: They sang a song, in a loud voice, to praise the Lamb. (12)

Questions.Q: What do you think "the blessing" means in this verse?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: When the one being blessed is God, the meaning of "to bless" refers to a person who blesses God is praising God by expressing a formal prayer of thanks and praise. In most modern English versions, this sense is translated by "praise" or "give thanks to". (See "blessing" in KBT in the "bless" entry.)
Questions.Alternative: What do you think "blessing" means in this verse?

Questions.Q: What did John hear?
Questions.A: He heard every creature in heaven and on earth and under the earth and on the sea singing a song of praise to the Lamb. (13)

Questions.Q: What did the four living creatures say?
Questions.A: They said "amen."/They agreed with what had just been said. (14)

Questions.Q: What did the elders do?
Questions.A: They fell down and worshiped [God and the Lamb]. (14)

Section.heading: Revelation 6:1-17 The things that John saw and heard after the Lamb opened the six seals from the scroll.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what John wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: He wrote about what he saw after the Lamb opened six of the seals.

Questions.Q: What did John see?
Questions.A: He saw the Lamb open the first of the seven seals. (1)

Questions.Q: What did he hear after the Lamb opened the seal?
Questions.A: He heard one of the four living creatures say "come!" in a loud voice. (1)

Questions.Q: What did he see after the Lamb broke the first seal?
Questions.A: He saw a white horse and a rider with a bow and crown [that God or an angel gave to him]. (2)

Questions.Q: What was the rider determined to do?
Questions.A: He rode out determined to conquer people [in a battle]. (2)

Questions.Q: What happened after the Lamb opened the second seal?
Questions.A: John heard the second living creature say, "come!" (3)

Questions.Q: Then what happened?
Questions.A: A fiery red horse came out. (4)

Questions.Q: What power did [God] give to the rider?
Questions.A: [He] gave him the power to take peace from the earth/bring war on the earth,
and to make men kill each other. (4)
Questions.Alternative: What power did God give to the rider?
What power did give to the rider?

Questions.Q: What did [God] give to this rider?
Questions.A: [He] gave him a large sword. (4)
Questions.Alternative: What did God give to this rider?
What was given to this rider?

Questions.Q: What happened after the Lamb opened the third seal?
Questions.A: John heard the third living creature say, "come!" (5)

Questions.Q: What did John see?
Questions.A: He saw a black horse. (5)

Questions.Q: What was the rider holding?
Questions.A: He was holding a pair of scales. (5)

Questions.Q: What did John hear a voice say?
Questions.A: [Because food was scarce], he heard a voice say, "A quart of wheat will cost a day's wages,
and three quarts of barley will cost a day's wages,
and do not damage the oil and the wine!" (6)

Questions.Q: What happened after the Lamb opened the fourth seal?
Questions.A: John heard the fourth living creature say "come!" (7)

Questions.Q: What did John see?
Questions.A: He saw a pale horse. (8)

Questions.Q: What was the rider of this horse called?
Questions.A: The rider was called the one who killed people/Death. (8)

Questions.Q: Who was following close behind Death?
Questions.A: The one named the place of the spirits of dead people/Hades was following him. (8)

Questions.Q: What power did [God] give to Death and Hades?
Questions.A: [He] gave them the power to kill one fourth of the people in the world. As a result, many died from fighting each other.
Many died from famine.
Many died from sickness.
Wild beasts killed many. (8)
Questions.Alternative: What power did God give to Death and Hades?
What power was given to Death and Hades?

Questions.Q: What did John see after the Lamb opened the fifth seal?
Questions.A: Under the altar he saw/He saw under the altar the souls of Christians whom [people] had killed. (9)

Questions.Q: What do you think an altar is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: An altar is a kind of table or platform where sacrifices of animals or other offerings are made to God.
Questions.Note: See "altar" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think the soul is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It is a person's inner being the self. The self in its relationship with God.
Questions.Note: See "soul" in KBT.

Questions.Q: For what reason were the Christians/they killed?
Questions.A: People killed them, because they had testified about God/proclaimed the word of God. (9)
Questions.Alternative: For what reason were the Christians killed?
For what reason were they killed?

Questions.Q: What did those people, who had been killed for their faithfulness to God, want him to do for them?
Questions.A: They wanted him to avenge their deaths and judge those responsible. (10)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to judge someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means someone/a judge will determine if a person is guilty or not of committing a crime. He does this by assessing the evidence connected to the person and what he may have done.
Questions.Note: See "judge" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did [God] give to each of them?
Questions.A: [He] gave each one a white robe. (11)
Questions.Alternative: What did God give to each of them?
What was given to each of them?

Questions.Q: What did [God] tell them to do?
Questions.A: [He] told them to wait a little longer, until [people] killed the rest of their fellow servants and brothers as they had been killed. (11)
Questions.Alternative: What did God tell them to do?
What were they told to do?

Questions.Q: What happened after the Lamb opened the sixth seal?
Questions.A: There was a big earthquake.
The sun turned black/dark.
The moon turned red as blood. (12)
The stars fell from the sky to earth. (13)
The sky receded as someone rolls up a scroll.
Every mountain and island was removed from where it had been. (14)

Questions.Q: What do you think the sky is in this verse?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The sky is the physical place above the earth where the stars and clouds are, and from which lightning and rain come down to the earth. (See "sky" in KBT in the "heaven" entry.)

Questions.Q: What did all the kings, princes, generals, the rich, the mighty, and all slaves and all free men do in response to those things happening?
Questions.A: They all hid in caves and among the rocks of the mountains. (15)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to be a slave of someone/something?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means the person is totally responsible to and dependent upon another person, or the person has become completely subservient to a dominating influence. (See "slave" in KBT in the "servant, slave" entry.)
Questions.Alternative: What do you think it means to be a slave of someone?
What do you think it means to be a slave of something?

Questions.Q: What did all the people want the mountains and the rocks to do?
Questions.A: They wanted the mountains and the rocks to fall on them and hide them from [God] and from the wrath of the Lamb. (16)

Questions.Q: For what reason did they want that to happen?
Questions.A: They wanted that to happen because the time for[God] and the [Lamb] to punish all their enemies had come. (17)

Section.heading: Revelation 7:1-8 Four angels marked 144,000 people of Israel with the mark of God.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what John wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: He wrote about the four angels he saw. (1)
He wrote about the angels putting a seal on some of the servants of God. (2-4)

Questions.Q: What did John see the four angels doing?
Questions.A: He saw them standing at the four directions/corners of the earth. (1)
He saw them holding back the four winds of the earth, so that no wind would blow on the land, or the sea or any tree. (1)

Questions.Q: What else did John see?
Questions.A: He saw another angel coming up from the east. (2)

Questions.Q: What did that angel have?
Questions.A: He had the seal of the living God. (2)

Questions.Q: What power did the four angels have?
Questions.A: They had the power to harm the land and the sea. (2)

Questions.Q: What did that angel say to the other four angels?
Questions.A: He told them not to harm the land or the sea or the trees, until he and the other angels put a seal on the foreheads of the servants of God. (2-3)

Questions.Q: Who were those people that the angels were going to seal?
Questions.A: They were 144,000 servants from the twelve tribes of Israel. 12,000 were sealed from each of the twelve tribes. (4-8)

Section.heading: Revelation 7:9-17 John saw a large crowd of people wearing white robes.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what John wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: He wrote about the people who were wearing white robes. (9)

Questions.Q: Who were all those people whom John saw?
Questions.A: They were people from every nation, tribe, people and language. (9)

Questions.Q: What were those people doing?
Questions.A: They were standing in front of the throne and in front of the Lamb.
They were wearing white robes and were holding palm branches in their hands. (9)
They were worshiping and praising God by saying that God and the Lamb had saved them from their sins. (10)

Questions.Q: What do you think "salvation" means?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The noun form (Greek sôtêria) and the adjective form (Greek sôtêrios) in the New Testament usually refer to eternal salvation from sin, evil and death.
Questions.Note: See "salvation" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Where were the angels standing?
Questions.A: They were standing around the throne
and around the elders and the four living creatures. (11)

Questions.Q: What did the angels do?
Questions.A: They bowed down with their faces to the ground and worshiped God. (11)

Questions.Q: In their worship of him, what did the angels say belongs to God?
Questions.A: They worshiped him saying that we must always praise him and that he is very powerful. (12)

Questions.Q: What did one of the elders ask John?
Questions.A: He asked John who those people, who were wearing white robes, were
and from where they came. (13)

Questions.Q: What did John tell the elder?
Questions.A: He told him that he, the elder, knew them/the answer/who they were and from where they came. (14)

Questions.Q: What did the elder say about those people?
Questions.A: He said they came out of the great tribulation/they survived terrible persecutions.
God forgave the sins of those people, because of Christ's death. As a result, John saw them wearing white clothes. (14)

Questions.Q: What were those people doing then/after that?
Questions.A: They were in front of the throne of God,
and they served him day and night in his temple. (15)
Questions.Alternative: What were those people doing then?
What were those people doing after that?

Questions.Q: What will the one/God who sits on the throne do?
Questions.A: He will be with them/watch over them. (15)
Questions.Alternative: What will the one who sits on the throne do?
What will God, who sits on the throne, do?
What will God do?

Questions.Q: What will they not ever have to endure again?
Questions.A: They will never be hungry or thirsty again.
They will never be burned by the sun or anything else. (16)

Questions.Q: What is the reason they will not have to endure those things?
Questions.A: They will not have to endure those things again, because the Lamb, who is in the center of the throne area, will be their shepherd and completely provide for them [eternal life]. (17)
Also God will wipe away every tear from their eyes. // God will remove every source of pain and sorrow. (17)

Section.heading: Revelation 8:1-5 The Lamb opened the seventh seal of the scroll.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what John wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: He wrote about the things he saw after the Lamb opened the seventh seal.

Questions.Q: What happened after the Lamb opened the seventh seal?
Questions.A: There was silence in heaven for about a half hour. (1)

Questions.Q: What did John see?
Questions.A: He saw seven angels standing before God. (2)

Questions.Q: What did [God or an angel] give the seven angels?
Questions.A: [God or an angel] gave them seven trumpets. (2)
Questions.Alternative: What did God or an angel give the seven angels?
What did God give the seven angels?
What did an angel give the seven angels?
What was given to the seven angels?

Questions.Q: What did the angel with the golden censer offer on the golden altar?
Questions.A: He offered a lot of incense with the prayers of the saints/God's people. (3)

Questions.Q: Where did the smoke of the incense and the prayers of the saints go?
Questions.A: They went up before God. (4)

Questions.Q: What did the angel do with the golden censer/incense container?
Questions.A: He filled it with fire from the altar and threw the fire upon the earth. (5)
Questions.Alternative: What did the angel do with the golden censer?
What did the angel do with the golden incense container?

Questions.Q: What happened after that?
Questions.A: There were thunder, rumblings, lightning, and an earthquake began. (5)

Section.heading: Revelation 8:6-9:21 The things that John saw and heard after each of the six angels blew his trumpet.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what John wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: He wrote about the things he saw after each of the six angels blew his trumpet.

Questions.Q: What happened after the first angel blew his trumpet?
Questions.A: After he blew his trumpet, hail and fire mixed with blood fell on the earth.
One third of the earth was burned up.
One third of the trees were burned up.
All the green grass was burned up. (7)

Questions.Q: What happened after the second angel blew his trumpet?
Questions.A: Something like a huge mountain, that was on fire, fell into the sea.
One third of the sea turned into blood. (8)
A third of the living creatures in the sea died.
One third of the ships were destroyed. (9)

Questions.Q: What happened after the third angel blew his trumpet?
Questions.A: A huge star, that was on fire, fell from the sky on one third of the rivers
and on the springs of water. (10)
One third of the water turned bitter.
Many people died from drinking that water. (11)

Questions.Q: What was the name of the star?
Questions.A: The star was called Wormwood. (11)
Questions.Note: Wormwood is a bitter herb.

Questions.Q: What happened after the fourth angel blew his trumpet?
Questions.A: A third of the sun, a third of the moon, and a third of the stars were struck/damaged. (12)

Questions.Q: What was the result of that?
Questions.A: The result was that the sun, the moon, and the stars did not shine for one third of the time. The sun did not shine during one third of the daytime. The stars and the moon did not shine for one third of the night. (12)

Questions.Q: What warning did the eagle give as it flew by?
Questions.A: The eagle said that a terrible thing was going to happen to those who live on the earth, when the last three angels blew their trumpets. (13)

Questions.Q: What did John see after the fifth angel blew his trumpet?
Questions.A: He saw a star/angel that had fallen/descended from the sky to the earth. (1)

Questions.Q: What did this star have?
Questions.A: He had the key to the shaft of the abyss. (1)

Questions.Q: What do you think the abyss is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The word "abyss" (Greek abussos) literally means a place that is so deep that it has no bottom to it. In Jewish tradition it referred first to the water under the earth, "the deep". It also referred to the place where certain evil spirits were put in prison and tormented after being expelled from heaven. They will be kept there till the Judgment. The abyss (bottomless pit) has this meaning in Rev. 9:1, 2, 11; 11:7; 17:8; 20:1, 3. (See "abyss" in KBT in the "Hell" entry.)

Questions.Q: What happened when the angel opened the abyss?
Questions.A: Smoke rose from the abyss and darkened the sun and the sky. (2)

Questions.Q: What came out of the smoke?
Questions.A: Locusts came out of the smoke with power [from God] like the power of scorpions of the earth. (3)

Questions.Q: What did [God] tell the locusts to do?
Questions.A: [He] told them not to harm the grass or any plant or tree. They could only harm those people who did not have the seal of God on their foreheads. (4)
Questions.Alternative: What did God tell the locusts to do?
What were the locusts told to do?

Questions.Q: What kind of power did [God] give to the locusts?
Questions.A: [He] only gave them power to torture, not to kill, the people for five months. (5)
Questions.Alternative: What kind of power was given to the locusts?

Questions.Q: What kind of pain/agony did the people endure?
Questions.A: The pain they suffered with was like the sting of a scorpion. (5)
Questions.Alternative: What kind of pain did the people endure?
What kind of agony did the people endure?

Questions.Q: What will men want during those days?
Questions.A: They will want to die, but instead they will continue to live. (6)

Questions.Q: What did the locusts look like?
Questions.A: They looked like horses ready for battle.
They wore what looked like crowns of gold on their heads.
They had faces like humans. (7)
They had hair like women's hair and teeth like lion's teeth. (8)
They had what looked like breastplates of iron.
Their wings sounded like the thunder of many horses and chariots rushing into battle. (9)
They had tails and stings like scorpions.
In their tails they had the power to torment people for five months. (10)

Questions.Q: Who was the king of those locusts?
Questions.A: He/Their king was the angel of the abyss, whose name was "Abaddon" in Hebrew and "Apollyon" in Greek. (11)

Questions.Q: What did John call this plague of locusts?
Questions.A: He called it the first woe/severe punishment. (12)

Questions.Q: What did John hear after the sixth angel blew his trumpet?
Questions.A: He heard a voice coming from the horns of the golden altar. (13)

Questions.Q: What did the voice say to the sixth angel?
Questions.A: The voice told the angel to release the four angels who were bound at the river Euphrates. (14)

Questions.Q: What were those four angels released to do?
Questions.A: They were released to kill one third of the people on the earth. (15)

Questions.Q: How many mounted troops were there?
Questions.A: There were two hundred million. (16)

Questions.Q: What did the horses and riders look like?
Questions.A: The riders had breastplates that were fiery red, dark blue, and yellow as sulfur in color.
The horses' heads looked like the heads of lions.
Fire, smoke and sulfur came out of the horses' mouths. (17)

Questions.Q: How did they kill one third of mankind on the earth?
Questions.A: They killed them by using the fire, smoke, and sulfur that was coming out of the mouths of the horses. (18)

Questions.Q: Where did the horses have their power?
Questions.A: Their power was in their mouths and in their tails. (19)

Questions.Q: What could the horses do with their tails?
Questions.A: They could injure people with their tails, since their tails were like snakes with heads. (19)

Questions.Q: What did the people do who had not been killed by the fire, smoke, and sulfur?
Questions.A: They did not repent of the things/[idols] they had made.
They did not stop worshiping demons, and idols of gold, silver, bronze, stone and wood. (20)
They did not repent of their murders, their magic arts, their sexual immorality, or their thefts. (21)

Questions.Q: What do you think a demon is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A demon is a spiritual being who serves Satan as his agent, being under his authority. They have power to oppress a human being and even take control of him. (See "demon" in KBT in the "evil spirit, unclean spirit" entry.)

Section.heading: Revelation 10:1-11 John saw a vision of an angel with a small scroll.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what John wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: He wrote about a small scroll which was held by the angel. The angel gave the scroll to John. (2, 9)

Questions.Q: What did John say about this angel?
Questions.A: He said he wore a cloud around him.
He had a rainbow above his head.
His face was like the sun/shone like the sun.
His legs were like pillars of fire/fiery columns. (1)

Questions.Q: What was the angel holding?
Questions.A: He was holding a little scroll open in his hand. (2)

Questions.Q: Where was the angel standing?
Questions.A: He stood with his right foot on the sea and his left foot on the land. (2)

Questions.Q: What happened when the angel shouted?
Questions.A: The voices of the seven thunders spoke. (3)

Questions.Q: What did the voice from heaven tell John to do?
Questions.A: The voice told him to seal up what the seven thunders said, and not to write it down. (4)

Questions.Q: What did the angel do?
Questions.A: He raised his right hand to heaven. (5)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for the angel to "swear by him who lives forever and ever...."?
Questions.A: It means that what he is about to say is true. (6)
Questions.Note: This answer is not necessarily from the text, but may have to be explained. This would especially be true for a non-native English speaker. Also see UBS.

Questions.Q: What did the angel say was going to happen when the seventh angel blew his trumpet?
Questions.A: He said that [God] will not delay/wait any longer. [He] will accomplish his purpose/plan which he had announced to his prophets [long ago]. (6-7)

Questions.Q: What did the voice from heaven tell John to do?
Questions.A: The voice told him to go to the angel and to take the scroll that he was holding open in his hand. (8)

Questions.Q: What did the angel tell John to do with the scroll, when he had retrieved it?
Questions.A: The angel told him to eat the scroll. (9)

Questions.Q: What did the angel tell John he would experience from eating the scroll?
Questions.A: He said it would be sweet like honey in his mouth, but it would turn his stomach sour. (9)

Questions.Q: What did John experience after he took the scroll from the angel and ate it?
Questions.A: He discovered that it tasted as sweet as honey in his mouth, but it turned his stomach sour. (10)

Questions.Q: What did [God] tell John to do?
Questions.A: [He] told him to prophesy about many peoples, nations, languages and kings. (11)
Questions.Alternative: What did God tell John to do?
What was John told to do?

Section.heading: Revelation 11:1-14 God will send two men to the earth to work as prophets for 1260 days.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what John wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: He wrote about two men who will witness for God; they will have power to punish people but they can not be harmed by people. (3, 5)

Questions.Q: What did [an angel or God] give to John?
Questions.A: [He] gave him a reed like a measuring rod/stick. (1)
Questions.Alternative: What did an angel or God give to John?
What did an angel give to John?
What did God give to John?
What was given to John?

Questions.Q: What was John supposed to do?
Questions.A: He was supposed to measure the temple of God and the altar,
and to count the worshipers there. (1)

Questions.Q: What was he not supposed to measure?
Questions.A: He was not supposed to measure the outer court. (2)

Questions.Q: What was the reason that he was not supposed to measure the outer court?
Questions.A: He was not supposed to measure the outer court, because [God] had given it to the Gentiles. (2)

Questions.Q: What will the Gentiles do to the holy city?
Questions.A: They will rule/control it for forty-two months. (2)

Questions.Q: Who do you think Gentiles are?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In this verse they are those people who do not believe in Jesus Christ.
Questions.Note: See "Gentiles" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What will the two witnesses do?
Questions.A: They will prophesy for 1,260 days. (3)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to prophesy?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means to speak out a direct message from God, to proclaim a message inspired by God. (See "prophesy" in KBT in the "prophet" entry.)

Questions.Q: What are the two witnesses called?
Questions.A: They are called the two olive trees and the two lamp stands. (4)

Questions.Q: What will happen to anyone who tries to harm those two men?
Questions.A: Fire will come from their mouths and kill the people who try to harm them. (5)

Questions.Q: What other power do those two men have?
Questions.A: They have the power to prevent it from raining during the time they are prophesying.
They have the power to turn water into blood.
They have the power to cause plagues to afflict people on earth. (6)

Questions.Q: What will happen to the two men, when they have finished with their testimony/proclaiming the message that God told them to give?
Questions.A: The beast will come up from the Abyss and attack the two men and kill them. (7)
Questions.Alternative: What will happen to the two men, when they have finished with their testimony?
What will happen to the two men, when they have finished proclaiming the message that God told them to give?

Questions.Q: What will happen to their bodies?
Questions.A: Their bodies will lie in the street of the great city. (8)

Questions.Q: What happened to their Lord in the great city?
Questions.A: He was crucified [by some soldiers]. (8)

Questions.Q: What do you think happened to someone when the soldiers crucified them?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: During that time Roman soldiers would crucify someone by either tying their arms to a crossbeam or pounding nails through their wrists. Then the person was pulled up on an upright post, which was planted in the ground, and tied or nailed to it at his ankles. (See "crucify" in KBT in the "cross" entry.)

Questions.Q: What bodies do you think are meant in this verse?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: They are the physical bodies of those men who were killed.
Questions.Note: See "body" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What will happen for three and a half days?
Questions.A: People from every tribe, language and nation will look at their bodies. They will not bury the bodies. (9)
