Questions.Q: For what reason will the people rejoice, when the two men are killed?
Questions.A: They will rejoice, because the two men had tormented them. (10)

Questions.Q: How will the people show their joy at the death of the two men?
Questions.A: They will send each other gifts. (10)

Questions.Q: What happened to the two men three and a half days later?
Questions.A: God gave them life again after three and a half days, and they stood up on their feet. (11)

Questions.Q: How did the other people react to those men coming back to life again?
Questions.A: They were very afraid. (11)

Questions.Q: Where did the two men go?
Questions.A: They went up to heaven in a cloud. (12)

Questions.Q: What happened at the same time that the two men went up to heaven?
Questions.A: There was a terrible earthquake. (13)

Questions.Q: What was the result of this earthquake?
Questions.A: One tenth of the city was destroyed.
Seven thousand people were killed.
The rest of the people were very much afraid and gave glory to God. (13)

Section.heading: Revelation 11:15-19 The seventh angel blew his trumpet.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what John wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: He wrote about the things that happened after the seventh angel blew his trumpet.

Questions.Q: What did the voices in heaven say about Christ?
Questions.A: He will reign over all the nations/people forever. (15)

Questions.Q: What are some of the things that the twenty-four elders said, as they worshiped God?
Questions.A: They called him almighty.
They thanked him, because he had demonstrated/shown his power and had begun to reign. (16-17)
They said the time had come for him to judge the dead
and to reward the prophets and to reward his saints
and to punish those who had killed many of God's people. (18)
Questions.Alternative: What are some of the things that the twenty-four elders said, as they worshipped God?
What did the twenty-four elders say as they worshiped God?

Questions.Q: What was it that John saw in heaven?
Questions.A: He saw the sacred chest/box that held God's covenant. (19)

Questions.Q: What do you think a covenant is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Here it refers to the agreement made at the time of Moses. A covenant is a strong, binding agreement made between two people, an act in which they commit themselves to one another. In the case of the covenant which God has made with his people, God is the initiator of the covenant; it is he who makes a promise and states the terms. (It is not a negotiated agreement between two equal parties in which terms are discussed until agreed upon.)
Questions.Note: See "covenant" in KBT.

Section.heading: Revelation 12:1-17 John saw a vision of a woman and a huge red dragon.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what John wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: He wrote about a pregnant woman who gave birth to a son and a dragon who wanted to kill the child and the woman. (2, 4)

Questions.Q: What sign/amazing sight appeared in heaven?
Questions.A: It was a woman who was clothed with the sun.
The moon was under her feet.
A crown of twelve stars was on her head. (1)
She was pregnant and was about to give birth. (2)
Questions.Alternative: What sign appeared in heaven?
What amazing sight appeared in heaven?

Questions.Q: What do you think a sign is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Like the English word "sign," the Greek word sêmeion is used to refer to all kinds of signs, such as signs or marks that distinguish one thing from another, or signs that give a warning. But "sign" is also used for several kinds of miraculous signs. In this verse it means a miraculous picture in the sky that shows how God is working in the world.
Questions.Note: See "sign" in KBT in the "miracle" entry.

Questions.Q: What was the next sign/sight that appeared in heaven?
Questions.A: It was a huge red dragon with seven heads and ten horns and seven crowns on his heads. (3)
Questions.Alternative: What was the next sign that appeared in heaven?
What was the next sight that appeared in heaven?

Questions.Q: What did the dragon do with his tail?
Questions.A: He swept a third of the stars out of the sky and threw them down to earth. (4)

Questions.Q: What did the dragon want to do?
Questions.A: He wanted to devour/eat up the child that was to be born to the woman. (4)

Questions.Q: To what kind of child did the woman give birth?
Questions.A: She gave birth to a son. (5)

Questions.Q: What will her son do?
Questions.A: He will rule the earth with a rod of iron/with complete authority. (5)

Questions.Q: What happened to the child?
Questions.A: [God] took him up to be with him and his throne/and sit beside him on his throne. (5)

Questions.Q: What happened to the woman who had just given birth?
Questions.A: She ran to a place in the desert that God had prepared for her. (6)

Questions.Q: What happened to her there?
Questions.A: [God] took care of her there for 1260 days. (6)

Questions.Q: Who won the war in heaven?
Questions.A: Michael and his angels won the war over the dragon and his angels. (7-8)

Questions.Q: What happened to the dragon and his angels, when they lost the battle with Michael and his angels in heaven?
Questions.A: [Michael and his angels] threw them out of heaven down to the earth. (9)

Questions.Q: What other names does the dragon have?
Questions.A: He is also named the devil and Satan. (9)

Questions.Q: For what reason were those in heaven rejoicing?
Questions.A: They were rejoicing, because the accuser of the Christians/brothers had been thrown out of heaven [by Michael and his angels]. (10)

Questions.Q: Who do you think the accuser is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The accuser is another expression that is used to refer to Satan. (See "accuser" in KBT in the "Satan" entry.)

Questions.Q: How were the Christians able to defeat the devil?
Questions.A: They defeated him by the blood of the Lamb/by the death of Jesus
and because they continued to believe what Jesus taught them. (11)

Questions.Q: For what reason will it be terrible for the people on earth?
Questions.A: It will be terrible, because the devil has gone down to the earth and he is very angry. (12)

Questions.Q: For what reason is the devil very angry?
Questions.A: He is angry, because he knows that his time is short/limited. (12)

Questions.Q: What did the dragon do, after he realized that he had been thrown down to the earth [by Michael and his angels]?
Questions.A: He pursued the woman, who had given birth to the boy. (13)
Questions.Alternative: What did the dragon do, after he realized that he had been thrown down to the earth by Michael and his angels?
What did the dragon do, after he realized that he had been thrown down to the earth?

Questions.Q: How did the woman escape the serpent?
Questions.A: [God or an angel] gave her two wings of a large eagle to fly to a place in the desert that [God] prepared for her where the serpent could not reach her. (14)

Questions.Q: How long will she stay in this place?
Questions.A: She will stay there for three and a half years and [God] will take care of her. (14)

Questions.Q: How did the serpent try to kill the woman?
Questions.A: He tried to drown her by spitting out a large amount of water out of his mouth. (15)

Questions.Q: How did the earth help the woman?
Questions.A: [God] caused a big hole to open in the earth, and the water went down the hole. (16)

Questions.Q: When the dragon could not kill her, what did he do next?
Questions.A: He went to fight against her offspring/descendants. (17)

Questions.Q: Who are those people/her offspring/descendants?
Questions.A: They are people who keep God's commands and who follow/believe the message about Jesus. (17)
Questions.Alternative: Who are those people?
Who are her offspring?
Who are her descendants?

Questions.Q: What do you think a commandment is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It is a definite and official order given by one person to another to carry out.

Section.heading: Revelation 13:1-10 John saw a vision of a beast coming out of the sea.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what John wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: He wrote about a beast that came out of the sea. The beast had authority to make war against those people who followed God. Everyone except God's people worshiped the beast. (, -8)

Questions.Q: What did the beast which John saw look like?
Questions.A: The beast had ten horns and seven heads.
There were ten crowns on his horns.
Each head had a blasphemous name on it. (1)
The beast resembled a leopard, he had feet like a bear and a mouth like a lion. (2)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to blaspheme?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means to insult someone. When someone says or writes something that is blasphemous, they are saying or writing irreverent or evil things about God.

Questions.Q: Where did this beast get all his power and authority?
Questions.A: The beast got his power and authority from the dragon. (2)

Questions.Q: What wound did the beast have?
Questions.A: One of his heads had a fatal wound, but the wound had healed. (3)

Questions.Q: What did all the people in the world think about the beast?
Questions.A: They all were amazed at the beast and they considered him as their god. (3)

Questions.Q: For what reason did people worship the dragon?
Questions.A: They worshiped him, because he had given authority to the beast [to rule people]. (4)

Questions.Q: Whom else did they worship?
Questions.A: They worshiped the beast by asking, "Who is like the beast? Who can make war against him?" (4)
Questions.Note: This is a rhetorical question. They believed that no one was like the beast and no one could fight against him.

Questions.Q: What kind of things did [God] allow the beast to say?
Questions.A: He said proud/boastful things and insulted God. (5-6)
Questions.Alternative: What kind of things did God allow the beast to say?
What kind of things was the beast allowed to say?

Questions.Q: How long did [God] allow the beast to have authority?
Questions.A: [God] allowed him to have authority for forty-two months. (5)
Questions.Alternative: How long did God allow the beast to have authority?
How long was the beast allowed to have authority?

Questions.Q: What power and authority did [God] give to the beast?
Questions.A: [He] gave the beast the power to fight the Christians and defeat them,
and he gave him authority over every tribe, people, language and nation. (7)
Questions.Alternative: What power and authority did God give to the beast?
What power and authority was given to the beast?

Questions.Q: Who will worship the beast?
Questions.A: All those people whose names are not in the book of life will worship the beast. (8)

Questions.Q: What is the book of life?
Questions.A: The book in which [God] has written the names of Christians is the book of life. (8)

Questions.Q: What will believers need during that time?
Questions.A: They will need to endure and continue faithful to [Christ]. (10)

Section.heading: Revelation 13:11-18 John saw a vision of a beast coming out of the earth.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what John wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: He wrote about the second beast which he saw and the things that the beast did.

Questions.Q: What did the second beast, which John saw, look like and sound like?
Questions.A: He had two horns like a Lamb has two horns.
He spoke like a dragon. (11)

Questions.Q: What did the beast make all the people do?
Questions.A: He made them worship the first beast. (12)

Questions.Q: What kind of things did the beast do to show that he had power?
Questions.A: He did various miracles, like making fire come down from heaven to earth. (13)

Questions.Q: How was the second beast able to deceive the people on the earth?
Questions.A: The beast could deceive people by the miracles [God allowed] him to do. (14)

Questions.Q: What did the second beast order the people to do?
Questions.A: The second beast made people set up an image of the first beast to honor him. (14)

Questions.Q: What did [God] allow the second beast to do?
Questions.A: [God] allowed him to breathe life into the image, so that he could talk and kill anyone who would not worship him. (15)
Questions.Alternative: What did God allow the second beast to do?
What was the second beast allowed to do?

Questions.Q: What did the second beast force all people to do?
Questions.A: He forced them to receive a mark on their right hand or on their forehead. (16)

Questions.Q: What was the purpose of having this mark?
Questions.A: Only people who had the mark could buy or sell anything. (17)

Questions.Q: What does the mark represent?
Questions.A: It represents the name of the [first] beast, or the number of his name. (17)

Questions.Q: What is the mark that people will be forced to have?
Questions.A: It is 666,
and it is also the number of a man. (18)

Section.heading: Revelation 14:1-5 John saw a vision of a Lamb and 144,000 men standing on Mount Zion.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what John wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: He wrote about the 144,000 people he saw standing with the Lamb. (1)

Questions.Q: What did [an angel or God] write on the foreheads of the 144,000 people with the Lamb?
Questions.A: [He] wrote the name of the Lamb and God's name. (1)
Questions.Alternative: What did an angel or God write on the foreheads of the 144,000 people with the Lamb?
What did an angel write on the foreheads of the 144,000 people with the Lamb?
What did God write on the foreheads of the 144,000 people with the Lamb?
What was written on the foreheads of the 144,000 people with the Lamb?

Questions.Q: What sounds did John hear coming from heaven?
Questions.A: He heard sounds like the roar of rushing waters,
and like the sound of loud thunder,
and like people playing their harps. (2)

Questions.Q: What were all those people doing?
Questions.A: They were singing a new song in front of the throne, the four living creatures and the elders. (3)

Questions.Q: Who could learn this song?
Questions.A: The only ones who could learn the song were the 144,000 people. (3)

Questions.Q: Who were those 144,000 people?
Questions.A: They were the ones from the earth whom [God] had saved from their sins. (3)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to redeem someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: With only one or two exceptions, in the New Testament the words "to redeem", "redemption", "ransom" refer to Christ's action in giving up his own life in order that those who believe in him may be forgiven their sins.
Questions.Note: See "redeem" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did John say about those people?
Questions.A: He said that they had never practiced evil with women.
They follow the Lamb wherever he goes/they are faithful disciples of his.
They wanted to do completely as God and the Lamb desired. (4)
They never lied.
People say that they only do good deeds. (5)

Section.heading: Revelation 14:6-13 John saw a vision of three angels, each of whom told messages to the people who lived on the earth.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what John wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: He wrote about three angels whom he saw flying in the air. Each one of them had a different message to tell people/to deliver to people.

Questions.Q: What was the message of the first angel who flew through the air?
Questions.A: He had the unchangeable/eternal gospel to tell. (6)

Questions.Q: What do you think "eternal gospel" means?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means unchanging, a message that God wanted people to repent. It means that this message is valid forever. In this context, the "eternal gospel" refers to the call to fear God in verse 7; it also refers to "the gospel", otherwise it would not be described as "eternal". The gospel is described as "eternal," because it relates to God's unchanging purposes and will therefore always continue to be valid.
Questions.Note: See "gospel" in KBT.

Questions.Q: To whom did he tell his message?
Questions.A: His message was for every nation, tribe, language and people. (6)

Questions.Q: What did the first angel say to the people?
Questions.A: He told them to fear God, give him glory and worship him. (7)

Questions.Q: For what reason are they to do that?
Questions.A: They need to do what the angel said, because the time of his judgment/the time for God to judge all people has come. (7)

Questions.Q: What was the message of the second angel?
Questions.A: He said that Babylon, the great city, had fallen/no longer exists. (8)

Questions.Q: What did Babylon do to the nations?
Questions.A: The people of Babylon caused people everywhere to do much evil. (8)

Questions.Q: What did the third angel say would happen to anyone who worshiped the beast and his image and received the mark?
Questions.A: God will severely punish them.
God will punish them in a hot fire of sulfur. (9-10)
Questions.Alternative: What did the third angel say would happen to anyone who worshipped the beast and his image and received the mark?

Questions.Q: Who will see them being tormented?
Questions.A: The angels and the Lamb will see them. (10)

Questions.Q: How long will anyone be tormented, who worships the beast and his image, or who receives the mark?
Questions.A: They will be tormented forever. (11)

Questions.Q: What will the saints need to practice?
Questions.A: They will need to practice endurance believing in Jesus. (12)

Questions.Q: Who are those saints?
Questions.A: They are those people who obey God's commandments and are faithful followers of Jesus. (12)

Questions.Q: What did John hear the voice say?
Questions.A: The voice told him to write "[God] will look well on the dead who die in the Lord from now on." (13)

Questions.Q: What did the Spirit say?
Questions.A: He said, "Even though people kill them, they will be in heaven. God will reward them." (13)

Section.heading: Revelation 14:14-20 John saw a vision of an angel who killed people on the earth with a sharp sickle.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what John wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: He wrote about the vision of an angel with a sickle whom he saw kill people on the earth. (16)

Questions.Q: Whom did John see sitting on a cloud?
Questions.A: He saw a person "like a son of man"/our Messiah. (14)

Questions.Q: What did this person have on his head and in his hand?
Questions.A: He had a crown of gold on his head.
He had a sharp sickle in his hand. (14)

Questions.Q: What did the angel tell that person to do?
Questions.A: The angel told him to take his sickle and gather people together. (15)

Questions.Q: Then what did the person on the cloud do?
Questions.A: He swung his sickle over the earth and gathered people on the earth together. (16)

Questions.Q: What did another angel have?
Questions.A: He had a sharp sickle. (17)

Questions.Q: What did another angel, who had charge of the fire, do?
Questions.A: He told the angel who had the sharp sickle to gather the people together, [who had rejected Christ]. (18)

Questions.Q: Why was the angel supposed to do that?
Questions.A: He was supposed to do that, because the time had come [when God will kill the people]. (18)

Questions.Q: What did the angel, who had the sickle, do then?
Questions.A: He swung his sickle over the people on earth to gather them together; and he killed them [as God wanted them killed]. (19)

Questions.Q: What happened to the people?
Questions.A: They were killed. (20)

Questions.Q: What covered the ground?
Questions.A: Blood covered the ground for about 300 kilometers/about 200 miles. (20)

Section.heading: Revelation 15:1-8 John saw a vision of seven angels who were holding seven plagues (disasters).

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what John wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: He wrote about the seven angels whom he saw with the last seven plagues. (1)

Questions.Q: What else did John see besides the seven angels and the seven plagues?
Questions.A: He saw a sea of glass mixed with fire,
and next to it he saw those who had been victorious over the beast. (2)

Questions.Q: What were those victorious people singing?
Questions.A: They sang the song of Moses, servant of God, and the song of the Lamb. (3)

Questions.Q: What did they sing about God?
Questions.A: They sang that his deeds are important and marvelous.
His ways are just and true. (3)
He alone is holy.
Everyone has seen his righteous acts/that he punished people according to what they did. (4)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to deal with someone else justly/in a just manner?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that someone is doing something in conformity with law or justice. It refers to God's faithful and consistent adherence to his covenant.
Questions.Note: See "just" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think it means for someone to deal with someone else justly?
What do you think it means for someone to deal with someone else in a just manner?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to be righteous?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that a person is in a state of having been accepted by God as right in his eyes. In this reference it refers to the fact that Christ was in the right with God. (See "righteousness" in KBT in the "just, justify..." entry.)

Questions.Q: What did John see next?
Questions.A: He saw in heaven the place where God is. (5)

Questions.Q: What do you think the tabernacle is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It is a place to worship God. The tabernacle was the portable sanctuary that the people of Israel built under God's direction in the early years of their history, while they were traveling in the wilderness. God was present in the tabernacle in a very special way. In some passages the reference is not to the man-made tabernacle which existed in this world, but to the corresponding tabernacle in heaven, the spiritual reality which the earthly tabernacle represents. (See "tabernacle" in KBT in the "tent" entry.)

Questions.Q: Who came out of the place where God is/temple?
Questions.A: The seven angels with the seven plagues came out of it. (6)
Questions.Alternative: Who came out of the place where God is?
Who came out of the temple?

Questions.Q: What were the angels wearing?
Questions.A: They were wearing clean, shining linen,
and they were wearing golden sashes around their chests. (6)

Questions.Q: What was in the seven golden bowls that one of the four living creatures gave to the seven angels?
Questions.A: That God was angry with people was represented as being in the seven bowls. (7)

Questions.Q: What happened to the temple?
Questions.A: It was filled with smoke from the brilliance and power of God. (8)

Questions.Q: For what reason could no one enter the temple?
Questions.A: No one could enter it until the seven plagues of the seven angels were completed. (8)

Section.heading: Revelation 16:1-21 The seven angels pour the seven plagues (disasters) down on the earth.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what John wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: He wrote about what happened after each of the seven angels poured out the contents of his bowl.

Questions.Q: What did the voice tell the seven angels to do?
Questions.A: It told the angels to pour the contents of the seven bowls of God's wrath on the earth. (1)

Questions.Q: What happened after the first angel poured out the contents of his bowl on the land?
Questions.A: Ugly and painful sores appeared on those people who had the mark of the beast and worshiped his image. (2)

Questions.Q: What happened after the second angel poured out the contents of his bowl on the sea?
Questions.A: The sea turned to blood and everything in it died. (3)

Questions.Q: What happened after the third angel poured out the contents of his bowl on the rivers and the springs?
Questions.A: The rivers and springs turned to blood. (4)

Questions.Q: For what reason did the angel say that God was just/fair in those punishments?
Questions.A: He said that, because people had killed the prophets and saints/people of God, they deserved those punishments. (5-6)
Questions.Alternative: For what reason did the angel say that God was just in those punishments?
For what reason did the angel say that God was fair in those punishments?

Questions.Q: What did John hear from the altar?
Questions.A: He heard [a voice] agree that God was true and just in his judgments. (7)

Questions.Q: What happened after the fourth angel poured out the contents of his bowl on the sun?
Questions.A: The sun became very hot and burned people severely. (8)

Questions.Q: What did the people do who had been burned?
Questions.A: They cursed God,
and they refused to repent and honor him. (9)

Questions.Q: What happened after the fifth angel poured out the contents of his bowl on the earth where the beast ruled people?
Questions.A: It became dark all over the earth. (10)

Questions.Q: What was the reaction of people to those punishments?
Questions.A: They gnawed/bit their tongues. (10)
They cursed God and refused to repent of the evil things they had done. (11)

Questions.Q: What happened after the sixth angel poured out the contents of his bowl on the Euphrates river?
Questions.A: The river dried up. (12)

Questions.Q: For what reason did that happen?
Questions.A: It happened so that the kings from the east could cross the river easily. (12)

Questions.Q: From where did the three demons come?
Questions.A: One came out of the mouth of the dragon, one came out of the mouth of the beast and one came out of the mouth of the false prophet. (13)

Questions.Q: What did the demons look like?
Questions.A: They looked like frogs. (13)

Questions.Q: What was the work of the three demons who appeared?
Questions.A: They went to gather together the kings of the whole world for the battle against God who will demonstrate that He is the most powerful one. (14)

Questions.Q: How did the [Lord] say he was coming?
Questions.A: [He] said he was coming like a thief. (15)
Questions.Alternative: How did the Lord say he was coming?
How did the say he was coming?

Questions.Q: Who did he say was to be well looked on [by Christ]?
Questions.A: [Christ] will look well on the one who is expecting his return and who is living as Christ desires. (15)
Questions.Alternative: Who did he say was to be well looked on by Christ?
Who did he say was to be well looked on?

Questions.Q: Where did they/the demons gather all the kings together?
Questions.A: They/the demons gathered them to a place called Armageddon. (16)
Questions.Alternative: Where did they gather all the kings together?
Where did the demons gather all the kings together?

Questions.Q: What happened after the seventh angel poured out the contents of his bowl into the air?
Questions.A: A loud voice from the temple said, "It is done!" (17)
There was lightning, thunder, and the worst earthquake the world had ever seen. (18)
The great city/Babylon split into three parts and the cities of the nations collapsed. (19)
All the islands and mountains were completely destroyed [by the earthquake]. (20)
Forty kilo hailstones fell on men. (21)

Questions.Q: What did the people do?
Questions.A: They insulted God because of the plague of hail. (21)

Section.heading: Revelation 17:1-18 John saw a woman riding on a beast that had seven heads and ten horns.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what John wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: He wrote about a woman whom he saw sitting on a scarlet beast. (3)

Questions.Q: What did one of the angels want to show to John?
Questions.A: The angel wanted to show him how [God] was going to punish the great prostitute. (1)

Questions.Q: What did the kings and the inhabitants do with the prostitute?
Questions.A: The kings did all kinds of evil along with her.
The inhabitants of the earth delighted to do the same kinds of evil that she did. (2)

Questions.Q: What did the angel do with John?
Questions.A: The angel carried him away in the Spirit into a desert. (3)
Questions.Note: UBS suggests saying, "The Spirit possessed me and the angel carried me off." Also see 21:10.

Questions.Q: What did the beast look like?
Questions.A: The beast was covered with names that insulted God,
and had seven heads and ten horns. (3)

Questions.Q: What was the woman wearing?
Questions.A: She was wearing purple and scarlet [clothes]
and gold [ornaments], precious stones and pearls. (4)

Questions.Q: What was in the golden cup that she was holding?
Questions.A: The contents of the cup represented all her evil deeds. (4)

Questions.Q: To what do you think he was referring by the "impurities"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "Impurities" in this verse refer to a state of contamination due to sinful behavior, making the person unfit for God's presence. (See "impure" in KBT in the "unclean" entry.)

Questions.Q: What evil things had the woman done?
Questions.A: She had killed those who followed Christ. // She was delighted to kill the saints. (6)

Questions.Q: How did John feel when he saw the woman?
Questions.A: John was greatly astonished/amazed/horrified/mystified. (6)

Questions.Q: What did the angel tell John that he would explain to him?
Questions.A: He told John that he would explain the mystery of the woman and the beast which she rides. (7)

Questions.Q: What did the angel say about the beast?
Questions.A: He said that the beast once was [alive], but [that he] is now [dead], and will come up out of the Abyss and [that he] will eventually be destroyed by [Christ]. (8)

Questions.Q: Who will be astonished when they see the beast?
Questions.A: All those people whose names are not written in the book of life will be astonished. (8)

Questions.Q: For what reason will they be astonished to see the beast?
Questions.A: They will be astonished, because it once was [alive], but is now [dead], and it will live again. (8)

Questions.Q: What are the seven heads of the beast?
Questions.A: They are seven hills and also seven kings. (9)

Questions.Q: What has happened to those kings?
Questions.A: Five of them have fallen/died.
One is king now,
and the other one has not yet come/appeared. (10)

Questions.Q: What is the beast?
Questions.A: It is an eighth king. (11)

Questions.Q: What are the ten horns?
Questions.A: They are ten kings who do not have a kingdom, but will rule people in the future. (12)

Questions.Q: What will these kings receive [from the beast]?
Questions.A: They will receive authority to become kings for one hour/for one hour to be kings. (12)
Questions.Alternative: What will these kings receive from the beast?
What will these kings receive?

Questions.Q: What will those ten kings do with their power?
Questions.A: They will make war against the Lamb. (14)

Questions.Q: Who will win this war?
Questions.A: The Lamb and his called, chosen and faithful followers will win. (14)

Questions.Q: Who is the Lamb?
Questions.A: He is the Lord of lords and King of kings. // He is the supreme one. (14)

Questions.Q: What are the waters where the prostitute sat?
Questions.A: They are people, multitudes, nations and languages. // They represent all the people of the earth. (15)
Questions.Note: See comment at 5:9.

Questions.Q: How will the beast and the ten horns feel about the prostitute?
Questions.A: They will hate her. (16)

Questions.Q: What will the beast and the ten horns do to the prostitute?
Questions.A: They will take away all her belongings and completely destroy her.
They will leave nothing in the city, as though they had killed and eaten the people of the city. (16)

Questions.Q: What do you think "flesh" means in this verse?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: This is not a literal eating, but a way to describe destruction. In this verse it means the muscle and sinew, the substance that covers the bones of a human body.
Questions.Note: See "flesh" in KBT.

Questions.Q: For what reason will the ten horns/kings want to do those things?
Questions.A: God put the desire into their hearts to do those things, in order to accomplish his purpose. (17)
Questions.Alternative: For what reason will the ten horns want to do those things?
For what reason will the ten kings want to do those things?

Questions.Q: What does the woman represent?
Questions.A: She represents the great city that rules over the kings of the earth. (18)

Section.heading: Revelation 18:1-24 God will destroy the city of Babylon.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what John wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: He wrote that [God] will destroy the city of Babylon.

Questions.Q: Who is the one that announced the fall/destruction of Babylon?
Questions.A: An angel, who had great authority and who shown very brightly, announced it. (1-2)
Questions.Alternative: Who is the one that announced the fall of Babylon?
Who is the one that announced the destruction of Babylon?

Questions.Q: What things did the angel say were living in Babylon?
Questions.A: He said that demons, and birds which people consider taboo were living there. (2)

Questions.Q: What do you think that demons and evil spirits are?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The terms "evil spirit", "unclean spirit", and "demon" are used interchangeably in the New Testament. They all refer to spiritual beings who serve Satan as his agents, being under his authority. These spiritual beings have power to oppress a human being and even take control of him.
Questions.Note: See "evil spirit" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Who are the ones who have benefited from this city?
Questions.A: The nations of the earth, the kings of the nations, and the merchants benefited. (3)

Questions.Q: What did another voice urge the people [of God] to do?
Questions.A: The voice urged them to leave the city. (4)
Questions.Alternative: What did another voice urge the people of God to do?
What did another voice urge the people to do?

Questions.Q: For what reason did they need to leave the city?
Questions.A: They needed to leave the city so that they did not do evil deeds.
Then God will not punish them as he does the wicked people. (4)

Questions.Q: What was the attitude of the people in that city?
Questions.A: They were proud; they thought that they could not be damaged or destroyed by anything/anyone. (7)

Questions.Q: What will happen to that city?
Questions.A: God will punish the people. They will be hungry. They will die. God will cause others to burn the city. (8)

Questions.Q: What will the kings of the earth feel, when the city is destroyed?
Questions.A: They will weep and mourn. (9)
They will be amazed that it could happen so quickly to such a powerful city. (10)

Questions.Q: For what reason will the merchants feel sad, when the city is destroyed [by God]?
Questions.A: They will feel sad, because no one will buy their cargo/goods anymore. (11)
Questions.Alternative: For what reason will the merchants feel sad, when the city is destroyed by God?
For what reason will the merchants feel sad, when the city is destroyed?

Questions.Q: For what reason will those people, who earn their living from the sea (i.e., captains, sailors, ship owners and all those who travel by ship), feel sad, when the city is destroyed [by God]?
Questions.A: They will be sad because they will lose customers for their trade and so lose money. (15-17)
Questions.Alternative: For what reason will those people, who earn their living from the sea (i.e., captains, sailors, ship owners and all those who travel by ship), feel sad, when the city is destroyed by God?
For what reason will those people, who earn their living from the sea (i.e., captains, sailors, ship owners and all those who travel by ship), feel sad, when the city is destroyed?

Questions.Q: For what reason will they throw dust on their heads?
Questions.A: They will do that to show their sadness. (19)

Questions.Q: For what reason will the saints, apostles and prophets rejoice over the destruction of that city?
Questions.A: They will rejoice, because God has punished Babylon for the way the evil people treated them. (20)

Questions.Q: What did the angel do?
Questions.A: He picked up a large heavy stone and threw it into the sea. (21)

Questions.Q: For what was this action a sign/symbol?
Questions.A: It was a way to show that God will destroy that city quickly and that the city will disappear forever. (21)
Questions.Alternative: For what was this action a sign?
For what was this action a symbol?

Section.heading: Revelation 19:1-10 John heard what sounded like a large crowd of people praising God in heaven.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what John wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: He wrote about a large crowd that was praising God. (1)

Questions.Q: What did John hear in heaven?
Questions.A: He heard the roar of a large multitude/crowd of people shouting. (1)

Questions.Q: For what reason were they shouting?
Questions.A: They were praising God for destroying the wicked city. (2-3)

Questions.Q: What did the twenty-four elders and the four living creatures do?
Questions.A: They bowed down and worshiped God. (4)

Questions.Q: Who told others to praise God?
Questions.A: A voice [perhaps an angel] that came from the throne told his servants to praise him. (5)

Questions.Q: What did John hear?
Questions.A: He heard a great multitude/crowd of people shouting. (6)

Questions.Q: What did the multitude/shouting sound like?
Questions.A: They/It sounded like rushing waters and thunder. (6)
Questions.Alternative: What did the multitude sound like?
What did the shouting sound like?

Questions.Q: What great event was about/going to take place?
Questions.A: There was to be a wedding between the Lamb and his bride/Christians. (7)
Questions.Alternative: What great event was about to take place?
What great event was going to take place?

Questions.Q: What was the bride's clothing?
Questions.A: It was fine linen which was bright and clean. (8)

Questions.Q: What did this fine linen represent?
Questions.A: It represented the righteous acts good deeds that the Christians did to please God. (8)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to be righteous?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that a person is in a state of having been accepted by God as right in his eyes. (See "righteous" in KBT in the "just, justify..." entry.)

Questions.Q: Who did the angel say is considered as fortunate?
Questions.A: Those who are invited [by God] to the wedding feast of the Lamb will be fortunate. (9)

Questions.Q: For what reason did the angel not allow/let John worship him?
Questions.A: He told John not to worship him, because he was also a servant of God. (10)
Questions.Alternative: For what reason did the angel not allow John worship him?
For what reason did the angel not let John worship him?

Section.heading: Revelation 19:11-21 John saw a white horse with/and someone riding on it.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what John wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: He wrote about the rider on a white horse, and what he did to the beast and his army.

Questions.Q: Who is the rider on a white horse?
Questions.A: He is called the one who is trustworthy and the one who always tells the truth [about God]. (11)

Questions.Q: What things did John say about the rider?
Questions.A: He said he is just. (11)
His eyes are like blazing fire.
He has many crowns on his head.
He has a name written on him that only he knows. (12)
He has on a robe that has been dipped in blood.
His name is the one who tells the message about God. (13)

Questions.Q: Who was following the rider on a white horse?
Questions.A: The armies of heaven were following him. (14)

Questions.Q: What were the armies riding?
Questions.A: They also were riding on white horses. (14)

Questions.Q: What were the armies wearing?
Questions.A: They were wearing fine linen that was white and clean. (14)

Questions.Q: What object came from his mouth?
Questions.A: A sharp sword came from his mouth. (15)

Questions.Q: What will he do with the sword?
Questions.A: He will use it to kill his enemies. (15)

Questions.Q: What name is written on his robe and his thigh?
Questions.A: The name was "King of kings and Lord of lords." // "The supreme leader." // "The most powerful ruler and the greatest leader." (16)

Questions.Q: What did the angel say to the birds?
Questions.A: He called them to come to the great feast of God. (17)

Questions.Q: What will they eat at that feast?
Questions.A: They will eat the dead bodies of kings, generals, mighty men, horses and their riders, and all people, whether free or slave or/and important people and unimportant people. (18)

Questions.Q: Who was leading the armies that fought against the rider on the horse and his army?
Questions.A: The beast and the kings of the earth led the enemy armies. (19)

Questions.Q: What happened to the beast and the false prophet?
Questions.A: [The Lord] captured them and threw them alive into the lake of burning sulfur. (20)

Questions.Q: What happened to the rest of the kings and their armies?
Questions.A: The rider on the horse killed them with the sword in his mouth,
and their bodies were eaten by the birds. (21)

Section.heading: Revelation 20:1-6 John saw an angel tie up the Devil, and throw him into a very deep pit and lock it, so that the Devil could not deceive the people for one thousand years.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what John wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: He wrote about the angel that tied up Satan and threw him into the Abyss. (1-3)

Questions.Q: What did John see an angel do to Satan?
Questions.A: He saw an angel bind Satan for a thousand years. (2)

Questions.Q: What else did the angel do to Satan?
Questions.A: He threw Satan into the Abyss and locked and sealed it. (3)
Questions.Note: It may be necessary to combine verses 2 and 3, so that it will be understood that the angel bound Satan, threw him into the Abyss and locked it for a thousand years.

Questions.Q: What will happen to Satan after the thousand years are over?
Questions.A: He will be set free [by God] for a short time. (3)

Questions.Q: What did those people do who had stayed true to Jesus Christ and been killed for his sake?
Questions.A: They came to life and ruled with Christ for 1000 years. (4)

Questions.Q: When do the rest of the dead come back to life again?
Questions.A: They will come back to life again after the 1000 years are over. (5)

Questions.Q: Who are the people taking part in the first resurrection?
Questions.A: Those who have followed/trusted Jesus during their lifetime on earth will take part in the first resurrection. (5)

Questions.Q: What will be the reward for those in the first resurrection?
Questions.A: They will be fortunate and belong completely to him.
The second death has no power over them.
They will be priests of God and Christ. // They will have access to God and to Christ.
They will reign with him for 1000 years. (6)

Section.heading: Revelation 20:7-10 God will release Satan from his prison for a period of time, and he will go out to deceive the people. Then God will throw Satan into the lake of fire.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what John wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: He wrote about what Satan will do when [God] releases him from his prison. (7-8)

Questions.Q: What will Satan do when [God] releases him from his prison?
Questions.A: He will go around to deceive people in all nations and try to get them to fight against God's people. (7-8)
Questions.Alternative: What will Satan do when God releases him from his prison?
What will Satan do when he is released from his prison?

Questions.Q: What did the armies of Satan do?
Questions.A: They marched across the earth and surrounded the camp of God's people. (9)

Questions.Q: What happened to the armies of Satan?
Questions.A: Fire came out of heaven and destroyed them. (9)

Questions.Q: What happened to Satan?
Questions.A: [The Lord] threw Satan into the lake of fire, to join the beast and the false prophet. (10)

Section.heading: Revelation 20:11-15 John saw God sitting on his large white throne and he saw God judge all of the dead people according to what they had done.

Questions.Q: In your own words tell the basic meaning (theme) of what John wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: He wrote about the time when God will judge all people according to what is written in his books about each person. (12)

Questions.Q: What did John see?
Questions.A: He saw a large white throne and [God] sitting on it. (11)

Questions.Q: What fled from his presence?
Questions.A: Earth and heaven fled from his presence. (11)

Questions.Q: Who were the ones being judged [by God]?
Questions.A: They were all the people of the world who had died. (12)
Questions.Alternative: Who were the ones being judged by God?
Who were the ones being judged?

Questions.Q: What happened to death and Hades?
Questions.A: [The Lord] threw them into the lake of fire. (14)

Questions.Q: What is the second death?
Questions.A: The lake of fire is the second death. (14)

Questions.Q: Whom did [the angels] throw into the lake of fire?
Questions.A: They threw into the lake of fire all those people whose names were not written in the book of life. (15)
Questions.Alternative: Whom did the angels throw into the lake of fire?
Who was thrown into the lake of fire?

Section.heading: Revelation 21:1-27 John saw a new heaven, a new earth and the new Jerusalem.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what John wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: He wrote about the new heaven, the new earth, and the new Jerusalem.

Questions.Q: What happened to the first heaven and the first earth?
Questions.A: They passed away/disappeared. (1)

Questions.Q: What replaced the first heaven and the first earth?
Questions.A: A new heaven and a new earth replaced them. (1)

Questions.Q: What came down out of heaven?
Questions.A: The Holy City, the new Jerusalem came down out of heaven. (2)

Questions.Q: Where will God live?
Questions.A: He will live with people. (3)

Questions.Q: What will God change for the people with whom he will live?
Questions.A: No one will die. People will not be sad, nor cry, nor have pain. (4)

Questions.Q: What is the one on the throne offering to anyone who is thirsty/wants to live forever?
Questions.A: He will cause them to live forever. (5-6)
Questions.Alternative: What is the one on the throne offering to anyone who is thirsty?
What is the one on the throne offering to anyone who wants to live forever?

Questions.Q: Who will be the ones to benefit from all this new order of things?
Questions.A: Those who overcome [the forces of evil] will benefit. (7)

Questions.Q: Who will be put into the lake of fire?
Questions.A: The cowards,
those who don't believe God,
who murder,
commit immorality,
practice magic,
tell lies,
and worship other gods will be there in the lake of fire. (8)

Questions.Q: What did the angel want to show to John?
Questions.A: He wanted to show him the bride, the wife of the Lamb. (9)

Questions.Q: What happened to John?
Questions.A: One of the angels carried him away to a mountain, as/because God's Spirit controlled John. (10)

Questions.Q: What did the angel show to him?
Questions.A: He showed John the Holy City, Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God. (10)

Questions.Q: What did the city look like?
Questions.A: It was shining with the presence of God. Its brilliance was like that of a precious jewel like jasper. (11)
It had a high wall around it and twelve gates, with an angel at each gate.
There were three gates on each side,
and each gate had the name of one of the tribes of Israel written on it. (12-13)
The wall of the city had twelve foundations which had the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb. (14)

Questions.Q: What did the angel have?
Questions.A: He had a gold measuring rod to measure the whole city, including its gates and walls. (15)

Questions.Q: What was the shape of that city?
Questions.A: It was square. Its length, width and height were the same. (16)

Questions.Q: How thick were the walls?
Questions.A: They were 66 meters/216 feet thick. (17)

Questions.Q: Of what was the city made?
Questions.A: The wall was made of jasper
and the city was made of pure gold. (18)
The foundations were decorated with different kinds of precious stones. (19-20)
Each of the twelve gates was made of a single pearl. (21)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means that something is pure?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that it is free from impurities, having nothing added or mixed in, unadulterated. (See "pure" in KBT in the "clean" entry.)

Questions.Q: For what reason is there no temple in the city?
Questions.A: No temple is needed, because God and the Lamb are its temple. (22)

Questions.Q: For what reason is there no need for the sun or the moon to give light?
Questions.A: The presence/brilliance of God and of Jesus Christ will provide the city with light. (23)

Questions.Q: What will the people of the world live in?
Questions.A: They will live in the light that shines from the city. (24)

Questions.Q: What will the kings of the earth bring into the city?
Questions.A: They will bring their glory/wealth into the city. (24)

Questions.Q: For what reason will the gates never be closed?
Questions.A: The gates will never be closed, because it will never be night there. (25)

Questions.Q: What will the peoples of the world bring into the city?
Questions.A: They will bring their wealth and valuable gifts into the city. (26)

Questions.Q: Who will live in that city?
Questions.A: Only those people whose names are written in the Lamb's book of life will live there or even enter there. (27)

Section.heading: Revelation 22:1-6 An angel showed John the river of life.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what John wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: He wrote about the things the angel showed to him.

Questions.Q: What did the angel show to John?
Questions.A: The angel showed him the river whose water causes those who drink from it to live forever. (1)

Questions.Q: What was standing on either side of the river?
Questions.A: The tree of life stood on either side of the river. (2)

Questions.Q: For what are the leaves of the tree used?
Questions.A: They are used to make the people happy and contented. (2)

Questions.Q: What will not be in the city?
Questions.A: Nothing that is under God's curse/God declares to be unacceptable will be in the city. (3)

Questions.Q: What will be in the city?
Questions.A: The throne of God and the Lamb will be in the city. (3)

Questions.Q: Who will serve him/God?
Questions.A: His servants/all the inhabitants of the city will serve him. (3)
Questions.Alternative: Who will serve him?
Who will serve God?

Questions.Q: What will be on the foreheads of God's servants?
Questions.A: His name will be on their foreheads. (4)

Questions.Q: For what reason will they not need a lamp or the sun for light?
Questions.A: They will not need a lamp or the sun for light because God will give them light. (5)

Questions.Q: How long will they reign?
Questions.A: They will reign forever. (5)

Questions.Q: What did the angel tell John that was really true and to be trusted?
Questions.A: He told him that the words [of this book] he has been hearing and seeing are true. (6)

Section.heading: Revelation 22:7-21 Jesus promised to return soon.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what John wrote in these verses.
Questions.A: He wrote about the fact that Jesus is coming soon. He wrote about who will be allowed into the city and who will not be allowed into it.

Questions.Q: Who did Jesus say will be helped much by God?
Questions.A: Those who follow/obey the words written in this book will be helped by God. (7)

Questions.Q: Whom did John attempt to worship?
Questions.A: John wanted to worship the angel who had been showing him all of these things. (8)

Questions.Q: What did the angel tell John?
Questions.A: He told John not to worship him, since he was a fellow servant with John. (9)

Questions.Q: Whom did the angel tell John to worship?
Questions.A: He told John to worship God. (9)

Questions.Q: What did the angel tell John to do with the words of prophecy in this book?
Questions.A: He told John not to seal/hide them. (10)

Questions.Q: For what reason was John not to seal the words?
Questions.A: He was not to seal the words, because the time is near/because everything will happen soon. (10)

Questions.Q: What are people told to do?
Questions.A: People are told to continue doing what they have been doing. (11)
Questions.Note: UBS states people are told to continue doing what they have been doing, since there is no time left for anyone to change their way of living.

Questions.Q: What message does Jesus repeat?
Questions.A: He repeated that he is coming back soon. (12)

Questions.Q: How will he reward everyone?
Questions.A: He will reward everyone according to what each person has done. (12)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus say about himself?
Questions.A: He said that he always existed and will always exist. (13)

Questions.Q: Who are those people whom God will help?
Questions.A: They are those who have asked God to forgive their sins and who have the right to the tree of life and the right to enter the city. (14)

Questions.Q: What kind of people are not allowed inside the holy city?
Questions.A: They are the dogs/depraved,
sorcerers,
the immoral,
murderers,
those who worship other gods
and liars. (15)

Questions.Q: Who is it that has given John this information to pass on to others?
Questions.A: Jesus has given it to John through his angel. (16)

Questions.Q: What relationship does Jesus have with David?
Questions.A: Jesus is a descendant of David. // David was an ancestor of Jesus. (16)

Questions.Q: Who will be able to drink the water of life/receive eternal life?
Questions.A: Anyone who wants to know God will be able to drink/receive eternal life. (17)
Questions.Alternative: Who will be able to drink the water of life?
Who will be able to receive eternal life?

Questions.Q: What will happen to anyone who adds anything to the words of this book?
Questions.A: God will add the plagues in this book to him. // God will punish him with the plagues in this book. (18)

Questions.Q: What will happen to anyone who takes away words from this book?
Questions.A: God will take away his share in the tree of life and in the holy city. // God will take away his right to eat the fruit of the tree of life and to enter the holy city. (19)

Questions.Q: Who says again that he is coming soon?
Questions.A: Jesus does. (20)

Questions.Q: What did John desire for all of God's people?
Questions.A: He desired that the Lord Jesus would show his great love to them all. (21)

Questions.Q: What is Paul's work?
Questions.A: Paul's work was, in Christ's name, to call the non-Jews of this world to believe in Christ.

Questions.Q: What does Paul think about his own position as an apostle/representative of Christ?
Questions.A: He is not worthy of it, but God chose him to do this work
Questions.Alternative: What does Paul think about his own position as an apostle of Christ?
What does Paul think about his own position as a representative of Christ?

Questions.Q: What two things is Christ?
Questions.A: He is a human being, and he is the Son of God.

Questions.Q: What shows that he is human?
Questions.A: He is a descendant of King David.

Questions.Q: What shows that Jesus is also the Son of God and came from God?
Questions.A: The way God's Holy Spirit used his power to raise him from death.

Questions.Q: (a) What has God called Paul to become?
Questions.A: God has called Paul to be one of Christ's servants and representatives of God in telling the good news.

Questions.Q: (b) What has God called the people in Rome to become?
Questions.A: God called the people of Rome to be God's own people, whom he loves.

Section.heading: Romans 1:8-17 Paul prays that God will give him the chance to go to Rome to preach the gospel.

Questions.Q: What news makes Paul happy?
Questions.A: He has heard that everyone everywhere is speaking of how the people in Rome to whom he is writing have believed in Christ.

Questions.Q: What good example does Paul show us?
Questions.A: He prays for them every time he prays to God.
Questions.Note: (Note that he says the same thing to every church that he writes to.)

Questions.Q: What is his additional prayer?
Questions.A: If God agrees, God will give him the chance to go and visit them in Rome.

Questions.Q: Give 4 reasons why Paul wants to go to Rome.
Questions.A: 1. To cause the Roman Christians to get some blessings from the Holy Spirit that will make them strong in their faith.
2. That their faith will also encourage him.
3. That he might cause some of them to become true Christians in the way he had done among others who are non-Jews.
4. God has given him the work of preaching the good news to everyone, what ever their language and whether or not they are educated.

Questions.Q: Why is Paul never ashamed of preaching the Good News?
Questions.A: God uses the preaching of the Good News to save those who believe.

Questions.Q: What is a summary of the Good News?
Questions.A: It tells how God causes people to be good people according to him/in his sight.

Questions.Q: How is the Good News a matter of believing from start to finish?
Questions.A: God calls people good as soon as they become Christians. As they go on believing in him, he calls them good until their lives end.

Questions.Q: What is this quotation from Habakkuk 2:4?
Questions.A: If a person believes in God, God will call him a good person and will give him life.

Questions.Q: What particular kind of wickedness is God particularly angry about, according to Paul?
Questions.A: He is angry against those who prevent others from knowing the true way.

Questions.Q: In what way has everyone, who is not yet a Christian, nothing to stand on to say that he does not know who God is?
Questions.A: God has already revealed his truth to them because, from the time God created the world, they have seen everything that he has made that shows that he alone is a great King and also he has very great power that has no end.

Questions.Q: If men, knowing whom God is, ignore him, what is the result?
Questions.A: 1. They don't respect him.
2. They don't thank him.
3. They become stupid and no longer able to understand the truth.
4. They leave off worshiping the great God who lives forever, thinking they are wise, and come to worship things that they themselves have made that are like a person or a bird or an animal.

Questions.Q: What does God do to those who ignore him?
Questions.A: He leaves them to themselves, and no longer helps them.

Questions.Q: What is the result of God leaving them to themselves?
Questions.A: 1. They become ever more wicked.
2. They follow their own bad desires.
3. They do shameful things to one another.
4. They turn God's truth into a lie, worshiping things God has created instead of God the Creator.

Questions.Q: What particular sins are here condemned by God?
Questions.A: Homosexuality; i.e., men having sexual intercourse with men, and women loving women very much.

Questions.Q: What other sins do men and women do when they refuse God's truth?
Questions.A: Greed,
jealousy,
murder,
fighting,
lying,
hatred,
gossiping,
slandering,
hating God,
belittling others,
boasting,
increasing in evil thoughts,
disrespect of parents,
not knowing what is good,
breaking their word,
refusing friendship,
and being pitiless.

Questions.Q: What is the summary of their wickedness?
Questions.A: They know God's law forbids these things but they go on doing wrong and support others to do the same.

Section.heading: Romans 2:1-16 God will judge people well.

Questions.Q: If I accuse my fellow man of wrong doing, why am I also accusing myself?
Questions.A: I do the same things.
Questions.Alternative: If I accuse another person of wrong doing, why am I also accusing myself?
If I accuse another of wrong doing, why am I also accusing myself?
If I accuse others of wrong doing, why am I also accusing myself?
If I accuse someone of wrong doing, why am I also accusing myself?
If I accuse someone else of wrong doing, why am I also accusing myself?

Questions.Q: Why is God alone able to judge well?
Questions.A: He sees all, knows all, and is sinless himself.

Questions.Q: What does God do to those who accuse others but do the same kind of wrong?
Questions.A: He will punish them.

Questions.Q: If God does not immediately judge us for accusing others, what does that show?
Questions.A: It shows that he is patient with us and wants us to repent and turn from our sin.

Questions.Q: What happens to stubborn people who refuse to repent?
Questions.A: On the day of God's anger, when he comes to judge all people, he will punish them.

Questions.Q: What, according to God, is the way to get greatness, a name and eternal life?
Questions.A: Patiently doing good.

Questions.Q: What, according to God, is the way to get punished?
Questions.A: Being argumentative, refusing to do what is good, doing evil.

Questions.Q: If God does not judge with favoritism, how will he judge the Jews first before the non-Jews?
Questions.A: He will judge all according to their deeds. But as the Jews were God's own chosen people in the first place, if they reject him, their punishment is severe. See also verses 12-16.

Questions.Q: Will God use one law or two laws to judge men?
Questions.A: He will judge men according to their own laws that they have, the Jews by their law, non-Jews by their own laws.

Questions.Q: How will this help men to get salvation?
Questions.A: It will not help them. By whatever law men live, they are guilty, so God will condemn them.

Questions.Q: Can anyone follow any law completely?
Questions.A: No.

Questions.Q: Will God therefore call anyone a good person?
Questions.A: Only one who perfectly follows the law will God call righteous.

Questions.Q: Is it possible to do good without knowing God's law?
Questions.A: Yes, the laws of different tribes/peoples all contain some things that God says are good.

Questions.Q: Do all men have God's laws in their heads?
Questions.A: Paul shows that God has put into everyone's head some knowledge of what is good and bad, so that if they do good, they have some small defense, and if they do bad, they have no excuse.

Questions.Q: If all this is so, what need is there to learn all of God's laws?
Questions.A: Unless we accept God's way of saving us through Christ, Christ as judge will condemn us under whatever law we have lived, because none of us is perfect.
Questions.Alternative: So, what does a person really need to be justified and accepted in the sight of God?
On what basis will God judge people?
On what basis will God judge people, even if they did not know about his laws?

Questions.Q: What are the secrets that God will judge?
Questions.A: actions (especially sinful ones) that people have tried to keep other people from finding out
actions that other people did not know about, but God does know about
hidden motives or intentions of the heart that are known only to God and the person being judged
things a person said, thought or did that they believed to be wrong, thus violating their own conscience

Questions.Q: How does God know about these secrets?
Questions.A: God knows/sees everything. Nothing can be hidden from Him.
Questions.Alternative: Do you think God will have to ask people questions to find out about these secrets?
How will God discover these secrets?
How will God discover these secret actions, motivations, and matters of personal conscience?
What does this tell us about what God sees?
What does this tell us about what God knows about people?
What does this tell us about what God knows?

Section.heading: Romans 2:17-29 The Jews fail to follow their own law.

Questions.Q: In what way is it dangerous to be a Jew?
Questions.A: It is easy to become proud.

Questions.Q: What have Jews to be proud about in their own eyes?
Questions.A: 1. They think that if they follow God's law, God will call them righteous.
2. They know God's law, and so know what is right.
3. They say that because of this they can teach others who don't know God's laws.
Questions.Note: N.B.: Are these metaphors well understood-guide of the blind; light for those who live in darkness; a leader of the foolish and a teacher of children?

Questions.Q: So what is wrong with the Jews?
Questions.A: 1. They don't teach themselves God's law.
2. They themselves are guilty of such things as stealing, adultery, stealing from fetish places.
Questions.Note: N.B.: Is it clear that Paul says that these things are wrong?

Questions.Q: Discuss: As God forbids Christians to worship a fetish, should we destroy any fetish worship place, fetish, idol, charm, talisman that does not belong to us?
Questions.Alternative: Discuss: As God forbids Christians to worship idols, should we destroy any shrine, fetish, idol, charm, talisman that does not belong to us?

Questions.Q: Why do non-Jews/Gentiles sometimes speak against God?
Questions.A: Because Jews who say they follow God's law do not follow what they know and teach themselves. They are hypocrites.
Questions.Alternative: Why do non-Jews sometimes speak against God?
Why do Gentiles sometimes speak against God?

Questions.Q: How do you understand the meaning of circumcision?
Questions.A: All Jewish boys were circumcised at the age of 8 days. It showed that the Jews were God's people who were following his laws.

Questions.Q: Has circumcision any value?
Questions.A: Yes, if you follow that law you are a true Jew. But if you do not follow God's law, your circumcision will not save you from God's punishment.
Questions.Note: N.B.: Is this well understood?

Questions.Q: How can one who is not circumcised be more pleasing to God than a Jew who is circumcised?
Questions.A: If he follows God's law well, he is better then a Jew who fails to follow God's law.

Questions.Q: What is a true Jew?
Questions.A: One who is circumcised and follows God's law perfectly. His heart is clean and free from all evil.

Questions.Q: What is true circumcision?
Questions.A: It is not cutting of the foreskin, but cutting the evil out of ones heart.

Questions.Q: Can we be truly circumcised by following the law truly?
Questions.A: It is not possible to follow all the law perfectly. So it is God's Holy Spirit who must take the evil from our hearts. Cutting the foreskin is not necessary.

Section.heading: Romans 3:1-8 Will God do us good if we do wrong?

Questions.Q: In view of Paul's previous statements, did the Jews have any advantages more than the non-Jews?
Questions.A: Yes. It was the Jews that God first caused to understand this thought.

Questions.Q: Since some of the Jews refused to obey God, will God break his word and not fulfill his promises to them?
Questions.A: No.

Questions.Q: Why is it necessary to understand that God is never guilty of doing evil?
Questions.A: God is never guilty of doing evil because he is the judge of all people. Only a just judge can judge well.

Questions.Q: What is this false argument that people sometimes bring against God?
Questions.A: They say that if their wickedness shows well that God alone is good, then God should be happy. Therefore, he does wrong to punish wrongdoers.
Questions.Alternative: What is this false argument that people sometimes bring against God saying he will not be just if he condemns them in his judgment?
What is this false argument that people sometimes bring against God saying he will not be fair if he condemns them in his judgment?
What is this false argument that people sometimes bring against God saying he will not be just if he condemns them?
What is this false argument that people sometimes bring against God saying he will not be fair if he condemns them?
Why do some people falsely argue that it is not fair for God to condemn them?

Questions.Q: What is the answer to that?
Questions.A: Same as in verse 4.

Questions.Q: What lie does Paul condemn?
Questions.A: Paul condemns the lie that some people have said that Paul teaches that we should do wrong so that people will see that God is good.

Questions.Q: (See verse 3.) Does Paul contradict himself?
Questions.A: No. He says the Jews had the advantage of knowing God's thoughts, but all Jews and non-Jews alike are under the power of sin.

Questions.Q: What kind of sins are common to all people?
Questions.A: No one is good, no one understands, no one looks for God; all have gone astray and have become useless. No one does good.

Questions.Q: How do you understand these metaphors/proverbs?
Questions.A: People are liars and deceivers. They speak curses and bad words. They are killers/murderers.
Everywhere they go they spoil everything. They cannot live in peace. They don't fear God.
Questions.Alternative: How do you understand these metaphors?
How do you understand these proverbs?

Questions.Q: Discuss: To what extent is it true that all people have done wrong?
In these verses what is shown as the reason why God has given us laws?
Questions.A: God gave us laws to show that everyone in his heart is a sinner.

Questions.Q: How will all people answer to God at the day of Judgment?
Questions.A: No one can say anything to defend himself, because the law shows that in some way or other he has done wrong.

Questions.Q: What do you say to the man who says "I am good because I follow God's law"?
Questions.A: He must see that he can never fully do everything God wants, so he is a sinner.

Section.heading: Romans 3:21-31 God will call people righteous people.

Questions.Q: Is there an answer to the problem revealed in verses 19-20? Where is it found?
Questions.A: Yes. God has revealed it both in his law and through his prophets.

Questions.Q: How does God answer our problems in the law and prophets but not through the law?
Questions.A: They both speak about believing in the Christ whom God will send.

Questions.Q: How are all people alike in two ways?
Questions.A: God says that all people have sinned and are not worthy that God should praise them.
Likewise, God will call all people who believe in Jesus Christ good people.

Questions.Q: How did God buy people back from sin? Did he use money?
Questions.A: He did not use money. He caused Jesus Christ to become the payment to free people from their sins.

Questions.Q: How did God reconcile/repair the breach between man and God?
Questions.A: He offered Christ as a sacrifice so that his blood might repair the breach.
Questions.Alternative: How did God reconcile the breach between man and God?
How did God repair the breach between man and God?

Questions.Q: Does that mean that all men are now reconciled to God?
Questions.A: No.

Questions.Q: How do we then become reconciled to God?
Questions.A: We must believe what it says in these verses and put our trust in Jesus Christ.

Questions.Q: What does that do for us?
Questions.A: God counts that to us as good works.

Questions.Q: How does all this show the goodness of God?
Questions.A: 1. It shows that he judges correctly.
2. In the past he was very patient with the sin that people do.
3. Now he says that those who believe in Jesus are good people.

Questions.Q: What does a Christian have to boast about?
Questions.A: We cannot boast since we cannot follow all of God's law correctly. So God has provided another way, which is that we believe in Christ. If we believe in him, God will call us good people.

Questions.Q: For whom is this good news-Jews, non-Jews or whom?
Questions.A: It is for all people everywhere. God is concerned about people of all races.

Questions.Q: If we cannot follow God's law well, should we leave off following it?
Questions.A: No, for the law of God is still good.

Section.heading: Romans 4:1-25 The reason why God called Abraham a good person.

Questions.Q: Did the Jews' ancestor Abraham have any good works to boast of?
Questions.A: Yes, but that was not what made God pleased with him.

Questions.Q: Why did God call Abraham a good person?
Questions.A: Because he believed that God would do what he said that he would do.

Questions.Q: Will God reward us for our good works?
Questions.A: No, because we can never do enough to obey all of his law.

Questions.Q: Will God reward us anyway?
Questions.A: Even though we are sinners, he will declare us innocent and call us good people, if we do not rely upon our good works, but we rely only on our belief in God.

Questions.Q: What is it that God is in fact doing when he calls us good because we believe in him?
Questions.A: He has forgiven our sins.

Questions.Q: Who are the circumcised?
Questions.A: The Jews.

Questions.Q: Was it because Abraham was circumcised that God said he was a good person?
Questions.A: No.

Questions.Q: Why [did God say Abraham was a good person]?
Questions.A: It was because Abraham believed God, that God was pleased with him, and later he told Abraham to circumcise himself in order to show that he believed in God.
Questions.Alternative: Why?
Why did God say Abraham was a good person?
Why did God consider Abraham to be righteous?

Questions.Q: If Abraham was circumcised, how can he be the leader/first among those who are uncircumcised?
Questions.A: Because he believed God even before he was circumcised, and that is what pleased God.
Questions.Alternative: If Abraham was circumcised, how can he be the leader among those who are uncircumcised?
If Abraham was circumcised, how can he be the first among those who are uncircumcised?

Questions.Q: How should we imitate Abraham?
Questions.A: Not by being circumcised, but by believing God.

Questions.Q: How then can those who are circumcised please God?
Questions.A: They too should believe in God.

Questions.Q: In short, what does that say about the position of Abraham?
Questions.A: He is the man whose faith in God all people should imitate.

Questions.Q: What promise did God make to Abraham?
Questions.A: He would give the whole world to Abraham and his descendants.

Questions.Q: Why [did he/God promise to give the whole world to Abraham and his descendants]?
Questions.A: God made that promise with Abraham because of how he believed in God.
Questions.Alternative: Why?
Why did God promise to give the whole world to Abraham and his descendants?
Why did he promise to give the whole world to Abraham and his descendants?

Questions.Q: What would make our believing in God to be nothing for us?
Questions.A: If God broke his word and said that only those who follow the law will get the whole world.

Questions.Q: What one thing is certain that God's law promises?
Questions.A: God will punish wrong-doers.

Questions.Q: What are some of the ways of preventing law breaking?
Questions.A: 1. Canceling the law.
2. Canceling the punishment.
3. Forgiveness.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think are some of the ways of preventing "law breaking"?
What are some of the ways of eliminating the problem of law breaking?

Questions.Q: Which of these is Paul speaking about in this passage?
How can we get that forgiveness?
Questions.A: By believing in God.

Questions.Q: In what way did God make Abraham the father of many nations?
Questions.A: Any one who believes in God the way Abraham believed in God can call Abraham his father whether he is a Jew or not a Jew; there is no difference.
Questions.Alternative: In what way did God make Abraham the father of people who belong to many nations?
In what sense did God make Abraham the father of many nations?
In what sense did God make Abraham the father of people who belong to many nations?
How did God make Abraham the father of many nations?
How did God make Abraham the father of people who belong to many nations?

Questions.Q: What two things can God do that show his power?
Questions.A: 1. Raise the dead.
2. Create something out of nothing or call something that will be as if it already exists.

Questions.Q: What made God's promise to Abraham in verse 17 seem impossible?
Questions.A: Abraham was nearly 100 years old and nearly dead.
His wife Sarah was also very old and had never given birth.

Questions.Q: As Abraham and his wife got old and still did not have a child, how was his faith in God?
Questions.A: He did not stop believing but his faith increased and he praised God, completely believing that
God could do what he had promised to do, that is, give them a child.

Questions.Q: Why were these words written in God's word book?
Questions.A: Not just for Abraham but for us all.

Questions.Q: What is it that God asks us to believe that is now different from what he asked Abraham to believe?
Questions.A: Abraham was asked to believe that he would become the father of many nations.
We are asked to believe that God raised our Lord Jesus Christ from death.

Questions.Q: What else is important for us to believe?
Questions.A: God let men kill Jesus Christ because of our sins and he raised him from death so that he could call us good people.

Section.heading: Romans 5:1-11 There now is peace between us and God.

Questions.Q: What are the results of our believing in Christ?
Questions.A: 1. God calls us good people.
2. Christ has brought peace between us and God.
3. He has given us blessings.

Questions.Q: What remains that we do not yet have but that we will get from God?
Questions.A: What remains is the greatness/glory in his presence.

Questions.Q: Why should suffering as Christians make us happy?
Questions.A: Suffering as Christians should make us happy because it causes us to develop patience.

Questions.Q: Show how patience helps us grow as Christians. How do we grow in this way?
Questions.A: If we have patience, it shows that we have grown in our faith, and this gives us hope that we will get greatness in his presence. If we have this hope, we will not be ashamed that we have believed in him.

Questions.Q: How does God add to this hope that he gives us?
Questions.A: The Holy Spirit makes us understand the great love with which God loves us.

Questions.Q: What shows that God's love is great?
Questions.A: We were unable to leave off doing bad, but when God decided that the time had come, he sent
Christ to die for sinners.

Questions.Q: For what reason will one man die for another? Compare and contrast this with Christ's dying for us.
What person will die for a bad man? Compare and contrast this with Christ's dying for us.
Questions.A: It shows God's love for us that Christ came and died for us while we were still sinners.

Questions.Q: What two things has Christ's death and the shedding of his blood done for us?
Questions.A: 1. God now calls us good people.
2. God is prevented from being angry with us.

Questions.Q: How does Christ's life save us?
Questions.A: His death saved us. By his resurrection he proved this to be true. By his living now in our hearts he shows that he will save us completely.

Questions.Q: What gives us additional confidence that Christ will save us?
Questions.A: We have the additional confidence that Christ will save us by the fact that the reconciliation between us and God has made us happy.

Section.heading: Romans 5:12-21 Jesus is different from Adam.

Questions.Q: Why do all human beings die?
Questions.A: All human beings die because Adam sinned and so sin came into the world, and everybody ever since has sinned. So God said that because of this all human beings will die.
Questions.Note: N.B.: Is this well understood?

Questions.Q: What is the difference between a sinner and a breaker of God's law, according to these verses?
