Questions.A: Both do wrong against God. Both are disobedient to God. But those who disobeyed God before God's many laws were given to men through Moses, were not guilty of those laws which they had never heard of before.

Questions.Q: Does death have power over men also since the time of Moses?
Questions.A: Yes.
Compare and contrast the effect on human beings of Adam's sin, and Jesus death.
1. Through Adam being the first man to sin, many die.
2. Through Christ's death many get blessings, which are that God has mercy on many people and calls them good people.

Questions.Q: Show again how what Christ did is different from what Adam did.
Questions.A: 1. Adam sinned once and God condemned him.
2. But because of Christ's death God declares many sinners to be innocent.

Questions.Q: Again show the difference between what Adam did and what Christ did.
Questions.A: 1. Adam's sin caused all human beings to come under the power of death.
2. But Christ's death causes all those on whom he has mercy to live and reign as kings with Christ in heaven.

Questions.Q: What was the good thing that Christ did that gives everyone the chance to have life?
Questions.A: His dying for us has given everyone the chance to have life.

Questions.Q: Compare Adam's disobedience of God with Christ's obedience.
Questions.A: 1. Adam's disobedience caused many to become sinners.
2. Jesus's obedience caused many to be called by God good people.

Questions.Q: If man knew what sin was from Adam's time, why did God add many laws in Moses's time?
Questions.A: To show how that man's sins were many.

Questions.Q: How can God's law be the beginning of God calling us good people?
Questions.A: The law teaches us how sinful we are. If we then repent of our sin, God will have mercy on us.

Questions.Q: In short, what did Adam's sin do, and what did God's mercy do?
Questions.A: 1. Adam's sin caused all men to die.
2. God's mercy, through our Lord Jesus Christ, causes us to get eternal life.

Section.heading: Romans 6:1-14 Sin no more has power over us.

Questions.Q: What erroneous teaching does Paul speak against?
Questions.A: That we should go on sinning so that God will have mercy on us.

Questions.Q: How should we think of sin, now that we are Christians?
Questions.A: We should think of sin as dead, and so it has no more power over us.

Questions.Q: What is the meaning of baptism, according to these verses?
Questions.A: When we get baptized, we enter Christ's family and are united with him. It is like we died with him, were buried with him and were raised from death with him, and we live a new life with him.

Questions.Q: In what two ways are we united to Christ by baptism?
Questions.A: United in his death, united in his resurrection.

Questions.Q: In what way can we say that we have been crucified with Christ?
Questions.A: In baptism, it is as if we were crucified too, and the sin that is in us is killed and removed, so that now it no more has power over us.

Questions.Q: In what way is sin like a master and the sinner is like a slave?
Questions.A: Because, if sin has power over us, it is like a master has power over his slave.

Questions.Q: What assures us that we will live with Christ?
Questions.A: That sin was killed in us when we died with Christ.

Questions.Q: Since God raised Christ from death what does that teach us about Christ?
Questions.A: He will no more die.

Questions.Q: What do these verses say that Christ's death and resurrection have done?
Questions.A: By his death Christ has completely conquered sin. Now he is free to worship God in heaven.

Questions.Q: By becoming Christians have we completely conquered sin as Christ did?
Questions.A: No, but when we are tempted to sin, we should think of sin as dead and of no interest or value to us.

Questions.Q: Show how Paul is not just teaching a theory but he knows how powerful sin is.
Questions.A: Although we have become Christians, he tells us that it is still possible for us to give in to temptation and sin.

Questions.Q: What kinds of sin do you think that Paul is thinking of in this verse, that we should especially avoid?
Questions.A: Sins of the body, e.g., adultery and other sexual sins.

Questions.Q: How do we fight the temptation to commit sins of the body?
Questions.A: We should offer our bodies, our whole self, to work for God.

Questions.Q: What, according to this verse, no more has power over us?
Questions.A: God's law does not have power over us.

Section.heading: Romans 6:15-23 Now we are God's slaves.

Questions.Q: God's law no more has power over us. What does this mean? Are we then free to sin?
Questions.A: We do not follow the law in order to make God say that we are good. But because he has forgiven us through Christ and called us good people, now we love him and want to follow his law.

Questions.Q: What is the result of following sin?
Questions.A: God will drive you from his presence forever.

Questions.Q: What caused the people to whom Paul is writing to reject sin as their master?
Questions.A: They heard God's word from some people, and opened their hearts to follow it.

Questions.Q: What is the master that they are now serving?
Questions.A: Goodness/righteousness.

Questions.Q: Up to now has Paul been speaking in everyday life language or in elder's language?
Questions.Note: Note answers.

Questions.Q: How have the lives of the people to whom Paul is writing changed?
Questions.A: Formerly they used their bodies to do things which made their hearts dirty, and their wickedness increased. Now they should go on doing good so that their hearts will get very white.

Questions.Q: What does this show about their former way of life?
Questions.A: They did not follow good ways.

Questions.Q: If you look back on your life before you became a Christian, what do you see?
Questions.A: 1. You got no profit from it.
2. You are now ashamed of the things you did.
3. You realize that God was going to drive you from his presence forever.

Questions.Q: If that is not the way I see my former way of life, have I truly repented and become a Christian?
What is the result of our becoming slaves of God?
Questions.A: God will make our hearts white, and we will get everlasting life.

Questions.Q: How does sin pay wages, but God makes a gift?
Questions.A: If we sin, our wages/reward is that God will drive us from him forever. But God through our Lord Jesus Christ gives eternal life. It is not something that we deserve, but he is willing to give it, if we believe in Jesus Christ.

Section.heading: Romans 7:1-6 The law cannot bind one who is dead.

Questions.Q: Show from the example of a husband and wife how the law cannot bind a dead person.
Questions.A: If a woman's husband dies, she is no longer bound to him. She can marry another man.

Questions.Q: What does this say about divorce?
Questions.A: If a woman divorces her husband and marries another man while her former husband lives, she is committing adultery.

Questions.Q: What power has the death of Christ cancelled?
Questions.A: We are no longer under the law of God, i.e., the Old Testament Law of Moses, but under Christ's power.

Questions.Q: Show how in fact God's law caused us to sin in our old life.
Questions.A: The law said that this and this is not good. Those same things our hearts wanted to do. So we did much bad.

Questions.Q: What was the result of the sins that we were doing?
Questions.A: They cut us off from God.

Questions.Q: Under what law do we now live as Christians?
Questions.A: Christians live under the way/law of the Holy Spirit.

Section.heading: Romans 7:7-25 The law teaches us what sin is.

Questions.Q: Was the law that God gave through Moses good or bad?
Questions.A: Good

Questions.Q: Why [was the law that God gave through Moses good]?
Questions.A: Because it shows us what is bad, for example, it shows us that it is bad to covet our fellow man's things.
Questions.Alternative: Why?
Why was the law that God gave through Moses good?
Why was the Law good?

Questions.Q: What is the danger in knowing what coveting is?
Questions.A: It increases in us the desire to get more things.

Questions.Q: What is the difference between one who knows the law of God and one who does not know it?
Questions.A: The one who does not know it, thinks that his way of life is right, but one who knows the law sees that he is a sinner.

Questions.Q: What then are the two purposes of God's law?
Questions.A: 1. To show us what things are wrong.
2. To show us that, if we follow the law, we will live forever with God.

Questions.Q: Why then does Paul say that in fact the law shows him that it is right that God remove him from his presence forever?
Questions.A: Because he sees that it is impossible for him to follow all the law, therefore he is a sinner. Therefore, God will condemn him.

Questions.Q: So, if God's law leads to death, is it good?
Questions.A: It is bad desires that kill. They increase when we come to know that such desires are bad. But the law is good in every way.

Questions.Q: In short, what is the relationship between God's law and sin?
Questions.A: The law shows that sin is very bad, and that I myself am not good. So it also shows that the hope that I have that my way of life pleases God is finished, for it shows that God is not pleased with me.

Questions.Q: Where does that law come from?
Questions.A: That law comes from God's Spirit.

Questions.Q: Show how there is a fight happening in our hearts.
Questions.A: We do not understand what prevents us from doing good. We want to do good but cannot. What we hate, that same thing we do.

Questions.Q: How does this fight in our hearts show that God's law is good?
Questions.A: If we hate what God's law says is sin, it shows that we agree God's law is right and good.

Questions.Q: Who is to be blamed for the sin that is in our hearts, since Paul says that we desire to do good?
Questions.A: Bad desires cause us to sin, even though we really see that such desires are bad. But we cannot escape condemnation by blaming sin on the Devil. We are answerable to God for our sin.

Questions.Q: What do these verses add to those that have gone before?
Questions.A: They say the same thing, that is, that his bad desires fight his good desires, and it seems that his bad desires are winning.

Questions.Q: Has Paul any hope that he will defeat the sinful desires in his heart?
Questions.A: Yes, God, through Jesus Christ our Lord, can save him.

Section.heading: Romans 8:1-17 Let the Holy Spirit have control of your hearts.

Questions.Q: How do we get free from the law that condemns us? See chapter 7.
Questions.A: Since we are now in Christ Jesus's family, the law that comes from God's Holy Spirit sets us free and gives us eternal life.

Questions.Q: If the law cannot make us good people, what can?
Questions.A: God can do it.

Questions.Q: In short, what did God send Christ to do?
Questions.A: God sent Christ to live as a human being, to live a sinless life, and to offer himself as a sacrifice for our sins.

Questions.Q: Did God condemn Christ to death?
Questions.A: He sent Christ to die on our behalf, so that by his death all sinners might be set free from God's condemnation and punishment.

Questions.Q: What more does the death of Christ do for us?
Questions.A: We are now free to follow God's Holy Spirit, and we are now able to follow all the things that God's law says are right.

Questions.Q: What shows the difference between one who follows his sinful desires and one who follows the Holy Spirit?
Questions.A: Those who follow the Holy Spirit rest their thoughts on the things that the Spirit wants them to do.

Questions.Q: What is the result of our resting our thoughts on bad desires?
Questions.A: God will drive us from his presence forever.

Questions.Q: In what way can those who rest their thoughts on sinful desires please God?
Questions.A: They cannot please God.

Questions.Q: What will show that a person does not belong to God?
Questions.A: A person who does not belong to God does not have the Holy Spirit in his heart.

Questions.Q: What is the Spirit of Christ?
Questions.A: The Spirit of Christ is the same as the Spirit of God, the Holy Spirit.

Questions.Q: If Christ's Spirit is in our hearts, do we yet die?
Questions.A: Like all human beings we will die, but our souls will not die.

Questions.Q: What life does this verse refer to?
Questions.A: The Holy Spirit gives us new life now, and it will continue also after our bodies die.

Questions.Q: Give two reasons why we should leave following our own bad desires?
Questions.A: 1. If we do not leave them, God will drive us from his presence forever.
2. If we do leave them, we will get eternal life.

Questions.Q: What shows that we are God's children?
Questions.A: The Holy Spirit leads us/is with us.

Questions.Q: What kind of master is our God?
Questions.A: Not one whom we fear, as a slave fears a master but a father who loves his children. That is why we call him Father.

Questions.Q: How can we know for sure that God is our father?
Questions.A: The Holy Spirit works in our hearts telling us that this is true, and making us call God as our Father.

Questions.Q: Since we are God's children, what two things can we be sure of getting?
Questions.A: 1. The wealth that we will share with Christ in heaven when we die.
2. The same kind of sufferings on this earth before we die, as Christ suffered on earth.

Questions.Q: What gives us hope in our sufferings on this earth?
Questions.A: They are small compared with the glory/greatness that we will get in heaven.

Questions.Q: How is everything that God created waiting for something to happen to God's children?
Questions.A: Every created thing will live for a while and will spoil. This is God's plan. But when all the people who are to become God's children have come to be so, at the end of the world, everything will be released from decay. There will be a new creation which will not die or spoil, just like God's children.

Questions.Q: Why is our life as Christians like a woman who groans when she is about to give birth?
Questions.A: Because we suffer now, and look forward to the time when God will come and take us as his children and set us free from this world.

Questions.Q: If God has saved us, what are we still waiting for?
Questions.A: We are still waiting for the day that God will take us to himself in heaven.

Questions.Q: How should we be waiting for that day?
Questions.A: We should be waiting for that day with patience.

Questions.Q: What do you say to someone who says that he doesn't know how to pray?
Questions.A: God's Holy Spirit helps us in our weakness. He prays for us, using words that we cannot say, to cry begging God for us.

Questions.Q: Does that mean that we say nothing?
Questions.A: No, we say what we can. If our heart truly wants something from God, the Holy Spirit will speak for us as our representative using the right words.

Questions.Q: How is God pleased with that?
Questions.A: God the Father knows and understands what God the Holy Spirit is saying. And because the Holy Spirit asks God for those things which God himself wants to give, then God will answer those prayers.

Questions.Q: What great comfort does this verse give also?
Questions.A: Those who love God, whom God has chosen to do what God has decided that he should do.

Questions.Q: What is the destiny that God has given all Christians?
Questions.A: God has given all Christians the destiny that they should become the children of God and be like Jesus who will become their elder brother.

Questions.Q: How does God cause this destiny in fact to happen?
Questions.A: He calls them to come to him. When they come to him he makes them become good people. Having made them good, he gives them greatness.

Questions.Q: What shows that we are on the side of victory?
Questions.A: Since God has not refused to give us even his own son, he is certainly not against us but is with us, and so no one can do anything against us. Since he chose his Son to stand in and die for us, we should not be surprised that he would also give us more blessings in addition.

Questions.Q: When the Devil accuses us in our hearts of doing wrong, or other people accuse us of doing wrong, who is the judge who will settle our case?
Questions.A: Christ/God.
Questions.Alternative: When the Devil or other people accuse us of doing wrong, who is the judge who will settle our case?
When someone accuses us of doing wrong, who is the judge who will settle our case?

Questions.Q: Why [will Christ settle our case] / defend us [and say that we are not guilty]?
Questions.A: Christ is the judge who will settle our case because he died and rose again. He has reconciled us to God and is now praying for us in heaven.
Questions.Alternative: Why?
Why will Christ settle our case?
Why will Christ defend us?
Why will Christ defend us and say that we are not guilty?
Why will Christ settle our case and say that we are not guilty?
Why can no one condemn us?

Questions.Q: Can Christ ever stop loving us?
Questions.A: No.

Questions.Q: What would the sufferings that we may suffer do to our relationship with Christ?
Questions.A: Even if we stop loving Christ, he will no stop loving us.

Questions.Q: If we suffer persecution and death, how can we say that nothing will happen to us?
Questions.A: Whether we live or die we belong to Christ. He still loves us and this persecution will make our faith increase and so we will win against the Devil.

Questions.Q: Summarize what Paul is saying in these verses.
Questions.A: Nothing, whether good or bad, real or unreal, can stop God, through Christ, loving us.

Section.heading: Romans 9:1-18 If God does what he wants, what can we say?

Questions.Q: What caused Paul great sorrow?
Questions.A: His own people, the Jews caused Paul great sorrow.

Questions.Q: Why [did the Jews cause Paul great sorrow]?
Questions.A: Because most of them still refused to believe that Jesus was the Christ that they had been waiting for to save them.
Questions.Note: N.B.: Is this clear from the translation?

Questions.Q: Is the love that you have for your own tribe/nation as great as that of Paul for his own people?
Questions.Note: Personal question - answers will vary. If the translation is clear, most respondents will probably indicate that Paul loved his people more.
Questions.Alternative: Is the love that you have for your own tribe as great as that of Paul for his own people?
Is the love that you have for your own nation as great as that of Paul for his own people?

Questions.Q: What privileges did the Jews have more than any other race?
Questions.A: It was them that God made his children; to them he revealed his greatness; and God became their master and they his people; to them God gave his law; them he taught how to worship him well; them he promised to give their own land. Their ancestors Abraham, Isaac and Israel (Jacob) were great men. Christ was descended from them.

Questions.Q: Why are the Jews now outside God's gifts and promise?
Questions.A: Not because God's word failed to happen, but because many Jews were not true Jews in their hearts.

Questions.Q: Who then are true Jews?
Questions.A: Those descended from Abraham through his son Isaac, those that God promised to give to him a long time ago.

Questions.Q: What was wonderful/amazing about the child that Sarah brought forth?
Questions.A: Both she and Abraham were very old and she had not given birth before this.
Questions.Alternative: What was wonderful about the child that Sarah brought forth?
What was amazing about the child that Sarah brought forth?

Questions.Q: What teaching does Paul use the birth of Esau and Jacob to show?
Questions.A: If God chooses one person to follow him and rejects another, we cannot complain. It is his affair. Before they were born, God chose the younger of the twins to be the one who would be the true descendant of Abraham.

Questions.Q: How does Paul show that if God chooses to love one and hate another, he does not do wrong?
Questions.A: If he chooses to have mercy on someone, and, since no one deserves any mercy, we cannot complain. It is not what we do for God that will make him have mercy on us.

Questions.Q: To what does this verse refer?
Questions.A: When the Jews were all slaves in Egypt, God caused the Egyptian King to go on refusing to let them go free, so that God could bring great troubles upon Egypt to show his great power and to make his name great on all the earth.

Questions.Q: How does this verse explain why some people are very stubborn against the Gospel?
Questions.A: Because God does not love them and so he makes them to become stubborn.

Section.heading: Romans 9:19-33 God has the right to have mercy on anyone he wants.

Questions.Q: What does Paul use the Proverb in verse 21 to teach?
Questions.A: God is creator, so he can create man how he wants—one for special purposes and another for ordinary purposes.

Questions.Q: What is the real reason that God is angry at some people?
Questions.A: God is angry at some people because they are sinners and deserve to be destroyed.

Questions.Q: Why does he have mercy on some who indeed deserve to be destroyed?
Questions.A: Because he is patient and does not destroy them for the sake of those others on whom he had decided that he will have mercy.

Questions.Q: Who therefore are the people that God has decided to have mercy?
Questions.A: God has decided to have mercy with all Christians, whether they are Jews or non-Jews.

Questions.Q: Discuss: When we see wickedness that God has not yet punished, what does this show?
Questions.A: Answer from these verses.

Questions.Q: How does what the prophet Hosea wrote show what Paul is saying?
Questions.A: He said that a time would come when God would include among his children those who formerly were outside his family, i.e., the non-Jew.

Questions.Q: Why did the prophet Isaiah say that a few Jews would be saved?
Questions.A: Because God would punish them severely for their sins, and only because he was merciful he left a few survivors.

Questions.Q: What did the non-Jews get, that they did not search for, and the Jews search for but did not get?
Questions.A: God called them good people.

Questions.Q: What shows that the Jews searched for this in the wrong way?
Questions.A: They thought that, if they tried to follow God's law exactly, this would please God.

Questions.Q: What then is wrong with that?
Questions.A: They became self-righteous and boastful, and stopped trusting in God that he would have mercy on them.

Questions.Q: What is the stone that caused the Jews to stumble?
Questions.A: They cannot believe that Jesus is the Christ.

Section.heading: Romans 10:1-21 The Jews have lost the way to heaven.

Questions.Q: What is good and what is bad about the way the Jews worship God?
Questions.A: They are very sincere and worship him hard, but in the wrong way. They refuse to follow the way that God uses to call them good people.

Questions.Q: How has Christ brought an end to trying to follow God's law?
Questions.A: It is not by following God's law that God will call us good people, but by believing in Christ.

Questions.Q: Is there no way that our following God's law can please God?
Questions.A: Yes, but only if we follow it perfectly. And none can do that.

Questions.Q: Why does Paul say that believing is not a matter of going to fetch Christ from heaven or from the dead?
Questions.A: Believing is not a matter of us doing impossible things like that.

Questions.Q: How hard or easy is it to believe God's work?
Questions.A: It is just a matter of saying what we know in our hearts to be true.

Questions.Q: What must someone do so that God will save him?
Questions.A: He must say in public that Christ is his master, and in his heart believe that God raised Christ from death.

Questions.Q: Connect "being called good" with "getting life" or "being saved".
Questions.A: If we believe, and say so in public, immediately God gives us life and calls us good people.
Questions.Alternative: Connect "having faith" and "proclaiming it", with "getting life" or "being saved".
What is the connection between having faith and proclaiming it and being saved?
What is the connection between proclaiming your genuine faith and being saved?
What is the connection between having faith and proclaiming it and "getting life" or "being saved"?
What is the connection between proclaiming your genuine faith and "getting life" or "being saved"?
What does God do when people proclaim their genuine faith in him?
What does God do if we proclaim our genuine faith in him?
What does God do if we put our faith in him and confess that publicly?
What does God do if we put our faith in him and proclaim that publicly?
What does God do if we put our faith in him and proclaim that?

Questions.Q: Why do that in public?
Questions.A: It is not good to be a secret Christian. He who is afraid to say he is a Christian, Christ will be ashamed of him.

Questions.Q: How can we avoid being ashamed in God's presence?
Questions.A: By believing in Christ and telling others that we believe.

Questions.Q: What is it that now makes no more difference between Jews and non-Jews?
Questions.A: It is by faith that anyone at all is saved. Anyone who calls on God to save him, God will save him.

Questions.Q: What do these verses tell us about one who calls on God to save him? How will he get to do that?
Questions.A: Only if a preacher is sent and preaches God's word, and the hearer believes and calls upon God.

Questions.Q: What does this say about preaching?
Questions.A: It says that God's word is good news, and so people will generally welcome it.

Questions.Q: Will everyone who hears God's word accept it?
Questions.A: No, just as only a few Jews in Isaiah's time accepted it.

Questions.Q: Summarize what Paul has been saying.
Questions.A: If no one tells the good news, then no one will hear it, let alone believe it.

Questions.Q: Can people say that they have never heard of the good news?
Questions.A: No, because, by now, says Paul, people everywhere have heard of the good news of Christ.

Questions.Q: Can those who are Jews argue that they heard but did not understand?
Questions.A: No, because of their stubbornness God said through Moses that he would use non-Jews to make then jealous and angry.

Questions.Q: How have Isaiah's words come true?
Questions.A: The non-Jews were not seeking God, but God went and revealed himself to them through the preaching of the Good News of Christ.

Questions.Q: What then is now God's attitude toward the Jews?
Questions.A: They are still stubborn and rebellious, but God is still calling on them to come back to himself.

Section.heading: Romans 11:1-12 Concerning the Jews that God has chosen.

Questions.Q: What thought is Paul rejecting here?
Questions.A: That God has rejected all of his people the Jews.

Questions.Q: What example from the Old Testament does Paul use to show this?
Questions.A: At the time of the prophet Elijah it seemed to him that only he remained a true worshiper of God and all the rest had gone to worship the fetish Baal. But God showed him that at least 7,000 had not bowed down to Baal at all.

Questions.Q: What does this example show for Paul in his own time?
Questions.A: There are many Jews who have become Christians.
Questions.Alternative: What does this example show for Paul during the time that he wrote this?
What does this example show during the time that Paul wrote this?
How does this example from long ago apply to the time in which Paul was writing?
How does this example from long ago apply to the present time?
What does this example show during the present time?
How does this example still apply now?

Questions.Q: What does God stand on to choose and save some Jews?
Questions.A: The same as for non-Jews, he has had mercy on some, though all deserve to be punished.

Questions.Q: Why do some Jews become stubborn?
Questions.A: They seek to follow God in their own way, that of trying to do many good works, and reject the true way which is to trust in Jesus Christ.

Questions.Q: If God makes a person stubborn, can we blame that person for his stubbornness?
Questions.A: Yes, because it is only if he keeps on being stubborn, that God takes away his understanding.
It is that God leaves him to his case, and so stubborn man continues his stubborn ways.

Questions.Q: Against whom did King David speak in this passage?
Questions.A: King David spoke against the Jews, his own people.

Questions.Q: What good thing did God cause to come from the Jews' refusal of Jesus Christ?
Questions.A: God went and offered salvation to those who were not Jews.

Questions.Q: How will the saving of the non-Jews benefit the Jews?
Questions.A: It makes them jealous, so perhaps they will come back to God.

Questions.Q: How will the saving of the Jews also benefit the non-Jews?
Questions.A: It will add to God's kingdom and bring greater blessings on all Christians.

Section.heading: Romans 11:13-24 The Jews' disobedience has caused God to bless the non-Jews.

Questions.Q: What do these verses add to verses 11 and 12?
Questions.A: They say the same thing.

Questions.Q: How do you understand the meaning of these proverbs?
Questions.A: The farm tree stands for the Jews, who are God's people, but because many rejected Jesus as the Christ, God cut them off from himself and took some of the non-Jews and joined them to his tree-his family-to become his people.

Questions.Q: What warnings does Paul give to the non-Jews? And why?
Questions.A: They should not boast that now they are better than the Jews, because:
1. They are only some of God's people and are not the leaders or the original members.
2. If they boast, they cease to trust in God's mercy.
3. So he may cut them off also.

Questions.Q: In short, what does this verse say?
Questions.A: If you continue to believe in God, he will not cut you off.

Questions.Q: What do these verses teach?
Questions.A: At some time in the future many Jews will become Christians. God will be very happy to welcome back those brought up as Jews because they are still his chosen people whom he rejected during the time of their unbelief. God has power to do this.

Section.heading: Romans 11:25-36 When God will save all the Jews.

Questions.Q: How long will the Jews stubbornly reject Jesus?
Questions.A: Until the total number of non-Jews who will become Christians has been reached.

Questions.Q: Then what will happen?
Questions.A: God will save all the Jews.

Questions.Q: What do these verses tell us about God's love and God's promises?
Questions.A: 1. The Jews became God's enemies because they rejected him, but he still loves them.
2. Despite their rejection of him, he has not broken the promises that he made to their ancestors, but has included the non-Jews in those promises.
3. If he decides to call someone to himself, he does not change his mind.

Questions.Q: Why did God have mercy on us non-Jews and give us the good news of Jesus Christ?
Questions.A: God had mercy on us non-Jews because most of the Jews rejected that good news.

Questions.Q: Why has God let the Jews be stubborn?
Questions.A: 1. So that he may have mercy on the non-Jews,
2. Then make Jew and non-Jews alike,
3. So that in the end he might have mercy also on the Jews.

Questions.Q: In what way are Jews and non-Jews all alike?
Questions.A: They are all sinners.

Questions.Q: Summarize Paul's praises of God in these verses.
Questions.A: He is very wise.
Man cannot understand his mind, or give any advice to him.
No one can make God owe him anything.
He is the creator and sustainer of all things. In the end, all things will go back to him.

Questions.Q: We have seen in the previous chapters that man cannot please God by following his law. So what does Paul say we should do to please God?
Questions.A: Offer our bodies as sacrifices to God.

Questions.Q: Why [should we offer our bodies as [living] sacrifices to God]?
Questions.A: We should offer our bodies as sacrifices to God because God has already had mercy on us and has saved us.
Questions.Alternative: Why?
Why should we offer our bodies as living sacrifices to God?
Why should we offer our bodies as sacrifices to God?
Why should we offer our bodies to God?

Questions.Q: What kind of sacrifice does he mean?
Questions.A: Our lives should be good and pleasing to God, and we should worship him from our hearts.

Questions.Q: How can we know what pleases God and what is good and what is the best way?
Questions.A: 1. To think of ourselves as greater than we are, i.e., we should not boast.
2. To think that we are weak and lacking in faith, i.e., false modesty.

Questions.Q: The human body has many parts. What does Paul use this proverb to teach?
Questions.A: We are all like parts of Christ's body, i.e., we are Christ's family which is called the church, and so we belong to one another.

Questions.Q: How is each one of us different from the other?
Questions.A: God has given each of us a different gift of power.

Questions.Q: Why has he given us these powers?
Questions.A: God has given us these powers to serve him within the church.

Questions.Q: What way should all of us use our gift?
Questions.A: To the fullest extent that God has given us power.

Questions.Q: List these gifts that Paul mentions.
Questions.A: Prophecy/revelation,
helping/serving others,
teaching God's word,
encouraging others,
giving money to others,
leading the church,
and helping others in trouble.

Questions.Q: Summarize the ways in which we should use these gifts that God has given us.
Questions.A: Cheerfully without grumbling,
willingly,
fully and without laziness,
and without asking for reward.

Questions.Q: List those things which are sins and so we must not do them.
Questions.A: Anything that is bad. Laziness. Not praying.

Questions.Q: How should we show that we love our fellow Christians?
Questions.A: 1. We should love from our hearts.
2. We should hold tight to what is good.
3. We should love on another like relatives love one another.
4. We should respect one another more than ourselves.
5. We should help others who suffer poverty.
6. We should welcome strangers.

Questions.Q: How should we show that we love our Lord Jesus Christ?
Questions.A: By working hard for him and by loving our fellow Christians.

Questions.Q: How should we stop our faith from getting smaller?
Questions.A: 1. By letting our hope that we will go to heaven make us happy.
2. By being patient in trouble.
3. By praying always.

Questions.Q: List the ways in which we should be like others.
Questions.A: 1. We should be happy with those who are happy and sad with those who are sad.
2. We should imitate humble people.

Questions.Q: List the ways that we should not be like others.
Questions.A: 1. We should not take revenge, but should bless those who cause us to suffer.
2. We should not fight others but live in harmony with them.
3. We should not be proud and boastful.

Questions.Q: What is the one teaching of these verses?
Questions.A: Love your enemy.

Questions.Q: What should we not do?
Questions.A: 1. We should not take revenge on those who do us wrong.
2. We should not repay evil for evil.

Questions.Q: How will we get revenge?
Questions.A: It is for God to avenge us, not ourselves.
Questions.Alternative: Who takes revenge for God's children?
Who takes revenge for God's people?
Who takes revenge for us?

Questions.Q: How should we act towards our enemy?
Questions.A: 1. We should try to live at peace with him.
2. We should always do what people will see is good.
3. If he is hungry, we should feed him, if he is thirsty, we should give him something to drink.

Questions.Q: If God takes revenge for us, is he asking us to be more loving than him to our enemy?
Questions.A: 1. The purpose of doing good to our enemy is to make him ashamed, so that he will repent and be reconciled with us and with God.
2. God usually delays his punishment of wrong doers till after they die. So he is very patient with them in their lifetime, wanting them to repent.

Questions.Q: Discuss: Who is my enemy?
Do these verses also apply to those who are enemies of our clan/tribe/country?
Questions.Alternative: Do these verses also apply to those who are enemies of our clan?
Do these verses also apply to those who are enemies of our tribe?
Do these verses also apply to those who are enemies of our country?

Section.heading: Romans 13:1-7 We should obey those who have earthly power over us.

Questions.Q: Why should we obey/respect those who have power over us?
Questions.A: We should obey/respect those who have power over us because civil/state/town authority comes from God.
Questions.Alternative: Why should we obey those who have power over us?
Why should we respect those who have power over us?
Why should we obey/respect the authorities/officials in our community?
Why should we obey the authorities in our community?
Why should we obey the officials in our community?
Why should we respect the authorities in our community?
Why should we respect the officials in our community?
Why should we obey our governing authorities?
Why should we respect our governing authorities?

Questions.Q: Who will get God's punishment?
Questions.A: Those who do/or speak against those who have authority will receive God's punishment.
Questions.Alternative: Who will get a deserved punishment?
Who will receive punishment?
Who will receive judgment?
Who will be punished by God?
Who will be judged by God?

Questions.Q: What is the purpose of those who have authority?
Questions.A: They have God's authority to praise those who do good and to punish those who do evil.

Questions.Q: How should we avoid trouble with the authorities?
Questions.A: By doing good.

Questions.Q: What are the reasons that we should obey them?
Questions.A: 1. To avoid punishment by them.
2. To avoid punishment by God.
3. Because we know in our heads that it is right to do this.

Questions.Q: Is Paul speaking only of Christian rulers?
Questions.A: No, because in his day those in authority were the Romans, who were not Christians or Jews.
Questions.Alternative: Do Paul's instructions apply only to Christian rulers?
Do these instructions apply only to Christian rulers?
Do these commands apply only to Christian rulers?
Do Paul's instructions apply only to rulers who believe in God?
Do these instructions apply only to rulers who believe in God?
Do these commands apply only to rulers who believe in God?

Questions.Q: What if the authorities order us to do something which is wrong in God's sight?
Questions.A: Then we obey God rather than man. (See Acts 4:19 and Matthew 23:15-21.)

Questions.Q: Discuss: Does every government that takes power have God's authority?
What about those who take power by force?
Are the strongest men those who have the right to rule over us?
Are we to fear/submit to/respect those who are strong authorities only?
Questions.Alternative: Are we to fear those who are strong authorities only?
Are we to submit to those who are strong authorities only?
Are we to respect those who are strong authorities only?

Questions.Q: What about paying taxes?
Questions.A: We should not avoid paying them.
Questions.Alternative: What does he teach about paying taxes?
What does this say about paying taxes?

Questions.Q: Why [should we pay taxes]?
Questions.A: We should not avoid paying taxes because the authorities are serious about their work of governing. They are doing God's work.
Questions.Alternative: Why?
Why should we pay taxes?
Why are we to pay taxes?
Why do we have to pay taxes?

Questions.Q: Discuss: How do we answer excessive or unjust taxation?
Besides taxes/money, what else might we owe someone [in authority]?
Questions.A: Respect and honor
Questions.Alternative: Besides taxes, what else might we owe someone?
Besides money, what else might we owe someone?
Besides taxes, what else might we owe someone in authority?
Besides money, what else might we owe someone in authority?

Section.heading: Romans 13:8-14 We should respect one another.

Questions.Q: What is the only debt that is good?
Questions.A: The only debt that is good is that we owe one another love—we should go on loving one another.
Questions.Alternative: What should we continue to owe?

Questions.Q: What is a summary of the commandments of God?
Questions.A: Love your fellow man like you love yourself.

Questions.Q: Why is adultery wrong?
Questions.A: It is stealing or spoiling another man's wife or a woman's husband; or it is taking a woman/man who is not yet your own; or it is being unfaithful to your own wife/husband.

Questions.Q: How is loving our fellow man the same as following God's law?
Questions.A: If we love our fellow man, we will not do him any wrong.
Questions.Alternative: How is loving others the same as following God's law?
How is loving our neighbors the same as following God's law?
How is loving other people the same as following God's law?

Questions.Q: Why does Paul warn them against sinning?
Questions.A: Because the day when Christ will return to save us is nearer than when we first believed in him.

Questions.Q: In short, how can we summarize the sins that we are to avoid?
Questions.A: Living like those who live in darkness.

Questions.Q: What particular sins does he mention?
Questions.A: Gluttony, drunkenness, adultery, rape, fighting, jealously.

Questions.Q: How do we avoid such sins?
Questions.A: By taking on the strength that God gives us to live the good life and fight evil. By letting Christ control us so that we don't think about the bad things that we want.

Section.heading: Romans 14:1-12 God alone has the right to accuse your fellow man.

Questions.Q: What kind of arguments between Christians does Paul speak against?
Questions.A: Paul spoke against arguments between Christians that were about food taboos and observing special days.

Questions.Q: Which of the two sides is "stronger"?
Questions.A: Those who will eat all foods, and who think all days are equal.

Questions.Q: How should "the strong" and "the weak" treat each other?
Questions.A: They should respect the other's beliefs and not criticize them.

Questions.Q: Why [should they accept/respect each other and not argue with each other or judge each other]?
Questions.A: "The strong" and "the weak" should respect the other's beliefs because God has accepted both the "strong" and the "weak".
Questions.Alternative: Why?
Why should they accept each other and not argue with each other or judge each other?
Why should they respect each other and not argue with each other or judge each other?
Why should they accept each other?
Why should they respect each other?

Questions.Q: Discuss: How does this affect the relationship between one Christian denomination and another?
Questions.Alternative: Discuss: How does this affect the relationship between groups of Christians with different opinions?
How does this affect the relationship between one Christian denomination and another?
How does this affect the relationship between groups of Christians with different opinions?
Discuss: How does this affect the relationship between different Christian churches?
How does this affect the relationship between different Christian churches?

Questions.Q: Why should we not criticize another's beliefs in these matters?
Questions.A: We should not criticize another's beliefs because each one of us is answerable only to God, who is the master of each one of us.
Questions.Alternative: Why does Paul say not to criticize another's beliefs in these matters?
Why does Paul say not to criticize other Christians who have different beliefs in these matters?
Why does Paul say not to criticize other Christians who have different beliefs about which days are special or which foods are acceptable?

Questions.Q: If our opinions differ about which days or foods are special, what is necessary that we do first?
Questions.A: We should keep to what we think is right.
Questions.Alternative: If our opinions differ about which days or foods are special, what should we do?
If our opinions differ about which days are special or which foods are acceptable, what should we do?
If our opinions differ about which days are special or which foods may be eaten, what should we do?
If our opinions differ about which days are special or which foods should not be eaten, what should we do?
If we disagree with other Christians about which days or foods are special, what should we do?
If we disagree with other Christians about which days are special or which foods are acceptable, what should we do?
If we disagree with other Christians about which days are special or which foods may be eaten, what should we do?
If we disagree with other Christians about which days are special or which foods should not be eaten, what should we do?

Questions.Q: For what reason only should we keep that opinion that we have about days and foods?
Questions.A: Only if we observe such days or reject unacceptable foods in order to respect/obey our Master Jesus.
Questions.Alternative: What is the only reason to hold strong opinions about days and foods?
What is the only reason to hold strong opinions about special days and acceptable foods?
What is the only reason that we should keep that opinion that we have about days and foods?
When is it okay to hold strong opinions about days and foods?

Questions.Q: What makes both opinions right?
Questions.A: They are right, if we both give thanks to God for what he gives us to eat.

Questions.Q: Discuss these verses. Do you have any proverbs like these?
What is Paul saying about Christians?
Questions.A: We belong to our Master Jesus Christ. So we live not for ourselves but for him. And if we have died, we died for him.

Questions.Q: What here is one of the reasons why Christ died and rose again?
Questions.A: That he might become the Master of those who have died as well as of those who still live.

Questions.Q: What does this mean?
Questions.A: When we die as Christians and we go to be with God, Christ remains our Master just as he is our Master while we live on earth.

Questions.Q: Why is it not right for us to criticize our fellow Christian?
Questions.A: Because each one of us will one day be criticized or praised by God himself when we stand before his judgment place.

Questions.Q: Does this verse apply only to Christians? What does it say?
Questions.A: Everyone, whether Christian or non-Christian, will kneel before our Master and agree that he is Master and Judge.
Questions.Alternative: Do these verses apply only to Christians? What does it say?
What does this passage say about who will acknowledge God?
What does this passage say about the people who will say that God is Lord?

Section.heading: Romans 14:13-23 Go on being patient with one another.

Questions.Q: What is Paul's opinion concerning foods?
Questions.A: No food is unclean by itself. All food is good for eating.

Questions.Q: How can what is good become not good for eating?
Questions.A: If we think that it is not right to eat certain foods, then for us it is not right, and becomes unclean to us.
Questions.Alternative: How can food that is okay to eat be considered unclean?
How can food that is okay to eat be considered unacceptable?
How can food that is "clean" be considered "unclean"?
How can food that is good become wrong to eat?

Questions.Q: Under what circumstances though I think all foods are good, will it be wrong for me to eat a food that some others taboo eating?
Questions.A: If I eat a food that my fellow Christian refuses to eat, and it causes him to be angry with me because I eat it, then it shows that I don't love him.

Questions.Q: What is the reason, then, for being like the "weaker" Christian?
Questions.A: So that I do not spoil/destroy one for whom Christ died, that is, a fellow Christian.

Questions.Q: What is Paul saying to the stronger Christian?
Questions.A: For the sake of the weaker Christian, avoid eating the foods that he avoids eating so as not to upset him and so that no one will think that what you think is good is evil.

Questions.Q: From this verse what do you see as a good definition of true religion?
Questions.A: True religion concerns goodness, peace and happiness which all come from the Holy Spirit—it is not a matter of taboos. It is positive, not negative.

Questions.Q: What is the result of true religion?
Questions.A: God is pleased and men will be pleased.

Questions.Q: If we are in doubt about whether or not to eat or drink something, what is the guiding rule?
Questions.A: Do what brings peace in the lives of people and causes people to help one another.

Questions.Q: How can eating or drinking spoil the work of God?
Questions.A: It is wrong to do this if it will cause a fellow Christian to enter sin.

Questions.Q: If we have any doubt about whether it is right to eat or drink something, how shall we decide the matter?
Questions.A: If we have any doubt, then we should avoid doing it. Because if we do anything not believing it to be right, then it is wrong. What we believe should guide us.

Section.heading: Romans 15:1-7 Let us each try to please his fellow Christian.

Questions.Q: Do these verses say anything different from the previous chapter?
Questions.A: No. They say that those who are strong in faith should be patient with those who have doubts about certain foods and drink, and so should do only what will help them grow in their faith.

Questions.Q: In what way is Christ an example for us in this matter?
Questions.A: He did not do what pleased just himself. When others insulted God, they also insulted him. So he humbled himself for the sake of others.

Questions.Q: How can reading God's word help us?
Questions.A: In it we read of others who suffered patiently and God helped them. So this should give us encouragement and hope.

Questions.Q: What else do Christians need other than patience and hope in sufferings?
Questions.A: Patience with one another, as Christ was patient with others, and unity.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that we should be united in voice and mind?
Questions.A: So as to give praise to God the Father of our Master Jesus Christ.

Questions.Q: What example does the author give to show us how we should accept each other?
Questions.A: In the same way that Christ accepts us.

Section.heading: Romans 15:8-21 God's word book speaks about the non-Jews praising God.

Questions.Q: What two things did Christ's coming do for the peoples of this world?
Questions.A: He came as a servant to the Jews:
1. To make God's promises to their ancestors come true.
2. To enable the non-Jews to praise God for his mercy to them.

Questions.Q: Why does Paul quote all these verses from the Old Testament?
Questions.A: To show that God promised in his word book that the non-Jews would one day come to share the same blessings that God gave to the Jews.

Questions.Q: Who is the person referred to in this verse?
Questions.A: Jesus Christ.
Questions.Note: Isaiah and Jesse are not the same person. Jesse was the father of King David.

Questions.Q: What does God want to see in our Christian lives?
Questions.A: Our believing is to be full of joy, peace and hope.

Questions.Q: Where do these things come from?
Questions.A: They come from the power of God's Holy Spirit.

Questions.Q: If Christians are mature and doing what God wants, is there any more need for them to read God's word book?
Questions.A: Paul wrote this letter to remind them of things that they had already learned, so that they would not forget. So we should always remind ourselves of what God has caused others to write down for us.

Questions.Q: What is Paul's authority for writing this letter?
Questions.A: God had made him a servant of Jesus Christ to work for those who are not Jews.

Questions.Q: In what way is Paul's preaching work like that of a priest/sacrifice offerer?
Questions.A: Those who hear Paul's words and believe in Christ, are offering to God. God will accept them because his Holy Spirit washes away their uncleanness and makes them fit for God.
Questions.Alternative: In what way is Paul's preaching work like that of a priest?
In what way is Paul's preaching work like that of a sacrifice offerer?

Questions.Q: Of what things can Paul boast?
Questions.A: What God has done through him to bring the non-Jews to obey God—such as preaching, miracles and the power of the Holy Spirit.

Questions.Q: How did Paul decide where to go and preach the Good News?
Questions.A: He would go anywhere where no one has yet preached the Good News.

Questions.Q: If Paul preached the Good News somewhere where people already knew about Jesus, what does he say he would be doing?
Questions.A: Building on another man's foundation.
Questions.Note: Ensure that the figure of speech/proverb about not building on another man's foundation (v. 20) is understood.
(Note: Paul is giving his personal ministry philosophy, not necessarily criticizing someone who preaches to those who have already heard the gospel.

Section.heading: Romans 15:22-33 Where Paul had decided to go next.

Questions.Q: Why had Paul not yet preached the Good News in Rome?
Questions.A: 1. He was too busy preaching in the region from Jerusalem to Illycricum, where as yet no one had preached.
2. Someone else had already first preached the Good News in Rome.

Questions.Q: Why is he now free to go to Rome?
Questions.A: He has completed his work in those other places, and he now wants to greet them on his way to Spain, where no one has yet preached the Good News.

Questions.Q: What does Paul expect to get from the Christians in Rome?
Questions.A: Paul expects to enjoy their company for a while and receive something to help him on his way to Spain.

Questions.Q: What will Paul do before going to Rome?
Questions.A: He wants to go to Jerusalem to take money to the Christians there who are suffering poverty.

Questions.Q: Where did this money come from?
Questions.A: It was given by the Christians in the lands of Macedonia and Achaia.

Questions.Q: From these verses what do we see as the reasons for giving money to other Christians?
Questions.A: 1. One should go to those who suffer poverty.
2. One should give willingly.
3. One should try to give back in material goods (this world's things) to those from whom one has received blessings which come from heaven.

Questions.Q: Has he said this before?
Questions.A: Yes. See verse 24.

Questions.Q: What more does Paul expect from his intended visit to the Roman Christians?
Questions.A: That Christ will give both him and them blessings.

Questions.Q: Why does Paul ask the Roman Christians to pray for him?
Questions.A: That when he reaches Jerusalem:
1. God will protect him from those in Judea who do not believe in Christ.
2. The poor Christians in Jerusalem will not refuse to receive the money which he is bringing to them.

Questions.Q: From your knowledge of Acts, do you know if this prayer was answered?
Questions.A: See Acts 21:27 to the end of Acts. Paul was arrested by the Jews who hated Christ, but was rescued by the Romans, who kept him in prison for 2 years and last sent him to Rome for trial by the Roman great king. So the prayer was answered, but it took a long time.

Questions.Q: Who is Phoebe and why does she deserve help?
Questions.A: She is one of the helpers/deaconesses in the church. She is one who brings Paul's letter. She is a good friend to many people and to Paul.

Questions.Q: Who are Pricilla/Prisca and Aquila?
Questions.A: Paul's fellow workers (3)
Questions.Note: Priscilla is the wife of Aquila. Paul had left them in Ephesus. Now they have returned to Rome. See Acts 18:2, 18, 26.
Questions.Alternative: Who are Pricilla and Aquila?
Who are Prisca and Aquila?

Questions.Q: What did they do for Paul?
Questions.A: They risked their lives for him.(4)

Questions.Q: Why is Epenetus remembered?
Questions.A: He was the first person to become a Christian in Asian land.

Questions.Q: What did Mary do?
Questions.A: She worked hard for the Roman Christians.

Questions.Q: What did Andronicus and Junias do?
Questions.A: They were in Prison with Paul. They became Christians even before Paul and are well known to the apostles.

Questions.Q: What did Apelles do well?
Questions.A: He suffered persecution and came out of it a true mature Christian.

Questions.Q: What did these three women do?
Questions.A: They worked hard for our Master Jesus.

Questions.Q: What did Rufus's mother do?
Questions.A: She welcomed Paul as if she was his mother.

Questions.Q: What are the greatest dangers to a church?
Questions.A: Those who are church members who cause disunity, and confusion and who teach things that are against what we have already learned.

Questions.Q: How do these people work?
Questions.A: With flattery and sweet talk, trying to deceive those people who are easily persuaded/who are unstable.

Questions.Q: What are these deceivers, really?
Questions.A: They only do what pleases themselves. It is not our Master Jesus that they worship.

Questions.Q: What is the best way of resisting such people?
Questions.A: Being on our guard against them, so that we are wise and willing to do good, but willing to do evil.

Questions.Q: Who in fact are we fighting when we oppose such people?
Questions.A: The Devil.

Questions.Q: What does this verse tell us about the way Paul wrote letters?
Questions.A: He used a secretary to write down what he said.

Questions.Q: For what does Paul praise God in these verses?
Questions.A: He can give us the strength to continue believing and to go on following the Good News that he preaches.

Questions.Q: What was hidden and is now revealed?
Questions.A: The Good News about Jesus Christ.

Questions.Q: In what way did God reveal something of that Good News even before Christ came?
Questions.A: Through what the prophets wrote in God's word book.

Questions.Q: What must be done with this Good News?
Questions.A: It must be preached to all peoples of this world so that they might believe and follow it.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul is writing a letter to Titus.

Questions.Q: Who wrote this letter?
Questions.A: Paul

Questions.Q: What does Paul say about himself?
Questions.A: He serves God.
He is an apostle of Jesus Christ.

Questions.Q: What does he say that his work of being an apostle is?
Questions.A: He helps people to trust in God.
He helps people to know the true teachings.

Questions.Q: To whom does Paul refer when he speaks of "the people God has chosen"?
Questions.A: The believers.

Questions.Q: What do you think God has chosen them for?
Questions.A: To belong to him; to follow him; to be his people.

Questions.Q: What do believers hope for?
Questions.A: Eternal life.

Questions.Q: How do they know that they will have eternal life?
Questions.A: God promised it, and he does not lie.

Questions.Q: How can people know about this message of eternal life?
Questions.A: God revealed it.

Questions.Q: How did God reveal it?
Questions.A: Through the message given to Paul and others.

Questions.Q: Then what did God do?
Questions.A: God gave Paul and others the work of telling people about it.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say about God here?
Questions.A: God is the one who saves us.

Questions.Q: To whom is Paul writing?
Questions.A: To Titus.

Questions.Q: Why does Paul say that Titus is his child?
Questions.A: Titus is like his child because he believes the gospel as Paul does.

Questions.Q: What does Paul want God and Jesus Christ to do for Titus?
Questions.A: To bless Titus and cause him to live in peace.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul tells Titus he is to appoint leaders for every church.

Questions.Q: In what place did Paul leave Titus?
Questions.A: In Crete.

Questions.Q: What was Titus to do there?
Questions.A: To finish the work which Paul had begun to do there.
To appoint leaders/elders for the churches in every town.

Questions.Q: What do you think those leaders/elders were to do?
Questions.A: To direct the affairs of the church, to preach, etc.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think those leaders were to do?
What do you think those elders were to do?

Questions.Q: What was the character/behavior of a leader/elder to be?
Questions.A: He should be a good, well-behaved person.
He should have only one wife.
His children should believe in Christ, and be disciplined and law-abiding.
He should be humble, patient/not quick tempered.
He should not be addicted to drink.
He should not be fierce and violent.
He should not like money a lot.
He should be a person who often invites people into his home.
He should live a well-disciplined life.
Questions.Alternative: What was the character of a leader to be?
What was the character of a elder to be?
What was the behavior of a leader to be?
What was the behavior of a elder to be?

Questions.Q: Why do you think it is necessary for a leader/elder of a church to be this kind of person?
Questions.A: Because he is doing the work of God.
Questions.Alternative: Why do you think it is necessary for a leader of a church to be this kind of person?
Why do you think it is necessary for a elder of a church to be this kind of person?

Questions.Q: What other thing is very necessary for a leader/elder of a church?
Questions.A: He must have a good understanding of the true teachings.
He must believe the true teachings firmly.
Questions.Alternative: What other thing is very necessary for a leader of a church?
What other thing is very necessary for a elder of a church?

Questions.Q: Why must the leader/elder believe the true teachings firmly?
Questions.A: So that he can teach others the true teachings.
So that he can correct people who teach errors.
Questions.Alternative: Why must the leader believe the true teachings firmly?
Why must the elder believe the true teachings firmly?

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul tells Timothy that those who are making trouble must be corrected.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say about those people who are making trouble?
Questions.A: They do not submit to anyone.
They speak foolishly.
They deceive people.

Questions.Q: Who in particular are making trouble?
Questions.A: Those who had been converted from Judaism.

Questions.Q: What do you think they would be teaching?
Questions.A: That a person who wants to become a believer must be circumcised.

Questions.Q: Why did Paul say the church leaders must stop those people from teaching?
Questions.A: They are upsetting people by teaching wrong doctrine.

Questions.Q: Why were those people teaching those things?
Questions.A: In order to get money.

Questions.Q: Who said that the people of Crete always lie?
Questions.A: A prophet of Crete.

Questions.Q: Do you think that God gave him the words to speak?
Questions.A: No, he was not a prophet of God.

Questions.Q: What else did he say about the people?
Questions.A: They are like evil beasts (treacherous, unruly).
They are lazy and greedy.

Questions.Q: Is what this person said true?
Questions.A: Yes, Paul says it is true.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Those people who are teaching lies live very wicked lives.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say that Titus must do?
Questions.A: He must rebuke strongly those people who are paying attention to the false teachers.

Questions.Q: Why must he rebuke them?
Questions.A: So that they will stop believing the lies.
So that they will firmly believe the truth.

Questions.Q: What sort of things are those people believing?
Questions.A: Myths, untrue stories; teachings from people who refuse to accept God's truth.

Questions.Q: Who is Paul speaking about when he speaks about "the pure"?
Questions.A: People who are really following God; who do what is right.

Questions.Q: What does Paul mean by "all things are pure"?
Questions.A: To a true believer there is no distinction between things being ritually clean and unclean.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say about the people who are not "pure" and do not believe in God?
Questions.A: All that they do and think about is evil.

Questions.Q: What do these people say about God?
Questions.A: They claim that they know him.

Questions.Q: Do they really know him?
Questions.A: No.

Questions.Q: How can people tell that those people do not know God?
Questions.A: Because they are always doing bad deeds, disobeying God.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul tells Titus that he is to teach how believers should behave.

Questions.Q: Paul has been talking about the disobedient people in Crete who are incapable of doing any good deeds. Now he speaks about the congregation of believers. What does he say Titus is to teach them?
Questions.A: How to live in a way which is consistent with the gospel.

Questions.Q: What should Titus teach the older men?
Questions.A: That they should be temperate/disciplined in all their desires.
That they should live steady, well-ordered lives.
That they should believe the truth.
That they should love people.
That they should endure suffering with steadfast faith.

Questions.Q: What should Titus teach the older women?
Questions.A: They should live in a way which is fitting for those who are believers.
They should not speak evil/lies against people.
They should not be addicted to drink.
They should teach younger women what is good.

Questions.Q: What should Titus teach the younger women?
Questions.A: To love their husbands and children.
To live good lives.
To look after their homes well.
To be kind to people.
To obey their husbands.

Questions.Q: What will be the result if the young women do not follow this kind of behavior?
Questions.A: People will speak evil about God's message.

Questions.Q: What should Titus teach the younger men?
Questions.A: To live disciplined lives.

Questions.Q: How is Titus himself to behave?
Questions.A: He is to live a very good life.
He is to teach sincerely, seriously.

Questions.Q: Why is it important for Titus to live this way?
Questions.A: In order to give a good example to those whom he is teaching.
So that people will not have any reason to criticize those who preach the gospel.

Questions.Q: What other group of people should Titus teach?
Questions.A: The slaves.

Questions.Q: What should Titus teach the slaves?
Questions.A: To obey their masters.
To try their best to please their masters.
Not to steal.
Not to be rebellious/contrary.
To be completely trustworthy.

Questions.Q: What will be the result if slaves behave like this?
Questions.A: Their behavior will cause people to honor God and his message.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul tells Titus that God revealed his grace to people in order to teach them to live good lives.
Titus is to teach these truths with authority.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say about God?
Questions.A: He has revealed his grace/love to people in order to save them.

Questions.Q: Who does God want to save?
Questions.A: All people.

Questions.Q: Do you think this means that everybody will be saved?
Questions.A: No, but this is what God wants.

Questions.Q: When people know about God's love and mercy, what will be the result?
Questions.A: They will know that they are to stop doing the things which displease God.
They will know that they should live good lives.

Questions.Q: What else encourages believers to live a good life?
Questions.A: The fact that Jesus Christ is going to come back again.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say about Jesus Christ?
Questions.A: He is God.
He is Savior.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus Christ do for people?
Questions.A: He gave up himself/his life for people.

Questions.Q: Why did Jesus Christ die for people?
Questions.A: In order to save them from being punished for their sins.
To keep people from doing sinful/evil things.
To cause people to live good lives/do good things.

Questions.Q: What is Titus to teach?
Questions.A: What Paul is writing in this letter.

Questions.Q: What should his attitude be as he teaches?
Questions.A: He should speak with authority.
He should not allow people to disregard his teaching.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul tells Titus that believers are not saved because of what they have done; they are saved because God has shown mercy to them.

Questions.Q: What further things does Paul tell Titus to teach people?
Questions.A: To obey those in authority.
To work hard.
Not to speak evil of anybody.
Not to quarrel.
To be kind and gentle towards everyone.

Questions.Q: Why do you think Paul talks about how bad we formerly were?
Questions.A: To show why we should be kind and gentle to those who are as bad as we once were.

Questions.Q: How did all believers behave previously?
Questions.A: They were foolish, disobedient, deceived, selfish, wicked, envious, hateful.

Questions.Q: Then what happened?
Questions.A: God saved people from all those sins they were doing.

Questions.Q: Was it because they were doing good things that God saved them?
Questions.A: No, they were not doing good things.

Questions.Q: Why, then, did he save them?
Questions.A: Because he was merciful to them.

Questions.Q: How did God save them?
Questions.A: Through his Holy Spirit who washed away their sins and made them new people.

Questions.Q: Because of whom have believers received the Holy Spirit?
Questions.A: Because of Jesus Christ, who saved them.

Questions.Q: Because of what Jesus Christ did, what does Paul say happened to believers?
Questions.A: God justified them.
They will live forever in God's place.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul tells Titus how to deal with those who cause divisions.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say is true?
Questions.A: All that he has been saying in verses 4-7.

Questions.Q: Why does Paul want Titus to continue teaching those things?
Questions.A: So that people will try harder to live good lives.

Questions.Q: What does Paul tell Titus to avoid?
Questions.A: Useless arguments.
Lists of ancestors.
Quarrels about the Law.

Questions.Q: Why should he avoid those things?
Questions.A: They are harmful.
They are unnecessary.

Questions.Q: If any person continues to argue and disagree, what should Titus do?
Questions.A: Warn him seriously two times.

Questions.Q: If the person does not change his behavior after being warned two times, what should Titus do?
Questions.A: He should have nothing more to do with him.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul tells Titus what arrangements he has made for the future, and sends greetings.

Questions.Q: What does Paul want Titus to do?
Questions.A: He wants him to come to meet him at the town of Nicopolis.

Questions.Q: When is Titus to go to Nicopolis?
Questions.A: When Paul sends Artemas or Tychicus to him.

Questions.Q: How long will Paul stay in Nicopolis?
Questions.A: Through the winter.

Questions.Q: What further instruction does Paul give Titus?
Questions.A: To help Zenas and Apollos and give them what they need.

Questions.Q: What does Paul want all the believers to do?
Questions.A: To learn to do good.
To help people who are in need.

Questions.Q: Who also sends greetings to Titus?
Questions.A: Everyone who is with Paul.

Questions.Q: To whom does Paul want to send greetings?
Questions.A: All the believers who love him.

Questions.Q: What does Paul want God to do for Titus and those with him?
Questions.A: To continue to bless them.

Questions.Q: The Corinthian church people belong to a larger group of people. Who are they?
Questions.A: Those people everywhere whom God has chosen for himself because they call Jesus Christ their Master.

Questions.Q: What else is expected from God's people apart from the fact that they call him Master?
Questions.A: That they live a good/holy life.

Section.heading: 1 Corinthians 1:4-9 The blessings that the Corinthian church people already have.

Questions.Q: What kind of blessings has God given to the Corinthian church people?
Questions.A: The ability to understand his/Christ's word well and to speak it well.

Questions.Q: When did this happen?
Questions.A: When the word of Christ was firmly established among them.

Questions.Q: What do they lack of the gifts of the Holy Spirit?
Questions.A: None
Questions.Alternative: Which of the gifts of the Holy Spirit are they lacking?
Which spiritual gifts are they lacking?
Which spiritual gifts do they lack?
What gifts of God do they lack?

Questions.Q: What makes them eagerly await the second coming of Christ?
Questions.A: Because they have all the gifts now.
Questions.Note: Use either this question (A) or the following question (B). It would be redundant to ask both questions.
question A (1Co 1:7)

Questions.Q: Now what do they do, after they have all the blessings and gifts of the Holy Spirit?
Questions.A: They eagerly await the second coming of Christ.
Questions.Note: Use either this question (B) or the preceding question (A). It would be redundant to ask both questions.
question B (1Co 1:7)
Questions.Alternative: Having received all the blessings and gifts of the Holy Spirit, what do they do?

Questions.Q: Why do we need strength from Christ?
Questions.A: So that on the day he returns no one can blame us for wrong doing.

Questions.Q: Why can we be sure that he will keep us strong in this way?
Questions.A: Because he has called us into the family of his son Jesus Christ our Master.

Section.heading: 1 Corinthians 1:10-17 How the church members have become disunited.

Questions.Q: What is troubling Paul?
Questions.A: The Corinthians have become disunited in thought and deed. They are fighting among themselves.

Questions.Q: How does Paul know this?
Questions.A: Chloe's family have told him about it.

Questions.Q: Describe this disunity.
Questions.A: Some say, "We follow Paul", others say, "We follow Apollos", others say, "We follow Peter", and yet others say, "As for us, we follow Christ".

Questions.Q: Whom should they all be following?
Questions.A: Christ

Questions.Q: What are the answers to each of these three questions?
Questions.A: 1. It cannot be done.
2. No.
3. No.
Questions.Note: These are rhetorical questions. If there is any problem understanding this, please write it down.

Questions.Q: Why is Paul happy that he only baptized a few people?
Questions.A: Because if he had baptized many, they would wrongly say that he had baptized them in his own name.

Questions.Q: Does this mean that most of the Corinthian Christians were not baptized?
Questions.A: No, probably Paul's helpers or other Christians baptized them.

Questions.Q: Was it wrong for Paul to baptize people?
Questions.A: No. He is saying that the most important work that Christ gave him to do was to preach the good news.

Questions.Q: Is this last sentence well understood? What is Paul saying?
Questions.A: It was not Paul's wisdom that made them become Christians, but the power of the death of Christ on the cross.

Section.heading: 1 Corinthians 1:18-31 How the people of the world think that God's word is foolish.

Questions.Q: What do the world's people think about the death of Christ on the cross?
Questions.A: They say it is foolishness. It makes no sense.

Questions.Q: For whom is it not foolishness?
Questions.A: For those whom God is saving, that is, for Christians.
Questions.Alternative: For whom is it not foolishness nor weakness?

Questions.Q: What power has the death of Christ on the cross?
Questions.A: It is the way God passes to us his power to do his work.
Questions.Note: Note: Ensure this sentence/concept is well understood.

Questions.Q: How are God's thoughts different from men's?
Questions.A: Even wise men are foolish in God's eyes. God's wisdom is quite different from men's. He makes all their wisdom come to nothing.

Questions.Q: What way is sure not to lead to heaven?
Questions.A: The wisdom of men.

Questions.Q: What way leads to heaven?
Questions.A: A way that men say is foolish, that is, the good news that Paul and his companions have been preaching that causes men to believe in Christ.

Questions.Q: Why do many Jews and many Greeks miss the way to heaven?
Questions.A: The Jews want to see a miracle first before they will believe. The Greeks want them to use wisdom to prove that the good news of Christ is true.

Questions.Q: Why do you think the Jews found that the cross was a thing that prevented them believing in Jesus?
Questions.A: They could not believe that the Christ whom they were waiting for as their King would allow himself to be killed as a criminal on a cross.

Questions.Q: What did the Greeks think about the cross?
Questions.A: It was all nonsense.

Questions.Q: Will Jews and Greeks never go to heaven then?
Questions.A: Those who believe in Jesus Christ and his death on the cross will go to heaven.

Questions.Q: What is Christ to those who believe in him?
Questions.A: He is the one through whom they will see the power and wisdom of God.

Questions.Q: Is God ever foolish or weak?
Questions.A: No. He is wiser and stronger than man. If we think God is weak or foolish, it is because we don't understand his thoughts.

Questions.Q: Why does Paul ask the Corinthians to remember the kind of people they were before they became Christians?
Questions.A: Because few of them were of any importance in the eyes of the people of this world, yet God chose them to become his people.

Questions.Q: What was God's purpose in choosing unimportant people to become his people?
Questions.A: To shame the world's wise men and its rulers and its noble men.
Questions.Note: Paul speaks of "things" (indicated by plural neuter in Greek) but is really speaking (at least primarily) of people. If this question causes confusion or responses suggest this is not clear, consider changes to make this understandable.

Questions.Q: What do we as Christians, since we are unimportant, have to boast about?
Questions.A: Nothing, except what the Lord has done for us.

Questions.Q: What is it that he has done for us?
Questions.A: He has made us members of Christ's family. This is God's wisdom, he makes us good people, he has chosen us for himself, he has bought us and has freed us.

Section.heading: 1 Corinthians 2:1-16 The true wisdom that comes from the Holy Spirit.

Questions.Q: Why would some people say that Paul should have used big words and wisdom to preach the good news of God in Corinth?
Questions.A: Because the Greeks, who were the main inhabitants of Corinth, expected all speakers to do this. It was their custom and way of life.

Questions.Q: What did Paul not do in Corinth?
Questions.A: He did not study the way the Greeks speak so as to imitate their wise thoughts and clever speaking.

Questions.Q: How and what did Paul preach?
Questions.A: He preached about Jesus Christ and the reason for his death on a cross. He was even afraid and trembling.

Questions.Q: Why was he trembling and afraid?
Questions.A: Because, compared with the Greeks, he was a poor speaker.

Questions.Q: How then did Paul hope to persuade his hearers?
Questions.A: It was the Holy Spirit who used Paul's words to persuade his hearers.

Questions.Q: What does this teach all preachers of the good news?
Questions.A: It is God's power, not men's clever words that persuade people to follow Christ.

Questions.Q: Did Paul preach nonsense or speak children's talk?
Questions.A: He taught God's wisdom to true believers. This wisdom was different from that of the rulers and peoples of today's world.

Questions.Q: What good is the wisdom of men?
Questions.A: It produces/repairs nothing.

Questions.Q: What was God's hidden purpose which is now revealed?
Questions.A: That we should get greatness/glory.
Questions.Alternative: What was God's purpose from that hidden wisdom and secret, that is now revealed?
What was God's secret plan that is now revealed?
What was God's plan that is now no longer a secret mystery?
