Questions.Q: What shows that the rulers of this world did not know God's wisdom?
Questions.A: Because they did not recognize Jesus as the Lord of Glory/the Great Master of all the world.
So they crucified him.

Questions.Q: To whom is God's wisdom revealed?
Questions.A: To those who love him.

Questions.Q: How is God's wisdom revealed to them?
Questions.A: By God's Holy Spirit.

Questions.Q: What shows that the Holy Spirit and God are one?
Questions.A: Because, as a man himself knows his own thoughts, so God knows his own thoughts.

Questions.Q: Why has God sent the Holy Spirit into our hearts?
Questions.A: So that we can understand the things which God has abundantly given us.

Questions.Q: Whose wisdom does Paul use in teaching and preaching?
Questions.A: The wisdom that comes from God's Holy Spirit.

Questions.Q: What did Paul teach and whom did he teach?
Questions.A: Meaning of those things that come from God and his Holy Spirit, to those people who have received the Holy Spirit in their hearts.
Questions.Alternative: What did Paul teach and who are the people who accept his teaching?
Questions.Note: For 1 Corinthians 2:14, use either the group A questions or the group B questions. It would be redundant to ask all 3 questions.
group A (1Co 2:14)

Questions.Q: What did Paul teach?
Questions.A: The meaning of those things that come from God and his Holy Spirit.
Questions.Note: For 1 Corinthians 2:14, use either the group A questions or the group B questions. It would be redundant to ask all 3 questions.
group B (1Co 2:14)

Questions.Q: Who were the people who received Paul's teaching?
Questions.A: Those people who have received the Holy Spirit in their hearts.
Questions.Note: group B (1Co 2:14)

Questions.Q: Why cannot a person who follows the wisdom of this world understand the things of God and his Spirit?
Questions.A: He can only understand them through God's Spirit.
Questions.Alternative: Why can a person who follows the wisdom of this world not understand the things of God and his Spirit?

Questions.Q: Who can understand what is in the heart of one in whom the Holy Spirit lives?
Questions.A: Only another person in whom the Holy Spirit lives.

Questions.Q: What great claim does Paul make on behalf of those in whom God's Holy Spirit lives?
Questions.A: They can understand/see the thoughts of Christ.

Section.heading: 1 Corinthians 3:1-23 Do not spoil God's worship place.

Questions.Q: When Paul first preached to the Corinthians were they people in whom God's Holy Spirit lived?
Questions.A: No.
Questions.Alternative: When Paul first preached to the Corinthian Christians, were they people already filled with and ruled by God's Holy Spirit?
When Paul first preached to the Corinthians, were they people already filled with and ruled by God's Holy Spirit?
When Paul first preached to the Corinthians, did they already have God's Holy Spirit?
When Paul first preached to the Corinthians, did they already have God's Holy Spirit living in them?
When Paul first preached to the Corinthians, did they already have the Holy Spirit living in them?

Questions.Q: To what does Paul compare one who has just become a Christian?
Questions.A: To a newborn baby.

Questions.Q: How does a baby grow?
Questions.A: By drinking mother's milk.

Questions.Q: If a person has just become a Christian does it mean that the Holy Spirit is not in him till he understands much more about the things of God?
Questions.A: No, but he learns slowly like a baby drinking milk until he is able to eat food.

Questions.Q: To what does Paul compare elders' talk?
Questions.A: Solid food.

Questions.Q: How are the Corinthians now? Have they grown?
Questions.A: He says they are acting like babies who have no understanding.

Questions.Q: Why?
Questions.A: Because they are fighting among themselves.
Questions.Alternative: Why does he say they are acting like babies?
Why does he compare them to infants?
What shows that they are like immature babies?

Questions.Q: What does this fighting show?
Questions.A: That they are still acting like people who follow the things of this world.

Questions.Q: What would show that church people have become worldly?
Questions.A: That they divide into parties, following different persons, and not united in following Christ.

Questions.Q: Who is Apollos?
Questions.A: After Paul founded the church in Corinth and went on a journey, Apollos arrived and taught the Christians. (See Acts 18:27-19:1.)

Questions.Q: What does Paul think of Apollos?
Questions.A: He says that Apollos, like himself, is a minister/pastor through whom they came to believe in Christ.

Questions.Q: How is Apollos different from Paul?
Questions.A: God gives each man his work to do.

Questions.Q: What is Paul's work? What is Apollos's work?
Questions.A: Paul planted the seed, that is, he founded the church. Apollos watered the seed, that is, he taught the Christians in order that they might grow as Christians.

Questions.Q: Who is the most important, Paul or Apollos?
Questions.A: Neither. God is the most important because only God can make his word grow and increase in people's hearts.

Questions.Q: The sower and the waterer, how are they the same and how are they different?
Questions.A: They work together in one work, but each has a different reward.

Questions.Q: If Paul and Apollos are like farmers, what are the Corinthians like?
Questions.A: God's farm.

Questions.Q: Paul uses another proverb. What does it teach?
Questions.A: The Corinthians are like God's building. Christ is the foundation. Paul is the master builder who laid the foundation. Apollos began building upon that foundation.

Questions.Q: What does Paul mean when he says, "There is no other foundation than Christ"?
Questions.A: There is no way to God except through Jesus Christ. Any teaching that leaves out Christ as the only way to God is false.

Questions.Q: What does Paul teach in this proverb?
Questions.A: Each man's work for Christ will be tested at the Day of Judgment when Christ returns.

Questions.Q: What have gold, silver and jewels in common?
Questions.A: They do not burn easily.
Questions.Alternative: In this proverb, what do gold, silver and jewels have in common?
What do gold, silver and jewels have in common?
What do gold, silver and precious stones have in common?

Questions.Q: What have wood, spear grass and thatch in common?
Questions.A: They burn easily.
Questions.Alternative: In this proverb, what do wood, spear grass and thatch have in common?
What do wood, grass and thatch have in common?
What do wood, hay and stubble have in common?

Questions.Q: Are you building with things that will not burn?
Questions.Note: Personal question - answers will vary, but should demonstrate an understanding of the symbolic language of the passage and reflect an understanding of temporal vs. eternal things.

Questions.Q: What happens to you if you have been building God's house with things that will burn?
Questions.A: In the Judgment day Christ will show that your work has been wasted and was for nothing but you yourself will be saved by God.

Questions.Q: Discuss: What kind of work for God will not be found to be for nothing?
What does this proverb teach?
Questions.A: Christians are like God's worship place in which his Holy Spirit is living.

Questions.Q: Is it wrong for us to spoil God's temple? How do you understand this?
Questions.A: There are several interpretations:
1. We should not do work in the church which is for nothing.
2. We should not harm fellow Christians.
3. We should not wrong ourselves.
4. We should not commit suicide.

Questions.Q: What does God think of the wisdom of the people of this world?
Questions.A: It is not wisdom. It achieves nothing.

Questions.Q: What does God do to the world's wise men?
Questions.A: He uses their own deceits to catch them.

Questions.Q: How should we become wise?
Questions.A: By becoming like a child/or like we are fools.

Questions.Q: Why is our boasting about human beings useless?
Questions.A: Because everything is ours since we belong to Christ. Everything that happens in the world, our life, our death, those who bring us God's word, now and in the future, are all for us. And Christ is for God.

Section.heading: 1 Corinthians 4:1-21 How for Christ's sake God's apostles have become as if they are fools.

Questions.Q: What are the three important things that an apostle should be?
Questions.A: 1. A servant of Christ.
2. One who reveals the secret things of God.
3. One whom people can trust.

Questions.Q: To whom, as an apostle, is Paul answerable?
Questions.A: Only God who sent him.

Questions.Q: Is Paul's conscience troubling him?
Questions.A: No, he is not aware that he has failed.

Questions.Q: For what is it that he is answerable?
Questions.A: His work as an apostle.
Questions.Note: NB. If this is not clear, make suggested alterations.

Questions.Q: Who does Paul tell them not to judge?
Questions.A: Himself and the other apostles, and in fact anyone.

Questions.Q: When is the time for judging?
Questions.A: When our Master comes again.

Questions.Q: Why will it then be possible to judge?
Questions.A: Because Christ will reveal the thoughts of all people.

Questions.Q: Who will receive praise from God?
Questions.A: The ones who have done well.

Questions.Q: What can prevent us from boasting of one man and despising another?
Questions.A: We should not go beyond what God's word allows.

Questions.Q: Why have we no right to boast of ourselves?
Questions.A: Because if we have anything, it has come from God and not from ourselves.

Questions.Q: Is Paul happy about the Corinthians?
Questions.A: No.

Questions.Q: What is he worried about?
Questions.A: They boast about their riches and power.

Questions.Q: What riches and power?
Questions.A: The blessings of being already members of the Kingdom of God.
Questions.Alternative: What are these things he mentions here: riches and power?
What are the riches and power he mentions here?
What are the riches and power he is talking about?
What riches and power is Paul referring to?
What riches and power is he referring to?
What does he mean by "riches and power"?

Questions.Q: What is Paul saying in this proverb?
Questions.A: It is as if he and the other apostles are being brought into the public games, where the people will make them play and then laugh at them and then kill them. This is what the Romans did to criminals. Later they sometimes did this to Christians.

Questions.Q: What is Paul saying here?
Questions.A: They think of themselves as wise, knowing all about Christian things. They think they are strong and deserving of respect. But not so.

Questions.Q: Describe the hard life that Paul and the other apostles have suffered.
Questions.A: They suffer hunger and thirst and lack of clothes. They are beaten. They have no house to live in. They work hard with their own hands to get money to eat.

Questions.Q: How are the apostles imitating Christ and his teachings?
Questions.A: When people insult them, they pray to God to bless those people. When people persecute them, they suffer patiently. When people speak against them, they answer humbly. They have become like rubbish, worthless, in the opinion of the people of this world.

Questions.Q: Why is Paul telling them all this?
Questions.A: To warn them of their faults, as a father warns his children.

Questions.Q: How is Paul different from other teachers of God's word that they have in Corinth?
Questions.A: Only Paul is their father, because he was the first to preach the good news to them.

Questions.Q: What is it that they should imitate?
Questions.A: Paul's way of life.

Questions.Q: Why is Paul sending Timothy to them?
Questions.A: To remind them of the way Paul lives the Christian life.
Questions.Note: NB. Is this well translated?

Questions.Q: Why does he say this last sentence?
Questions.A: To show that he is not a hypocrite.

Questions.Q: What makes some of the Christians in Corinth arrogant?
Questions.A: They think that Paul will never come and visit them again.

Questions.Q: If Paul returns to visit them, what will he do?
Questions.A: He will see whether their deeds are greater than their words.

Questions.Q: How do we as Christians show that what we say about our belief in Christ is true?
Questions.A: By living the Christian life.

Questions.Q: What is Paul's warning?
Questions.A: He will punish them unless they repent. But he prefers that they repent so that he will not have to punish them.

Questions.Q: Will he really beat them?
Questions.A: Probably he is using a proverb.

Section.heading: 1 Corinthians 5:1-13 Drive the wrong doer from your church.

Questions.Q: What troubles Paul?
Questions.A: One of the church members at Corinth is making love to his father's wife/his father's other wife.

Questions.Q: Why is this bad?
Questions.A: Even those who don't worship God say that this is wrong. It is incest, i.e. loving her when you and she are closely related.

Questions.Q: What have the Corinthian Christians done about this?
Questions.A: Nothing. They remain proud of themselves.

Questions.Q: What should they do?
Questions.A: 1. They should be ashamed and weep.
2. They should excommunicate (drive) that man from their church.

Questions.Q: What is Paul telling them to do?
Questions.A: To meet, and in the power/with the authority of our master, Jesus Christ, put that man into the Devil's hands.

Questions.Q: Who is giving them this authority?
Questions.A: Paul tells them that if he was there he would do this. But in his absence they themselves have the power to do this.

Questions.Q: What does it mean to put that man into the Devil's hands?
Questions.A: He is no longer allowed to come to church or to be with Christians. He is not under God's protection anymore.

Questions.Q: What is the purpose of this excommunication?
Questions.A: That the man's soul may be saved on the day Christ returns.

Questions.Q: What is the meaning of "yeast" in this proverb?
Questions.A: It stands for sin.

Questions.Q: What is he teaching?
Questions.A: 1. If they don't remove that man from the church, he will cause all the other church members to sin like him. Or
2. That sin of that man will cause him to go on to sin in every other way.
Questions.Alternative: What is Paul teaching in these verses?

Questions.Q: Explain how what the Jews did before the Passover is a lesson for us.
Questions.A: They removed all yeast from their houses and ate unleavened bread. This was to show that they were cleansing their hearts. As for us Christians we cleanse our hearts of the sins and hatred of our life as non-Christians and we should do good and speak the truth.

Questions.Q: How have the Corinthian Christians misunderstood something he wrote in a previous letter?
Questions.A: They understood him to say that they should avoid all non-Christians because all non-Christians are sinners.

Questions.Q: What is he really teaching?
Questions.A: They should avoid any so called Christians who commit such sins as adultery or rape, who are greedy for money, who worship fetishes, who insult people, who are drunkards, or are corrupt.

Questions.Q: Why should we avoid such so-called Christians?
Questions.A: Because they bring the name of Christ and Christians into disrespect and disrepute.

Questions.Q: How can we be in the world but not belong to it?
Questions.A: We have to live on this earth but we should avoid the sins that worldly people do.

Questions.Q: What is it that Christians should do and not do, according to this verse?
Questions.A: It is not their business to judge non-Christians. But it is their business to judge church members and to expel any wrongdoer.

Questions.Q: Who will judge non-church goers?
Questions.A: God

Section.heading: 1 Corinthians 6:1-11 Christians should not take one another to court.

Questions.Q: What was shameful in taking a case to a judge who does not worship God?
Questions.A: All disputes between Christians should be settled by Christians.

Questions.Q: Does this verse not contradict 5:13?
Questions.A: No. It is only when Christ comes again that he will give Christians authority over others, over even God's angels.

Questions.Q: Why then should the Corinthians be ashamed?
Questions.A: As [future] judges of all the people of the world [and the angels], they ought to be able to judge small matters among themselves.

Questions.Q: Does it mean that we not Christ or God will be the judges of the people of the world?
Questions.A: He will be the Judge and he will then give us power over others, just as a chief has power to judge.

Questions.Q: How do these verses add to verses 1-5?
Questions.A: If a Christian has a dispute with another Christian, it should be judged by another Christian, one who is able to settle the case wisely.

Questions.Q: Since the Corinthian Christians take one another to court, what does that show?
Questions.A: That they are not living as Christians should live - they have been defeated by the Devil.

Questions.Q: How are they behaving towards one another?
Questions.A: They are wronging and stealing from one another.

Questions.Q: If my Christian brother does me wrong should I not take him to court?
Questions.A: No, I should be patient with him and let the case be settled by another church member.

Questions.Q: Name all the sins which Paul speaks against.
Questions.A: Worship of fetishes, adultery, fornication, homosexuality, stealing, greediness, drunkenness, slandering and swindling.

Questions.Q: Can such sinners ever enter God's Kingdom?
Questions.A: Yes, if they repent and turn from their sins. Some of the Corinthian Christians had been like that.

Questions.Q: How is a sinner changed and what happens to him?
Questions.A: The Holy Spirit washes away his sins in the name of Jesus Christ and presents him to God and frees him from his guilt.

Section.heading: 1 Corinthians 6:12-20 Your bodies are like God's worship place.

Questions.Q: If Christians say, "I am permitted to do anything I want", what do you answer from this verse?
Questions.A: If something seems to be permissible, also ask yourself, does it help you, does it help your fellow men? If it is going to get control over you, then stop it.

Questions.Q: In this verse what sins is Paul speaking against?
Questions.A: Greediness for food, adultery and rape.

Questions.Q: What do these sins have in common?
Questions.A: They are all sins of the body.

Questions.Q: From this verse how do you answer the one who says that he can use his body in any way he wishes?
Questions.A: We should use our body, as well as our heads and hearts, to worship God and he will take care of our bodies in return.

Questions.Q: If we as Christians belong to Christ, what does God promise to do with our bodies?
Questions.A: He will raise them from death to life again, as he raised Christ from death.

Questions.Q: Why does Paul say that it is very bad especially for a Christian to sleep with a prostitute?
Questions.A: Because as Christians every part of our body belongs to Christ. [Would we expect Christ to lie with a prostitute?]

Questions.Q: In the verse quoted from God's word book, (Genesis 2:24), who is it that become united?
Questions.A: Husband and wife.

Questions.Q: What is Paul teaching?
Questions.A: Sexual intercourse makes a marriage because in this way man and woman become united. So if a man has intercourse with a prostitute, it is as if he has married her.

Questions.Q: Discuss: What does this teach us concerning a man having intercourse with his girl friend or his promised wife before he has taken her to his house?
Questions.A: Suggested answers: He should refrain from intercourse till he has brought her to his house and married her. Or if he has had intercourse with her he should by all means marry her.
Questions.Note: NB. If these teachings cannot be understood from the verses as translated, suggest alterations.

Questions.Q: How do we unite with Christ?
Questions.A: Not by sexual intercourse. But the Holy Spirit makes us to be of one mind/united with Christ.

Questions.Q: What do adultery and rape have in common?
Questions.A: They are sins against one's own body. (See 6:13.)

Questions.Q: What of all other sins? Are they sins?
Questions.A: Yes, but they are sins against other people.
Questions.Alternative: What about all other sins? Aren't they sins?

Questions.Q: Give two reasons why it is wrong to use our bodies for sexual sins.
Questions.A: 1. Our bodies belong to God not to ourselves alone.
2. The Holy Spirit lives in our bodies.

Questions.Q: Give another illustration, using a building, to explain Paul's teaching.
Questions.A: Just as it would be wrong to use a church as a brothel, so it would be wrong to use our bodies to sleep with a prostitute.

Questions.Q: What does this "golden rule" say?
Questions.A: Use your bodies in such a way that people will see how you live and will praise God.

Questions.Q: Why does Paul say that if a man does not marry he does well?
Questions.A: Paul was unmarried. He believed that the end of the world was coming soon, so that people should pay attention to that and not to marrying. (See verse 26.)

Questions.Q: Does he say that marriage is wrong?
Questions.A: Not at all.

Questions.Q: What reason does he give that it is good for men and women to marry?
Questions.A: So that they will not be tempted to commit adultery and rape.

Questions.Q: Why does Paul give this command?
Questions.A: 1. The same reason as in 7:2, that is, to prevent the other from committing adultery with another person.
2. Because the husband and his wife belong to each other, that is, they have the right to ask the other for sexual intercourse.
Questions.Note: NB. Is this well understood?

Questions.Q: What exception does Paul give to this rule?
Questions.A: 1. First they should agree together not to sleep together.
2. It should be for a short time.
3. It should be for the purpose of having time for more prayer.
4. Then they should come to sleep together again.

Questions.Q: Why should it be for a short time alone?
Questions.A: If not so the Devil will tempt them to love another woman/man.

Questions.Q: Does Paul speak of a man's wife or wives?
Questions.A: He speaks of a man having only one wife.

Questions.Q: These things are not a law but are permission/are good advice. Which things?
Questions.A: 1. Verse 5 - The refraining from sexual intercourse for a little time. OR
2. That every one should marry. This is the preferred interpretation.
Questions.Alternative: These things are not a law but are permission. Which things?
These things are not a law but are good advice. Which things?

Questions.Q: Why is it only permission/good advice?
Questions.A: Because some can refrain from marriage and be happy, but others cannot be happy until they marry. Each one has his gift from God which is different from his fellow man's.
Questions.Alternative: Why is it only permission?
Why is it only good advice?

Questions.Q: Whom does Paul advise not to marry if they are able to refrain from marriage?
Questions.A: Unmarried men and widows.

Questions.Q: What is marriage to prevent from happening?
Questions.A: It is not good that a man remains single, but be always wanting a wife. Or for a woman (widow) to remain single, and always be wanting a husband.

Questions.Q: What is Paul teaching?
Questions.A: It is wrong for a man to divorce his wife or for a wife to divorce her husband. But if they do separate neither husband or wife should marry another person. They should try to be reconciled.

Questions.Q: What kind of law is this?
Questions.A: It definitely comes from our Master Jesus Christ.

Questions.Q: Does Paul encourage a Christian to marry a non-Christian?
Questions.A: No. (See 2 Corinthians 6:14.)

Questions.Q: What then is he saying?
Questions.A: That if, for example, the husband becomes a Christian, but his wife does not, this is not a reason for him to divorce her.

Questions.Q: How then should he act? What should he do?
Questions.A: If the wife is willing to stay with him, he should not divorce her.
Questions.Alternative: How then should the Christian partner act? What should he do?

Questions.Q: What does this verse say?
Questions.A: The same as 7:12, but in the case where the woman is a Christian and her husband is not.

Questions.Q: What is the reason for all this?
Questions.A: 1. A Christian makes his/her non-Christian wife/husband no longer to be unclean in the sight of God.
2. This is also the same for their children.

Questions.Q: Does that mean that the non-Christian wife/husband has become a Christian or will go to heaven?
Questions.A: No. He has to make his own decision. (See verse 16.)
Questions.Alternative: Does that mean that the non-Christian wife has become a Christian or will go to heaven?
Does that mean that the non-Christian husband has become a Christian or will go to heaven?

Questions.Q: Is the child of a person who is a Christian also a Christian?
Questions.A: No. He has to make his own decision.

Questions.Q: What is Paul teaching here?
Questions.A: If the non-Christian wife/husband wants to leave her husband/his wife, let him do so, and do not force him/her to return.

Questions.Q: Why so?
Questions.A: Because God wants us to live at peace with one another.

Questions.Q: Does this give permission to divorce and remarriage?
Questions.A: Some commentators say that this is so. Others say it is not so. The main thing is to avoid fighting.

Questions.Q: Why does he think that a Christian wife might save her husband (and a husband save his wife)?
Questions.A: Because this should be one of the reasons that a Christian will remain with her non-Christian husband (wife).

Questions.Q: What does Paul mean by "saving"?
Questions.A: That God will save the husband/wife because of the way that wife/husband lives and speaks.

Section.heading: 1 Corinthians 7:17-24 Continue to live how you were living when God called you to follow him.

Questions.Q: What is it that Paul says that we should not change?
Questions.A: The way we are living (status) at present - married, unmarried, circumcised, uncircumcised, slave or freeman.
Questions.Alternative: What is it that Paul says that believers should not change?
What does Paul say that believers should not change?
What does Paul say that we should not change?

Questions.Q: Why?
Questions.A: God has called us live in peace (i.e., not to struggle to resolve intractable relationships problems with non-believers to) (15)
Our civil status or lot in life is of less importance than keeping God's commands. (19)
The time is short, Christ will return soon (or the time that each of us has to live for God on earth is limited) (29)
Questions.Alternative: Why does Paul say that believers should continue in their current situation?
Questions.Note: Since some of the possible answers are found in the preceding and following sections, it might be necessary to read the surrounding verses or come back to this question again after looking at the following section.
Since this section does not clearly address the question of why, the main thing is to ensure that the respondent gives a reasonable answer and does not come to any incorrect conclusions.

Questions.Q: Do we change our sinful way of life?
Questions.A: Yes.

Questions.Q: What is more important than the "status" that we have, that is, married, unmarried, slave or freeman?
Questions.A: Following God's commands.

Questions.Q: Is Paul saying that slavery is good?
Questions.A: No, because he says that if a slave has the chance to get free, he should do so. No one should willingly become the slave of another man - verse 23.

Questions.Q: How has the coming of Christ changed slavery?
Questions.A: Both master and slave now belong to Christ, who is over both master and slave.

Questions.Q: Is Paul saying that slaves are now free and freemen are now slaves?
Questions.A: No. Both are free from sin and the Devil and now serve Christ.

Questions.Q: What was the great price that Christ paid?
Questions.A: He gave his own life to buy us from sin.

Section.heading: 1 Corinthians 7:25-40 Continuing on the subject of marriage.

Questions.Q: Summarize these verses.
Questions.A: It is wise not to change one's status by marrying or divorcing.

Questions.Q: Is it wrong to marry?
Questions.A: No.

Questions.Q: Why does Paul advise them not to marry?
Questions.A: So as to avoid the kind of troubles that married people suffer.

Questions.Q: Is Paul making a law for them?
Questions.A: No, he is only giving them good advice.

Questions.Q: What time is now not much?
Questions.A: Some say: the time when Christ will come again, others say: the troubles that Christ said would come upon all people before Christ returns.
Questions.Alternative: What time is now short?
What is going to come soon?
What time is coming to an end?
What time is coming to an end soon?

Questions.Q: Why does Paul give this advice in these verses?
Questions.A: Because of how the world is now changing.

Questions.Q: Should we not care for our wives and children anymore? Should we refuse to perform funerals anymore?
Questions.A: No, Paul wants us to live our lives so that the Kingdom of God is more important than the things of this world.
Questions.Alternative: Should we stop caring for our wives and children, no longer express emotions, or quit our jobs?
Should we stop caring for our wives and children, deny our emotions, or quit our jobs?

Questions.Q: Can an unmarried person please God?
Questions.A: Yes, but since he/she is also trying to please his wife/her husband, he/she does not have all his/her time to go to God. He/she cannot do both well.

Questions.Q: Why does Paul give this advice?
Questions.A: It is for their own good, that they might do what is right and worship our Master with all their hearts.

Questions.Q: When is it good to marry?
Questions.A: When the girl who is promised in marriage is already of marriageable age, and the man is unable to control himself.

Questions.Q: What does this verse say about your marriage customs?
Questions.A: A man should not sleep with his wife until he has married her.

Questions.Q: What permission does Paul give here?
Questions.A: If a man is promised to a woman, but he can control himself, and no one is forcing him to marry, and he decides not to marry, then he is free to remain unmarried.

Questions.Q: In Paul's opinion, is it better to marry or not to marry?
Questions.A: Not to marry.
Questions.Alternative: In Paul's opinion is it better to marry or not to marry?
Does Paul think it is better to marry or not?
Does Paul think it is better to marry or stay single?
Does Paul think it is better to marry or remain unmarried?

Questions.Q: What is Paul's advice to widows?
Questions.A: Do not marry again. But if they marry, they should marry a Christian.

Section.heading: 1 Corinthians 8:1-13 Concerning food and animals killed and given to fetishes.

Questions.Q: What do you think was the question that the Corinthians had asked Paul and he is now answering?
Questions.A: Should we eat food or animals killed for fetishes/idols?
Questions.Alternative: What question do you think the Corinthians had asked Paul, which he is now answering?
What question do you think the Corinthians asked Paul that he is now answering?

Questions.Q: Why does he speak about knowledge and being wise? What did the Corinthians say in addition to their question?
Questions.A: Fetishes are nothing, therefore, they said, they can eat food/meat offered to them.
Questions.Alternative: Why does he speak about knowledge and being wise? What did the Corinthians say that we understand from Paul's answer to them in these verses?
Why does he speak about knowledge and being wise? From the way Paul answers their question in these verses, what can we understand that the Corinthians said?
Why does he speak about knowledge and being wise? From the way Paul answers their question in these verses, what did the Corinthians say or think?

Questions.Q: How does Paul answer their "wisdom"?
Questions.A: If a person is clever, or has knowledge, he will become proud.

Questions.Q: How should he use his knowledge?
Questions.A: He should use it to strengthen his fellow Christians in their faith.

Questions.Q: What is the best kind of knowledge that a person/man should want?
Questions.A: To know and love God so that God will know him, that is, God will accept him as his own person.
Questions.Alternative: What is the best kind of knowledge that a person should want?
What is the best kind of knowledge that a man should want?

Questions.Q: What does this teach us about fetishes?
Questions.A: 1. They have no power in this world.
2. There are many fetishes, some say some are on the earth and some in heaven.
3. Some people call them master and worship them as if they are God.
Questions.Alternative: What does this teach us about idols?

Questions.Q: What do we learn about God from this verse?
Questions.A: 1. He alone exists - there is no other.
2. He created us.
Questions.Note: NB. Is it absolutely clear that Paul is saying that fetishes do not exist, except that people believe that they exist?

Questions.Q: Whom are we permitted to call our Master?
Questions.A: God and Jesus Christ.
Questions.Alternative: Whom are we permitted to call Lord?
Who may we call Lord?
Who is it right to call our Lord?

Questions.Q: What shows that Jesus Christ is equal to God?
Questions.A: Because through Christ, God created the world and gave us life.

Questions.Q: What kind of people are those whose consciences are weak, that is, their hearts are troubled concerning eating food that has been offered to fetishes?
Questions.A: They are those who have recently become Christians and they still believe that fetishes exist and have power.
Questions.Alternative: What kind of people are those whose consciences are weak, that is, their hearts are troubled concerning eating food that has been offered to idols?

Questions.Q: What, for such people, is the result of eating fetish food?
Questions.A: Their hearts become dirty.
Questions.Alternative: What, for such people, is the result of eating food sacrificed to idols?
What do such people think will happen if they eat food sacrificed to idols?

Questions.Q: What foods does Paul taboo/prohibit eating?
Questions.A: None
Questions.Alternative: What foods does Paul prohibit eating?
What foods does Paul forbid?
What kinds of food does Paul say are not allowed?
What foods does Paul taboo eating?
What foods does Paul say not to eat?

Questions.Q: How can we please God in what we eat?
Questions.A: It does nothing for us in God's sight to eat or to taboo any food.

Questions.Q: Why then does Paul taboo the eating of food that has been offered to fetishes?
Questions.A: Because if we eat it, and one who has a weak conscience [that is, one who believes that fetishes exist and have power] sees us, he will fall into sin. [He might also eat it and feel guilty. Or, he might become judgmental. Or, he might go back to worshiping fetishes and stop believing in Christ.]
Questions.Alternative: Why then does Paul taboo the eating of food that has been offered to idols?
Why then does Paul prohibit the eating of food that has been offered to idols?
Why then does Paul prohibit the eating of food sacrificed to idols?
Why then does Paul say not to eat food that has been offered to idols?
Why then does Paul say not to eat food sacrificed to idols?

Questions.Q: If you through eating fetish food cause a fellow Christian to sin, what is that to you?
Questions.A: It shows you do him wrong and you cause his faith to stop and so you do wrong to Christ.
Questions.Alternative: If you through eating food sacrificed to idols cause a fellow Christian to sin, what is that to you?
If you cause a fellow Christian to sin by eating food sacrificed to idols, why is that a problem for you?

Questions.Q: What rule does Paul give us about fetish foods?
Questions.A: If our eating such food causes a fellow Christian to sin, then we should not eat such food anymore.
Questions.Alternative: What rule does Paul give us about foods sacrificed to idols?
What rule does Paul make regarding foods sacrificed to idols?
What rule does Paul give us about foods offered to idols?

Section.heading: 1 Corinthians 9:1-27 Christ's apostles have the right to receive food.

Questions.Q: Why does Paul have to say that he is free?
Questions.A: Because in 8:13 he puts himself under a law, which is not really a law, for the sake of others. But he is free to live how God tells him.

Questions.Q: What shows that he is free?
Questions.A: He is an apostle of Jesus.
Questions.Alternative: What else is he, in addition to being a freeman?
What important "right" does Paul assert?
What important claim does Paul make about himself?

Questions.Q: What shows that he is truly an apostle of Jesus?
Questions.A: 1. He has seen Jesus with his own eyes.
2. They, the Corinthians, came to believe in Jesus because of Paul's work for Jesus.

Questions.Q: Who of all people should not say that Paul is not an apostle?
Questions.A: The Corinthians.

Questions.Q: Why so?
Questions.A: Because they became Christians through Paul's work.

Questions.Q: What two rights does Paul claim for himself and all apostles?
Questions.A: 1. To get food and drink for the work he does.
2. To be accompanied on his journeys by a Christian wife.

Questions.Q: Of Paul, Peter and Jesus's brothers, which ones had a wife who accompanied him on his journeys?
Questions.A: All except Paul.

Questions.Q: Why does Paul ask this question?
Questions.A: Because the Corinthians never offered him any money for food and drink.

Questions.Q: What proverbs or examples does Paul use to teach?
Questions.A: 1. A soldier does not serve at his own expense, paying for his own food.
2. A farmer eats food from his own farm.
3. The owner of a cow drinks the cow's milk.
4. A cow that treads (guinea) corn to thresh it for the farmer is allowed to eat some of it.
Questions.Note: NB. If there is any problem concerning the cow/ox being used to thresh corn, write down the problem.

Questions.Q: What do these proverbs and the law in verse 10 teach?
Questions.A: They teach that those who do God's work, like teaching God's word, should get money for their food and drink.

Questions.Q: Did Paul and his fellow teachers claim food and drink from the Corinthians while he was in their town?
Questions.A: No.

Questions.Q: Why not?
Questions.A: So that nothing would prevent the preaching of Christ's good news from going forward.

Questions.Q: Why would accepting food and drink hinder God's work?
Questions.A: Because some would falsely accuse Paul of preaching only to get money.
Questions.Note: NB. Is this well understood?

Questions.Q: What further illustration/proverb does Paul use to prove his case?
Questions.A: Priests/Sacrifice offerers eat some of the meat that people offer to God.
Questions.Alternative: What further illustration does Paul use to prove his case?
What further proverb does Paul use to prove his case?

Questions.Q: Is Paul wanting something from them for his preaching to them?
Questions.A: No.

Questions.Q: Why?
Questions.A: So that he can boast that he is working for them for nothing.
Questions.Alternative: Why not?
Why does Paul not want anything from them?
Why does Paul not want anything from them for his preaching to them?
Questions.Note: NB. Is it clear that "for nothing" means "without receiving any payment"?

Questions.Q: Do you understand why Paul cannot boast about the fact that he preached to them, but he can boast that when he preached, he did not collect money from them?
Questions.A: If it had been true that he chose of his own will to preach, then he could rightly claim payment. But as it was God who forced him to become a preacher, like a master makes a slave work for him, he cannot claim a reward, he is only doing his duty. If he fails to preach, God will punish him.

Questions.Q: Will Paul get any reward at all?
Questions.A: His reward in this life is the right to refuse a reward from men. But we know that now he has received his reward from God in heaven.

Questions.Q: What other right does Paul refuse to use?
Questions.A: To be free from following any man.

Questions.Q: Why did he make himself everyone's slave?
Questions.A: To make as many as possible become Christians.

Questions.Q: In what way did Paul become a slave to everyone?
Questions.A: When he lived among Jews he followed their laws, although, he was free from following those laws, so as to win Jews for Christ. But when he lived among those who are not Jews, he did not follow the Jews' laws.

Questions.Q: Why would some accuse Paul of being against God's law?
Questions.A: Because the Jews received their laws from God.

Questions.Q: Is Paul really free from God's law?
Questions.A: He is free from the laws of God in the Old Testament, but is now under Christ's law in the New Testament.
Questions.Note: NB. If this is not understood, make suggestions for alterations.

Questions.Q: How did Paul help those whose faith in Christ was weak?
Questions.A: He became like them.

Questions.Q: In what way can we become like those whose faith is weak in order to help them?
Questions.A: For example, if we want to help someone who believes that it is wrong to eat certain foods, then for his sake we will not eat such foods, though there is no law of God that forbids us to eat such foods. (See 1 Corinthians 8:9-13.)

Questions.Q: Summarize the rule that Paul has made for himself.
Questions.A: Everyone he meets, he becomes like them, in order that by any way that is good to save some for God.

Questions.Q: What does Paul use this proverb about running to teach?
Questions.A: The proverb: Train for the race every day and then run so as to win the race. The reward is a crown/hat of leaves. The meaning: try hard to live the Christian life, and do not slacken. Try to be better than other people in following Christ. Your reward is a place of authority in heaven.

Questions.Q: What does Paul use this proverb about boxing to teach?
Questions.A: He is controlling his body so that he does not give in to the bad desires of his heart.

Questions.Q: What does Paul fear?
Questions.A: That if he lets his sinful desires control him, he himself will lose his place in heaven, even though he has faithfully preached the Gospel for a long time.
Questions.Note: NB. If this is not clear, suggest alterations.

Questions.Q: Discuss: What warning does this give to church elders, pastors, teachers and others?

Section.heading: 1 Corinthians 10:1-11:1 Why we should leave off worshiping fetishes.

Questions.Q: What, according to Paul, is the meaning of the Jews following the cloud and passing through the Red Sea unharmed?
Questions.A: It was like a baptism. Showing that they were followers of Moses.

Questions.Q: What was the meaning of the food and water that the Jews received in the desert?
Questions.A: It all came from God and Christ.

Questions.Q: What was the punishment for those who did not please God?
Questions.A: They all died on the way from one side of the desert to the other.

Questions.Q: Why does Paul teach the Corinthians about the Jews in the desert?
Questions.A: He says that the punishments that God used to punish them should warn us not to be like them.

Questions.Q: What sins did those Jews commit?
Questions.A: Wanting bad things, and worshiping fetishes, eating and drinking excessively and dancing fetish dances.

Questions.Q: What happened to the Jews who committed fornication and adultery?
Questions.A: 23,000 died in one day.

Questions.Q: What sin caused some to be bitten by snakes?
Questions.A: They spoke against God, tempting him to punish them.

Questions.Q: What happened to those who grumbled against God?
Questions.A: God sent an angel to kill them.

Questions.Q: In short, why were they punished? What is the real reason for punishment?
Questions.A: So as to warn us not to sin again.

Questions.Q: Why were all these events written down in the Old Testament?
Questions.A: To warn us who live in today's world not to sin again.

Questions.Q: Why does he say we live in the last days of this world?
Questions.A: Because at the end of the world God will judge all people.

Questions.Q: What kind of sin does Paul think the Corinthians are guilty of?
Questions.A: Pride, that is, they thought that because they are Christians, God is pleased with them, just as Jews thought God was pleased with them because they were his people.

Questions.Q: Do you have a proverb that says, "Pride comes before a fall"?
What does this verse teach us about temptation that comes from the Devil and about trouble?
Questions.A: 1. Any such temptation or trouble that comes to you, many people are already experiencing it all the time. It is nothing new.

2. God has promised and will not break his word that he will not let any trouble test you which you cannot get out of. He will show you a way out so that you can resist the temptation and endure the trouble and get patience.

Questions.Q: How should Christians who live in a pagan world begin to avoid sinning?
Questions.A: They should leave off/run from worship of fetishes.

Questions.Q: Why do Christians celebrate/eat the Lord's supper/food?
Questions.A: 1. To remember our Master Christ and his death. The bread represents his body, the drink represents his blood.
2. And to show that, though we are many, we are united.
Questions.Alternative: Why do Christians celebrate the Lord's supper?
Why do Christians celebrate the Lord's food?
Why do Christians eat the Lord's supper?
Why do Christians eat the Lord's food?

Questions.Q: What is the meaning of the sacrifice of animals that the Jews offer?
Questions.A: 1. They are united together.
2. They are worshiping God.

Questions.Q: If Christians join in the sacrifices offered to fetishes and eat the meat that is sacrificed to fetishes what does that show?
Questions.A: That they are worshiping fetishes and are united with fetish worshipers.
Questions.Alternative: If Christians join in the sacrifices offered to idols and eat the meat that is sacrificed to idols what does that show?
If believers join in the sacrifices offered to idols and eat the meat that is sacrificed to idols what does that show?
If Christians join in the sacrifices offered to idols or eat food sacrificed to idols what does that show?
If Christians eat food sacrificed to idols what does that show?
If Christians participate in pagan sacrifices what does that show?

Questions.Q: Does that show that fetishes really do exist and that sacrificing to fetishes has a value?
Questions.A: No, what they do not know, but which is true, is that the fetishes are really the devil and it is the devil that fetish worshipers are worshiping.
Questions.Alternative: Does that show that idols have power or that sacrificing to them has real meaning?
Does that mean that food offered to idols has some significance, or that idols are real gods?

Questions.Q: Why will God be angry at Christians who eat fetish sacrifices?
Questions.A: Because it shows they are worshiping the devil, not God.
Questions.Alternative: Why will God be angry at Christians who eat food sacrificed to idols?
Why will God be angry at people who take communion and also eat food sacrificed to idols?
Why will God be angry at people who participate in the Lord's Table and also eat food sacrificed to idols?

Questions.Q: What answer do some Christians give to Paul's warning?
Questions.A: They say that they are free to eat anything because there is no longer any food that is tabooed.

Questions.Q: How does Paul answer this objection?
Questions.A: Just because it is okay for you personally to do something, love for others should keep you from doing it if it will cause someone else to stumble.

Questions.Q: What is it that is not always good or helpful to others?
Questions.A: The freedom that we have to eat any food.

Questions.Q: In short what is Paul forbidding?
Questions.A: The eating of meat that has been sacrificed to fetishes.

Questions.Q: Are there any exceptions to this rule?
Questions.A: We may eat meat that is sold in the market place. But we must not ask if it has already been sacrificed to fetishes.

Questions.Q: What does this verse teach us about food?
Questions.A: All food is a gift from God the Creator to us human beings.

Questions.Q: What rule does Paul make for a Christian going to eat with a fetish worshiper?
Questions.A: We may go and eat anything that is offered to us and we should not ask if the food has been sacrificed to fetishes.
Questions.Alternative: What rule does Paul make for a Christian going to eat with an idol worshiper?
What rule does Paul give for Christians going to eat with idol worshipers?
What rule does Paul make for a believer going to eat with an idol worshiper?
What rule does Paul make for a Christian going to eat with an idol worshipper?
What rule does Paul give for Christians going to eat with idol worshippers?
What rule does Paul make for a believer going to eat with an idol worshipper?
What rule does Paul make for a Christian going to eat with a fetish worshipper?

Questions.Q: What if someone tells us, without our asking, that it is fetish food, what then?
Questions.A: We should refuse to eat it.
Questions.Alternative: What if someone tells us, without our asking, that it is food sacrificed to idols?
What should we do if someone tells us that the food was sacrificed to idols?
What should we do if someone tells, without our asking, us that the food was sacrificed to idols?
What should we do if someone tells us that the food was offered to idols?

Questions.Q: Why should we refuse to eat it?
Questions.A: For the sake of the one who told us it is fetish food so as not to cause that man to enter sin.

Questions.Q: What two answers will some Christians give to Paul's rule that you should refuse to eat food that you know is fetish food?
Questions.A: 1. Why should I be concerned when someone tells me it is fetish food [food sacrificed to an idol]?
2. If I thank God, not a fetish/idol, for my food, is that not enough to permit me to eat it?
Questions.Alternative: What two answers will some Christians give to Paul's rule that you should refuse to eat food that you know is food sacrificed to idols?
What two answers will some Christians give to Paul's rule not to eat food sacrificed to idols?
What might some Christians say about Paul's rule that you should not eat food that you know was sacrificed to idols?
What might some Christians say about Paul's rule that you should not eat food that you know was offered to idols?

Questions.Q: How does Paul give a rule that summarizes all that he has said from verses 14-30?
Questions.A: What ever you eat or you drink or you do, do it so that people will praise God. Do not do anything that will make people angry with you. Imitate Paul who tried to please people in what he did.

Questions.Q: Why did Paul try to please others?
Questions.A: So that God might save them.

Questions.Q: Why should we imitate Paul?
Questions.A: Because he imitated Christ.

Questions.Q: Discuss: If fetish worshipers get angry with you because you refuse to eat fetish food, should you eat or continue to refuse to eat? Think what Christ would do. Did he ever eat food that was sacrificed to fetishes?
Questions.Alternative: Discuss: If fetish worshippers get angry with you because you refuse to eat fetish food, should you eat or continue to refuse to eat? Think what Christ would do. Did he ever eat food that was sacrificed to fetishes?

Discuss: If idol worshippers get angry with you because you refuse to eat food sacrificed to idols, should you eat or continue to refuse to eat? Think what Christ would do. Did he ever eat food that was sacrificed to idols?

Discuss: If idol worshipers get angry with you because you refuse to eat food sacrificed to idols, should you eat or continue to refuse to eat? Think what Christ would do. Did he ever eat food that was sacrificed to idols?

Section.heading: 1 Corinthians 11:2-16 How women should behave in church.

Questions.Q: Why does Paul say that a man who covers his head when praying or prophesying and a woman who does not cover her head when praying or prophesying, is bringing shame upon himself/herself?
Questions.A: Because it would show that they do not agree that man is under Christ and woman is under man.
Questions.Alternative: Why does Paul say that a man who covers his head when praying or prophesying and a woman who does not cover her head when praying or prophesying, is bringing shame upon himself?
Why does Paul say that a man who covers his head when praying or prophesying and a woman who does not cover her head when praying or prophesying, is bringing shame upon herself?

Questions.Q: How do you understand what Paul is saying?
What does it mean for a woman to shave her head?
Questions.A: It was shameful or dishonoring (perhaps to show mourning or as a form of punishment).
Questions.Note: Bible scholars and historians have offered many different interpretations of this passage and attempted to provide cultural information to explain (or explain away) Paul's teaching.

Different denominations and churches have taken very different approaches to understanding and applying this teaching. Respondents who are part of a church may attempt to use their church's teaching to explain this. The translation should not unnecessarily favor a particular denominational interpretation.

Respondents who are unchurched or unfamiliar with the Bible or ancient cultures may attempt to understand this using their own culture. The translation should attempt to avoid confusion that might arise from the cultural context.

Questions.Q: If a woman refuses to cover her head when prophesying or praying, what is she doing?
Questions.A: She is refusing to accept the authority of man over her and so she deserves to have her hair shaved off as a punishment.

Questions.Q: Discuss: Is Paul making a rule for all time or is what he says a custom which is different from time to time and from tribe to tribe?
Why did God create man first and woman second?
Questions.A: So that through man, God's greatness might be seen and through woman, man's greatness might be seen.

Questions.Q: Does this mean that in woman is not seen the greatness of God?
Questions.A: It seems to mean that man is first among equals, for whatever greatness man gets from God, it is shared with his wife.

Questions.Q: In what way did God use man to create woman?
Questions.A: According to Genesis 2:21-23, God took a bone from man's body and used it to make a woman.

Questions.Q: Why did God make a woman?
Questions.A: To help man and to be his wife.

Questions.Q: In summary what does Paul say is the reason a woman should cover her head?
Questions.A: To show that she is under her husband's authority and that she honors God's angels.

Questions.Q: Can men live without women or women live without men?
Questions.A: If they do for long, the human race will become extinct.

Questions.Q: How did a woman come from a man?
Questions.A: In the way God created woman from man's bone.

Questions.Q: How does a man come from a woman?
Questions.A: By her giving birth to a child.

Questions.Q: Does man get life from a woman or woman from a man?
Questions.A: No, life comes from God.

Questions.Q: What are Paul's last arguments for his case?
Questions.A: 1. What he says is that this is the custom which God's church people have been following.
2. People everywhere say that long hair is a shame for a man, but long hair makes a woman beautiful.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say that the Corinthian Christians are doing wrong?
Questions.A: When they go to church, they divide up into many groups.

Questions.Q: Why is this not good?
Questions.A: It shows that Christians are not united.

Questions.Q: Is it always wrong to have arguments among Christians?
Questions.A: No. If some people are wrong and some are right, then a discussion/argument will reveal who is right and who is wrong.

Questions.Q: What was wrong with the way they were eating our Master's supper?
Questions.A: Each brought food and ate it alone by himself; some even got drunk, while others on the other hand sat and had nothing to eat. That is, those who had brought food did not share it.

Questions.Q: What does their behavior show about their thoughts?
Questions.A: They had no respect for their fellow church members, especially those who were poor and had little food, and so they were not respecting the church.

Questions.Q: Why does he tell them to eat at home first?
Questions.A: Our Master's supper is not a full meal, but a small meal to remember Christ's death.

Questions.Q: Is what happened at the first Master's supper just the opinion of Paul?
Questions.A: No, it is a teaching that has come from Christ himself.

Questions.Q: What two things does the bread of our Master's supper show?
Questions.A: 1. It represents Christ's body. When Christ died he died for us. So the bread is for us.
2. It reminds us always of Christ.

Questions.Q: Is the drinking of the wine part of our Master's supper?
Questions.A: Yes. It follows the eating of the bread.

Questions.Q: What two things does the wine of our Master's supper show?
Questions.A: 1. It represents his blood which sealed the new covenant/oath.
2. It reminds us always of Christ.

Questions.Q: How often should Christians eat our Master's supper?
Questions.A: It does not say.

Questions.Q: Until when should Christians continue to eat our Master's supper?
Questions.A: Until his second coming.

Questions.Q: In short what is the meaning of the bread and the wine?
Questions.A: Christians are again telling one another of the reason why Christ died.

Questions.Q: If we show disrespect to our Master's supper what does that show?
Questions.A: That we disrespect Christ's body and blood, that is, we have no respect for the reason for his death.

Questions.Q: How can we avoid disrespect to our Master's supper?
Questions.A: By looking into our hearts before we come to eat and drink.

Questions.Q: In short what should we remember if we are to avoid God judging us guilty of disrespect?
Questions.A: The bread stands for Christ's body.
The wine stands for Christ's blood.
They both stand for his death for us.

Questions.Q: Why have some Corinthian Christians become weak and sick and some have died?
Questions.A: God has judged them guilty of disrespect to our Master's supper and has punished them.

Questions.Q: In what way is God merciful in his disciplining of Christians?
Questions.A: He disciplines us now in order to save us from being judged and punished in the same way that he will punish the bad people of this world.

Questions.Q: What two simple rules will help them to have respect for our Master's supper?
Questions.A: 1. Wait till all have arrived - wait for one another to arrive.
2. If anyone is hungry, let him eat at home before coming to eat at church.

Section.heading: 1 Corinthians 12:1-11 The gifts that the Holy Spirit has given.

Questions.Q: What makes people worship fetishes?
Questions.A: Something is taking them to worship them - it is the Devil. (See 10:30.)
Questions.Alternative: What makes people worship idols?

Questions.Q: If someone says, "Jesus is my Master", who or what caused him to say it?
Questions.A: God's Holy Spirit.

Questions.Q: If he curses Jesus, where do his words come from?
Questions.A: It is not from the fetish, since fetishes are nothing, they can't talk. It is from the Devil. (See 10:20.)

Questions.Q: How many gifts has the Holy Spirit given?
Questions.A: Many different kinds.

Questions.Q: Is there one way of using these gifts?
Questions.A: There are many different ways.

Questions.Q: Do these gifts come from many spirits?
Questions.A: No, all come from the same Holy Spirit.

Questions.Q: Are they given only to a few people?
Questions.A: No, God gives each person his gift, which may be different from that of another person.

Questions.Q: Why are these gifts given?
Questions.A: They are for use in the church for worshiping the same Master Jesus Christ; they are for the benefit of us all.

Questions.Q: What do we learn about God, the Holy Spirit and Jesus Christ in these verses?
Questions.A: They are all united, they are all God.

Questions.Q: Describe two gifts given by God's Spirit.
Questions.A: 1. The ability to understand the meaning of God's hidden things.
2. The ability to teach the truth.

Questions.Q: Describe two gifts mentioned here.
Questions.A: 1. The ability of believing firmly.
2. The ability to heal sick people.

Questions.Q: Describe 5 gifts mentioned here.
Questions.A: 1. The ability to perform miracles.
2. The ability to prophesy - speak what God reveals.
3. The ability to know whether it is God's spirit or a fetish which is in a person.
4. The ability to speak a language that they don't themselves understand.
5. The ability to interpret that language.

Questions.Q: In short what do we learn about these gifts?
Questions.A: 1. The Holy Spirit works through those to whom the gifts are given.
2. He gives everyone his gift.
3. We use those gifts to work for God.

Section.heading: 1 Corinthians 12:12-31 The body has many parts.

Questions.Q: What does Paul use this proverb to show?
Questions.A: Just as a human body has many parts, all working together in unity, so the church has many parts working together in unity. (See also verse 27.)

Questions.Q: What are the 2 signs of unity in the church?
Questions.A: 1. The baptism for all.
2. The Holy Spirit in all.

Questions.Q: What does this baptism do for our relationship with other tribes and social classes?
Questions.A: We all belong to one family.

Questions.Q: What does this proverb teach in respect of the church?
Questions.A: No one member of the whole church of Christ can say that he is not a member just because he does not have the same gift as a fellow member.

Questions.Q: What also does this proverb teach in respect of the church?
Questions.A: There would be something wrong with the church if everyone was a pastor, or everyone was a prophet, because all the gifts are needed for a strong church.

Questions.Q: What else does this proverb teach?
Questions.A: None of us, as members of the church, can do without the other members and their gifts. They are someone to us. The smaller need the greater.

Questions.Q: What else does this proverb teach us?
Questions.A: The more important members need the less important members, just as much as the lesser need the greater.

Questions.Q: What parts of the body does Paul now speak of?
Questions.A: Sexual parts.

Questions.Q: Can we live without them?
Questions.A: No.

Questions.Q: How does this proverb show that God's values are different from men's values?
Questions.A: God gives more honor to humble people than to proud people; more attention to those who have small gifts than to those who have big gifts.

Questions.Q: What more teaching does Paul want to show in this proverb?
Questions.A: 1. Christians should be united.
2. Each one of us should look after our fellow Christians.
3. If one of us suffers trouble, the rest of us also suffer.
4. If one of us gets praise, all of us are happy.

Questions.Q: List [the order of importance of] the gifts given by the Holy Spirit to members of the church.
Questions.A: 1. Apostles.
2. Prophets.
3. Teachers.
4. Miracle doers.
5. Healers of sick people.
6. Helpers.
7. Those who deal with the daily business of the church.
8. Those who speak in languages that they themselves don't understand.
Questions.Alternative: List the order of importance of the gifts given by the Holy Spirit to members of the church.
List the gifts given by the Holy Spirit to members of the church.

Questions.Q: Discuss: Why are miracle workers and healers lower than teachers? Why are speakers of the languages lower than administrators?
Questions.Note: Most churches believe that there are no more apostles after the death of those who knew Christ himself.

Questions.Q: Should we be content with the gift that God has given us?
Questions.A: It is good to pray that, if God agrees, he will give us more gifts. But note well, if he does, these gifts are not for our use but for God.

Section.heading: 1 Corinthians 13:1-13 How we should love one another.

Questions.Q: In short, what is it that Paul says is greater than all the gifts that God gives us?
Questions.A: That we love our fellow man.

Questions.Q: What gifts are less important than having love for our fellow man?
Questions.A: 1. Speaking other languages.
2. Prophecy.
3. Faith to do miracles.
4. Giving my things to the poor.
5. Letting them kill me (by fire) because I believe in Jesus.
Questions.Alternative: What gifts are less important than having love for others?
What gifts are less important than having love for our neighbors?
What gifts are less important than having love?
What gifts are less important than showing love for our fellow man?
What gifts are less important than showing love for others?
What gifts are less important than showing love for our neighbors?
What gifts are less important than showing love?
What gifts are less important than love?

Questions.Q: What do you say about a person who has great faith but no love?
Questions.A: He is nothing/of no importance in God's eyes.

Questions.Q: What shows that we have love for our fellow man?
Questions.A: We are patient with him, we are kind, we are not jealous, we don't boast, we are not proud and we don't insult others. We don't force others to do what we want, we don't get angry and we don't seek revenge. We are not happy when someone does wrong, we are happy when someone does good. We are patient with our fellow man in everything, we trust him in everything, we hope that he will not do what is not good and we are always patient.
Questions.Alternative: What shows that we have love for others?
What shows that we have love for our neighbors?
What actions or attitudes show that we have true love?

Questions.Q: What will cease before love?
Questions.A: The power to prophesy, the power to speak in other languages, wisdom (and other gifts).

Questions.Q: What does it mean that they will cease before love?
Questions.A: 1. When a man gets old, his powers that he has from God may cease but his love for his fellow men continues.
2. Towards the end of the world these gifts will cease before men cease to love.

Questions.Q: Why will gifts cease before love?
Questions.A: Because they are given to us so that we can help other Christians. But we are to love all people always and to love God even after we die.

Questions.Q: On what day will we understand everything?
Questions.A: When Jesus comes again.
Questions.Note: NB. Is it clear that this refers to Jesus's second coming?

Questions.Q: Why will we understand everything?
Questions.A: Jesus will be here in person and he will reveal everything that has been hidden.

Questions.Q: Why will what is not good finish on that day?
Questions.A: Because Jesus is God and will rule a kingdom in which there is no more bad.

Questions.Q: What does Paul use the proverb to show?
Questions.A: Our present life is like that of a child, who knows only childhood things and whose wisdom is small. In our life when Jesus comes again we will know all things.

Questions.Q: What two other proverbs does Paul use to describe this life of ours on earth?
Questions.A: A riddle and a mirror that is not clear.

Questions.Q: When Jesus returns, how will our knowledge be?
Questions.A: Like that of God and how God knows us very well now.

Questions.Q: What will pass leaving only faith, hope and love?
Questions.A: All gifts from God to man.

Questions.Q: In verse 8 Paul says that only love will continue, but now he says that also faith and hope will continue. How is this so?
Questions.A: If we love our fellow man we will also trust him and hope in him. If we love God we will also trust him and hope in him. (Also see verse 7.)

Questions.Q: In what way is love greater than faith and hope?
Questions.A: 1. When we see (God and) Jesus face to face we will continue to love him, but we do not any more need to trust and hope in one whom we now see face to face.
2. Our faith saves ourselves. Our love saves others.

Questions.Q: Can we just love God and our fellow man and leave off trusting and hoping?
Questions.A: No, because our trust in Jesus makes us love him and hope for his coming. Our love for our fellow man makes us trust him and hope for him to do what is good.
Questions.Alternative: If we love God and our fellow man, are faith and hope necessary?
Can we just love God and others and leave off trusting and hoping?
If we love God and others, are faith and hope necessary?
Can we just love God and other people and leave off trusting and hoping?
If we love God and other people, are faith and hope necessary?
Can we just love God and our neighbors and leave off trusting and hoping?
If we love God and our neighbors, are faith and hope necessary?

Questions.Q: Are faith, hope and love gifts from God in the same way as prophecy, wisdom, etc.?
Questions.A: 1. They are greater/more useful gifts. (See 12:31.)
2. They are gifts, without which we cannot be Christians.
3. Therefore everyone should ask God for them.
4. As for the other gifts we can ask God, and if he agrees he will give them to us.
5. But these other gifts do not make God think we are better people because we have gifts.

Section.heading: 1 Corinthians 14:1-40 Concerning prophecy and speaking in other languages.

Questions.Q: This verse is connected with Ch. 13. What is the connection between love and prophecy?
Questions.A: Love is something we should all get in our hearts. But prophecy is the most important of all God's other gifts.
Questions.Alternative: This verse is connected with chapter 13. What is the connection between love and prophecy?
This verse is connected with the previous chapter. What is the connection between love and prophecy?
What is the connection between love and prophecy?

Questions.Q: Why is prophecy very important?
Questions.A: It is God speaking directly through a person, revealing his thoughts to human beings.

Questions.Q: Why is prophecy more important than speaking in another language?
Questions.A: 1. Other people can understand prophecy since it is spoken in our language.
2. If someone speaks in another language, neither he nor other people understand him.

Questions.Q: If that is so, what use is speaking in another language?
Questions.A: He is speaking to God and praising him, but only God understands what he is saying.

Questions.Q: What good does prophecy do?
Questions.A: It helps other Christians, it strengthens their faith and it gives them comfort.

Questions.Q: In short why is prophecy more useful than speaking in another language?
Questions.A: It helps others, but another language helps only the one who speaks.

Questions.Q: So does Paul say that it is not good to speak in another language?
Questions.A: He wishes all to have the gifts of prophecy and speaking in another language.

Questions.Q: Under what circumstances can speaking in another language be as useful as prophesying?
Questions.A: When the speaker can also interpret the language into the language of his fellow church members.

Questions.Q: What does this add to the previous verses?
Questions.A: That Paul himself did not speak to the Corinthians in a language that he did not understand.

Questions.Q: What do these proverbs teach?
Questions.A: We must speak a language that our fellow men will understand, if not so they will not mind us.

Questions.Q: What is the thing that really separates one people from another?
Questions.A: That they each speak a different language.

Questions.Q: For what reason should we ask the Holy Spirit to give us gifts?
Questions.A: So as to help our fellow church members.

Questions.Q: What gift is better than speaking in other languages?
Questions.A: The power to interpret other languages.

Questions.Q: Why is speaking in other languages that we don't hear not helpful?
Questions.A: 1. The speaker does not understand his own words.
2. The hearers do not understand him and so they cannot agree or disagree with him.

Questions.Q: How should we worship God in prayer and song?
Questions.A: With heart and mind, that is, with sincerity and understanding.

Questions.Q: In what language should we pray and speak in church?
Questions.A: In a language that our fellow church members can understand.

Questions.Q: When is it right to pray in another language that we don't hear?
Questions.A: When we pray alone to God.

Questions.Q: In what ways does Paul say it is wrong to be childish and right to be childish?
Questions.A: They should think like adults in respect of the gifts of speaking; but like children they should be free of bad thoughts and deeds.

Questions.Q: Looking at verses 21 and 22, say how speaking in foreign languages is a warning to those who don't believe.
Questions.A: If people refuse to believe God's words when he speaks to them in their own language, he sends people speaking foreign languages. This warns them that God is not happy with them. A sign without an interpretation is a worry to people.

Questions.Q: Show how verse 22 does not contradict 23-24.
Questions.A: When God sends people speaking in foreign languages to us it is God warning us. If we speak in a language that is the gift of the Holy Spirit it does not help our fellow believers, and it seems like madness to those who do not belong to our church. But if we speak in our own language what God reveals to us (prophesy) and a non-member comes in and hears us, maybe that person will hear God speaking to him and will repent of his sins and believe that God is truly among us.

Questions.Q: In summary how does Paul recommend that they should conduct their church services?
Questions.A: Freely, but in an orderly way; everyone taking part as God leads him, but one after the other and in order; in a way which will help one another and make their faith increase.

Questions.Q: What kind of things are good for a church worship service?
Questions.A: Songs, teaching, prophesy (what God reveals to someone) and speaking in a language that the speaker does not understand if someone can interpret it.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say about prophesying?
Questions.A: All who have the gift of prophecy have the right to speak, but in order one after the other.

Questions.Q: How should others in the congregation treat those that prophesy?
Questions.A: They should listen carefully.

Questions.Q: What is the reason for people being allowed to prophesy in church?
Questions.A: To teach and encourage fellow church members.

Questions.Q: How do you understand these verses?
Questions.A: 1. A prophet has control over the words that he speaks. He can wait till the time is right for him to rise and speak.
2. God does not want noisy, disorderly church meetings.

Questions.Q: Give two reasons why women should keep quiet in church meetings.
Questions.A: 1. So that the meetings do not become disorderly.
2. Because women are under men's authority.

Questions.Q: If a woman has a question to ask, how will she get an answer?
Questions.A: By asking her husband at home, that is, if he is a Christian and has been with her at church.

Questions.Q: Discuss: Is Paul making a rule for all times and all peoples or is he only repeating what was the Jewish and Christian custom of his time?
Why does Paul ask these (rhetorical) questions? What is he saying?
Questions.A: They in Corinth have no right to change the customs that have been accepted in the other churches, especially since they were not the first Christians.

Questions.Q: From whom does Paul say that this law about women comes?
Questions.A: From our Master Jesus Christ.

Questions.Q: What should they do to someone who says he is a prophet or that God is with him, and he does not agree with this rule about women?
Questions.A: They should ignore him and leave him to himself.

Questions.Q: How does Paul summarize this chapter?
Questions.A: 1. Everything in church must be done well and in the right way.
2. Prophecy is a gift to be desired more than others.
3. Speaking in a language that a person doesn't understand is not forbidden (but see v.28 there must be an interpreter).

Questions.Q: Why is it good to remind people of what they believe?
Questions.A: So that they will continue to believe and not fall back.

Questions.Q: How can God stop saving them?
Questions.A: If they stop believing the good news.

Questions.Q: What are the most important things that we should believe in the good news of Jesus Christ?
Questions.A: 1. That he died to wash away our sins.
2. He was buried and on the third day God raised him from death.

Questions.Q: Why is this good news not an invention by Paul?
Questions.A: 1. He received this teaching from others.
2. It was foretold in the Old Testament.

Questions.Q: To whom did Jesus appear after he rose from death?
Questions.A: Peter, then to Peter and the other apostles, then to 500 disciples at one time, most of whom were still living at the time Paul was writing this letter, then to James, then to all his apostles and then finally to Paul.

Questions.Q: Why does Paul liken himself to a child who is born late?
Questions.A: Because he was the last of the apostles to see the resurrected Christ.

Questions.Q: Why was Paul not worthy to be an apostle?
Questions.A: Because before he saw Christ on the road to Damascus, he persecuted God's church people.

Questions.Q: Why did he become an apostle?
Questions.A: Because God had mercy on him and made him become what he is now.

Questions.Q: Is Paul boasting?
Questions.A: He says he has worked harder than all the other apostles, but it is with God's strength that he has done this. He became an apostle, not because he was good, but because God had mercy on him.

Questions.Q: What difference is there between Paul's preaching of the good news and the other apostles' preaching?
Questions.A: None. It is the same message preached by them all and the same message that all the Corinthians have believed.

Questions.Q: Some Corinthians said that people who have died will not rise to life again. Why is this teaching wrong?
Questions.A: Because all the apostles have taught that Christ himself was raised from death.

Questions.Q: How is our belief that we will rise again connected to our belief that Christ rose again?
Questions.A: If one is false, both are false. If one is true, both are true.

Questions.Q: If it is not true that God raised Christ from death what does that show?
Questions.A: 1. That the preaching of the good news is for nothing and is a lie.
2. That the Corinthians believing the good news is for nothing.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say in addition to verses 13-15?
Questions.A: He repeats his thoughts and adds that our being free from sins is because Christ rose from death. If he did not rise then what we believe is a lie and our sins remain on us.

Questions.Q: If our faith is a lie, what of those who were Christians and have died?
Questions.A: It means that they too have no hope of rising from death.

Questions.Q: What thing if it was removed from our belief would make our case worse than that of all other people?
Questions.A: Our hope to rise from death and live with Christ in heaven.

Questions.Q: Is there any difference between "hope in Christ" and "belief in Christ" in these verses?
Questions.A: Hope means belief that we will get something in the future.

Questions.Q: In what way is Christ a leader in his death? What does his death guarantee?
Questions.A: He is the first to rise from death and not die a second time. His rising again shows that those who believed in him and died will rise to life again like him.

Questions.Q: Contrast Adam with Christ.
