Questions.A: Because Adam sinned, death came into the world. Because of Christ's death and resurrection, all who follow Christ will rise from death.

Questions.Q: In what order will the resurrection happen?
Questions.A: Christ has already risen and gone to heaven. When he returns, God will raise all Christians to life.

Questions.Q: In what order will the end of the world come?
Questions.A: Christ will come again as King of the world. He will raise his people to life, he will collect all power from men and he and God will fight and defeat all his enemies. Then he will hand the Kingdom of the world back to God.

Questions.Q: What is the last enemy that Christ will defeat?
Questions.A: Death

Questions.Q: What will happen to Christ after all these things?
Questions.A: He will hand all power back to God.

Questions.Q: What additional reason does Paul give for believing the resurrection of all believers?
Questions.A: That some people get baptized on behalf of some who died before getting baptized.

Questions.Q: Is this a good practice?
Questions.A: Paul does not say it is good. In fact throughout the history of the church, most Christians have said that it is wrong to do this.

Questions.Q: How does Paul show from his own daily life that he and his companions believe that Christians will be raised from death?
Questions.A: 1. If he did not believe it, he would not be prepared to suffer hardships and face death every day, since such suffering is of no value and does not bring happiness.
2. If we have no hope of the resurrection, we might as well eat and drink and enjoy this short life that we live.

Questions.Q: What is Paul's advice to the Corinthian church?
Questions.A: 1. Avoid bad friends/companions.
2. Repent of your sins.
3. Be ashamed that some of you do not yet know God.

Section.heading: 1 Corinthians 15:35-58 What a person's body will become when God raises him from death.

Questions.Q: What important points does Paul use this proverb to teach about the resurrection body?
Questions.A: 1. The old body must die before the new body can begin.
2. The new body is different from the old body.
3. It is God who gives each seed a different body.
4. Each kind of seed grows into a body that differs from others.

Questions.Q: What one point does Paul make in these verses?
Questions.A: Everything in the universe has a different body.

Questions.Q: Compare the new (spiritual) body with the old body.
Questions.A: The old body:
Weak
Not beautiful.
Flesh and bones.
Its/his soul lives in it.
The new body:
Strong
Beautiful
A new body.
Its/his soul lives in it.

Questions.Q: Contrast the first and second Adam.
Questions.A: First:
The first man God created.
He lived as a man
Second:
Jesus Christ, born as a man.
He lived as a man, but he was also the source of life.

Questions.Q: What false teaching can be understood here?
Questions.A: That Christ was not born but came straight from heaven to earth.

Questions.Q: What is the true teaching about Christ's coming to earth?
Questions.A: He was part of God in heaven. He entered the earth as a human baby and lived as a human. After his death he rose to life with a new body that looks like a human, but is different. With that body he returned to heaven to be with God.

Questions.Q: How are Christians both like the first Adam and the second Adam (Christ)?
Questions.A: Our bodies on this earth are like that of the first Adam. Our resurrection bodies will be like Christ's resurrection body.

Questions.Q: Why cannot our bodies live in God's Kingdom in heaven?
Questions.A: Because our bodies die, but everything in heaven lives forever.

Questions.Q: Describe, in order, what will happen at the end of the world.
Questions.A: 1. God's trumpet will sound.
2. God will raise to life those who have died.
3. Christians who have died and Christians who are alive at the time of the end will be suddenly changed and will be given bodies that will never die again.

Questions.Q: What happens to death?
Questions.A: It will be no more. Death will no more have power to pain and to kill people.

Questions.Q: Who will collect back/destroy the power of death?
Questions.A: God
Questions.Alternative: Who will destroy the power of death?
Who will collect back the power of death?

Questions.Q: What is the connection between death, sin and the law?
Questions.A: The law shows up peoples' sins, and because people sin they die.
Questions.Note: NB. A full discussion of this may be found in Romans 4:15, Romans 5:12-14 and Romans 7:8-12.

Questions.Q: For what, then, should we thank God?
Questions.A: That through our Master Jesus Christ he has caused us to have power over death.

Questions.Q: In what way have we power over death?
Questions.A: If we believe in Jesus Christ, then after our earthly bodies die, our souls will go to be with God and we will get new bodies at the end of the world.

Questions.Q: Since this is so, can we relax and know that we need do nothing except believe in Christ?
Questions.A: Our belief that certainly we will go to heaven and also rise from death at the end of the world should make our faith stronger and make us work even harder for our Master Jesus Christ.

Questions.Q: What further comfort do we have in our work for him?
Questions.A: There is nothing that we do for him which is for nothing.
Questions.Alternative: Is our labor for Him in vain?

Section.heading: 1 Corinthians 16:1-4 Concerning the collection for fellow Christians.

Questions.Q: Who was suffering poverty?
Questions.A: The Christians living in Jerusalem and Judea.

Questions.Q: How does Paul advise them to collect the money for these Christians?
Questions.A: Every Sunday they each are to put aside a part of the money each has gained. If one has gained much, he should put aside much. If he has gained little, he should put aside little. Then when Paul comes to collect the money it is all there ready for him in one place.

Questions.Q: How will the money reach the poor Christians?
Questions.A: The Corinthians will choose men to take it. Paul will give them letters which give them the right to take the money to the poor people in Jerusalem and Paul will also go if it seems right.

Section.heading: 1 Corinthians 16:5-12 What Paul has decided to do.

Questions.Q: When Paul reaches Corinth what does he hope to do?
Questions.A: To spend a long time with them during the winter/time of wind and cold.
Questions.Note: Macedonia is to the north of Corinth. Ephesus is across the sea to the east.

Questions.Q: From these verses how do you think he feels towards them?
Questions.A: He loves them so that a quick visit is not enough.
Questions.Alternative: From these verses (5-7), how do you think he feels towards them?
From these verses, how do you think Paul feels towards them?
How do you think Paul feels towards them?
How do you think Paul feels towards the Corinthians?
How do you think Paul feels towards the people he is writing to in Corinth?
How do you think Paul feels towards the people he is writing to?

Questions.Q: What is keeping Paul in Ephesus?
Questions.A: There is much work to be done despite many enemies who want to stop him.

Questions.Q: Why do you think the Corinthians may not respect Timothy?
Questions.A: 1. He was a young man.
2. He was Paul's helper and not an apostle.

Questions.Q: How does Paul show his love and respect for Timothy?
Questions.A: He wants the Corinthians to respect him and make him happy and send him back to Paul in life and health/in peace.

Questions.Q: How can Apollos help the Corinthians?
Questions.A: He is a good preacher. (See 1 Corinthians 3:4-6, 22.)

Questions.Q: How are these verses a summary of our Christian life?
Questions.A: We should be careful - avoiding evil.
We should be strong in our faith and courageous.
We should do our work with love.

Questions.Q: Why should the Corinthians respect and follow Stephanas?
Questions.A: 1. He and his family were the first to become Christians in the land where Corinth is.
2. He has worked very hard for all God's people.

Questions.Q: Who also deserves respect?
Questions.A: Those who are helping Stephanas.

Questions.Q: What general principle does this state?
Questions.A: Respect also the servants, helpers and companions of people whom you respect.

Questions.Q: Compare the proverb: Because of his master they give his dog a morsel.
Why is Paul so happy with Stephanas, Fortunatus and Achaicus? Where did they come from?
Questions.A: They came from Corinth, probably bringing the letter to which Paul is replying. They made him happy, on behalf of the Corinthians, just as they made the Corinthians happy.

Questions.Q: What do we learn of church meetings from this verse?
Questions.A: People met for church services and meetings in a person's house. They did not at that time have church buildings.

Questions.Q: What do we learn about the way Paul wrote letters?
Questions.A: He usually dictated his letters to a secretary and wrote at the end a greeting and his name in his own hand.

Questions.Q: What will happen to those who do not love our Master Jesus Christ?
Questions.A: God will curse him, but he still has the chance to repent up to his death.

Section.heading: 1 John 1:1-4 John wrote to the Christians and told them that he [and the other apostles] have seen and touched the Word of Life. John told the Christians this, because he wanted them to have fellowship with him [and the other apostles] in the same way that he [and the other apostles] have/had fellowship with the Father and Jesus.

Questions.Q: What reasons did John give for writing this letter?
Questions.A: John told the Christians about the Word of life. He wanted them to have fellowship with the Father and with Jesus Christ. (3)
The apostle John wanted the Christians and the apostles, including himself, to have complete joy. (4)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to have fellowship with someone else?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means to have companionship. The word "fellowship" refers to a relationship between two or more people all of whom have something in common or all of whom/who participate in the same activity. The same Greek word may also be translated in certain contexts as "sharing", "participation", or "partnership".
Questions.Note: See "fellowship" in KBT.

Questions.Q: To whom does the expression "Word of life" refer?
Questions.A: It refers to Jesus Christ.
Questions.Note: Omit or reword this question if the translation does not have the expression "Word of life."
Questions.Alternative: What does the expression "Word of life" mean?

Questions.Q: What did John say about the Word of life?
Questions.A: He said the Word of life has always existed. (1)

Questions.Q: How did he know about this Word of life?
Questions.A: He heard the Word of life.
He saw the Word of life.
He studied/observed the Word of life.
He touched/handled the Word of life. (1)

Questions.Q: How could John have heard, seen, and touched the Word of life?
Questions.A: He could do those things, because the Word of life became a human being. (2)

Questions.Q: What did John call that Word in this verse?
Questions.A: He called the Word the/that life. (2)

Questions.Q: With whom was that life?
Questions.A: That/The life was with the Father. (2)

Questions.Q: What else did he say about that life?
Questions.A: He said that/the life is eternal. (2)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for something to be eternal?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that it will last forever/it will never end.

Questions.Q: Who did he say Jesus Christ is?
Questions.A: He said he is the Son of the Father/God. (3)

Questions.Q: What do you think is the meaning of "Christ"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "Christ" is the English rendering of the Greek word Christos, which means "anointed one."
Questions.Note: See "Christ" in KBT.

Section.heading: 1 John 1:5-10 God is light and there is no darkness in him at all. John told the Christians that, if they live in the light where God is, they will have fellowship with him and he will have fellowship with them.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what John said in these verses.
Questions.A: John said that God is light, there is no darkness in him at all. (5)
If anyone wants to have fellowship with God he must walk in the light. (6-7)

Questions.Q: Who do you think God is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In English, the term "God" with a capital "G" is used to refer to the one supreme Creator. The term "god" with a small "g", as in "a god" or "many gods", can refer to any spiritual being that people worship. The Greek word theos can be used in the same two ways.
Questions.Note: In many languages the term for God is a proper name and cannot be used to refer to anyone except the one supreme creator of the world. It cannot be pluralized. (Or, if it can be pluralized, the meaning may be something very different from the English "gods". In one language, the plural form of God, meant "God and those who follow him" and was an appropriate way to translate "saints".) (See "God" in KBT.)

Questions.Q: In your language, do you use the word "light" as a figure? If you use the figure, what does it mean?
Questions.Note: Some languages have a problem in translating the word for light in a figurative sense.

Questions.Q: What do you think "light" means in this verse?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Light refers to truth or divine truth.
Questions.Note: -OR-
Light refers to knowledge of God or revelation about him.

Questions.Q: What do you think "darkness" means in this verse?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Darkness refers to spiritual or moral sin/all that is evil.

Questions.Q: Where did John get this message?
Questions.A: He heard it from him [Jesus Christ]. (5)

Questions.Q: If we say we have fellowship with God, but at the same time, we walk in the darkness/do evil deeds, what are we saying?
Questions.A: We are lying and
we are not putting the truth into practice/not living by the truth. (6)
Questions.Alternative: If we say we have fellowship with God, but at the same time, we walk in the darkness, what are we saying?
If we say we have fellowship with God, but at the same time, we do evil deeds, what are we saying?

Questions.Q: If we walk in the light/do not do evil deeds, we will have fellowship with God. With whom else will we have fellowship?
Questions.A: We will have fellowship with other believers. (7)
Questions.Alternative: If we walk in the light, we will have fellowship with God. With whom else will we have fellowship?
If we do not do evil deeds, we will have fellowship with God. With whom else will we have fellowship?

Questions.Q: How does God forgive our sins?
Questions.A: He forgives us because Christ died for us. (7)

Questions.Q: What does a person do when he sins?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He disobeys God. He deliberately keeps on doing those things that please himself and displease God.
Questions.Note: See "sin" in KBT.

Questions.Q: If we say that we have not sinned, what are we doing?
Questions.A: We are deceiving/fooling ourselves, and we are not telling the truth. (8)

Questions.Q: What are we to do when/if we have sinned?
Questions.A: We are to confess/admit/acknowledge our sins to God. (9)
Questions.Alternative: What are we to do when we have sinned?
What are we to do if we have sinned?

Questions.Q: Then what will God do?
Questions.A: God will forgive us of our sins,
and purify/cleanse us from all unrighteousness/wickedness. (9)

Questions.Q: What do you think happens when someone forgives someone else?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Forgiveness always involves two people, one of whom has done something wrong to the other and offended him. Forgiveness takes place when the one who was offended sets aside his right to justice and decides not to punish the offender as he deserved. If the one who offended repents and accepts this forgiveness, then the result is that the relationship between the two, which was broken by the offense, is restored, and the guilt of the offender is removed.
Questions.Note: See "forgive" in KBT.

Questions.Q: How do we know that God will really do that?
Questions.A: We know that he will because God does what he says he will do, and because God does everything correctly. (9)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when someone is faithful?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that someone will do what he says he will do. A person is worthy of being believed by someone else. They are trustworthy, reliable. (See "faithful" in KBT in the "believe" entry.)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to deal with someone else justly?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He does only what is right to do. Doing something in conformity with law or justice. It refers to God's faithful and consistent adherence to his covenant.
Questions.Note: See "just" in KBT.

Questions.Q: If we say that we have not sinned, what do we think about God?
Questions.A: We think that God is a liar, because God has said that all people have sinned. (10)

Questions.Q: What is meant by "his word has no place in our lives"?
Questions.A: It means that we have not believed his word nor allowed it to change our lives. (10)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus Christ do for all the people of the world?
Questions.A: He died to save people from their sins. (2)

Questions.Q: What do you think this verse means by this "world"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It is all the people who live on the earth.
Questions.Note: See "world" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What does it mean to you that Jesus became the atoning sacrifice for everyone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He died to take the punishment for our sins. The penalty for sin was death, but "God graciously permitted the death of a sacrificial victim to substitute for the death of the sinner". The sin of the person having been transferred to the victim, atonement was made, that is, fellowship between the person and God was restored. Jesus is the sacrificial victim who paid the price for everyone's sins.
Questions.Note: See "atonement" in KBT.

Questions.Q: To whom did John write this letter?
Questions.A: He wrote it to the Christians/his children. (1)
Questions.Note: (Note:Translator's Notes on 1, 2, and 3 John states that John was an old man and expressed an affectionate, fatherly attitude to the believers to whom he was writing by calling them "my children.")

Questions.Q: If someone does sin, who will come to their defense?
Questions.A: Jesus Christ will speak to the Father in their defense. (1)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the Father will listen to Jesus Christ?
Questions.A: He will listen to Jesus, because he is completely good. (1)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to be righteous?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that God has accepted that person as right in his eyes. In this reference it refers to the fact that Christ was in the right with God. (See "righteousness" in KBT in the "just, justify..." entry.)

Questions.Q: What do you think this verse means by the "whole world"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It is all the people who live on the earth.
Questions.Note: See "world" in KBT.

Questions.Q: For whose sins did Jesus Christ die?
Questions.A: He died for us, [the Christians whom John calls "dear children"].
He died to save everyone (i.e., the "whole world").
Questions.Alternative: For whom did Jesus Christ die?
Why did Jesus Christ sacrifice his life?
Questions.Note: Depending on how a respondent answers, it might be necessary to ask follow-up questions to explore the theological implications of how Jesus' sacrifice for the whole world is different from his sacrifice for believers.

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when someone makes a sacrifice?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "Sacrifice" is the religious act of making a gift to God, or to some other powerful spiritual being. The gift is given in order to establish, maintain, or restore a proper relationship between the sacrificer and the deity. Something is given up in order to achieve a purpose.
Questions.Note: See "sacrifice" in KBT.

Questions.Q: How can we be sure that we really know God?
Questions.A: We can be sure that we know him, if we obey his commands. (3)

Questions.Q: What is a person doing who/when he says that he knows God but does not do what he commands him to do?
Questions.A: He is lying. (4)
Questions.Alternative: What is a person doing who says that he knows God but does not do what he commands him to do?
What is a person doing when he says that he knows God but does not do what he commands him to do?

Questions.Q: What did John say about a person who obeys what God has said?
Questions.A: He shows that he really loves God. (5)

Questions.Q: How can a Christian be sure that he is in a continuing relationship with God?
Questions.A: A person who is in a continuing relationship with God is living/conducting himself in the same manner that Jesus Christ lived/conducted himself. (6)

Section.heading: 1 John 2:7-14 John wrote that Christians are to love one another.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what John said in these verses.
Questions.A: He wrote them about a command which was to love their fellow believers. (7-8, 10)

Questions.Q: About what did John write them?
Questions.A: He wrote them about a command. (7)

Questions.Q: What did he say about this command?
Questions.A: He said it was not a new command.
He said they had heard it before. (7)

Questions.Q: When was the first time that they heard that command?
Questions.A: They had heard the command since the beginning [when they started to follow Christ]. (7)

Questions.Q: About what did John write them?
Questions.A: He wrote that they needed to hear that command again, since it had a new meaning. (8)

Questions.Q: What was the new meaning of that command?
Questions.A: It was that they were to love one another as Christ had shown how to love people by the way he lived. (8)

Questions.Q: Why is this true?
Questions.A: This is true because the darkness of evil is passing and the true light, which is the truth about God, is becoming known to people. (8)

Questions.Q: What did John say about any person who says he is in the light, that is, he lives good as God does good; and yet hates his brother?
Questions.A: That person is still living in the darkness, that is, he is doing evil. (9)

Questions.Q: What do you think John meant when he said his "brother"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In this reference "brother" means fellow believer or fellow Christian. (See "brother" in KBT in the "disciple" entry.)

Questions.Q: What did John say about a person who loves his brother?
Questions.A: He said that person is living in the light, that is, he lives good as God does good;
and there is nothing in him to make him stumble. (10)
Questions.Note: Translator's Notes states that this could mean either to make himself sin or to make someone else sin.

Questions.Q: What did John say about a person who hates his brother?
Questions.A: He said that person is living and walking in the darkness, that is, he is doing evil.
He does not know what he is doing, because the darkness/[evil] has made him like a blind person. (11)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that John wrote to those he called "dear children"?
Questions.A: He wrote to them because [God] had forgiven their sins. (12)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that [God] forgave their sins?
Questions.A: He forgave their sins because of what Jesus did for them. (12)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that God forgave their sins?
Why did God forgive their sins?
What is the reason that their sins were forgiven?
Why were their sins forgiven?
On what account were their sins forgiven?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that John wrote to those he called "fathers"?
Questions.A: He wrote to them because they have known [Jesus Christ] who has always existed. (13-14)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that John wrote to those he called "young men"?
Questions.A: He wrote to them because they have overcome/defeated the evil one. (13-14)

Questions.Q: Who do you think the evil one is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In this reference the evil one is Satan, who is the chief enemy of God. He is the supreme evil spiritual being who leads and directs all other evil spiritual beings. (See "evil one" in KBT in the "Satan" entry.)

Questions.Q: What other reason did John give for writing to those he called "children"?
Questions.A: He wrote to them because they have known the Father/God. (13)

Questions.Q: What other reasons did John give for writing to those he called "young men"?
Questions.A: He wrote to them because they were courageous/steadfast/firmly trusting Christ,
and because the word of God lives in them. (14)

Section.heading: 1 John 2:15-17 Christians are not to love the evil ways which unbelievers live nor love the things that do not pertain to God.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what John said in these verses.
Questions.A: He said that they are not to love the things that do not pertain to God. (15)

Questions.Q: What two things did John say were impossible for anyone to love at the same time?
Questions.A: A person cannot love God and the evil things of the world at the same time. (15)

Questions.Q: What is meant by "the things of the world"?
Questions.A: The things which non-believers crave/desire strongly.
The things which a person sees and lusts for/wants/covets.
The things in this life of which people are proud to have. (16)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that it is impossible for anyone to love these things and to love God at the same time?
Questions.A: It is impossible for anyone to do this, because the desire for these things does not come from God. The desire for these things comes from the evil world. (16)

Questions.Q: What did John say about the world and these desires?
Questions.A: They will end/pass away. (17)

Questions.Q: What did he say about a person who does God's will?
Questions.A: He will live forever. (17)

Section.heading: 1 John 2:18-27 John warned the Christians about false teachers who will come to them and say that God is not the only god and Jesus is not the son of god.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what John said in these verses.
Questions.A: They must always pay attention/continue believing/obeying God's word/message. (24)
He was writing about people who are trying to deceive the Christians. (26)

Questions.Q: What time did John say people are living in now?
Questions.A: They are living in the last hour/the time when the world is about to end. (18)

Questions.Q: How did they know that the world is about to end?
Questions.A: The believers had been told that the antichrist was coming;
and now many antichrists have come before the end of the world. (18)

Questions.Q: What do you think the antichrist is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The meaning is probably "one who opposes the Christ (the Messiah)". Christians had been taught to expect one particular person, the antichrist, a man who will have supernatural power from Satan.
Questions.Note: See "antichrist" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did John say about those enemies of Christ?
Questions.A: They did not really belong to the group of believers.
They were never true believers. (19)

Questions.Q: What is the reason it is clear that they never were true believers?
Questions.A: They went out from/left meeting with the believers. (19)

Questions.Q: What did John say that identifies the true believers?
Questions.A: True believers have received an anointing [with the Holy Spirit] from [Christ]/the Holy One. (20)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to anoint someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "Anointing" here refers to the Holy Spirit whom every Christian receives as a sign that he has been chosen by God as one of his people. The Holy Spirit communicates to God's people, revealing the truth about Jesus Christ to them.
Questions.Note: See "anoint" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Who do you think the Holy One is in this verse?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In this verse "Holy One" is used to describe God the Father and God the Son. Anything that is "holy" for God must reflect his character by being physically unblemished or reflecting, to some degree, his purity. (See "holy one" in KBT in the "holy" entry.)

Questions.Q: What do they know now since they received the Holy Spirit?
Questions.A: They now know the truth. (20)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that John wrote to them?
Questions.A: He wrote to them because they knew the truth,
and because false teachings are not a part of the truth. (21)

Questions.Q: Who did John say the liar is?
Questions.A: He is the one who says that Jesus is not the Christ. (22)

Questions.Q: What did John call a person who says that Jesus is not the Christ?
Questions.A: He said a person like this is the antichrist. (22)

Questions.Q: What else does the antichrist do?
Questions.A: He denies the Father and the Son. (22)

Questions.Q: If a person denies/rejects the Son/Jesus Christ, what is he also doing?
Questions.A: He is also denying/rejecting the Father/God. (23)
Questions.Alternative: If a person denies the Son Christ, what is he also doing?
If a person denies the Jesus Christ, what is he also doing?
If a person rejects the Son Christ, what is he also doing?
If a person rejects the Jesus Christ, what is he also doing?

Questions.Q: If someone accepts/acknowledges the Son/agrees that Jesus is the Son of God, what will be the result?
Questions.A: He will have a close relationship/fellowship with God the Father. (23)
Questions.Alternative: If someone accepts the Son of God, what will be the result?
If someone accepts the Son, what will be the result?
If someone acknowledges the Son of God, what will be the result?
If someone acknowledges the Son, what will be the result?
If someone agrees that Jesus is the Son of God, what will be the result?

Questions.Q: What message is John talking about in this verse?
Questions.A: The message they heard from the beginning. (24)
Questions.Note: Translator's Notes states that this message is the one they heard from the time they began to follow Christ.

Questions.Q: What did John say will be the result if they do continue to believe this message?
Questions.A: They will have a close relationship/fellowship with Jesus Christ and with God the Father. (24)

Questions.Q: What did John say [Christ] has promised Christians?
Questions.A: He has promised all believers eternal life. (25)
Questions.Alternative: What did John say Christ has promised Christians?
What did John say God has promised Christians?
What did John say he has promised Christians?
What did John say has been promised to Christians?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for a person to have eternal life?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that a person will live forever with God.
Questions.Note: This eternal life is in the spiritual realm not the physical.

Questions.Q: Where does the Holy Spirit remain that they received from him/Christ?
Questions.A: The Holy Spirit remains with them. (27)
Questions.Alternative: Where does the Holy Spirit remain that they received from him?
Where does the Holy Spirit remain that they received from Christ?

Questions.Q: Whom did they need to teach them?
Questions.A: They did not need anyone else. (27)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they did not need anyone else to teach them?
Questions.A: They did not need anyone else because the Holy Spirit teaches/taught them about all things. (27)

Questions.Q: What did John tell them they are to do?
Questions.A: They are to remain in close relationship with Christ. (27)

Section.heading: 1 John 2:28-3:10 John encouraged the Christians to remain in fellowship with God (continue to communicate with God) and to live their lives in a way that pleases God.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what John said in these verses.
Questions.A: He told them that they are to live/stay in close relationship/fellowship with him/Christ. (28)
If they do this they will be confident and unafraid when he/Jesus Christ comes back. (28)

Questions.Q: What did John say they know if they know that he/Christ is righteous?
Questions.A: They know that a person who does right is God's child. (29)
Questions.Alternative: What did John say they know if they know that he is righteous?
What did John say they know if they know that Christ is righteous?

Questions.Q: How do we know that the Father loves us very much?
Questions.A: We know that he loves us very much because [he] calls us his children. (1)

Questions.Q: What do you think "God the Father" means?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that God is the father of Jesus Christ and of anyone who accepts Jesus as their Savior and Lord.
Questions.Note: See "God the Father" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think the title "God the Father" means?
What do you think the term "God the Father" means?
Who is the author talking about when he says "the Father"?
What does the expression "the Father" mean?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the unbelievers/non-Christians do not know the believers?
Questions.A: They do not know them because they do not know him/God. (1)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that the unbelievers do not know the believers?
What is the reason that the non-Christians do not know the believers?

Questions.Q: What do we not know yet?
Questions.A: We do not know what we will be like in the future. (2)

Questions.Q: What will happen to us in the future?
Questions.A: We will/are going to become like him/Jesus Christ. (2)

Questions.Q: When will that happen?
Questions.A: It will happen when Jesus Christ comes back again, and we see him. (2)

Questions.Q: What does everyone do who has this hope?
Questions.A: They all purify themselves. (3)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when someone purifies himself?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means he continually makes an effort to keep himself free from sin. (See "purify" in KBT in the "clean" entry.)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to hope in something?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means to have a desire to see something happen or to obtain something.

Questions.Q: What did John say about him/Christ?
Questions.A: He said that he was pure. (3)
Questions.Alternative: What did John say about him?
What did John say about Christ?

Questions.Q: What is a person doing when he sins?
Questions.A: He is disobeying [God's] law/doing what [God] has said he was not to do. (4)

Questions.Q: What did he say sin is?
Questions.A: He said sin was lawlessness. (4)

Questions.Q: What do you think lawlessness means?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means (1) any action that is contrary to a law, disobeying the law, or (2) the quality of being disobedient to the law. (See "lawlessness" in KBT in the "sin, sinner" entry.)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that [Christ] came into the world?
Questions.A: He came in order to take away people's sins. (5)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that Christ came into the world?
What is the reason that came into the world?

Questions.Q: What does not exist [in Christ]?
Questions.A: There is no sin in him. (5)
Questions.Alternative: What does not exist in Christ?
What does not exist?

Questions.Q: What will those who are united to him/continually have a close relationship to him do about sin?
Questions.A: Those people will not continually sin. (6)
Questions.Alternative: What will those who are united to him do about sin?
What will those who continually have a close relationship to him do about sin?

Questions.Q: What did John say about anyone who continually sins?
Questions.A: Anyone who continually sins has not seen or known him/[Christ]. (6)

Questions.Q: What warning did John give to them?
Questions.A: He told them that they were not to believe the people who try to deceive them. (7)

Questions.Q: What kind of person is truly righteous before God?
Questions.A: He/She is a person who does what is right. (7)

Questions.Q: What did John say about Christ?
Questions.A: He said that he is righteous. (7)

Questions.Q: To whom does a person belong who continually sins?
Questions.A: That person belongs to the devil. (8)

Questions.Q: Who do you think the devil is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The form diabolos "the Devil" is the Greek equivalent of the Hebrew word "Satan". (See "devil" in KBT in the "Satan" entry.)

Questions.Q: What has the devil been doing?
Questions.A: He has been sinning continually ever since the beginning. (8)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that God's Son came to this world?
Questions.A: He came in order to destroy the devil's work. (8)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that someone who is a child of God does not continually sin?
Questions.A: He will/does not continually sin, because God's seed/nature/character is [now] in him. (9)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that someone who is a child of God can not continually sin?
Questions.A: He can not continually sin, because he has been born of God. (9)

Questions.Q: How do we know which people belong to God?
Questions.A: Anyone who does what is right belongs to God. (10)

Questions.Q: How do we know which people belong to Satan?
Questions.A: Anyone who does not do what is right belongs to Satan.
Anyone who does not love other believers /Christians belongs to Satan. (10)

Section.heading: 1 John 3:11-24 John wrote that Christians are to love each other in the same way that Christ loved them. They are to love one another, both in what they say and in what they do. They are to help anyone who has a material need. If a Christian hates his brother, he is a murderer in his heart.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what John said in these verses.
Questions.A: All believers are to love one another. (11)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when someone loves someone else?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The person who loves another person seeks the good of that person. His attitude to the one whom he loves is an attitude of persistent and selfless goodwill.
Questions.Note: See "love" in KBT.

Questions.Q: When did they first hear that message?
Questions.A: They have/had been hearing it from the [time when they became Christians]. (11)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that John said believers must not be like Cain?
Questions.A: They are not to be like Cain, because he murdered his own brother. (12)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Cain killed his brother?
Questions.A: Cain killed his brother because his own deeds were sinful; he belonged to Satan;
and he killed him because his brother did what was right. (12)

Questions.Q: About what did John tell the believers that they are not to be surprised?
Questions.A: They are not to be surprised that non-Christians hated them. (13)

Questions.Q: What did John say that the Christians knew?
Questions.A: They knew that they [now] belonged to God and will always live with him. (14)

Questions.Q: How do the Christians know this?
Questions.A: They know this because they love other Christians. (14)

Questions.Q: What is shown about someone who does not love other Christians?
Questions.A: That shows/It means that he does not belong to God/is still [spiritually] dead. (14)

Questions.Q: What did John say about a person who hates other Christians?
Questions.A: [In God's sight] he is a murderer. (15)

Questions.Q: What do we know about a person who is a murderer?
Questions.A: He does not [belong to God]. // He will not always live [with God]. (15)

Questions.Q: What did Jesus do to show us what it means to love people?
Questions.A: He has shown/showed this by dying voluntarily for us. (16)

Questions.Q: What are we also to do?
Questions.A: We are to be willing to die for other Christians. (16)

Questions.Q: What did John say about a person who refuses to help other Christians?
Questions.A: He asked: How could that person say he loves/loved other people? (17)

Questions.Q: What did John say believers are not to do?
Questions.A: They are not just to say that they love one another. (18)

Questions.Q: But what did John say is important that they do?
Questions.A: They are to do deeds which show that they love others. (18)

Questions.Q: How do believers know that they belong to [God who shows them what is true]/the truth?
Questions.A: They know by the fact that they love one another. (19)
Questions.Alternative: How do believers know that they belong to the truth?
How do believers know that they are of the truth?
How do believers know that they belong to God who shows them what is true?
How do believers know that they belong to God who shows them the truth?

Questions.Q: How will they feel when they pray?
Questions.A: They will not be afraid. // They will be peaceful. (19)

Questions.Q: What does the "heart" mean to you?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The most common use of the word "heart" in the Bible is to refer to the spiritual center or innermost part of a human being. In Hebrew and Greek "heart" is most commonly associated with thoughts and ideas.
Questions.Note: See "heart" in KBT.

Questions.Q: If a believer knows he has done something wrong, how does he feel?
Questions.A: He feels guilty. (20)

Questions.Q: What is the believer to remember at that time?
Questions.A: He is to remember that God knows everything about him. (20)

Questions.Q: What will be the result, if we know in our hearts that we have not sinned?
Questions.A: We will have confidence before God. // We will be able to pray to God without fear. (21)

Questions.Q: What will we receive from him/God?
Questions.A: We will receive from him whatever we ask. (22)
Questions.Alternative: What will we receive from him?
What will we receive from God?

Questions.Q: Why is this true?
Questions.A: This is true, because we obey his commands
and do what pleases him. (22)

Questions.Q: What two things does he/God command us to do?
Questions.A: He commands us to believe in his Son Jesus Christ
and he commands us to love one another. (23)
Questions.Alternative: What two things does he command us to do?
What two things does God command us to do?

Questions.Q: What does someone do when he believes?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He puts his trust and commitment in another person.
Questions.Note: See "believe" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Who commanded believers to love one another?
Questions.A: Jesus Christ commanded us. (23)
Questions.Note: UBS and Translator's Notes state that this could be either God or Jesus

Questions.Q: What will be the result, if a person obeys [God's] commands?
Questions.A: He will live united with [God], and [God] will live in him. (24)
Questions.Alternative: What will be the result, if a person obeys God's commands?
What will be the result, if a person obeys commands?

Questions.Q: How do we know that [God] is living in us?
Questions.A: The Holy Spirit causes us to know this. (24)
Questions.Alternative: How do we know that God is living in us?
How do we know that he is living in us?
How do we know that Jesus is living in us?
How do we know God is living in us?
How do we know he is living in us?
How do we know Jesus is living in us?

Questions.Q: Who has given us the Holy Spirit?
Questions.A: God gave him to us. (24)

Section.heading: 1 John 4:1-6 John wrote that Christians are to test what is taught by different teachers to determine if it really is from God or not. The teachers that say Jesus came from God in human form are teaching a message that is from God.

Questions.Q: What did John tell the believers they are not to do?
Questions.A: They are not to believe every teacher who says he is from God. (1)

Questions.Q: What are they to do instead?
Questions.A: They are to test what the teachers say to find out whether or not they are truly from God. (1)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that John felt it was necessary to warn the Christians about false teachers?
Questions.A: He told them that there were many false prophets who were [teaching what they claim are messages from God]. (1)

Questions.Q: What do you think a false prophet did?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A false prophet was a person who claimed to be a prophet of God, but was not. His messages were deceptive and led to confusion. (See "false prophet" in KBT in the "prophet" entry.)
Questions.Alternative: What do you think false prophets do?
What do you think a false prophet does?

Questions.Q: How will the believers know whether a teacher is from God or not?
Questions.A: A teacher who/that acknowledges that Jesus Christ came into the world as a human being is speaking by the power of the Spirit of God. (2)

Questions.Q: Who do you think the Spirit of God is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: This is the most common reference of the word "spirit" in the New Testament. When it occurs in the phrases "the Holy Spirit", "the Spirit of God", "the Spirit of the Lord", etc., it is clear that the Holy Spirit is meant. (See "spirit of God" in KBT in the "spirit" entry.)
Questions.Alternative: Who do you think the spirit of God is?

Questions.Q: What did John say about those teachers who refuse to acknowledge Jesus?
Questions.A: He said those teachers are not from God. (3)

Questions.Q: What did John say about the spirit of the antichrist?
Questions.A: He said the believers had already heard that the power/spirit of the antichrist was coming.
This power/spirit is already in the world. (3)

Questions.Q: Whom did John say the believers have overcome/defeated?
Questions.A: They overcame/defeated those teachers who were teaching lies. (4)
Questions.Alternative: Whom did John say the believers have overcome?
Whom did John say the believers have defeated?

Questions.Q: How were they able to overcome/defeat them?
Questions.A: They were able to overcome/defeat them, because the power of the Holy Spirit which they had was greater than the power of Satan. (4)
Questions.Alternative: How were they able to overcome them?
How were they able to defeat them?

Questions.Q: What did John say about those lying teachers?
Questions.A: He said that they are ones who do not know God,
and they speak from the viewpoint of those people. (5)

Questions.Q: Who listens to those lying teachers?
Questions.A: The non-Christians listen to them. (5)

Questions.Q: Who listens to those who are from God?
Questions.A: Those people who know God listen to them. (6)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that other people will not listen to those who are from God?
Questions.A: They will not listen, because they do not know God. (6)

Questions.Q: What did John say believers can now do?
Questions.A: They can tell the difference between those who are speaking the truth and those who are speaking lies. (6)

Section.heading: 1 John 4:7-21 John wrote that Christians are to love each other, because God loves them. Everyone who loves other Christians is a son of God. Anyone who does not love other Christians does not know God, because love comes from God.

Questions.Q: What did John say that Christians are to do?
Questions.A: He told them that they are to love one another. (7)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Christians are to love one another?
Questions.A: People who know God are to love one another, because God makes us able to love others. (7)

Questions.Q: What did he say about anyone who loves people?
Questions.A: He said that person is a child of God and knows God. (7)

Questions.Q: What did he say about a person who does not love people?
Questions.A: He said that person does not know God. (8)

Questions.Q: Why is this true?
Questions.A: It is true, because God loves all people. (8)

Questions.Q: What did God do to show that he loves people?
Questions.A: He showed that he loves people by sending his Son to this world so that people might have eternal life because of what he did for them. (9)

Questions.Q: What did God's Son do for all people of the world?
Questions.A: He died so that God could forgive people for their sins. // He took our place of punishment for sin. (10)

Questions.Q: What do you think atonement means?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The penalty for sin was death, but "God graciously permitted the death of a sacrificial victim to substitute for the death of the sinner". The sin of the person having been transferred to the victim, atonement was made; that is, fellowship between the person and God was restored. Thus it is through the blood of Christ, which represents his life given as an atonement, that human beings receive forgiveness. (See "atonement" in KBT in the "reconcile" entry.)

Questions.Q: What shows people what it really means to love someone?
Questions.A: The way that God loves people shows how they are to love others. (10)

Questions.Q: What did John say is the reason Christians are to love one another?
Questions.A: They are to love one another, because God loves us in such a very great way. (11)

Questions.Q: Who has seen God?
Questions.A: No one has seen him. (12)

Questions.Q: How can believers know that God lives in them?
Questions.A: If they love one another, it is evident that he lives in them. (12)

Questions.Q: Since God lives in them, what is the love they have for others like?
Questions.A: It is the same kind of love that God has for people. (12)

Questions.Q: How do the believers know that they live in God and that he lives in them?
Questions.A: They can know this, because he has given them his Spirit. (13)

Questions.Q: What additional fact did John say proved that the Christians live in God?
Questions.A: The additional fact is that John and others with him have seen the Son whom God sent to be the savior of the world. (14)

Questions.Q: What must a person do in order to have God live in him and he live in God?
Questions.A: A person must acknowledge that Jesus is the Son of God. (15)

Questions.Q: What did John say believers know and on what do they rely?
Questions.A: They know and rely on the love God has for them. (16)

Questions.Q: What did John say about anyone who lives knowing that God loves him?
Questions.A: He said that person is united to God and God is united with him. (16)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that [God] will help us to love others?
Questions.A: God will help us to love others so that we will have confidence/not be afraid on the day of judgment. (17)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that God will help us to love others?
What is the reason that God's love is perfected among us?
What is the reason that God's love is made complete among us?
What is the result of having God's love in us?

Questions.Q: Who are we like in this world?
Questions.A: We are like him/[Christ]. (17)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that we do not have to be afraid of what [God] will do to us?
Questions.A: God loves us and if we know/believe that he does we do not have to be afraid of what he might do to us. (18)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that we do not have to be afraid of what God will do to us?
What is the reason that we do not have to be afraid of what will happen to us on the day of judgment?
What is the reason that we do not have to be afraid?

Questions.Q: What did John say about anyone who is afraid [of God]?
Questions.A: He said that the person who fears [God] does not love God completely. (18)
Questions.Alternative: What did John say about anyone who is afraid of God?
What did John say about anyone who is afraid?

Questions.Q: How is it possible for us to love people?
Questions.A: We can love people because God loved us first. (19)

Questions.Q: Who did John say is a liar?
Questions.A: The person who says he loves God but hates other Christians. (20)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that did show he is lying?
Questions.A: He is lying, because anyone who does not love his brother whom he has seen, cannot love God whom he has not seen. (20)

Questions.Q: What command did God give us?
Questions.A: God commanded that whoever loves God must also love other Christians. (21)

Section.heading: 1 John 5:1-12 Anyone who believes that Jesus is the son of God will always live with God and will be children of God.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what John said in these verses.
Questions.A: The believer is able to obey God's commands because his faith gives him the strength to resist evil ways of non-Christians. (3-4)

Questions.Q: What did John say is evidence that a person is God's child?
Questions.A: He believes that Jesus is the Christ. (1)

Questions.Q: Since the Christian loves the Father, whom is he also expected to love?
Questions.A: He loves the children of the Father, that is, other Christians. (1)

Questions.Q: How can they know that they love other Christians?
Questions.A: They love God.
They obey God's commands. (2)

Questions.Q: How did John explain the relationship between loving God and obeying him?
Questions.A: He said the fact that the believers love God is shown when they obey God's commands. (3)

Questions.Q: How hard is it for believers to do what God said they are to do?
Questions.A: John said that God's commands are not too hard for believers to obey. (3)

Questions.Q: What are believers able to do?
Questions.A: Believers are able to resist/defeat the evil ways of non-Christians. (4)

Questions.Q: How are believers able to do that?
Questions.A: Christians/believers do that by believing that Jesus is the Son of God. (5)

Questions.Q: About whom was John speaking here?
Questions.A: He was speaking about Jesus Christ. (6)

Questions.Q: What evidence did John give that Jesus is really this one?
Questions.A: Jesus revealed himself publicly through his water baptism.
He revealed himself publicly also through his blood/death. (6)

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason that John repeated that Jesus revealed himself not only at the time of his water baptism, but also at the time of his death?
Questions.A: It was perhaps to correct what the false teachers were teaching; they were saying that Christ did not really die.

Questions.Q: What further evidence is there that Jesus is the Christ?
Questions.A: The Holy Spirit also declared that this is true. (6)

Questions.Q: So then, what affirms the fact that Jesus is the Son of God?
Questions.A: These affirm that fact:
the Holy Spirit who speaks to us,
the water by which he was baptized,
and his blood/death. (7-8)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the witness of these three is so important?
Questions.A: It is the witness that God himself has given. (9)

Questions.Q: What did John say here to show the importance of God's witness about his Son?
Questions.A: People accept the witness of human beings. Much more powerful/convincing is the witness of God himself. (9)

Questions.Q: Now when a person accepts/believes that witness which God has given, what happens?
Questions.A: He has that same witness within himself; that is, he believes it to be true. (10)
Questions.Alternative: Now when a person accepts that witness which God has given, what happens?
Now when a person believes that witness which God has given, what happens?

Questions.Q: If a person does not believe that Jesus is God's Son, what is he actually saying?
Questions.A: He says that God is a liar. (10)

Questions.Q: So then, what is the witness God has given Christians?
Questions.A: God has made eternal life available to them. (11)
They receive eternal life through living in union with the Son. (11)
Whoever is not living in union with the Son does not have eternal life. (12)

Section.heading: 1 John 5:13-21 John wrote this because he wanted the Christians to know that they have eternal life. Also every Christian can be sure that, if/when he prays to God according to His will, God will hear him and give him that for which he prays.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what John said in these verses.
Questions.A: Believers are able to know that they have eternal life. (13)
Believers are able to know that their prayers will be answered. (14-15)

Questions.Q: What assurance did John give the believers in these verses?
Questions.A: God hears what they ask. (14)
God will give them that for which they ask. (15)

Questions.Q: In order for God to hear the believers when they pray, what condition must they meet?
Questions.A: That for which they ask must be in line with/agree with God's will for them. (14)

Questions.Q: What situation did John present here?
Questions.A: A person knows his fellow Christian is committing a sin. (16)

Questions.Q: What is that person to do?
Questions.A: He is to pray to God for that Christian. (16)

Questions.Q: But John said there is one kind of sin for which the Christian is not to pray. What is that sin?
Questions.A: It is a sin that will lead to rejecting Christ. (16)

Questions.Q: What did John say about sin?
Questions.A: Every person who does wrong is sinning. (17)
Not every sin is the kind that leads to rejecting Christ. (17)

Questions.Q: What did John say believers know?
Questions.A: They know that no child of God continually sins. (18)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that this is so?
Questions.A: The Son of God protects him from Satan. (18)
Satan is not able to control/harm him. (18)

Questions.Q: What is another thing that believers know?
Questions.A: They know that even though the world is under the control of Satan, Christians belong to God. (19)

Questions.Q: What else do believers know?
Questions.A: They know that the Son of God has come into the world.
They know that the Son of God has caused them to understand that God is indeed the true God.
They know that their lives are lived in union with God and with his Son.
They know that Jesus Christ causes them to live eternally. (20)

Questions.Q: What warning did John give the believers?
Questions.A: They are to guard themselves against worshiping false gods. (21)

Section.heading: 1 Peter 1:1-12 Everyone who believes in the Lord Jesus Christ should praise God, since he raised Jesus from the dead and gave them eternal life. Because of this they have the hope that God will keep his promise and provide a place for them in heaven to live with him forever.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the basic meaning (theme) of what Peter said in these verses?
Questions.A: Peter praised God for the eternal life he has given all believers. He praised God for all of the blessings/benefits that belong to them because they are now his people. (3-4)

Questions.Q: Who was the writer of this letter?
Questions.A: He was Peter.
He was an apostle of Jesus Christ. (1)

Questions.Q: What do you think an apostle does?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He is a person sent by Jesus Christ. The general meaning of the Greek word apostolos is "envoy", "appointed representative", "someone who is sent on a mission". In the New Testament it develops the specific sense of an appointed representative of Jesus Christ. In Acts and the rest of the New Testament, the term "apostle" is the most common term that is used to refer to those who were commissioned by Jesus Christ to be founders of the church .
Questions.Note: See "apostle" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the meaning of "Christ"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "Christ" is the English rendering of the Greek word Christos, which means "anointed one."
Questions.Note: See "Christ" in KBT.

Questions.Q: To whom was Peter writing?
Questions.A: He wrote to God's chosen people who were living as refugees in the provinces of Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia and Bithynia. (1)

Questions.Q: Who do you think God is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He is the supreme being to be worshiped. In English, the term "God" with a capital "G" is used to refer to the one supreme Creator. The term "god" with a small "g", as in "a god" or "many gods", can refer to any spiritual being that people worship. The Greek word theos can be used in the same two ways.
Questions.Note: In many languages the term for God is a proper name and cannot be used to refer to anyone except the one supreme creator of the world. It cannot be pluralized. (Or, if it can be pluralized, the meaning may be something very different from the English "gods". In one language, the plural form of God, meant "God and those who follow him" and was an appropriate way to translate "saints".) (See "God" in KBT.)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that these people belong to God?
Questions.A: God had chosen them to be his people. (2)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to be holy?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: They are good as God desires. Someone who is "holy" is set apart [by God] and dedicated to the service or worship of God. Anything that is "holy" for God must reflect his character by being physically unblemished or reflecting, to some degree, his purity.
Questions.Note: See "holy" in KBT.

Questions.Q: How did God accomplish this?
Questions.A: He did it through the sanctifying work of the Holy Spirit. (2)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to sanctify someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that someone dedicates someone else to the service of God. (See "sanctify" in KBT in the "holy, holiness..." entry.)

Questions.Q: Who do you think the Holy Spirit is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He is God's spirit, through whom he acts, reveals His will, and empowers individuals. (See "Holy Spirit" in KBT in the "spirit" entry.)

Questions.Q: What did God want/intend for them to do/become as a result of (his) doing all that?
Questions.A: He wanted them to obey Jesus Christ and be forgiven for their sins because of the death of Christ. (2)
Questions.Alternative: What did God want for them to do as a result of (his) doing all that?
What did God want for them to become as a result of (his) doing all that?
What did God intend for them to do as a result of (his) doing all that?
What did God intend for them to become as a result of (his) doing all that?

Questions.Q: What is Peter's desire for them?
Questions.A: He desired that God give them much grace and much peace. (2)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to have grace?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that a person shows that he accepts and loves another person even when they do not deserve it.
Questions.Note: See "grace" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to be at peace?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: To be at peace is to have a mental or spiritual condition marked by freedom of disquieting or oppressive thoughts or emotions.
Questions.Note: See "peace" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that we should give thanks to the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ?
Questions.A: Due to his great mercy, he gave us eternal life. (3)

Questions.Q: What do you think "God the Father" means?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that God is the father of Jesus Christ and of anyone who accepts Jesus as their Savior and Lord.
Questions.Note: See "God the Father" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think the title "God the Father" means?
What do you think the term "God the Father" means?

Questions.Q: What does it mean to you to have someone as your lord?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A lord is someone who has power and exercises it responsibly. To call someone your lord means that you have given them control over your life. The Lord in this case is Jesus. Every Christian strives to make Jesus lord in his or her life by giving Him complete control. (See "Lord" in KBT in the "God" entry.)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when someone shows mercy to someone else?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "Mercy" in the New Testament is an act of kindness by God or someone else toward people who are in need. The person (God or man) acts to relieve some kind of suffering or distress.
Questions.Note: See "mercy" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did God do in order to give us this eternal life?
Questions.A: He raised Jesus Christ from the dead. (3)

Questions.Q: What is the result of God giving us this eternal life?
Questions.A: It gives us hope that God will keep his promise. (3)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to hope in something?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means to have a desire to see something happen or to obtain something.

Questions.Q: How can they be sure that they are going to receive that for which they hope?
Questions.A: God will make sure that they will obtain that for which they hope. (4)

Questions.Q: Where does God keep/reserve this eternal life for them?
Questions.A: He keeps it for them in heaven. (4)
Questions.Alternative: Where does God keep this eternal life for them?
Where does God reserve this eternal life for them?

Questions.Q: Where do you think heaven is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It is that part of God's creation above the earth and the waters, including "air" and "space," and serves as home for God and the spirits who serve Him.
Questions.Note: See "heaven" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What is the character of those things which God keeps for them?
Questions.A: They are permanent, as they can never perish, spoil or fade away. (4)

Questions.Q: How are all believers protected [from evil]?
Questions.A: They are protected because they believe that God has power to protect them. (5)
Questions.Alternative: How are all believers protected from evil?
How are all believers protected?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to have faith in someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Faith is the quality of trusting someone. It is the act of wholeheartedly and steadfastly believing in the existence, power, and benevolence of a supreme being. (See "faith" in KBT in the "believe, believing, belief, faith, trust" entry.)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that God protects them?
Questions.A: He does it in order that they might attain [God's] salvation at the end of time. (5)

Questions.Q: What do you think "salvation" means?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The noun form (Greek sôtêria) and the adjective form (Greek sôtêrios) in the New Testament usually refer to eternal salvation from sin, evil and death. "To save" or "salvation" may refer either to rescuing from a physical danger (like death or captivity to an enemy) or to rescuing from spiritual and eternal danger (captivity to sin and condemnation by God).
Questions.Note: See "salvation" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to save you?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that a person will rescue someone else out of a dangerous situation.
Questions.Note: See "save" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the believers are/were happy in spite of the fact that they had to suffer various trials/hardships?
Questions.A: They have the hope of God saving them in the future.
Questions.Note: This answer is derived from verse 5.
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that the believers are happy in spite of the fact that they had to suffer various trials?
What is the reason that the believers are happy in spite of the fact that they had to suffer various hardships?
What is the reason that the believers were happy in spite of the fact that they had to suffer various trials?
What is the reason that the believers were happy in spite of the fact that they had to suffer various hardships?
What is the reason that the believers were happy in spite of having to suffer various trials?
What is the reason that the believers were happy in spite of having to suffer various hardships?

Questions.Q: How long will these trials last?
Questions.A: They will last for only a little while. (6)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they experience these trials?
Questions.A: They/You suffer in order to prove that they really believe God. (7)

Questions.Q: If they believe God, what will the result be?
Questions.A: They will be praised, honored, and given glory [by God]. (7)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when you honor someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: When you honor someone you show high regard or appreciation for them.

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when you give glory to someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: When you give glory to someone you reveal the greatness of someone, you demonstrate or show openly that someone is worthy of receiving honor.
Questions.Note: See "glory" in KBT.

Questions.Q: When will that happen?
Questions.A: That will happen when Jesus Christ returns again. (7)

Questions.Q: Gold was considered valuable by people. What is better than gold?
Questions.A: It is better to believe God. (7)

Questions.Q: In spite of the fact that they have never seen Jesus Christ, what is/was their attitude toward him?
Questions.A: They loved him.
They believed in him. (8)
Questions.Alternative: In spite of the fact that they have never seen Jesus Christ, what is their attitude toward him?
In spite of the fact that they have never seen Jesus Christ, what was their attitude toward him?
Although they had never seen Jesus Christ, what was their attitude toward him?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when someone loves someone else?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The person who loves another person seeks the good of that person. His attitude to the one whom he loves is an attitude of persistent and selfless goodwill.
Questions.Note: See "love" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What does someone do when he believes?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He puts his trust and commitment in another person.
Questions.Note: See "believe" in KBT.

Questions.Q: How happy are/were they?
Questions.A: They are/were so happy that it cannot/could not be expressed in words. (8)
Questions.Alternative: How happy are they?
How happy were they?

Questions.Q: What were they receiving because they believed in Christ?
Questions.A: [God] had saved them [from their sins]. (9)

Questions.Q: What do you think the soul is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It is a person's inner being, the self. The self in its relationship with God.
Questions.Note: See "soul" in KBT.

Questions.Q: For what did the prophets search intently?
Questions.A: They wanted to know the way in which [God] would save all believers. (10)

Questions.Q: What do you know about prophets?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A prophet is someone who speaks for God and is inspired by Him. He often foretells future events. Prophets were mainly spokespersons who called His people to obedience by appealing to Israel's past and future.
Questions.Note: See "prophet" in KBT.

Questions.Q: About what had the prophets told the people before?
Questions.A: They told that God had compassion toward them. (10)

Questions.Q: Who revealed these things to the prophets?
Questions.A: The Spirit of Christ revealed that to them. (11)

Questions.Q: What specifically did the prophets predict about Christ?
Questions.A: They predicted that he would have to suffer and then [God would take] him back to heaven. (11)

Questions.Q: What did the prophets try to find out/understand?
Questions.A: They tried to find out/understand when this would happen, and how it would take place. (11)
Questions.Alternative: What did the prophets try to find out?
What did the prophets try to understand?

Questions.Q: What did [God] reveal to the prophets about their work?
Questions.A: He revealed that the things/the gospel [of salvation] they were teaching was not for their own benefit, but for all believers. (12)
Questions.Alternative: What did God reveal to the prophets about their work?
What was revealed to the prophets about their work?

Questions.Q: What do you think the gospel is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The word "gospel" is a translation of the Greek noun euangelion. In the New Testament the noun euangelion is used in a restricted sense. It does not mean just any kind of good news, but specifically the good news or joyful report that God has made a way of salvation for sinful human beings. In the New Testament it is used always with this one sense and is usually translated in the RSV and most modern English versions as "gospel".
Questions.Note: See "gospel" in KBT.

Questions.Q: How did it happen that they heard this gospel?
Questions.A: Preachers/teachers taught them by the power of the Holy Spirit, who was sent from heaven [by God]. (12)

Questions.Q: What do you think someone is doing when they preach?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: When someone preaches they are proclaiming the gospel to those who are listening. This also means that a person/preacher urges others to accept or abandon an idea or course of action.

Questions.Q: Who else would like to understand more about this gospel?
Questions.A: The angels would like to know/experience it/the gospel as we people know it. (12)

Questions.Q: What do you know about angels?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Angels are spiritual messengers, who either deliver a message to humans, carry out God's will, praise God, or guard God's throne.
Questions.Note: See "angel" in KBT.

Section.heading: 1 Peter 1:13-25 Everyone who believes in Jesus Christ should live holy lives like God who is completely good/holy.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the basic meaning (theme) of what Peter said in these verses?
Questions.A: He told of their need to obey God and to be good as God is completely good/live a holy life. (13, 15)

Questions.Q: What three things did Peter tell them to do in this verse?
Questions.A: They should be alert in their thinking.
They should be self-controlled.
They should hope in the fact that [God] is going to help them when Jesus Christ comes again. (13)

Questions.Q: How are they supposed to conduct themselves as children [of God]?
Questions.A: They are to be obedient [to him].
They are not to follow their former evil ways. (14)
Questions.Alternative: How are they supposed to conduct themselves as children of God?
How are they supposed to conduct themselves as children?

Questions.Q: What should they do instead of following their former evil ways?
Questions.A: They should be holy in all that they do. (15)

Questions.Q: What pattern/example are they to follow as they strive to live a holy life?
Questions.A: They should be holy even as [God] is holy. (15)
Questions.Alternative: What pattern are they to follow as they strive to live a holy life?
What example are they to follow as they strive to live a holy life?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they must live a holy life?
Questions.A: They must live a holy life because he/[God] is holy. (16b)

Questions.Q: When they pray to God, what do they call him?
Questions.A: They call him [our] Father. (17)

Questions.Q: How or in what way does God judge people?
Questions.A: He judges all people the same, according to what they have done. (17)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to judge someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means someone/a judge will determine if a person is guilty, or not, of committing a crime. He does this by assessing the evidence connected to the person and what he may have done.
Questions.Note: See "judge" in KBT.

Questions.Q: How should they live?
Questions.A: They should live in fear of God, so that they do not displease Him. (17)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to redeem someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: With only one or two exceptions, in the New Testament the words "to redeem", "redemption", "ransom" refer to Christ's action in giving up his own life in order that those who believe in him may be forgiven their sins.
Questions.Note: See "redeem" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What didn't [God] use to redeem them from the empty/worthless ways that they learned from their ancestors?
Questions.A: He didn't use perishable things like silver or gold. (18)
Questions.Alternative: What didn't God use to redeem them from the empty ways that they learned from their ancestors?
What didn't God use to redeem them from the worthless ways that they learned from their ancestors?

Questions.Q: What did [God] use in order to redeem them?
Questions.A: He used the blood of Christ/the death of Christ. (19)
Questions.Alternative: What did God use in order to redeem them?
What was used in order to redeem them?
What did God use to redeem them?
What was used to redeem them?

Questions.Q: To what did Peter compare Christ?
Questions.A: He compared him to a lamb without any blemish or defect. (19)

Questions.Q: When did [God] choose Christ?
Questions.A: [God] chose him/Christ before the world was created. (20)
Questions.Alternative: When did God choose Christ?
When was Christ chosen?

Questions.Q: What do you think Peter meant by "the world" in this verse?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In this reference it meant the entire universe that God created, the whole creation, including both heaven and earth.
Questions.Note: See "world" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think Peter meant by the world in this verse?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that [God] revealed Christ in these last days?
Questions.A: [He] did it so that people would know Christ. (20)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that God revealed Christ in these last days?
What is the reason that Christ was revealed in these last days?
Why did God reveal Christ in these last days?
Why was Christ revealed in these last days?
What is the reason that God revealed Christ in these last times?
What is the reason that Christ was revealed in these last times?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they are able to believe in God and have their faith and hope in him?
Questions.A: He raised Christ from the dead. Therefore, they can believe God to take care of them. (21)

Questions.Q: What happened when they obeyed the truth?
Questions.A: Their "hearts" were right with God, and now they had a sincere love for their brothers. (22)

Questions.Q: What do you think Peter meant when he said "their brothers"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He meant those who were fellow-believers in Jesus. (See "brothers" in KBT in the "disciple" entry.)

Questions.Q: What did Peter tell them they should do from now on?
Questions.A: They must see to it that they love one another with all their hearts. (22)

Questions.Q: What does the "heart" mean to you?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The most common use of the word "heart" in the Bible is to refer to the spiritual center or innermost part of a human being. In Hebrew and Greek the word "heart" is most commonly associated with thoughts and ideas.
Questions.Note: See "heart" in KBT.

Questions.Q: How were they born again?
Questions.A: They were born again through believing God's word. (23)

Questions.Q: What are people like?
Questions.A: People are like grass which withers and dies. (24)

Questions.Q: How permanent are people?
Questions.A: They are like the wild flowers whose blossoms look beautiful for only a short time and then fall off. (24)

Questions.Q: How does the word of the Lord differ from people, grass, and flowers?
Questions.A: People, grass, and flowers are all perishable, while the word of the Lord remains forever. (25)

Questions.Q: What did [the preachers/teachers] preach to them?
Questions.A: They preached the word of the Lord. (25)
Questions.Alternative: What did the preachers preach to them?
What did the teachers preach to them?

Section.heading: 1 Peter 2:1-12 Everyone who believes in Jesus Christ should continually fellowship with him. Jesus was called the living stone and all believers were called the chosen people of God.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the basic meaning (theme) of what Peter said in these verses?
Questions.A: As children of God, all believers should rid themselves of their previous evil deeds. Instead, they should desire to obey God's word. (1-2)

Questions.Q: What did Peter tell them they should do?
Questions.A: They must stop doing any kind of evil deeds such as:
malice/intending to harm another person
deceit
hypocrisy
being jealous
slandering/defaming someone. (1)

Questions.Q: Instead of doing the evil deeds mentioned in verse 1, what should they do?
Questions.A: They should love pure spiritual milk/[the word of God]. (2)

Questions.Q: What do you think he meant by "pure milk" in this verse?
