Questions.A: Key Term Check: "Pure milk" is used here in a figurative sense; it refers to teaching that is true, unspoiled by distortion or lie. The Greek word logikos, translated "spiritual" by RSV, probably here means "figurative," an indication that "milk" is a comparative illustration. (See "pure" in KBT in the "clean" entry.)

Questions.Q: How strongly are they supposed to love pure spiritual milk/God's word?
Questions.A: They should love pure spiritual milk/[God's word] just as strongly as newborn babies [are always thirsty for milk]. (2)
Questions.Alternative: How strongly are they supposed to love pure spiritual milk?
How strongly are they supposed to love God's word?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they should love pure spiritual milk/God's word in this way?
Questions.A: They should love pure spiritual milk/[God's word] so that they believe God more. (2)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that they should love pure spiritual milk in this way?
What is the reason that they should love God's word in this way?

Questions.Q: What other reason did Peter give for why they should love pure spiritual milk/God's word?
Questions.A: They know how kind/loving the Lord is. (3)
Questions.Alternative: What other reason did Peter give for why they should love pure spiritual milk?
What other reason did Peter give for why they should love God's word?

Questions.Q: What did Peter tell them to do?
Questions.A: He told them to come to him/[the Lord]. (4)

Questions.Q: To what did Peter compare Christ?
Questions.A: He compared him to a stone which is alive. (4)

Questions.Q: How have men treated the living stone [the Lord]?
Questions.A: They have rejected him. (4)
Questions.Alternative: How have men treated the living stone?
How have men treated the Lord?

Questions.Q: How did God treat the living stone?
Questions.A: God chose him and he is precious to him. (4)

Questions.Q: To what did Peter compare believers?
Questions.A: He said they were like stones which are/were alive. (5)

Questions.Q: What did he say was happening to them?
Questions.A: He said [that it was like God] was building them into a house where his Spirit lives. (5)

Questions.Q: What do you think something spiritual is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Something spiritual is relating to or consisting of spirit. It is of the nature of spirit rather than material. Spiritual things can not be seen with the human eye. (See "spiritual" in KBT in the "spirit" entry.)

Questions.Q: What service/work will they do as they serve the Lord?
Questions.A: They are to serve as priests by offering spiritual sacrifices to God that are acceptable to him. (5)
Questions.Alternative: What service will they do as they serve the Lord?
What work will they do as they serve the Lord?

Questions.Q: What do you know about priests?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In this verse the Greek noun hierateuma "priesthood" is used. The particular part of meaning in focus in this passage seems to be the idea of entering into God's presence, becoming his servants and offering "spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ". Another intermediary apart from Jesus Christ is not needed; the believer can enter into God's presence directly through him.
Questions.Note: See "priest" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when someone sacrifices something to God?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In this context it means to worship God and to devote themselves to God. When someone sacrifices something to God they are doing it in order to establish, maintain, or restore a proper relationship with him.
Questions.Note: See "sacrifice" in KBT.

Questions.Q: To what do you think Peter was referring as "scripture"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The scriptures are the contents of the Old Testament as God gave them to men to write down.
Questions.Note: See "scripture" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What does a person do when he trusts someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He has a confident dependence in the character, ability, strength or truth of someone. (See "trust" in KBT in the "believe" entry.)

Questions.Q: Since [God] has appointed [Christ] as the cornerstone in Zion, what can anyone who trusts/believes in him be sure of?
Questions.A: They will never be disappointed/put to shame. (6)
Questions.Alternative: Since God has appointed Christ as the cornerstone in Zion, what can anyone who trusts in him be sure of?
Since God has appointed Christ as the cornerstone in Zion, what can anyone who believes in him be sure of?

Questions.Q: How do those who believe in [Christ] regard him?
Questions.A: He is like the stone that is precious. (7)
Questions.Alternative: How do those who believe in Christ regard him?
How do those who believe in regard him?

Questions.Q: How do those who do not believe in [Christ] regard him?
Questions.A: He is like the stone which was rejected by the builders. (7)
Questions.Alternative: How do those who do not believe in Christ regard him?
How do those who do not believe in regard him?

Questions.Q: Even though these builders rejected this stone, what did this stone finally become/turn out to be?
Questions.A: This stone became/proved to be a very valuable stone/the capstone [chosen by God]. (7)
Questions.Alternative: Even though these builders rejected this stone, what did this stone finally become?
Even though these builders rejected this stone, what did this stone finally turn out to be?

Questions.Q: In addition to being the capstone, what else does this stone do?
Questions.A: People stumble and fall over it. (8)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that people stumble?
Questions.A: They stumble because they disobey the message [from God]. (8)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that this is true?
Questions.A: This is what [God] destined for those who disobey his word. (8)

Questions.Q: What did Peter say about the believers in contrast to the unbelievers?
Questions.A: He said they were the people that [God] had chosen,
a royal priesthood/priests who serve God,
a holy nation/a nation dedicated to God's service,
a people belonging to God. (9)

Questions.Q: What does the word "nation" mean to you?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "Nation" refers to the people who make up that nation. This community of people possesses a more or less defined territory of land and government.

In this verse "nation" is used figuratively to refer to all believers, who are united as a people by their allegiance to God and a common set of values and whose "kingdom" or "land" is spiritual/heavenly.
Questions.Note: See "nation" in KBT in the "gentile" entry.

Questions.Q: What is the purpose that [God] made them his possession?
Questions.A: They were to give him praise/tell about the wonderful things he has done for calling them out of darkness into his marvelous light. (9)
Questions.Alternative: What is the purpose that God made them his possession?
What is the purpose that he made them his possession?
Why did God make them his possession?
For what purpose did God make them his possession?

Questions.Q: What do you think "darkness" means in this verse?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Darkness refers to spiritual or moral sin and separation from God.

Questions.Q: What do you think "light" means in this verse?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Light refers to truth or divine truth.
Questions.Note: Light refers to knowledge or knowledge of God or revelation about him.

Questions.Q: When they were ignorant of God and sinning against him what did [he] do for them?
Questions.A: [He] made them his people.
[He] had mercy on them. (10)
Questions.Alternative: When they were ignorant of God and sinning against him what did he do for them?
When they were ignorant of God and sinning against him what did do for them?

Questions.Q: What reason did Peter give concerning/as to why they should not do evil things?
Questions.A: They should not do those things because [they are people of God]. (11)
Questions.Alternative: What reason did Peter give concerning why they should not do evil things?
What reason did Peter give as to why they should not do evil things?
Why did Peter say they should not do evil things?

Questions.Q: What other reason did Peter give concerning why they should not do evil things?
Questions.A: Those things [are a hindrance to their following Christ]. (11)

Questions.Q: What do you think "flesh" means or is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that all of mankind was made of skin and bones and represents the human tendency to want to satisfy physical desires rather than to be obedient to God.
Questions.Note: See "flesh" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Instead of doing evil things, what should they do as they live among the unbelievers?
Questions.A: They should live correctly as God desires them to live. (12)

Questions.Q: Even though unbelievers might accuse them of doing bad things, if they make a practice of doing good deeds, what will those unbelievers have to admit?
Questions.A: The unbelievers will have to admit that what they have done is good. They will praise God because of that. (12)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when someone glorifies God?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that they honor him. They praise God.
Questions.Note: See "glorify" in KBT.

Questions.Q: When will this happen?
Questions.A: This will happen when God comes [to judge people] or when people believe God. (12)

Section.heading: 1 Peter 2:13-25 All those who believe [in Christ] should obey every authority.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what Peter said in these verses.
Questions.A: All believers must submit to/obey those who are their rulers. Slaves should obey their masters. (13-14, 18)

Questions.Q: What did Peter tell them to do?
Questions.A: He said they should submit themselves to every authority. (13-14)

Questions.Q: Who is supreme in authority among all human leaders?
Questions.A: The king. (13)

Questions.Q: Who has appointed governors?
Questions.A: The king. (14)

Questions.Q: What tasks/work did the king appoint the governors to do?
Questions.A: They are to punish those who do evil deeds, and to praise/commend those who do good. (14)
Questions.Alternative: What tasks did the king appoint the governors to do?
What work did the king appoint the governors to do?

Questions.Q: What is God's will for them to do?
Questions.A: It is his will that through the good deeds they do, people will not be able to lie about them. (15)

Questions.Q: How should they live?
Questions.A: They should live as ones who had God as their chief leader/like free men. (16)

Questions.Q: What should they not do with their freedom?
Questions.A: They should not do any evil deeds. (16)

Questions.Q: Instead of trying to find an excuse for sinning, what should they do?
Questions.A: They should live as servants of God. (16)

Questions.Q: What do you think a servant does?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A servant is a person who is required to work for another person and obey him. Servants are usually paid for their work, while slaves are not paid.
Questions.Note: See "servant" in KBT.

Questions.Q: To whom should they show respect?
Questions.A: They should respect everyone. (17)

Questions.Q: To whom should they show love?
Questions.A: They should love their fellow believers. (17)

Questions.Q: Whom should they fear [with the sense of reverence]?
Questions.A: They should fear God. (17)
Questions.Alternative: Whom should they fear with the sense of reverence?
Whom should they fear?

Questions.Q: To whom should they show honor?
Questions.A: They should honor their leader/chief. (17)

Questions.Q: How should a servant treat/work for his master?
Questions.A: He should be submissive and should show him respect. (18)
Questions.Alternative: How should a servant treat his master?
How should a servant work for his master?

Questions.Q: How should a servant treat/work for his master if he is harsh?
Questions.A: He should be submissive and show him the same respect that he would a master who is kind and considerate. (18)
Questions.Alternative: How should a servant treat his master if he is harsh?
How should a servant work for his master if he is harsh?

Questions.Q: What will happen to someone who endures unjust suffering because he follows/obeys God?
Questions.A: [God] will commend him. (19)
Questions.Alternative: What will happen to someone who endures unjust suffering because he follows God?
What will happen to someone who endures unjust suffering because he obeys God?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when someone/a person is unjust to someone else?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Someone/a person is unjust when he is not just or fair in his treatment of someone else/others.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think it means when someone is unjust to someone else?
What do you think it means when a person is unjust to someone else?

Questions.Q: What reward will a person receive if he endures the beatings he deserves for doing wrong?
Questions.A: He will not receive a/any reward. (20)

Questions.Q: What will happen to a person who/if he suffers when he has done good things and yet/still he endures?
Questions.A: God will bless him for suffering in this way. (20)
Questions.Alternative: What will happen to a person who suffers when he has done good things and yet he endures?
What will happen to a person who suffers when he has done good things and still endures?
What will happen to a person if he suffers when he has done good things and yet he endures?
What will happen to a person if he suffers when he has done good things and still endures?

Questions.Q: What has [God] called all believers to experience?
Questions.A: He called them to endure suffering even though/when they have done good things. (20-21)
Questions.Alternative: What has God called all believers to experience?
What have all believers been called to experience?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they should be willing to do this?
Questions.A: They should be willing to do this because Christ suffered for them and, in this way, gave them an example to follow. (21)

Questions.Q: What did Christ do as their example?
Questions.A: He committed no sin and never told a lie. (22)

Questions.Q: What did Christ do when [people] insulted him?
Questions.A: He did not answer back with an insult. (23)
Questions.Alternative: What did Christ do when people insulted him?
What did Christ do when insulted him?

Questions.Q: What did Christ do when [people] made him suffer?
Questions.A: He did not threaten them. (23)
Questions.Alternative: What did Christ do when people made him suffer?
What did Christ do when made him suffer?

Questions.Q: What did Christ do when he suffered unjustly in this way?
Questions.A: He trusted [God], who will punish people for their bad treatment to others. (23)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to deal with someone else justly?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Doing something in conformity with law or justice. In this reference it refers particularly to God's faithful and consistent adherence to his covenant.
Questions.Note: See "just" in KBT.

Questions.Q: When Christ died on the cross, what did he do for us?
Questions.A: He personally paid the penalty for our sins by his death. (24)

Questions.Q: What do you know about the cross?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The cross consisted of two pieces of wood. One piece was a thick wooden post which was planted upright in the ground. The other piece was the cross-beam, which was fastened across the upright post so that it formed a + or T shape.
Questions.Note: See "cross" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What does a person do when he sins?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He disobeys God. He deliberately keeps on doing those things that please himself and displease God.
Questions.Note: See "sin" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Christ died for us?
Questions.A: He did it/died so that we might no longer sin, but instead make a practice of doing good/living for righteousness. (24)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to be righteous?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means to live as God desires a person to live. It means that a person does what is right in the sight of God, consistent with God's laws, upright. A person is in a state of having been accepted by God as right in his eyes. (See "righteousness" in KBT in the "just, justify..." entry.)

Questions.Q: What body do you think is meant here?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In this reference it is Jesus's physical body.
Questions.Note: See "body" in KBT.

Questions.Q: How have they been saved from their sins?
Questions.A: They were saved by his death on the cross. (24)
Questions.Note: UBS states that this is a metaphor in which healed is used in place of spiritual health/salvation.

Questions.Q: What did Peter tell them they were like?
Questions.A: They were like sheep who had strayed from their [shepherd]. (25)

Questions.Q: What had they done now?
Questions.A: They had returned to [Christ], who would care well for them. (25)

Section.heading: 1 Peter 3:1-7 Wives should obey or submit to their husbands. Husbands should be understanding of their wives and be respectful of them.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what Peter said in these verses.
Questions.A: Peter told how wives and husbands should conduct themselves in their relationship with each other. (, )

Questions.Q: What did Peter tell [believing/Christian] wives they should do?
Questions.A: They should submit to/obey their husbands. (1)
Questions.Alternative: What did Peter tell believing wives they should do?
What did Peter tell Christian wives they should do?
What did Peter tell christian wives they should do?
What did Peter tell wives they should do?

Questions.Q: How may a believing wife influence her non-believing husband to become a believer in [God's] word?
Questions.A: She may be able to influence him, without saying anything, through her conduct. (1-2)
Questions.Alternative: How may a believing wife influence her non-believing husband to become a believer in God's word?
How may a believing wife influence her non-believing husband to become a believer in word?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that she will not have to say anything to her husband to influence him to become a believer?
Questions.A: He will see that she lives good/properly and submits to him. (2)

Questions.Q: From where should a wife's beauty not come?
Questions.A: It should not come from/depend on the way she dresses, the jewelry she wears, or how she fixes her hair. (3)

Questions.Q: Instead, from where should a wife's beauty come?
Questions.A: Her husband should think of her as beautiful, because her "heart" is good. (4)

Questions.Q: What does God think of character like that?
Questions.A: God considers character like that very valuable. (4)

Questions.Q: How did the women, who lived long ago and believed in God, make themselves beautiful?
Questions.A: They did it by submitting themselves to their husbands. (5)

Questions.Q: Whom did Peter mention as an example of one of those women/wives in the past?
Questions.A: Sarah. (6)
Questions.Alternative: Whom did Peter mention as an example of one of those women in the past?
Whom did Peter mention as an example of one of those wives in the past?

Questions.Q: What did Sarah do to show respect to Abraham?
Questions.A: She obeyed him and acknowledged him as her leader. (6)

Questions.Q: What did Peter say wives could consider themselves, if they did what is right and did not give in to fear?
Questions.A: They could consider themselves like/as though they were Sarah's daughters. (6)

Questions.Q: How should husbands treat their wives?
Questions.A: They should be considerate of them
and should treat them with respect, since they are weaker physically. (7)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the husbands should treat their wives with respect?
Questions.A: They too (as well as their husbands) will have eternal life with [God].
Then [God] will listen to and will answer their prayers. (7)

Section.heading: 1 Peter 3:8-22 Believers that/who obey God can expect that some people will do bad things to them. Their suffering should never be the result of doing evil actions to others. Christ suffered for doing good things. It is his example that all believers should follow.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what Peter said in these verses.
Questions.A: A believer must not retaliate against those who do evil deeds to him. Instead he must live as God wants him to live. (10-11)

Questions.Q: To whom did Peter speak?
Questions.A: He spoke to all of them [the believers]. (8)

Questions.Q: What did he tell them to do?
Questions.A: He said they must live in harmony/unity with one another,
be sympathetic [toward one another],
love one another as brothers,
be compassionate [toward one another],
and be humble [with one another]. (8)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to be compassionate to someone else?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: This takes place when someone shows deep feeling for and understanding of the misery and suffering that someone else is experiencing.
Questions.Note: See "compassion" in KBT in the "mercy" entry.

Questions.Q: What did Peter tell them not to do, if someone did something evil to them or insulted them?
Questions.A: He said they must not retaliate against the person; and they must not insult the person. (9)

Questions.Q: What should they do instead of retaliating?
Questions.A: They should speak well of the person/bless them. (9)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to bless someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means to make someone happy, to give good fortune or satisfaction, to confer prosperity upon someone. (See both "grace" and "bless, blessed, blessing" in KBT.)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they should bless their enemies/adversaries?
Questions.A: They have been dealt with mercifully by God. They should deal with others in the same way. (Exegetical position 1) (9)
God has called them specifically to show good to others. As a result of this, God will help them. (Exegetical position 2) (9)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that they should bless their enemies?
What is the reason that they should bless their adversaries?

Questions.Q: What must a person not do if he wants to love/enjoy life and see good/prosperous days?
Questions.A: He must not say evil things
and he must stop telling lies. (10)
Questions.Alternative: What must a person not do if he wants to love life and see good days?
What must a person not do if he wants to love life and see prosperous days?
What must a person not do if he wants to enjoy life and see good days?
What must a person not do if he wants to enjoy life and see prosperous days?

Questions.Q: What must a person do, if he wants to love/enjoy life and see good/prosperous days?
Questions.A: He must stop doing what is bad and do good.
He must live peacefully. (11)
Questions.Alternative: What must a person do, if he wants to love life and see good days?
What must a person do, if he wants to love life and see prosperous days?
What must a person do, if he wants to enjoy life and see good days?
What must a person do, if he wants to enjoy life and see prosperous days?

Questions.Q: How does anyone know that God will help him/her?
Questions.A: The Lord watches over/cares for those who are righteous
and listens to their prayers. (12)
Questions.Alternative: How does anyone know that God will help him?
How does anyone know that God will help her?

Questions.Q: How does the Lord respond to people who do evil deeds?
Questions.A: The Lord opposes/is against those people who do evil deeds. (12)

Questions.Q: Who will harm someone who is eager to do good things?
Questions.A: Usually no one will harm such a person. (13)
Questions.Note: This is implied.

Questions.Q: If they should suffer because they do what is good/right, what should they feel?
Questions.A: They should feel that [God] will help them/that [God] will look well on them. (14)
Questions.Alternative: If they should suffer because they do what is good, what should they feel?
If they should suffer because they do what is right, what should they feel?

Questions.Q: How were they to feel toward those who opposed/threatened them?
Questions.A: They were not to be afraid of them nor to worry. (14)
Questions.Alternative: How were they to feel toward those who opposed them?
How were they to feel toward those who threatened them?

Questions.Q: Instead of being afraid of those who opposed them, what should they have done?
Questions.A: They should have acknowledged/reverenced Christ as their Lord. (15)

Questions.Q: What should they be ready to do at all times?
Questions.A: They should always be prepared to answer those who ask them to explain [why they believe in Jesus]. (15)

Questions.Q: With what manner should they answer them?
Questions.A: They should answer them/their accusers with gentleness and respect. (16)

Questions.Q: What will happen to those who insult them and speak evil of their good conduct?
Questions.A: They/Those who insult the believers will be ashamed of what they have said/say about them. (16)

Questions.Q: What do you think the conscience is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The conscience is the sense of right and wrong within the individual. The awareness of the moral goodness or blameworthiness of one's own conduct.

Questions.Q: If it is God's will for anyone to suffer, for what is it better to suffer?
Questions.A: It is better for someone to suffer for doing good than to suffer for doing evil. (17)

Questions.Q: Who showed them that it is better to suffer for doing good than for doing evil?
Questions.A: Christ is the/our/their example. (18)

Questions.Q: How did he show this?
Questions.A: He died for everyone's sins even though he was righteous/without sin. (18)

Questions.Q: How do they/believers know that his death was sufficient payment/punishment for everyone's sins?
Questions.A: He died once and for all, for everyone's sins. (18)
Questions.Alternative: How do they know that his death was sufficient payment for everyone's sins?
How do they know that his death was sufficient punishment for everyone's sins?
How do believers know that his death was sufficient payment for everyone's sins?
How do believers know that his death was sufficient punishment for everyone's sins?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Christ died for everyone?
Questions.A: He died in order to bring them to God. (18)

Questions.Q: What does the translation in your language mean in 3:18b-19?
What happened to Christ after he was put to death [by people]?
Questions.A: He rose again to life by the spirit. (18)
Questions.Alternative: What happened to Christ after he was put to death by people?
What happened to Christ after he was put to death?

Questions.Q: After Christ died, what did he do through/in his spirit?
Questions.A: He went and preached to the spirits in prison. (19)
Questions.Alternative: After Christ died, what did he do through his spirit?
After Christ died, what did he do in his spirit?

Questions.Q: Who were these spirits to whom Christ preached?
Questions.A: They were the spirits of people who had lived during the time of Noah when he was building the ark. (20)

Questions.Q: What kind of lives had these people lived?
Questions.A: They had been disobedient to God. (20)

Questions.Q: What did God do, even though these people disobeyed him?
Questions.A: He waited patiently for them [to repent of their sins]. (20)

Questions.Q: How many people [did God save] in the ark?
Questions.A: Only eight people were saved. (20)
Questions.Alternative: How many people did God save in the ark?
How many people in the ark?

Questions.Q: Of what was this water a sign/symbol?
Questions.A: Baptism. (21)
Questions.Alternative: Of what was this water a sign?
Of what was this water a symbol?

Questions.Q: What do you think happens when someone is baptized?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In ordinary language the Greek verb baptizô (and related words) had both literal and figurative uses. The literal sense of baptizô was "to plunge or drench or immerse something", usually in water. In religious contexts, however, it came to have two more specific senses:
Questions.Note: (a) to wash someone or something in or with water to make him or it ceremonially clean

(b) to wash someone in or with water as part of their initiation into the religious community. When a person is baptized he is showing publicly his commitment to and union with Jesus Christ. (See "baptize, baptism" in KBT.)

Questions.Q: Peter told them that baptism saves them. What did he mean by that?
Questions.A: When believers are baptized, it is not the baptismal water that makes them clean before God and acceptable to him, but it is a sign to God that they are making an appeal to him for or from a clear conscience through [their faith in] the resurrection of Jesus Christ. (21)

Questions.Q: What else does baptism symbolize?
Questions.A: It symbolizes Jesus Christ [dying and] rising from the dead to save them. (21)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to save you?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that a person will rescue someone else from/out of a dangerous situation. In this case Jesus came to mankind to rescue them from an eternity in Hell.
Questions.Note: See "save" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus Christ do after he rose from the dead?
Questions.A: He went back to heaven and is now at the right side of God. (22)

Questions.Q: What is he doing there?
Questions.A: He is ruling over all angels and authorities. (22)

Section.heading: 1 Peter 4:1-11 Since Christ suffered physically, all believers/Christians should be prepared to suffer for doing the will of God. By enduring physical suffering as Christ did, believers/Christians are given the ability to live lives that are free from the power of sin.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what Peter said in these verses.
Questions.A: All believers should follow the example that Christ gave in overcoming suffering to do the will of God. This will give them the ability to live a life that is free from sin. (1-2)

Questions.Q: In order to face/endure suffering, what should they do?
Questions.A: They should prepare/strengthen themselves to endure/overcome suffering, just as Christ endured/overcame his sufferings. (1)
Questions.Alternative: In order to face suffering, what should they do?
In order to endure suffering, what should they do?

Questions.Q: If they [patiently] endure physical sufferings, of what can they be sure?
Questions.A: They can be sure that they do not have to habitually sin. (1)
Questions.Alternative: If they patiently endure physical sufferings, of what can they be sure?
If they endure physical sufferings, of what can they be sure?

Questions.Q: Instead of living to do bad things, what should they do?
Questions.A: They should strive to do what God wants them to do. (2)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that it is necessary for them to live a different/new/changed life style?
Questions.A: In the past they sinned like the heathens/unbelievers do. (3)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that it is necessary for them to live a different life style?
What is the reason that it is necessary for them to live a new life style?
What is the reason that it is necessary for them to live a changed life style?

Questions.Q: What sort of things did they used to do?
Questions.A: They spent their time in indecency, lust, drunkenness, orgies, drinking parties and the disgusting worship of idols. (3)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to worship an idol?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that a person gives respect and devotion to a physical object as a god. The idol can be a representation or symbol of a deity or any other being or thing made or used as an idol of worship. (See "idol" in KBT in the "God" entry.)

Questions.Q: Now that they have stopped doing as the heathens/unbelievers do, what did the heathens/unbelievers think of them?
Questions.A: The heathens/unbelievers were amazed/surprised that they no longer participated with them in these activities. (4)
Questions.Alternative: Now that they have stopped doing as the heathens do, what did the heathens think of them?
Now that they have stopped doing as the heathens do, what did the unbelievers think of them?
Now that they have stopped doing as the unbelievers do, what did the heathens think of them?
Now that they have stopped doing as the unbelievers do, what did the unbelievers think of them?

Questions.Q: How did the heathens treat them because of this?
Questions.A: They abused/insulted them. (4)

Questions.Q: What will the heathens have to do because of all the bad deeds they have done?
Questions.A: They will have to tell [God]/give an account to [God] of all their bad deeds. (5)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they will have to do this?
Questions.A: [God] is prepared to judge those who are living and those who are dead. (5)

Questions.Q: What was the purpose that [Christ] preached the gospel to those who are now dead?
Questions.A: [He] preached the gospel to them so that even though they died, they might live with God [by receiving and believing the gospel]. (6)
Questions.Note: The UBS favors using "Christ" as the subject "who preached the gospel".
Questions.Alternative: What was the purpose that Christ preached the gospel to those who are now dead?
What was the purpose that preached the gospel to those who are now dead?

Questions.Q: What did Peter tell them to do, since they were living in the last days?
Questions.A: They should be self-controlled and alert, so that they could pray. (7)

Questions.Q: What was the most important thing that they should do?
Questions.A: They should love one another very much. (8)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they should love one another?
Questions.A: When they love one another, they will be ready/willing to forgive/overlook the sins of one another. (8)

Questions.Q: How were they supposed to welcome others into their homes?
Questions.A: They were supposed to do it without grumbling/complaining. (9)

Questions.Q: How were they supposed to use the abilities that [God] had given to them?
Questions.A: They were supposed to use them to help others. (10)
Questions.Alternative: How were they supposed to use the abilities that God had given to them?
How were they supposed to use the abilities that had been given to them?
How were they supposed to use the abilities they had received?
How were they supposed to use the gifts that God had given to them?
How were they supposed to use the gifts that had been given to them?
How were they supposed to use the gifts they had received?

Questions.Q: What should a person do if God has given him the ability/gift to preach?
Questions.A: He must preach God's messages/word. (11)
Questions.Alternative: What should a person do if God has given him the ability to preach?
What should a person do if God has given him the gift to preach?

Questions.Q: What should a person do if God has given him the ability/gift to help others/of helping others?
Questions.A: He must help others with all the strength that God gives him. (11)
Questions.Alternative: What should a person do if God has given him the ability to help others?
What should a person do if God has given him the ability of helping others?
What should a person do if God has given him the gift to help others?
What should a person do if God has given him the gift of helping others?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Peter gave them this advice?
Questions.A: He told them those things so that everyone will praise God. (11)

Questions.Q: Whom should we always praise?
Questions.A: Jesus Christ. (11)
Questions.Note: UBS states "to him" immediately follows Jesus Christ and most likely refers to him and not to God.

Section.heading: 1 Peter 4:12-19 Believers/Christians will suffer as Christ suffered. They should not be surprised that they are facing physical suffering. They should be glad, because it means that they suffer as Christ suffered.

Questions.Q: About what did Peter tell them not to be surprised?
Questions.A: They should not be surprised that they were suffering. (12)

Questions.Q: What should they do/their attitude be, when these things happen/come?
Questions.A: They should rejoice/be glad that they are suffering as Christ suffered. (13)
Questions.Alternative: What should they do when these things happen?
What should they do when these things come?
What should their attitude be when these things happen?
What should their attitude be when these things come?

Questions.Q: If they rejoice when they suffer as Christ suffered, how will they feel, when people see how wonderful Christ is?
Questions.A: They will be very happy. (13)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they should feel blessed/happy, when people insult them because they are followers of Christ?
Questions.A: This means that the Spirit of God abides with them. (14)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that they should feel blessed, when people insult them because they are followers of Christ?
What is the reason that they should feel happy, when people insult them because they are followers of Christ?

Questions.Q: Of what must any of them be careful in regard to suffering?
Questions.A: Each of them must be sure that the reason he is suffering is not because he is a murderer, or a thief, or a criminal, or a meddler in other people's affairs. (15)

Questions.Q: However, if they suffer because they are Christians, what should they do and not do?
Questions.A: They should not be ashamed of being Christians.
They should praise God because they belong to Christ. (16)

Questions.Q: What do you think a Christian is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A Christian is someone who belongs to Christ.
Questions.Note: This term occurs only three times in the New Testament and was originally used by outsiders as a name for the followers of Christ. (See "Christian" in KBT in the "disciple" entry.)
Questions.Alternative: What do you think a christian is?

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason for a person or place to have a name?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A name is a label which identifies a person or place.
Questions.Note: See "name" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What time has arrived for something to happen?
Questions.A: The time has come for [God] to start judging his own people. (17)

Questions.Q: What did Peter say about those who do not believe the Good News/gospel from him?
Questions.A: They will be punished by [God]. (17)
Questions.Alternative: What did Peter say about those who do not believe the Good News from him?
What did Peter say about those who do not believe the gospel from him?

Questions.Q: What did he ask them?
Questions.A: If it is hard for the righteous to be saved [by God]/If there will be difficulties for good people before they are saved [by God], what will become of the ungodly and the sinner? (18)

Questions.Q: What should those who suffer according to God's will do?
Questions.A: They should continue to do good and entrust themselves into the care of [God]. (19)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when someone is faithful?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that they are worthy of being believed/trusted by someone else. They are trustworthy, reliable. (See "faithful" in KBT in the "believe" entry.)

Section.heading: 1 Peter 5:1-11 Peter encouraged the elders to take good care of the believers in their churches. He told the younger church members to be submissive to those members that were older.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what Peter said in these verses.
Questions.A: Peter told the elders/church leaders the way in which they were to rule over their people and care for them. (2-3)

Questions.Q: To whom did Peter give some advice?
Questions.A: He gave advice to the elders/leaders [of the believers]. (1)

Questions.Q: What do you think an elder is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: An elder is a leader of the Christian believers.

Questions.Q: What right did Peter have to give advice/make an appeal to these elders?
Questions.A: He was an elder. (1)
He was a witness of Christ's sufferings. (1)
He will see how wonderful Christ is, along with other believers. (1)
Questions.Alternative: What right did Peter have to give advice to these elders?
What right did Peter have to make an appeal to these elders?

Questions.Q: What did Peter tell the elders that they should do?
Questions.A: They should be shepherds/take care of the believers that God has entrusted to them. (2)

Questions.Q: In what manner should they do this work?
Questions.A: They should do it willingly. (2)

Questions.Q: Instead of doing this work for money, how were they to do this work?
Questions.A: They were to do it eagerly from a real desire to serve the believers. (2)

Questions.Q: Instead of placing themselves above those of whom they were in charge, what should these elders do?
Questions.A: They should be examples to those whom they served. (3)

Questions.Q: If these elders followed/obeyed Peter's advice, what will happen when [Christ], who is the Chief Shepherd, appears?
Questions.A: He will reward them. (4)
Questions.Alternative: If these elders followed Peter's advice, what will happen when the Chief Shepherd appears?
If these elders followed Peter's advice, what will happen when Christ, who is the Chief Shepherd, appears?
If these elders followed Peter's advice, what will happen when Christ appears?
If these elders obeyed Peter's advice, what will happen when the Chief Shepherd appears?
If these elders obeyed Peter's advice, what will happen when Christ, who is the Chief Shepherd, appears?
If these elders obeyed Peter's advice, what will happen when Christ appears?

Questions.Q: What must the younger men do?
Questions.A: They must submit themselves to the older men. (5)

Questions.Q: What should all of them do in their relationship to each other?
Questions.A: They should humble themselves and serve one another. (5)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they should follow this command?
Questions.A: God opposes/resists the proud, but God helps the humble. (5)

Questions.Q: In view of the fact that God resists the proud, but shows favor to the humble, what should they do?
Questions.A: They should humble themselves before God. (6)

Questions.Q: If they do humble themselves before God, what will he do to/for them?
Questions.A: He will exalt/honor them when he desires to honor them. (6)
Questions.Alternative: If they do humble themselves before God, what will he do to them?
If they do humble themselves before God, what will he do for them?

Questions.Q: What are they supposed to do with their worries/concerns/cares/problems?
Questions.A: They should cast/tell/commit them to him/[God]. (7)
Questions.Alternative: What are they supposed to do with their worries?
What are they supposed to do with their concerns?
What are they supposed to do with their cares?
What are they supposed to do with their problems?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they should cast/commit their cares to him?
Questions.A: He cares/is concerned for them. (7)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that they should cast their cares on him?
What is the reason that they should commit their cares to him?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that it is important for them to be alert and on their guard?
Questions.A: It is because their enemy, the Devil, is going around like a roaring lion seeking/looking for someone to destroy. (8)

Questions.Q: What do you know about the Devil?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "Devil" is the Greek equivalent of the Hebrew "Satan." Satan is the chief enemy of God. He is the supreme evil spiritual being who leads and directs all other evil spiritual beings. (See "Devil" in KBT in the "Satan" entry.)

Questions.Q: In order to win over/in their fight with the Devil, what should they do?
Questions.A: They should keep on trusting God. They must not obey the Devil. (9)
Questions.Alternative: In order to win over the Devil, what should they do?
In order to win in their fight with the Devil, what should they do?

Questions.Q: Who else besides the Christians to whom Peter wrote were suffering for their faith?
Questions.A: Their fellow believers throughout the world were also suffering as they were suffering. (9)

Questions.Q: Why do you think that Peter told them this fact?
Questions.A: He told them that in order to give them another reason to trust God more and not to obey the Devil. (9)

Questions.Q: In the midst of all these sufferings, who (is the one who) helps them?
Questions.A: God is the one who helps them. (10)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that God called/chose them?
Questions.A: He has called them to share his eternal glory in union with Christ. (10)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that God called them?
What is the reason that God chose them?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for something to be eternal?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that it will last forever/it will never end.

Questions.Q: What will happen to them after they have suffered a little while?
Questions.A: God will help them to trust him completely and God will encourage them. (10)

Questions.Q: How did Peter express his gratitude for all of God's help on their behalf?
Questions.A: He said that all power belonged to him forever. (11)

Section.heading: 1 Peter 5:12-14 Peter sent his final greetings to the Christians.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what Peter said in these verses.
Questions.A: Peter greeted those to whom he was writing. (13)

Questions.Q: Who helped Peter write this letter?
Questions.A: Silas helped him. (12)

Questions.Q: How did Peter regard Silas?
Questions.A: He considered him to be a [Christian] brother whom he could trust. (12)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Peter wrote this letter?
Questions.A: He wrote it in order to encourage those to whom he wrote,
and to let them know about how God truly wanted to help them. (12)

Questions.Q: What did he exhort them to do about this help from God?
Questions.A: He told them to remember that. (12)

Questions.Q: Who else sent greetings to those to whom he wrote?
Questions.A: The believers in Babylon and Mark sent their greetings. (13)

Questions.Q: How did Peter tell those believers that they should greet one another?
Questions.A: They were to greet one another with the kiss of [Christian] love. (14)

Questions.Q: What did Peter wish for all those who belong to Christ?
Questions.A: He wanted them all to live peacefully. (14)

Questions.Q: Retell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: He sends greetings to the believers in the city of Thessalonica.

Questions.Q: Who wrote this letter?
Questions.A: Paul did. Silas and Timothy were not co-authors, but merely joined in the greeting.

Questions.Q: To whom was this letter written?
Questions.A: To the congregation/group of God's people in the city of Thessalonica.

Questions.Q: What does Paul want God to do for them?
Questions.A: He wants God to bless them.

Questions.Q: Retell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: He thanks God for them and prays for them.
He knows God has chosen them to be his people.

Questions.Q: What does Paul always say in his prayers?
Questions.A: He thanks God for the Thessalonian believers.

Questions.Q: What does Paul remember about them when he is praying for them?
Questions.A: The way they put their faith into practice.
Because they loved people they worked hard for them.
They steadfastly hope for/look forward to what the Lord Jesus Christ has for them.

Questions.Q: What does Paul tell the believers?
Questions.A: That God loves them.

Questions.Q: What has God done for them?
Questions.A: He has chosen them to be his own people.

Questions.Q: How did Paul know that God had chosen the Thessalonians?
Questions.A: The Holy Spirit gave Paul special power when he told them the message.
The Holy Spirit gave Paul assurance that the message was true.

Questions.Q: Paul taught them God's message. How else was he a help to them while he lived among them?
Questions.A: His way of life/conduct also helped them believe God's message.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: The believers patterned their lives after Paul's and the Lord's.
They accepted God's message with joy.
They became examples to believers in other places.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say about the Thessalonians in this verse?
Questions.A: They received God's message.

Questions.Q: How did they receive it?
Questions.A: With much joy.

Questions.Q: In what way does Paul say they imitated him and the Lord?
Questions.A: By enduring suffering. (Or, by enduring suffering with joy).

Questions.Q: Because they received the message in that way, what happened?
Questions.A: They became an example to believers in other places.

Questions.Q: To whom did they become an example?
Questions.A: To all the believers in the provinces of Macedonia and Achaia.

Questions.Q: What else does Paul say about the Thessalonian believers?
Questions.A: They told people God's message.

Questions.Q: What happened because of that?
Questions.A: People living in far places heard about their faith in God.

Questions.Q: What do people in other places say about the Thessalonians?
Questions.A: They talk about how the Thessalonians welcomed Paul.
They talk about how the Thessalonians turned from worshiping idols to worshiping the true God.

Questions.Q: What does Paul tell them about God's Son?
Questions.A: God raised him from death.
God's Son will rescue them from God's anger/punishment for sin.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul reminds the Thessalonians of his former visit with them.
On that visit God gave him courage to tell God's message.
He spoke only as God wanted him to.
He showed his love for the Thessalonians.

Questions.Q: What was Paul's opinion of his former visit among the Thessalonians?
Questions.A: It was not a failure.

Questions.Q: What had happened to Paul before he arrived in Thessalonica?
Questions.A: He had been mistreated and insulted at Philippi.

Questions.Q: Did the Thessalonians know about that?
Questions.A: Yes.

Questions.Q: When Paul arrived at Thessalonica, what did God help him to do?
Questions.A: To tell God's message, even though there was much opposition.

Questions.Q: How was Paul able to do that?
Questions.A: God gave him courage.

Questions.Q: What are the reasons Paul gives that they can trust his message?
Questions.A: He did not teach error.
He did not have impure motives.
He did not try to trick anyone.

Questions.Q: Paul gives another good reason why they can trust his message. What is it?
Questions.A: He spoke only as God wanted him to speak.

Questions.Q: Why does it not bother Paul if people criticize his work?
Questions.A: He is not trying to please men, but God.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say about his speech when he was with the Thessalonians?
Questions.A: His talk/words were sincere.

Questions.Q: The Thessalonians know he spoke that way. Who else does he say is witness to the way he spoke?
Questions.A: God himself.

Questions.Q: Did Paul have a right to make demands on them or on others?
Questions.A: Yes.

Questions.Q: For what reason did he have that right?
Questions.A: He was an apostle of Christ.

Questions.Q: What kind of demands do you think Paul might have made as an apostle of Jesus Christ?
Questions.A: To be taken care of; to have housing, meals; to be given money, special attention, special treatment, etc.

Questions.Q: Did Paul make any such demands on them?
Questions.A: No.

Questions.Q: What was his attitude as he taught them?
Questions.A: Affectionate, as a mother would care for her children.

Questions.Q: What had Paul come to do for them?
Questions.A: Teach them the gospel.

Questions.Q: What else was he willing to do?
Questions.A: Share himself/give his life for them.

Questions.Q: Why was he willing to do that?
Questions.A: He loved them very much.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: He reminds them that his conduct among them was above reproach.

Questions.Q: How did Paul work while he lived among them?
Questions.A: He worked very hard; many hours.

Questions.Q: What was the reason he did that?
Questions.A: So that he would not be a (financial) burden to them.

Questions.Q: How does Paul describe his conduct while he lived among them?
Questions.A: It was holy, righteous, without fault.

Questions.Q: Who were witnesses to this?
Questions.A: The Thessalonians and God.

Questions.Q: Why do you think Paul says that both the Thessalonian believers and God were witness to his good behavior?
Questions.A: To show that not only was his life pure and consistent outwardly, but also that his inward motives were right; only God could see that.

Questions.Q: How does Paul describe his attitude towards them?
Questions.A: He compares it to the attitude of a father to his children.

Questions.Q: In what way did Paul act like a father to the Thessalonians?
Questions.A: He encouraged them and urged them to keep on living the kind of life that is appropriate for God's people.

Questions.Q: What does God want for the Thessalonian believers?
Questions.A: That they share in his kingdom and in his glory.

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to share in God's kingdom and glory?
Questions.A: To be ruled by God, who is a just ruler; to experience his greatness and majesty and beauty, etc.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul thanks God that they believed the message he taught them was really from God.

Questions.Q: For what is Paul giving thanks to God here?
Questions.A: Because the Thessalonians recognized that what Paul was telling them was from God.

Questions.Q: How were they able to do that?
Questions.A: God directed their thinking so that they recognized the message as God's truth.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul compares the suffering of the Thessalonian believers to that which the Judean believers endured.

Questions.Q: To whom does Paul compare the Thessalonian believers?
Questions.A: The believers in Judea.

Questions.Q: In what way are the Thessalonian believers like the Judean believers?
Questions.A: The Thessalonians were persecuted by their countrymen; the Judeans were persecuted also by their countrymen--the Jews.

Questions.Q: In what way do you think they may have suffered?
Questions.A: Slander, imprisonment, verbal and physical abuse, destruction of property, etc.

Questions.Q: What are some of the bad things that the Jews had done?
Questions.A: They killed the Lord Jesus.
They also killed the prophets.
They persecuted Paul and his companions.

Questions.Q: What is God's reaction to such actions?
Questions.A: He is displeased.

Questions.Q: What else have the Jews done?
Questions.A: They tried to stop Paul from telling God's message to the Gentiles.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say is his purpose in telling the Gentiles God's message?
Questions.A: So that they will be saved.

Questions.Q: What will happen to the Jews for all the bad things they have done?
Questions.A: God will punish them/judge them.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul longs to see the Thessalonians, and has tried very hard to visit them.

Questions.Q: How did Paul feel while he was separated from the Thessalonians?
Questions.A: He missed them very much.

Questions.Q: What did Paul try very hard to do?
Questions.A: To visit the Thessalonians.

Questions.Q: Why was Paul not able to visit them again?
Questions.A: Satan hindered him.

Questions.Q: How do you think Satan hindered him?
Questions.A: Perhaps by unfavorable circumstances, unrest, danger, no money, etc.

Questions.Q: What evidence of his achievement will Paul present to the Lord Jesus when he comes?
Questions.A: The Thessalonian believers.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the reason Paul can be happy before the Lord about his work with the Thessalonian believers?
Questions.A: The Thessalonians believed the word of God that Paul taught them.
They stood firm in their faith even though they were persecuted.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul sent Timothy to the Thessalonians to help them believe firmly in God.

Questions.Q: When the separation from the Thessalonian believers continued, how did Paul feel?
Questions.A: Worried, anxious.

Questions.Q: What did he decide to do?
Questions.A: To send Timothy to them.

Questions.Q: What did he hope Timothy would do for them?
Questions.A: Help them believe firmly in Christ so that they would not turn back when people persecuted them.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say about Timothy?
Questions.A: He is their fellow believer.
He is Paul's companion in preaching the gospel.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say about afflictions/persecutions?
Questions.A: Persecutions are inevitable for believers.
Questions.Alternative: What does Paul say about afflictions?
What does Paul say about persecutions?

Questions.Q: Was this the first time the Thessalonians had heard this?
Questions.A: No. Paul had told them this before.

Questions.Q: What did Paul want to learn about the Thessalonians?
Questions.A: If they were still firmly believing in God.

Questions.Q: What was Paul afraid might have happened to the Thessalonians?
Questions.A: That Satan might have tempted them to stop believing in Christ.

Questions.Q: If so, how would Paul feel?
Questions.A: That all his work for them had been for nothing.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: The report Timothy brought back from the Thessalonians encouraged Paul.

Questions.Q: When Timothy arrived back from the Thessalonians, what did he tell Paul?
Questions.A: That the believers were continuing to believe firmly in Christ.
That the believers were continuing to love one another.

Questions.Q: What else did Timothy tell Paul?
Questions.A: That the Thessalonians wanted to see Paul very much.

Questions.Q: How did Paul feel when he heard Timothy's report?
Questions.A: He was encouraged.

Questions.Q: What makes Paul really joyful, and encourages him to keep on in his ministry?
Questions.A: To learn that the Thessalonians are continuing to believe firmly in Christ.

Questions.Q: For what does Paul thank God?
Questions.A: For the great joy the Thessalonian believers give him.

Questions.Q: What does Paul specifically pray for?
Questions.A: That he would see them in person.

Questions.Q: Why does he want to see them again?
Questions.A: In order to teach them what they still do not know about what they should believe.

Questions.Q: What do you think they still might not know?
Questions.A: Perhaps they might still not know how to recognize what is right and what is wrong; they might not understand how much God loves them, how very wise he is, etc.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul prays that God will make it possible for him to visit the Thessalonians.
Paul prays that God will cause the Thessalonians to love people more and more.

Questions.Q: To whom does Paul direct his prayer in this verse?
Questions.A: To God the Father, and to the Lord Jesus.

Questions.Q: What is Paul's request?
Questions.A: That he will be able to visit the Thessalonians.

Questions.Q: What does Paul want God to do for the Thessalonians?
Questions.A: Cause them to love one another more and more.

Questions.Q: What will be the result if they do that?
Questions.A: God will make their inner life strong.
They will be without fault when they stand in the presence of God.

Questions.Q: When will they stand in the presence of God?
Questions.A: When the Lord Jesus comes again.

Questions.Q: When the Lord Jesus comes again, who will be with him?
Questions.A: All who belong to him.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: They are to please God by keeping themselves morally pure.

Questions.Q: What had the Thessalonians previously learned from Paul?
Questions.A: How they should live in order to please God.

Questions.Q: What does Paul want them to do now?
Questions.A: To do even more to please God.

Questions.Q: How does Paul let them know it is very important for them to do that?
Questions.A: He begs and urges them to do it.

Questions.Q: What is God's will for the Thessalonians?
Questions.A: He wants them to be holy/pure.

Questions.Q: If they are to be holy/pure, what must they avoid?
Questions.A: Sexual immorality.
Questions.Alternative: If they are to be holy, what must they avoid?
If they are to be pure, what must they avoid?

Questions.Q: In what specific relationship does Paul say they are to be holy/pure?
Questions.A: In their marriage relationship.
Questions.Alternative: In what specific relationship does Paul say they are to be holy?
In what specific relationship does Paul say they are to be pure?

Questions.Q: What people follow their lustful desires within their marriage relationship?
Questions.A: The heathen who do not know God.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say is another reason they should keep themselves morally pure?
Questions.A: In order to avoid sinning against a fellow believer.

Questions.Q: What will happen if they disobey in these matters?
Questions.A: The Lord will punish those who disobey.

Questions.Q: Why is it a serious matter to reject what Paul is teaching about these matters?
Questions.A: Because it is God who has called them to a holy/pure life; if they disobey they are disobeying God, not Paul.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: They should behave in such a way that they win the respect of unbelievers.

Questions.Q: Concerning their conduct toward others, what is the first thing Paul tells them?
Questions.A: They are to continue loving people.

Questions.Q: Who has taught them that they should love people?
Questions.A: God

Questions.Q: Paul commends them for loving people. But what does he urge them to do?
Questions.A: To love people more and more.

Questions.Q: What does Paul instruct them to do in these verses?
Questions.A: To live quiet lives.
To mind their own affairs.
To earn their own living.

Questions.Q: Why should they conduct their lives in this way?
Questions.A: They will win the respect of unbelievers.
They will not be dependent on anyone for what they need.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: They should encourage one another by talking about the time when Jesus will come back to earth.

Questions.Q: What is Paul writing to them about here?
Questions.A: About people who have already died.

Questions.Q: Why is he writing about that?
Questions.A: He wants them to know the truth about those who have died.
He does not want them to grieve over them like the heathen grieve over those who have died.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say they all believe?
Questions.A: That Jesus died and then rose again.

Questions.Q: What will happen to the believers who have already died when Jesus returns?
Questions.A: They will be resurrected and will return with Jesus.

Questions.Q: What will happen to those who are still alive when Jesus returns?
Questions.A: They will also meet the Lord, but will follow the dead.

Questions.Q: How can they be sure that what Paul teaches is true?
Questions.A: What he is teaching them is the word of the Lord.

Questions.Q: When the time comes for Jesus to descend from heaven, what will announce his coming?
Questions.A: People will hear a loud command.
The archangel will call.
A trumpet will sound.

Questions.Q: What will happen next?
Questions.A: Jesus will come down.
The believers who have already died will rise first.
Then the believers who are alive will go together with them to meet the Lord in the clouds.

Questions.Q: From that time on, where will all believers be?
Questions.A: With the Lord.

Questions.Q: Having told them those things, now what does Paul tell them?
Questions.A: They are to encourage/comfort one another by talking about those things.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: The believers should be watchful and alert as they wait for Jesus to return.

Questions.Q: What did the Thessalonians already know about when Jesus would return?
Questions.A: They knew that Jesus would return unexpectedly.

Questions.Q: What figure does Paul use to describe the Lord's return?
Questions.A: Like a thief who comes when people are sleeping.

Questions.Q: Will the unbelievers be expecting the Lord to return?
Questions.A: No.

Questions.Q: What will happen to them?
Questions.A: They will not be able to escape God's punishment.

Questions.Q: Why does Paul say the Lord's return should not take believers by surprise?
Questions.A: Because they are not like people in darkness who cannot see.

Questions.Q: What do you think "darkness" here means?
Questions.A: Darkness may illustrate sin and unbelief, or lack of knowledge.

Questions.Q: How does Paul describe the Thessalonian believers?
Questions.A: They all belong to the daytime.

Questions.Q: What do you think this means?
Questions.A: Daytime is characterized by light; light is an attribute of God; believers belong to God. Light is also figurative for knowledge.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say people do at night?
Questions.A: Either they sleep, or they carouse/get drunk.

Questions.Q: Since believers belong to the day, what are Paul's instructions to them?
Questions.A: They should be alert, like people who are sober.
They should be ready, waiting for the Lord to come back.

Questions.Q: What does Paul tell the believers to do in order to be ready for the Lord to come back?
Questions.A: As a soldier prepares himself by putting on a covering that will protect him, so also believers should have a covering. This covering is: to believe in God, to love other people, and to be sure of their salvation.

Questions.Q: How do you think these things protect believers?
Questions.A: They protect believers from committing sin, and from the doubts Satan would tempt them with in times of trouble/persecution.

Questions.Q: How does Paul say believers can be sure of their salvation?
Questions.A: Paul tells them that God determined/decreed that he would save them by having the Lord Jesus Christ die for them.

Questions.Q: Now what does Paul instruct the believers to do?
Questions.A: To continue to encourage one another.
To continue to help/strengthen one another.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul says they are to respect their teachers/leaders in the church.

Questions.Q: Paul urges them to respect their leaders. Who has given these leaders their authority?
Questions.A: The Lord.

Questions.Q: Why does Paul say they should love and respect their leaders?
Questions.A: Because of the work their leaders do.

Questions.Q: What else does Paul urge the believers to do?
Questions.A: To live in harmony with one another.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul tells them how they can do good to various people.

Questions.Q: What instructions does Paul give the Thessalonians in this verse?
Questions.A: Rebuke the idle.
Encourage the timid ones.
Help the weak ones.
Be patient with all people.

Questions.Q: Why do you think he said to rebuke the people who are idle?
Questions.A: Laziness is not pleasing to God.

Questions.Q: When someone wrongs them what should they do?
Questions.A: They should not retaliate.

Questions.Q: What should they do instead?
Questions.A: They should do good to that one.

Questions.Q: What should believers always aim to do?
Questions.A: Do good to everyone.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: They are to cultivate spiritual attitudes that please God.

Questions.Q: What does Paul instruct the believers to do in these verses?
Questions.A: To be joyful.
To pray to God.
To thank God in all circumstances.

Questions.Q: Why is it important for them to do this?
Questions.A: Because this is God's will for them.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: They are not to stifle the Holy Spirit.
They are to accept what they have tested and found to be good.

Questions.Q: What does Paul tell them not to do?
Questions.A: They are not to quench/stifle the Holy Spirit.

Questions.Q: How could they do that?
Questions.A: By rejecting messages from God given by his servants.

Questions.Q: Instead of rejecting the messages from God given by his servants, what does Paul say they are to do?
Questions.A: They are to put everything to the test, and then accept the good.

Questions.Q: How do you think they could test things?
Questions.A: They could ask themselves if it followed the teachings of God's word.

Questions.Q: If they have tested something and found it is good, what does Paul say they are to do?
Questions.A: They are to accept it; continue doing it.

Questions.Q: If they have found that it is not good, what are they to do?
Questions.A: Reject it; do not do it.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: His prayer for the Thessalonian believers is that they will be without fault when the Lord Jesus Christ comes back.

Questions.Q: How does Paul describe God in this verse?
Questions.A: As the God who gives inner peace.

Questions.Q: What is Paul's prayer/wish for the Thessalonians?
Questions.A: That God would make them completely holy.
That their whole being would be without fault when the Lord Jesus comes back.
Questions.Alternative: What is Paul's prayer for the Thessalonians?
What is Paul's wish for the Thessalonians?

Questions.Q: Does Paul believe his prayer will be answered?
Questions.A: Yes.

Questions.Q: How do you know?
Questions.A: Paul knows his prayer will be answered because God is faithful; he will do it.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul concludes his letter with greetings, requests, and a blessing.

Questions.Q: What does Paul ask the Thessalonians to do for him?
Questions.A: To pray for him.
To give his greetings to all the believers.

Questions.Q: What does Paul instruct them to do with this letter he is writing to them?
Questions.A: He instructs them to read the letter to all the believers.

Questions.Q: Does Paul consider it very important that they obey this?
Questions.A: Yes.

Questions.Q: How do you know?
Questions.A: He commands them, in the authority the Lord has given him, to do it.

Questions.Q: How does Paul close his letter?
Questions.A: With a prayer/wish that the Lord will bless them all.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul is writing a letter to Timothy.

Questions.Q: Who is writing this letter?
Questions.A: Paul

Questions.Q: What does Paul say about himself?
Questions.A: He is Jesus Christ's representative/apostle.

Questions.Q: How did Paul become an apostle?
Questions.A: God and Christ Jesus commanded that he have this office.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say about God?
Questions.A: He is the one who has saved them.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say about Christ?
Questions.A: He is the one who will bring about all God has promised.

Questions.Q: To whom is Paul writing?
Questions.A: Timothy

Questions.Q: How does Paul refer to Timothy?
Questions.A: As his true child in the faith.

Questions.Q: What do you think Paul means by that?
Questions.A: Just as a true father gives life to his son, so also Paul helped Timothy to receive eternal/spiritual life by believing in Christ.

Questions.Q: What does Paul want God and Christ Jesus to do for Timothy?
Questions.A: To bless him.
To be merciful to him.
To give him peace.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Timothy is to command certain people not to teach false doctrines.
Timothy is to command these people also not to be always thinking about stories and genealogies.

Questions.Q: Why had Paul previously urged Timothy to stay in Ephesus?
Questions.A: So that he could tell certain people who lived there some things.

Questions.Q: What did Paul want Timothy to tell/command these people?
Questions.A: They were not to teach lies to people.
They were not to waste their time by always thinking about stories and genealogies.
Questions.Alternative: What did Paul want Timothy to tell these people?
What did Paul want Timothy to command these people?

Questions.Q: Why did Paul say these people should not always think about/discuss these things?
Questions.A: They lead to questions, and arguments.
They are no help to them spiritually.
Questions.Alternative: Why did Paul say these people should not always think about these things?
Why did Paul say these people should not always discuss these things?

Questions.Q: What does Paul say will happen if these people listen to Timothy?
Questions.A: They will love people.

Questions.Q: But in order to love people, what does Paul say they must first be sure they are doing?
Questions.A: Have good motives for what they do.
Do only what they know they should do.
Sincerely believe the true teachings.

Questions.Q: Some of the people left the true teachings. What has happened to them?
Questions.A: They are wasting their time with useless discussions.

Questions.Q: Since these people are discussing these matters so much, what does it appear they want?
Questions.A: To be known as teachers of the Law.

Questions.Q: Does Paul say they are qualified to be teachers of the Law?
Questions.A: No.

Questions.Q: Why does he say they are not qualified?
Questions.A: Because they do not even understand the topic they are discussing.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: The Law is good if it is used correctly.

Questions.Q: Paul had just said that certain people in Ephesus were talking a lot about the Law, but did not really understand the purpose of the Law. What does he say about the Law in this verse?
Questions.A: The Law is good if it is used properly.

Questions.Q: What must a person know about the Law in order to use it properly?
Questions.A: God did not intend the Law to be used against good people; he intended it for people who do not obey what God has taught.

Questions.Q: Paul then gives a list of some of the bad things people do which makes them accountable to the Law. Give an example of each of them.
How does Paul describe the gospel?
Questions.A: It is glorious (or, from the glorious and blessed God).

Questions.Q: Who gave Paul the authority to teach this gospel?
Questions.A: God

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul is grateful to Christ Jesus for appointing him to serve him.

Questions.Q: For what does Paul give thanks to God?
Questions.A: Because Christ Jesus thought Paul was trustworthy enough to serve him.

Questions.Q: How was Paul able to serve God?
Questions.A: Christ Jesus gave him the strength to serve him.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say about his former conduct?
Questions.A: He used to say bad things about Jesus.
He used to persecute the Christians.
He used to behave in an insolent, insulting manner toward God.

Questions.Q: But what does Paul say happened to him?
Questions.A: God did not punish him even though he deserved it.
God helped him/favored him even though he did not deserve that help/favor.

Questions.Q: Why did the Lord not punish Paul?
Questions.A: Because Paul did not know he was doing anything wrong.

Questions.Q: Why did Paul not know he was doing wrong?
Questions.A: Because at that time Paul had not yet believed in Christ Jesus.

Questions.Q: Because the Lord so greatly favored him, what changes took place in Paul?
Questions.A: He believed in Christ Jesus.
He loved people (or, he loved Christ).

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: The fact that Christ Jesus showed mercy to Paul, the worst of sinners, is proof that he will surely show mercy to any sinner.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say is completely true?
Questions.A: That the reason Christ Jesus came into the world was so that he could save sinners.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say about himself?
Questions.A: He is the worst of all sinners/he has done the greatest kind of evil.

Questions.Q: Why did Christ Jesus not punish Paul?
Questions.A: So that people would see that he is very patient.

Questions.Q: In order for sinners to receive mercy from Christ Jesus, what must they first do?
Questions.A: Believe in Christ.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: God is King.

Questions.Q: Who does Paul say is King?
Questions.A: God

Questions.Q: What does Paul say about the King?
Questions.A: The King rules over people forever.
The King cannot die.
No one can see the King.
He is the only true God.
All people should praise and adore the King forever.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul encourages Timothy to believe he is capable of doing what Paul is telling him to do.

Questions.Q: What is the urgent command Paul is giving to Timothy?
Questions.A: He is to reprove those who are teaching a false doctrine (1:3).

Questions.Q: How does Paul encourage Timothy to do this?
Questions.A: Paul reminds Timothy that people previously prophesied that Timothy would do the things Paul is telling him to do.

Questions.Q: What does Paul tell Timothy to be sure to continue to do?
Questions.A: Continue to believe the true teachings.
Continue to do only what he knows God wants him to do.

Questions.Q: What happened to some people who did not continue to do what they knew God wanted them to do?
Questions.A: They believed lies.
They stopped believing in Jesus Christ.

Questions.Q: Hymenaeus and Alexander were two leaders of the heretics in Ephesus. What did Paul say he had done to them?
Questions.A: Turned them over to Satan.

Questions.Q: Why did he do that?
Questions.A: So that they would learn not to speak evil about God.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul urges believers gathered in public worship to pray for everyone.
God wants all people to know the true message.
Paul was sent to tell people the true message.

Questions.Q: Paul is instructing Timothy how the congregation should conduct their worship of God. What is the first thing he urges them to do?
Questions.A: To pray for everyone.

Questions.Q: What should they pray?
Questions.A: They should ask God to help all people.
They should thank God for what he does for all people.

Questions.Q: In addition to telling them to pray for everyone, who does Paul say they should pray for especially?
Questions.A: For rulers and all others who are in authority.

Questions.Q: Why should they pray for these people?
Questions.A: So that everyone can live quietly and peacefully.

Questions.Q: If everyone can live quietly and peacefully, how will this affect believers?
Questions.A: They will be able to serve and worship God more freely.

Questions.Q: What is it that Paul says is good and pleases God?
Questions.A: It pleases God when believers pray for all people.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say about God?
Questions.A: He wants to save everyone.
He wants everyone to know the true teaching.

Questions.Q: What else does Paul say about God?
Questions.A: There is only one God.

Questions.Q: How can people come before God?
Questions.A: Only through a mediator.

Questions.Q: Who is that mediator?
Questions.A: Jesus Christ.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say about Jesus Christ?
Questions.A: He is a man.

Questions.Q: What did Jesus Christ do?
Questions.A: Died to pay the ransom for people's sins.

Questions.Q: Did Jesus Christ do this willingly?
Questions.A: Yes.

Questions.Q: How do you know?
Questions.A: He gave himself, as a sacrifice.

Questions.Q: For whom did Jesus Christ die?
Questions.A: For all people.
