Questions.Q: Since Christ died for all people, all people should know about it. Who is to tell them about it?
Questions.A: Paul is one who is to tell them.

Questions.Q: Who told Paul to preach this message?
To whom was Paul appointed to preach?
Questions.A: To the Gentiles/non-Jews/people of all nations.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul gives instruction about public worship to men and to women.

Questions.Q: Paul continues to talk about prayer. Who does he say should pray in public?
Questions.A: Men

Questions.Q: What does he say about men who pray?
Questions.A: They should be dedicated/committed to God.
They should not be angry.
They should not be quarrelsome.

Questions.Q: Paul also has instructions for women. How does he say that women should dress?
Questions.A: Modestly and sensibly.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say women should not do in order to make themselves beautiful?
Questions.A: They should not do their hair in fancy ways.
They should not adorn themselves with gold and jewels.
They should not wear expensive clothes.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say are fitting/proper ornaments for a godly woman?
Questions.A: Her good deeds.
Questions.Alternative: What does Paul say are fitting ornaments for a godly woman?
What does Paul say are proper ornaments for a godly woman?

Questions.Q: Paul has further instructions for women. About what does he tell them here?
Questions.A: How they should behave when they are learning.

Questions.Q: How should they behave?
Questions.A: They should be quiet.
They should be submissive to those who are teaching.

Questions.Q: What does Paul not permit in a public worship service?
Questions.A: He does not permit a woman to teach men.
He does not permit a woman to have authority over men.

Questions.Q: Paul has given instructions for women's behavior in a public worship service. What does he say are the reasons why women should behave in this way?
Questions.A: God made Adam first before he made Eve.
Satan deceived Eve but did not deceive Adam.

Questions.Q: What do you think Paul implies by these reasons?
Questions.A: Man has authority over woman.

Questions.Q: Because Satan deceived Eve, what happened?
Questions.A: Eve disobeyed God's commandment.

Questions.Q: Even though Eve disobeyed God, Paul says there is hope for women. What is it?
Questions.A: They will be saved from sin as they bear children.

Questions.Q: What else must they do?
Questions.A: Women must trust, believe what God says.
Women must love other people.
Women must be modest, discreet.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul tells Timothy that pastors must be men of very good character and behavior.

Questions.Q: Paul has been telling Timothy how people should behave in public worship. What does he now begin to tell Timothy about?
Questions.A: Pastors/church leaders.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say about the work of a pastor?
Questions.A: It is a good work.

Questions.Q: In order to be a pastor, how must a man live/conduct himself?
Questions.A: He must live in such a way that no one has reason to reproach/blame him for anything.
Questions.Alternative: In order to be a pastor, how must a man live?
In order to be a pastor, how must a man conduct himself?

Questions.Q: Why must a pastor be such a good person?
Questions.A: Because the work he does is honorable/noble (3:1).

Questions.Q: What specific things does Paul require of a pastor?
Questions.A: A pastor must have only one wife.
A pastor must be moderate/circumspect.
A pastor must be reasonable/orderly.
A pastor must act in a dignified/proper manner.
A pastor must be hospitable.
A pastor must be able to teach people well.
A pastor must not drink too much wine.
A pastor must not be belligerent/hostile but gentle.
A pastor must not be quarrelsome.
A pastor must not be greedy.
A pastor must manage his household well.
A pastor must not be a new convert/believer.
A pastor must live/conduct himself in such a way that non-believers speak well of him.

Questions.Q: Paul said a pastor must manage his household well. How must his children behave in order to show that he is doing that?
Questions.A: His children must obey him.
His children must respect him.

Questions.Q: Why is it necessary that a pastor manage his household well?
Questions.A: If a man does not manage his own house well, he will not manage God's house well either.

Questions.Q: Why should a recent convert/believer not be a pastor?
Questions.A: Because he might become conceited.
Questions.Alternative: Why should a recent convert not be a pastor?
Why should a recent believer not be a pastor?

Questions.Q: What will happen to a person who is conceited?
Questions.A: God will condemn a conceited person.

Questions.Q: Why do you think God will condemn a conceited person?
Questions.A: God condemned Satan because he was conceited. Therefore he will also condemn anyone else who is conceited.

Questions.Q: Why must a pastor conduct himself in such a manner that non-believers will speak well of him?
Questions.A: Because he will get a bad reputation if he does not conduct himself properly.

Questions.Q: What figure does Paul use to describe what has happened when a pastor gets a bad reputation?
Questions.A: He has fallen into a trap.

Questions.Q: Who has set the trap?
Questions.A: Satan

Questions.Q: Why do you think Satan set that trap?
Questions.A: He wants to destroy the character and influence of the pastor.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Deacons must also have a very good character and behavior.
Their wives must also have a good character.

Questions.Q: What specific things does Paul say about deacons?
Questions.A: A deacon must be respectable.
A deacon must be sincere.
A deacon must not drink too much wine.
A deacon must not be greedy.
A deacon must sincerely believe the true teaching.
A deacon must live in such a way that when people evaluate/examine his conduct they will not find anything wrong.
A deacon must have a wife who lives/conducts herself properly.
A deacon must have only one wife.
A deacon must manage his household well.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say about a deacon's wife?
Questions.A: A deacon's wife must have a good character.
A deacon's wife must not speak evil about other people.
A deacon's wife must be temperate/moderate.
A deacon's wife must be dependable in everything she does.

Questions.Q: If a deacon does his duties well, what will be the result?
Questions.A: People will respect him.
He will be able to speak confidently about Christ.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: It is very important that God's family know how they should live/conduct themselves because they make up God's household.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say he is hoping to do?
Questions.A: To come to see Timothy soon.

Questions.Q: Why then did he write this letter?
Questions.A: In case he could not come as soon as he wanted to, Timothy would have the instructions.

Questions.Q: What are these instructions?
Questions.A: Timothy is to tell people how they should behave in the household of which God is the head.

Questions.Q: What does he call the household of which God is the head?
Questions.A: The Church.

Questions.Q: What important work does the Church do?
Questions.A: It teaches and defends the truth.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say is certainly true?
Questions.A: That the things God has revealed concerning the believer's religion are very great/wonderful.

Questions.Q: About whom is Paul speaking in this verse?
Questions.A: About Christ.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say about him?
Questions.A: He appeared to man in a human body.
The Holy Spirit proved that he was righteous.
Angels saw him.
People preached about him in many places.
People in the world believed what he said.
God took him to heaven.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul tells Timothy that in later times some people will stop believing the true teachings. They will follow false teaching.

Questions.Q: What did the Holy Spirit say will happen in later times?
Questions.A: Some people will stop believing the true teaching.

Questions.Q: What will these people pay attention to instead?
Questions.A: They will pay attention to what is taught by evil spirits.

Questions.Q: What do these evil spirits do?
Questions.A: They deceive people.

Questions.Q: How will the evil spirits teach these lies?
Questions.A: They will use people who are hypocrites.
They will use people who tell lies.
They will use people who do not feel guilty about the evil things they do.

Questions.Q: What do these people teach?
Questions.A: They teach that people should not get married.
They teach that people should not eat certain foods.

Questions.Q: Why is it wrong to forbid people to eat certain foods?
Questions.A: Because God has created these foods to be eaten.

Questions.Q: In what manner/attitude are believers supposed to eat?
Questions.A: They are to be thankful when they eat.
Questions.Alternative: In what manner are believers supposed to eat?
In what attitude are believers supposed to eat?

Questions.Q: Do you think that all food which God has created is good?
Questions.A: Yes.

Questions.Q: How do we know?
Questions.A: Because everything which God has created is good.

Questions.Q: How should a believer receive all food?
Questions.A: He should receive it as from God.
He should thank God for it.

Questions.Q: Is God displeased with any food we eat?
Questions.A: No, all food is acceptable to God.

Questions.Q: How do we know all food is acceptable to God?
Questions.A: Because God says it is.
Because the believer prayed/thanked God for it.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul tells Timothy he is to teach the truth and to live a godly life.

Questions.Q: What does Paul tell Timothy to do?
Questions.A: Teach what Paul has just told him in verses 1-5.

Questions.Q: If he does, what will that indicate?
Questions.A: That he is a good servant of Jesus Christ.

Questions.Q: What must Timothy continue to do in order to be a good servant?
Questions.A: He must continue to remember and to follow the true teaching he has learned.

Questions.Q: What is Timothy not to do?
Questions.A: He is not to pay attention to useless stories.

Questions.Q: What should he do instead?
Questions.A: Train himself/practice living in a manner which will please God.

Questions.Q: What figure does Paul use here?
Questions.A: That of an athlete, training himself physically.

Questions.Q: Which is of greater value, to train as an athlete, or to train oneself to live in a manner which pleases God?
Questions.A: To train oneself to live in a manner which pleases God is of greater value.

Questions.Q: If a person lives in a manner which pleases God, what benefit will this be to him?
Questions.A: It will benefit him in this present life.
It will benefit him also in the life to come.

Questions.Q: How does Paul show that he considers what he has just said very important?
Questions.A: He states that what he has just said is a true saying, and is to be believed.

Questions.Q: For what do believers struggle and work hard?
Questions.A: To live lives that please God.

Questions.Q: Why do they struggle and work hard to live lives that please God?
Questions.A: Because they expect that God will benefit their lives.

Questions.Q: Why do believers believe that God will benefit their lives when they live in a manner that pleases God?
Questions.A: God is alive, and therefore able to do this.
God saves people, and therefore wants to do this.

Questions.Q: Who does God save?
Questions.A: Those who believe in him.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul tells Timothy he is to show the believers by example how they are to conduct themselves.

Questions.Q: Paul has been writing about how believers should live. What does he now tell Timothy to do?
Questions.A: To command and teach these things to others.

Questions.Q: What does Paul warn Timothy about?
Questions.A: The fact that some might not listen to him because he is young.

Questions.Q: What is Timothy not to do?
Questions.A: Not to let anyone think he is spiritually immature.

Questions.Q: How can Timothy prevent people from thinking he is spiritually immature?
Questions.A: By being an example to the believers.

Questions.Q: What does Paul tell Timothy to do in order to be a good example?
Questions.A: He should speak good things.
He should live/conduct himself properly.
He should love people.
He should trust God.
He should be morally pure.

Questions.Q: What does Paul tell Timothy to do in his public ministry?
Questions.A: Read the Scriptures to the people.
Tell the people how they should behave.
Teach the people the true teaching.

Questions.Q: What did Paul warn Timothy to be sure to do?
Questions.A: Do what God had given him special ability to do.

Questions.Q: How did Timothy know what ability God had given him?
Questions.A: The prophets told him.

Questions.Q: When did the prophets tell him/prophesy about him?
Questions.A: When the elders laid their hands on him.
Questions.Alternative: When did the prophets tell him?
When did the prophets prophesy about him?

Questions.Q: What does Paul exhort Timothy to do?
Questions.A: Earnestly do the things Paul has been talking about.

Questions.Q: Why should Timothy do these things?
Questions.A: So that people can see he is making progress/improving in his ability to do them.

Questions.Q: What is Timothy to make sure he does?
Questions.A: Conduct himself properly.
Teach the people well.

Questions.Q: Why should he do these things?
Questions.A: He will save himself.
He will save those he teaches.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul tells Timothy how he is to treat older men, younger men, older women, younger women.

Questions.Q: Paul tells Timothy how to treat people. What is the first thing he tells him?
Questions.A: Regarding older men, he is not to speak harshly with them.

Questions.Q: How instead is he to treat them?
Questions.A: As he would treat his father.

Questions.Q: How is he to treat younger men?
Questions.A: As he would treat his own brothers.

Questions.Q: With regard to women, how is he to treat older women?
Questions.A: As he would treat his mother.

Questions.Q: How is he to treat younger women?
Questions.A: As he would treat his sisters.

Questions.Q: In treating them as sisters, how will he behave towards them?
Questions.A: In a manner that is morally pure.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul tells Timothy that relatives are to care for their widows.

Questions.Q: Is the church responsible to care for all widows?
Questions.A: The church is to care for them only if they have no relatives/are all alone.

Questions.Q: Who are the first people who are responsible to care for a widow?
Questions.A: The widow's own children or grandchildren.

Questions.Q: Why do children and grandchildren have this responsibility?
Questions.A: By caring for her they are repaying her for all that she has done for them in the past.

Questions.Q: Why should children and grandchildren fulfill this responsibility?
Questions.A: Because it pleases God to have them do so.

Questions.Q: What does a widow do who is really in need and who has no one to care for her?
Questions.A: She confidently expects that God will look after her.
She continues to ask God to help her.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say about a widow who lives in a wasteful, luxurious manner?
Questions.A: Even though she is physically alive, she is spiritually dead.

Questions.Q: What does Paul tell Timothy here?
Questions.A: Timothy is to command that people look after their own relatives and family.

Questions.Q: Why should Timothy give these commands?
Questions.A: So that no one can reproach them.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say about a person who does not take care of his relatives?
Questions.A: He has refused to obey the true teachings.

Questions.Q: Why do you think Paul says such a one is worse than an unbeliever?
Questions.A: Even unbelievers take care of their family members. So if a believer refuses to do so, he is worse than a heathen/unbeliever.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: The church should recognize and help those widows who really need help.

Questions.Q: In order for a widow to receive help from the church, what kind of a person must she be?
Questions.A: She must be at least sixty years old.
She must have been morally faithful to her husband.
People must know that she has done good deeds.

Questions.Q: What are some of the good deeds which a widow should be known for?
Questions.A: She has raised her children properly.
She has been hospitable.
She has served believers.
She has helped people who were in trouble.
She has tried to help people as much as possible in every way.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Timothy should not enroll younger widows on the list of widows the church is to help.

Questions.Q: Give the reasons why Paul says the church should not enroll younger widows on the list of widows the church is to help.
Questions.A: Younger widows may want to remarry.
Younger widows may stop working.
They then begin to gossip and become involved in other people's affairs.

Questions.Q: When do younger widows want to marry again?
Questions.A: When their sexual desires become greater than their desire for Christ.

Questions.Q: Why would a younger widow be guilty if she married again after the church had enrolled her as a widow?
Questions.A: Because she would not be doing what she had first promised Christ she would do.

Questions.Q: When younger widows do not work, what do they begin to do?
Questions.A: They go from house to house visiting people.

Questions.Q: When they do that, what happens?
Questions.A: They begin to gossip, becoming involved in other people's affairs.

Questions.Q: Why is that bad?
Questions.A: It is bad because they say things they should not say.

Questions.Q: Because of the problems which younger widows have if they promise to remain a widow, what does Paul say younger widows should do?
Questions.A: They should remarry.
They should have children.
They should manage their homes.
They should do nothing for which an enemy can reproach them.

Questions.Q: Why does Paul give this advice to younger widows?
Questions.A: Because some younger widows have stopped obeying Christ.

Questions.Q: What happens when they do that?
Questions.A: They begin to follow/obey Satan.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say in this verse?
Questions.A: A woman who is a believer should take care of widows in her family.

Questions.Q: Why should she do this?
Questions.A: So that the church will not have to care for them.

Questions.Q: Why is it good if the church does not need to care for them?
Questions.A: Then the church will be able to care for widows who are all alone/in real need.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul tells Timothy to instruct the church to honor the elders who manage the church well.

Questions.Q: The church is supposed to honor certain elders. What must these elders do in order to receive this honor?
Questions.A: They must manage the church well.

Questions.Q: Which elders should be specially honored?
Questions.A: Those who preach.
Those who teach.

Questions.Q: Why should the church honor these elders?
Questions.A: Because the Scriptures say that the one who works should receive benefits/rewards from that work.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul tells Timothy to instruct the church concerning elders who sin; they are to be corrected publicly.

Questions.Q: Paul now talks about what to do if elders of the church sin. When is Timothy to listen to someone who is accusing an elder of sinning?
Questions.A: When there are two or three other people who also agree that the elder did wrong.

Questions.Q: Where is Timothy supposed to rebuke the elders who sin?
Questions.A: In front of all the believers in the church.

Questions.Q: Why is he to do it publicly?
Questions.A: So that the other elders (or, believers) will fear to sin.

Questions.Q: Who has witnessed/observed what Paul is telling Timothy here?
Questions.A: God, Jesus Christ, and the angels.
Questions.Alternative: Who has witnessed what Paul is telling Timothy here?
Who has observed what Paul is telling Timothy here?

Questions.Q: What is Timothy to do about these instructions?
Questions.A: He is to obey them.

Questions.Q: How is Timothy to judge the case of an elder?
Questions.A: He is not to decide before the case begins whether or not the elder is guilty.
He is not to allow his feelings for the elder to influence him.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul tells Timothy to investigate a man carefully before he appoints him as an elder.

Questions.Q: Paul has just been talking about rebuking an elder who sins. Now what does he say to Timothy in this verse?
Questions.A: Timothy should not be quick in appointing a person to the office of elder.

Questions.Q: Why should he not be quick in making such an appointment?
Questions.A: Because this man may have sinned in the past, and Timothy would not know about it.

Questions.Q: In this connection, why do you think Paul admonishes Timothy to keep himself pure?
Questions.A: If Timothy appoints an elder without first carefully investigating him, he may find that he is endorsing a man who is not worthy of this high office in the church.

Questions.Q: What does Paul advise Timothy to do?
Questions.A: He should drink a little wine.

Questions.Q: Why should he do this?
Questions.A: To cure his stomach which was often upset.

Questions.Q: What happens when people sin openly?
Questions.A: Other people know what they have done and so are able to make a decision on that basis.

Questions.Q: What happens when people sin secretly?
Questions.A: Other people do not find out about what they have done until later.

Questions.Q: How should this fact influence Timothy as to whom he appoints to a church office?
Questions.A: He should not make a hasty decision.

Questions.Q: What happens when people do good deeds openly?
Questions.A: Other people will know about what they have done right away.

Questions.Q: What happens when people do good deeds secretly?
Questions.A: Other people will eventually find out about the good deeds they have done.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Timothy is to teach those who are slaves that a slave must show honor to his master.

Questions.Q: What does Paul want all slaves to know?
Questions.A: That they should respect their masters.

Questions.Q: What would happen if the slaves did not show honor to their masters?
Questions.A: People would speak against God's name/character.
People would speak against what the apostles teach.

Questions.Q: About which slaves in particular does Paul write in this verse?
Questions.A: Those whose masters are also believers.

Questions.Q: What does he say about them?
Questions.A: They are to be sure to show honor to their masters.

Questions.Q: Why might some slaves not show honor to masters who are believers?
Questions.A: Because they have equal status with them as brothers in the church.

Questions.Q: Why should these slaves serve their masters even more faithfully?
Questions.A: Because those who benefit from their service are also believers whom they love.

Questions.Q: What does Paul again remind Timothy he is to do?
Questions.A: He is to teach the people all that Paul has written.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul warns Timothy against those who teach false doctrines.

Questions.Q: In warning Timothy about a false teacher, what does Paul say the false teacher does?
Questions.A: He teaches differently than Paul teaches.
He disagrees with the correct teaching which Jesus Christ taught.
He disagrees with the teaching about how believers should live/conduct themselves.

Questions.Q: What else does Paul say about the false teacher?
Questions.A: He is conceited.
He knows nothing.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say the false teacher has a great interest in?
Questions.A: He has an unnatural desire to question things.
He has an unnatural desire to argue about words.

Questions.Q: Because the false teachers do these things, what happens?
Questions.A: They envy one another.
They argue with one another.
They suspect that other people have bad motives for things they are doing.
They disagree with one another.

Questions.Q: Why do these people do all these bad things?
Questions.A: Because they have bad attitudes.
Because they do not understand the true teachings.

Questions.Q: Why then do these people practice religion?
Questions.A: Because they think it will make them rich.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Contentment with what a person has is what benefits that person.

Questions.Q: Paul has just said that some people practice religion thinking it will make them rich. What does he say here about true religion?
Questions.A: It will benefit a person greatly.

Questions.Q: What things are necessary in order for a person to benefit?
Questions.A: He must live in a manner which pleases God.
He must be content.

Questions.Q: What reasons does Paul give as to why people should be content?
Questions.A: Since people brought nothing with them when they came into the world, they have no reason to complain if they have nothing.
Since they cannot take anything with them when they die, they have no reason to have more than they need.
Since they have enough food and clothing, they should be satisfied.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say happens to those who want to become rich?
Questions.A: They are tempted to do things which they should not do.
They are forced to accept the results of what they have done.
They foolishly desire to do things which will later cause them problems.

Questions.Q: What happens to people who do these foolish things?
Questions.A: They become ruined and destroyed.

Questions.Q: How does Paul know that people who want to get rich will only hurt themselves?
Questions.A: Because many evil things happen to people when they greatly desire to have money.

Questions.Q: What has happened to some people who have greatly wanted money?
Questions.A: They have stopped believing the true teaching.
They have become very unhappy.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: He tells Timothy he should live/conduct himself in a manner which will please God.

Questions.Q: Paul has been talking about people who want to be rich. What does he tell Timothy here?
Questions.A: Timothy is to avoid doing what people who want to be rich do.

Questions.Q: Instead, what is Timothy supposed to do?
Questions.A: Do what is right.
Live/conduct himself in a manner which pleases God.
Love people.
Be patient when life becomes difficult.
Be gentle.

Questions.Q: In this verse Paul gives Timothy some instructions. What is the first thing he tells him to do?
Questions.A: He should put all his effort into living in a way which is in accord with what he has believed.

Questions.Q: What is the next thing Paul tells him to do?
Questions.A: He should keep on believing and obeying God in order to receive the reward which God will give him.

Questions.Q: What is that reward?
Questions.A: Eternal life/to live with God forever.

Questions.Q: Why should Timothy try so hard to live that kind of life?
Questions.A: Because that was the kind of life God called him to.

Questions.Q: When did God call him to live that kind of life?
Questions.A: When he told others about his faith in Jesus Christ.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul tells Timothy to obey what he has told him to do.
He is to do this until Jesus Christ returns.

Questions.Q: Paul is giving Timothy a commandment. In whose presence is he giving this commandment?
Questions.A: In the presence of God and Jesus Christ.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say God does?
Questions.A: He gives life to all things which have life.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say Christ Jesus did?
Questions.A: He told what he believed to Pontius Pilate.

Questions.Q: What does Paul command Timothy to do?
Questions.A: To obey Paul's instructions regarding Timothy's ministry.

Questions.Q: How should Timothy obey these instructions?
Questions.A: Without failing in any of them.
In such a way that no one can reproach Timothy.

Questions.Q: How long should Timothy do that?
Questions.A: Until Jesus Christ comes back.

Questions.Q: When will Jesus Christ come?
Questions.A: He will come when God wants him to come.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say about God?
Questions.A: He is blessed.
He is the only ruler who also reigns over other rulers.
He lives forever.
He lives in light.
No one has ever seen him.
No one is able to see him.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul tells Timothy that rich people should trust in God, not in their riches.

Questions.Q: What was Timothy to tell rich people?
Questions.A: To believe that God will give them the things they need.
To be rich in good deeds as well as money.
To be willing to share their things with other people.
To be generous.

Questions.Q: What else was he to tell them?
Questions.A: They should not be proud.
They should not depend on their riches to help them in the future.

Questions.Q: Why should rich people not depend on their riches to help them in the future?
Questions.A: Because they do not know if they will still have their riches in the future.

Questions.Q: Why should people trust in God?
Questions.A: Because God gives believers plenty of everything.

Questions.Q: Why does he do this?
Questions.A: God gives believers these things so that they may enjoy them.

Questions.Q: If rich people do the things which Paul says they should do, what will happen?
Questions.A: They will store away treasure for themselves in the future.

Questions.Q: What is this treasure?
Questions.A: The promise of eternal life.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul tells Timothy to guard carefully the true teachings.

Questions.Q: What is Timothy supposed to do?
Questions.A: He is not to change the true teachings.
He is not to listen to lies.

Questions.Q: What do some people call those lies?
Questions.A: Knowledge

Questions.Q: Why does Paul tell Timothy not to listen to those lies?
Questions.A: Because some people have believed those lies and as a result have stopped believing the true teachings.

Questions.Q: Paul now concludes his letter. What does he want God to do for Timothy and the believers there?
Questions.A: He wants God to bless them.

Section.heading: 2 Corinthians 1:1-11 God will help us in our troubles.

Questions.Q: Why should God be praised?
Questions.A: God should be praised because he is the merciful one and the one who comforts us.

Questions.Q: Why does God comfort us?
Questions.A: God comforts us so that we can comfort others.

Questions.Q: What is the second reason that God gives us comfort?
Questions.A: To help us to suffer the same sufferings as Christ suffered.

Questions.Q: How do both the good and the bad things that happen to Paul help the Corinthians?
Questions.A: If Paul suffers trouble it happens so that God can comfort and save them. If Paul gets comfort (from God) he can comfort them and help them to patiently endure the same sufferings that Paul suffers and so Paul and the Corinthians share the same sufferings and the same comforts.

Questions.Q: What good does Paul see in the great trouble he suffered in Asia?
Questions.A: When he thought he and his friends were about to die, this taught them to trust only in God.

Questions.Q: How did they understand God's power?
Questions.A: If God can raise people from death, surely he can save them from dying.

Questions.Q: What is Paul's hope?
Questions.A: That God will go on saving him from death.

Questions.Q: What strengthens his hope?
Questions.A: The prayers of the Corinthians strengthens his hope.

Questions.Q: What two reasons have they for praying for Paul?
Questions.A: 1. That God will save Paul.
2. That when God saves Paul they, who are many, can thank God.

Section.heading: 2 Corinthians 1:12-2:4 Paul does not change his mind.

Questions.Q: Against what accusations is Paul defending himself?
Questions.A: That he used cunning and lies to speak to the Corinthians.

Questions.Q: Is Paul guilty of cunning and lies?
Questions.A: No. His conscience tells him that he always spoke the truth to them and treated them with the love that comes from God.

Questions.Q: What other accusations does Paul deny?
Questions.A: That he wrote difficult things in his letters.

Questions.Q: Why is Paul now writing this letter?
Questions.A: So that they can fully understand his thoughts and therefore be happy to boast about him on the day that Jesus Christ returns.

Questions.Q: What did Paul plan to do, but did not do?
Questions.A: Paul planned to visit the Corinthians on his way to and from Macedonia.

Questions.Q: What 3 reasons did Paul have for wanting to visit them?
Questions.A: 1. He thinks that they will be happy to see him.
2. His visit will bring them blessings.
3. They can help him on his way to Judea.

Questions.Q: But Paul did not visit them as he planned. What does he now fear?
Questions.A: Paul fears that they are accusing him of saying, "Yes" but meaning "No".

Questions.Q: What makes God different from the fetishes that the people of this world worship?
Questions.A: God is true. When he says something he does not change his word/mouth.
Questions.Alternative: What makes God different from the idols that the people of this world worship?
What makes God different from idols?

Questions.Q: What is the connection between God's promises and Christ?
Questions.A: Whatever God has promised, Christ will do.

Questions.Q: What should be our response to God's promises?
Questions.A: Amen. Let them be as he has promised, so that God may get greatness.

Questions.Q: What is the connection between God's promises and his Holy Spirit?
Questions.A: His Holy Spirit is like a tribal mark to show that he owns us. Likewise, he is in our hearts to show us that a time is coming when truly he will come and take us to himself.

Questions.Q: Why did Paul change his mind and not come to visit them?
Questions.A: So that he would not have to punish them at that time.

Questions.Q: What should be the true attitude/thoughts of a church pastor/leader towards his church people?
Questions.A: He will not force them to do or believe what he teaches. He will treat them kindly and do what will do them good.
Questions.Alternative: What should be the true attitude of a church pastor towards his church people?
What should be the true attitude of a church leader towards his church people?
What should be the true thoughts of a church pastor towards his church people?
What should be the true thoughts of a church leader towards his church people?

Questions.Q: Is it on the faith of a church leader that church members stand firm?
Questions.A: Whether or not the leader is good, the church members should stand firm in their belief in Christ.

Questions.Q: What are Paul's feelings towards the Corinthians?
Questions.A: He loves them. What makes him happy also makes them happy.

Questions.Q: Why did he write them a letter?
Questions.A: He wrote a letter to show how much he loved them.

Questions.Q: Was he happy to write the letter?
Questions.A: No.

Questions.Q: Why not?
Questions.A: He was not happy to write the letter because he was very troubled about someone's behavior.

Questions.Q: Why did he not go to see them himself?
Questions.A: He wanted to deal with their problems in a letter so that when he did come to see them the problem would have been solved and so they could be happy together.

Questions.Q: What troubled Paul as he wrote the letter?
Questions.A: It was that one of the Corinthians had sinned against all of them, or at least some of them were very unhappy about it.
Questions.Note: See 1 Corinthians 5:1-5.

Questions.Q: What is Paul advising them to do?
Questions.A: They should stop punishing him, forgive him and comfort him.

Questions.Q: Why should they forgive him?
Questions.A: Clearly he is repentant. If they don't forgive a repentant man he will lose all hope of forgiveness.
Questions.Note: Note: Ensure that this is clear.

Questions.Q: What is the meaning of forgiveness?
Questions.A: You show that you really love the sinner.

Questions.Q: For what other reason did Paul write that other letter?
Questions.A: To see whether or not the Corinthians would obey him in everything.

Questions.Q: Is Paul now changing his mind about their obeying him? Does he put himself under their authority?
Questions.A: No. He has asked them to forgive the sinner. So he must also join them in forgiving anything that the man has done wrong to Paul.

Questions.Q: What further reason is here given for forgiving other's sins?
Questions.A: The reason for forgiving other's sins is to prevent the Devil from having power over us.

Questions.Q: How could the Devil have power over us if we don't forgive?
Questions.A: 1. The sinner will despair of forgiveness and will return to his sin.
2. The others will hate him.
3. The church will remain divided.

Questions.Q: What troubled Paul at Troas?
Questions.A: He couldn't find his fellow Christian Titus.

Questions.Q: What does this show about Paul?
Questions.A: He was a human being like all of us.

Section.heading: 2 Corinthians 2:14-17 We are Christ's followers and apostles.

Questions.Q: How does Paul see God's victory? Whom has he defeated?
Questions.A: God has caused Christ to defeat the Devil. Now Paul and his companions are going round in God's victory procession telling the news of Christ and his victory everywhere.

Questions.Q: To whom is Christ's victory something sweet?
Questions.A: Christ's victory is sweet to those to whom God will give eternal life.

Questions.Q: How does Paul answer his own questions in verse 16?
Questions.A: One who is preaching as God's apostles in Christ's name in sincerity knowing that God sees and hears all: one who doesn't sell God's word for profit.

Section.heading: 2 Corinthians 3:1-18 How the new covenant/oath is greater than the old one.

Questions.Q: What accusation is Paul defending himself against?
Questions.A: That he is again boasting so that he may prove that he and his companions have done good.

Questions.Q: What shows that Paul's work has been well done?
Questions.A: The fact that the Corinthians became Christians when he preached to them shows that Paul's work has been done well.

Questions.Q: How does this show that his work was well done?
Questions.A: Their lives and the way they live clearly show to everyone that the Holy Spirit has changed their hearts to follow God.

Questions.Q: How do you see the work of man and Christ and God the Father and God the Holy Spirit in causing people to follow Christ?
Questions.A: Man preaches the word of God about Christ to people, and the Holy Spirit works in their hearts to turn them to God.
Questions.Note: N.B. Is this metaphor of letter writing well understood?

Questions.Q: What gives Paul power to say that what has happened to the Corinthians is Paul's work?
Questions.A: Paul had the power to say that what has happened to the Corinthians is his work because he did it all, trusting in God through Christ.

Questions.Q: Where did Paul get his qualification/ability/wisdom to do this work?
Questions.A: Paul got his qualification/ability/wisdom to do this work from God.
Questions.Alternative: Where did Paul get his qualification to do this work?
Where did Paul get his ability to do this work?
Where did Paul get his wisdom to do this work?

Questions.Q: What is the difference between the old Covenant and the new Covenant?
Questions.A: 1. The old came through Moses, the new through the Holy Spirit.
2. The old shows us that we have sinned and deserve to die. The new gives us life.

Questions.Q: How was the old Covenant written down?
Questions.A: God wrote it on two flat carved stones.

Questions.Q: How was this brought to the Israelites?
Questions.A: Moses carried them down the mountain to give to them.

Questions.Q: Why did Moses's face shine?
Questions.A: Moses's face shone because God had revealed his greatness/shining light to Moses.

Questions.Q: Why did God's law show his greatness?
Questions.A: Because:
1. It showed men's sins and condemned them to death.
2. God revealed his greatness and light to Moses on the mountain when he gave him his law.

Questions.Q: Why is the work of the Holy Spirit greater than that of God's law?
Questions.A: Because the Holy Spirit declares us not guilty of breaking his law even though we are sinners.
Questions.Note: Note: These are very difficult verses to translate. Any improvement is welcome.

Questions.Q: Why did Moses cover his face with a cloth/veil?
Questions.A: Moses covered his face with a cloth/veil so that the Israelites/Jews could not see the shininess of his face disappearing.
Questions.Alternative: Why did Moses cover his face with a cloth?
Why did Moses cover his face with a veil?

Questions.Q: Who is it that are like blind people?
Questions.A: The Israelites.

Questions.Q: What is this proverb about the cloth/veil teaching? Do they wear a cloth over their eyes when they listen to the old covenant book?
Questions.A: No, they don't wear a cloth on their faces. This is a proverb which says that they cannot understand what is read to them.
Questions.Alternative: What is this proverb about the cloth teaching? Do they wear a cloth over their eyes when they listen to the old covenant book?
What is this proverb about the veil teaching? Do they wear a cloth over their eyes when they listen to the old covenant book?

Questions.Q: How can the Israelites come to understand Moses's book?
Questions.A: Only Christ can give them understanding.

Questions.Q: In what way does Christ help them and us to understand?
Questions.A: Christ, through God's Holy Spirit, gives understanding and sets us free from the old law.

Questions.Q: What keeps Paul and his companions from being discouraged in their work?
Questions.A: He knows that they are not worthy of the work of a minister, but it is God who has given it to them.

Questions.Q: What ways of preaching has Paul refused to follow?
Questions.A: Paul refused to follow secret things and bad ways and deception and changing God's word.

Questions.Q: What is his reason for always telling the truth?
Questions.A: 1. He wants everyone to say that he does well because he tells the truth.
2. He knows that God sees all he does and hears all he says.

Questions.Q: Who will not understand the good news?
Questions.A: Those who do not believe in Christ will not understand the good news.

Questions.Q: Why don't they believe in Christ?
Questions.A: Because they are among the people of this world and the Devil has control over them.

Questions.Q: What is the Devil doing to them?
Questions.A: He is covering their eyes/minds so that they will not see the light which comes from the good news which speaks of Christ's greatness.

Questions.Q: What is it that the Devil doesn't want at all?
Questions.A: That when people see Christ as he really is, they will see God.

Questions.Q: What shows that Paul is a humble person?
Questions.A: 1. He says that he does not speak about himself but about Christ.
2. He tells everyone to obey Christ, not himself, as master.
3. For Christ's sake, he is their servant.

Questions.Q: Against what accusation is he defending himself?
Questions.A: That he and his companions want to be masters over the Corinthians.

Questions.Q: Refer back to verse 4. Contrast those who believe in Christ with those who do not believe.
Questions.A: 1. The Christian has his eyes open.
. The unbeliever is blind.
2. The Christian knows God.
. The unbeliever does not know God.
3. The Christian sees how Christ lived on earth and sees God's greatness in Christ.
. The unbeliever does not understand Christ at all.

Questions.Q: What is the meaning of the proverb "God's inheritance/property is in pots"?
Questions.A: Our bodies are like weak pots. Of ourselves we have no strength. Our strength comes from God.
Questions.Alternative: What is the meaning of the proverb "God's inheritance is in pots"?
What is the meaning of the proverb "God's property is in pots"?

Questions.Q: Does this mean that the pots become strong?
Questions.A: No. Our bodies remain weak, but our hearts become strong with God's strength.

Questions.Q: In what ways did God show his strength in the weak bodies of Paul and his companions?
Questions.A: They suffered cruelty, but their persecutors could not stop their work. They were troubled but not discouraged. They suffered persecution but God did not leave them. They were beaten to the ground but not killed.

Questions.Q: Why did God allow Paul and his companions to suffer in this way?
Questions.A: 1. They suffered the kind of sufferings that Jesus Christ suffered while he lived on earth.
2. In their present sufferings people will see that Christ is now alive and is giving strength to their hearts.

Questions.Q: How can our sufferings help others?
Questions.A: Our sufferings will help others if we suffer persecution while preaching the good news of Christ to others, because some who hear us may become Christians. And so through us facing death on earth others may receive eternal life in heaven.

Questions.Q: What made Paul and his companions continue to preach God's word?
Questions.A: Paul and his companions continued to preach God's word because, despite their sufferings, they continued to believe.

Questions.Q: What is it they continued to believe?
Questions.A: 1. That God raised our Master Jesus Christ to life.
2. That because of that he will raise up Paul, his companions, the Corinthians and all Christians to life in heaven with Jesus.

Questions.Q: Continuing the thought of verses 10 and 11, what other reason does Paul give for his sufferings?
Questions.A: Everything that happens to him and his companions happens so that God can go on saving more and more people and then there will be more and more people to praise his greatness.
Questions.Note: N.B. Is this verse well translated?

Section.heading: 2 Corinthians 4:16-5:10 This world is not our home.

Questions.Q: Why does Paul not lose hope?
Questions.A: Paul does not lose hope because in his troubles God is saving many people. Verse 15.

Questions.Q: How can Paul manage to continue through his troubles?
Questions.A: God gives him encouragement and new strength every day.

Questions.Q: Why does he not want to get sweet life on this earth like most people?
Questions.A: 1. Because he knows that the greatness which he will get in God's presence is far greater than his present sufferings.
2. Because the troubles will not last long, but the greatness in heaven will last forever.

Questions.Q: From these verses can you say what is the meaning of hope in God?
Questions.A: Our eyes rest on what is ahead and which we cannot see. What we see now will not last. But what we don't see, that is, heaven will last forever.

Questions.Q: Why should we not worry about the decay of our human body?
Questions.A: Because we have a better place to live in that God has made for us in heaven.

Questions.Q: Since Paul knows that he has a better living place/house in heaven what does he think of life in this world?
Questions.A: Life in this world is not sweet. His body is suffering. So he would like to leave this life. It is not death he longs for but for the new life in heaven, where he will have a new body.
Questions.Alternative: Since Paul knows that he has a better living place in heaven what does he think of life in this world?
Since Paul knows that he has a better house in heaven what does he think of life in this world?

Questions.Q: How does he want this to happen?
Questions.A: He wants to die and immediately have his new body in heaven, without any delay. He does not want to be homeless for any time at all. He wants his body to be changed immediately from the old body to the new body. He wants this present life to turn into life without end.

Questions.Q: Where does he want to live this new life?
Questions.A: He wants to live in heaven with God.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that God created us?
Questions.A: That we might go to live with him in heaven forever.

Questions.Q: What shows us that we will go to live with God in heaven?
Questions.A: God has sent his Holy Spirit to live in our hearts.
Questions.Note: N. B. Is it clear that the Holy Spirit has come to live in our hearts?

Questions.Q: What gives Paul the hope that he will go to heaven?
Questions.A: The fact that the Holy Spirit lives in us gives Paul the hope that he will go to heaven. (See verse 5.)

Questions.Q: Are we at home with God at the moment?
Questions.A: No, we live on earth and have not yet reached our home in heaven with God.

Questions.Q: How do we go through life before reaching heaven?
Questions.A: We walk, not seeing the way ahead, but we believe that God is leading us.

Questions.Q: Does Paul like this life on earth?
Questions.A: He would like to go home to heaven now.

Questions.Q: What does Paul want to do more than even to go to heaven?
Questions.A: To please our Master Jesus whether he lives on earth or goes to heaven.

Questions.Q: Why does Paul mention the judgment day in this verse?
Questions.A: Because we should all be trying to please Christ as Paul says in verse 9 and because Christ will judge us to see what we have done, whether good or bad.

Section.heading: 2 Corinthians 5:11-6:2 Paul and his companions' work is to preach how God through Christ reconciles man to himself.

Questions.Q: How does Paul show that his reasons for his way of life and teaching people to follow Christ are good?
Questions.A: He says that he does this because he fears God.

Questions.Q: What kind of fear of God should we have?
Questions.A: We should have a fear of God that we will displease him; this is better than fear that he will punish us.

Questions.Q: Against what accusation is Paul defending himself now?
Questions.A: That he is boasting.

Questions.Q: Why is he showing that his thoughts are good?
Questions.A: So that those of the Corinthians who are his friends can defend him against those who speak against him.

Questions.Q: How is the way that Paul's accusers think, wrong?
Questions.A: They look on the face but not at the heart.

Questions.Q: How can Paul be mad on God's behalf? What is he saying?
Questions.A: He lives only to serve God and Christ. Therefore, to ordinary people and those who think bad thoughts, it is like he is mad.

Questions.Q: Is Paul really mad?
Questions.A: No.

Questions.Q: In short, what is he saying in this verse?
Questions.A: However they see Paul's thoughts, Paul is working only for God and for them.

Questions.Q: What is the driving force behind Paul's actions?
Questions.A: Christ's love for us.

Questions.Q: In what way did Christ show his love for us?
Questions.A: He died for us all and God raised him to life.

Questions.Q: Why did Christ die?
Questions.A: Christ died so that while they live on earth all people might live no more for themselves, but for Christ.

Questions.Q: Does this mean that all will go to heaven?
Questions.A: No, only those who believe in Christ will go to heaven.

Questions.Q: Before Paul believed in Christ, how did he look at him?
Questions.A: Paul looked at Christ only on the face.

Questions.Q: And what did he see?
Questions.A: He thought that Christ was a deceiver and a blasphemer against God.

Questions.Q: What changes a person's thoughts about Christ?
Questions.A: God

Questions.Q: How?
Questions.A: He makes a person who is on Christ's side into a new person. His old life is finished, he has started to live a new life.

Questions.Q: In short, what is the message that Paul preaches and the work God has given him?
Questions.A: That through Christ God has reconciled us to himself, and that Paul's work is to tell this message to everyone.

Questions.Q: What does this reconciliation do for us?
Questions.A: God will no longer punish us for our sins.

Questions.Q: If all men are thus reconciled to God, what need is there for Paul to tell everyone about it?
Questions.A: The message is that God has provided the way through which all people may be reconciled to God and have their sins forgiven. But people must accept this for themselves. God will not accept those who refuse him.

Questions.Q: Show how Paul is Christ's representative.
Questions.A: He is speaking God's message about Christ's death, and on Christ's behalf, is begging all people, including any of the Corinthians who don't yet believe in him, to become united with God.

Questions.Q: In what way did God make us into good people?
Questions.A: For our sake, God treated Christ as if he were a wrong doer.

Questions.Q: How did God treat Christ?
Questions.A: He let bad people kill him on the Cross. He was punished but he did not do wrong. We have done wrong and deserve to be punished, but because of Christ's death for us, we are free and have become Christ's people.

Questions.Q: What is the grace/great thing, that God has done for the Corinthians (and us)?
Questions.A: He punished Christ to let us go free.
Questions.Alternative: What is the grace that God has given the Corinthians (and us)?
What is the great thing that God has done for the Corinthians (and us)?

Questions.Q: Against what danger is Paul warning them?
Questions.A: That they see what Christ has done and refuse or neglect to accept it for themselves.

Questions.Q: Why is it important to accept it?
Questions.A: It is important to accept it because today is the right time. Tomorrow may be too late.

Section.heading: 2 Corinthians 6:3-13 The sufferings of Paul and his fellow apostles.

Questions.Q: What two things do Paul and his companions do to show they are servants of God?
Questions.A: 1. They avoid doing anything that will lead people into sin.
2. They pass through many sufferings.

Questions.Q: In what ways are Paul's sufferings a lesson to us?
Questions.A: 1. He suffered persecution, hardship and trouble patiently.
2. Despite beatings, imprisonment, people rioting against him, despite getting very tired and going without sleep and food, he treated others with goodness, wisdom, patience and kindness.

Questions.Q: What made Paul do good in return for evil?
Questions.A: The Holy Spirit was in his life, making him love others truly. God gave him power to speak the truth.

Questions.Q: What weapons did Paul use?
Questions.A: Speaking the truth with the power of God.

Questions.Q: In what ways did bad people say that he was the opposite of what he truly was?
Questions.A: They did not respect him. They accused him of doing wrong. They accused him of lying. They called him worthless.

Questions.Q: How did Paul come through these problems?
Questions.A: 1. Though nearly dead, he survived.
2. Though punished, he did not die.
3. Though suffering persecution, he remained happy.

Questions.Q: How could Paul's poverty make others rich? How did he have everything and nothing at the same time?
Questions.A: Because he had the power and blessings of God, which do not finish and so he could give them to those who wanted to receive them.

Questions.Q: 1. How would you react to such suffering as Paul suffered?
2. How could you remain happy despite persecution?
3. What are true riches?
4. How can you make others rich with the blessings of God?
What is Paul teaching here?
Questions.A: 1. He is being truthful and honest and open and loving to the Corinthians.
2. He wants them to be the same to him.

Section.heading: 2 Corinthians 6:14-7:1 Do not be united with unbelievers.

Questions.Q: In what ways should believers in Christ not be united with unbelievers?
Questions.A: 1. Believers should not marry unbelievers.
2. Believers should not join in sacrifices to fetishes, or eat food/meat offered to fetishes.
3. Believers should not attend fetish worship.
Questions.Note: N.B. Are the proverbs well understood? Do they say the same thing in the first half of the verse? If the verses seem to say that believers should not even live with unbelievers, then the verse is not well translated. Is it clear that light refers to good and darkness refers to bad?

Questions.Q: Why cannot Christians share in non-Christian worship?
Questions.A: Because God lives in our hearts, and the Devil lives in unbelievers' hearts and God and the Devil cannot live together.

Questions.Q: What do you understand about God and his people from this verse from the Old Testament?
Questions.A: 1. God is our master, we are his people, therefore, it is a two-way relationship.
2. It is a two-way agreement which man is always the first to break.
3. It is a promise by God that he will live and work with his people everywhere - he is not fixed to any place.

Questions.Q: This is a command from the Old Testament. What is it saying?
Questions.A: God's people should live separately from nonbelievers.

Questions.Q: Why do you think God thought it wise for his people to live separately from unbelievers?
Questions.A: God said that it was wise for his people to live separately from unbelievers because unbelievers would lead his people to sin.

Questions.Q: 1 Referring to verses 6:14-7:1 discuss:
1. In what ways Christians today should be separate from non-Christians.
2. How can we be freed from everything that makes our body and heart dirty?
How is following God both positive and negative (do and do not)?
Questions.A: 1. We should avoid everything that makes body and heart dirty.
2. We should respect and fear God and get white hearts.

Questions.Q: What are Paul's feelings towards the Corinthians?
Questions.A: 1. He loves them very much.
2. He is ready to live or die with them.
3. He trusts them.
4. He is proud of them.
5. He is encouraged by them.
6. They make him happy, despite all his troubles.

Questions.Q: What effect did the troubles that Paul met in Macedonia have on him?
Questions.A: He suffered persecution and he was afraid and very anxious, that is, troubles for both the body and the heart.

Questions.Q: How did Paul receive comfort in his troubles?
Questions.A: God caused the coming of Titus to comfort him and heal his heart.

Questions.Q: Discuss: How many of God's blessings to Christians are brought by other human beings?
What also comforted Paul?
Questions.A: 1. That Titus told Paul that the Corinthians had comforted/encouraged Titus by their words and actions.
2. That Titus told him how much the Corinthians loved Paul.
Questions.Note: Paul is probably referring to what he wrote in 1 Corinthians 5:1-5.

Questions.Q: When the Corinthians read what Paul wrote, what did they feel towards Paul?
Questions.A: They were not happy, but they wanted to see him very much and they remained on his side.

Questions.Q: Was Paul sorry that his letter did not make them happy?
Questions.A: Yes and No. He was sorry that he had to hurt them - this shows how he loved them. He also was not sorry because their unhappiness made them repent of their sins.

Questions.Q: How does God bring good out of bad? What sorrow is good?
Questions.A: He punishes us only to make us repent of our sins so that we may turn to doing good and get life.

Questions.Q: How does the sorrow that the people of this world have separate us from eternal life?
Questions.A: Many who are not Christians and who suffer troubles blame God and get angry or full of hate for God and other people.
Questions.Note: N.B. If you do not agree, note down alternative.

Questions.Q: In short, how did the Corinthians react to Paul's letter? How did they feel and what did they do?
Questions.A: They became serious. They hurried to defend themselves. They realized that they had done wrong by not minding what the wrongdoer was doing. Now they were keen to do what was right and they punished him. And also they wanted Paul to come to them.

Questions.Q: What punishment did they give to the wrongdoer?
Questions.A: They excluded him from church. (See 1 Corinthians 5:5.)

Questions.Q: Was this punishment to last forever?
So why did Paul write that letter to them?
Questions.A: Paul wrote that letter to them so that they might see how much they really loved Paul.

Questions.Q: What do you understand that to mean?
Questions.A: As they had previously followed his teachings and loved him, but now some were turning away from him, now he showed them how they had gone astray, and his letter caused them to come again to his side.

Questions.Q: What additional proof does Paul give that he always tells the truth?
Questions.A: He boasted to Titus that the Corinthians would do what was right, and when Titus came to them he saw that this was true.

Questions.Q: Why did Titus, remembering the Corinthians, love them?
Questions.A: Because they welcomed him as Paul's representative, in fear, and got ready to do everything that he told them to do.

Questions.Q: What did he tell them to do?
Questions.A: He told them to do all the things in 1 Corinthians, especially excluding the wrongdoer from their church.

Section.heading: 2 Corinthians 8:1-24 Concerning the collection for the poor Christians in Judea.

Questions.Q: What did not prevent the Macedonian Christians from giving money to the poor Christians in Judea?
Questions.A: Their own sufferings and poverty did not prevent them from giving money to the poor Christians.

Questions.Q: Why is Paul so pleased with the Macedonians?
Questions.A: 1. They gave willingly and not as a force.
2. They gave more than they were able.
3. They begged Paul/Titus to be allowed to give.
4. They gave themselves to God and then to Paul and his companions.

Questions.Q: Why does Paul want the Corinthians to add to the collection for the Judeans?
Questions.A: 1. It was they who began the collection, giving to Titus to give to the Judeans.
2. That they may show how much they love God's people who are poor.

Questions.Q: What additional reason does Paul give why the Corinthians (and all Christians) should give generously?
Questions.A: 1. They are already rich in gifts from God, such as faith, ability to speak well and wisdom.
2. They already have shown how seriously they worship God and how much they love Paul.

Questions.Q: Discuss: Is Paul using sweet talk? Does he speak the truth?
Why does Paul speak like this?
Questions.A: Paul spoke like that to test their love for the poor Christians, so as to see if it is true or not.

Questions.Q: What example does Paul give that shows generosity?
Questions.A: Jesus Christ.

Questions.Q: How was Jesus generous?
Questions.A: He had all the riches and blessings of heaven. Yet for our sakes he left all that and became a poor man on earth so that we might get blessings.

Questions.Q: Discuss: How did Christ's poverty get us blessings?
Who began this collection for the Judean Christians?
Questions.A: Paul, but the first to give were the Corinthians.

Questions.Q: What was wrong with the giving of the Corinthians?
Questions.A: They did not finish collecting the money.

Questions.Q: How will God look at our giving to the poor?
Questions.A: 1. We must be willing, giving from the heart.
2. We must give according to what we have.

Questions.Q: What does Paul mean that God doesn't look at what we don't have?
Questions.A: He doesn't ask us to give more than we have.

Questions.Q: What is one reason that Paul gives here for giving to fellow Christians who suffer poverty?
Questions.A: One reason that Paul gave for giving to Christians who were suffering in poverty was so that all may have equality.

Questions.Q: How can the poor help the rich?
Questions.A: If the poor become rich and the rich become poor, the first can help the second.

Questions.Q: How do you understand this reference from the Old Testament?
Questions.A: The Jews lived in the desert and every day God gave them food from heaven. Every night it lay on the ground for them to gather in the morning. Though some gathered much and some gathered little, when they put it in a measuring bowl it became exactly the same amount for each person.

Questions.Q: What does this Old Testament passage teach?
Questions.A: We should not be greedy, but share our things with those who suffer poverty, so as to make them equal.

Questions.Q: How many men is Paul sending to Corinth?
Questions.A: Paul sent Titus and two others to Corinth.

Questions.Q: Why?
Questions.A: 1. To collect the money from them for the poor Christians in Judea.
2. To do what will give glory to God and to show how much he wants to help the Judeans.
3. He wants to avoid any criticism about the way he is to collect this money and take it to Judea.
Questions.Alternative: Why did Paul send those men?
Why did Paul send them?

Questions.Q: What shows that the second man can be trusted?
Questions.A: He has been chosen by other churches to accompany those who take the money.

Questions.Q: What shows that this third man can be trusted to look after the money?
Questions.A: In many ways and at many times he has shown that he eagerly worships God.

Questions.Q: What shows that Titus can be trusted?
Questions.A: He is Paul's companion and fellow worker and they are both working for the Corinthians.

Questions.Q: What shows that all three men can be trusted?
Questions.A: They are good men whose good way of life causes people to praise Christ.

Questions.Q: What is Paul afraid of?
Questions.A: Paul is afraid that his boasting that the Corinthians are generous is for nothing.

Section.heading: 2 Corinthians 9:1-15 More about the collection for the poor.

Questions.Q: Why did the Macedonian Christians give money to the poor Judean Christians?
Questions.A: The Macedonian Christians gave money to the poor Judean Christians because Paul told them that the Corinthians were eager to give.

Questions.Q: Was that true?
Questions.A: Yes. (See 8:11.)

Questions.Q: What is Paul now afraid of?
Questions.A: That the Corinthians will not be ready to hand over the money to Paul when he comes to them on his way to Judea.

Questions.Q: What if they are not ready?
Questions.A: Both Paul will be ashamed and they will be ashamed.

Questions.Q: How is Paul both forcing them and not forcing them to give?
Questions.A: He is giving them time to collect the money together. He is being both firm and patient, both cautious and trusting.

Questions.Q: What advice does Paul give to all people about giving money to those in need?
Questions.A: 1. If you give more, God will bless you more.
If you give less, God will bless you less.
2. Give willingly, not as if it is a force/obligatory.
3. Decide what to give and don't go back on it.

Questions.Q: How is it that, if we give, we will receive?
Questions.A: If we go on giving generously to others, God will give us enough for our needs and will add more that we can use to do many kinds of kindness to others.

Questions.Q: What makes a giver able to go on giving?
Questions.A: 1. If he gives willingly, he will be able to go on giving willingly.
2. Since God gives seed to plant and food to eat, then, if we give to others he will give us the food we need and will add more so that we can give to others.

Questions.Q: If we give generously and God gives us back generously, can we say that we deserve to be rich?
Questions.A: No, for God is the giver. He gives so that we can give to others.

Questions.Q: What other blessing comes from giving generously to others?
Questions.A: Those many others who receive from us will be blessing/thanking God.

Questions.Q: Who should get thanks for what we give to others?
Questions.A: God, since he is the giver of all things.

Questions.Q: What is the connection between faith in God and giving to others?
Questions.A: If we give generously to others, it shows that our faith in Christ is true.

Questions.Q: Should we give only for this reason?
Questions.A: No. God wants us to give without it hurting, that is, generously.

Questions.Q: How can the blessings we get from God cause others to love us?
Questions.A: If we share what God has given us with others, those others will praise God and love us.

Questions.Q: What blessing does Paul refer to in this verse?
Questions.A: Probably Paul is speaking of how God gave his son, Jesus Christ, to us. (See 8:9.)

Section.heading: 2 Corinthians 10:1-18 How Paul answers his accusers.

Questions.Q: Against what accusations is Paul defending himself?
Questions.A: That when he is among them, he is afraid, but when he is away from them he is hard on them.

Questions.Q: How is he hard on them when he is not with them?
Questions.A: He is hard on them in his letters to them. (See 10:10.)

Questions.Q: What does he advise them to do?
Questions.A: He advised them to stop accusing him of being afraid.

Questions.Q: What will Paul do when he comes to them?
Questions.A: He is afraid that he will have to be hard on them.

Questions.Q: Against what other accusation does Paul defend himself?
Questions.A: That he and his companions live like the people of this world.

Questions.Q: Is this accusation true?
Questions.A: No. As human beings they live in the world but their thoughts are not like those of the people of this world.

Questions.Q: Why is Paul's life like a war? What does he fight?
Questions.A: He is fighting evil and lies and boasting and speaking against the wisdom of God.

Questions.Q: What are Paul's weapons?
Questions.A: The power of God through Paul's preaching God's word.
Questions.Note: N.B. If this is not clear, make suggested alternative.

Questions.Q: Against whom is Paul threatening to use his weapons?
Questions.A: Paul is threatening to use his weapons against those at Corinth who refuse to obey him.

Questions.Q: What other things did the Corinthians say that are not true?
Questions.A: That Christ is in them, but not in Paul.

Questions.Q: What else did they accuse Paul of doing?
Questions.A: Boasting of his authority over them.

Questions.Q: Is this true?
Questions.A: Yes.

Questions.Q: Why did Paul boast of his authority?
Questions.A: Paul boasted of his authority because it was given to him by God, not to decrease their faith, but to increase it. It is a power for their good.

Questions.Q: What else do they accuse him of?
Questions.A: They said that his letters are strong and forceful, but when he is among them he is weak.

Questions.Q: What is his answer?
Questions.A: What he writes in his letters, he will do when he comes to them.

Questions.Q: In what way is Paul afraid and why?
Questions.A: He is afraid to compare himself with those who think of themselves as great people, because such a comparison would be wrong in God's sight.

Questions.Q: Why are such persons' thoughts foolish?
Questions.A: Such people are foolish because they compare themselves with one another and do not ask if they are pleasing God.
Questions.Note: N.B. This is a difficult thing to translate. Make any suggestions for improvement.

Questions.Q: How much boasting does Paul say is good for him to do?
Questions.A: Only what is true.

Questions.Q: What can he boast of?
Questions.A: Only of the work that God has given him to do, which includes preaching to the Corinthians.

Questions.Q: What is he not permitted to boast of?
Questions.A: Anything that other persons have done.

Questions.Q: What two things does Paul hope to do?
Questions.A: 1. To do more work among them in Corinth.
2. To preach the good news in towns beyond Corinth.

Questions.Q: What can prevent preachers taking the good news from our town to other towns?
Questions.A: Our own lack of faith, which means that preachers must spend more time with us before it is safe to leave us and go elsewhere.

Questions.Q: What two warnings does Paul give about boasting?
Questions.A: 1. We can only boast of what God has done.
2. We should not praise ourselves, but wait for God to praise us.

Section.heading: 2 Corinthians 11:1-33 Concerning liars who say they are apostles and concerning Paul's sufferings.

Questions.Q: Is Paul really being foolish?
Questions.A: No, but if they think he is foolish, he asks them to be patient with him.

Questions.Q: What proverb does Paul use?
Questions.A: He is a father who has promised his daughter (the Corinthians) in marriage.

Questions.Q: What is he afraid of?
Questions.A: Another man has seduced his daughter.
Questions.Note: N.B. Is the extension of the proverb understood?

Questions.Q: What does that mean?
Questions.A: Other teachers are teaching them things which are different from what Paul has taught them.

Questions.Q: Discuss what the snake did to Eve. See Genesis 3.
Is it possible to preach a different Jesus, a different Holy Spirit, a different Good News? What does Paul mean?
Questions.A: These lying teachers speak about Jesus and the Holy Spirit and the Good News, but they teach lies about all these.
Questions.Note: N.B. If this is not well translated, make suggested alterations.

Questions.Q: What did the Corinthians think of these lying teachers?
Questions.A: 1. That they are great apostles.
2. That they are good speakers.

Questions.Q: In what way does Paul say he is inferior to these liars and in what way is he superior?
Questions.A: He is not a good speaker like them, but he has more wisdom than them.

Questions.Q: In what other ways did the Corinthians think Paul was unimportant?
Questions.A: Because when he stayed with them, preaching and teaching, he did not collect any money for food and lodging.

Questions.Q: Why did he not collect money from them?
Questions.A: He did not collect money from them in order to help them in every way possible, to make them more important than himself.

Questions.Q: How did Paul's humility bring him trouble?
Questions.A: The Corinthians thought that as he collected nothing, his teaching was also worthless.

Questions.Q: Discuss: Do people think something that is free is worthless and something that what you pay for is valuable?
How did Paul receive money for food and lodging?
Questions.A: The Macedonian church people sent him money.

Questions.Q: Is it right to accept money from other churches where you are not at the moment working?
Questions.A: Yes, if they give willingly. That is the way missionaries are supported.

Questions.Q: Now that Paul has explained why he collected nothing from the Corinthians, will he now change his mind?
Questions.A: No, he will collect nothing for himself, but only for the poor Christians who are in Judea. (See Ch. 8 and Ch. 9.)

Questions.Q: Discuss: If a worker refuses money for his work, does it show that he despises those he works for? Were the Corinthians right in thinking this about Paul?
Since Paul did not accept money from the Corinthians, how does that cause the lying teachers to have nothing to stand on to make themselves equal to Paul?
Questions.A: Because they collected too much money from the Corinthians. (See 11:20.)

Questions.Q: Should it surprise us that there are some people who are liars who say they are true apostles?
Questions.A: No, because even the Devil can tempt us by disguising himself as one of God's angels to speak to us.

Questions.Q: What will happen to such men?
Questions.A: God will punish them.

Questions.Q: Discuss: How can you distinguish liars from true men among those who call themselves apostles in today's churches?
What is Paul doing here? Is he true or false?
Questions.A: He is being ironic. He is pretending to be a fool and he is pretending that the Corinthians are wise.

Questions.Q: What is he asking them to do?
Questions.A: Since they are wise and are patient with fools, they should be patient with Paul, who is a fool.

Questions.Q: What is Paul complaining about?
Questions.A: The Corinthians are patient with lying teachers who treat them cruelly, but they are not patient with Paul, who loves them very much.

Questions.Q: Is Paul really ashamed that he was not like the lying teachers?
Questions.A: No, he is being ironical.
Questions.Note: N.B. Is this clear? If not make alterations.

Questions.Q: What are the ways in which Paul is equal to the lying teachers?
Questions.A: Like them, he is a Hebrew, an Israelite, a descendant of Abraham, a servant of Christ.

Questions.Q: In what ways is Paul better than the lying teachers?
Questions.A: 1. He has worked harder than them.
2. He has been imprisoned more times than them.
3. He has been beaten many times without number.
4. He has faced death many times.
5. Five times he has been given 39 lashes of a whip by the Jews.
6. Three times the Romans have beaten him with sticks.
7. Once they threw stones at him.
8. Three times he has been shipwrecked in which he once spent a day and a night in the water.

Questions.Q: Who were Paul's enemies on his journeys?
Questions.A: Thieves, and Jews, and non-Jews and lying fellow Christians were Paul's enemies.

Questions.Q: Where did he meet danger?
Questions.A: In towns, on roads between towns, and on the sea, in fact, everywhere that he traveled.

Questions.Q: What other troubles did he suffer on his journeys?
Questions.A: Paul suffered hard work, lack of sleep, hunger, thirst and cold.

Questions.Q: What other things troubled Paul on his journeys?
Questions.A: His watching over the churches and their troubles. If any church member's faith is weak, he weeps for him; if any has fallen into sin, his heart grieves for him.

Questions.Q: Why is Paul not ashamed of all the sufferings he has suffered?
Questions.A: Paul is not ashamed of all the sufferings he has suffered because they are all for Christ's sake and because he truly follows him.

Questions.Q: Discuss: If someone says that he knows that he is a good follower of Christ because God has blessed him with riches and a sweet life, how will you answer him from Paul's life and travels?
What does this verse show about a true pastor?
Questions.A: He loves his church people and sympathizes with them in their troubles.

Questions.Q: How does Paul's boasting contrast with that of the lying teachers?
Questions.A: He boasts of the things that show that he is weak. They boast of things that show they are strong.

Questions.Q: Why are the things that Paul boasts of more valuable than what the lying teachers boast of?
Questions.A: Because they are the kind of sufferings that Jesus Christ himself suffered.

Questions.Q: Discuss: When you read this account of Paul's escape from Damascus, do you want to laugh or cry? Do you see it as a time when Paul was weak or strong, wise or foolish? (See Acts 9:21-23.)

Section.heading: 2 Corinthians 12:1-10 Concerning some visions/revelations that God revealed to Paul.

Questions.Q: Describe the revelations that God gave to Paul 14 years before this.
Questions.A: God took him very high up, whether his body and soul, or only his soul he cannot tell, and he heard sweet things that he cannot tell in words, nor is he, as a human being, permitted to tell them.

Questions.Q: Why does he boast of that revelation and not of other things?
Questions.A: That vision was something only God revealed to him. He did nothing to deserve it. He can only say how weak he is.

Questions.Q: What other things is it not right to boast about?
Questions.A: It is not right to ask for praise from people for something which they have not seen us do or heard us say. So it is not right for him to boast of things that only he knows about or has seen.

Questions.Q: How did God make sure that Paul did not boast about these revelations?
Questions.A: By letting a messenger of the Devil hurt his body with something like a thorn.

Questions.Q: What do you understand this to be?
