Questions.A: Probably it was a painful sickness that troubled him from time to time.

Questions.Q: From this verse, how do you understand the source of pain and suffering?
Questions.A: It comes from the Devil but only with God's permission.

Questions.Q: Will God always answer our prayer that he cure our sicknesses?
Questions.A: God is in control. Therefore he can answer yes or no. If it is his will that we go on suffering, he will let us get weak in order to give us much strength/help.

Questions.Q: What kind of help does God give?
Questions.A: God gives strength to endure suffering, to remain happy and to go on believing in him and his goodness.

Questions.Q: Why then can Paul boast of his weakness and sickness?
Questions.A: Paul can boast of his weakness and sickness because it is God who will help him and make his strength to remain in Paul during his weakness.

Questions.Q: Discuss: Is it strong men or weak men whom God enables to do his will in every way?
What makes Paul able to be happy to suffer weakness, insults, accusations, persecution and troubles?
Questions.A: 1. He suffers all these things for the sake of Christ.
2. In his suffering, God gives him strength.

Questions.Q: Discuss: Can a person suffer trouble and it is not for Christ's sake, and be happy?

Section.heading: 2 Corinthians 12:11-21 Paul's great love for the Christians at Corinth.

Questions.Q: Why is Paul continuing to boast like a foolish man?
Questions.A: Because the Corinthians had said that he was nothing in comparison with those other apostles whom they greatly respected.

Questions.Q: When Paul lived among them at Corinth, what showed that he was a true apostle?
Questions.A: He did many miracles while suffering persecution patiently.

Questions.Q: Although he did these miracles among them, what do you think made some of the Corinthians despise him?
Questions.A: 1. His humility and timidity. 10-11
2. His inability to speak well. 11:6
3. His refusal to accept money from them for his food and lodging. 11:7 and 12:13
4. They thought he loved other churches better than Corinth. 12:13

Questions.Q: Discuss: Was it right for Paul to ask forgiveness from the Corinthians for not accepting food and lodging money from them? Had he done wrong?
What reasons does Paul give for his refusing money from them?
Questions.A: They are like his children. It is for parents to look after their children, not for children to look after their parents.

Questions.Q: What shows how much Paul loved the Corinthians?
Questions.A: He is willing for their sake to tire himself out and to spend all he has to help them.

Questions.Q: What hurts Paul in his love for them?
Questions.A: What hurts Paul in his love for them is that they do not love him in return.

Questions.Q: Against what accusation does Paul now defend himself?
Questions.A: That he used others to cheat the Corinthians.

Questions.Q: How does Paul show this to be a lie?
Questions.A: The persons he has sent them are Titus and one other, and Titus certainly is as honest as Paul, since he is Paul's fellow worker and they do everything together.

Questions.Q: What other accusations does Paul now defend himself against?
Questions.A: That he wants them to be judges of his case and to hear the defense that he has just given to their many accusations.

Questions.Q: What is his answer?
Questions.A: Because he is a Christian, and belongs to Christ, only God can be the judge of his case against them.

Questions.Q: What is the real purpose of Paul's letter to the Corinthians?
Questions.A: The purpose of Paul's letter to the Corinthians is to strengthen their faith in Christ.

Questions.Q: What is the use of this letter to us today?
Questions.A: That we may learn from it and that our faith may grow strong.

Questions.Q: If Paul goes to Corinth to greet them again, what is he afraid that he will find?
Questions.A: That among the Corinthians there will be quarrelling, jealousy, anger, divisions, slander, gossip, arrogance, and disrespect, adultery and every kind of sin.

Questions.Q: Why will Paul be ashamed?
Questions.A: He has boasted to others that the Corinthians have done well in their Christian life. Perhaps he will find that it is untrue.

Questions.Q: What will add to Paul's grief over these sins?
Questions.A: Some have been sinning for a long time and have not repented despite warnings.

Section.heading: 2 Corinthians 13:1-10 Paul's last message to them.

Questions.Q: When Paul comes to Corinth again, how will he judge the cases of sin-doers?
Questions.A: 1. Fairly. At least two witnesses are needed to prove every accusation.
2. He will not be lenient or soft.

Questions.Q: What further proof will Paul show when he comes to Corinth again, that Christ speaks through him?
Questions.A: He will not fear to punish unrepentant sin-doers.

Questions.Q: Was Christ weak or strong? What is Paul's teaching?
Questions.A: Christ had God's power, but he allowed men to crucify him and God raised him to life again, and again gave him his power.

Questions.Q: In what way is Paul imitating Christ's life?
Questions.A: Just as Christ allowed men to be cruel to him, so Paul suffers persecution. But just as Christ had power after his resurrection so Paul had power to judge the Corinthians.

Questions.Q: How can we, as Christians, see whether we are following Christ?
Questions.A: We should see whether Christ is truly in our hearts.

Questions.Q: How does this self-judgment help Paul in his case against the Corinthians?
Questions.A: If they can truly say that Christ is in their hearts, they should see also that Christ is in Paul.

Questions.Q: For what two reasons does Paul want them to repent of their sins?
Questions.A: 1. So that he will not have to punish them.
2. So as to make him happy.

Questions.Q: What reason is not important to him?
Questions.A: That their good life shows that Paul has done well in his work for God.

Questions.Q: Why cannot Paul fight against the truth?
Questions.A: Whatever is the truth pleases him. So even if it should show that he is wrong and the Corinthians right, that pleases him.

Questions.Q: What again shows Paul's love for the Corinthians?
Questions.A: 1. He prefers to use his authority as an apostle not to punish them, but to cause their faith to increase.
2. He only wants them to become true Christians, whatever happens to him.

Questions.Q: What kind of life does Paul want the Corinthians to live?
Questions.A: A happy life, aiming to be true Christians: helping one another, being united and living in peace.

Section.heading: 2 John 1-3 John greeted the recipients of his letter.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what John said in these verses.
Questions.A: John wrote this letter to a lady chosen [by God] and to her children. (1)
He told them that God the Father, and his Son, Jesus Christ will continue to show favor to them. (3)

Questions.Q: What do you think "God the Father" means?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that God is the father of Jesus Christ and of anyone who accepts Jesus as their Savior and Lord.
Questions.Note: See "God the Father" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think the title "God the Father" means?
What do you think the term "God the Father" means?

Questions.Q: What do you think is the meaning of "Christ"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "Christ" is the English rendering of the Greek word Christos, which means "anointed one."
Questions.Note: See "Christ" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to bless someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means to make someone happy, to give good fortune or satisfaction, to confer prosperity upon someone.
Questions.Note: See "bless" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did John call himself?
Questions.A: He called himself the elder. (1)

Questions.Q: What do you think an elder is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: An elder is a leader in the Christian church.

Questions.Q: How did John feel about that lady and her children?
Questions.A: He loved that lady and her children because they believed God's true message. (1-2)

Questions.Q: Who else loved that lady and her children?
Questions.A: Other Christians loved that lady and her children. (1)

Questions.Q: How long will they know God's true message?
Questions.A: They will always know God's true message. (2)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for something to be eternal?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that it will last forever/it will never end.

Questions.Q: In what ways will God the Father and the Son show favor to them/show them favor?
Questions.A: They will favor them with grace, mercy, and peace. (3)
Questions.Alternative: In what ways will God the Father and the Son show favor to them?
In what ways will God the Father and the Son show them favor?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to have/use grace?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that a person shows that he accepts and loves another person even when they do not deserve it.
Questions.Note: See "grace" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think it means to have grace?
What do you think it means for someone to have grace?
What do you think it means for someone to experience grace?
What do you think it means to use grace?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when someone is merciful to someone else?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "Mercy" in the New Testament is an act of kindness by God or someone else toward people who are in need. The person (God or man) acts to relieve some kind of suffering or distress.
Questions.Note: See "mercy" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to be at peace?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: To be at peace is to have a mental or spiritual condition marked by freedom of disquieting or oppressive thoughts or emotions.
Questions.Note: See "peace" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What affect will God's favor have upon their lives?
Questions.A: They may experience God's favor as they put into practice God's true message they have learned from him
and as they love one another. (3)
Questions.Note: This interpretation was taken from Translator's Notes.

Section.heading: 2 John 4-6 John encouraged the Christians to continue loving each other.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what John said in these verses.
Questions.A: John asked them to love one another. (5)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when someone loves someone else?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The person who loves another person seeks the good of that person. His attitude to the one whom he loves is an attitude of persistent and selfless goodwill.
Questions.Note: See "love" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did John say had made him very happy?
Questions.A: He was happy that some of the lady's children were living according to what God wanted them to do. (4)

Questions.Q: What did John write the lady about?
Questions.A: He wrote her about a command. (5)

Questions.Q: What do you think a commandment is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It is a definite and official order given by one person to another to carry out.

Questions.Q: How long did they have this command?
Questions.A: They had this command since they first heard the message about Jesus Christ. (5)

Questions.Q: How do we show love to others?
Questions.A: We show love to others by doing the things God tells us to do. (6)

Questions.Q: What have they heard from the beginning?
Questions.A: They have heard God's command to love one another. (6)

Section.heading: 2 John 7-13 John warned the Christians about false teachers who will come to them and tell them things that Christ did not teach to them. Those teachers do not believe that Jesus is the son of God.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what John said in these verses.
Questions.A: He told the Christians to watch out for those who want to deceive them with their false teachings. (7)

Questions.Q: Where did John say many deceivers have gone?
Questions.A: They have gone out into the world. (7)

Questions.Q: What do you think this verse means by the "world"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It is all the people who live on the earth.
Questions.Note: See "world" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did those deceivers teach?
Questions.A: They taught that Jesus Christ did not come as a human being. (7)

Questions.Q: What do you think he meant by "flesh" in this verse?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He meant that Jesus came into this world as a physical human being.
Questions.Note: See "flesh" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did John call a person who does not believe that Jesus Christ came as a human being?
Questions.A: He called a person like this the deceiver and the antichrist/an enemy of Christ. (7)

Questions.Q: What do you think the antichrist is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The meaning is probably "one who opposes the Christ (the Messiah)". Christians have been taught to expect one particular person, the antichrist, a man who would have supernatural power from Satan.
Questions.Note: See "antichrist" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: Who do you think the antichrist is?

Questions.Q: What did John tell the Christians?
Questions.A: He warned them to watch out/to be very careful [that they were not deceived by those who would try to lead them astray]. (8)

Questions.Q: For what were they to watch out?
Questions.A: They were to watch/be careful that they did not lose/give up their reward from God. (8)

Questions.Q: What did John say they were to do?
Questions.A: They were to make sure that they will receive their full reward [from God]. (8)

Questions.Q: What did John say about anyone who does not stay with/follow the things that Christ taught?
Questions.A: That person does not have God/fellowship with God. (9)
Questions.Alternative: What did John say about anyone who does not stay with the things that Christ taught?
What did John say about anyone who does not follow the things that Christ taught?

Questions.Q: Who do you think God is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In English, the term "God" with a capital "G" is used to refer to the one supreme Creator. The term "god" with a small "g", as in "a god" or "many gods", can refer to any spiritual being that people worship. The Greek word theos can be used in the same two ways.
Questions.Note: In many languages the term for God is a proper name and cannot be used to refer to anyone except the one supreme creator of the world. It cannot be pluralized. (Or, if it can be pluralized, the meaning may be something very different from the English "gods". In one language, the plural form of God, meant "God and those who follow him" and was an appropriate way to translate "saints".) (See "God" in KBT.)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to have fellowship with someone else?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The word "fellowship" refers to a relationship between two or more people who all have something in common or who participate in the same activity. The same Greek word may also be translated in certain contexts as "sharing", "participation", or "partnership".
Questions.Note: See "fellowship" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Who did John say has fellowship with both God and his Son?
Questions.A: He said those who follow the true teachings [of Christ] have fellowship with God and his Son. (9)

Questions.Q: What did John say they were to do when people came to their homes who do not follow the teachings [of Christ]?
Questions.A: They were not to invite them into their homes.
They were not to welcome them/greet them. (10)
Questions.Alternative: What did John say they were to do when people came to their homes who do not follow the teachings of Christ?
What did John say they were to do when people came to their homes who do not follow the teachings?

Questions.Q: What did John say about anyone who welcomes those who do not follow the teachings [of Christ]?
Questions.A: He said that anyone who does this is actually helping the [deceivers] do their wicked work. (11)
Questions.Alternative: What did John say about anyone who welcomes those who do not follow the teachings of Christ?
What did John say about anyone who welcomes those who do not follow the teachings?

Questions.Q: What did John say he still wanted to tell them?
Questions.A: He said he had a lot he wanted to tell them. (12)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that he did not say everything in this letter?
Questions.A: He said he wanted, rather, to visit with them and talk with them personally. (12)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to hope in something?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means to have a desire to see something happen or to obtain something.

Questions.Q: What was his reason for wanting to visit with them face to face?
Questions.A: He wanted to make them very happy, as well as to make himself happy. (12)

Questions.Q: Who also sent greetings to the lady?
Questions.A: The children of the lady's sister who is chosen [by God] sent greetings. (13)

Section.heading: 2 Peter 1:1-11 God's divine power has given us everything [all the resources] that we need to live a Christian life. Peter encouraged the Christians to make use of what God had given them, so that they would become better Christians.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what Peter said in these verses.
Questions.A: Peter told how God wants believers to live. (5-8)

Questions.Q: Who wrote this letter?
Questions.A: Peter. (1)

Questions.Q: What did Peter say about himself?
Questions.A: He said that he was a servant.
He also said that he was an apostle of Jesus Christ. (1)

Questions.Q: What do you think a servant does?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A servant is a person who is required to work for another person and obey him. Servants are usually paid for their work, while slaves are not paid.
Questions.Note: See "servant" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think an apostle does?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The general meaning of the Greek word apostolos is "envoy", "appointed representative", "someone who is sent on a mission". In the New Testament it develops the specific sense of an appointed representative of Jesus Christ. In Acts and the rest of the New Testament, the term "apostle" is the most common term that is used to refer to those who were commissioned by Jesus Christ to be founders of the church, and who then took up that function and position.
Questions.Note: See "apostle" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think is the meaning of "Christ"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: "Christ" is the English rendering of the Greek word Christos, which means "anointed one."
Questions.Note: See "Christ" in KBT.

Questions.Q: To whom did Peter write this letter?
Questions.A: He wrote it to those who had believed in Jesus Christ. (1)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to have faith in someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Faith is the quality of trusting someone. It is the act of wholeheartedly and steadfastly believing in the existence, power, and benevolence of a supreme being. (See "faith" in KBT in the "believe, believing, belief, faith, trust" entry.)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they believed in Jesus Christ?
Questions.A: Jesus Christ caused them to believe, since God and Jesus Christ are just/righteous. (1)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for God/Jesus Christ to be righteous?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It is God's activity of putting things right, especially of bringing people into good standing with himself.
Questions.Note: In this sense "the righteousness of God" describes God's powerful action of bringing about what is right, with reference to saving people from their sin. (See "righteousness" in KBT in the "just, justify..." entry.)
Questions.Alternative: What do you think it means for God to be righteous?
What do you think it means for Jesus Christ to be righteous?

Questions.Q: Who do you think God is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In English, the term "God" with a capital "G" is used to refer to the one supreme Creator. The term "god" with a small "g", as in "a god" or "many gods", can refer to any spiritual being that people worship. The Greek word theos can be used in the same two ways.
Questions.Note: In many languages the term for God is a proper name and cannot be used to refer to anyone except the one supreme creator of the world. It cannot be pluralized. (Or, if it can be pluralized, the meaning may be something very different from the English "gods". In one language, the plural form of God, meant "God and those who follow him" and was an appropriate way to translate "saints".) (See "God" in KBT.)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to be a savior?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The personal noun "Savior" (Greek sôtêr) is used in the New Testament to mean "one who saves from spiritual and eternal danger". It may refer to either God or Jesus Christ.
Questions.Note: See "savior" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think it means for someone to be a saviour?

Questions.Q: What was Peter's wish/desire for those to whom he was writing?
Questions.A: His desire was that God continue to help them very much and cause them to be peaceful in [their hearts]. (2)
Questions.Alternative: What was Peter's wish for those to whom he was writing?
What was Peter's desire for those to whom he was writing?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to have/use grace?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that a person shows that he accepts and loves another person even when they do not deserve it.
Questions.Note: See "grace" in KBT.
Questions.Alternative: What do you think it means to have grace?
What do you think it means for someone to have grace?
What do you think it means for someone to experience grace?
What do you think it means to use grace?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to be at peace?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: To be at peace is to have a mental or spiritual condition marked by freedom of disquieting or oppressive thoughts or emotions.
Questions.Note: See "peace" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What does it mean to you to have someone as your lord?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A lord is someone who has power and exercises it responsibly. To call someone your lord means that you have given them control over your life. The Lord in this case is Jesus. Every Christian strives to make Jesus lord in his or her life by giving Him complete control. (See "Lord" in KBT in the "God" entry.)

Questions.Q: What has [Jesus Christ] given to us believers?
Questions.A: He has given us everything we need to live a righteous/good life. (3)
Questions.Alternative: What has Jesus Christ given to us believers?
What has given to us believers?

Questions.Q: How was he able to do this?
Questions.A: He could do this because of his great/innate power. (3)

Questions.Q: How do we actually obtain the help/things we need to live this righteous/good life?
Questions.A: We obtain those things through knowing [God] who called us. (3)
Questions.Alternative: How do we actually obtain the help we need to live this righteous life?
How do we actually obtain the help we need to live this good life?
How do we actually obtain the things we need to live this righteous life?
How do we actually obtain the things we need to live this good life?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that he called us?
Questions.A: He called/chose us to be a part of who he is. He wanted us to know how wonderful and good he is. (3)

Questions.Q: What do you think God's glory means?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: UBS states that "glory" here should be understood as the very nature or the very person of God, whom people praise, and to the privilege God gives his people of sharing the praise God receives.
Questions.Note: See "glory" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What has God given us [believers] because of his glory and goodness?
Questions.A: God has given us his great and precious gifts/grace/help which he had promised. (4)
Questions.Alternative: What has God given believers because of his glory and goodness?
What has God given us believers because of his glory and goodness?
What has God given us because of his glory and goodness?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to make a promise?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that someone will make a declaration that he will do or refrain from doing something specified. (See "promise" in KBT in the "covenant" entry.)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that God gave his promised grace/help to us?
Questions.A: He did this in order that we not do bad deeds as unbelievers do.
He also did this in order that we become like Him. (4)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that God gave his promised grace to us?
What is the reason that God gave his promised help to us?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that they should, in addition to believing/having faith, also do the things mentioned in verse 5-7?
Questions.A: Because they are becoming like God, [they should strive to do these things in order to make their believing/faith mature]. (5)
Questions.Note: UBS states "For this reason" refers back to verses 3 and 4.
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that they should, in addition to believing, also do the things mentioned in verse 5-7?
What is the reason that they should, in addition to having faith, also do the things mentioned in verse 5-7?

Questions.Q: If they believe/have faith, what must they also do/add to it?
Questions.A: They must also do/show good [to others]. (5)
Questions.Alternative: If they believe, what must they also do?
If they believe, what must they also add to it?
If they have faith, what must they also do?
If they have faith, what must they also add to it?

Questions.Q: In addition to doing good [to others], what else must/should they do?
Questions.A: They should increase their knowledge [of what is required of them to live as believers and how to do it]. (5)
Questions.Alternative: In addition to doing good to others, what else must they do?
In addition to doing good to others, what else should they do?
In addition to doing good, what else must they do?
In addition to doing good, what else should they do?

Questions.Q: In addition to having goodness and knowledge, what other things must they strive to do/obtain?
Questions.A: They should control themselves.
They should endure their sufferings.
They should do what God wants [godliness].
They should deal kindly with others [brotherly kindness].
They should show love to others. (6-7)
Questions.Alternative: In addition to having goodness and knowledge, what other things must they strive to do?
In addition to having goodness and knowledge, what other things must they strive to obtain?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when someone loves someone else?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The person who loves another person seeks the good of that person. His attitude to the one whom he loves is an attitude of persistent and selfless goodwill.
Questions.Note: See "love" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What will happen if they continue to do/have these/those things?
Questions.A: They will know Jesus Christ better. (8)
Questions.Alternative: What will happen if they continue to do these things?
What will happen if they continue to do those things?
What will happen if they continue to have these things?
What will happen if they continue to have those things?

Questions.Q: If someone does not have these/those things/does not do these/those things, what does it show about him?
Questions.A: It shows that he has forgotten that [God] has forgiven him when he sinned in the past. (9)
Questions.Alternative: If someone does not have these things, what does it show about him?
If someone does not have those things, what does it show about him?
If someone does not do these things, what does it show about him?
If someone does not do those things, what does it show about him?

Questions.Q: What does a person do when he sins?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He deliberately keeps on doing those things that please himself and displease God.
Questions.Note: See "sin" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What should the fellow believers do, so that they will be sure to do/have all of the above qualities and not forget that God has forgiven them?
Questions.A: They should strive to show/prove by what they do that God has chosen them to be his people and called them to follow him. (10)
Questions.Alternative: What should the fellow believers do, so that they will be sure to do all of the above qualities and not forget that God has forgiven them?
What should the fellow believers do, so that they will be sure to have all of the above qualities and not forget that God has forgiven them?

Questions.Q: Of what can they be sure, if they do this?
Questions.A: They can be sure that they will never fall/stop believing/abandon their faith [in God]. (10)

Questions.Q: If they never stop believing/abandon their faith, but instead prove that God has chosen and called them, what will happen in the end/finally?
Questions.A: [God] will welcome them to live forever where Christ will rule forever. (11)
Questions.Alternative: If they never stop believing, but instead prove that God has chosen and called them, what will happen in the end?
If they never stop believing, but instead prove that God has chosen and called them, what will finally happen?
If they never abandon their faith, but instead prove that God has chosen and called them, what will happen in the end?
If they never abandon their faith, but instead prove that God has chosen and called them, what will finally happen?

Questions.Q: What do you think the kingdom of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means for Christians/believers to enter God's rule in the future only. UBS states, "The place where our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ rules eternally".
Questions.Note: See "kingdom of God" in KBT.

Section.heading: 2 Peter 1:12-21 Peter told the Christians that he would continue to remind them of all that God had given to them to help them live Christian lives.

Questions.Q: What did Peter say that he would do as long as he lived?
Questions.A: He would continue to remind them of the things he had been telling them. (12-13)

Questions.Q: How did they know that Peter [and the other apostles] were not making up stories when they told them about the power/might of the Lord Jesus Christ and of his coming/return?
Questions.A: Peter [and the other apostles] had been eyewitnesses of his greatness. (16)
Questions.Alternative: How did they know that Peter was not making up stories when they told them about the power of the Lord Jesus Christ and of his coming?
How did they know that Peter was not making up stories when they told them about the power of the Lord Jesus Christ and of his return?
How did they know that Peter was not making up stories when they told them about the might of the Lord Jesus Christ and of his coming?
How did they know that Peter was not making up stories when they told them about the might of the Lord Jesus Christ and of his return?
How did they know that Peter and the other apostles were not making up stories when they told them about the power of the Lord Jesus Christ and of his coming?
How did they know that Peter and the other apostles were not making up stories when they told them about the power of the Lord Jesus Christ and of his return?
How did they know that Peter and the other apostles were not making up stories when they told them about the might of the Lord Jesus Christ and of his coming?
How did they know that Peter and the other apostles were not making up stories when they told them about the might of the Lord Jesus Christ and of his return?

Questions.Q: What did they already know?
Questions.A: They already knew the things he had been telling them about. (12)

Questions.Q: How well did they know those things?
Questions.A: They knew that what they had been taught was the truth. (12)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Peter was so insistent on reminding them about these/those things?
Questions.A: He knew that he was going to die soon
and he wanted them to have a way to remember the things/what he had told them they must do. (14-15)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that Peter was so insistent on reminding them about these things?
What is the reason that Peter was so insistent on reminding them about those things?

Questions.Q: How did Peter know that he was going to die soon?
Questions.A: The Lord Jesus Christ had told/revealed it to him. (14)

Questions.Q: What had Peter and [the other apostles] actually seen and heard?
Questions.A: They saw and heard that God really/truly honored Christ. (17-18)
Questions.Alternative: What had Peter and the other apostles actually seen and heard?
What had Peter and actually seen and heard?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when you honor someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: To honor someone is to show high regard or appreciation for them.

Questions.Q: Where were Peter and [the other apostles] when they saw this and heard God speaking?
Questions.A: They were on the mountain where God was also present. (17-18)
Questions.Alternative: Where were Peter and the other apostles when they saw this and heard God speaking?
Where were Peter and when they saw this and heard God speaking?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for something to be holy?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Anything that is "holy" is set apart [by God] and dedicated to the service or worship of God. Anything that is "holy" for God must reflect his character by being physically unblemished or reflecting, to some degree, his purity.
Questions.Note: See "holy" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Where did the voice come from?
Questions.A: It came from God. (17-18)
Questions.Note: UBS states that "majestic glory" is a euphemism for God and is used in order to avoid mentioning the divine name.

Questions.Q: What was shown by what happened on the holy mountain?
Questions.A: It showed that the words/prediction of the prophets were true. (19)

Questions.Q: What do you know about prophets?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A prophet is someone who speaks for God and is inspired by Him. He often foretells future events. Prophets were mainly spokespersons who called His people to obedience by appealing to Israel's past and future.
Questions.Note: See "prophet" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What is the reason that it was important for them to pay attention to what the prophets said?
Questions.A: They should pay attention to them because what they said is like a lamp shining in a dark place. (19)

Questions.Q: In what way do you think what the prophets said is like a lamp?
Questions.A: It helps people to know how to live correctly, and it helps them to know the truth.

Questions.Q: How long should they pay attention to the prophets message?
Questions.A: They should pay attention to the message until Christ returns. (19)

Questions.Q: What does it mean to you to talk about the "heart"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The most common use of the word "heart" in the Bible is to refer to the spiritual center or innermost part of a human being. In Hebrew and Greek "heart" is most commonly associated with thoughts and ideas.
Questions.Note: See "heart" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did Peter say about all prophecy of scripture?
Questions.A: He said that all prophecy was not created by the prophets. (20)

Questions.Q: To what do you think Peter was referring as "scripture"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The scriptures are the contents of the O.T. as God gave them to men to write down.
Questions.Note: See "scripture" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do you think a prophecy is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A prophecy is a message from God that is given through the mouth of a prophet, an inspired message. (See "prophecy" in KBT in the "prophet" entry.)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that this is true?
Questions.A: Everything that they have prophesied/predicted did not simply come from their own minds/thoughts, but they spoke God's message as they were controlled by the Holy Spirit. (21)

Questions.Q: Who do you think the Holy Spirit is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: He is God's spirit, through whom he acts, reveals His will, and empowers individuals. (See "Holy Spirit" in KBT in the "spirit" entry.)

Section.heading: 2 Peter 2:1-22 Peter warned the Christians about false teachers that will come to them to teach them false doctrines and immoral ways of living. He knew that the false teachers could cause the Christians not to believe correctly in God.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what Peter said in these verses.
Questions.A: Peter warned those to whom he was writing to beware of false teachers. (1)

Questions.Q: In the past God spoke/communicated his message to his people through the prophets he sent. What happened then?
Questions.A: There were also false prophets who came [and taught/told the people lies]. (1)
Questions.Alternative: In the past God spoke his message to his people through the prophets he sent. What happened then?
In the past God communicated his message to his people through the prophets he sent. What happened then?

Questions.Q: What do you think a false prophet did?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A false prophet was a person who claimed to be a prophet of God but was not. His messages were deceptive and led to confusion. (See "false prophet" in KBT in the "prophet" entry.)

Questions.Q: Just as there were false prophets among the people in the past, what did Peter say will happen in the future?
Questions.A: There will also be false teachers among them. (1)

Questions.Q: What will these false teachers teach?
Questions.A: They will teach lies that will cause the believers not to believe Christ correctly. (1)

Questions.Q: Even though the Lord Jesus died for them, what will these false teachers do?
Questions.A: They will deny/reject him. (1)

Questions.Q: What will happen to these false teachers because of what they teach?
Questions.A: They will be punished soon [by God]. (1)

Questions.Q: Even though these false teachers teach lies, what will many people do?
Questions.A: Many people will imitate them to do evil things/to live evilly. (2)

Questions.Q: What will happen because of the bad conduct of those who follow the teachings of the false teachers?
Questions.A: Other people will speak disreputably about the gospel/about the truth that Jesus taught. (2)

Questions.Q: What will these false teachers [try to] do by/with their lies?
Questions.A: They will tell stories that they have made up [in order to get the money/property of those they teach]. (3)
Questions.Alternative: What will these false teachers try to do by their lies?
What will these false teachers try to do with their lies?
What will these false teachers do by their lies?
What will these false teachers do with their lies?

Questions.Q: What did [God] decide, long ago, to do to these false teachers?
Questions.A: [God] decided to condemn and punish them. (3)
Questions.Alternative: What did God decide, long ago, to do to these false teachers?
What fate was determined long ago for these false teachers?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means if/that someone condemns someone else?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that someone pronounces someone else guilty with the clear implication that the person will be punished for what he did. (See "condemn" in KBT in the "judge, judgment" entry.)
Questions.Alternative: What do you think it means if someone condemns someone else?
What do you think it means that someone condemns someone else?

Questions.Q: What did God do to the angels who sinned?
Questions.A: He threw them into hell. (4)

Questions.Q: What do you know about the angels who sinned?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: They are those fallen angels/spirit beings who sided with Satan against God, who fell with Satan from heaven, and who now serve him.
Questions.Note: (See "angel" in KBT.)

Questions.Q: What do you know about hell?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It is a place where those who have rejected the Lord will spend eternity. It is a place where there is constant pain and darkness.
Questions.Note: See "hell" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What are those angels doing there?
Questions.A: They are held in a darkness that is like chains, waiting for the time they will be judged [by God]. (4)

Questions.Q: What other example did Peter give to show that God does not spare the wicked but instead punishes them?
Questions.A: He gave the example of the godless people living long ago during the time of Noah. (5)

Questions.Q: What did God do to all those godless people?
Questions.A: He brought a flood upon them [and drowned them/they drowned]. (5)

Questions.Q: Who were the only ones whom God saved from this flood?
Questions.A: Noah and his seven [companions/relatives] were the only ones who survived the flood. (5)

Questions.Q: What kind of a person was Noah?
Questions.A: He preached righteousness/what was good/the right way to live. (5)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to be righteous?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that a person is in a state of having been accepted by God as right in his eyes. (See "righteousness" in KBT in the "just, justify..." entry.)

Questions.Q: What did God do to the wicked people living in Sodom and Gomorrah?
Questions.A: He destroyed them when he burned their cities to ashes. (6)

Questions.Q: What does this example teach/show us?
Questions.A: It shows us that God punishes the godless. (6)
Questions.Alternative: What does this example teach us?
What does this example show us?

Questions.Q: How many people, who were living in Sodom and Gomorrah, did God destroy?
Questions.A: He destroyed everyone except Lot. (7)

Questions.Q: What kind of person was Lot?
Questions.A: He was a righteous/good man. (7)

Questions.Q: How did Lot feel about the immoral conduct of the lawless people he lived among?
Questions.A: He was distressed about it. (7)

Questions.Q: What specifically caused Lot to be distressed as he lived among these lawless people day after day?
Questions.A: He was distressed by the evil/criminal things he saw these people doing
and the evil things he heard them saying. (8)

Questions.Q: What do you think the soul is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It is a person's inner being the self. The self in its relationship with God.
Questions.Note: See "soul" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What does the way in which God dealt with those good and those bad people mentioned above teach us?
Questions.A: It teaches us that the Lord knows how to rescue godly people from their trials and that he will judge and punish wicked people. (9)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to judge someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means someone/a judge will determine if a person is guilty or not of committing a crime. He does this by assessing the evidence connected to the person and what he may have done.
Questions.Note: See "judge" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Who will God especially punish?
Questions.A: He will punish those who do bad things that they desired to do and who despise [God's] authority. (10a)

Questions.Q: What is the character of these false teachers?
Questions.A: They are bold and arrogant. (10b)

Questions.Q: How do they show this/their arrogance?
Questions.A: They are not afraid to slander/offend celestial beings. (10b)
Questions.Alternative: How do they show this arrogance?
How do they show their arrogance?

Questions.Q: Who are the angels much mightier and stronger than?
Questions.A: They are stronger than those false teachers. (11)
Questions.Note: This could be interpreted different ways. They could be stronger than the false teachers or stronger than the celestial beings. See UBS.

Questions.Q: What do you know about angels?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Angels are spiritual messengers who either deliver a message to humans, carry out God's will, praise God, or guard God's throne.
Questions.Note: See "angel" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What do the angels refuse to do, even though they are much mightier and stronger than those false teachers?
Questions.A: They refuse to offend celestial beings in the presence of the Lord. (11)
Questions.Note: This could be interpreted different ways. The angels refuse to offend the celestial beings or they refuse to offend the false teachers. (See UBS.)

Questions.Q: What are those people like who teach lies?
Questions.A: They are like wild animals whose lot/fate is to be caught/hunted and killed [by men]. (12)

Questions.Q: What will happen to those people, since they are depraved and attack with insults anything they do not understand?
Questions.A: They will be destroyed [by God] like people who kill wild animals. (12)

Questions.Q: What else will happen to those teachers who teach lies because of all the suffering they have caused others?
Questions.A: They will be repaid with suffering [by God]. (13)

Questions.Q: How do these people feel about the things that they do?
Questions.A: They enjoy doing openly all kinds of evil deeds. (13)

Questions.Q: What happens when those false teachers join the believers in their meals/love feasts?
Questions.A: They are a shame and a disgrace to them/the believers/to God. (13)
Questions.Alternative: What happens when those false teachers join the believers in their meals?
What happens when those false teachers join the believers in their love feasts?

Questions.Q: How do these false teachers conduct themselves among/act toward women?
Questions.A: Whenever they look at a women, they only have evil thoughts/wishes of committing adultery with her. (14)
Questions.Alternative: How do these false teachers conduct themselves among women?
How do these false teachers act toward women?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to commit adultery with another person?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: Adultery is the act of unfaithfulness in marriage that occurs when one of the marriage partners voluntarily engages in sexual intercourse with a person of the opposite sex who is not their marriage partner.

Questions.Q: What do these teachers seduce the unstable people to do?
Questions.A: They seduce them to commit sin. (14)
Questions.Note: This answer may not be derived easily from the context. See UBS.

Questions.Q: What will God do to them because of all the things that they did?
Questions.A: God will punish them. (14)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for God to put a curse on someone?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that God will pronounce a punishment on someone or condemn a person to be cut off from all of God's blessings. (See "curse" in KBT in the "bless, blessed, blessing" entry.)

Questions.Q: What have these false teachers left/abandoned?
Questions.A: They have left the true/good way. (15)
Questions.Alternative: What have these false teachers left?
What have these false teachers abandoned?

Questions.Q: Whose way have they followed instead?
Questions.A: They have followed the path/way of Balaam, the son of Beor. (15)

Questions.Q: Of what was Balaam guilty of doing?
Questions.A: He loved the money that he would get for doing wrong. (15)

Questions.Q: How was Balaam rebuked for the insane/evil things he was doing?
Questions.A: His donkey spoke with a human voice and rebuked him for what he was doing. (16)
Questions.Alternative: How was Balaam rebuked for the insane things he was doing?
How was Balaam rebuked for the evil things he was doing?

Questions.Q: What are those men [who teach lies] like?
Questions.A: They are like dried up springs
and clouds that are blown along by a storm because they are useless.
What they teach does not help anyone. (17)
Questions.Alternative: What are those men who teach lies like?
What are those men like?

Questions.Q: What will their ultimate fate/punishment be?
Questions.A: [God] will punish them in the dark pit [of hell]. (17)
Questions.Alternative: What will their ultimate fate be?
What will their ultimate punishment be?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that [God] will punish them like this/that?
Questions.A: He will punish them because of the proud and stupid statements they make and because of the seductive things they do and say. (17-18)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that God will punish them like this?
What is the reason that God will punish them like that?
What is the reason they will be punished like this?
What is the reason they will be punished like that?

Questions.Q: Who are those people that these/the false teachers can most easily influence into following their example/conduct?
Questions.A: They are new Christian converts who have recently escaped from their previous evil habits/way of life. (18)
Questions.Alternative: Who are those people that these false teachers can most easily influence into following their example?
Who are those people that these false teachers can most easily influence into following their conduct?
Who are those people that the false teachers can most easily influence into following their example?
Who are those people that the false teachers can most easily influence into following their conduct?

Questions.Q: What do these/the false teachers promise to those who follow their teachings?
Questions.A: They tell them that they will be free [to do whatever they want to do]. (19)
Questions.Alternative: What do these false teachers promise to those who follow their teachings?
What do the false teachers promise to those who follow their teachings?

Questions.Q: How do we know that what they say is a lie?
Questions.A: We know they lie because even these false teachers are not free but are themselves slaves to destructive habits/sins. (19)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to be a slave of someone/something?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means the person is totally responsible to and dependent upon another person, or the person has become completely subservient to a dominating influence. (See "slave" in KBT in the "servant, slave" entry.)
Questions.Alternative: What do you think it means to be a slave of someone?
What do you think it means to be a slave of something?

Questions.Q: What truth does their situation/conduct show/prove?
Questions.A: It shows that a person is a slave of anything that has conquered him/controls his life or what he does. (19)
Questions.Alternative: What truth does their situation show?
What truth does their situation prove?
What truth does their conduct show?
What truth does their conduct prove?

Questions.Q: What is the condition of those who have changed the way they live after they believe in Jesus, but then do what they did before they believed Jesus?
Questions.A: They are worse off at the end than they were in the beginning. (20)

Questions.Q: What would be better for anyone who has known what God wants him to do, but who stops obeying that which he had been taught?
Questions.A: It would have been better for them never to have known what God wanted him to do. (21)

Questions.Q: What do you think a commandment is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It is a definite and official order given by one person to another to carry out.

Questions.Q: What example did Peter give concerning false teachers and those who might follow them?
Questions.A: He quoted two proverbs; one about the tendency of a dog to return to what he has vomited up
and the other about how natural it is for a pig to go back to wallowing in the mire even if it has just been washed/bathed [by someone]. (22)

Section.heading: 2 Peter 3:1-18 The Lord will return to the earth to judge the people who reject God. So all Christians should be alert and not be led astray by the things that the false teachers are saying. Instead all Christians should try to live lives that are pleasing to the Lord.

Questions.Q: About what did Peter warn them?
Questions.A: Peter warned them that in the last times scoffers will come who will deny the second coming of Christ. (4)

Questions.Q: What kind of people did Peter say they should be?
Questions.A: They should live holy and godly lives/live lives completely dedicated to God. (11)

Questions.Q: How many letters did Peter write to those to whom he is now writing?
Questions.A: He wrote two letters to them. This is his second letter. (1)

Questions.Q: What was Peter's purpose in writing those letters to them?
Questions.A: His intention was to stimulate them to practice pure/correct thinking [doctrine]. (1)

Questions.Q: Of whose teachings did Peter want to remind them?
Questions.A: He reminded them of the predictions/teachings of the prophets of long ago
and the command from our Lord and Savior. (2)

Questions.Q: Who had taught these people the command of our Lord about which Peter was writing?
Questions.A: The apostles taught them. (2)

Questions.Q: What important thing should they be aware of that will happen in the last days?
Questions.A: Some people will come/appear who are controlled by their own evil desires. (3)

Questions.Q: What will these/those people do?
Questions.A: They will make fun of/ridicule [the believers]. (3)
Questions.Alternative: What will these people do?
What will those people do?

Questions.Q: In what way will they ridicule them?
Questions.A: They will make fun of the believers, saying that [Christ] promised to come but that he has not come. (4)

Questions.Q: How did they try to prove that Christ will not return?
Questions.A: They said that nothing about the world has changed since [God] created the world. (4)

Questions.Q: What fact did they deliberately forget?
Questions.A: They forgot that a long time ago, by God's command, the heavens were created and the earth was formed out of water and with water. (5)

Questions.Q: Where do you think these heavens are?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: UBS states that "heavens" here refers to the dome-like structure that is above the earth and shields the earth from the water that is above the dome.
Questions.Note: See "heaven" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What else did they deliberately forget?
Questions.A: They forgot that a long time ago [God] used water to flood the earth. (6)

Questions.Q: For what did Peter say the heavens and the earth are reserved?
Questions.A: They are reserved to be burned by fire when [God] will judge and punish ungodly people. (7)

Questions.Q: What did Peter tell the believers not to forget?
Questions.A: They should not forget that the Lord considers one day like a thousand years and a thousand years like one day. (8)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that the Lord has not fulfilled his promise [to send Christ back here yet]?
Questions.A: He is patient with everyone. He does not want anyone to perish. Instead he wants all people to repent and to believe him. (9)
Questions.Alternative: What is the reason that the Lord has not fulfilled his promise to send Christ back here yet?
What is the reason that the Lord has not fulfilled his promise?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when someone repents?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that the person regrets his sins and unbelief, turns from it, and follows God.
Questions.Note: See "repent" in KBT.

Questions.Q: How will the day of the Lord come?
Questions.A: He will come unexpectedly as a thief comes unexpectedly. (10)

Questions.Q: What will happen when he comes to judge?
Questions.A: The heavens will disappear with a roar,
the heavenly bodies will burn up,
and the earth and everything in it will vanish. (10)

Questions.Q: What did Peter say they should do as they wait for the day of God to come?
Questions.A: They should do their best to make it come soon. (12)

Questions.Q: When the heavens have burned up, what will happen to the heavenly bodies?
Questions.A: They will melt because of the intense heat. (12)
Questions.Alternative: When the heavens have burned up, what will happen to the elements?
When the heavens have burned up, what will happen to the things in the universe?
When the heavens have burned up, what will happen to all material things?
When the heavens have burned up, what will happen to all things?
When the heavens have burned up, what will happen to everything else?
When the heavens have burned up, what will happen to everything that makes up the universe?

Questions.Q: To what do we Christians/believers look forward?
Questions.A: We anticipate new heavens and a new earth where everyone will live according to God's will/live the way God wants them to live. (13)
Questions.Alternative: To what do we Christians look forward?
To what do we believers look forward?

Questions.Q: How do we know that this will happen?
Questions.A: [God] has promised us that it will happen. (13)

Questions.Q: What should they do as they wait for all these things to happen?
Questions.A: They should try their best not to sin
and be at peace with him/God. (14)

Questions.Q: What should we think/understand about the fact that the Lord is patient with us people?
Questions.A: He is patient with us because he wants to give us/sinners the opportunity to [repent, believe and] be saved. (15)
Questions.Alternative: What should we think about the fact that the Lord is patient with us people?
What should we understand about the fact that the Lord is patient with us people?

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to save you?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that a person will rescue someone else out of a dangerous situation. In this case Jesus came to man kind to rescue them from an eternity in Hell.
Questions.Note: See "save" in KBT.

Questions.Q: About what had Peter written them?
Questions.A: He wrote them about how they could be saved [from their sins]. (15)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Peter was able to write about this?
Questions.A: God had caused him to know what to write. (15)

Questions.Q: What had Peter written about in all his letters?
Questions.A: He wrote about how they could be saved. (16)

Questions.Q: What do some people, who are ignorant and unstable, do when they read and try to explain Peter's letters?
Questions.A: They distort the meaning of his letters just as they do the other passages of scripture. (16)

Questions.Q: What will happen to those people because they distort the meaning of the scriptures?
Questions.A: God will punish them. (16)

Questions.Q: What warning did Peter give to the people to whom he was writing?
Questions.A: He warned them to be on guard so they would not be led away/astray by the errors of lawless people. (17)

Questions.Q: What will happen to them if they should be led astray?
Questions.A: They will fall from their secure position/no longer believe Jesus Christ. (17)

Questions.Q: Instead of listening to those who teach the scriptures falsely, what should they do?
Questions.A: They should continue to experience the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. (18)

Questions.Q: Of what is Christ worthy?
Questions.A: We should continually praise Christ. (18)

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: This is a letter from Paul to the believers in Thessalonica.

Questions.Q: Who wrote this letter?
Questions.A: Paul. Silas and Timothy were not co-authors, but merely joined in the greeting.

Questions.Q: To whom is the letter written?
Questions.A: To the believers in the city of Thessalonica.

Questions.Q: What does Paul want God to do for them?
Questions.A: To bless them and give them peace.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul thanks God for them.
He tells others that the faith of the Thessalonian believers is very strong.

Questions.Q: Why does Paul say it is right for him to thank God frequently for them?
Questions.A: Because they are believing in God more and more.
Because they are loving one another more and more.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say he does?
Questions.A: He tells people in other churches about the Thessalonian believers.

Questions.Q: Why is Paul so glad to tell about them in other churches?
Questions.A: Even though the Thessalonians are being persecuted they continue to believe in God.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: God will judge all people justly.
He will do this when the Lord Jesus returns from heaven.

Questions.Q: Even though the Thessalonians are being persecuted, they continue to believe. What does Paul say this shows people?
Questions.A: That God will judge all people justly.

Questions.Q: How does their suffering show that?
Questions.A: God is using suffering to make them worthy/fit for his Kingdom; that is his reward for their suffering. Therefore, God is seen to be just by rewarding them, and punishing those who persecute them.

Questions.Q: When will God give relief to those who are now suffering?
Questions.A: When the Lord Jesus descends from heaven, accompanied by his powerful angels.

Questions.Q: Who will the Lord punish when he comes?
Questions.A: Those who are not God's people, and do not obey the gospel.

Questions.Q: What will their punishment be?
Questions.A: They will be banished forever from the presence of the Lord.
They will be banished forever from the glory God has because he is so powerful.
They will experience suffering forever.

Questions.Q: On that day, when the Lord comes back, what will those who believe in him do?
Questions.A: They will praise him and they will marvel because of what he has done for those who believed in him.

Questions.Q: Will the Thessalonians be there? Why?
Questions.A: Yes, they will be there, because they believed the message that Paul told them.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul prays that God will make them worthy of the kind of life he wants them to live.

Questions.Q: What does Paul ask God to do for the Thessalonians?
Questions.A: Make them worthy of the life he wants the believers to live.
Help them to live the way they desire to live.

Questions.Q: How will God do this?
Questions.A: By his power.

Questions.Q: Why does Paul so frequently pray this for the believers?
Questions.A: In order that their lives will make others praise the Lord.
In order that they will share in the Lord's glory.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: They should not believe false reports which say the Lord has already come back to earth.

Questions.Q: What was causing the Thessalonians to be confused/upset?
Questions.A: Some people were saying that the day of the Lord had already come.
Questions.Alternative: What was causing the Thessalonians to be confused?
What was causing the Thessalonians to be upset?

Questions.Q: Where did that wrong information come from?
Questions.A: People who claimed to have messages from the Holy Spirit.
People who claimed Paul had written that in some letters.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul tells them that the Lord will come back only after the final rebellion takes place, and after a certain wicked person appears.

Questions.Q: How can they know that the Lord has not yet come?
Questions.A: Before he comes many people will rebel against God.
A very wicked/lawless man will appear in the world.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say will be the end of this wicked/lawless man?
Questions.A: He will be destroyed.
Questions.Alternative: What does Paul say will be the end of this wicked man?
What does Paul say will be the end of this lawless man?

Questions.Q: When this man appears, what will he do?
Questions.A: He will oppose God in every way.
He will declare himself above God.

Questions.Q: Then what will he finally do?
Questions.A: He will publicly proclaim that he is God.

Questions.Q: Was this the first time Paul had told them those things?
Questions.A: No.

Questions.Q: When had he told them that before?
Questions.A: When he had been with them in Thessalonica.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: The wicked one will not appear until God allows it.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say here that he told them before?
Questions.A: This wicked one cannot be revealed now because he is being restrained.

Questions.Q: Who do you think is restraining him?
Questions.A: The Holy Spirit, the Lord Jesus, or God.

Questions.Q: What is already going on in this world?
Questions.A: Satan is secretly doing his work.

Questions.Q: What do you think his work might be?
Questions.A: Causing people to reject all law--both human law and God's divine law.

Questions.Q: When will Satan's work no longer be hidden/secret?
Questions.A: When the wicked one appears and works openly in the world.
Questions.Alternative: When will Satan's work no longer be hidden?
When will Satan's work no longer be secret?

Questions.Q: What will happen to the wicked one when the Lord Jesus comes?
Questions.A: The Lord will destroy him.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: The main purpose of the wicked one is to deceive those who will perish.

Questions.Q: From whom will the wicked one get his power?
Questions.A: From Satan.

Questions.Q: How will this power be revealed?
Questions.A: By the supernatural signs and amazing deeds that he will do.

Questions.Q: Who will he deceive?
Questions.A: Those who will perish.

Questions.Q: Why is Satan able to deceive them?
Questions.A: Because they have refused to believe God's true message.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say God will do?
Questions.A: He will send a delusion which will permit/cause people to believe those lies.

Questions.Q: What is God's purpose in doing that?
Questions.A: So that those who have chosen to do what is wicked will be justly punished by God.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: God chose the Thessalonians and called them to be saved and glorified.

Questions.Q: For what is Paul continually thanking God?
Questions.A: That God chose the Thessalonians to be saved.

Questions.Q: How/by what means were they saved?
Questions.A: The Holy Spirit set them apart.
They believed the true message.
Questions.Alternative: How were they saved?
By what means were they saved?

Questions.Q: From whom did they hear the true message?
Questions.A: From Paul.

Questions.Q: For what reason did God save them?
Questions.A: So that they would share the glory the Lord Jesus has.

Questions.Q: Now what does Paul urge them to do?
Questions.A: Continue believing what he has taught them.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: He prays that God will help them to continue doing what is good.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say the Lord Jesus Christ and God their Father has done for them?
Questions.A: Loved them.
Encouraged them.
Caused them to hope for/confidently look forward to what God has promised.

Questions.Q: What does Paul pray that God will do for them in their present situation?
Questions.A: Encourage them.
Help them to continue doing and speaking what is good.
Questions.Alternative: What does Paul want God to do for them?

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul asks the Thessalonians to pray that many more people will believe the message.

Questions.Q: In order that many more people will believe, what does Paul request the believers to do?
Questions.A: Pray for him and his companions.

Questions.Q: How should they pray?
Questions.A: That the message will spread rapidly, and that many people will respect it/honor it.

Questions.Q: Among whom had the message previously spread rapidly?
Questions.A: Among the Thessalonians.

Questions.Q: What else does Paul ask them to pray about?
Questions.A: That Paul would be rescued from those who oppose him.

Questions.Q: What is the reason they oppose him?
Questions.A: They do not believe the message.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: The Lord will surely give them inner strength, and protect them from the evil one.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say about the Lord here?
Questions.A: He is faithful/trustworthy.

Questions.Q: Because the Lord is faithful/trustworthy, what can the believers be sure he will do for them?
Questions.A: Protect them from the evil one.
Questions.Alternative: Because the Lord is faithful, what can the believers be sure he will do for them?
Because the Lord is trustworthy, what can the believers be sure he will do for them?

Questions.Q: How does Paul feel about the Thessalonians?
Questions.A: He has confidence in them.

Questions.Q: What does he say he is sure they are doing and will keep on doing?
Questions.A: Obeying what Paul has told them, and is telling them in this letter.

Questions.Q: What does Paul pray that the Lord will do for the Thessalonians?
Questions.A: Assure them of God's love.
Make them steadfast in their faith.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul tells them to dissociate themselves from any believer who refuses to work.
He commands those who are not working to settle down and earn their own living.
They should take note of anyone who does not obey Paul's commands.

Questions.Q: What command does Paul give here?
Questions.A: They should keep away from any believer who is lazy.

Questions.Q: By what authority does he give this command?
Questions.A: By the authority which the Lord has given him.

Questions.Q: How were Paul and his companions an example to the Thessalonians when they lived among them?
Questions.A: They did not expect others to support them.
Instead, they worked very hard in order to pay for whatever they received.

Questions.Q: Did Paul and his companions have a right to get food from the Thessalonians?
Questions.A: Yes.

Questions.Q: Why do you think so?
Questions.A: As teachers and apostles they had that right.

Questions.Q: Why, then, did they not use that right?
Questions.A: They wanted to provide an example for the Thessalonians to follow.

Questions.Q: When Paul previously lived with them what had he told them about working?
Questions.A: He had told them that if a believer refuses to work, then the other believers should not feed/support him.

Questions.Q: Why, then, is Paul telling them these things again?
Questions.A: He had been informed that some were not working at all; they were being a nuisance/interfering with others.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say to those who are not working?
Questions.A: He commands them to settle down and earn their own living.

Questions.Q: What does he say to those who are working?
Questions.A: They are doing right; he urges them not to become tired of doing it.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say they should do with anyone who will not work?
Questions.A: They should take note of him.
They should not associate with him.

Questions.Q: What will that accomplish in the person who is not working?
Questions.A: It will make him ashamed of his conduct.

Questions.Q: What should be the attitude in which the believers do that?
Questions.A: As to a brother who needs to be warned, not as to an enemy.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: He wants God to bless them.
He concludes his letter with greetings.

Questions.Q: Paul is concluding his letter. What does he say?
Questions.A: He prays that the Lord will give them peace at all times.

Questions.Q: Who does he say is the source of that inner peace?
Questions.A: The Lord Jesus.

Questions.Q: Why does Paul make it very clear that he is writing these final words in his own handwriting?
Questions.A: So that they would know it was truly from Paul.

Questions.Q: What does he want the Lord Jesus Christ to do for them?
Questions.A: Be with them all.
Continue to act graciously toward them/bless them.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul is writing a letter to Timothy.
He wants God to bless Timothy.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say about himself?
Questions.A: He is Jesus Christ's representative/apostle.

Questions.Q: What does Jesus Christ want Paul to tell people?
Questions.A: That God has promised that people could live eternally.

Questions.Q: How are people able to live eternally?
Questions.A: By being joined to Jesus Christ.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say about Timothy?
Questions.A: He loves him as if he were his own son.

Questions.Q: What does he want God to do for Timothy?
Questions.A: To bless him.
To be merciful to him.
To give him inner peace.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: He thanks God that Timothy sincerely believes in Christ Jesus.
He wants very much to see him.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say about God?
Questions.A: He is the one his ancestors also worshiped/served.

Questions.Q: How does Paul worship God?
Questions.A: With a clear conscience/sincerely.

Questions.Q: How often does Paul pray for Timothy?
Questions.A: Repeatedly. During the day and during the night.

Questions.Q: Paul says he remembers Timothy's tears. What do you think is the reason Timothy wept?
Questions.A: Because he was sad at being separated from Paul.

Questions.Q: What would make Paul very happy?
Questions.A: If he could see Timothy again.

Questions.Q: Paul thanked God for Timothy. What was Paul remembering that made him thankful for Timothy?
Questions.A: He was remembering that Timothy sincerely believed in Christ Jesus.

Questions.Q: Who else in Timothy's family believed in Christ Jesus?
Questions.A: His grandmother and his mother.

Questions.Q: What influence do you think they had on Timothy as a child?
Questions.A: They taught him the Scriptures and likely influenced him to believe in Christ Jesus when he was still young.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Timothy is to keep on doing what God has appointed him to do.

Questions.Q: Because Paul is sure Timothy believes in Christ Jesus, what does he tell Timothy?
Questions.A: He reminds Timothy of the responsibility God gave him.
He urges Timothy to continue fulfilling it.

Questions.Q: When did God assign this responsibility to Timothy?
Questions.A: When Paul put his hands on him.

Questions.Q: Why did Paul put his hands on him?
Questions.A: To show people that Timothy had been assigned to serve Jesus Christ.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul tells Timothy not to be ashamed of the message about the Lord.
Not to be ashamed of Paul.
To be willing to endure suffering for the sake of the good news.

Questions.Q: Paul has just said the Holy Spirit would help Timothy. Because of this help, what is Timothy to do?
Questions.A: He is not to be ashamed of telling others about the Lord.
He is not to be ashamed to have people know that he is a friend of a prisoner.

Questions.Q: Why was Paul in prison?
Questions.A: He was put in prison because he told people about Jesus Christ.

Questions.Q: What does Paul tell Timothy he should do?
Questions.A: Be willing to suffer like Paul is suffering as he tells people the good news.

Questions.Q: How would Timothy be able to endure the suffering that would likely come as a result of telling/teaching the good news?
Questions.A: God would give him strength for it.
Questions.Alternative: How would Timothy be able to endure the suffering that would likely come as a result of telling the good news?
How would Timothy be able to endure the suffering that would likely come as a result of teaching the good news?

Questions.Q: What does Paul say God has done for believers?
Questions.A: He has saved them.
He has called them to be holy/his special people.

Questions.Q: Did God do this because they were good people and deserved it?
Questions.A: No.

Questions.Q: Why, then, did he do it?
Questions.A: Because God himself planned to favor them.

Questions.Q: How would God fulfill his plan to favor them?
Questions.A: Through what Christ Jesus would do for them.

Questions.Q: Paul says that God planned to favor people a very long time ago. How has this plan been revealed at this time?
Questions.A: Through sending the Savior, Christ Jesus.

Questions.Q: When Christ Jesus came, he did some very important things for believers. What did he do?
Questions.A: He ended the power of death/made death of no consequence.
Through hearing and responding to the good news, believers will live forever.

Questions.Q: What did God appoint Paul to do?
Questions.A: He was sent as Christ's representative/apostle to proclaim and teach the good news.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say is one of the results of his telling the good news?
Questions.A: He is suffering as a prisoner does.

Questions.Q: Why is Paul not ashamed of being a prisoner because he preached about Christ?
Questions.A: Because he knows Christ Jesus, whom he has trusted.
Because he is sure that Christ is able to keep the good news/message safe until Christ comes again.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Timothy is not to allow anyone to change the message that he learned from Paul.

Questions.Q: Paul has some instructions for Timothy as he continues teaching others. What are they?
Questions.A: He is to teach the same message that he learned from Paul.
He is to trust in Christ Jesus and love others.

Questions.Q: b How will Timothy be able to do that?
Questions.A: Christ Jesus will enable him to do it.

Questions.Q: What is another important instruction Paul gives Timothy concerning the message he is teaching others?
Questions.A: He is to allow no one to change the message which God has given him.

Questions.Q: How is Timothy to do that?
Questions.A: Through the Holy Spirit's help.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Onesiphorus was a great encouragement to Paul.

Questions.Q: Paul has told Timothy about his suffering and imprisonment. What does he tell Timothy here?
Questions.A: Almost all the believers in Asia turned away from Paul during this time.

Questions.Q: What do you think it means that they "turned away" from Paul?
Questions.A: Perhaps they did not take his side when he was accused, or try to help him when he was in prison; perhaps they were afraid or ashamed to do so.

Questions.Q: There was one person who had not turned away from Paul. Who was he?
Questions.A: Onesiphorus

Questions.Q: What does Paul want God to do for him?
Questions.A: To be kind to the family of Onesiphorus.

Questions.Q: Why did Paul want God to do this for him?
Questions.A: He was not ashamed of Paul for being in prison.
He encouraged/cheered Paul.

Questions.Q: When did Onesiphorus help Paul?
Questions.A: When Paul was in prison in Rome and when Paul was in Ephesus.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Timothy is to teach reliable men who will then teach others.

Questions.Q: Why do you think Paul felt as though Timothy were his son?
Questions.A: They shared the same faith in Christ; Paul was teaching Timothy; Paul was older than Timothy.

Questions.Q: What does Paul instruct Timothy to do?
Questions.A: To let Jesus Christ make him strong in his work for Christ.

Questions.Q: What else did Paul instruct Timothy to do?
Questions.A: Timothy should teach what he had learned from Paul to people whom he knew would then teach other people that same message.

Questions.Q: Do you think this is an important instruction?
Questions.A: Yes, because this is the way the good news about Jesus Christ keeps spreading to people who do not know it.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Timothy is to endure suffering for Jesus Christ just as Paul is doing.

Questions.Q: Paul says Timothy is to endure suffering just as Paul is. With what figure does he compare their suffering?
Questions.A: A good soldier.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say is the aim of every soldier?
Questions.A: To please his captain.

Questions.Q: What does a soldier do in order to please his captain?
Questions.A: He does not get involved in civilian affairs because this would distract him from serving his captain.

Questions.Q: What can believers who follow Christ Jesus learn from this example?
Questions.A: Believers also should have the aim of trying to please their captain, Christ Jesus.
Believers also should not get involved in things which would keep them from obeying his orders.
