Questions.Q: What does Paul compare a follower of Jesus Christ to in this verse?
Questions.A: An athlete.

Questions.Q: What does he say about an athlete?
Questions.A: An athlete obeys the rules of the contest because he knows he will not win the prize unless he does.

Questions.Q: What can a believer learn from this example?
Questions.A: A believer must discipline himself to follow the teachings of Christ Jesus. If he does not obey those teachings, he will not get his reward.

Questions.Q: To what does Paul compare a follower of Jesus here?
Questions.A: To a hard-working farmer.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say about this farmer?
Questions.A: The farmer who works hard should be the first one to have a share of the crop.

Questions.Q: What can believers learn from this example?
Questions.A: Those who work hard for Jesus Christ will be rewarded.

Questions.Q: What does Paul tell Timothy to do in this verse?
Questions.A: Think about what Paul has been saying.

Questions.Q: Why should Timothy do this?
Questions.A: If he does the Lord will help him to understand what Paul has been saying.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: If Timothy remembers Christ Jesus he will be able to endure suffering.
Paul endures suffering in order to help believers, and because he knows his message is true.

Questions.Q: Paul says that Timothy will be able to endure suffering if he remembers Jesus Christ. What are some of the things about Jesus Christ that he is to remember?
Questions.A: God raised him from death.
He was the Messiah, descended from King David.

Questions.Q: As a result of Paul teaching this information about Jesus Christ, what has happened to him?
Questions.A: He is suffering because some people opposed that message.
He has been put in prison as if he were a criminal.

Questions.Q: Even though Paul is chained in prison, he is not discouraged. Why is he not?
Questions.A: He knows that the message from God cannot be put in chains/confined.

Questions.Q: What do you think he means by that?
Questions.A: The message is still being told by others even though Paul is in prison.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say is the reason he is suffering?
Questions.A: In order that those whom God has chosen will be saved.

Questions.Q: How are they saved?
Questions.A: Through what Jesus Christ has done.

Questions.Q: What does salvation result in?
Questions.A: Eternal glory/be forever with the Lord in his glorious place.

Questions.Q: As Paul thinks of "eternal glory," he is reminded again of how important it is for Timothy to endure suffering. He quotes a saying/hymn that is true. What does Paul say will encourage believers who are suffering because they believe in Christ?
Questions.A: If believers, like Christ, are put to death, they know they will also live with him eternally.
Questions.Alternative: As Paul thinks of "eternal glory," he is reminded again of how important it is for Timothy to endure suffering. He quotes a saying that is true. What does Paul say will encourage believers who are suffering because they believe in Christ?

As Paul thinks of "eternal glory," he is reminded again of how important it is for Timothy to endure suffering. He quotes a hymn that is true. What does Paul say will encourage believers who are suffering because they believe in Christ?

Questions.Q: If believers patiently endure suffering, what will happen when they die?
Questions.A: They will reign/rule with Christ.

Questions.Q: What would happen if believers say they do not know Christ?
Questions.A: He will say he does not know them.

Questions.Q: Supposing believers were not faithful to Christ, how would Christ respond to them?
Questions.A: He would continue to be faithful.

Questions.Q: Why does Christ continue to be faithful?
Questions.A: He can never be untrue to his own character.

Questions.Q: How is this both an encouragement and a warning?
Questions.A: If a believer repents of not being faithful, Christ will respond in faithfulness and forgive. If a person does not repent, Christ will respond in faithfulness to his just nature and punish that person.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Timothy is to make sure his work is such that God can approve it.

Questions.Q: What is Timothy to tell the people he is teaching?
Questions.A: They are not to quarrel about words.

Questions.Q: How does Paul show that this command is very important?
Questions.A: He tells Timothy to solemnly command them in God's presence.

Questions.Q: Why does Paul give this strict command?
Questions.A: Because when teachers quarrel, they weaken the faith of those who hear them.

Questions.Q: What does Paul encourage Timothy to do?
Questions.A: Do his best to be the kind of person that God will approve of.

Questions.Q: To whom should Timothy compare himself?
Questions.A: To a workman who does good work.

Questions.Q: As a teacher, what must Timothy do?
Questions.A: Teach the message correctly.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: God's true message can be depended upon.

Questions.Q: Why does Paul tell Timothy to avoid foolish talk?
Questions.A: It will weaken the faith of those who do it.
It will weaken the faith of those who hear it.

Questions.Q: Paul names two men who were guilty of such talk. What are their names?
Questions.A: Hymenaeus and Philetus.

Questions.Q: What were those men teaching that was not true?
Questions.A: They were saying that God had already raised the dead people spiritually, and will not raise their physical bodies.

Questions.Q: What was the result of such teaching?
Questions.A: Some of the people were confused, and did not know what to believe.

Questions.Q: What does Paul compare God's message to?
Questions.A: A strong foundation.

Questions.Q: How do you think the true message is like a strong foundation?
Questions.A: False teaching cannot shake/destroy God's true message.

Questions.Q: There are two things [from the Old Testament] written on this solid foundation. What are they?
Questions.A: "The Lord knows the people who really belong to him."
"Let every person who calls on the Lord/confesses the name of the Lord/calls Jesus Lord stop doing wrong."
Questions.Alternative: There are two things from the Old Testament written on this solid foundation. What are they?
There are two things written on this solid foundation. What are they?

Questions.Q: How do these sayings identify the true believers?
Questions.A: God knows who they are.
Man can know who they are because of how they behave.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul tells Timothy to strive to be a person who works well for the Lord.

Questions.Q: Paul wants Timothy to see how important it is for him to turn away from wrongdoing. What illustration does he use to show that?
Questions.A: In a large house there are many kinds of utensils.

Questions.Q: What are the ones made of gold and silver used for?
Questions.A: For special occasions.

Questions.Q: What are the ones made of wood and clay used for?
Questions.A: For ordinary use.

Questions.Q: If anyone wants to be like the gold and silver utensils, used for special purposes, what must he do?
Questions.A: Rid himself of what is bad.

Questions.Q: Then what will he be?
Questions.A: Ready for any kind of good work.

Questions.Q: If Timothy wants to be that kind of person, what does Paul tell him to do?
Questions.A: Avoid doing the bad things that some young people desire to do.

Questions.Q: What instead should he do?
Questions.A: Earnestly do right.
Believe the true teaching.
Love others.
Be at peace with other believers.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul tells Timothy that instead of arguing with those who oppose him, he is to instruct them kindly.

Questions.Q: What does Paul tell Timothy in this verse?
Questions.A: He is not to get involved in foolish arguments.

Questions.Q: How do those arguments usually end?
Questions.A: In quarrels.

Questions.Q: Instead of quarreling, what should Timothy do?
Questions.A: He should be kind to everyone.
He should be a good teacher.
He should be patient with people.

Questions.Q: How should Timothy answer his opponents?
Questions.A: He should instruct them kindly.

Questions.Q: Why should he do this?
Questions.A: In order that they might change their thinking, and acknowledge the message as true.

Questions.Q: Paul had another reason for telling Timothy to instruct his opponents with gentleness. What is it?
Questions.A: To free them from the trap set by the devil.

Questions.Q: What was the devil's purpose in trapping them?
Questions.A: So that they would do what he wants them to do.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Evil people will make life difficult in the last days.

Questions.Q: What is the first thing Paul wants Timothy to know?
Questions.A: In the last days there will be difficult times.

Questions.Q: Why will life be so difficult?
Questions.A: Because evil people will make it difficult for others to conduct themselves as they should.

Questions.Q: What are some of the evil things these people will do? (See verses 2-4).
Will these people continue to worship God?
Questions.A: They will go through religious ceremonies, but they will not let God change their natures.

Questions.Q: What does Paul tell Timothy to do about such people?
Questions.A: He should avoid them.

Questions.Q: What do some of those people do?
Questions.A: Persuade people to let them into their homes.

Questions.Q: What do they do when they are in the homes?
Questions.A: Deceive weak/foolish women into believing what they say is true.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say about those women?
Questions.A: They are sad because of the bad things they have done.

Questions.Q: What else does Paul say about those women?
Questions.A: They will listen to anybody, but are not able to recognize what is true.

Questions.Q: To whom does Paul compare those evil people he has been talking about?
Questions.A: Two men in the Old Testament named Jannes and Jambres.

Questions.Q: How are those two men like those evil people?
Questions.A: Just like Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses, so also those people oppose the true message.

Questions.Q: What else does Paul say about those people?
Questions.A: Their minds are corrupt/think only what is bad.

Questions.Q: Paul says those people who oppose the truth will not continue to succeed. Why not?
Questions.A: Because people will see that such people are foolish/stupid.

Questions.Q: In this regard also they are similar to which other two men?
Questions.A: Jannes and Jambres.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Timothy is to continue to live by what he has learned and firmly believes.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say Timothy has known/has followed closely in Paul's life?
Questions.A: His teaching.
His conduct.
His purpose in life.
How he trusted God.
How patient he was.
How he loved people.
How he endured what he suffered.
How people persecuted him.
Questions.Alternative: What does Paul say Timothy has known in Paul's life?
What does Paul say Timothy has followed closely in Paul's life?

Questions.Q: In what places was Paul persecuted?
Questions.A: In the cities of Antioch, Iconium, and Lystra.

Questions.Q: What happened every time the people persecuted him?
Questions.A: The Lord rescued him.

Questions.Q: As Paul thinks about the many times he had been persecuted, what does he tell Timothy?
Questions.A: Everyone who wants to live a godly life because he is united to Christ will be persecuted.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say about those evil and deceitful men who persecute believers?
Questions.A: They will continue to deceive other people.
They will be deceived by others.

Questions.Q: But as for Timothy, what does Paul tell him to do?
Questions.A: He must continue to believe what he has learned and firmly believes.

Questions.Q: How can he so confidently believe those things?
Questions.A: Because he has confidence in the people who have taught him.

Questions.Q: What is another reason Timothy can believe what he has learned?
Questions.A: Because what he has learned is correct according to the Scriptures.
Those Scriptures he has known since he was a child.

Questions.Q: How will Timothy benefit from the Scriptures?
Questions.A: From the Scriptures he will understand that salvation is through faith in Jesus Christ.

Questions.Q: What else does Paul say about the Scriptures?
Questions.A: Everything that men wrote in the Scriptures is inspired by God.

Questions.Q: In what ways can Scripture be used?
Questions.A: To teach people what is true.
To cause people to know when they are wrong.
To correct people.
To train people to do right.

Questions.Q: What is God's purpose in giving us the Scriptures?
Questions.A: In order that a person who serves God may be fully qualified and equipped to do every kind of good work.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul urges Timothy to continue to preach the true message.
He urges him to do all he is expected to do as a servant of God.

Questions.Q: How would Timothy know that Paul is giving him a very important command?
Questions.A: Paul says he gives the command in the presence of God and of Christ Jesus.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say about Christ Jesus here?
Questions.A: He is going to judge the people who are living and the people who have died.
He will come back to earth and rule.

Questions.Q: What is the first thing Paul commands Timothy to do?
Questions.A: To preach the true message to people.

Questions.Q: When should Timothy preach this true message?
Questions.A: He should be ready to do it at any time.

Questions.Q: In preaching this true message, there are some things Paul says Timothy should do. What are they?
Questions.A: Tell people when they are doing wrong.
Tell them to stop doing wrong.
Tell them what they ought to do.

Questions.Q: What should Timothy's attitude be as he teaches?
Questions.A: Very patient.

Questions.Q: Why does Paul urge Timothy to teach people in this way?
Questions.A: Paul says a time is coming when people will not want to listen to good teaching.

Questions.Q: What will they rather do?
Questions.A: They will bring in teachers who will teach them what they want to hear.

Questions.Q: What happens when people no longer want to listen to the true message?
Questions.A: They will turn their attention to legends/strange stories.

Questions.Q: But as for Timothy, what does Paul urge him to do?
Questions.A: Always control himself.
Be willing to suffer.
Tell people the good news about Jesus Christ.
Do everything he should do as a servant of God.

Questions.Q: Why does Paul give this command to Timothy?
Questions.A: The time will soon come for Paul to die.

Questions.Q: As Paul thinks back on his life, what does he say he has done?
Questions.A: He has exerted himself, as an athlete would compete to win.
He has finished what God wanted him to do, as a runner who finishes the race.
He has been loyal/true to the faith.

Questions.Q: Having done that, what is Paul now anticipating?
Questions.A: That there will be a reward for him because he has done what is right.

Questions.Q: Who will give Paul that reward?
Questions.A: The Lord.

Questions.Q: What does Paul say about the Lord?
Questions.A: He judges rightly.

Questions.Q: When will Paul get that reward?
Questions.A: On the day when the Lord judges people.

Questions.Q: Will Paul be the only one to receive a reward on that day?
Questions.A: No, all those who are looking forward eagerly for the Lord to come will also receive a reward.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul requests Timothy to come to him soon.
Paul also requests that he bring Mark with him, and certain other things that he needs.

Questions.Q: Why do you think Paul wanted Timothy to come as soon as possible?
Questions.A: Paul expected to be killed soon (4:6).

Questions.Q: What had happened to Paul's companions?
Questions.A: Demas left Paul in order to enjoy himself. He went to the city of Thessalonica.
Crescens went to the land of Galatia.
Titus went to the district of Dalmatia.

Questions.Q: Who is the only one with Paul?
Questions.A: Luke

Questions.Q: Whom did Paul want Timothy to bring with him?
Questions.A: Mark

Questions.Q: Why did Paul want Mark with him?
Questions.A: Because Mark could help Paul.

Questions.Q: What was another reason Paul wanted Mark there?
Questions.A: Paul had sent his helper Tychicus to the city of Ephesus.

Questions.Q: What are some of the things Paul wanted Timothy to bring with him?
Questions.A: His coat, which he had left with Carpus in the city of Troas.
Books
Most of all he wanted the parchments.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul warns Timothy against Alexander.

Questions.Q: Who is Alexander?
Questions.A: A man who makes things from copper.

Questions.Q: What had been Paul's experience with him?
Questions.A: He had wronged Paul very much.

Questions.Q: What will happen to Alexander because of that?
Questions.A: The Lord will punish him for what he did.

Questions.Q: What does Paul tell Timothy concerning this man?
Questions.A: Timothy must be alert/on guard so that he will not wrong him too.

Questions.Q: Why does Paul think Alexander might wrong Timothy too?
Questions.A: Because Alexander very strongly opposes the message which they teach.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul's friends abandoned him when he needed their help.
Paul is confident that the Lord will rescue him from every evil.

Questions.Q: What happened to Paul the first time he defended himself in court?
Questions.A: No one went along to help defend him.

Questions.Q: Where were his friends?
Questions.A: They deserted him/abandoned him.

Questions.Q: As Paul remembers this, what is his prayer/wish for them?
Questions.A: That God will forgive them for leaving him.
Questions.Alternative: As Paul remembers this, what is his prayer for them?
As Paul remembers this, what is his wish for them?

Questions.Q: Even though Paul's friends left him on that day, the Lord did not. What did the Lord do for him?
Questions.A: The Lord strengthened him so that he could thoroughly preach the good news/message.
The Lord rescued him out of a dangerous situation.

Questions.Q: Because of experiences like this, what is Paul confident of?
Questions.A: The Lord will rescue him from every evil.
The Lord will bring him safely to heaven.

Questions.Q: In thinking of this, what does Paul do?
Questions.A: He praises the Lord.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what Paul said.
Questions.A: Paul concludes his letter with various greetings and instructions.

Questions.Q: Who are the friends Paul sends greetings to here?
Questions.A: Priscilla and Aquila, and the family of Onesiphorus.

Questions.Q: He tells what has happened to two other friends. Who are they?
Questions.A: Erastus, who remained at Corinth.
Trophimus, who remained at Miletus because he was ill.

Questions.Q: What does Paul tell Timothy here?
Questions.A: Several of the believers send greetings to Timothy.

Questions.Q: What does Paul want God to do for Timothy?
Questions.A: To bless him.

Section.heading: 3 John 1-4 John greeted his friend Gaius.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what John said in these verses.
Questions.A: John wrote to his friend Gaius. (1)
John was happy because he heard that Gaius was faithfully doing what God wanted him to do. (3)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when someone is faithful?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that they are worthy of being believed in by someone else. They are trustworthy, reliable. (See "faithful" in KBT in the "believe" entry.)

Questions.Q: What did John call himself?
Questions.A: He called himself the elder. (1)

Questions.Q: What do you think an elder is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: An elder is a leader in the Christian church.

Questions.Q: How did John feel toward Gaius?
Questions.A: He loved him very much. (1)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means when someone loves someone else?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The person who loves another person seeks the good of that person. His attitude to the one whom he loves is an attitude of persistent and selfless goodwill.
Questions.Note: See "love" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did John pray to happen to Gaius?
Questions.A: He prayed for him to be in good health.
He prayed for him to prosper/succeed in everything he did just as his soul/spiritual life was doing well. (2)

Questions.Q: What do you think the soul is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In the Greek "soul" is used in place of "heart" which NIV uses. Depending on the context, "soul" in this sense refers to a person's ambitions, desires, or feelings, or his life in relationship to God.
Questions.Note: See "soul" in KBT.

Questions.Q: How did John get that report about Gaius?
Questions.A: Some Christians told John. (3)

Questions.Q: What did John say made him the most happy?
Questions.A: He was happy when he heard that those who were like his children/people he had helped to know Jesus were living according to the truth/[the way God wanted them to live]. (4)

Section.heading: 3 John 5-8 John encouraged Gaius to continue helping those Christians who were preaching the truth.

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words the basic meaning (theme) of what John said in these verses.
Questions.A: John told Gaius that he was faithful in helping those Christians. (5)
Questions.Note: Translator's Notes states those Christians were traveling preachers.

Questions.Q: What do you think John meant when he said "the brothers"?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In this reference "brother" means fellow believer or fellow Christian. (See "brother" in KBT in the "disciple" entry.)

Questions.Q: What relation did Gaius have with those Christians that he helped?
Questions.A: He didn't have any relation with them, they were strangers to him. (5)

Questions.Q: How did John know about the help Gaius had given those strangers?
Questions.A: Those strangers had told the church about Gaius's love for them. (6)

Questions.Q: What do you think the church is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It is a group of believers-in-Christ who live in one place.
Questions.Note: See "church" in KBT.

Questions.Q: What did John tell Gaius to do?
Questions.A: He was to continue to help those strangers in a way that was fitting for those who are God's servants. (6)

Questions.Q: Who do you think God is?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In English, the term "God" with a capital "G" is used to refer to the one supreme Creator. The term "god" with a small "g", as in "a god" or "many gods", can refer to any spiritual being that people worship. The Greek word theos can be used in the same two ways.
Questions.Note: In many languages the term for God is a proper name and cannot be used to refer to anyone except the one supreme creator of the world. It cannot be pluralized. (Or, if it can be pluralized, the meaning may be something very different from the English "gods". In one language, the plural form of God, meant "God and those who follow him" and was an appropriate way to translate "saints".) (See "God" in KBT.)

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Gaius needed to care for those strangers in that manner?
Questions.A: The reason they were travelling around was to tell people about Jesus Christ.
They did not receive any help from the unbelievers/those who are not Christians. (7)

Questions.Q: What do you think "because of the Name" means?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: In this reference it means (to act) for the sake [lit. name] of Christ i.e. to do something to promote the cause, honor or reputation of Christ.
Questions.Note: See "name" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Who do you think the pagans are?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: The pagans are those people who do not believe in Jesus. (See "pagans" in KBT in the "gentile" entry.)

Questions.Q: What did John say all believers are to do?
Questions.A: He said all believers are to help those strangers who were serving Christ. (8)

Questions.Q: What happened when the believers did that?
Questions.A: They helped in their work of [telling people] the true things [which God has revealed]. (8)

Section.heading: 3 John 9-15 John told Gaius not to do the things that Diotrephes did.

Questions.Q: What did John tell Gaius not to do?
Questions.A: John told Gaius not to follow the conduct of a person who does evil things. (11)

Questions.Q: What had John done?
Questions.A: He wrote a letter to the church. (9)
Questions.Note: Translator's Notes states that "church" here means the group of Christians in the place where Diotrephes was. That was probably in the same place where Gaius lived, or nearby.

Questions.Q: How did Diotrephes react/respond to what John had written?
Questions.A: He did not accept or obey what John had written. (9)
Questions.Alternative: How did Diotrephes react to what John had written?
How did Diotrephes respond to what John had written?

Questions.Q: What is the reason that Diotrephes refused to accept the things John said?
Questions.A: Diotrephes loved to be first/wanted to be the leader of the church himself. (9)

Questions.Q: What did John say that he wanted to do when he came to that church?
Questions.A: He wanted to tell/warn the people there about the things that Diotrephes was doing. (10)

Questions.Q: What things did John say Diotrephes was doing?
Questions.A: He was gossiping/said bad things about John and his companions.
He did not welcome and care for the strangers who were Christians.
He stopped other people in the church from welcoming and caring for the strangers.
He sent out/expelled from the church those people who wanted to welcome and care for the strangers. (10)

Questions.Q: What kind of conduct did John tell Gaius to follow?
Questions.A: He was to follow the conduct of someone who does good things. (11)

Questions.Q: What reason did John give for making that choice?
Questions.A: A person who does good things belongs to God.
A person who does bad things has not seen God/does not belong to God. (11)

Questions.Q: Who were the ones who approved of Demetrius?
Questions.A: All the people in that place who knew him approved of him.
The truth itself/He lived according to the true things [which God has revealed].
John and his friends approved of him. (12)

Questions.Q: What did John tell Gaius about his and his friends' testimony?
Questions.A: He said that Gaius knew that John and his friends only said things which were true. (12)

Questions.Q: What did John say about writing more to Gaius?
Questions.A: He had more to write to him but he didn't want to do it in a letter. (13)

Questions.Q: Instead of writing to him, what did John want to do?
Questions.A: He wanted to visit Gaius in his place and talk with him about those things. (14)

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to hope in something?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means to have a desire to see something happen or to obtain something.

Questions.Q: What did John want [God] to do for Gaius?
Questions.A: He wanted [God] to bless Gaius with peace. (15)
Questions.Alternative: What did John want God to do for Gaius?
What did John want for Gaius?
What blessing did John want for Gaius?
What blessing did John want God to give to Gaius?
Questions.Note: Some versifications have all this content as v. 14, where others break it into two verses, ending with v. 15

Questions.Q: What do you think it means for someone to be at peace?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: It means that they have a mental or spiritual condition marked by freedom of disquieting or oppressive thoughts or emotions.
Questions.Note: See "peace" in KBT.

Questions.Q: Who sent their greetings to Gaius?
Questions.A: Gaius's friends who were with John sent their greetings to him. (15)

Questions.Q: What did John ask Gaius to do?
Questions.A: He asked Gaius to greet each of John's friends who were there with Gaius. (15)

Questions.Q: Describe Job's character.
Questions.A: Perfect, upright, feared God, and eschewed evil. (1)

Questions.Q: How many sons and daughters did Job have at the beginning?
Questions.A: Seven sons and three daughters (2)

Questions.Q: How many sheep, camels, oxen and donkeys did Job have at the beginning?
Questions.A: 7000 sheep, 3000 camels, and 500 yoke/pairs of oxen, and 500 female donkeys (3)
Questions.Alternative: How many sheep, camels, oxen and asses did Job have at the beginning?

Questions.Q: How did Job's wealth compare to others?
Questions.A: He was the greatest of all the men of the east (3)

Questions.Q: What did Job do continually?
Questions.A: Offered burnt offerings for his family (4-5)

Questions.Q: What did God say about Job?
Questions.A: He was a perfect and an upright man, who feared God, and turned away from evil (8)

Questions.Q: According to Satan, why did Job serve God?
Questions.A: Because God put a hedge around him and blessed him (9-11)

Questions.Q: What four things did God allow Satan to do in his first assault against Job?
Questions.A: Take away his oxen, donkeys, sheep, camels, and his servants and children died (12-19)

Questions.Q: What did Job do when all this happened?
Questions.A: Worshiped (20)

Questions.Q: What did Job say when all this happened?
Questions.A: "Naked I came from my mother's womb, and naked shall I return. the LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away; blessed be the name of the LORD." (21-22)

Questions.Q: What did Satan say that Job would do if his bone and flesh were touched?
Questions.A: Job would curse God to his face (1-5)

Questions.Q: How did Satan afflict Job?
Questions.A: With boils (6-8)

Questions.Q: How did Job's wife question him?
Questions.A: Do you still retain your integrity? (9)

Questions.Q: How did Job reply to his wife?
Questions.A: You speak as one of the foolish women speaks (10)

Questions.Q: Who were Job's three friends?
Questions.A: Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite (11)

Questions.Q: What did Job's three friends do?
Questions.A: They sat down with him on the ground seven days and seven nights, and none spoke a word to him (12-13)

Questions.Q: What did Job say about the day he was born?
Questions.A: He cursed it (1-10)

Questions.Q: What did Job wish had happened at his birth?
Questions.A: He wished he had died (11-23)

Questions.Q: What did Job say had come upon him?
Questions.A: The thing which he greatly feared (24-26)

Questions.Q: What did Eliphaz imply was the reason for Job's condition?
Questions.A: He was reaping the wickedness that he had sown (7-8)

Questions.Q: What else did Eliphaz hint was the reason for Job's condition?
Questions.A: That Job claimed to be purer than God (17-19)

Questions.Q: What did Eliphaz suggest that Job do?
Questions.A: Seek God (1, 8)

Questions.Q: For what did he say people are born?
Questions.A: Trouble (7)
Questions.Alternative: To what did he say man was born?
For what did he say man is born?
To what did he say people are born?
Unto what did he say man is born?

Questions.Q: What did he imply that Job's troubles were?
Questions.A: The chastening of the Almighty (17-18)

Questions.Q: How long did he think Job would live?
Questions.A: To a full age (26)

Questions.Q: What did Job wish God would do to him?
Questions.A: Destroy him (8-10)

Questions.Q: What did Job wish to understand?
Questions.A: Where he had erred (24)

Questions.Q: What did Job think his friends were doing to him?
Questions.A: Digging a pit for him (27)

Questions.Q: What did Job say when he laid down at night?
Questions.A: When shall I arise, and the night be gone? (4)

Questions.Q: What was the condition of Job's flesh?
Questions.A: Clothed with worms and clods of dust; skin broken and loathsome (5)

Questions.Q: For what did Job ask pardon?
Questions.A: His transgression (20-21)

Questions.Q: To what did Bildad compare Job's words?
Questions.A: A strong wind (1-2)

Questions.Q: What did he imply that Job's children had done?
Questions.A: Sinned (3-4)

Questions.Q: What did Bildad imply about Job?
Questions.A: That Job was a hypocrite and not upright (6, 13, 20)

Questions.Q: What did Job recognize that God had created?
Questions.A: The earth, sun, stars and constellations (5-10)

Questions.Q: What did Job recognize if he tried to justify himself?
Questions.A: His own mouth would condemn him (20)

Questions.Q: How did Job consider his days?
Questions.A: Swifter than a runner, ships or an eagle (25-26)

Questions.Q: Of what was Job's soul weary?
Questions.A: Life (1)

Questions.Q: How did Job describe the process God used to form/create him?
Questions.A: He molded him like clay, poured him out like milk and curdled him like cheese, clothed him with skin and flesh, and knit him together with bones and sinews. (8-11)
Questions.Note: Answers may vary if translation is less literal or alternative metaphors are employed to convey the sense of what Job was saying.
Questions.Alternative: How did Job describe the process God used to form him?
How did Job describe the process God used to create him?

Questions.Q: Of what did Job realize he was full?
Questions.A: Confusion (15)

Questions.Q: Of what did Zophar accuse Job?
Questions.A: Lying (1-4)

Questions.Q: What did he suggest that Job do?
Questions.A: Prepare his heart by putting away iniquity and wickedness (13-14)

Questions.Q: How did Job consider his understanding compared to his friend?
Questions.A: Not inferior (3)

Questions.Q: Who could teach them?
Questions.A: The beasts, fowls, earth and the fishes (7-8)

Questions.Q: In whose hand is the soul and breath of every person/man?
Questions.A: The LORD's (9-10)
Questions.Alternative: In whose hand is the soul and breath of every person?
In whose hand is the soul and breath of every man?

Questions.Q: With whom is wisdom [found]?
Questions.A: The aged (12-13, 16)
Questions.Alternative: With whom is wisdom found?
With whom is wisdom?

Questions.Q: What did Job call his friends?
Questions.A: Forgers of lies and physicians of no value. (4)

Questions.Q: What did he tell his friends to do?
Questions.A: Hold their peace, let him alone, and let come on him what will (13)

Questions.Q: How did Job declare his trust in God?
Questions.A: Though he slay me, yet will I trust in him (15)

Questions.Q: What is/are short and full of trouble?//What is/are full of trouble?
Questions.A: A man's life/days (1-2)
Questions.Alternative: What is short and full of trouble?
What are short and full of trouble?
What is full of trouble?
What are full of trouble?

Questions.Q: What example of hope from nature does Job give?
Questions.A: A tree, if it be cut down, will sprout again (7-9)

Questions.Q: What question does Job ask concerning the resurrection?
Questions.A: If a man die, shall he live again? (14)
Questions.Alternative: What question does Job ask about the resurrection?
What question does Job ask in this verse?
What question does Job ask about death?

Questions.Q: What does Eliphaz imply about Job's words?
Questions.A: Job is trying to sound wise, but his words are empty/devoid of wisdom. (2)
Job's words are unprofitable. (3)
Questions.Alternative: What does Eliphaz imply about the way Job is talking?

Questions.Q: What does Eliphaz infer from Job's words?
Questions.A: Eliphaz infers that Job is in sin and does not fear God. (4)
He believes that Job's speech is coming from a heart full of iniquity. (5-6)
Questions.Alternative: What does Eliphaz infer from the way Job is talking?
What does Eliphaz believe about Job's speech?
What does Eliphaz infer that Job utters?

Questions.Q: Who does he say suffers torment and is filled with terror?
Questions.A: the wicked man (20-26)

Questions.Q: According to Eliphaz what are some troubles the wicked face?
Questions.A: They dwell in desolate cities and houses and will not be rich. (28-34)

Questions.Q: What did Job say his friends were?
Questions.A: miserable comforters (1-2)
Questions.Alternative: How did Job describe his friends?

Questions.Q: How did Job say he could speak if they were in his place?
Questions.A: He could speak as they were, heaping up words against them. (3-4)

Questions.Q: What did Job do before God?
Questions.A: cried (or poured out tears) (20)

Questions.Q: What did Job say awaited him?
Questions.A: the grave and corruption (1, 13-16)

Questions.Q: Why were his eyes dim?
Questions.A: from sorrow (7)

Questions.Q: What did Job say were past?
Questions.A: his days
his plans/purposes
his desires
Questions.Alternative: What did Job say was past?
What did Job say had passed?
What did Job say had ceased?

Questions.Q: Why did Bildad want Job to stop talking?
Questions.A: Bildad wanted to speak. (1-2)

Questions.Q: What did Bildad imply that Job was?
Questions.A: wicked (5, 21)

Questions.Q: What did Job's friends do to him with words?
Questions.A: tormented him and broke him in pieces (2)
cast reproach upon him and wronged him (3)

Questions.Q: Who did Job say had turned against him?
Questions.A: his friends/those whom he loved (19)

Questions.Q: How did Job describe his physical condition?
Questions.A: His bones stuck to his skin and flesh. (20)

Questions.Q: How did Job declare his faith in a resurrection?
Questions.A: “After my skin has been destroyed, yet in my flesh shall I see God.” (25-26)

Questions.Q: What did Zophar infer about Job?
Questions.A: that he was a wicked hypocrite (5, 29)

Questions.Q: What did he say would reveal his iniquity?
Questions.A: the heavens (27)

Questions.Q: What question really troubled Job?
Questions.A: Why do the wicked live, become old, yes, are mighty in power? What is the Almighty, that we should serve him? and what profit should we have, if we pray to him? (7-15)

Questions.Q: How is the end of the one who dies in full vigor similar to the one who dies in bitterness of soul?
Questions.A: They both lie down in the dust, and the worms cover them. (22-26)

Questions.Q: What did Job think of the answers given by his friends?
Questions.A: They were false. (34)

Questions.Q: Of what does Eliphaz accuse Job?
Questions.A: That he was wicked and had not cared for the naked, thirsty, hungry, widows and fatherless (5-10)

Questions.Q: What does Eliphaz suggest that Job should do?
Questions.A: Return to the Almighty and put away iniquity. (21-23)

Questions.Q: What did Eliphaz think would happen if Job followed his advice?
Questions.A: The LORD would hear Job and shine His light on Job's path. (26-28)

Questions.Q: Whom did Job wish to find?
What did Job realize that God knew about him?
Questions.A: the way that he lived (10)

Questions.Q: What did Job esteem more than food?
Questions.A: God's word (12)

Questions.Q: What are some things done to orphans, widows and the poor?
Questions.A: They take away their animals and cause them to be naked and hungry (2-12)

Questions.Q: Why don't wrongdoers like daylight?
Questions.A: They are afraid they will be seen. (13-17)

Questions.Q: According to Bildad, what chance is there of a person/man being righteous before God?
Questions.A: very little, or none (4-6)
Questions.Alternative: According to Bildad, what chance is there of a person being righteous before God?
According to Bildad, what chance is there of a man being righteous before God?

Questions.Q: What questions did Job ask Bildad showing how little he helped Job?
Questions.A: How have you helped him who is without power? (2)
How have you saved the arm that has no strength? (2)
How have you counseled him that has no wisdom, and declared sound knowledge? (3)
With whose help have you uttered words, and whose breath has come out from you? (4)
Questions.Note: Job's words might be rendered as rhetorical questions or as ironic statements or a combination of the two. This question should be worded accordingly so that it makes sense.
Questions.Alternative: What did Job say to Bildad to show how little he had helped Job?
What did Job say to Bildad to show that he had not really helped?

Questions.Q: Upon what did God suspend the earth?
Questions.A: He hangs the earth on nothing (7)

Questions.Q: What was Job going to hold fast?
Questions.A: His integrity and righteousness (6)

Questions.Q: Who has little hope?
Questions.A: The hypocrite (8-10)

Questions.Q: What does God bring to light?
Questions.A: The thing that is hid (11)

Questions.Q: What cannot be obtained by gold, silver, or precious jewels?
Questions.A: Wisdom and understanding (12-19)

Questions.Q: From where does wisdom and understanding come?
Questions.A: Fearing the LORD and departing from evil (20-28)

Questions.Q: What did Job long for?
Questions.A: The former days when God preserved him, when he was respected and when he helped others (1-20)

Questions.Q: How was Job regarded prior to his affliction?
Questions.A: One that gave counsel (21-25)

Questions.Q: Who mocked Job?
Questions.A: The young men (1)

Questions.Q: What did they not hesitate to do to Job?
Questions.A: Spit in his face (10)

Questions.Q: How did Job feel that God had become to him?
Questions.A: Cruel (21)

Questions.Q: With what did Job make a covenant?
Questions.A: He made a covenant with his eyes not to look (lustfully) at a girl/virgin (1)
Questions.Alternative: What kind of covenant did Job make?

Questions.A: Excellent in power, and in judgment, and in plenty of justice (23-24)

Questions.Q: What is God's purpose in speaking to Job in this chapter?
Questions.A: God wants Job [and his friends] to understand that humans [like Job and his friends] do not have enough understanding [and cannot see the full picture] in order to make sense of his circumstances.

Questions.Q: Who answers Job in this chapter?

On what were its footings set, or who laid its cornerstone? (6)

Have you entered into the springs of the sea? (16)
Have you comprehended the vast expanses of the earth? (18)

Questions.Q: What is a covenant?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A covenant is an agreement, an especially binding promise. If a person on one side of the covenant does not do as both have agreed, there usually is a strong punishment for him or he pays compensation to the other person. Similar agreements now are called contracts. When God makes an agreement with people, however, he makes a firm promise of what he will do and says what they must do.
Questions.Note: See "covenant" in KBT.

If the language has a special name to refer to these kinds of agreements, ask the respondent to tell you the kinds of situations in which the people make the agreements. Listen for any points where it would not be appropriate to state that God made that kind of an agreement. Then adjust the translation as necessary.

Questions.Q: What is a covenant?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A covenant is an agreement, an especially binding promise. If a person on one side of the covenant does not do as both have agreed, there usually is a strong punishment for him or he pays compensation to the other person. Similar agreements now are called contracts. When God makes an agreement with people, however, he makes a firm promise of what he will do and says what they must do.
Questions.Note: See "covenant" in KBT.

If the language has a special name to refer to these kinds of agreements, ask the respondent to tell you the kinds of situations in which the people make the agreements. Listen for any points where it would not be appropriate to state that God made that kind of an agreement. Then adjust the translation as necessary.

Questions.Q: What does the word "fountain" refer to?

Questions.Q: Why do you think Solomon refers to the wife as a "fountain"?
Questions.A: One's wife is a source of blessing and refreshment.
As a fountain gives forth water, a wife produces children.
In an arid place, a source of pure water is valuable and worthy of protection.

Although this idea is not explicitly referenced here, one would naturally want to protect the purity of a fountain or cistern used for drinking water. In the same way, the son is being warned to avoid impurity that would diminish the happiness to be found in a fulfilling relationship with his wife.
Questions.Note: Omit this question if the translation does not use figurative language here.

The Hebrew word for "fountain," is derived from the root meaning "to dig," which goes back to the idea of a "cistern" in verse 15. In Hebrew thought, a wife who bore children was regarded as "blessed" and as a blessing to her husband.
In places where a well or fountain is usually communal and cannot be thought of as private property, give careful consideration about how best to convey this idea.

Questions.Q: Does this verse mean that it is okay to have more than one wife?
Questions.A: No. The wife one marries in one's youth is to continue to be loved and cherished even in old age (as described in verse 19).
Questions.Note: Select appropriate wording for this question based on your knowledge of their practices regarding polygamy.

We know that Solomon ended up having many wives, but this verse and the surrounding context speak of a single wife and suggest an intimate marriage relationship that would not likely exist in the context of a polygamous arrangement. (See Ecc. 9:9 and Mal. 2:14)

Questions.Q: To what is one who sings songs to a heavy heart compared?
Questions.A: Like one who takes away a garment in cold weather, or like [pouring] vinegar on soda. (20)
Questions.Note: The Hebrew word "neter" is used only twice in the Old Testament (also in Jeremiah 2:22). It refers to a naturally occurring alkali (something like sodium carbonate). Some exegetes prefer to interpret this word in this verse as "wound", since pouring vinegar on a wound stings and irritates, thus conveying the sense of an inappropriate or hurtful action. The response should match the exegetical decision used in the translation.

Questions.Q: What does an angry look bring?
Questions.A: A backbiting tongue, or cruel words (23)
Questions.Note: Some older translations interpret the second clause of this verse as meaning that an angry look stops or drives away a backbiting tongue. However, most modern scholars and translations understand the verse to describe the opposite relationship: just as the north wind brings rain, a backbiting or sly tongue brings an angry look. The Hebrew syntax supports this interpretation through parallelism and an implied verb ("brings") in the second line.

Questions.Note: Scholars generally regard it as unclear whether the entire chapter can be attributed to King Lemuel.

The name Lemuel means “for God” or “devoted to God.” Since there is no biblical or other historical record of a king by that name, it could be that Lemuel was a pet name for Solomon, used by his mother, and that Solomon wrote down her advice as she would have expressed it. Other theories are that Lemuel is actually King Hezekiah or a fictional character.

What can't a man know though he seek to find it?
What can no one discover?
What can no one comprehend?

Questions.Q: What is alike to both the righteous and the wicked?
Questions.A: Death (1-3)

Questions.Q: What is better than a dead lion?
Questions.A: A living dog (4-6)

Questions.Q: With whom should you live joyfully?
Questions.A: The wife whom you love (7-9)

Questions.Q: What should you do with all your might?
Questions.A: Whatever your hand finds to do (10)

Questions.Q: What happens to all?
Questions.A: Time and chance (11)

Questions.Q: What does man not know?
Questions.A: His time (when death or something bad will happen) (12)
Questions.Alternative: What does no one know?
What do people not know?

Questions.Q: What is better than weapons of war?
Questions.A: Wisdom (13-18)

Questions.Q: What object shows what a little folly can do to a person of reputation?
Questions.A: Dead flies cause the ointment of the apothecary to stink (1-3)

Questions.Q: What should you do when the spirit of a ruler rises up against you?
Questions.A: Leave not your place; for yielding pacifies great offenses (4)

Questions.Q: What might happen to one who digs a pit?
Questions.A: Fall in the pit (8)

Questions.Q: What will be required if one does not sharpen his axe?
Questions.A: More strength (10)

Questions.Q: Of what is a fool full?
Questions.A: Words (14)

Questions.Q: Why does a building decay?
Questions.A: Slothfulness (18)

Questions.Q: What answers all things?
Questions.A: Money (19)

Questions.Q: Why should you not curse the king or the rich?
Questions.A: It will be told (20)

Questions.Q: Why should you cast your bread upon the waters?
Questions.A: You shall find it after many days (1-2)

Questions.Q: When should one plant?
Questions.A: In the morning whether it is windy or cloudy (3-6)

Questions.Q: For what things will God bring youth into judgment?
Questions.A: All their doings (9-10)

Questions.Q: What should a person do in their youth?
Questions.A: Remember his Creator (1)

Questions.Q: What are some problems with old age?
Questions.A: Eye sight dims, teeth fall out, hearing diminishes, fear, desire fails (1-5)

Questions.Q: Where will man/people eventually return?
Questions.A: To the dust of the earth (6-8)
Questions.Alternative: Where will man eventually return?
Where will people eventually return?

Questions.Q: By what means did the Teacher teach the people?
Questions.A: Acceptable and upright words of truth (9-11)

Questions.Q: Of what is there no end?
Questions.A: Making books (12)

Questions.Q: What did Solomon give as a conclusion?
Questions.A: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man (13)

Questions.Q: What will God bring into judgment?
Questions.A: Every work with every secret thing (14)

Questions.Q: What color does the lady say she is?
Questions.A: Black (5-6)

Questions.Q: Why did she want to know where her lover kept his flock?
Questions.A: Because she loved him and wanted to be able to be near him [and not with his companions] (7)
Questions.Alternative: Why did she want to know where her lover pastured his flock?
Why did she want to know where her lover pastured his sheep?
Why did she want to know where her lover stayed?
Why did she want to know where her lover abided?

Questions.Q: To what did she compare her love?
Questions.A: A company of horses in Pharaoh's chariots and a cluster of henna blossoms in the vineyards of Engedi (9, 14)

Questions.Q: To what did he compare the eyes of his love?
Questions.A: Doves' eyes (15)

Questions.Q: What kind of banner was over her?
Questions.A: Love (4)

Questions.Q: What was her beloved like?
Questions.A: A roe or a young hart (9, 17)

Questions.Q: What time had come?
Questions.A: The singing of birds (12)

Questions.Q: What spoils the vines?
Questions.A: Little foxes (15)

Questions.Q: Who was she seeking?
Questions.A: He whom her soul loved (1-4)

Questions.Q: Who surrounded Solomon's bed?
Questions.A: 60 valiant men (7-8)

Questions.Q: How was the interior of Solomon's chariot finished?
Questions.A: (Embroidered or inlaid) with love (9-10)

Questions.Q: To what was her love's neck compared?
Questions.A: The tower that David built for an armory (4)

Questions.Q: What was not in her?
Questions.A: Any spot (7)

Questions.Q: What was under her tongue?
Questions.A: Honey and milk (11)

Questions.Q: How did her beloved rank among thousands?
Questions.A: The most chief (10)

Questions.Q: How lovely was her beloved?
Questions.A: Altogether lovely (16)

Questions.Q: What did she claim about her beloved?
Questions.A: I am my beloved's, and my beloved is mine (3)

Questions.Q: What was laid up for the beloved?
Questions.A: All manner of pleasant fruits, new and old (13)

Questions.Q: What is cruel as the grave?
Questions.A: Jealousy (6)

Questions.Q: What cannot quench love?
Questions.A: Many waters (7)

Questions.Q: Of what nation and city did Isaiah's prophecy concern?
Questions.A: Judah (1)

Questions.Q: Who were the kings that reigned when Isaiah prophesied?
Questions.A: Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah (1)

Questions.Q: Whom did Judah provoke to anger?
Questions.A: The Holy One of Israel (4)

Questions.Q: To what did Isaiah liken Judah?
Questions.A: A body that was sick, wounded, bruised, and full of sores (5-6)

Questions.Q: In what didn't God delight?
Questions.A: The (11)
blood of bullocks, or of lambs, or of he goats (11)

Questions.Q: What did God want Judah to do?
Questions.A: Cease to do evil and learn to do well (16-17)

Questions.Q: What could God do for their sins?
Questions.A: Make them white as snow (18)

Questions.Q: What would result if Judah was willing and obedient?
Questions.A: Eat the good of the land (19)

Questions.Q: Who could not judge the fatherless and widows?
Questions.A: The princes (23)

Questions.Q: From where will the law and the word of the LORD go forth?
Questions.A: Zion, Jerusalem (3)

Questions.Q: Into what will nations beat their swords and spears?
Questions.A: Plowshares and pruning hooks (4)

Questions.Q: What will the nations learn no more?
Questions.A: War (4)

Questions.Q: Who will be humbled?
Questions.A: The lofty looks of man (11-12, 17)

Questions.Q: Who will be exalted?
Questions.A: The LORD (11, 17)

Questions.Q: What did the LORD take away from Jerusalem and Judah?
Questions.A: Bread, water, men of war, judges, prophets, counselors, artificers, and orators (1-3)

Questions.Q: Why was Jerusalem ruined and Judah fallen?
Questions.A: Their tongue and their doings are against the LORD (8)

Questions.Q: Who would oppress and rule over them?
Questions.A: Children and women (12)

Questions.Q: What was said about the daughters of Zion?
Questions.A: They are haughty, walk with stretched forth necks and wanton eyes, walking and mincing as they go, and making a tinkling with their feet (16)

Questions.Q: What was the LORD going to do to these daughters of Zion?
Questions.A: The LORD would bring sores on their heads, make them bald, and take away their jewelry, fine clothes and headdresses (17-24)

Questions.Q: What would happen to the men of Judah and Jerusalem?
Questions.A: Fall by the sword (25)

Questions.Q: What will the LORD wash away?
Questions.A: The filth of the daughters of Zion (4)

Questions.Q: What will a tabernacle provide?
Questions.A: A shadow in the day time from the heat, place of refuge, and a covert from storm and rain (6)

Questions.Q: Who is likened to a vineyard?
Questions.A: The house of Israel (1-10)

Questions.Q: Instead of bring forth good grapes what did the vineyard bring forth?
Questions.A: Wild grapes, briers and thorns (2, 4, 6)

Questions.Q: Why did God's people go into captivity?
Questions.A: They regard not the work of the LORD, neither consider the operation of his hands and because they have no knowledge (12-13)

Questions.Q: What has enlarged itself?
Questions.A: Hell (14)

Questions.Q: What was pronounced upon those that call evil good and good evil?
Questions.A: Woe (20)

Questions.Q: Upon who else are woes pronounced?
Questions.A: Those who are wise in their own eyes (21)
Those who are heroes at drinking wine (22)
Those who acquit the guilty for a bribe, and deprive the innocent of his right (23)
Questions.Alternative: Against who else are woes pronounced?

Questions.Q: What did Isaiah see in the year that Uzziah died?
Questions.A: He saw the LORD sitting on a throne, high and lifted up (1)

Questions.Q: What did the seraphim cry?
Questions.A: Holy, holy, holy, is the LORD of hosts: the whole earth is full of his glory (2-3)

Questions.Q: What did Isaiah say when he heard the cry and saw the house filled with smoke?
Questions.A: Woe is me! for I am undone; because I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell in the middle of a people of unclean lips: for my eyes have seen the King, the LORD of hosts (5)

Questions.Q: How did Isaiah reply when the voice of the Lord said “Whom shall I send?
Questions.A: Here am I; send me (8)

Questions.Q: What was he to tell the people?
Questions.A: Hear you indeed, but understand not; and see you indeed, but perceive not (9-10)

Questions.Q: What happened in the days of Ahaz, king of Judah?
Questions.A: Rezin the king of Syria, and Pekah the son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up toward Jerusalem to war against it, but could not prevail against it (1)

Questions.Q: What did the LORD tell Isaiah to tell Ahaz?
Questions.A: Take heed, and be quiet; fear not, neither be fainthearted for the fierce anger of Rezin with Syria, and of the son of Remaliah (3-4)

Questions.Q: What was going to happen to Ephraim?
Questions.A: Be broken, that it be not a people (8)

Questions.Q: What sign was the LORD going to give?
Questions.A: A virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel (14)

Questions.Q: What would be taken away?
Questions.A: The riches of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria (4)

Questions.Q: Who should we fear?
Questions.A: The LORD of hosts (12-13)

Questions.Q: What is the reason some would speak not according to the law and to the testimony?
Questions.A: Because there is no light in them (20)

Questions.Q: What would those who walked in darkness see?
Questions.A: A great light (2)

Questions.Q: What would the child born to them be called?
Questions.A: Wonderful, Counselor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace (6)

Questions.Q: Who would devour Israel?
Questions.A: The Syrians and the Philistines (12)

Questions.Q: What caused them to err?
Questions.A: The leaders (16)

Questions.Q: To whom will woe be pronounced?
Questions.A: Those who decree unrighteous decrees against the needy, poor, widows and fatherless (1-2)

Questions.Q: Who was sent against a hypocritical nation?
Questions.A: Assyria (5-6)

Questions.Q: Who will return to the mighty God?
Questions.A: A remnant from Israel (20-22)

Questions.Q: Why shouldn't the people of Zion be afraid of Assyria?
Questions.A: In a little while the indignation would cease and the burden will be taken away and the yoke shall be destroyed because of the anointing (24-27)

Questions.Q: What will come forth out of the stem of Jesse?
Questions.A: A rod, a Branch (1)

Questions.Q: What aspects of the spirit would rest on him?
Questions.A: The spirit of the LORD, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the LORD (2)

Questions.Q: How will he judge the poor?
Questions.A: With righteousness (4)

Questions.Q: What creatures are mentioned as having peace with one another?
Questions.A: Wolf with lamb, leopard with kid, calf and young lion, cow and bear, and sucking child with asp (6-8)

Questions.Q: What will fill the earth?
Questions.A: The knowledge of the LORD (9)

Questions.Q: Who will the Lord gather from the four corners of the earth?
Questions.A: The outcasts of Israel, and the dispersed of Judah (11-12)

Questions.Q: What will the LORD JEHOVAH be to them?
Questions.A: Their strength, song; and salvation (2)

Questions.Q: How will they draw water out of the wells of salvation?
Questions.A: With joy (3)

Questions.Q: What will they say in that day?
Questions.A: Praise the LORD (4)

Questions.Q: Why will they sing?
Questions.A: For He has done excellent things (5)

Questions.Q: What did Isaiah see?
Questions.A: The burden of Babylon (1)

Questions.Q: What was coming?
Questions.A: The day of the LORD (6, 9)

Questions.Q: For what will the world be punished?
Questions.A: Their evil and iniquity (11)

Questions.Q: Who will the LORD stir up against the Babylonians?
Questions.A: The Medes (17)

Questions.Q: What shall become of Babylon?
Questions.A: As when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah (19)

Questions.Q: Upon whom will the LORD have mercy?
Questions.A: Jacob (1)

Questions.Q: What were the five I wills of Lucifer?
Questions.A: I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of God, I will sit also on the mount of the congregation, in the sides of the north, I will ascend above the heights of the clouds, I will be like the most High (13-14)

Questions.Q: Into what will the LORD make Babylon?
Questions.A: A possession for the bittern (22-23)

Questions.Q: Whom else will the LORD break?
Questions.A: The Assyrian (25)

Questions.Q: Why shouldn't the Philistines rejoice?
Questions.A: The LORD would send famine and slay their survivors (29-31)

Questions.Q: On what nation is judgment prophesied?
Questions.A: Moab

Questions.Q: How would the Moabites respond to the sudden destruction of their cities?
Questions.A: Weep, wail, cry in distress

Questions.Q: To what are the daughters of Moab compared?
Questions.A: As a wandering bird cast out of the nest (2)

Questions.Q: What shall be taken away and cease?
Questions.A: Gladness, joy, singing, and shouting (10)

Questions.Q: Who would become a ruinous heap?
Questions.A: Damascus (1)

Questions.Q: Who would be made thin?
Questions.A: The glory of Jacob (4)

Questions.Q: Why would his strong cities be forsaken?
Questions.A: Because they forgot the God of their salvation, and were not been mindful of the rock of their strength (9-10)

Questions.Q: To what land was woe pronounced in this chapter?
Questions.A: The land which is beyond the rivers of Ethiopia: (1)

Questions.Q: Upon what nation is judgment prophesied in this chapter?
Questions.A: Egypt (1)

Questions.Q: What did the LORD cause Isaiah to do as a sign to Egypt and Ethiopia?
Questions.A: Walk naked and barefoot three years (2-4)

Questions.Q: Who was said to have fallen?
Questions.A: Babylon (9)

Questions.Q: How would Judah be carried away?
Questions.A: With a mighty captivity (17)

Questions.Q: Who would be fastened as a nail in a sure place?
Questions.A: Eliakim the son of Hilkiah (20-23)

Questions.Q: What will happen to the nail?
Questions.A: It will be removed, cut down, and fall (25)

Questions.Q: Whose strength was to be laid waste?
Questions.A: The ships of Tarshish (14)

Questions.Q: Who would be forgotten for seventy years?
Questions.A: Tyre (15)

Questions.Q: What shows that God is not a respecter of people?
Questions.A: As with the people, so with the priest; as with the servant, so with his master; as with the maid, so with her mistress; as with the buyer, so with the seller; as with the lender, so with the borrower; as with the taker of usury, so with the giver of usury to him. The land shall be utterly (1-3)
emptied (1-3)

Questions.Q: What will happen to the earth?
Questions.A: The earth will be utterly broken down, dissolved, moved exceedingly, reel to and fro like a drunkard, and removed like a cottage, and it shall fall, and not rise again (19-20)

Questions.Q: Why would Isaiah exalt the Lord and praise him?
Questions.A: He has done wonderful things and His counsels are faithfulness and truth (1)

Questions.Q: To whom was the Lord a strength?
Questions.A: The poor and needy (4)

Questions.Q: What will the Lord swallow up in victory?
Questions.A: Death (8)

Questions.Q: What will the Lord wipe away?
Questions.A: All tears and the rebuke of His people (8)

Questions.Q: Who will the LORD keep in perfect peace?
Questions.A: The person whose mind is stayed on God, because he trusts in God (3)

Questions.Q: What is the way of the just?
Questions.A: Uprightness (7)

Questions.Q: What is the desire of our heart/soul?
Questions.A: The LORD's name and renown; God himself (8-9)
Questions.Alternative: What is the desire of our heart?
What is the desire of our soul?

Questions.Q: For what will the LORD punish the inhabitants of the earth?
Questions.A: For their iniquity (21)

Questions.Q: Who will blossom and bud, and fill the face of the world with fruit?
Questions.A: Israel (6)

Questions.Q: Who will worship the LORD on the holy mountain at Jerusalem?
Questions.A: Those who were ready to perish in the land of Assyria, and the outcasts in the land of Egypt (13)

Questions.Q: Upon who is woe pronounced?
Questions.A: The drunkards of Ephraim (1)

Questions.Q: What will the LORD be to the residue of His people?
Questions.A: A crown of glory, and a diadem of beauty (5)

Questions.Q: What is the rest and refreshing?
Questions.A: Stammering lips and another tongue (11-12)

Questions.Q: What was the word of the LORD to them?
Questions.A: Precept on precept, precept on precept; line on line, line on line; here a little, and there a little (10, 13)

Questions.Q: What did the LORD lay in Zion?
Questions.A: For a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious corner stone, a sure foundation (16)

Questions.Q: How will the LORD visit Ariel?
Questions.A: With thunder, and with earthquake, and great noise, with storm and tempest, and the flame of devouring fire (1, 6)

Questions.Q: To what did the LORD compare the vision of Ariel?
Questions.A: As the words of a book that is sealed, which men deliver to one that is learned, and to him that is not learned (11-12)

Questions.Q: How did that people draw near and honor the LORD?
Questions.A: With their mouth, and with their lips they honor God, but their heart was far from Him (13)

Questions.Q: Of whom did the rebellious children fail to ask counsel?
What would the rebellious people not hear?
Questions.A: The law of the LORD (9)

Questions.Q: What did they want the prophets to prophesy?
Questions.A: pleasant things and illusions (10)

Questions.Q: Eventually what would they hear a voice say?
Questions.A: This is the way, walk you in it (21)

Questions.Q: Upon whom is woe pronounced in this chapter?
Questions.A: Those who go down to Egypt (1)

Questions.Q: Who will defend Jerusalem?
Questions.A: The LORD of hosts (5)

Questions.Q: On what land will come up thorns and briers?
Questions.A: On the land of God's people (13)

Questions.Q: What is the effect of righteousness?
Questions.A: Quietness and assurance (17)

Questions.Q: What will happen to those who spoil and deal treacherously?
Questions.A: They will be spoiled and dealt treacherously (1)

Questions.Q: With what has the LORD filled Zion?
Questions.A: Judgment and righteousness (5)

Questions.Q: What positions does the LORD hold?
Questions.A: Judge, lawgiver, and king (22)

Questions.Q: What will come on all nations?
Questions.A: The indignation of the LORD (2)

Questions.Q: What should we seek out?
Questions.A: The book of the LORD (16)

Questions.Q: How will the desert blossom?
Questions.A: Abundantly as the rose (1-2)

Questions.Q: What will be said to those of a fearful heart?
Questions.A: Be strong, fear not: behold, your God will come and save you (4)

Questions.Q: What will happen to the blind, deaf, lame and dumb?
Questions.A: The eyes of the blind shall be opened, the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped, the lame man leap as a hart, and the tongue of the mute sing. (5-6)
Questions.Note: See Matthew 15:30-31

Questions.Q: In what will wayfaring men not err?
Questions.A: The way of holiness (8)

Questions.Q: How will the ransomed of the LORD return to Zion?
Questions.A: With songs and everlasting joy on their heads (10)

Questions.Q: Who sent Rabshakeh to Jerusalem to Hezekiah with a great army?
Questions.A: Sennacherib king of Assyria (2)

Questions.Q: In what language did Rabshakeh speak to the people who were on the wall of Jerusalem?
Questions.A: Jewish (11-13)

Questions.Q: What logic did Rabshakeh use to try to persuade the Jews not to trust in the Lord?
Questions.A: If the gods of the other lands could not deliver them, how would the LORD deliver Jerusalem? (18-20)

Questions.Q: What did Hezekiah do when he heard the message of Rabshakeh?
Questions.A: He rent his clothes, covered himself with sackcloth, went into the house of the LORD, and sent his servants to Isaiah (1-4)

Questions.Q: What message did Isaiah have for Hezekiah?
Questions.A: Be not afraid of the words which the servants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed. The LORD will cause him to fall by the sword in his own land (6-7)

Questions.Q: What did Hezekiah do when he received a letter from Rabshekah?
Questions.A: He read it, went up to the house of the LORD, and spread it before the LORD (14-20)

Questions.Q: What did the Lord tell Isaiah concerning Assyria?
Questions.A: They would not come into Jerusalem or shoot an arrow there (29, 33-35)

Questions.Q: How many Assyrians did the angel of the Lord kill?
What happened to Sennacherib king of Assyria?
Questions.A: His sons struck him with the sword (37-38)

Questions.Q: What did Isaiah tell Hezekiah to do?
Questions.A: Set his house in order because he was going to die (1)

Questions.Q: How did Hezekiah react to this message?
Questions.A: He prayed and wept (2-3)

Questions.Q: How many years was the life of Hezekiah extended?
Questions.A: 15 years (5)

Questions.Q: What sign was given to Hezekiah?
Questions.A: The shadow of the sun dial would go backwards ten degrees (7-8)

Questions.Q: Who can praise the LORD?
Questions.A: The living (18-19)

Questions.Q: What did Hezekiah lay on his boil?
Questions.A: A lump of figs (21)

Questions.Q: What did Hezekiah show to Merodachbaladan, king of Babylon?
Questions.A: Everything in his house including his silver, gold, spices, precious ointment, and armor (1-4)

Questions.Q: What did Isaiah prophesy would happen?
Questions.A: All that was in his house would be carried to Babylon and his sons would be made eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon (5-7)

Questions.Q: What did Isaiah prophesy of John the Baptist?
Questions.A: That he would be a voice crying in the wilderness and what he would say (3-4)

Questions.Q: To what is the word of God contrasted?
Questions.A: Grass withering and flowers fading (8)

Questions.Q: What has God done?
Questions.A: He has measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, meted out heaven with the span, comprehended the dust of the earth in a measure, weighed the mountains in scales, and the hills in a balance (12)

Questions.Q: Compared to God what are the nations?
Questions.A: As a drop of a bucket, and as the small dust of the balance (15)

Questions.Q: On what does God sit?
Questions.A: The circle of the earth (22)

Questions.Q: What will happen to those who wait on the LORD?
Questions.A: They shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint (31)

Questions.Q: Why should we not fear?
Questions.A: God will strengthen, help, and uphold us (10, 13)

Questions.Q: Who is Isaiah prophesying about in these verses?
Questions.A: Jesus (1-3)
Questions.Note: See Matthew 12:17-20

Questions.Q: Who created the heavens and the earth and gave breath to the people?
Questions.A: God the LORD (5)

Questions.Q: To whom will the LORD give his glory?
Questions.A: Not to another god (8)

Questions.Q: Who will be greatly ashamed?
Questions.A: Those who trust in idols, who say to the molten images, “You are our gods.” (17)

Questions.Q: Why did the LORD pour out His fury on Israel?
Questions.A: They would not walk in his ways, neither were they obedient to his law (24-25)

Questions.Q: When will God be with you?
Questions.A: When you pass through the waters, the rivers, and the fire (2)

Questions.Q: What does The LORD want us to be?
Questions.A: Witnesses (10, 12)

Questions.Q: What are we to understand?
Questions.A: The LORD is God, there was no God before or after Him and there is no other savior besides Him (10-11)

Questions.Q: What does the LORD do with regard to our transgressions and sins?
Questions.A: He blots out our transgressions and does not remember our sins (25)

Questions.Q: What will the LORD pour out?
Questions.A: Water on him that is thirsty and His spirit and blessings (3)

Questions.Q: What did the LORD say regarding himself?
Questions.A: I am the first, and I am the last; and beside me there is no God. (6, 8)
I am the LORD that makes all things; that stretches forth the heavens alone; that spreads abroad the earth by myself. (24)

Questions.Q: What phrases show there is but one LORD?
Questions.A: I am the LORD, and there is none else, there is no God beside me. I am the LORD, and there is none else. the Holy One of Israel. There is no God else beside me, there is none beside me. (5-6, 11, 18, 21)

Questions.Q: To what is one compared who strives with his Maker?
Questions.A: A piece of clay striving with the potter (9)

Questions.Q: Why did the LORD form the earth?
Questions.A: To be inhabited (18)

Questions.Q: What will every knee do?
Questions.A: Bow to the LORD (23)

Questions.Q: What is one weakness of idols/gods made with human/man's hands?
Questions.A: They cannot answer, nor save a person out of his trouble (6-7)
Questions.Alternative: What is one weakness of idols made with human hands?
What is one weakness of idols made with man's hands?
What is one weakness of gods made with human hands?
What is one weakness of gods made with man's hands?

Questions.Q: What is one aspect of God that is different from gods made by man?
Questions.A: He can declare the end from the beginning (9-10)

Questions.Q: How did Babylon treat God's people?
Questions.A: They showed them no mercy (6)

Questions.Q: Who will not be able to save Babylon from the judgment that would come?
Questions.A: The astrologers, stargazers, or monthly prognosticators (13-14)

Questions.Q: How did Israel swear by the name of the LORD and make mention of God?
Questions.A: Not in truth, nor in righteousness. (1)

Questions.Q: How did God describe Israel?
Questions.A: They were obstinate, their neck was an iron sinew, and their brow brass (4)

Questions.Q: To whom is there no peace?
Questions.A: The wicked (22)

Questions.Q: What does the LORD say about forgetting us?
Questions.A: Even though a woman can forget her sucking child, God will not forget us (15)

Questions.Q: With whom will the LORD contend?
Questions.A: God will contend with him that contends with you (25)

Questions.Q: What questions did the LORD ask?
Questions.A: Why, when I came, was there no man? When I called, was there none to answer? Is my hand shortened at all, that it cannot redeem? Have I no power to deliver? (2)

Questions.Q: What will the LORD do for Zion?
Questions.A: He will comfort Zion/Israel.
He will have compassion on her ruins
He will make her desert places like the garden of the LORD

Questions.Q: What is a covenant?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A covenant is an agreement, an especially binding promise. If a person on one side of the covenant does not do as both have agreed, there usually is a strong punishment for him or he pays compensation to the other person. Similar agreements now are called contracts. When God makes an agreement with people, however, he makes a firm promise of what he will do and says what they must do.
Questions.Note: See "covenant" in KBT.

If the language has a special name to refer to these kinds of agreements, ask the respondent to tell you the kinds of situations in which the people make the agreements. Listen for any points where it would not be appropriate to state that God made that kind of an agreement. Then adjust the translation as necessary.

Questions.A: He wanted to hear a word from the LORD (17)

Questions.Q: What did Zedekiah do for Jeremiah?
Questions.A: He commanded that they should commit Jeremiah into the court of the prison, and that they should give him daily a piece of bread (20-21)

Questions.Q: Why did some want Jeremiah put to death?
Questions.A: They said he weakened the hands of the men of war that remained in Jerusalem and that he sought not the welfare of the people, but the hurt (4)

Questions.Q: Where did they cast Jeremiah?
Questions.A: In a dungeon where there was no water but mire (6)

Questions.Q: What did Ebedmelech do for Jeremiah?
Questions.A: He along with others drew Jeremiah out of the dungeon (7-13)

Questions.Q: How could Zedekiah prevent Jerusalem from being burned with fire?
Questions.A: If he would go forth to the king of Babylon's princes (17-18)

Questions.Q: How long did Jeremiah stay in the court of the prison?
Questions.A: Until the day that Jerusalem was taken (28)

Questions.Q: What did the king of Babylon do to Zedekiah?
Questions.A: He slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes, put out Zedekiah's eyes, bound him with chains and carried him to Babylon (5-7)

Questions.Q: What did the Chaldeans do in Jerusalem?
Questions.A: Burned the king's house and broke down the walls of Jerusalem (8)

Questions.Q: Whom did the Chaldeans leave in Jerusalem?
Questions.A: The poor of the people (9-10)

Questions.Q: What did Nebuchadrezzar charge concerning Jeremiah?
Questions.A: Take him, look well to him, and do him no harm but do to him even as he says (11-14)

Questions.Q: What did Jeremiah prophesy concerning Ebedmelech the Ethiopian?
Questions.A: God would deliver him, and he would not fall by the sword (15-18)

Questions.Q: What decision did Nebuzaradan (the captain of the guard) give Jeremiah to make?
Questions.A: To either go to Babylon with him or stay in the land (4)

Questions.Q: Whom did the king of Babylon make governor over the cities of Judah?
Questions.A: Gedaliah, the son of Ahikam (5)

Questions.Q: What did Nebuzaradan (the captain of the guard) give Jeremiah when he let him go?
Questions.A: A ration and a gift (5)

Questions.Q: What choice did Jeremiah make?
Questions.A: To go to Mizpah to Gedaliah and stay with him among the people who were left in the land (6)

Questions.Q: Who returned to Judah?
Questions.A: The Jews that were in Moab, among the Ammonites, Edom, and that were in all the countries (11-12)

Questions.Q: Who told Gedaliah that Ishmael was going to kill him?
Questions.A: Johanan the son of Kareah (13-16)

Questions.Q: How did Gedaliah die?
Questions.A: Ishmael and ten men struck Gedaliah with the sword (1-2)

Questions.Q: Where did Ishmael throw the bodies of the men he killed that were from Samaria?
Questions.A: Into the middle of the pit (5-9)

Questions.Q: Who rescued those whom Ishmael carried captive?
Questions.A: Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces that were with him (10-14)

Questions.Q: What did the people who were left in Judah request of Jeremiah?
Questions.A: Pray for them that the LORD would show them what they should do (1-3)

Questions.Q: What would happen to the people if they stayed in Judah?
Questions.A: God would build and plant them and deliver them from the king of Babylon (9-12)

Questions.Q: What would happen to the people if they went to Egypt?
Questions.A: The sword and famine would follow them to Egypt and they would die (13-22)

Questions.Q: What attitude did the men have who said that Jeremiah spoke falsely?
Questions.A: Pride (2)

Questions.Q: To where did Johanan and his captains take the remnant of Judah including Jeremiah?
Questions.A: Egypt (5-7)

Questions.Q: Who did Jeremiah prophesy would attack Egypt and burn the houses of their gods?
Questions.A: Nebuchadrezzar the king of Babylon (10-13)

Questions.Q: How did the Jews who went into Egypt reply to Jeremiah's prophecy?
Questions.A: They did not listen to him (13-17)

Questions.Q: What did Jeremiah prophesy regarding Pharaohhophra king of Egypt?
Questions.A: He would be given into the hands of his enemies that sought his life (30)

Questions.Q: What did Jeremiah prophesy regarding Baruch's life?
Questions.A: His life would be given for a prey (5)

Questions.Q: Against what nation did Jeremiah prophesy in this chapter?
Questions.A: Egypt (2)

Questions.Q: In contrast to other nations what was God going to do to Jacob?
Questions.A: Although God would punish Jacob, He was going to save then, enable them to return to their land and be at rest (27-28)

Questions.Q: Against what nation did Jeremiah prophesy in this chapter?
Questions.A: Philistia (1)

Questions.Q: Against what nation did Jeremiah prophesy in this chapter?
Questions.A: Moab (1)

Questions.Q: Who was cursed?
Questions.A: He that does the work of the LORD deceitfully (10)

Questions.Q: Why was Moab destroyed?
Questions.A: For magnifying himself against the LORD (42)
