Questions.Q: Against what nations did Jeremiah prophesy in this chapter?
Questions.A: Ammon, Edom, Damascus, Kedar, and Elam (1, 7, 23, 28, 34)

Questions.Q: Against what nation did Jeremiah prophesy in this chapter?
Questions.A: Babylon (1)

Questions.Q: Who first devoured Israel?
Questions.A: The king of Assyria (17)

Questions.Q: Who has not been forsaken?
Questions.A: Israel and Judah (5)

Questions.Q: What should be declared in Zion?
Questions.A: The work of the LORD (10)

Questions.Q: How was the earth made?
Questions.A: God made the earth by his power, he established the world by his wisdom, and stretched out the heaven by his understanding (15)

Questions.Q: What was the Lord going to use as his weapons of war?
Questions.A: Jacob and Israel as his battle ax (19-23)

Questions.Q: Who is mentioned among the nations against Babylon?
Questions.A: The Medes (28)

Questions.Q: What did Jeremiah write in a book?
Questions.A: All the evil that should come on Babylon (60)

Questions.Q: What was Seriah to do with the book that Jeremiah had written?
Questions.A: Bind a stone to it, cast it into the middle of Euphrates, and say, Thus shall Babylon sink and (63-64)
not rise (63-64)

Questions.Q: How many persons were carried captive into Babylon?
What did Evilmerodach king of Babylon do for Jehoiachin king of Judah?
Questions.A: Brought him out of prison, set up his throne, changed his garments and fed him every day (31-34)

Questions.Q: Where was Judah at the time of the writing of this book?
Questions.A: In captivity (3)

Questions.Q: Why did the LORD afflict Judah?
Questions.A: For the multitude of her transgressions and grievous sins (5, 8)

Questions.Q: What was the attitude of the writer of this book regarding the punishment of Judah?
Questions.A: He wept and was sick inside (11)

Questions.Q: What do all that pass by Jerusalem do?
Questions.A: They clapped their hands, hissed and wagged their heads at Jerusalem (15)

Questions.Q: What did the LORD fulfill?
Questions.A: His word (17)

Questions.Q: What should the people do to the LORD?
Questions.A: They should cry out, weep and pour out their heart to the LORD (18-19)

Questions.Q: Why are we not consumed?
Questions.A: Because of the LORD's mercies and his compassions (22-23)

Questions.Q: What is good for a man/person?
Questions.A: That he both hope and quietly wait for the salvation of the LORD and bear the yoke of his youth (25-27)
Questions.Alternative: What is good for a man?
What is good for a person?

Questions.Q: What did the Lord hear?
Questions.A: Jeremiah's voice and the reproach of those that rose against him (56, 61-62)

Questions.Q: To what is the cruelty of people compared?
Questions.A: Ostriches in the wilderness (3)

Questions.Q: The punishment of the iniquity of God's people was greater than the punishment of what city?
Questions.A: Sodom (6)

Questions.Q: What does the writer want the LORD to remember, consider and behold?
Questions.A: Their reproach (1)

Questions.Q: What question does the writer ask the LORD?
Questions.A: Why do you forget us forever, and forsake us so long time? (20)

Questions.Q: What prayer does the writer pray to the LORD?
Questions.A: Turn you us to you, renew our days as of old (21)

Questions.Q: Where was Ezekiel when he wrote this book?
Questions.A: Among the captives by the river of Chebar (1-3)

Questions.Q: What came out of the whirlwind?
Questions.A: The likeness of four living creatures (4-5)

Questions.Q: What four faces did each one have?
Questions.A: Man, lion, ox, and eagle (6, 10)

Questions.Q: What was in the wheels?
Questions.A: The spirit of the living creature (16, 20-21)

Questions.Q: What was the appearance of the one on the throne?
Questions.A: A man of the likeness of the glory of God (26, 28)

Questions.Q: What did Ezekiel do when he saw the appearance of the one on the throne?
Questions.A: He fell on his face and heard the voice of one that spoke (28)

Questions.Q: How did God describe Israel to Ezekiel?
Questions.A: A rebellious nation that rebelled and transgressed against God, impudent and stiff-hearted (3-4)

Questions.Q: What would Israel know?
Questions.A: That there has been a prophet among them (5)

Questions.Q: Of what was Ezekiel not to be afraid?
Questions.A: Their words or looks (6)

Questions.Q: What was Ezekiel to do?
Questions.A: Speak (7)
God's word to them whether they heard or not (7)

Questions.Q: What was sent to Ezekiel?
Questions.A: A hand with a roll of a book (9-10)

Questions.Q: What was Ezekiel to do with the roll of a book?
Questions.A: Eat it (1-3)

Questions.Q: To what people was Ezekiel to speak?
Questions.A: The house of Israel, the exiles (4-7, 11)

Questions.Q: What did the LORD make Ezekiel to be?
Questions.A: A watchman (17)

Questions.Q: Under what circumstance would their blood be on Ezekiel's hands?
Questions.A: If he failed to give warning (18, 20)

Questions.Q: For how many days was Ezekiel to lie on his left side and what did these days represent?
Questions.A: 395 days which was the years of the iniquity of the house of Israel (4-5)

Questions.Q: For how many days was Ezekiel to lie on his right side and what did these days represent?
Questions.A: 40 days which was the years of the iniquity of Judah (6)

Questions.Q: What was Ezekiel to do with each of the three parts of his hair?
Questions.A: Burn one part, cut up another part with a knife and scatter the third part in the wind (1-2)

Questions.Q: What judgments was God going to send on the three parts of Jerusalem?
Questions.A: Death by pestilence, famine and the sword (12)

Questions.Q: Against whom did Ezekiel pronounce judgment in this chapter?
Questions.A: Israel (1-7)

Questions.Q: What would the remnant that escaped do?
Questions.A: They shall remember God among the nations where they shall be carried captives (8-9)

Questions.Q: What would they know?
Questions.A: That God is the LORD (10, 13, 14)

Questions.Q: What was near?
Questions.A: The day of trouble (7)

Questions.Q: What would not be able to deliver them in the day of the wrath of the LORD?
Questions.A: Their silver and their gold (19)

Questions.Q: Where did the spirit lift Ezekiel?
Questions.A: Between the earth and the heaven, and brought him in the visions of God to Jerusalem (3)

Questions.Q: What did Ezekiel see in the visions?
Questions.A: The great abominations that the house of Israel committed (6, 9, 13, 15)

Questions.Q: What were twenty-five men in the temple worshiping?
Questions.A: The sun (16)
Questions.Alternative: What were twenty-five men in the temple worshipping?

Questions.Q: Upon whose foreheads did the man, clothed with linen, set a mark?
Questions.A: The men that sigh and that cry for all the abominations (4)

Questions.Q: What happened to those on whom there was no mark?
Questions.A: They were slaughtered (5-7)

Questions.Q: With what was the man clothed in linen to fill his hands?
Questions.A: Coals of fire from between the cherubim (2, 6-7)

Questions.Q: What were the four faces like on the wheels?
Questions.A: A cherub, a man, a lion, and an eagle (14)

Questions.Q: What happened to Pelatiah the son of Benaiah when Ezekiel prophesied?
Questions.A: He died (13)

Questions.Q: What would God be to those whom He scattered among the countries?
Questions.A: As a little sanctuary (16)

Questions.Q: What will God give to those He gathers and assembles out of the countries?
Questions.A: The land of Israel. Also a new spirit and a heart of flesh (17-20)

Questions.Q: Where did Ezekiel dwell according to the LORD?
Questions.A: In the middle of a rebellious house (1-2)

Questions.Q: In what manner was Ezekiel a sign to the house of Israel?
Questions.A: As Ezekiel removed his stuff and went to another place so would the house of Israel remove and go into captivity (3-13)

Questions.Q: What shall come to pass and be no more prolonged?
Questions.A: The words of the LORD (25-28)

Questions.Q: To whom did Ezekiel prophesy in this chapter?
Questions.A: The prophets of Israel that prophesy out of their own hearts, that follow their own spirit, and have seen nothing (1-3)

Questions.Q: How did the false prophets mislead the people?
Questions.A: They proclaimed peace, but there was no peace. (10, 16)

Questions.Q: What did the false prophetesses make?
Questions.A: Magic bands and veils for people's heads (17-21)

Questions.Q: How had they profaned God?
Questions.A: They put to death some who should not die and to kept others alive who should not live. They lied. (19)
They disheartened the righteous with falsehood when God did not cause him grief, but encouraged the wicked not to turn from his wicked way. (22)

Questions.Q: What did the Lord tell the house of Israel to do?
Questions.A: Repent, and turn from idols; and from all abominations (6)

Questions.Q: What three men, if they were in Israel at that time, would only be able to deliver their own souls?
Questions.A: Noah, Daniel, and Job (14, 16, 18, 20)

Questions.Q: What four sore judgments was the LORD going to send on Jerusalem?
Questions.A: Sword, famine, noisome beast, and pestilence (21)

Questions.Q: What object lesson did the LORD give to Ezekiel to show what would happen to the inhabitants of Jerusalem?
Questions.A: A vine tree (2-6)

Questions.Q: What did Jerusalem do?
Questions.A: Trusted in her own beauty, played the harlot, and poured out her fornications/sexual immorality on every one that passed by (15)

Questions.Q: To what did the LORD compare Jerusalem?
Questions.A: As a wife that commits adultery, which takes strangers instead of her husband (32)

Questions.Q: What proverb would be used against Jerusalem?
Questions.A: As is the mother, so is her daughter (44)

Questions.Q: What did the first eagle represent in the parable?
Questions.A: The king of Babylon would come to Jerusalem, and take the king and the princes thereof, and lead them to Babylon (1-6, 11-12)

Questions.Q: What did the second eagle represent?
Questions.A: The king of Egypt (7-10, 15-18)

Questions.Q: What proverb were they no longer to use in Israel?
Questions.A: The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge (2-3)

Questions.Q: Who would die?
Questions.A: The soul that sins (4, 13, 18, 20, 24)

Questions.Q: What should a person do regarding their transgressions?
Questions.A: Repent and turn from all his transgressions and make himself a new heart and a new spirit (30-31)

Questions.Q: For whom is this chapter a lamentation?
Questions.A: The princes of Israel (1, 14)

Questions.Q: To what is the mother of the princes of Israel compared?
Questions.A: A lioness and a vine in blood (2, 10)

Questions.Q: For what purpose did the elders of Israel come to Ezekiel?
Questions.A: To inquire of the LORD (1)

Questions.Q: How did the LORD respond?
Questions.A: I will not be inquired of by you (3, 31)

Questions.Q: How would the LORD plead with Israel when He gathers them out of the countries where they were scattered?
Questions.A: Like He pleaded with their fathers in the wilderness of the land of Egypt (34-36)

Questions.Q: What did the LORD tell Ezekiel to do because of the coming judgments?
Questions.A: Sigh, cry and howl (6, 12)

Questions.Q: What did the LORD tell the wicked prince of Israel to do?
Questions.A: Remove the diadem, and take off the crown: exalt him that is low, and abase him that is high (25-26)

Questions.Q: What object lesson did the LORD use to show how He was going to pour out his fury on Jerusalem?
Questions.A: Fire melting metal in the middle of a furnace (18-22)

Questions.Q: Of what did the priests make no difference?
Questions.A: Between the holy and profane (26)

Questions.Q: What motivated her princes?
Questions.A: To get dishonest gain (27)

Questions.Q: What was the LORD not able to find?
Questions.A: A man, that should make up the hedge, and stand in the gap before God for the land, that God would not destroy it (30)

Questions.Q: Who did Aholah represent?
Questions.A: Samaria (4)

Questions.Q: Who did Aholibah represent?
Questions.A: Jerusalem (4)

Questions.Q: Into whose hands was Aholah delivered?
Questions.A: The Assyrians (9)

Questions.Q: Who would judge Aholibah?
Questions.A: The Babylonians, Chaldeans, Pekod, Shoa, and Koa (23-24)

Questions.Q: What happened to Ezekiel's wife after he spoke to the people in the morning?
Questions.A: She died (18)

Questions.Q: What did the people want to know?
Questions.A: They wondered why Ezekiel was not crying or acting the way a person normally would when his wife had died.

Questions.Q: What was Ezekiel to the house of Israel?
Questions.A: A sign to them; that they would know that God is the LORD. (24, 27)

Questions.Q: Against what four nations was judgment prophesied in this chapter?
Questions.A: Ammon, Moab, Edom and the Philistines (2, 11, 13, 16)

Questions.Q: Who was the Lord GOD going to bring against Tyre?
Questions.A: Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon (7)

Questions.Q: What all would fall into the middle of the seas in the day of the ruin of Tyre?
Questions.A: Their riches, merchandise, mariners, pilots, caulkers, and men of war (27, 34)

Questions.Q: What did the prince of Tyre say?
Questions.A: I am a God, I sit in the seat of God, in the middle of the seas (2)

Questions.Q: What are some phrases in this portion of scripture that some use as a description of Satan?
Questions.A: You are the anointed cherub, you were perfect in your ways from the day that you were created, till iniquity was found in you, your heart was lifted up because of your beauty, I will cast you to the ground. (12-17)

Questions.Q: Against whom else did Ezekiel prophesy?
Questions.A: Sidon (21-22)

Questions.Q: Where did the LORD say Israel would dwell?
Questions.A: In their land that God gave to my Jacob (25-26)

Questions.Q: Why was the LORD going to make Egypt desolate and waste?
Questions.A: Egypt said, The river is mine, and I have made it (9)

Questions.Q: What would Egypt no longer do?
Questions.A: Exalt itself any more above the nations (15)

Questions.Q: Why was Egpyt given to Nebuchadrezzar, king of Babylon?
Questions.A: Because they worked for God (18-20)

Questions.Q: When the LORD sets a fire in Egypt who else will be destroyed?
Questions.A: All her helpers (8)

Questions.Q: To what was the Assyrian compared?
Questions.A: A cedar in Lebanon (3-9)

Questions.Q: What would happen to the Assyrian?
Questions.A: It fell and was cast down to hell (10-16)

Questions.Q: What would happen to Pharaoh, king of Egypt?
Questions.A: Brought down (2, 18)

Questions.Q: What would the king of Babylon spoil?
Questions.A: The pomp of Egypt (11-12)

Questions.Q: On what other nations was judgment prophesied?
Questions.A: Asshur, Elam, Meshech, Tubal, Edom, Sidon (22, 24, 26, 29, 30)

Questions.Q: When is the blood required at the watchman's hand?
Questions.A: If he does not sound a warning when the enemy comes or if he does not warn the wicked from his way (6, 8)

Questions.Q: To whom was Ezekiel set as a watchman?
Questions.A: House of Israel (7)

Questions.Q: In what does the LORD have/take no pleasure?
Questions.A: The death of the wicked (11)
Questions.Alternative: In what does the LORD have no pleasure?
In what does the LORD take no pleasure?

Questions.Q: When do the righteous die?
Questions.A: When the righteous turns from his righteousness, and commits iniquity (18)

Questions.Q: When do the wicked live?
Questions.A: When he turns from his wickedness, and does that which is lawful and right. (19)

Questions.Q: How did the mouth of the people differ from the heart?
Questions.A: With their mouth they show much love, but their heart goes after their covetousness (31)

Questions.Q: What charges did the LORD make against the shepherds of Israel?
Questions.A: The shepherds fed themselves but did not feed the flock and ruled over them with cruelty. (2-4, 8)

Questions.Q: Who would be a shepherd to Israel?
Questions.A: The Lord GOD (11-16)

Questions.Q: What kind of showers would the LORD send?
Questions.A: Showers of blessing (26)

Questions.Q: Why was the LORD against Mt. Seir?
Questions.A: They had a perpetual hatred, and had shed the blood of the Israelites by the force of the sword (5, 12-13)

Questions.Q: What was the LORD going to do for the mountains of Israel?
Questions.A: They would shoot forth their branches, and yield fruit to the people of Israel (8)

Questions.Q: Why was the LORD going to gather Israel from all countries and bring them into their own land?
Questions.A: For His holy name's sake, which they had profaned among the heathen (22-24)

Questions.Q: What was the LORD going to do for Israel?
Questions.A: He would give them a new heart and a new spirit and would take away the stony heart out of their flesh, and give them a heart of flesh. Also, He would cause them to walk in His statutes (25-28)

Questions.Q: What will the heathen know?
Questions.A: That God is the LORD (36-38)

Questions.Q: Where did the spirit of the LORD set Ezekiel?
Questions.A: In the middle of a valley which was full of bones (1)

Questions.Q: What was Ezekiel to prophesy to the bones?
Questions.A: The Lord GOD will cause breath to enter into you, and you shall live (4-6)

Questions.Q: What was Ezekiel to prophesy to the wind?
Questions.A: Breathe into these slain, that they may live (9)

Questions.Q: What did the bones represent?
Questions.A: The whole house of Israel (11)

Questions.Q: What did the two sticks becoming one represent?
Questions.A: Judah and Israel would become one nation (16-22)

Questions.Q: Who was with Gog that Ezekiel prophesied against?
Questions.A: Gog, the land of Magog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal (1-6)

Questions.Q: What will the LORD rain against Gog when he comes against Israel?
Questions.A: Great hailstones, fire, and brimstone (22)

Questions.Q: Where will Gog fall?
Questions.A: On the mountains of Israel (4)

Questions.Q: How long will it take Israel to bury Gog?
Questions.A: Seven months (12)

Questions.Q: What will the LORD pour out on the house of Israel?
Questions.A: His Spirit (29)

Questions.Q: What was the man in the vision doing with the reed?
Questions.A: Measuring the building (5)

Questions.Q: What was measured in this chapter?
Questions.A: The temple (1)

Questions.Q: What in particular is described mostly in this chapter?
Questions.A: The chambers (1-13)

Questions.Q: Like what was the voice of the God of Israel?
Questions.A: A noise of many waters (2)

Questions.Q: Of what was the house of Israel to be ashamed?
Questions.A: Their iniquities (10)

Questions.Q: Which gate shall be shut and not opened?
Questions.A: The gate of the outward sanctuary which looks toward the east (1-2)

Questions.Q: What were the priests to teach God's people?
Questions.A: The difference between the holy and profane (23)

Questions.Q: What was to be given to the priests?
Questions.A: The meat, sin, and trespass offerings and the first of all the first fruits of all things (29-30)

Questions.Q: What were the princes of Israel to remove?
Questions.A: Violence and spoil (9)

Questions.Q: From where do the sons of the prince get their inheritance?
Questions.A: The prince (16-18)

Questions.Q: What was on both sides of the river?
Questions.A: Trees (7)
Questions.Note: See also Revelation 22:1-2

Questions.Q: What was in the river?
Questions.A: Fish (9-10)

Questions.Q: For what will the leaf of the trees be used?
Questions.A: Medicine (12)
Questions.Note: See Revelation 22:2

Questions.Q: Who will inherit the land?
To whom will the land be divided?
Questions.A: The tribes of Israel (1-29)

Questions.Q: What will be the names of the gates of the city?
Questions.A: The tribes of Israel (31-34)

Questions.Q: What will be the name of the city?
Questions.A: The LORD is there (35)

Questions.Q: Where did Nebuchadnezzar put the vessels which he had taken from the house of God in Jerusalem?
Questions.A: Into the treasure house of his god in the land of Shinar (1-2)

Questions.Q: What were the qualifications of those chosen to be taught the learning and the tongue of the Chaldeans?
Questions.A: Children in whom was no blemish, but well favored, and skillful in all wisdom, and cunning in knowledge, and understanding science, and such as had ability in them to stand in the king's palace (4)

Questions.Q: What names were given to Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah?
Questions.A: To Daniel the name of Belteshazzar; to Hananiah, Shadrach, to Mishael, Meshach, and to Azariah, Abednego (6-7)

Questions.Q: What did Daniel purpose in his heart that he would not do?
Questions.A: He would not defile himself with the portion of the king's meat, nor with the wine which he drank (8)

Questions.Q: How did those who ate vegetables appear after ten days of eating vegetables?
Questions.A: Their countenances appeared fairer and fatter in flesh than all the children which did eat the portion of the king's meat (15)

Questions.Q: What did God give the four who ate the vegetables?
Questions.A: Knowledge and skill in all learning and wisdom: and Daniel had understanding in all visions and dreams (17)

Questions.Q: When the king inquired of them regarding wisdom and understanding, how much better were they than the magicians and astrologers?
Questions.A: Ten times better (20)

Questions.Q: What did Nebuchadnezzar remember about his dream?
Questions.A: Nothing (5)

Questions.Q: What was the king going to do to all the magicians and astrologers because they could not make known the meaning of the dream?
Questions.A: Cut them in pieces, and make their houses a dunghill (5, 12)

Questions.Q: What did Daniel and his friends do?
Questions.A: Daniel went in, and desired of the king that he would give him time, and that he would show the king the interpretation. Then Daniel made the thing known to Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, that they would desire mercies of the God of heaven concerning this secret (13-18)

Questions.Q: What did God do for Daniel?
Questions.A: Revealed to Daniel the secret in a night vision (19)

Questions.Q: Of what was the image in the dream made?
Questions.A: The head was of fine gold, his breast and his arms of silver, his belly and his thighs of brass, his legs of iron, his feet part of iron and part of clay (32-33)

Questions.Q: What did the stone that was cut without hands do?
Questions.A: Struck the image on his feet that were of iron and clay, and broke them to pieces and became a great mountain (34-35)

Questions.Q: Who was the head of gold?
Questions.A: Nebuchadnezzar (38)

Questions.Q: What did the other parts of the body represent?
Questions.A: Other kingdoms which would follow (39-43)

Questions.Q: What did the king acknowledge?
Questions.A: That Daniel's God is a God of gods, and a Lord of kings, and a revealer of secrets (47)

Questions.Q: To what position did the king promote Daniel?
Questions.A: Ruler over the whole province of Babylon, and chief of the governors over all the wise men of Babylon (48)

Questions.Q: What did Daniel request?
Questions.A: That Nebuchadnezzar set Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, over the affairs of the province of Babylon (49)

Questions.Q: What would happen to those who refused to bow down to Nebuchadnezzar's image?
Questions.A: Cast into the middle of a burning fiery furnace (6)

Questions.Q: Who refused to worship the image?
Questions.A: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego (12)

Questions.Q: How hot was the furnace heated?
Questions.A: Seven times more than it was accustomed to be heated (19)

Questions.Q: What happened to those who threw the three Hebrew men into the furnace?
Questions.A: The flames of the fire killed them (22)

Questions.Q: What did Nebuchadnezzar see when he looked into the furnace?
Questions.A: Four men loose, walking in the middle of the fire, and the form of the fourth was like the Son of God (24-25)

Questions.Q: What didn't the fire do to the three Hebrew children?
Questions.A: It did not singe the hairs of their head, neither were their coats changed, nor the smell of fire had passed on them (27)

Questions.Q: What decree did Nebuchadnezzar make?
Questions.A: That every people, nation, and language, which speak any thing amiss against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, shall be cut in pieces, and their houses shall be made a dunghill (29)

Questions.Q: What did the king do for the three Hebrew children?
Questions.A: Promoted them (30)

Questions.Q: What was Daniel's reaction when he heard the dream which Nebuchadnezzar had?
Questions.A: Astonished for one hour (19)

Questions.Q: Who was the tree that grew and was strong?
Questions.A: Nebuchadnezzar (20-22)

Questions.Q: How long would Nebuchadnezzar dwell with the beasts and eat grass?
Questions.A: Seven years (23)
Questions.Alternative: How long would Nebuchadnezzar live with the beasts and eat grass?
How long would Nebuchadnezzar live like an animal and eat grass?

Questions.Q: What would Nebuchadnezzar learn from this experience?
Questions.A: That those who walk in pride God is able to abase. (23, 37)

Questions.Q: What vessels did Belshazzar use to drink wine?
Questions.A: The golden and silver vessels which his father Nebuchadnezzar had taken out of the temple in Jerusalem (2-4)

Questions.Q: What appeared on the wall of the king's palace?
Questions.A: A man's hand writing (5)

Questions.Q: What did Belshazzar know?
Questions.A: All about how his father, Nebuchadnezzar, was deposed from his throne and was made like the beasts and ate grass (18-22)

Questions.Q: What was the interpretation of the writing on the wall?
Questions.A: God numbered Belshazzar's kingdom, and finished it. He was weighed in the balances, and are found wanting. His kingdom was divided, and given to the Medes and Persians (25-28)

Questions.Q: To what position was Daniel promoted?
Questions.A: Third ruler in the kingdom (29)

Questions.Q: What happened to Belshazzar?
Questions.A: That night he was slain (30)

Questions.Q: Who took the kingdom?
Questions.A: Darius the Median (31)

Questions.Q: To what position did Darius promote Daniel?
Questions.A: First president over the 120 princes (1-3)

Questions.Q: What were the other presidents and princes not able to find in Daniel?
Questions.A: Any fault (4-5)

Questions.Q: What decree did the other presidents and princes get Darius to sign?
Questions.A: Whoever shall ask a petition of any God or man for thirty days, save of King Darius, shall be cast into the den of lions (6-9)

Questions.Q: What did Daniel do after the decree was signed?
Questions.A: Prayed three times a day as he did before (10)

Questions.Q: What did the king reluctantly do?
Questions.A: Had Daniel cast into the den of lions (14-16)

Questions.Q: What did the king believe?
Questions.A: That God would deliver Daniel (16)

Questions.Q: What did the king do that night?
Questions.A: Fasted (18)

Questions.Q: What did the king find the next morning?
Questions.A: That Daniel was not hurt by the lions (19-23)

Questions.Q: What did the king do to those who accused Daniel?
Questions.A: Cast them and their families into the den of lions (24)

Questions.Q: What was the next decree that King Darius wrote?
Questions.A: That in every dominion of the kingdom of Darius men tremble and fear before the God of Daniel (25-27)

Questions.Q: In what reigns did Daniel prosper?
Questions.A: In the reign of Darius, and in the reign of Cyrus the Persian (28)

Questions.Q: What was the appearance of the first beast?
Questions.A: A lion with eagle's wings (4)

Questions.Q: What was the appearance of the second beast?
Questions.A: A bear with three ribs in its mouth (5)

Questions.Q: What was the appearance of the third beast?
Questions.A: A four headed leopard with four wings of a fowl on its back (6)

Questions.Q: What was the appearance of the fourth beast?
Questions.A: Dreadful, terrible, and exceedingly strong; and it had great iron teeth and ten horns (7)

Questions.Q: What was the appearance of the Ancient of days?
Questions.A: His garment was white as snow, and the hair of his head like the pure wool (9)

Questions.Q: What were the four beasts?
Questions.A: Four kings, which shall arise out of the earth (17)

Questions.Q: What were the ten horns of the fourth beast?
Questions.A: Ten kings that shall arise (24)

Questions.Q: Whose kingdom is an everlasting kingdom?
Questions.A: The most High (27)

Questions.Q: What did the ram with two horns represent?
Questions.A: The kings of Media and Persia (3-4, 20)

Questions.Q: What did the he goat represent?
Questions.A: The king of Greece (5-8, 21)

Questions.Q: What did the great horn between the eyes of the goat represent?
Questions.A: The first king of Greece (5, 21)

Questions.Q: What came up after the great horn was broken and what do these represent?
Questions.A: Four horns that came up which represented four kingdoms that shall stand up out of the nation (8-10, 22)

Questions.Q: How long shall the sanctuary be trodden under foot?
Who will stand before the Prince of princes and be broken?
Questions.A: A king of fierce countenance, and understanding dark sentences, (23-25)

Questions.Q: What did Daniel understand?
Questions.A: The number of the years, whereof the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah the prophet, that he would accomplish seventy years in the desolations of Jerusalem (2)

Questions.Q: For whom did Daniel confess?
Questions.A: Judah, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and all Israel, including those in all the countries where God had driven them (4-16)

Questions.Q: Who touched Daniel while he was praying?
Questions.A: Gabriel (21)

Questions.Q: How many weeks were determined on God's people?
Questions.A: Seventy weeks (24)

Questions.Q: How many weeks would there be from the going forth of the commandment to restore and to build Jerusalem to the Messiah the Prince?
Questions.A: Sixty-nine weeks (25)

Questions.Q: When was Jerusalem destroyed again?
Questions.A: After the Messiah was cut off (26)

Questions.Q: When will the sacrifice cease?
Questions.A: In the midst of the seventieth week (27)

Questions.Q: How long was Daniel mourning and eating no flesh?
Questions.A: Three full weeks (2-3)

Questions.Q: When did the man clothed in linen hear?
Questions.A: From the first day that Daniel set his heart to understand, and to chasten himself before God (12)

Questions.Q: Why didn't he respond sooner?
Questions.A: The prince of the kingdom of Persia withstood the man clothed in linen one and twenty days (13)

Questions.Q: Who would come after the prince of Persia?
Questions.A: The prince of Greece (20)

Questions.Q: How many kings would there be in Persia?
Questions.A: Four (1-2)

Questions.Q: Who will be strong and do great exploits?
Questions.A: The people that do know their God (32)

Questions.Q: Who will exalt himself and magnify himself above every god?
Questions.A: The king who shall speak marvelous things against the God of gods (The Anti-Christ?) (36)

Questions.Q: Who would stand up for Daniel's people during the time of trouble?
Questions.A: Michael (1)

Questions.Q: Who will shine as the stars?
Questions.A: They that be wise and they that turn many to righteousness (3)

Questions.Q: Until when was the book to be sealed?
Questions.A: The time of the end (4, 9)

Questions.Q: How long will it be from the time that the daily sacrifice is taken away, and the abomination that makes desolate is set up?
Over how many provinces did the king of Persia and Media reign?
What did Queen Vashti refuse to do?
Questions.A: To come at the king's commandment and show her beauty (9-12)

Questions.Q: Why were the wise men so concerned about Vashti's behavior?
Questions.A: All the women would despise their husbands and there would be no end of disrespect and discord. (17-18)

Questions.Q: What did Memucan recommend that the king do?
Questions.A: Give her royal estate to another that is better than she (19-20)

Questions.Q: What did the king's servants suggest that he do to replace Vashti?
Questions.A: Bring all the fair virgins to the keeper of the king's women and let the maiden that pleased the king be chosen as queen. (1-4)

Questions.Q: Who raised Esther?
Questions.A: Her cousin Mordecai (5-7)

Questions.Q: What didn't Esther reveal when she was taken?
Questions.A: Her people nor her kindred (8-11, 19-20)

Questions.Q: Who was made queen instead of Vashti?
Questions.A: Esther (17)

Questions.Q: What did Mordecai overhear and tell Esther about?
Questions.A: Two of the king's chamberlains, Bigthan and Teresh, of those which kept the door, were angry, and sought to lay hands on the king Ahasuerus (21-22)

Questions.Q: Where was the investigation and following results recorded?
Questions.A: In the book of the chronicles before the king. (23)

Questions.Q: Whom did the king promote above all the princes?
Questions.A: Haman, the Agagite (1)

Questions.Q: Who refused to bow to Haman?
Questions.A: Mordecai (2)

Questions.Q: What did Haman seek to do?
Questions.A: Destroy all the Jews that were throughout the whole kingdom of Ahasuerus, (5-6)

Questions.Q: What did Haman by offering money persuade the king to write and publish to all his provinces?
Questions.A: Letters, to destroy, to kill, and to cause to perish, all Jews, both young and old, little children and women, in one day (8-15)

Questions.Q: What did Mordecai do when he perceived what was done?
Questions.A: Rent his clothes, put on sackcloth with ashes, and cried with a loud and a bitter cry even before the king's gate (1-2)

Questions.Q: What did the Jews do in each of the provinces?
Questions.A: Great mourning , fasting, weeping, wailing; and many lay in sackcloth and ashes (3)

Questions.Q: What did Mordecai request Esther to do?
Questions.A: Go in to the king, to make supplication to him, and to make request before him for the Jews (7-8)

Questions.Q: What usually happened to a person who came into the king's court not invited?
Questions.A: Put to death, except such to whom the king held out the golden scepter (11)

Questions.Q: What did Mordecai tell Esther would happen to her if she did nothing?
Questions.A: Enlargement and deliverance would arise to the Jews from another place; but she and her father's house would be destroyed (14)

Questions.Q: What question did Mordecai ask Esther?
Questions.A: Who knows whether you are come to the kingdom for such a time as this? (14)

Questions.Q: How did Esther respond?
Questions.A: She decided to go and said “If I perish, I perish”. (16)

Questions.Q: What did the king do when Esther entered the inner court?
Questions.A: The king held out to Esther the golden scepter that was in his hand and asked of her request (1-3)

Questions.Q: What did Esther request of the king?
Questions.A: Let the king and Haman come that day to the banquet that she had prepared (4-5)

Questions.Q: At the banquet what did Esther request?
Questions.A: Let the king and Haman come to the banquet that she would prepare for them the next day (6-8)

Questions.Q: What caused Haman indignation?
Questions.A: Haman saw that Mordecai stood not up, nor moved for him (9)

Questions.Q: What did his wife and friends suggest that Haman do?
Questions.A: Build a gallows fifty cubits high and request permission of the king to hang Mordecai on it. (14)

Questions.Q: How did the king sleep that night?
Questions.A: He could not sleep (1)

Questions.Q: What did the king have read to him that night?
Questions.A: The book of records of the chronicles; here it was written, that Mordecai had told of Bigthana and Teresh, who sought to lay hand on the king Ahasuerus (1-2)

Questions.Q: What did the king ask?
Questions.A: What honor and dignity has been done to Mordecai for this? (3)

Questions.Q: What did the king ask Haman?
Questions.A: What shall be done to the man whom the king delights to honor? (6)

Questions.Q: Whom did Haman think that the king wanted to honor?
Questions.A: He thought the king wanted to honor him. (6)

Questions.Q: How did Haman suggest that the king show his honor?
Questions.A: Array the man with the king's royal apparel and crown and bring him on the king's horse through the street of the city, and have the kings noble princes proclaim before him, Thus shall it be done to the man whom the king delights to honor. (7-9)

Questions.Q: Whom did the king ask Haman to honor?
Questions.A: Mordecai (10-11)

Questions.Q: What did Haman's wife and wise men recognize?
Questions.A: That Haman was going to fall before Mordecai (13)

Questions.Q: What did Esther request of the king at the banquet?
Questions.A: That the Jews be spared (1-4)

Questions.Q: What did Esther reveal to the king?
Questions.A: That the adversary and enemy was wicked Haman. (5-6)

Questions.Q: How did Haman react?
Questions.A: He was afraid and fell on the bed where on Esther was (6-8)

Questions.Q: What did the king think Haman was doing?
Questions.A: About to rape Esther (8)

Questions.Q: Where was Haman hanged?
Questions.A: On the gallows that he had prepared for Mordecai (9-10)

Questions.Q: What did the king give to Mordecai?
Questions.A: The king's ring and royal apparel of blue and white, with a great crown of gold, and with a garment of fine linen and purple (2, 15)

Questions.Q: Who was set over the house of Haman?
Questions.A: Mordecai (2)

Questions.Q: What did Esther request of the king?
Questions.A: That a letter be written to reverse the letters devised by Haman, which he wrote to destroy the Jews which were in all the king's provinces: (3-6)

Questions.Q: What were the contents of the decree sealed and sent to all the provinces?
Questions.A: The king granted the Jews to protect themselves; to destroy, kill and annihilate all the people that would assault them, and to plunder their prosperity (11-12)

Questions.Q: How did the Jews react when the decree came to them?
Questions.A: The Jews had joy and gladness, a feast and a good day. (15-16)

Questions.Q: Who helped the Jews?
Questions.A: All the rulers of the provinces, and the lieutenants, and the deputies, and officers of the king (3)

Questions.Q: What did the Jews do to their enemies?
Questions.A: Struck them with the stroke of the sword, and slaughter, and destruction (5-6)

Questions.Q: What happened to the sons of Haman?
Questions.A: They were killed and then hanged on the gallows (7-10)

Questions.Q: What is the purpose of the days of Purim?
Questions.A: For the Jews each year to remember this great deliverance (28)

Questions.Q: Where was the greatness of Mordecai written?
Questions.A: In the book of the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia (2)

Questions.Q: From where had the Israelites come out when this book was written?
Questions.A: Egypt (1)

Questions.Q: What did the LORD Command Moses to do?
Questions.A: Number the men of Israel age twenty and upwards able to go to war (2-3)

Questions.Q: How many that were able to go to war were numbered?
What tribe was not numbered?
What was the duty of the Levites?
Questions.A: Take down, carry and set up the tabernacle and vessels (50-51)

Questions.Q: Where did the Levites camp?
Questions.A: Round about the tabernacle (53)

Questions.Q: Which tribes camped east of the tabernacle?
Questions.A: Judah, Issachar, Zebulun (3-9)

Questions.Q: Which tribes camped south of the tabernacle?
Questions.A: Reuben, Simeon, Gad (10-17)

Questions.Q: Which tribes camped west of the tabernacle?
Questions.A: Ephraim. Manasseh, Benjamin (18-24)

Questions.Q: Which tribes camped east of the tabernacle?
Questions.A: Dan, Asher, Naphtali (25-31)

Questions.Q: Why did Nadab and Abihu die?
Questions.A: They offered strange fire before the LORD (4)

Questions.Q: Which sons of Aaron continued as priests?
Questions.A: Eleazar and Ithamar (4)

Questions.Q: Whom did the Lord take from among the tribes of Israel instead of every firstborn who opens the womb?
Questions.A: The Levites (12)

Questions.Q: Who were the sons of Levi?
Questions.A: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari (17)

Questions.Q: Where did the Gershonites camp and what were their duties?
Questions.A: West of the tabernacle, and they took care of the tent, coverings, hangings, curtains , and the cords (21-26)

Questions.Q: Where did the Kohathites camp and what were their duties?
Questions.A: South of the tabernacle, and they took care of the ark, table, candlestick, altars, and the vessels of the sanctuary (27-31)

Questions.Q: Where did the Merarites camp and what were their duties?
Questions.A: North of the tabernacle, and they took care of the boards, bars, pillars, and sockets (33-37)

Questions.Q: Who camped east of the tabernacle?
Questions.A: Moses, Aaron and his sons (38)

Questions.Q: Who had the oversight of the things in the tabernacle?
Questions.A: Eleazar (the son of Aaron the priest) (16)

Questions.Q: What were the Kohathites not to watch?
Questions.A: When the holy things were covered (18-20)

Questions.Q: Under whose authority were the duties of the Gershonites?
Questions.A: Ithamar the son of Aaron the priest (28)

Questions.Q: Under whose authority were the duties of the Merarites?
Questions.A: Ithamar the son of Aaron the priest. (33)

Questions.Q: Whom did the Israelites put out of the camp?
Questions.A: Every leper, and every one that has an issue, and whoever is defiled by the dead: (2-4)

Questions.Q: When a person sinned what was he to add to his restitution?
Questions.A: A fifth part (6-8)

Questions.Q: If the spirit of jealousy came on a man who suspected his wife committed adultery what was the wife made to drink?
Questions.A: Water mixed with dust of the tabernacle floor (17-26)

Questions.Q: What happened to the woman if she was guilty of adultery?
Questions.A: Her belly would swell and her thigh would rot (27)

Questions.Q: What did the vow of the Nazarite consist of concerning wine, hair, and dead bodies?
Questions.A: Drink no wine or strong drink, no razor come on his head, come at no dead body (2-8)

Questions.Q: What was Aaron to say when he blessed the Israelites?
Questions.A: The LORD bless you, and keep you: The LORD make his face shine on you, and be gracious to you: The LORD lift up his countenance on you, and give you peace. (23-26)

Questions.Q: How many carts and oxen were given to the sons of Gershon for service?
Questions.A: Two wagons and four oxen (7)

Questions.Q: How many carts and oxen were given to the sons of Merari for service?
Questions.A: Four wagons and eight oxen (8)

Questions.Q: How many carts and oxen were given to the sons of Kohath for service?
Questions.A: None (9)

Questions.Q: What did the leaders of each tribe do for twelve consecutive days?
Questions.A: Each of them offered one silver charger, one silver bowl full of fine flour mingled with oil, one spoon of gold, full of incense, one young bullock, one ram, one lamb, one kid of the goats, two oxen, five rams, five he goats, and five lambs (10-88)

Questions.Q: What did Moses hear when he went into the tabernacle after the dedicatory offering?
Questions.A: The voice of one speaking to him from off the mercy seat (89)

Questions.Q: How was the candlestick/lampstand made?
Questions.A: Of beaten gold, according to the pattern which the LORD had showed Moses (4)
Questions.Alternative: How was the candlestick made?
How was the lampstand made?

Questions.Q: Why were the Levites purified?
Questions.A: That they may execute the service of the LORD (11)

Questions.Q: The Levites were dedicated to the Lord instead of what persons?
Questions.A: Instead of the firstborn of all the children of Israel (16-18)

Questions.Q: What age group of Levites did the service of the tabernacle?
What did the Israelites celebrate on the fourteenth day of the first month?
Questions.A: The Passover (4)

Questions.Q: Who was cut off from among the people?
Questions.A: The man that declines the Passover (13)

Questions.Q: How were strangers to celebrate the Passover?
Questions.A: The same way as the Israelites (14)

Questions.Q: What covered the tabernacle when it was set up?
Questions.A: A cloud (15)

Questions.Q: What was the appearance of the cloud in the evening?
Questions.A: Fire (15)

Questions.Q: How did the Israelites know when to move or stay?
Questions.A: When the cloud was taken up (17-23)

Questions.Q: Who was to gather at the tabernacle when both trumpets sounded?
Questions.A: All the assembly (2-3)

Questions.Q: Who was to gather if just one trumpet sounded?
Questions.A: The princes which were heads of thousands (4)

Questions.Q: For what other three purposes were the trumpets to be sounded?
Questions.A: When they moved, when they went to war, and in their solemn days (5-10)

Questions.Q: What was the order of their march when the Israelites moved?
Questions.A: Judah, Issachar, Zebulun, the sons of Gershon and Merari bearing the tabernacle, Reuben, Simeon, Gad, The Kohathites bearing the sanctuary, Ephraim, Mannaseh, Benjamin, Dan, Asher, Naphtali (14-28)

Questions.Q: Whom did Moses want to go with them?
Questions.A: His father-in-law (29-32)

Questions.Q: What did the Lord send when the people complained about their hardships?
Questions.A: Fire (1-3)

Questions.Q: What did the people desire rather than manna?
Questions.A: Flesh (4-6)

Questions.Q: When was the manna provided?
Questions.A: When the dew fell in the night (9)

Questions.Q: What did Moses desire rather than carry all the people himself?
Questions.A: That God would kill him (10-15)

Questions.Q: On whom did God put His Spirit to help Moses carry the burden of the people?
Questions.A: Seventy men of the elders of Israel (16-17)

Questions.Q: How much meat did the Lord say He would provide?
Questions.A: Meat for a whole month, until it come out of their nostrils (18-20)

Questions.Q: What question did the Lord ask Moses when he doubted God's ability to provide so much meat?
Questions.A: Is the LORD's power limited (lit. is the Lord's hand short)? (23)

Questions.Q: How deep was the pile of quail that the Lord provided?
Questions.A: Two cubits high (about 3 feet or 90 centimeters) (31)

Questions.Q: What did the Lord send while the meat was still between their teeth?
Questions.A: A very great plague (33)

Questions.Q: Why did Miriam and Aaron speak against Moses?
Questions.A: Because of the Ethiopian woman whom he had married (1-2)

Questions.Q: How meek was Moses?
Questions.A: Above all the men which were on the face of the earth (3)

Questions.Q: How did the Lord speak to Moses?
Questions.A: Mouth to mouth (8)

Questions.Q: What judgment fell on Miriam?
Questions.A: Leprosy (9-14)

Questions.Q: How many men did Moses send to explore the land of Canaan?
Questions.A: Twelve (4-15)

Questions.Q: What were the men to find out about the land?
Questions.A: What the people were like: strong or weak, few or many (18)
What the land was like: good or bad, fat or lean (17-20)
Whether the cities were open camps or fortified strongholds (19)
Whether there were trees/wood in the land. (20)

Questions.Q: What were the men to bring back?
Questions.A: The fruit of the land (20-24)

Questions.Q: How long did the men explore the land?
Questions.A: Forty days (25)

Questions.Q: What report did the men give Moses?
Questions.A: The land flows with milk and honey; Nevertheless the people be strong that dwell in the land, and the cities are walled, and very great: and we saw the children of Anak . The Amalekites dwell in the land of the south: and the Hittites, Jebusites, and the Amorites, dwell in the mountains: and the Canaanites dwell by the sea, and by the coast of Jordan (26-29)

Questions.Q: Who encouraged Moses to take possession of the land?
Questions.A: Caleb (30)

Questions.Q: Why were the rest of the men afraid to attack Canaan?
Questions.A: They are stronger than we. The land eats up the inhabitants thereof; and all the people that we saw in it are men of a great stature. (31-33)

Questions.Q: Where did the whole congregation desire to return?
Questions.A: Egypt (1-4)

Questions.Q: How did Joshua and Caleb respond?
Questions.A: The land, which we passed through to search it, is an exceeding good land. If the LORD delight in us, then he will bring us into this land, and give it us; a land which flows with milk and honey. Only rebel not you against the LORD, neither fear you the people of the land; for they are bread for us: their defense is departed from them, and the LORD is with us: fear them not. (6-9)

Questions.Q: What did the congregation want to do to Joshua and Caleb?
Questions.A: Stone them (10)

Questions.Q: What did the Lord tell Moses that He would do?
Questions.A: Strike the Israelites with a pestilence, and disinherit/dispossess them (11-12)

Questions.Q: Why did Moses intercede?
Questions.A: The nations which heard the fame of God would say "Because the LORD was not able to bring this people into the land which he swore to them, therefore he killed them in the wilderness." (13-19)

Questions.Q: How did the Lord respond to the intercession of Moses?
Questions.A: I have pardoned according to your word. (20)

Questions.Q: Who would die in the wilderness?
Questions.A: All that were from twenty years old and upward which murmured against God. (22-29)

Questions.Q: Who would enter in the promised land?
Questions.A: Caleb, Joshua, and the little ones (30-31, 38)

Questions.Q: How long would they wander in the wilderness?
Questions.A: Forty years (32-34)

Questions.Q: What happened to those who searched out the land but brought back the report of unbelief?
Questions.A: Died by a plague (36-37)

Questions.Q: What did the people decide to do after the plague?
Questions.A: To go to the promised land (39-40)

Questions.Q: What happened to these people?
Questions.A: The Amalekites and the Canaanites attacked them and beat them down. (41-45)

Questions.Q: How did the offering of the Israelites compare with the offerings of the foreigners who lived with them?
Questions.A: The same offering was made by both (13-16)
Questions.Alternative: How did the offering of the Israelites compare with the offering God expected of the foreigners who lived with them?
How did the offering of the Israelites compare with the offerings of the strangers who lived with them?
How did the offering of the Israelites compare with the offerings of the strangers who dwelled with them?

Questions.Q: What type of sin is being forgiven in verses 22-29?
Questions.A: Sin of ignorance (22-29)

Questions.Q: What type of sin resulted in being cut off from the people?
Questions.A: A presumptuous sin (30-31)

Questions.Q: What happened to the man who gathered sticks on the Sabbath?
Questions.A: Stoned to death (32-36)

Questions.Q: Why were the Israelites to put tassels on the hems of their clothing?
Questions.A: To cause them to remember all the commandments of the LORD, and do them (38-40)

Questions.Q: What did Korah, Dathan and Abiram do?
Questions.A: They said Moses and Aaron took too much on them seeing that all the congregation was holy. They desired to be priests also (1-11)

Questions.Q: What happened to Korah and his followers?
Questions.A: The earth split up and swallowed them up (28-35)

Questions.Q: What was the purpose of the sign/memorial made from the censers?
Questions.A: remind the Israelites that no one except a descendant of Aaron should come to burn incense before the LORD (37-40)
Questions.Alternative: What was the purpose of the sign made from the censers?
What was the purpose of the memorial made from the censers?

Questions.Q: How many people died in the plague in addition to the incident involving Korah?
How many rods were laid before the Lord in the tabernacle?
Questions.A: Twelve (2)

Questions.Q: What happened to the rod with Aaron's name on it?
Questions.A: It budded, brought forth buds, bloomed blossoms, and yielded almonds. (8)

Questions.Q: What was the responsibility of Aaron and his sons?
Questions.A: Keep charge of the sanctuary, the altar, everything within the veil, and the priesthood (1-2, 5, 7)

Questions.Q: What were the duties of the Levites?
Questions.A: Minister to the priests and keep the charge of the tabernacle (2-4, 6)

Questions.Q: Who was to receive a share of the offerings?
Questions.A: Aaron and his family (8-19)

Questions.Q: Who was not to receive an inheritance of the land?
Questions.A: Aaron (20)

Questions.Q: What was given to the children of Levi for an inheritance?
Questions.A: Tithes (21-24)

Questions.Q: What were the Levites to give to Aaron the priest?
Questions.A: A tenth part of the tithe (the heave offering) (25-29)

Questions.Q: What animal was used for the cleansing of the priests?
Questions.A: A red heifer (2-10)

Questions.Q: Touching what caused a person to become unclean?
Questions.A: A dead body, a bone of a man, or a grave (11-22)

Questions.Q: Who died at Kadesh?
Questions.A: Miriam (1)

Questions.Q: What did the Lord tell Moses to do to provide water for the Israelites?
Questions.A: Speak to the rock (8)

Questions.Q: What did Moses do instead?
Questions.A: He struck the rock with his rod twice (9-11)

Questions.Q: As a result of this disobedience what would not the Lord allow Moses and Aaron to do?
Questions.A: Bring the congregation into the promised land (12)

Questions.Q: Who would not allow Israel to pass through their country?
What did Moses do to Eleazar before Aaron died?
Questions.A: Stripped Aaron of his garments, and put them on Eleazar his son (28)

Questions.Q: What three kings did Israel defeat?
Questions.A: Arad the Canaanite, Sihon king of the Amorites, and Og the king of Bashan (1-3, 21-35)

Questions.Q: Why did the Lord send poisonous snakes to bite the Israelites?
Questions.A: The people spoke against God, and against Moses, complained about the lack of bread, and water; and loathed the light bread (4-7)

Questions.Q: What was the remedy for the snake bites?
Questions.A: Looking on a brass serpent that Moses made and put on a pole (8-9)

Questions.Q: What did the Israelites sing at the well?
Questions.A: Spring up, O well (16-18)

Questions.Q: Of what nation was Balak king?
Questions.A: Moab (4)

Questions.Q: What did Balak want Balaam to do?
Questions.A: Curse Israel (5-6)

Questions.Q: What did God tell Balaam not to do?
Questions.A: Don't go with the Moabites and do not curse Israel for they are blessed. (12)

Questions.Q: How was Balak's second approach to Balaam different from the first?
Questions.A: He sent more honorable princes with promises of promotion (15-17)

Questions.Q: What did Balaam do that showed he was wavering?
Questions.A: He invited them to stay that night and said he would inquire of the LORD (18-19)

Questions.Q: When Balaam went with the princes of Moab what stood in his path?
Questions.A: An angel of the LORD (22-24)

Questions.Q: What did the donkey do when it saw the angel the first time?
Questions.A: Thrust herself to the wall, and crushed Balaam's foot against the wall: (23)

Questions.Q: What did the donkey do when it saw the angel further on ahead?
Questions.A: Fell down and talked to Baalam (25-30)

Questions.Q: What did the donkey ask Baalam?
Questions.A: What have I done to you to make you beat me these three times?

Questions.Q: How did Baalam answer the donkey?
Questions.A: You have made a fool of me! If only I had a sword in my hand, I would kill you right now.

Questions.Q: Then what did the donkey say to Baalam?
Questions.A: The donkey tried to help Baalam understand that since she did not normally behave in this way, she must have had a good reason.

Questions.Q: At this point in the conversation with his donkey, did Baalam know about the angel?
Questions.A: No.
Questions.Note: Although the text does not say this explicitly, it is implied by two things: 1) it says the donkey saw the angel, but it doesn't say anything about the men seeing the angel; 2) Baalam's reaction to the donkey shows that he did not understand why she had behaved as she had.

Questions.Q: What happened next so Baalam could understand why his donkey had behaved as she had?
Questions.A: The LORD made it so Baalam could see the angel.
The angel explained why the donkey had turned away from the path and why God was opposing Baalam's plans.

Questions.Q: What did the angel of the Lord tell Balaam to do?
Questions.A: Go with the men: but only the word that I shall speak to you, that you shall speak (35)

Questions.Q: Where did Balak take Balaam?
Questions.A: Into the high places of Baal, that there he might see the utmost part of Israel (41)

Questions.Q: How did Balaam wish to die?
Questions.A: The death of the righteous (10)

Questions.Q: Why was Balak frustrated?
Questions.A: He blessed Israel rather than curse them (11-12)

Questions.Q: On what mountain did they build seven altars the second time?
Questions.A: Pisgah (13-14)

Questions.Q: In what ways is God not like a man?
Questions.A: God is not a man, that he should lie (19-20)

Questions.Q: To what two animals did Balaam liken Israel?
Questions.A: Unicorn, lion (21-24)

Questions.Q: On what mountain did Balak build seven altars the third time?
Balaam prophesied that Israel's king would be greater than which king?
Questions.A: Agag (7)

Questions.Q: What was all that Balaam said he would say to Balak?
Questions.A: What the LORD said (12-13)

Questions.Q: What six nations would be conquered or destroyed?
Questions.A: Moab, Edom, Seir, Amalek, Kenites, Asshur, Eber (15-25)

Questions.Q: Of what were many of the Israelite men guilty?
Questions.A: Prostitution/sexual immorality, sacrificing to and bowing down to idols (1-3)

Questions.Q: What was to be done to those who worshiped Baal of Peor?
Questions.A: They were to be slain (4-5)
Questions.Alternative: What was to be done to those who worshipped Baal of Peor?
What was to be done to those who worshiped Baal-Peor?

Questions.Q: What did Phinehas do to the Israelite man and Midianite woman?
Questions.A: Thrust a javelin through both of them (6-8, 11-15)

Questions.Q: How many died in the plague?
How were the Israelites to treat the Midianites?
Questions.A: Be hostile to the Midianites and strike them (17-18)

Questions.Q: When Moses took his second census how many were numbered?
How was the census used to divide the land?
Questions.A: To many was given more inheritance, and to few was given the less inheritance: the inheritance was given according to those that were numbered. (53-56)

Questions.Q: How many Levites were numbered?
Who were the only ones still alive at the second census that were alive at the first census?
Questions.A: Caleb and Joshua (63-65)

Questions.Q: What incident prompted the laws of inheritance to be given?
Questions.A: The daughters of Zelophehad explained that their father died without having any sons (1-11)

Questions.Q: Whom did the Lord choose to succeed Moses?
Questions.A: Joshua (18-19)

Questions.Q: What was Moses to give him?
Questions.A: honor (20-23)

Questions.Q: How many lambs were offered each day as a burnt offering?
What was to be presented on the first day of each month as a burnt offering?
Questions.A: Two young bullocks, and one ram, seven lambs of the first year without spot (11-15)

Questions.Q: When was the Passover to be held?
Questions.A: In the fourteenth day of the first month (16)

Questions.Q: When were they to hold a sacred assembly and do no regular work?
Questions.A: In the first and seventh month of the feast of unleavened bread. Also in the day of the first fruits. (18, 25-26)

Questions.Q: What was the offering for on the tenth day of the seventh month?
Questions.A: A holy convocation which included a burnt, meat, sin, and drink offerings (7-11)

Questions.Q: What began on the fifteenth day of the seventh month?
Questions.A: A feast which included burnt, meat, drink, and sin offerings (12)

Questions.Q: What must a man do who makes a vow to the Lord?
Questions.A: He shall do according to all that proceeds out of his mouth (2)

Questions.Q: Who can disallow a vow of a young woman in the day he hears of it?
Questions.A: Her father (3-5)

Questions.Q: Who can disallow a vow of a married woman when he hears of it?
Questions.A: Her husband (6-8, 10-15)

Questions.Q: What is said about vows of widows and divorced women?
Questions.A: All her vows shall stand (9)

Questions.Q: Who were the Israelites to fight against before Moses died?
Questions.A: Midianities (1-3)

Questions.Q: How many kings of Midian were killed?
Questions.A: Five (7-8)

Questions.Q: Who else was killed with the sword?
Questions.A: Baalam (8)

Questions.Q: Why was Moses angry when the army returned?
Questions.A: They saved all the women alive who had caused the Israelites, through the counsel of Balaam, to sin against the LORD in the matter of Peor (14-16)

Questions.Q: What else did the soldiers capture besides people?
Questions.A: Sheep, cattle, and donkeys (32-35)

Questions.Q: What did the Reubenites and the Gadites request?
Questions.A: Land east of Jordan (1-5)

Questions.Q: Why did Moses at first deny their request?
Questions.A: He thought they would discourage the Israelites and compared them to those at Kadesh who refused to take the promised land. (6-15)

Questions.Q: What did the Reubenites and Gadites offer to do if Moses would grant their request?
Questions.A: Their men would go across Jordan and fight until Israel subdued its enemies before returning to their families east of Jordan. (16-19)

Questions.Q: What other tribe was given land east of Jordan?
Questions.A: Half the tribe of Manasseh (33)

Questions.Q: What is summarized in this chapter [in verses 1-49]?
Questions.A: The journeys of Israel from Egypt to the plains of Moab by Jordan near Jericho
Questions.Alternative: What is summarized in this chapter in verses 1-49?
What is summarized in this chapter?

Questions.Q: What were the Israelites to do when they crossed over Jordan?
Questions.A: Drive out all the inhabitants of the land, destroy all their pictures and molten images, pluck down all their high places: and dwell in the land (51-54)

Questions.Q: What would happen if the Israelites disobeyed?
Questions.A: Those which they let remain would be barbs/pricks in their eyes and thorns in their sides, and would trouble them (55-56)

Questions.Q: Who set the boundaries of the land of Canaan for the Israelites?
Questions.A: The LORD (1-12)

Questions.Q: This land was to be divided among how many tribes?
Questions.A: 9 ½ tribes West of Jordan and 2 ½ tribes East of Jordan. (13)

Questions.Q: How many men from each tribe were appointed to help assign the land?
Questions.A: One prince of every tribe (18)

Questions.Q: Why was land around the towns given to the Levites?
Questions.A: For their cattle, and for their goods, and for all their beasts. (3)

Questions.Q: How many towns in total were to be given to the Levites?
How many towns were to be selected as cities of refuge?
What type of killers was to be put to death?
Questions.A: Those who purposely killed someone (16-21)

Questions.Q: What type of killers was allowed to go to a city of refuge?
Questions.A: Ones who accidentally killed someone (22-23)

Questions.Q: What could happen to a killer who stepped outside a city of refuge?
Questions.A: He could be killed by a revenger of blood (26-28)

Questions.Q: At least how many witnesses were required before a man was put to death?
Questions.A: Two (30)

Questions.Q: Why must a daughter who inherits land marry within their own tribe?
Questions.A: So their inheritance would remain in the tribe of the family of their father. (6-9)

Questions.Q: Where did Moses give these commands?
Questions.A: In the plains of Moab by Jordan near Jericho. (13)

Questions.Q: With whom does the genealogy of this chapter begin?
Questions.A: Adam (1-4)

Questions.Q: From which son of Noah did Abraham and Isaac descend?
Who were the sons of Isaac?
Questions.A: Esau and Israel (Jacob) (34)

Questions.Q: How many sons did Israel have?
Questions.A: Twelve (1-2)

Questions.Q: Which son of Israel was the forefather of David?
How were Abishai, Joab, and Asahel related to David?
Questions.A: Nephews (16)

Questions.Q: Where were Absalom and Adonijah born unto David?
Questions.A: Hebron (1-4)

Questions.Q: Where was Solomon born unto David?
Questions.A: Jerusalem (5)

Questions.Q: In this section who are the men listed?
Questions.A: Kings of Judah (10-16)

Questions.Q: Whose descendants are listed in the first part of this chapter?
Questions.A: Judah (1-23)

Questions.Q: What was the prayer of Jabez?
Questions.A: Oh that you would bless me indeed, and enlarge my coast, and that your hand might be with me, and that you would keep me from evil, that it may not grieve me! (9-10)

Questions.Q: Whose descendants are listed in the last part of this chapter?
Questions.A: Simeon (24-43)

Questions.Q: Whose descendants are listed in the first part of this chapter?
Questions.A: Reuben (1-10)

Questions.Q: Why was the birthright of Reuben given to the sons of Joseph?
Questions.A: He defiled his father's bed. (1-2)

Questions.Q: Whose descendants are listed in the middle of this chapter?
What was said about the faithfulness to God of the half-tribe of Manasseh?
Questions.A: They transgressed against the God of their fathers, and went a whoring after the gods of the people of the land (23-25)

Questions.Q: What happened to the Reubenites, Gadites, and half-tribe of Manasseh?
Questions.A: The kings of Assyria carried them away (26)

Questions.Q: Whose descendants are listed in this chapter?
Questions.A: Levi (1-30)

Questions.Q: Who were two of David's musicians?
Questions.A: Heman and Asaph (31-47)

Questions.Q: Who were the ones who presented offerings?
Questions.A: Aaron and his sons (48-53)

Questions.Q: What did the other tribes give the Levites?
Questions.A: Cities and suburbs (54-81)

Questions.Q: The descendants of which six tribes are given in this chapter?
Questions.A: Issachar, Benjamin, Naphtali, Manasseh, Ephraim, and Asher

Questions.Q: What notable leader came from the tribe of Ephraim?
Questions.A: Jehoshua (Joshua) (27)

Questions.Q: From which tribe was Saul?
Questions.A: Benjamin (33)

Questions.Q: Where were the genealogies of all Israel recorded?
Questions.A: In the book of the kings of Israel and Judah (1)

Questions.Q: Why were the people of Judah taken captive to Babylon?
Questions.A: Because of their transgression (1)

Questions.Q: What were some of the duties of the Levites?
Questions.A: Porters, keepers of the gates, overseers of the vessels and instruments of the sanctuary, makers of ointment and show bread (17, 28, 33)

Questions.Q: How did Saul die?
Questions.A: After being hit by an archer Saul fell on his own sword (1-7)

Questions.Q: What did the Philistines do with Saul's corpse?
Questions.A: They fastened his head in the temple of Dagon (8-10)

Questions.Q: What did the men of Jabeshgilead do with the bodies of Saul and his sons?
Questions.A: They took their bodies, brought them to Jabesh and buried them (11-12)

Questions.Q: Why did Saul die?
Questions.A: Because of his transgression and also for asking counsel of one that had a familiar spirit (13-14)

Questions.Q: Who was anointed king over Israel?
Questions.A: David (1-3)

Questions.Q: What was called the City of David after he captured it?
Questions.A: Zion (4-9)

Questions.Q: Who is listed as one of David's mighty men, yet David had him killed?
Questions.A: David's mighty men (41)
Questions.Note: See II Samuel 23

Questions.Q: What was the dexterity of those who came to David at Ziklag?
Questions.A: They could hurl stones and shoot arrows with either hand (1-7)

Questions.Q: How swift were the Gadites who came to David?
Questions.A: As the roes on the mountains; (8-15)

Questions.Q: How often did men come to help David?
Questions.A: Day by day (22)

Questions.Q: What was said about the men of Issachar?
Questions.A: They were men that had understanding of the times, to know what Israel ought to do (32)

Questions.Q: What was said about the unity of those who came to make David king over all Israel?
Questions.A: They were of one heart to make David king (38)

Questions.Q: How did they move the ark?
Questions.A: In a new cart (1-8)

Questions.Q: What happened to Uzzah when they tried to bring back the ark?
Questions.A: The Lord struck and killed him when he put forth his hand to hold the ark (9-11)

Questions.Q: Where did they bring the ark instead of taking it to the City of David?
Questions.A: Into the house of Obededom (12-14)

Questions.Q: What did David perceive when Hiram sent materials and laborers to him?
Questions.A: That the LORD had confirmed him king over Israel (1-2)

Questions.Q: What did David do in Jerusalem?
Questions.A: He took more wives at Jerusalem: and had more sons and daughters (3-7)

Questions.Q: What did David do to the gods of the Philistines?
Questions.A: He burned them (8-12)

Questions.Q: How did would David know when he should go to battle?
Questions.A: When he heard a sound of going in the tops of the mulberry trees (13-17)

Questions.Q: What did David recognize was wrong with the way he tried to bring the ark the first time?
Questions.A: They did not move it the way it should be moved (sought him not after the due order) (12-13)

Questions.Q: How was the ark brought in the second attempt?
Questions.A: The Levites carried the ark of God on their shoulders with the poles, as Moses had commanded. (15)

Questions.Q: What music was involved in bringing back the ark?
Questions.A: Singing with instruments of music, psalteries and harps and cymbals (16-28)

Questions.Q: Who despised David when she saw him dancing?
Questions.A: Michal (29)

Questions.Q: Into what structure was the ark set?
Questions.A: A tent (1)

Questions.Q: What are we to do to the LORD?
Questions.A: Give thanks, call on his name, make known his deeds, sing to him, talk of all his wondrous works, glory in his holy name, and seek the LORD (8-11)

Questions.Q: Who is great and greatly to be praised?
Questions.A: The Lord (25)

Questions.Q: What caused David concern?
Questions.A: That he lived in a house of cedar while the ark of the covenant remained under curtains (1)

Questions.Q: Who did Nathan say would build a house for God?
Questions.A: One of David's sons (2-15)

Questions.Q: Who is like unto God?
Questions.A: There is none like Him (20-22)

Questions.Q: Where did the Lord give David victory?
Questions.A: Over the Philistines, Moabites, Syrians, Edomites, and several other kingdoms (1-13)

Questions.Q: Who was over David's army?
Why did David want to show kindness to Hanun?
Questions.A: Because his father showed kindness to David (1-2)

Questions.Q: What did Hanun do to David's men?
Questions.A: Shaved them, cut off their garments in the middle hard by their buttocks, and sent them away (3-5)

Questions.Q: After being defeated who was no longer willing to help the Ammonites again?
Questions.A: The Syrians (6-19)

Questions.Q: What was placed on David's head?
Questions.A: The crown of the king of Rabbah (1-3)

Questions.Q: Whom did Elhanan kill?
Questions.A: Lahmi the brother of Goliath (5)

Questions.Q: Whom did Jonathan son of Shimea kill?
Questions.A: The son of the giant, a man of great stature, with six fingers on each hand, and six toes on each foot (6)

Questions.Q: What did Satan tempt David to do?
Questions.A: Number Israel (1-7)

Questions.Q: Which of the three choices did David choose as punishment for his sin?
Questions.A: Three days the sword of the LORD, even the pestilence, in the land, and the angel of the LORD destroying throughout all the coasts of Israel (8-13)

Questions.Q: How did David's sin affect others?
Questions.A: Seventy thousand men died (14-17)

Questions.Q: Where did David build an altar to the LORD?
Questions.A: In the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite (18-28)

Questions.Q: What did David insist on doing?
Questions.A: Paying the full price for the oxen, the wood, and the wheat that he used in the offerings (22-25)

Questions.Q: What did David do before his death?
Questions.A: David prepared abundantly things like iron nails, cedar trees, brass, gold, silver and stone (1-5, 14-16)

Questions.Q: What did David charge Solomon to do?
Questions.A: To build a house for the LORD God of Israel (6-13)

Questions.Q: What did David command the leaders of Israel to do?
Questions.A: Help Solomon build the sanctuary of the LORD and bring into it the ark of the covenant and the holy vessels of God (17-19)

Questions.Q: How did David divide up the Levites?
Questions.A: 24.000 for the work of the house of the LORD; 6000 were officers and judges, 4000 were porters, and 4000 praised the LORD with the instruments (2-5)

Questions.Q: What did the Levites no longer need to carry?
Questions.A: The tabernacle or any of its vessels (26)

Questions.Q: What were the duties of the Levites?
Questions.A: To wait on the sons of Aaron for the service of the house of the LORD, including the offerings and the praises (28-32)

Questions.Q: By what means were the descendants of Aaron divided according to their service?
Questions.A: They were divided by lot (1-5)

Questions.Q: What was the service of the sons of Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun?
Questions.A: Prophesy with harps, with psalteries, and with cymbals (1)

Questions.Q: Who was over the treasures of the house of God?
Questions.A: Ahijah and the sons of Jehieli; Zetham, and Joel his brother (20, 22)

Questions.Q: What was Shelomith over?
Questions.A: All the treasures of the dedicated things (26-28)

Questions.Q: At what interval of time did a new group of twenty-four thousand come to serve the king?
Questions.A: Monthly (1-15)

Questions.Q: What were some of the tasks that David had men over?
Questions.A: The king's treasures, storehouses, tillage of the ground vineyards, wine cellars, olive and sycamore trees, the cellars of oil, herds, camels and flocks (25-31)

Questions.Q: Who was David's counselor?
Questions.A: Ahithophel (33)

Questions.Q: Whom did David gather to hear his charge?
Questions.A: All the princes of Israel, the captains, the stewards, his sons, with the officers, and with the mighty and valiant men (1)

Questions.Q: How did David tell Solomon to serve God?
Questions.A: With a perfect heart and with a willing mind: for the LORD searches all hearts, and understands all the imaginations of the thoughts (9)

Questions.Q: What was given to Solomon so he would know how to build the house of God?
Questions.A: Patterns (11-12, 19)

Questions.Q: Who would help Solomon in the building of the house of God?
Questions.A: The priests, Levites, willing skillful men, the princes and all the people (20-21)

Questions.Q: What did David prepare for the house of God?
Questions.A: Gold, silver, brass, iron, wood, precious stones, and marble (1-5)

Questions.Q: What question did David ask?
Questions.A: And who then is willing to consecrate his service this day to the LORD? (5)

Questions.Q: With what attitude did the people respond?
Questions.A: With perfect heart they offered willingly to the LORD gold, silver and precious stones (6-9)

Questions.Q: What did David pray regarding Solomon?
Questions.A: Give to Solomon a perfect heart, to keep God's commandments, testimonies, and statutes, and to do all these things, and to build the palace, for the which I have made provision (19)

Questions.Q: How long did David reign as king?
Questions.A: Forty years; seven years reigned he in Hebron, and thirty and three years reigned he in Jerusalem. (26-27)

Questions.Q: Tell [me] the main events recorded in this passage.
Questions.Alternative: Tell the main events recorded in this passage.
Tell me the main events recorded in this passage.
What were the main events recorded in this passage?
What events are recorded about in this passage?
What events are written about in this passage?

Questions.Q: Where did these events happen?
Questions.A: In the country of Egypt
Questions.Alternative: Where did the events described take place?
Where did the events described happen?
Where did the events recorded in this passage take place?
Where did the events recorded in this passage happen?
Where did the events written about in this passage happen?
Where do the events in this section take place?

Questions.Q: Approximately how many of the descendants of Jacob of Israel went to Egypt?
Questions.Alternative: Approximately how many of the descendants of Jacob went to Egypt?
Approximately how many of the descendants of Israel went to Egypt?
How many descendants of Jacob went to Egypt?
How many descendants of Israel went to Egypt?

Questions.Q: Where did Joseph die?
Questions.A: In Egypt (5-6)

Questions.Q: What can be said regarding the growth of the Israelites in Egypt?
Questions.A: Increased abundantly, and multiplied (7)
Questions.Alternative: What happened while the Israelites were living in Egypt?
What happened while the people of Israel were living in Egypt?

Questions.Q: What did the new king of Egypt fear?
Questions.A: If Egypt got into a war the Israelites would join up with their enemy (8-10)
Questions.Alternative: What did Pharaoh fear?

Questions.Q: Why did the Egyptians make the Israelites work as slaves?
Questions.A: They were trying to keep them from continuing to grow stronger. They thought that if they worked hard they would die or not have the strength to continue to bear children. (10-12)

Questions.Q: What two cities in Egypt did the Israelites build?
Questions.A: Pithom and Raamses (11)

Questions.Q: How did the Egyptians make the Israelites suffer?
Questions.A: Made their lives bitter with hard bondage (11-14)

Questions.Q: What did the king of Egypt tell the Hebrew midwives to do?
Questions.A: Kill the boy babies but let the girls live (15-16)
Questions.Alternative: What did Pharaoh tell the Hebrew midwives to do?

Questions.Q: Why didn't the Hebrew midwives obey Pharaoh?
Questions.A: They feared God (17-21)

Questions.Q: After the midwives refused to kill the boy babies, what did Pharaoh command?
Questions.A: Every son that is born you shall cast into the river, and every daughter you shall save alive. (22)

Questions.Q: Of what tribe was Moses?
Questions.A: Levi (1)

Questions.Q: How was baby Moses spared from being killed?
Questions.A: His mother put him in an ark and floated him in the river and Pharaoh's daughter saw it and rescued him (2-6)

Questions.Q: Who was paid to nurse Moses?
Questions.A: Moses's mother (7-9)

Questions.Q: Who gave Moses his name?
Questions.A: Pharaoh's daughter (10)

Questions.Q: What caused Moses to flee from Pharaoh to the land of Midian?
Questions.A: Pharaoh sought to kill him (11-15)

Questions.Q: With whom did Moses live in Midian?
Questions.A: Reul (Jethro) (16-22)

Questions.Q: What did the Israelites do after the king of Egypt died?
Questions.A: They sighed by reason of the bondage, and they cried, and their cry came up unto God (23-25)

Questions.Q: How did God catch Moses' attention?
Questions.A: A bush that was burning but not consumed (1-3)

Questions.Q: What did God say to Moses?
Questions.A: I have seen the affliction of my people which are in Egypt, and I will deliver them and bring them to the place of the Canaanites (4-9)

Questions.Q: What did God ask Moses to do?
Questions.A: Go to Pharaoh and bring my people the Israelites out of Egypt (10)

Questions.Q: How was Moses to reply when the Israelites asked what was the name of God?
Questions.A: I AM THAT I AM (13-15)

Questions.Q: What was Moses to tell the elders of Israel?
Questions.A: That God had appeared to Moses and would bring Israel out of Egypt into the land of Canaan. (16-17)

Questions.Q: What were they to ask of the king of Egypt?
Questions.A: Permission to go three days' journey into the wilderness in order to sacrifice to the LORD (18)

Questions.Q: What showed the foreknowledge of God?
Questions.A: God knew the king of Egypt would not grant this request and that He would have to strike Egypt with miracles/plagues. (19-20)

Questions.Q: How were the Israelites to leave Egypt?
Questions.A: With the gold, silver and raiment of Egypt (21-22)
