Questions.Q: What three signs would Moses perform in the sight of the elders in case they would not believe him?
Questions.A: Rod turned into a snake, hand became leprous, water turned to blood (1-9)

Questions.Q: What other excuse did Moses offer?
Questions.A: That he was not eloquent, but rather was slow of speech, and of a slow tongue. (10)

Questions.Q: Whom did God offer to Moses as a spokesman?
Questions.A: Aaron (11-17)

Questions.Q: Why did the Lord seek to kill Moses on the way to Egypt?
Questions.A: Because he had not circumcised his son (18-26)

Questions.Q: Whom did the Lord send to the wilderness to meet Moses?
Questions.A: Aaron (27-28)

Questions.Q: What was the reaction of the elders of Israel to the words which the Lord had spoken to Moses?
Questions.A: They believed (29-31)

Questions.Q: How did Pharaoh react when Moses first requested him to let Israel go?
Questions.A: He told Moses and Aaron that they made the Israelites from their burdens and they should get back to work. (1-5)

Questions.Q: What did Pharaoh command the taskmasters?
Questions.A: Make the Israelites gather their own straw and still require them to make the same number of bricks as when straw was provided for them. (6-13)

Questions.Q: What did the officers of the Israelites say to Moses after being beaten?
Questions.A: You have made us obnoxious to Pharaoh and his officials and have put a sword in their hand to kill us. (14-21)

Questions.Q: What did Moses say to God?
Questions.A: Why is it that you have sent me? For since I came to Pharaoh, he has done evil to this people; and you haven't delivered your people (22-23)

Questions.Q: What did the Lord say to Moses?
Questions.A: He had heard the groaning of the Israelites and would bring them out with a strong hand. (1-5)

Questions.Q: What did the Lord tell Moses to say to the Israelites?
Questions.A: That God would bring them to the land promised to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob (6-9)

Questions.Q: What did the Lord tell Moses to tell Pharaoh?
Questions.A: To let the Israelites go out of his land (10-11)

Questions.Q: Of which son of Levi was Moses a descendant?
Questions.A: Kohath (16-20)

Questions.Q: What relation was Korah to Moses?
Questions.A: First cousin (18-20)

Questions.Q: What were the names of Aaron's sons?
Questions.A: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar (23)

Questions.Q: What would the Egyptians know when the Lord sent judgments on Egypt?
Questions.A: That Israel's God was the LORD (4-5, 17)
Questions.Note: See also Exodus 8:22 and 9:14

Questions.Q: How old were Moses and Aaron when they spoke to Pharaoh?
Questions.A: 80 & 83 respectively (7)

Questions.Q: What did Pharaoh's magicians do when Aaron's rod became a serpent?
Questions.A: They cast down their rods and they became serpents (8-13)

Questions.Q: What did Aaron's rod do to the rods of Pharaoh's magicians?
Questions.A: Aaron's rod swallowed up their rods (12)

Questions.Q: What was the first plague that was put on the Egyptians?
Questions.A: The waters in the rivers turned to blood and the fish died (14-21)

Questions.Q: What was Pharaoh's reaction when his magicians imitated this plague?
Questions.A: Pharaoh's heart was hardened, neither did he listen to Moses and Aaron (22-23)

Questions.Q: To what extent did frogs invade Egypt?
Questions.A: Even into their beds and ovens (1-6)

Questions.Q: When did Pharaoh want the frogs to depart?
Questions.A: "Tomorrow" (9-10)

Questions.Q: What did Pharaoh do when he saw that there was relief from the frogs?
Questions.A: He hardened his heart and would not listen to Moses and Aaron (15)

Questions.Q: What was the first plague that Pharaoh's magicians could not duplicate?
What did they have to admit?
Questions.A: This is the finger of God (19)

Questions.Q: After what plague did Pharaoh offer his first compromise?
Questions.A: Flies (20-24)

Questions.Q: How did God make a difference between the Israelites and the Egyptians?
Questions.A: Where the Israelites lived there were no flies, murrain on the cattle, hail, darkness, or death of the first born but these plagues struck the Egyptians (21-23)
Questions.Note: See also Exodus 9:4, 26; 10:23; 11:7

Questions.Q: What was Pharaoh's first compromise?
Questions.A: Sacrifice to God in the land rather than in the wilderness (25)

Questions.Q: What was Pharaoh's second compromise?
Questions.A: Sacrifice to the LORD in the wilderness; but don't go very far away (Moses had requested to go a three days journey) (28)

Questions.Q: What was the fifth plague?
Questions.A: Murrain (infectious disease) on the cattle (1-7)

Questions.Q: What was the sixth plague?
Questions.A: Boils on man and beast breaking forth with sores and blisters (8-12)

Questions.Q: What was the seventh plague?
Questions.A: Hail and fire that destroyed plants and animals (13-35)

Questions.Q: How could the Egyptians be spared from this seventh plague?
Questions.A: They could bring their animals into their houses so they would not be killed by the hail (20)

Questions.Q: What would future generations of Israelites know as a result of these plagues?
Questions.A: The things and signs God wrought in Egypt and that they would know that God is the LORD. (2)

Questions.Q: What was Pharaoh's third compromise and how did Moses refuse?
Questions.A: He offered to let the men go and worship but Moses said they would go with their entire families and flocks in order to hold a feast. (7-11)

Questions.Q: What was the eighth plague?
Questions.A: Locusts (12-20)

Questions.Q: What was the ninth plague?
Questions.A: Darkness (21-23)

Questions.Q: What was Pharaoh's fourth compromise and how did Moses refuse?
Questions.A: Go serve the Lord but don't take any animals. Moses said they must take the cattle to offer sacrifices. (24-26)

Questions.Q: What would Moses never see again according to Pharaoh?
Questions.A: His face (27-29)

Questions.Q: What were the Israelites to borrow from their neighbors?
Questions.A: Jewels of silver and gold (2-3)

Questions.Q: What would happen to the Egyptians during the tenth plague?
Questions.A: The firstborn of man and animals would die at midnight. (4-6)

Questions.Q: What were the Israelites to do on the tenth day of the month?
Questions.A: Take a male lamb without blemish (3-5)

Questions.Q: What were the Israelites to do on the fourteenth day of the month?
Questions.A: Kill the lamb and put the blood on the two side posts and on the upper door post of their houses. Also they were to roast the lamb and eat it with unleavened bread. (6-10)

Questions.Q: How were the Israelites to be dressed when they ate the Passover lamb?
Questions.A: Loins girded and with shoes on feet. (11)

Questions.Q: What would God do when He saw the blood on the doorpost?
Questions.A: Pass over (13, 23)

Questions.Q: What would that day be throughout all generations?
Questions.A: A memorial (14, 24-27)

Questions.Q: Approximately how many Israelite men left Egypt?
Questions.A: Six hundred thousand (37)

Questions.Q: How long did the Israelites live in Egypt?
Questions.A: Four hundred and thirty years. (40)

Questions.Q: What was required of a stranger in order for them to keep the Passover?
Questions.A: Be circumcised (48)

Questions.Q: What was the purpose of the Feast of Unleavened Bread?
Questions.A: For a memorial that with a strong hand has the LORD brought them out of Egypt. (3-10)

Questions.Q: What was to be set apart to the Lord?
Questions.A: Firstborn of every male child and animal (11-16)

Questions.Q: Why didn't God lead the Israelites by way of the land of the Philistines?
Questions.A: Lest the people repent when they see war, and they return to Egypt: (17-18)

Questions.Q: What did Moses take with him when he left Egypt?
Questions.A: The bones of Joseph (19)

Questions.Q: How did God lead the Israelites?
Questions.A: By day in a pillar of a cloud and by night in a pillar of fire (21-22)

Questions.Q: What did Pharaoh do when he realized he had let Israel go from serving Egypt?
Questions.A: He pursued the Israelites with all his horses and chariots and his army, and overtook them encamping by the sea. (1-9)

Questions.Q: How did the Israelites react when the saw the Egyptians marching after them?
Questions.A: They were afraid and they said to Moses that it had been better for them to serve the Egyptians, than die in the wilderness. (10-12)

Questions.Q: What did Moses say to the people?
Questions.A: Fear not, stand still, and you shall see the salvation of the LORD (13-14)

Questions.Q: What did God tell Moses to say to the people?
Questions.A: Go forward (15)

Questions.Q: What did God put between the Israelites and the Egyptians?
Questions.A: The pillar of the cloud (19-20)

Questions.Q: By what means did God cause the sea to go back?
Questions.A: A strong east wind (21)

Questions.Q: How did Israel cross the sea?
Questions.A: On dry ground (22)

Questions.Q: What difficulty did the Egyptians have crossing?
Questions.A: Apparently the ground became so muddy that they took off their chariot wheels (23-25)

Questions.Q: What did God tell Moses to do so the waters would come back?
Questions.A: Stretch out his hand over the sea (26-27)

Questions.Q: What happened to Pharaoh's army?
Questions.A: The waters returned, and covered the chariots, and the horsemen, and all the host of Pharaoh that came into the sea after them (28-30)

Questions.Q: What was the reaction of Israel when they saw what God had done?
Questions.A: They feared the LORD, and believed the LORD, and his servant Moses. (31)

Questions.Q: What was the subject of the song the Israelites sang?
Questions.A: How Israel crossed the Red Sea on dry ground but the Egyptians who pursued were drowned (1-18)

Questions.Q: Who else sang a song?
Questions.A: Miriam and all the women (20-21)

Questions.Q: What problem did they encounter at Marah?
Questions.A: Bitter water (22-24)

Questions.Q: How was the problem solved?
Questions.A: Moses cast a tree into the waters (24-25)

Questions.Q: What did God promise that He would not put on the Israelites if they obeyed the voice of the Lord?
Questions.A: The diseases of the Egyptians (26)

Questions.Q: What was at Elim?
Questions.A: Twelve wells of water, and seventy palm trees (27)

Questions.Q: How did God promise to answer the complaints regarding hunger?
Questions.A: God supplied bread (manna) in the morning and quail in the evening. (2-18)

Questions.Q: What happened to the bread that was left over until the next day?
Questions.A: It bred worms, and stank (19-20)

Questions.Q: What were they to do differently on the sixth day?
Questions.A: Gather twice as much (22-30)

Questions.Q: What did the Israelites call the food that God provided?
Questions.A: Manna (31)

Questions.Q: How long did the Israelites eat this food?
Questions.A: Forty years, until they came to the borders of the land of Canaan. (35)

Questions.Q: How did God solve the thirst problem?
Questions.A: He had Moses strike a rock and water came out so the Israelites could drink (1-7)

Questions.Q: Who came and fought against Israel?
Questions.A: Amalek (8)

Questions.Q: Who held up Moses' hands?
Questions.A: Aaron and Hur (9-13)

Questions.Q: What did Moses call the altar which he built?
Questions.A: Jehovahnissi (15)

Questions.Q: Who was Moses' father-in-law?
Questions.A: Jethro (1)

Questions.Q: What advice did he give to Moses?
Questions.A: Appoint God fearing men (13-27)
to be rulers of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens: And let them judge the people at all seasons: and every great matter they would bring to Moses, but every small matter they shall judge (13-27)

Questions.Q: What did God want Israel to be?
Questions.A: A kingdom of priests, and a holy nation (5-6)

Questions.Q: What would happen to the people who touched the mountain at Sinai?
Questions.A: They would be put to death. (12)

Questions.Q: What visible and audible manifestations occurred when the Lord descended on Mount Sinai?
Questions.A: Thunder, lightning, a thick cloud, the voice of the trumpet, smoke, fire and the whole mount quaked (15-19)

Questions.Q: Whom did the Lord call to the top of the mountain?
Questions.A: Moses (20)
Questions.Alternative: Who went up to the top of the mountain?

Questions.Q: List the Ten Commandments.
Questions.A: You shall have no other gods before me. You shall not make to you any graven image. You shall not take the name of the LORD your God in vain. Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy. Honor your father and your mother. You shall not kill. You shall not commit adultery. You shall not steal. You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor. You shall not covet. (2-17)

Questions.Q: What physical phenomena accompanied the giving of the Ten Commandments?
Questions.A: Thunder, lightning, the noise of the trumpet, and the mountain smoking (18)

Questions.Q: What instructions were given regarding an altar of stone?
Questions.A: Do not build it of hewn stone (25)

Questions.Q: After how many years would a Hebrew servant be freed?
Questions.A: Six (2)

Questions.Q: What happened if a servant loved his master and did not wish to go out free?
Questions.A: His ear would be pierced with an awl and he would serve his master the rest of his life (5-6)

Questions.Q: For what acts of violence were laws given?
Questions.A: Killing a man, stealing a man, cursing his father, or his mother, fighting, putting out an eye, knocking out a tooth, wounding a hand or foot, and burning (12-27)

Questions.Q: What happened to the owner of an animal that killed a person if that owner had knowledge that the animal previously had a record of violence?
Questions.A: He was put to death. (29)

Questions.Q: What was to be done to a man who killed a thief that was breaking in?
Questions.A: Nothing (2)

Questions.Q: What was required of a man who let his animal graze in another man's field?
Questions.A: He must make restitution of the best of his field. (5)

Questions.Q: What was required of a man who enticed a virgin who was not betrothed?
Questions.A: He should marry her, but if her father refuses to give her to him, he shall pay money according to the dowry of virgins. (16-17)

Questions.Q: What was to be done to a person who lay with an animal?
Questions.A: Put to death (19)

Questions.Q: What was to be done to a person who sacrificed to any god, except the Lord only?
Questions.A: Utterly destroyed (20)

Questions.Q: Who was not to be mistreated?
Questions.A: Any widow, or fatherless child. (21-22)

Questions.Q: What should you not circulate?
Questions.A: A false report (1)

Questions.Q: What should you do if you see your enemy's animal going astray?
Questions.A: Bring it back to him (4)

Questions.Q: Why shouldn't you take a bribe?
Questions.A: The gift blinds the wise, and perverts the words of the righteous. (8)

Questions.Q: What was the Sabbath for?
Questions.A: That they, their animals, their servants, and the stranger may be refreshed. (12)

Questions.Q: What were the three annual feasts?
Questions.A: Feast of unleavened bread, feast of harvest, and the feast of ingathering (14-17)

Questions.Q: What was the Angel sent to do?
Questions.A: To keep them in the way, and to bring them into the place which God prepared. (20)

Questions.Q: What were the Israelites to do to the inhabitants of the promised land?
Questions.A: Overthrow them (24)

Questions.Q: What, besides the Angel, did God send before the Israelites?
Questions.A: Hornets (28)

Questions.Q: Why didn't God drive out the inhabitants of the land all at once?
Questions.A: Otherwise the land would become desolate, and the beast of the field multiply against them (29-30)

Questions.Q: How did the Israelites reply when Moses told them the words of the Lord?
Questions.A: All that the LORD said we will do, and be obedient (1-3, 7)

Questions.Q: What did the Lord say He would give Moses on the mountain?
Questions.A: Tables of stone, and a law, and commandments (12)

Questions.Q: How long was Moses on the mountain?
Questions.A: Forty days and forty nights. (18)

Questions.Q: With what attitude were the Israelites to give an offering?
Questions.A: Willingly (2)

Questions.Q: What helped Moses in the building of the tabernacle?
Questions.A: Patterns (9, 40)
Questions.Note: See also Exodus 26:30

Questions.Q: What pieces of furniture were overlaid with pure gold?
Questions.A: Ark, table, candlestick (10-30)

Questions.Q: What was to be set on top of the ark?
Questions.A: The mercy seat (21)

Questions.Q: What was to be placed in the ark?
Questions.A: The testimony (21)

Questions.Q: From what material was the lampstand made?
Questions.A: Pure gold (31)

Questions.Q: How many lamps were in the lampstand?
Questions.A: Seven (32)

Questions.Q: What four materials covered the tabernacle?
Questions.A: Fine twined linen, goats' hair, rams' skins dyed red, badgers' skins. (1-14)

Questions.Q: What divided the holy place and the Most Holy?
Questions.A: A veil (33)

Questions.Q: What was put in the Most Holy?
Questions.A: The mercy seat upon the ark of the testimony (34)

Questions.Q: What was put in the holy Place?
Questions.A: The table and the candlestick (35)

Questions.Q: What was the altar for burnt offerings overlaid with?
Questions.A: Brass (2)

Questions.Q: What were the dimensions of the court of the tabernacle?
Questions.A: 50 cubits by 100 cubits (9-13)

Questions.Q: How often was the lamp in the tabernacle to burn?
Questions.A: Always (20)

Questions.Q: Who was selected for the priesthood?
Questions.A: Aaron and his sons (1)

Questions.Q: What garments were to be made for the priests?
Questions.A: A breastpiece, an ephod, a robe, a woven tunic, a turban and a sash (4)

Questions.Q: What was engraved on the stones for the shoulders of the ephod?
Questions.A: The names of the sons of Israel (9-12)

Questions.Q: What was engraved on the stones for the breastplate?
Questions.A: The names of the sons of Israel (21, 29)

Questions.Q: What was put at the hem of the priest's robe?
Questions.A: Pomegranates of blue, and of purple, and of scarlet, and bells of gold (33-34)

Questions.Q: What different offerings were made when consecrating priests?
Questions.A: Sin, burnt, wave, heave (14, 18, 24, 28)

Questions.Q: How many lambs were offered each day?
Where was the altar of incense placed?
Questions.A: Before the veil that is by the ark of the testimony, before the mercy seat (6)

Questions.Q: How often did Aaron make atonement?
Questions.A: Once a year (10)

Questions.Q: How did the ransom offering of the rich compare to the offering of the poor?
Questions.A: Exactly the same, half a shekel (15)

Questions.Q: Where was the basin for washing placed?
Questions.A: Between the tabernacle of the congregation and the altar (18)
Questions.Alternative: Where was the laver for washing placed?

Questions.Q: What would happen to a priest if he made an offering without washing?
Questions.A: He would die (20-21)

Questions.Q: Who was anointed with the holy anointing oil?
Questions.A: Aaron and his sons (30)

Questions.Q: Whom did the Lord call and appoint to make the items for the tabernacle and the priesthood?
Questions.A: Bezaleel and Aholiab (2, 6)

Questions.Q: What would happen to someone who profaned the Sabbath?
Questions.A: They were put to death (14)

Questions.Q: Who wrote on the tablets of stone that were given to Moses?
Questions.A: The finger of God (18)

Questions.Q: What did the people request of Aaron while Moses was on Mount Sinai?
Questions.A: Make us gods, which shall go before us (1)

Questions.Q: Who made the gold calf?
Questions.A: Aaron (4)

Questions.Q: What reasoning did Moses use in his intercession with God to spare Israel?
Questions.A: The Egyptians would say that it was with evil intent that God brought Israel out, to kill them in the mountains and to wipe them off the face of the earth. (12)
Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, who you promised to multiply as the stars of heaven, and give this land (13)

Questions.Q: How did Moses react when he saw the calf and the dancing?
Questions.A: He was so angry that he cast the tables down and broke them and he ground the calf to powder and made the Israelites drink it when mixed with water. (19-20)

Questions.Q: How did Aaron lie when confronted by Moses?
Questions.A: He said he cast the gold into the fire and out came the calf. (24)

Questions.Q: How many Israelites were killed that day?
Questions.A: Three thousand men (28)

Questions.Q: What was Moses willing to allow to happen if God did not forgive their sin?
Questions.A: Have his name blotted out of God's book (32)

Questions.Q: How did the Lord speak to Moses?
Questions.A: Face to face (11)

Questions.Q: What didn't Moses want to happen if the Lord's presence was not with them?
Questions.A: To go to the promised land. (15)

Questions.Q: How did the Lord respond when Moses desired to see God's glory?
Questions.A: When God's glory passed by, God would put Moses in a crack of a rock, and cover him with His hand while He passed by. After He removed His hand, Moses would see His back parts, but not His face. (17-23)

Questions.Q: Who cut the second set of tablets of stone?
Questions.A: Moses (1-4)

Questions.Q: What is a covenant?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A covenant is an agreement, an especially binding promise. If a person on one side of the covenant does not do as both have agreed, there usually is a strong punishment for him or he pays compensation to the other person. Similar agreements now are called contracts. When God makes an agreement with people, however, he makes a firm promise of what he will do and says what they must do.
Questions.Note: See "covenant" in KBT.

If the language has a special name to refer to these kinds of agreements, ask the respondent to tell you the kinds of situations in which the people make the agreements. Listen for any points where it would not be appropriate to state that God made that kind of an agreement. Then adjust the translation as necessary.

Questions.Q: What was the covenant that God was going to make with Israel?
Questions.A: God would perform miracles among the nations; and all the people would see the Lord work.
God would drive out the [pagan] nations [of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites and the Jebusites] (to give their land to Israel).
The people were to obey God's commandments and worship Him alone (not the pagan gods/idols).
They also were to observe the required feasts and perform the required sacrifices.

Questions.Q: Why were the Israelites not to make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land of Canaan?
Questions.A: It could be a snare and cause them to sacrifice to their gods (12-17)

Questions.Q: How long did Moses neither eat bread nor drink water?
Questions.A: Forty days and forty nights (28)

Questions.Q: Why were Aaron and the Israelites afraid to come near Moses?
Questions.A: The skin of his face shone (29-30)

Questions.Q: What did Moses put on his face?
Questions.A: A veil (33-35)

Questions.Q: With what attitude were people to bring their offerings for the tabernacle?
Questions.A: With heartfelt willingness/generosity (5, 21-22, 29)

Questions.Q: Who made the various items for the tabernacle?
Questions.A: The wise hearted and Bezaleel and Aholiab (10, 25-26, 30-35)

Questions.Q: How much did the people bring as offerings?
Questions.A: Much more than enough (5-7)

Questions.Q: What items did Bezaleel make that are described in this chapter?
Questions.A: Ark, table, candlestick, altar, oil and incense (1, 10, 17, 25, 29)

Questions.Q: What items did Bezaleel make that are described in this chapter?
Questions.A: Altar of burnt offering, basin, and court (1, 8, 9)

Questions.Q: How much gold was used in the holy place?
Questions.A: 29 talents, and 730 shekels (24)

Questions.Q: How much silver was used?
Questions.A: 100 talents, and a 1775 shekels (25)

Questions.Q: How much bronze was used?
Questions.A: 70 talents, and 2400 shekels (29)

Questions.Q: What priestly garments were made?
Questions.A: Ephod, breastplate, robe, coats, turban, bonnets, breeches, and a girdle (2, 8, 22, 27-29)

Questions.Q: What words were inscribed on the crown?
Questions.A: HOLY TO THE LORD (30)

Questions.Q: When the work of the tabernacle was finished and Moses saw it, what did he do?
Questions.A: Moses blessed them (32-43)

Questions.Q: What happened when Moses finished erecting the tabernacle?
Questions.A: A cloud covered the tent of the congregation, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle (34-35)

Questions.Q: How did Israel know when to move?
Questions.A: When the cloud was taken up from over the tabernacle (36-37)

Questions.Q: What was above the tabernacle at night?
Questions.A: Fire (38)

Questions.Q: To what extent had the Lord increased the number of the Israelites?
Questions.A: As the stars of heaven for multitude. (10)

Questions.Q: To whom does judgment belong?
Questions.A: God (17)

Questions.Q: Why did the Israelites not enter the promised land after sending out the spies?
Questions.A: They did not believe the LORD their God (32)

Questions.Q: How did Caleb follow the Lord?
Questions.A: Wholly (36)

Questions.Q: What was Moses to do for Joshua?
Questions.A: Encourage him (38)

Questions.Q: To what did Moses compare the way the Amorites chased the Israelites?
Questions.A: As bees do (44)

Questions.Q: Israel was not to possess land belonging to whose descendants?
Questions.A: Esau and Lot (Moab, Ammon) (5, 9, 19)

Questions.Q: What did Israel do to Sihon, king of Heshbon?
Questions.A: Struck him, and his sons, and all his people and took all his cities. (24-37)

Questions.Q: How many cities were taken from Og King of Bashan?
Questions.A: Sixty (1-10)

Questions.Q: What was unusual about his bed?
Questions.A: It was huge: nine cubits long and four cubits wide (11)

Questions.Q: To whom was given the kingdom of Og?
Questions.A: Reubenites, Gadites and half the tribe of Manasseh (12-20)

Questions.Q: From where was Moses able to see the land beyond Jordan?
Questions.A: The top of Pisgah (21-29)

Questions.Q: What were the Israelites not to do to the Lord's commandments?
Questions.A: Add to or take away from them (1-2)

Questions.Q: What would other nations say if Israel kept the commandments?
Questions.A: Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people. And what nation is there so great, that has statutes and judgments so righteous as all this law (3-8)

Questions.Q: To whom were they to teach the commandments?
Questions.A: Their sons, and sons' sons; (9-13)

Questions.Q: What were the Israelites not to make?
Questions.A: Graven images of anything including beast, winged fowl, creeping things (or creature that moves along the ground), or fish (14-24)

Questions.Q: What would happen to them if they made idols?
Questions.A: They would be scattered among the nations (25-28)

Questions.Q: What would happen if they sought the Lord with all their heart?
Questions.A: They would find Him (29-31)

Questions.Q: Why were the Israelites shown signs and wonders?
Questions.A: That they might know that the LORD he is God; there is none else beside him (32-35)

Questions.Q: Who would the Lord drive out before them?
Questions.A: Nations greater and mightier than Israel (36-38)

Questions.Q: What would be the reward for keeping the commandments?
Questions.A: That it may go well with them, and with their children, and that their days would be prolonged on the earth (39-40)

Questions.Q: What did Moses want the people of Israel to do?
Questions.A: Listen to the commandments/statutes/ordinances
Learn/remember them
Obey them carefully

Questions.Q: Where had the people heard these commandments/statutes/ordinances before?
Questions.A: God spoke them to the people at Mount Horeb.
Questions.Note: See Exodus 20:2-17
This question should be skipped unless the respondent is someone who is expected to have familiarity with the Ten Commandments.
Questions.Alternative: Where had the people heard these commandments before?
Where had the people heard these statutes before?
Where had the people heard these ordinances before?

Questions.Q: What is a covenant?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A covenant is an agreement, an especially binding promise. If a person on one side of the covenant does not do as both have agreed, there usually is a strong punishment for him or he pays compensation to the other person. Similar agreements now are called contracts. When God makes an agreement with people, however, he makes a firm promise of what he will do and says what they must do.
Questions.Note: See "covenant" in KBT.

If the language has a special name to refer to these kinds of agreements, ask the respondent to tell you the kinds of situations in which the people make the agreements. Listen for any points where it would not be appropriate to state that God made that kind of an agreement. Then adjust the translation as necessary.

Questions.Q: When did the Lord make the covenant with Israel?
Questions.A: during the lifetime of those people [to whom Moses was talking] (3)
when they were at Mount Horeb (2, 4)
when Moses was standing between the Lord and the people (5)

Questions.Q: How did the Lord communicate his covenant/commandments?
Questions.A: Face to face (4)
He also wrote the commandments on two stone tablets. (22)
Questions.Alternative: How did the Lord communicate his covenant?
How did the Lord communicate his commandments?

Questions.Q: Why were the people afraid to go up on the mountain [to stand before the Lord]?
Questions.A: Because of the fire (5)
They had seen God's glory and greatness (24)
They though they would die if they continued to hear the voice of the living God speaking from the midst of the fire. (25-26)
Questions.Alternative: Why were the people afraid to go up on the mountain to stand before the Lord?
Why were the people afraid to go up on the mountain?

Questions.Q: Which commandments are repeated here [that were originally given in Exodus 20]?
Questions.A: The Ten Commandments:
You shall have no other gods before Me. (7)
You shall not make or worship idols. (8-9)
You shall not take the name of the Lord your God in vain. (11)
Observe the Sabbath day to keep it holy. (12)
Honor your father and your mother. (16)
You shall not murder. (17)
You shall not commit adultery. (18)
You shall not steal. (19)
You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor. (20)
You shall not covet. (21)
Questions.Alternative: Which commandments are repeated here that were originally given in Exodus 20?
Which commandments are repeated here?

Questions.Q: Describe the way God spoke to the Israelites.
Questions.A: His voice came out of the midst of the fire, the cloud and the thick gloom/darkness. (22-23)
His voice was loud/great. (22)
His voice was frightening (24-26)

Questions.Q: What did God give to Moses?
Questions.A: two tablets of stone [with the Ten Commandments written on them] (22)

Questions.Q: What did the people want Moses to do for them?
Questions.A: Go near and hear all that the Lord had to say; then tell them what the Lord said. (27)

Questions.Q: Was the Lord pleased with this request?
Questions.A: Yes (but He wished that the people would fear/revere Him enough to obey) (28)

Questions.Q: What did the Lord tell Moses to do?
Questions.A: Send the people to their tents (30)
Stand by God to hear the rest of the commandments/statutes (31)
Teach the people to obey (31-33)

Questions.Q: What instructions did God give his people in this chapter?
Questions.A: Love the Lord your God with all your heart. (4)
Impress God's commandments on their children. (7-9, 20-25)
Do not forget God. (8-12)
Serve God alone; do not follow false gods/idols. (13-16)
Do what is right and good in the LORD's sight. (18)

Questions.Q: When God said to tie the commands on their bodies and write them on their houses, what did He mean?
Questions.A: He wanted his people to constantly remember his commands.
He wanted his people to read the Scriptures often.

Questions.Q: What does God mean when he says he is a jealous God?
Questions.A: He does not share His glory with idols/false gods. He wants people to worship Him alone. He deserves all our worship.

Questions.Q: What scripture plainly declares that there is just one God?
Questions.A: Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God is one LORD: (1-4)

Questions.Q: What should our attitude be toward God?
Questions.A: Love the LORD your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your might (5)

Questions.Q: When should we teach our children about God and his commandments?
Questions.A: All the time: when you sit in your house, and when you walk by the way, and when you lie down, and when you rise up. (6-7)

Questions.Q: Where were they to write the commandments?
Questions.A: On the posts of their house, and on their gates (8-9)

Questions.Q: When should we be careful not to forget God?
Questions.A: When we are blessed with houses, food, etc. (10-12)

Questions.Q: What were they to answer when asked, “What is the meaning of the testimonies, statutes and judgments?”
Questions.A: We were Pharaoh's slaves in Egypt; and the LORD brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand: And the LORD commanded us to do all these statutes, to fear the LORD our God, for our good always (20-25)

Questions.Q: What were the Israelites to do to the nations that lived in the land?
Questions.A: Utterly destroy them and their idols and altars (1-5)
Questions.Alternative: What were the Israelites to do to the nations that inhabited the land?
What were the Israelites to do to the peoples that lived in the land?
What were the Israelites to do to the peoples that inhabited the land?
What were the Israelites to do to the nations that dwelled in the land?

Questions.Q: Why did the Lord choose Israel?
Questions.A: Because the LORD loved them, and because he would keep the oath which he had sworn to their fathers (6-10)

Questions.Q: What four things would the Lord do for the Israelites if they kept the commandments?
Questions.A: Bless the fruit of their womb, and the fruit of their land, there shall not be male or female barren among them, take away from them all sickness, and will put none of the evil diseases of Egypt (11-16)

Questions.Q: What question did the Lord know that the Israelites would ask in their heart?
Questions.A: These nations are more than I; how can I dispossess them? (17)

Questions.Q: How did the Lord answer that question?
Questions.A: Remember what the LORD God did to Pharaoh, and to all Egypt. Also God would send hornets against their enemies. (18-21)

Questions.Q: How would the Lord drive out the nations that occupied Canaan?
Questions.A: With a mighty destruction but not all at once (22-24)

Questions.Q: Why were the Israelites not to take the silver and gold from the graven images into their houses?
Questions.A: God said they could be ensnared by it (25)
They could become a cursed/detestable thing like the idols (26)

Questions.Q: Of what did Moses remind the Israelites?
Questions.A: All the way which the LORD their God led them for forty years in the wilderness, that they would know that man does not live by bread only, but by every word that proceeds out of the mouth of the LORD (1-5)

Questions.Q: To what kind of land was the Lord bringing the Israelites?
Questions.A: A land of brooks of water, of fountains , of wheat, barley, vines, fig trees, pomegranates, oil olive, and honey (6-9)

Questions.Q: What were the Israelites to do when they had eaten and were satisfied?
Questions.A: Bless the LORD for the good land which he had given them (10-16)

Questions.Q: Who gives the ability to get wealth?
Questions.A: The LORD their God (17-18)

Questions.Q: What would happen to the Israelites if they forgot the Lord and followed other gods?
Questions.A: They would perish (19-20)

Questions.Q: Why was the Lord going to drive out the Anakites?
Questions.A: Because of the wickedness of these nations (1-6)

Questions.Q: How did the Lord describe the Israelites?
Questions.A: Stiff necked people who provoked the LORD to wrath, rebellious and corrupted (6-14)

Questions.Q: What did Moses do to the idol cast in the shape of a calf?
Questions.A: Burnedb it with fire, stamped it, ground it into dust and cast the dust into a brook (15-21)

Questions.Q: What prevented the Lord from destroying Israel?
Questions.A: The prayer of Moses (22-29)

Questions.Q: Where did Moses put the second set of the ten commandments?
Questions.A: In an ark of acacia wood (1-5)

Questions.Q: Who was separated to carry the ark and pronounce blessings?
Questions.A: The tribe of Levi (6-11)

Questions.Q: What did the Lord require of Israel?
Questions.A: Fear the LORD, walk in all his ways, love him, serve the LORD with all their heart and with all their soul, and keep the commandments and statutes of the LORD. (12-13)

Questions.Q: What belongs to God?
Questions.A: The heavens and the earth and all that is in them (14)

Questions.Q: What causes does the Lord defend?
Questions.A: The fatherless and widow, and the stranger (18-19)

Questions.Q: What rains would the Lord give them if they hearkened unto his commandments?
Questions.A: The rain of your land in his due season, the first rain and the latter rain (13-14)

Questions.Q: What was the extent of the land to be given them?
Questions.A: From the wilderness and Lebanon, from the river Euphrates, even to the uttermost sea. (24)

Questions.Q: What did the Lord set before them?
Questions.A: A blessing and a curse; A blessing, if they obeyed the commandments of the LORD and a curse, if they did not obey the commandments of the LORD (26-29)

Questions.Q: What were the Israelites to destroy when they got into the land the Lord would give them?
Questions.A: All the places where the nations served their false gods: their altars, pillars, groves/trees. (1-3)
The idols/images of their false gods. (3)

Questions.Q: Where were they to bring their offerings, sacrifices and tithes when they crossed over Jordan?
Questions.A: The place which the LORD your God shall choose out of all your tribes to put his name (4-14)

Questions.Q: What were they not to eat?
Who were they not to forsake?
Questions.A: The Levite (19)

Questions.Q: To what were they not to add to or diminish?
Questions.A: What God had commanded (32)

Questions.Q: What was to be done to the prophet or dreamer of dreams who tried to cause the Israelites to follow other gods?
Questions.A: Put to death (1-5)

Questions.Q: What was to be done to a relative that tried to get them to follow other gods?
Questions.A: Stoned to death (6-11)

Questions.Q: What should be done to a city that followed other gods?
Questions.A: Utterly destroyed and burned with fire (12-18)

Questions.Q: What had God chosen Israel to be?
Questions.A: A holy people to the LORD , a peculiar people to himself (1-2)

Questions.Q: What beasts were the Israelites not allowed to eat?
Questions.A: Camel, hare, coney/rock badger/hyrax, swine/pig (3-8)
Questions.Alternative: What animals were the Israelites not allowed to eat?
What meat were the Israelites not allowed to eat?
What kinds of meat were the Israelites not allowed to eat?
What were the Israelites not allowed to eat?

Questions.Q: What things in the water were they not to eat?
Questions.A: Whatever that does not have fins and scales (9-10)

Questions.Q: What birds were they not to eat?
Questions.A: Any kind of eagle, ossifrage, vulture, osprey, buzzard, glede, kite, falcon, owl, hawk, stork, raven, or heron; ostrich, gull, cuckoo, swan, pelican, cormorant, hoopoe/lapwing; bats (11-20)
Questions.Alternative: What flying animals were they not to eat?

Questions.Q: How would a person tithe who lived a long way from the place where the Lord chose to set his name?
Questions.A: Turn it into money, go to the place which the LORD chose, and buy food there (22-27)

Questions.Q: What were they to do every third year?
Questions.A: Bring all the tithe and lay it up within their gates for the Levite, stranger, fatherless, and the widows which were within their gates to eat (28-29)

Questions.Q: What were the Israelites to do at the end of every seventh year?
Questions.A: Release their neighbors of their debts (1-11)

Questions.Q: What was Israel to do to nations in regard to borrowing and lending?
Questions.A: Lend to them but not borrow (6)

Questions.Q: How were they to send away a Hebrew servant when released?

Questions.Q: What was to be done to a servant who did not wish to be released?

Questions.Q: Where were they to observe the Passover?
Questions.A: In the place which the LORD shall choose to place his name (1-8)

Questions.Q: When were they to keep the Feast of Weeks?
Questions.A: Seven weeks from such time as you begin to put the sickle to the corn. (9-12)

Questions.Q: How was every man to give?
Questions.A: As he is able, according to the blessing of the LORD which He has given (13-17)

Questions.A: A gift blinds the eyes of the wise, and perverts the words of the righteous. In other words they could not judge correctly if they had taken bribes. (18-20)

Questions.Q: What happened to a person who served other gods?
Questions.A: Stoned to death (1-7)

Questions.Q: Why did Israel desire a king?

Questions.Q: What are some abominations to the Lord?

Questions.Alternative: What are some of the abominable practices of the nations that the Lord told his people not to follow?
What are some of the abominable things the Lord told his people not to do?

Questions.Q: Who would the Prophet that the Lord was going to raise up be like?
Questions.A: Moses (15-19)

Questions.Q: What was the punishment for a prophet who spoke presumptuously or who prophesied in the name of another god?
Questions.A: Death

Questions.Q: How has a prophet spoken if what he says does not come to pass?
Questions.A: Presumptuosly or in the name of other gods (20-22)

Questions.Q: What example of unintentional murder was given?
Questions.A: A man chopping wood. His axe head flies off the handle and kills another man accidentally. (1-10)

Questions.Q: What example of intentional murder was given?
Questions.A: A man who hates his neighbor, lies in wait for him, rises up against him, and smites him to death (11-13)

Questions.Q: What were they Israelites not to remove?
Questions.A: Their neighbor's landmark. (14)

Questions.Q: How many witnesses were required to establish a matter?
Questions.A: Two or three (15)

Questions.Q: What was done to a false witness?
Questions.A: Do to him, as he had thought to have done to his brother (16-21)

Questions.Q: What were the priests to say to the Israelites on the verge of battle?
Questions.A: Let not your hearts faint, fear not, and do not tremble, neither be you terrified because of them; for the LORD your God is he that goes with you, to fight for you against your enemies, to save you. (1-4)

Questions.Q: Whom did the officers excuse from going to battle?
Questions.A: Men who built a new house not yet dedicated, men who planted a vineyard and have not eaten of it, men who have betrothed a wife and not taken her, and those who were fearful and fainthearted (5-9)

Questions.Q: What did the Israelites offer when they went near a city to fight?
Questions.A: Peace (10-11)

Questions.Q: How were the Israelites to treat cities very far from them compared to cities which were given to them for an inheritance?
Questions.A: In the cities far away the women, little ones, and cattle were taken as spoil, but in the cities which were given as an inheritance nothing was spared alive. (12-18)

Questions.Q: What kind of trees could be used in the siege of a city?
Questions.A: Trees which bore nothing that they could eat (19-20)

Questions.Q: What was done if a slain man was found and it was not know who killed him?
Questions.A: The elders of the city nearest to where the body was found would cut off the head of a heifer, wash their hands over it and confess that they were innocent. (1-9)

Questions.Q: What must a man do if he desires to take a wife from among the captives?
Questions.A: Bring her home, and she shall shave her head, pare her nails, and mourn her father and her mother a full month (10-14)

Questions.Q: How much was the inheritance of the firstborn son compared to the others?
Questions.A: Double (15-17)

Questions.Q: What was to be done to a rebellious son?
Questions.A: Stoned to death (18-21)

Questions.Q: How long was the body of a cursed man allowed to hang on a tree?
Questions.A: Only during the daytime (22-23)

Questions.Q: What was a person to do with an animal or item they had found?
Questions.A: Return it to the owner (1-4)

Questions.Q: What was a person not to wear?
Questions.A: Clothing that pertained to the opposite sex or clothing made of mixed fibers, such as wool and linen (5, 11)

Questions.Q: How was a new house to be built?
Questions.A: With a battlement for the roof (8)

Questions.Q: What were they not to plow with?
Questions.A: An ox and a donkey together (10)

Questions.Q: What happened to a woman who her husband finds out after marrying that she was not a virgin?
Questions.A: Stoned to death (13-21)

Questions.Q: What happened to a man and woman found in adultery?
Questions.A: Both of them would be killed (22)

Questions.Q: What must a man do who lies with a virgin and they are discovered?
Questions.A: Give fifty shekels of silver to the girl's father, and marry the girl (28-30)

Questions.Q: Who was not allowed into the assembly of the LORD even to the tenth generation?
Questions.A: A bastard, Ammonite or Moabite (1-8)

Questions.Q: What sanitation rule was given?
Questions.A: Dig a hole outside the camp, do your bowel movement, then cover it. (12-14)

Questions.Q: To whom were they not to charge interest?
Questions.A: To their brothers (19-20)

Questions.Q: What was said concerning vows?
Questions.A: Do not delay to pay it (21-23)

Questions.Q: What were they allowed to eat from their neighbor's land?
Questions.A: All the grapes they wanted but they could not put any in a vessel. Ears of corn they could pluck with their hand; but they could not use a sickle (24-25)

Questions.Q: Who should a person not take to be his wife?
Questions.A: A woman whom you had previously married and and divorced and then later was married to another man. (1-4)

Questions.Q: How long after marriage was a man free not to go to war?
Questions.A: One year (5)
Questions.Alternative: How long after marriage was a man exempt from having to go to war?

Questions.Q: What was to be done to kidnappers?
Questions.A: Put to death (7)

Questions.Q: How often should you pay a servant who is poor?
Questions.A: Every day before sunset (14-15)

Questions.Q: For whose sin was a person put to death?
Questions.A: Their own (16)

Questions.Q: What were the stranger, fatherless and widows allowed to eat?
Questions.A: Sheaves forgotten in the field, olives that did not fall when they beat their olive trees, the gleanings of the grapes of their vineyards (19-22)

Questions.Q: What was the maximum number of blows a man could receive during a beating?
What were they not to muzzle?
Questions.A: The ox when he treads out the corn. (4)

Questions.Q: What was the marriage duty of a surviving brother?
Questions.A: If his brother die without having children he shall take the widow to be his wife (5-10)

Questions.Q: What was the law concerning weights and measures?
Questions.A: They should have a perfect and just weight, a perfect and just measure (12-16)

Questions.Q: What were the Israelites to do to the Amalekites?
Questions.A: Blot out the remembrance of Amalek (17-19)

Questions.Q: What were the Israelites to bring to the priest in a basket?
Questions.A: The first of all the fruit of the earth (1-15)

Questions.Q: What kind of people were the Israelites to be to the LORD?
Questions.A: High above all nations, in praise, in name, and honor; and that they would be a holy people to the LORD (16-19)

Questions.Q: What were the Israelites to write on large stones?
Questions.A: All the words of the law (1-10)

Questions.Q: What were they not to use when they built an altar of these stones?
Questions.A: Iron tools (5-6)

Questions.Q: From what mountain were curses pronounced?
What would come upon the Israelites if they observed the commandments of the LORD?
Questions.A: Blessings (1-14)

Questions.Q: What would come upon the Israelites if they did not obey the commandments of the LORD?
Questions.A: Curses (15-48)

Questions.Q: What would the nation be like that would be brought against them?
Questions.A: A nation whose tongue you shall not understand. A nation of fierce countenance (49-63)

Questions.Q: Where would they be scattered?
Questions.A: Among all people, from the one end of the earth even to the other (64-68)

Questions.Q: How can a person deceive himself?
Questions.A: Walk in the imagination of his heart (19-21)

Questions.Q: What curse would come on the land if they forsook the covenant of God?
Questions.A: The whole land would be destroyed. It would become like burning brimstone and salt. No crops or vegetation would grow there. (22-28)

Questions.Q: What belongs to God?
Questions.A: Secret things (29)

Questions.Q: What belongs to us?
Questions.A: Those things which are revealed (29)

Questions.Q: What would happen if they returned to the LORD with all their heart in the places where they were scattered?
Questions.A: The LORD would turn their captivity, have compassion, and gather them from all the nations (1-10)

Questions.Q: Where were the commandments?
Questions.A: Very near to them, in their mouth, and in their heart. (11-14)

Questions.Q: What did the LORD set before them?
Questions.A: Life and good, and death and evil; vs.19 life and death, blessing and cursing (15-20)

Questions.Q: What charge did the Moses give Joshua?
Questions.A: Be strong and of a good courage: for you must go with this people to the land which the LORD has sworn to their fathers to give them; and you shall cause them to inherit it. (1-8)

Questions.Q: To whom did Moses deliver the law?
Questions.A: The priests (9-13)

Questions.Q: What supernatural signs occurred at the inauguration of Joshua?
Questions.A: The LORD appeared in the tabernacle in a pillar of a cloud: and the pillar of the cloud stood over the door of the tabernacle (14-15)

Questions.Q: Who gave Moses the song that he was to write?
Questions.A: The Lord (16-22)

Questions.Q: Where was the Book of the Law to be placed?
Questions.A: In the side of the ark of the covenant (23-26)

Questions.Q: What did Moses know would happen after his death?
Questions.A: Israel would utterly corrupt themselves, and turn aside from the way (27-29)

Questions.Q: What we ascribe to God?
Questions.A: Greatness (3-4)

Questions.Q: What illustration describes how God kept Israel in the wilderness?
Questions.A: As the apple of his eye (10)

Questions.Q: What illustration describes how God carried Israel?
Questions.A: As an eagle stirs up her nest, flutters over her young, spreads abroad her wings, takes them, bears them on her wings: (11)

Questions.Q: What was wrong with Jeshurun?
Questions.A: Jeshurun waxed fat, and kicked; then he forsook God which made him, and lightly esteemed the Rock of his salvation. (15-18)

Questions.Q: Where was Moses to die?
Questions.A: Mount Nebo, which is in the land of Moab, that is over against Jericho (48-52)

Questions.Q: What did Moses do for the Israelites before he died?
Questions.A: Blessed them (1)

Questions.Q: Which tribes did he mention?
Questions.A: Reuben, Judah, Levi, Joseph (Ephraim, Manasseh), Zebulun, Issachar, Gad, Dan, Naphtali, and Asshur (2-25)

Questions.Q: What did the LORD enable Moses to see?
Questions.A: The land that God had promised to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob (1-4)

Questions.Q: Who knows the location of Moses' grave?
Questions.A: No man (5-6)

Questions.Q: How old was Moses when he died?
Whom did Israel follow after the death of Moses?
Questions.A: Joshua (8-9)

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what happened in this chapter.
How might King David have avoided the confusion over who would be the next king and prevented the conflict between Solomon and Adonijah?
Questions.A: He should have rebuked Adonijah when he was younger, to correct his improper behavior. (6)
He should have made it clear to everyone that he planned to give the throne to Solomon.

Questions.Q: What physical problem did King David have?
Questions.A: He was very old and was unable to stay warm (1)

Questions.Q: How did Abishag serve King David?
Questions.A: She lay next to him to keep him warm (2)
She took care of him and waited on him (4)
Questions.Note: Answers should not imply any kind of sexual relationship, since the passage makes it clear that this was not the case.

Questions.Q: Who made himself king without David knowing it?
Questions.A: Adonijah the son of Haggith and David (5-11)

Questions.Q: What did Bathsheba do under the guidance of Nathan?

Questions.Q: According to David's instruction, who was appointed king of Israel?
Questions.A: Solomon (28-40)

Questions.Q: Upon hearing this, what did Adonijah do?
Questions.A: He caught hold on the horns of the altar (41-53)

Questions.Q: Whom did David charge Solomon to put to death?
Questions.A: Joab and Shimei (5-6, 8-9)

Questions.Q: How many years did David reign as king?
Questions.A: Forty (10-12)

Questions.Q: For what request was Adonijah put to death?
Questions.A: He requested Abishag the Shunammite be given to him as a wife (13-25)

Questions.Q: Who killed Joab and was put over Solomon's army?
Questions.A: Benaiah (28-35)

Questions.Q: Who was put in the priesthood as a replacement for Abiathar?
Whom else did Benaiah kill?
Questions.A: Shimei (36-46)

Questions.Q: Whom did Solomon marry?
Questions.A: The daughter of Pharaoh king of Egypt (1-2)

Questions.Q: What opportunity was given to Solomon when the Lord appeared to him?
Questions.A: To ask of the Lord what he wanted (4-5)

Questions.Q: For what did Solomon ask?

Questions.Q: In addition to Solomon's request, what else did the Lord say would be given to him?
