Questions.Q: What incident demonstrated the wisdom that God gave Solomon?
Questions.A: He determined which of the women was the mother of the child (16-28)

Questions.Q: Who supplied provisions for Solomon?
Questions.A: Twelve officers over all Israel, each man his month in a year made provision (7, 27-28)

Questions.Q: How did Solomon's wisdom compare to others?
Questions.A: Solomon's wisdom excelled the wisdom of all the children of the east country, and all the wisdom of Egypt. For he was wiser than all men (29-31)

Questions.Q: How many proverbs and songs did Solomon speak?
Questions.A: Three thousand proverbs: and his songs were a thousand and five (32)

Questions.Q: Of what other subjects did Solomon speak?
Questions.A: Trees, plants, animals and birds, reptiles and fish. (33)

Questions.Q: From where did people come to hear Solomon's wisdom?
Questions.A: From all kings of the earth (34)

Questions.Q: What did Solomon request from Hiram, king of Tyre?
Questions.A: Timber from cedar trees (1-6)

Questions.Q: What was Solomon to do for Hiram?
Questions.A: Give to Hiram twenty thousand measures of wheat and twenty measures of pure oil each year (7-12)

Questions.Q: How many Israelites did Solomon use to prepare materials for the temple?
Questions.A: 30,000 to work in Lebanon, 70,000 to bare burdens, 80,000 hewers in the mountains, and 3,300 supervisors. (13-18)

Questions.Q: How many years after Israel left Egypt did Solomon begin to build the temple?
What were the dimensions of the temple?
Questions.A: Length 60 cubits, breadth 20 cubits, height 30 cubits (2-3)

Questions.Q: What was built around the temple?
Questions.A: Chambers (5-6)

Questions.Q: What noise/sound was not heard in the construction of the temple/in the temple during the/its construction?
Questions.A: The sound of neither hammer nor ax nor any tool of iron (7)
Questions.Alternative: What noise was not heard in the construction of the temple?
What sound was not heard in the construction of the temple?
What noise was not heard in the temple during the construction?
What sound was not heard in the temple during the construction?
What noise was not heard in the temple during its construction?
What sound was not heard in the temple during its construction?

Questions.Q: What did the Lord promise Solomon if he kept God's statutes?
Questions.A: God would dwell among the Israelites, and not forsake them (11-13)

Questions.Q: With what material was the inside of the temple overlaid?
Questions.A: Pure gold (21-22)

Questions.Q: How many years did it take to build the temple?
Questions.A: Seven (38)

Questions.Q: How many years did it take to build Solomon's house?
Questions.A: Thirteen (1)

Questions.Q: Who did [all] the metal/bronze/brass work for the temple?
Questions.A: Hiram out of Tyre, who was a widow's son of the tribe of Naphtali, and his father was a man of Tyre, a worker in brass (13)
Questions.Alternative: Who did all the metal work for the temple?
Who did all the bronze work for the temple?
Who did all the brass work for the temple?
Who did the metal work for the temple?
Who did the bronze work for the temple?
Who did the brass work for the temple?

Questions.Q: What did Solomon bring to the temple when it was finished?
Questions.A: The things which David had dedicated; even the silver, the gold, and the vessels (51)

Questions.Q: What did the priests bring to the temple?
Questions.A: The ark of the LORD, the tabernacle of the congregation, and all the holy vessels that were in the tabernacle (3-9)

Questions.Q: What filled the temple when the priests came out of the holy place?
Questions.A: The glory of the LORD (10-11)

Questions.Q: What could not contain God?
Questions.A: The heaven and heaven of heavens and much less the temple (27)

Questions.Q: What did Solomon request of the Lord when people prayed toward the temple?
Questions.A: To hear from heaven and forgive (30-49)

Questions.Q: What did Solomon want all the peoples of the earth to know?
Questions.A: That the LORD is God, and that there is none else (60)

Questions.Q: How many animals did Solomon offer at the dedication of the temple?
What did Solomon build at Ezion-Geber?
Questions.A: A navy of ships (26)

Questions.Q: Whose sailors served in the same fleet with Solomon's men?
Questions.A: Hiram's servants who were experienced sailors and had knowledge of the sea (27-28)

Questions.Q: What did the Queen of Sheba say when she saw the achievements and wisdom of Solomon?
Questions.A: The half was not told me: your wisdom and prosperity exceeds the fame which I heard (1-10)

Questions.Q: How much gold did Solomon receive each year?
Questions.A: 666 talents of gold (14-17)

Questions.Q: Of what materials did Solomon make his throne?
Questions.A: Ivory overlaid with the best gold (18-20)

Questions.Q: Why weren't any of Solomon's vessels made of silver?
Questions.A: Silver wasn't worth much because Solomon made silver to be in Jerusalem as stones (21, 27)

Questions.Q: How did the riches and wisdom of Solomon compare to other kings?
Questions.A: Solomon exceeded all the kings of the earth for riches and for wisdom. (23-25)

Questions.Q: How many chariots and horsemen did Solomon have?
Questions.A: 1,400 chariots and 12,000 horsemen (26, 28-29)

Questions.Q: How many wives and concubines did Solomon have?
Questions.A: Seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines (1-3)

Questions.Q: Why was the LORD angry with Solomon?
Questions.A: Because his heart was turned from the LORD and built high places, burnt incense and sacrificed to the gods of his foreign wives (4-10)

Questions.Q: What did the LORD say would happen to the kingdom?
Questions.A: God would rend the kingdom from Solomon, and will give it to his servant (11-13)

Questions.Q: Who were Solomon's adversaries?
Questions.A: Hadad the Edomite and Rezon the son of Eliadah (14-25)

Questions.Q: With what object did Ahijah the prophet illustrate to Jeroboam that he would become king of ten tribes?
Questions.A: By tearing Jeroboam's new garment in twelve pieces and giving him ten (26-33)

Questions.Q: When would this division of the kingdom occur?
Questions.A: After Solomon's son began to reign (34-39)

Questions.Q: Who tried to kill Jeroboam?
Questions.A: Solomon (40)

Questions.Q: How long did Solomon reign in Jerusalem?
Questions.A: Forty years (41-42)

Questions.Q: Who reigned as king after Solomon died?
Questions.A: Rehoboam his son (43)

Questions.Q: What did Jeroboam request of Rehoboam?
Questions.A: Make the grievous service of Solomon, and his heavy yoke which he put on us, lighter, and we will serve you. (1-4)

Questions.Q: Whose advice did Rehoboam reject?
Questions.A: The old men (5-8)

Questions.Q: What advice did Rehoboam follow?
Questions.A: The advice of the young men who advised him to add to the yoke and chastise with scorpions rather than whips (9-15)

Questions.Q: What did Israel do to Adoram, who was over the tribute?
Questions.A: They stoned him with stones (18)

Questions.Q: Whom did Israel make as their king?
Questions.A: Jeroboam (20)

Questions.Q: Why did Jeroboam set up golden calves at Bethel and Dan?
Questions.A: Because he was afraid if the people went to Jerusalem to worship they might turn again to Rehoboam and kill him (26-33)

Questions.Q: What did the man of God from Judah prophesy against Jeroboam's altar?
Questions.A: A child named Josiah would be born to the house of David; and on the altar he would offer the priests of the high places that burn incense on it, and men's bones would be burned on it. Also, the altar would be broken, and the ashes would be poured out. (1-3)

Questions.Q: What happened to Jeroboam when he tried to seize the man of God/ordered the man of God to be seized?
Questions.A: His hand, which he put forth against him, dried up (4-5)
Questions.Alternative: What happened to Jeroboam when he tried to seize the man of God?
What happened to Jeroboam when he ordered the man of God to be seized?
What happened to Jeroboam when he ordered them to seize the man of God?

Questions.Q: Why did the man of God refuse Jeroboam's invitation?
Questions.A: Because God had told him to eat no bread, nor drink water, nor go back by the same way that he had come (6-10)

Questions.Q: How did the old prophet at Bethel persuade the man of God to come to his house?
Questions.A: He said he was a prophet also and claimed an angel spoke to him, telling him to bring him back to his house to eat bread and drink water. But he lied to him. (11-19)

Questions.Q: What happened to the man of God?
Questions.A: A lion met him on his way home and killed him (20-26)

Questions.Q: What was the sin of the house of Jeroboam that led to its downfall?
Questions.A: He made of the lowest of the people priests of the high places (33-34)

Questions.Q: What did Jeroboam tell his wife to do?
Questions.A: Disguise herself, and go to Ahijah the prophet, and find out what would become of their sick child. (1-4)

Questions.Q: What did the Lord reveal to the prophet Ahijah?
Questions.A: That Jeroboam's wife would be coming and to tell her that God would bring evil on the house of Jeroboam and that the child would die. (5-13)

Questions.Q: What would happen to Israel?
Questions.A: Israel would be smitten and scattered (14-16)

Questions.Q: How corrupt did Judah become?
Questions.A: They built high places, images, and groves, allowed sodomites in the land: and they did according to all the abominations of the nations which the LORD cast out before the Israelites (21-24)

Questions.Q: What did Shishak king of Egypt do?
Questions.A: He took away the treasures of the house of the LORD the treasures of the king's house, and he took away all the shields of gold which Solomon had made. (25-26)

Questions.Q: What did Rehoboam substitute for/make to replace what was/the treasures that were taken from the temple?
Questions.A: Brass shields (27-28)
Questions.Alternative: What did Rehoboam substitute for the treasures that were taken from the temple?
What did Rehoboam make to replace what was taken from the temple?
What did Rehoboam substitute for what was taken from the temple?
What did Rehoboam make to replace the treasures that were taken from the temple?

Questions.Q: What can be said of Abijam's three year reign as king of Judah?
Questions.A: He walked in all the sins of his father, which he had done before him: and his heart was not devoted to God (1-8)

Questions.Q: How did Asa do in his forty-one year reign over Judah?
Questions.A: Asa did that which was right in the eyes of the LORD. He took away the male shrine prostitutes and removed all the idols that his fathers had made (9-15)

Questions.Q: How did Nadab do in his two year reign over Israel?
Questions.A: He did evil in the sight of the LORD (25-26, 31-32)

Questions.Q: How did Baasha become king of Israel?
Questions.A: Baasha killed Asa, and reigned in his stead (27-30)

Questions.Q: What can be said of Baasha's twenty-four year reign as king of Israel?
Questions.A: He killed Jeroboam's whole family, according to Ahijah's prophecy, but he still did evil in the sight of the LORD, and walked in the way of Jeroboam (29-34)

Questions.Q: Who prophesied against Baasha?
Questions.A: Jehu the son of Hanani (1-7)

Questions.Q: How did Zimri become king?
Questions.A: Zimri went in and struck Elah the son of Baasha, and killed him and reigned in his stead (8-14)

Questions.Q: How many days did Zimri reign as king of Israel?
Questions.A: Seven (15-20)

Questions.Q: How did Omri do in his twelve year reign as king over Israel?
Questions.A: Omri worked evil in the eyes of the LORD, and did worse than all that were before him (21-28)

Questions.Q: What city did Omri build?
Questions.A: Samaria (24)

Questions.Q: How did Ahab do in his twenty-two year reign over Israel?
Questions.A: Ahab the son of Omri did evil in the sight of the LORD above all that were before him (29-33)

Questions.Q: Whom did Ahab marry?
Questions.A: Jezebel the daughter of Ethbaal king of the Sidonians (31)

Questions.Q: How was Joshua's prophecy in Joshua 6:26 fulfilled when Jericho was rebuilt?
Questions.A: Two of Hiel's sons died as was prophesied. (34)

Questions.Q: What did Elijah say would not happen for the next three years?
Questions.A: Dew or rain (1)

Questions.Q: How was Elijah fed during this time?
Questions.A: Ravens fed him (2-5)

Questions.Q: What did Elijah ask the widow of Zarephath to do for him?
Questions.A: Bring him a little water in a vessel and a morsel of bread (6-13)

Questions.Q: What miracle of provision did the LORD perform for the widow?
Questions.A: The flour was not used up and the jug oil did not run dry, until the day that the LORD sent rain on the earth. (14-16)

Questions.Q: What other miracle did the LORD perform for the widow?
Questions.A: Raised the woman's son from the dead. (17-24)

Questions.Q: What did the LORD tell Elijah to do?
Questions.A: Show himself to Ahab (1-2)

Questions.Q: What did Obadiah do when Jezebel was killing the LORD's prophets?
Questions.A: He took one hundred prophets, and hid them by fifty in a cave, and fed them with bread and water (3-6)

Questions.Q: Why was Obadiah afraid to tell Ahab that Elijah was there?
Questions.A: He was afraid that the Spirit of the LORD would carry Elijah somewhere and when he told Ahab, and Ahab could not find Elijah that Ahab would kill him (7-15)

Questions.Q: What did Ahab call Elijah?
Questions.A: He that troubles Israel (16-18)

Questions.Q: How much was Elijah outnumbered on Mt. Carmel? // How many false prophets came up against Elijah on Mt. Carmel?
Questions.A: 850 false prophets against Elijah (850 to 1) (19)
Questions.Alternative: How much was Elijah outnumbered on Mt. Carmel?
How many false prophets came up against Elijah on Mt. Carmel?

Questions.Q: What did Elijah ask the people of Israel?
Questions.A: How long halt you between two opinions? if the LORD be God, follow him: but if Baal, then follow him. (20-21)

Questions.Q: What would be the sign of the one true God?
Questions.A: The God that answers by fire (22-24)

Questions.Q: How long did Elijah give the prophets of Baal to call on their god?
Questions.A: From morning until the time of the evening sacrifice (25-29)

Questions.Q: How much water did Elijah pour on his sacrifice and wood?
Questions.A: Twelve barrels (30-35)

Questions.Q: Why did Elijah want God to answer his prayer?
Questions.A: For it to be known that The LORD is God in Israel, and that he was God's servant, and that he did all these things at God's word (36-39)

Questions.Q: What did they do to the prophets of Baal?
Questions.A: Slaughtered them (40)

Questions.Q: What did Elijah hear?
Questions.A: A sound of abundance of rain (41)

Questions.Q: What sign was given to Elijah's servant that it was going to rain?
Questions.A: A little cloud out of the sea, like a man's hand (42-44)

Questions.Q: How fast did Elijah run?
Questions.A: Faster than Ahab rode (44-46)

Questions.Q: Why did Elijah flee from Jezebel?
Questions.A: She was wanting to kill him for killing her prophets (1-3)

Questions.Q: For what did Elijah pray?
Questions.A: That he might die (4)

Questions.Q: Who provided food for Elijah giving him strength to get to Horeb?
Questions.A: An angel of the LORD (5-8)

Questions.Q: What question did the LORD twice ask Elijah?
Questions.A: What do you here, Elijah? (9, 13)

Questions.Q: How did the LORD speak to Elijah?
Questions.A: With a still small voice (11-12)

Questions.Q: How did the LORD respond to Elijah's statement that he was the only one left of the LORD's prophets?
Questions.A: I have left me seven thousand in Israel, all the knees which have not bowed to Baal (10, 14, 18)

Questions.Q: Whom did the LORD tell Elijah to anoint?
Questions.A: Hazael to be king over Syria: Jehu to be king over Israel: and Elisha to be prophet in Elijah's place (15-17)

Questions.Q: What was Elisha doing when Elijah found him?
Questions.A: Plowing with twelve yoke of oxen before him (19-20)

Questions.Q: What did Elisha do to his yoke/pair of oxen and plow/plowing equipment?
Questions.A: He took a yoke of oxen, slaughtered them, and boiled their flesh with the instruments of the oxen, and gave to the people to eat. (21)
Questions.Alternative: What did Elisha do to his pair of oxen and plow?
What did Elisha do to his pair of oxen and plowing equipment?
What did Elisha do to his yoke of oxen and plow?
What did Elisha do to his yoke of oxen and plowing equipment?

Questions.Q: Who threatened to take Ahab's wives, children, silver and gold?
Questions.A: Benhadad the king of Syria (1-12)

Questions.Q: Why did the LORD give Ahab victory over Benhadad?
Questions.A: Because the Syrians said that the LORD was God of the hills, but not of the valleys; therefore God delivered them that they would know who was the LORD (13, 28)

Questions.Q: For what did the prophet condemn Ahab?
Questions.A: Because he let Benhadad go whom God appointed to utter destruction (34-43)

Questions.Q: Why did Naboth refuse to sell Ahab his vineyard?
Questions.A: Because he believed that the LORD forbid him from giving his inheritance to Ahab (1-6)

Questions.Q: What did Jezebel have done to Naboth?
Questions.A: She had false witnesses accuse Naboth of blaspheming and then had him stoned to death. (7-16)

Questions.Q: What did Elijah prophesy about Ahab?
Questions.A: In the place where dogs licked the blood of Naboth, they would also lick Ahab's blood (17-22, 24)

Questions.Q: What did Elijah prophesy would happen to Jezebel?
Questions.A: The dogs would eat Jezebel by the wall of Jezreel. (23)

Questions.Q: Who was partly responsible for Ahab's vile behavior?
Questions.A: Jezebel (25-26)

Questions.Q: Why was the disaster prophesied against Ahab delayed until his son?
Questions.A: Because he humbled himself before God (27-29)

Questions.Q: What did Ahab ask Jehoshaphat to do?
Questions.A: To go with Ahab to battle to Ramoth Gilead (1-4)

Questions.Q: What did Jehoshaphat first want to do?
Questions.A: Inquire at the word of the LORD (5)

Questions.Q: What did Ahab's four hundred prophets tell Ahab to do?
Questions.A: Go up against Ramothgilead to battle; for the LORD shall deliver it into the hand of the king (6, 10-13)

Questions.Q: Why did Ahab hate Micaiah?
Questions.A: Because he did not prophesy good concerning Ahab, but evil. (7-8, 18)

Questions.Q: What did Micaiah say would happen to Israel?
Questions.A: Israel would be scattered on the hills, as sheep that have not a shepherd (17)

Questions.Q: What did Ahab order to be done to Micaiah?
Questions.A: Put him in prison, and feed him with bread and water of affliction (26-27)

Questions.Q: What happened to Ahab in the battle?
Questions.A: He was smitten with an arrow and he died (29-40)

Questions.Q: What did Jehoshaphat get rid of out of the land of Judah?
Questions.A: Sodomites (41-47)

Questions.Q: What happened to Jehoshaphat's ships?
Questions.A: They were broken at Eziongeber (48-49)

Questions.Q: How did Ahaziah do in his two year reign over Israel?
Questions.A: He did evil in the sight of the LORD, and walked in the way of his parents Ahab and Jezebel (51-53)

Questions.Q: What did the LORD tell Joshua to do?
Questions.A: Lead Israel over (1-2)
Jordan (1-2)

Questions.Q: What was the extent of the land that was promised to Israel?
Questions.A: From the wilderness and Lebanon even to the river Euphrates, all the land of the Hittites, and to the great sea (3-4)

Questions.Q: How did the LORD promise to be with Joshua?
Questions.A: As He was with Moses (5)

Questions.Q: What was Joshua to do in order to be prosperous and successful?
Questions.A: Keep the book of the law in his mouth; meditate on it day and night, and observe to do according to all that is written in it. (6-9)

Questions.Q: What were the Reubenites, Gadites and half the tribe of Manasseh to do?
Questions.A: Their strong men who were able to be soldiers were to pass over Jordan armed and help the other tribes until the LORD gave them rest (10-18)

Questions.Q: Who hid the men that Joshua sent to spy out Jericho?
Questions.A: Rahab (1-8)

Questions.Q: What had the people of Jericho heard about Israel?
Questions.A: How the LORD dried up the water of the Red sea and how they utterly destroyed Sihon and Og (9-11)

Questions.Q: What did Rahab ask of the spies?
Questions.A: Save alive her father, mother, bothers, and sisters, and all that they had (12-14)

Questions.Q: How did the spies escape from Jericho?
Questions.A: By a cord through the window (15-16)

Questions.Q: How were the Israelites to know which was Rahab's house?
Questions.A: By the scarlet cord in the window (17-20)

Questions.Q: What report did the spies bring to Joshua?
Questions.A: All the inhabitants of the country were afraid because of Israel. (24)

Questions.Q: How did the Israelites know when to start marching toward Jordan?
Questions.A: When they saw the priests bearing the ark of the covenant (1-8)

Questions.Q: What miracle was given to let them know that God would drive out the inhabitants of the land?
Questions.A: When the waters of Jordan were cut off from the waters that come down from above; and they stood on a heap (9-17)

Questions.Q: What did they do with the twelve stones that they got from the midst of Jordan?
Questions.A: Joshua put them in Gilgal (1-9, 19-24)

Questions.Q: What did the waters of Jordan do after everyone had crossed over?
Questions.A: They returned to their place, and flowed over the banks, as they did before the miracle (10-18)

Questions.Q: What was the reaction of the kings west of Jordan when they heard that the LORD had dried up Jordan?
Questions.A: Their heart melted, neither was there spirit in them any more (1)

Questions.Q: Whom did Joshua circumcise at Gilgal?
Questions.A: Those that were born in the wilderness (2-9)

Questions.Q: What else did Israel keep at Gilgal?
Questions.A: The passover (10)

Questions.Q: When did the manna cease?
Questions.A: After they had eaten of the old corn and the fruit of the land (11-12)

Questions.Q: Whom did Joshua encounter near Gilgal?
Questions.A: The captain of the host of the LORD (13-15)

Questions.Q: How often did the Israelites march around Jericho the first six days?
Questions.A: Once (1-14)

Questions.Q: How often did they march around Jericho on the seventh day?
Questions.A: Seven times (15)

Questions.Q: What were they Israelites to abstain from?
Questions.A: the accursed thing – all that was in the city (18)

Questions.Q: What was to be done with the silver and gold?
Questions.A: Brought into the treasury of the LORD (19, 24)

Questions.Q: What happened to the walls of Jericho when the Israelites shouted?
Questions.A: Fell down flat (20)

Questions.Q: Who were the only inhabitants of Jericho that were spared?
Questions.A: Rahab, the harlot and all that were with her in the house (17, 21-23, 25)

Questions.Q: Why did Israel send only 3000 men to fight against Ai?
Questions.A: They thought Ai was a small town and easy to conquer (2-9)

Questions.Q: Why was Israel defeated by Ai?
Questions.A: Israel had sinned by taking of the accursed thing, and had also stolen and put it among their own stuff. (10-13)

Questions.Q: How did Joshua find out that Achan was the one who sinned?
Questions.A: He made all Israel come by tribes, families, households and by man until Achan was revealed. (1, 14-18)

Questions.Q: What was Achan's confession?
Questions.A: I have sinned against the LORD. When I saw a beautiful garment, silver, and gold, then I coveted them, and took them; and hid them in my tent. (19-21)

Questions.Q: What was done to Achan, his family and his possessions?
Questions.A: They were stoned and burned with fire (22-26)

Questions.Q: What military strategy did Joshua use to defeat Ai?
Questions.A: He set ambushes behind and at the side of Ai. When the bulk of Israel pretended to flee the ambushes attacked Ai and set it on fire. (1-27)

Questions.Q: How many of the men of Ai were lured from the city?
What did Joshua do to the king of Ai?
Questions.A: Hanged him on a tree (28-29)

Questions.Q: What did Joshua build on Mount Ebal?
Questions.A: An altar to the LORD (30-33)

Questions.Q: What did Joshua read to the whole assembly of Israel?
Questions.A: All the words of the law, the blessings and curses, according to all that is written in the book of the law (34-35)

Questions.Q: How did the people of Gibeon fool Israel?
Questions.A: By taking old wine bottles, wearing old clothes and shoes, and bringing moldy and dry bread and pretending to be ambassadors from a far country. (1-13)

Questions.Q: What did the men of Israel fail to do?
Questions.A: Pray (ask counsel of the Lord) (14-15)

Questions.Q: What did Joshua make the Gibeonites to become?
Questions.A: Hewers of wood and drawers of water (16-27)

Questions.Q: Who joined forces to attack Gibeon?
Questions.A: The kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon (1-5)

Questions.Q: How did the LORD kill more of them than with Israelite swords?
Questions.A: With hailstones (7-11)

Questions.Q: What other miracle occurred during the battle?
Questions.A: The sun stood still, and the moon stayed, until the people had avenged themselves on their enemies. (12-15)

Questions.Q: What did Joshua do to the five kings?
Questions.A: Killed them and hanged them on five trees (16-27)

Questions.Q: What other cities did Joshua destroy?
Questions.A: Makkedah, Libnah, Gezer, and Debir (28-43)

Questions.Q: What did Joshua do to the horses and chariots of Hazor and the kings with him?
Questions.A: Hamstrung their horses, and burnt their chariots with fire (1-15)

Questions.Q: What caused the kings to come against Joshua in battle?
Questions.A: The LORD hardened their hearts, that they should come against Israel in battle (16-23)

Questions.Q: What kings did Moses conquer?
Questions.A: Sihon and Og (1-6)

Questions.Q: How many kings did Joshua conquer?
Questions.A: Thirty-one. (7-24)

Questions.Q: What did the LORD say to Joshua when he was old?
Questions.A: There remains yet very much land to be possessed. (1-8)

Questions.Q: To whom was given the land east of the Jordan?
Questions.A: The tribes of Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh (9-13, 15-32)

Questions.Q: What was the inheritance of the tribe of Levi?
Questions.A: The offerings of the LORD (14, 33)

Questions.Q: Whom did the Israelites kill with the sword?
Questions.A: Balaam (22)

Questions.Q: Who was Caleb?
Questions.A: He was one of the 12 spies that went into Canaan while Moses was leading the Israelites in the wilderness. He was now an old man.

Questions.Q: What made Caleb special?
Questions.A: He and Joshua were the only spies (of the twelve sent by Moses) who were faithful and trusted God to help them defeat the Canaanites.
He was allowed to enter the promised land because of his faithfulness (all the other men his age had died in the wilderness).
He had been promised a special inheritance because of his faithfulness.
Even though he was old, he was still strong and ready to fight to clear the land of God's enemies.

Questions.Q: Whose children became two tribes?
Questions.A: Joseph (1-5)

Questions.Q: How did Caleb serve the LORD?
Questions.A: He wholly followed the LORD (6-9)

Questions.Q: What did Caleb request of Joshua?
Questions.A: The mountain where the Anakims lived (10-15)

Questions.Q: The allotment for which tribe is described in this chapter?
Questions.A: Judah

Questions.Q: What did Caleb offer to the man who captured Kirjath-sepher?
Questions.A: Achsah his daughter to wife (16)

Questions.Q: Which tribe's boundaries are described in this chapter?
Questions.A: Joseph (Ephraim and Manasseh) (1-10)

Questions.Q: Which tribe's boundaries are described in this chapter?
Questions.A: Manasseh and Ephraim (1-13)

Questions.Q: How did Joshua reply when the people of Joseph felt that their allotment was too small?
Questions.A: You are a great people, and have great power. The mountain shall be yours. You shall drive out the Canaanites, though they have iron chariots, and though they be strong. (14-18)

Questions.Q: What were the three men from each tribe sent out to do?
Questions.A: Go through the land, and divide the land into seven parts, and bring the description to Joshua for an inheritance for the remaining seven tribes (1-9)

Questions.Q: How was it determined what land would belong to which tribes?
Questions.A: Cast lots (6, 10)

Questions.Q: Which tribe's boundaries are described in this section?
Questions.A: Benjamin

Questions.Q: Whose inheritance was taken from the share of Judah because Judah's portion was more than they needed?
Questions.A: Simeon (1-9)

Questions.Q: Which tribe received the third lot whose boundaries are described?
Questions.A: Zebulun (10-16)

Questions.Q: Which tribe received the fourth lot whose boundaries are described?
Questions.A: Issachar (17-23)

Questions.Q: Which tribe received the fifth lot whose boundaries are described?
Questions.A: Asher (24-31)

Questions.Q: Which tribe received the sixth lot whose boundaries are described?
Questions.A: Naphtali (32-39)

Questions.Q: Which tribe received the seventh lot whose boundaries are described?
What was given to Joshua?
Questions.A: The city Timnathserah in mount Ephraim (49-51)

Questions.Q: What six cities were selected to be cities of refuge?
Questions.A: Kedesh in Galilee, Shechem in Ephraim, and Hebron in Judah. And on the other side Jordan Bezer in Reuben, Ramoth in Gad, and Golan in Manasseh. (1-9)

Questions.Q: From where did the descendants of Aaron get their towns?
Questions.A: Out of the tribes of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin (4, 9-19)

Questions.Q: From where did the rest of the Kohathites get their towns?
Questions.A: Of the tribes of Ephraim, Dan, and half the tribe of Manasseh (5, 20-26)

Questions.Q: From where did the Gershonites get their towns?
Questions.A: Of the tribes of Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and half the tribe of Manasseh in Bashan (6, 27-33)

Questions.Q: From where did the Merarites get their towns?
Questions.A: Of the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun (7, 34-42)

Questions.Q: How many of God's good promises to Israel failed?
Whom did Joshua send back across Jordan after doing their duty?
Questions.A: The Reubenites, Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh. (1-9)

Questions.Q: What did they build near Jordan?
Questions.A: An altar (10)

Questions.Q: Why did the rest of Israel want to go to war against them?
Questions.A: They thought the altar was in rebellion against God turning away from Him (11-20)

Questions.Q: What reason did they give for building the altar?
Questions.A: So their children would know that they had a part in Israel and they do the service of the Lord (21-29)

Questions.Q: What did they name the altar?
Questions.A: Ed: (witness between us that the LORD is God.) (30-34)

Questions.Q: How could one of Israel chase a thousand?
Questions.A: Because the LORD fights for them (1-11)

Questions.Q: What would happen to Israel if they intermarried with the surviving nations?
Questions.A: The LORD would no more drive out the nations , but they would be snares, traps, scourges in their sides, and thorns in their eyes, until they perished from the promised land . (12-13)

Questions.Q: What did Joshua realize was about to happen to him?
Questions.A: He would die (14-16)

Questions.Q: What did Joshua summarize when he assembled the tribes together?
Questions.A: The history from the time Abraham left his father until the occupation of the promised land. (1-14)

Questions.Q: What choice did Joshua give the Israelites?
Questions.A: Whether they would serve the gods which Abraham's father served, the gods of the Amorites, or the LORD God (14-15)

Questions.Q: What was Joshua's choice?
Questions.A: To serve the LORD (15)

Questions.Q: What was the reply of the people?
Questions.A: We will also serve the LORD; for he is our God (16-21)

Questions.Q: What symbol was placed under an oak tree as a witness?
Questions.A: A great stone (22-27)

Questions.Q: How long did Israel serve the LORD?
Questions.A: All the days of Joshua, and all the days of the elders that outlived Joshua, and which had known all the works of the LORD (28-31)

Questions.Q: Whose bones were buried at Shechem?
Questions.A: Joseph (32-33)

Questions.Q: What did a man from Saul's camp bring to David?
Questions.A: Saul's crown and bracelet (1-10)

Questions.Q: What did David have done to the Amalekite who claimed to have killed Saul?
Questions.A: Had a young man kill him (11-16)

Questions.Q: What did David say about the mighty?
Questions.A: How are the mighty fallen! (19, 25, 27)

Questions.Q: What did the men of Judah do to David at Hebron?
Questions.A: They anointed David king over the house of Judah. (1-7)

Questions.Q: Whom did Abner make as king over Israel?
Questions.A: Ishbosheth the son of Saul (8-10)

Questions.Q: How long was David king over just Judah?
Questions.A: Seven years and six months (11)

Questions.Q: Who pursued after Abner and was killed by Abner?
Questions.A: Asahel (12-23)

Questions.Q: What eventually happened as the war between the house of Saul and the house of David continued?
Questions.A: David waxed stronger and stronger, and the house of Saul waxed weaker and weaker (1)

Questions.Q: What did Abner decide to do regarding the kingdom of Israel?
Questions.A: Translate the kingdom from the house of Saul, and to set up the throne of David over Israel and over Judah (6-12)

Questions.Q: What did David ask Abner to bring with him?
Questions.A: Michal, Saul's daughter (13-16)

Questions.Q: Who killed Abner without David's permission?
What did Recab and Baanah do to Ishbosheth, son of Saul?
Questions.A: They stabbed him and beheaded him, and brought the head of Ishbosheth to David (1-8)

Questions.Q: What did David's men do to Recab and Baanah?
Questions.A: They killed them, cut off their hands and their feet, and hanged them up over the pool in Hebron (9-12)

Questions.Q: What did the elders of Israel do to David?
Questions.A: They anointed David king over Israel (1-3)

Questions.Q: How old was David when he became king of Judah?
Questions.A: Thirty years old (4)

Questions.Q: What city did David conquer and call the City of David?
Questions.A: Zion (5-10)

Questions.Q: What did Hiram, king of Tyre, do for David?
Questions.A: Sent messengers to David, and cedar trees, and carpenters, and masons: and they built David a house (11-12)

Questions.Q: Whom did David defeat twice?
Questions.A: The Philistines (17-25)

Questions.Q: What happened to Uzzah?
Questions.A: Because Uzzah put forth his hand to the ark of God, God struck him and he died by the ark of God (1-8)

Questions.Q: At whose house did the ark remain for three months?
Questions.A: Obededom (9-11)

Questions.Q: What did David do when he brought the ark to the City of David?
Questions.A: David danced before the LORD with all his might (12-15)

Questions.Q: What was Michal's reaction to David's dancing before the Lord?
Questions.A: She despised him in her heart (16-20)

Questions.Q: What happened to Michal?
Questions.A: She became barren (21-23)

Questions.Q: Instead of David who would build a house for God's name?
Questions.A: His offspring after him (1-13)

Questions.Q: How long would David's kingdom endure?
Questions.A: For ever (13-16)

Questions.Q: What did David do to the chariot horses that belonged to the king of Zobah?
Questions.A: Hamstrung them (3-4)

Questions.Q: What did David do with the silver, gold, and brass that were brought to him?
Questions.A: Dedicated it to the LORD (9-12)

Questions.Q: Who was over David's army?
Questions.A: Joab (16)

Questions.Q: Who were David's priests?
Questions.A: Zadok the son of Ahitub, and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar (17)

Questions.Q: To whom of the house of Saul did David show kindness?
Questions.A: Mephibosheth (1-6)

Questions.Q: What benefits did David provide for him?
Questions.A: Eat at David's table, as one of the king's sons (7-13)

Questions.Q: What did Hanun do to David's men?
Questions.A: Shaved off one half of their beards, cut off their garments in the middle, even to their buttocks, and sent them away (1-5)

Questions.Q: What was the battle plan of Joab and Abishai?
Questions.A: Part of the army was under Joab and part under Abishai. When one group needed it the other part would come and help (9-12)

Questions.Q: At the time when kings go to war where was David?
Questions.A: David tarried still at Jerusalem saw a woman washing herself (1)

Questions.Q: What resulted from David's affair with Bathsheba?
Questions.A: Bathsheba became pregnant (2-5)

Questions.Q: How did David attempt to cover up this sin?
Questions.A: Brought home her husband and tried to get him to go in to his wife (6-13)

Questions.Q: How did David have Uriah put to death?
Questions.A: He had Joab put him in the hottest part of the battle so he would be smitten and die. (14-25)

Questions.Q: What did David then do with Bathsheba?
Questions.A: Married her (26-27)

Questions.Q: How did Nathan cause David to recognize his sin?
Questions.A: Telling a story of a rich man who killed a poor man's lamb (1-6)

Questions.Q: What would not depart from David's house?
Questions.A: The sword (7-12)

Questions.Q: What did David do after Nathan spoke to him?
Questions.A: He said “I have sinned against the LORD” (13)

Questions.Q: What opportunity did David give to the enemies of the Lord?
Questions.A: To blaspheme (14)

Questions.Q: What happened to the child that Uriah's wife bore to David?
Questions.A: The child died (15-18)

Questions.Q: How did David respond upon hearing of the death of the child?
Questions.A: David got up, washed, anointed himself, and changed his clothes. Then he went into the house of the LORD, and worshiped. Then he went to his own house and requested food to eat. (19-20)

Questions.Q: How did David explain his behavior?
Questions.A: While the child was yet alive, I fasted and wept: 23But now he is dead, why should I fast? can I bring him back again? (21-23)

Questions.Q: Who afterwards was born to David and Bathsheba?
Questions.A: Solomon (24-25)

Questions.Q: What did David take from the head from the king of Rabah?
Questions.A: The king's crown (26-31)

Questions.Q: What did Amnon the son of David do to Tamar the sister of Absalom?
Questions.A: He raped her (1-14)

Questions.Q: After the sin what did Amnon do to Tamar?
Questions.A: He hated her (15-19)

Questions.Q: What did Absalom have his servants do to Amnon?
Questions.A: He had his servants kill him (20-29)

Questions.Q: To where did Absalom flee?
Questions.A: To Talmai, the son of Ammihud, king of Geshur (37-38)

Questions.Q: Tell in your own words what happened in this chapter.
Do you think Joab and Absalom acted properly to get David's attention and restore the relationship between the king and his son?
Questions.Note: Answers may vary with personal and cultural perspective, but should reflect understanding that their actions - though extreme - did seem to produce the desired result.

Questions.Q: Whom did Joab use to tell David a story so that Absalom would be brought back?
Questions.A: A wise woman of Tekoah (1-20)

Questions.Q: Where did David want Absalom to go?
Questions.A: To his own house (21-24)

Questions.Q: How long did Absalom live in Jerusalem without seeing David?
Questions.A: Two years (25-28)

Questions.Q: How did Absalom finally get to see David?
Questions.A: He had his servants set Joab's field on fire (29-33)

Questions.Q: How did Absalom steal the hearts of Israel?
Questions.A: He made it publicly known that he wished to be judge of the land. Also when any man came near to him, he put forth his hand, and took him, and kissed him. (1-6)

Questions.Q: What did Absalom appoint himself to be at Hebron?
Questions.A: The one who reigns (7-11)

Questions.Q: Whom did Absalom send for? // For whom did Absalom send? // Who did Absalom call?
Questions.A: Ahithophel, David's counselor (12)
Questions.Alternative: Whom did Absalom send for?
For whom did Absalom send?
Who did Absalom call?

Questions.Q: When David fled Jerusalem who remained at Jerusalem to inform him?
Questions.A: Zadok the priest, his son Ahimaaz, Abiathar and his son Jonathan (13-29)

Questions.Q: Whom else did David send to Jerusalem to frustrate Ahithophel's advice?
Questions.A: Hushai (30-37)

Questions.Q: What did Ziba do for David?
Questions.A: Brought him two hundred loaves of bread, and one hundred bunches of raisins, and one hundred bunches of summer fruits, and a bottle of wine (1-4)

Questions.Q: What did Shimei do to David?
Questions.A: Cast stones at David and cursed him (5-13)

Questions.Q: Whose prophecy did Absalom fulfill?
Questions.A: Nathan's (20-22)
Questions.Note: See also 12:11-13

Questions.Q: How did Absalom regard Ahithophel's advice?
Questions.A: As if a man had inquired at the oracle of God (23)

Questions.Q: Whose advice, regarding pursuing David, did Absalom think was better than that of Ahithophel?
Questions.A: Hushai (1-14)

Questions.Q: Whom did Hushai tell about the counsel that he and Ahithophel had given to Absalom?
Questions.A: He told Zadok and to Abiathar the priests (14-16)

Questions.Q: Why did Hushai tell this this information?
Questions.A: So that they would send their sons Ahimaaz and Jonathan to warn David (14-16)

Questions.Q: How did Ahimaaz and Jonathan find out what Hushai told Zadok and Abiathar?
Questions.A: Zadok and Abiathar sent the message via a maidservant (17)

Questions.Q: Why didn't Ahimaaz and Jonathan come to talk to their fathers directly?
Questions.A: They could not be seen entering the city [because Absalom would find out they were taking secret messages to David] (17)

Questions.Q: What did the lad see that caused trouble for Ahimaaz and Jonathan?
Questions.A: He saw them getting the [secret] message [from the maidservant] to take to David. (18)

Questions.Q: How did Jonathan and Ahimaaz hide?
Questions.A: In a well [in Bahurim] (18-22)

Questions.Q: Who helped Jonathan and Ahimaaz hide?
Questions.A: A woman [presumably the wife of the man whose house had a well in the courtyard] (18-22)

Questions.Q: What did Ahithophel do when he saw his advice was not followed?
Questions.A: He hanged himself (23)

Questions.Q: Who did Absalom appoint over his army?
Questions.A: Amasa (24-26)

Questions.Q: What did Shobi, Makir, and Barzillai do for David?
Questions.A: Brought beds, and basins, earthen vessels, wheat, barley, flour, parched corn, beans, lentils, parched vegetables, honey, butter, sheep, and cheese (27-29)

Questions.Q: What command did David give his army regarding Absalom?
Questions.A: Deal gently for my sake with Absalom. (1-5)

Questions.Q: What happened to Absalom in the forest?
Questions.A: His head got caught in a tree and the mule he was riding on went away. (6-10)

Questions.Q: What did Joab do to Absalom?
Questions.A: He took three darts, and thrust them through the heart of Absalom. (11-15)

Questions.Q: Who ran to David but had no news concerning Absalom?
Questions.A: Ahimaaz (19-30)

Questions.Q: Who brought the news concerning Absalom's death to David?
Questions.A: Cushi (31-33)

Questions.Q: Why did Joab tell David to stop mourning for Absalom?
Questions.A: If David did not quit mourning no one would continue to follow him. (1-8)

Questions.Q: Who did David refuse to kill when he returned to Jerusalem?
Questions.A: Shimei (16-23)

Questions.Q: Why did Barzillai turn down David's offer to go to Jerusalem?
Questions.A: He was old and did not want to be a burden to the king. (31-40)

Questions.Q: Who rebelled against David?
Questions.A: Sheba, the son of Bichri (1-2)

Questions.Q: Who did Joab kill that could have become commander of the army?
Questions.A: Amasa (4-13)

Questions.Q: What did the wise woman do to spare the city which Joab was seeking to destroy?
Questions.A: She arranged to have the head of Sheba cut off and thrown over the wall to Joab (14-22)

Questions.Q: Who was hanged and exposed by the Gibeonites?
Questions.A: Seven male descendants of Saul (1-9)

Questions.Q: What did Rizpah do?
Questions.A: She did not allow either the birds of the air to rest on the bodies by day, nor the beasts of the field by night. (10)

Questions.Q: What was unusual about the man that Jonathan son of Shimeah killed?
Questions.A: He was a man of great stature, that had on every hand six fingers, and on every foot six toes (20-21)

Questions.Q: To whom did David sing?
Questions.A: The Lord (1-51)

Questions.Q: Who struck the Philistines until his hand grew tired and froze to the sword?
Questions.A: Eleazar (9-10)

Questions.Q: Who stood in the middle of a field of lentils and defended it?
Questions.A: Shammah (11-12)

Questions.Q: What did David do with the water that was brought from Bethlehem?
Questions.A: He poured it out to the LORD (13-17)

Questions.Q: Who went down into a pit and killed a lion on a snowy day?
Questions.A: Benaiah (20-23)

Questions.Q: Who was the last person mentioned among David's mighty men?
Questions.A: Uriah the Hittite (24-39)

Questions.Q: What did David command Joab to do?
Questions.A: Number the people (1-9)

Questions.Q: What did David realize he had done?
Questions.A: He had sinned greatly (10)

Questions.Q: What three options did Gad offer David as punishment?
Questions.A: Seven years of famine, flee three months before his enemies, or three days' pestilence (11-17)

Questions.Q: What did Araunah offer to give to David?
Questions.A: Oxen for burnt sacrifice and wood. (18-23)

Questions.Q: Why did David insist on paying?
Questions.A: He would not offer burnt offerings to the LORD of that which cost him nothing (24-25)

Questions.Q: What did Solomon request when the LORD appeared to him at night?
Questions.A: Wisdom and knowledge, that he might judge God's people, that were so great (7-10)

Questions.Q: What did the LORD give to Solomon?
Questions.A: Riches, and wealth, and honor in addition to wisdom and knowledge (11-12)

Questions.Q: Where did Solomon get many of his horses and chariots?
Questions.A: Egypt (14-17)

Questions.Q: What did Solomon determine to do?
Questions.A: Build a house for the name of the LORD (1)

Questions.Q: What did Solomon request from Huram king of Tyre?
Questions.A: A man skilled in working in gold, silver, brass/bronze, and iron; and in purple, crimson/scarlet, and blue fabrics; and in engraving. (7)
Cedar, cypress/fir, and algum/sandalwood trees, out of Lebanon (8)

Questions.Q: Whom did Solomon make to be bearers of burdens?
Questions.A: Strangers that were in the land of Israel (17-18)

Questions.Q: Where did Solomon build the temple?
Questions.A: At Jerusalem in mount Moriah, in the place that David had prepared in the threshing floor of Ornan (1-2)

Questions.Q: What were the dimensions of the temple?
Questions.A: The length was 60 cubits, and the breadth 20 cubits. The length the porch was 20 cubits, and the height was an 120 cubits (3)

Questions.Q: What were the dimensions of the most holy house?
Questions.A: 20 cubits by 20 cubits (8)

Questions.Q: How much brass was used for the various items?
Questions.A: The weight of the brass could not be found out. (18)

Questions.Q: What were some items made of gold?
Questions.A: Candlesticks, tables, basins, flowers, lamps, tongs, snuffers, basins spoons, and censers (7-8, 19-22)

Questions.Q: How many sheep and oxen were sacrificed?
Questions.A: It could not be told nor numbered for multitude (6)

Questions.Q: What was in the ark?
Questions.A: The two tablets (with the commandments) that which Moses put in it (10)

Questions.Q: How many priests sounded with trumpets?
How many sounds did the trumpeters and singers make?
Questions.A: One (13)

Questions.Q: What filled the house of the Lord?
Questions.A: A cloud: for the glory of the LORD had filled the house of God. (13-14)

Questions.Q: What did the LORD say to David regarding his desire to build a house for God?
Questions.A: He did well in that it was in his heart (8)

Questions.Q: What can not contain God?
Questions.A: The heavens, even the highest of heavens, cannot contain God; how much less the temple which Solomon built (18)

Questions.Q: When did Solomon wish the eyes of God to be on the house of God?
Questions.A: Day and night (20)

Questions.Q: What request does Solomon repeatedly make in his prayer to God?
Questions.A: Hear (from heaven) (23-39)

Questions.Q: Who knows the hearts of men?
Questions.A: God only know the hearts (30)

Questions.Q: What would cause foreigners to come and pray toward the temple?
Questions.A: Hearing about God's power (32)

Questions.Q: Who has not sinned?
Questions.A: There is no one who does not sin (36)

Questions.Q: What happened when Solomon ended his prayer?
Questions.A: The fire came down from heaven, and consumed the burnt offering and the sacrifices; and the glory of the LORD filled the house. (1-3)

Questions.Q: How many animals were sacrificed at the dedication of the house of God?
Questions.A: 22,000 oxen and 120,000 sheep (4-5)

Questions.Q: What did God request of His people before He would hear from heaven?
Questions.A: Humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways (14)

Questions.Q: What did God promise Solomon if he would keep His commandments?
Questions.A: God would establish the throne of his kingdom, and there shall not fail a man to be ruler in Israel. (17-18)

Questions.Q: What was promised to Solomon if he disobeyed his commandments?
Questions.A: God would cast them out of His sight, and will make them and the temple to be a proverb and a byword among all nations (19-22)

Questions.Q: What did Solomon build in Jerusalem and Lebanon?
Questions.A: The store cities. all the chariot cities, and the cities of the horsemen (6)

Questions.Q: Why didn't Solomon want Pharaoh's daughter to live in the house of David?
Questions.A: Because the places the ark of the Lord had entered were holy (11)

Questions.Q: How did Solomon's servants bring back gold from Ophir?
Questions.A: In ships (17-18)

Questions.Q: How did the queen of Sheba intend to test Solomon?
Questions.A: With hard questions (1-2)

Questions.Q: What did the queen of Sheba say when she heard the wisdom of Solomon and saw his kingdom?
Questions.A: The one half of the greatness of Solomon's wisdom was not told me but exceeded the fame that she heard. (3-8)

Questions.Q: Of what material did Solomon make shields?
Questions.A: Gold (16)

Questions.Q: Of what material did Solomon make his throne?
Questions.A: Ivory overlaid with pure gold. (17)

Questions.Q: Why weren't things made of silver?
Questions.A: Solomon made silver in Jerusalem as common as stones (20, 27)

Questions.Q: How did Solomon's riches and wisdom compare to that of other kings?
Questions.A: Passed all the kings of the earth (22-23)

Questions.Q: How long did Solomon reign?
Questions.A: Forty years (30)

Questions.Q: What did Jeroboam request from Rehoboam?
Questions.A: Ease somewhat the grievous servitude and the heavy yoke that Solomon put on them (1-5)

Questions.Q: Whose advice did Rehoboam follow?
Questions.A: That of the young men (6-14)

Questions.Q: Whose prophecy was fulfilled as a result of Rehoboam's actions?
Questions.A: Ahijah (15-17)

Questions.Q: What did the Israelites do to Hadoram, who was in charge of Rehoboam's labor?
Questions.A: Stoned him with stones. (18-19)

Questions.Q: What did Shemaiah tell Rehoboam to do?
Questions.A: Not go up, nor fight against Israel but return every man to his house (1-4)

Questions.Q: Why did the priests and Levites all go to Judah and Jerusalem?
Questions.A: Jeroboam and his sons had cast them off from executing the priest's office (13-17)

Questions.Q: Who did Rehoboam appoint as chief prince?
Questions.A: His son Abijah, born of his wife Maachah, who was the daughter of Absolom (20-23)

Questions.Q: Why did the LORD allow Shishak king of Egypt to attack Jerusalem?
Questions.A: Because Judah had transgressed against the LORD. (1-4)

Questions.Q: Why wasn't Jerusalem destroyed at this time?
Questions.A: The princes of Israel and the king humbled themselves; and they said, The LORD is righteous (5-8, 12)

Questions.Q: What did Rehoboam make to replace the gold shields that Shishak had taken?
Questions.A: Shields of brass (9-11)

Questions.Q: Why did Rehoboam do evil?
Questions.A: Because he did not prepare his heart to seek the LORD (14)

Questions.Q: How many troops were involved in the battle between Abijah and Jeroboam?
Questions.A: 400,000 from Judah and 800,000 from Israel (2-3)

Questions.Q: Why did God rout Jeroboam and all Israel before Abijah and Judah?
Questions.A: Because Judah relied on the LORD God of their fathers. (13-18)

Questions.Q: How did God view Asa?
Questions.A: Asa did that which was good and right in the eyes of the LORD (2-7)

Questions.Q: What was Asa's prayer before fighting the Ethiopians?
Questions.A: LORD, it is nothing with you to help, whether with many, or with them that have no power: help us, O LORD our God; for we rest on you, and in your name we go against this multitude. O LORD, you are our God; let no man prevail against you. (11)

Questions.Q: What did Azariah prophesy?
Questions.A: To Asa he said “The LORD is with you, while you be with him; and if you seek him, he will be found of you; but if you forsake him, he will forsake you”. (1-7)

Questions.Q: How did Asa respond to this prophesy?
Questions.A: He took courage, and put away the abominable idols out of all the land and renewed the altar of the LORD (8)

Questions.Q: What was done to those who did not seek the LORD?
Questions.A: They put to death (13)

Questions.Q: Why did Asa remove Maachah from her position?
Questions.A: Because she had made an idol in a grove (16)

Questions.Q: Why did Asa give silver and gold to Benhadad king of Syria?
Questions.A: Because Baasha, king of Israel, had come against Asa and Asa wanted Benhadad to break his agreement with Baasha so he would depart (1-6)

Questions.Q: What did Hanani the seer say to Asa?
Questions.A: He told him that because he had relied on the king of Syria and not relied on God, the army of the king of Syria had escaped from his hand. He had done a foolish thing, and from then on he would be at war. (7-9)

Questions.Q: How did Asa react to Hanani's words?
Questions.A: Asa was angry with the seer, and put him in a prison house (10)

Questions.Q: How did Asa die?
Questions.A: He had a severe disease in his feet (12-13)

Questions.Q: Why was the LORD with Jehoshaphat?
Questions.A: Because he walked in the first ways of his father David. He did not consult the Baals but sought to the God of his father and walked in his commandments. (1-6)

Questions.Q: Why did Jehoshaphat send officials and Levites to all the towns of Judah?
Questions.A: To teach the law of the LORD (7-9)

Questions.Q: What did Ahab ask Jehoshaphat to do?
Questions.A: To go with him to fight against Ramoth-gilead (1-3)

Questions.Q: What did Jehoshaphat want to do first??
Questions.A: Inquire at the word of the LORD (4)

Questions.Q: What did Ahab's four hundred prophets say to do?
Questions.A: Go up to Ramoth-gilead, for the LORD would deliver it into the hand of the king (5, 9-11)

Questions.Q: Why did Ahab hate Micaiah?
Questions.A: He never prophesied good to Ahab, but always evil (6-8)

Questions.Q: What did Micaiah prophesy?
Questions.A: That Israel would be scattered and the every man should return to his home (12-24)

Questions.Q: What did Ahab do to Micaiah?
Questions.A: Put him in prison, and feed him with bread and water of affliction (25-27)

Questions.Q: How did Ahab die?
Questions.A: He was wounded by a random arrow and died that evening (28-34)

Questions.Q: Why was the wrath of God on Jehoshaphat?
Questions.A: Because he helped the ungodly, and loved them that hated the LORD (1-2)

Questions.Q: What were some good things though that Jehoshaphat did?
Questions.A: He took away the groves out of the land, and prepared his heart to seek God. He also set Levites, priests, and the chief of the fathers of Israel, for the judgment of the LORD, and for controversies and charged them to judge in the fear of the LORD with a perfect heart. (3-11)

Questions.Q: What did Jehoshaphat do when the Moabites and Ammonites came against him?
Questions.A: He set himself to seek the LORD, and proclaimed a fast throughout all Judah (1-13)

Questions.Q: What did the Spirit of the LORD empower Jahaziel to say regarding the battle?
Questions.A: Be not afraid nor dismayed by reason of this great multitude; for the battle is not yours, but God's. You shall not need to fight in this battle: set yourselves, stand still, and see the salvation of the LORD for the LORD will be with you. (14-17)

Questions.Q: With what did the Levites praise the Lord?
Questions.A: A loud voice on high (18-19)

Questions.Q: What happened when those who went before the army began to sing and to praise?
Questions.A: The LORD set ambushes against the children of Ammon, Moab, and mount Seir, which were come against Judah; and they were smitten. (20-23)

Questions.Q: How long did it take Jehoshaphat's men to carry away the spoil?
Questions.A: Three days (24-26)

Questions.Q: Why did the Lord destroy the ships that Jehoshaphat made?
Questions.A: Jehoshaphat joined himself with Ahaziah king of Israel, who did very wickedly, to make the ships (35-37)

Questions.Q: What did Jehoram do to his brothers?
Questions.A: He killed them with the sword (4)

Questions.Q: Why didn't the Lord destroy the house of David?
Questions.A: Because of the covenant that he had made with David, and as he promised to give a light to him and to his sons for ever. (5-7)

Questions.Q: Why did Libnah revolt against Jehoram?
Questions.A: Because he had forsaken the LORD (10)

Questions.Q: Who prophesied how Jehoram would die?
Questions.A: Elijah the prophet (12-20)

Questions.Q: Who encouraged Ahaziah to do wrong?
Questions.A: His mother, Athaliah the daughter of Omri, was his counselor to do wickedly (1-4)

Questions.Q: What brought about Ahaziah's downfall?
Questions.A: He went out with Jehoram, the son of Ahab, against Jehu the son of Nimshi, whom the LORD had anointed to cut off the house of Ahab (5-7)

Questions.Q: Who had Ahaziah put to death?
Questions.A: Jehu and his men (8-9)

Questions.Q: What did Athaliah, the mother of Ahaziah, proceed to do?
Questions.A: She destroyed all the entire royal family (10)

Questions.Q: How long was Joash hid in the temple of God while Athaliah ruled?
Questions.A: Six years (11-12)

Questions.Q: Who arranged to install Joash as king?
Questions.A: Jehoiada (1-11)

Questions.Q: What was Athaliah's reaction when Joash was installed as king?
Questions.A: She rent her clothes and cried Treason, Treason (12-13)

Questions.Q: Where did they put Athaliah to death?
Questions.A: At the entering of the horse gate (14-15)

Questions.Q: What did they do to the temple of Baal and the priest of Baal?
Questions.A: Broke down the temple and killed the priest of Baal (16)

Questions.Q: How long did Joash do right in the eyes of the LORD?
Questions.A: All the days of Jehoiada the priest. (1-2, 14-16)

Questions.Q: What was made and placed outside the temple to collect the money to repair the temple?
Questions.A: A chest (8-13)

Questions.Q: What did Joash and the officials of Judah do after the death of Jehoida?
Questions.A: They left the house of the LORD God of their fathers, and served groves and idols (17-18)

Questions.Q: What did Joash have done to Jehoida's son who prophesied against him?
Questions.A: Stoned him (19-22)

Questions.Q: Who invaded Judah?
Questions.A: The army of the Syrians (23-24)

Questions.Q: What did the servants of Joash do to him?
Questions.A: Killed him on his bed (25-27)

Questions.Q: What was lacking in Amaziah's actions regarding the LORD?
Questions.A: He did not have a perfect heart (1-2)

Questions.Q: Why did the man of God say the troops from Israel should not join Judah?
Questions.A: The LORD was not with Israel and if Israel went with Judah God would make them fall before the enemy (6-10)

Questions.Q: What did Amaziah do with the gods of Seir?
Questions.A: He set them up to be his gods, and bowed down himself before them, and burned incense to them (14-16)

Questions.Q: What happened when Amaziah attacked Israel?
Questions.A: Judah was beaten, Amaziah was brought to Jerusalem, and part of the wall of Jerusalem was broken down (17-24)

Questions.Q: How did Amaziah die?
Questions.A: A conspiracy was made against him in Jerusalem; and he fled to Lachish: but was killed there (25-28)

Questions.Q: When did God give Uzziah success?
Questions.A: As long as he sought the LORD, God made him to prosper (3-5)

Questions.Q: What did skillful men invent for Uzziah?
Questions.A: Devices to shoot arrows and large stones (15)

Questions.Q: What led to Uzziah's downfall?
Questions.A: When he was strong, his heart was lifted up to his destruction (16)

Questions.Q: What did the priests tell Uzziah not to do?
Questions.A: Burn incense to the LORD (17-18)

Questions.Q: With what disease did the LORD afflict Uzziah when he was angry?
Questions.A: Leprosy (19-21)

Questions.Q: Who wrote about other events in Uzziah's reign?
Questions.A: Isaiah (22-23)

Questions.Q: How did Jotham differ from his father Uzziah?
Questions.A: He did not enter into the temple of the LORD (1-2)

Questions.Q: How did Jotham become powerful?
Questions.A: Because he walked steadfastly before the Lord his God (6)

Questions.Q: Why did the LORD allow Ahaz to be defeated by the king of Syria?
Questions.A: He made idols for worshiping the Baals, burned incense/sacrifices, and burned his children in the fire. (1-5)

Questions.Q: What did the Israelites do to Judah?
Questions.A: They killed in Judah one hundred twenty thousand in one day, killed Maaseiah the king's son, carried away captive two hundred thousand, women, sons, and daughters, and took also away much spoil (5-8)

Questions.Q: Who told the army of Israel not to bring back the captives from Judah?
Questions.A: The prophet Obed inspired heads of the children of Ephraim, to stand up against them that came from the war (9-13)

Questions.Q: What did Ahaz do in his time of trouble?
Questions.A: He sacrificed to the gods of Damascus, who had defeated him, thinking, “Since the gods of the kings of Aram have helped them, I will sacrifice to them so they will help me.” (22-25)

Questions.Q: What did Hezekiah do in the first month of his reign?
Questions.A: He opened the doors of the house of the LORD, and repaired them and had the Levites carry the filthiness out of the holy place (1-5)

Questions.Q: What did Hezekiah realize was the reason Judah had fallen?
Questions.A: Their fathers trespassed, did that which was evil in the eyes of the LORD, forsook God, and turned away from the LORD. (6-10)

Questions.Q: What did the priests and Levites bring out of the temple?
Questions.A: All the uncleanness that they found (16)

Questions.Q: What did the priests and Levites bring back into the temple?
Questions.A: All the vessels, which king Ahaz cast away in his transgression. (18-19)

Questions.Q: Why did Hezekiah and all the people rejoice?
Questions.A: The service of the house of the LORD was set in order suddenly (25-36)

Questions.Q: What did Hezekiah invite all Judah and Israel to celebrate at Jerusalem?
Questions.A: To keep the Passover that the fierceness of God's wrath may turn away from them they might find compassion (1-9)

Questions.Q: What did Hezekiah pray regarding those who had not purified themselves?
Questions.A: May the Lord, who is good, pardon everyone who sets their heart on seeking God, even if they are not clean according to the rules of the sanctuary. (18-20)

Questions.Q: How long had it been since Jerusalem had such a celebration?
Questions.A: Since the time of Solomon (26)

Questions.Q: What did Hezekiah order the people to do?
Questions.A: Give the portion of the priests and the Levites, that they might be encouraged in the law of the LORD (4-8)

Questions.Q: What did Hezekiah have prepared in the temple of the LORD?
Questions.A: Chambers for the offerings, tithes and the dedicated things (9-13)

Questions.Q: Who was in charge of distributing the contributions?
Questions.A: Kore the son of Imnah the Levite (14)

Questions.Q: Why did Hezekiah block the fountains and the stream that flowed through the land?
Questions.A: So the kings of Assyria would not find water (1-4)

Questions.Q: Who was with Judah to help fight their battles?
Questions.A: The LORD (8)

Questions.Q: Who sent messengers to Judah telling them not to trust in what Hezekiah said?
Questions.A: Sennacherib king of Assyria (9-19)

Questions.Q: What did the LORD send in response to the prayer of Hezekiah and Isaiah?
Questions.A: An angel (20-22)

Questions.Q: How did Manasseh lead Judah?
Questions.A: He did what was evil in the sight of the LORD, following the detestable practices of the nations the Lord had driven out before the Israelites. (2)
He rebuilt the high places, erected altars for the Baals (false gods), worshiped all the host of heaven and built altars for them in the two courts of the house of the LORD. (3-5)
He sacrificed his children by fire, practiced divination and witchcraft, used enchantments, and consulted mediums and spiritists. (6)
He made a carved idol to put in the house of God. (7)
He led the people astray, so that they did more evil than the nations the Lord had destroyed before the Israelites. (9)

Questions.Q: What did the captains of the king of Assyria do to Manasseh?
Questions.A: They took Manasseh among the thorns, and bound him with fetters, and carried him to Babylon (10-11)

Questions.Q: What did Manasseh do in his distress?
Questions.A: He sought the LORD his God, humbled himself greatly before the God of his fathers and prayed (12-13)

Questions.Q: What did Manasseh get rid of?
Questions.A: The strange gods, and the idol out of the house of the LORD, and all the altars that he had built in the house of the LORD (14-16)

Questions.Q: How was Amon unlike his father Manasseh?
Questions.A: He did not humble himself before the LORD (21-23)

Questions.Q: How did Amon die?
Questions.A: His servants conspired against him, and killed him in his own house (24)

Questions.Q: How old was Josiah when he began to reign as king of Judah?
Questions.A: Eight years old (1)

Questions.Q: What did Josiah begin to do in the eighth year of his reign?
Questions.A: Seek after the God of David his father: (2-3)

Questions.Q: What did Josiah do in the twelfth year of his reign?
Questions.A: He began to purge Judah and Jerusalem from the high places, groves, carved images, and molten images. Also, he burnt the bones of the priests on their altars, and cleansed Judah and Jerusalem (3-7)

Questions.Q: What did Josiah do in the eighteenth year of his reign?
Questions.A: He gave money to workmen to repair the house of the LORD (8-13)

Questions.Q: What did Hilkiah the priest find in the temple?
Questions.A: A book of the law of the LORD given by Moses. (14-18)

Questions.Q: What was Josiah's reaction when he heard the words of the law?
Questions.A: He rent his clothes and inquired concerning the words of the book (19-21)

Questions.Q: What did Huldah the prophetess say?
Questions.A: God would bring judgment on Judah but not during the days of Josiah (22-28)

Questions.Q: What did Josiah cause everyone in Jerusalem and Benjamin to do?
Questions.A: He read to all the book of the law and caused all to serve the LORD (29-33)

Questions.Q: What was celebrated in the eighteenth year of Josiah's reign?
Questions.A: The Passover (1-19)

Questions.Q: What led to Josiah's death?
Questions.A: He did not listen to what Necho king of Egypt said and instead made war with him (20-27)

Questions.Q: What did the king of Egypt do to Jehoahaz?
Questions.A: Put him down from being king of Judah (1-4)

Questions.Q: Who did the king of Egypt make king over Judah?
Questions.A: Eliakim the brother of Jehoahaz, and turned his name to Jehoiakim (4-5)

Questions.Q: Who bound Jehoakim and took articles from the temple?
Questions.A: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon (6-8)

Questions.Q: What did Nebuchadnezzar do to Jehoiachin?
Questions.A: Brought him to Babylon (9-10)

Questions.Q: Whom did Nebuchadnezzar make king of Judah?
Questions.A: Zedekiah his brother (10-11)

Questions.Q: Before which prophet did Zedekiah refuse to humble himself?
Questions.A: Jeremiah (12)

Questions.Q: Against whom did Zedekiah rebel?
Questions.A: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon (13)

Questions.Q: Why did the LORD continue to send messengers to Judah?
Questions.A: Because he had compassion on his people, and on his dwelling place (15-16)

Questions.Q: What did Nebuchadnezzar do to the structures in Jerusalem?
Questions.A: Burnt the house of God, broke down the wall of Jerusalem, and burnt all the palaces (17-19)

Questions.Q: How long did those carried to Babylon remain as servants?
Questions.A: Until the reign of the kingdom of Persia (20-21)

Questions.Q: Who made a proclamation to rebuild the temple at Jerusalem?
Questions.A: Cyrus king of Persia (22-23)

Questions.Q: What message did Elijah have for Ahaziah king of Israel?
Questions.A: That he would not recover from his sickness but would die. (1-6, 16-17)

Questions.Q: What happened to the first two groups of fifty that were to get Elijah?
Questions.A: Fire came down from heaven and consumed them (7-12)

Questions.Q: How was the third group of fifty spared?
Questions.A: The third captain of fifty fell on his knees before Elijah, and sought him to spare their lives (13-15)

Questions.Q: What did the prophets at Bethel and Jericho realize?
Questions.A: That the Lord would take Elijah away that day (1-5)

Questions.Q: How did Elijah and Elisha cross over Jordan?
Questions.A: Elijah took his mantle, struck the waters, and they went over on dry ground. (6-8)

Questions.Q: What did Elisha request of Elijah?
Questions.A: A double portion of Elijah's spirit (9-10)

Questions.Q: How was Elijah taken up to heaven?
Questions.A: A chariot and horses of fire caught up Elijah in a whirlwind into heaven. (11-12)

Questions.Q: What did Elisha do with the cloak of Elijah?
Questions.A: He struck the Jordan River and crossed on dry land (13-14)

Questions.Q: How did Elisha heal the waters?
Questions.A: He cast salt in the waters (19-22)

Questions.Q: What happened to the children who mocked Elisha?
Questions.A: Two bears came out of the woods and tare forty-two children. (23-25)

Questions.Q: Why did Jehoram, king of Israel ask Jehoshaphat, king of Judah to help him?
Questions.A: He asked him to go to battle with him against the king of Moab (1-10)

Questions.Q: What did Jehoshaphat want to do?
Questions.A: Inquire of the LORD by a prophet (11)

Questions.Q: Who did Elisha request before replying to the kings?
Questions.A: A minstrel (12-15)

Questions.Q: What did the Moabites think when they saw the sun shining on the water?
Questions.A: They thought it was blood and that the kings were slain (16-23)

Questions.Q: What did the king of Moab do when he saw the battle had gone against him?
Questions.A: He tried to break through to the king of Edom: but when he could not he took his oldest son and offered him for a burnt offering (24-27)

Questions.Q: In what miraculous way did the widow woman pay her debts?
Questions.A: At Elisha's command she borrowed many vessels and the Lord filled them with oil, which she sold and used the money to pay her debts (1-7)

Questions.Q: What did the Shunammite woman and her husband make for Elisha?
Questions.A: A little guest chamber, which contained a bed, table, stool, and a candlestick (8-10)

Questions.Q: What miraculous thing happened to the Shunammite woman?
Questions.A: She had a child when her husband was old (11-17)

Questions.Q: What did the Shunammite woman say that showed her faith?
Questions.A: When her child died and Elisha asked about her child she replied “It is well.” (18-26)

Questions.Q: What did Elisha tell Gehazi to do?
Questions.A: Lay Elisha's staff on the child (27-31)

Questions.Q: What miracle happened for the son of the Shunammite woman?
Questions.A: He raised back to life (32-37)

Questions.Q: What happened to the pot of stew?
Questions.A: Some shredded gourds were put in it and it became poisonous, but Elisha put some meal in the pot and it was okay. (38-41)

Questions.Q: How were the hundred men fed?
Questions.A: A man brought twenty loaves of barley bread and some heads of new grain and God multiplied it so there was enough to feed them all (42-44)

Questions.Q: Who suggested that Naaman see Elisha?
Questions.A: A little maid taken captive out of Israel who was servant to Naaman's wife (1-3)

Questions.Q: What did Elisha tell Naaman to do?
Questions.A: Go and wash in Jordan seven times (8-10)

Questions.Q: Who convinced Naaman that he should obey Elisha?
Questions.A: His servants (11-13)

Questions.Q: What did Elisha do when Naaman wanted to give him a gift?
Questions.A: He refused to accept it (14-16)

Questions.Q: What did Gehazi do?
Questions.A: He lied to Naaman saying that Elisha requested a talent of silver, and two changes of garments. (20-24)

Questions.Q: What happened to Gehazi?
Questions.A: He became a leper (25-27)

Questions.Q: What happened to the axe head?
Questions.A: It accidentally fell into the water, but Elisha cast in a stick and the iron did swim (1-7)

Questions.Q: Why did the king of Syria want to capture Elisha?
Questions.A: Because Elisha told the king of Israel the words that the king of Syria spoke (8-14)

Questions.Q: What did Elisha say when his servant was afraid?
Questions.A: Fear not: for they that be with us are more than they that be with them (15-17)

Questions.Q: What happened to the men who were sent to capture Elisha?
Questions.A: They were smitten with blindness (18-23)

Questions.Q: How did Israel suffer when Benhadad besieged Samaria?
Questions.A: There was a great famine in Samaria (25)

Questions.Q: What did Elisha prophesy would happen at Samaria?
Questions.A: A measure of fine flour would be sold for a shekel, and two measures of barley for a shekel (1-2)

Questions.Q: What did the four men with leprosy decide to do?
Questions.A: Go to the camp of the Syrians (3-5)

Questions.Q: Why did the Syrians flee?
Questions.A: They heard a noise of chariots, horses, and a great host and they thought the king of Israel has hired against them the kings of the Hittites and Egyptians, to fight them (6-8)

Questions.Q: Why did the men with leprosy decide to tell the news to the city gatekeepers?
Questions.A: They realized they were not doing well by not telling the king's household (9-11)

Questions.Q: Why was the king of Samaria skeptical?
Questions.A: He thought it was a plan of the Syrians to draw them out of the city in order to capture them and get into Samaria (12-15)

Questions.Q: What happened to the man who did not believe Elisha's prophecy?
Questions.A: He was trampled to death (16-20)

Questions.Q: How does the story of the woman wanting her land back show God's perfect timing?
Questions.A: Just as Gehazi was telling the story of the restoration to life of the lady's boy, the woman arrived wanting the king to restore her land. (1-6)

Questions.Q: How did Hazael become king of Syria?
Questions.A: He spread a thick cloth soaked with water over the face of Benhadad until he died and Hazael then reigned as king (15)

Questions.Q: Who did Jehoram king of Judah marry?
Questions.A: The daughter of Ahab (16-23)

Questions.Q: Who followed Jehoram as king of Judah?
Questions.A: Ahaziah the son of Jehoram (24-29)

Questions.Q: Who was anointed king of Israel to destroy the house of Ahab?
Questions.A: Jehu (1-9)

Questions.Q: What was prophesied would happen to Jezebel?
Questions.A: The dogs would eat Jezebel in the portion of Jezreel, and there none would bury her (10)

Questions.Q: How did Jehu drive his chariot?
Questions.A: Furiously (20)

Questions.Q: What did Jehu do to Jehoram?
Questions.A: Jehu drew a bow with his full strength, and struck Jehoram between his arms, and the arrow went out at his heart (24-26)

Questions.Q: What did Jezebel do when Jehu entered Jezreel?
Questions.A: She painted her face, and tired her head, and looked out at a window. (30)

Questions.Q: What happened to Jezebel?
Questions.A: Some eunuchs threw her out the window and she was trampled. When they were to bury her all they found was the skull, the feet, and the palms of her hands (31-37)

Questions.Q: What happened to Ahab's seventy sons?
Questions.A: They were beheaded and their heads were brought to Jehu in baskets (1-8)

Questions.Q: How did Jehu destroy the worshipers of Baal?
Questions.A: He gathered them to the house of Baal and had them killed with the sword (18-28)
Questions.Alternative: How did Jehu destroy the worshippers of Baal?

Questions.Q: From what didn't Jehu depart?
Questions.A: The sins of Jeroboam, in particular the golden calves that were in Bethel, and Dan. (29)

Questions.Q: What did Athaliah do?
Questions.A: Upon seeing the death of her son she destroyed the whole royal family (except one). (1)

Questions.Q: Whom did Jehosheba hide?
Questions.A: Joash the son of Ahaziah (2-3)

Questions.Q: What did Jehoiada do regarding Joash?
Questions.A: Made him king (4-12)

Questions.Q: What did Jehoiada have done to Athaliah?
Questions.A: Had her killed (13-16)

Questions.Q: How old was Jehoash when he began to reign?
Questions.A: Seven (17-21)

Questions.Q: When did Jehoash do right in the sight of the Lord?
Questions.A: During the time in which Jehoiada the priest instructed him (1-2)

Questions.Q: Was Jehoash complete in his obedience to the Lord?
Questions.A: No
Questions.Alternative: Did Jehoash obey the Lord completely?
Did Jehoash follow the Lord in everything?
Was Jehoash completely obedient to God?

Questions.Q: What things did Jehoash fail to do?
Questions.A: The high places [where people worshiped idols] were not removed.
The people were allowed to continue to offer sacrifices and burn incense to false gods.

Questions.Q: What was done with the money that was put in the chest of Jehoiada?
Questions.A: They gave the money to them that repaired the house of the LORD (4-16)

Questions.Q: What did Jehoash do with [all the] things/offerings that had been dedicated [to the Lord] by previous kings of Judah/his predecessors Jehoshaphat, Jehoram, and Ahaziah?
Questions.A: He sent it to Hazael king of Syria (17-18)

Questions.Q: How did Jehoash die?
Questions.A: His servants arose, and made a conspiracy, and killed him in the house of Millo (20)

Questions.Q: Into whose hands was Israel delivered during the reign of Jehoahaz son of Jehu?
Questions.A: Hazael king of Syria, and Benhadad the son of Hazael, all their days (1-9)

Questions.Q: What did Elisha tell Joash, king of Israel, to do?
Questions.A: Take arrows and strike the ground (14-18)

Questions.Q: Why was Elisha angry?
Questions.A: Because the king only struck the ground three times after being told of the arrow of deliverance from Syria (19)

Questions.Q: What happened when a corpse/dead man was thrown/cast into the tomb/sepulcher/grave of Elisha?
Questions.A: He revived, and stood up on his feet (20-21)
