Questions.Q: How many times did Jehoash beat Benhadad king of Syria?
Questions.A: Three times (22-25)

Questions.Q: What did Amaziah do to the men who had killed his father Joash, king of Judah?
Questions.A: He killed them (1-6)

Questions.Q: What did Jehoash, king of Israel, do to Amaziah, king of Judah?
Questions.A: Jehoash king of Israel took Amaziah king of Judah captive (8-16)

Questions.Q: How did the reign of Amaziah end?
Questions.A: When he fled to Lachish; some from Jerusalem who made a conspiracy against him went to Lachish, and killed him there (17-20)

Questions.Q: What did Jeroboam restore/reconquer/recover for Israel?
Questions.A: He restored the coast of Israel from the entering of Hamath to the sea of the plain, according to Jonah, the prophet (23-29)
Questions.Alternative: What did Jeroboam restore for Israel?
What did Jeroboam reconquer for Israel?
What did Jeroboam recover for Israel?

Questions.Q: How long did Azariah reign as king of Judah?
Questions.A: 52 years (1-7)

Questions.Q: Who struck Zechariah and became king of Israel?
Questions.A: Shallum the son of Jabesh (8-13)

Questions.Q: Who struck Shallum and became king of Israel?
Questions.A: Menahem (14-18)

Questions.Q: What did Pul, king of Assyria, take from Israel?
Questions.A: A thousand talents of silver (19-20)

Questions.Q: How did the kingdom of Pekahiah end?
Questions.A: Pekah the son of Remaliah, a captain of his, conspired against him, and struck him in Samaria, in the palace of the king's house (21-26)

Questions.Q: What happened to Pekah, king of Israel?
Questions.A: Hoshea the son of Elah made a conspiracy against Pekah the son of Remaliah, and struck him, and killed him, and reigned in his stead (27-31)

Questions.Q: What can be said of the reign of Jotham, king of Judah?
Questions.A: He did that which was right in the sight of the LORD: however, the high places were not removed: the people sacrificed and burned incense (32-35)

Questions.Q: How did Ahaz, king of Judah, live?
Questions.A: Ahaz did not that which was right in the sight of the LORD but he made his son to pass through the fire, and he sacrificed and burnt incense in the high places, and on the hills, and under every green tree. (1-4)

Questions.Q: Who came to war against Ahaz?
Questions.A: Rezin king of Syria and Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel (5-6)

Questions.Q: Who did Ahaz hire to help deliver him?
Questions.A: Tiglathpileser king of Assyria (7-9)

Questions.Q: What did Ahaz have Uriah the priest do?
Questions.A: Build an altar like the one that was at Damascus (10-16)

Questions.Q: What did the king of Assyria do to Israel during the reign of Hoshea?
Questions.A: He took Samaria, and carried Israel away into Assyria (1-6)

Questions.Q: How did Israel respond to the words of the prophets sent to them?
Questions.A: They would not hear, but hardened their necks, and they rejected God's statutes, followed vanity, made molten images, worshiped all the host of heaven, and served Baal. (13-17)

Questions.Q: Who did the king of Assyria place in the cities of Samaria?
Questions.A: Men from Babylon, Cuthah, Ava, Hamath, and Sepharvaim (24)

Questions.Q: How did Hezekiah, king of Judah live?
Questions.A: He did that which was right in the sight of the LORD. He removed the high places, broke the images, cut down the groves, and broke in pieces the brazen serpent that Moses had made. He trusted in the LORD (1-6)

Questions.Q: What did Hezekiah give to the king of Assyria?
Questions.A: All the silver that was found in the house of the LORD, and the gold from the doors of the temple (13-16)

Questions.Q: Who did the king of Assyria send against Jerusalem?
Questions.A: Tartan, Rabsaris and Rabshakeh along with a great host (17)

Questions.Q: Who did Rabshakeh say Judah should not trust?
Questions.A: Neither Egypt nor the LORD (19-22, 29-31)

Questions.Q: What logic did Rabshakeh use to try to show that the LORD was not able to deliver Judah?
Questions.A: The gods of Hamath, Arpad, Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivah could not deliver them so how could the God of Hezekiah deliver Jerusalem? (33-35)

Questions.Q: What did Hezekiah do when he heard the words of Rabshakeh?
Questions.A: He went into the house of the LORD (1)

Questions.Q: To whom did Hezekiah send his servants?
Questions.A: Isaiah the prophet (2-5)

Questions.Q: What did Isaiah prophesy?
Questions.A: God would send a blast on the king of Assyria, he shall hear a rumor, and shall return to his own land; and God would cause him to fall by the sword in his own land. (6-7)

Questions.Q: What did Hezekiah do with the letter he received from the messengers of Rabshakeh?
Questions.A: He read it, went up into the house of the LORD, and spread it before the LORD. (9-14)

Questions.Q: What did Hezekiah want all the kingdoms of the earth to know?
Questions.A: That the God of Israel is the only LORD God (15-19)

Questions.Q: What did Isaiah say regarding the prayer of Hezekiah?
Questions.A: God heard his prayer (20)

Questions.Q: How would the Lord turn Assyria back?
Questions.A: By the way by which they came (28)

Questions.Q: How many Assyrians did the angel of the Lord kill?
How did Sennacherib, king of Assyria, die?
Questions.A: His sons struck him with the sword (36-37)

Questions.Q: What did Isaiah tell Hezekiah when Hezekiah was sick unto death?
Questions.A: Set your house in order; for you shall die (1)

Questions.Q: What did the Lord grant to Hezekiah after he prayed?
Questions.A: A fifteen year extension to his life (2-6)

Questions.Q: How was Hezekiah healed?
Questions.A: A lump of figs was laid it on his boil (7)

Questions.Q: What happened to the shadow?
Questions.A: The shadow of the sun dial of Ahaz went ten degrees backward (8-11)

Questions.Q: What did Hezekiah show the Babylonians?
Questions.A: All the house of his precious things, the silver, gold, spices, the precious ointment, his armory, and all that was found in his storehouses. (12-15)

Questions.Q: What did Isaiah prophesy the Babylonians would do?
Questions.A: All that was in his house would be carried into Babylon and the king of Babylon would make eunuchs of his sons (16-19)

Questions.Q: What engineering feat did Hezekiah accomplish?
Questions.A: A pool, and a conduit, which brought water into the city (20)

Questions.Q: What did Manasseh build again which his father Hezekiah had destroyed?
Questions.A: The high places and altars for Baal (1-9)

Questions.Q: What did the prophets say would happen to Judah?
Questions.A: Such evil that whoever hears of it, both his ears shall tingle. Also they would be delivered into the hand of their enemies (10-15)

Questions.Q: How did the reign of Amon son of Manasseh come to an end?
Questions.A: His servants conspired against him, and killed him in his own house (18-23)

Questions.Q: How old was Josiah when he began to reign?
Questions.A: Eight years old (1)

Questions.Q: What did Josiah repair?
Questions.A: The house of the LORD (3-7)

Questions.Q: What was found in the house of the Lord?
Questions.A: The book of the law (8)

Questions.Q: What was Josiah's response to the word of the Lord/(words of the) book of the law?
Questions.A: He rent his clothes and commanded Hilkiah the priest, and others to inquire of the LORD (10-13)
Questions.Alternative: What was Josiah's response to the word of the Lord?
What was Josiah's response to the words of the book of the law?
What was Josiah's response to the book of the law?

Questions.Q: What did Huldah the prophetess say concerning Josiah?
Questions.A: Whereas judgment would come on Judah, because Josiah humbled himself he would die in peace and not see the judgment. (14-20)

Questions.Q: What did Josiah read to the people?
Questions.A: All the words of the book of the covenant which was found in the house of the LORD (1-3)

Questions.Q: What are some things that Josiah removed from in or near the temple?
Questions.A: All the vessels that were made for Baal, idolatrous priests, the grove from the house of the LORD, the houses of the sodomites, the high places, the horses and chariots of the sun, the altars, the high places, and the images (4-14)

Questions.Q: What did Josiah do at Bethel?
Questions.A: He broke down the altar and the high place that Jeroboam had built and burned the bones from the sepulcher as had been prophesied by a man of God many years before (15-18)

Questions.Q: How did the Passover that Josiah kept compare to those of other kings?
Questions.A: There was not held such a passover from the days of the judges, nor in all the days of the kings (21-25)

Questions.Q: How did Josiah die?
Questions.A: Josiah went against Pharaohnechoh, king of Egypt and was killed by him at Megiddo (29-30)

Questions.Q: Who ended the [three-month] reign of Jehoahaz king of Judah?
Questions.A: Pharaohnechoh put him in bands at Riblah in the land of Hamath, that he might not reign in Jerusalem (31-35)
Questions.Alternative: Who ended the three-month reign of Jehoahaz king of Judah?
Who ended the reign of Jehoahaz king of Judah?

Questions.Q: What did Pharaoh rename Eliakim?
Questions.A: Jehoiakim (34)

Questions.Q: Who invaded Judah during the reign of Jehoiakim?
Questions.A: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon (1-7)

Questions.Q: What did Nebuchadnezzar remove from the temple?
Questions.A: All the treasures of the house of the LORD, and the treasures of the king's house (8-13)

Questions.Q: Whom did Nebuchadnezzar carry into exile?
Questions.A: The princes, the mighty men of valor, the craftsmen and smiths, and Jehoiachin, king of Judah, to Babylon (14-16)

Questions.Q: Whom did Nebuchadnezzar make king of Judah?
Questions.A: Mattaniah, Jehoiachin's uncle, and changed his name to Zedekiah. (17-20)

Questions.Q: What happened to Zedekiah?
Questions.A: The king of Babylon killed the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes, and blinded the eyes of Zedekiah (1-7)

Questions.Q: What did the Babylonians do to the temple?
Questions.A: Burned the house of the LORD, and the king's house (8-9)

Questions.Q: What did the Babylonians do to the walls of Jerusalem?
Questions.A: Broke them down (10)

Questions.Q: What else was carried into Babylon?
Questions.A: The pillars of brass, the bases, and the bronze sea that were in the house of the LORD, and the pots, shovels, snuffers, spoons, and all the vessels of brass with which they ministered. Also, the fire pans, bowls, and things made of gold and of silver (13-17)
Questions.Alternative: What else was taken away into Babylon?

Questions.Q: Who was released from prison and allowed to eat at the king of Babylon's table?
Questions.A: Jehoiachin king of Judah (27-30)

Questions.Q: What was Amos' occupation?
Questions.A: A herdsman (1)
Questions.Note: He was also a gatherer of sycamore fruit (See Amos 7:14)

Questions.Q: When did Amos prophesy?
Questions.A: In the days of Uzziah king of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash king of Israel, two years before the earthquake. (1)

Questions.Q: Upon what places did Amos prophesy punishment?
Questions.A: Damascus, Gaza, Tyre, Edom and Ammon (3-13)

Questions.Q: Upon what additional places did Amos prophesy punishment?
Questions.A: Moab, Judah, and Israel (1-6)

Questions.Q: What did Israel command its prophets?
Questions.A: To not prophesy (12)

Questions.Q: Who will not be able to deliver himself?
Questions.A: The mighty, he that handles the bow, he that is swift of foot, or he that rides the horse (14-15)

Questions.Q: To whom does GOD reveal his secrets?
Questions.A: His servants the prophets (7)

Questions.Q: How will the LORD punish the transgressions of Israel?
Questions.A: The horns of the altar shall be cut off, the winter house with the summer house; and the houses of ivory shall perish, and the great houses shall have an end (14-15)

Questions.Q: What punishments did the LORD send on Israel?
Questions.A: Lack of food in all their cities (6)
Lack of rain (7-8)
blight, mildew and locusts to destroy their crops (9)
Plagues [like those sent on Egypt] (10)
Destruction [like that of Sodom and Gomorrah] (11)
Questions.Alternative: What five things did the LORD give or send and yet Israel would not return to the LORD?

Questions.Q: How was Israel to prepare?
Questions.A: To meet God (12)

Questions.Q: Who formed the mountains and created the wind?
Questions.A: The LORD, The God of hosts (13)

Questions.Q: Who should Israel seek?
Questions.A: The LORD (4-6)

Questions.Q: The Lord mentions his power over nature to show that he also has power to punish and destroy the wicked. What examples does he give to show this?
Questions.A: He made the Pleiades and Orion (constellations\stars). (8)
He made day and night (changes deep darkness into morning and darkens day into night). (8)
He controls the rain or causes floods (calls for the waters of the sea and pours them out on the surface of the earth). (8)

Questions.Q: Why would God not allow the Israelites to live in their stone houses or drink the wine from their vineyards?
Questions.A: They hated people/prophets who reproved/judged them and who spoke with integrity. (10)
They abused the poor (by imposing heavy rent and exacting a tribute). (11)
They perverted justice (12)

Questions.Q: What did the LORD know?
Questions.A: Their manifold transgressions and mighty sins (12)

Questions.Q: What should Israel hate?
Questions.A: Evil (15)

Questions.Q: What will the day of the LORD be?
Questions.A: Darkness, and not light (18, 20)

Questions.Q: Into what would the Lord cause Israel to go?
Questions.A: Captivity beyond Damascus (27)

Questions.Q: To whom was woe prophesied?
Questions.A: Those who are at ease in Zion, and trust in the mountain of Samaria (1)

Questions.Q: What indicated their prosperity and pleasure?
Questions.A: They lie on beds of ivory and drink wine in bowls (4-6)

Questions.Q: What was the Lord going to raise up?
Questions.A: A nation that would afflict Israel (14)

Questions.Q: What did the Lord set in the middle of Israel?
Questions.A: A plumb line (7-8)

Questions.Q: Who told Amos not to prophesy again at Bethel?
Questions.A: Amaziah the priest of Bethel (10-13)

Questions.Q: What occupation did Amos have before the Lord called him to prophesy?
Questions.A: Herdsman, and a gatherer of sycamore fruit (14-15)
Questions.Note: See also Amos 1:1

Questions.Q: What did Amos prophesy would happen to Israel?
Questions.A: Go into captivity (17)

Questions.Q: What did the Lord show Amos?
Questions.A: A basket of summer fruit (1-2)

Questions.Q: What kind of famine would Israel experience?
Questions.A: A famine in the land, not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but of hearing the words of the LORD (11-12)

Questions.Q: Where will people try to escape?
Questions.A: In the top of Carmel and in the bottom of the sea (2-3)

Questions.Q: How was the LORD going to sift Israel?
Questions.A: Like as corn is sifted in a sieve (9)

Questions.Q: What promise was given to Israel?
Questions.A: God would plant them on their land, and they shall no more be pulled up out of their land (14-15)

Questions.Q: What are some questions that Habakkuk asked?
Questions.A: O LORD, how long shall I cry, and you will not hear? Why do you show me iniquity, and cause me to behold grievance? (1-3)

Questions.Q: What is happening to justice?
Questions.A: The law is paralyzed, so that justice is never upheld.
False/perverted justice is going forth.

Questions.Q: Who was raised up to march through the land and possess places that were not theirs?
Questions.A: The Chaldeans (6)

Questions.Q: What kind of people are the Chaldeans?
Questions.A: The Chaldeans are terrifying and fearsome.

Questions.Q: For what did the LORD ordain and establish them?
Questions.A: For judgment and for correction (12)

Questions.Q: How shall the just live?
Questions.A: By his faith (4)

Questions.Q: What inanimate objects will communicate?
Questions.A: The stone and the beam (11)

Questions.Q: Before whom shall the earth keep silence?
Questions.A: The LORD (20)

Questions.Q: For what did Habakkuk pray?
Questions.A: For God to revive His work and in wrath to remember mercy (2)

Questions.Q: What did the LORD thresh in his anger?
Questions.A: The heathen (12)

Questions.Q: In spite of fruit, crop and animal failures what was Habakkuk going to do?
Questions.A: Rejoice in the LORD and joy in the God of his salvation (17-18)

Questions.Q: What kinds of problems were the people of Judah experiencing?
Questions.A: Drought. (6, 10-11)
Poverty or scarcity (6, 9-11)

Questions.Q: Who was causing this?
Why?
Questions.A: The people were building and enjoying their own luxurious houses but ignoring God’s house, which was lying in ruins. (2-11)
Questions.Alternative: Why was God punishing the people?
Why was God punishing the people of Judah?
Why was God causing drought?
Why was causing the people to experience drought and poverty?

Questions.Q: How did the people respond to God’s command?
Questions.A: The leaders and all the people obeyed and began working on God’s house. (12-14)
Questions.Alternative: How did the people respond to God’s exhortation?
How did the people respond to God’s challenge?
What did the people do when God spoke to them about this?

Questions.Q: When did the word of Yahweh come by the hand of Haggai the prophet?
Questions.A: The word came in the second year of Darius the king, in the sixth month, on the first day of the month.
Questions.Alternative: When did the word of the LORD come by the hand of Haggai the prophet?
When did the word of the LORD come through Haggai the prophet?
When did the LORD speak to Haggai the prophet?
When did the LORD first speak to Haggai the prophet?
When did the LORD first speak through Haggai the prophet?
When did God first speak through Haggai the prophet?
When did Haggai the prophet hear God speak the first time?
When did Haggai receive this prophetic word from God?
Questions.Note: Use either this question (A) or the following question (B). It would be redundant to ask both questions.
question A (Hag 1:1)
The sixth month of the Hebrew lunar calendar.

Questions.Q: During the reign of which king did Haggai prophesy?
Questions.A: Darius (1)
Questions.Note: Use either this question (B) or the preceding question (A). It would be redundant to ask both questions.
question B (Hag 1:1)

Questions.Q: To whom did Haggai prophesy?
Questions.A: Zerubbabel, governor of Judah, and Joshua, the high priest. (1)
Questions.Alternative: To whom did the word of Yahweh come?
To whom did the word of the LORD come?

Questions.Q: What did the people say?
Questions.A: They said it was not time for them to build the LORD’s house.
Questions.Alternative: What did Yahweh claim the people said?
What did the LORD claim the people said?

Questions.Q: What question did the LORD ask through Haggai?
Questions.A: Is it time for you to live in your paneled houses, while the LORD’s house lies in ruins?

Questions.Q: What was the condition of Yahweh’s house while the people lived in their finished houses?
Questions.A: Yahweh’s house laid ruined.
OR It was in ruins.
OR It had not been rebuilt.
Questions.Alternative: What was the condition of the LORD’s house while the people lived in their finished houses?
What was the condition of the LORD’s house while the people lived in their paneled houses?
What was the condition of the LORD’s house while the people lived in luxurious houses?
What was the condition of the LORD’s house?

Questions.Q: What did the Lord ask them to consider?
Questions.A: Their ways (5-7)
He asked the people to think about what was happening to them and ponder how their disregard for his house was causing them to experience want.
Questions.Alternative: What did the Lord ask them to think about?

Questions.Q: Why was there drought in the land?
Questions.A: Because God’s house lay in ruins, while the people were busy taking care of their own houses. (9-11)
Questions.Alternative: Although the people sowed much seed and looked for much, why did Yahweh blow it away and bring drought upon all the labor of their hands?
Although the people planted and expected a good harvest, why did the LORD bring drought upon the land and cause their labor to produce so little?

Questions.Q: How did Zerubbabel and Joshua the high priest respond to the words of Haggai?
Questions.A: They obeyed (12)
Questions.Alternative: How did Zerubbabel the governor, Joshua the priest, and all the remnant of the people respond to Yahweh’s voice and the words of Haggai the prophet, whom Yahweh had sent?
How did Zerubbabel the governor, Joshua the priest, and all the remnant of the people respond to the LORD’s voice and the words of Haggai the prophet, whom the LORD had sent?
How did Zerubbabel, Joshua, and all the remnant of the people respond to the LORD?
How did the people respond to the LORD?
How did the people respond?
How did the leaders and the people respond?
How did the governor, the priest, and the people respond to the LORD’s voice and the words of the prophet?

Questions.Q: How did Yahweh respond to the people’s obedience?
Questions.A: He sent a message through Haggai his messenger to tell them, “I am with you!”
Questions.Alternative: How did the LORD respond to the people’s obedience?
What did the LORD do when he saw the people’s obedience?
What did the LORD do when he saw the people begin to obey him?
What did the LORD do when he saw that the people were obeying him?

Questions.Q: When did Yahweh stir up Zerubbabel the governor, Joshua the priest, and all the remnant of the people’s spirits to go and work on the house of Yahweh of hosts, their God?
Questions.A: He stirred them up in the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month, in the second year of Darius the king.
OR on September 21 of the second year of King Darius’s reign
OR 23 days after he first spoke to them through Haggai
Questions.Alternative: When did the LORD stir up Zerubbabel the governor, Joshua the priest, and all the remnant of the people’s spirits to go and work on the house of the LORD, their God?
When did the LORD stir up Zerubbabel the governor, Joshua the priest, and all the remnant of the people’s spirits to go and work on the house of God?
When did the LORD stir up Zerubbabel, Joshua, and all the remnant of the people to work on the house of God?
When did the LORD stir up the leaders and the people to work on the house of God?
When did the LORD move the people to work on the house of God?
Questions.Note: The sixth month of the Hebrew lunar calendar.

Section.heading: Hag 2:1-9 The Promised Glory of the Temple

Questions.Q: How did the Temple the people were working to restore compare with the original Temple?
Questions.A: It was inferior. (3)
OR It seemed like nothing in comparison to the original. (3)
OR It did not have the same glory or splendor as the original. (3)
Questions.Alternative: How did the house the people were working to restore compare with the original house?
How did the former house compare with the original one?
How did the former Temple compare with the original one?
How did the former house of the LORD compare with the original one?

Questions.A: He told them to be strong and work because he was with them. (4-5)
He told them not to fear (because his Spirit was with them and he was going to restore the glory of the Temple). (5-9)
He said he would cause the treasures (silver and gold) of the nations to be brought in. (6-8)
He said he would make the glory/splendor of the Temple/his house even greater than it was before. (7-9)
He promised peace. (9)

In spite of that, how did Yahweh encourage the people?

In spite of that, how did God encourage the people to be strong and work?

Questions.Q: When did the word of Yahweh come by the hand of Haggai the prophet?
Questions.A: The word came in the seventh month on the twenty-first day of the month.
OR on October 17 of that same year [the second year of King Darius].
OR about one month later.
OR a little less than one month later.

Questions.A: Yahweh/God declared that they should be strong and work because because he was with them. (4)

Section.heading: Hag 2:20-23 Zerubbabel Chosen as a Signet

Questions.Q: What is God promising to do?
Questions.A: Shake the heavens and the earth. (21)
Overthrow royal thrones and destroy the [military] power of foreign kingdoms. (22)
Honor his servant, [governor] Zerubbabel, and establish his authority. (23)
Questions.Note: There is figurative and apocalyptic language used in this passage. Commentators are nearly unanimous in asserting that Zerubbabel is a representative of the house of David, through whom Christ comes and that the prophecies here primarily apply to the eternal kingdom of Jesus. No universal overthrow of human kingdoms occurred during the time of Zerubbabel, nor the kinds of natural disasters that might be associated with the idea of shaking the heavens and the earth. Other places in Scripture where such prophecies are repeated suggest a future and final fulfillment in the last days. Unless this passage includes supplemental and explicit explanations, most respondents will probably not be able to fully grasp the significance of God’s promise here. Watch carefully for responses that suggest a definite misunderstanding that would not leave room for a clear interpretation when seen in the light of other relevant passages of Scripture.

Questions.Q: What do these verses show about the power of God?
Questions.A: He has the power and authority over everything, people (including kings, political leaders, and soldiers) as well as the entire natural world. He controls the entire course of history.

Questions.Q: What do you think it means to make someone like a signet ring?
Questions.A: Key Term Check: A king or other powerful person would use a signet ring to mark an official document or decree as authentic. It therefore represented his power and authority and was treated as a valuable possession, typically inseparable from its owner. If a person is said to be like a signet ring, it probably means that they are very special and that they derive their power and authority from the one on whose finger they sit.

Questions.Q: Why do you think the king wanted the animals to wear mourning clothes?
Questions.Note: This was (at least) to show [God] the extent of their sorrow for their sins [so he would relent and not punish them]. It is also possible that because the people had used their animals in sinful ways (e.g., as sacrifices to idols, or for transporting people or objects used in their pagan worship), they reasoned that the animals also needed to included in the mourning process.

Although some commentators have suggested that the word "animals" might refer to people who are like ignorant animals (in their disregard for God), the explicit wording in v. 7 indicating the animals included in the ban strongly suggests otherwise.
It is interesting to note that in God's final words to Jonah at the end of the book, he mentions the animals in his explanation to Jonah for why he is showing compassion on Nineveh.
