Questions.Q: Why did Jonah say he was right to be angry?
Questions.A: He didn't really give a reason. He just asserted that he was indeed justified in his anger.

Questions.Q: Who had tended and made the plant grow?
Questions.A: God

Questions.Q: How long had the plant grown and died?
Questions.A: It grew up one night and died early the next morning.
Questions.Note: If the translation in the target language follows the Hebrew closely, God literally says it died "in a night". The point is that the plant died quickly (in perhaps 24-36 hours). Watch for confusion that might cause the respondent to miss that point.

Questions.Q: What question did God ask Jonah?
Questions.A: [You/Jonah cared so much about this plant.] Should not I/God pity Nineveh, that great city, in which there are more than 120,000 persons who do not know their right hand from their left, and also much cattle? (10-11)
Questions.Alternative: What did God say to Jonah?

Questions.Q: Why did God say he should be concerned about Nineveh?
Questions.A: It was a large city with a lot of people [and animals].
The people of Nineveh were living in spiritual darkness. Unlike the people of Israel, they did not have much information about who God was or how he wanted them to live.
Questions.Note: God was not asserting that the people of Nineveh were innocent. But he was drawing a connection between their ignorance and their sinfulness.
Questions.Alternative: What reasons did God give Jonah for his decision to show mercy to Nineveh?
Why did God say he should show compassion toward Nineveh?
Why did God say he should have mercy on Nineveh?

Questions.Q: What do you think the lesson of this story is?
Questions.A: It is impossible to run away from God to a place where he cannot see you. (1:3-17)
God is merciful and compassionate. (1:17-2:10, 3:10, 4:2, 11)
We should care about other people [and their spiritual condition] more than we care about our own comfort. (4:8-11)
We should be happy when God shows mercy to people [even if they are our enemies].
Questions.Alternative: What do you think we are supposed to learn from this story?
What lessons can we learn from this story?
What can we learn from this story?
What should we learn from this story?

Questions.Q: Who did the LORD love and who did he hate?
Questions.A: He loved Jacob and hated Esau (2-3)

Questions.Q: Where will the name of the LORD be great?
Questions.A: Among the Gentiles from the rising of the sun even to the going down of the same (11)

Questions.Q: What should the lips of priests do?
Questions.A: Keep knowledge (7)

Questions.Q: What questions did Malachi ask?
Questions.A: Have we not all one father? has not one God created us? why do we deal treacherously every man against his brother, by profaning the covenant of our fathers? (10)

Questions.Q: How did someone deal with the wife of his youth?
Questions.A: Treacherously (14)

Questions.Q: How did they weary the LORD with their words?
Questions.A: When they said, Every one that does evil is good in the sight of the LORD, and he delights in them; or, Where is the God of judgment? (17)

Questions.Q: Of what messenger was Malachi prophesying?
Questions.A: The fore-runner for the Messiah, John the Baptist (1)
Questions.Note: Non-Christians or those unfamiliar with the Gospels will probably not know that this refers to John the Baptist (see Matthew 11:10), but responses should indicate that this messenger is not God/Messiah himself.

Questions.Q: How had they robbed God?
Questions.A: In tithes and offerings (8)

Questions.Q: What blessings would those who brought their tithes receive?
Questions.A: God would rebuke the devourer so he could not destroy the fruits of their ground (10)
nor would their grapes fall from the vine before they were ripe (11)
Their land would be so blessed that other nations would notice it (12)

Questions.Q: For whom would a book of remembrance be written?
Questions.A: Those who feared the LORD and honored his name (16)

Questions.Q: What will happen to the proud and wicked?
Questions.A: Be burned up (1)

Questions.Q: Who will arise for those that fear the name of the LORD?
Questions.A: The Sun of righteousness (2)

Questions.Q: Who will turn the hearts of the fathers to the children?
Questions.A: Elijah the prophet (5-6)
Questions.Note: Respondents familiar with the Gospel may also say John the Baptist (see Luke 1:17)

Questions.Q: During the reign of what kings did Micah prophesy?
Questions.A: Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah (1)

Questions.Q: As what was the Lord going to make Samaria?
Questions.A: a heap of the field, and as plantings of a vineyard (6)

Questions.Q: What was said about her wound?
Questions.A: Incurable (9)

Questions.Q: Against whom is woe pronounced?
Questions.A: Those who devise iniquity and work evil on their beds (1-2)
Questions.Alternative: To whom is woe pronounced?
Against whom is judgment pronounced?
Against whom are these words of judgment being spoken?
To who is woe pronounced?

Questions.Q: To whom does God's word do good?
Questions.A: Him that walks uprightly (7)

Questions.Q: What did the LORD say concerning the prophets that made His people to err?
Questions.A: They would not have a vision, they would be ashamed and not have an answer from God (5-7)

Questions.Q: What did Micah declare?
Questions.A: To Jacob his transgression, and to Israel his sin (8)

Questions.Q: Why did the heads judge, the priests teach and the prophets divine?
Questions.A: For reward, hire, and money (11)

Questions.Q: What was going to happen to Zion and Jerusalem?
Questions.A: Plowed as a field, and Jerusalem shall become heaps (12)

Questions.Q: What will be established in the last days?
Questions.A: The mountain of the house of the LORD (1)

Questions.Q: What will go from Zion and Jerusalem?
Questions.A: The law and the word of the LORD (2)

Questions.Q: Into what will strong nations beat their swords and spears?
Questions.A: Plowshares and pruning hooks (3)

Questions.Q: What will they no longer learn?
Questions.A: War (3)

Questions.Q: What do not nations know or understand?
Questions.A: The thoughts of the LORD or his counsel (11-12)

Questions.Q: What did Micah prophesy regarding the birth/origin of the eternal ruler/Messiah [(Jesus)]?
Questions.A: That he would be born in Bethlehem Ephrathah (2)
Questions.Note: See Matthew 2:4-5
Questions.Alternative: What did Micah prophesy regarding the birth of the eternal ruler (Jesus)?
What did Micah prophesy regarding the birth of the eternal Messiah (Jesus)?
What did Micah prophesy regarding the origin of the eternal ruler (Jesus)?
What did Micah prophesy regarding the origin of the eternal Messiah (Jesus)?
What did Micah prophesy regarding the birth of the eternal ruler?
What did Micah prophesy regarding the birth of the eternal Messiah?
What did Micah prophesy regarding the origin of the eternal ruler?
What did Micah prophesy regarding the origin of the eternal Messiah?

Questions.Q: As what will the remnant of Jacob be?
Questions.A: As a dew from the LORD, as the showers on the grass and as a lion (7-8)

Questions.Q: What will be cut off?
Questions.A: enemies (9)
horses and chariots (10)
cities/strongholds (11)
witchcraft/sorcery (12)
graven images (13)
Questions.Alternative: What will be brought to an end?
What will be eliminated?
What will come to an end?
What will God bring to an end?
What will God destroy?

Questions.Q: With what is the LORD not pleased?
Questions.A: Thousands of rams, ten thousands of rivers of oil or your firstborn given as an offering (6-7)

Questions.Q: What does the LORD require of you?
Questions.A: Do justly, love mercy, and walk humbly with God (8)

Questions.Q: Because of the condition of people who should we look to?
Questions.A: To the LORD, the God of our salvation (2-7)

Questions.Q: Why should not our enemies rejoice when we fall?
Questions.A: Because we shall arise; when we sit in darkness, the LORD shall be a light (8)

Questions.Q: In what does God delight?
Questions.A: Mercy (18)

Questions.Q: Who did Nahum prophesy against?
Questions.A: Nineveh (1)

Questions.Q: How is God toward his adversaries?
Questions.A: The LORD revenges, is furious, and reserves wrath for his enemies (2)

Questions.Q: How is God toward those that trust in Him?
Questions.A: The LORD is good, a strong hold in the day of trouble; and knows them that trust in him (7)

Questions.Q: What was Judah to behold on the mountains?
Questions.A: The feet of him that brings good tidings, that publishes peace (15)

Questions.Q: What will happen to Nineveh?
Questions.A: It would be spoiled, empty, void and waste (8-10)

Questions.Q: Who was against Nineveh?
Questions.A: The LORD of hosts (13)

Questions.Q: Who was laid waste?
Questions.A: Nineveh (7)

Questions.Q: Who would receive no healing?
Questions.A: The king of Assyria (18-19)

Questions.Q: Concerning whom did Obadiah prophesy?
Questions.A: Edom (1)

Questions.Q: What caused them to be proud?
Questions.A: They lived high in the clefts of the rocks (3-4)

Questions.Q: Whom will the LORD destroy?
Questions.A: The wise men out of Edom (8)

Questions.Q: Over what did they rejoice?
Questions.A: The children of Judah in the day of their destruction (12)

Questions.Q: What will be done to them?
Questions.A: As they did, it shall be done to them: their reward shall return on their own head. (15)

Questions.Q: What will remain of the house of Esau?
Questions.A: Nothing (18)

Questions.Q: During the reign of what king of Judah did Zephaniah prophesy?
Questions.A: Josiah the son of Amon, king of Judah (1)

Questions.Q: Who will the LORD punish in Jerusalem?
Questions.A: The men that are settled on their lees: that say in their heart, The LORD will not do good, neither will he do evil (12)

Questions.Q: What kind of a day is the day of the LORD?
Questions.A: A day of wrath, a day of trouble and distress, a day of devastation and desolation, a day of darkness and gloominess, a day of clouds and thick darkness (15-16)

Questions.Q: What will not be able to deliver people in the day of the LORD's wrath?
Questions.A: Silver or gold (18)

Questions.Q: What should a nation do before the day of the LORD's anger comes on it?
Questions.A: Seek the LORD, seek righteousness and meekness (1-3)

Questions.Q: What nations will be as Sodom and Gomorrah?
Questions.A: Moab and Ammon (9)

Questions.Q: To whom is woe pronounced?
Questions.A: Her that is filthy and polluted (1-4)

Questions.Q: What does the LORD do every morning?
Questions.A: He brings his judgment to light (5)

Questions.Q: What is the LORD's determination?
Questions.A: To gather the nations in order to pour on them my indignation (8)

Questions.Q: What will the LORD in the middle of them do?
Questions.A: He will save, he will rejoice over them with joy (17)

Questions.Q: What will the LORD turn back?
Questions.A: Their captivity (20)

Questions.Q: Whose prophecy did Cyrus king of Persia fulfill in issuing a proclamation to rebuild the temple?
Questions.A: Jeremiah (1-4)

Questions.Q: What did Cyrus bring forth that Nebuchadnezzar had taken out of Jerusalem?
Questions.A: The vessels of the house of the LORD (7-11)

Questions.Q: Who was the first person named as one who went out of captivity?
Questions.A: Zerubbabel (2)

Questions.Q: What was the size of the congregation that went out of captivity?
Questions.A: 42,360 plus 7,337 servants and maids, including 200 hundred singing men and women (64-65)

Questions.Q: What did Jeshua and Zerubbabel first build?
Questions.A: The altar of the God of Israel, to offer burnt offerings thereon (1-2)

Questions.Q: After this what did Jeshua and Zerubbabel begin to build?
Questions.A: The house of the LORD (8)

Questions.Q: For what did the people sing, praise and give thanks unto God?
Questions.A: Because the LORD is good, for his mercy endures for ever toward Israel. And also because the foundation of the house of the LORD was laid (11)

Questions.Q: What did the old men do who had seen the first temple?
Questions.A: Wept with a loud voice (12)

Questions.Q: What did the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin want to do?
Questions.A: Join with them in building the temple (1-2)

Questions.Q: After Zerubbabel refused them what three things did these adversaries do?
Questions.A: They weakened the hands of the people of Judah, troubled them in building, and bribed counselors against them, to frustrate their purpose (3-10)

Questions.Q: What did they write to try to convince King Artaxerxes to cause the rebuilding to stop?
Questions.A: That if Jerusalem was rebuilt the Jews would not pay toll, tribute, and custom, and thus damage the revenue of the kings. Also they requested that a search be made in the book of the records to know that this city is a rebellious city (11-16)

Questions.Q: What did Artaxerxes command?
Questions.A: That the Jews cease working, and that this city be not built, until another commandment was given from him. (21-24)

Questions.Q: What were the names of the prophets who inspired the Jews to keep start building again?
Questions.A: Haggai and Zechariah (1-2)

Questions.Q: To whom did Tattenai send a letter regarding the progress of the work?
Questions.A: Darius the king (6)

Questions.Q: What did Darius tell Tattenai to do?
Questions.A: Let the work of this house of God alone; let the governor of the Jews and the elders of the Jews build this house of God in his place. (7)

Questions.Q: How was the cost of rebuilding to be paid?
Questions.A: Out of the king's goods, even of the tribute (8)

Questions.Q: What was the prayer request of Darius?
Questions.A: For the life of the king, and of his sons (9-10)

Questions.Q: What did Darius order to happen to anyone who altered his edict?
Questions.A: Let timber be pulled down from his house, and let him be hanged thereon; and let his house be made a dunghill (11)

Questions.Q: When was the temple finished?
Questions.A: On the third day of the month Adar, which was in the sixth year of the reign of Darius the king (14-15)

Questions.Q: How did the Israelites celebrate the dedication of the house of God?
Questions.A: With joy they gave offerings and kept the passover and the feast of unleavened bread (16-22)

Questions.Q: Of whom was Ezra a descendant?
Questions.A: Aaron the chief priest (1-5)

Questions.Q: What did Ezra prepare his heart to do?
Questions.A: To seek the law of the LORD, and to do it, and to teach in Israel statutes and judgments (10)

Questions.Q: Who sent a letter authorizing supplies and materials to be given to Ezra for the house of God?
Questions.A: King Artaxerxes (11-25)

Questions.Q: What was to be done to any one who would not observe the law of God and the king?
Questions.A: Let judgment be executed speedily on him, whether it be to death, or to banishment, or to confiscation of goods, or to imprisonment. (26)

Questions.Q: What did Ezra proclaim at the river of Ahava?
Questions.A: A fast, to seek God for direction (21)

Questions.Q: Why was Ezra ashamed to ask for an escort of soldiers?
Questions.A: Because he had spoken to the king, saying, The hand of our God is on all them for good that seek him; but his power and his wrath is against all them that forsake him. (22)

Questions.Q: How did Ezra handle the accounting of the silver and gold brought to Jerusalem?
Questions.A: He weighed the silver, and the gold, and the vessels before they left and also when they got to Jerusalem. (24-34)

Questions.Q: From what had the people of Israel not separated themselves?
Questions.A: They had not separated themselves from the people of the lands, and did according to their abominations, even taking of their daughters for themselves (1-2)

Questions.Q: What was Ezra's reaction when he heard this report?
Questions.A: He rent his garment and mantle, and plucked off the hair of his head and beard, and sat down astonished. (3-5)

Questions.Q: To what extent did Ezra say was the guilt and iniquities of Israel?
Questions.A: Our iniquities have increased over our head, and our trespass has grown up to the heavens (6-7)

Questions.Q: How did Ezra consider the punishment of God?
Questions.A: Less than their iniquities deserved (13)

Questions.Q: Who gathered to Ezra as he was praying and confessing?
Questions.A: A very great congregation of men and women and children (1)

Questions.Q: What did the Israelites make a covenant to do?
Questions.A: Put away all the wives that they had taken from the countries of the land, and such as are born of them (2-3)

Questions.Q: Which of Elkanah's wives had children first?
Questions.A: Peninnah (2)

Questions.Q: Why was Hannah so downhearted?
Questions.A: Because she had no children and Peninnah provoked her about this (6-8)

Questions.Q: What did Hannah vow when she prayed?
Questions.A: If the Lord would give her a boy then she would give him to the LORD all the days of his life (11)

Questions.Q: What did Eli think as he observed Hannah pray?
Questions.A: He thought she was drunk (13)

Questions.Q: What did Hannah do with Samuel after he was weaned?
Questions.A: She brought him to the house of the LORD in Shiloh and lent him to the Lord all the days of his life (24-28)

Questions.Q: What could be said about the spiritual condition of the sons of Eli?
Questions.A: They knew not the Lord and did wickedly including (12-17)
fornication (12-17)

Questions.Q: What did Samuel's mother bring him each year?
Questions.A: A coat (19)

Questions.Q: How many children did Hannah have after Samuel?
Questions.A: Three sons and two daughters. (21)

Questions.Q: What did Eli hear that his sons were doing?
Questions.A: Laying with the women that assembled at the door of the tabernacle (22)

Questions.Q: What did the man of God prophecy against the House of Eli?
Questions.A: His sons, Hophni and Phinehas, would both die in one day (31-34)

Questions.Q: Who would the LORD raise up?
Questions.A: A faithful priest (35)

Questions.Q: Who did Samuel think had called him at night?
What did Eli tell Samuel to say when he realized it was the LORD calling?
Questions.A: Speak, LORD; for your servant hears. (8-9)

Questions.Q: What did the LORD say to Samuel?
Questions.A: That God was going to judge the house of Eli because his sons were vile and Eli did not restrain them. (11-14)

Questions.Q: Who recognized that Samuel was established to be a prophet of the LORD?
Questions.A: All Israel from Dan even to Beersheba knew that Samuel was established to be a prophet of the LORD. (20)

Questions.Q: What did Israel do when they brought the Ark of the Covenant into camp?
Questions.A: All Israel shouted with a great shout, so that the earth rang again (5)

Questions.Q: Who was killed when the Philistines captured the ark?
Questions.A: 30,000 footmen plus Eli's sons Hophni and Phineas (10-11)

Questions.Q: What happened to Eli when he heard that the ark was captured?
Questions.A: He fell from off the seat backward by the side of the gate, and his neck broke, and he died: for he was an old man, and heavy. (18)

Questions.Q: What happened to the wife of Phinehas when she heard that her husband was killed?
Questions.A: She gave birth to a son and (19-21)

Questions.Q: Why did she name the child Ichabod?
Questions.A: Because the glory was departed from Israel: the ark of God was taken and her father in law and her husband died. (21-22)

Questions.Q: What happened when the ark was set beside Dagon?
Questions.A: Dagon fell down twice before the ark, the second time its head and hands broke off. (2-4)

Questions.Q: How did the LORD afflict the people of Ashdod, Gath, and Ekron?
Questions.A: Tumors (6-12)

Questions.Q: What did the people of Ekron decide to do with the ark?
Questions.A: Send away the ark of the God of Israel, and let it go again to his own place. (11)

Questions.Q: What did the Philistines send with the ark as a guilt offering?
Questions.A: Five golden tumors, and five golden mice (4)

Questions.Q: How did the Philistines determine whether the disaster that had come upon them was from the LORD or by chance?
Questions.A: They took two milk cows, and tied them to the cart, and shut up their calves at home and the cows pulled the cart to Bethshemesh rather than returning to their calves (7-12)

Questions.Q: Why did God strike down 50,070 men of Bethshemesh?
Questions.A: Because they had looked into the ark of the LORD. (19)

Questions.Q: Who was asked to come and get the ark?
Questions.A: The inhabitants of Kirjathjearim (21)

Questions.Q: How long did the ark remain at Kiriath Jearim?
Questions.A: Twenty years (1-2)

Questions.Q: How did the LORD help Israel in battle against the Philistines?
Questions.A: The LORD thundered with a great thunder on that day on the Philistines, and discomfited them (10)

Questions.Q: What did Samuel call the stone he set up near Mizpeh?
Questions.A: Ebenezer, saying, Till now has the LORD helped us (12)

Questions.Q: Where did Samuel judge Israel?
Questions.A: In circuit to Bethel, Gilgal, Mizpeh, and Ramah (15-17)

Questions.Q: For what two reasons did Israel want a king?
Questions.A: Because Samuel's sons did not walk in his ways and because Israel wanted to be like other nations (5)

Questions.Q: What did the LORD tell Samuel when he prayed regarding a king?
Questions.A: They have not rejected you, but they have rejected me, that I should not reign over them (6-9)

Questions.Q: What did Samuel warn the people that a king would do to them?
Questions.A: He would take their sons to be soldiers, their daughters to be cooks, and their substance. They would be his servants. (10-18)

Questions.Q: How did Israel react to Samuel's warning?
Questions.A: They still wanted a king (19-20)

Questions.Q: What can be said about Saul's physical stature?
Questions.A: From his shoulders and upward he was taller than any of the people (2)

Questions.Q: What caused Saul and his servant to seek out a seer?
Questions.A: They could not find the donkey's belonging to Saul's father (3-10)
Questions.Alternative: What caused Saul and his servant to seek out a prophet?
Why did Saul and his servant to seek out a prophet?
Why did Saul and his servant look for a prophet?
What caused Saul and his servant to seek out the prophet?
Why did Saul and his servant look for a seer?
What caused Saul and his servants to seek out a seer?

Questions.Q: When did the LORD talk to Samuel about Saul?
Questions.A: the day before Saul came to the city where Samuel was (15-16)

Questions.Q: What had the LORD revealed to Samuel the day before?
Questions.A: Tomorrow about this time I will send you a man out of the land of Benjamin, and you shall anoint him to be captain over my people. (15-16)

Questions.Q: Why was Saul hesitant to receive the words of Samuel?
Questions.A: He was from the smallest of the tribes of Israel and his family the least of all the families of the tribe of Benjamin (21)

Questions.Q: Why did Samuel have Saul send his servant on ahead when they were leaving town?
Questions.A: So that Samuel could show Saul the word of God. (27)

Questions.Q: What did Samuel do to Saul?
Questions.A: Anointed him with oil to be captain over the Lord's inheritance? (1)

Questions.Q: What did Samuel prophesy would happen to Saul?
Questions.A: The Spirit of the LORD will come on Saul, and he would prophesy with them, and be turned into another man. (2-7)

Questions.Q: Where was Saul when Samuel wanted to present him to the people at Mizpeh?
Questions.A: Hid among the stuff. (21-22)

Questions.Q: What did the people shout when Samuel presented Saul?
Questions.A: God save the king (24)

Questions.Q: Who accompanied Saul to Gibeah?
Questions.A: A band of men, whose hearts God had touched (26-27)

Questions.Q: What did Nahash the Ammonite threaten to do?
Questions.A: Thrust out the right eyes of the men of Jabeshgilead (1-2)

Questions.Q: By what means did Saul gather his army?
Questions.A: He took a pair/yoke of oxen, cut them in pieces, and sent them throughout all the coasts of Israel, saying, Whoever does not come forth after Saul and after Samuel, so shall it be done to his oxen. (7)

Questions.Q: What did Samuel do at Gilgal?
Questions.A: He made Saul king and sacrificed peace offerings (14-15)

Questions.Q: How had Samuel behaved himself?
Questions.A: Uprightly. He did not steal, defraud, oppress or take bribes (1-5)

Questions.Q: What would happen to Israel if they did not obey they voice of the LORD?
Questions.A: The hand of the LORD would be against them, as it was against their fathers (15)

Questions.Q: Why did God send thunder and rain during the wheat harvest?
Questions.A: So they would see that their wickedness was great, in asking for a king (17)

Questions.Q: What did Samuel consider would be sin for him?
Questions.A: Ceasing to pray for them (23)

Questions.Q: What did Saul do when he became impatient regarding the arrival of Samuel?
Questions.A: Offered a burnt offering. (8-12)

Questions.Q: What would happen to Saul's kingdom as a result of this?
Questions.A: His kingdom would not continue: and the LORD sought a man after his own heart, to be captain over his people (14)

Questions.Q: Who were the only ones is Israel with swords?
Questions.A: Saul and Jonathan (22)

Questions.Q: What did Jonathan and his armor-bearer do with out telling Saul?
Questions.A: They went up to a garrison of Philistines and killed 20 of them (1-14)

Questions.Q: What caused the panic among the Philistines?
Questions.A: The earth quaked (15)

Questions.Q: Why did Saul want to kill his son Jonathan?
Questions.A: Saul charged his men that day not to eat until evening but Jonathan had not heard this command and ate some honey. (27, 43-44)

Questions.Q: Who was commander of Saul's army?
Questions.A: Abner, the son of Ner, Saul's uncle (50)

Questions.Q: What did Samuel tell Saul to do the Amalekites?
Questions.A: Attack the Amalekites and totally destroy everything that belongs to them. Do not spare them; put to death men and women, children and infants, cattle and sheep, camels and donkeys. (3)

Questions.Q: What did Saul spare?
Questions.A: Agag the king of the Amalekites and the best of the sheep, oxen, fatted calves, lambs, and all that was good (8-9)

Questions.Q: How did Saul lie to Samuel?
Questions.A: He told Samuel "I have performed the commandment of the LORD" (13)

Questions.Q: Who did Saul blame?
Questions.A: The people (15, 21)

Questions.Q: What is better than sacrifice?
Questions.A: To obey (22)

Questions.Q: What is like the sin of witchcraft?
Questions.A: Rebellion (23)

Questions.Q: What did Samuel say regarding Saul as king?
Questions.A: The Lord had torn the kingdom of Israel from him and had given it to one of his neighbors who was better than he. (26-28)

Questions.Q: What did Samuel do to Agag?
Questions.A: Hewed Agag in pieces (33)

Questions.Q: When did Samuel again see Saul?
Questions.A: Samuel came no more to see Saul until the day of his death (35)

Questions.Q: Where did Samuel go to anoint the next king?
Questions.A: To Jesse the Bethlehemite (1)

Questions.Q: What does the LORD look at when viewing a man?
Questions.A: The heart (7)
Questions.Alternative: What does the LORD look at?
What does the LORD consider when looking at a man?
What does the LORD consider when looking at a person?
What does the LORD look at when viewing a person?
What does the LORD look at when considering a man?
What does the LORD look at when considering a person?
What does the LORD look at when he observes a person?

Questions.Q: What is the difference between how people/men look at others and how God sees people?
Questions.A: People are only able to see the outward appearance, but God can see our hearts/thoughts. (7)
Questions.Alternative: What is the difference between how people look at others and how God sees people?
What is the difference between how men look at others and how God sees people?

Questions.Q: Where was David when the other brothers were attending the sacrifice?
Questions.A: Keeping the sheep (11)

Questions.Q: What did Samuel do to David?
Questions.A: He took a horn of oil, and anointed him in the presence of his brothers (13)

Questions.Q: Why did Saul want David at his house?
Questions.A: An evil spirit from the LORD troubled him and it was recommended that someone play a harp to soothe him (16)

Questions.Q: How big was Goliath?
Questions.A: His height was six cubits and a span.(Approximately 9 feet six inches tall) (4)

Questions.Q: How did Goliath challenge Israel?
Questions.A: If a man from Israel fought and killed him then the Philistines would be their servants. However if he killed the Israelite then Israel would be their servants. (8-10)

Questions.Q: How did David happen to be at the battle scene?
Questions.A: He was bringing food to his three oldest brothers who were in Saul's army. (17-18)

Questions.Q: What did Saul offer to the man who killed Goliath?
Questions.A: Great riches and his daughter (25)

Questions.Q: What did David's oldest brother accuse him of?
Questions.A: Pride, and naughtiness of heart (28)

Questions.Q: Why did Saul at first refuse David's offer to fight Goliath?
Questions.A: He thought David was not able to go against the Philistine to fight him: because he was but a youth, and Goliath was a man of war. (33)

Questions.Q: What had David previously killed?
Questions.A: A lion and a bear (34-37)

Questions.Q: What did Saul provide David for the battle?
Questions.A: His armor, helmet of brass and a coat of mail. (38-39)

Questions.Q: What did David instead use as weapons?
Questions.A: Five smooth stones and his sling (40)

Questions.Q: How did Goliath mock David?
Questions.A: Am I a dog, that you come to me with staves? I will give your flesh to the fowls of the air, and to the beasts of the field. (42-44)

Questions.Q: How did David attack Goliath?
Questions.A: David and ran toward the Philistine, put his hand in his bag, took a stone, and slung it, and struck the Philistine in his forehead (45-50)

Questions.Q: How did David cut off Goliath's head?
Questions.A: He took Goliath's sword and cut off his head (51)

Questions.Q: When did the Israelites pursue the Philistines?
Questions.A: When they saw the Philistines fleeing after Goliath's death. (52)

Questions.Q: What was David carrying when he was brought before Saul?
Questions.A: Goliath's head (57)

Questions.Q: Who made a covenant with David?
Questions.A: Jonathan, Saul's son. (3)

Questions.Q: To what position did Saul promote David?
Questions.A: Saul set him over the men of war (5)

Questions.Q: What made Saul so jealous of David?
Questions.A: When the women sang "Saul has slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands." (6-9)

Questions.Q: With what did Saul try to kill David?
Questions.A: A javelin (10-11)

Questions.Q: Why was Saul afraid of David?
Questions.A: Because the LORD was with him, and was departed from Saul (12-15)

Questions.Q: What was the reaction of Israel and Judah to David?
Questions.A: They loved David (16)

Questions.Q: Why did Saul ask David to provide a hundred Philistine foreskins as a price for Michal?
Questions.A: He was hoping the Philistines would kill him (25)

Questions.Q: What did David give to Saul for Michal?
Questions.A: Two hundred foreskins of the Philistines (27)

Questions.Q: Who did Saul ask to kill David?
Questions.A: Jonathan and his servants (1)

Questions.Q: What did Saul do with his spear?
Questions.A: Threw it at David but it missed and went into the wall (10)

Questions.Q: Who let David down through a window that he might escape?
Questions.A: Michal, David's wife (12)

Questions.Q: To whom did David go when he escaped?
Questions.A: Samuel (18)

Questions.Q: What did Jonathan want David to promise?
Questions.A: To not cut off kindness from Jonathan's house for ever (14-16)

Questions.Q: How did Jonathan love David?
Questions.A: As he loved his own soul. (17)

Questions.Q: What was the sign that Jonathan would give David if he should flee from Saul?
Questions.A: Jonathan would shoot three arrows and tell the lad gathering them that the arrows were beyond him. (18-22)

Questions.Q: What kind of bread did the priest of Nob give David?
Questions.A: Hallowed bread: (6)

Questions.Q: Who was there with Abimelech the priest that day?
Questions.A: Doeg, an Edomite, the chief herdsmen for Saul. (7)

Questions.Q: What else did Abimelech give David?
Questions.A: Goliath's sword (8-9)

Questions.Q: Why did David pretend to be a mad man in the presence of the king of Gath?
Questions.A: He was sore afraid of Achish the king of Gath whose servants said “ Is this not David of whom they sang David has slain his thousands” (10-15)

Questions.Q: Who became David's followers at the cave of Adullam?
Questions.A: Every one that was in distress, in debt, and was discontented (2)

Questions.Q: Who did Saul command Doeg to kill?
Questions.A: The priests (18)

Questions.Q: Who escaped and fled to David?
Questions.A: Abiathar (20)

Questions.Q: What did David and his men do for the people of Keilah?
Questions.A: Delivered them from the Philistines (5)

Questions.Q: Who was willing to turn David over to Saul?
Questions.A: The men of Keilah (7-12, 19-20)

Questions.Q: How often did Saul seek to kill David?
Questions.A: Every day (14)

Questions.Q: What did David do to Saul in the cave?
Questions.A: Cut off the skirt of Saul's robe but did not kill him (3-4)

Questions.Q: Why didn't David kill Saul?
Questions.A: He was anointed of the LORD (6)

Questions.Q: What did Saul acknowledge?
Questions.A: David was more righteous than Saul (16-20)

Questions.Q: What did David promise to Saul?
Questions.A: He would not kill off Saul's descendants or wipe out his name from his father's family. (21-22)

Questions.Q: What did Nabal refuse to give David's servants?
Questions.A: Bread, water, and meat (11)

Questions.Q: What did Abigail do to avoid disaster?
Questions.A: She brought two hundred loaves, two bottles of wine, five sheep ready dressed, five measures of parched corn, one hundred clusters of raisins, and two hundred cakes of figs to David (18, 23-31)

Questions.Q: What happened to Nabal?
Questions.A: His heart died within him, and he became as a stone (36-38)

Questions.Q: What did Abigail become?
Questions.A: The wife of David (42)

Questions.Q: What did Abishai ask permission to do when he and David went into Saul's camp at night?
Questions.A: Kill Saul with a spear as he was sleeping (7-8)

Questions.Q: What did David take from near Saul's head?
Questions.A: Saul's spear and a cruse of water (12)

Questions.Q: What did Saul admit after realizing that David had spared his life again?
Questions.A: He had sinned, played the fool, and erred exceedingly (21)

Questions.Q: Where did David flee for one year and four months?
Questions.A: In the country of the Philistines (7)

Questions.Q: Why didn't David leave a man or women alive from the cities he raided?
Questions.A: Lest they should tell the Philistines about what he had done (11)

Questions.Q: Who did the Lord no longer answer by the prophets or by dreams?
Questions.A: Saul (6, 15)

Questions.Q: Who did Saul want the woman at Endor with a familiar spirit to bring up?
Questions.A: Samuel (11)

Questions.Q: What was going to happen to Saul and his sons?
Questions.A: They would die in one day (19)

Questions.Q: Why didn't the Philistine commanders want David fighting with them against the Israelites?
Questions.A: They were afraid that in the mist of battle David would turn against them (4)

Questions.Q: What did Achish then ask David to do?
Questions.A: Return into the land of the Philistines (7, 10)

Questions.Q: What did David find when he returned to Ziklag?
Questions.A: The Amalekites had burned Ziklag with fire and taken their wives, sons, and daughters captives (1-5)

Questions.Q: How did David encourage himself when he was distressed?
Questions.A: David encouraged himself in the LORD his God. (6)

Questions.Q: What did David recover when he pursued after the Amalekites?
Questions.A: All that the Amalekites had carried away (18-19)

Questions.Q: What share of the plunder was given with those who stayed behind?
Questions.A: The same as those who went to battle (24)

Questions.Q: Who else was given some of the plunder?
Questions.A: To the elders of Judah, even to his friends (26-31)

Questions.Q: Who was killed on Mount Gilboa?
Questions.A: Saul and his three sons (1-6)

Questions.Q: What did the Philistines do to the body of Saul?
Questions.A: They cut off his head and fastened his body to the wall of Bethshan (9-10)

Questions.Q: What did the men of Jabesh Gilead do?
Questions.A: They took the bodies of Saul and his sons from the wall of Bethshan, burnt them and took their bones, and buried them under a tree at Jabesh (11-13)

Questions.Q: Who was the first tribe to go against the Canaanites?
Questions.A: Judah (1-3)

Questions.Q: How did Adonibezek “reap what he sowed?”
Questions.A: When the Israelites captured him they cut off his thumbs and great toes. He had previously done that to seventy kings. He said, “God has paid me back for what I did to them” (6-7)

Questions.Q: Who was given Caleb's daughter to marry?
Questions.A: Othniel (12-15)

Questions.Q: Why didn't Judah drive out the inhabitants of the valley?
Questions.A: They had chariots of iron. (16-20)

Questions.Q: Who else failed to drive out the inhabitants in their land?
Questions.A: Benjamin, Manasseh, Ephraim, Zebulun, Asher, Naphtali (21-36)

Questions.Q: What did the angel of the LORD say to Israel?
Questions.A: They had not obeyed the Lord, who told them to break down the altars and not to make a covenant with the nations of the lands they possessed. (1-5)

Questions.Q: What arose after Joshua and the elders died?
Questions.A: Another generation after them, who knew neither the Lord nor what he had done for Israel (10)
Questions.Alternative: What grew up after Joshua and the elders died?

Questions.Q: What did the Israelites do provoke the anger of the Lord?
Questions.A: They forsook the LORD and served Baal and Ashtaroth. (11-13)

Questions.Q: To whom did the LORD deliver Israel?
Questions.A: Into the hands of spoilers that spoiled them, and he sold them into the hands of their enemies (14-15)

Questions.Q: Who did the LORD raise up to help them?
Questions.A: Judges, which delivered them out of the hand of those that spoiled them (16-18)

Questions.Q: What happened after the judge died?
Questions.A: They returned, and corrupted themselves more than their fathers, in following other gods to serve them, and to bow down to them (19-23)

Questions.Q: Why did the LORD leave some nations?
Questions.A: To prove Israel by them, to know whether they would listen to the commandments of the LORD (1-6)

Questions.Q: What judge delivered Israel from the king of Mesopotamia?
Questions.A: Othniel (7-11)

Questions.Q: What physically was different about Ehud?
Questions.A: He was left handed (12-16)

Questions.Q: What physically was different about Eglon?
Questions.A: He was very fat (17-26)

Questions.Q: How long did Israel have rest from the Moabites?
Questions.A: Eighty years (27-30)

Questions.Q: By what means did Shamgar strike down the Philistines?
Questions.A: An ox goad (31)

Questions.Q: With how many chariots did Sisera oppress the Israelites?
Questions.A: Nine hundred (1-3)

Questions.Q: What lady judged Israel?
Questions.A: Deborah (4-11)

Questions.Q: How was Sisera killed?
Questions.A: When he fled to the tent of Jael, she gave him milk to drink and he fell asleep. Jael then took a nail from the tent and with a hammer drove it through his temples. (12-23)

Questions.Q: What did Deborah and Barak do after the victory?
Questions.A: They sang praise to the Lord (1-31)

Questions.Q: What did the angel of the LORD say to Meroz?
Questions.A: Curse Meroz; because they came not to the help of the LORD against the mighty. (23)

Questions.Q: What did the mother of Sisera cry out?
Questions.A: Why is his chariot so long in coming? why tarry the wheels of his chariots? (24-28)

Questions.Q: What did the Midianites do to Israel?
Questions.A: They destroyed the increase of the earth, and left no sustenance for Israel. And Israel was greatly impoverished because of the Midianites (1-6)

Questions.Q: Where did the angel of the LORD appear to Gideon?
Questions.A: By the wine press where Gideon threshed wheat (11)

Questions.Q: What did the angel say to Gideon?
Questions.A: The LORD is with you, you mighty man of valor. (12)

Questions.Q: What did Gideon ask the angel?
Questions.A: If the LORD be with us, why then is all this befallen us? and where be all his miracles which our fathers told us of? (13)

Questions.Q: What was the first sign that God gave to Gideon?
Questions.A: Fire out of the rock that consumed the flesh and the unleavened cakes. (14-22)

Questions.Q: What did Gideon and his ten servants do?
Questions.A: Throw down the altar of Baal that his father had, and cut down the grove that was by it: And build an altar to the LORD (25-28)

Questions.Q: What did Joash, the father of Gideon say to those who wanted to kill Gideon?
Questions.A: Let Baal plead for himself, because one has cast down his altar. (29-32)

Questions.Q: What two signs did God give Gideon with the fleece of wool?
Questions.A: One day the fleece of wool was wet and the ground dry. The next day the fleece was dry and the ground was wet. (36-40)

Questions.Q: How many men left Gideon because they were afraid?
How many passed the water test?
What did Gideon hear when he went near the camp of the Midianites?
Questions.A: He heard a man tell a dream and another give the meaning, which was that God would deliver Midian into the hands of Israel through Gideon (9-15)

Questions.Q: With what were Gideon's men equipped?
Questions.A: Each had a trumpet, an empty pitcher and a lamp inside the pitcher (16-19)

Questions.Q: What did Gideon's men shout?
Questions.A: The sword of the LORD, and of Gideon. (20-23)

Questions.Q: What did Gideon do to the men of Succoth?
Questions.A: Taught them with thorns of the wilderness and briers (1-16)

Questions.Q: What did Gideon do to the tower of Peniel?
Questions.A: Beat it down (17)

Questions.Q: What did Gideon do to Zebah and Zalmunna?
Questions.A: Killed them, and took away the ornaments that were on their camels' necks. (18-21)

Questions.Q: What mistake did Gideon make?
Questions.A: He made an ephod of the gold they took as spoils, and put it in his city, even in Ophrah: and the thing became a snare to Gideon, and to his house. (22-27)

Questions.Q: How long did the land enjoy peace during Gideon's lifetime?
Questions.A: Forty years (28)

Questions.Q: What happened after Gideon died?
Questions.A: The Israelites turned again to worship the Baals and made Baal-Berith their god (33)
They did not remember the LORD their God, who had delivered them out of the hands of all their enemies. (34)
They also failed to show any loyalty to the family of Jerub-Baal (that is, Gideon) (35)

Questions.Q: How many of Jerubaal's/Gideon's sons did Abimeilech murder?
Questions.A: Seventy (1-21)
Questions.Alternative: How many of Jerubaal's sons did Abimeilech murder?
How many of Gideon's sons did Abimeilech murder?

Questions.Q: How did the citizens of Shechem die?
Questions.A: They were in a tower to which Abimelech set on fire (46-49)

Questions.Q: How did Abimelech die?
Questions.A: When Abimelech approached a tower in Thebez a woman of that city dropped a piece of a millstone on Abimelech's head, and broke his skull. As he was about to die he asked his armor bearer to kill him with a sword because he did not want it said that a women killed him. (50-57)

Questions.Q: Who led Israel for twenty-three years?
Questions.A: Tola (1-2)

Questions.Q: Who led Israel for twenty-two years, and had thirty sons?
Questions.A: Jair (3-5)

Questions.Q: How long were the Israelites oppressed by the Philistines and the Ammonites?
Questions.A: Eighteen years (6-9)

Questions.Q: How did the LORD reply when the Israelites cried out unto Him?
Questions.A: Did not I deliver you from the Egyptians, and from other enemies when they oppressed you; and you cried to me, and I delivered you out of their hand. Yet you have forsaken me, and served other gods, go and cry to the gods which you have chosen; let them deliver you in the time of your tribulation. (10-14)

Questions.Q: Who did the elders of Gilead ask to lead them in war against the Ammonites?
Questions.A: Jephthah (1-11)

Questions.Q: What did the king of Ammon do with the message that Jephthah sent him?
Questions.A: He did not listen to the words of Jephthah (12-28)

Questions.Q: What did Jephthah vow unto the LORD?
Questions.A: If the Lord would deliver the children of Ammon into his hands, Then it shall be, that whatever comes forth of the doors of my house to meet me I will offer it up for a burnt offering. (29-40)

Questions.Q: How did the Gileadites determine if a man was an Ephraimite?
Questions.A: If he could not pronounce Shibboleth (1-7)

Questions.Q: What other three judges are mentioned in this chapter?
Questions.A: Ibzan, Elon, and Abdon (8-13)

Questions.Q: How long were the Israelites oppressed by the Philistines?
Questions.A: Forty years (1)

Questions.Q: What did the angel of the LORD say to Manoah's wife regarding the son that was to be born of her?
Questions.A: No razor shall come on his head: for the child shall be a Nazarite to God from the womb: and he shall begin to deliver Israel out of the hand of the Philistines. (2-7)

Questions.Q: What happened when Manoah presented his offering?
Questions.A: The angel of the LORD ascended in the flame of the altar (15-21)

Questions.Q: What did Manoah's wife name her son?
Questions.A: Samson (24)

Questions.Q: Who did Samson want for a wife?
Questions.A: A woman in Timnath of the daughters of the Philistines (1-4)

Questions.Q: What did Samson kill with his bare hands?
Questions.A: A young lion (5-9)

Questions.Q: How did the companions of Samson find out the meaning of his riddle?
Questions.A: From Samson's wife (10-18)

Questions.Q: How did Samson get the thirty changes of garments?
Questions.A: He killed thirty men of Ashkelon and took their clothes (19)

Questions.Q: What happened to Samson's wife?
Questions.A: She was given to his companion, whom he had used as his friend (20)

Questions.Q: What did Samson do with the foxes?
Questions.A: He caught three hundred foxes, turned them tail to tail, and put a firebrand in the middle between two tails. When he had set the brands on fire, he let them go into the standing corn of the Philistines. (1-6)

Questions.Q: What did Samson do with the jawbone?
Questions.A: Killed a thousand Philistines (9-19)

Questions.Q: How long did Samson judge Israel?
Questions.A: Twenty years (20)

Questions.Q: Where did Samson take the doors of the city of Gaza?
Questions.A: To the top of a hill that is before Hebron. (1-3)

Questions.Q: Who was offered money to determine the secret of Samson's strength?
Questions.A: Delilah (4-16)

Questions.Q: What was the secret of Samson's strength?
Questions.A: His consecration to God as a Nazarite, having never cut his hair. (17-19)

Questions.Q: What did the Philistines do to Samson?
Questions.A: Took him, put out his eyes, and brought him to Gaza, bound him with fetters of brass; and made him grind in the prison house (20-21)

Questions.Q: How did Samson die?
Questions.A: He pulled down the pillars of a great building where 3000 Philistines were celebrating their victory over him. The collapsing building killed both him and the Philistines. (22-31)

Questions.Q: What did Micah and his mother have made?
Questions.A: A graven image and a molten image (1-5)

Questions.Q: What was said about Israel in those days?
Questions.A: There was no king in Israel, but every man did that which was right in his own eyes. (6)

Questions.Q: Who did Micah hire?
Questions.A: A young man out of Bethlehemjudah of the family of Judah, who was a Levite (7-13)

Questions.Q: In what condition did the men of Dan find the inhabitants of Laish?
Questions.A: Unsuspecting/careless, quiet/peaceful and secure (1-10)

Questions.Q: What did the men of Dan take from Micah?
Questions.A: The carved image, the ephod, the household idols, the molten image and his priest. (11-26)

Questions.Q: Why was there no one to rescue Laish?
Questions.A: They were far from Sidon, and had no relationship with anyone else (27-28)

Questions.Q: What did the Israelites rename the city of Laish when they rebuilt it?
Both Judges 18 and 19 begin with the same phrase. What do you is the significance of that phrase?
Questions.A: The author probably believed that the absence of a strong king to establish order allowed lawlessness to prevail.
"In those days Israel had no king" also shows that these events were probably written down during the time when there was a king.

Questions.Q: What did the wicked men of Gibeah want to do to the Levite?
Questions.A: They wanted to have (homosexual) relations with him (22)

Questions.Q: What did the wicked men of Gibeah do to the Levite's concubine?
Questions.A: They raped her and abused her all the night until the morning, until she finally died (12-26)

Questions.Q: What did the Levite do with his dead concubine?
Questions.A: He divided her with a knife, together with her bones, into twelve pieces, and sent her into all the areas of Israel. (27-30)

Questions.Q: What did the Israelites ask the men of Benjamin to do?
Questions.A: Deliver the men, the children of Belial, which were in Gibeah, in order to put them to death, and put away evil from Israel. (1-13)

Questions.Q: What was unique about the seven hundred chosen men from Benjamin?
Questions.A: They were left-handed; every one could sling stones at a hair and not miss. (14-16)

Questions.Q: What military technique did Israel use against Benjamin similar to what Joshua used against Ai?
Questions.A: They pretended to flee drawing Benjamin out of the city so the men lying in wait could set the city on fire and ambush them (17-45)

Questions.Q: How many of the men of Benjamin fell?
Questions.A: About twenty-five thousand (46-48)

Questions.Q: How many young women of Jabesh-Gilead were available to be wives for the remaining Benjamites?
How did the rest of the Benjamites obtain their wives?
Questions.A: They caught a girl of the daughters of Shiloh who was dancing at the yearly feast. (15-24)

Questions.Q: With what sad words does the Book of Judges end?
Questions.A: In those days there was no king in Israel: every man did that which was right in his own eyes. (25)

Questions.Q: What was the condition of the wall of Jerusalem and its gates?
Questions.A: The wall was broken down, and the gates burned with fire. (3)

Questions.Q: What did Nehemiah do when he heard about the remnant that survived the exile and about the condition of Jerusalem?
Questions.A: He wept, mourned certain days, fasted, and prayed (4)

Questions.Q: What did Nehemiah confess in his prayer?
Questions.A: The sins of the Israelites, which they had sinned against God (5-7)

Questions.Q: What did Nehemiah ask God to remember?
Questions.A: The words God had spoken to Moses “If you turn to me, and keep my commandments, and do them; though there were of you cast out to the uttermost part of the heaven, yet will I gather them from there, and will bring them to the place that I have chosen to set my name” (8-9)

Questions.Q: What was Nehemiah's position?
Questions.A: The king's cupbearer (11)

Questions.Q: What did King Artaxerxes perceive about Nehemiah?
Questions.A: His countenance was sad (1-3)

Questions.Q: For what did Nehemiah request permission?
Questions.A: To be sent to rebuild Jerusalem (4-5)

Questions.Q: What letters did Nehemiah ask the king to write?
Questions.A: One to the governors beyond the river, that they would convey him over till he came into Judah; and another to Asaph the keeper of the king's forest, that he would give him timber to make beams (6-9)

Questions.Q: Why were Sanballat and Tobiah disturbed?
Questions.A: That a man had come to seek the welfare of the Israelites (10)

Questions.Q: What did Nehemiah do at night?
Questions.A: Surveyed the walls and the gates (11-16)

Questions.Q: What did Nehemiah tell the priests, nobles and officials?
Questions.A: Come, and let us build up the wall of Jerusalem (17-18)

Questions.Q: How did they reply?
Questions.A: Let us rise up and build (18)

Questions.Q: What did Sanballat and Tobiah do when they heard the plans to rebuild?
Questions.A: They laughed us to scorn, and despised us, and said, What is this thing that you do? will you rebel against the king? (19)

Questions.Q: How did Nehemiah reply to them?
Questions.A: God will prosper us and we will build: but you will have no portion, right, or memorial, in Jerusalem. (20)

Questions.Q: What was repaired and rebuilt in this chapter?
Questions.A: Gates, doors, locks, bars, and towers of the wall (1-32)

Questions.Q: What did Tobiah say would break down their stone wall?
Questions.A: A fox (1-3)

Questions.Q: With what attitude did the builders of the wall work?
Questions.A: With all their heart (6)

Questions.Q: What did Sanballat and Tobiah plot to do?
Questions.A: To fight against Jerusalem, and to hinder it. (7-8)

Questions.Q: What did Nehemiah do to meet this threat?
Questions.A: He prayed, set a watch and told the people to remember the Lord and to fight for their families and houses. (9-14)

Questions.Q: What did those who carried materials hold in one hand?
Questions.A: A weapon (16-17)

Questions.Q: What did the builders have girded to their sides?
Questions.A: A sword (18)

Questions.Q: How would the rest know if an attack took place at another section?
Questions.A: They would hear the sound of a trumpet (19-20)

Questions.Q: How often did the men change their clothes?
Questions.A: It appears that they did not change clothes but only took them off while washing (23)

Questions.Q: What did Nehemiah cause to stop after hearing the cry of the poor?
Questions.A: Usury (6-10)

Questions.Q: What did Nehemiah command to be given to the poor?
Questions.A: Their lands, their vineyards, their olive groves, and their houses, also the hundredth part of the money, and of the corn, the wine, and the oil (11-12)

Questions.Q: What object lesson did Nehemiah give regarding those who kept not their promise?
Questions.A: He shook his lap indicating that God would shake out every man from his house that did not perform this promise (13)

Questions.Q: How did Nehemiah differ from the previous governors?
Questions.A: He did not take from them bread, wine, and silver (14-19)

Questions.Q: After hearing that the wall was rebuilt what did Sanballat request Nehemiah to do?
Questions.A: To meet together in one of the villages in the plain of Ono (1-2)

Questions.Q: How did Nehemiah reply to Sanballat's request?
Questions.A: I am doing a great work, so that I cannot come down: why should the work cease, whilst I leave it, and come down to you? (3-4)

Questions.Q: How did Nehemiah reply to Sanballat's accusations?
Questions.A: There are no such things done as you say, but you feign them out of your own heart (5-8)

Questions.Q: For what did Nehemiah pray?
Questions.A: O God, strengthen my hands (9)

Questions.Q: Who did Tobiah and Sanballat hire to prophesy against Nehemiah?
Questions.A: Shemaiah (10-14)

Questions.Q: How long did it take to complete the walls?
Questions.A: Fifty-two days (15)

Questions.Q: For what purpose did Tobiah send letters?
Questions.A: To put Nehemiah in fear (19)

Questions.Q: Who did Nehemiah put in charge of Jerusalem?
Questions.A: His brother Hanani (1-2)

Questions.Q: When were the gates to be opened and shut?
Questions.A: When the sun was hot, thus in the day time (3)

Questions.Q: How many people returned to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel?
Questions.A: 42,360 plus 7,337 man and maid servants, and 245 singing men and women (6-7, 66)

Questions.Q: What did Ezra read aloud form morning until noon?
Questions.A: The book of the law of Moses. (1-3)

Questions.Q: Where did Ezra stand when he read?
Questions.A: On a high wooden platform built for the occasion. It was above all the people. (4-5)

Questions.Q: What did the Levites do regarding the Law?
Questions.A: They read in the book in the law of God distinctly, and gave the sense, and caused the people to understand the reading (7-8)

Questions.Q: What was their strength?
Questions.A: The joy of the LORD (10)

Questions.Q: What did they build for their celebration in the seventh month?
Questions.A: Booths (13-18)

Questions.Q: From what did the Israelites read for one-fourth of the day?
Questions.A: The book of the law of the LORD (3)

Questions.Q: What did the Israelites do another one–fourth of the day?
Questions.A: They confessed, and worshiped the LORD (3)

Questions.Q: What did the Lord make?
Questions.A: The heavens (i.e., the sky and space), with all the stars, the earth, all that is on it, the seas, and all that is in them (6)
Questions.Alternative: What did the LORD create?
What did God make?
What did God create?

Questions.Q: What does the Lord do for his creation?
Questions.A: He preserves it.
He gives life to all (living) things.

Questions.Q: What period of Israel's history was summarized in their confession?
Questions.A: From Abraham until the captivity (7-32)

Questions.Q: In all that happened to the Jews even when they did wrong how was the Lord?
Questions.A: God was just and did right (33)

Questions.Q: What did they put in writing and seal?
Questions.A: A sure covenant (38)

Questions.Q: What types of people signed the covenant?
Questions.A: Officials, priests, Levites, and chiefs of the people (1-27)

Questions.Q: What did the rest of the people bind themselves to do?
Questions.A: To walk in God's law, and to observe and do all the commandments of the LORD our Lord (28-29)

Questions.Q: What did they promise not to do on the Sabbath?
Questions.A: Buy any ware or victuals (31)

Questions.Q: What did they promise to bring to the priests and the Levites?
Questions.A: First fruits, first born and tithes (35-39)

Questions.Q: How did they determine who was to live in Jerusalem?
Questions.A: The people also cast lots, to bring one of ten to dwell in Jerusalem (1)

Questions.Q: Where did the rest of the Israelites live?
Questions.A: In all the cities of Judah, every one in his inheritance (20)

Questions.Q: When were the family heads of the Levites and priests recorded?
Questions.A: To the reign of Darius the Persian (22)

Questions.Q: Who was brought to Jerusalem for the dedication of the wall?
Questions.A: The Levites and the singers (27-29)

Questions.Q: Where was the sound of rejoicing heard?
Questions.A: Afar off (43)

Questions.Q: What did Eliashib the priest provide for Tobiah?
Questions.A: A great chamber in the courts of the house of God (4-5)

Questions.Q: What did Nehemiah do when he heard this?
Questions.A: Cast out all of Tobiah's stuff (6-9)

Questions.Q: For what did Nehemiah rebuke the rulers?
Questions.A: Because the portions of the Levites and singers had not been given to them (10-13)

Questions.Q: What did Nehemiah want God to do regarding him?
Questions.A: To remember him (14, 22, 29, 31)

Questions.Q: What did Nehemiah do regarding the Sabbath?
Questions.A: He commanded that the gates should be shut, and charged that they should not be opened till after the Sabbath. He also set some of his servants at the gates, that there should no burden be brought in on the Sabbath day and threatened to lay hands on the merchants if they came again on the Sabbath (15-22)

Questions.Q: What caused Solomon to sin?
Questions.A: Outlandish women (26)

Questions.Q: What did Nehemiah do to the son-in-law of Sanballat?
Questions.A: Chased him away (28)

Questions.Q: During what period did the story of Ruth occur?
Questions.A: In the days when the judges ruled. (1)

Questions.Q: Who went to Moab?
Questions.A: Elimelech, his wife Naomi, and the name of his two sons Mahlon and Chilion. (2)

Questions.Q: Who was the first to die in Moab?
Questions.A: Elimelech (3)

Questions.Q: Who did Naomi's sons marry?
Questions.A: Orphah and Ruth (4)

Questions.Q: What happened to these sons?
Questions.A: They died (5)

Questions.Q: Why did Naomi decide to return from the country of Moab?
Questions.A: She heard in the country of Moab that the LORD had visited his people in giving them bread. (6-7)

Questions.Q: Why did Naomi encourage her daughters-in-law to stay in Moab?
Questions.A: She felt they had a better chance to find a husband in Moab (8-13)

Questions.Q: Who went back to her people?
Questions.A: Orphah (14-15)
Questions.Alternative: Who went back to her own people?
Who returned to her people?
Who returned to her own people?
Who went back to her homeland?

Questions.Q: How did Ruth reply?
Questions.A: Do not urge me to leave you, or to return from following after you. Where you go, I will go; and where you lodge, I will lodge. Your people will be my people, and your God will be my God. (16-18)
Questions.Alternative: How did Ruth respond?
What was Ruth's response?

Questions.Q: Why did Naomi want to be called Mara?
Questions.A: Because she felt the Almighty has dealt very bitterly with her. (19-21)
Questions.Alternative: Why did Naomi say that she should be called Mara?
Why did Naomi say that she should be called Mara instead of Naomi?

Questions.Q: At what season did Ruth and Naomi return to Bethlehem?
Questions.A: In the beginning of barley harvest. (22)

Questions.Q: To whom was Boaz related?
Questions.A: Elimelech (1)
Questions.Alternative: Who was Boaz's relative?
Who was Boaz's deceased relative?
Who had been related to Boaz?
Who had been part of the same family as Boaz?
To who was Boaz related?

Questions.Q: What did Ruth do in the field of Boaz?
Questions.A: Gleaned (2-4)

Questions.Q: What did Boaz ask Ruth to do?
Questions.A: Glean in his field, and abide with his maidens (5-9)

Questions.Q: What had Boaz heard about Ruth?
Questions.A: All that she had done for her mother in law since the death of her husband (10-12)
Questions.Alternative: What had people told Boaz about Ruth?
What had Boaz heard people saying about Ruth?

Questions.Q: What did Boaz tell his young men to do?
Questions.A: Let Ruth glean even among the sheaves, and reproach her not: And let fall also some of the handfuls of purpose for her, and rebuke her not (13-17)
Questions.Alternative: What instructions did Boaz give to his young men?
What instructions did Boaz give to his workers?
What did Boaz tell his workers to do?
What instructions did Boaz give to the young men who worked for him?

Questions.Q: How long was Ruth allowed to glean in the field of Boaz?
Questions.A: To the end of barley harvest and of wheat harvest (18-23)

Questions.Q: Where did Ruth lie down after Boaz fell asleep?
Questions.A: At the feet of Boaz (1-14)

Questions.Q: What did Ruth bring to Naomi?
Questions.A: Six measures of barley (15-18)

Questions.Q: What was the method of confirming a transfer of property?
Questions.A: A man plucked off his shoe, and gave it to his neighbor: (1-8)

Questions.Q: What did Boaz buy and acquire?
Questions.A: All that was Elimelech's, and all that was Chilion's and Mahlon's, and Ruth to be his wife (9-12)

Questions.Q: Who was Ruth's great-grandson?
Questions.A: David (13-22)

Questions.Q: What type of living things could be offered as a burnt offering?
Questions.A: Bullock, goat, lamb, turtledoves or pigeons. Of the animals it said males without blemish. (5, 10, 14)

Questions.Q: Who sprinkled the blood on the altar?
Questions.A: The priests, Aaron's sons (5, 11)

Questions.Q: Of what did the grain offering consist?
Questions.A: Fine flour with frankincense put on it. (1)

Questions.Q: What was not to be included in any grain offering?
Questions.A: Leaven or honey (11)

Questions.Q: With what was every grain offering to be seasoned?
Questions.A: Salt (13)

Questions.Q: What offering is described in this chapter?
Questions.A: Peace

Questions.Q: In what condition did the animals have to be in order to be offered?
Questions.A: Without blemish (1, 6)

Questions.Q: What were they not to eat?
Questions.A: Fat or blood (17)

Questions.Q: What was a priest to bring as a sin offering if he sins unintentionally?
Questions.A: A young bullock without blemish (1-12)

Questions.Q: What was the whole congregation to bring as a sin offering?
Questions.A: Young bullock (13-21)

Questions.Q: What was a ruler to bring as a sin offering?
Questions.A: A kid of the goats, a male without blemish (22-26)

Questions.Q: What was a common person to bring as a sin offering?
Questions.A: An unblemished female goat or lamb (27-35)

Questions.Q: What four things are mentioned for which a person could be guilty?
Questions.A: Not offering to testify when they hear a public charge to testify regarding something they have seen or known about (1)
touch any unclean animal or carcass (2)
Touch human uncleanness (3)
Impulsively swear to do something, whether good or bad, and it is hidden from him, and then he comes to realize it later (4)

Questions.Q: What should the person do who is guilty in one of these four things?
Questions.A: Confess that he has sinned and bring his trespass offering to the LORD (5)

Questions.Q: How did the offering for sin vary depending on what the person could afford?//How was the sin offering determined?
Questions.A: If he could not afford to bring a lamb, then he could bring for his trespass two turtledoves, or two young pigeons. But if he could not afford that, then he could bring for his offering the tenth part of an ephah of fine flour (6-13)
Questions.Alternative: How did the offering for sin vary depending on what the person could afford?
How was the sin offering determined?

Questions.Q: In order to make restitution what did a person who sinned unintentionally add to the offering?
Questions.A: A fifth part (15-16)

Questions.Q: For what other sins did a person add a fifth part as restitution?
Questions.A: That which he took violently away, or the thing which he has deceitfully gotten, or that which was delivered him to keep, or the lost thing which he found (1-7)

Questions.Q: What was to be kept burning?
Questions.A: The fire on the altar (8-13)

Questions.Q: What was done to the clay pot in which the meat for the sin offering was cooked?
Questions.A: It was broken (28)

Questions.Q: What two offerings were similar?
Questions.A: Sin offering and trespass offering (7)

Questions.Q: What offering was made as an expression of thankfulness?
Questions.A: Peace offering (11-12)

Questions.Q: What happened to a person who ate fat or blood?
Questions.A: He was cut off from his people (25-26)

Questions.Q: Who was given a share of the offerings?
Questions.A: The priests, Aaron and his sons (28-38)

Questions.Q: Who observed the consecration of Aaron and his sons?
Questions.A: The congregation (1-5)

Questions.Q: How long did the consecration ceremonies for Aaron and his sons last?
Questions.A: Seven days (31-36)

Questions.Q: Who stood before the Lord near the tabernacle?
Questions.A: All the congregation (5)

Questions.Q: Where did Moses and Aaron go after sacrificing the offerings?
Questions.A: Into the tabernacle of the congregation (22-23)

Questions.Q: What happened when they came out?
Questions.A: The glory of the LORD appeared to all the people and a fire consumed the burnt offering. When all the people saw this, they shouted, and fell on their faces. (23-24)

Questions.Q: What happened to Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aaron?
Questions.A: They offered strange fire before the LORD, a fire from the LORD devoured them (1-2)

Questions.Q: What were Aaron and his sons not to drink?
Questions.A: Wine or strong drink (8-9)

Questions.Q: What were Aaron and his sons to do?
Questions.A: Teach the Israelites all the statutes which the LORD had spoken to them by the hand of Moses (10-11)

Questions.Q: What type of animals were the Israelites allowed to eat?
Questions.A: Whatever parts the hoof, and is cloven footed, and chews the cud (1-8)

Questions.Q: What type of creatures in the sea were the Israelites allowed to eat?
Questions.A: Whatever has fins and scales (9-12)

Questions.Q: What birds were the Israelites not allowed to eat?
Questions.A: Any kind of eagle, ossifrage, vulture, osprey, buzzard, glede, kite, falcon, owl, hawk, stork, raven, or heron; ostrich, gull, cuckoo, swan, pelican, cormorant, hoopoe/lapwing; bats (13-19)
Questions.Alternative: What birds were they not to eat?
What birds were the Israelites not to eat?
What flying animals were they not to eat?
What flying animals were the Israelites not to eat?
What flying animals were the Israelites not allowed to eat?

Questions.Q: What type of flying insects were the Israelites allowed to eat?
Questions.A: Locusts, beetles, and grasshoppers (20-23)

Questions.Q: In what category were animals that walk on their paws?
Questions.A: Unclean (27-28)

Questions.Q: What other types of creatures were they not to eat?
Questions.A: Every creature that creeps/moves on the earth/ground, whether it moves on its belly or walks on all fours or on many feet (41-42)

Questions.Q: For how long was a woman ceremonially unclean after giving birth to a baby boy?
Questions.A: Seven days (1-2)

Questions.Q: On what day was a baby boy to be circumcised?
Questions.A: Eighth (3)

Questions.Q: How many more days was a woman purified from her bleeding after the birth of a baby boy?
Questions.A: Thirty- three (4)

Questions.Q: How did the time of uncleanness and purifying differ for a woman who gave birth to a daughter?
Questions.A: Twice as long (Fourteen days and sixty six days) (5)

Questions.Q: For what skin disease are extensive regulations given?
Questions.A: Leprosy (1-59)

Questions.Q: Who was involved in the ceremonial cleansing of the leper?
Questions.A: The priest (1-32)

Questions.Q: What was to be done to a house in which the leprosy continued to spread?
Questions.A: It was torn down and the stones, timber and mortar carried outside the city to an unclean place. (44-45)

Questions.Q: For what three conditions were laws given in this chapter?
Questions.A: A man with an unusual bodily discharge
A man who has an emission of semen
A woman who has her regular flow of blood (menstruation). (1-33)

Questions.Q: What happened to the scapegoat?
Questions.A: Aaron shall confess over it all the iniquities of the Israelites and send it away into the wilderness (10, 21-22)

Questions.Q: How often was atonement made for the Israelites?
Questions.A: Once a year (33-34)

Questions.Q: Where were the sacrifices to be brought?
Questions.A: The door of the tabernacle of the congregation (1-9)

Questions.Q: What was to be done to a person who ate blood?
Questions.A: Cut off from among his people (10)

Questions.Q: Where is the life of a creature?
Questions.A: In the blood (11, 14)

Questions.Q: With what persons of the opposite sex was an Israelite not to have sexual relations?
Questions.A: Those near of kin, including mother, step-mother, sister, step-sister, granddaughter, step-daughter, aunt, daughter-in-law, sister-in-law, woman put apart for her uncleanness, neighbor's wife (6-20)

Questions.Q: What is said of sexual relations with someone of the same sex?
Questions.A: Do not do it - it is an abomination (22)

Questions.Q: What is said of sexual relations with an animal?
Questions.A: Do not do it - it is a perversion/confusion (23)

Questions.Q: What did the land do to those who practiced such abominations?
Questions.A: It vomited out its inhabitants (the nations that preceded Israel) (24-28)

Questions.Q: Why are we to be holy?
Questions.A: Because the Lord your God is holy. (1-2)

Questions.Q: Which of the ten commandments are repeated in this chapter?
Questions.A: Honor/respect your mother and father. (3)
Observe the Sabbath. (3)
Don't make idols. (4)
Don't steal. (11, 13)
Don't misuse God's name. (12)
Don't lie/bear false witness. (11-12)
Questions.Note: See Exodus 20:2-17
This question should be skipped unless the respondent is someone who is expected to have familiarity with the Ten Commandments.

Questions.Q: What was to be left for the poor?
Questions.A: the grain in the corners of the field and the gleanings (9-10)

Questions.Q: How should we treat our neighbors?
Questions.A: Don't hate or hold a grudge, but rather love your neighbor as yourself (16-18)

Questions.Q: What was the law concerning tattoo marks?
Questions.A: You shall not print any marks on you (28)
Questions.Alternative: What was the law concerning tattoos?
What is said about tattoo marks?

Questions.Q: What is said about weights and standards?
Questions.A: The people were commanded to have just balances, just weights, and just measures. (35-36)

Questions.Q: For what sins was a person put to death?
Questions.A: Sacrificing children to Molech/Molek, cursing father or mother, adultery, homosexuality, having sexual relations with an animal, being a medium or spiritist/wizard (1-16, 27)

Questions.Q: For what sins was a person cut off from their people?
Questions.A: turning to mediums and spiritists (6)
seeing the nakedness of a near relative (17)
lying with a woman during her monthly period/uncleanness (18)

Questions.Q: Who was a priest not to marry?
Questions.A: a widow, a divorced woman, or a woman defiled by prostitution (7, 13-15)

Questions.Q: What physical defects were not allowed in a priest who made offerings?
Questions.A: No one with any defect was allowed, including the blind, the lame, hunchbacks, dwarves, or anyone with these defects: broken foot or hand, slit/disfigured face, scurvy/eczema, scabs, crushed testicles. (16-23)

Questions.Q: What were they not to eat?
Questions.A: any animal found dead, either of natural causes or that had been killed by wild beasts (8)

Questions.Q: Who was not allowed to eat of the holy things?
Questions.A: No one outside a priest's family, including a priest's guests or his hired workers (but slaves could); also, if a priest's daughter married anyone other than a priest, she could not eat any of the sacred contributions. (10-13)

Questions.Q: What were some of the feasts they were to keep during the year?
Questions.A: Passover, unleavened bread, first fruits, trumpets, atonement, tabernacles, booths (4-44)

Questions.Q: How long were the lamps to burn?
Questions.A: continually (1-4)

Questions.Q: What happened to the man who blasphemed the name of the LORD?
Questions.A: The congregation was to stone him to death. (10-16)

Questions.Q: How was the law different for a stranger?
Questions.A: There was no difference, but rather the same law for the stranger as well as for the Israelite. (17-22)

Questions.Q: What occurred every seventh year?
Questions.A: A Sabbath of rest to the land, where the fields were not sowed nor the vineyards pruned (1-7)

Questions.Q: What occurred every fiftieth year?
Questions.A: A year of jubilee where lands and people were restored and again no work done. (8-17)

Questions.Q: How was an Israelite to treat a poor Israelite whom he had purchased?
Questions.A: He was not to charge him usury/interest. (36-37)
He was not to treat him (harshly) as a slave. (39, 42-43)
Instead, he was to treat him as a hired servant. (40)
This was not to be perpetual bondage. He could only require the person to serve him until the Year of Jubilee. Then he had to be released (along with his family). (40-41)

Questions.Q: Who could redeem a fellow Israelite who had sold himself [into slavery]?
Questions.A: One of his kin (47-52)
Questions.Alternative: Who could redeem a fellow Israelite who had sold himself into slavery?
Who could redeem a fellow Israelite who had sold himself?
Who could buy back a fellow Israelite to free him from slavery?
Who could buy back a fellow Israelite out of slavery?
Who could help a fellow Israelite get free from slavery?
Who could help a fellow Israelite get out of slavery?

Questions.Q: What benefits would result if they kept God's commandments?
Questions.A: Rain in due season; the land would yield crops and trees would yield fruit. (4)
The people would eat their fill and have extra food. (5, 10)
The people would dwell in the land safely. (5)
Peace/freedom from fear and war. (6)
God would remove wild beasts from the land. (6)
The people would have victory over their enemies. (7-8)
God would show them favor, increase their numbers, and keep his covenant with them. (9)
God would live among them and not despise/reject them. (11-12)

Questions.Q: What problems would result if they did not keep God's commandments?
Questions.A: Sudden terror, wasting diseases and fever that would destroy their sight and sap their strength. They would sow seed in vain and their land and trees would not bear fruit. They would be defeated by their enemies, plagues, wild beasts, pestilence, eat the flesh of sons and daughters, cities waste, scattered among the heathen, no power to stand before enemies. (14-38)

Questions.Q: What would happen if in their enemies' land they confessed their iniquities?
Questions.A: God would remember His covenant with their ancestors; and would remember the land. God would not cast them away that He might be their God. (39-46)

Questions.Q: Why did God remind the people that he had freed them from slavery to Egypt?
Questions.A: He said this to show the people that he really cared about them and had the power to do all the good things he was promising if they would obey him.

Questions.Q: What was added to the price of redemption?
During the reign of what king did Zechariah prophesy?
Questions.A: Darius (1)

Questions.Q: What did the former prophets cry out?
Questions.A: "Turn away from your evil ways, and from your evil deeds." (4)

Questions.Q: How long did the LORD have indignation against Judah?
Questions.A: 70 years (12)

Questions.Q: What did the LORD say would be built in Jerusalem?
Questions.A: God's house (16)

Questions.Q: What was the man in the vision holding in his hand?
Questions.A: a measuring line (1)

Questions.Q: Who would be a wall about Jerusalem?
Questions.A: The LORD would be a wall of fire round about. (4-5)

Questions.Q: What do those who touch Zion touch also?
Questions.A: the apple of God's eye/God's prized possession (7-8)

What do those who harm Zion harm?
Harming Zion is like harming whom?
Harming Zion is like harming what?
In warning the nations not to harm Zion, what does God say Zion is like?

Questions.Q: Who stood before the angel of the LORD?
Questions.A: Joshua the high priest, and Satan standing at his right hand to accuse/resist him (1)

Questions.Q: What did the LORD say to Satan?
Questions.A: “The LORD rebuke you, Satan!” (2)
“The LORD, who has chosen Jerusalem, rebuke you!” (2)
“Is not this man [like a] a burning stick snatched from the fire?” (2)

Questions.Q: What was done for Joshua with regard to clothing?
Questions.A: His filthy garments were taken away and exchanged for a clean turban on his head and a change of garments. (3-5)

Questions.Q: What would be brought forth?
Questions.A: God's servant, the Branch (8)

Questions.Q: What did Zechariah see after being wakened out of his sleep?
Questions.A: a gold candlestick and two olive trees by it (1-3)
