Questions.Q: What did the word of the Lord say to Zechariah?
Questions.A: Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, says the LORD of hosts. (6)
Questions.Alternative: What did the Lord say to Zechariah?
What did God say to Zechariah?

Questions.Q: Who would lay the foundation of the house of the LORD and finish it?
Questions.A: Zerubbabel (9)

Questions.Q: What is not to be despised?
Questions.A: the day of small things (10)
Questions.Alternative: What should not be despised?
What did the LORD say not to despise?

Questions.Q: What did Zechariah see at the start of this chapter?
Questions.A: a flying scroll (1-4)

Questions.Q: What else did Zechariah see?
Questions.A: a woman sitting in a basket/ephah (5-8)

Questions.Q: Who had wings like the wing of a stork?
Questions.A: two women (9)

Questions.Q: Where did the two women take the basket?
Questions.A: to the country of Babylonia (11)

Questions.Q: What were the horses that came from between the mountains?
Questions.A: the four spirits of heaven (or of the heavens) (1-5)

Questions.Q: Upon whom was the crown set?
Questions.A: Joshua (11)
the son of Josedech, the high priest (11)

Who was crowned?
Who received the crown?

Questions.Q: What was the name of the man who would build the temple?
Questions.A: the Branch (12-13)

Questions.Q: What did the LORD of hosts say?
Questions.A: Execute true justice, and show mercy and compassion to one another. (9)
Do not oppress widows, nor the fatherless/orphans, the stranger, nor the poor. (10)
Do not plot evil against each other in your hearts. (10)
Questions.Alternative: What did the LORD of hosts command?
What did the LORD command?
What did God command?

Questions.Q: How did the people react to these words?
Questions.A: They refused to listen, they made their hearts hard as stone/flint so as not to hear the law or the words of the prophets. (11-12)

Questions.Q: For whom was the LORD jealous?
Questions.A: Zion (2)

Questions.Q: What will the LORD do for his people?
Questions.A: save them and bring them to Jerusalem (7-8)

Questions.Q: What blessings will the remnant of God's people experience?
Questions.A: prosperity, fruit/crops/produce, and dew/rain (12)
Questions.Alternative: What will the remnant of God's people possess?

Questions.Q: What does the LORD hate?
Questions.A: when people plot evil in their hearts against their neighbors, and love false oaths (lies that they swear are the truth) (17)

Questions.Q: What will many people and strong nations do?
Questions.A: seek the LORD of hosts in Jerusalem (22)

Questions.Q: Against what nations is judgment pronounced in this chapter?
Questions.A: Hamath, Tyre, and Sidon

Questions.Q: Why should Jerusalem rejoice greatly and shout?
Questions.A: Their king comes (9)

Questions.Q: What kind of prisoners should return to the fortress?
Questions.A: prisoners of hope -OR- prisoners with hope (12)

What kind of prisoners should return to the stronghold?

Questions.Q: For what should you ask in the time of the latter rain?
Questions.A: Showers of rain, to every one grass in the field. (1)

Questions.Q: What will the LORD do for the house of Judah and the house of Joseph?
Questions.A: strengthen, save, and have mercy on them (6)

Questions.Q: What did the LORD call the two staffs that He took?
Questions.A: Favor and Union (7)

Questions.Q: What happened to the two staffs?
Questions.A: They were cut in pieces. (10-11, 14)

Questions.Q: What prophecy did Zechariah make that Judas Iscariot fulfilled?
Questions.A: Judas sold Jesus for thirty pieces of silver. (12-13)

Questions.Q: What will the LORD make Jerusalem for all people?
Questions.A: an immovable/heavy rock (3)

Questions.Q: Like whom will the feeble among Jerusalem be?
Questions.A: David (8)
Questions.Alternative: Like whom will the feeblest among the people of Jerusalem be?
Like whom will the weakest among the people of Jerusalem be?
Like whom will the weakest among the inhabitants of Jerusalem be?
Who will the weakest people of Jerusalem be like?

Questions.Q: What will the LORD do to the nations that come against Jerusalem?
Questions.A: destroy them (9)

Questions.Q: On whom will the inhabitants of Jerusalem look?
Questions.A: on him whom they have pierced (10)

Questions.Q: What will be opened to the house of David?
Questions.A: A fountain for sin and for uncleanness (1)

Questions.Q: What phrase in Zechariah did Jesus quote referring to himself?
Questions.A: “Strike the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered.” (7)
Questions.Note: See Matthew 26:31.
This question should be skipped unless the respondent is someone who is expected to have familiarity with Matthew's gospel.

Questions.Q: Who will battle against Jerusalem?
Questions.A: all nations (2)
Questions.Alternative: Who will fight against Jerusalem?
Who will fight Jerusalem?
Who will go into battle against Jerusalem?

Questions.Q: What will happen to Jerusalem?
Questions.A: It will be captured, (2)
the houses will be ransacked/looted, (2)
and the women will be raped. (2)
Half of the people will go into captivity, (2)
And the other half will be left to live in the ruins of the city. (2)

Questions.Q: How much of Jerusalem will go into captivity?
Questions.A: half of the city (2)
Questions.Note: This question can be skipped if the respondent has already given the answer in response to the previous question.

Questions.Q: Who will fight against these nations?
Questions.A: the LORD (3)
Questions.Alternative: Who will fight against those nations?
Who will fight against the nations that have gathered to fight against Jerusalem?
Who will fight the nations that come against Jerusalem?

Questions.Q: What will happen to the mount of Olives?
Questions.A: It will be split in two [from east to west, forming a great valley]. (4)

Questions.Q: What will go out from Jerusalem?
Questions.A: living waters (8)

Questions.Q: What is said about the LORD?
Questions.A: The LORD shall be king over all the earth: in that day shall there be one LORD, and his name one. (9)

Questions.Q: With what plague will the LORD strike those who fight against Jerusalem?
Questions.A: Their flesh will rot while they are standing on their feet, and their eyes will rot in their sockets, and their tongues will rot in their mouths. (12)

Questions.Q: What will those who are left of the nations do each year?
Questions.A: They will go up every year to worship the King, the LORD of hosts, and to keep the feast of tabernacles. (16)

Questions.Q: What will happen to those who do not worship?
Questions.A: They will have no rain. (17-19)

Questions.Q: What will be [written] on the bells of the horses?
Questions.A: “Holy to the LORD.” (20)
Questions.Alternative: What will be on the bells of the horses?
What will be written on the bells of the horses?
